docs.title: PITF Wiki
docs.text:
Welcome to the fan wiki for PITF: Paranatural Incident Task Force, a Monster of the Week actual-play campaign run by Andre. The campaign is framed as a television show: sessions open cold, cut to credits, and follow a small FBI task force through an alternate early 1990s in which the strange cases are real and the cover stories are worse.

Spoilers

This wiki covers every recorded session and spoils all of them.

docs.title: Aaron Richters
docs.text:
Aaron Richters is a Spud Hut distribution-center worker in Dahlonega, Georgia, who walked out for a smoke break and never returned, becoming one of the missing people in The Things in Appalachia.

Type NPC (minor, never seen) Aliases Aaron; Richters Affiliation Spud Hut, Georgia Regional Distribution Center Status Missing (as of Appalachia 04) First appearance Appalachia 02 (mentioned)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Aaron is never seen on screen. He is known only through what his co-workers and the distribution center report: a smoker and a habitual no-show, with about nine unexcused absences in two years (Appalachia 03). He has also vanished before, when a hunting buddy offered an impromptu trip (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Appalachia 02, Edward Nick Sr. arrives for dinner at the trailer park in gray Spud Hut coveralls, exhausted. He explains that a co-worker, Aaron, went out for a smoke break in the middle of a shift and never came back, so Ed Sr. and a colleague named Ben had to cover. Servicing the plant machinery takes three people, and corporate will not shut the line down. Kurt asks Ed Sr. to call if Aaron does not turn up (Appalachia 02).

That episode's cold open shows an unnamed worker in a gray jumpsuit, with cigarettes and a lighter, who hears a baby-like cry from the woods behind the plant, squeezes into a cave and is attacked. The episode does not name him (Appalachia 02).

In Appalachia 03, Andrew phones the distribution center from the payphone at the Consolidated Gold Mine. The operator, Stacy, verifies his badge with the FBI and, eight minutes later, reports that the worker did not clock out the previous day and did not come in that day. She gives his name as Aaron Richters and offers to connect Andrew to Jan, who runs the center. His initials do not match the "HF" on the lighter recovered from the Dead Man in the Cave, so the players wonder whether the dead man is a different victim (Appalachia 03).

In Appalachia 04, Sheriff Burke tells Andrew that a check of Aaron's house has made him an officially missing person, and Andrew supplies the name. Burke later complains that he has five missing people in two days (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: Aaron's fate is never stated. It is never established whether he is the man in the cold open or the Dead Man in the Cave, or whether he was taken by the ape-men or by Jan Martense's operation (see Jan's Conspiracy). In Appalachia 09, the handler Clive is told about the missing kids, the truck driver and the Spud Hut workers, but Aaron is not named.

docs.title: Abelforth Whateley
docs.text:
Abelforth "Abe" Whateley was a space-obsessed teenager of Radford, Virginia and the twin brother of Wilbur Whateley. Three years before the task force arrived, he was believed to have robbed a Radio Shack in a homemade spacesuit and run away; the team later found a desiccated teenager nailed to the wall of the Whateley family's cellar.

Type NPC Aliases Abe; Abelforth Radford (Molly Underhill's usage in Radford Horror 05) Affiliation Whateley family Status Presumed dead; the sheriff's office was awaiting DNA and dental results in Radford Horror 08 First appearance Radford Horror 02 (discussed, never seen alive) Played by Andre (never appears in person)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Abe is known only through other people's accounts and his belongings. He was sixteen in the story's present, with a space and UFO obsession that began around age twelve; before that, his father said, he was "a fire truck kid" (Radford Horror 02). His room at the Whateley house was kept untouched like a shrine: a shuttle poster, star-and-moon pajamas, a UFO painting, and shelves of UFO and pop-science books. The Biz found old tennis shoes in the closet, close to the size of the footprints leading into the woods (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Abe and Wilbur were identical twins and childhood friends of Amanda Lucky. Their father Yobiah Whateley told the team that Abe's interest in space began at about twelve, and that the loss of the family dog shortly before Abe's "episode" had hit him hard. Abe talked to the man at the Pay n' Stay (Rutherford) and urged his mother to get Usenet access (Radford Horror 02). A neighbor, Meg Gunderson, blamed the whole affair on Abe and assumed drugs. The Biz speculated that Amanda might have been Abe's girlfriend; Andrew replied that she had been dating someone else at the time (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: The Radio Shack robbery
docs.text:
Three years before the story, Abe skipped a school presentation on a Mercury-replica spacesuit he had made. He threw a cinder block through a Radio Shack window wearing the suit, tried to take heavier equipment but could not lift it (which is how the police got his fingerprints), and left with lightweight modems, a cellular phone and other portable gear in a garbage bag. He bought a bus ticket to Richmond and was never seen again (Radford Horror 02). See Radio Shack spacesuit robbery.

The Biz found a hollowed-out copy of Where the Sidewalk Ends in Abe's room holding about $120-130, which led Andrew Howard to conclude the robbery was not about money. The Biz also found an AM/FM receive-only radio tuned to the same station the Pay n' Stay man listened to, where Art Bell airs later in the evening, plus overdue library books on astronomy and ufology. The Biz's early theory was that Abe had been contacted by aliens and was living in the woods (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: The APB
docs.text: In Radford Horror 05, Molly Underhill reported that the only database hit on fingerprints from a rooftop crime scene was the old electronics-store robbery, so "Abelforth Radford" was probably back in town. She put out an APB and sent someone to photograph his brother for up-to-date images (Radford Horror 05). Maybelline Augustine, mother of Phoebe Augustine, told Andrew that one of the twins had had an intense crush on Phoebe when they were younger, though she was not sure which, "because twins"; Phoebe had been badly affected by what happened to the boys (Radford Horror 05). See The Spaceman.

docs.title: The cellar
docs.text: At night, Kurt found rotten cellar doors with a padlock under a tarp at the back of the Whateley garage. Inside the low cellar, behind hanging tarps, the team found the discarded pieces of a spacesuit, a dog skeleton, and a desiccated body in a NASA T-shirt, nailed through the wrists and ankles to the wall, with the side of the head stove in. The body was too dry for the damp conditions, and a fibrous, root-like growth was wrapped around a floor joist. The face was too withered to read, but the team took the body to be Abelforth's (Radford Horror 06). The crucifixion echoed the method used on Amanda; see Crucifixion MO.

docs.title: The sheriff's theory
docs.text: After the climax, the sheriff told the team that the hidden basement held a spaceman costume with a journal, and that the cadaver was probably Abelforth, who "never ran away at all." His theory was that Wilbur came downstairs dressed as his brother, pretended to leave, then climbed back in through his window and came down as himself, so that both boys appeared to have gone. Wilbur's journal has entries for April 16-18; the players worked out that Abe's disappearance matched April 17, the entry reading "I did something." On April 16 Wilbur wrote that Abe would not stop looking for the dog, and a later entry mentions that Abe was always telling him about picking up radio on fillings. The team concluded that the creature in the journal, the Radford Moth, had manipulated Wilbur (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Wilbur Whateley: identical twin; the sheriff concluded Wilbur killed him.
  • Yobiah and Irene Whateley: his parents.
  • Amanda Lucky: childhood friend.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Dante repeatedly called him "Albert", and the twins' names were mixed up at the table throughout the arc (Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 08).
  • Dante joked that the family had only itself to blame for naming the boys Abelforth and Wilbur (Radford Horror 02).
  • It is never established which twin was older, or which twin had the crush on Phoebe.

docs.title: Agent Murphy
docs.text:
Agent Murphy is a black-suited man who stepped out in front of the task force's car on a Radford mountain highway, claimed to be with the NSA, burned Kurt with a handheld beam device, and died in the woods soon afterward.

Type NPC (deceased) Aliases The NSA man; burning man; the hitchhiker; Murphy Affiliation Claimed NSA; never verified Status Dead; remains collected by the team First appearance Radford Horror 03 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Murphy is a man in a black suit with a briefcase and a flashlight-shaped beam device (Radford Horror 03). His badge and wallet ID name him as NSA, but his real identity is never learned. The table treated him as a Men in Black type.

docs.title: The hit-and-run
docs.text:
At dusk, Kurt and the Biz were driving a commandeered diesel car up the mountain (see Howard and his wife) at about 50 mph when a large silent dark object circled over them and flared blue under their flashlights. Murphy stepped out ahead of the car and Kurt hit him (Radford Horror 03).

Kurt and the Biz found him on the road, vomiting blood and clutching the flashlight and briefcase. He refused a hospital and tried to walk back into the woods, saying he was camping and had no identification with him. When Kurt grabbed him, he pulled out a badge: "I'm Agent Murphy. I'm NSA. You are fucking this up for me. Get back in your car and drive away." (Andre, as Agent Murphy.) Kurt kept hold of him, and Murphy turned the flashlight on him. It gave an intense blue-purple flash and a rapid electric clacking, set Kurt's shirt on fire for 3 harm, and blinded both agents for 30 to 45 seconds. Kurt then bit open the "LSD tooth", one of his special molars, and spat the dose into Murphy's mouth. Murphy screamed and fled, firing the device wildly behind him so that a tree burst into flame, and dropped off a small ledge into the dark (Radford Horror 03).

Kurt did not believe Murphy was NSA, since the CIA had no portable beam weapons and he doubted the NSA did. The Biz suspected a secret NSA project, and Andrew leaned toward aliens (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Death in the woods
docs.text: The players did not see Murphy's end. In a cut-away in Radford Horror 03, a panicking Murphy with a fractured skull and one eye partly out of its socket shot at birds until the device overheated and he vanished in a pulse of light. The cold open of Radford Horror 04 follows directly, showing what the pulse left: his slumped, smoldering figure against a tree in the burning woods as a coyote begins to eat him (Radford Horror 03; Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: The remains
docs.text:
After the team left the ER, Kurt followed faded blood to a clearing where mildly high coyotes were devouring what was left. A circle of ground had been melted to glass. Of Murphy there remained the back of the suit, the back of the skull, a little brain, and the briefcase reduced to a melted wad. Kurt found a handful of scorched teeth for dental identification, along with the NSA ID, and bagged about two pounds of remains. Kurt assumed the device had exploded, but no trace of it could be found (Radford Horror 04).

The warped briefcase held a melted wireless telegraph with a Morse key, and loose, badly burned pages on plain paper with no letterhead. Kurt said, "I've seen some classified NSA documents in my time, and this doesn't look like any of 'em." (Radford Horror 04) See Murphy's briefcase and documents and Flashlight weapon.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: Kurt carried the remains in a cooler, along with a dog skull and a couple of beers, into the Ferry Lodge (Radford Horror 05). In Radford Horror 07, when the team found Dean Lawson's Samsonite briefcase, Dante asked whether it matched the NSA agent's; Andre said Murphy's was not a brand the team recognized (Radford Horror 07). In Radford Horror 08, Kurt's illegal contact examined the badge. It appeared genuine, but no one by that name appears in the records. Kurt concluded, "I didn't kill an NSA agent, officially." (Radford Horror 08) The cleanup crew at the end of that episode carried the same kind of flashlight; see The cleanup crew.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Who Murphy really was and who sent him.
  • How he came to carry a portable beam weapon, and whether he was connected to the silent craft that circled the car at the moment he appeared.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• After the fight Kurt put on a welding mask before handling the remains: "Never approach a hitchhiker without a welding mask." (Radford Horror 04)
  • Dante objected at the table that the FBI would never let a man they had just hit with their car, vomiting blood, walk off into the forest (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Alberta Wilmarth
docs.text:
Alberta Wilmarth ("Alby") is the owner of a Utah ranch near Ballard who hires Andrew Howard to force the exhumation of her dead mother, and who dotes on her enormous goose, Nancy.

Type NPC (client) Aliases Alberta; Alby; Madeline (Bigelow's slip); the client; the goose's owner Affiliation Owner of Sherman Ranch; landlord of Robert Bigelow Status Alive (as of Walkers 05); lives off-site First appearance Walkers 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Alberta is a ranch owner who tends the pig pen and wears sunscreen on her nose (Walkers 02). She believes in aliens but not ghosts, and is "on the right side of history" for it, according to Rita's Andrew (Walkers 02). She is blunt and practical: when the team finds a cavern under her land she guesses a natural gas bed and worries about mineral rights and foundations (Walkers 05).

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Her mother, Shelly Wilmarth, died of a heart attack in winter 1990, alone with the cattle, and had refused to leave the ranch. Alberta says she has only brothers, so there is no secret twin (Walkers 01). She no longer lives on the property and has rented the big house and barn to the billionaire Robert Bigelow (Walkers 02, Walkers 05).

docs.title: Walkers 01: the client
docs.text:
Alberta visits Andrew's apartment with a box of documents and tapes and says, "I need you to force the Mormon church to exhume my mom." The box holds an obituary, a yearbook photo, a reunion photo and a VHS copy of local news footage of a community-centre protest in which her mother appears. Her ranch tenant, "the space guy," has seen the dead woman walking the edge of the property at night. Her pitch is: "She's not a ghost... She's just alive again." Andrew feeds her leftovers. She leaves dazed after he works doppelgangers back onto his list, and calls the ranch "cursed" (boiled cattle, missing pets, UFO lights, Navy radiation investigators) (Walkers 01). See Alberta's box.

Alberta tells Andrew her mother died "two years ago," but the obituary clipping she hands over dates the death to the winter of 1990; the discrepancy is never addressed (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Walkers 02: at the ranch
docs.text:
Andrew has stayed in touch with her (Zack jokes, "They're dating"). She offers the "grandma cottage" on the ranch (guest double-wide) and promises to warn security so the team is not shot. At the pig pen she greets "Detective Howard" until he corrects her to "special agent," then settles on "Howard." She is surprised the FBI took her seriously. She asks Walt Murphy to fix fence posts that were pulled up overnight, which she blames on coyotes, and says the ranch always hums at night, perhaps from the substation. She urges the team to look into the exhumation, and Kurt promises they will. She says she will never sell to the town (Walkers 02).

When Nancy the goose charges Kurt, she calls her a "big softie," and Walt's vow to eat the goose draws: "Don't you dare, Walt. She's a beautiful, innocent, pure soul." Bigelow calls her "Madeline" and corrects himself (Walkers 02).

docs.title: Walkers 03 and 04: offscreen
docs.text: She does not appear. The team recaps her request, and the exhumation plan continues (Walkers 03); see Exhumation of Shelly Wilmarth. In Walkers 04, Walt notes that the goose's owner loves it, so no one will kill it (Walkers 04).

docs.title: Walkers 05: the cavern
docs.text:
Around 5 p.m. the team finds Alberta in her pickup bed with the goose calm in her lap. Kurt tells her the exhumation is going through, that the car vanished and reappeared magnetized, and that a coyote on two legs followed him. She replies, "If he's on two legs and following you, that's probably one of the weird ones," and "There's a reason I don't live here anymore." When she moves to set the goose down, the team flees. Later Kurt phones her about the cavern, and she asks them to tell no one until she works out "the play" (Walkers 05); see The cavern.

After this she is mentioned in the arc only as the goose's owner and the exhumation's requester (Walkers 07).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Andrew Howard: her point of contact; she trusts him (Walkers 02). See Andrew Howard.
  • Nancy the goose: docile only with Alberta (Walkers 02).
  • Robert Bigelow: her tenant at the big house.

docs.text:
Quote

"She's not a ghost... She's just alive again." (Walkers 01)

Quote

"There's a reason I don't live here anymore." (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Her surname is spelled "Wilmarth" by Andre; Dante heard "Wilmerth" (Walkers 03).

docs.title: Amanda Lucky
docs.text:
Amanda Lucky is the 17-year-old cheerleader whose disappearance from a locked third-story bedroom brings the task force to Radford, Virginia in the first case of the campaign. Her body, crucified and partly eaten, is found by the interstate.

Type NPC (victim) Aliases Amanda Affiliation Patient of Dr. Lawrence Lori; girlfriend of Dean Lawson Status Dead (body found in Radford Horror 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01 (as a case file) Played by Andre (never appears alive on screen, except in a flashback cold open)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Sheriff Roosevelt describes Amanda as a cheerleader and "real kind of all-American girl" who had nevertheless landed in the cells a couple of times for intoxication, and who had been seen "running around with a couple of boys, not just her boyfriend": Dean Lawson, the biker Matt McCready and, back in middle school, the Whateley twins (Radford Horror 01). She vanished in her pajamas with no belongings (Radford Horror 02). Her parents, Liam Lucky and Sarah, are devout Catholics who wait by the phone. Both point the finger at McCready, and her father says she had been seeing a therapist, Dr. Lori, for her grades (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: The disappearance
docs.text:
The task force's case file says Amanda vanished from her locked third-story bedroom and that the only witness, an insomniac four-year-old named Tyler, saw a spaceman take her (Radford Horror 01). The file puts her disappearance two days earlier; the sheriff says three. The bedroom hangs over a carport with a long drop and no impact marks. The door was locked from inside. The agents found:

  • a loosened drainpipe above the window;
  • a hollow bedpost holding bottles of Xanax and Vicodin prescribed by Dr. Lori (see Amanda's prescriptions);
  • a diary with its pages removed (see Amanda's diary);
  • a bent metal smokestack on the roof, reachable by a trellis, with scratch marks.

They concluded she left voluntarily, upward onto the roof (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: The investigation
docs.text: The pill stash led the team to Dr. Lori. He said he had treated her for about three years for anxiety and depressive tendencies, prescribed only Xanax, and denied writing Vicodin. Under pressure he said Amanda told him Dean Lawson was involved in drugs. The pharmacist, however, showed a Vicodin record under Lori's name from about a year earlier (Radford Horror 02). Kurt later found a pink butterfly hair tie in the Augustine barn, a clue pointing toward Phoebe Augustine (Radford Horror 03). The fingerprints on the roof matched the old spaceman robbery (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: The body
docs.text:
At the end of Radford Horror 04, Molly Underhill told the team that the body of a young girl, probably Amanda, had been found by the interstate. Much of the face was gone and some organs eaten, which the examiner put down to an animal after death (Radford Horror 04). Dr. Harvey Mauden, who had delivered her as a baby, performed the autopsy in the next episode:

  • She had been crucified, but was not restrained when she died.
  • She was dressed in a nightgown, so had no pockets, and was barefoot.
  • Toxicology found a lot of opiates and traces of Xanax, enough to sedate someone who should not have been walking.
  • A needle mark from the previous couple of days sat among older scars, suggesting a past drug habit.
  • A pink butterfly hair tie was stuck in her blood-matted hair, like the one from the Augustine barn.
  • She had been dead no more than a couple of hours.

(Radford Horror 05). The cold open of that episode was a flashback of her. At the scene, a diffuse ring of blood spatter about five feet across lay over her bare footprints, which led back into the woods; there was no sign of anyone pursuing her (Radford Horror 05). See Highway crime scene and Crucifixion MO.

In Radford Horror 06, the doctor reported that about five percent of her blood volume was an unidentified foreign substance, and that her blood showed markers of severe malnutrition even though her body did not (Radford Horror 06). In Radford Horror 07, Dante resolved to have Dean's heroin compared with what was in her system (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: In Radford Horror 08, the sheriff told the team that Dr. Lori and Derek Augustine had both confessed to an inappropriate sexual relationship with Amanda. Each had learned the other was involved, and Derek then attacked Lori believing he was doing the same to his daughter. Dante's own theory was that Amanda was crucified, escaped thanks to her heroin tolerance, and was then killed by "the mob" to stop information spreading; the team did not settle whether the Radford Moth was responsible. Wilbur's journal contains the line "I don't think Amanda knows, but I feel like Phoebe might." (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Dean Lawson: boyfriend. Phoebe did not get along with him and had fought with Amanda about him, according to Phoebe's mother (Radford Horror 05).
  • Phoebe Augustine: friend.
  • Abelforth and Wilbur Whateley: childhood friends who lived down the street. The sheriff said she had been "involved" with the twins when they were in middle school (Radford Horror 01).
  • Matt McCready: friend. He told the team that Dean threatened to have him killed when he asked when Dean had last seen her, and that about a week earlier Amanda had seemed to want to tell him something at school (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• During Radford Horror 08, Dante pitched a joke cold open in which Amanda's corpse explodes and a thousand moths come out (Radford Horror 08).
  • The episodes never establish who killed her.

docs.title: Amos Shaw
docs.text:
Amos Shaw is the unnaturally fit preacher of Marblehead's ocean-obsessed church, who serves fishy communion wine and owns the blood-soaked house the team finds in The Summer Service.

Type NPC Aliases Mr. Shaw; the preacher; the priest Affiliation Sons of Adam; Marblehead Board of Selectmen Status Alive and in the early stage of bloating at the selectmen's meeting (Summer Service 04) First appearance Summer Service 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Shaw is about 60 but built like a bodybuilder, with a healthy glow and a bounding, light-footed gait. His grip is iron, and Kurt Larson suspects steroids. He wears homemade white vestments imitating Catholic ones and insists on "Mr. Shaw," not "Father" (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
At the 9 p.m. service, Shaw reads Revelation 13 (the seven-headed beast from the sea) and preaches that angels are terrifying monsters built by God to wipe out sin, and that good is not the same as nice. He argues that Noah's "floodgates of heaven" imply a source of holy water, and that the world comes from water and returns to it. He asks, "Was Christ not himself a fisherman?", which goes over well with the fishermen in the pews. Communion is wine only, the "Blood of the Lamb" (Summer Service 01). See Communion wine and Second coming and eschaton.

Afterward he introduces himself to the team, calls Jester "very devout," and tells Andrew Howard, who complains that everyone takes him for a fed, to "be yourself." He recommends the fish breakfast, says he is trying a "new format" with softer notes, and scolds the Biz for swearing in "God's house." Asked about the wine, he calls it "a local variety." Kurt catches a flicker of reaction when the flavor is mentioned, but cannot interpret it (Summer Service 01).

In Summer Service 03, Huell Kendrick walks into an unlocked house whose door has been open for days. The mail is all addressed to Amos Shaw. Inside are crucifixes, a bachelor's furnishings, a burned-out pan, a blood smear, a long gouge through the hallway wall, a burst-open bathroom door and a wrecked bathroom. The bedroom shelves hold academic biblical books beside fringe Lemuria material, clerical garments (some missing) hang in the closet, and the nightstand holds an improvised grocery bag with about ten pounds of clear crystal spheres like Jester's (Summer Service 03). See Amos Shaw's house and Crystal marbles.

Donald McManley judges the blood three or four days old, and because Andrew met Shaw alive in that window, the dead body is someone else's. At the 7 a.m. service Shaw is absent; a replacement preacher, opalescent and bloated, hands Andrew the cup and says "Blood of Christ" (Summer Service 03). See The Mayor of Marblehead.

At the evening selectmen's meeting in Summer Service 04, the team sees that the actual priest is also among the selectmen. Dante confirms with Andre that he is the man whose house looked as if someone had exploded in it. He smiles amiably at the team and shows an early stage of the bloating that is far advanced in the mayor and the chief of police. Andre rules that the team has grounds to arrest him on suspicion of murder, and Andrew asks to pull him aside after the meeting (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes never identify the body in his house or explain what burst the bathroom door from inside, and they do not say why Shaw missed the 7 a.m. service.

docs.text:
Quote

"Was Christ not himself a fisherman?" Andre (as Amos Shaw) (Summer Service 01)

Quote

"Be yourself... There are worse things to be." Andre (as Amos Shaw), to Andrew (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Andrew Howard (duplicate)
docs.text:
Andrew Howard (duplicate) is the flawed, sickly skinwalker copy of FBI agent Andrew Howard who takes his place after the Ballard gym fight, travels with the task force while secretly working for the skinwalkers, and dies in the cavern under the community center.

Type Skinwalker clone (played by a player in secret) Aliases Skinwalker Howard; fake Howard; X Howard; the replica; clone Andrew; Andrew Howard's double; the double Affiliation Skinwalker faction Status Dead: shot in the back in the cavern, left in the collapsing cavern while the creature that controlled him escaped (Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 07 Played by Rita (secretly, from the end of the gym scene in Walkers 07 to the middle of Walkers 09); Andre afterward

Which Andrew is which

In Walkers 06 Rita still plays the real Andrew, and the only hint of a double is a dream he remembers. The switch happens in Walkers 07 at the end of the gym scene: when the double's tendrils enter Andrew's mouth and "everything goes black," Andre hands Rita a private document and tells her, "you are not in Andrew Howard's body. You are in a replica." The gym double and the replica are the same individual: when Rita asks whether she is a new copy rather than "the one that barfed in his mouth," Andre answers, "You are the one that barfed in his mouth." Rita plays the replica for the rest of Walkers 07, all of Walkers 08 and the first part of Walkers 09, without the other players' characters knowing. The real Andrew's later story is on Andrew Howard (the Monstrous).

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In the school gym the real Andrew finds a man identical to himself sitting on a stool; the double waves enthusiastically and greets him (Walkers 07). When pepper spray hits him, his head briefly vanishes, revealing cross-sections of colors "not supposed to be in the human head," and he collapses in a grand mal seizure (Walkers 07).

The replica that leaves the gym is badly hurt and passes as the real man: sunny, fussy about FBI protocol (wants to call things in and not disturb scenes), insistent that he is "not a hippie" while knowing meditation techniques, and keen to take analog photographs of every scene (Walkers 08). By Walkers 09 he is sickly, sweaty and bruised on the arms, and refuses to open his mouth (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Abilities and flaws
docs.text:
• Copies are grown from tissue samples and are made in a hurry. Rita's private document says the replica is wrong and deteriorates over time, and that the sickness is leukemia; Andre explains that the faction took Andrew's tissue from the cut left by the ring on the mayor's hand, and Huell's from the bite of the "homeless" man (Walkers 07). See Replication.
  • The replica can eat only sugar, like other skinwalker hosts, and carries a tendril-bearing creature that can enter a victim's mouth (Walkers 08). See Pilot and host biology.
  • Tells in Walkers 08: a roll of 3 in a firefight makes him panic and shatter one of the car's windows, and he is shot in the shoulder; when he tries to heal the Biz, nothing happens; Rita jokes, "Since apparently I can be shot now"; and he is fascinated by the pilot organ the team recovers (Walkers 08).

docs.title: Walkers 06: dream
docs.text: Before he woke in the fridge, the real Andrew had dreamed of taking out the trash at his D.C. apartment and meeting a naked version of himself, who chased him through the alleys into the desert, smiling (Walkers 06).

docs.title: Walkers 07: replacement
docs.text:
At the gym the double tells Andrew, "We can do this the easy way or the hard way." The easy way is to open his mouth unnaturally wide and extend fine gray tendrils from his throat to "kiss" Andrew; the hard way is a shotgun. Andrew asks, "What, replacing me? With you, I assume?" After a long fight, the double, with a chunk of his shoulder blown off by a grenade, crawls over the pinned Andrew, and sweet-tasting vomit and tendrils enter Andrew's mouth. Rita is then told that the skinwalker faction already holds about 60 percent of the town (Walkers 07).

The replica staggers out, bloodied, to Huell, telling him townsfolk tried to kidnap him and that he used a grenade. He leaves the double out of the story he tells Kurt and the Biz (Walkers 07). See Ballard High School and Plastic-wrapped bodies.

docs.title: Walkers 08: inside the team
docs.text:
The replica photographs the Roosevelt police station, argues for procedure at the ambush site, and keeps the iridescent pilot organ in a Tupperware (Walkers 08). See Pilot organ in Tupperware and Sugar clues.

The team does not learn what he is during the session. At its end Rita tells the table that she was the one who stole the sugar from the break room, because it is all she can eat, and that she deliberately got hold of the Biz's blood so the faction could begin preparing a copy of him, though without his memories they could not yet replace him (Walkers 08).

docs.title: Walkers 09: unmasking
docs.text:
An unrecorded session ("08.5") came between Walkers 08 and Walkers 09. What happened in it is known only from Walkers 09: the replacement rode with the team, spent an afternoon with the goose Nancy and rode in the Humvee with the National Guard major (Walkers 09). See Lost episodes.

The party marks itself with Sharpie to tell skinwalkers apart, and the duplicate wears a mark. A naked, subtly inhuman "runner" approaches the group shouting that he is the real Howard and asking Huell to check whether the other eats solid food. Kurt asks the marked Howard to open his mouth for a check; he refuses, shoots Kurt in the leg and bolts. Huell chases him down on horseback. When Huell shoves his fingers into the duplicate's mouth, gray tendrils pull a memory out of him: his father, Thomas Kendrick, eating bacon. Andre then announces, "Now that the game is up, Rita, let's swap back who we're controlling": Rita returns to the real Howard and Andre takes over the skinwalker Howard, who has four harm (Walkers 09).

In the cavern the skinwalker Howard limps about wearing the real Howard's suit. Cornered, he attacks the party. Kurt and the real Howard bring him to one harm, and the real Howard shoots him in the back, shouting, "You weren't even gonna tell my mom that I got stolen?" The creature wriggles out of his mouth and scurries away, and the body is left in the collapsing cavern (Walkers 09). See The cavern, The portal and Skinwalkers.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• The real Andrew: the original, who calls his copy the "clone freak" and demands his pants back (Walkers 09).
  • The Biz: the duplicate took his blood (Walkers 08).
  • Huell: the copy's tendrils pulled a memory from Huell's mouth; a separate clone, Skinwalker Huell, also exists.

docs.title: Andrew Howard (the Monstrous)
docs.text:
Andrew Howard (the Monstrous) is the real Andrew Howard after he dies in the Ballard gym fight and revives at the bottom of the Roosevelt morgue pile, changed into something inhuman: two heartbeats, a craving for blood, a running speed of about 35 mph and a body that shrugs off small-arms fire.

Type Player character (changed playbook) Aliases Monstrous Andrew; the real Howard; the Runner; Divine Howard Affiliation Paranatural Incident Task Force Status Alive (as of Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 08 (closing scene) Played by Rita

Which Andrew is which

From the end of the gym fight in Walkers 07 until the unmasking in Walkers 09, the Andrew traveling with the team is the duplicate. This page covers the original man, who is absent from the team's story for those sessions. His earlier life is on Andrew Howard.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In his Walkers 08 scene he wakes naked, bound in duct tape and plastic at the bottom of the morgue pile in Roosevelt, covered in corpse fluid and shot through the heart. Rita describes the rebuilt character as a "beefy boy" who still has some ethereal quality, "just darker now" (Walkers 08). In Walkers 09 he wears a space-blanket toga and bloody underwear for a time and carries Nancy the goose (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Background
docs.text: The real Andrew was replaced in the Ballard school gym, where the faction cloned him from tissue taken when the mayor's ring cut his hand (Walkers 07). See Andrew Howard (duplicate). His death is never shown. His own account in Walkers 09: he lost time after pulling the pin on a grenade in the gym and took a couple of his attackers with him, was shot point-blank in the chest, and woke in the morgue under a pile of bodies. He estimates he was gone a day or two. He says he found "no God up there" and wonders whether "dad alien" was there either (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Walkers 08: reborn
docs.text: After the other players sign off, Andre cuts to "the other Andrew Howard," who is dead and finds it agonizing, since "he had always been told that being dead doesn't hurt." Something violent shifts inside him and he spasms back to life, naked and wrapped in plastic at the bottom of the corpse pile in the police station morgue. Andre tells Rita her class has changed to the Monstrous and that she must rebuild the character. "They killed you. It just didn't stick," Andre says, and adds that this was always going to happen if Andrew died; the inhuman parts of him "refuse to let you die," at the cost of his humanity. Rita retires the Divine playbook but keeps What I Need When I Need It, which is tied to an item (Walkers 08). See Roosevelt police station.

docs.title: Walkers 09: the Runner
docs.text:
A naked, blood-covered, subtly inhuman Andrew Howard sprints toward the party at inhuman speed. The party has marked itself with Sharpie to tell skinwalkers from people, and the Howard beside Huell, who is the duplicate, and Huell both shoot at the runner; the runner drops, rolls and keeps coming. He shouts that he is the real Howard, asks Huell to check whether the other eats solid food, and cries that he woke under a pile of dead naked people. Kurt cuffs and tapes him; he notes he is the first of the skinwalkers to talk or show self-preservation, and the most durable. The runner tells Huell: "I would like my pants back from the clone freak, if possible." (Walkers 09)

Once the duplicate is exposed, Rita returns to playing the real Howard. He eats freeze-dried mac and cheese and keeps it down, and Kurt agrees to unhandcuff him. Kurt sends word to the Guard: "Other Howard is not to be trusted. This is the new Howard." Nancy arrives along his trail, and Rita jokes that Nancy is Andrew's middle name. Huell holds a gun on him and asks about a cigar-shaped craft, a test of identity. In the cavern he recovers his ruined suit, fanny pack and religious pendant from a Ziploc bag marked "Hazardous" with several exclamation points, and he shoots the duplicate in the back. The skinwalkers' return fire cannot hurt him. Andre remarks, "It's funny, Howard, that the way that you proved you were human was by being bulletproof." (Walkers 09) See Andrew's pendant and What I Need When I Need It bag.

He ends the arc with the surviving party: fast, bulletproof, uncanny, with the goose, pendant and bag, and angry for the first time. He takes a few dozen blurry Polaroids as hazmat teams clear bodies (Walkers 09). See Hazmat cleanup teams.

docs.title: Abilities and equipment
docs.text:
• Playbook: Monstrous, formerly Divine. He dropped Lay on Hands and Cast Out Evil and kept What I Need When I Need It. Stats: Charm -1, Cool -1, Tough 2, Weird 3. The leukemia that Andre mentions during the same conversation ("you have leukemia, and you don't feel great") belongs to the replica Rita is still playing, as first established in her Walkers 07 briefing, and not to the real Andrew (Walkers 07, Walkers 08).
  • Moves: Rita chose the Immortal and Unquenchable Vitality moves, with Resilience again; Mental Dominion, Unnatural Appeal, Preternatural Speed and Unholy Strength were all discussed. Any time harm is healed she says he heals an extra point, and wounds count as one harm less (Walkers 08).
  • Natural attack and curse: Rita chose a ranged life drain. Andre offered Feed (needing regular blood) or Vulnerability (an allergy to metal), and the character does drink blood, in Andre's words "a very tough boy who now has to drink blood" (Walkers 08).
  • Physical: runs about 35 mph ("About that. Since I woke up. In the morgue."); shrugs off two harm from small arms (Walkers 09).
  • See Game mechanics and Andrew's Condition, the later arc's treatment of his blood hunger and bullet resistance.

docs.text:
Quote

  • In Walkers 09 Rita jokes that Andrew's middle name is Nancy, after the goose (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Andrew Howard
docs.text:
Andrew Howard is an FBI special agent, the nominal leader of the Paranatural Incident Task Force, and a lifelong member of the Aetherius Society who sincerely believes that benevolent extraterrestrial Masters are guiding humanity.

Type Player character Aliases Howard; "Andrew the Alien"; "Half-Gallon Howard"; Special Agent Howard; Detective Howard; Officer Howard; "Changeling" (the Radford Moth); "Twinky Doomguy" (table nickname) Playbook The Divine (to Walkers 07); the Monstrous (from Walkers 08) Affiliation FBI; Paranatural Incident Task Force; Aetherius Society Home Washington, DC (apartment); raised in California Status Alive, changed, and on rabies treatment (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Rita

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Andrew is 34 at the start of the campaign, "the baby face of the bunch," a lanky "green bean" of a man who passes the Bureau's fitness tests and knows his exact body measurements. He wears a suit and tie almost everywhere, including a pig pen, and prefers it to the blazer Kurt Larson recommends. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 04, Appalachia 08, Walkers 04)

Everyone he meets takes him for a federal agent on sight. A Radford security guard told him he looked "the most like a Fed of anyone I've ever seen," a Georgia motel clerk saw through a Bigfoot T-shirt at once, and the table measures other characters on a "scale of one to Howard." He never denies it. (Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 01, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 06)

In manner he is friendly, earnest, polite ("sir," "ma'am") and painfully awkward. He infodumps about UFOs, rambles honestly to his superiors and raises his hands when a child hugs him. Rita plays him with Charm at -1 and has explained what that means: not that he is a bad person or annoying, "it's just you can always tell there's something wrong with me." He does better with children, older people and dogs. (Summer Service 03, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 07, Walkers 03)

At home he lives alone in a small DC apartment with no pets, eats bland food ("allergy to spice"), avoids the news, jogs in high white socks and a sweatband, and belongs to mail and BBS fandom communities. He sleeps in a full set of striped pajamas, hat included. He barely listens to music; the table's verdict is that the music he would like "doesn't exist yet." (Radford Horror 01, Walkers 01, Walkers 03, Walkers 07)

Since his death and return in Utah he has been subtly different: an uncanny tint to his skin, perhaps slightly taller, an unnerving aura, and a healthy look that comes from drinking blood. Andre describes it as "the very subtle change that has come over Andrew Howard since he died." (Walkers 09, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Andrew is from California and was raised alone by a devout mother inside her church, the Aetherius Society. He was homeschooled, grew up with a family doctor who was also a member, and describes the whole thing as being "raised in a really weird sort of situation" and, later, as a cult he has been in since childhood. He has never known his father. (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 01, Walkers 03, Radford Horrors 03)

The faith teaches that the Masters are humanoid, mostly off-planet and telepathic, that Jesus is one of them, and that cosmic forces pushing humanity toward violence are held back by a "spiritual battery" of good energy. In the campaign's opening flashback his mentor Mr. King told him that "the next master is coming" within a few years, and that "Jesus and the Buddha were not wholly of this world, and neither are you." (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 01, Walkers 01)

His childhood was marked by sleep trouble: "succubus" sleep paralysis, dreams of gray men or aliens crouching over him or licking his face, and an episode in which his mother tied him in a sleeping bag for about a week because, he says, "I kept lashing out." (Summer Service 03, Appalachia 03)

At the FBI he was a desk worker who "had no expectations of being a field agent." He did casework on a serial-killer investigation, knew corpses only from Academy photographs, and was known around the office as "Andrew the Alien," which he found "rad." His file lists other insulting names. He had been tased but never shot. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 05, Appalachia 06, Walkers 01, Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
Reassigned in spring 1992 and warned by his boss to "be the most normal thing in your environment," Andrew took charge of the new task force and briefed it in his own terms: "we're gonna, you know, travel around, find monsters and shit." He was the only member who knew that Kurt was CIA rather than FBI, and he wondered whether the group had been assembled as a punishment. (Radford Horror 01)

In Radford, Virginia he did the reading and the talking. He found the gutted diary of Amanda Lucky, the alien-abduction book in Abelforth Whateley's room and the missing-dog files, and his questions to the parents surfaced Dr. Lawrence Lori. He hoped throughout for a classic abduction and was let down: "Really was hoping for, like, a tractor beam." (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 04)

When Kurt was badly hurt, Andrew led a healing rite, Lay On Hands, and it worked for the first time in his life. The cost was shared harm and a nosebleed that ran on and off for days and had to be irrigated at the hospital. He was euphoric anyway. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05)

At the old-town church he was overwhelmed by dread before the door opened. Inside, the Radford Moth addressed him telepathically: "Changeling. You can help me. You have the understanding." Wilbur Whateley told him, "You, of all people, you have to understand." A mind-controlled Huell Kendrick shot him in the chest; Andrew watched the bullet slow before it struck his breastbone. He laid hands on the Biz and on Kurt until he was vomiting blood, swung a hammer and missed, and crawled out with his harm track full. As the church burned he heard: "Save me, child! You know the ones who made me—". (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08)

In the aftermath he fired the church mace for the first time, at a searcher wearing the shadow poncho; what came out was "nothing," which erased the man's head in cross-section and then restored it. He needed three people's worth of blood, gave a hospital speech about the Masters that was met with a long silence (Manipulate Someone, 5), and closed the case with a plain verdict: "Look, aliens exist. My coworkers are great. For the most part. The Biz needs a better diet. I am out of my depth." (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
In Marblehead Andrew speed-read the Sons of Adam Bible "with a sick intensity," recognized its Lemuria allusions from his fringe reading, and guessed the plot early: "Man, I think they might sacrifice people to a lake monster." He declined the communion wine. A page from the Radford ER about a possible clotting disorder went nowhere, because the lab had lost his samples. (Summer Service 01)

Unrecorded session

Summer Service 02 was never recorded. Later recaps say Andrew and Kurt went down in an experimental submarine with college students, found the stealth wreck with a piece "eaten" out of it, and sat dark while the humming, ring-shaped angel thing passed. See Lost episodes. (Summer Service 03)

A gray-skinned visitor came to him in a dream to apologize: "I'm really sorry about all the stuff that's gonna happen to you." He hid the dream from the team while privately wondering, in Rita's words, "Is my dad an alien? Why did he kiss me on the mouth?" He attended the service alone, carried the wine to Donald McManley, and delivered the result to the car: "Guys, we have worms!" Learning that Kurt had brought the Davy Crockett prompted "I'm sorry, you have a nuke?" (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04)

At Arnold Weathers' house he told Madeline Weathers that Jesus is "an all-powerful alien that came to Earth to help us," then turned his holy weapon on the worm-ridden dog Puddles. It beheaded the dog and passed straight through Kurt's hand. Rita's reaction: "Oh shit. Shit, I forgot this wasn't pepper spray." He ended that session carrying worms, a twisted ankle and two more harm from healing. (Summer Service 05)

In the finale he panicked over the nuclear weapon, scraped Jester off the car, backed over him and stepped away to vomit ("I need to look at mud"), and landed the decisive blow on the creature with a captured flashlight weapon that burned his hand. He then phoned Big Bill and enforced the cover story on the team: "Terrorists, okay. Terrorists." (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
Now officially a field agent, Andrew visited Dr. Arthur, his childhood doctor and fellow member (minor characters), who explained his healing as higher powers channeled with backlash, offered a meditation seminar and recommended tampons for the nosebleeds. (Appalachia 01)

In Dahlonega he lectured on Bigfoot hunting, proposed a werewolf, was adored by Harvey the Great Dane, and was taken aside by Prim Greengrass to confess his embarrassing middle name. One night he sleepwalked, or was compelled, for miles through the woods past the Death Cave and woke with a stranger's bloody lighter and no memory. In the cave he healed Kurt again, using a "frequencies" bracelet from his doctor as a focus, and went unstable. Mother Dahlia Riversand told him, "You've got the devil standing right behind you." (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04)

The Clinton surveillance scandal landed on him. He pleaded to Big Bill that "We're not surveilling Bill Clinton. We're surveilling dead Chewbacca," and the next day Fox 5 Atlanta caught him on camera in a deputy's uniform. His sweating "Thank you for your time again" aired about every ten minutes for the rest of the day. (Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08)

Underground, having been sworn in as a deputy, he was thrown through a ceiling and juggled by an ape-man, with every blow cancelled by what Andre calls his "magic shield." He declared it "the greatest day of my life," shielded Huell during the retreat, and severed the arm of Big Bob with the "absence" from his pepper spray. He ended the last recorded session of the arc with a dislocated knee, unable to walk, and about six gold bars in his satchel. (Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09)

Unrecorded session

The finale, Appalachia 10, was never recorded. Later episodes establish that Jan Martense shot Andrew in the face that same day, that he recovered "remarkably well," and that he left hospital in about half the expected time. Andrew says only that it "felt like" he was shot; Kurt covers for him with "Thank God for helmets." (Walkers 01, Walkers 02)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
The arc opened with Andrew waiting an hour and a half outside the Oval Office with forgotten Yeti fur in his bag. George H. W. Bush called him the task force's "only true believer" and charged him with the survival of the country; Andrew answered with a long lecture on the Aetherius Society while the President's face went blank. Back at the office Alberta Wilmarth asked him to get her mother exhumed, and he took the case to Utah. (Walkers 01)

At the Sherman Ranch he "vibrated" at every mention of the ranch hum, photographed each light and scorch mark, cited the 1950s Levelland case, and won over Walt Murphy with encyclopedic UFO knowledge. At the Ballard bar, where he turned red over the talk about the town water and was consoled with a root beer float, the Biz gave him the name "Half-Gallon Howard"; by Andre's count he was called it at least five times that evening. When a judge balked at the exhumation on religious grounds, Andrew had Big Bill telephone him, and the order went through. During the night event he believed he was buried alive, sealed himself in the refrigerator and levitated inside the white ring; in the morning he was furious to have missed an abduction. Mayor Wilford Hiram cut his hand with his rings in a handshake. (Walkers 02, Walkers 03, Walkers 04, Walkers 05)

He then recalled a dream of finding himself, naked, eating garbage outside his apartment and being chased into the desert by that smiling self. An anonymous note appeared in his bed ("I know you aren't one of them; you have angels") inviting him to the Ballard High School gym at 1 a.m., alone. He decided to go. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: The gym
docs.text:
That night Andrew first tackled a naked intruder at the guest house and, panicking, used Cast Out Evil on him without understanding what he had done. At the gym two upright horses showed him in, and on a stool sat another Andrew Howard, who trotted over to shake his hand and offered "the easy way or the hard way." Andrew pepper-sprayed his double, was stamped on and shot, pulled the pin on a grenade from his bag, and was pinned under a horse while the wounded double crawled over him. Its tendrils entered his mouth and everything went black. (Walkers 07)

From that moment Rita played a copy: see Andrew Howard (duplicate). The other players had been sent out of the call for the gym scene, and before bringing them back Andre gave Rita a private handout and told her, "You are not in Andrew Howard's body. You are in a replica." He confirmed that she was now playing the same double Andrew had just fought, grenade wounds included, and that the real Andrew's fate was unknown. The Skinwalker faction had grown the double in a hurry from tissue taken by the mayor's ring. It gave the team a cleaned-up story and travelled with them for the rest of the arc, sickly, easier to hurt than Andrew had ever been, unable to heal anyone, and quietly working for the faction. The rest of the table did not learn of the swap until Walkers 09. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08)

docs.title: Death and return
docs.text:
The real Andrew died. At the end of Walkers 08, after the other players had logged off, Andre cut to "the other Andrew Howard" in a scene with Rita alone. Andrew had been shot through the heart; dying was agonizing, which surprised him, "because he had always been told that being dead doesn't hurt"; and the inhuman parts of him then refused to let him die, leaving him with two heartbeats and rearranged innards. He woke naked, wrapped in plastic and duct tape, at the bottom of the corpse pile in the Roosevelt police station morgue. Rita rebuilt him in the same scene as a new playbook, the Monstrous: see Andrew Howard (the Monstrous). (Walkers 08)

Unrecorded session

Walkers 08.5 was never recorded. In Walkers 09 Andrew says that he realized the police in the station were not real cops, broke out, and spent an afternoon explaining himself to Nancy the goose; he had been gone about two days. Over the same stretch the duplicate rode with the team and the National Guard. (Walkers 09)

He reappeared as a naked, blood-covered figure with a gunshot wound in his chest, sprinting at about 35 mph toward the convoy. Rita was still playing the duplicate, which carried the party's X mark, and Andre voiced the newcomer. The duplicate and Huell both shot at him; he kept coming, shouting that he had been "shot in the chest and woke up under a pile of dead naked people" and that "there was no God up there." Kurt had him handcuffed, gagged and put in a Humvee with a medic. The duplicate then refused a mouth check, shot Kurt in the leg and ran, and gave itself away when its tendrils reached for Huell. With that Andre said, "Now that the game is up, Rita, let's swap back who we're controlling." Andrew was fed rations, which the sugar-eating copies could not have kept down, and was uncuffed. Andre observed: "It's funny, Howard, that the way that you proved you were human was by being bulletproof." (Walkers 09)

In the cavern under the community center he recovered his ruined suit, his fanny pack and his pendant, the last in a bag marked "Hazardous" with several exclamation points. Angry for the first time in his life, he shot his duplicate in the back while shouting, "You weren't even gonna tell my mom that I got stolen?" He left Utah fast, bulletproof and carrying the goose. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
Andrew typed his last Utah report on Christmas Eve, did some "religious soul-searching" ("Have I been chosen?") and went home to California. He now craved very rare steak, which Rita put down to "iron deficiency." Drawn to the Roulet House by the foil-wrapped letter, he froze, starstruck, at his first sight of a Grey, chased it, took a rifle shot to the face that left only broken skin on his forehead, and picked up its dropped VSS. He hid the face shot from the team and spent the night shouting at the woods. He also had his first ever hangover. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

At the Brooks Pharmacy siege Officer Todd handed him operational command. He stalled the gunman on the phone, was bitten by the old woman in the VW Beetle, and on storming the store was seized by a craving at the sight of a hostage's blood. He took a penalty for the rest of the fight rather than drink. His healing failed on the Biz; he tied a tourniquet instead and licked the blood from his hands. When the "alien" was unmasked as a man in a foam-latex mask, he kicked over a display stand. (Roulet Estate 03)

The epilogue is the first full statement of Andrew's condition. His doctor and church officials were evasive, X-rayed him without showing him the films, and treated him as a "special horse"; he sensed for the first time that they did not know what they were talking about. The doctor began mailing him human blood weekly, disguised as frozen orange juice. On desk duty in New York for the World Trade Center bombing investigation, he was thawing blood in a Brita pitcher when Ross Perot telephoned. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
Back from New York, Andrew found Huell in a wheelchair, searched the Biz's abandoned apartment and turned up the Moby-Dick book cipher (Investigate a Mystery, 12). He asked Huell, and then Kurt, whether the Biz might be a double agent. In Moscow, Boris Yeltsin asked the Biz about him; the Biz praised him and left out his abilities. (Radford Horrors 01)

With Daniel Webster now running the team, Andrew was "having a great time not being in charge." He travelled with powdered pig blood and a bloodletting kit and explained them as a doctor's diet for anemia. When he drank the rehydrated blood at the diner, Webster wrote "Andrew Howard is a vampire?" in his notebook. At the Safe Environment Fund site Andrew tore barbed wire apart bare-handed and shot a guard in the leg; the guard fired back, and the bullet slowed to a stop an inch from Andrew's chest. Webster saw him take the shot. (Radford Horrors 02)

After a mouse bite at the Pay n' Stay the team was given rabies treatment. Andrew dreamed of losing at beach volleyball to his alien dad, who mouthed "Don't take it." He reacted badly to the immunoglobulin, with a 104 F fever and yellow-tinged eyes, and discharged himself for fear the doctors would find out what he was. A Gatorade-and-blood slurry revived him at once. (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

At the Roanoke mental hospital he used magic (13 on Use Magic) to loosen the knots in Wilbur Whateley's mind, and Wilbur woke asking for his brother. In the most recent episode he was last seen lifting Kurt into a tree one-handed, by the belt, while Webster watched. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Huell Kendrick: Andrew's roommate on the road and phone confidant. Huell shot him at Radford ("Hey Howard, you've been shot, buddy. Welcome to the team"), treats him paternally, and is the keenest user of "Half-Gallon Howard." Andrew was stung when Huell quipped that he "didn't notice when you got replaced with an alien." (Radford Horror 08, Walkers 07, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Kurt Larson: Andrew calls him "Kurtis" and trusts his worldly knowledge. Kurt looks after him, coaches him ("Stand up straight, son"), tells him he has "no game," and talks him through his dreams with a "dad tulpa" theory. (Radford Horror 04, Appalachia 07, Walkers 02, Radford Horrors 03)
  • Dick "The Biz" Baxter: Andrew supervises him loosely, backs him in fights he tells him not to start, and later quietly doubts his loyalty while asking the others not to say so. The Biz gave him the nickname "Half-Gallon Howard." (Summer Service 01, Walkers 03, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Daniel Webster: his replacement as team lead, who judged him "a freak, but he's not a threat to me" after watching him survive a gunshot and drink blood. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Big Bill: his boss, whom he addresses as "Mr. Sir Nelson" and dreads phoning. After Big Bill's firing Andrew was known as his former "pet." (Summer Service 03, Appalachia 07, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Diane: a friendly working relationship; he monologues to her about a "beautiful, grand, peaceful future," embellishes his reports to her with aliens, and they exchange Christmas gifts. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 01, Roulet Estate 01)
  • His mother (minor characters): devout, never seen on screen. She stayed a month in his DC apartment while he slept on the pullout, pushes church socials, and received a fish-in-a-bikini ornament from Marblehead. (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 04)
  • His father: unknown to him; he does not know what the man looks like and supposes he was "probably just some schmuck that got my mom pregnant." A gaunt, grinning dream figure who kisses him on the mouth recurs from The Summer Service onward, and Andrew wonders whether it is his father and whether his father is an alien. (Summer Service 03, Radford Horrors 03)
  • Alberta Wilmarth and Nancy the goose: Alberta thinks well of him and the table jokes that they are dating. Nancy began by stealing his jacket and ended as his friend. (Walkers 02, Walkers 04, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Abilities and equipment
docs.text:
See Game mechanics for the rules behind these.

Playbook and ratings. Andrew began as the Divine. His Charm is -1 and his Act Under Pressure rolls are made at -1; Rita calls Tough his best stat and says "I'm not Cool. I'm Tough. And Weird." At the rebuild Rita set his ratings at Charm -1, Cool -1, Tough 2 and Weird 3, noting that a later advance could raise Tough to 3; by Radford Horrors 02 she gives them as "three Tough and three Weird. That's all my stats." (Radford Horror 02, Summer Service 03, Walkers 08, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03)

As the Divine:

  • Lay On Hands. Heals others at a cost to himself, always with a nosebleed. Used at Radford, Marblehead and Dahlonega. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 03)
  • Cast Out Evil. Used twice on the night of the gym; in Rita's words, "he does it when he's panicking." (Walkers 07)
  • A way with text. +1 on rolls involving books, newspapers or other writing. (Radford Horror 02, Walkers 06)
  • Protection. Bullets and impacts slow before they reach him. From Appalachia 08 he reduces all incoming harm by two. (Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 08)

As the Monstrous: he dropped Lay On Hands and Cast Out Evil, on the reasoning that the change had cut him off from their source. Rita chose the Feed curse (blood), a "life drain" natural attack that works at short range, and the moves Unquenchable Vitality, Immortal and Preternatural Speed; she also spoke of taking his old resilience again, and weighed Mental Dominion, Unnatural Appeal and Unholy Strength without settling on them. In play he runs at about 35 mph, shrugs off small-arms fire, tears barbed wire by hand and needs blood regularly. He can still Use Magic, as he did on Wilbur Whateley in Radford Horrors 04. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09, Roulet Estate 02, Radford Horrors 04)

Gear:

  • Andrew's satchel. A beat-up 20-inch leather bag, "the bag of many wonders," from which he can produce any small thing he could plausibly own: an umbrella, a quarter, a claymore, a grenade, blood bags. He forgets what is in it. The move behind it, What I Need When I Need It, survived the rebuild because, as Rita put it, it belongs to the bag and was never really his power. (Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 04, Appalachia 07, Walkers 07, Walkers 08, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Church mace / pepper spray. A church-issued canister, carried for years as self-defense, that sprays a void which passes through matter. It does 3 harm and is dangerous to allies. (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 09, Walkers 07)
  • Andrew's pendant. A religious pendant from his mother and "the guy" that gives kinetic protection; with it he negates three harm rather than two. He does not wear it at home. (Walkers 01, Walkers 04, Walkers 09, Roulet Estate 01)
  • Cameras. A flash camera shattered in the Georgia mines, another smashed in the gym, and a Polaroid with three treasured Ballard photographs. (Appalachia 09, Walkers 07, Roulet Estate 01)
  • Other. Service pistol, pager, walkie-talkie, notebook, a "frequencies" bracelet from his doctor, and a Fossil watch with glow-in-the-dark hands. (Appalachia 03, Walkers 03)

Harm and dread. He filled his harm track at the Radford church and was at five harm and unstable when the gym went black. His dread stood at 5 in Marblehead and had reached 18 by the night of the gym. (Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 03, Walkers 07)

docs.title: Memorable quotes

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The table usually calls him "Howard." "Half-Gallon Howard" was coined by Ezra, as the Biz, at the Ballard bar in Walkers 03, topping a local's "ten-thousand-gallon Tom." Zack took it up at once and uses it most, and in Radford Horrors 01 it is Zack whom Ezra asks to remind him of the joke. The name followed Andrew back to FBI headquarters; see Running gags. (Walkers 03, Walkers 04, Radford Horrors 01)
  • His middle name was confided privately in Appalachia 02 and not said at the table ("I got three first names"). In Walkers 09 Rita gives it as Nancy, the same as the goose. (Appalachia 02, Walkers 09)
  • His church is unnamed at first ("the Masters," "Mr. King's organization," "Andrew's cult") and is first called the Aetherius Society in Walkers 01. Rita and Andre later wondered whether it knew about the dark side of his powers, or had itself not been told the full story. (Radford Horror 08, Walkers 01, Walkers 08)
  • "'Cause Rita called dad," Dante's explanation of the exhumation order at the top of Walkers 05, is a joke about Big Bill, whom Andrew had phone the judge. (Walkers 04, Walkers 05)
  • The table's later shorthand for the Utah events is loose. Dante calls the copy "Dummy Andrew" and once tells Andrew "you were an alien replacement who was dying," and he opens Radford Horrors 04 recalling that Andrew "got shot in, like, the face or something" at the fence, where Radford Horrors 02 has the bullet stop short of his chest. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Rita insists he is "something else," not a vampire; as Dante points out, he walks in sunlight and has a reflection. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Slips at the table: Andrew has been called "Arnold," Andre once reaches for "Kingsley" as Mr. King's name, and Big Bill once calls Kurt "Howard." (Radford Horror 08, Walkers 06)
  • He rolled a d100 to choose his dinner at the Spud Hut. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Arnold Weathers
docs.text:
Arnold Weathers is a wealthy Marblehead selectman who is kept chained inside his island house, a bloated worm host found in a tub of black fluid and destroyed by Huell and Andrew.

Type NPC / worm host Aliases Arnold; Uncle Arnold; Mr. Weathers; putty man Affiliation Marblehead Board of Selectmen Relatives Madeline Weathers (niece) Status Destroyed (Summer Service 05) First appearance Summer Service 03 (unseen, in the cold open)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: When the team finds him, Arnold is bloated, hairless and soft, like overcooked vegetables or a rotting pumpkin, with broken handcuffs cut into his wrists (Summer Service 05). His house is a walled, late-1970s home on the bird-sanctuary island, priced by the GM at roughly $700,000 to $800,000 in 1992 money; see Arnold Weathers' house.

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
In the cold open of Summer Service 03, Jester carries a tray of food at night to an ornate chained house overlooking the sea, calls "Arnold? Buddy, you feelin' any better?" and slides the tray through the mail slot. A wet, drooling, dog-like growl answers, the tray is yanked inside and the door thumps. The growl turns to crazed barking (Summer Service 03).

At the Board of Selectmen meeting, the empty plaque reads "Arnold Weathers." The councilmen nervously eye the empty seat, and his absence alarms them (Summer Service 04).

After the meeting, his niece Madeline reports him missing: he missed a meeting to help sell her car four days ago, his gate is padlocked and the police did nothing. She blames the church. The mail pile goes back about a week, longer than her four days. Gate and door are padlocked from outside (Summer Service 05).

Inside, the team fights his bloated white Doberman, Puddles. Upstairs, a trail of dark, foul-smelling fluid leads to the bathroom. When Andrew Howard switches on the light, Arnold lunges out of a tub of black liquid, trying to flee, not to attack. Andrew body-blocks him and Arnold ruptures into worms; Huell Kendrick kicks off his jaw and a strip of face, stomps the knee, and the head comes off on the sink as the body collapses into worms. The team shuts the door and moaning continues behind it (Summer Service 05).

His bedroom holds two near-identical sets of the town's financial books and a shoebox of clear marbles (Summer Service 05). See Two sets of financial books and Crystal marbles.

docs.title: Abilities and weaknesses
docs.text: Like other infected hosts, he ruptures into worms when struck. See The worms and Worm bags.

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes never say who chained Arnold or when he became infected. Jester feeding him in the cold open of Summer Service 03 and the chained house the team enters in Summer Service 05 point to the same man, but the cold open never shows his face.

docs.title: Big Bill
docs.text:
Big Bill Nelson is the senior FBI official to whom Andrew Howard reports, and the superior who shields, scolds and cleans up after the Paranatural Incident Task Force from its founding until he is forced out in January 1993.

Type NPC Aliases Big Bill Nelson; Nelson; Bill Affiliation FBI; head of the Foreign Influence Task Force Status Alive; fired (as of Roulet Estate 03) First appearance Radford Horror 01 (named); Summer Service 03 (heard) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Big Bill is heard far more often than he is seen: for most of the campaign he is a voice on a payphone or a number on a pager. When he finally walks into the office he proves to be about six foot seven, heavy and middle-aged. (Roulet Estate 01)

On the phone he is skeptical but quick, gruff but protective of his agents, and by his own account fine with being called "Sir." Andrew considers him the one person in his chain of command who is "actually intimidating." As the 1992 election approaches he sounds increasingly stressed and weary, and his last appearance is warm but defeated. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04, Walkers 04, Walkers 06, Roulet Estate 01)

He is married; his wife appears only in one cold open, asking what "they" want in the middle of the night. He has an unnamed male secretary. (Summer Service 06, Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Position
docs.text:
Big Bill is the head of the FBI's Foreign Influence Task Force, which became the parent of Andrew's team "since it was determined that alien visitations are foreign by definition." Andre later calls it "the umbrella organization of the task force." Big Bill has "a lot of sway within the FBI." (Summer Service 03, Appalachia 07)

The chain of command given at the task force's founding runs from Andrew to Big Bill, then to Deputy Director Floyd Clark, then to President George H. W. Bush, which puts the agents "three levels down from the president." Roulet Estate 02 instead has him working directly under the FBI Director. Reports on the team's cases are code-word classified SKYHOOK, and the full version of each goes to Big Bill. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03, Appalachia 01, Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
Big Bill is named, but never seen, when the task force is set up. His one standing instruction is that anything unusual the team finds goes up the chain of command, which Andrew takes to mean "tell your boss first." (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 05)

Among the burned papers taken from Agent Murphy (Murphy's briefcase and documents) is a fragment reading "…ig Bill," which Kurt guesses is "Big Bill." Nothing more comes of it. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Big Bill speaks for the first time when Andrew briefs him by phone from Marblehead on the dive, the stealth wreck and its capacitor turret, the humming lit vessel (the angel thing), the Sons of Adam, the crystal marbles and the communion wine. He treats it as a counterintelligence matter, says he will take it to the Oval Office and try for a Navy submarine survey, promises Andrew he will be the first to know if they find a big squid, and orders the team to find the missing EPA/USGS survey team before the National Guard arrives. His secretary later takes Kurt Larson's request to have Jordan Gramoire assigned to the deployment. (Summer Service 03)

The next day he reports that a Los Angeles-class attack submarine has been retasked and is hours away, while the Guard is delayed by washed-out roads. Andrew tells him the wine is full of worms; Kurt, shivering, admits to "chicken pox and nerve agent and worms." Big Bill's order is to keep Larson alive. (Summer Service 04)

During the siege of the hotel he cannot be reached, and the switchboard can only promise to wake him. (Summer Service 05)

The finale opens on him: a phone rings in a dark bedroom and he tells his wife he has to go to work. At the end he is fifteen miles from Marblehead behind roads four feet under water, waiting for a boat, after two days stuck in mud with a convoy. He confirms that a submarine was lost and orders that the true purpose of Andrew's task force stay out of everything but the classified report. The public explanation is to be "terrorists" (see Terrorist cover story). (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
In October 1992 Big Bill sits beside Kurt at a House subcommittee hearing on Marblehead and has two of the chairman's questions struck on national-security grounds. He then sends Huell Kendrick, on his day off, to check on Donald McManley. (Appalachia 01)

Once the Georgia case turns out to involve the Covenant, he relays through McManley that it must be handled strictly by the book, with warrants, paperwork and clean hands, because of Ruby Ridge and "that thing in Marblehead." (Appalachia 03)

When the Clinton surveillance scandal breaks, every pager on the team shows his number. He berates Andrew, demands an inventory of men and equipment and an itinerary by fax, does not want to hear about bears, and is told the body count. He orders silence and says he will brief the President and fly down. His later pages go unanswered because the phones at the Spud Hut distribution center are down; Rita says the next call from him is Andrew's main worry. (Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
Big Bill gives Andrew several hard refusals to share his ape-man photographs with fandom contacts, then approves the Utah trip and its airfare: it is Andrew's task force. The players read the approval as a wish to get the team out of the public eye days before the election, as with Georgia. He phones ahead to the FBI Salt Lake City field office. (Walkers 01, Walkers 02)

When a judge with religious objections refuses the exhumation of Shelly Wilmarth, Andrew calls Big Bill, who talks to the judge for twenty minutes and leaves him shaken and compliant. Later, at Kurt's request and with reluctance about one more complication on top of "the political stuff," he puts the Utah National Guard on standby. (Walkers 04, Walkers 06)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
A flashback shows the aftermath in Roosevelt. The agents send word up the chain of a government cover-up, and Big Bill flies in because at least fifty or sixty Guardsmen are dead. His debrief begins apoplectic and works its way down. He then builds the public story: a radical domestic insurgency, a cult compound beneath the community center, and a Jonestown-style killing when investigators arrived. (Roulet Estate 01)

On Christmas Eve 1992 he visits the PITF office in person, eats two biscochitos and half a gingerbread man, and delivers the news. President-elect Ross Perot believes the task force was a cover for Bush's use of the FBI against political enemies; Perot has asked Bill to resign, will disband and reassign the task force on Inauguration Day, and is forming his own. He hands Andrew a padded envelope from an FBI courier, pockets three more cookies and leaves. (Roulet Estate 01)

On Inauguration Day he is due to be fired and does not pick up when Andrew calls from Rhode Island. Afterward he is confirmed fired, and Andrew, seen as his "pet," is kept on desk duty. (Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Andrew Howard: his direct report and, in the Bureau's eyes, his protege. Andrew's phone manner with him is awkward to the point of "Mr. Sir Nelson." (Summer Service 03, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Kurt Larson: Kurt calls him directly more than once, and Bill defends him before Congress. (Summer Service 03, Appalachia 01, Walkers 06)
  • Donald McManley: Bill sends Huell to pull him out of his breakdown and uses him to carry orders to the field. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 03)

docs.text:

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• His surname, Nelson, is spoken only in The Radford Horror and The Summer Service, where he answers the phone as "Big Bill Nelson" or "Nelson here." From The Things in Appalachia onward he is only ever "Big Bill." (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 06)
  • "The Protestants" in his cold-open line are evidently the armed Sons of Adam congregation besieging the team's hotel. (Summer Service 06)
  • At the end of his call with Kurt about the National Guard he signs off "Do your best, Howard." (Walkers 06)
  • The ape-man Big Bob is briefly misnamed "Big Bill" at the table and corrected. (Appalachia 09)
  • By his count there are only four FBI officers in Georgia, which is why a state police claim of FBI surveillance in Dahlonega points straight at Andrew's team. (Appalachia 07)
  • He promised to fly down to Dahlonega, but the arc's finale, Appalachia 10, was never recorded, and no later episode says whether he arrived.
