docs.title: Bill Clinton
docs.text:
Bill Clinton is the Governor of Arkansas and Democratic presidential nominee in the campaign's alternate 1992, whose candidacy is wrecked by a surveillance scandal in Dahlonega, Georgia that the public blames on the Paranatural Incident Task Force. He is a fictional version of the real politician, written as a character in the show's alternate history; nothing here describes the real person.

Type NPC (fictionalized historical figure; never appears on screen) Aliases Clinton; Gov. Clinton; William Clinton Affiliation Democratic Party; Governor of Arkansas Status Alive; lost the 1992 election First appearance Mentioned from Appalachia 01; never seen

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Clinton never appears in a scene. He exists as a newspaper item, a press conference, a set of leaked Polaroids, a late-night monologue and a very long running joke. For the full account of the affair, see Clinton Surveillance Scandal. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 07, Walkers 01)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
On the Dahlonega Times page that carries the grainy Bigfoot photograph sending the team to Georgia, below the fold, is a notice that Clinton will give a big campaign speech in Atlanta in a couple of days. (Appalachia 01)

In the same session the Biz accepts a secret job, through a sweepstakes mailing he recognizes as a KGB front, to hide a camera and microphone in Room 111 of the Smith Hotel in Dahlonega. He installs them alone, facing the bed, in a room staged with wine and chocolates and booked by an armed, military-looking man under mismatched names. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)

Days later Donald McManley asks the team whether they have seen the news. A Georgia State Police official has held a press conference claiming the FBI is in Dahlonega surveilling presidential candidate Bill Clinton, and that fingerprints on something "recovered from the scene" match an unnamed FBI agent. Big Bill pages everyone, berates Andrew Howard by phone, and says he will brief the President and fly down. (Appalachia 07)

Quote

"We're not surveilling Bill Clinton. We're surveilling dead Chewbacca." (Rita as Andrew Howard, Appalachia 07)

The team spends the next day dodging reporters. A Fox 5 Atlanta crew recognizes Andrew outside the Spud Hut plant and asks him on live television about the "Bill Clinton wiretap" and whether it is "the next Watergate". He answers "Nothing" and walks off, and the clip of him turning back, sweating, to say "Thank you for your time again" is replayed about every ten minutes. Inside, Jan Martense asks whether they were spying on the candidate; Kurt answers "oddly enough, no". (Appalachia 08)

Unrecorded session

The end of the Georgia case, Appalachia 10, was never recorded. By the start of Walkers 01, Clinton had been photographed in a Georgia hotel room, the Polaroids had leaked, the official story put the surveillance on Jan Martense, and the Georgia State Police had named the Biz and recovered his night-vision goggles from a rose bush.

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
The scandal makes the Biz "the most hated cop in America". The FBI's line is that the Bureau had nothing to do with it, and it sends him onto David Letterman's show to say so. Letterman's monologue recaps the story ("President Bush's FBI was caught surveilling Governor Clinton in a hotel room in Georgia. Or did they?") and adds that the allegations "hit a lot harder when there's Polaroids". On the couch the Biz says that none of the team knew Clinton was in town, and jokes coyly that he was in Dahlonega "having an affair with Bill Clinton". Letterman then reveals something the Biz did not know: the Polaroids were taken with a Russian camera. (Walkers 01)

Quote

"Maybe he's a Republican." (Ezra as the Biz, asked why Jan Martense would surveil Clinton, Walkers 01)

In the Oval Office, George H. W. Bush tells Andrew he expects to lose to Clinton within days, and that an ape-man criminal surveilling Clinton in the same Georgia town as the task force is not coincidence but "enemy action". By the end of the session, polling since what Andre calls "the double scandal" has Ross Perot above 45 percent. (Walkers 01)

In Utah the Biz is recognized everywhere: by FBI agent Carl Gardner ("the fella who spied on Clinton... had it coming"), by Bigelow's security, and by the bartender Maggie. Bigelow, who has researched the team, says the Clinton affair "didn't even make the list" of interesting stories about them. (Walkers 02, Walkers 03)

Quote

"I don't think Bill Clinton would be caught dead in Ballard, Utah." (Andre as Maggie, Walkers 03)

Clinton loses. Andre's summary of the alternate election is that Perot "just needed two October surprises" and one event supplied both: the incumbent was caught spying on a challenger who was having a sex scandal, "Watergate and Monica Lewinsky at the same time". (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Afterwards
docs.text:
The task force carries the blame. The Biz is "the guy who everyone blames the Bill Clinton thing on"; Perot regards the unit as Bush's instrument against political enemies; and Daniel Webster arrives in Radford knowing the Biz as the man "busted for taking pictures of the presidential candidate in a hotel room". Dante's comment at the table is that "the Bill Clinton thing was real". (Roulet Estate 02, Radford Horrors 02)

The first people to interrogate the Biz in Russia, the ones who kicked him, asked about Bill Clinton. They were gone by April 1993, replaced by captors interested only in aliens. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Who took the pictures
docs.text:
The episodes never show the photographs being taken, and the session that closed the Georgia case was not recorded.

  • The public version, and the FBI's, puts the surveillance on Jan Martense. (Walkers 01)
  • The Biz did plant a camera in Room 111 for what Andre describes as a KGB front, and Letterman's Polaroids came from a Russian camera. Dante's table joke when the Biz has no bug left for Jan is that he used "them all up on Clinton". (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 08, Walkers 01)
  • When the story first breaks, the Biz suggests that someone is trying to "fake some kind of Watergate-type deal", and Kurt agrees that a secret task force would be the ideal group of federal agents to pin it on. (Appalachia 07)
  • It is never established who booked Room 111.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Kurt, long out of the country, does not know who Bill Clinton is; Andre reminded the table that it was October 1992. (Appalachia 07)
  • Table theories about Clinton include that he is the Ape Man's father, that he is raising a clone army, and that "the sex scandals were a cover-up for Scanners". (Appalachia 08)
  • After the portal under the mines, the Biz wished the state police would come and look: "This is way weirder than Bill Clinton." (Appalachia 09)
  • Ezra's joke about the Russians who had prepared for a Clinton presidency: "That's the Bill Clinton team. They're in Siberia right now". (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Billy Thornton
docs.text:
Billy Thornton is a homeless man who haunts the Pay n' Stay motel and the woods nearby in Radford, and who tells the task force that chimpanzees, John Travolta and "some ladies" abducted him.

Type NPC Aliases The homeless man; "Bob or Bill" (the Pay n' Stay teenager's guess); the chimp man Affiliation None; known to the Radford Sheriff's Department Status Alive but not found (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horrors 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Billy is a rambling man who paces outside the Pay n' Stay and asks arriving agents whether they are the police. He is a heroin user; according to Molly Underhill, he had only recently stopped using in front of the elementary school (Radford Horrors 02; Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: The abduction story
docs.text:
Outside the Pay n' Stay, the homeless man told the team that people were kidnapping others in town. He said he had been put in a car, "beat up by chimpanzees", and then "John Travolta touched me inappropriately." Pressed by the agents, he added that the kidnappers picked him up in a van with the chimps and Travolta, that "some ladies" were present but did not touch his "bait and tackle", and that they "got me with their mind control ray." (Radford Horrors 02) The team took the chimpanzee part half-seriously, a callback to Zack's earlier joke about "space chimpanzees". When he left, he told them they should not stay at the Ferry Lodge.

Later in the episode, Kurt asked the IRS agents watching from the white van about a molestation complaint from a local; one replied, "Yeah, he talked to us too. Yeah, he got molested by monkeys and John Travolta." (Radford Horrors 02) See IRS Criminal Investigations.

docs.title: Tracking him down
docs.text:
In Radford Horrors 04, Harold, the Blockbuster clerk, said he had seen a homeless man dragged into a van and driven away, and that he had once given the man a sandwich a month and a half or two months earlier. Kurt took this to be the same man. Sheila, the diner waitress, said she had fed him pancakes a couple of times and saw him every day or two. The teenage staffer at the Pay n' Stay, Charm, had not seen him in a day and guessed his name was "Bob or Bill". Molly Underhill then named him: "Yeah, Billy Thornton." She said that when she offered to take a police report he muttered something about "the Israelis" and stumbled off. Kurt asked her to feed him and offer a cot if he turned up, and she mentioned that she had seen gray vans herself and assumed they were connected to the town's construction (Radford Horrors 04).

Kurt considered it interesting that if the gray van crew had taken Billy, they had let him go, perhaps because no one would believe him. The team never found him again (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"Homeless man claims kidnapped by chimps and molested by John Travolta. There were ladies present." Dante (as Kurt), reading from his notebook (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The line about John Travolta became a running joke at the table, along with ponytails (Radford Horrors 04).
  • Zack established that Huell believes Travolta is a Mormon rather than a Scientologist (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The Biz's guards
docs.text:
The Biz's guards are the Russian guards assigned to watch over Dick "The Biz" Baxter in the Hotel Metropol in Moscow. They work three rotating eight-hour shifts: one weeps at soap operas, one is a hard-ass, and one is nice. A separate guard from the president's convoy dies in the ambush in Radford Horrors 03.

Type NPC group Aliases The Biz's guard; Moscow guards Affiliation Russian government Status Unknown First appearance Radford Horrors 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: None of the guards is named. A guard is with the Biz at all times, and he is not allowed to leave, though the bars on his window were fitted after the fact and a fall from it would be survivable (Radford Horrors 01). In Radford Horrors 03, Andre explained that the guards work three rotating eight-hour shifts: one is "kind of an asshole and a hard-ass" who has beaten the Biz, and the other two are pretty nice (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The crying guard
docs.text: In Radford Horrors 01, the guard on duty sits through about three hours of the Russian-dubbed telenovela Los ricos también lloran (The Rich Also Cry) with the Biz, tearing up the whole time. The Biz disliked the fancy borscht that came with his room service and gave it to the guard, who has been eating it and quietly crying ever since. When the soap ends, a Russian-dubbed episode of Roseanne comes on. When a higher-ranking officer arrives with an invitation from the president to the opera, the guard guiltily puts down his bowl of borscht, and the officer side-eyes him. Later the guard leads the Biz to the bathroom to clean up, and the Biz worries that he has been measuring him for the suit in his sleep (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: The wake-up call
docs.text: In Radford Horrors 03, the Biz is woken by banging, and his guard, who had been fast asleep on duty, opens the door. An official the Biz has not seen before throws him clean clothes and tells him to be ready to ride with the president, Boris Yeltsin. The Biz asks the guard, one of the nice ones, who the visitor was; the guard says only that he is a colonel who often travels with the president (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The convoy
docs.text:
In the convoy, the Biz sits in a squat rear car between guards with bulletproof windows. None of them are people he knows. They refuse his request for coffee, and a guard with a thermos of black tea will not hand it over; they also decline to give him vodka (Radford Horrors 03).

When a car rams the president's limousine and explodes, the guards bail out. One guard shields the unconscious president with his body. The Biz persuades him (Manipulate Someone, 11 on the dice) to help move the president to the rear car. The guard is shot in the back seat and is dead by the time the Biz looks over his shoulder. A quick-release key from his body opens the trunk, and the Biz later props the body up beside the car as a decoy (Radford Horrors 03). See Convoy ambushers and Wheat field near Moscow.

Quote

"And he's just really fucking up the feng shui, frankly." Ezra (as the Biz), removing the dead guard from the back seat (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The guard who dies is one of the convoy's escorts, not one of the three who watch the Biz at the hotel.
  • The security guard in the Pinball Emporium case is an unrelated character; see Douglas Pinball Emporium.

docs.title: Boris Yeltsin
docs.text:
Boris Yeltsin is the President of Russia in the campaign's alternate 1993, the man who holds Dick "The Biz" Baxter in Moscow and questions him about everything the Paranatural Incident Task Force has seen. He is a fictional version of the real politician, written as a character in the show's alternate history; nothing here describes the real person.

Type NPC (fictionalized historical figure) Aliases Yeltsin; President Yeltsin; the president Affiliation Russian government Status Alive; recovering from a concussion and wounds (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Roulet Estate 03 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Yeltsin is polite, calm and dry, and he speaks English with the Biz. He cuts and lights a Cuban cigar for his prisoner with a small silver lighter, pats the seat beside him at the opera, and orders him scrambled eggs and ketchup after the ambush. He wears a big black coat when travelling, rides in an armored limousine and drinks strong black tea from a huge thermos. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

He makes small talk about Moscow hotels (the remodeled Baltschug Kempinski has better creature comforts than the Hotel Metropol, but "you cannot beat an in-house opera") and is a Star Wars fan. He calls the Biz "Baxter" or "Mr. Baxter", and once "Richard". (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

He conducts the important conversations himself, and he explains why:

Quote

"I have faith in my military officers, but I do not have faith that my military officers are my military officers." (Andre as Yeltsin, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
After the siege at the Brooks Pharmacy the Biz vanishes from an American hospital. Ezra chose abduction by the Russians as the consequence of his character's earlier dealings, and Andre agreed. The Biz is held at the abandoned Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp, beaten and questioned, then left in silence for two weeks until a senior officer orders him put on a plane. In Moscow he is shackled to a chair in the former Soviet Parliament building for an hour before Yeltsin walks in. (Roulet Estate 03)

Quote

"Tell me everything you know about the humanists." (Andre as Yeltsin, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
By early April 1993 the Biz has been moved to the Hotel Metropol and has spoken with Yeltsin several times. His first captors, who kicked him and asked about Bill Clinton, are gone; the new ones ask only about aliens and already know many specifics. Yeltsin has also asked a little about Ross Perot. (Radford Horrors 01)

Yeltsin summons the Biz to his box in the Metropol's opera house and, during a comic opera, works through his questions. (Radford Horrors 01)

  • Marblehead. Soviet detectors recorded a surge in the cosmic microwave background the previous year and triangulated it to the Marblehead nuclear incident. He knows about the engineered worms and has intelligence about a second organism; the Biz confirms the sea creature.
  • Ballard. He asks about the "people who were not people" at the Utah ranch. The Biz explains the skinwalkers, and Yeltsin compares them to Koschei the Deathless. He fears that his own officers have been replaced, and says Russia is "developing a test".
  • The weapon. From a silk handkerchief he unwraps a broken, half-melted device identical to the team's flashlight weapon, taken from a man in very dark welding-style glasses. Several teams of Russian scientists could not identify it. The Biz tells him what it is.
  • Andrew Howard. "Tell me about Andrew Howard." The Biz praises his former boss, leaves out his abilities, and says he never heard him mention family.
  • The Biz himself. "Mr. Baxter, are you a communist?" The Biz says he is not really ideological.

Quote

"Nuclear reactors do not emit cosmic microwave background." (Andre as Yeltsin, Radford Horrors 01)

Quote

"We are no longer communist here either." (Andre as Yeltsin, Radford Horrors 01)

Throughout, the Biz plays up how seriously the United States takes the threat. His Manipulate Someone roll is an 11, and Andre rules that the Russians are "a hundred percent buying exactly what you are selling". (Radford Horrors 01)

About three months into the Biz's stay, at around three in the morning, the president meets him in the Metropol lobby and asks him to come and look at "an unusual aircraft crash in Oryol Oblast". On the road the convoy is ambushed: a car rams the limousine and explodes, and gunmen speaking Chechen and Russian open fire. The Biz finds the president unconscious under a guard who is shielding him, drags him to the rear car, and drives out through a wheat field under fire, with Ezra burning Luck more than once on the way. The guard dies in the back seat. The Biz treats the president's concussion from the medical cooler in the trunk, hides him in the wheat, fights a gunman who follows the car's trail, and flags down a Russian helicopter. (Radford Horrors 03)

Quote

"Richard, there has been an unusual aircraft crash in Oryol Oblast. I need you to come take a look at it with me and tell me what you see." (Andre as Yeltsin, Radford Horrors 03)

Yeltsin, sutured at the head and torso, receives the Biz at dawn on a cleared hospital floor, tells him "you may have saved my life", compliments the "fairly impressive stunt driving", and says his intelligence services think the attack was "opportunistic" and "fairly half-assed". He then continues the journey in his hospital bed, by helicopter and jeep, with the Biz helping to push the bed through an airlock into the tent over the crashed craft at the Oryol crash site. (Radford Horrors 04)

There he has doctors wake the crash survivor and questions it in Russian and then English. It answers "Survey"; that its people are "Not aliens. The opposite of aliens"; and "Servitors... need resources." The doctors warn against pushing further and Yeltsin stops. In private he asks the Biz what he makes of it, and points out that the being accepts O-negative blood: why would that work on an alien? (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• The Biz. Prisoner, then informant, then the man who saved his life. The Biz, for his part, is afraid of being sent back to "the frozen shit bucket and the kicking" if he is caught lying or seems less valuable. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 04)
  • His own military. He trusts his officers but not that they are still his officers, which is why he meets the Biz in person and keeps only trusted guards near the survivor. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 04)
  • The colonel. An unnamed colonel travels with him and fetches the Biz for him. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text:
• Who the humanists are, and why Yeltsin asked about them first. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Where the Russians got their detailed knowledge of the team's cases, and who the man in welding glasses was. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • What "test" Russia is developing. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Who organized the convoy ambush; one gunman in mismatched gear was not obviously Chechen. See Convoy ambushers. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Yeltsin is never named during the ambush session, where Andre says only "the president". In the next session Zack asks which Russian president this is, and Andre answers "Yeltsin". (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Yeltsin's "Richard" is the only time he uses the Biz's first name. In the following session Andre begins a guard's line with "Richard" and corrects it to "Mr. Baxter". (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Zack admitted at the table that he would not be calling Andre on any details: "I don't know shit about Yeltsin." (Radford Horrors 04)

  • Radford Horrors 01
  • Radford Horrors 03 (called only "the president")
  • Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Briggs
docs.text:
Briggs is a drunk, one-footed fisherman and veteran who lives on a barely floating boat at the old docks of Marblehead, Massachusetts, and the first local to give the task force an outsider's view of the town's church.

Type NPC Aliases None (calls everyone "officer") Affiliation None; Catholic, wary of the local church Status Alive (as of Summer Service 01) First appearance Summer Service 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Briggs has a prosthetic foot, peeling, sunburned feet and a lawn chair beside a tiny, rickety boat in the harbor, where Andrew finds him asleep or passed out. He advertises a "luxury pleasure cruise" and addresses every member of the team as "officer" (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Looking for a poor boatman who would complain about "supernatural ocean shit," Andrew Howard finds Briggs at the old working docks while the team kills time before the Scott girl gets home from school (Summer Service 01).

Briggs blames "the goddamn Russians" for the bombing at 3 a.m. about a week and a half earlier, and thinks the Soviet collapse was a ploy. Glass from the blast cut him in a sensitive spot, and the wound became infected and had to be drained by a doctor in Salem. He says the town has since had dead fish, weird weather, headaches and bad moods, and fears that "the next one will be more successful." He was in bed on his boat during the blast, which blew out the windows of everyone near the shore (Summer Service 01). Kurt Larson shows him his double bullet wound and bonds with him as a fellow veteran (Summer Service 01).

Asked about the church, Briggs says it is against alcohol (and the town loved Prohibition), baptizes around forty white-clad people and babies in the sea, and speaks in tongues; he suspects an "old-time religion" older than the colonists. He vouches that the cemetery keeper, O'Donnell, is not one of them, advises the team to see the fort, and tells them to avoid local seafood ("stick to good old Mickey D's"). He identifies the "island" across the bay as the wealthy part of town, with Castle Rock, lobster boats and a bird sanctuary (Summer Service 01).

He also shares a seagull heresy and tells an eel anecdote about a drunken co-captain singing show tunes (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Treats Kurt as a fellow veteran.
  • Is Catholic and distrusts the Sons of Adam, the church led by Amos Shaw.

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"Maybe the next one will be more successful." Andre (as Briggs), on the blast (Summer Service 01)

Quote

"No, I think every damned soul becomes a seagull. That's my little heresy on top of Catholicism..." Andre (as Briggs) (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Briggs blames the Russians for the blast, a theory he shares with other locals; see The Marblehead explosion for the blast itself.
  • When Zack (as Huell Kendrick) asks "what is the strangest thing you've ever seen while fishing?", Briggs answers with the eel anecdote.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 01

docs.title: Carl Gardner
docs.text:
Carl Gardner is a hearty, back-slapping FBI agent at the Salt Lake City field office who briefs the task force on the Sherman Ranch reports and hands over the case file.

Type NPC Aliases Gardner; Agent Gardner Affiliation FBI, Salt Lake City field office Status Alive (as of Walkers 02) First appearance Walkers 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Gardner is short and heavy, hearty, with what Andre describes as "big cop energy." He thumps people on the back hard enough to move Andrew Howard, calls them "son," and speaks folksily; he has heard of Kurt's UTAW division as "those boys, explode the cigars and all that." He works alongside Agent Philip Bishop, a tall, thin, silent man with a thin mustache; the two read as a comedy duo (Walkers 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
When Big Bill phones ahead, the secretary sends the team to Gardner and Bishop in the second-floor conference room, where a corkboard is covered in strings and Post-its. Gardner's rundown: a Native American former Army Ranger on the ranch says he shot a snooper by the barn (no physical evidence); a young woman reported seeing her dead mother (checked for twins, none); cattle mutilation was blamed on lightning; and reports of lights and lost time were blamed on drinking. He is skeptical of all of it, and refers to the ranch employee in dated, offensive terms (Walkers 02). See Livestock mutilations.

He says the billionaire renting the ranch "skeeves me the hell out": a Texan into UFOs with security, scientists and "a couple of Navy guys." He leaves to find the name, returns with Robert Bigelow's, and notes it was Bigelow's security man who fired the shot. He gives the team a copy of the case file, to be "checked in" when they leave, and recommends Bigelow's hotel chain, Budget Suites of America (Walkers 02). See Robert Bigelow.

Gardner is investigating a "drinking fountain pervert" case; when Rita asks if the building's fountains are safe, he pauses and calls for another test kit (Walkers 02). See Ballard water contamination. He tells the team to say they are "a friend of Bonaparte" at a nearby gas station for 20% off. He recognizes the Biz as "the fella who spied on Clinton... had it coming," prefers Leno to Letterman, and dislikes Clinton. He also recommends Utah food: funeral potatoes, dirty soda, Jell-O salad and Frog Eye Salad (Walkers 02).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Salt Lake City scenes introduce the "drinking fountain pervert" case that recurs through the arc.
  • A running gag from this scene: dentists' conferences have bumped the team from hotels on the last three or four cases (Walkers 02).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 02

docs.title: Carter
docs.text:
Carter is Kurt Larson's former CIA fixer turned overseas arms dealer, whose life Kurt once saved and who supplies the deniable M28 Davy Crockett as a final favor.

Type NPC (offscreen) Aliases Jimmy; Kurt's weapons contact Affiliation Formerly CIA; now an arms dealer Status Alive (as of Summer Service 04) First appearance Summer Service 03 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Carter never appears onscreen. He is a former CIA fixer, now an overseas arms dealer who spends much time in the United States. Kurt worked with him for about five years. Kurt does not know whether "Carter" is a first or last name; all he knows is that the man's first name is Jimmy. Iran-Contra was Carter's idea, and it ended both his and Kurt's careers (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
After the dive to the stealth wreck, Kurt phones an old weapons contact for something big enough to kill the "glowy ring" and offers options such as a Davy Crockett, a MOAB, a MOP or an anti-materiel rifle. The contact is not named in this episode. He promises a deniable weapon "in a day or two," with serial numbers filed off and the item deleted from inventory, and says hello to Kurt's wife. Andre (as Carter) tells Kurt: "You didn't get this from me. You don't know me. In fact, I don't exist." Kurt reminds him of an earlier conversation about "if I ever had to shoot Godzilla" (Summer Service 03).

The next session opens with a recap that identifies the contact as Carter, a CIA fixer Kurt knew and once saved the life of. Dante burns one of Kurt's Luck points, at the GM's offer, for "a really good weapon that is potentially more inconvenient and dangerous." Without the Luck burn, the GM says, it would have been a Scorpion (Summer Service 04).

Carter's courier, an unnamed man (Andre) in a military-surplus armored truck outside the Marblehead post office, delivers a 7x4x4 ft crate. He says Carter sends his love, this is the last one, and after it they are even. The crate holds an M28 Davy Crockett with one W54 warhead. Carter has welded on an aftermarket coincidence rangefinder and filed off the serial numbers, rewriting them in Sharpie. The courier leaves quickly, saying the town creeps him out (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Chief of Police is also addressed as Jimmy in Summer Service 04. See Chief of Police.
  • Kurt never learns whether Carter is a first or last name.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Summer Service 03 (as the unnamed weapons contact)
  • Summer Service 04

docs.title: Charm
docs.text:
Charm is the teenage clerk of the Econo Thrift Pay n' Stay motel in Radford, who tells the team the bedbugs were wiped out by a chlorine tent while hiding the motel's rabid rodent and bat problem.

Type NPC Aliases Pay n' Stay clerk Affiliation Pay n' Stay Status Alive (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horrors 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Charm is a teenage girl who drives on a learner's permit and works in an office entirely filled with Lisa Frank Trapper Keeper stationery. She keeps the room keys chained to large red rulers because people kept stealing them (Radford Horrors 02). She replaced the motel's old UFO-obsessed clerk, Rutherford, who was let go when the motel was found to be within a thousand feet of a school. She introduces herself as "Charm", and calls the agents "my first repeat" since they had stayed at the motel before, during the Radford Horror arc (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
When the team checked in, Charm gave them two doubles. Kurt hosed both rooms with a mix of juvenile hormone and nicotine pesticide, and Charm, seeing it, told him the bedbugs had already been wiped out by a three-day chlorine tent. Kurt's attempt to read her (Manipulate Someone, 6) failed, but she let slip a "but" and admitted only to mold (Radford Horrors 02).

At about 3 a.m. a rabid mouse bit Daniel Webster on the chest, and Kurt killed it with his spear gun (see Rabid mouse). Charm came running down, admitted that a bat infestation was giving the mice rabies, offered the team their money back and said she does not sleep at the motel herself. She also offered to drive the agents to the hospital on her learner's permit. "I'm sorry. God, I hate this place." Everyone received rabies shots at the Radford ER (Radford Horrors 02).

In Radford Horrors 04, the team finds the teenage girl at the motel dragging stained laundry out of a room in hip waders and rubber gloves. The health department had hung up on her when she called, and she is working the summer to buy a horse: "I am getting that fucking horse." She had not seen Billy Thornton in a day, guessed his name was "Bob or Bill", and said he goes to the woods to do heroin (Radford Horrors 04). She is not named in that episode, but is evidently Charm.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horrors 02
  • Radford Horrors 04 (as the unnamed teenage staffer)

docs.title: Chief of Police
docs.text:
The Chief of Police is the hostile, bloated head of the Marblehead police and a member of the Marblehead Board of Selectmen.

Type NPC Aliases Jimmy; the chief Affiliation Marblehead police; Board of Selectmen Status Alive (as of Summer Service 04) First appearance Summer Service 04 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The chief is bloated, with the near-translucent skin that marks the advanced stage of the town's sickness; see The glow. He glares at the team on arrival and then at Jester (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
At the 6:30 p.m. selectmen's meeting in the town hall, the chief sits in one of the eleven plaque-marked chairs and glares at the team. He refuses Kurt Larson's request to smoke. Andre describes the room as hostile but sincere fanatics. The team debates arresting the chief for concealing evidence (Summer Service 04).

When Dante (as Kurt) asks about the melted, glassy shoreline, the chief goes very still. The mayor suggests lightning or dynamite fishing, asks where the team saw it, and tells "Jimmy" to look into it (Summer Service 04). See Melted shoreline.

Earlier in the episode, as the team left the lighthouse, Andrew caught the tail end of a police car driving away. The episodes do not link the chief personally to it (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• His first name, Jimmy, matches Carter's; the episodes do not connect the two.
  • His own name is never given.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 04

docs.title: Clive
docs.text:
Clive is the large-animal handler who trained the ape-men of Jan Martense's gold-mining operation beneath Dahlonega, Georgia, and who guides the task force out of the mines in Appalachia 09.

Type NPC Aliases The worker; large-animal handler; animal handler Affiliation Jan's Conspiracy; Spud Hut Status Alive at the end of Appalachia 09; said in Walkers 01 to have helped the team survive the mines First appearance Appalachia 09 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Clive is a man locked in the kennel security office beneath the plant. He later appears in a face shield and the upper half of a bear suit, carrying a 12-gauge shotgun, a clicker and ketamine powder. He says he has not seen the sun in two months. He is cooperative but defensive (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Clive says he worked at zoos and on big-game preserves in Central Africa, has handled elephants and hippos ("Don't work with hippos"), and went to Michigan State. He mentions a Minneapolis zoo with some bitterness. Jan hired him for a third of the gold, and the first rule of the job was "Don't ask questions about the ape-men." He has spent the last two months underground training a new shift (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
Clive is first met in the sealed sub-basement under the Spud Hut Georgia Regional Distribution Center. Kurt and Andrew follow a voice in the dark past a straw-floored kennel to a locked door, where a man begs to be let out and insists that "the shift" must be brought back. He asks whether "the rejects got out". Kurt hotwires a forklift to burst the door. The man returns in a face shield and bear suit with a shotgun, and the party takes more bear suits, shotguns, pepper spray and air horns from his stock (Appalachia 09).

He explains the operation: ape-men dig the gold because they do not talk and can recognize gold. They arrive looking about six and are full-grown in about two months, and the operation has run a year and a half. He trains them with clickers and positive and negative reinforcement, and keeps them addicted to ketamine so that they focus. A shift of twenty-five must be led back and fed within twenty-two minutes. Defending the work, he says "Again, I'm not a moral philosopher. We eat meat." When the Biz asks whether the ape-men are people, he calls them "solidly morally ambiguous" (Appalachia 09).

When told about the missing kids, the truck driver and the Spud Hut workers, Clive is dismayed: Jan told him he had "taken care of" the escapees. The party tells him Jan tried to kill them. Clive had been locked in by the security lockdown when the power went out and guesses that Jan did it on purpose (Appalachia 09).

He gives his name only after the party finds the "crack in the air" and its gas pipe. He insists the ape-men are not people, compares training them to teaching elephants to paint, and says he urged Jan to sell ape-men. Kurt points out that nobody asked where the ape-men came from. Andrew grows surly with him. In the tunnels Clive sets out treats for the shift, but the shift has not had its ketamine, so the party packs Combos with a ketamine paste. He warns of Big Bob and sprints through the dark with no light when the party runs (Appalachia 09).

After Big Bob dies, Clive says he once dissected a dead ape-man and found an adrenaline gland about twice the size of a fist, and that he will "kinda miss Big Bill" (Andre corrects the slip to Big Bob). When Huell, the Biz and Andrew press him about jail, Kurt tells them to stop turning their only guide against them, and jokes about recruiting him into the CIA. Clive leads them past four more corners to an unguarded ladder that emerges in the woods outside the plant. He explains that the handlers relied on the ape-men's fear of dark tunnels and lit only the routes they wanted (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Epilogue
docs.text: The finale of the arc (Appalachia 10) was never recorded. In Walkers 01, Kurt tells the imprisoned Jan that the animal handler is "how we managed to survive the mines, for the most part", and that until Jan tried to kill them, the handler "said you were the best boss he ever had". Jan answers that hiring the handler halved his take and doubled the risk of a leak, and that he brought him in only because he could not handle the ape-men himself. The handler is never named in that episode (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Jan Martense: his employer, whom he admired until Jan locked him in with the shift (Appalachia 09).
  • Kurt: shields him from the others' questions and is his main ally in the party.
  • Andrew: grows surly with him over the ape-men.

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"Look, look, man, I just work here, and the first thing that Jan told me when he was hiring me for the job was, 'Don't ask questions about the ape-men.'" Andre (as Clive) (Appalachia 09)

Quote

"Again, I'm not a moral philosopher. We eat meat." Andre (as Clive) (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Andre once calls Big Bob "Big Bill" in Clive's voice and corrects himself.
  • Clive's name is spoken once, midway through the session; before that he is "the worker" or "the man with no name".

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 09
  • Walkers 01 (mentioned, unnamed)

docs.title: Daniel Webster
docs.text:
Daniel Webster is an FBI Special Agent who is put in charge of the former task force agents when they are sent back to Radford, Virginia in April 1993; he is the second player character of Ezra, played alongside Dick "The Biz" Baxter.

Type Player character Aliases Special Agent Webster; Agent Webster; Dan; "Officer Webster" (the lawyers' slip) Affiliation FBI; reports to Director Rudy Giuliani Status Alive (as of Radford Horrors 04); on rabies treatment First appearance Radford Horrors 01 Played by Ezra

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Ezra's own description is "a man who looks about twenty-five percent more like a Fed than Andrew Howard": square-jawed, "identifiably from a distance Mormon," with shiny shoes, the hair and the briefcase. The table's shorthand is that Andrew Howard looks like The X-Files while Webster looks like Law & Order, a recruiting ad or Silence of the Lambs; Zack calls him "the Bean to Howard's Ender." His first act on screen is to give the team "the hairy eye" across a waiting room. (Radford Horrors 01)

He is in his late forties, dresses in suits and travels with spares. In style he is the opposite of the Biz, whom the table describes as a greasy, zoot-suited gambler type. Dante's joke is that Webster "looks like he has a son named Enoch." (Radford Horrors 02)

Ezra gives him no special voice: he speaks "in a normal, boring voice," formal and dry, and insists on being called Webster. He tends to stay at the back of the group and writes notes hastily and constantly. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Webster comes from rural Utah, not far from the ranch the team investigated in The Walkers in Skin. He was raised in a polygamist household that was "not super orthodox," of the kind where boys were put out at around sixteen, and he is still a Mormon. He grew up "a fairly avid outdoorsman." (Radford Horrors 02)

In 1978 he worked at the State Department, where he handled the United States side of the logistics for the operation that rescued Ross Perot's employees during the Iranian revolution. He never went over himself. That history is why President Perot trusts him. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: What he believes about the team
docs.text:
Webster arrives convinced that the old Paranatural Incident Task Force was a unit that President George H. W. Bush used for "political corruption dirty work," staffed with agents the president could manipulate, and that "all of the alien stuff is just cover." This is the same belief that led Ross Perot to disband the task force in Roulet Estate 01. Andre adds that Webster thinks its members are "all dirty as hell" and covered something up in Radford, and that he may fear a serious criminal operation is still running there. He counts Andrew as a known weirdo and treats Kurt Larson's wetwork background as close enough to a disgrace. He has heard both office rumors about Andrew (that he was sleeping with former Director Sessions, or had dirt on him) and has not picked one. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

His view of the individual agents is unflattering: the Biz was caught photographing Bill Clinton in a hotel room (the Clinton surveillance scandal), Kurt "has probably skinned at least two people," and Huell Kendrick is a chain-smoker on crutches. Watching them at the diner, he starts to call them the "worst political wetworks group I've ever" met, and is cut off by the table's laughter. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
Assignment. Webster first appears in the waiting room outside the director's office at FBI headquarters, on the morning that Giuliani takes over the Bureau. Giuliani says that he and Webster "came to an understanding" earlier, then gives the orders: Webster has operational authority, and Andrew, Kurt and Huell are consultants "strictly there for informational purposes." The goals are to find out what happened to the missing FBI task force that Perot sent to Radford, and to establish an acceptable fact pattern for the original investigation. (Radford Horrors 01)

The Biz is in Moscow throughout the arc, and the two characters never share a scene. (Radford Horrors 01)

Arrival in Radford. Webster books the whole team onto one flight, already fuming that he could not get a helicopter, and is alarmed by the clanking of their luggage at Roanoke. On the drive Kurt rides with him to "vibe check" him; Webster's Investigate a Mystery concludes that Kurt is hiding most of his career and has "skinned somebody." At the Ferry Lodge he books two doubles and insists on bunking with Kurt, and when IRS Criminal Investigations agents storm the lobby he sides with them, tries to tackle the document-shredding clerk, and scolds Kurt for answering a police raid with a drawn gun and a grenade. (Radford Horrors 02)

At the Lonely Mountain Diner he watches Andrew mix a maroon powder into hot water and writes "Andrew Howard is a vampire?" in his notebook. He then reads the full original case file, takes Molly Underhill aside for her own version, and comes away distrusting both the cartel explanation and the convenient church fire. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

The fence. Webster chooses to visit the missing agents' camp at the Sportsman RV Campground first and documents it with photographs and video. Following the missing agents' map to the Safe Environment Fund fenced site, he fails his Act Under Pressure roll (5) and is left hanging from the barbed wire by his coat and vest until Andrew lifts him down "like a child." When armed guards of the Safe Environment Fund arrive he shouts "FBI! Get on the ground!" and levels his shotgun, fails Manipulate Someone (5), and is tasered. He takes 1 harm (torn skin on the neck, a damaged shoulder tendon) and his shotgun goes off wide. (Radford Horrors 02)

In the exchange that follows he clearly sees Andrew shot (Investigate a Mystery 10) and tells himself it was armor, a taser-addled misperception, or "something weird." He demands an ambulance over the guards' radio and gives his badge number. Further in, he tastes the pearlescent goo Kurt scrapes from a branch: eye-wateringly bitter, then cold sweats, nausea, a sweet aftertaste and compulsive salivation. Andre's recap the following session sums up the flavor as "batteries and baby shit." (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

On the drive back Ezra says that the team's behavior fits no political conspiracy Webster can construct: nobody has mentioned Clinton, the Bush family or the Kennedys, only aliens, moths, woods and bad hotels. Rita's summary is that Daniel is "having to do some recalculations this evening." (Radford Horrors 02)

The mouse. At the Pay n' Stay Webster leaves his camcorder running in a corner and wedges the door. At about 3 a.m. a foaming rabid mouse crawls up his stomach; his Kick Some Ass (9, mixed) flicks it off with his gun barrel, and it bites him through the shirt on the nipple for 1 harm before Kurt pins it to the floor with his spear gun. (Radford Horrors 02)

At the Radford ER the bite has swollen to the size of a gumball. The others receive rabies immunoglobulin by IV; Webster gets about twenty injections around the wound. Forty-five minutes after they fall asleep he is paged by Giuliani about "the thing with the fence." Webster claims probable cause and asks to press charges against the guard as leverage; Giuliani warns of the Bivens lawsuit, a retroactive warrant and a possible reprimand, and asks whether Webster has worked out the team's "angle." Webster says he sees nothing of political importance and is told to keep an eye out. Four hours with FBI counsel follow. He then accepts Sheriff Underhill's offer of her mother-in-law suite. (Radford Horrors 03)

The reprimand arrives by the next session: the President wants no more "cowboy shit" and everything by the book. (Radford Horrors 04)

The skeptic. While the team works the disappearance of Elizabeth George from the Douglas Pinball Emporium, Webster hears about the "face in a bag" from the Georgia case and visibly feels his career flash before his eyes. He calls Giuliani again, reports no link to "political wetwork," and passes along the team's theories about the gray van crew and the LA treatment cover story. His Manipulate Someone (10, Charm +1) leaves the Director disappointed but still trusting; Giuliani wants the missing agents found within twenty-four hours, dead or alive. (Radford Horrors 04)

After the visit to Wilbur Whateley at the Roanoke mental hospital he asks whether they have just tortured a mental patient. At the campfire that night Kurt tells him the true story of the Spaceman, which is mundane enough to make him feel better. A Sharp roll of 12 then lets him add things up: Andrew's satchel produces more than it could hold, Andrew keeps showing casual superhuman strength, Webster is increasingly sure he saw him shot, and Andrew keeps drinking blood. He chooses not to confront him. The arc's most recent image is Andrew lifting Kurt into a tree one-handed while Webster watches. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Andrew Howard: Webster replaces him as leader. He rates Andrew the least threatening member of the team at first, is surprised by his strength, and by the fourth session suspects that something is wrong with him (see Andrew's Condition). (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Kurt Larson: the agent he distrusts most, rooms with, and will not let out of his sight. He is convinced the spear gun will eventually be used on him, yet says he trusts Kurt "more than the townsfolk" and does not question his Vietnam credentials. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Huell Kendrick: noted mainly as a chain-smoker on crutches. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Rudy Giuliani: his superior, who asks him to watch the team and report their "angle." (Radford Horrors 03)
  • The team as a whole: they do not trust him yet either, and follow him into the hospital hallway to eavesdrop on his call. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Abilities and equipment
docs.text:
Webster's playbook is never named at the table; Andre lets Ezra allocate his ratings as play goes on. Two are stated: Sharp +1 and Charm +1. See Game mechanics. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

Roll Result Episode Investigate a Mystery on Kurt 8 (7 on the dice, Sharp +1) Radford Horrors 02 Read a Bad Situation at the Ferry Lodge 7 Radford Horrors 02 Act Under Pressure at the fence 5, fail Radford Horrors 02 Manipulate Someone on the guards 5, fail Radford Horrors 02 Investigate a Mystery after the shooting 10 Radford Horrors 02 Kick Some Ass on the mouse 9, mixed Radford Horrors 02 Manipulate Someone on Giuliani 10 Radford Horrors 04 Sharp, at the campfire 12 Radford Horrors 04

Harm. 1 harm from the taser and 1 harm from the mouse bite, followed by rabies treatment. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03)

Gear. Shabby 1990s body armor, a pump-action shotgun, a scoped .44 "Dirty Harry" revolver, a camera, a camcorder, a tape recorder whose tapes he changes, a flashlight, a pen and notepad, and spare suits. He also brought his own silverware for fear of being poisoned, and says he will make a daily phone call or people will come looking for him. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"Kurt, your reaction to somebody announcing that they're the police cannot be to pull a gun on them." Ezra (as Daniel Webster) (Radford Horrors 02)

Quote

"I don't want you to take offense at any of this, but I am recording everything. It's for my own protection." Ezra (as Daniel Webster) (Radford Horrors 02)

Quote

"Without using words like 'aliens,' what do you think we're going to find in these woods?" Ezra (as Daniel Webster), to which Dante (as Kurt Larson) replies: "Foreign element." (Radford Horrors 02)

Quote

"Yeah, I mean, the Pay n' Stay part isn't even the second-worst thing about my day. But it's not good. Pay n' Stay is not getting a good review." Ezra (as Daniel Webster) (Radford Horrors 03)

Quote

"Could people stop going missing?" Ezra (as Daniel Webster) (Radford Horrors 03)

Quote

"I'm trying to put together a story that isn't weird, and I'm coming up extremely short. It's just weird." Ezra (as Daniel Webster) (Radford Horrors 04)

Quote

"I mean, did we just torture a mental patient for no reason?" Ezra (as Daniel Webster) (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Ezra had not prepared the character. Asked for a name at the table, he answered: "Fuck me, I didn't actually come up with one." He then settled on Daniel Webster and hoped it was not the name of a real person. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Ezra was muted when the GM first asked what Webster looks like. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Asked by Rita how old Daniel is, Ezra answered that he is in his late forties. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • When Andrew tries "Daniel," "Dan" and "Danny Boy," Webster asks to be called simply Webster. Kurt calls him Dan anyway. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Three sessions in, Ezra missed a cue addressed to "Daniel Webster" and apologized: "I forgot that my character's name was that." (Radford Horrors 04)
  • The 1978 rescue of Perot's employees from Iran, which Webster worked on, is real history borrowed for the campaign's alternate history. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: David Letterman
docs.text:
David Letterman is the real-life talk-show host who, shortly before the 1992 election, interviews the Biz about the Georgia scandal on Late Night with David Letterman and becomes his ally for the rest of the mystery.

Type NPC (real person, fictionalized) Aliases Letterman Affiliation Late Night with David Letterman Status Alive (as of Walkers 01) First appearance Walkers 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Letterman first appears in the cold open of Walkers 01, as a broadcast on a wood-paneled tube television in a dilapidated room. The announcer bills Gary Oldman talking Dracula, musical guest Patti Smith, and "a late-night special interview: the most hated cop in America." Letterman's monologue jokes about the election, the Clinton Polaroids, Ross Perot and CNN's exhausted anchors (Walkers 01).

He is sharp and sarcastic at first, introducing the Biz as "the most hated cop in America, some would say," but becomes sincerely curious once the interview goes off script. He loves magic (Walkers 01).

docs.title: The Letterman taping
docs.text:
The FBI had wanted a PR representative to do a news tour, but every show insisted on someone actually involved, so the Bureau ordered the Biz onto Letterman's couch, with Huell waiting backstage in reserve. During the Oldman segment break Letterman sits with the Biz ("You look nervous") and offers to bring Huell out for support. After the break he introduces "Richard Baxter" and forgets Huell's surname until Huell supplies "Kendrick" (Walkers 01).

The Biz's remark that he did not know shooting a Polish person could make him the most hated man in America leaves Letterman's face frozen. Ezra then rolls Manipulate Someone at -2 and burns a Luck point to turn the roll into a 12. A 12 or better lets the Biz make someone his ally for the rest of the mystery, and he picks Letterman rather than the audience. Letterman goes off-script and starts genuinely talking with him (Walkers 01).

Letterman asks why gold miner Jan Martense would surveil Clinton, and tells the Biz the Polaroids were taken with a Russian camera, which is news to the Biz. Because of the ally result, he says "Sure" when the Biz offers a card trick. The Biz rolls Act Under Pressure and gets a 10: a marked-card trick with an FBI twist, using his wallet and badge on the desk. The patter is rough, but there are more claps than boos (Walkers 01).

Afterward Letterman says "This interview did not go where I expected," and calls Huell "Detective Hendricks". A PA gives the Biz Letterman's personal phone number. Ezra remarks, "That was worth the luck point." (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• The Biz: his ally for the rest of the mystery, by the result of the Luck-burned Manipulate Someone roll.
  • Huell: Letterman forgets his surname, then calls him "Detective Hendricks".

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Letterman's misnaming of Huell as "Hendricks" is Andre's slip at the table, which the players noticed.
  • The players joked during the session that "it's not Fallon".

docs.title: Dead Man in the Cave
docs.text:
The Dead Man in the Cave is an unidentified middle-aged smoker whose shredded remains are found in a crevice cave near the freeway outside Dahlonega, Georgia; only his face, some gray cloth and a lighter marked "HF" are recovered.

Type NPC (deceased, unidentified) Aliases Exploded Man; HF Status Dead Location The Death Cave First appearance Appalachia 02 (cold open, if the same man); Appalachia 03 (remains)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The man was middle-aged, with salt and pepper in his beard, and his face looked older than his mid-30s hair color implied. Andre describes a smoker's pallor. The team found shreds of gray fabric and a cigarette pack among the remains, but no wallet. Huell studies the recovered face and does not recognize him (Appalachia 03).

docs.title: The cold open
docs.text: The cold open of Appalachia 02 follows an unnamed man in a gray jumpsuit and safety glasses who steps out of the Spud Hut distribution plant for a cigarette. He is drawn into the woods by a sobbing noise like a baby's, squeezes into a narrow fissure with the words "Hold your horses. It's okay. I'm coming," finds an ancient pickaxe by the light of his lighter, and is attacked by a humanlike figure with glinting eyes (Appalachia 02). The episode never says so, but the gray clothing, the cigarettes, the lighter, the pickaxe and the cave match what the team later finds.

docs.title: The discovery
docs.text:
In Appalachia 03, Andrew wakes in the woods with no memory of how he got there, holding a bloody steel cigarette lighter he has never seen. Following a blood trail the next morning, the team finds a crevice in the rock within earshot of the freeway. The Biz is told to stand guard while Andrew, Kurt and Huell squeeze through into a sandy chamber (Appalachia 03).

The chamber is splattered with blood and holds an old bloody pickaxe, skin, bones, hair and a man's folded face stuck to the wall. Andrew bags the face and tosses it to Huell. Kurt finds no powder marks and no chemical smell. In his judgment the man was shredded and smashed against the walls "like gators have been at a body", with bones split open, tooth marks on them, and the muscle, organs and fat missing (Appalachia 03).

The lighter is stainless steel, a little more upscale than a gas-station lighter, with "HF" written on the bottom in Sharpie, and a glob of dark hair and fat stuck to it (Appalachia 03).

docs.title: Evidence and aftermath
docs.text:
Huell stores the face in the hotel mini fridge. In Appalachia 04, he hands it to Dr. McManley, who says "Kinky" and, when Andrew protests, "It's an expression, son." (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04)

The Biz later brags to Big Bill about the "face in a bag" to soften news for an old friend (Appalachia 04). In Appalachia 07, Andrew includes "one exploded man" in his tally of the dead for Big Bill, noting that the team has only his face (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Identity
docs.text:
When Andrew phones the Spud Hut distribution center in Appalachia 03, the missing worker turns out to be Aaron Richters. Dante and Ezra immediately note that his initials do not match "HF", and Andrew concludes it may be "another missing man". The episodes never say who the dead man was, whether he was Aaron, or whose lighter it was. His death is not addressed in Walkers 01.

Not the truck driver

In Appalachia 08, people repeatedly say that a man "exploded" in the crashed Spud Hut truck. That is a separate victim, the truck driver. In Appalachia 07, Andrew distinguishes the "exploded man" from another dead man who was shot.

docs.title: Dead NSA Man in Black
docs.text:
The Dead NSA Man in Black is a gray-haired man in a black suit, carrying NSA identification, whom Jan Martense hit with his car and killed about five years before the events of The Things in Appalachia; the ape woman who began Jan's ape-men breeding program was found in his van.

Type NPC (minor, deceased, known by report only) Aliases NSA man; man in the black suit Affiliation NSA (by his ID) Status Dead (killed about five years before 1992) First appearance Walkers 01 (recounted by Jan)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Jan describes him as Hispanic, over 50, with close-cropped hair that was gray, wearing a black suit and carrying NSA ID. Jan did not keep or remember the name on the card (Walkers 01).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The only account is Jan's, told to Kurt at the CIA black site Omaha after the events of the Dahlonega case. About five years earlier, drunk and driving in the Georgia countryside at night, Jan hit and killed a man in a black suit who was crossing the highway. He searched the body, found the NSA identification, put the man in the passenger seat of his own car, and drove it into a lake ("No body, no crime"). In the man's van he heard a strange noise and found an ape woman strapped to a gurney and being fed drugs. He took her, saw a way to make money, and named her Shelly. She became the start of the breeding program that produced the ape-men (Walkers 01).

Later in the episode, Dante has Kurt ask Jan roughly where the collision happened so that the car might be found, and Andre tells him he gets the name of the lake (Walkers 01). The name is not spoken at the table.

The collision happened long before the campaign began and was never played. It is known only from Jan's account in the epilogue of the arc.

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text:
• Why a man with NSA identification had a drugged ape woman in his van, and what she is. Dante notes after the interview that this answers nothing about her origin.
  • Which lake holds the car.
  • Whether he is connected to the man in a black suit the team hit on a road earlier in the campaign, who carried a flashlight that burns things. Dante raises the link and the players joke that men in black suits keep walking into the road at night, and that they might be aliens unaware of Earth customs. Nobody in the episodes confirms a connection (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Dean Lawson
docs.text:
Dean Lawson is the Miata-driving boyfriend of Amanda Lucky and a teenage heroin dealer whom the task force never meets, though his buried cash and hidden heroin end up in their car. He vanishes before they can find him.

Type NPC (never seen in person) Aliases Dean; Lawson Affiliation Lawson family (parents own a cabin at Stately Acres) Status Missing (as of Radford Horror 08) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Andre (offscreen)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Dean plays football at the high school that Sheila attended, and his parents bought him a red Miata with the muffler cut off. Sheila calls him "a real piece of work" (Radford Horror 01). Phoebe's mother, Maybelline Augustine, says his parents are never home, that he is up in the house by himself, and that "that boy needs Jesus" (Radford Horror 05). Dean is never met in person in any episode.

docs.title: Suspect
docs.text:
Sheila identified him when his Miata roared past the diner in the first episode (Radford Horror 01). Under pressure, Dr. Lori named him as the person Amanda said was involved in drugs (Radford Horror 02). During the chase in Radford Horror 03, the team saw a red Miata pulling out of the woods near the armed campers and then turn onto a dirt road (Radford Horror 03).

Phoebe did not get along with him and had fought with Amanda over him (Radford Horror 05). In Radford Horror 06, Matt McCready said Dean had threatened to have him killed when he asked when Dean last saw Amanda, and that Dean had been hanging around with people who looked "real methy". The sheriff reported that the school had filed enough truancy reports on Dean that it called the police, and that Dean's parents could not be reached (Radford Horror 06). The cold open of that episode showed an unidentified teenager digging in a dark yard and burying three Ziploc bags of cash; the team's later discovery suggests it was Dean (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: The cabin and the stash
docs.text: In Radford Horror 07, the team went to Stately Acres to find him. The guard, Douglas Douglas, told them he had seen Dean carrying a shovel to the family cabin: "Burying bodies? I don't know." He added that he hated "that little shit", who had kicked one of his cats. At the Lawson cabin, Kurt and the others dug where the ground had been disturbed and uncovered several Ziploc bags holding about $40,000 in cash and a small tin-colored key. A loose floorboard under the bed in an untouched child's bedroom hid a locked Samsonite briefcase, which the key opened. It held four neat parcels of lightly cut heroin from somewhere in South America (Radford Horror 07). The charter pilot Freak later bought a bump from a young man whose description matched Dean's, and said the heroin came from "a bunch of Mexicans" (Radford Horror 07). See Dean Lawson's heroin and cash and The cartel.

docs.title: Vanishing
docs.text: The team kept the cash and drugs, which Diane referred to as "the budget", and spent some of the money on an air conditioner. They tipped off the sheriff that Dean was probably involved in the heroin trade. The sheriff replied that Dean's parents had not been able to reach him and nobody had seen his car. Kurt wondered whether Dean was the man the cartel had knocked down and beaten near the church. The police blamed "the cartel" for the heroin found in the church (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 07 has the cash and key buried in the cabin's yard and the heroin under the bedroom floorboard. In Radford Horror 08, the players' recaps reverse this, putting the heroin in the dug-up yard and the money in the floorboards.
  • Dean is the team's top interview target in Radford Horror 02 but is never interviewed.
  • Dante joked in Radford Horror 03 that owning a Miata cost Dean his status as official boyfriend.

docs.title: Deborah Wells
docs.text:
Deborah Wells is the Ballard, Utah school superintendent, town treasurer and church-events organiser who, with the mayor, pushes the town's community center project; the team never meets her, only hears about her and finds her desk.

Type NPC (offscreen) Aliases Superintendent Wells; the busybody; Misabelle (GM slip); Deborah Affiliation Ballard town government Status Unknown (never met; last evidence is her abandoned desk, Walkers 06) First appearance Walkers 02 (named only) Played by Not portrayed

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Wells is never seen. She is described only by role: superintendent of the public school, handler of church community events, and town treasurer (Walkers 02). A Ballard store clerk calls her "the goddamn busybody" and blames her and the mayor for the community center (Walkers 02).

docs.title: Walkers 02 to 04: the community center
docs.text:
At the Ballard general store, a clerk resents the community center, blames the mayor (Wilford Hiram) and Wells, and says she would prefer a clinic. The team adds the community center, the mayor and Wells to its list of leads (Walkers 02). See Community center.

In Maggie's bar, the bartender, who went to every grade of school with Wells and dislikes her, says the center is being built half the county away from the community and that Pueblo ruins were bulldozed for it despite a protest. She says Wells "dug in like a child" once people objected and thinks that gives Wells leverage. (Walkers 03).

In Walkers 04 Rita recalls that "Deborah mentioned how bad it was" at Ballard High School, and Dante asks whether she also mentioned someone hiding toilet seats in the walls (Walkers 04). See Ballard High School.

docs.title: Walkers 06 and 07: City Hall
docs.text: In abandoned-looking Ballard City Hall, the team finds two heavily used desks. One, piled with New York Post newspapers that stop about three months earlier and buried under hundreds of Tootsie Roll wrappers, is the mayor's; the other is Wells's (Walkers 06). See Sugar clues. The team later recaps her and the mayor among the City Hall evidence (Walkers 07); see also Disappearances in Ballard.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Speaking as the bartender, Andre first called her "Misabelle," then asked the table to "retcon that in your minds" (Walkers 03).

docs.text:

  • Desk seen: Walkers 06

docs.title: Delilah
docs.text:
Delilah is the red-haired, camcorder-carrying member of the Circle Chasers, a teenage Bigfoot-hunting group in Dahlonega, Georgia, who films the rabbit snatch and eats heroic quantities of spuds.

Type NPC (minor) Affiliation The Circle Chasers Status Alive (as of Appalachia 07) First appearance Appalachia 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Delilah is red-haired and hauls around a big, expensive VHS camcorder to document the chase. She wears flats rather than hiking boots (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Appalachia 01
docs.text: The team meets the Circle Chasers outside their trailer. Sloth introduces himself, Eddie, Vanessa, Delilah and the dog Harvey as they explain how they triangulated sightings between town and Auraria. A redheaded woman films the team the whole time with a big home video camera and tells them to "pretend like I'm not here" (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: Appalachia 02
docs.text: The Chasers arrive at the rabbit-snatch area after a howl in the woods. Delilah rewinds the camcorder and shows the team a three-second clip of the flashlight darting across the trail, ending with a rabbit frozen on the path and a gray man-sized blur grabbing it. Kurt notes each person's footwear to rule them out as fakers: hiking boots for the men and Vanessa, and flats for Delilah (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Appalachia 07
docs.text: At the original Spud Hut, Delilah is told she needs ID for a margarita spud. Kurt orders one and immediately hands it to her. The Biz orders two bacon burger spuds, eats about one and a quarter, and passes the rest to Delilah when she asks. She also devours four chicken pot pie spuds back to back, declaring that "if it's on the garbage can, it is a cheat day" (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Fellow Circle Chasers: Sloth, Eddie Jones, Vanessa and Harvey.
  • Kurt: hands her the margarita spud (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • When the Chasers appear in Appalachia 07, the table compares them to the Scooby-Doo gang, and Andre names Delilah as the Daphne (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Derek Augustine
docs.text:
Derek Augustine is a Radford pharmacist and romance novelist, publishing as "Marcus Heat", who writes in a converted barn behind his house. He is the father of Phoebe Augustine, and tortures Dr. Lori in the belief that Lori took his daughter.

Type NPC Aliases Mr. Augustine; Marcus Heat (pen name); the barn writer; the novelist Affiliation Augustine family Status In custody (as of Radford Horror 08) First appearance Radford Horror 03 (as the unnamed barn writer) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Derek writes on a typewriter in the barn behind the Augustine house, an office conversion with frosted aftermarket windows, a record player playing light jazz, a couch, a mini fridge and no phone (Radford Horror 03). He smokes outside, locks the barn behind him, and walks back to the house for dinner. Andre described his novel in progress as "the shittiest romance novel that anyone has ever seen" (Radford Horror 03). See Augustine house and barn. The books he has published are gross and pretentious, and one tries to imitate James Joyce (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The barn
docs.text:
On a stakeout, the team watched Dr. Lori storm out of the barn after a heated meeting with the writer. Kurt then hid in the barn's hayloft for roughly two hours while Derek wrote. When the writer left for dinner, Kurt searched the barn and found plot notes, dates paired with acronyms he did not recognize, and, in the couch cushions, a small hair tie with a pink butterfly. He radioed that the stakeout was "probably a dud" but that he had "found evidence of an affair, possibly with an underage person." (Radford Horror 03)

In Radford Horror 05, the team learned from Molly Underhill that Mr. Augustine was one of the town's pharmacists and that his pen name was Marcus Heat. Dante made him a prime suspect in the theft of records from the pharmacy and speculated that the novels might be a money-laundering front. Rita planned to look for a Marcus Heat novel (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: The interview
docs.text: When Phoebe vanished, the team visited the family. Derek said Amanda had visited Phoebe a few weeks earlier for a school project, so the hair clip may have fallen off then. He said he had filled Amanda's opioid prescription a couple of times, assuming it was for wisdom teeth, and that he knew about the "record error" but could not discuss it. His eye flickered when Dr. Lori was mentioned. Of Lori he said, "I always got kind of a weird vibe from the man... he likes jazz too much." Derek also handed Kurt a Polaroid of a nightdress identical to the one Phoebe had been wearing, for use with the APB (Radford Horror 05). See Phoebe Augustine.

docs.title: The torture
docs.text: In Radford Horror 06, the Biz watched from the water tower as a van with U-Haul branding stopped outside Lori's office and the driver punched Lori repeatedly and dragged him into the back. About four hours later, highway patrol found the van's occupants at a motel, where one man was torturing the other with pliers and a blowtorch. The torturer, held at state police headquarters, was Derek, who believed Lori had kidnapped his daughter and was trying to get information out of him. Derek said he had gotten the idea from the team's earlier conversation, which Andre said he was probably reading too much into. Dante called him an amateur for the blowtorch (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: The confession
docs.text: In Radford Horror 08, the sheriff reported that Derek and Dr. Lori had both confessed to an inappropriate sexual relationship with Amanda Lucky. Each had found out about the other, and Derek then went "medieval" on Lori after getting the idea that Lori was doing the same to his daughter. They were both going to prison. The police also suspected Derek of breaking into Lori's office and leaving animal feces in his toilet. While recovering in the hospital, Andrew asked Diane for Derek's books from the Radford used bookstore, picking whichever made him feel the grossest (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Derek Edwards
docs.text:
Derek Edwards is a tall, bearded amateur photographer and contractor for Auraria's small newspaper, the Gold Bug, whose Chewbacca costume was stolen from Apollo's dry cleaners and later turned up on a dead man.

Type NPC (minor) Aliases Derek Richter (Andre's slip) Affiliation The Gold Bug (contract photographer) Status Alive (as of Appalachia 06) First appearance Appalachia 06 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Derek is quite tall, with a very long beard, a ponytail and a vest. He has no military record. He uses computers a great deal and runs the newspaper's website, and he puts out hunting-blind cameras to photograph deer. He is cooperative (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
After the team finds a dead man in a Chewbacca costume on Frotter Comstock's land, Kurt goes to the Gold Bug to find the source of the newspaper's Bigfoot photo. A pinched older woman at the shopfront names the photographer as "Derek Richter", and Andre immediately corrects it to Derek Edwards. She says he is a contractor rather than staff, and volunteers that she believes he is gay, which prompts Andrew to point out that gay people can have friends. She fetches a number from a dusty Rolodex (Appalachia 06).

A young-sounding man who gives his name as Carlos, and who says he is a friend of Mr. Edwards, answers the phone and hands it to an older-sounding Derek. Derek says the photos came from a motion-sensor camera, so nobody helped him. When Kurt mentions the Chewbacca costume, Derek says his own was stolen: he sent it to be dry cleaned eight months earlier and it vanished from the rack. He had bought it for cash at Comic-Con, with no receipt, and says it smelled strongly like "fat nerd", which is why he was having it cleaned. The cleaners was Apollo's, down on Second (Appalachia 06).

At Apollo's, the man at the front desk confirms the theft. The latch on the double door of the storage area had been broken for months, and he paid Derek $100 for the loss. He recognizes the photo of the dead man as an out-of-town drifter who stood around watching, sometimes with a walkie-talkie, and who he thinks stayed at the Motel and Suites. The lead points the team toward the dead man, later identified as Troy Cleaver, and not toward Derek (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The name "Derek Richter" was Andre's slip: he notices at once that he had already used "Richter" for Aaron Richters and corrects himself.
