docs.title: Diane
docs.text:
Diane is the secretary of the Paranatural Incident Task Force, who runs its barbershop headquarters in Washington, D.C. and serves as the agents' phone contact in the field.

Type NPC Aliases Andrew's secretary Affiliation FBI; Paranatural Incident Task Force; later FBI records Status Alive (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Diane is introduced as "30-something," with big, out-of-date hair, spinning in a barber chair. She chain-smokes, lighting each new cigarette from the last, plays solitaire with her own deck of cards, and sings "Natural Woman" to give Andrew Howard privacy. She is warm and quick-witted, and she was assigned to the barbershop with no briefing at all. (Radford Horror 01)

Her voice is dry and practical. She calls Andrew "Howard" or "Mr. Howard," and later addresses every agent as Mr. and surname. (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 03, Roulet Estate 03)

At the Christmas party of 1992 Andre describes her as "pretty, like, bubbly," someone who likes people and takes an interest in them. She is married, is very close to a niece, "does something with gourds" that none of the agents has bothered to understand, and keeps three Southwestern landscapes at her desk. She loves crafts and shops at "Wally World." (Radford Horror 08, Walkers 01, Roulet Estate 01)

The episodes disagree about whether she has children. In Walkers 01 she passes on pogs that "my son's friend left" at her house, and in Walkers 06 she advises Kurt "as a mother"; in Roulet Estate 01 Andre tells the players that she "doesn't have kids." (Walkers 01, Walkers 06, Roulet Estate 01)

Andrew's verdict, once the task force is gone, is that "she was the best person on our team. She actually did her job correctly." (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
Andrew meets Diane on the task force's first morning at the D.C. barbershop and hands her his parking tickets. She identifies the jars of Ephedrine and Mandrax that Huell Kendrick finds behind the plumbing as old "stakeout candy," runs outside to move the Lincoln Continental away from a meter maid, and lends Huell her cards. When she notices a landmine in the basement arsenal, Andrew gives her a speech about benevolent aliens guiding humanity; she resolves to trust "the institution and you personally." (Radford Horror 01)

During the Radford case she is the voice on the other end of the phone. Kurt Larson calls her from the Pay n' Stay and later asks her to cross-check highway-patrol roadkill data, and Andrew gives her as the contact for the elderly couple whose car the team commandeers, so that they can be reimbursed. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03)

After the church fight she drives out to the Radford ER, having been told the team would probably die. She asks for the keys to their illegally parked car; Andrew freezes and admits it is full of drugs and money, and she is relieved that it is only heroin. Over the week-long hospital stay she fetches books from the used bookstore, including the novels of Derek Augustine. Back in Washington she spends some of Dean Lawson's heroin and cash, which she calls "the budget," on two window air conditioners that make the lights flicker, and helps name the office mascot, OJ the stuffed alien. Kurt sets up regular phone check-ins with her before the team leaves for Marblehead. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
When Andrew phones to say "I found an arm," Diane arranges a forensics team and passes on the secretary pool's gossip about its leader, Donald McManley: good, abrasive, and the reason his last secretary quit. She asks the team to keep the Biz from fighting him. She will not say the word "moth" on the phone, spelling it out as "M-O-T-H" in case the NSA, "the Puzzle Palace," is listening, and promises to "send in the cavalry" if something big tries to kill them. She also holds Andrew's mail from the Radford ER at the office. (Summer Service 01)

She later pages Andrew to say that the CDC, FEMA and the NCEH are all calling the secretary pool, that the governor may call out the National Guard, and that the toxin that hit the team is "not VX exactly" but close and appears synthetic (see Synthetic nerve agent). Told that Andrew now suspects an "alien submarine," she replies that this is not very different from a sea monster. Andrew tells McManley to call her if the team has not turned up by the next day. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: Diane staffs the front desk of the PITF office, buys supplies out of drug-money "petty cash," hands out popcorn, and brings up the dossier on the Dahlonega disappearances with the hope that this case will be "less national-newsy." (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
After the Georgia case makes the task force famous, members of the public start turning up at the office, including a woman whose dead mother is haunting her (Alberta Wilmarth). Diane asks what to do with them, and the team settles on a tip box, which she treats as a craft project. She gives Huell some pogs that her son's friend left at her house. (Walkers 01)

From Utah, Kurt phones her to verify the alibi phone call of Yusuf Ansari. She agrees to have it run and asks "Any ape men?" (Walkers 06)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
On Christmas Eve 1992 Diane decorates the office. Her tree trips the breaker and wipes Andrew's last Utah report; she finds an extension-cord arrangement that works and tunes the stereo to "Rockin' Around the Christmas Tree." Her Secret Santa gifts are watercolor paper for Kurt's daughter, a hand-knit sweater for Andrew, scotch for Huell and new shoes for the Biz. In return she receives a pashmina shawl from Andrew, scotch from Huell, Southwestern scratch-off tickets from the Biz (some already scratched), and from Kurt a Herman Miller chair stamped as NSA property, after which she proposes wheeling her old chair to the curb and setting it on fire; Kurt agrees they will have to, "for the bugs." Kurt's gift to Andrew, a fake alien fetus in a jar, horrifies her. Big Bill then arrives with the news that the task force will be disbanded. (Roulet Estate 01)

On Inauguration Day the drunk agents wake her and make her drive them about seven hours to Rhode Island, with five stops for Corn Nuts and one, against her wishes, to pick up the Finnish Hare Krishna Monk. The next morning the hungover agents find what looks like a body under a blanket in the back seat of the agents' car; it is Diane, asleep, and she is the one who can tell them how they got to the Roulet House. When the Roulet Intruder opens fire she panics, and when it steals the car she is stranded with them and walks with the party to the Clown Mansion. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

Once the local police arrive she makes small talk with the uniforms and is sent home by way of the airport. After the task force is dissolved she is reassigned to FBI records, which she finds quiet. She phones Andrew to check on everyone: Kurt is busy, Huell talked her ear off about Roseanne, and she cannot reach "Mr. Baxter." (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text: It is Diane who alerts Andrew that nobody can reach the Biz, who left the hospital months earlier. Still in records, she runs checks for Kurt: narrowing the window of the disappearance, pulling international flights, collecting newspapers and looking into missing submarines, of which she knows only those lost at Marblehead. In Radford the team considers putting her on the Safe Environment Fund as well. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Andrew Howard: her boss, whom she trusts personally. Andrew is known to embellish his reports to her with aliens, where Kurt tells her the literal truth. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 01)
  • Kurt Larson: her most frequent caller for records work. Asked to look him in the eye and say he does not look like a fed, she answers, "You do look like a fed." (Radford Horror 08, Walkers 06)
  • The team: she worries about them in the field, and is sorry to see the task force go: "I've been really enjoying spending time with you people." (Summer Service 01, Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"My life has gotten a lot more surreal since about 6 this morning. But you know what? I'm going to trust that you people know what you're doing." Andre (as Diane) (Radford Horror 01)

Quote

"If it seems like a big— I can't say it— if it seems like a big thing is gonna try to kill you guys, let me know so I can send in the cavalry." Andre (as Diane) (Summer Service 01)

Quote

"You guys are the weirdest cops." Andre (as Diane) (Roulet Estate 01)

Quote

"I can't believe the fucking gray alien stole our car." Andre (as Diane) (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Dick "The Biz" Baxter
docs.text:
Dick "The Biz" Baxter is an FBI counterintelligence agent and founding member of the Paranatural Incident Task Force, played by Ezra.

Type Player character Aliases The Biz; Dick; Special Agent Dick Baxter; "Richard Baxter" (Letterman, Yeltsin); Noah Mueller (passport alias); "Bizarino" (Kurt) Affiliation FBI (Counterintelligence); Paranatural Incident Task Force; secret contact of Russian intelligence Status Alive, held in Russia as a guest of Boris Yeltsin; blind in one eye (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Ezra

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The Biz is a stocky man in his forties, about 200 lb, with what the table calls a "normal middle-aged shape": too big for a cave crevice in Georgia, a chimney in Rhode Island and an air vent in a pharmacy. He first appears in a brown windbreaker, khakis and shiny shoes, and later settles into sport jackets and black rather than a suit. Ezra's mental image is a competent mid-forties character from a Japanese or Korean film, with nice clothes, a rough look and a casino-and-cigarette-smoke air. A hotel clerk in Dahlonega calls him "kind of hot, bigger guy". His colleagues note that he always looks pale and sweaty. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 04, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 06, Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

He is cynical, paranoid, deadpan and tired. He drinks, smokes, avoids confrontation, dislikes driving and describes himself as not a deeply curious person. He prefers working people face to face to reading files, and his best-used talent is tidying away evidence of his own crimes. His diet runs to corn dogs, donuts, sunflower seeds, Corn Nuts and black coffee, and his digestive troubles are one of the campaign's longest running gags. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Appalachia 01)

After The Walkers in Skin he has a mouth full of gold fillings, and a scar where a chunk was bitten out of his cheek. By The Radford Horrors he is about 35 lb lighter, clean-shaven and blind in one eye. (Walkers 05, Walkers 07, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
The Biz served in Vietnam as a radio operator in signals intelligence. He was not in active combat, but he had to run from the Viet Cong at the very end, which Ezra says traumatized him, and he came home with lasting damage to his appetite and his nerves. He then spent his career in FBI Counterintelligence in Washington, DC, mostly on nuclear-security work, where he once ran a canary trap using almost 1,000 copies of a fake reactor plan, each with a different error. He only ever went to zoos for dead drops. He speaks and reads some Russian and can recognise Chechen. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 04, Summer Service 04, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 03)

His private life is a mess. He has a gambling problem, a shabby DC apartment, repossession letters for a car about $2,500 behind on payments, and by his own account was for years "more into cocaine and lying to people", which is where the nickname comes from. He grew up Catholic and, by his own account, talked to God until his thirties without anything ever happening. His closest friend outside work is Jeff "Apple" Appleby, a DC lawyer turned federal judge, whom he once talked down from a Las Vegas rooftop while blackout drunk. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 08, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 07)

Before the task force he thought anyone who believed in the paranormal was nuts. (Appalachia 04)

At character creation Ezra gave him two ex-wives: a high-school sweetheart he has not spoken to in many years, and a more recent wife whose departure, bound up with his money troubles, is the sorer spot. One of them is from Radford. In Appalachia 07 Ezra decided that the Biz is not "a finalize-the-divorce kind of guy", so the second marriage was never formally ended, and on Letterman the Biz jokes that he is already estranged from his wife. He has no children. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 04, Appalachia 07, Walkers 01)

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
Assigned to the new task force under Andrew Howard, the Biz staked out its barbershop headquarters for hours before going in, decided his new boss was an actual lunatic, and introduced himself as "Dick" and then with "My friends call me the Biz." (Radford Horror 01)

In Radford he did the hands-on scouting. He tracked footprints at the Whateley house, searched its rooms, found the radio and the library books, and planted a bug in the office of Dr. Lawrence Lori. He later burgled that office to get the bug back, photographed the patient files and stole a prescription pad. After the team's car struck Agent Murphy and Murphy's flashlight weapon went off, the Biz chased him, fired a warning shot and missed, then cleaned glass, blood and burned trees off the road. The same night he charmed the motel clerk Rutherford into selling him $40 of DMT, and from his car, with night vision, he watched the craft skim the treetops behind the houses where a dog and then Phoebe Augustine vanished. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05)

He was the task force's skeptic. He told the team that aliens were "back off the menu", called Andrew's theology blasphemy, and raised the secrecy question in the FBI huddle. He spent the stakeout at the Alpine Lodge water tower as spotter, then explored the Whateley cellar and hid a live radio bug behind the flag patch of the spaceman suit. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06)

The fight in the old-town church ended his skepticism. With no armor and no melee weapon he shot the Radford Moth, was slashed across the chest, tore its wing with his bare fingers, climbed to its face and gouged out its eyes. Its psychic blow left him seizing on the floor of the burning building. He burned a Luck point to wake, collapsed short of the door and was dragged out by Kurt Larson. He reached 5 harm and was stabilized by Andrew and Kurt. (Radford Horror 07)

He left hospital with burns, several pounds of thigh tissue missing and recurring butterfly nightmares, having bet drug money on the Cubs and lost. Back at the church, his search showed that the gore and dog collars had been removed in a cover-up. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
In Marblehead the Biz stole and hid one of the crystal marbles, licked it, tested it with a new pocket knife and later told the team the marbles were diamonds. Unknown to him, he was himself under FBI counterintelligence surveillance. He did not drink the communion wine and was never infected by the worms. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04)

He became the party's chief investigator, twice rolling 14 at the lighthouse, and talked the assistant Henry away from Donald McManley. His 1986 Buick Regal, which had once carried a severed arm, ended up as the mount for Kurt's Davy Crockett. A career in nuclear security left him appalled at a loose nuclear weapon; he said nothing and smoked. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04)

This arc also revealed his secret. Instructions he had received required a 1980 reprint of Moby Dick. He bought one, sent the team away, called a recorded "promotional sweepstakes" from a distant payphone and decoded its number lists with the book cipher. The message, from Russian intelligence, said that submarines had been lost near Massachusetts, cause unknown, with instructions to follow. He concluded the Russians were probably not behind the case and kept the message to himself. (Summer Service 04)

At Arnold Weathers' house his panicked burst of gunfire destroyed the hallway decor and hit nothing else. He planted a bug, took the marbles, and helped pass the sixty-pound warhead out of a window as police climbed the stairs. Having bought welding goggles and earplugs in advance, he lost rock-paper-scissors to Huell Kendrick for the honour of firing the weapon, and drove the survivors out while they slept. He finished the case unharmed. (Summer Service 05, Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
On 3 October 1992 a sweepstakes mailer that the Biz recognised as a KGB front sent him to a payphone and the "Canada maple syrup sweepstakes line". The decoded message offered $10,000 and information on the "Massachusetts matter" for a favor in Georgia. Paying a homeless man $50 to collect from the old drop spot, he received a covert microphone and film camera and flash-paper orders: install the camera in room 111 of the Smith Hotel in Dahlonega before midnight two days later, retrieve it after 24 hours, and mail the undeveloped film. By chance the team was booked next door. The desk clerk reported the room's booker as suspicious and lent the Biz the master key. He hid the camera facing the bed and the microphone on the bedside drawer and left no prints. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)

On the case itself he found the shoe in the tree, held hands in the human chain in the mine, and climbed out last as the tunnel collapsed. He declared himself "three for three" on real creatures. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04)

Unrecorded session

Appalachia 05 was never recorded. The next recorded session shows only the aftermath: the Biz wandered in wearing slept-in clothes with a badly twisted ankle, the door of the room next to the team's had been broken down, and state police pulled a night-vision headset out of the hotel bushes for the Secret Service. What happened that night has never been stated on a recording. (Appalachia 06)

He developed film in the hotel bathroom and came out pale and distracted, then went to "retrieve the thing". The next day state police announced that the FBI had been surveilling candidate Bill Clinton in Dahlonega, with fingerprints on recovered equipment matching an unnamed agent. The Clinton surveillance scandal put Andrew on live television and the whole team in hiding from the press. The Biz, by then sleepless and frayed, floated the theory that it was a fake Watergate-style smear, and admitted in passing that he had no bugs left because he had used them all on Clinton. (Appalachia 06, Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08)

Under the Spud Hut plant he was the only one to hear the door squeak and see the hairy arm, dropped on reflex at the Claymore warning, and photographed the crack in the air with his spy camera on a timer. He fought Big Bob, was thrown by him, and left the mine carrying an unreasonable amount of gold. (Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09)

Unrecorded session

The finale, Appalachia 10, was never recorded. Dialogue in the next episode establishes that the Biz shot a Polish man in the woods with a shotgun and had a heart attack around that time. The Georgia State Police released his name and recovered his night-vision monocular from a rose bush, making him "the most hated cop in America". Officially it was Jan Martense who was caught surveilling Clinton. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
A few days before the election the FBI ordered the Biz onto David Letterman's show, the one concession to programmes that wanted someone actually involved. Sweating through his makeup, he opened with a joke the audience found "complicated", then burned a Luck point to turn a Manipulate Someone roll into a 12 and made Letterman an ally. Letterman told him on air that the Clinton Polaroids were taken with a Russian camera, which was news to him. He closed with a marked-card trick using his wallet and badge; the patter was rough but it earned more claps than boos, and a production assistant gave him Letterman's personal number. He came out of it hated less, more famous and harder to read. (Walkers 01)

In Ballard he was recognised on sight as the man who spied on Clinton, first by FBI agent Carl Gardner. He worked as the team's fixer: a contact in Salt Lake City, Drebin, supplied the ground-penetrating radar, and his DC informant Hooster took an order for a bomb collar. (Walkers 02, Walkers 03, Walkers 04)

The night event at the ranch hit him hardest. Part of his visual field crumbled and he lost every filling in his mouth; he was treated with cocaine and spent a day at the dentist getting gold replacements on the FBI's tab. Still slurring, he tested Yusuf Ansari with a trick question and argued for paying the $10,000 and letting the local police think they had won. (Walkers 05, Walkers 06)

When the naked intruder broke into the guest house, the Biz looped his belt round the man's neck and had a piece of his cheek bitten out. In the next session's tactical entry and firefight he stepped on plate glass, was winged, and killed the first gunman with a head shot. During this period the duplicate Andrew secretly took a sample of his blood. He rode out the finale on horseback with binoculars and kept a private hypothesis about Howard to himself. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
At the office Christmas party the Biz gave a Georgia gold nugget to carolers, scratch-off tickets to Diane and a floppy disk marked "Mystery Government Files" to Kurt, and planned a Vegas trip with his judge friend. On Inauguration Day 1993 he woke in the Roulet house and vomited into a Stetson that was not his, with a holster but no gun. He and Kurt were the only ones to spot the grey face on the roof, took charge of restoring transport, bluffed his way to a telephone at the Clown Mansion and made the official call to the FBI. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

At the Brooks Pharmacy siege he climbed to the roof, opened the door with a credit card and wedged himself into the drop ceiling as a fail-safe. When the gunman was about to spot Kurt, the Biz fired first. The return shot from a Mosin-Nagant went through the ceiling into his thigh for 3 harm and he fell onto the tile. Andrew's healing failed, and a tourniquet saved him. (Roulet Estate 03)

He then vanished from the hospital, and his teammates assumed he had run. In fact the Russians had taken him. They had his leg treated at a good Russian hospital, then held him in a freezing cell at the abandoned Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp, where he was beaten and interrogated and then left for two weeks in near silence, making up sea shanties and talking to a cockroach. When a senior officer looked in through the door slot, the Biz welcomed him in polite Russian. He was flown to Moscow and handcuffed to a chair in front of Boris Yeltsin, who put a Cuban cigar in his mouth, lit it and told him to start talking. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
By early April 1993, about three months after his abduction, the Biz was living under guard in the Hotel Metropol on stroganoff, champagne and dubbed soap operas, passing the borscht he did not like to a friendly guard. His first captors had asked about Clinton; the new ones asked only about aliens. His strategy was to exaggerate how seriously the United States takes the paranatural and hide that Ross Perot might axe the task force, and a Manipulate Someone roll of 11 sold it. In Yeltsin's opera box he stonewalled on the Marblehead explosion, explained skinwalkers, identified a half-melted flashlight weapon, and praised Andrew Howard while leaving out his abilities. He scouted escape routes and hid bed sheets but did not want to run. (Radford Horrors 01)

In Washington his teammates searched his apartment. They found his gold, cash and cocaine under a floorboard, the torn-up Moby-Dick with circled words, bills for classified ads in three DC papers, a granted six-month leave for a "family emergency", and a bug-out briefcase holding Swiss francs, a revolver and a Swiss passport in the name Noah Mueller. Andrew asked whether the Biz was a double agent; Kurt answered that there are degrees. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

Summoned at 3 a.m. to ride in Yeltsin's convoy toward Oryol Oblast, the Biz woke as ambushers rammed the presidential limousine. He burned Luck to get Yeltsin into a car, drove it blacked-out into a wheat field, carried the president into the wheat and ambushed a pursuer with a guard's knife. The man gouged one of his eyes, blinding it, before collapsing from blood loss. A helicopter collected them both. (Radford Horrors 03)

Yeltsin then took him to the Oryol crash site, where a triangular craft had destroyed a farmhouse. The Biz witnessed the questioning of the crash survivor, who spoke of "Survey" and servitors, noticed its resemblance to the change in Andrew Howard since his death, and told Yeltsin honestly that these were not the beings he knew. He remains in Russia. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Andrew Howard: The Biz began by thinking him a lunatic and mocks him as a "tight-ass Fed", but to Yeltsin he called Howard a remarkable agent and a mentor. Andrew, for his part, assumed the missing Biz was probably dead. (Radford Horror 01, Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Huell Kendrick: His brother "in all things greedy". Huell backed him up on Letterman, beat him at darts and gave him a dead lookalike's ID for Christmas. (Appalachia 09, Walkers 01, Walkers 03, Roulet Estate 01)
  • Kurt Larson: His "brother in all things sketchy". Kurt dragged him out of the burning church, and the Biz took a rifle round to protect Kurt in Rhode Island. (Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 09, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Boris Yeltsin: Captor turned patron, who usually calls him "Mr. Baxter" and owes him his life. (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)
  • His handlers: An old voice on a sweepstakes line, paying in cash and information. (Summer Service 04, Appalachia 01)
  • Jeff "Apple" Appleby: Drinking friend and federal judge. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Abilities and equipment
docs.text:
The Biz's playbook is never named at the table. The moves he is seen to use are listed below; see Game mechanics for the rules as played. (Radford Horror 02, Walkers 01, Walkers 04, Appalachia 09)

  • Concealing a crime: +1 when hiding evidence of a crime. Andre remarked that "your crime move is the one that by far gets the most use".
  • Fixer: to buy, sell or hire, roll +Charm.
  • Grifter: before manipulating someone, ask the Keeper what will convince them.
  • Charlatan: to make people think he is using magic, roll +Cool. Ezra took it with a saved level-up just before the Letterman taping: between cases the Biz had been teaching himself conjuring tricks so that he could pass off what he had seen Howard really do as "woo-woo powers" of his own. The card trick on Letterman is the only time he performs.
  • Advanced moves: Investigate a Mystery and Manipulate Someone, marked as advanced with a second level-up in the same session.

Ratings. Charm +2 at the start, +3 by The Walkers in Skin; Sharp +3; Tough 0. Cool rose from 0 to +1 as his first improvement and was +2 by Roulet Estate 03. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 04, Walkers 04, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 03)

Luck and harm. He burned Luck in the church fire, on Letterman and again during the convoy ambush in Russia, which left him three Luck before he is Doomed. His injuries include burns and a mauled thigh from the moth, a heart attack, lost fillings, a bitten cheek, a rifle wound to the thigh and a lost eye. (Radford Horror 07, Walkers 01, Radford Horrors 03)

Gear. Night-vision goggles, repeatedly lost; a spy camera and bugs; binoculars, pager and handcuffs; a flask, lighter and cigarettes; his Buick Regal; a cheap Casio scrambled at the ranch; and a share of the Georgia gold. He refuses to carry a bigger gun. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 06, Walkers 03, Walkers 04, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Dick or Richard? In Radford Horror 07 Ezra says the name is "not even short for Richard", and in Appalachia 02 that his passport reads Dick. Letterman nevertheless introduces "FBI agent Richard Baxter", Yeltsin calls him Richard once (a slip: when a guard begins a line with "Richard" in Radford Horrors 04, Andre corrects it to "Mr. Baxter"), and when Andre asked for the Biz's actual name in Roulet Estate 03, Ezra answered, "Richard Baxter. A.k.a. Dick." (Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 02, Walkers 01, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Where was the gold? In the Roulet Estate 03 epilogue the players agree that his teammates buried his share and left him a cryptic message, and Andre rules that it is in a park near his home. One session later the team finds "all of the Biz's share of the gold" under his apartment floorboard. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Faith. In Radford Horror 04 Ezra describes him as someone who grew up Catholic and is not particularly religious, but in Walkers 08 he says, "The Biz is a Presbyterian, I think I've decided." By his time in Moscow the Biz admits to "some kind of spiritual awakening maybe beginning to take root". (Radford Horror 04, Walkers 08, Radford Horrors 01)
  • The handlers. Andre calls the sweepstakes mailer "a KGB front" in Appalachia 01; elsewhere the Biz's contact is simply Russian intelligence. (Summer Service 04, Appalachia 01)
  • Secret scenes. Andre ran the Biz's spy scenes in Appalachia with the other players out of the call, though he admitted that "they know the gist". (Appalachia 01)
  • The abduction. After the pharmacy siege Ezra suggested that the Biz would either be abducted from hospital by the Russians or go to ground, and left the choice to Andre, who picked "abducted and still in custody, because that's more interesting". Ezra played Daniel Webster in the Virginia scenes that followed. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 02)
  • The voice. Ezra began with no planned voice, used a Columbo impression on the radio, and settled into Boston slang and accent, which he admits he keeps forgetting. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 01, Walkers 03, Roulet Estate 02)
  • In Radford the diner waitress Sheila remembers him as the one who blew up the toilet. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Ezra has said that if the Biz dies, his next character will be an Australian bush pilot. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Donald McManley
docs.text:
Donald McManley is the abrasive FBI forensic examiner who works out of an RV crime lab and is called in whenever a Paranatural Incident Task Force case produces a body, a sample or a face in a bag.

Type NPC Aliases McManley; Dr. McManley; Doc McManley; Don; the examiner; the M.E. Affiliation FBI forensics Status Alive (as of Radford Horrors 04); en route to Radford First appearance Summer Service 01 (mentioned); Summer Service 03 (in person) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
McManley's reputation arrives before he does: Diane reports from the secretary pool that he is good at his work, abrasive, called the team "flatfoots," and drove his previous secretary to quit. (Summer Service 01)

In person he is straight-laced and impatient, with a line in dark jokes that he delivers without a laugh and sometimes has to label ("See, that was a joke"). He does not "eat cholesterol," loves MRE instant coffee, is fussy about hygiene, and sleeps in floral pajamas and a nightcap with a shotgun to hand. He is openly contemptuous of rural Georgia and its "yokels." (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 04)

He is variously described as a forensic examiner, a forensic scientist, a medical examiner and "Dr." McManley, and he states that he is a badged federal agent. Andre confirms that he served in Vietnam. He is not in the team's chain of command: when Ezra took him for their boss, Andre corrected him that McManley is "your… pet medical examiner," and that the boss is Big Bill. Under the new FBI leadership of 1993 he still has a reputation for being abrasive but very good at his job. He "might be a little tainted" by his part in the team's cases, but he is not under suspicion, and his personal friendships with high-ranking FBI people are "why he is able to be kind of a jerk." (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 07, Walkers 08, Radford Horrors 04)

He travels with McManley's RV and a rotating set of browbeaten interns: two in Marblehead, three teenagers at one point in Georgia, and two again later. He will not drive the RV as far as Utah, preferring to fly "like God intended." At home he lives in a quaint cottage with rose bushes and many locks, kept clean but full of reptile terrariums, including tortoises and a very fat tegu named Cartwright. (Summer Service 03, Appalachia 06, Appalachia 07, Walkers 03, Appalachia 01)

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
After Andrew Howard finds the severed arm in Marblehead, Diane arranges for McManley's team to arrive the next morning. (Summer Service 01)

Unrecorded session

McManley's arrival in Marblehead is not seen: Summer Service 02, the session in between, was never recorded. By Summer Service 03 he is already set up in town and knows about the nerve agent.

He is found working from a large mobile home outside Amos Shaw's house. He reports a full body's worth of blood, mostly in the bathroom, and a broken bathroom door that suggests a second party; because Andrew met Amos Shaw alive after the blood was shed, he reasons the victim is someone else. He accepts Huell Kendrick's "wellness check" explanation for having been inside, bags the crystal marbles without knowing what they are, and chooses not to inform the Marblehead police. (Summer Service 03)

Later, parked beside the post office, he and two interns put the communion wine under a microscope and find it swimming with the worms. He tells Andrew to get ivermectin from a large-animal vet and says he will call the CDC. (Summer Service 03)

He is reluctant to help fetch the drug ("just drive to Salem") until the Biz's Manipulate Someone (13) wins the loan of his assistant Henry ("You can take Henry. He's useless anyway"), who sets off on a Vespa in the storm and stops answering his radio. (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05)

With no hot water in the RV, McManley takes a room at the team's hotel, the Ram and Arms Inn. There he is shown the still-living severed head of Puddles ("it's really bad"), wonders aloud why the cult does not simply contaminate the grocery stores, and notes that Jester took a phone call and all but ran out of the door. When armed church members surround the hotel at about 4 a.m. he joins the defense with his shotgun, and after Kurt leads the group to the RV he drives it out, up on two wheels in the gusts. The RV is abandoned behind the abandoned gas station. (Summer Service 05)

Unrecorded session

McManley does not appear in the recorded finale. Summer Service 06 establishes that the team left the lab technicians with the RV, which happened in the unrecorded session "05.5." McManley later says that on the same evening as the dog's head he punched a worm-puppeted corpse in the street, which is not seen in any recorded episode. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
By October 1992 McManley is on leave and close to being fired. Big Bill sends Huell to check on him. He answers the door of his cottage with a shotgun, a cigarette and an open bathrobe; the windows are covered in foil, takeout bags are piling up, and Saturday Night Live is on. Huell finds a second, dusty toothbrush and razor in the bathroom and three or four bottles of ivermectin, all but one used. McManley describes what he saw in Marblehead and spirals into an existential crisis. (Appalachia 01)

Huell's Manipulate Someone, at -1 forward because McManley hates him, comes up 3, and Zack spends a point of Luck. The two commiserate over Roseanne. McManley promises to return to work on Monday, says he should call someone named Keith, and drags his television to the curb. The team then invites him to Dahlonega, partly to get him out of the house. (Appalachia 01)

He radios ahead as he arrives with the mobile lab, delighted to hear there is a face in a bag, and relays Big Bill's order to handle the case by the book. Finding no RV hookups in town, he takes rooms at the Smith Hotel and runs a generator. He receives the folded face, Gene's shoe with its tuft of pale hair, and a small blood sample from the creature Kurt shot, complains that Kurt should have used a larger caliber, and proposes that the attacker was a huge man on meth and PCP. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04)

Unrecorded session

His analysis of the blood, which identified an ape-human hybrid and gave the Ape-Men their name, came back during Appalachia 05, which was never recorded. It is known from the team's references in Appalachia 06 and 08.

He collects the body of Troy Cleaver, noting that the bandolier of the Chewbacca costume had been removed and mud rubbed into the fur, and sends three teenage interns to sort and dust a dumpster's worth of garbage bags at the Motel and Suites. (Appalachia 06)

It is McManley who breaks the news of the Clinton surveillance scandal to the team, quipping that for all they know he could have been the spy. He takes custody of the SHA tracking device, endures the drunk Biz interrogating his interns in the cramped RV, and is asked at the freeway crash site to work out where the dirt in the Spud Hut truck came from. He is then called to process the blood-soaked cab. (Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
McManley pages Huell early in the Utah case with one demand: tell him the moment it looks real, because he has to fly and needs time to repack. Huell puts off the call, then makes it at about 3 a.m. and hangs up. McManley eventually takes down Andrew's wish list for a field kit, warns that the expenses will have to be justified, and still maintains that the ape-men should have been "basically chimpanzees." Evidence piles up for him in the meantime, including a carbonized crow in a dog-waste bag. (Walkers 03, Walkers 04, Walkers 05)

He arrives a day later than planned and under fire. On the road between Ballard and Roosevelt a spike strip rolls his Suburban and four townspeople attack without making any demands: a woman with a shotgun, an older man with a handgun and two children with kitchen knives. McManley and his two interns kill all four, and one intern is shot in the leg. He did not realize that two were children until it was over, and he looks worse than he did after "the worms incident." He refuses Andrew's offer of a meditation technique and instead takes a cigarette from Huell, despite having quit. (Walkers 08)

At the Roosevelt police station he examines the prisoners and performs the autopsy that explains the arc. In general terms, he finds that the bodies are not ordinary people but manufactured hosts, each steered by a separate creature inside the skull, and he lays out how the two depend on each other (see Pilot and host biology and Skinwalkers). The removed organ goes into break-room Tupperware (Pilot organ in Tupperware). He is the last to learn that the adult and the child he shot on the road were hosts too. (Walkers 08)

Unrecorded session

In the unrecorded session "08.5" the team left McManley, his interns and a few Guardsmen at the Roosevelt police station to continue the autopsies. This is known from Walkers 09 and Roulet Estate 01.

The team collects him, the interns and the Guardsmen from the station at the end and drives them toward a hospital. In the medical tent outside Roosevelt he limps to Andrew's bed with his analysis of the white powder that covered the Guardsmen: a mix of sedatives and hypnotics with something unidentified, which only the rising wind kept from overdosing the soldiers. His case of autopsy samples is among the little evidence that survives. (Walkers 09, Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text: McManley is only mentioned: as the examiner the agents would need to establish a cause of death for the remains in the Roulet basement, and in a later phone call in which Andrew asks Diane not to tell him about Huell's Roseanne habit. (Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text: During Huell's months of convalescence McManley sends him only a curt get-well card. When the team finds pearlescent goo in Radford, Kurt wants a sample sent to him, and Huell phones from a payphone. McManley agrees to bring the RV and is expected the following day. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Huell Kendrick: McManley hates him from Marblehead onward, where Huell mocks his pajamas and McManley cuts off his goat-racing story. The Roseanne visit softens this into a bond "in an odd, antagonistic way," and Huell becomes the one who phones him. He calls Huell "Kendrick." (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 01, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Andrew Howard: a target for teasing and stare-downs, and someone he will not let touch him. (Appalachia 04, Walkers 08)
  • Kurt Larson: treats McManley as the team's pathologist; McManley knows him as "Larson." (Summer Service 03, Walkers 08)
  • Dick "The Biz" Baxter: bristles at him before they meet, talks him out of an assistant, and is ignored when he makes Clinton jokes. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 04, Walkers 05)

docs.title: Doug
docs.text:
Doug is the tendril-mouthed man of two Walkers in Skin cold opens: a large, dead-eyed trailer-dweller in the Utah desert who eats Jell-O and passes grey tendrils from his mouth, in the second case into a woman's mouth.

Type NPC / entity (cold-open character) Aliases Tendril-mouthed man; cold-open man Affiliation None established Status Unknown First appearance Walkers 04 (cold open) Played by Andre (narration)

Name

The name "Doug" is spoken only in Walkers 06. The man in the Walkers 04 cold open is never named, but the two scenes share the same trailer details, the Jell-O, a wrapped figure in a chair and the same tendrils, so they are treated here as one man.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In the Walkers 04 cold open, a pale, morbidly obese man in a wife beater walks through the desert with a shovel to a trailer whose lights come on automatically. The entryway holds a large cross and a mirror. He takes something from the fridge and sits in a recliner; a human-shaped figure wrapped in something shiny is propped in the other chair. He lifts a large plate of Jell-O to his chin, and fine grey tendrils spool out of his mouth onto it while his dead eyes watch the muted TV (Walkers 04).

In Walkers 06 a woman arrives at a desert trailer, takes the spare key from under a ceramic frog, and finds a pile of mail, the TV on low, cabinets of hundreds of Jell-O packages and a fridge of Jell-O plates with rotting food shoved to the back. She says, "What the fuck, Doug." She finds a human-shaped figure wrapped in black garbage bags propped in a chair, with flies audible. Then a big man in a white tank top strikes her, lifts her and kisses her. His eyes are flat black like a shark's, and grey tendrils pour from his mouth into hers while she screams (Walkers 06).

docs.title: History
docs.text: Both appearances are cold opens without the player characters, and each ends with a cut to the credits. See The show for the cold-open format. The trailer, the Jell-O and the wrapped figure recur in both scenes. The wrapped figures resemble the Plastic-wrapped bodies seen elsewhere in the arc.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• How Doug's tendrils, the Jell-O and the sugar hoarding in Ballard relate. See Sugar clues.
  • Whether he is a Skinwalker. The later Andrew Howard duplicate also extends grey tendrils from its throat into its victim's mouth (Walkers 07).
  • Where the trailer is, and whether Doug is connected to the Ballard events at all.

docs.title: Douglas Douglas
docs.text:
Douglas Douglas is a lonely security guard at the Stately Acres gated community near Radford, living in a guard shack full of vintage pinball machines. After the task force helps him, he wins a lawsuit against his employer and uses the settlement to open the Douglas Pinball Emporium.

Type NPC Aliases The guard; the pinball guy; Douglas Affiliation Stately Acres property-management company (formerly); owner of the Douglas Pinball Emporium Status Alive (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 07 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Douglas is a guard who lives in a temporary guard shack at the entrance of Stately Acres. A bed stands against one wall and the rest of the shack is filled with about thirty years of vintage pinball machines, including Universal Monsters Mummy and Dracula tables and a Bozo clown machine misprinted with the year 3056. He recommends buying machines broken at estate sales on Saturday mornings. He feeds stray cats, hates Dean Lawson for kicking one, and assumes coyotes got his own dog. He is on a "pinhead" mailing list, although no other pinheads live nearby (Radford Horror 07). He tells Andrew that he "look[s] the most like a Fed of anyone I've ever seen" and offers advice on his tie.

docs.title: Radford Horror: the guard shack
docs.text:
When the team asked the guard's name, the table suggested Clyde Behringer, George number five and Jared Fogle before Andre settled on Douglas Douglas, "like the writer", and then corrected himself to Frederick Douglass (Radford Horror 07).

Douglas explained that his company would fire him if he left his post. He has to buy all his food from the company, supplies drop only every three months, and he gets one unpaid month off every three. Andrew wrote down Department of Labor numbers for him. Douglas told the team that Dean Lawson had been seen several times with a shovel at the family cabin ("Burying bodies? I don't know"), and let them look around. The Biz took a shovel from the community tool shed while Andrew kept Douglas talking about his plans for a pinball hall. Douglas then asked, embarrassed, whether they had any toilet paper; Kurt brought some from the trunk, and Douglas shook his hand for twenty seconds (Radford Horror 07). Zack's character Huell whispered "Serial killer" to Andrew as a joke. In Radford Horror 08, the table calls him "the pinball guy" and Andre calls him "the definitely intentional NPC that I definitely had a plan for" (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Radford Horrors: the Emporium
docs.text:
When the team returned to Radford, a neon "Douglas Pinball Emporium" stood in a former laundromat painted black across from the diner (Radford Horrors 02). In Radford Horrors 03, Molly Underhill led the team there, and Douglas greeted them as "minus the sports-coat guy" (the Biz). He explained that the agents had changed his life: after they loaned him toilet paper and gave him the Department of Labor number, he called, and "there ended up being a big lawsuit. Paid for this place."

He then reported that his overnight security and maintenance worker, Elizabeth George, was gone when he arrived to open. A letter on her door said she was in inpatient psychiatric treatment in Los Angeles, which he did not believe. The Flash Gordon machine she had been repairing stood opened up on the floor, there was a bloodstain in the parking lot, and the hand towels in the employee bathroom were missing. The team found a broken tine from a Taser, a smear of blood and a single hair, and learned that the front-porch camera's tape had been replaced with a partly recorded-over tape from another day (Radford Horrors 03). See LA treatment cover story.

In Radford Horrors 04, he is offscreen; the team works from diner camera footage showing a gray van crew raiding his shop (Radford Horrors 04). See also Emporium intruder.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Zack joked that there is a zero percent chance the pinball guy does not "fuck those machines" (Radford Horror 08).
  • In Radford Horror 08, Kira asked whether the team ever brought the pinball guy his toilet paper (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Douglas Scott
docs.text:
Douglas Scott is the big, gentle, lumberjack-looking father of Lena Scott and husband of Irene Scott, a Marblehead local who hoped the missing scientists would call back.

Type NPC Aliases Douglas; Mr. Scott Affiliation Scott family Status Alive (as of Summer Service 03) First appearance Summer Service 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Douglas is big and gentle and looks like a lumberjack (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Douglas collects Lena from school and arrives at the Scott home while the team is interviewing Irene. When Lena shouts "Strangers!" and climbs into Andrew Howard's lap, he warns the team not to give her coffee again: "We have run the experiment." The family describes the field trip to the fort the day after the blast, when Lena wandered to the beach and was found unconscious. Douglas says he had hoped to hear back from the scientists, and asks whether the blood samples they drew were ever sent off (Summer Service 01).

In Summer Service 03, the family arrives at the lighthouse as visitors, and the parents ask whether the team is reopening it. After Andrew warns that soldiers are coming and Kurt Larson warns about the water and the fish, Douglas tells Irene they could close early and take the long weekend, and the family leaves (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Drebin
docs.text:
Drebin is a Salt Lake City equipment dealer with mutton-chop sideburns and a pet iguana who rents the task force a ground-penetrating radar and is the first to spot the cavern beneath Sherman Ranch.

Type NPC Aliases Salt Lake City radar dealer; equipment dealer; radar rental man Affiliation Independent equipment dealer, Salt Lake City Status Alive (as of Walkers 05) First appearance Walkers 04 (unnamed) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In Walkers 05 Drebin is a patient man with big mutton chops who explains the radar's use at length. His iguana Herbert, with "mad lizard eyes," travels in his truck. In Walkers 04 the players had already given the unnamed dealer an odd smell (mothballs with nicotine), mutton chops, an iguana, model trains and ham radio (Walkers 04).

docs.title: Walkers 04: sourcing the radar
docs.text: As a Plan B for the exhumation, Kurt tries to source ground-penetrating radar. The Biz uses the Fixer move (a Charm roll, result 12, with Kurt assisting) and reaches a Salt Lake City dealer who is a friend of his ex-wife's brother. The dealer sells equipment for finding wrecked cars in lakes, and tells an anecdote that every small-town lake is full of corpses. He rents the radar for $800 and promises to deliver and demonstrate it the next day, roughly a two-hour drive away (Walkers 04). See Ground-penetrating radar.

docs.title: Walkers 05: the demonstration
docs.text:
Drebin delivers the unit, shaped like a push lawnmower, and demonstrates it on the ranch's septic tank, which shows a void about 10 feet down; an empty coffin shows a void, a full one does not. He then spots a big signal 70 feet down, "like a cave." Kurt's Sharp roll (double 5 plus 3, 13, treated as 12) reveals that the cave extends under the whole property with no shallower gradient. Drebin shows off Herbert and drives away, to return in 24 hours to collect the radar (Walkers 05). See The cavern and Sherman Ranch.

The dealer who arrives in Walkers 05 introduces himself as the man who rented them the radar, so he is the same person the Biz phoned in Walkers 04.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The name Drebin is spoken only in Walkers 05.

docs.title: Eddie Jones
docs.text:
Eddie Jones is a member of the Circle Chasers, the teenage Bigfoot hunters of Dahlonega, Georgia, who holds the theory that Bigfoot is a population of feral humans and who asks Kurt what life in the CIA is like.

Type NPC (minor) Aliases Eddie; Ed Affiliation The Circle Chasers Status Alive (as of Appalachia 07) First appearance Appalachia 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Eddie is a young member of the Chasers who is introduced by Sloth along with the rest of the group, which also includes Delilah, the camcorder-carrying redhead (Appalachia 01). He is talkative and likes to theorize, and Vanessa calls him "Ed" when she shoots his ideas down (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Appalachia 01
docs.text: Eddie is among the Chasers who meet the team at their silver crop-circle trailer to explain how they triangulated Bigfoot sightings: several in town and a couple around Auraria, so the creature should be somewhere between. The group runs a bulletin board system and hands Kurt a card with its number. Kurt gives them his pager number and warns them about the religious oddballs in town (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: Appalachia 02
docs.text: When the Chasers meet the team at the rabbit-snatch area, Eddie argues that Bigfoot is feral humans, citing feral pigs, which change within a single generation once loose from a farm: people who live in the woods may transform into a wild form. Vanessa favors an undiscovered hominid. Andrew thinks the creature in the footage is a werewolf, and Sloth agrees. Eddie wants to take the footage to the local news to "build our brand" and says the group will celebrate at the Spud Hut, which is closed for the night. He has been working through the seafood spuds (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Appalachia 07
docs.text: At the original Spud Hut, Eddie asks the counter man for the highest-protein item on the menu, and the counter man recommends the chicken parmesan spud but refuses to discuss the secret menu in front of outsiders. Eddie also sidles up to Kurt and asks what working for the CIA is like (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Eduardo Hooper
docs.text:
Eduardo Hooper is a drunk, bolo-tied dealer of dangerous 1960s chemistry sets whom the team meets at the original Spud Hut in Appalachia 07.

Type NPC (minor) Aliases Hooper Status Alive (as of Appalachia 07) First appearance Appalachia 07 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Hooper wears a cowboy hat and a bolo tie set with Santa Fe gemstones that he says his "grandpappy" gave him. He is visibly drunk, uses phrases such as "very mentionable" and "namby-pamby", and ends his scene with a sloppy salute. His wife, whose hand carries about forty rings, waits in the car (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Hooper is at the Spud Hut counter when the team arrives. He orders a Hawaiian luau spud, a clam chowder spud for his wife and, in a lowered voice, one of the "special taco, taco spuds" from the secret menu, which turns out to have a whole octopus on top. He greets the team as "fellow Spud Hut aficionados" and, once he has his order, begs them not to say he told them about the secret menu (Appalachia 07).

He tells them that he sells chemistry sets, but not the "namby-pamby" safe kind: he has a storage facility full of dangerous ones from the 1960s, and "they got uranium in them." Kurt asks for a business card as an off-the-books source, and Hooper hands one over with a drunken magician's flourish, introducing himself as "Eduardo Hooper, at your service". The Biz already has a card. His wife calls him back to the car and he leaves (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Items
docs.text: • Hooper's business card: a contact for dangerous 1960s chemistry sets, taken by Kurt (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"They got uranium in them." Andre (as Eduardo Hooper), on his chemistry sets (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Edward Nick
docs.text:
Edward Nick is a five- or six-year-old boy from the Dahlonega Trailer Park who was playing with Gene Cartwright when Gene vanished, and who told the sheriff he had seen Bigfoot.

Type NPC (minor) Aliases Ed; the Nick boy Affiliation Nick family, trailer 513 Status Alive, at home (as of Appalachia 04) First appearance Appalachia 01 (named in the case file) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Edward has big dark eyes and a bowl haircut. When the team visits he is transfixed by Looney Tunes (the opera cartoon in which Bugs Bunny plays Brunhilde) and answers without turning from the television. He is a fan of the Hardy Boys and owns a Bigfoot book for teenagers that his father's eccentric sister gave him; it gave him nightmares for a while (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Appalachia 01
docs.text: Sheriff Burke gives the team the case-file names: missing woman Willow Greengrass, her sister Primenthol Greengrass, missing boy Gene Cartwright (7), and the witness Edward Nick (5), who said he saw Bigfoot (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: Appalachia 02
docs.text:
The team visits the Nicks' trailer on Wednesday morning. The mother lets them in after Kurt says they are "the Federales". Andrew crouches to talk to Edward and receives a Transformers toy and a juice box. Edward hands over a scribbled drawing of a crouched hairy figure, says "He was fast" and pantomimes scrabbling on all fours. He says the sighting was "yesterday"; his mother corrects him that it was three days earlier (Appalachia 02).

His mother thinks the Bigfoot book is where the idea came from. She doubts a bear took Gene, since there would have been a mess, and says the people at Auraria "always gave me the heebie-jeebies". She directs the team to the bent tree at the wood line, where Gene was playing when the screaming started. In the field Huell climbs the tree and retrieves a child's shoe with a tuft of pale hair caught in the laces. Back at the trailer, the mother relays what she got out of Ed: something appeared out of nowhere, grabbed Gene and ran into the woods (Appalachia 02).

Edward's father, Edward Nick Sr., works at the Spud Hut distribution center and arrives at dinner in gray coveralls to report that his co-worker Aaron has gone missing (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Appalachia 04
docs.text: Gene's mother, Monica Cartwright, tells the team that Gene was playing in the woods with "the Nick boy," who started screaming his head off (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The Nicks live in trailer 513 and the Cartwrights in trailer 920 (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Howard and his wife
docs.text:
Howard and his wife are a very elderly Jewish couple of Radford whose old diesel sedan the task force commandeers in a McDonald's drive-thru to chase a tailing van. They get it back dented.

Type NPC (pair) Aliases The elderly couple; the Jewish couple Affiliation None Status Alive (as of Radford Horror 06) First appearance Radford Horror 03 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The couple are very elderly. They tell Andrew how tough it is to be one of three Jewish families in the whole town (Radford Horror 03). They drive a small, old diesel sedan, which Andre describes as the "old lady Benz". Howard is practical about first aid, and his wife is quick to suggest leaving a car she does not trust.

docs.title: The commandeering
docs.text:
To shake a white van that was tailing them, the team led it into a McDonald's drive-thru that wraps around the building, so that people could swap cars out of its sight. Kurt and the Biz approached the car ahead in line and claimed to be FBI. The couple only went along after Kurt showed them the scars from two Vietnam gunshot wounds in the same arm. The old woman said, "I think we should get out of the car, Howard." (Andre, as the old woman.) (Radford Horror 03) The couple were then put in the agents' other car with Andrew and Huell. The team ordered food, including two 20-piece McNuggets and Diet Cokes "dino-sized" for the Jurassic Park promotion, and the front car picked up the couple's order by mistake.

Kurt and the Biz drove the couple's diesel up the mountain after the van. It topped out at 70 mph, so they lost the van but kept its plate. The Biz tore off the rearview mirror to look up at the silent object overhead, and Kurt then hit Agent Murphy with the car (see Agent Murphy). The sedan ended up with a cracked windshield, a dented hood and no mirror (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Waiting by the road
docs.text: Meanwhile Andrew kept the couple company. They ate his food, though they had wanted the nuggets, and were noticeably upset about missing their lunch. Andrew asked about being Jewish in a town of Christians, and recommended meditation when they got stressed. By then the couple put the odds at about 20 percent that they had been kidnapped by lunatics. At the roadside meeting afterward, Howard took one look at Kurt's burns, wrapped him in his jacket, found ibuprofen (up to 1,600 milligrams "in a pinch"), and warned that the swelling could close his throat. The couple then drove off in their busted car (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Later mentions
docs.text: In Radford Horror 04, Dante suggested that one of the real FBI agents photograph the damaged car for the file (Radford Horror 04). In Radford Horror 06, when the team needed a vehicle, Andre reminded them that they had given the couple's car back, and Dante objected to the phrase "carjacked": "Commandeer is the preferred nomenclature." (Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The old man's name, Howard, is also what the other agents call Andrew Howard, which led to some confusion at the table.

docs.title: Elijah Ray
docs.text:
Elijah Ray is the bigamist prophet who leads the Covenant, a religious community occupying the ghost town of Auraria, Georgia, and the last person known to have seen the missing Willow Greengrass.

Type NPC (minor; never met on screen) Aliases The Reverend; the prophet Affiliation The Covenant Status Alive (as of Appalachia 04) First appearance Appalachia 02 (mentioned)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The team never speaks to Elijah Ray in the recorded sessions; he is described only by others. Primenthol Greengrass calls him "genuinely a pretty nice guy. For a bigamist," and says she never heard of him being inappropriate with anyone he was not married to (Appalachia 02). In Appalachia 04, a Covenant woman tells the team he used to teach at Harvard and now teaches a comparative religions course in the community's one-room schoolhouse (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: Appalachia 02
docs.text: Prim tells the team the story of the Covenant. Ray had a prophetic dream, then a shooting star was seen over the area and he heard about it on TV, and a few days later he moved the whole congregation to Auraria, bought cheap land and tried to grow potatoes. The community believes a holy meteor struck there and that the clay is infused with divine energy. Ray's youngest wife, Angie, is about 25 now; she was 20 and he was 38 when they married (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Appalachia 04
docs.text:
At the Covenant, a young woman tells the team that Ray, the last person to see Willow Greengrass, handles the community's official liaising. A member named River says Ray sent Willow out to scout peach orchards, that she was on her way back with samples when she vanished, and that she was upset after a fight with her sister. River adds that Ray encourages members not to spend too much time with family (Appalachia 04).

River and Mother Dahlia Riversand also explain that "corporate goons" showed up about a year earlier with paperwork claiming the land and threatening eviction. Ray says the claim is bullshit. The community sells preserves and quilts and has an orchard deal in the works to pay for a lawyer, and members call Auraria the promised land and the Garden of Eden (Appalachia 04).

Rita (as Andrew) tells the group she has "an idea" for meeting Ray, "but not for today", and the team leaves without speaking to him; Dante (as Kurt) later calls him "the Reverend guy" (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The cold open of Appalachia 04 shows an older man with high cheekbones and striking features baptizing a door-to-door salesman in red clay by the river, chanting in Latin; the salesman vanishes beneath the mud. The episode never says whether this man is Ray. Ray is not mentioned again in the recorded sessions.

docs.title: Elizabeth George
docs.text:
Elizabeth George is the overnight security guard and repair technician at the Douglas Pinball Emporium in Radford, tased and carried off by masked men while repairing the Flash Gordon machine.

Type NPC Aliases Lisbeth George; Lizbeth Affiliation Douglas Pinball Emporium Status Missing, probably taken by the gray van crew First appearance Radford Horrors 03 (cold open) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Elizabeth is Douglas Douglas's overnight worker, a combination security guard and maintenance technician who fixes machines that have problems, does some cleaning for the next day, and keeps break-ins out. She had worked at the Emporium for about six months, since it opened (Radford Horrors 03). She never appears alive on screen, and her appearance and manner are not described.

docs.title: The cold open
docs.text: The third episode of The Radford Horrors opened with a long pan down a dark aisle of chiming pinball machines: muffled thrashing and cursing, a thump and the crack of a Taser, a woman's limp, twitching arm flopping into view, and a man in a black balaclava stepping out to help carry her away. Then it cut to credits (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The investigation
docs.text:
Douglas told the team she was gone when he arrived to open. A letter on her door claimed she was in inpatient psychiatric treatment in Los Angeles. The Flash Gordon machine was opened up mid-repair, there was a bloodstain in the parking lot, and the hand towels in the staff bathroom were missing. Kurt's luminol search, helped by the arcade's black lights, found a broken Taser tine with blood in the neon carpet, a blood smear and a single hair on the corner of a machine, and a missing first-aid kit. There were no fingerprints, and a faint smell of bleach suggested gloved people had cleaned up and missed some spots. At the back of the lot, a section of fence had been cut, a vehicle driven through, and the fence reattached. The front-porch camera's tape had been swapped for a partly recorded-over one (Radford Horrors 03).

Kurt recognized the pattern of the Los Angeles letter from other missing Radford residents who were officially said to be in drug or psychiatric facilities there; see LA treatment cover story.

In Radford Horrors 04, security footage from the diner across the street showed a gray van pulling up in the early hours (the diner closed at 1 a.m.; the footage showed it at about four or five). Five men got out, one with a long brown ponytail and others with military haircuts, and several had their faces covered. Something that was not human moved in the Emporium window, and after two or three minutes three of the men carried out two bags (Radford Horrors 04). Dante theorized that the crew was sent to clean up an alien presence in the building, possibly a juvenile moth or a thrall like the astronaut kid, and that Elizabeth was caught in the crossfire. Zack wondered if a remote recording device had been hidden in the machine. See Emporium intruder. Her fate is never resolved.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Andre first called her "Lizbeth Geor-", then corrected himself in Radford Horrors 03; in Radford Horrors 04 he calls her "Lisbeth George".

docs.title: Esteban
docs.text:
Esteban is a McDonald's worker in Marblehead whose clothes smell of beans, a problem the team traces to his church-going uncle.

Type NPC Aliases Bean boy Affiliation McDonald's; his uncle belongs to the church Status Alive (as of Summer Service 05) Played by Andre First appearance Summer Service 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Esteban works four days a week. His mother is in the hospital, his girlfriend says he smells like beans (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Before the selectmen's meeting, the team drives to McDonald's in formal wear past storefronts being boarded up against the storm; Andre has Esteban at the counter "again." Dante (as Kurt Larson) rolls an 11 on Investigate and confirms that Esteban, and a shirt from his home, strongly smell of beans. Esteban realizes that his uncle, who is in "that church" and volunteers to do the laundry, has been putting bean juice in the wash "to keep me a virgin." The team's advice is absurd: Andrew Howard suggests showering at his girlfriend's and coming out in a towel, Huell Kendrick, played by Zack, says "Take the biggest knife in your kitchen," and the Biz says "You never know when you might need to make someone smell like beans." Esteban thanks them with a basket of fries with extra salt (Summer Service 04).

Later that night, Huell visits McDonald's. Esteban is off sleeping before a test; a teenage girl covering for him says he "figured it out. It was his uncle" (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Andre slipped between the names Alejandro, Jose and Esteban before settling on Esteban ("Esteban. Ding.").

docs.title: The Finnish Hare Krishna Monk
docs.text:
The Finnish Hare Krishna Monk is an unnamed, orange-robed hitchhiker whom the task force picked up during their drunken drive to Rhode Island and who stays with them through the first two episodes of The Roulet Estate.

Type NPC Aliases The monk; orange-robed monk; Hare Krishna Affiliation Hare Krishna (as Diane assumed); revealed to be Finnish in Roulet Estate 02 Status Alive; sent on to Pawtucket by taxi in Roulet Estate 02 First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The monk is bald, wears an orange robe and carries a backpack stocked with screwdrivers, a camp frying pan, camp plates and a canteen. He is friendly and expressive, and communicates mostly through gestures and a language none of the agents can place. Kurt rolls a 7 on a Sharp check and rules out every Asian or Middle Eastern language he knows; Kurt also asks the monk for Gatorade "in every language". (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
The monk is first seen on the stairs of the abandoned house the agents wake up in, after a blackout drinking binge that followed the disbanding of the task force. Huell hands him his unloaded gun to see whether he would shoot; the monk gives it back, and Huell concludes the agents did not kidnap him. Outside, he has built a campfire and is frying Spam. (Roulet Estate 01)

Diane, who drove the agents about seven hours to Rhode Island, explains that she did not want to pick him up because she feared a Hare Krishna scam, but the drunk agents insisted. She thinks he did not want to come. He serves the group a breakfast of reconstituted eggs, Spam and thick instant coffee, and points at the house, saying something before shrugging. The only word anyone understands is "Pawtucket," which prompts him to give a double thumbs-up and produce screwdrivers. (Roulet Estate 01)

When a sniper opens fire, the monk tackles Andrew behind the car as a window explodes and drags him inside. He then locks himself in a bathroom and chants quietly there as evening falls. Kurt tells him he may stay inside as a civilian. (Roulet Estate 01)

In Roulet Estate 02 he hides during the gunfire in the basement, sprints after the stolen car shouting "Pawtucket!" and gives up after about a hundred feet. The agents struggle over what to do with the man they have half-kidnapped, and he accompanies them on the hike to the clown mansion. Back at the house he watches the agents carry guns down the chimney with saucer-shaped eyes. When Andrew mimes a warning about the drugged water and tries to take the monk's bottle, a Manipulate Someone roll (a natural 12, 11 after modifiers) makes the monk drop it in disgust, and Andre rules that Andrew finally recognizes the language: Finnish. (Roulet Estate 02)

Kurt orders a taxi to Pawtucket with his own money. It arrives at the Roulet house, where Kurt hands the monk the team's card and a wad of cash. The monk shouts something incomprehensible from the cab as he leaves. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: Kurt feels responsible for the "kidnapped" man; the table's running joke is that the agents will keep kidnapping him until they get him to Pawtucket. Zack (as Huell) questions why the monk was brought so far and voices the monk's contempt for the agents ("Ah, perverts."). (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Andre voiced the monk's Finnish as invented gibberish, so his lines differ from scene to scene.
  • It is never established why he wanted to go to Pawtucket or what he was trying to say about the house.

docs.title: Sheriff Frank Roosevelt
docs.text:
Sheriff Frank Roosevelt is the sheriff of Radford, Virginia, a tired, by-the-book lawman who is sick of UFO talk, blames tourists and perverts for Radford's troubles, and steps back after a heart attack before the task force's return visit.

Type NPC Aliases Roosevelt; Frank; the sheriff; the previous sheriff (Radford Horrors) Affiliation Radford Sheriff's Department Status Alive; stepped back from the job after a heart attack (as of Radford Horrors 02) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Roosevelt is an older, chubbier Black man in a traditional sheriff's uniform with a star and no hat. He has a big, firm, warm handshake and introduces himself as Frank (Radford Horror 01). He is named only in the first episode; in later episodes he is simply "the sheriff". He has not worked with the FBI before and wants everything done by the book.

docs.title: Radford Horror: the first case
docs.text:
Roosevelt first spoke to the team by phone, where Molly Underhill handed him the call as "Frank", and he recommended aluminum foil on the bed feet at the Pay n' Stay to keep out bedbugs. He then met the team at the Lonely Mountain Diner. He had Deputy Molly Underhill check the team's credentials with the FBI, and set ground rules: "I just want to make sure there isn't gonna be any... and you'll pardon my French, cowboy bullshit going on." Kurt introduced Andrew as "Arnold" by mistake. The Biz's attempt to play the case down as make-work from Washington ran into Roosevelt's response: "I have two people missing, so I don't think it's nothing." (Radford Horror 01)

He briefed the team on Amanda Lucky and Mrs. Whateley. He recalled busting some high school kids with a drill about four years earlier, and had recently seen Amanda with the biker Matt McCready. He doubted that four-year-old Tyler saw what he said he saw, and said that Radford's only real problem was "the tourists... dumb as hell". He was fed up with UFO stories (Radford Horror 01). The sheriff said Mrs. Whateley had vanished "this morning" while also saying the woods had been searched "since last night".

In Radford Horror 02 he took the team to the Whateley house and the Radio Shack robbery file. He listed his department as himself, one deputy, a patrolman and some emergency deputies, with "a little bit of a meth problem". He had been on paternity leave when Abelforth Whateley robbed the store. His notes in the missing-dog file read "Perverts???", and he rejected the suggestion that someone was "fishing" for the dogs: "It's not fishing. It's perverts. You don't go fishing for perverts." (Radford Horror 02) See Radford's missing dogs.

In Radford Horror 05 he introduced the coroner, Dr. Mauden, to the team, and the town imposed a curfew on his orders (Radford Horror 05). In Radford Horror 06, with Wilbur Whateley, Dr. Lori and Derek Augustine all missing, he told Andrew, "it's usually not this bad." (Radford Horror 06)

In Radford Horror 08 he presented the official theory: a hidden basement with a spaceman costume and a journal, a cadaver likely Abelforth's, Wilbur as a serial killer who impersonated his brother, and a link to the cartel via the heroin found in the church. He closed the kidnapping case, handed the team the legible pages of Wilbur's journal, and told them Dean Lawson's car was missing. As the team left, he confessed to an irrational hatred of Bigfoot: "Whenever somebody says Bigfoot to me, I just want to punch them in their face." Dante told him, "about 12 pounds of poopy in a 10-pound bag." (Radford Horror 08) See The cartel.

docs.title: Radford Horrors: stepping back
docs.text: The task force returned to Radford a little less than a year later. By then, Molly Underhill is sheriff after a "battlefield promotion". The old sheriff had a heart attack earlier in the year, is on an hour a day of meditation, and is supposed to avoid stress. He is alive and does not appear (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Molly Underhill: his deputy and successor.
  • Kurt Larson: the sheriff accepts him as the team's consultant.
  • Andrew Howard: leader of the visiting task force.
