docs.title: Freak
docs.text:
Freak is a scarred Vietnam veteran and charter pilot at Roanoke Airport who flies the task force over Radford in his baby-blue Cessna, Annabelle, and recognizes the heroin in their possession.

Type NPC Aliases Francesco; Francisco; "Francisco Airlines" Affiliation Independent charter pilot, Roanoke Airport Status Alive, asleep in a lawn chair (as of Radford Horror 07) First appearance Radford Horror 07 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Freak wears an unbuttoned Hawaiian shirt and flip-flops, and is badly sunburned. His legs are scarred by burns and missing chunks, which Kurt recognizes as fragmentation-grenade shrapnel wounds. He drinks, smokes and snorts heroin (Radford Horror 07). When Kurt addresses him as Freak he protests, "Oh, oh, oh, please, my dad calls me Freak... You can call me Francesco." After landing, he says, "Thank you for flying Francisco Airlines." His plane is a baby-blue Cessna that looks painted with house paint. Inside are a four-inch disco ball, black lights, neon suede seat covers and a smell of weed. He calls the plane Annabelle.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 07, the team drove to Roanoke Airport to rent a plane for an aerial survey of the woods around Radford. An attendant in red sunglasses sent them to Freak, who was asleep beside his Cessna. His opening line was "I don't fly Feds." Dante offered a baggie of heroin from Dean Lawson's stash, saying, "We're cool Feds. Let us in the plane." Kurt's Manipulate Someone roll only partly succeeded, so Freak asked for proof; Kurt snorted a bump with him. Freak quoted $200 plus gas, or the baggie, and Kurt paid $1,000 from the cash (Radford Horror 07).

The takeoff barely cleared a tall pine. Freak said pilots who fly Air Force One train at Roanoke to cure their fear of death, and that the only good thing about Vietnam was that "I functionally was not married." Kurt replied that Vietnam was where he met his wife. The engine missed every couple of seconds. Over Radford, Kurt spotted a clearing with a dilapidated building whose roof had caved in and a flash of dazzling blue beneath it. Freak circled low and the team saw an old church; the blue did not flash again. Andrew became severely airsick. See Old-town church (Radford Horror 07).

On approach to Roanoke the engine cut out, and Freak asked Kurt to kick a panel; Andre noted this was the first time he had rolled for an NPC's equipment. The engine restarted after twenty or thirty tense seconds ("There's some dirt in the fuel line, it clogs sometimes"). Landing, Freak snorted more heroin and said, "I love Mexican heroin... I've had this exact stuff before." He had bought it at a party from a young man, and when Dante gave a description of Dean Lawson, Freak agreed that sounded like him. He said the dealer got it from "a bunch of Mexicans", pointing the team toward the cartel. Kurt offered him sunscreen, and Freak fell asleep in his lawn chair (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horror 07

docs.title: Frederick
docs.text:
Frederick is a young German tourist who vanishes from a tour of the Consolidated Gold Mine near Dahlonega, Georgia, leaving his Game Boy behind; one of his shoes is later found at the bottom of a hidden shaft.

Type NPC (missing person) Aliases German boy Status Missing, presumed dead by the team (as of Appalachia 04) Location Consolidated Gold Mine First appearance Appalachia 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Frederick is a heavyset boy in overalls with a gray Game Boy, who trails behind his tour group paying no attention to the guide. His mother stands at the front with a disposable wind-up camera and a rigid stare (Appalachia 03).

docs.title: The disappearance
docs.text: The cold open of Appalachia 03 shows a bearded tour guide in a Dahlonega mine explaining that the town's mines connect to each other and to natural caves, and that sealed shafts are deadly ("we've lost a couple people"). Frederick hears giggling down a roped-off passage and the camera zooms into black. The guide hears clanging, finds the rope poles tipped over and picks up the Game Boy, still bleeping on the floor (Appalachia 03).

docs.title: The search
docs.text:
At the sheriff's station the team learns that the boy went missing on the mine tour about an hour and a half earlier. Because Kurt has spelunking experience, the sheriff enlists the team. In the mine Kurt calls "Wo bist du, Frederick? Komm her, Frederick!" Deeper in, the team is attacked in the dark by a pale, furry, very fast creature, which Kurt shoots before it flees. They follow its blood trail to a vertical shaft with coiled cables from an old elevator. At the bottom lies a single small, German-looking tennis shoe, which they take. A cave-in behind them seals the way they came (Appalachia 03).

When the team emerges, Huell bluntly says the boy is probably dead and hands over the shoe, and a German woman from the tour group bursts into tears. Kurt suggests that if someone took the boy, they carried him to the surface by a route the team could not follow (Appalachia 03).

docs.title: The mother
docs.text:
In Appalachia 04, Frederick's puffy-faced mother speaks only German and is interviewed on an old speakerphone through an FBI translator in the sheriff's station break room. She says that they were in the "American gold tunnels" while her son played his video game, that she heard a noise and clattering but no scream, and that when she turned the corner he was gone and the game was left behind. She asks why the search of the cave has stopped. Kurt answers that the shoe led toward an exit that is partly buried by a cave-in, and that the area showed signs of recent activity, even vehicles (Appalachia 04).

Sheriff Burke complains to the team that he now has five missing people in two days (the cases include Frederick, Gene Cartwright and Aaron Richters) (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: Frederick's fate is never stated. In Appalachia 09, the party tells the handler Clive that there were two missing kids, a truck driver and a Spud Hut worker, in the mining operation's tunnels, but the episodes never say whether the boys were taken by the ape-men or by the operation itself.

docs.title: Frotter Comstock
docs.text:
Frotter Comstock is a bearded, tax-dodging moonshiner on a ridge outside Auraria, Georgia, who saw a pair of eyes at his homestead and on whose land the corpse of a man in a Chewbacca costume is found.

Type NPC (minor) Aliases Comstock; Frotter Home Comstock's Property Status Alive (as of Appalachia 06) First appearance Appalachia 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Frotter is a 50-something bearded bootlegger in overalls who carries a lantern and hauls a cart of bottles and chemistry equipment. He is talkative and pedantic, proud of belonging to a long line of Comstock bootleggers, and makes a pear liquor that he boasts will put a drinker on another plane of existence. He calls his place "mi casa" and the agents "Federales" (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06).

docs.title: Appalachia 02
docs.text:
Kurt, Andrew, Huell and the Biz meet Frotter on a trail in the woods near the Covenant. He relaxes when Kurt says they are Federales and not ATF. He explains that he has been helping the Covenant fix a methanol problem in their ritual beverage: natural yeast produces an enzyme that breaks down the pectin in fruit skins into methanol, and the thermostat on their old McMurray still has started to stick. Kurt asks about "Primenthol Greengrass" (he means the missing Willow), and Frotter knows only that she went missing (Appalachia 02).

He describes drunken hunting accidents involving the Daniel boys, and says that a couple of weeks earlier someone skulked around his ridge homestead. He saw only a pair of eyes in the dark, "tall, but, you know, not unusually so", which then ran off. The team marks his ridge on their map together with the road spot and the rabbit site, and the line points toward town (Appalachia 02).

Quote

"Good luck keeping those cultists from going blind." Dante (as Kurt), to Frotter (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Appalachia 06
docs.text:
At the hotel breakfast, Frotter arrives with the sheriff. He complains that the agents would not come shoot "that bear" for him ("what do I even pay taxes for?"), and the sheriff points out that he does not pay taxes and that the IRS has visited three or four times. Frotter reports a dead Bigfoot on his land and refuses to touch it for fear of diseases (Appalachia 06).

At his property, the outbuildings are hastily wrapped in blue weather tarps, and a large streak of gore next to a shack is introduced as "the bear incident". The "squatch" lies in a copse about 50 feet down the path. Andrew's investigation shows that it is a man in an expensive Chewbacca costume, soaked in real blood and shot in the back of the head like a gangland execution. When told it is a man in a costume, Frotter blames the bear, blurts "Wait, wait, hang on. He was shot?", and asks whether the dead man had really long hair (Appalachia 06).

Frotter whispers to Andrew that if the agents do not get a warrant for the buildings, he will let them search the property without one. Kurt checks one building anyway and concludes that Frotter is trying to brew beer with marijuana instead of hops. His guns are almost all shotguns and small-caliber pistols, and Kurt estimates the murder weapon was roughly a .357 Magnum. Frotter drives off in the sheriff's squad car, waving (Appalachia 06).

The dead man is later associated with Troy Cleaver.

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"Listen, the day that I touch an undiscovered species— a corpse in the woods is the day that Frotter Comstock has lost his edge." Andre (as Frotter Comstock) (Appalachia 06)

Quote

"Sir, next time someone shows up with a dead Bigfoot, you should check if it's a man in a suit." Zack (as Huell), to Frotter (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Frotter's name is spelled with two Ts. Ezra jokes in Appalachia 06 about "Frotter Cumsock", and Rita notes that a search finds no Frotter Comstocks (Appalachia 06).
  • Kurt asks him about "Primenthol Greengrass" when the missing woman is Willow (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Gene Cartwright
docs.text:
Gene Cartwright is a seven-year-old boy from a Dahlonega trailer park who vanished from the field behind it, setting off the missing-persons case that draws the task force to Georgia in The Things in Appalachia.

Type NPC (missing child) Aliases Gene Affiliation Cartwright family, Dahlonega Trailer Park Status Missing; presumed dead by the team (as of Appalachia 04) First appearance Appalachia 01 (mentioned)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Edward Nick's mother put Gene at "probably seven years old. He might have been eight", and the older of the two boys. He lived in trailer 920 at the far end of the park, while the Nicks lived in 513. Sheriff Burke's file lists him as a missing boy of seven. His shoes were red with white soles (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02). The team never meets him.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Gene vanished about a week before the task force was assigned the case. Burke's file names him alongside Willow Greengrass, her sister Primenthol Greengrass and the five-year-old witness Edward Nick (Appalachia 01).

Edward's mother told the team that Gene was by the bent tree at the wood line when the screaming started. Edward told her that something appeared out of nowhere, grabbed Gene and took off into the woods. In the field behind the park, Huell climbed the tree and recovered a child's shoe with a tuft of pale hair caught in the laces. The hair felt like soft body hair and still had its ends. Kurt and Huell agreed the boy was almost certainly dead. Kurt then phoned Sheriff Burke, who asked whether the shoe was "red with a white sole". It was. See Gene's Shoe and The Field and Bent Tree (Appalachia 02).

In Appalachia 04 the team visited his mother, Monica Cartwright, at the Dahlonega Trailer Park. She said Gene had been playing in the woods with the Nick boy, who started screaming; when she ran out, Gene was gone. She told the agents not to come back unless they found her son. Outside, Kurt said the boy was almost certainly dead, and Andrew said they would have to call child protective services if he turned up alive. Monica also described a naked, hairy figure like Chewbacca at the end of her driveway a month earlier (see The Bigfoot Hoax).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: Gene's fate is never resolved in the recorded episodes, and the shoe's hair is never tied to a particular creature. A second missing boy, Frederick, later vanished near the old mines (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Dr. McManley's very fat pet tegu, which tries to climb Huell's leg in the first episode, is named Cartwright; Zack's Huell greets the lizard by that name again in Appalachia 04 (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 04).

docs.title: George H. W. Bush
docs.text:
George H. W. Bush is the President of the United States for most of the campaign, the man at whose request the Paranatural Incident Task Force was created and who loses the 1992 election to Ross Perot. He is a fictional version of the real president, written as a character in the show's alternate history; nothing here describes the real person.

Type NPC (fictionalized historical figure) Aliases Bush Sr.; President Bush; the President; "the big man upstairs" Affiliation President of the United States (until January 1993) Status Alive; out of office First appearance Walkers 01; mentioned from Radford Horror 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Bush is folksy and blunt, and calls Andrew Howard "son". In his one scene he sits on the edge of his desk, turned about 45 degrees away from his visitor. He says he never believed in what he calls "wacky tobacky hootenanny bullshit", and that the photographs in the task force's files, the moth and the worms, make his skin crawl. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Founding the task force
docs.text:
In spring 1992 the FBI stands up a new unit at the President's request. The agents reassigned to it hear it described in different ways: the Biz is told the President wants an exploratory task force on "possible technological threats to national security"; Kurt is told he will be "hunting for ghosts and little green men for the president"; Huell is told it is "some kind of make-work task force the president's idiot brother wanted". Bush sits at the top of its chain of command, above Andrew, Big Bill and Deputy Director Floyd Clark. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03)

Bush later gives Andrew his own account, which replaces the office rumor Huell heard: "my son asked me to." The son "has an interest in these things" and made him promise that if he won the election he would get to the bottom of it. Bush was "humoring the boy", and thought it was probably a waste of government resources. The players confirm with Andre that the son is George W. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: In office
docs.text: During the Marblehead crisis Big Bill takes the team's reports to the Oval Office, and the team's reporting is classified under the code word SKYHOOK with the President at the top of the distribution. During the Georgia scandal Big Bill again says he will brief the President. (Summer Service 03, Appalachia 07)

docs.title: The Oval Office
docs.text:
A few days before the election, after the Georgia case, Andrew waits an hour and a half outside the Oval Office and is then shown in, shedding a clump of Yeti fur on the carpet. (Walkers 01)

Bush has read the files. He quotes the after-action report on Andrew being "dribbled like a basketball" and tells him he is sturdy. He says Andrew is the only true believer on the team, the others having a "grudging appreciation", and that Kurt's file is interesting reading: he sleeps better knowing Castro has people like that haunting him. He asks why Andrew believed before any of it happened, and calls the answer moral courage. (Walkers 01)

He expects to lose to Bill Clinton within days. He does not accept that an ape-man criminal was caught surveilling Clinton in the same Georgia town as his task force by chance: he reads it as an attempt to break the continuity of leadership, by China, by Soviet remnants, or by "something from somewhere else". He warns that enemy agents may be inside American organizations. See Enemy Action. (Walkers 01)

Quote

"There is coincidence, there is miracle, and there is enemy action." (Andre as Bush, Walkers 01)

Quote

"You, Andrew Howard, are personally responsible for the survival of the United States of America." (Andre as Bush, Walkers 01)

Andrew replies that this has been his responsibility his whole life, and explains the Aetherius Society, the Masters and the "spiritual battery" of good energy at length. The scene ends on a slow zoom on Bush's face "just slowly going blank". (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Defeat
docs.text:
The "double scandal" sinks him. Polls put Perot above 45 percent with Bush clearly ahead only in Texas, and Perot wins. In Andre's account of the alternate election, "the incumbent got caught spying on the challenger". (Walkers 01, Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

His successor believes the task force was a cover for Bush weaponizing the FBI against political enemies, and disbands it on Inauguration Day 1993. Daniel Webster arrives at the next case holding the same theory: that the team was Bush's political dirty-work unit and that the "alien stuff" is a cover. (Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Andrew Howard. The one agent he sends for in person, and the one he charges with the country's survival whatever the next administration says. (Walkers 01)
  • Big Bill. The channel between the task force and the Oval Office. (Summer Service 03, Appalachia 07)
  • George W. Bush. "The boy", whose interest in "these things" prompted the task force. His father is not sure he is "ever gonna make something of himself". (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 01 has Huell's boss blame the task force on "the president's idiot brother"; in Walkers 01 Bush himself says it was his son. No brother is ever mentioned again. (Radford Horror 01, Walkers 01)
  • Ezra, on Bush calling the adult George W. "the boy": "if there was ever a guy in his fifties to refer to as 'the boy'..." (Walkers 01)
  • Bush tells Andrew there is "a really good chance" that Governor Clinton will be in his chair within days; the same session ends with Perot, not Clinton, leading the polls. (Walkers 01)
  • Zack twice supplied real-history footnotes: he said "Bush Jr." for the 1992 president by mistake, and noted that the real Bush left office with about 53 percent approval. (Appalachia 07, Walkers 01)
  • Dante, defending a stolen car in the Marblehead finale: "this is the George Bush Senior administration. There's no way worm people have rights." (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Gray-skinned dream visitor
docs.text:
The gray-skinned dream visitor is a nude, dead, deformed gray man who appears in Andrew Howard's sleep-paralysis dream to warn him away from the water.

Type NPC (dream apparition) Aliases Dead gray man Status Dead by his own account; identity never established Played by Andre First appearance Summer Service 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Pool-water caustics swirl across Andrew's ceiling and he is paralyzed. A nude man with gray skin squats at the foot of the bed. His skull is swollen, with a seam between the halves that throbs along the crest, and his eyes are large and bloodshot. He is gentle, near tears and apologetic (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The visitor apologizes for "all the stuff that's gonna happen to you," says Andrew's friends seem nice, and repeatedly tells him to stay away from the water. He says "they damaged it" and that "it can't cool itself anymore," and asks whether Andrew is high enough in his government to order a nuclear strike, which "might work." He adds "I wish I wasn't dead," asks Andrew to hug his mom for him, kisses him on the lips and vanishes. Andrew then dreams of losing his bingo card at a high school function until his pager wakes him. Andre has Andrew roll for dread; Rita rolls a 7 and Andrew takes 5 dread (Summer Service 03).

Andrew tells no one about the dream. Rita explains at the table that he is desperately pretending it never happened, wondering whether the visitor was his dad, whether his dad is an alien, and why the visitor kissed him on the mouth (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text:
• The visitor's identity. He says he is dead.
  • Whether the "it" that "can't cool itself" is the humming lit vessel the team saw on the dive. The episodes never say; see The angel thing.
  • The visitor says "It's not like the bug thing", which may refer to the Radford moth. See The Radford Moth.

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"Hi, Andrew. I'm really sorry about all the stuff that's gonna happen to you. Your friends seem like nice people. You should stay away from the water." Andre (as the gray-skinned visitor) (Summer Service 03)

Quote

"Are you high enough in your government to order a nuclear strike? That might work." Andre (as the gray-skinned visitor) (Summer Service 03)

Quote

"I wish I wasn't dead. Give your mom a hug for me, and please stay away from the water." Andre (as the gray-skinned visitor) (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 03

docs.title: Harold
docs.text:
Harold is a sad teenage Blockbuster Video clerk in Radford who lets the task force copy the diner's security tape in the store's back room, and who tells them he saw a man dragged into a van.

Type NPC Aliases Blockbuster clerk Affiliation Blockbuster Video, Radford Status Alive (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horrors 04 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Harold is a sad-looking teenager at the Blockbuster register. The employee area where he lets the team work smells of weed and has a tiny VHS-player television. He watches chemtrail documentaries with his uncle, and gives his name only as "They call me Harold." (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Kurt wanted the diner security tape copied because magnetic media is fragile. At Blockbuster, a sweat-soaked Andrew (who kept asking "Is it bright in here?" and told Harold, "I wouldn't worry about me. I don't think it's contagious. It might be rabies.") showed his badge. Harold warned them off the Pay n' Stay, with its rabid mice, recommended the Ferry Lodge and offered DayQuil. He let them use the back-room TV, and they photographed the footage and copied the tape. Kurt hid the backup in an evidence bag in a hollow tree twenty minutes' walk into the woods, rather than at the store (Radford Horrors 04).

While Andrew explained the Aetherius Society to him, Harold said that he had once seen a homeless man dragged into a van while he was closing up, and agreed that a ponytailed man may have been involved. He had given the man a sandwich a month and a half or two months earlier. The team connected this to Billy Thornton, who claimed to have been kidnapped by chimps and "John Travolta", and to the gray van crew, one of whom has a ponytail (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Harold complains that an old woman rents Saturday Night Fever every day and returns it unrewound; she has burned out eight copies. The table followed up with "Does she have a ponytail?", feeding the Travolta and ponytail running gags (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Harrison
docs.text:
Harrison is a stoned, apologetic Ballard high schooler caught hiding in the Sherman Ranch barn on a dare, who tells the team about the stench at his school.

Type NPC Affiliation Ballard High School student Status Alive (as of Walkers 04) First appearance Walkers 04 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Harrison is polite, apologetic and bad at crime. He wears a holographic snap bracelet, carries a backpack of rolling papers, abysmal weed, textbooks and dog-eared Goosebumps books (Welcome to Dead House, Monster Blood, Stay Out of the Basement), and wants to impress a girl (Walkers 04).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
While the team guards the guest house against the goose, the Biz spots a glint near the barn. Kurt and Huell enter and, with a Read a Bad Situation roll (9), find two extremely stoned teenagers hiding behind equipment; the glint was the snap bracelet (Walkers 04).

The party plays rough FBI ("decontamination protocol," a flashlight in the eyes). Walt Murphy recognizes Harrison, whom he has not seen since the boy was about seven. Harrison explains the dare: spend an hour on the ranch looking for ghosts or aliens. He says his school has about 60 students from the whole county and an eye-watering smell this semester that students blame on sewage or a dead thing in the air conditioning. Kurt connects the smell to the town's odd-tasting water. He also describes the school's "virginity anthem," sung to the tune of "We Are the Champions"; the Biz makes him sing part of it at gunpoint until Rita stops it (Walkers 04). See Ballard High School and Ballard water contamination.

His silent friend gives his name as Marshall Crichton and will not say why he came. Their weed comes from Chuck, a friend of Harrison's brother, for $25. At the guest house Kurt takes their weed and returns good weed; a Manipulate Someone roll (10) frightens Harrison into taking it. The boys bike off from the front gate (Walkers 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Walt's reaction: "You guys are the weirdest fucking cops I've ever met."
  • Marshall Crichton's one line: "We're the fucking worst at crime." (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 04

docs.title: Dr. Harvey Mauden
docs.text:
Dr. Harvey Mauden is the town doctor and coroner of Radford, Virginia, a devout Catholic who delivered Amanda Lucky as a baby and later performs her autopsy.

Type NPC Aliases Dr. Mauden; the coroner; town doctor; autopsy doctor Affiliation Radford, Virginia; works with the Radford Sheriff's Department Status Alive (as of Radford Horror 07) First appearance Mentioned in Radford Horror 04; first seen in Radford Horror 05 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Mauden is an older man who wears a small gold cross around his neck. He is kind, grave and polite. He offers the visiting agents Vicks VapoRub for the smell of the morgue but says he usually avoids it himself, because smells can be diagnostic. He is Radford's family doctor and its coroner, and he used to work at the town's addiction clinic, which is how he recognizes needle scars (Radford Horror 05). He is not the psychiatrist; that is Dr. Lawrence Lori (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Radford Horror 04
docs.text: Mauden is first mentioned at the end of the episode, when Molly Underhill tells the team that a young girl's body, probably Amanda Lucky's, has been found by the interstate. It is going to Dr. Mauden, the family doctor for many families in town, who delivered her. The autopsy is set for a couple of hours later and the agents are invited. Molly says he is "pretty troubled by the whole situation" (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Radford Horror 05
docs.text:
At the sheriff's station the sheriff introduces Mauden to the team as the doctor who will perform the autopsy. He tells them he delivered Amanda, says a Hail Mary over the covered body, switches on a tape recorder and describes her injuries: part of the face missing, a large ragged abdominal wound with organs removed, and puncture wounds in the wrists and ankles. He attributes the face and belly damage to coyotes after death. Kurt's questions establish that the nails were pulled through the limbs and that lividity shows she was nailed up, so she was crucified. Old needle scars, six or seven months old, and one fresh needle mark appear. Mauden privately tells the agents he suspects a spree-type serial killer who may be crucifying women. A pink butterfly hair tie is found stuck in Amanda's hair, and the team recalls seeing a matching one in the Augustine barn (Radford Horror 05).

Later that day he reports the toxicology screen: trace Xanax and a large quantity of opiates, enough to chemically sedate a person. The working theory is that Amanda was drugged and held, and could walk only because of a prior tolerance. Blood the team collected in the woods is given to him for a toxicology match, with a species test if there is no match (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Radford Horror 06
docs.text: Mauden tells the team that the blood from the tree matches Amanda's tox report. About five percent of the blood volume is foreign matter that none of his drug tests identify; he has sent it off for analysis, which will take a couple of weeks. Her blood also shows markers of severe malnutrition, although her body shows no physical signs of it. He recognizes the markers from a mission in sub-Saharan Africa. He has also examined Wilbur Whateley, whom he had advised to use a stationary bike, and says Wilbur was well cared for with only mild pressure injuries and that "there was nobody home" (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: Radford Horror 07
docs.text: The team finds his family-medicine clinic using a stolen phone book. Kurt Larson asks him to compare the heroin recovered from Dean Lawson with the substance in Amanda's blood. Stunned by the quantity ("That's a lot of heroin"), he takes a test-tube sample to send to a friend, since he lacks the equipment locally (Radford Horror 07). See Dean Lawson's heroin and cash.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Amanda Lucky: he delivered her and performed her autopsy.
  • Molly Underhill: works alongside her and passes on his findings through her.
  • The task force: cooperative; he calls them "Agents" and shares results.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Rita spelled the name out at the table in Radford Horror 05 ("Maud... Mauden"), and it may be heard as "Maud."
  • In Radford Horror 05, Kurt's player Dante had the coroner standing by while the agents talked over the body, a running joke about conversing with the dead.

docs.title: Harvey
docs.text:
Harvey is the enormous black Great Dane of the Circle Chasers, a teenage Bigfoot-hunting group in Dahlonega, Georgia, who say he is trained to smell the paranormal.

Type NPC (dog) Aliases the Great Dane Affiliation The Circle Chasers Owner Sloth Status Alive (as of Appalachia 07) First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Harvey is an enormous black Great Dane. The Chasers say they have trained him to smell the paranormal. It works for aliens, they say, but they are not sure about Bigfoot, and they credit him with leading them straight to their last crop circle (Appalachia 01). In Appalachia 02 one of the Chasers remarks that Harvey loves bugs, and Sloth says he does not usually like strangers.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Appalachia 01 the team meets the Chasers on the road to the sheriff's station, at their streamlined silver trailer painted with a crop circle. Sloth introduces the group and pats the dog, and Andre has Harvey answer "Woof" after each of the Chasers' claims, a running joke in the episode.

In Appalachia 02 the Chasers arrive near the woods trail where the agents are investigating (see Woods Trail and Rabbit Site). Harvey sprints out of the woods, jumps up, puts his paws on Andrew's shoulders and licks his face.

In Appalachia 07, at the Original Spud Hut, Harvey knocks Andrew over. Rita rolls a tough check for Andrew and gets a 13, and Andre rules that Andrew reflexively scoops up the huge dog and cradles it like a baby while it licks his face, which he calls a classic Shaggy and Scooby-Doo moment. Vanessa blurts out "Bear vomit", and the teens go on to describe the bear vomit and the blinking tracking device they found in it (see SHA Tracking Device). Sloth asks for his dog back. Zack asks whether the dog just winked at him, and Sloth answers, "It's a tic."

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: Harvey adores Andrew, the one agent he takes to at once. The Chasers play as the campaign's Scooby-Doo gang, with Harvey in the Scooby role (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 07).

  • Appalachia 02
  • Appalachia 07

docs.title: Henry
docs.text:
Henry is Donald McManley's "useless" assistant, sent to Salem by Vespa to fetch ivermectin, who calls in with a gore-covered umbrella having "killed something."

Type NPC Aliases The assistant; Ivermectin boy; the Ivermectin assistant Affiliation McManley's team Status Alive (as of Summer Service 05) Played by Andre First appearance Summer Service 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Henry is confused by the request for "worm medicine" and has no rain gear. He rides a Vespa (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Donald McManley is reluctant ("you guys can just drive to Salem"), but a Manipulate Someone roll of 13, made with the Biz as the team's most charming member, gets him to lend his assistant: "You can take Henry. He's useless anyway." The team sends Henry to Salem for ivermectin and any broad-spectrum antiparasitic, with a concealed carry permit as makeshift FBI cover. He asks for an umbrella (none to spare) and leaves into the storm (Summer Service 04). See Ivermectin.

After the hotel siege, a muffled signal from the Salem direction proves to be Henry (Andre): "I just killed a guy, I think. Or something." The team finds him on a Vespa with a gore-covered umbrella, the scooter soaked in blood and viscera. He hands over a pharmacy bag with the ivermectin ("Here's your worm pills. I'm going to bed"), shoves the Vespa off the road and climbs into the cramped vehicle: "I hate it here. It sucks so bad." His last line closes the session (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes do not say what he killed near Salem; Dante (as Kurt Larson) guesses it was an infected person, "if they exploded."

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • A different assistant, in pajamas, answers the RV door earlier in Summer Service 05, while Henry is still out. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Summer Service 04
  • Summer Service 05

docs.title: The "homeless" man
docs.text:
The "homeless" man is a ragged stranger in the alley beside the Ballard grocery store who bites Huell Kendrick's wrist, shouts "Pig!" and takes his dollar, in a town where locals insist there are no homeless people.

Type NPC (unidentified) Aliases The hobo; the homeless biter Affiliation Unknown; later linked to the Skinwalker faction Status Unknown First appearance Walkers 06 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A ragged man whose voice "sounded like he smoked asbestos" (Walkers 06).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
At the Ballard general store, a "homeless" man in the alley asks Huell for a dollar. When Huell holds it out, the man lunges and bites. Huell's Kick Some Ass roll is double ones, a 4 with +2, a failure. The man bites Huell's wrist, shouts "Pig!", grabs the dollar and runs. The listless clerk says "we don't got homeless in Ballard," fetches a first aid kit and bandages him (Walkers 06). Huell later tells the others that if they meet a homeless person they should not give him money, and Ezra jokes that the "hobo" must be the one leaving the anonymous notes (Walkers 06).

In Walkers 07 Huell's hand is swelling from the bite (he says, "It'll buff"). A private handout to Rita explains the faction's method: it clones people from tissue samples, Andrew's from the cut made by the mayor's ring and Huell's from the "hobo bite" (Walkers 07). The bite is therefore the source of tissue for Skinwalker Huell. See Replication.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Who the man was, and whether he was a skinwalker or a hired or controlled person.
  • What the "Pig!" outburst means, if anything.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 06
  • Referenced: Walkers 07

docs.title: Hooster
docs.text:
Hooster is the Biz's confidential informant in Washington, D.C., a "criminal MacGyver" on parole who agrees to build a bomb collar, supply thermite and sell a net gun to deal with the Sherman Ranch goose.

Type NPC (heard by phone only) Aliases The bomb-collar guy Affiliation Informant of Dick "The Biz" Baxter Status Alive (as of Walkers 04) First appearance Walkers 04 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Hooster is a D.C. informant out on parole and working shifts at Arby's. His wife is pregnant again (conjugal visits). He has elaborate crime tools, including an electromagnet for store windows and movie-style traps (Walkers 04). The Biz arrested him, and Hooster says: "You're the nicest guy I've ever been arrested by." Hooster sent the Biz dirty magazines in jail (Walkers 04).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
After the goose steals Howard's jacket and torments the team, the Biz decides he wants a bomb collar to "give the goose as a peace offering." He uses the Fixer move (Charm, result 12) to reach Hooster by phone. Hooster agrees to make a bomb collar with minimal collateral damage and absolutely no dogs, off the books and for cash; to supply thermite; and to sell a net gun as an anti-goose measure. He refuses to make fake FBI badges. He will mail the package in a flat-rate envelope after his Arby's shift (Walkers 04). See Nancy the goose.

His price is a policeman's ball invitation for him and his wife, plus help with D.C. parking tickets, which the Biz accepts. Howard excuses himself to the bathroom to avoid the call. Huell's request for a revolver-shotgun hybrid is forgotten before the call ends. The package is due in a few days (Walkers 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Andre spells the name "Hooster"; the table joked "Cooster" and "Booster."

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 04

docs.title: Horace Cromwell
docs.text:
Horace Cromwell is the banker on the Marblehead Board of Selectmen, a silent, bloated and visibly tense man at the back of the selectmen's meeting in The Summer Service.

Type NPC Aliases The banker Affiliation Marblehead Board of Selectmen Status Alive (as of Summer Service 04) First appearance Summer Service 04 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Cromwell is a large man who sits at the back of the room without speaking. His name plaque reads "Horace Cromwell" with "Banker" beneath it. He looks more bloated than most of the other selectmen, though less so than the mayor and the chief of police, and he moves restlessly, like someone struggling not to vomit, with his arms tense on the table (Summer Service 04). See The glow.

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text: At the 6:30 p.m. board meeting in the town hall, Zack (as Huell Kendrick) uses Read a Bad Situation to ask whether there are dangers the team has not noticed. Andre points out two things: the councilmen nervously eye the empty seat of Arnold Weathers, and Cromwell is restless and tense. Huell asks, "You're doing alright there, Horace?" Cromwell nods jerkily, waves the question away and says "I'm fine." Then something odd happens in his neck, so that he seems to swallow twice (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes never explain what happened in Cromwell's throat. The infection that bloats the selectmen is later tied to the worms.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 04

docs.title: Huell Kendrick
docs.text:
Huell Kendrick is a divorced, chain-smoking, knife-carrying FBI agent from Louisiana and a founding member of the Paranatural Incident Task Force, played by Zack.

Type Player character Aliases "Detective Hendricks" (Letterman's slip); "Toothbrush Man" (Jester); "Kendrick" (McManley); "sweetie" (Sheila) Affiliation FBI; Paranatural Incident Task Force; formerly a narcotics unit and a sheriff's office Status Alive, on crutches with a steel plate in his foot (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Zack

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Huell is in his fifties, a smoker with poor cardio who gets winded on an uphill path. He first appears in a gross detective coat with "cool-ass facial hair" and a taste for country music. The table has described his build several ways: Zack's "goblin-bellied," Andre's "built like an alcoholic," Dante's "Disco Elysium skinny fat," and later Rita's "kind of a beanpole," fairly tall and thin but still about 50 pounds heavier than Andrew Howard. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 04, Appalachia 03, Radford Horrors 02)

His manner is laconic and deadpan, with dry cop humor, crude asides and a habit of odd questions ("Hey, Howard, you ever been shot?"). He is polite to witnesses with a bite ("Not to be rude, sir"), flips off people who annoy him, and likes a cool entrance: he cleans his fingernails with a knife during an interview and holds his flashlight under his gun. Zack plays him as a man who shrugs things off ("You know, I'm a cool tough guy") over a sad, solitary home life. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 01, Summer Service 05, Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 03)

He started the campaign as the team's skeptic beside the equally doubtful Biz, answering Andrew's alien theories with "swamp gas" and insisting a missing girl was a runaway. That position eroded after he was lifted into the air by the thing over Radford, and by the end of the first case he was sad and shaken that cryptids are real. He has remained the voice of procedure: warrants, probable cause, "it'll be in my report." (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 08, Appalachia 06, Walkers 09)

His tastes are fixed points of the show's period setting: Ecto Cooler, Crystal Pepsi, Sour Patch Kids, Corn Nuts, pogs, ALF, Ms. Pac-Man and, at his lowest, Roseanne. He prefers Nirvana to the Red Hot Chili Peppers. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 04, Walkers 01, Walkers 07, Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Huell was raised in Louisiana and has decades of law-enforcement experience. Before the FBI he was a narcotics cop, worked for a sheriff's office (where the record for a missing person coming home was about 11 hours), did undercover work among "hillbillies," and says he once worked for a city. He went to college ("that's why I gotta be a detective") and did not serve in Vietnam ("I didn't go to no war"). He has first-aid training and carries a full kit. He also tells a goat-racing story from South Dakota, which nobody lets him finish. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 03, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 04, Walkers 01, Walkers 07)

He is divorced; in the first episode his ex-wife, "the battle-axe," had just taken half his belongings. He has a daughter in college whom he sees around New Year, and Zack calls him "the silver medal parent." His father was Thomas Kendrick, remembered at a late-summer table with a big plate of bacon; his grandfather called odd backwoods communities "the water people." (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 08, Appalachia 01, Roulet Estate 01, Walkers 09)

Huell reached the task force as a punishment. After an incident that is never described, his boss told him he was not fired and charges would not be pressed, but that he was off his investigation and his team, "your name is mud," and he was being sent to "some kind of make-work task force the president's idiot brother wanted." (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
Huell reported to the task force's D.C. barbershop office, opened a ream of fax paper with a needlessly large knife angled so everyone could see, and found a hidden cabinet of old "stakeout candy" while clearing the bathroom. He decorated his desk with postcards of the World Trade Center and the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building. In Radford he separated and interviewed Liam Lucky, privately questioned young Tyler about the spaceman, photographed the Lucky house, and concluded Amanda Lucky was a runaway. He ended the first night at the Pay n' Stay with a rash. (Radford Horror 01)

He led the questioning of Yobiah Whateley about the spacesuit and the dogs, and plotted the missing dogs on a motel tourist map, showing that every house bordered the woods. At Dr. Lori's office he read the psychiatrist as buttoned-down but capable of violence if cornered, and his help let the Biz plant a bug that promptly rolled into a vent. His attempts to get the bug back (a lost-jacket story, then feigned interest in the window) failed, and the experience from the failed roll levelled him up. That night he scouted a clearing on foot, heard tense Spanish, snapped a twig, slipped away from an armed group with flashlights, and later gave a wounded Kurt first aid. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03)

Having taken no precautions, Huell caught the motel's bedbugs. The welts across his stomach became a running subplot: a diner waitress threatened arson, the hospital steam-sterilized his clothes, and he spent the day in scrubs and then in the Biz's thrift-store slacks and a "Radford, Virginia, UFO USA" flying-saucer T-shirt. He ordered a pancake stack taller than his head, asked the blunt questions at the autopsy, and still refused to believe in the UFO: "I wasn't in the car that saw it personally." (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05)

Cruising the suburbs with Kurt, Huell spotted a figure in an astronaut suit at the tree line, ran it down and tackled it. Under the helmet was one of the Whateley twins. Huell put his knife to the boy's face; the boy said, "It's okay. You don't have to fight this," and something overhead lifted them both. Huell hung on above the tree line, smelling rotting wood and black mold, then fell: 4 harm, a broken right ulna, and unconsciousness. Kurt splinted the arm with a stilt. The same ER doctor who had treated his bedbugs that morning told him, "Huell—twice in a day, you are not having a good life, my friend." The cover story was that he fell off the water tower. Afterwards he was wistful and undecided about what he had met. (Radford Horror 06)

Still concussed and one-armed, he packed weapons, cigarettes, water, Everclear and dog treats for the raid on the old-town church. He eased the door open, recognized the smell from when he "got picked up," tackled Wilbur Whateley, and shot the Radford Moth. The creature then took his mind and made him shoot Andrew in the chest; the bullet slowed before it struck Andrew's breastbone. Huell cut off one of its legs with bolt cutters, threw Wilbur clear of the burning building, and freed the Biz from under it, at which point its proboscis went into his stomach and filled all seven of his harm boxes. Kurt dragged him out. (Radford Horror 07)

In hospital he welcomed Andrew to the "shot" club, admitted "I confess I didn't shoot you on purpose, Howard," and collected his medical records as proof he was not in hell. He searched the burned church and found no trace of the moth's body. Back in Washington a courier delivered a 25-pound stuffed alien from his old narcotics colleagues with the note "Ha ha, fuck you, Huell." He gave it to Andrew, and it became the team mascot, OJ. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
In Marblehead Huell bought the trash bag for the severed arm, started a feud with the desk clerk Jester by asking for a toothbrush (the inn, he was told, was "not a bed-and-toothbrush"), and heckled the service at the colonial church. When Amos Shaw offered communion wine, Kurt only sipped. Huell drank all of it. (Summer Service 01)

Unrecorded session

Summer Service 02 was never recorded. Later recaps establish that Huell, Kurt and Andrew were exposed to the nerve agent in the water during it. (Summer Service 03)

The wine carried the worms. Awake for about 48 hours, full of nervous energy and hungry, Huell walked to McDonald's for fries and passed a house whose door had stood open for days. Inside Amos Shaw's house he found signs of a struggle, a burner left on, clerical garments and about ten pounds of crystal marbles, and called the FBI switchboard from a payphone. The call brought forensic examiner Donald McManley and his RV to the scene. Andrew then noticed that Huell was visibly more muscular, that his hairline had advanced, and that he had the same youthful glow as the priest and Jester. Huell was torn about taking ivermectin: "I need more information about worms." (Summer Service 03)

"Jacked" on worms, he helped Kurt mount the Davy Crockett on the Biz's Buick Regal, borrowed Andrew's spare suit for the Board of Selectmen, and advised Esteban to "Take the biggest knife in your kitchen." (Summer Service 04)

At Arnold Weathers' house he shot Puddles through the forehead to no effect and was bitten and dragged; later he helped Andrew destroy Arnold Weathers himself, taking worms through his sock. He found the two sets of financial books and a shoebox of marbles, gave Madeline Weathers his favorite knife, and insulted McManley's pajamas. Overnight he no longer slept and healed completely within an hour. Curious, he cut his own arm open: the worms in his flesh burrowed away from the air and his blood was darker than normal. When armed church members surrounded the Ram and Arms Inn, he phoned the FBI to report a police posse and demand a helicopter, then fired at the sidewalk as a diversion so the others could reach McManley's RV. (Summer Service 05)

Unrecorded session

A session known as "05.5" was played between episodes 05 and 06 and never recorded. In Radford Horrors 04 Andre and Dante recall that the team hit Huell with their own car "when you were all wormed up," which Zack had forgotten. No recorded episode shows it, so it belongs to one of the arc's two lost sessions. (Summer Service 06, Radford Horrors 04)

In the finale the deworming agent took hold: he lost the worm "luster," got a pounding headache, and Zack removed the bonus from his sheet. He missed Jester with the flashlight weapon; Jester screamed "It's you, Toothbrush Man!" and bit his neck through the car window before being scraped off. Huell then beat the Biz at rock-paper-scissors for the right to fire the Davy Crockett at the angel thing. The roll was a mixed 7, and Zack burned a Luck point to make it a success, narrated at his request as a sudden sneeze that jerked the weapon onto target. He passed out in the back seat, visibly losing muscle and hair and regaining wrinkles, and ended the arc feverish in a National Guard medical tent, vomiting dying worms. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
Weeks of passing dead worms left Huell gray and haggard. He admitted, "You know, I kinda miss them, to be honest." Big Bill sent him on his day off to check on McManley, who was on leave and close to being fired. McManley hated him, and the persuasion roll was a 3, but Huell burned a Luck point and the two bonded over Roseanne; McManley agreed to come back to work, and Huell left with the pizza. He also had a new, embarrassingly large knife with a dragon on the hilt, "Nippon Steel." (Appalachia 01)

In Dahlonega he climbed a tree twice, ruining his suit and bruising himself, to retrieve a child's shoe with pale hair caught in the laces, and concluded Gene Cartwright was dead: "Listen, buddy, he was dead 45 minutes after the last person saw him." He slept through Andrew's sleepwalk, squeezed into the Death Cave, studied the folded face and stored it in the hotel mini fridge, and glimpsed a strangely familiar man in a cowboy hat entering the room next door. At Auraria he greeted the Covenant with a cheeky salute and needled a member about cheeseburgers until he stormed off. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04)

He argued for a warrant before searching Frotter Comstock's buildings, tested the Spud Hut savant with a coin flip, and bought dinner for the Circle Chasers: "Sure, we found ten grand in a garbage can. Fuck it, it's on me, boys." At the freeway crash site he was the one who connected the SHA logo on the Spud Hut truck to the tracking device. (Appalachia 06, Appalachia 07)

Disguised as press with a tape recorder and lanyard, he entered the distribution center. In the break room ambush he shot an ape-man through the neck; it slammed his head into a cinder-block wall, and Kurt's Claymore left him with a ruptured eardrum. Andrew and the Biz then pulled most of an ape-man jawbone out of his left buttock, and Kurt numbed the wound with cocaine. High, limping and worried about becoming a were-ape, Huell loaded up on an unreasonable amount of gold bars, was lifted and crushed by Big Bob until Andrew severed the creature's arm, and climbed the exit ladder only to find he could no longer walk. (Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09)

Unrecorded session

The finale, Appalachia 10, was never recorded. Its only trace on Huell's side is a phone call in the next episode, in which Andrew asks him, "When I did the weird shit, you weren't dying, were you?" Huell supposes he "must not have been." What Andrew did is not explained. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
Huell waited backstage, armed, while the Biz was sent onto David Letterman's show; the FBI had told the producers he had an anxiety disorder. Brought out for support, he defended the Biz with a Rodney King joke and flashed his gun. Letterman forgot his surname and called him "Officer Hendricks," then "Detective," and a bartender in Utah later remarked, "I guess if you're gonna be a hostage, you might as well be an armed hostage." Back at the office he collected pogs from Diane. (Walkers 01, Walkers 03)

In Utah he offended a local agent with "So— Mormons, am I right?", came out "con" on the Ballard community center, and tried to flirt with the Ponytail Lady using the Clinton scandal. He distracted Nancy the goose with lunch meat and was bitten on the nose so hard it swelled shut. In the Ballard bar he won at darts on a Luck point and drunkenly told Maggie about the town water. He was also McManley's designated contact, and put off calling him until 3 a.m. on the night the team's car vanished: "Yeah, I think there's aliens and shit. You should be over here." (Walkers 02, Walkers 03, Walkers 04)

When the Plymouth Voyager vanished, Huell worked out that it had gone straight up and that the ground beneath it had been very hot. It turned up in Roosevelt flattened into the road, and he lifted the wreck free with his back on a roll of double sixes. The same session established that he cannot ride a bicycle. During the night event his world tipped like the inside of a tumble dryer and he crashed through a card table while drawing on the refrigerator. (Walkers 04, Walkers 05)

He repaired the ground-penetrating radar with gum-wrapper foil, found the key to the sugar-filled refrigerator at Ballard City Hall, and spent the day with a dread he could not place. An anonymous page promised information about "your colleague" if he came alone to the general store. Nobody met him. Instead a "homeless" man in the alley bit his wrist, shouted "Pig!" and ran, in a town the clerk said had no homeless. (Walkers 06)

The bite was a tissue sample. The next episode's cold open showed Huell's face rising from a tank of dark liquid, and Andre confirmed in the same episode that the skinwalker faction was growing a copy of him from it. Unaware, Huell helped subdue a naked intruder in the guest double-wide, then chauffeured Andrew to a 1 a.m. meeting at Ballard High School, straightened his tie and waited in the car. After an explosion he stabilized the bloodied "Andrew" who staggered out, not knowing it was a duplicate. Inside he faced ten or twelve coyotes that rose onto their hind legs and unrolled one of the plastic-wrapped bodies falling from the gym ceiling. (Walkers 07)

He threw a brick through the glass door of the Roosevelt police station ("I don't give a shit about these cops. I'm the FB-fucking-I"), patched up Yusuf Ansari, and asked the locals whether the coyotes seemed like "regular coyotes." (Walkers 08)

Unrecorded session

Walkers 08.5 was never recorded. Huell began the finale unstable and one harm from death from earlier injuries, and with the battery missing from his police walkie-talkie. (Walkers 09)

The finale's cold open panned down to a wet, sullen, naked Huell eating Twizzlers at the community center. The real one was on horseback with the National Guard. He spotted a naked, blood-covered figure sprinting toward them: the real Andrew. His own double then dragged him from the saddle and got a tendril into his mouth for an instant, which made him smell his childhood bedroom; his horse trampled it and crushed its head. When the duplicate Andrew shot Kurt and fled, Huell rode it down, bandaged the wounds he had just inflicted, and put his fingers in its mouth. Its tendrils lunged for him and pulled up a memory of his father eating bacon. Winged in the arm by a stray bullet, he rode back to the others and fell off his horse from blood loss. He recovered enough to hold Andrew at gunpoint for an identity test ("Tell me something about a cigar-shaped craft"). In the cavern Zack made the roll for the team's grenade assault, which destroyed the machinery behind the portal and stranded 50 to 60 skinwalkers, and then rolled a 14 to get everyone up the collapsing stairs. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
At the office Christmas party Huell gave the carolers his leftover cigarettes, traded scotch with Diane, gave the Biz the ID of a recently dead lookalike, and received a gold Dunhill lighter and cigar cutter from Andrew. He was not told about Andrew's changed physiology. He woke hungover under a couch in the Roulet house, face to face with a mummified cat, put on a pink fluffy bathrobe, and handed the Finnish Hare Krishna monk his unloaded gun to see whether he would shoot. Chasing the Roulet Intruder through the woods, he was shot in the shin with a VSS rifle and went down. Zack: "That's the end of Huell's career." (Roulet Estate 01)

Too big for the chimney, he stayed below while Kurt and Andrew found the hidden attic lair, and searched the Clown Mansion crawl space in the name of probable cause. He was also the one who asked, "Do we have any particular reason to assume the gray alien is the serial killer?" (Roulet Estate 02)

At the Brooks Pharmacy siege he answered the young cop's "So, aliens, huh?" with a raised finger, knocked out and handcuffed the biting old woman in the VW Beetle, and stormed the front with Andrew. He tackled the gunman and pinned him, taking a Mosin-Nagant round through the foot for three harm. He kept, in Andre's words, "most of" the foot. (Roulet Estate 03)

By March 1993 the task force had been disbanded and Huell was on workers' compensation in a wheelchair, nearly broke, living in a filthy apartment where an unfriendly neighbor hauled him up the steps. He rated his mood 3 to 4 "on a scale of one to suicide." A child in the elevator asked about his foot: "Got shot by an alien." He spent his days drinking and watching Roseanne, and talked Diane's ear off about it on the phone. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
Andrew found him there months later, skipping physical therapy among Doritos and cinnamon Pop-Tarts. Huell claimed "I got so much going on," held out through fifteen minutes of Roseanne, and agreed to help look for the missing Biz. At the Biz's apartment he checked the medicine cabinet (no psychiatric medication, a great deal of aspirin). Asked whether the Biz could be a double agent, he replied: "Of course, I didn't notice when you got replaced with an alien, so—" (Radford Horrors 01)

He returned to Radford under Daniel Webster on crutches, with a steel plate in his foot, DEET, and a police-dog training glove he wore because "the last homeless guy I talked to bit me." He set off the smoke alarm in an airliner lavatory. At the Lonely Mountain Diner he asked to taste Andrew's rehydrated blood ("Tastes like blood"), failed to finish a huge breakfast and vomited across the bathroom, leaving with "Sorry about the mess." At the Sportsman RV Campground he searched the missing task force's tents and kept their map, then insisted on hiking to the fenced site and jolted his foot going over the wire. (Radford Horrors 02)

He stayed in the background of the next session, then waited in the car "out of shame" while Kurt apologized to Sheila for the bathroom. He phoned McManley ("Get down here, we've got goo"), mimed threatening Harold the Blockbuster clerk, and pitched a tent that leaned 20 degrees. (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Andrew Howard: his usual roommate and the believer to his skeptic. Huell shot him under the moth's control and has apologized more than once, the second time with a stick of gum. Andrew gave him the Dunhill lighter and phones him as a confidant; Huell treats him paternally, feeds his UFO fixation ("Keep looking at the sky, Howard") and is the most persistent user of "Half-Gallon Howard." He was left out of the loop on Andrew's condition. (Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 06, Walkers 01, Walkers 04, Walkers 07, Roulet Estate 01)
  • Dick "The Biz" Baxter: fellow divorced cynic and back-seat drinking partner, whom Ezra calls his brother in "all things greedy." Huell nearly died pulling him from under the moth. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 07, Appalachia 09)
  • Kurt Larson: his partner on the ground team. Kurt dragged him out of the burning church, splinted him with a stilt, taught him to fire a nuclear weapon and treated his wounds with cocaine. (Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 06, Appalachia 09)
  • Donald McManley: in Andrew's words, "they bond in a really odd, antagonistic sort of way." Huell insulted his pajamas and flicked a cigarette butt at him, but is also the one who talked him back to work and the one he pages first. McManley sent a curt get-well card. (Summer Service 05, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 07, Walkers 05, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Jester: a mutual dislike that began with a refused toothbrush and ended with a bite to the neck. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 06)
  • Diane: shared cigarettes on his first day, pogs, and matching bottles of scotch at Christmas. (Radford Horror 01, Walkers 01, Roulet Estate 01)
  • Nancy the goose: bit his nose and fouled his pillow. (Walkers 03, Walkers 04)

docs.title: Abilities and equipment
docs.text:
Huell's playbook is never named in the episodes. For how the rules are used at this table, see Game mechanics.

Ratings. Cool +3 is his defining stat ("I'm plus three on Cool, so I'm so fucking cool") and the highest on the team. He has Sharp +1 and Charm -1. Tough is +1 in the first arc and +2 by The Radford Horrors. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horrors 02)

Moves.

  • Uses Cool in place of Sharp for Investigate a Mystery and for Read a Bad Situation. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03)
  • +1 when interrogating an uncooperative person for the first time. (Radford Horror 02)
  • First aid with a full kit: roll Cool; on a 10+ the patient is stabilized and healed of 2 harm, on a 7-9 he chooses one. He has used it on Kurt, Andrew, the Biz, Yusuf, an intruder, a skinwalker and himself. (Summer Service 05, Appalachia 03, Walkers 07, Walkers 09)
  • A move from the Crooked playbook, which Zack calls "my Hoodlum ability": Tough instead of Charm to Manipulate Someone when using violence. This was his first advance, deferred for a session while Zack read the options. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06)
  • He reached level four in the Marblehead finale. (Summer Service 06)

Harm, Luck and dread. He has seven harm boxes and has filled all of them once. His Luck began at seven and does not come back; three points are known to have been spent, on the Davy Crockett shot, on McManley and on a darts game. Andre's borrowed "dread" track stood at 11 marks for Huell in Utah and, per Zack, had not risen "since we nuked a kaiju." (Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01, Walkers 03, Walkers 07)

Worm strength. While infected in Marblehead he had a separate bonus to Tough, needed no sleep and healed fully in an hour. All of it ended with the cure. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05, Summer Service 06)

Gear.

  • A .38 revolver and badge; by The Radford Horrors his sheet lists a revolver and a shotgun. He has borrowed an M16 and Kurt's P90. (Radford Horror 03, Walkers 06, Walkers 07, Radford Horrors 02)
  • An unnecessarily large knife, worn to make others feel inadequate. His favorite, Muriel, went to Madeline Weathers; its replacement is bigger and has a dragon on the hilt. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 01)
  • First aid kit, camera, cigarettes, and a jar for samples. (Summer Service 05)
  • A supply of wolf urine he refused to leave behind in Radford, for reasons never stated. (Radford Horror 08)
  • Crutches, DEET and a police-dog training glove. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• His ex-wife's name was never fixed. Asked to name his favorite knife in Summer Service 05, Zack could remember only that her name began with an M and settled on "I think it was Muriel," so the knife is Muriel. In Walkers 07 Huell, shaken awake, says "God damn it, Margaret." In Roulet Estate 01 Zack admits, "I don't remember what I named either my ex-wife or college-age daughter," and Andre does not remember either; the daughter has no name in any recorded episode. (Summer Service 05, Walkers 07, Roulet Estate 01)
  • His sidearm is a .38 revolver, as Andre confirms in Radford Horror 03. Kurt's hospital remark that "9mm doesn't look too impressive" about the wound Huell gave Andrew is the only suggestion otherwise. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 08)
  • He was shot twice in The Roulet Estate: in the shin by the intruder's rifle in the woods, and through the foot at the pharmacy. The foot wound is the one that put him in a wheelchair, and Andre's recap in Radford Horrors 02 credits it to "the guy who was pretending to be an alien in those people's attic." (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Huell has been bitten by a worm-ridden Doberman, a desk clerk, a goose, a stranger in an alley, a coyote and an old woman. His dog-training glove is the result. (Summer Service 05, Summer Service 06, Walkers 03, Walkers 06, Walkers 07, Roulet Estate 03)
  • The non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable was retconned into the show as an OVA Huell watched on hotel cable while falling asleep. (Appalachia 02)
  • His postcards and his O.J. Simpson line are deliberate period irony. He also believes John Travolta is a Mormon rather than a Scientologist. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Zack was "kinda hoping" Huell would be hit by the moth's mind control, "'cause it's more interesting," and had him sleep through a team meeting "because I think it's in character. To be shitty about it." (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 07)
  • He had told McManley that watching Roseanne was rock bottom, then took it up himself; Zack had forgotten the earlier conversation until Andre reminded him. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Irene Scott
docs.text:
Irene Scott is the chatty, friendly mother of Lena Scott, who runs Scott Insurance from the family home in Marblehead.

Type NPC Aliases Irene; Mrs. Scott Affiliation Scott Insurance ("we do boats and cars") Status Alive (as of Summer Service 03) First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Irene is young, friendly and talkative. She offers visitors coffee, pop, snack cakes and Necco Wafers (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Kurt Larson phones the number listed for "Lana Scott" from the missing scientists' contact list, reasoning that an individual is more likely a recent arrival than a long-rooted family. Irene answers "Scott Insurance, we do boats and cars." She says her daughter was on a ventilator for a couple of hours at the big hospital in Salem and is back at school, and that the scientists drew blood, promised follow-up and vanished. Kurt claims to be an FBI consultant, and Irene asks if it is terrorism (Summer Service 01).

At the Scott home, the sign reads "Scott Insurance, Boat Specialty." Irene asks to see ID. She and her husband Douglas Scott, who says he hoped to hear back from the scientists, describe Lena's collapse on the beach the day after the blast (Summer Service 01).

At the lighthouse, Irene recognizes Andrew Howard ("Mr. Howard, right?") and asks whether the team is reopening the lighthouse. After the team's warnings, the family flees (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Irene Whateley
docs.text:
Irene Whateley is the mother of the Whateley boys in Radford, Virginia, a patient of Dr. Lawrence Lori who walked into the woods one evening after seeing something through her kitchen window, and whose body is later found in the old church.

Type NPC Aliases Mrs. Whateley; Irene Affiliation Whateley family Status Dead (body found in Radford Horror 08) First appearance Radford Horror 01 (as "Mrs. Whateley," unseen) Played by Andre (voiced through others)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Irene never appears alive on screen. She is described by others: her husband Yobiah Whateley, a churchgoing man of about sixty; Dr. Lori, who calls her "a pretty strong one"; and the sheriff. Yobiah says she has had some depression since her son Wilbur's accident. Lori treated her for night terrors and insomnia, which he guesses were PTSD-related, starting a year and a half before her disappearance. She stopped coming six months before, unable to tolerate the tremors from the lithium and the side effects of the Prozac (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Radford Horror 01
docs.text: In his briefing, Sheriff Roosevelt mentions a second disappearance: a neighbor named Mrs. Whateley, who saw something out her kitchen window while making dinner, put down her pan, walked into the night and never came back. The team notes that the case looks different from Amanda Lucky's but that the two may be linked (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: Radford Horror 02
docs.text:
The team chooses the Whateley disappearance over a visit to Dr. Lori because it seems more pressing. At the Whateley house the sheriff shows them the kitchen, where a window by the mud door looks out on woods. Yobiah tells Kurt that Irene "saw something out the kitchen window" that he did not see, dropped the pan so that hot water went everywhere, ignored him and walked into the woods. He thought she was chasing off a coyote. Asked whether she seemed angry or scared, he says she "seemed surprised." Outside, the team finds two sets of footprints, one following the other deeper into the woods until the trail is lost in the ground cover. In the parents' bedroom the Biz finds nothing packed and no jewelry taken, so Irene expected to go to bed that night, along with leftover Prozac and lithium prescribed by Lori, meaning she had stopped taking them (Radford Horror 02).

When the team visits Lori, he tells them Irene came to him a year and a half earlier and that nothing in her history would explain wandering off (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Radford Horror 08
docs.text: After the fight at the burning church, the sheriff tells the team that Mrs. Whateley's remains were found in the back of the church, burned and disemboweled. Back at the church it is added that she was found crucified and, like Amanda, had organs missing. When the team returns to the church, a humanoid fat stain on the floor marks where she lay. The team agrees to let the police pin everything on Wilbur (Radford Horror 08). See Old-town church and Crucifixion MO.

docs.text:

  • Wilbur Whateley and Abelforth Whateley: her sons.
  • Dr. Lawrence Lori: her psychiatrist; Lori's patients included both Irene and Amanda.

docs.text:

  • Andre first said Irene started seeing Lori "about a year ago," then corrected it to a year and a half ago, stopping six months before.
  • Yobiah was first called "Josiah" and corrected to Yobiah.

docs.title: Jan Martense
docs.text:
Jan Martense is the tall, gaunt East German manager of the Spud Hut Georgia Regional Distribution Center and the head of a secret gold-mining operation staffed by bred ape-men, the main antagonist of The Things in Appalachia.

Type NPC (antagonist) Aliases Jan; Yan; Jan Martens Affiliation Spud Hut; Jan's Conspiracy Status Alive; captured and held at Black Site Omaha (as of Walkers 01) First appearance Appalachia 03 (mentioned); first seen in Appalachia 08 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Jan is very tall (Andre puts him at about six foot four or five), thin and sweaty, in a suit that does not quite fit, with stubble, close-set eyes and slightly greasy short hair. The table compared him to Nosferatu, "trash Dracula", Siegfried and Roy, and the villains of Die Hard. He speaks formally ("Yes, yes, okay") and likes the word "chicanery" (Appalachia 08). In captivity he is cheerful and candid, calls Kurt "Mr. Kurtis", and is unrepentant ("That's business", "exigencies of war") (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Jan tells Kurt that he grew up in East Germany and "gets" the spook arrangement between the CIA and FBI. A Spud Hut employee in Appalachia 08 had guessed he was "Polish or Irish or something" (Appalachia 08).

By his own account in Walkers 01, about five years before the case Jan was driving drunk in the Georgia countryside when he hit and killed a man in a black suit who carried NSA identification (see Dead NSA Man in Black). He put the body in the passenger seat of the man's car and drove it into a lake. In the man's van he found an ape woman strapped to a gurney and being fed drugs. He kept her, hoping to make money, and called her Shelly. Because she aged quickly, he first tried every kind of ape semen, posing as a representative of a Saudi buyer, and when none worked he used his own, by artificial insemination. Only the male offspring lived; a lab told him the chromosome numbers did not line up. The ape-men proved very strong and able to recognize gold, so he put them to work mining it, planning to melt it down, sell it to a dealer and launder the proceeds through acquaintances. He kept the ape-men secret so as not to need contractors, and hired an animal handler only because he could not manage them himself.

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
Jan is first mentioned when a Spud Hut phone worker offers to get "Jan" for Andrew (Appalachia 03).

In Appalachia 08 the team meets him after his receptionist Charlene leads them through the plant. He calls the driver's death a "tragic accident" and an "employee loss", promises to check every outgoing truck against its manifest, and asks whether the agents were the FBI men spying on a presidential candidate. Kurt introduces himself as CIA, assisting the FBI. Jan declares that he will not tolerate "any chicanery at my facility", keys the "Special Projects" door, and takes them to the lowest floor ("Down here we do the toppings"). He sends them to wait in a break room (code 441) while he makes a call, and heads back to the elevator. The room holds the ape-men. Kurt's Read a Bad Situation roll had marked Jan as "squirrelly", but the team could not tell whether that meant guilt or ordinary corporate nerves. See Special Projects Level and The Break Room (code 441).

The cold open of Appalachia 09 follows Jan hurrying down a hallway, brushing off his secretary Marlene ("Not now, Marlene") and the waiting reporters, unlocking a service lift with a key on his belt, and wheeling a large animal crate to a red pickup truck. The animal handler Clive later tells the team that Jan's first condition of employment was "don't ask questions about the ape-men", that the operation had run about a year and a half, and that Jan "kept getting more" ape-men. The conspiracy comprised five people: Jan, Clive, a mercenary who smelted the gold, and two bodyguards, with a target of at least $100 million. In the gold room the team finds about half the gold gone. Clive says the fake Bigfoot sightings were Jan's idea to discredit the real ones. When Kurt describes the dead man in a Bigfoot costume found in the forest, Clive confirms that he was the mercenary; Kurt assumes that Jan killed him, which nobody confirms (see The Bigfoot Hoax and Troy Cleaver).

Unrecorded session

The finale, Appalachia 10, was never recorded. Its events are known only from Kurt's references to it in Walkers 01.

docs.title: The finale, as recapped
docs.text: In the unrecorded finale, Jan meant the team to die, with ketamine and shotguns. Kurt shot Jan, and Jan shot Andrew in the face. A falling ape then crushed Jan, breaking his skull. Jan fled the Spud Hut facility shortly before it exploded (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Captivity
docs.text:
In Walkers 01 Kurt interviews Jan at Black Site Omaha, five stories below the ocean surface. Jan wears a loose gray jumpsuit and still carries stitches and the bruising from his broken skull. They trade jabs ("Kurtis, you shot me." / "You shot my leader in the face. Seemed only fair.") and agree to a quid pro quo. Kurt teaches him to make improvised playing cards from napkins and coasters, since cards are banned. Jan concedes the team "was intended to die", says hiring the animal handler halved his take and doubled the risk of a leak, and names the Spud Hut accountant Clyde Harvard as the one other insider. He says he buys his ketamine from a high schooler. He does not know why the Spud Hut facility exploded, and Kurt keeps the portal secret from him (see The Crack in the Air). Kurt assumes Jan "took care of" the mercenary in the woods; Jan does not deny it.

Elsewhere in the episode, Jan is the man the public blames for the Georgia hotel-room surveillance of Governor Clinton, whose Polaroids were taken with a Russian camera (see Clinton Surveillance Scandal). On Late Night with David Letterman, the Biz jokes "Maybe he's a Republican" and "Jan is Polish... they were part of the USSR".

In Appalachia 08 Dante protests that Andre has made "a Polish character that's named J-A-N and is pronounced Jan", Kurt asks for "Jan Martin", and in Appalachia 09 Dante accuses Andre of switching the name from Jan to Yan and back again. In Walkers 01, Kurt addresses him as "Mr. Martense" after Andre prompts "Kevin".
