docs.title: Jeremy
docs.text:
Jeremy is a former door-to-door vacuum cleaner salesman and recovering Quaalude addict who is baptized into the Covenant in the red-clay river near Auraria, Georgia.

Type NPC Aliases the salesman Affiliation The Covenant (recruit) Status Unknown; baptism shown in the cold open (as of Appalachia 04) First appearance Appalachia 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In the cold open of Appalachia 04 he is a sweating man in a brown suit with a suitcase of vacuum cleaner brochures and a big brown Bakelite vacuum cleaner. His brand is a running question. Mother Dahlia Riversand says it was "like, a Con-A-Wear, something like that. It looked cheap", but Zack presses her on whether it was a Kirby, and Andre retcons it to a Kirby.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The episode opens on a horror-styled scene in a gas-lit tent near Dahlonega. Jeremy changes into a thin white robe and follows a candlelit path to a river red with clay, where four women in white dresses kneel in the mud. An older man with high cheekbones kisses his forehead and hands him a jar of dark liquid with peaches floating in it. After Jeremy drinks, the sound goes muffled and the camera unsteady. The man wades in with a candle, chants in Latin and plunges Jeremy under the mud, and he vanishes beneath the surface. The older man is not named in the scene. See Covenant Peach Preserves and Covenant Beliefs (Appalachia 04).

Later in the same episode the team visits Auraria, and Dahlia invites them to "the baptism this evening" for a door salesman who came to sell to the Covenant and whom they "managed to talk into it". When Andrew asks to speak with him, Dahlia at first refuses, saying he is "in preparation for his christening". She relents after Rita rolls an 8 to Manipulate Someone and Andrew plays lost and haunted. She tells Andrew she can see the devil standing right behind him, and lets him talk to Jeremy through the tent wall.

Jeremy assumes the FBI is there about "those deaths" and swears he did not know the vacuum cleaners were "like that"; Andrew explains he is not there about that. Jeremy says he got hooked on Quaaludes and lost his wife, his children and his job, then took up selling vacuum cleaners, only for the machines to kill some people, so he switched companies. His car broke down near Auraria, and he tried to sell vacuum cleaners to a community that has no electricity. He calls Elijah Ray "a special man that knows things" and thinks the Covenant may manage his life better than he has. He is out of Quaaludes and asks Andrew for some. Dahlia promises that at the least the Covenant will not give him more (Appalachia 04).

The team leaves without stopping the ceremony, so the cold open is presumably his baptism. His fate afterward is not shown.

docs.title: Jester
docs.text:
Jester is the devout desk clerk of the team's hotel in Marblehead, a church member and selectman who owns a bag of crystal marbles and feeds Arnold, and who ends infected and killed while driving the stolen FBI car.

Type NPC Aliases J. Evans ("businessman"); desk clerk; front desk man; "Toothbrush Man" (Jester's cry to Huell) Affiliation Sons of Adam; Marblehead Board of Selectmen Status Dead (Summer Service 06) Played by Andre First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Jester wears a name tag reading "Jester" and has a Crypt Keeper haircut (Summer Service 01); by the cold open of Summer Service 03 his shoulder-length hair is ratty. He is rude ("do I look like a convenience store?") and very devout; Amos Shaw calls him "a little intense." In Summer Service 04 he looks like Jesse Ventura without the glow or joy, dour enough to "take a bone away from a dog," and wears a suit about thirty years out of date (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
At the front desk he serves fish breakfast at 6 a.m. and refuses Huell Kendrick a toothbrush: "bed-and-breakfast, not a bed-and-toothbrush." The Biz finds an open bag on his desk holding about a dozen crystal marbles, warmer than glass and hard enough to blunt a steel knife, and steals one. Kurt overhears Jester arguing in the back room about "weather," "quarantine" and "unbeliever." At the end of the session Jester is frantically searching his desk and ignores the team; Huell's later taunt about the marble suggests he was looking for the one the Biz took (Summer Service 01). See Crystal marbles.

In the cold open of Summer Service 03, he carries a tray to a chained house at night and talks to "Arnold" as a sick friend; see Arnold Weathers. Later Huell sees him looking haunted; he gives Huell an appraising nod and goes into the back room (Summer Service 03).

Jester has told the team he sits on the town council, so the selectmen treat the meeting as one he arranged. At six o'clock he waits impatiently in the lobby in a suit about thirty years out of date and leads the team there. He sits at the plaque "J. Evans, businessman." He warns the team not to leave "whatever that is" (the Davy Crockett warhead) in a room; Kurt says it is laundry, and Jester points to the washing machine. At the meeting the mayor remarks that Jester should have talked to the board first so it was not taken by surprise, and Jester sinks down in his chair; the chief of police glares at him (Summer Service 04). See Chief of Police.

During the siege night he is absent from the desk after a phone call; McManley notes he "practically ran out the door," and Kurt says "he's definitely involved" (Summer Service 05).

In the arc finale, the team spots their FBI car near the back of the convoy on the flooded freeway, crawling along with one man at the wheel until it sticks in a water-filled dip and falls behind. The driver gets out to hunt through the car and its trunk for something to wedge under the wheels, and as the team pulls up behind him he turns out to be Jester, now worm-infected. When a bump sends Huell's flashlight blast wide and sets one of the FBI car's tires on fire, he screams "It's you, Toothbrush Man!", dives through the window of the team's car and sinks his teeth into Huell's neck. Andrew swerves to scrape him off against the stuck car, Huell leans out to help, Jester's body slams into its windshield and is dragged away, and Andrew backs over him. He dies, blood, bile and worms gushing from his mouth (Summer Service 06). See Flooded freeway and marsh and Worm bags.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: Jester and Huell dislike each other over the toothbrush; as the fight begins Zack (as Huell) says "Guess what? We took your marble" (Summer Service 06).

See Ram and Arms Inn.

docs.title: Kurtis "Kurt" Larson
docs.text:
Kurtis "Kurt" Leonard Larson is a Vietnam veteran and former CIA case officer from the agency's UTAW branch who serves the Paranatural Incident Task Force as its consultant, burglar, interrogator and tactical lead, played by Dante.

Type Player character Aliases Kurt; Kurtis; "Special Agent Kurtis"; Larson; "Mr. Kurtis" Playbook The Expert Affiliation Paranatural Incident Task Force (consultant on loan); CIA; formerly UTAW Family Wife Huyen; son Benji Walther Larson; twin daughters Peggy Browning Larson and Melanie Colt Larson Status Alive (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Dante

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Kurt is in his late forties, about 46, and complains about his spine. He wears a mustache, which he scratches to hide his lip movements, and dresses like a suburban father: a short-sleeved white shirt with no tie, a fanny pack and a "utility dad belt." Dante pictures him in khakis and a polo with yellow-tinted aviators over his actual glasses. He is slight and not physically imposing; Andre pictures him as smaller than the Biz. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06)

His body is a record of his career. He has two overlapping bullet holes in his lower arm from being shot in exactly the same spot twice, years apart; a Vietnamese spear scar through the shoulder; hearing damage from a hand grenade that went off in his tent; scars that creep up his neck; and "a whole host of little holes" under his shirt. The campaign adds a moth scar on his neck and a bite-and-stab wound in his leg. Andre once described his face as "an open, honest war criminal face." (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horrors 02, Walkers 03, Walkers 04, Walkers 06)

His manner is friendly, folksy and chatty. He calls people "Slick," "buddy" and "son," calls the FBI agents "boys," "Federales" and fellow "alphabet boys," apologizes for swearing, over-tips, and likes to introduce himself by his full name: "Kurtis Leonard Larson." Under the patter he is deadpan, sardonic and given to gallows humor, Vietnam anecdotes and tall tales that nobody can check. He calls himself a "Midwest boy," and one episode cut to credits on his Minnesota-flavored "Aw heck." He likes jazz, smokes only for cover or to ingratiate himself, and prefers McDonald's to local cooking. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 09, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Vietnam
docs.text: Kurt spent about five years in Vietnam. His stories from it include pretending to be dirt, eating in trenches, Viet Cong tunnels and prison camps, a dog he named Willie Pete, and a pair of stilts he carried from the war until 1992. He says he was an advisor to Marines, has been exposed to Agent Orange, and has been in an internment camp. In his own words he has "been in many wars." (Radford Horror 08, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 08, Walkers 02, Walkers 04, Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: CIA and UTAW
docs.text:
Kurt was a CIA case officer in UTAW, the Unorthodox Tactics and Warfare division, which trains its people "not to jump to conclusions, but instead maintain a possibility space of potential likelihoods." Its unofficial motto, as Kurt quotes it, is "anything done in defense of the American people is legal." UTAW experimented with bombs on bats, dolphins, dogs, gerbils, rats and cats, with lasers, with psychic dream exercises and with LSD, and worked on plots against Castro; an FBI agent in Salt Lake City knows it as the "explode the cigars" outfit. The experience left Kurt convinced that animals make bad operational tools. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 04, Summer Service 06, Walkers 02, Radford Horrors 03)

The jobs he claims include toppling a despot, posing as an insurance salesman (he "made a sale"), posing as a male prostitute, impersonating a general, crawling three miles through a sewer pipe, hiding in a septic tank, poisoning the Cuban dictator through a handshake, accounting for "three of Castro's body doubles," and accidentally exploding Castro's dog. He mentions Colombia, Korea, Kuwait, Dubai (which he is "not allowed to talk about") and being summoned to South America to torture a man. He says he was legally declared dead years ago. Most of these are stories Kurt tells in passing, and nothing on screen confirms them. (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 01, Summer Service 04, Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 07, Walkers 05, Roulet Estate 01)

He also has a history with the strange. He is "on the fence" about whether he once killed a vampire, and he took part in a tulpa summoning on LSD; pressed on whether he merely tried, Dante answered, "Tried nothing. Carl is dead." The agency trained him to resist psychic intrusion and interrogation, and Andre treats him as one of only two task force members, with Andrew Howard, who have real psychic defenses. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 07, Walkers 01, Radford Horrors 04)

The Iran-Contra affair ended the careers that he and his arms-dealing associate Carter had had. By 1992 he was on loan to the FBI Counterterrorism Task Force, carrying case officer credentials and interagency loan paperwork but no badge. In the fall of 1992 George H. W. Bush called his file "interesting reading" and said he slept better knowing Castro had people like that haunting him. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 04, Walkers 01)

docs.title: Family
docs.text: Kurt's wife, Huyen, is a former Viet Cong fighter who once tortured him; Dante summed the marriage up as "enemies to lovers." She cooks mostly Vietnamese food, keeps the language alive around the house and, as Kurt puts it, does "a great augmenting" of the children's education at home. Andre has called Kurt the only happily married player character. They have three children, each with a gunmaker for a middle name: a son, Benji Walther Larson, who is nineteen and "got real into Nirvana," and twin daughters, Peggy Browning Larson and Melanie Colt Larson. The family car is a minivan, which Kurt drives carefully. (Radford Horror 02, Appalachia 07, Walkers 02, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
Kurt's boss at the Counterterrorism Task Force, a man who said he had been in Hanoi, downsized him with a favorite analogy about wanting a German Shepherd and getting a crocodile, and sent him to the new task force under Andrew Howard on a contract of "a couple of years." The team assembled at the D.C. barbershop on May 24, 1992. Kurt cracked the keypad on its steel basement door with luminol and a black light (the code was 4-5-1) and cartwheeled down the stairs into a panic room of Vietnam-era arms. He then drove the team to Radford, Virginia to look for the missing Amanda Lucky, serving cucumber sandwiches and juice boxes packed by his wife. On the first morning he spotted the rooftop watcher on the post office, memorized the plates in its lot, found the pills hidden in Amanda's bedpost, and climbed the trellis to find where a rope had been tied on her roof. (Radford Horror 01)

He took point on the interviews, questioning Yobiah Whateley, Dr. Lori and the town pharmacist, then staked out the Augustine barn alone, lying in the hayloft for more than two hours and leaving with a hair tie and copies of Derek Augustine's notes. That evening he noticed a white van tailing the team and, to turn the tables, commandeered the car of an elderly couple at a drive-thru; they went along only after he showed his Vietnam scars. Driving their diesel up the mountain, he was the first to notice a silent object in the sky, and then hit Agent Murphy at about 50 mph when the man stepped into the road. Kurt grabbed him as he tried to leave, and Murphy set him on fire with the flashlight weapon; Kurt bit open a hollow molar and spat LSD into Murphy's mouth. He took 3 harm, with charred circles on his chest, and was healed in the car by Andrew's laying on of hands and Huell's first aid. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03)

After the emergency room, still slightly high, he tracked blood with luminol and a black light, collected Murphy's teeth, ID and about two pounds of remains, and opened Murphy's briefcase in a welding mask. He led the autopsy of Amanda Lucky, finding the crucifixion wounds, the needle marks and the butterfly hair tie that matched the one from the barn. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05)

On the night stakeout he marked the craft with a black-painted Super Soaker full of glow-stick fluid and radioed, "Target is marked... It's got the Whateley boy." Something then struck at his mind for 2 harm and a spell of blindness. He splinted Huell's arm with a stilt, tailed the craft by car, and led the break-in at the Whateley house, where he crawled through the cellar to a mummified teenager nailed to the wall. He blamed himself when Wilbur Whateley slipped out the moment the yard watch was dropped. (Radford Horror 06)

The case ended at the old-town church. Posing as a private investigator, Kurt charmed the guard Douglas Douglas, dug up Dean Lawson's cash in the yard of the Lawson cabin and found his heroin under a bedroom floorboard, and snorted heroin to win over the pilot Freak, from whose plane he spotted the church. Inside he fought the Radford Moth: he resisted its mind three times, shot it, took its proboscis through the thigh, and burned it with an Everclear Molotov that rained fire on him too. He cut Phoebe Augustine free and carried her out on an amphetamine tooth, dragged out Huell and then the Biz, took a burning beam, and padlocked the door behind them. He reached five harm before Andrew healed him. With soldiers closing in, the episode cut to credits on his "Aw heck." (Radford Horror 07)

He took charge of the escape from the cleanup crew with hand signals, duct-tape bandages and an ambush in which he hid under bloody leaves as bait, and came away with one of their flashlight weapons and a shadow poncho, which he handed to Molly Underhill in tinfoil as "special federal evidence." After a week in the Radford ER he tested both by the river and supplied the cover story for the sheriff. An illegal contact later checked Murphy's badge for him: it looked genuine, but nobody of that name existed in the records. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
In Marblehead, Massachusetts, Kurt did most of the phone work as an "FBI consultant," bonded with the veteran Briggs, and learned that FBI counterintelligence was watching the Biz, which he kept from the Biz. At the colonial church he only pretended to finish the communion wine, and felt sweaty and off afterward. (Summer Service 01)

Unrecorded session

Summer Service 02 was never recorded. Later recaps say that Kurt, Huell and Andrew were exposed to the nerve agent at the stealth wreck, that Kurt's hands got wet and he was hit hardest, and that it was Kurt who described the wreck's radar-minimizing shape and capacitor turret. (Summer Service 03)

He spent the rest of the case sick: adult chicken pox, nerve-agent effects and, it was presumed, the worms. He slept in the back seat under a space blanket and carried a -1 to everything. What he had seen underwater frightened him enough to call an old weapons contact, and at the cost of a Luck point Carter delivered an M28 Davy Crockett with one W54 round. Kurt was as pleased as "a kid on Christmas." (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04)

He picked the locks at the lighthouse and at Arnold Weathers' house. There the worm-ridden dog Puddles bit deep into his forearm, and Andrew's church mace, fired to save him, beheaded the dog and passed through Kurt's hand. He took 3 harm and lost about a tenth of his blood. He still ran kitchen experiments on the worms (vodka, heat and salt kill them), talked Madeline Weathers out of burning the church by showing her his grenades, and, when armed church members surrounded the hotel at 4 a.m., passed the sixty-pound warhead out of a window and led the team unseen to McManley's RV. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05)

In the finale he was the team's radio liaison and arms expert. He negotiated with the radio contact, revealed the Davy Crockett with "Can you keep a secret?", and taught the others to fire it while lying in the back seat. Huell won the right to fire and remembered Kurt's stance tip as he slipped. Kurt used his amphetamine tooth twice and noticed that the Geiger counter spiked when the creature died, not when the warhead went off. He helped Andrew give the Guard the terrorist cover story. He ended the arc asleep in a National Guard medical tent after antivirals and chicken soup. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
On October 3, 1992, Kurt testified to a House subcommittee about Marblehead in an old service suit, dodging without lying, with his CIA boss sitting silently in the room. Sent to Dahlonega, Georgia, he treated Bigfoot as an assassination target and read a big-game hunting book for weaknesses. (Appalachia 01)

He ran the field procedure: inverted-wedge searches, a photograph of every print, and luminol at each scene. In the hidden tunnel under the Consolidated Gold Mine he took point on the strength of his Vietnam tunnel experience, was mauled by one of the ape-men and shot it, which produced the team's only blood sample. He argued that the creature was an animal but that the blinking red light on it meant people were involved. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04)

At Auraria he pressed women's-shelter cards on members of the Covenant and promised to report them to child protective services. When a dead "Bigfoot" turned up on Comstock's property, he ruled out UTAW because the man in the costume wore no body armor, identified a Navy SEAL trident tattoo, and read him as a hired mercenary who had been double-crossed. At the Spud Hut he bought a margarita spud with three fake IDs, and he opened his escape kit to disguise Andrew and hand out Hawaiian shirts. (Appalachia 04, Appalachia 06, Appalachia 07)

Inside the distribution center he introduced himself to Jan Martense as CIA, put on a European accent for a reporter ruse, and propped the break room door with his shoe. When the ape-men came out, one punched his dog whistle into his throat, and with four closing on him he set down a Claymore and yelled "Ear pro!" Underground he quieted the screaming Sheriff Burke, numbed Huell's wound with cocaine, hotwired a forklift, and got the working shift of ape-men to take ketamine-filled Combos by eating one himself. He led the stand against Big Bob with a near-fatal chest shot, and took a "reasonable amount" of gold for his wife and kids. He protected the handler Clive from the rest of the party. (Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09)

Unrecorded session

Appalachia 05 and the finale, Appalachia 10, were never recorded. Kurt's interrogation of Jan in the next episode establishes that Kurt shot Jan in the finale, and that Jan was captured. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
Kurt was ordered to stay away from the Letterman taping and spent it five stories under the ocean at Black Site Omaha, interviewing Jan ("Kurtis, you shot me." / "Ah, you shot my leader in the face. Seemed only fair."). He traded for Jan's account of how he came by the first ape woman, Shelly, kept the crack in the air secret from him, and kept his promise to ask the guard for playing cards. In the following weeks he arranged a CIA job for the Spud Hut savant and sourced a P90. (Walkers 01)

At Sherman Ranch he refused to disarm on Robert Bigelow's porch, spread the warning about Ballard's water, and promised Alberta Wilmarth the exhumation of her mother. He led the field work after the dusk event, when the watch his wife gave him stopped, and found the scorch marks on the engine. Walking to the big house alone, he was stalked by an upright coyote and handled it with baloney and a "verbal flashbang." His Vietnam stilts were lost with the crushed rental car. (Walkers 02, Walkers 03, Walkers 04)

During the night event he believed he was in Saigon and hid behind a dresser with the P90, shouting in Vietnamese. He bit his LSD tooth to reach "a more familiar broken state," then pulled the levitating Andrew down by the ankle. He ran the ground-penetrating radar, got Yusuf Ansari to admit his innocence, broke a lockpick at Ballard City Hall, and threw his broken watch into the beam. At his request the Utah National Guard went on standby. (Walkers 05, Walkers 06)

When a naked intruder broke into the double-wide he shot the man's foot with the P90, took a chokehold, and ran the aftermath. He was not at Ballard High School when Andrew was replaced by a duplicate, and he worked beside the duplicate without knowing. The next day he was the tactical lead in Roosevelt: he ran procedure at the road ambush, rammed two fleeing men with Betsy, and led the breach of the police station. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08)

Unrecorded session

Walkers 08.5 was never recorded, and no later recap says what Kurt did in it.

In the finale he rode a horse beside the Guard convoy (horses being nonferrous), recruited Ned Simpson and his killdozer as "an asset," and recognized that the cloud over the ranch was the farmhouse floating in the sky. He proposed sabotaging the substation. When a second Andrew appeared, Kurt held the newcomer at gunpoint and cuffed him, then asked the Andrew he had been travelling with to open his mouth; that one, the duplicate, shot Kurt in the leg and ran. Kurt uncuffed the real Andrew. For the infiltration of the community center he marked his brow with Sharpie and stripped, and in the cavern he threw grenades into the crowd and through the portal and sprayed a flame light until it melted. He took a Humvee ("I'm the chain of command. We're moving."), drove out still naked, and put on record by radio that a cover-up was under way that the team had not caused. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
On Christmas Eve 1992 Kurt fixed the office gas heater, restored the power by sneaking into the neighbors' building, and gave Diane a Herman Miller chair stamped as the property of the NSA. He gave Andrew a fake alien fetus in a jar, and the Biz gave him a floppy disk marked "Mystery Government Files." He had kept a Ziploc of the white powder from Utah. In January he woke in an armchair in the Roulet house holding an empty peppermint schnapps bottle, and with the Biz he spotted a grey face peeking over the roof. (Roulet Estate 01)

He opened the safe with a fire poker at the cost of his shin, took fingerprints from the VSS rifle, lost a minute of time, and pocketed the visitation tapes. Digging in the basement he hallucinated a Vietnamese prison guard and emptied his sidearm into the hole. He found the chimney passages and led the climb to the attic lair. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

At the Brooks Pharmacy siege he invented a burning-tire smoke screen, stripped to his underwear for the ruse, picked the back door and bound the gunman with that underwear. When the task force was disbanded he was sent to Sri Lanka, then recalled after Waco to train American agencies; in April 1993 he was lecturing at Quantico on silent breach coordination. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
In early April 1993 Kurt was at a school science fair, where his daughter Peggy won gold with a projectile-stabilization project and he kept up his cover as a "continuous improvement consultant." Called to the Biz's apartment by Andrew, he found the bug-out briefcase in a heat vent and concluded that the Biz had meant to return and had been intercepted. Asked whether he himself was a double agent, he said, "Not currently." (Radford Horrors 01)

Back in Radford under Daniel Webster, who refused to let him out of his sight, he argued a spear gun through airport security by showing his spear scar, and held a grenade as a dead man's switch when IRS Criminal Investigations stormed the Ferry Lodge. At the Safe Environment Fund site he fired a P90 burst into the air after guards tasered Webster, found a thoroughly professional cleanup, and scraped pearlescent goo from a branch. That night he pinned the rabid mouse to the floor with the spear gun. After rabies shots he led the investigation at the Douglas Pinball Emporium and did most of the detective work that followed, including the questioning of Wilbur Whateley. In the closing image of the latest session, Andrew lifts him one-handed into the tree where he sleeps, at the campground. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Andrew Howard: Kurt is patient with Andrew's inexperience and treats him as a protégé; Andrew is awed by him. He calls Andrew "son" and "square," and Rita has answered him with "Dad." (Radford Horror 05, Appalachia 03, Roulet Estate 02, Walkers 05)
  • Dick "The Biz" Baxter: friendly from the first day; Kurt teases him, calls him "Bizarino" and trusts him to lead, while keeping the counterintelligence investigation from him. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 01, Appalachia 08, Roulet Estate 02)
  • Huell Kendrick: friendly; Kurt covers for his embarrassments. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Daniel Webster: Webster has seen the scars on Kurt's neck and believes he once skinned two men. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Donald McManley: Kurt treats him as the team pathologist. (Summer Service 03)
  • Carter: an old associate in experimental weaponry who supplied the Davy Crockett. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04)
  • Walt "Coyote" Murphy: a friendly peer, whom Kurt nicknames "Yote." (Walkers 04, Walkers 05)

docs.title: Playbook and moves
docs.text:
Kurt is built on the Expert playbook of Monster of the Week. For more on the rules as played, see Game mechanics. (Walkers 04)

  • Ratings: Sharp +3 (reached by Summer Service 01), Cool +2, Charm 0, Tough 0, Weird +1. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 01, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Haven: an armory, which in the fiction is the Vietnam-era arsenal in the basement of the task force office. (Radford Horror 01, Walkers 04)
  • Preparedness: a Sharp roll to have the right item on hand. It has produced a portable darkroom, Tiger Balm, a Claymore, an escape kit and a pack of baloney. (Radford Horror 05, Summer Service 01, Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08, Walkers 04)
  • Often Right: anyone who takes his honest advice gets +1. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 08)
  • Dark Past: taken as a level-up at the start of Radford Horror 05. Dante floated it as the mechanism behind the weapons contact. (Summer Service 03)
  • Luck: he burned a Luck point to obtain the Davy Crockett. (Summer Service 04)
  • Later level-ups: Dante announced further level-ups in Walkers 06 and Walkers 08 without saying at the table what he took.

docs.title: Gear
docs.text:
• The teeth: four hollow molars, each holding a different drug. The LSD tooth was used on Agent Murphy and during the Utah night event; the amphetamine tooth gives +1 forward. A private CIA dentist refills them between missions. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 06, Walkers 05)
  • Investigation kit: luminol and a black light, a crime-scene camera, fingerprint powder, lockpicks and bump keys, bolt cutters, duct tape, rubber gloves, a tape recorder, and a welding mask later lined with tinfoil. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 07, Walkers 06)
  • The fanny pack: service weapon, pager, case officer credentials, concealed carry permit, interagency loan paperwork, handcuffs, flashlight, handheld radio and, in Marblehead, two hand grenades. (Summer Service 04)
  • The travel case and trunk: a huge wheeled case that takes 75 percent of the trunk, with a wetsuit, waders, wolf urine, a spike strip, caltrops, a steel plate, MREs and a pair of stilts. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Summer Service 06)
  • The escape kit: makeup, prosthetics, wigs, sunglasses, several outfits, and fake IDs and press credentials from several countries. (Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08)
  • Weapons: a service pistol; Claymore mines; Molotovs; the M28 Davy Crockett; the P90; a spear gun he sleeps with; and captured flashlight weapons. (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05, Walkers 01, Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"Not your average spook. I think of myself as more of a Casper." Dante (as Kurt) (Radford Horror 01)

Quote

"I got shot in the exact same place, twice, in Vietnam, five years apart. Now, that's a sacrifice." Dante (as Kurt) (Radford Horror 03)

Quote

"Listen. Once immolated, twice shy, let me tell ya." Dante (as Kurt) (Radford Horror 04)

Quote

"Moth to a flame, bitch!" Dante (as Kurt) (Radford Horror 07)

Quote

"I spent a lot of time in Vietnam pretending to be dirt." Dante (as Kurt) (Radford Horror 08)

Quote

"All right, boys, raise your hand. Who wants to cause a nuclear incident?" Dante (as Kurt) (Summer Service 06)

Quote

"Just remember, anything done in service to the American people is legal. At least that's what they always told me in my unit." Dante (as Kurt) (Appalachia 03)

Quote

"I'm CIA. I'm certified for anything." Dante (as Kurt) (Appalachia 09)

Quote

"Parlez-vous français?" Dante (as Kurt) (Walkers 04)

Quote

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Attendance: Kurt is present in all 37 recorded canon sessions. His only absence is the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist, in which Dante plays Derk. His part in the unrecorded sessions is known only where a later recap mentions him; see Lost episodes.
  • Names: "Kurt" and "Kurtis" are used interchangeably at the table. Zack once called him "Kirk." (Walkers 06)
  • UTAW: Dante first expands the acronym as the "unorthodox tactics and weapons division," says "Unorthodox Tactics and Weapons" again in Summer Service 06, and at once corrects himself to "Tactics and Warfare." It has twice been misheard as "Utah." (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 06)
  • The bullet holes: Kurt says the two wounds in the same spot came "three years apart" in Radford Horror 01 and "in Vietnam, five years apart" in Radford Horror 03.
  • The children's ages: in Radford Horror 02 Kurt says, "Boy's nineteen, girls are both thirteen." In Radford Horrors 01, set a year later, Andre needed a child of elementary-school age for the science fair, and Dante made the twins nine. When Kurt shows a family photo in Appalachia 07 he says the three are "all grown up."
  • Stilts: a pair of stilts in the trunk is a running gag. One became Huell's splint and another Kurt's crutch; the originals, which had shrapnel in them, were lost in Utah. (Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 05, Walkers 04)
  • Dentists: Kurt holds that every hotel the team books fills up with a dentists' conference, "like a curse or something." (Appalachia 02, Walkers 02)
  • Verbal psionic flashbang: his technique of breaking an opponent's concentration with a line such as "The accident wasn't your fault." He has used it on a giant moth and, in French, on a coyote. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08, Walkers 04)
  • Visualizing the polygon: a CIA "polygon of defense" exercise he does for hours at a time. (Walkers 01, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Predictions: in 1992 he says of the World Trade Center, "Those things will stand for a thousand years, I swear," and predicts electric cars within three years. (Radford Horror 01)
  • Bessie: when Huell asks for the P90, Kurt tells him to "treat Bessie right." The team's car is the similarly named Betsy. (Walkers 06)
  • He never votes ("conflict of interest") and says ketamine "might be the only drug I have a problem with." (Walkers 05, Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Dr. Lawrence Lori
docs.text:
Dr. Lawrence Lori (M.D., Ph.D.) is the only psychiatrist in Radford, Virginia, the treating doctor of both Amanda Lucky and Irene Whateley, who becomes a prime suspect for the task force, is bugged and burgled by the team, is tortured by Derek Augustine, and finally confesses to an inappropriate sexual relationship with Amanda.

Type NPC Aliases Dr. Lori; Dr. Laurie; Dr. Lawrence; the psychiatrist; the shrink Occupation Psychiatrist, private practice in a brownstone (Dr. Lori's office) Status In custody and going to prison (as of Radford Horror 08) First appearance Mentioned in Radford Horror 01; first seen in Radford Horror 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Lori is a buttoned-down, suit-wearing man who keeps his office in a nondescript brownstone. He is about 5'7" to 5'8" with a beard, mustache and brown hair, and drives a brown station wagon (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 04). Huell reads him as capable of violence if cornered. Derek Augustine tells the team he always got "kind of a weird vibe from the man" because "he likes jazz too much" (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Radford Horror 01
docs.text: Lori is introduced by Amanda's parents, Liam Lucky and his wife, who say she was seeing a therapist "for her grades" for about a year, that her grades got better, and that "we only have the one therapist in town." The team does not meet Lori yet (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: Radford Horror 02
docs.text: The team visits his brownstone office after the Whateley house. His receptionist offers lemon candies and pages him, and after about fifteen minutes of small talk he comes out with a nervous teenage patient. Lori tells the agents that Irene Whateley began treatment a year and a half ago and quit six months earlier over lithium tremors and Prozac side effects. He denies ever prescribing Amanda Vicodin, saying there is no reason to give it for an anxiety disorder, and refuses to discuss patients without consent, but under pressure he names her boyfriend Dean Lawson as involved in drugs. Before leaving, the Biz plants a bug in the office; it rolls into a vent. At the pharmacy afterward, the team learns a Vicodin record for Amanda under Lori's name exists, and that the other Vicodin prescriptions from Lori are mostly for seventeen- and eighteen-year-olds (Radford Horror 02). See the bug in Dr. Lori's vent.

docs.title: Radford Horror 03
docs.text: Listening in from the car, the Biz hears Lori on a heated phone call before he hurries out. Kurt tails him to a ranch house, where Lori storms into a converted backyard barn, argues with the man inside, and leaves in a huff; the team later learns this is the Augustine house and barn. Andrew chooses to lose him rather than be seen (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Radford Horror 04
docs.text: The Biz breaks into the office at night, retrieves the bug from the furnace vent and photographs the files, but wrecks the back of a locked filing cabinet while trying to open it, so Lori will know someone was there. At the Pay n' Stay the team asks about a fishing-hat guest, Red Dutchford; his height, beard and brown station wagon match Lori's, but the clerk does not recognize the description (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Radford Horror 05
docs.text: Lori is not seen in person. The developed photos show Amanda's file: Xanax prescribed with a stated reason, doses later raised without explanation, no mention of opiates, and extra appointments that taper into "no shows" (patient files). Derek Augustine says Lori came by upset about a prescription he had not written (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Radford Horror 06
docs.text: Highway patrol finds two men in a motel, one torturing the other with pliers and a blowtorch. The victim, identified from his wallet, is Lori, and he is hospitalized. The torturer is Derek Augustine, who believes Lori kidnapped his daughter Phoebe (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: Radford Horror 08
docs.text: The sheriff reports that Lori and Augustine have both confessed to an inappropriate sexual relationship with Amanda Lucky. Each had discovered the other's involvement, and Augustine then came to believe Lori was doing the same to his daughter Phoebe. Both are going to prison. The sheriff also believes Augustine broke into Lori's office, where animal feces were left in the toilet (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Amanda Lucky: patient; the later confession concerns her.
  • Irene Whateley: patient.
  • Derek Augustine: visited him angrily; later tortures him; both confess.
  • The task force: bugged and burgled by the Biz and suspected throughout.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• His name is spelled variously as Lori, Laurie and Lawrence in the episodes; the wiki uses "Lori."
  • Whether the prescriptions Lori denied writing were forged, or entered in error at the pharmacy, is never established.

docs.title: Lena Scott
docs.text:
Lena Scott is a friendly six-year-old in Marblehead who hugs strangers and fell ill on the beach the day after the offshore explosion.

Type NPC Aliases Lana Scott; Lena Affiliation Scott family Status Alive (as of Summer Service 03) Played by Andre First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Lena is about six. She greets strangers by shouting "Strangers!" and hugging them, and after her coffee she answers a good deal with "Coffee." Her father warns visitors not to give her any (Summer Service 01). At the lighthouse she is serious, nods gravely and waves vigorously (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
The missing scientists' contact list names a "Lana Scott," which the team takes to be her. Her mother Irene Scott says she spent a couple of hours on a ventilator at the hospital in Salem and is back at school (Summer Service 01).

On the school field trip to the fort the day after the blast, Lena wandered to the beach and was found unconscious. Her symptoms were breathing trouble, vomiting, racing pulse, pinhole pupils, trembling, compulsive movements and sweating; she improved after about eight hours and was fine in a day or two. The scientists said it was not natural gas and planned toxin labs. Dante (as Kurt Larson) remarks that the symptoms match a stimulant or amphetamine overdose (Summer Service 01).

When the team visits the Scott home, she climbs into Andrew Howard's lap (Summer Service 01).

At the lighthouse she runs straight to Andrew and hugs him again, saying "Hi" and then telling him "I got an A in school for art." Her parents arrive and, after the team's warnings, take her home (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The transcribed contact list spells her name "Lana," while the Scott family and Andre say "Lena."
  • At the table, guest player Kira says she wants to adopt Lena (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Liam Lucky
docs.text:
Liam Lucky is the father of missing teenager Amanda Lucky and a worker at the Radford Arsenal, where he does something classified.

Type NPC Affiliation Radford Arsenal (classified work) Family Wife Sarah; daughter Amanda (only child) Residence Lucky house, Radford, Virginia Status Alive (as of Radford Horror 01) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Liam and his wife Sarah keep an extremely Catholic home, with devotional candles, shrines to the Virgin Mary and, in place of a television, a six-foot-tall oak carving of the crucifixion. When the task force arrives they are waiting by the phone for news of their daughter, visibly distressed (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 01, Sheriff Roosevelt takes the team to the Lucky house, where Amanda's third-story bedroom window sits above a sheltered carport with a two-story drop and no signs of impact. Huell separates Liam from the others to walk around the house with him, and rolls Investigate a Mystery (an 11, total 14, for hold 2). Huell concludes that the parents were asleep, genuinely do not know what happened and are innocent. Liam makes a slightly odd mention of his job and, pressed, says he works for the Arsenal on something classified that he cannot discuss. Asked about Amanda's medications, the Luckys say she had been seeing a therapist for her grades for about a year, that her grades improved, and that Radford has only the one therapist, Dr. Lawrence Lori. Both parents point the finger at Amanda's biker friend Matt McCready, who lives with his father at a tourist ski lodge in the mountains and smokes pot, which they do not approve of (Radford Horror 01).

Liam's workplace ties him to local legend. The Pay n' Stay clerk (see Rutherford) tells the team his father believed Radford was cursed because the armory made the guncotton for the atom bomb (Radford Horror 01).

Liam does not appear again. Amanda's body is found in Radford Horror 04 and examined in Radford Horror 05, but her parents are not shown.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Liam's classified work is never explained.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Ma Gramoire
docs.text:
Ma Gramoire is a tiny, blunt, absinthe-drinking old woman of Marblehead, poisoned by the sea, the last known contact of the missing scientists, who later sends Madeline Weathers to the team.

Type NPC Aliases Ma Family Son Jordan, in the National Guard Status Alive (as of Summer Service 05) First appearance Summer Service 01 (by phone) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Ma Gramoire is 4'7", wide and solid, with a cane and a permanent baked-in squint. She is folksy and profane ("sun in my buns"), calls Kurt "son," drinks absinthe over ice, and distrusts the government, the water and fish. Her house, marked "Gramoire Residence," is a slightly broken-down suburban house on the main island (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
She is on the missing scientists' contact list. When Kurt Larson phones, she is hard of hearing ("Don't shout at me") and hangs up on hearing "FBI": "I don't talk to feds" (Summer Service 01).

In person she says she will speak to the government only if it brings back her National Guard son Jordan. Dante rolls a 7 on Manipulate Someone for Kurt, a partial success: she will help only if he does something right away to show he means it. Kurt calls Big Bill from her phone, and Big Bill's secretary agrees to request Jordan Gramoire for the deployment. She then gives Kurt a grilled cheese and absinthe and says she was poisoned by dipping a toe in the sea. The scientists visited her in the hospital, had interviewed other victims and had got nowhere with the Board of Selectmen; they planned to check the town's only lighthouse. Kurt leaves her house drunk (Summer Service 03). See The lighthouse.

In Summer Service 05, Madeline Weathers says Ma Gramoire told her the team was in town. After the team learns that vodka kills the worms, Dante (as Kurt) speculates that this is why Ma Gramoire, a steady absinthe drinker, is unaffected (Summer Service 05). See Madeline Weathers.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Bonds with Kurt over distrust of fish and water.
  • Her son Jordan Gramoire is in the National Guard; she says he "just don't call."

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"I've never liked people who can read." Andre (as Ma Gramoire), about the scientists (Summer Service 03)

Quote

"That'll put hair on your chest. They say it makes people insane, but I've been drinking it for years." Andre (as Ma Gramoire), about absinthe (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• When her name comes up in Summer Service 01, Zack says, "I've always wanted to meet an orc."
  • Dante wants to call her last, "'cause I wanna know what the fuck a Ma Gramoire is before I talk to it." (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:

docs.title: Madeline Weathers
docs.text:
Madeline Weathers is the niece of the missing selectman Arnold Weathers, a Beetle-driving young woman who comes to the task force for help in the storm-lashed Marblehead of The Summer Service and ends the case vowing to burn down the town's church.

Type NPC Aliases Madeline Affiliation None; relative of Arnold Weathers; hostile to the Sons of Adam church Status Alive (as of Summer Service 05) First appearance Summer Service 05 Played by Andre (game master)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Madeline is a young woman in a raincoat who drives a VW Beetle and plays Nirvana's "Smells Like Teen Spirit" at high volume (Summer Service 05). She is by turns darkly funny and frightened. She wants "somebody normal" to help her, and she distrusts both the church and the local police, saying she thinks they are "all fucking involved" (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
After a hostile Board of Selectmen meeting, Andrew Howard sees Madeline pacing the town hall parking lot in the rain, repeatedly looking at the team's car. She asks whether he is a cop, then demands his "position on Jesus Christ." Andrew answers that Jesus was an all-powerful alien who came to help guide humanity, and she says she just wants someone normal (Summer Service 05).

She reports that her uncle Arnold has not been seen for four days: he missed a meeting to help her sell her car, his gate is padlocked, and the police did nothing. She blames the church. Ma Gramoire had told her the team was in town. Madeline leads them in her Beetle toward the walled house on the island across the flooded bridge; at a red light she floors it and the team briefly loses her (Summer Service 05).

At the house, Kurt Larson picks the padlocks and Madeline opens the front door with her own key. She waits outside with Andrew while the others search the house. Kurt warns her to eat only sealed, imported food and no fish, and she mentions shopping at Whole Foods in Salem (Summer Service 05).

Afterwards Andrew shows her the severed head of the family dog and she screams, recognizing Puddles. He explains the parasite and the contaminated food and tells her Arnold will not recover. She says "I thought he meant botulism!" Madeline vows to burn the church. Andrew admits he is bad at comforting people and asks her to let the FBI do its job; Kurt shows her his hand grenades and asks her to wait because kidnapped scientists might still be inside. She makes him promise that "all of those motherfuckers are going to pay" (Summer Service 05).

Before the team leaves, the Biz plants a bug in her house, the team gives her pager numbers, Kurt gives her a joint and teaches her to make a Molotov cocktail, and Huell Kendrick gives her his favorite knife, Muriel, named for his wife. Kurt tells her to bar her window with a two-by-four and to get Ivermectin, lying to a veterinarian if she has to; she plans to go to Salem the next day. She asks for a grenade and a gun and is refused (Summer Service 05).

She is last seen alive at home and does not appear in Summer Service 06. It is never shown whether she carries out her threat.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Arnold Weathers: her uncle. He was infected and found in his upstairs bathtub, and he was destroyed by Andrew and Huell. Madeline does not witness it, though she later sees the head of his dog.
  • Andrew Howard: her main contact; the only team member who stays with her through the fight.
  • Kurt Larson: advises her on food, the Molotov and Ivermectin, and talks her down.
  • Ma Gramoire: sent her to the team.

docs.title: Abilities and equipment
docs.text: Madeline has no special abilities. At the end of her scene she holds Huell's knife Muriel, the team's pager numbers, a joint and Molotov instructions.

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

Andre (as Madeline): "Okay, tell me your position on Jesus Christ." (Summer Service 05)

Quote

Rita (as Andrew Howard): "He's an all-powerful alien that came to Earth to help us, guide us to a better future." (Summer Service 05)

Quote

Zack (as Huell Kendrick), handing over the knife: "There is no battle-axe in the world that is more of a battle-axe than this woman." (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Zack cannot remember the name of Huell's wife, so the table settles on "Muriel" for the knife; Ezra suggests "Muriel's Bane" (Summer Service 05).
  • The storm that frames her scene is named Tropical Storm Andrew 2, a gag on the lead character's name.

docs.text: • Summer Service 05

docs.title: Maggie
docs.text:
Maggie is the young, blunt bartender of Ballard, Utah, who gives the team their best picture of the town's gossip, tells the ball-lightning story and mothers Andrew Howard with root beer floats.

Type NPC Aliases The bartender Affiliation Works at the bar, Ballard Status Alive (as of Walkers 03) First appearance Walkers 03 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Maggie is young, attractive and blunt, and fiercely protective of the bar's licensing. She is profane ("pardon my French"), fixes the bar's cassette jukebox, and keeps order: "Not in the bar. Not again... Parking lot." She introduces herself only at the end of the night: "I'm Maggie, by the way. Not that anyone asks." (Walkers 03)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
After meeting Sheriff McDermish, the team goes to the nervously quiet bar across from the courthouse. Maggie glares at Andrew Howard and demands ID, saying "I had to make sure it wasn't another Mormon fed." She makes him drink a free vodka-Coke shot, then softens and gives him a root beer float, and later half-gallon milkshakes on the house, waving off his attempt to pay. The Biz coins "Half-Gallon Howard" (Walkers 03).

She recognizes the Biz from TV as the man who "spied on Bill Clinton" and gave a weird interview, and remembers Huell on the couch looking like an armed hostage. She says, "I don't think Bill Clinton would be caught dead in Ballard, Utah." She also serves the sheriff red wine in a pint glass of ice ("Coming up, you fucking freak") (Walkers 03). See Clinton Surveillance Scandal.

Maggie's gossip includes:

  • The community center is being built half the county away from the community, pushed by Deborah Wells, whom she has known since the first grade and dislikes; Pueblo ruins were bulldozed for it despite a protest. See Community center.
  • Ballard has about 30 blackouts a year, four new school computers that never worked, a stink at the high school, and people who can get a college degree "magically disappear." See Disappearances in Ballard.
  • The crazy rich guy renting the ranch refused a drink in a weird way and warned her off the water.
  • She saw what she thinks was ball lightning streak past her car on the ranch's back road and shoot straight up; the man with her swears they nearly got abducted (Walkers 03). See The dusk event.

When a drunk Huell tells her the town water has semen in it, the party half-confirms it, and she reasons it must be bulk-bought animal semen with a paper trail (Walkers 03). See Ballard water contamination.

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"I had to make sure it wasn't another Mormon fed." (Walkers 03)

Quote

"Turns out it is really hard to chain yourself to adobe." (Walkers 03)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• In the graveyard scene, Andre asked whether he had given the dead mother a name yet, and Zack answered "Maggie", mixing her up with the bartender (Walkers 03).
  • She refuses to let the sheriff show the table where a quarter of one buttock was shot off: "Parking lot."

docs.text: • Walkers 03

docs.title: Margaret Roulet
docs.text:
Margaret Roulet was a UFO believer who lived with her husband at 118 Benefit Street in Exeter, Rhode Island, and whose reported "visitations" and disappearance drew the task force to the Roulet House.

Type NPC Aliases Roulette; the wife; owner of the house Status Dead; identified in Roulet Estate 02 First appearance Roulet Estate 01 (as an unnamed owner)

docs.title: Background
docs.text: In the recap that opens Roulet Estate 02, Andre explains the origin of the trip: a member of the Keely Network message boards who knew Andrew wrote to say that their friend Margaret Roulet had been having "visitations" and then vanished. The letter reached Andrew on Christmas Eve, inside a foil-wrapped envelope handed over by Big Bill (see Foil-Wrapped Letter). (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: What the agents learn
docs.text: In Roulet Estate 01 the agents do not know the owners' names. From the library, Andrew deduces that they were a husband and wife and that the wife was the more devout believer. A partly coded notebook logs several months of incidents ending in the fall of 1992, and the VHS rack includes tapes labelled "September '92 visitation," "May '91 visitation" and "Lights in the sky, July '92" (see Visitation Tapes). The safe in the bedroom holds only a sheet of wedding photos, apparently from the 1950s or 60s and taken in Arizona. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Death
docs.text:
In the basement, Kurt digs into the trash pit, hallucinates grasping hands, and fires into the hole. When he comes to, a withered, sleeved human hand is sticking out of the dirt, shot several times. Andrew fetches the wedding photos, and Andre rules that the ring on the hand matches the one in the photos: it is Margaret. The agents dig further and find parts of two bodies, too decayed for a cause of death, with the cloth bleached and dissolved, apparently by something caustic poured in to control the smell. See Roulet Basement. (Roulet Estate 02)

The agents later discover that someone had been living in a hidden attic above the house, probably for at least a year, and photographing the sleeping occupants (see Hidden Attic Lair and The Roulet Intruder). The owners had fitted inside locks to their bedroom doors. The episodes never establish who killed her, or whether the intruder did. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: The agents assume that her husband, Mr. Roulet, is the second body.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Andre's recap spells her surname both "Roulette" and "Roulet"; the shorter spelling is used on this wiki.
  • After reading the library in Roulet Estate 01, Andrew tells Kurt the case is "just like the letter said", a classic case of two people being abused by the Greys. See The Greys. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Roulet Estate 01 (as one of the unnamed owners)
  • Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Matt McCready
docs.text:
Matt McCready is a leather-jacketed teenage biker in Radford, Virginia, the unofficial boyfriend of Amanda Lucky, who lives and works at the Alpine Lodge ski resort.

Type NPC Aliases McCready; biker boy Residence Alpine Lodge Family Father Ed McCready (Radford Horror 01); his uncle owns the lodge (Radford Horror 06) Status Alive (as of Radford Horror 06) First appearance Mentioned in Radford Horror 01; seen in Radford Horror 06 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: When the team finally meets him, Matt is a teenager at the night desk of the lodge's visitor center. He is friendly, wry and guilelessly helpful, and he gets a visibly lost look when Amanda comes up. The Luckys say he rides a motorcycle and smokes pot (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: Radford Horror 01 to 03: a name on the list
docs.text: Sheriff Roosevelt identifies Amanda's biker friend as "Ed McCready's boy, Matt McCready." Liam Lucky and his wife point the finger at him, saying he lives with his father, Ed, at a tourist ski lodge in the mountains, separate from the Ferry Lodge where the team tried to find rooms (Radford Horror 01). In Radford Horror 02 Yobiah Whateley lists the McCreadys among his sons' schoolmates, and the pharmacist says "McCready works up at his folks' place" (Radford Horror 02). In Radford Horror 03 the team calls him the unofficial boyfriend, in contrast to the official boyfriend Dean Lawson, and notes that he lives at the ski lodge outside of town, but has not yet interviewed him (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Radford Horror 06: the night watch
docs.text:
The team plans a stakeout from the ski lodge's water tower. At the off-season Alpine Lodge visitor center, Andrew finds Matt on night watch because town kids have been spray-painting the property. He serves sad instant coffee and writes a Sharpie liability waiver for climbing the water tower, which the agents sign. He gives them the key to the locked ladder and asks for it back before they leave.

Matt tells them he was Amanda's friend; he calls her "a very internal person" whose smile lit up the room, "nice to be with, hard to be close to." He says Dean Lawson threatened to shoot him or have him killed when he asked when Dean last saw Amanda, that Dean has scary, "methy" friends, and that Dean has a family cabin about a mile from the lodge, which he marks with an X on a tourist map. About a week earlier, Amanda had seemed to want to tell him something at school but never got to it. He adds that the lodge gets UFO hunters every year and sells merchandise, and that while maintaining the ski lifts he felt something big and silent pass over him, smelling like compost or "an old closet." He now carries a shotgun.

After the encounter with the craft, Andrew throws the key back at the visitor center door and Matt catches it mid-joint (Radford Horror 06). See Lawson cabin.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Amanda Lucky: friend and unofficial boyfriend.
  • Dean Lawson: threatened him.
  • Andrew Howard: the agent he deals with.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Radford Horror 01 has Matt living with his father Ed at the lodge, while in Radford Horror 06 he says his uncle owns the resort and he helps out. The episodes never address how the two fit together.

docs.text:
• Radford Horror 01 (mentioned)
  • Radford Horror 02 (mentioned)
  • Radford Horror 03 (mentioned)
  • Radford Horror 06

docs.title: Maybelline Augustine
docs.text:
Maybelline Augustine is the devout, hospitable mother of Phoebe Augustine and wife of Derek Augustine, who gossips with the task force about Dean Lawson and later reports her husband missing.

Type NPC Aliases Mrs. Augustine; Maybelline Family Husband Derek Augustine; daughter Phoebe; a younger son Residence Augustine house and barn, Radford, Virginia Status Alive (as of Radford Horror 06) First appearance Radford Horror 03 (named only); met in Radford Horror 05 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Maybelline is hospitable, pouring Andrew a glass of sweet tea and apologizing that she has no cold filtered water, and devout, with strong opinions about who goes to church. When her husband grows agitated at the agents' questions, she pulls him back down to the couch and tells him, "They know what they're doing. They're the FBI. Let's just let them work" (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Radford Horror 03
docs.text: Tracing the barn where Dr. Lori went in a huff, the team looks up the address and finds it belongs to Derek and Maybelline Augustine. Andrew phones Molly Underhill about the family, and she says they have a son of about eleven and an older daughter, attend church, and have never crossed the radar of law enforcement. The Augustines are not seen (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Radford Horror 04
docs.text: Molly pages the team early in the morning: neighbors heard a scream in the woods, and the Augustines found that their daughter Phoebe was not in her bed. Police and neighbors comb the woods near the Augustine house (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Radford Horror 05
docs.text:
When the team arrives, a part-time deputy is sitting with Derek and Maybelline. They describe Phoebe's ordinary evening, her fight with Laura Nichols and a scream before dawn. Andrew takes Maybelline into the kitchen for sweet tea, leaving Kurt alone with her husband. In the kitchen she tells Andrew that:

  • Amanda had seemed off and out of it the last couple of times she visited.
  • The fate of the Whateley boys hit Phoebe hard, since one of the twins, she is not sure which, had a serious crush on Phoebe when they were younger.
  • Phoebe fought with Amanda a couple of times over Amanda's boyfriend, Dean Lawson.
  • Dean's parents are never home, so he lives alone in that house, drives wildly around town and does not go to church. She would not be surprised if he were up to something "unwholesome": "That boy needs Jesus."

(Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: Radford Horror 06
docs.text: Maybelline reports her husband missing; the sheriff relays this along with the missing-person reports for Wilbur Whateley and Dr. Lori. Derek is actually in police custody for torturing Dr. Lori. The team drops its planned interview with her and moves on to finding Dean Lawson (Radford Horror 06). See Dr. Lori.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Derek Augustine: husband, a novelist who writes in the backyard barn.
  • Phoebe Augustine: daughter.
  • Andrew Howard: the agent who talks with her in the kitchen.

docs.text:
• Radford Horror 03 (named only)
  • Radford Horror 04 (mentioned)
  • Radford Horror 05
  • Radford Horror 06 (mentioned)

docs.title: The Mayor of Marblehead
docs.text:
The Mayor of Marblehead is the unnamed, bloated and near-translucent head of the town's Board of Selectmen, who also preaches the sermons in the Sons of Adam church in place of Amos Shaw.

Type NPC Aliases The mayor; the new priest; replacement preacher Affiliation Marblehead Board of Selectmen; Sons of Adam Status Alive (as of Summer Service 04); not seen afterwards First appearance Summer Service 03 (as the unnamed new priest) Played by Andre (game master)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The mayor's skin has a pallor that Andre describes as "opalescent translucency," and his body is swollen like a drowned man's. In the church he is the most advanced case of the town's glow that Andrew Howard sees (Summer Service 03). At the selectmen's meeting he, the chief of police and a few others are the most bloated people in the room (Summer Service 04). In manner he is polite but hostile. Andre tells the players that the council gives off the vibe of fanatics who are not necessarily insincere (Summer Service 04). He is never given a name.

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
The new priest. At the early service, Andrew finds that the priest from the previous visit is not in the pulpit. A stranger, glowing even more than the congregation, preaches against doubt and the secular world. At communion he studies Andrew and says "Blood of Christ." Andrew keeps the wine in his mouth; his Manipulate Someone roll fails with a 6, and the priest watches him leave, clearly not believing that he swallowed it (Summer Service 03).

Threats to the scientists. The EPA field journal found in the lighthouse basement records that the missing survey team was threatened by senior town officials, including the mayor, after they went before the Board of Selectmen. Kurt Larson admits that his first impulse is to kidnap and interrogate the mayor (Summer Service 03).

The selectmen's meeting. At the 6:30 p.m. meeting in the town hall, Andre reveals that the mayor was the replacement priest. Shaw, whose house looked as if someone had exploded in it, also attends and shows early bloating. The mayor asks how the investigation is going. Asked about the scientists, he says they came to the board just over a week earlier, mentioned that they were making little progress and might return to Washington for resources, and were not heard from again. He adds that the tone of their questioning, which accused the town of poisoning its fish with agricultural runoff, "was not very well received here." Asked what is behind the sicknesses, he answers "Satan": the second coming is imminent, and as "game day" nears the devil must work in the open. He calls the dead fish "a blight" curable only by prayer and "preparation for the eschaton" (Summer Service 04). See Second coming and eschaton.

He says that Jester "probably should have talked to some of us" before inviting the team, so that the board could have worked out the timeline, and gives Jester a look that makes him sink in his chair. When Kurt asks about the melted shoreline, the mayor suggests lightning or dynamite fishing, and tells the chief of police, "Jimmy," to look into it (Summer Service 04). The session ends with the team debating arrests and the mayor still in the room.

The mayor does not appear in Summer Service 05 or Summer Service 06. His fate is never stated.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Chief of Police: takes orders from the mayor at the meeting.
  • Jester: rebuked by the mayor for not warning the board.
  • Amos Shaw: the mayor preaches in his place; Shaw sits in the audience at the selectmen's meeting.

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

Andre (as the mayor): "As we get closer to, let's call it game day, you know, the devil is going to be forced to undertake more and more of his works out in the open." (Summer Service 04)

Quote

Andre (as the mayor): "Only through diligent prayer and preparation for the eschaton can we rid ourselves of this curse." (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Summer Service 03 never identifies the new preacher; Summer Service 04 reveals that he is the mayor.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Summer Service 03 (as the new priest)
  • Summer Service 04

docs.title: Minor characters: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: Minor characters of The Things in Appalachia: the one-scene locals, bystanders, handlers and passing voices who do not have pages of their own.

docs.title: Angie
docs.text: Angie is the youngest wife of Covenant prophet Elijah Ray. Primenthol Greengrass tells the team she is about twenty-five now, and that she married Elijah at twenty when he was thirty-eight. She is only ever mentioned, and Huell writes down the age gap with a skeptical face. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Apollo's Dry Cleaners Owner
docs.text: The owner of Apollo's Dry Cleaners is embarrassed that the latch on his storage-area double doors had been broken for months. He reimbursed Derek Edwards $100 when the Chewbacca costume Derek had left for cleaning vanished. Shown the dead man's photograph, he recognizes an out-of-town drifter who loitered nearby, sometimes talking on a walkie-talkie, and guesses he was staying at the Motel and Suites. He also offers to clean the blood off Andrew's Bigfoot T-shirt. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Ben
docs.text: Ben is a Spud Hut distribution-center worker who covered the shift of his missing co-worker Aaron Richters along with Edward Nick Sr. The plant needs a three-person crew to service its machinery, so the loss of one man strains the other two. Ben is only mentioned, at the Nicks' dinner table. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Bigfoot Hunters' Redhead
docs.text: A redheaded member of the Circle Chasers films the team's first meeting with the group on a camcorder, telling them to "pretend like I'm not here." Her filming makes Andrew uneasy. In Appalachia 02 a red-haired woman with a camcorder leads the group out of the woods, and Delilah is the one who plays back the footage. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Cab Driver
docs.text: A kindly Dahlonega cabbie picks up the bloody, pajama-clad Andrew at dawn after his sleepwalk and assumes "girl trouble." He lays a stained vomit towel on the seat, offers Neosporin and a first-aid kit from his trunk, and drives Andrew to the Smith Hotel for free. When Andrew claims to be an FBI agent, the driver answers with two skeptical thumbs up. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Carlos
docs.text: Carlos is the man who answers the phone when Kurt calls Derek Edwards, the photographer. He gives his name and says he is a friend of Mr. Edwards. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Cartwright (tegu)
docs.text: Cartwright is the very large, fat tegu lizard that climbs Huell's leg when he visits Donald McManley's reptile-filled cottage. McManley warns Huell, "Watch out, Cartwright might come for ya." The name is also the surname of the missing boy Gene Cartwright. The tegu shares the cottage with other lizards and tortoises. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Charlene
docs.text: Charlene is the big-haired, sheepish receptionist at the Spud Hut corporate plant. She first takes the team for reporters, then unlocks the door at the sheriff's urging because "a man exploded today." She explains the fishy smell as the new special taco sauce, recites the "never touched by human hands" guarantee, and leads the team through corridors of potato sacks to her boss, Jan Martense. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Charlie Briggs
docs.text: "Charlie" (Charles) Briggs is the credited photographer of the grainy Bigfoot photograph in the Dahlonega Times, rated by Kurt about "50th percentile" for fakery. No contact details are printed. Appalachia 06 names the photographer of the Gold Bug's Bigfoot photos as Derek Edwards, and the episodes never reconcile the two names. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Clover
docs.text: Clover is a shy young Covenant woman in Auraria, roughly Willow Greengrass's peer, who agrees to talk to Kurt as an equal even though she says the team should see Elijah Ray. She tells them Willow had a yeast infection, was sent by Elijah to scout peach orchards, and fought with her sister. She blames the river runoff from the Spud Hut plant for the camp's frequent infections, and she is unmoved by Kurt's women's-shelter cards ("We're getting a boiler"). (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Clyde Harvard
docs.text: Clyde Harvard is a complaining Spud Hut accountant who knew about Jan Martense's mine. When Kurt interviews Jan at the Omaha black site, Jan dismisses him ("Fuck him") and names him as the only other insider who might have leaked. His whereabouts are never given. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Cold-open Spud Hut Worker
docs.text: The unnamed Spud Hut employee of the second cold open wears a gray jumpsuit and safety glasses and steps outside for a smoke break. He follows baby-like sobbing into a rocky fissure, finds an ancient pickaxe in the sand and raises it before something perched in the crevice attacks him. His smoke break matches the disappearance of Aaron Richters, which Edward Nick Sr. reports later in the same episode. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Congressman Bradley
docs.text: Congressman Bradley chairs the House subcommittee investigating the Marblehead incident. He is polite but probing, pressing Kurt about the worms in the communion wine, the anthelmintic compound, a gap in testimony before the power plant attack, and a road stop off a highway. Big Bill has the last two questions struck on national-security grounds, and Bradley ends the session. See also the House Subcommittee. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Consolidated Gold Mine Tour Guide
docs.text: The old, bearded, suspendered guide of the Consolidated Gold Mine appears in the third cold open, showing visitors gold glints in the rock and warning that sealed shafts have already cost "a couple people." After the search for Frederick he turns out to be the mine's owner, and he doubts that anyone could mine in secret beneath his property, comparing it to "building the Batcave." Andrew's cult theory darkens the sheriff's face, not the guide's. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Cowboy-hat Man
docs.text: Huell glimpses a laughing man in a big cowboy hat and dark sunglasses entering the room next door to the team at the Smith Hotel, and finds him oddly familiar for a split second. He is one of the guests of the mysterious room 111 party. His identity is never established. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Curly-haired Blonde Woman
docs.text: This chatty woman in a bathrobe lives in the room next to the team. She sees a bloodied Andrew in the hall and asks "Are you okay, honey?" before a suited man steers her back inside. Her allegiance is never established. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Dahlonega Deputies
docs.text: The sheriff's deputies who staff the search of the Consolidated Gold Mine are uneasy about caves and greet the dishevelled team with "My lord, what happened?" Earlier, Sheriff Burke admits his deputies should have looked up into the trees where Gene Cartwright's shoe was hung. They are part of the Dahlonega Sheriff's Department. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Daniel Boys
docs.text: The Daniel boys are rowdy local hunters, called "river people" or "water people," blamed for the drunken hunting accidents Mrs. Nick and Frotter Comstock describe. Kurt and Zack's table treats "water people" as a running term for them. They are only ever mentioned. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Dr. Arthur
docs.text: Dr. Arthur is Andrew Howard's childhood family doctor and a fellow member of the cult in which Andrew was raised. He works from a home office full of beaded curtains and incense haze, calls Andrew "boy" and "son," and runs blood tests in-house. He explains that ritual healing is a higher power acting through the healer, with backlash: his own testicle retracted after he healed a broken leg. He recommends tampons for Andrew's nosebleeds and offers a meditation seminar in a couple of weeks. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Edward Nick Sr.
docs.text: Edward Nick Sr. is a Spud Hut distribution-center worker and the father of the child witness Edward Nick. He arrives at dinner in gray coveralls, exhausted, to report that his co-worker Aaron left on a smoke break and never returned. He recalls that the last federal agents in the area were ATF, after moonshiners, and that a man lost an arm in the plant's gears last year. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Eric
docs.text: Eric is the teenage counter worker at the Dahlonega McDonald's who fears the store will close and he will be fired. He once tried a trial shift at the Spud Hut plant ("too many frickin' potatoes") and recommends Stigley's Pub and the original Spud Hut to the team. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: FBI Translator
docs.text: An unnamed German translator is patched into the sheriff's station break-room speakerphone ("Guten Tag. I can begin whenever you're ready"). Through her, Frederick's mother tells the team what happened in the tunnels. She stays on the line to talk to the sheriff afterward. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Fed-looking Man and Forest Ranger Woman
docs.text: In the Smith Hotel parking lot, a van-life camper and a shiny black Ford truck have a fender bender. The truck's driver looks like a fed, in black sunglasses and suit with a clipboard, and the camper's driver wears a forest-ranger uniform. They swap insurance details while the team watches without approaching, and nothing further is learned about them. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Frederick's Mother
docs.text: The mother of the missing German boy Frederick is first glimpsed in the cold open with a disposable wind-up camera at the front of the Consolidated Gold Mine tour. Later she screams in tears when the team produces her son's shoe. Interviewed by speakerphone, she says Frederick was playing his video game in the "American gold tunnels," that she heard a clatter but no scream, and that he was gone when she turned the corner. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Gary Oldman and Patti Smith
docs.text: Gary Oldman, who is billed to talk about Dracula, and musical guest Patti Smith are the other announced guests on the night the Biz appears on Late Night with David Letterman. Oldman's cancellation opens the slot for the Biz, who is sweating through his makeup. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Gold Bug Woman
docs.text: An older, pinched newspaper employee at the Gold Bug produces a dusty Rolodex and identifies the photographer of the Bigfoot photos as Derek, with a bigoted remark about him that Andrew snaps back at. She lets Kurt phone Derek Edwards from her desk. The paper itself is described under Gold Bug. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Hotel Breakfast Employee
docs.text: A kid at the hotel's continental breakfast explains "pig tips" ("mostly the front end") among the "wonderful rainbow of pork products." Kurt takes three. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Investigator
docs.text: A chain-smoking man sits in his car at the Spud Hut corporate entrance, investigating the company. Kurt tells him in confidence that the wrecked truck held only dirt and that there has been tunnel activity, and the man guesses "Gold mining?" He salutes, mutters "What kind of Scooby-Doo-ass bullshit is going on in this town?", and warns that the Spud Hut executive is high-strung. It is never established whether he is the auditor of Appalachia 06. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Jan's Bodyguards
docs.text: Two unnamed bodyguards are the last members of the five-person ring behind the gold mining, alongside Jan Martense, the handler Clive and the mercenary who smelted the gold. They are never seen. Their fate is not stated. See Jan's Conspiracy. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Jeff "Apple" Appleby
docs.text: Jeff Appleby, nicknamed Apple, is an old Washington, D.C. drinking buddy and lawyer of the Biz, now newly appointed a federal judge. He pages the Biz and invites him to Las Vegas to celebrate. The Biz recalls talking him down from a Vegas rooftop and stopping him from vomiting off a casino. Appleby says Spud Hut's shrimp scampi once gave him food poisoning. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Jenny Maxine
