docs.text: "Jenny Maxine" is the name, with several X's, on the Motel and Suites register for a scatological porn shoot with "gentleman friends." The clerk has barred her from returning and warns the team not to open the green garbage bag of her linens. She is never seen. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Keith
docs.text: At the end of Huell's visit, McManley says, "I should call Keith, too." Keith is never explained. In McManley's bathroom Huell notices a second toothbrush and razor in a cabinet, covered in a fine layer of dust. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: KGB Sweepstakes Contact
docs.text: The old-sounding voice on the "Canada maple syrup sweepstakes line" is the Biz's handler. He offers the Biz $10,000 and information on the "Massachusetts matter" in exchange for the favor of planting a camera in room 111. Andre voices him as an old man who calls the Biz "sweetie". See KGB. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Kurt's CIA Boss
docs.text: A silent figure in a black suit and a tie covered in nautilus images sits at Kurt's House subcommittee testimony beside Big Bill. He is the man who gave Kurt the "alligator spiel." (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Marlene
docs.text: Marlene is Jan Martense's secretary. In the ninth episode's cold open she warns that reporters are waiting, and Jan snaps "Not now, Marlene" before slipping out the back. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Matthew Napolitano
docs.text: Matthew Napolitano is an invented Italian hitman on the FBI's most-wanted list. Dante invokes him as a joke when Edward Nick's drawing of a crouching hairy figure is judged "dead accurate." He never appears in the story. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: McManley's Interns
docs.text: McManley's interns are three teenagers who are trained to sort, bag and dust evidence in his RV lab. They ride a moped back to the RV after going through the dead drifter's trash, and later sweat through the Biz's drunken mock interrogation ("Which one of you was looking at Bill Clinton with a telescope?"). In the Walkers in Skin arc two interns are with McManley in the ambushed Suburban, one with a leg wound. See also McManley's RV and Donald McManley. (Appalachia 04, Appalachia 06, Appalachia 07, Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Mr. Mitles
docs.text: Mr. Mitles is the local Presbyterian preacher, of average size with a good bass preaching voice and one leg. Huell raises him with Mrs. Nick as a Bigfoot suspect and rules him out: "He only got the one leg." His name is of uncertain spelling. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Omaha Desk Guard
docs.text: The unnamed desk guard at CIA black site Omaha clears Kurt for four hours after he hands over a pack of ordinary cigarettes. Kurt later keeps a promise to Jan Martense by asking the guard for anti-suicide playing cards. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: River
docs.text: River is Willow Greengrass's close friend, a middle-aged Covenant woman with long dark hair who works the stills. She says Willow was upset because her sister kept pressing her to leave, that they had a big fight a couple of days before the disappearance, and that Elijah Ray discourages contact with family. She does not believe the sister is a murderer. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Room 111 Booker
docs.text: The man who booked room 111 of the Smith Hotel is never seen. The desk clerk describes him as armed, rude, Midwestern and military-looking, with short hair, and says he bribed the clerk $100 for silence. When the Biz hears the description he says, "That is him." See Room 111. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Sarah Nick
docs.text: Sarah Nick (called Mrs. Nick) is Edward Nick's mother, a welcoming, slightly anxious woman with long curly hair. She lets the team in after Kurt says "We're with the Federales," offers tuna green bean casserole, and points them to the bent tree where Gene was last seen. She doubts a bear was responsible and calls the Covenant "heebie-jeebies." (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Spud Hut Corporate Auditor
docs.text: A financial auditor from Spud Hut Corporate has been following the team. When Kurt calls him, he meets them at the Spud Hut for lunch and pays, remarking that the case is "more cloak-and-dagger than I'm accustomed to." He does not recognize the dead drifter and says he is not on the employee list. It is never established whether he is the same man as the investigator of Appalachia 08. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Spud Hut Truck Driver
docs.text: The heavyset driver of the seventh cold open eats a congealing hamburger to "Radar Love," with a mustard-stained photo of a blonde on his dash. Something enters through the rear window; he reaches for the Glock under his seat and misses. At the crash site the cab holds blood on every surface, eight gunshots and no body. He is the victim of the Thing That Attacked the Spud Hut Truck. (Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Stacy
docs.text: Stacy is the phone worker at the Spud Hut Regional Distribution Center who jokes about "hunting season." She verifies Andrew's badge by phoning the FBI (about eight minutes), then reports that Aaron Richters did not clock out the day before and has about nine unexcused absences in two years. She offers to connect him to Jan. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Stony Covenant Man
docs.text: At the Auraria community center, Kurt and Huell needle a stony young Covenant man with talk of cheeseburgers and stuffed-crust pizza until he storms off, chanting Latin and calling it "devil talk." See The Covenant. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: String Bean
docs.text: String Bean is the absent sheriff's deputy, away with family troubles, whose spare uniform from the trunk of the sheriff's car becomes Andrew's disguise at Spud Hut Corporate. Andrew recites his exact measurements while changing behind the car. The uniform is wrecked in the fight beneath the plant. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Suited Man with Military Haircut
docs.text: In the Smith Hotel hall, a suited man with a military haircut whispers to the bathrobed woman, steers her into the next-door room and glares at Andrew. He is one of the "scary guys" the desk clerk mentions, and it is never established whether he is the man who booked room 111. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Unnamed Homeless Man
docs.text: At the Biz's old park bench, a homeless man retrieves the KGB dead-drop bag for about $50, returning in fifteen minutes with it taped and unopened. He is honest about wanting to open it, propositions the Biz ("I won't kiss you, but I'm game"), and says he will spend the money on heroin. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Walter Sellers
docs.text: Walter Sellers is a regional-level bodybuilder and football player whom Sheriff Burke names as the strongest man in town: "ain't too bright, but strong as hell." The team never meets him. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Minor characters: Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable (non-canon one-shot)
docs.text:
Non-canon

These characters appear only in Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, a non-canon one-shot presented as an in-universe anime OVA. Nothing here is part of the main campaign's continuity.

Minor characters of the one-shot who do not have their own pages, in alphabetical order. For the principal cast, see Mirabeth, Derk, Colonel Sparago, Ovain, Delta, Miguel and Addison.

docs.title: Addison's Son
docs.text: The miserable teenage son of the exhausted Addison, still working on a bad flag for the children's event while his mother hovers and critiques every line. Derk compliments the flag and then cheerfully tells him that Ovain is coming to kill the president. The boy hyperventilates, then sobs quietly, and runs to his mother crying, "Mommy, I don't wanna get killed with the president." He leaves with her soon after. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Anna
docs.text: Mirabeth's daughter, who wanted to be a ballerina and refused the family hero "legacy." The disagreement caused a big fight, and Mirabeth was thrown out of Anna's ninth birthday party. Anna is mentioned only in Mirabeth's backstory and never appears. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Derk's Father
docs.text: An alien royal who left the five-year-old Derk on a high-gravity planet for what he intended as a few months. It turned out to be fourteen years, during which Derk survived on scorpions. Introducing Derk, Dante joked that his father might have died in a war or gone to pick up cigarettes. The father never appears, and Derk's mother is said to have died when he was little ("I think"). (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Library Staff
docs.text: The staff of the capital's Public Library. They ask Derk to use his "inside voice" and sit him in the children's room among the toddlers. After he eats nearly half the snack table, they call child services and Animal Control about a "shaved baboon." The detective who later questions Mirabeth says the Animal Control call ended in a riot. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Mirabeth's Nemesis
docs.text: A slightly older rival from before Mirabeth became a mentor, now living in a retirement home. She is mentioned in Mirabeth's backstory and never seen. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Moraniel
docs.text: Spokesman of the Alien Faction at the safety briefing. When Derk approaches, Moraniel introduces himself, asks Derk what he is, concludes he is a lost child and shoos him back toward his "state appointed" guardian, Mirabeth. As Derk leaves, he overhears the group say that they need standards on who counts as an alien and that Derk looks like a stepped-on Gandekian. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Roped-Area Guards
docs.text: Guards posted at the roped-off marble floor of the Presidential Event Hall. One says he has heard nothing about the heroes, and the other suggests calling for confirmation, but both freeze when Mirabeth uses Symbol of Authority and says the president wants "inconspicuous" heroes. One later asks Derk to show his kung fu, hands him a quarter, and wishes him "Godspeed" after Derk bends it. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Sarah
docs.text: A kind girl of about fourteen at the pre-event social. She tells Derk that the bully is a jerk, introduces herself, and offers to show him her own flag. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The Bully
docs.text: A teenager at the social who tells Derk he looks "super fucked up," insults his intelligence and stomps off after calling him weird. Derk misses the point of the insult, and Sarah befriends him instead. The bully is never named. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The Detective
docs.text: A grizzled old detective who interviews Mirabeth during the long debriefing after the Ovain fight. He asks how she got Derk into the flag competition and whether she had anything to do with the Animal Control call to the library, and he tells her that the call ended in a riot. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The Monk
docs.text: An older, heavyset woman martial-arts monk, deputized alongside the Secret Service on the morning of the presidential event. She recognizes Mirabeth and is on mostly unfriendly terms with her, though she does not hate her. After Mirabeth rolls a 12 on Pierce the Mask, the monk's shoulders slump, and she lets Mirabeth's presence pass and tells the other monks. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The Wand Guard
docs.text: A chubby, older, profusely sweating security guard at the door of the event hall. He scans Derk with the superhuman-and-metal wand, getting a "tink, tank" off his head, and forgets to scan Mirabeth. Inside, she sweet-talks him into lending her the wand, which she uses to convince the roped-area guards. He is left standing nervously ("It's my job, man"), and Colonel Sparago later says that Mirabeth used "sexual wiles" on a man who has been struggling lately. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Weasel-Man Trainer and Lizard-Man Protege
docs.text: An elderly weasel-man trainer and his enormous lizard-man protege, glimpsed in the crowd at the safety briefing. Mirabeth has been handing her business cards to other trainers' fighters, and the trainer puts his body between her and the protege and shuffles him into the tent. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Wisukonshin McDonald's Staff
docs.text: The workers at a McDonald's in Wisukonshin, where the lost Derk ends up. Derk goes in to ask where he is, and they tell him and give him a package of nuts because he looks so sad. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Minor characters: Radford (The Radford Horror and The Radford Horrors)
docs.text: This page lists the minor and offscreen characters of the two Radford arcs, from clerks and deputies to people who are only ever mentioned.

docs.title: Agent Cooper
docs.text: Agent Cooper is an FBI agent working at the barbershop headquarters when the team is reassigned. He refuses to take the boxes of files stacked in the bathroom, insisting that Records "doesn't want" them, which leaves Andrew to clear them out himself. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: Airport security agents
docs.text: Unnamed agents at the airport flag Kurt's spear gun because the weapons-transport paperwork was lost and he has no FBI badge. After Kurt shows the Vietnam spear scar in his shoulder, one agent pinches the bridge of his nose and lets the gun through, while another swabs Andrew's blood powder. The airport is in chaos from a strike, and the team cannot find its colleagues to vouch for it. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Andrew's mother
docs.text: Andrew's mother is a devout single mother who has been staying with him in Washington for about a month. She pushes church socials and insists on visiting the office, and Andrew sleeps on the pullout couch while she stays. She is never seen onscreen. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Apartment office staff
docs.text: The manager, a maintenance man and two or three secretaries run the office of the Biz's apartment building. When Andrew asks about the Biz they ask "Is he dead?", and they appear to be running a betting pool on it; half of them look disappointed when the answer is no. They hand Andrew the emergency key without asking for ID. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Bryson Garland
docs.text: Bryson is the son of Toby Garland and made the volcano at the school science fair. He is mentioned only; Kurtis privately wonders whether the boy has a learning disability. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Campground teen
docs.text: A teenager manning the gate of the Sportsman RV Campground lets the team in politely. He mentions in passing that the local cops are behind on their berth fees. (Radford Horrors 02) See also the Sportsman RV Campground.

docs.title: Captured stranger
docs.text: One of the poncho-wearing searchers in the woods around the old town, he is kicked and sprayed by Andrew's mace and suffers a violent seizure. The team ties him up and takes his shadow poncho and flashlight. When they return along the trail it "ended", and he is gone, so his fate is never learned. (Radford Horror 08) See Shadow poncho and Flashlight weapon.

docs.title: Cold-open teenager
docs.text: An unidentified teenager is shown in a dark yard burying three Ziploc bags of cash in the cold open of Radford Horror 06. The episode never names him. Radford Horror 07 identifies him as Dean Lawson: the agents dig the cash up in the yard of the Lawson cabin and find his heroin under a bedroom floorboard. (Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07) See also Dean Lawson's heroin and cash.

docs.title: Derek (Phoebe's ex)
docs.text: Derek is Phoebe's boyfriend of about a year, who broke up with her amicably a year before the story. He is mentioned only and is a different person from the novelist Derek Augustine, Phoebe's father. (Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: Dog owners
docs.text: A suburban family whose dog was taken from the backyard around 3 a.m. They panic when the Biz knocks on their door, and their yard becomes the pickup site for the white powder. (Radford Horror 04) See Radford's missing dogs.

docs.title: Donna Greensby
docs.text: Donna Greensby is one of six missing people on the posters Molly gives the team, with a phone number for the lawyers who threaten anyone who asks questions. She is never met. (Radford Horrors 02) See Molly Underhill.

docs.title: Donner
docs.text: Donner is an FBI colleague whom Andrew's boss says has been working closely with him on his current cases and will handle the transition when the task force is reassigned. He is only named. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: Dr. Lori's receptionist
docs.text: The receptionist at Dr. Lori's office is friendly and offers lemon candies, mentions her fifteen-year-old, and pages the doctor when Kurt arrives with his cover story and the names of the missing. When Huell returns later, she turns firm: she blocks him from the window and locks the door behind him. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03) See Dr. Lawrence Lori.

docs.title: Ed McCready
docs.text: Ed is the father of Matt McCready and lives with him at the tourist ski lodge in the mountains. In the first episode the Luckys and Sheriff Roosevelt point the team toward the lodge, but Ed is not yet met. (Radford Horror 01) See Alpine Lodge.

docs.title: Elderly witness
docs.text: An elderly neighbor of the Augustine house saw Phoebe flee into the woods. Her account helps the team understand where Phoebe went. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Elizabeth Murkowski
docs.text: Elizabeth Murkowski is another of the six missing people on the posters Molly hands over. Nothing else is learned about her. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: FBI counsel
docs.text: Unnamed FBI lawyers put Webster through a four-hour debrief in the hallway over the fence incident with the Safe Environment Fund. (Radford Horrors 03) See Bivens lawsuit and Daniel Webster.

docs.title: FBI courier
docs.text: An unnamed courier delivers the "Radford, Virginia" case folder in the first episode and checks Andrew's ID. He returns in Radford Horror 08 with the crate holding the alien plush and the Marblehead case file, joking about "the alien guys" while Kurt winks that "there are aliens". A courier also figures in the Roulet Estate arc, where Big Bill hands Andrew an envelope from an FBI courier. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 08, Roulet Estate 01) See OJ the stuffed alien.

docs.title: Ferry Lodge clerk (1992)
docs.text: The woman at the Ferry Lodge desk apologizes that an oral surgeons' convention has booked the whole lodge, offers a single bed, and sends the team to the Pay n' Stay. (Radford Horror 01) See Pay n' Stay.

docs.title: Ferry Lodge desk clerk (1993)
docs.text: Under the lodge's new management, the desk clerk pitches the "Alpine Relaxation Package" and flinches at the word "FBI". When IRS agents raid the lodge she shreds documents and starts a fire; Andrew catches her and she is handcuffed and interrogated by four IRS agents. Kurt admires her decisiveness and jokes that he would recruit her. (Radford Horrors 02) See Ferry Lodge management.

docs.title: Flight attendant
docs.text: A flight attendant chews out Huell over the lavatory smoke alarm, reminding him that "there was a law". (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Floyd Clark
docs.text: Floyd Clark is the FBI deputy director. In The Summer Service, Andre lays out the chain of command: Andrew reports to Big Bill, and Nelson reports to Clark, who reports to Bush Sr. In The Roulet Estate, Andre says rumors have Clark replacing the director later that year. He is never seen. (Summer Service 03, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Harvey Milk's owner
docs.text: An old woman on Berkeley Street is the repeat complainer in the sheriff's missing-dog folder, regularly reporting that her Doberman, Harvey Milk, has vanished. She is offscreen. (Radford Horror 02) See Radford's missing dogs.

docs.title: Hospital nurse
docs.text: At the Roanoke mental hospital, an unnamed nurse at the front desk warns the team of "no touching", signs them in and escorts them out. She is stunned when Wilbur wakes. (Radford Horrors 04) See Wilbur Whateley.

docs.title: Huell's narcotics colleagues
docs.text: Huell's former coworkers in the narcotics unit send a stuffed alien to the office with an insulting note. The plush becomes the mascot OJ the stuffed alien. (Radford Horror 08) See Huell Kendrick.

docs.title: Huyen
docs.text: Huyen is Kurtis's wife, said to be a former Viet Cong, who home-schools their children and is a "wonderful cook". She is mentioned in the Radford Horror episodes and again in Radford Horrors 01, but never appears. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 08, Radford Horrors 01) See Kurt Larson.

docs.title: Laura Nichols
docs.text: Laura Nichols is a classmate and friend of Amanda Lucky who fought with Phoebe Augustine. The team never interviews her. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 05) See Amanda Lucky and Phoebe Augustine.

docs.title: Letterman-jacket teen
docs.text: A muscular high schooler in a letterman jacket speaks for the pair at the armed camp in the clearing, claiming that they are simply camping. (Radford Horror 03) See Uncle Trevor and Armed group in the woods.

docs.title: Luke Dunhill
docs.text: Luke Dunhill appears on one of Molly's six missing-person posters. Nothing more is learned about him. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Man in the suit
docs.text: An unidentified smoker examines the ash pile left by the exploded assailant in the Radford Horror 07 cold open, leading soldiers and men in volcanologist-style suits. He seems to lead the cleanup crew, but the episode does not say so. (Radford Horror 07) See Agent Murphy.

docs.title: Mary
docs.text: Mary is Tyler's mother and a trailer neighbor of the Luckys. Sheriff Roosevelt names her once; she is reluctant to wake her son ("he had a dream") and provides Tang. (Radford Horror 01) See Tyler and Tyler's trailer.

docs.title: Masked kidnapper
docs.text: A man in a black balaclava is seen in the Radford Horrors 03 cold open carrying the tased Elizabeth George. He is never identified, but he may belong to the gray van crew. (Radford Horrors 03) See Elizabeth George.

docs.title: Meg Gunderson
docs.text: Meg Gunderson is a nosy, gossipy neighbor of the Whateleys who makes lunch for the team and suspects murder. She blames Abe's drug use, and reveals the spacesuit robbery of the Radio Shack as well as Abe's past with Amanda. (Radford Horror 02) See Radio Shack spacesuit robbery and Abelforth Whateley.

docs.title: Melanie Colt
docs.text: Melanie Colt is the twin sister of Kurtis's daughter Peggy. She is mentioned only. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Mike Roundhauer
docs.text: Mike Roundhauer is another of the six people on Molly's missing posters, which the lawyers' number is attached to. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Monica Appleton
docs.text: Monica Appleton appears on one of Molly's missing posters, alongside Phoebe Augustine. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Officer Aina
docs.text: Officer Aina (the name is of uncertain spelling) is a highway patrol dispatcher who takes Howard's report ("FBI?"), jokes about the good binoculars, and later pages the team about the motel arrest. (Radford Horror 06) See Highway Patrol and state police.

docs.title: Pay n' Stay teenage staffer
docs.text: A girl in hip waders and rubber gloves hauls stained laundry at the Pay n' Stay during the rodent crisis. She is vaccinated, says the health department hung up on her, and mutters "I hate it here... I am getting that fucking horse." She may be Charm, the clerk from the previous visit, but she is not named. (Radford Horrors 04) See Billy Thornton.

docs.title: Peggy Browning
docs.text: Peggy Browning is Kurtis's nine-year-old daughter. She wins gold at the school science fair with a projectile-stabilization project, comparing a potato against ballistics gel with spin-stabilized, fin-stabilized and smoothbore versions and a failed gyroscopic attempt. (Radford Horrors 01) See Kurt Larson.

docs.title: Ponytailed man
docs.text: A long-haired man who moves "like a poser" leads or accompanies the gray van crew on the diner tape of the Pinball Emporium raid. He is never named. (Radford Horrors 04) See Diner security tape and Gray van crew.

docs.title: Radford ER doctor
docs.text: The emergency room doctor treats the team repeatedly across both arcs. In Radford Horror 08 he is exasperated at having treated them four times in three days; he offers ice chips and real coffee, lectures about fiber, and personally brings the Biz kale salads with chopped boiled egg. In Radford Horrors he greets them with "Not again. Not you guys.", identifies rabies from the impaled mouse and runs the vaccine series, giving Kurt a field kit. He is never named. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 08, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03) See Radford ER.

docs.title: Ralphie
docs.text: Ralphie is Kurt's supply contact, who can deliver developing gear from a stash. He is offstage. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Roanoke Airport attendant
docs.text: An attendant with a "white-man afro" and red sunglasses sends the party to Freak and buzzes them in. (Radford Horror 07) See Freak.

docs.title: Russian officer
docs.text: An unnamed officer of higher rank than the Biz's guard delivers Yeltsin's summons and a perfectly fitted suit, speaking unaccented English and side-eyeing the guard. (Radford Horrors 01) See Boris Yeltsin and Russian-style suit.

docs.title: Russian soldier donor
docs.text: A shirtless, half-conscious soldier is connected by tubes to the crash survivor. He is unnamed and his fate is unknown. (Radford Horrors 04) See Crash survivor.

docs.title: Safe Environment Fund lawyers
docs.text: Several lawyers film the team's trespass at the fenced site and repeatedly ask whether the agents have a warrant. They refuse to comment on bleach, and one calls Webster "Officer Webster". (Radford Horrors 02) See Safe Environment Fund.

docs.title: Safe Environment Fund security guards
docs.text: At least three armed guards on ATVs patrol the fenced site, with unarmed medics and escorts arriving later. One tases Webster, and another is shot in the leg by Andrew and carried off. A radio voice from the property owner demands that the team leave, then later orders the guards to stand down. (Radford Horrors 02) See Safe Environment Fund fenced site.

docs.title: Samson
docs.text: Samson is a part-time deputy at the highway scene, whom Molly tells the team to look for. He says he has not done a shift in a while and lost his badge, and that it has been quiet "except for the dogs". (Radford Horror 05) See Highway crime scene.

docs.title: Sarah Lucky
docs.text: Sarah Lucky is Amanda Lucky's distraught Catholic mother, who waits by the phone with her husband Liam. The household is full of shrines and a six-foot crucifixion carving. They blame Matt McCready and did not know the diary was gutted. (Radford Horror 01) See Lucky house.

docs.title: Tasing security guard
docs.text: The Safe Environment Fund guard who tased Webster is already fired by the time the team learns of him. Hearing impaired, he claims he did not believe the FBI would carry a spear gun, and the Bureau may press charges. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03) See Kurt's spear gun.

docs.title: The Biz's first captors
docs.text: The men who first held the Biz in Russia kicked him, kept him with a frozen latrine bucket and asked him about Bill Clinton. They are "long gone" by the time Yeltsin's people take over. (Radford Horrors 01) See Dick Baxter and Bill Clinton.

docs.title: The colonel
docs.text: The colonel wakes the Biz and orders him ready in five minutes. He often travels with the Russian president, though the Biz's guard does not know his name. (Radford Horrors 03) See Biz's guards.

docs.title: The priest
docs.text: The priest at the Radford church gives the closing sermon at the community meeting about the curfew. Audience members ask about a serial killer and about dogs, and one mutters "God damn perverts." (Radford Horror 05) See Curfew and community meeting.

docs.title: Toby
docs.text: Toby is a hostile FBI coworker of the Biz who glares at him and squeezes a stress ball. He should not be confused with Toby Garland. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: Toby Garland
docs.text: Toby Garland is a chatty PTA dad and the owner of Garland Air Conditioning Repair. He meets Kurtis at the science fair, asks about his job and about keeping up family ties, and is the father of Bryson. (Radford Horrors 01) See Garland Air Conditioning Repair.

docs.title: Todd (FBI)
docs.text: Todd is an FBI acquaintance of Kurtis who takes him to the men's room ("Come piss with me") and tells him that Perot has fired Director Sessions. He does not know who the replacement is. (Radford Horrors 01) See Ross Perot and William Sessions.

docs.title: Todd (Kurt's late colleague)
docs.text: A different Todd was Kurt's colleague who "used to buy" landmines and died in a car accident. He is mentioned only and is not the FBI Todd of 1993. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: Uncle Trevor
docs.text: Uncle Trevor is a tall, thin man in his late thirties or early forties in an oversized coat, introduced by the teen as his uncle although the two look nothing alike. He seems "methy" and jumpy, and twice reaches into his coat before stopping himself. (Radford Horror 03) See Letterman-jacket teen.

docs.title: Unnamed female deputy
docs.text: A Southern-sounding deputy ("Man, y'all just don't sleep good, do ya?") offers coffee, photographs the footprints at the Whateley house and says she gets "a bad vibe" off Dr. Lori. The episode does not say whether she is Molly Underhill. (Radford Horror 06) See Whateley house.

docs.title: William Sessions
docs.text: William Sessions is the FBI Director whom Perot fires after a poor meeting; he stood by the Radford reports and had confirmed the "giant bug" report to Perot before being dismissed. He is never seen. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02) See Ross Perot.

docs.title: Minor characters: The Roulet Estate
docs.text: Minor characters of The Roulet Estate, in alphabetical order. The principal figures of the arc have their own pages: Margaret Roulet, Mr. Roulet, The Finnish Hare Krishna Monk, Officer Todd and Diane.

docs.title: Andrew's Doctor
docs.text: The physician who treats Andrew Howard after the task force is disbanded. In Roulet Estate 01 Andrew has not yet had a checkup since Utah and plans to visit his physician, who is "out in California," when he goes home. In the epilogue he spends a week at home with his doctor and church officials, who tell him his powers can be unpredictable in a crisis and promise tests. They X-ray him but never show him the films or any paperwork, and Andrew realizes for the first time that they do not know what they are talking about and that he is the "special horse," the test case. The doctor then insists on mailing him human blood every week, disguised as frozen orange juice in dry ice. It is never established whether this is the same California physician mentioned in Roulet Estate 01. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 03) See also Frozen Blood Shipments.

docs.title: Bruce
docs.text: The ancient, senile owner of the clown mansion, the neighboring Victorian that the agents reach after a long cold walk. When the Biz knocks, Bruce answers only "We don't want any." The Biz uses his playbook ability to ask what will convince the target, learns that the old man is stuck in a rhythm and must be jolted out of it, and flashes his badge very forcefully. Bruce lets the agents in and wanders backward away from them. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Businessman Hostage
docs.text: A man in a suit among the hostages at the Brooks pharmacy. The gunman lets him out twice. The first time he runs out with a brick-sized cellular phone, warns that nobody is to go behind the building, gives the number 401-998-3147 and goes back inside. The second time he holds up a sheet of paper with the number written on it, after Andrew Howard has stalled by pretending he dialed a wrong number. (Roulet Estate 03) See also Brick Cellphone.

docs.title: Chubby Local Police Officer
docs.text: A local officer in a "little police outfit" who is supposed to be on holiday break when he arrives at the Roulet house in response to a report of bodies. He goes to the basement, confirms "Yep, that's two corpses," says he will call the medical examiner and take statements, and asks for a description of the thief for an all-points bulletin on the agents' stolen car. Andrew describes a bald figure, and when he later blurts out that the figure had nipples, a passing officer gives him a very slow thumbs-up. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Clown Mansion Woman
docs.text: A much younger woman at the clown mansion, whom the agents take to be Bruce's wife or daughter. She wears a silk bathrobe printed entirely with clowns and says the agents look like they are all freezing. She shows them to the kitchen phone, which Andrew uses to try Big Bill and the Biz uses to report the double homicide to the FBI. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Elevator Kid
docs.text: A child in a yellow shirt with a mustard stain who rides the elevator of Huell Kendrick's apartment building all day. He asks what happened to Huell's foot. Huell first answers "Got shot by an alien," then agrees it was diabetes, and the kid remarks that you can lose a foot to diabetes. He pushes all the buttons as Huell leaves. (Roulet Estate 03) See also Huell's Apartment Building.

docs.title: FBI DC Operator
docs.text: The polite operator who answers when the Biz phones the FBI's Washington office from the clown mansion as Special Agent Dick Baxter. She finds him in the system and logs a double homicide at 118 Benefit Street, Exeter, Rhode Island, with shots fired by "entities unknown" and a stolen vehicle. She is not familiar with the task force, but promises a local unit and backup, and warns that snowstorms may delay help by a couple of hours. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: FSB Officer
docs.text: A silent escort who accompanies the Biz on his first-class flight from Vorkuta to Moscow. The Biz is handcuffed beside him, and the officer eats the Biz's steak on the plane but lets him keep the rest of the meal. He later stares at the Biz in the room in the former Soviet Parliament building. (Roulet Estate 03) See also Russian Government / FSB.

docs.title: Markeith
docs.text: An employee of the Brooks pharmacy who keeps the back service entrance locked, according to a police officer at the scene. He never appears; the locked door matters because Kurt Larson has to pick the lock at the back of the building. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Mrs. McGann
docs.text: Huell Kendrick's unfriendly neighbor. In March 1993 she hauls his wheelchair up the steps to the elevator landing after he guilts her into it. When Huell asks after her husband she answers, "You know, still dead." (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Pharmacist and Hostages
docs.text: The 20 to 30 people held inside the Brooks pharmacy by the masked gunman. The store has been ransacked, and the pharmacist later tells police that the gunman was searching the back for beta blockers and could not find the supply. One hostage is left with a gut wound beside the front counter, and the pool of blood triggers Andrew's craving. Another hostage cowers behind the front checkout counter, and his gaze gives Kurt Larson a fix on the gunman's position. (Roulet Estate 03) See also Beta Blockers.

docs.title: Ranasinghe Premadasa
docs.text: The prime minister of Sri Lanka. In the April 1993 epilogue Kurt Larson says that he was dispatched to Sri Lanka to fight the LTTE and "successfully, if not prevented, then at least postponed" Premadasa's assassination, before being called back after Waco to help train American agencies. Premadasa never appears. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Salvation Army Carolers
docs.text: Teenage carolers who arrive at the task force office on Christmas Eve 1992 collecting for the Salvation Army. Huell Kendrick donates the rest of his cigarettes and the Biz donates a gold nugget. The kids whisper about whether the nugget is real, sing an encore of "Silent Night" and light up the cigarettes as they leave. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Senior Russian Officer
docs.text: A mustached officer with steel eyes and a red, runny nose who looks through the slot of the Biz's cell at Vorkuta. The Biz greets him in polite Russian, and the officer, repulsed, orders a guard to "get this man on a plane." (Roulet Estate 03) See also Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp.

docs.title: Taxi Dispatcher and Driver
docs.text: The dispatcher quotes a three-hour wait when Kurt Larson orders a taxi to Pawtucket for the monk, using his own money. When the cab arrives, Kurt points to it, gives the Finnish Hare Krishna monk a wad of bills and the team's card, and tells the driver to get him where he is going. The monk shouts something incomprehensible out the window as he leaves. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: The Two Cowardly Cops
docs.text: Two officers who crouch behind a squad car at the Brooks pharmacy, gesturing frantically, and then will not cross the parking lot to help. When asked, they give big thumbs-ups instead. Huell Kendrick vows to get them fired. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Unnamed NSA Agent
docs.text: The owner of the Herman Miller chair that Kurt Larson steals as Diane's Secret Santa gift. The chair is stamped "Property of the National Security Agency," and Kurt calls its owner "a weenus." Diane says she will burn her old chair "for the bugs." (Roulet Estate 01) See also NSA and Herman Miller NSA Chair.

docs.title: Vorkuta Guards
docs.text: The jailers of the Biz at Vorkuta, including "the kickiest" guard, who handles him roughly, and a less kicky guard with whom the Biz is on semi-good terms, who is absent in the scenes shown. The beatings have stopped about two weeks before the epilogue scene, and the Biz is left with bread pushed through a slot. (Roulet Estate 03) See also Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp.

docs.title: William S. Sessions
docs.text: The FBI Director in 1993. Andrew Howard's colleagues at the Bureau run betting pools on whether he is blackmailing Sessions or having sex with him, since he is the highest-ranking person not yet replaced. Rumor has it that Floyd Clark (of uncertain spelling) will replace Sessions later that year, which is when the pools are expected to resolve. (Roulet Estate 03) See also FBI.

docs.title: Minor characters: The Summer Service
docs.text: These are the minor and background characters of the Marblehead case, from the families on the previous team's contact list to the sailors in the finale's cold open. Bigger roles such as Ma Gramoire, Jester and Esteban have their own pages.

docs.title: Big Bill's secretary
docs.text: An unnamed male secretary at FBI headquarters who is never seen. When Kurt phones Big Bill from Ma Gramoire's kitchen, he is transferred to the secretary, who agrees to put in a request for Ma Gramoire's son to join the Guard deployment, which cheers the old woman up. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Big Bill's wife
docs.text: Heard rather than seen in the finale's cold open. A phone rings in a dark bedroom, Big Bill answers under the blanket, and when his wife asks what they want in the middle of the night he sighs and says he has to go into work: "The Protestants are trying to kill my detectives." (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Carter's courier
docs.text: A friendly driver of a military-surplus armored truck who delivers the heavy crate Kurt ordered from his old contact Carter. He says Carter sends his love, that this is the last favor, and that afterward they are even. On his way out he says he is going to get sushi, and Kurt warns him not to eat anything in town. Andre then quips that sushi was not popular in 1992 and tells the table to pretend he said crab legs. The crate holds the Davy Crockett. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Cartwright family
docs.text: One of the families on the previous team's contact list, along with Ma Gramoire, Lena Scott and O'Donnell. Andre reads out the list in Summer Service 01 and Dante calls Lena Scott first. The team never interviews the Cartwrights. The surname recurs in the Things in Appalachia with Gene Cartwright. (Summer Service 01; Appalachia 02)

docs.title: College researcher
docs.text: A young woman who appears only in the unrecorded Summer Service 02. She had found a dead body under the sunken wreck, and she took the team down to it in an experimental submarine. This is known only from the recap in Summer Service 03, which also says the team suspected the body belonged to one of the missing EPA researchers. See The stealth wreck and the experimental submarine. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Dr. Khan
docs.text: The doctor at the Radford ER who phones Andrew in Summer Service 01 to say that the lab mixed up his clotting-disorder blood samples after his nosebleed and that he has discarded what was left. He promises to mail an information packet, and Andrew gives the task force office address so that Diane can hold it. Andre stumbles over the name on the call, saying "Khan" and then "Kahn." (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Esteban's uncle
docs.text: An unseen member of the Marblehead church who volunteers to do his nephew's laundry and adds bean juice to the wash. As Esteban puts it, his uncle is "in that church and he's trying to keep me a virgin." Esteban works out what is happening and thanks the team with a basket of fries with extra salt. In Summer Service 05 a girl covering his shift at McDonald's confirms that he has figured out it was his uncle. (Summer Service 04; Summer Service 05)

docs.title: FBI counterintelligence agent
docs.text: Also called the watcher or the roof watcher. A young agent with binoculars on the roof of a store, surveilling the Biz. Kurt spots him and chases him to the foot of a fire escape. The man greets Kurt by name ("Hi, Mr. Larson. This is awkward"), shows his counterintelligence credentials and runs off after Kurt tells him to get out of there. Kurt tells the rest of the team only that it was "some skeletons in my closet." See also FBI counterintelligence. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: FBI switchboard operator
docs.text: The unnamed operators of the FBI switchboard, reached by payphone or hotel phone. In Summer Service 03 the operator authenticates Huell by name and badge number, warns of a chemical-weapon exposure alert on Marblehead and promises reinforcements. In Summer Service 05, with Big Bill unreachable, Kurt asks the switchboard for someone with decision-making power. The operators report that the National Guard is stuck about forty miles out in the storm and cannot send a helicopter. (Summer Service 03; Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Harvard's Bait Shop owner
docs.text: A middle-aged woman who greets Huell as "officer" and sells him a large trash bag for the severed arm. Huell hands over five dollars and takes no change. He also asks about the shop's axolotls, which her cousin draws. See Harvard's Bait Shop. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Jordan Gramoire
docs.text: Ma Gramoire's son, a National Guardsman. She says she will talk to the government when it brings her son back: "He's still alive, he just don't call." Kurt asks Big Bill's secretary to have Jordan assigned to the Marblehead deployment, and the secretary says he will put in the request. Jordan is never seen. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: M.E. assistant in pajamas
docs.text: Also called the RV assistant. One of Donald McManley's assistants, who stays in the mobile lab. He answers the door when Andrew brings back the living head of Puddles and wordlessly takes the writhing bag, and he is left behind with the RV when the team heads out in the finale. He is not named and is a separate person from Henry, who spends the night out on a Vespa. (Summer Service 05; Summer Service 06)

docs.title: McDonald's girl
docs.text: A teenager covering Esteban's shift at the McDonald's when Huell walks in after cutting his own arm. She reports that Esteban "figured it out. It was his uncle" and has gone to sleep before a test. Esteban himself is not on screen. See McDonald's. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Mr. Miller
docs.text: The smoking gunner of the boat crew in the cold open of Radford Horror 08, which teases the Marblehead case. The commander says, "Mr. Miller, you may fire when ready." Miller takes a long drag on his cigarette and answers, "All right, smile, you son of a bitch," and then everything explodes at once before the credits. His fate is not shown. See Boat crew. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: O'Donnell
docs.text: Also called Denver O'Donnell. The keeper of Marblehead's cemetery. Briggs says he "does a good job" and that his family has been in town a "long, long time." Asked whether it is the church's graveyard, Briggs says he does not think so, since it is the town's only one, and that he has never heard the keeper say any of the weird things. The previous team's contact list includes a Denver O'Donnell, and the episodes do not say whether this is the same man. The team never talks to him. See The cemetery. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Old jogging woman
docs.text: A soaked woman of about ninety who appears in the cold open of Summer Service 04, jogging in the rain until her daughter comes out to fetch her. She tells her daughter, "Pastor says God is coming," promises not to let her go to hell, and runs off into the rain. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Readful Things clerk
docs.text: The clerk at the Readful Things bookstore, where the Biz goes for his 1980 edition of Moby Dick. She has the glow, a sallow face and a fishy open mouth, and she follows him around the shop with her head like a goldfish. See also The glow. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Sergeant Jefferson
docs.text: A National Guard sergeant who broadcasts on all frequencies that the Guard has arrived in Marblehead and taken command, and who asks for a consult with the FBI agents. He gives his name as both Sergeant Jefferson and Sergeant Johnson, and Andre notes that it is clearly the same voice repeating the message. Kurt answers but gets no reply, which tells the team that the Guard has a more powerful transmitter than they do. He is never met. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The suited man
docs.text: Also called the Edgar suit guy, after Andre's description of "big Edgar suit energy." A man in a suit at the back of the town hall meeting who unnerves the room. As the team leaves, Andre describes him standing motionless in the parking lot in the rain, soaking wet, staring at them. He is never explained. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Toilet guy
docs.text: Also called the alley watcher. A man watching the team's hotel from the alley under the second-floor bathroom window. Andrew drops onto him with a toilet tank lid, which hits him on the head with a "wet crunch," and the man falls limp. While the players settle on a cover story in Summer Service 06, Dante asks whether the one man they killed was "Jester or the guy out the window with the toilet," and Rita counts both: "Two men." See Toilet tank lid. (Summer Service 05; Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Unnamed hotel guest
docs.text: A man who cowers in the corner of his room when Andrew kicks in the door during the hotel siege. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: USS Oklahoma City captain and sonar operator Davy
docs.text: The submarine crew in the finale's cold open. Davy reports that the bogey has gone on land, then a small explosion, then "the craziest sound I've ever heard." After the bogey returns, closing at 60 to 70 knots, the captain, "done with this spooky shit," orders a full about and everything conventional fired. The last glimpse is of the pursuit at 80 knots, and their fate is not shown. Big Bill later says that a submarine was lost. See USS Oklahoma City. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Young lieutenant
docs.text: The officer at the National Guard checkpoint at the entrance to Marblehead. He first turns the team away, saying nobody is in or out of the town because of a biological incident, then takes them to an older officer once they say they are the FBI agents the Guard asked for. See National Guard checkpoint and Older Guard officer. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Minor characters: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text: This page lists the minor and one-scene characters of The Walkers in Skin, the Utah arc set around Ballard, Roosevelt and the Sherman Ranch.

docs.title: Armed townsfolk at the gym
docs.text: Unnamed Ballard locals who file into the school gym behind the duplicate of Andrew Howard, flanked by upright horses. One shotguns the real Andrew, and many die when a grenade goes off in the gym. Afterward the duplicate tells the party that townsfolk tried to kidnap him. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: Ballard general store clerk
docs.text: A middle-aged, lifelong Ballard resident with an enormous beehive hairdo, who sells the party bologna, white bread and cheap beer. She insists the town is normal ("the ranch is weird, but that's the county"), resents the community center, blames the mayor and Deborah Wells, and misses Reagan. She tells Andrew about Edward Douglas and recommends the diner's funeral potatoes. Her name is never given. See Ballard general store. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: Ballard grocery clerk
docs.text: The only person on duty at the Ballard grocery when Huell goes there after a mysterious page. Listless and unhelpful, she patches the bite on his wrist, offers "ham or something," and tells him Ballard has no homeless people. She suggests the page was a prank. See the "homeless" man. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Big-house doorman
docs.text: A curt, unfamiliar doorman at Bigelow's big house who tells Kurt, at night, that Bigelow is asleep and to come back tomorrow. Kurt leaves before he "escalates." He is a man the party has not seen before. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Bigelow's enforcer
docs.text: A big, burly guard at Bigelow's compound in Ballard who serves the team pancakes, cheap syrup and coffee on paper plates while the rest of the staff, armed with SPAS-12s and M16s, stay on edge. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Bigelow's staff psychiatrist
docs.text: An unnamed psychiatrist employed by Bigelow. After the night event, the party gives him a 45-minute debrief, deliberately leaving out the levitation and the vanished fillings. See the night event. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Bud
docs.text: Sheriff McDermish's deadpan seven-year-old son. He answers the door of the sheriff's trailer ("My daddy's on the shitter. Can I help you?"), watches Aladdin on VHS and beats his father at Monopoly. In Walkers 06 the sheriff, fleeing the state, tells his son to get his backpack because they are going "to see the aunts." (Walkers 03, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Carl (Roosevelt cop)
docs.text: A hungover Roosevelt police officer whose entire contribution to the investigation is the word "Ham." He microwaves Canadian bacon, eats Lucky Charms from a coffee cup, eavesdrops on the party's whispered conference and chokes on hot ham. The "ham guy" became a running joke at the table. See Roosevelt Police Department. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Chuck
docs.text: An offscreen teenager who grows sickly yellow marijuana behind his parents' trailer and sells it for $25. He is a friend of Harrison's brother and the source of the weed the two boys are carrying when the party catches them. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Cold-open patrolman
docs.text: A Native American man in a big cowboy hat who patrols the ranch at night with a shotgun, an ATV and a dog, seen only in the cold open of Walkers 02. He whistles for the dog, finds nothing and drives off, and a coyote then steps out from behind the sheep and stands up on two legs. Gardner later describes a Native American former Army Ranger who reported shooting at a snooper near the barn; that man is the gate guard Walt, whom the patrolman resembles, though the cold open never names him. See upright coyotes. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: Confused Roosevelt resident
docs.text: An older man in Roosevelt whose car was stolen and whose job did not open. He likes Wheel of Fortune and plans to eat unheated TV dinners and read a book, since the power is off ("Get an electric oven, they said"). (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Coyote-feeding woman
docs.text: An unnamed woman in the cold open of Walkers 05. She drives a pickup into the desert with a bulging backpack, and as coyotes circle the truck she scoops white powder with a coffee cup and pours it down the throat of one whose mouth opens unnaturally wide, with grey fibers moving inside. Her identity and purpose are never explained. See upright coyotes. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Craig
docs.text: A name dropped in a joke. In Walkers 06, during banter about ghosts and tulpas, Dante (as Kurt) says, "tulpas are definitely real, or Craig had telekinesis." Rita answers, "I'm saying he had telekinesis." Craig is never explained. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Doug's victim
docs.text: A woman who lets herself into Doug's desert trailer with the spare key hidden under a ceramic frog. She finds a hoard of Jell-O and a garbage-bag-wrapped figure, and Doug's grey tendrils infest her. Her fate is not shown. See Doug's trailer. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Eager Roosevelt officer
docs.text: A young, starstruck Roosevelt cop who leaks the lead about the junkyard to the party and is proud of how quickly Yusuf confessed ("I've never had a case come together so quickly"). He boasts that the suspect confessed after "30, 45 minutes of working him over." (Walkers 05, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Ed Shepherd
docs.text: A missing Ballard local, named only by the sheriff: his trailer is empty and his mail is piling up. He is one of the examples of the disappearances in Ballard. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Edgar Roberto
docs.text: A teenage delinquent who stole every toilet seat in the Ballard school without knowing why. Sheriff McDermish names him as his usual culprit for local mischief. (Walkers 03)

docs.title: Edward Douglas
docs.text: A Ballard resident mentioned by the beehive clerk, who shot half his right foot off and drove an hour in a manual car to get it treated. He is never met. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: Elderly farmer
docs.text: A maimed skinwalker in the cavern, missing an arm with his torso blown open. He vomits his brain-creature into a tank and dies, while the other copies stand silently entangling their tendrils. See skinwalkers and the cavern. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: FedEx truck driver
docs.text: A driver turned back at the bridge blockade, which is manned by skinwalkers in stolen police uniforms. His fate is unknown. See the bridge blockade. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Good Hills Diner waiter
docs.text: A glum teenager with bad acne who mixes up the party's waffle and pancake order at the Good Hills Diner, where Andrew attempts the French Toast Castle. See Good Hills Diner. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Herbert
docs.text: Drebin's pet iguana, who rides on his shoulder and has "mad lizard eyes." Drebin shows him off to the party before leaving to return with the ground-penetrating radar. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Hertz clerk
docs.text: A voice on the phone from Hertz Rent-A-Car who pages Andrew to report the rental Plymouth Voyager blocking East Lagoon Street in Roosevelt. She spells out "L-A-G-O-O-N" and tells him to keep better track of his car. See the Plymouth Voyager. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Kurt's wife
docs.text: Kurt's wife is never seen. In Walkers 01 she is established as an excellent cook with Vietnamese leanings, whom Dante jokes is ex-Viet Cong; in Walkers 02 Kurt says she mostly cooks Vietnamese food; in Walkers 03 he mentions a watch his wife bought him on vacation. (Walkers 01, Walkers 02, Walkers 03)

docs.title: Marina
docs.text: A staffer at Bigelow's research operation who has recurring nightmares of drowning. Bigelow mentions her when asked whether his staff have had psychological symptoms. See Bigelow's research operation. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Marshall Crichton
docs.text: Harrison's silent friend, who joins him in the barn and refuses to say why he came. Kurt nicknames him Snake Eyes before he gives his name. He tells Harrison, "We're the fucking worst at crime." (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Officer Hernandez
docs.text: A polite Roosevelt police officer who winces at swearing. He assumes the wrecked Voyager is the work of vandals with a roller crusher and a flatbed and plans to check the junkyards. After seeing Andrew's FBI ID he waives the tickets, recommends the diner and arranges the loan of the squad car Betsy. See Roosevelt Police Department. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Philip Bishop
docs.text: Gardner's tall, thin, silent FBI partner, who has a thin mustache and blinks owlishly. He stiffens at Huell's "So, Mormons, am I right?", which is followed by about four minutes of sweaty silence. He confirms the former Ranger's account of the shooting and the lack of evidence. See the FBI Salt Lake City field office. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: Ranch gate guard
docs.text: An unnamed guard who lets the party out of the ranch gate after the dusk event. The episodes treat him as a separate person from Walt. See the dusk event. (Walkers 03)

docs.title: Roadside ambushers
docs.text: A matronly woman with a double-barrel shotgun, a pot-bellied man with a handgun and two children with kitchen knives, who ambush McManley on the road with a spike strip and roll his Suburban. McManley kills all four, and is shaken afterward that two were children. Two of the bodies, one child and one adult, are found to be carrying dead pilots in their skulls. See pilot and host biology. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Roosevelt dentist
docs.text: A dentist working from a spare room, who has never seen every filling in a patient's mouth vanish. The only material on hand is gold, so he spends five hours replacing the Biz's fillings with non-magnetic gold on the company's dime. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Roosevelt hospital doctors
docs.text: Doctors at the Roosevelt hospital who keep the hospital's generator running for a single ventilator patient after the ambulance and radio are stolen. Smoke is visible outside the door. See Roosevelt, Utah. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Roosevelt repair-shop mechanic
docs.text: A mechanic who tells the party that every drivable car in town has been stolen and the rest sabotaged by hand, with batteries removed, wires and belts cut, tires slashed and sugar in the gas tanks. The party concludes that someone wants nobody to leave. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Salt Lake FBI secretary
docs.text: The friendly front-desk secretary at the Salt Lake City field office, who confirms that Big Bill called ahead and gives the party directions. See the FBI Salt Lake City field office. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: Shelly (FBI staffer)
docs.text: A staffer at the Salt Lake City office, heard on the intercom when Gardner asks for another drinking-fountain test kit; he calls her "a peach." She is unrelated to Shelly Wilmarth. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: Stewart's checkout lady
docs.text: A chatty elderly cashier at Stewart's grocery in Roosevelt who thanks the party for not patronizing the Dollar Tree "interloper" and guesses they are Feds. She winks at Andrew as "Half-Gallon Howard" after he buys a half-gallon of ice cream, and she is reading a "Mormon smutty" pirate romance. The total is $19.43. See Stewart's. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: The medic
docs.text: A kindly National Guard medic who treats Howard, Huell and Kurt in the field. When the Guard collapses, he panics because he has no chain of command, and Kurt takes his Humvee ("I'm the chain of command. We're moving."). See the National Guard. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Thomas Kendrick
docs.text: Huell's father, seen only in a memory. When the tendrils of a captured skinwalker enter Huell's mouth, they pull up a scene of his father eating a plate of bacon while his mother needles him about cholesterol. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Unknown pager caller
docs.text: A man's voice that pages Huell and says, "I have something you should see. It's about your colleague," telling him to come alone to the back room of the Ballard grocery. Nobody shows up, and the number is unlisted. The caller's identity is never established. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Molly Underhill
docs.text:
Molly Underhill is a towering sheriff's deputy in Radford, Virginia who becomes the task force's steadiest local ally, rescues the team from the burning church, keeps their secrets, and by 1993 is sheriff after a "battlefield promotion."

Type NPC Aliases Deputy Underhill; Sheriff Underhill; Molly Affiliation Radford Sheriff's Department Status Alive; sheriff (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In Radford Horror 01 Molly is a big woman of about 45 and 5'11", a little heavy but muscular, with some gray in her hair. On the phone and radio she is folksy and friendly ("what can I do you for?") and blunt (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 07). In The Radford Horrors Andre describes her as six-two and "built like a brick shithouse," a little chubby, tired and sardonic (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
Radford Horror 01. Molly answers the phones at the station and fetches the sheriff when the team calls. When Sheriff Roosevelt asks her to phone in the team's credentials to double-check them, she reads Kurt's case officer credentials and tells him, "Oh, you're a spooky spook" (Radford Horror 01).

Radford Horror 03. Andrew phones her about the Augustine household. She says she thinks she has met Derek, that the couple have a son of about eleven and an older daughter, that they attend church and have never crossed the radar of law enforcement, and that her own daughter has mentioned the son from school (Radford Horror 03).

Radford Horror 04. She pages the team early in the morning: Phoebe Augustine is missing from her bed. She brings coffee, hands out flashlights, assigns the shared radio channel 25.0, and calls a boat owner and a pilot in Salem with an ultralight. Afterward she takes the agents aside and tells them a mutilated girl's body, probably Amanda Lucky's, has been found by the interstate. "It's been a person every day," she says, and admits, "I was skeptical, but y'all were right. Whatever's going on here is fucked up." (Radford Horror 04)

Radford Horror 05. She radios news that the fingerprints from the roof are back; the only database hit is the earlier spaceman robbery, which points to Abelforth. The sheriff puts out an APB on Abelforth and on the spaceman sketch, and she brings in a tech from Roanoke for the assays. She shows the team photos of the scene where Amanda was found, announces the curfew and the community meeting at the church, and leads the team into it. She calls the break-in at Dr. Lori's office a prank and tells the team Derek Augustine is one of the town's pharmacists as well as a romance novelist (Radford Horror 05).

Radford Horror 07. She is a radio voice. She tells Kurt about the town's overdoses and a D.A.R.E. visit to the high school after one ended up in the ER, adding that she would love to "personally unpack" whoever is bringing the heroin in. Later she takes the team's call for help for the injured Phoebe and Wilbur in the woods (Radford Horror 07).

Radford Horror 08. Molly finds the badly hurt team after the fight at the burning church, shouting for them through the trees. Kurt gives her the foil-wrapped shadow poncho and the flashlight weapon; she shoves them in her back pocket, helps load the team onto a stretcher lowered from a helicopter and later returns the flashlight and foil in the hospital. She also tells the sheriff that the team had asked about the heroin (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The Radford Horrors (1993)
docs.text:
Radford Horrors 02. Molly is now sheriff after a "battlefield promotion": Frank Roosevelt had a heart attack earlier in the year and has stepped back, though he is fine. She recaps the previous case for Daniel Webster and the team. Phoebe had gone to a rehab in California "like Narconon," but no one could reach her and scary lawyers threatened anyone who asked questions. The FBI then sent a task force, which stopped in briefly and also vanished. She digs up the lawyers' phone number, a map marked with the missing agents' campsite and a set of missing-person posters, and suspects the cartel is back (Radford Horrors 02).

Radford Horrors 03. She brings coffee, jokes that the team got "Pay n' Stayed," offers the mother-in-law suite at the back of her home as lodging, brings the Elizabeth George case, and drives them to the arcade. She explains that officially the missing people are in LA treatment (Radford Horrors 03). See LA treatment cover story.

Radford Horrors 04. Kurt phones her about Billy Thornton. She knows him and says they get along now that he has stopped doing heroin in front of the school, and agrees to offer him food and a cot (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• The task force: friendly and cooperative; keeps their evidence secret.
  • Frank Roosevelt: her sheriff in The Radford Horror; he steps back after a heart attack before her promotion.
  • Dr. Harvey Mauden: coroner who works with her office.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Molly is introduced at about 5'11" in Radford Horror 01 and described as six-two in Radford Horrors 03.
  • Her last name was uncertain to Andre at the table, who briefly lost it in Radford Horror 03.
