docs.title: Monica Cartwright
docs.text:
Monica Cartwright is the alcoholic mother of the missing boy Gene Cartwright, who tells the task force about off-season Jeep hunters and a naked, hairy figure resembling Chewbacca.

Type NPC Aliases Cartwright; Gene's mother Residence Dahlonega Trailer Park Status Alive (as of Appalachia 04) First appearance Appalachia 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Monica is gruff and blunt. The team finds her in her trailer with wine bottles on the couch, offering them warm white wine and spraying a noisy air conditioner with WD-40. She admits she was drunk when she saw the hairy figure (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The players chose to visit "dead kid mom" before the Covenant. Monica deflated when the agents said they had not found her son, and she said she had already talked to the police. She told them Gene had been playing in the woods with the Nick boy (Edward Nick), who started screaming his head off; when she ran out, Gene was gone, and she searched for days. The only people she saw were men in a Jeep, dressed in gray jumpsuits and sunglasses, carrying shotguns, with a big cage in the back. She took them for drunk off-season hunters, and they told her to leave.

She added that about a month earlier a naked, hairy figure who looked "exactly like Chewbacca" stood at the end of her driveway with a backpack, as if on a smoke break, until a regular-sized black sedan pulled up and he got in the back. Sheriff Burke brushed her off, telling her she was drunk, and she admitted she was. She asked whether the agents had found "that cult lady" (Willow Greengrass) and whether they thought it was related. As they left she told them, "Don't come back unless you find my son." Outside, the team agreed Gene was almost certainly dead, since his shoe had been found in a tree (Appalachia 04). Her Chewbacca figure is later tied to the costume found in the mines (see The Bigfoot Hoax).

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"Don't come back unless you find my son." Andre (as Monica Cartwright) (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Appalachia 04

docs.title: Motel and Suites Clerk
docs.text:
The Motel and Suites Clerk is the tired, dry, cooperative man behind bulletproof glass at a de-branded Holiday Inn near Dahlonega, Georgia, who confirms that the drifter later found dead in a Chewbacca costume had stayed there as "John Doe".

Type NPC (unnamed) Affiliation Motel and Suites Status Alive (as of Appalachia 06) First appearance Appalachia 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The clerk has worked at the motel for a few months. He sits behind bulletproof glass with a money slot, offers a "two-for-one special on pillows", and is weary and cooperative. The Holiday Inn part of the sign has been chiseled off because the motel lost the rights, though the imprint of the letters remains, and the air conditioners rattle at frequencies that drift in and out of phase (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
When the team visits, the clerk recognizes the drifter's photo. The man stayed for a while, then "didn't re-up or take his stuff", so the clerk tossed it the day before. The register lists him as "John Doe", and he paid in cash. The clerk saw him with a walkie-talkie a couple of times, and a man in a motorcycle helmet picked him up on an ATV once or twice. He also had a female caller a couple of times (see Troy Cleaver for the dead man).

He warns the agents, "If you see a green garbage bag back there, don't open the green garbage bag." It holds the linens from a scatological pornographic shoot by a guest who registered as "Jenny Maxine", and such messes happen "conservatively four times a year". He never lets those guests back. When Kurt has the team search the dumpster, the clerk, who cannot open the office door during business hours, passes his phone through the money slot so Kurt can call McManley. The clerk remembers that the dead man took a pair of snakeskin cowboy boots from the room, and the team finds them in the trash. He says the man's room is already rented to a family and promises to call if they leave. He also gives Andrew a fatherly pat through the slot and a pep talk that he is in the right line of work (Appalachia 06). The dumpster search turns up the items described in Dead Man's Briefcase.

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"If you see a green garbage bag back there, don't open the green garbage bag." Andre (as the Motel and Suites Clerk) (Appalachia 06)

Quote

"Yeah, but it's obvious you put it on 'cause you took off your cop outfit." Andre (as the Motel and Suites Clerk), on Andrew's Bigfoot T-shirt (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Appalachia 06

docs.title: Mother Dahlia Riversand
docs.text:
Mother Dahlia Riversand is a big, imposing elder of the Covenant who receives the task force in the ghost town of Auraria, Georgia.

Type NPC Aliases Dahlia; Mother Riversand Affiliation The Covenant Status Alive (as of Appalachia 04) First appearance Appalachia 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Dahlia is big and imposing, disapproving and bossy, with stiff speech. She runs the Covenant's one-room schoolhouse, where the children learn Latin and their times tables, and Elijah Ray teaches comparative religion (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
As the team walks toward the tents in Auraria, Dahlia intercepts them and tells them to introduce themselves "instead of just skulking around like thieves in the night". She offers a member named River, who knew the missing Willow Greengrass, and sets the team up in the community center, the only other building in town, staying in the room to prevent "funny business". She hands out brochures and invites them to "the baptism this evening" for a door salesman, Jeremy, whom the Covenant "managed to talk into it". She refuses Andrew access to him until Rita rolls an 8 to Manipulate Someone and Andrew plays lost and haunted. Dahlia then says Andrew has "the devil standing right behind" him, and allows him to speak to Jeremy through a tent wall.

She explains the Covenant's land dispute with "corporate goons" who arrived about a year earlier with eviction paperwork (see The Land Dispute). The orchard deal and the sale of preserves are meant to fund a lawyer, and she fetches copies of the letters, which name only a law firm, Jackson and Lee's. She says river water is boiled and treated with chlorine tablets, after a stretch of intestinal and GI trouble, and that one member lost two toes to an infected toenail. The Covenant keeps promising a boiler, and she says it would already be built if they had not had to save for the lawyer.

When a stray remark that she "watched my husband explode" confuses the table, Ezra's Biz asks her to explain. She says her husband, drunk on newly discovered sake in Japan, stepped in front of a 320-mph bullet train and "turned into a paste". She then came to Georgia to stay with family, met Elijah Ray, and he changed her life (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"He turned into a paste. At least he didn't feel a thing." Andre (as Mother Dahlia Riversand) (Appalachia 04)

Quote

"You've got the devil standing right behind you. Do you know that?" Andre (as Mother Dahlia Riversand) (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Appalachia 04

docs.title: Mr. King
docs.text:
Mr. King is Andrew Howard's mentor in a cosmic-leaning organization, seen only in a flashback in which he gives Andrew the "anthill" speech and tells him that "the next master is coming."

Type NPC Aliases Kingsley Affiliation A cosmic-leaning group awaiting "the next master" (see The Masters) Status Unknown First appearance Radford Horror 01 (flashback) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Andrew does not often get to talk to Mr. King one-on-one, so the conversation is a notable one in his life. Andre voices him with a vaguely Indian accent (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: Radford Horror 01
docs.text:
While Andrew's boss at the FBI warns him that leading the task force "has boondoggle written all over it," the episode cuts to a flashback of an earlier conversation in another office. Mr. King tells Andrew that at the FBI he will find himself in the midst of people all committed to a common purpose, "like standing in the middle of an anthill," and that it would be easy to get caught up in the secular bustle and act as if it were his purpose too. "But it isn't. Not entirely. You serve a higher purpose."

He goes on to say that the next master is coming, "maybe next year, maybe in three or four, but not ten," and that whether this is a triumph or a tragedy depends on how well the organization opens the minds of secular people to "his truth and his laws." Andrew's purpose is to help the organization "fight back against the forces of silence that would cover up the influences of the cosmic to protect the petty mundane." He calls Andrew "the tip of the spear." As he leaves, he adds the line below (Radford Horror 01).

Andre (as Mr. King)

Andrew, Jesus and the Buddha were not wholly of this world, and neither are you. Remember that.

docs.title: Radford Horror 08
docs.text: Recovering after the fight at the church, Andrew's mother wants to visit him in D.C.; Rita, as Andrew, tells her over the phone to "talk to Mr. King," that it is all part of the plan. Later in the same scene Andre says Andrew's mother thinks he should go to more church social functions, and asks "What's his name? Kingsley?" The episode does not make clear whether this is the same man (Radford Horror 08). See The Masters.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Mr. King is never seen outside the flashback, and the episodes do not say what the organization is, who the "forces of silence" are, or whether he has any connection to the task force's creation.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 01 (flashback)
  • Radford Horror 08 (mentioned)

docs.title: Mr. Roulet
docs.text:
Mr. Roulet is the never-named husband of Margaret Roulet, a gun collector who owned the Rhode Island house the task force investigates.

Type NPC Aliases The husband; owner of the house Status Presumed dead (the second body in the basement pit, never confirmed) First appearance Roulet Estate 01 (as an unnamed owner)

docs.title: Description and background
docs.text:
In Roulet Estate 01 Andrew learns from the library that the house belonged to a husband and wife, and that the wife was the more devout UFO believer. Wedding photos from the 1950s or 60s, apparently taken in Arizona, show a curly-haired woman and a man with close-cropped military hair. The house has a combination-locked steel door hiding a weapons closet whose empty racks once held about twenty firearms; only a World War II flamethrower was left behind. The man is never given a first name. (Roulet Estate 01)

In Roulet Estate 02 the agents find guns that look like they came from his closet in the Hidden Attic Lair, including a Kalashnikov and Russian World War II-era pistols, many of them loaded. Andre notes that "the gentleman of the house was a firearm collector", and the agents reason that this explains how the intruder came by a Soviet VSS rifle and makes a KGB plot less likely. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Fate
docs.text:
Parts of two bodies are found in the Roulet Basement trash pit. Margaret is identified by her ring; the second body is never identified, though the agents assume it is her husband. The attic lair also held older Polaroids of other, unidentified sleepers. (Roulet Estate 02)

At the pharmacy siege, a police officer reports that the gunman has a machine gun, a flamethrower and an old wooden rifle, and the intruder is later seen carrying a Mosin-Nagant. The episodes do not say whether these came from the Roulet collection. See The Roulet Intruder. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Roulet Estate 01
  • Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Naked intruder
docs.text:
The naked intruder is an enormous, pain-immune, naked man who lets himself into the Sherman Ranch double-wide with a key and a shotgun, bites a chunk from the Biz's cheek, is emptied by Andrew's Cast Out Evil, and dies in Roosevelt hours later.

Type NPC / possessed or controlled victim Aliases Carter (?); the giant intruder; entity in the intruder Affiliation Unknown Status Dead (died about 5 a.m., Walkers 07) First appearance Walkers 07 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A giant, bald, dark-skinned man about 6'7" to 6'8" and roughly 300 lbs, naked, carrying an over-under shotgun, who at first crawls on all fours. His strength is big-man strength rather than supernatural. He feels no pain, even with his feet shot up (Walkers 07).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
About 11 p.m. the Biz wakes on edge, senses movement outside and hears scratching at the front door; something skitters around the house. Hinges squeak in the back mud room, and the laundry-room door opens by millimeters as a wide, bald head pokes out near the floor. Huell orders "Hands up, buddy," and the man lunges, throwing Huell into the Biz (Walkers 07). See Guest double-wide.

In the fight the real Andrew Howard wakes and tackles the man from behind as one shotgun barrel fires into the ceiling, then is slammed through the drywall. Kurt forces the second barrel into the wall and is choked. The Biz loops his belt around the man's neck and has a chunk of his cheek bitten out; the piece is too small to sew back. Kurt's P90 and Huell's pistol shoot the man's feet with no visible reaction. Andrew declines a skull shot (risking the Biz) and uses Cast Out Evil (12) with his hands on the man's face: a black-light glow passes through him and bluish-white light streams from his eyes and mouth, and the man goes limp. Andrew does not understand what he did (Walkers 07).

Afterward the man is catatonic: pulse and breath but no muscle tension and fixed pupils. The team handcuffs him; Huell's first aid (15) stabilizes him. A key is in the back door: the man let himself in. Andrew keeps it. Zack declares the man's name to be Carter, and the others go along with it, though nothing in the scene supports it (Walkers 07).

About 11:15 p.m. Walt "Coyote" Murphy arrives by Jeep, sees the man and asks "Is that... you?", implying he recognizes him. Warned about Ballard, where half the high school is missing, Walt drives the body to the small emergency room in Roosevelt, avoiding Ballard. He returns about 5 a.m., exhausted: the man's breathing weakened on the drive, he did CPR while driving, and the man died on the heart-lung machine (Walkers 07). See Roosevelt, Utah.

The same night, Bigelow reports all recordings and three employees stolen; Bigelow says "somebody had keys to the whole fucking place," and the intruder had used a key at the double-wide too (Walkers 07). See Bigelow's recordings.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• What left the man. After the fight Rita and Dante remark that "there was a thing in him" and that "something left"; the characters themselves know only that the man collapsed, unconscious, and died hours later.
  • Whether he was a Skinwalker, a controlled victim, or the "Carter" Zack named him.
  • Why Walt seemed to recognize him, and how he obtained a key.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 07

docs.title: Nancy the goose
docs.text:
Nancy is Alberta Wilmarth's enormous, aggressive goose, a comic menace who besieges the Sherman Ranch guest house, bites Huell, steals Andrew Howard's jacket and finally befriends the real Howard after his return.

Type Animal (apparently mundane) Aliases Nancy; the goose; Alberta's goose; Betsy (Huell's misnomer) Affiliation Owned by Alberta Wilmarth Status Alive (as of Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 02 Home Sherman Ranch

docs.title: Description
docs.text: An enormous goose that spreads its wings, hisses, honks, charges and bites. It is smart: it tests the house for entry, pops up at windows, watches Kurt and shadows Howard, whom it seems to sense is "weak of will." It is docile only with its owner and eats meat scraps. Per the ranch security woman, it is "happy when she feels powerful," so the advice is to run. Pepper spray is reportedly useless (Walkers 02). Rita sums it up in Walkers 04: "it likes one person, and everyone else is dinner" (Walkers 04).

docs.title: Walkers 02: first charge
docs.text: Nancy charges Kurt, then jumps into Alberta's arms and hisses at him. Alberta calls her a "big softie"; Walt vows to eat her ("One of these days I am gonna eat that thing"), and Alberta forbids it. The goose's repeated window jump-scares become a running gag (Walkers 02).

docs.title: Walkers 03: the siege
docs.text: An extremely angry goose waits outside the guest house. Kurt wants "Ham bang it is" because the flashbangs are on the plane; Huell throws lunch meat and rolls a flat 10, and the goose goes for the ham while the party runs. Halfway to the car it returns, and Huell's Act Under Pressure (8) is only a partial success: the goose bites his nose so hard it bleeds and swells shut. Walt calls the goose "my biggest problem in life." On their return a goose-shaped silhouette rushes them and rattles the doorknob (Walkers 03). See Guest double-wide.

docs.title: Walkers 04: Operation Get Goose Out
docs.text: The goose scuttles out of the dark and steals the baloney. Later it bolts into the guest house, and Huell traps it inside (Act Under Pressure 12). In "Operation Get Goose Out," it drops onto Howard's head from above the door; his pendant's force field repels it (Andrew's pendant). Kurt pries it off with stilts (9), but it escapes with Howard's jacket, eats a French toast castle from a takeout box, and leaves dung on Huell's pillow. Walt scolds Howard for letting it take the jacket ("That's showing weak. Now it knows you're weak"), noting that the owner loves the goose so no one will kill it. In Howard's dream that night, the goose, in the form of the cremated crow, pins him and explains radar physics, entirely correctly. The Biz arranges a bomb collar, thermite and a net gun from Hooster (Walkers 04). Rita asks, "what if it's not really a goose?"

docs.title: Walkers 05: dropped from the roof
docs.text: Alberta holds the goose calmly in her lap. While the party digs near the big house, Dante spots eyes watching from the roof, rules out the goose because the eyes would be front-facing, and Andre amends it to a single eye. As the party backs away, the goose drops from above at about 50 feet, and everyone runs. Dante later jokes about chaining the car, Betsy, to the ground, and warns Drebin that "there's a swan around here that'll pick a fight with anything" (Walkers 05).

docs.title: Walkers 06 and 07: blamed first
docs.text: When part of the radar is found chewed from underneath, the players blame the goose, ape men and squirrels (Walkers 06). During the naked intruder's attack, the Biz says, "Probably just the fucking goose again"; afterward the goose honks around the mud room, and Huell insists, as a dumb joke, that her name is Betsy (Walkers 07). See Naked intruder.

docs.title: Walkers 09: the returned Howard
docs.text: Nancy arrives along the real Howard's trail, having befriended him, hisses over his shoulder, and hops back into his arms as the cavern collapses. The party guesses her name is "Beatrice" (Walkers 09). See Andrew Howard (the Monstrous). In a line about an unrecorded session, Rita as the duplicate Howard says he spent the whole afternoon explaining the situation to the goose (Walkers 09); see Andrew Howard (duplicate).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Huell's "Betsy" is a deliberate joke that collides with the party's car, also called Betsy; see Betsy (Walkers 07).
  • Recurring jokes include Jurassic Park (Walkers 03 and 04), "Elsa. Scatter." (Walkers 03) and the Alien scene (Walkers 05). In Walkers 09, Rita jokes that Nancy is Howard's middle name.
  • Quote from Dante as Kurt in Walkers 05: "I've eaten in trenches and felt less pressure from the enemy forces than this goddamn goose."

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 02, Walkers 03, Walkers 04, Walkers 05
  • Walkers 06 (mentioned), Walkers 07, Walkers 09

docs.title: The major
docs.text:
The major is the unnamed commander of the Utah National Guard convoy that backs the task force in the finale of The Walkers in Skin. The players also call him "the general."

Type NPC Aliases National Guard major; the general Affiliation National Guard (Utah) Status Unknown; absent after the battle at the field (Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 09 (he had already met the party in an unrecorded session) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The major is a skeptical career officer who commands a column of Humvees and armored personnel carriers. He is never named. The players call him both "the major" and "the general," and they clearly mean the same man (Walkers 09).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
At the start of Walkers 09, Andre recaps the unrecorded session before it: the party fetched horses to get around a roadblock, took a generator to the radio station, called the National Guard, and met the Guard on horseback outside Ballard. They then fought through the Ballard-Roosevelt barricade and cleared the police station (Walkers 09).

In the finale the convoy drives back through dark, abandoned Ballard toward the community center. The duplicate Andrew Howard rides in the major's Humvee. As the radio dissolves into static, the major gets out and asks the party about electromagnetic interference. Kurt Larson tells him the ranch recorded bursts that killed its cameras and urges him to stay alert; Kurt also warns him to bail out if a vehicle starts to rise. The major is doubtful but goes along (Walkers 09).

Kurt pitches Ned Simpson and his homemade killdozer as an "asset," and the major agrees after a long stare through the window, then slows the convoy to 20 mph so the rest of the column does the same. When Kurt points out that the cloud crossing the sun is the ranch farmhouse floating in the sky, the major's jaw drops open (Walkers 09).

After invisible waves shove the vehicles and freeze everyone mid-sentence, the major concedes that the cars are a liability, halts the convoy, and orders the heavy equipment carried, body armor worn, the horses taken and civilians left behind. He also agrees to try a megaphone surrender first. Kurt advises that the megaphone team should not be where the bulk of the force is, and the major sends volunteers in an armored personnel carrier around the left of the hill. Andrew gives him the nod; the loudspeaker announces "This is the National Guard, please, sir" and is answered by a hail of bullets. The main force swings around the right (Walkers 09).

He is not seen again. After the white powder knocks out everyone left on the field, Kurt refers to him as "the general... or, you know, the major" being "gone" as the survivors try to gather what evidence remains. It is never established whether he lived (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Takes tactical advice from Kurt, who tells him "This isn't anything worse than Iraq." Andre notes that Iraq has not happened yet.
  • Rides with the duplicate Howard, who is secretly a skinwalker played by Rita.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 09
  • The unrecorded session between Walkers 08 and 09 (Walkers 08.5), known only by recap

docs.title: Ned Simpson
docs.text:
Ned Simpson is an extravagantly blond feed-store worker who builds an armored bulldozer and leads the charge on the skinwalker stronghold in the finale of The Walkers in Skin.

Type NPC Aliases the killdozer driver Status Unknown (his killdozer is last seen up in a tree, Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 09 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Ned is blond and blue-eyed to an extravagant degree, goofy, cheerful and patriotic. His wife left him last year, and he works at a feed store. He spent about six months welding the killdozer, an armored bulldozer with mounted machine guns, a load of pipe bombs and a flamethrower (Walkers 09).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Ned first appears as a killdozer with mounted machine guns closing in behind the convoy, seen through binoculars. He announces that he "fucking knew that that whole collapse business was a ruse" and wants to fight the "communist menace." Kurt Larson slows to talk to him, calls him "an asset" in CIA terms, and pitches him to the duplicate Andrew Howard and the major, who agree to take him along. Ned gives a goofy thumbs-up and seals his welded window (Walkers 09).

When the convoy halts, Ned refuses to leave the vehicle ("I did not spend six months welding this thing to just leave it behind"), so it is stuffed with grenades, radio gear and heavy supplies. He then charges into the pile of cars at the community center, shouting "Die, commie freaks!" The killdozer circles, pulping cars and the naked skinwalkers, and later begins to levitate intermittently under the ranch's electromagnetic waves; Kurt calls out that he may want to get out soon. Afterward the party sees the killdozer up in a tree. Ned himself is not seen again (Walkers 09).

Quote

"It's the time for every patriot to take up arms and/or bulldozers and fight the communist menace." (Andre as Ned, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Dante's table summary of the finale: "Got the real Andrew back, fucking killdozered a community center."
  • Zack kept joking that Ned must be Mormon.

docs.title: Officer Todd
docs.text:
Officer Todd is a nervous local police officer at the Brooks Pharmacy hostage situation who hands operational command to Andrew Howard and briefs the task force on the gunman.

Type NPC Aliases Todd Affiliation Local Rhode Island Police Status Alive (as of Roulet Estate 03) First appearance Roulet Estate 03 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Todd is one of the two officers crouched behind a squad car outside the Brooks Pharmacy. He is visibly relieved to find real FBI agents on the scene. He lives in the town and knows the store. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
When Kurt, Andrew, the Biz and Huell take cover next to the squad car after the young officer who drove them is shot, one of the cops asks Andrew whether they are the FBI. On hearing the answer he says, "I officially surrender operational command of this hostage situation to the FBI." Andrew's reaction is "Oh, maybe don't do that." (Roulet Estate 03)

Todd then briefs the agents:

  • When he and his partner answered the call about the agents' stolen car, they went inside and found the gunman, who appeared to be an alien, holding everyone at gunpoint on the floor. He was naked and shouting in American English.
  • The gunman wants a fueled car with no tracking devices (specifically a Range Rover), no more police cars in the lot, and every cop to come inside within ten minutes, naked and with handcuffs, so he can cuff them to shopping carts. Otherwise he will start killing hostages.
  • He shot a pharmacist, Todd thinks non-fatally, and was seen taking pills.
  • He claimed to have a rocket-propelled grenade. Todd did not see it, but did see a flamethrower, a machine gun and a big old-fashioned wooden rifle (see Mosin-Nagant).
  • The building has wraparound windows and a door on the corner set at about 45 degrees. A service entrance at the back is kept locked by someone named Markeith.

More police cars are on the way but delayed by snow. (Roulet Estate 03)

Todd asks Kurt whether they want to sneak in and take the gunman down, and Kurt asks him about the pharmacy's other entrances. After that, the agents run the siege themselves. See The Roulet Intruder. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Old Woman in the Lime-Green VW Beetle
docs.text:
The Old Woman in the Lime-Green VW Beetle is an elderly bystander at the Brooks Pharmacy siege who berates the half-naked Andrew Howard, bites both him and Huell Kendrick, and is knocked out and handcuffed by Huell.

Type NPC Aliases Old woman; biting prude Status Arrested by Huell (as of Roulet Estate 03) First appearance Roulet Estate 03 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: She is an elderly, prudish woman who drives a lime-green VW Beetle. After she bites Andrew, Andre notes that Andrew now knows for a fact that she has every one of her teeth. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
During the Brooks Pharmacy siege, the gunman cuts his deadline to two minutes and demands that every cop, meaning anyone with a gun, walk up to the store naked with handcuffs held above their heads. Andrew takes his shirt off while stalling the gunman on the phone and ends up with his shirt off and his pants on. (Roulet Estate 03)

While Kurt and the Biz are working on the building's back door and roof, the old woman pulls up beside Andrew, points at his chest and demands, "What on earth are you doing, young man? Have you no decency? This is a public place. You can't be out here getting high and naked and gurning in public." When Andrew identifies himself as Special Agent Howard, she answers, "Your special agent of depravity!" while poking him in the nipple. (Roulet Estate 03)

Andrew drags her to the ground behind the car, and she screams "Help! Rape!" Rita chose a Manipulate Someone roll rather than fighting her; it came up 4, and the woman bit Andrew for 2 harm. Zack (as Huell) took over with a roll of 11 and chose to force her where he wanted her. She bit his shoulder for 2 harm, and he punched her unconscious and handcuffed her hands behind her back. The two police officers behind their squad car gestured that they would not cross the open space to take her, and Huell vowed to get them fired. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Older Guard officer
docs.text:
The older Guard officer is an unnamed National Guard officer in command of the checkpoint at the entrance to Marblehead, who debriefs the task force at the end of The Summer Service.

Type NPC Aliases The older officer Affiliation National Guard Status Alive (as of Summer Service 06) First appearance Summer Service 06 Played by Andre (game master)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Andre describes him as an older gentleman in a lieutenant's uniform. A young lieutenant at the checkpoint first turns the team away, saying that nobody may enter or leave after "a biological incident" and offering to divert them to a hotel set up outside town. When Kurt says they are the FBI agents the Guard has been looking for, the young lieutenant takes them to the older officer (Summer Service 06). His name is never given.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The officer tells the team he has been told they have a canister of liquid that they call worm cure. Kurt Larson says it should kill the worms but not human tissue and hands over the half-empty anti-worm agent canister, which the officer sends to the chemist. Kurt explains that the team has been intercepting a splinter group of bioterrorists who tried to cause an incident at the nuclear plant. The officer calls it "a clusterfuck" and sends them to a tent with a phone (Summer Service 06).

After the team's call to Big Bill, in which the two agree to tell everyone that terrorists were responsible, the officer asks Andrew Howard for his account. He mentions the "real weird murals" in City Hall and says the group failed to take down the plant but killed a few of the guards. Andrew cites the group's literature about returning to the ocean and describes a parasite put into much of the local food supply; Kurt and Andrew say that the origin of the canister and any link to the synthetic nerve agent are unclear. The officer replies that his field medics are reporting "profoundly wild things," that the military is distributing deworming medicine, and that some patients will not pull through. See Terrorist cover story (Summer Service 06).

He sends the team to the medical tent for antivirals and hot soup. As he leaves to speak to his superior "about worms," he mentions that "someone used a tactical nuke at the nuclear power plant" and that it will be hard to keep out of the news. The team feigns surprise ("That scoundrel. What?"); the weapon in question is the team's own M28 Davy Crockett (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Addison
docs.text:
Non-canon

Addison belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Addison is an exhausted, poor mother at the pre-event social who pays Mirabeth a $400 down payment on an invented essential-oil business. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type NPC (non-canon one-shot) Status Alive; leaves the social with her son First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Addison hovers over her teenage son while he works on his flag for the children's event, critiquing every line he draws. The pair look very poor, and a pile of abandoned flags sits beside them. At the social (The Flag Contest), Mirabeth uses Assess the Situation to find the person least willing to attend, and Andre describes Addison and her son as the weak point she senses. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Mirabeth lures Addison away on the pretext of a chat while Derk talks to her son. She improvises a pitch about "the oil pyramid" (see The Oil Pyramid), telling Addison that a parent's financial stability is what steadies a child's life. Mirabeth rolls a 10 on Provoke Someone, and Addison pays $400 down. (Philosopher's Fist)

Her son then runs over sobbing, "Mommy, I don't wanna get killed with the president," after Derk has told him that Ovain is coming to kill the president. Addison asks whether there is a threat, hears that the tournament has been suspended after an incident with a competitor, and says she needs to make some calls. She hurries her son to the car, promising to call Mirabeth about the oils. Mirabeth gives her a business card. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Mirabeth's Bridge-Club Friend
docs.text:
Non-canon

This character belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Mirabeth's Bridge-Club Friend is the harried, unnamed organizer of the president's children's event, who arguably owes Mirabeth a favor. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type NPC (non-canon one-shot) Affiliation Committee for the president's children's event Status Alive First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A harried, middle-aged woman who answers the video phone in the middle of organizing the event for the president. She knows Derk as "that poor boy with the horse feed," and her first guess when Mirabeth calls is "Oh god, are you in jail?" (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
After the tournament briefing, Mirabeth learns that the national-holiday logo event for disadvantaged children (The Flag Contest) is being run partly by an old bridge buddy on the committee. Mirabeth calls her from a street-corner video phone outside Miguel's stand, while Derk's noisy lunch goes on behind her ("it's like Animal Planet!"). (Philosopher's Fist)

The friend says the age limit is fifteen, and Mirabeth claims Derk is fourteen. Mirabeth's Pierce the Mask roll is a 3, so the friend offers only a place on the wait list and, when Mirabeth asks about friends for Derk, the address of a social in the Capital a couple of hours away. Late that night she phones to say a spot has opened. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Colonel Sparago
docs.text:
Non-canon

Colonel Sparago belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Colonel Sparago is the profane, exasperated safety officer of the World Martial Arts Tournament, who hates both lead characters. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type NPC (non-canon one-shot) Aliases Sparago Affiliation World Martial Arts Tournament Status Alive First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Sparago is sarcastic, profane and perpetually ready to give up ("Do what you want"). Andre describes him as hating Derk and Mirabeth personally "for different reasons," and probably forty to fifty percent of the entrants as well. It is his job to guarantee the safety of the event, and he regards the entrants as "a bunch of fucking nightmares." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Sparago runs the safety briefing in the tent at the Athletes' Village. He asks the crowd to raise a hand if they are enormously strong, psychic or able to channel ki into blasts, then threatens to feed anyone who kills an audience member "to the dumbest motherfucker here." He quizzes Derk on the two rules (do not kill the audience, do not kill the judges). He also asks Derk whether he has testicles "or some reasonable analog," which sends Mirabeth into a rage. Derk answers with a garbled chant ("Kill the audience. Don't kill the judgers."), and Sparago says, "Close enough." (Philosopher's Fist)

When Ovain breaks down, Sparago begs the crowd for marijuana or Xanax ("It's a code three"), but it is too late. Derk jumps in front of the blast, and a stunned Sparago calls him "Comrade Doggy" and asks why he saved him. He has his aide Mr. Cartwright explain Ovain's state. He then says that champions usually wait until they win before turning on the president, which is why the victory punch is sedated, and goes to call the Secret Service. The unspoken implication is that another dead president would end the tournament for good. (Philosopher's Fist)

After the fight, Sparago interrupts Mirabeth's interview with a detective. He tells her the president is fine and Ovain is on his way out into space, and accuses her of smuggling Derk past the detector with "sexual wiles" against a guard who has been struggling in life. He calls Derk "a natural disaster with legs and a mouth" and lists $125,000 in property damage (mostly impact craters), a ruptured gas line, four financial-district blocks of West City evacuated and damage to the ozone layer. He grants that "Derk" is at best a nickname, says Derk needs a sponsor and must learn to bend his knees when he lands, and orders Mirabeth out. When she says she hopes to see him at next year's tournament, he replies, "You know that I will." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Delta
docs.text:
Non-canon

Delta belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Delta is a small psychic alien entrant who rides on Derk's shoulders in the briefing tent. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type NPC (non-canon one-shot) Affiliation Entrant in the World Martial Arts Tournament First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Delta is clearly an alien, "maybe an inch taller" than Derk, and raises a hand when Colonel Sparago asks who has psychic powers. When Delta asks Derk what he is and Derk says he does not know, Delta announces, "I'm a quadrillion." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text: In the briefing tent at the Athletes' Village, Derk stands on his chair to see the stage and offers the entrant behind him a ride on his shoulders, which Delta accepts. Delta climbs down when Sparago demands to know who spoke up, then climbs back on. Delta tells Derk, "Wow, you're kinda dumb, aren't you?" and says "That's okay. Honestly, I could tell." When Derk whispers to Mirabeth that he has "been on asteroid before," Delta cuts in that "Asteroid's not a drug" and asks whether they know Ovain. Delta appears only in the tent. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Derk
docs.text:
Non-canon

Derk belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Derk is a brain-damaged, near-indestructible alien prince and one of the two player characters of the one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type Player character (non-canon one-shot) Aliases Dirk; Dirk Half Scion of Cantus; Derk Sauce Affiliation Mentee of Mirabeth; entrant in the World Martial Arts Tournament Status Alive, lost in Wisukonshin at the end of the one-shot First appearance Philosopher's Fist Played by Dante

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Derk is the prince of a human-like alien race, one of several princes. He is very strong, very dim and almost impossible to hurt: a punch to the groin from Ovain makes an alarmingly metallic sound, and bed bugs cannot bite him (it kills them). He mispronounces words ("extratermestinal"), takes idioms literally ("inside voice," "rocks are good for your bones") and has no sense of social context. In the library he answers the librarian with his hand clamped over his mouth, taking the request for an "inside voice" literally, as he later explains to Mirabeth. (Philosopher's Fist)

He is joyfully honest and oblivious. His favorite things are hot dogs and dogs, and he assumes that anyone in charge is a werewolf. He can count to ten on his fingers and says he is "learning my consonants." He does not know how old he is and goes with whatever Mirabeth tells him at the moment. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Derk's given birth name is "Dirk Half Scion of Cantus," though he believes it is "Derk Sauce." His father left him on a high-gravity planet at about age five for what was meant to be a few months, and Derk stayed for fourteen years. His mother died when he was little, though he says only "I think." Living that long under high gravity left him with brain damage and the education of a five-year-old, and he lived on scorpion meat. He escaped the planet by getting good at jumping, reached escape velocity purely by accident and held his breath through space until he collided with Earth. (Philosopher's Fist)

On Earth he lived on horse feed (Omolene) until he met Fatty Gibbs, a sumo wrestler who showed him other food and gave him an old couch. Fatty died of a coronary artery problem earlier last year, and Derk agreed to enter the tournament because the Philosopher's Stone could bring him back. Mirabeth found Derk hauling a hill to clear room for bean fields in hillfolk farm country, decided he looked like a chosen hero and recently adopted him as her mentee. (Philosopher's Fist)

Mirabeth suspects that "Derk" is a fragment of his real name that he remembers; Colonel Sparago grants only that it is a nickname based on a name. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The briefing. In the safety-briefing tent at the Athletes' Village, Derk stands on his chair to see the stage and offers Delta a ride on his shoulders. He answers Sparago's quiz on the two rules with the chant "Kill the audience. Don't kill the judgers," and Sparago says, "Close enough." When the tournament is suspended over a doping scandal, he whispers to Mirabeth that he has "been on asteroid before." Mirabeth sends him to say hello to Ovain, and he greets the levitating champion with "Hi! Mirabeth says you're weird!" When Ovain blasts Sparago, Derk leaps in front shouting "Get down, Mr. Doggy!" and the blast backscatters into Ovain's eyes. (Philosopher's Fist)

The trip to the capital. Mirabeth sends Derk to chat with the Alien Faction, who decide he is a lost child and shoo him back to his "guardian." As he leaves, he overhears them wondering what happened to "that Gandekian," who "looks like someone stepped on him." To get past the compound wall, he jumps with Mirabeth on his shoulders and twists his ankle. He lands by Miguel's stand and hands over $100 for hot dogs that cost a dollar each; he receives 98 and eats them all. He then jumps to the capital in about fifteen minutes, washes in a wishing-well fountain and ends up in the children's room of the Public Library, where he draws a flag among the toddlers. (Philosopher's Fist)

The social and the president. At the community-center social, a teenager insults him and stomps off, and a girl named Sarah befriends him. Coached by Mirabeth, he tells another teenager that Ovain is coming to kill the president, and the boy breaks down sobbing. The next morning he passes security by claiming a metal plate in his head and presents Derk's Flag to the Werewolf President, who gives him a presidential-seal sticker. Mirabeth stations him under the skylight of the Presidential Event Hall, and when a guard asks him to prove he can do kung fu, he twists a quarter through ninety degrees with two fingers ("Iron fist"). (Philosopher's Fist)

The fight with Ovain. When Ovain crashes through the skylight, Derk grabs him by the tail and slams him into the floor ("Dating is hard, but you can't take it out on dogs"), then bear-hugs him so that a ki blast hits the floor and both fall into the basement. He tries to bond over their fathers, and Ovain asks how scorpions taste. Derk jumps him back out through the skylight into space. Asked telepathically "What are you?", he thinks as hard as he can "I like hot dogs!" and springboards off Ovain back toward Earth. His aim is off and he re-enters over the ocean. (Philosopher's Fist)

Aftermath. Sparago later calls him "a natural disaster with legs and a mouth." At 2 a.m. Derk spends his last $2 on a video call to Mirabeth: "Grandpa, I need you to go pick me up. I don't know where I am. And I'm scared." He reads a sign as "Forester" or "Farm Mister," and a McDonald's worker tells him he is in Wisukonshin and gives him a package of nuts. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Mirabeth is his mentor and self-declared guardian. He calls her Mirabeth, "Mama" and, on the phone, "Grandpa." She keeps him on protocols such as "follow the arrows until you get to a door"; to signal his location, he jumps straight up repeatedly.
  • Fatty Gibbs is the friend he hopes to resurrect.
  • Ovain grows curious about him and calls him "a strange but worthy adversary."

(Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Abilities and equipment
docs.text: The one-shot uses a Masks-style Powered by the Apocalypse game (see Game System). Derk is built on the Bull playbook. In that playbook he rolls Danger instead of Savior when defending someone and Danger instead of Freak for Unleash Your Powers, which Dante called "physics." He has a base -1 to Superior and takes 1 harm from the wall jump. His jumps reach escape velocity but are uncontrolled: they coat him in insects, damage the ozone layer and leave him hot to the touch. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
• "Get down, Mr. Doggy!" (Dante, as Derk)
  • "Kill the audience. Don't kill the judgers." (Dante, as Derk)
  • "Rocks are good for your bones." (Dante, as Derk)
  • "Hey, be nice to him! He liked my flag!" (Dante, as Derk)
  • "I like hot dogs!" (Dante, as Derk)

(Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Dante told Matt that Derk's name "is canonically spelled with an E," though his birth name is given as Dirk.
  • Andre remarked that "it's amazing how Derk being fucking stupid has dominated the tone of this one-shot," and Dante admitted he pushed "the onus of actual thinking" onto Rita.
  • While Derk eats the hot dogs, Dante says out of character: "I ate nothing but scorpion meat for 14 years. Earth food is fucking incredible."
  • Derk's flag includes a corgi-like dog; Matt's own corgi flags on the table's Discord got a mention during the scene.

(Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Fatty Gibbs
docs.text:
Non-canon

Fatty Gibbs belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Fatty Gibbs was a very sweet sumo wrestler and Derk's friend, who died of a coronary artery problem earlier last year. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type NPC, mentioned only (non-canon one-shot) Status Dead First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Andre describes Fatty as a morbidly obese, very strong sumo wrestler and a proficient regional fighter, though not world-class, and "just the nicest person that you have ever met in your life." He made friends with Derk shortly after Derk landed on Earth, showed him how to buy food other than horse feed, and gave him his old couch. He was almost the only person who was kind to Derk before Derk met Mirabeth. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text: Fatty died earlier last year. Derk agreed to enter the World Martial Arts Tournament because its grand prize, the Philosopher's Stone, can be used to resurrect him. The tournament is suspended during the one-shot, which ends with this goal unfulfilled. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Miguel
docs.text:
Non-canon

Miguel belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Miguel is the honest vendor of a hot dog taco stand who gives Derk 98 hot dogs and $2 change for a $100 bill. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type NPC (non-canon one-shot) Affiliation Owner of Miguel's hot dog taco stand First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Miguel runs a street stand about a quarter mile outside the athletes' compound. He sells a hot dog in a taco shell with spicy cheese, remarkably fresh tomatoes and pico de gallo, at a dollar apiece. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Derk and Mirabeth land beside the stand after the wall jump, catching Miguel mid-drop with a hot dog in his tongs. He greets them with "Hola, señor" and a stiff welcome. Mirabeth gives Derk the cash to hand over, and Derk passes Miguel a hundred-dollar bill. Miguel, who is honest, empties the cart to pile up 98 hot dogs and returns $2. Derk tries to give the $2 back for more, but Miguel refuses ("Sir, sir, no, no more, no") and wheels his cart away, dry-heaving as Derk eats them all. (Philosopher's Fist)

The $2 later pays for Derk's video call from Wisukonshin.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Mirabeth
docs.text:
Non-canon

Mirabeth belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Mirabeth is a vain, scheming 72-year-old would-be mentor with godlike beauty and legendary speed, and one of the two player characters of Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type Player character (non-canon one-shot) Aliases Meribeth; Mirabel (variant spellings) Affiliation Mentor of Derk Status Alive, setting out to rescue Derk at the end of the one-shot First appearance Philosopher's Fist Played by Rita

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Mirabeth is a glamorous old lady, "so stylin'" in Andre's words, compared by Andre and Dante to Gillian Anderson, who somehow gets hotter every year. She says "dear," "sweetie" and "ta-ta," and answers outrage with a flat "Rude." Rita played her with a single old-person voice; when Andre encouraged her to try an anime "dub voice," she said she had only the one. Mirabeth takes offense when people ask Derk "what are you?" (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Background
docs.text:
Rita described the concept as a lovely old lady who "was supposed to have mentored somebody and now it's embarrassing." Rita first said Mirabeth was 68 and then settled on 72. Mirabeth is a widow with two grown daughters, who now keep her grandchildren away because she was "really weird for a while" before she started looking for someone else's children to mentor. She had believed the hero "legacy" had to pass down within the family. Her daughter Anna wanted to be a ballerina and refused it, causing a big fight, and Mirabeth was thrown out of Anna's ninth birthday party. Her biggest enemy is a slightly older rival from before she became a mentor, now in a retirement home. (Philosopher's Fist)

She lives thinly on Social Security with no credit-card debt, and her mentor insurance has lapsed. Her earlier recruiting got her asked to leave places and nearly put on lists barring her from schools, "all a misunderstanding, she swears"; her godlike beauty is the only reason she is not on any. Andre suggested that she once tried to recruit Ovain in a conversation that was "a fucking disaster from top to bottom," and she has been handing business cards to other trainers' fighters at the tournament. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The briefing. Mirabeth hands out cards in the briefing tent, where a weasel-man trainer hides his lizard-man protege from her. She objects loudly when Colonel Sparago asks Derk about his "breeding gorbles" and threatens to call the police. After Ovain's outburst she slaps at Mr. Cartwright twice, rolls a 4 and marks Insecure. (Philosopher's Fist)

The social. She eavesdrops on the Pure Human Martial Artists, learns that they expect the "freaks" to be shot by the Secret Service, and passes off her snooping as a lost earring. She then asks whether the president's office has any child-outreach program she can sneak Derk into, and learns of the children's flag event (The Flag Contest). After the wall jump, she lobbies her bridge-club friend by video phone, claiming Derk is 14. She covers the 400 miles to the capital by speed-walking the shoulder of I-95 in pumps behind her parasol. At the social she sells Addison the invented Oil Pyramid for a $400 down payment. (Philosopher's Fist)

The event. At security she helps Derk past the guard's wand with her beauty and never gets scanned herself. A heavyset woman monk among the deputized martial artists recognizes her, but Mirabeth rolls a 12 on Pierce the Mask and the monk lets it pass. She borrows the Detector Wand, tells the guards at the roped-off floor that the president wants "inconspicuous" heroes, and freezes them with Symbol of Authority. She works out that the skylight is the hall's weak point and stations Derk under it. When Derk prepares another jump, she raises a Divine Armor force field around herself and the Werewolf President for about thirty minutes, and the Secret Service moves them to a safe room. (Philosopher's Fist)

Aftermath. After about eighteen hours of debriefing, Mirabeth is questioned by a detective and then by Sparago, who accuses her of using "sexual wiles" on a guard and orders her out. She promises to get Derk insurance and says she hopes to see Sparago at next year's tournament ("You know that I will"). At 2 a.m. she gets Derk's call, removes her curlers, puts on makeup and sets out with her umbrella to fetch him from Wisukonshin. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Derk is her recently adopted mentee. She treats him as a child (kid movie tickets, claiming he is 14) or as an adult (21 for bars) as suits her, once asking "do we know that 21 is an adult in your species?" She has never taught him numbers.
  • Sparago hates her, and she trades barbs with him.

(Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Abilities and equipment
docs.text: Mirabeth uses Legacy-playbook abilities in a Masks-style game (see Game System): godlike beauty, legendary speed (a dignified power-walk rather than a sprint), Symbol of Authority (an order given to an NPC) and Divine Armor (limited-range force-field bubbles). Her Danger is -1. Notable rolls: Assess the Situation 7, 9, 9 and 7; Provoke Someone 10; Pierce the Mask 12 on the monk and a failed 3 on the friend call; Symbol of Authority (Savior) 8. Gear includes the parasol, business cards and curlers. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
• "You can definitely do that, dear. It's called a punch." (Rita, as Mirabeth, when Sparago asks who can channel ki)
  • "You cannot question us about our genitals." (Rita, as Mirabeth)
  • "Social Security in this country should really be looked at." (Rita, as Mirabeth; Andre, as Sparago: "That is literally part of the president's platform.")

(Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Her lies mount over the session: the lost earring, claimed child-psychology credentials, the oil MLM and Derk's age.
  • Dante called her parasol run "Fucking speedster Mary Poppins."

(Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Mr. Cartwright
docs.text:
Non-canon

Mr. Cartwright belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Mr. Cartwright is Colonel Sparago's clipboard aide, who explains why Ovain broke down and shrugs off Mirabeth's slap. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type NPC (non-canon one-shot) Aliases Mr. Briggs Affiliation Aide to Colonel Sparago First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: He is a young or middle-aged man with a receding hairline and big wire-framed glasses, who slinks out of the crowd with a clipboard when Sparago calls for him. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Andre first called him Mr. Briggs, then asked the table to name him and renamed him Mr. Cartwright on the spot. After Ovain's outburst, he explains that Ovain's handlers put him on online dating as part of his treatment and that it has gone badly ("millionaire famous athlete, like seven and a half feet tall, kind of a no-brainer, right?"). He adds that Ovain "may have been doing some journaling recently about killing the president again." (Philosopher's Fist)

Mirabeth slaps at him twice in quick succession. Her Directly Engage a Threat roll is a 4, so he simply ignores her and she marks Insecure. He answers that it is a "shockingly tough dating market out there." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Ovain
docs.text:
Non-canon

Ovain belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Ovain is an anxious, many-eyed alien, the previous tournament champion and a former world conqueror, who attacks the president and is fought into space by Derk. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type NPC (non-canon one-shot) Aliases Ovane (variant spelling) Affiliation World Martial Arts Tournament Status Alive, leaving the planet First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Ovain is a big, smooth alien who wears no clothes, with weird "foam-rubber flesh," radially symmetric hands, a bunch of eyes and a tail. He can levitate and fire jets of white ki fire from his fingers, and he is about seven and a half feet tall. He is chronically anxious: he stands with his arms crossed, rocking and murmuring "This year, this year, this year, it's gonna be okay" in the briefing tent, and he struggles with being a person in public. Andre voiced him. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Ovain won last year's tournament. About ten years earlier he took over the world, then finished a nervous breakdown, became catatonic and was institutionalized. As part of his rehabilitation, the authorities encourage him to funnel his energy into the tournament instead of world domination. His aide Mr. Cartwright says that a program of online dating, added to his treatment, has gone badly and that he has been journaling about killing the president again. Mirabeth once tried to recruit him, in a conversation Andre calls "a fucking disaster from top to bottom." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
When the tournament is suspended over a doping scandal, Ovain starts to panic ("Not this year, not this year, no") and rises out of his chair. Derk walks over and tells him that Mirabeth says he is weird. Ovain, now ten feet in the air with white fire gathering at his hands, points at Colonel Sparago and screams "You did this!" Derk intercepts the blast, and it backscatters into Ovain's eyes. Ovain shoots up through the tent roof and vanishes into the sky. That night the news on the motel TV shows him fighting the nation's military at the edge of the capital. (Philosopher's Fist)

At the Presidential Event Hall the next morning, he crashes through the stained-glass skylight shouting "Not this time! You goddamn dog man! You're not taking this room!" at the Werewolf President. Derk slams him down by the tail and then bear-hugs him, so that his ki jet hits the floor and both fall into the basement. Ovain cries, "You're ruining it! Why, why does this always happen? It's just like Father." Derk tries to bond over dad problems, and Ovain asks how scorpions taste ("Really bad." "Good!") before punching Derk in the groin to no effect. He asks "What are you?" and begins charging a building-shaking attack, with energy dripping off him and congealing into a fluid web. Derk jumps him out through the skylight into space, where Ovain asks again, telepathically, what Derk is. (Philosopher's Fist)

As Derk springboards away, Ovain tells him, "You have been a strange but worthy adversary. I salute you. I am leaving this planet and its Tinder. I'm going back home." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The Werewolf President
docs.text:
Non-canon

The Werewolf President belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Werewolf President is the genial, unnamed werewolf head of state of the one-shot's world. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type NPC (non-canon one-shot) Aliases The president; Mr. Doggy; dog man; werewolf Affiliation Head of state of the one-shot's single world country Status Alive First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The president is a genial "good old boy" with body hair poking up out of his collar and pronounced canines. Society treats his werewolfism as normal, and he turns into a wolf; Derk thinks of him as a dog and calls him "Mr. Doggy." Derk also keeps assuming that anyone in charge, including Colonel Sparago, must be a werewolf. The president's name is never given. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Twice in forty years a tournament champion has taken over the world and killed the president, so the tournament is on thin ice. The current president is a moderate opponent of it: he has not moved to ban it, but if he had the votes in the World Congress he would certainly not veto a bill. (Philosopher's Fist)

At the Presidential Event Hall, Derk presents him with Derk's Flag. He praises the hot dog as a patriotic food and the taco shell as "multiculturalism right there," is troubled by the giant scorpions "attacking the earth" and, on learning that the dog is him, says privately, off the record, that turning into a dog is "pretty cool." He promises to give the flag "real serious consideration" and gives Derk a presidential-seal sticker to "show that you met me." (Philosopher's Fist)

When Ovain attacks, Mirabeth shields the president with a force field and the Secret Service takes him to a safe room. He survives unhurt, and afterward he is taken on a walk to calm him down. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Phoebe Augustine
docs.text:
Phoebe Augustine is Amanda Lucky's horse-loving friend in Radford, Virginia, who is taken from her bed in the night, found alive and crucified above the pulpit of the old church, and rescued by Kurt, only to be reported missing again in 1993.

Type NPC Aliases Phoebe Family Father Derek Augustine; mother Maybelline Augustine; a younger brother Residence Augustine house and barn Status Rescued in Radford Horror 07; reported missing again in Radford Horrors 02 First appearance Mentioned in Radford Horror 03; first seen in Radford Horror 07 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Phoebe is a "horse girl": her room is full of horse things and has none of the UFO material the team had half expected. She is unconscious whenever the team sees her and never speaks on screen (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
Radford Horror 03. She is named, along with Laura Nichols, as a friend of Amanda Lucky and a lead to interview. While searching the Augustine barn, Kurt finds a pink butterfly hair tie in the couch cushions (Radford Horror 03).

Radford Horror 04. Early in the morning Molly Underhill pages the team: Phoebe is missing from her bed, and has been gone perhaps an hour. An elderly neighbor heard a scream at the end of the block and saw a young woman run into the woods, wearing only a long T-shirt, her feet already cut by brambles. The neighbor says the scream woke her and that Phoebe said nothing and ignored calls to come back. Kurt follows her blood trail to a spot about twenty feet from the edge of the river, where it stops (Radford Horror 04). See The Radford Moth.

Radford Horror 05. Kurt searches her room: one bedroom slipper by the window, the other across the room at an odd angle, as if she walked to the window and ran off so fast she left them behind. From this the team concludes she saw something from the window and fled. Her diary shows Amanda was seeing someone besides Dean Lawson and that Phoebe disliked Dean. Her parents say she fought with Laura Nichols, that she and Amanda fought over Dean, and that one of the Whateley twins had a crush on her. Her father hands over a Polaroid of the night dress she wore for the APB (Radford Horror 05).

Radford Horror 06. She is still missing. Her father is found torturing Dr. Lori, whom he believes kidnapped her (Radford Horror 06). See Dr. Lori.

Radford Horror 07. In the old church the team sees a woman crucified to the wall above the pulpit, and Kurt recognizes her as Phoebe. With his multi-tool he works the nails out (a 10 on Act Under Pressure) and gets her down, unconscious, then carries her out of the burning church during the fight with the moth (an 11). He radios Molly: "We got the Phoebe Augustine girl and the Whateley boy" (Radford Horror 07). See Crucifixion MO.

Radford Horror 08. In his journal, Wilbur Whateley records that Amanda and Phoebe visited, that he does not think Amanda knows about his secret "but I feel like Phoebe might" (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text: In 1993 Sheriff Underhill tells Daniel Webster and the team that Phoebe is missing again: after she vanished, the sheriff's office was told she had gone to a rehab in California "like Narconon," but no one could reach her, no one in her family knew of any drug problem, and scary lawyers threatened anyone who asked (Radford Horrors 02). See LA treatment cover story.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Amanda Lucky: friend; they fought over Dean.
  • Derek Augustine and Maybelline Augustine: parents.
  • Wilbur Whateley: one of the Whateley twins had a crush on her; Wilbur mentions her in his journal.
  • Kurt Larson: her rescuer.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Wilbur's journal gives only the name "Phoebe," alongside Amanda; the wiki takes this to be Derek's daughter.

docs.title: Ponytail Lady
docs.text:
Ponytail Lady is the fan name for the blonde, holstered staffer at Robert Bigelow's rented big house, who greets the task force with sweet tea, shows them the camera footage, lends them bicycles and later shares a night watch with the replica of Andrew Howard.

Type NPC Aliases blonde guard; unnamed security woman; woman at the big house Affiliation Bigelow's research operation Status Alive (as of Walkers 07) First appearance Walkers 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: She is a blonde woman in sunglasses and a ponytail, with a hip holster. When Zack asks whether she is attractive, Andre rules "Reasonably." She is never named; "Ponytail Lady" is the players' label for her (Walkers 02, Walkers 07).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
When the party arrives at the big house in Walkers 02, she is waiting by the door and greets Walt, asking "These the feds?" She asks them to leave their weapons at the door. Kurt Larson answers "No," so they talk on the porch, where she goes to fetch Bigelow and offers sweet tea; the party asks for well water, and she brings out fresh buttered bread and a pitcher of sweet tea. She tells the party she recognizes "your friend from Leno." Her house rules are that the most important thing is to keep Bigelow happy and the second is to keep the goose Nancy happy. She then goes back inside to make sure the roast does not burn (Walkers 02).

In Walkers 04 the party hikes back to the big house after their rental disappears, and Andre describes her as the woman they met "the other day." She has already looked at the camera footage and takes them to a bank of TVs with the tape cued up. The blurry image shows the car as a slightly different patch of gray beside the house, which seems to rise but is too indistinct to point out to anyone. She tells them the electromagnetic meters spiked, and that the spikes line up with the substation pop and the earlier moment the car shifted, although the graph is noisy. She then lends the party dusty road bikes for the trip to Roosevelt, asking them to "bring these back, or pay us back for them" (Walkers 04). See also Bigelow's recordings.

In Walkers 07 the group sets shifts at the big house, and Andrew takes the first watch with the Ponytail Lady while the rest sleep upstairs. By this point Andrew is the replica, which Rita has been secretly playing since the end of the gym scene earlier in the same episode; she mulls over "blowing myself up." The watch carries past midnight into November 3rd, Election Day (Walkers 07). See Andrew Howard (duplicate).

docs.title: Primenthol "Prim" Greengrass
docs.text:
Primenthol "Prim" Greengrass is the sister of the missing Covenant member Willow Greengrass, a podiatrist and former member of the Covenant who had been staying in Dahlonega, Georgia for about a month when Willow disappeared.

Type NPC Aliases Prim; Primenthol Affiliation Former member of The Covenant Occupation Podiatrist Status Alive (as of Appalachia 04) First appearance Appalachia 01 (named in the case file)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Prim has long flowing hair and wears unremarkable clothes. She is staying in room 11 of the former Best Western Hotel and Suites, which has bedbugs; she keeps bedbug traps at the foot of the bed, and there is only the one chair. She had been expecting the police (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Background
docs.text: According to Prim, their mother joined the Covenant when the sisters were very young, and both girls were renamed "in the style of the group" at age three. Prim left the Covenant, went to college and became a podiatrist. Their mother died a couple of years ago, and Prim kept the name rather than changing it out of respect. She is no longer a church member and says much of the doctrine fails the "sniff test". She jokes that she got off easier than Willow, since "there's a good nickname for Primenthol" (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Sheriff Burke's case file lists her alongside the missing Willow, Gene Cartwright and Edward Nick. The sheriff tells the team she was already back in town before Willow disappeared, about a month earlier. Zack's Huell says he thinks she might be lying (Appalachia 01).

In Appalachia 02 the team interviews her. Zack questions her "Commander Shepard style". Willow had no enemies, suitors or outside friends, and Prim is certain Willow would have come to her. She explains that the Covenant's clay baptisms, divine meteor and visionary peach drink are mostly harmless, and calls its prophet Elijah Ray "a pretty nice guy. For a bigamist". A prophetic dream and a TV report of a shooting star led him to move the congregation to Auraria. Prim warns the team never to accept a vision quest (see Covenant Peach Preserves). She also takes Andrew into the bathroom to learn his embarrassing middle name, which stays secret at the table, and remarks that he is a feminine guy; the table piles on.

In Appalachia 04 she is only mentioned. A Covenant member, River, says Willow was upset because her sister kept trying to convince her to leave.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Zack played the interview as a Commander Shepard-style questioning, and the table made paragon and renegade jokes at Prim's expense (Appalachia 02).
  • In the same episode Kurt asks the bootlegger Frotter Comstock whether he knows "a Primenthol Greengrass", when the missing woman is Willow.

docs.title: Unnamed pharmacist
docs.text:
The unnamed pharmacist is the nervous counter pharmacist at the Radford pharmacy who admits off the record that the paper record for Amanda Lucky's Vicodin prescription is missing.

Type NPC Aliases the pharmacist Affiliation Radford pharmacy Status Alive (as of Radford Horror 02) First appearance Radford Horror 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: He is a middle-aged man working the counter ("Next, one at a time, please. What's the name?"). He is cooperative but increasingly nervous as the questions go on (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
After the interview with Dr. Lori, Kurt Larson and the agents visit the pharmacy with the bottle of Vicodin found in Amanda's room. The pharmacist confirms the computer holds a record of Vicodin for Amanda Lucky under Dr. Lori, entered about a year earlier, started about four months after her Xanax and filled regularly since. He explains that prescriptions are phoned in, logged in a paper book, then entered into the computer, and that anyone with the password could alter the computer records. Most of the pharmacy's Vicodin, he says, goes to Lori's older teenage patients. He will not name suspects among the stock-room teenagers, but says he would never let Dean Lawson near the store; McCready, he adds, "works up at his folks' place," and he rules out the Whateley boys and the Nichols girl.

He calls his boss, then goes to the back to look for the paper original. When he returns fifteen or twenty minutes later he says he cannot talk to them. Kurt makes a Manipulate Someone roll (a 10) and the pharmacist tells him, off the record, that he cannot find the paper copy, which he calls "a big problem." Kurt leaves him the number of the Pay n' Stay (Radford Horror 02).

In Radford Horror 05, Molly Underhill tells the team that Mr. Augustine is one of the town's pharmacists as well as a romance novelist, and Dante names him prime suspect for the stolen paperwork. When Kurt asks Augustine about the prescriptions, Augustine says he filled the prescription for Amanda "a couple of times" and that he has already been told of the "record error" (Radford Horror 05). See Derek Augustine.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• It is never established whether the counter pharmacist of Radford Horror 02 is Derek Augustine or one of his colleagues; the team suspects Augustine because of the paperwork, but Andre never says so.
  • The pharmacy's brand is never named; Ezra jokes that it could be a Walgreens or a grocery-store pharmacy.

docs.title: The radio contact
docs.text:
The radio contact is an unnamed, cheerful voice on the task force's pocket radio who supplies the anti-worm agent, tracks the angel thing and plans the nuclear shot with Kurt in the finale of The Summer Service.

Type NPC (voice only) Aliases Mystery voice; unnamed radio contact Affiliation The mystery covert group Status Unknown (as of Summer Service 06) First appearance Summer Service 06 Played by Andre (game master)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The contact is heard only over the radio. He is cheerful and casual and swears freely. He is relieved when Kurt Larson tells him the team already knows about the worms and the creature, and delighted by Kurt's news of the Davy Crockett. He says he is allowed to tell them only things they already know, and that some things in life have to remain a mystery (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Earlier contact. In Summer Service 05, voices on the team's frequency snap, "We're the goddamn Marines. Get off the line," and order everyone to switch to frequency B. In Summer Service 06 the contact apologizes for "my commanding officer's rudeness earlier" and says "we were in a tight situation, and he got a little heated." Later in the same episode Andre has the team receive updates from "the Marines," which ties the two together (Summer Service 05; Summer Service 06).

The call. In the finale the radio crackles as the glowing angel thing turns back toward the sea. The voice asks whether the explosion was the team; it was the claymore they set off on the truck. He tells them, "you pissed it off." Kurt summarizes the situation (worm-controlled people and the big glowing thing), and the voice reveals that his side has an agent for the worms and a "Casaba," which cannot be fired from the ground and cannot be flown in the storm (Summer Service 06).

Kurt asks "Can you keep a secret?" and reveals the team's Davy Crockett with its W54 warhead. The voice does not recognize the model name ("It might be different where I'm from"), learns that the yield is half a kiloton, and calls it the best news he has heard all day. They agree on a plan: the creature is heading for the nuclear power plant, where the convoy of infected will engage plant security and force the creature out of the water, and the team will take a long shot from a vantage point. The voice offers to track the creature and report its positions (Summer Service 06).

The agent. The voice describes the anti-worm agent as a liquid poison. He will dump some in the ocean to deal with contaminated fish, and Kurt suggests crop-dusting after the storm. He says, "we're gonna have to kill all these people," but "better to do it once they no longer have special support," and adds that the agent "won't kill anything else, probably." Andrew Howard grabs the radio and asks whether the "advanced team" was dead at the bottom of the ocean; the voice answers, "Oh, you do know about the advanced team," and apologizes that the broad-spectrum nerve agent leaked when "we got blown up." He warns the team not to soften up the convoy beforehand because "they got like eight" worm bags. Kurt winks at the radio and the voice winks back (Summer Service 06).

The shot. After the creature dies, the contact whoops, "That was awesome!", tells the team to get away from there, urges them to get iodine, and says he will leave "a little present on the road" and dump the rest of the agent in the ocean. The team later finds the half-empty canister on the freeway (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: His name, his commanding officer, his organization and what "where I'm from" means. He claims experience with nuclear plants ("I've done this before"), which Kurt doubts (Summer Service 06).

docs.text:
Quote

Andre (as the radio contact): "I'm only allowed to tell you stuff you already know." (Summer Service 06)

Andre (as the radio contact): "I don't recognize the model name. It might be different where I'm from." (Summer Service 06)

Quote

Andre (as the radio contact): "Oh, those things are way overbuilt. It'll be fine. They're designed for you to fly a 747 into 'em." (Summer Service 06)

Quote

Andre (as the radio contact): "That was awesome! Get the fuck away from there." (Summer Service 06)
