docs.title: Ram and Arms innkeeper
docs.text:
The Ram and Arms innkeeper is the very old, cheerful and formal keeper of the Ram and Arms Inn in Marblehead, who checks the task force in at the very end of The Radford Horror and gives them the Sons of Adam Bible.

Type NPC Aliases The innkeeper Affiliation Ram and Arms Inn; evidently the Sons of Adam Status Alive (as of Radford Horror 08) First appearance Radford Horror 08 Played by Andre (game master)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: He is a very old man, sunken into himself with age, with what Andre calls the "Crypt Keeper haircut," long only around the outside of his head. Andre says he looks as if the team has startled him back to life. He is cheerful and formal (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The last third of Radford Horror 08 is the opening of the Marblehead case. When the team arrives at the inn, he offers four single rooms and a hot fish breakfast at 6 a.m. sharp, and laundry service. He says business has been quiet "except for those fellas from the government" about a week earlier, meaning the missing EPA/USGS survey team. He agrees to send up what the survey team left behind, on condition that the new guests pay the cleaning fee for the rooms (Radford Horror 08).

He offers the team a choice of Bibles: King James, Gideon's, or "the local flavor, which I highly recommend, the Sons of Adam Bible." They take the local one, a thick, clearly self-published volume with an illustration of Jesus parting the water inside the front cover, and he invites them to attend services. About fifteen minutes later he hauls up a large cardboard box of the survey team's belongings, which the team searches in Andrew Howard's room: suitcases, clothes, IDs, technical manuals, sampling equipment and several wallets (Radford Horror 08); see Survey team's field notes and Sons of Adam Bible.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• In Summer Service 01, Andre describes the man at the same front desk as having "the Crypt Keeper haircut" and shows that his name tag reads "Jester." The episodes strongly imply that the innkeeper of Radford Horror 08 and Jester are the same man, but never state it outright, and the innkeeper is not seen again as such.
  • His promotion of the Sons of Adam Bible and its services is the only sign of his affiliation with the church; the episodes never state it.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Red Dutchford
docs.text:
Red Dutchford is the name a Pay n' Stay guest in a fishing hat and heavy coat registered under, a man who drove a brown station wagon and stayed in the motel for only a few hours on the day the team's belongings were disturbed.

Type NPC (alias; identity never established) Aliases fishing-hat man Location Pay n' Stay Status Unknown First appearance Radford Horror 04 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: According to the night clerk Rutherford, the guest wore a big fishing hat, sunglasses and a heavy coat. He checked in around 2 p.m., took a room on the far side of the building, rolled up in a brown station wagon, left no contact information and was seen leaving that evening. The clerk assumed he was a prostitute (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The Biz asks Rutherford whether anyone has been around the motel, because the agents' belongings had been shifted while they were out; the cleaning service had not come that day. Rutherford volunteers the fishing-hat guest and, on the Biz's prompting, says he signed in as "Red Dutchford" (Radford Horror 04).

The players notice that Dr. Lori drives a brown station wagon, and the Biz describes the doctor to Rutherford: five foot seven or eight, with a beard, mustache and brown hair. Rutherford says the man had facial hair and brown hair and was neither particularly tall nor short, but does not recognize the description as anyone local. Zack points out that station wagons of the era were almost all brown.

Kurt bump-keys the far-side room (Act Under Pressure, with a Help roll from Andrew, who keeps the clerk talking until about two in the morning). The room had never been lived in and had been wiped down, but not thoroughly, and Kurt lifts a partial fingerprint, which the team plans to compare against prints from Lori's office. Earlier, the windowsill of the team's own room had yielded only glove prints (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Dutchford is never mentioned again after Radford Horror 04, and it is never established who searched the team's rooms. The players wonder whether it was Dr. Lori, but nothing confirms it.

docs.title: Robert Bigelow
docs.text:
Robert Bigelow is a Texas real estate billionaire and UFO researcher who rents the big house and barn on Sherman Ranch near Ballard, Utah, and hosts the task force during The Walkers in Skin. He shares his name with a real-world businessman; in Walkers 06 Andre confirms that it is "the same guy," and that the real Bigelow's company holds the patent for inflatable space habitats.

Type NPC Aliases Bigelow; the space guy; the billionaire; Mr. Moneybags; Roger Bigelow (slip) Affiliation Bigelow's research operation Status Alive (as of Walkers 08); fate unknown afterward First appearance Walkers 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In Walkers 02 he is a sour-faced, middle-aged man in an expensive suit who talks UFOs and space, and who has a satellite-phone meeting to get to. Andre admits at the table that the character "almost got his own voice, and then I got lazy." In Walkers 07 he is furious, storming around a house full of sleepy, confused staff (Walkers 02, Walkers 07).

docs.title: Meeting the task force
docs.text:
Carl Gardner of the Salt Lake City field office names Bigelow as a real estate baron who is renting the ranch house; Bigelow's security man had reported shooting someone, though the physical evidence did not support it. Gardner also recommends Bigelow's hotel, the Budget Suites of America (Walkers 02).

At the big house Bigelow tells the party that the quantity of reported UFO phenomena stands out across a radius of hundreds of miles. He has researched the team ("a lot of interesting stories follow in your wake") and says the Bill Clinton affair "didn't even make the list." He slips by calling Alberta Wilmarth "Madeline." His staff record everything onto big tape reels, with unexplained heat signatures and electromagnetic and electrical readings, and he says some of the sheep exploded. He already knows about the live sperm in Ballard's water (water contamination), adds that it also contains a lot of arsenic, and says his people run theirs through reverse osmosis (Walkers 02). See Sherman Ranch phenomenon.

In Walkers 03 and Walkers 04 he is mostly offscreen. His staff, many of them on university rotations, are fed from the food he buys in bulk, and Walt "Coyote" Murphy clears the party's night patrol with him. In Walkers 03 a Ballard local says Bigelow gave him the same warning about the tap water, without saying why (Walkers 03).

docs.title: The white ring and the Black Sun
docs.text: After a white floodlight wakes the party, Bigelow phones to ask, "Do you folks see a light?" He then shows them a sky-camera video of a bright white ring and asks about the Black Sun: the Nazis appropriated it, he says, but it has a long history in pagan mythology. He quotes Revelation 6:12. Several staff have had nightmares (one, Marina, dreams only of drowning). He has his staff psychiatrist debrief the party for about 45 minutes and arranges for a dentist in Roosevelt. He calls the event "one of the most clear-cut events we've ever had here," notes a "definite nonlinear trajectory" on many of his graphs and says they "may be on the verge of making contact." Kurt (addressing him as "Mr. Moneybags") persuades him to set up "a big ring of cameras" around the party (Walkers 05). See the white ring.

docs.title: Protocol blue
docs.text: In Walkers 07 Bigelow rages that someone has stolen all his hard drives, tapes and recordings, along with three of his employees, and that the barn has been cleared out too: "Somebody had keys to the whole fucking place." He sends two guards to follow Coyote and the injured intruder to the hospital. After Kurt Larson tells him of the missing students, the cover-up and the sheriff's flight, he declares "protocol blue," unlocks "the big cabinet," and his staff come downstairs with SPAS-12 shotguns and M16s. He sets a defensive perimeter around the ground floor and asks the party to stay as backup (Walkers 07). See Bigelow's recordings.

docs.title: Walkers 08
docs.text: Bigelow appears only as the offscreen host of the armed compound, where one of his burly enforcers makes pancakes for the on-edge, armed staff. The party considers recruiting the remainder of his security force, and Rita worries aloud about "worm people" among his staff (Walkers 08).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Walkers 06, Andre first calls the real-world Bigelow "Roger" before correcting himself to Robert.

docs.title: Rooftop watcher
docs.text:
The rooftop watcher is an unidentified man with binoculars and a small electronic device who is seen on rooftops in Radford, Virginia, and whose white van, fitted with fake plates, tails the task force.

Type NPC (unidentified) Aliases man on the post office roof; man in the white van; white van crew Affiliation Unknown; not the sheriff's department Status Unknown First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In Radford Horror 01 the watcher is a man in black with hair and no hat, holding binoculars; he ducks when he realizes he has been noticed and is more careful afterward (Radford Horror 01). In the cold open of Radford Horror 02, the man on a rooftop has close-cropped light brown hair, sunglasses and a nondescript dark suit, and carries a flashlight, a briefcase and a small electronic device (Radford Horror 02). The episodes never say outright whether these are the same man.

docs.title: Radford Horror 01
docs.text: While the team eats at the Lonely Mountain Diner, Kurt goes out to use a payphone and spots a man in black with binoculars on the roof of the post office across the street, apparently looking in the team's direction. He phones the sheriff's station and asks Deputy Underhill whether the sheriff's department has any stakeouts or surveillance in the area; she says, "No, not to my knowledge." Kurt memorizes the cars in the post office lot (a Sharp roll of 13) on his way back and quietly warns the team. The waitress, Sheila, checks the window and sees the man but does not recognize him. Kurt tells her that around 85% of the time it is just a birdwatcher (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: Radford Horror 02
docs.text: The episode opens with a cold open on a rooftop. A man watches something through binoculars, is startled by what he sees and swears under his breath, sets a flashlight aside, keys at a small electronic device from his briefcase, snaps the case shut, runs down the fire escape, gets into a white van and speeds off (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Radford Horror 03
docs.text: Driving back from a stakeout, the team realizes a white van is tailing their car at a discreet distance. They pull into a McDonald's drive-thru to break the van's line of sight; the van parks across the street in the Radio Shack lot, then pulls away while they are still ordering. The team gets its license plate number (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Radford Horror 04
docs.text: Kurt asks the sheriff to run the plates of the van that was tailing them, noting that it fled when the team tried to approach it. The team's rooms at the Pay n' Stay are searched the same day, but nothing ties the search to the watcher (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Radford Horror 05
docs.text: The plates come back invalid: they belong to someone else. Molly Underhill puts out an APB for an unmarked white van, and the diner's waitress asks whether the van is connected to "the guy on the roof" (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Radford Horror 06
docs.text: The team remarks that their sedan is the car "that's been clocked by the guys that are tailing us." The U-Haul that kidnaps Dr. Lori the same night is a different vehicle, driven by Derek Augustine (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The episodes never reveal who the watcher and the van crew work for, why they followed the task force, or what the electronic device does. Their plates were borrowed, and no link to the cleanup crew or the NSA is ever stated.

docs.title: Ross Perot
docs.text:
Ross Perot is the President of the United States in the campaign's alternate 1993, the winner of a 1992 election that the Paranatural Incident Task Force helped to upend. He is a fictional version of the real businessman and candidate, written as a character in the show's alternate history; nothing here describes the real person.

Type NPC (fictionalized historical figure) Aliases Perot; President Perot; the President-elect Affiliation President of the United States (from January 1993) Status Alive, in office (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Roulet Estate 03 (voice only); first mentioned in Appalachia 07 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Perot is almost entirely an offstage character. He is heard once, on the telephone, and otherwise acts through subordinates: Big Bill carries his decisions to the team before the inauguration, and FBI Director Rudy Giuliani carries them afterwards. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)

Andre looked up the real Perot's voice before performing the phone call; Dante said the result sounded like a D&D goblin. (Roulet Estate 03)

He has no patience for paranormal reporting. Shown the team's Radford file, his reaction, as Andre recapped it, was "What the fuck is this? This says it was like a giant bug." Huell Kendrick is more hopeful: Perot will straighten out the economy, because "He's a businessman." (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: The 1992 campaign
docs.text:
During The Things in Appalachia, in October 1992, Perot is the third candidate in a race between George H. W. Bush and Bill Clinton. When the Georgia scandal breaks, Huell predicts that it is "not going to stop my man Ross Perot", and Zack looks up the real result for the table: about 19 percent of the vote, one of the most successful third-party runs. (Appalachia 07)

The Georgia case changes the race. After the Clinton surveillance scandal, which Andre calls "the double scandal", Perot is above 45 percent in most polls and Bush is clearly ahead only in Texas. Andre later explained the alternate history: Perot "just needed two October surprises", and one event supplied both, with the incumbent caught spying on a challenger who was himself caught in a sex scandal. (Walkers 01, Walkers 08)

The Walkers in Skin is set in the days around the election. The race is described as a tight three-way contest a few days out; Election Day, November 3, 1992, falls during the night at Ballard High School; the next morning Donald McManley reports that the count is unfinished and that Perot has taken Ohio. As the team drives out of Roosevelt with the wounded, the radio announces that Perot has won. (Walkers 02, Walkers 07, Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: President-elect
docs.text:
On Christmas Eve 1992 Big Bill tells the team what the President-elect thinks of them. Perot believes the task force is "a cover for Bush's weaponization of the FBI against his political enemies". He has asked Big Bill to resign, will disband and reassign the task force on Inauguration Day, and is forming a task force of his own to look into the "insurgency incidents", the official cover story for the Utah disaster. Dante's hope that Perot might reward the team for winning him the election comes to nothing. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

The team's drunken trip to the Roulet house on Inauguration Day 1993 began, according to Diane, with talk of finding proof for Ross Perot. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: President
docs.text:
By spring 1993 the task force is gone and its members are scattered. Andrew Howard is alone in a New York hotel room when the phone rings and the President himself is on the line. Andrew asks whether he has the right Andrew Howard. (Roulet Estate 03)

Quote

"This is the President of the United States. I need you to come in. Something's happened in Virginia." (Andre as Perot, Roulet Estate 03)

What had happened is laid out at the start of The Radford Horrors. More people had gone missing in Radford. Perot sent five career agents of his own choosing, the missing FBI task force, and they vanished too. He then read the original team's classified reports, found them unacceptable, and when Director William Sessions stood by them ("it's a giant bug") fired him on the spot, with no transition. Giuliani, a New York lawyer and longtime friend and supporter of Perot, was appointed the same morning. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

Perot's orders, relayed by Giuliani, bring the old team back only as consultants under Special Agent Daniel Webster, whom he trusts: find the missing agents, and establish an "acceptable fact pattern" for the first Radford case. After the standoff at the Safe Environment Fund fence, Webster is reprimanded: the President wants no more "cowboy shit" and everything done by the book. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

In Moscow, Boris Yeltsin asks the Biz a few questions about Perot. The Biz says he knows very little, and keeps to himself his belief that Perot will probably "ax the whole thing". The impression he gets is that the Russians had hoped to destabilize the United States and now face a counterpart they do not understand. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Daniel Webster. Webster did State Department logistics in 1978 for the operation to rescue Perot's employees in Iran, and Perot trusts him. Webster shares Perot's view of the old task force: that Bush picked a group of "fuck-up agents" he could use for political dirty work. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Rudy Giuliani. A vocal supporter made FBI Director on the morning Sessions was fired. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)
  • The task force. Perot disbanded it as a political instrument of his predecessor, then had to call its leader personally when his own team disappeared. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)
  • George H. W. Bush. His defeated predecessor, whose FBI he distrusts. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text:
• What Perot found "unacceptable" in the Radford reports. Dante's guess was that he does not like reading that it was "aliens and shit"; Ezra's was that he objected to a cover story. Andre's recap in the next session supports Dante: Perot could not believe the report said a giant bug. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)
  • It is never established whether the task force Perot promised for the "insurgency incidents" is the same group as the five agents lost in Radford. (Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The players call the setting "the Perot-verse". Zack first asked "Have we entered the Perot-verse?" on the in-fiction Election Day. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08, Radford Horrors 04)
  • When Andre settled on a domestic insurgency as the cover story for Utah, Dante's reaction was: "Guess what, Ross Perot? You're gonna have a rough first fucking day." (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Webster's reference to the 1978 Iran rescue is to a real event in Perot's business career. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • While the table speculated about the future of the Perot-verse, Andre offered a bureaucratic mistake in which the United States accidentally nukes North Dakota. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Rudy Giuliani
docs.text:
Rudy Giuliani is the FBI Director in the campaign's alternate 1993, installed by President Ross Perot after William Sessions is fired, who puts Daniel Webster in charge of the task force and demands an "acceptable fact pattern" for the Radford case.

Type NPC Aliases Director Giuliani Affiliation FBI (Director) Status In office (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horrors 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Giuliani is a balding, dark-haired, lawyerly man with an expensive watch and a red tie. He introduces himself as "a lawyer from New York" with a long career in corruption investigation and a friend of the president for many years. He is new to the job and says so ("I'm still very new here"). When he walks out of his office, Kurt's player Dante reacts with "My God, it's Dick Cheney." Over the later episodes he is brisk and skeptical ("maybe they're legitimately insane") but not unfriendly toward Webster (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 04).

In this alternate timeline Andre describes him as an up-and-coming New York lawyer known for high-profile anti-corruption cases, with a flair for the dramatic (Radford Horrors 02). See Alternate history.

docs.title: Radford Horrors 01
docs.text:
The team arrives at FBI headquarters the morning after finding signs of the Biz's abduction. The building is tense: in a corridor an acquaintance named Todd tells Kurtis that Perot fired Director Sessions about three hours earlier. Giuliani, appointed that morning at Perot's request, invites the team in and says Daniel Webster and he "came to an understanding" earlier. He explains that there are a number of missing people, that the original FBI task force sent to investigate has gone AWOL, and that Perot found its classified reports unacceptable while Sessions stood by their quality. The old team are to act as consultants under Webster's operational authority, "strictly there for informational purposes." Their goals are to establish what happened to the previous FBI team (see missing FBI task force) and, second, to establish an acceptable fact pattern for the previous investigation. The episode ends on his question "Now, what can you tell me about Radford, Virginia?" (Radford Horrors 01).

Andre (as Giuliani)

...to establish an acceptable fact pattern for the previous investigation.

See Acceptable fact pattern.

docs.title: Radford Horrors 02
docs.text: He does not appear. Andre recaps how Perot read the intelligence from the team's last case ("What the fuck is this? This says it was like a giant bug."), Sessions confirmed "it's a giant bug," and Perot fired him and appointed Giuliani. The priorities Giuliani gave the team are to find and recover the previous task force and to determine an acceptable fact pattern for the previous case. The team flies out about noon the next day (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Radford Horrors 03
docs.text: After the standoff at the fenced Safe Environment Fund site, Giuliani calls Webster on a hospital hallway phone: "tell me about this thing with the fence." Webster claims probable cause and says the guard shot at them and one agent fired back. Giuliani warns that a Bivens lawsuit is expected, that the FBI is getting a retroactive warrant to avoid the "poison fruit" provision, that FBI counsel will decide whether the probable-cause claim is defensible, and that a formal reprimand is possible. Had they found the missing agents, he adds, it would be a different story. He asks whether the team wants to press charges against the guard who tased them, and mentions that the lawyers who contacted the FBI reported a spear gun (Radford Horrors 03). See Bivens lawsuit.

docs.title: Radford Horrors 04
docs.text: Webster calls him again. Giuliani recalls the spear gun and calls it reckless to run "lunatics in the field," then hears about the team's rabies treatment. He wants the missing FBI agents found in the next twenty-four hours, "dead or alive." Webster passes on the team's suspicions about the Safe Environment Fund and the missing people's letters about an addiction center in LA; Giuliani asks whether it is "Narcanon with an A or with an O" and says he already has a man looking into the fund (Radford Horrors 04). See Safe Environment Fund.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Ross Perot: the president who appointed him.
  • Daniel Webster: his man in charge of the team.
  • The task force: consultants who report through Webster; he is skeptical of them.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Giuliani asks whether "Narcanon" is spelled with an A or an O; the organization he means is Narconon.

docs.title: Rutherford
docs.text:
Rutherford is the Pay n' Stay motel clerk in Radford, Virginia, a UFO believer who listens to Art Bell, never seems to leave his desk, preaches the Anunnaki, and sells the Biz DMT; his name is given only in Radford Horror 04.

Type NPC Aliases Pay n' Stay clerk; Sailor; night clerk; Mr. Hotel; the weirdo at the Pay n' Stay Occupation Motel clerk at the Pay n' Stay Status Alive at his post (as of Radford Horror 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01 (unnamed) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Rutherford is a sketchy, dirty-looking man with big, unkempt hair, sitting behind the open front-office window of the Econo-Thrift Pay n' Stay with UFO posters on the walls, a conspiracy radio program on (Art Bell) and a book about abductions in front of him. He rents rooms at $26 a night, cash only, keeps the keys "hostage" while he talks, and sells coffee at 50 cents a cup. He never seems to leave his desk. Kurt calls him "Sailor" (Radford Horror 01). In Radford Horror 04 he greets the Biz as "Mr. G.I. Tract," a callback to the team's stomach trouble, and the Biz calls him "Mr. Hotel" (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Radford Horror 01
docs.text: When the team checks in, the clerk warns them to be careful around Radford: there are "people walking around this place [who] haven't even been born," people go missing, and there are lights in the sky. He says his father believed Radford was cursed because the local armory made the guncotton for the atom bomb (see Radford Arsenal). He believes in good and bad aliens but thinks the bad ones dominate, remarking that "when they're sending UFOs, they aren't sending their best" (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: Radford Horror 02
docs.text: He does not appear. The twins' father, Yobiah Whateley, says Abelforth talked to "that weirdo down at the Pay n' Stay" a couple of times and calls him a pervert, adding that the boy tried to convince him to get something called Usenet. Dick Baxter finds the missing boy's radio tuned to the same station the clerk listens to (Radford Horror 02). See Abe's radio.

docs.title: Radford Horror 04
docs.text:
The Biz chats up the clerk, who gives his name as Rutherford. He theorizes that the visitors are punishing humanity for its sin (citing Richard Feynman on physics having known sin), that Radford is cursed, and that they are the Anunnaki, spirits who created the universe to harvest energy from it and who can be seen by taking certain substances known to ancient peoples. After a Manipulate Someone roll of 10, he sells the Biz $40 of DMT ("Dimitri") in a Jack Daniel's bottle with a hole melted in the top as a pipe. He says "it's all legal... you can't make spirituality illegal" and is not religious. Asked whether anyone has been around, he says cleaning comes only every second Thursday, that he "mists" the rooms with Jack Daniel's between guests, and that a guest in a fishing hat checked in under the name Red Dutchford. Andrew later keeps him talking until about two in the morning while Kurt bump-keys that guest's room (Radford Horror 04).

Andre (as Rutherford)

It's like a roller coaster, except you talk to God.

Andre (as Rutherford)

You watch out for those aliens. Don't let 'em put you in a pain dimension.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Andre produced the name Rutherford at the table with a random name generator, as Ezra points out in Radford Horror 04.

docs.title: Sheila
docs.text:
Sheila is the chatty waitress at the Lonely Mountain Diner in Radford, Virginia, who feeds the task force across both Radford cases and eventually supplies the camera footage of the gray van raid.

Type NPC Aliases Diner waitress; the waitress Affiliation Lonely Mountain Diner Status Alive (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Sheila is a friendly, talkative local with a dry sense of humor, opinionated about Forest Service funding. She works the 1950s-style vinyl diner, where the menu runs to a "heart attack special," All-Americans and a superb blackcurrant pie (Radford Horror 01). By The Radford Horrors she calls Kurt "secret agent man" and Huell "sweetie," and serves a local root beer made with real sarsaparilla ("which is illegal") (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
On the team's first morning in Radford, Sheila serves breakfast and blames the disappearances on careless hikers, the woods and bears. When Kurt quietly warns the team about the man on the post office roof, Sheila checks the window and sees him, but does not recognize him ("So this isn't like a clock tower situation?"). She does recognize the red Miata with the cut muffler that roars past and names its driver as Dean Lawson, and she calls Sheriff Frank Roosevelt a "straight shooter." (Radford Horror 01)

Four episodes later the team returns for lunch. The waitress asks whether the white van is linked to "the guy on the roof" (see Rooftop watcher) and is asked to report any unmarked white van. Huell orders a pyramid stack of pancakes taller than his head; his bedbug bites are obvious, and the waitress threatens to burn the diner down for the insurance money if bedbugs return, blaming the Pay n' Stay as "Motel Patient Zero." (Radford Horror 05)

Radford Horror 05

"If this place gets bedbugs again, I'm going to burn it to the ground for the insurance money, and you didn't hear me say that."

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
When the task force returns, Sheila greets Kurt as "secret agent man," asks after "the one who blew up the toilet" (the Biz, Dick Baxter) and Huell's foot, and calls the team local heroes for saving "that lady." She is horrified by the state of the bathroom. Across the street the former laundromat has become the neon Douglas Pinball Emporium. (Radford Horrors 02)

In Radford Horrors 04 Kurt volunteers to face her over the bathroom. His Manipulate Someone roll succeeds: he apologizes for Huell, later offers a hundred-dollar tip and asks for her camera footage. She fixes the "on the fritz" camera and finds the raid on the emporium: a gray van at about 4 to 5 a.m., five men (one with a long brown ponytail, the rest with military haircuts, some with covered faces), a non-human shadow moving inside the window, and three men carrying out two bags before the van peels out. See Diner security tape and Gray van crew. (Radford Horrors 04)

She adds that gray vans started appearing a couple of months earlier, around the "right to roam" fuss over the woods and possibly tied to the Safe Environment Fund, and that vans also crowded around the Ferry Lodge during "the raid"; she dislikes the Lodge's new snooty owners. Kurt takes the tape, promising to return it, and gives her his number. She also tells the team that the homeless man (Billy Thornton) hangs around the Pay n' Stay, and she has been feeding him pancakes. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Sheila is named aloud in Radford Horror 01 and Radford Horrors 02; in Radford Horror 05 and Radford Horrors 04 the team deals only with "the waitress."
  • Kurt's Manipulate Someone roll in Radford Horrors 04 comes up 11, despite his Charm of 0.

docs.title: Shelly (ape woman)
docs.text:
Shelly is an ape woman whom Jan Martense found drugged in the van of a dead man with NSA identification and later used to breed the ape-men of the Dahlonega gold mines.

Type NPC (creature) Aliases Shelly; the ape woman Affiliation Held by Jan's Conspiracy Status Unknown (as of Walkers 01) First appearance Walkers 01 (described in an interview)

Shelly never appears on screen. Everything known about her comes from Jan's account to Kurt at Black Site Omaha in Walkers 01.

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Jan named her Shelly and thought of her as "a bright chimp". She was "just a primate", with nothing supernatural about her, but she was very strong, unusually good at voice mimicry, and aged unusually quickly. This held even more true of her offspring. Jan says they "went through a lot of monkey food" (Walkers 01).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
About five years before the case, Jan hit and killed a man in a black suit who was crossing a Georgia highway at night (see Dead NSA Man in Black). In the man's van he found an ape woman strapped to a gurney and being fed drugs. He kept her, hoping to make money. She aged fast, so Jan tried every kind of ape semen, posing as a representative of a Saudi buyer, and when nothing worked he used his own through artificial insemination. The offspring aged even faster, only the males lived, and a lab told him the chromosome numbers did not line up. The ape-men were strong and could recognize gold, which led to the mining operation beneath the Spud Hut plant (see Spud Hut Georgia Regional Distribution Center) (Walkers 01).

The ape-men's rapid growth matches what the animal handler Clive said in Appalachia 09: when brought to him they looked about six and were full-grown in about two months (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: Jan says only Clive and he ever saw Shelly alive "while not trying to kill you", and he gives no account of what became of her. The episodes never explain what she really is or why an NSA-linked man was carrying her drugged in a van. Kurt remarks that this ties Jan's story to the other man in a black suit the team hit on the road in Radford, who carried a flashlight that burns things.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • "Shelly" is also the name of Shelly Wilmarth, the dead mother whose apparent return drives the next arc. The episodes do not say whether the shared name is deliberate.

docs.title: Shelly Wilmarth
docs.text:
Shelly Wilmarth is Alberta Wilmarth's mother, who died of a heart attack out with the cattle on the family ranch near Ballard, Utah, yet appears on a local news broadcast and is said to walk the ranch at night. Her case brings the task force to Utah in The Walkers in Skin.

Type NPC (dead; apparent revenant) Aliases Alberta's mother; Revenant Shelly Wilmarth; the apparition; the dead mother Status Dead and buried; the exhumation is ordered but never shown. The nature of the apparition is never explained First appearance Walkers 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Shelly is never seen directly; she exists in photographs, an obituary clipping and a few seconds of news footage. According to Alberta, she was "just a heart attack. She was out with the cattle." Her grave lies in the churchyard cemetery under a big black granite slab laid over the top of the plot (Walkers 01, Walkers 03).

docs.title: Alberta's request
docs.text: Alberta arrives at the PITF office with a box of documents and tapes (Alberta's box): a yearbook photo, a photo from a family reunion five or six years earlier, the obituary clipping, and a VHS copy of local news footage of a protest about the community center, in which her mother appears just before a cut. Alberta wants the Mormon church forced to exhume her mother. She says other people have seen Shelly too, including the man renting the ranch, who did not know she was dead. Andrew Howard rules out a secret twin, since Alberta has only brothers, and a doppelganger goes on the list of possibilities (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Investigation
docs.text:
In Salt Lake City, Carl Gardner says the Bureau has already looked into the young woman's report and checked for twins. Robert Bigelow refers to Alberta's apparition at the big house. Whether it is a ghost, a shapeshifter or a hallucination is not settled (Walkers 02).

The party tells Sheriff McDermish they want an exhumation, and he asks whether they have checked for twins. They find the grave after about half an hour of searching (Walkers 03). Andrew gets a court order through Big Bill, and it is expected to go through the day after tomorrow (Walkers 04, Walkers 05).

In Walkers 06 the party repairs the ground-penetrating radar and pushes it over the grave, comparing the readings with neighboring graves and the dirt beside it. They conclude, with about 85 percent confidence, that there is something solid in the coffin. By Walkers 07 the exhumation order is set for the next morning, but the digging is never shown. See Exhumation of Shelly Wilmarth.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The date of her death is inconsistent. In Walkers 01 Alberta says her mother "died two years ago" and the obituary reads winter 1990. In Walkers 05, when Rita asks, Andre answers that she died "about, I think, like two months ago."
  • Two other characters share the name: the "ape woman" Jan Martense named Shelly (Shelly (ape woman)), who Andre admits he named while drunk, and a staffer addressed as "Shelly" on the intercom at the Salt Lake City field office.

docs.title: Sheriff Carter Burke
docs.text:
Sheriff Carter Burke is the haggard sheriff of Dahlonega, Georgia, who brings the task force into the missing-persons case in The Things in Appalachia, follows the team into the Spud Hut mines and ends the recorded arc hugging a tree.

Type NPC Aliases Sheriff Burke; Burke; the sheriff; Dahlonega sheriff; Auraria sheriff Affiliation Dahlonega Sheriff's Department Status Alive, shaken, holding gold (as of Appalachia 09) First appearance Appalachia 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Burke is a haggard older Black man with thinning hair and severe IBS. His office walls are hung with animal heads and guns. He answers his phone with "Dahlonega sheriff's station. This is Sheriff Burke speaking." He is cooperative and wants to be kept informed, and grows more frustrated and overwhelmed as the disappearances pile up. He calls Andrew "Detective Howard" at first and "son" later (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 08).

Andre names him in Appalachia 01, 02, 04 and 09. In Appalachia 03 and 06 to 08 he is only "the sheriff", but he is plainly the same man.

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
In Appalachia 01 the front-desk woman fetches him from the restroom, where he has been for about twenty minutes with IBS. He treats Andrew as the team's lead. He explains that the manhunt for the missing boy found little, that he suspects coyotes, a bear or a wandering stranger, and that he thinks Willow Greengrass left the cult. He copies the case file names for them: Willow, her sister Primenthol Greengrass, the missing boy Gene Cartwright and the witness Edward Nick. He dismisses the recent Bigfoot sightings as pranks and says he would "take the Bigfoot stuff over the gold stuff": he finds the town's gold-rush tourism grim, since slaves dug the tunnels and the Trail of Tears followed. He points out through the bars of the evidence locker the only evidence in Willow's case, a bag of peaches (see Bag of Peaches).

By phone in Appalachia 02 he asks whether the shoe is "red with a white sole", confirms that it matches Gene's, admits his deputies should have looked up, apologizes for the volunteers who trampled the scene, and asks to see the shoe once forensics is done.

In Appalachia 03 the sheriff is brisk and worried, loading squad cars for the search for Frederick, a German boy who vanished from a tour of the Consolidated Gold Mine. He makes Kurt, who has spelunking experience, responsible for the safety of the searchers, briefs the team on mine hazards, takes the left fork himself and mutters about "too many people going missing". His face darkens when Andrew suggests a cult. See Consolidated Gold Mine.

In Appalachia 04 he calls Howard in for a "man-to-man" at the Dahlonega Sheriff's Station. He has five missing people in two days, and the FBI arrived before it was even clear there were two. He has asked the state police for help and asks the team to call them too (see Georgia State Police). "If we were a beach town, I would close the beach," he says. Kurt suggests a curfew and a "truth-adjacent" cover story about a fatal tick-borne disease, and Burke says Kurt's "agency boy" attitude "scans". He names the bodybuilder Walter Sellers as the strongest man in town, clears the break room for a speakerphone call between Frederick's mother and an FBI translator, and tells the team, "Just don't affect my tourism". Monica Cartwright reveals that he dismissed her Chewbacca sighting because she was drunk.

In Appalachia 06 he walks into the hotel with Frotter Comstock and lectures Andrew for calling the dead man "capped": "Son, a man is dead," even if he is dressed in a Chewbacca costume (see Troy Cleaver).

In Appalachia 07 he calls the team out to the Spud Hut truck crash and walks them through the evidence at the Freeway Crash Site: the cab with eight gunshots and no body, and bags of "Potatoes" that spill dirt or hold a whole octopus. He suggests a chat with the Spud Hut people, and relays word from a state police friend that the Secret Service had tipped them off about surveillance equipment.

In Appalachia 08 he leads the way to Spud Hut Corporate, swears Andrew in as a deputy, and dresses him in the spare uniform of an absent deputy, String Bean. He coaxes the receptionist Charlene into opening the door. In the ape-man fight he screams continuously and dives through the "break room" door when the Claymore appears (see The Break Room (code 441)).

In Appalachia 09 he opens the episode screaming shrilly in the middle of the party, and then hyperventilates. He demands to know why the FBI showed up before anything was wrong, with spying on presidential candidates, ape-men and explosions all at once, and he takes the team for the Men in Black. Dick Baxter uses his Grifter move to steer the conversation. Dante has him face the back of Kurt's head to keep him calm. He is told to keep watch, shoots badly (a 6), and takes some of the gold, saying "we're gonna figure out the legality of this later" (see Gold Bars). The recorded arc ends with the sheriff hugging a tree and swaying gently.

Unrecorded session

His role in the finale, Appalachia 10, is unrecorded and is not mentioned in Walkers 01.

docs.title: Sheriff McDermish
docs.text:
Sheriff McDermish is the heavyset, part-time sheriff of Ballard, Utah, a veteran who files the exhumation paperwork for the task force and later flees the state with his young son.

Type NPC Aliases the sheriff; Sheriff of Ballard; Ballard sheriff Affiliation Ballard's one-man sheriff's department Status Alive; left Utah (Walkers 06) First appearance Walkers 03 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: McDermish is very heavyset, folksy and eager to help ("consider me a resource"). He has lived in Ballard his whole life and describes the sheriff's job as "more of, like, a part-time thing." He works out of a double-wide station, where a Monopoly game is always underway on a folding card table. He is not Mormon, though his father was. Over a bar scene with Kurt Larson, he trades war stories and explains that a quarter of one buttock was shot off, leaving him with ingrown hairs and periodic abscesses (Walkers 03).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
When the party visits the station in Walkers 03, a boy of about seven answers the door: "My daddy's on the shitter. Can I help you?" The boy, Bud, is told to amuse himself with the Aladdin VHS while his father talks with the visitors. McDermish serves sweet tea and agrees to take the exhumation request to the court, warning that the judge is a cantankerous man who stalled a custody-related exhumation fifteen years earlier. He asks, "Y'all check for twins?" At the bar he drinks red wine over ice, and Kurt and Huell warn him not to drink the tap water or let his son drink it. See Exhumation of Shelly Wilmarth and Ballard water contamination.

By Walkers 06 he is a nervous chain-smoker with a "haunted look." At his trailer he tells Kurt that a county spot check found more than 50 percent of the high school's students absent, that parents are not answering, that houses have stood empty for days and that the diner is nearly empty; he gives Kurt a Post-it note of names and addresses. He asks whether Kurt needs a shotgun and hands over a Remington Model 870, saying he keeps a Colt he got in the service. While Kurt phones Big Bill to request the Utah National Guard, the sheriff overhears and relaxes. He drives off with his son, vowing, "I am not gonna stop driving until we are across state lines" (Walkers 06). See Disappearances in Ballard.

Later episodes mention him only as the sheriff who left. In Walkers 07 Kurt tells Robert Bigelow that the sheriff left town, and in Walkers 08 Rita remarks that Ballard had only one sheriff and he left because the party told him to.

Quote

"I figured, you know, present the smallest possible horizontal target. And then they shot me in the ass. Communism is a terrible ideology." (Andre as Sheriff McDermish, Walkers 03)

Quote

"I am so goddamn glad the professionals are on it. Give 'em hell, son." (Andre as the sheriff, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Sloth
docs.text:
Sloth is the armed marksman of the Circle Chasers, a group of young Bigfoot hunters in Dahlonega, Georgia, and the owner of the Great Dane Harvey.

Type NPC Aliases Norville Rutger; Norville Affiliation The Circle Chasers Status Alive (as of Appalachia 07) First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Sloth carries a pistol on his belt. Another Chaser, a tall, blond, all-American man, says that Sloth "doesn't look like it, but he was a competitive sharpshooter in his youth" (Appalachia 01). Sloth speaks for the group when the team first meets them.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Appalachia 01 Sloth introduces himself, Eddie Jones, Vanessa, Delilah and Harvey. He explains the group's plan to search the zone between the town sightings and the sightings around Auraria, and, when Dante's Kurt warns him that people have gone missing in the woods, answers that "you gotta respect the power of nature" and pats his pistol.

In Appalachia 02 he joins the Chasers on the woods trail, where he tells Harvey to get down off Andrew and remarks that the dog does not usually like strangers. He sides against the agents' overthinking of the creature's tracks, and pushes hard for the group to go to McDonald's.

In Appalachia 07 he is at the Original Spud Hut, where he asks Andrew for his dog back and orders the buffalo cauliflower spud with blue cheese.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Sloth's real name, Norville Rutger, comes up only in Appalachia 07, where it is spoken in passing and is of uncertain spelling (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Smith Hotel Desk Clerk
docs.text:
The Smith Hotel Desk Clerk is the young, eager and chatty clerk of the Smith Hotel in Dahlonega, Georgia, who gossips about the suspicious guests in room 111 and lends the Biz the master key.

Type NPC (unnamed) Aliases the clerk; night clerk; the kid at the front desk Affiliation Smith Hotel Status Alive (as of Appalachia 03) First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The clerk is young, eager and talkative, and eager to help the FBI guests, whom he winks at and salutes in the hallway (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Appalachia 01 the team picks the stately Smith Hotel over the "Express & Suites". The clerk has only two rooms left because of a conference of dental oncologists in town, and the team ends up in rooms 109 and 110 on the second floor at $55 per person per room. He mentions the hotel's old horse stable and mineshaft, and recommends the continental breakfast, with goat products and peach preserves from the religious community in Auraria. He describes the community as a gold-rush ghost town taken over about ten years earlier by people in long dresses, living in tents with no electricity and talking about the end of the world, and advises against staying there after dark ("I'm just not that big into getting wicker-manned"). He says he turned away teenage "UFO people" who wanted one room for four people and a dog (see The Circle Chasers). Off the record, he thinks the missing boy ran away and the woman left the cult.

In Appalachia 02 the Biz is considering the lock of Room 111 when the clerk comes to report the room as suspicious. It was booked under one name and paid for with a card in another, and the man who booked it offered him $100 to keep quiet. The man was carrying a gun and sounded like he was from the Midwest, which the Biz recognizes immediately ("That is him"). The clerk fetches the master key, which lets the Biz plant a spy camera and microphone (see Spy Camera and Microphone). Asked by the Biz about prostitution in town, he says there is none (try Atlanta). Later he salutes the agents in the hall and gives them a thumbs-up.

In Appalachia 03 the night clerk recognizes "Agent Howard" returning in the small hours, fetches another master key to let him in, and gossips again about the neighboring room, where "scary guys" have offered him money. He says he already told Andrew's partner, "kind of hot, bigger guy, sports jacket", meaning the Biz. He winks at Andrew and later brings up the hotel's depleted first-aid kit. See Next-door Hotel Guests.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Appalachia 07 a boy of about seventeen at the same front desk gives his name as Talila, "Tully" for short (see Tully). The episodes never say whether he is the clerk of the earlier episodes.

docs.title: Spud Hut Counter Savant
docs.text:
The Spud Hut Counter Savant is an unnamed teenage worker at the original Spud Hut in Dahlonega, Georgia, who has perfect recall, keeps a cryptogram secret menu, and is eventually placed in a CIA job by Kurt.

Type NPC (unnamed) Aliases counter kid; savant kid; savant worker; counter man; savant teen; grill-station savant Affiliation Spud Hut; later CIA Status Alive; given a CIA job by Kurt (as of Walkers 01) First appearance Appalachia 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The savant is polite, brisk and slightly robotic, with hair slicked down by sweat and formal speech ("Next customer, please"). He recites about a hundred specials from memory, with no menu board anywhere. Dante's Kurt compared the Spud Hut to hiring the memory savant Kim Peek to remember the menu (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 07).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Appalachia 02, at the Original Spud Hut, he recites the specials while the line behind him grows restless, and instantly names "the first one" (the Cobb salad spud) and "the twenty-third one" (the curry chicken spud). Kurt asks how many matchsticks he just dropped, and the boy answers "forty-three", which is exactly right. Kurt tells him to get out of there because his mind is an incredible gift, and the boy says, "I can't leave the Spud Hut. The Spud Hut changed my life." He later locks up and walks across the parking lot into the woods. See Spud Hut Menu.

In Appalachia 06 the counter kid has worked 793 days and recalls customers by order and date. Shown a photo of the dead man in the Chewbacca costume (see Troy Cleaver), he says the man came in on three occasions (four, nine and 25 days earlier), paid cash, wore a holster, had no ID in his wallet and arrived by ATV, and once appeared alongside a man in a business suit, though the two did not speak. Huell tests him with a coin flip, and he calls "tails" correctly. Asked about the man's gun, he answers, "I don't know about handguns. I haven't read that book yet." Kurt promises to get him out ("You will be hearing from Langley"), and compares him to the character in Rain Man. The kid replies that "Spud Hut saved my life".

In Appalachia 07 the counter man is again at the register. He reaches under the counter for a briefcase, unlocks it with two keys, and hands the team a sheet of handwritten cryptic symbols: "That is the menu. I designed the cryptogram myself." He asks Huell for ID before serving a margarita spud. The team sends the cryptogram to the NSA codebreakers, whom the CIA calls the "Puzzle Palace". See Cryptogram Secret Menu.

In Appalachia 09 Kurt remarks that Spud Hut has "a fucking polymath savant working at the goddamn Spud Hut grill station", and the animal handler Clive confirms he "knows the whole menu".

In Walkers 01, Dante says that in the weeks after the Georgia events Kurt made sure the savant teen from Spud Hut got a job at the CIA, "whether he likes it or not".

docs.title: Troy Cleaver
docs.text:
Troy Cleaver is the name of the dead man found in a stolen Chewbacca costume on Frotter Comstock's land, an ex-military drifter who staged fake Bigfoot sightings around Dahlonega, Georgia, and who, according to Clive, was the mercenary who smelted gold for Jan's Conspiracy.

Type NPC (deceased) Aliases John Doe; the drifter; the Chewbacca man; the hoaxer; the mercenary; the Bigfoot guy Affiliation Jan's Conspiracy Status Dead, shot in the back of the head First appearance Appalachia 06 (as an unidentified body); named in Appalachia 07 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The body was a white man of 25 to 35 with a military haircut, scars, fit build and calloused hands. His face was crumpled with the eyes hanging out. Under the costume he wore a plain white T-shirt, blue jeans, nondescript sneakers and white socks, with every clothing tag cut out, even the one on the belt. His pockets were empty. He had a small anchor tattoo on a bicep and a small trident tattoo on a calf, which Kurt took to be a Navy SEAL emblem (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Frotter Comstock reported a dead Bigfoot on his land and refused to touch it for fear of disease. Andrew Howard looked down from the hilltop and found a man in an expensive Chewbacca costume soaked in real blood, with a wound like a gangland execution. Kurt found no body armor and ruled out UTAW ("he's not one of my boys"). Blood pooling matched the way the body lay, and the spatter showed he was shot standing, dead-center from behind; Kurt's best guess for the weapon was a .357 Magnum fired at point-blank range (Appalachia 06).

Ezra's character, the Biz, found ATV tracks that stopped near the body and continued down the mountain toward the freeway. He also found a snapped plaster-of-Paris toe matching the fake Bigfoot footprints in the mud. The molds were missing, so someone had cleaned up after the killing. The costume's bandolier had also been removed. The costume itself was traced to Derek Edwards, who said it vanished from Apollo's dry cleaners eight months earlier (see Chewbacca Costume) (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: Tracing the drifter
docs.text:
The Spud Hut counter savant recognized the photo: the man had visited three times (4, 9 and 25 days earlier), paid cash, wore a holster and had no ID. He arrived by ATV, and once he was in the restaurant at the same time as a man in a business suit, though the two did not speak. The Spud Hut auditor said he was not on the plant's employee list. The owner of Apollo's described him as an out-of-town drifter who stood watching, sometimes on a walkie-talkie. The clerk at the Motel and Suites said he registered as "John Doe", paid cash, was picked up on an ATV by a helmeted man once or twice, and had a female caller a couple of times. His belongings were thrown out after he stopped renewing the room (Appalachia 06).

In the motel dumpster the team found his briefcase with a false lining shaped for a high-caliber handgun, about $10,000 in hundreds and twenties, a coil of animal hair in one snakeskin boot, and a walkie-talkie in the other. Kurt read him as a mercenary, possibly sent to kill someone and double-crossed, and the team later spent part of the cash on dinner for the Circle Chasers (Appalachia 06, Appalachia 07).

The name Troy Cleaver first appears in the recap that opens Appalachia 07, when Andre refers to the garbage the team had been searching as Troy Cleaver's. The photos had been sent to the FBI for identification at the end of the previous session, but the episodes never show the identification being made (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Role in Jan's operation
docs.text:
In the mines beneath the Spud Hut plant, Clive described Jan's conspiracy as five people: Jan, Clive, a mercenary who melted the gold down, and two bodyguards. Dante and Ezra's characters recognized the mercenary as "the Bigfoot guy", and Kurt told Clive that a man in a Bigfoot costume with ex-military tattoos had been found dead in the forest. Clive was dismayed that the Chewbacca costume had been used: he did not know where the mercenary got it, and said he had told him people would know it was Chewbacca. He explained that some of the workers had escaped and been seen, that Jan told him the mercenary had put one of them down, and that the fake sightings were meant to discredit the real ones (Appalachia 09).

In the epilogue, Kurt asks Jan about "the mercenary, who I assume you took care of in the woods"; Jan does not dispute it (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• It is never established who pulled the trigger. Frotter Comstock was suspected only briefly, and Kurt did not think he was the killer. Kurt assumes Jan was responsible, but no one confirms it.
  • It is never established whether Cleaver is the naked, hairy "Chewbacca" figure that Monica Cartwright saw at her driveway before getting into a black sedan, or who the helmeted ATV rider and the businessman at the Spud Hut were.

  • Walkers 01 (referenced in the epilogue)

docs.title: Talila "Tully"
docs.text:
Talila "Tully" is a seventeen-year-old front-desk clerk at the Smith Hotel in Dahlonega, Georgia, who overhears Andrew Howard blurting out the case's body count to Big Bill and offers him his mother's fax machine.

Type NPC Aliases Tully; Talila Affiliation Smith Hotel Status Alive (as of Appalachia 07) First appearance Appalachia 07 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Tully is about seventeen and works the hotel's front desk and lobby in the evening. When Andrew asks his name, he says it is Talila, apologizes that it is a family name, and says he goes by Tully; Andre describes a single tear (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
On the night of the Clinton surveillance story, Andrew took a phone call from Big Bill in the hotel lobby. Big Bill demanded an inventory of men and equipment and an itinerary by fax, and Andrew, flustered, volunteered the body count: two dead kids, the exploded man in the cave, the executed man in the Chewbacca costume and one missing man. Big Bill told him to say nothing to anyone and said he would brief the President and come down himself (Appalachia 07).

Tully had overheard. He asked whether five people were dead and whether the state police being in town was connected, and Andrew denied both. When Andrew asked for a computer or fax machine, Tully refused on behalf of the hotel but offered to call his mom, who had one. Andrew declined and asked him to keep quiet about the call, which Tully agreed to do. Andrew left with finger guns, and Tully saluted them. The team instead planned to fax the itinerary from the sheriff's station (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The episodes never say whether Tully is the same young, eager desk clerk who helped the team earlier in the arc (see Smith Hotel Desk Clerk). Tully's name is given only here.

docs.text: • Appalachia 07

docs.title: Tyler
docs.text:
Tyler is a four-year-old boy from the trailer across the street from the Lucky house in Radford, Virginia, who saw a "spaceman" above the missing girl's home.

Type NPC (witness) Aliases None Affiliation None Status Alive (as of Radford Horror 01) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Tyler is an insomniac four-year-old in Pooh Bear pajamas, miserable at being woken. He knows Amanda Lucky only from trick-or-treating, has seen spacemen only on TV, and wants to be one when he grows up. His mother Mary, named once by Sheriff Frank Roosevelt, is reluctant to wake him ("he had a dream") and provides orange Tang. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
On the task force's first morning investigating Amanda Lucky's disappearance, the team crosses the street from the Lucky house, about 100 feet away. Dick Baxter gives Tyler an FBI sticker, and Kurt Larson gives him a "Viet Cong tooth" and tells him they are secret agents. Tyler says he saw a light and a spaceman all in white with a helmet, up above the Lucky house, who "just went down" without obviously falling or using a ladder, and who was gone when Tyler came back from telling his parents. Asked by Kurt, he insists: "He was a spaceman. He looked like a spaceman." Told he could grow up to be an agent, he answers: "I want to be a spaceman." (Radford Horror 01)

Huell Kendrick speaks to Tyler privately while his parents are out of the room. Sheriff Roosevelt does not think he saw a spaceman and says he "had a dream." Kurt proposes a man in a motorcycle suit and helmet, and privately a person in a hazmat suit; the Biz also suspects a sleepy child mistook a motorcyclist. Nothing is confirmed in the episode. (Radford Horror 01)

The figure later becomes known as The Spaceman, eventually tied to Abelforth Whateley's homemade spacesuit and then to Wilbur Whateley; see Spaceman suit. Tyler does not appear again.

docs.text:
• After the interview, Ezra (as the Biz) quips: "Unreliable witnesses. People going missing. Yep, this is exactly the same as investigating KGB agents."
  • He thanks Kurt for the tooth at the end of the scene.

docs.title: Vanessa
docs.text:
Vanessa is a teenage member of the Circle Chasers, the Bigfoot-hunting group in Dahlonega, Georgia, who argues for an undiscovered hominid and who produces the blinking tracking device found in a pool of bear vomit.

Type NPC Affiliation Circle Chasers Status Alive (as of Appalachia 07) First appearance Appalachia 01 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Vanessa is described as the shorter, chubbier woman of the group, and she wears hiking boots (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Appalachia 01
docs.text: When the team first meets the Chasers beside their crop-circle trailer, Vanessa says the people of Auraria were "really nice" and "much nicer than that hotel guy" (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: Appalachia 02
docs.text: Vanessa and the others come out of the dark after the team hears an unearthly howl on the trail near Auraria. In the group's debate about what the creature is, Sloth and Andrew lean toward a werewolf, Eddie Jones argues for feral humans, and Vanessa dismisses Eddie's idea as dumb, arguing that Bigfoot is "clearly an undiscovered hominid living in the American forests". Kurt checks the group's footwear against the sneaker print found beside the giant footprints, and her hiking boots do not match (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Appalachia 07
docs.text: At the Spud Hut, Vanessa runs up out of breath and gasps "Bear vomit." The Chasers explain that they found bear vomit full of blood and a blinking light, which they took with them. After the Spud Hut closes, Vanessa checks that the agents will be "cool" and invites them into the group's blacklit RV. There the Chasers hand over a Ziploc bag holding the device and describe being chased by a bear "with, like, half a face" (see Half-faced Bear). Kurt tells them it was not a bear and warns them to stay away. The Biz later reads the etching on the device: "Inventory Control, SHA Tracking, SS994-0851" (see SHA Tracking Device) (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text: She is one of the five Chasers with Sloth, Eddie, Delilah and the Great Dane Harvey.

docs.title: Walt "Coyote" Murphy
docs.text:
Walt "Coyote" Murphy is a veteran ranch hand and gate guard on Robert Bigelow's research staff at Sherman Ranch near Ballard, Utah, who guides the task force on night patrols and joins the final battle of The Walkers in Skin.

Type NPC Aliases Walt; Coyote; Yote; Walter Affiliation Bigelow's research operation Status Alive, unconscious in an APC at the end of Walkers 09 First appearance Walkers 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Walt is a Native American man, fairly muscular, friendly and slightly rattled, who is divorced. The cold open of Walkers 02 shows a Native American man in a big cowboy hat patrolling the ranch with a shotgun; he fits Walt's description, but the episode never names him. In-fiction, he tells the party he served in the Gulf War and got home about a year ago; the Salt Lake City agents call him a former Army Ranger. For six months in the summer of 1986 he tried to get people to call him "Coyote." He drives a Jeep, rides an ATV, and asks that guns not be fired near him unless his earplugs are in: "There's been enough of that for one lifetime" (Walkers 02, Walkers 04).

docs.title: The barn snooper and the goose
docs.text: Walt is the gate guard for Bigelow. He is the "former Army Ranger" of the field office's rundown, who fired on a snooper by the barn and claimed to have hit him, though no evidence was found. He tells the team that he gave a warning before firing and that the figure came at him "at pretty high speed", and Bigelow says he has "total faith in Walt's judgment". He is at constant war with Nancy the goose; the goose bites him, and he vows, "One of these days I am gonna eat that thing" (Walkers 02). In Walkers 03 he says he wasn't kidding about the goose being his biggest problem in life, offers the party brownies and cold soup, and arranges the night-patrol ride-along.

docs.title: Patrol and skepticism
docs.text: On the patrol in Walkers 04 he falls in love with Kurt Larson's P90 ("It's like a space gun or something"), complains about city council meetings that are ninety-five percent Mormon, and takes the party to a burned crow, which he thinks might be ball lightning. During about thirty minutes of UFO talk in the car, his opinion of Howard shifts significantly. He is the skeptic and prefers mundane explanations for the vanished car (a big cargo plane and a skyhook, or a helicopter lowering a cable), as the party debates in the vanishing car incident. He recognizes the teenager Harrison from childhood and says he shot at a guy not two months ago. Of the party he says, "You guys are the weirdest fucking cops I've ever met" (Walkers 04).

docs.title: The night of the light
docs.text: In Walkers 05 he is exhausted, makes coffee, apple cider and hot chocolate, and drives the party to Roosevelt the next morning. Kurt calls him "Yote."

docs.title: The naked intruder
docs.text: In Walkers 07 he arrives by Jeep at 11:15 p.m., squints at the restrained naked intruder ("Is that... you?"), and responds to the party's account of the man's behavior with "pick a fucking lane." He drives the catatonic man to the small emergency room in Roosevelt and returns at about 5 a.m. to report that the man died on the operating table, after going downhill during the drive until Walt was doing CPR while driving. See the naked intruder.

docs.title: The finale
docs.text: In Walkers 09 Coyote volunteers for the substation sabotage and pulls out his "illegal-ass" rocket-propelled grenade. He and two National Guardsmen with a box of grenades take an APC back toward the substation. Afterward the party finds the APC on its side among dead bodies and burned-out station wagons, with the substation blown apart by grenades. Coyote, inside, calls out, "your friend was naked and running for ya"; Rita (as Andrew) thanks him for not shooting her when they met. The party tips the APC over to free them, and Coyote and the Guardsmen crawl out of a shot-out window, then lose consciousness from the dust stirred up. The party hauls them into their vehicle. See the substation.

docs.title: Wilbur Whateley
docs.text:
Wilbur Whateley is the comatose-seeming identical twin of Abelforth Whateley, a teenage butterfly collector from Radford, Virginia, who raised the Radford Moth, became its thrall and was blamed by the police as a serial killer.

Type NPC Aliases Wilbur; Astronaut Kid; the Whateley boy; the astronaut twin Affiliation Whateley family Status Alive, in a Roanoke mental hospital (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Wilbur is Abe's identical twin. In his room, pinned butterflies and insects surround a boy slumped in a wheelchair by the window, barely reacting; his shoes are a little small for the footprints found outside. His legs are thin, his hands clammy and his feet clean (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 06). When he is finally seen awake in the church he is naked, small and scarred on the side of his head (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: Background
docs.text: At fifteen, on a learner's permit, Wilbur crashed coming down from the mountains in the rain with a high blood alcohol level, spun out, hit a tree and struck his head on the dash, leaving a big scar. A passer-by called it in. Afterwards he did not speak, could not write and could carry on an action only once someone started it for him; the family paid a "quack" for eye-movement communication, and a nurse visits a couple of times a week. Before the crash the family had sent him to military school after he acted out. The twins are sixteen at the time of the case, with the crash three years earlier. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
Wilbur is first met sitting catatonic in his room while the task force investigates the disappearance of his mother Irene Whateley and the "spaceman" robbery by his brother Abe (Radford Horror 02).

In Radford Horror 06 the team keeps watch on the house at night. A figure in a handmade Apollo 11 suit jogs willingly into the woods; when Huell Kendrick catches him, he says "You don't have to fight this" and "It's worth it" as the craft lifts him away, and Huell, still clinging, loses his grip and falls, breaking his arm. Dante (as Kurt Larson) radios "It's got the Whateley boy" as the craft dives behind the Whateley residence. Inside, the team finds Wilbur in his bed with clammy hands and thin legs; smelling salts rouse him only to a vacant stare and soft crying. That night he slips out of his window as soon as the back watch is dropped, and the next morning a missing-person report is filed for him. (Radford Horror 06) See The Spaceman and Spaceman suit.

In the old church, the team finds him holding a pinned moth. He tells them, "It's okay. You don't have to do this." Tackled by Huell Kendrick and handcuffed by Andrew Howard, he says "I've been with it for so long... it's more sentient than we are... it has to breed. They're born pregnant," and tells Andrew that he "of all people" should understand; Rita (as Andrew) answers "Neither are you." Wilbur is psychically linked to the creature: he screams as if shot when it is hurt, dislocates both shoulders by thrashing, loses his fingernails and ends catatonic. Huell throws him out of the burning building. (Radford Horror 07)

Sheriff Frank Roosevelt presents the police theory: a hidden basement with a spaceman costume and a journal; a cadaver most likely Abelforth's; Wilbur a serial killer who impersonated his brother's departure, with a cartel link through heroin found in the church. The team reads Wilbur's journal, which records finding a larva on June 3rd, its hatching on August 15th, a voice in his head ("She's talking all the time now") and entries from April 16 to 18 matching Abelforth's death. They conclude the moth manipulated Wilbur, and agree to let the police pin everything on him, uncertain whether he is faking catatonia. (Radford Horror 08)

Huell, on Wilbur

"A man will do a lot for some moth strange." (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
Molly Underhill recaps that the Whateley boy faked catatonia and is held at a mental hospital in Roanoke (Radford Horrors 02); see Roanoke mental hospital.

In Radford Horrors 04 the task force visits him an hour before closing. The nurse warns "no touching." Kurt gets only a flicker from Wilbur, then holds the moth goo sample (see Pearlescent goo) under his nose, and Wilbur stiffens, his eyes going waxy. Andrew rolls 13 on Use Magic and chooses to heal one harm, loosening what he senses as crooked mental knots from years of being "ridden shotgun." Wilbur wakes and asks, "Where's my brother?" (Radford Horrors 04)

He recognizes them "from the church," dreams of "drowning in blue," and says something was "wearing" him. He found an oversized Morpho menelaus caterpillar in the woods that did not belong in Virginia and that may have killed the dog. When Kurt presses, he panics: "like the ocean... like a mother... in the basement... It was pregnant. It needed to breathe... it needed hosts, like a parasitic wasp. Those women--". As the nurse escorts them out he adds, "I found it under a white oak." (Radford Horrors 04) See Moth life cycle.

docs.title: Relationships
docs.text:
• Abelforth Whateley: his twin; the police believe the basement body is Abelforth's, killed around April 17th. Wilbur's first words on waking are about his brother.
  • The moth: its thrall, who adored it ("She's so beautiful... she's mine") and killed with its help (Radford Horror 08).
  • Andrew Howard: the moth called Andrew a "changeling" who has "the understanding"; Wilbur says Andrew of all people should understand. Andrew later heals him.
  • Yobiah and Irene Whateley: his parents; see Yobiah Whateley.

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
• "It's not wrong when you eat a chicken. And it has to breed." (Radford Horror 07)
  • "I found it under a white oak." (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The twins' names are repeatedly mixed up at the table (Albert, Walter, Wilbur and Abelforth in Radford Horror 06; Dante, as Kurt, calls Wilbur "Gilbert" once in Radford Horrors 04).
  • In Radford Horror 06 the hunters cannot tell which twin is under the Apollo suit, since they are identical twins; Radford Horror 07 and 08 establish that it was Wilbur, and that Abelforth had died in April.
  • Dante, out of character: "Faith healing Wilbur Whateley was not on my bingo card." (Radford Horrors 04)
  • Andre's narration in Radford Horrors 04 says Wilbur pretended to be catatonic for "five years," though every earlier episode puts the accident three years back.

docs.title: Wilford Hiram
docs.text:
Wilford Hiram is the mustached, ring-wearing mayor of Ballard, Utah, who pushes the community center project, turns out to be a skinwalker who replaced the real mayor months before the task force arrived, and is last seen carrying supplies in the cavern under that center.

Type NPC Aliases the mayor; Mayor of Ballard; Ballard mayor Affiliation Ballard town government; later the skinwalker faction Status Unknown (last seen in the cavern, Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 02 (mentioned); Walkers 05 (in person) Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Hiram has a big mustache and large rings, drives a nice new Cadillac, and constantly crunches lemon candies from a tin without sucking on them. In person he is cold and evasive, and Dante notes his odd way of eating the candies ("Who the hell eats a lemon candy like that?"). When asked where he gets them, he answers, "Special order. They're from Spain" (Walkers 05, Walkers 06).

docs.title: Before the arrival
docs.text: In Walkers 02 a local complains about having to drive around the substation to reach the community center, blaming "the mayor and... the goddamn busybody," meaning Deborah Wells. See Ballard town government and the community center.

docs.title: Walkers 05
docs.text: He arrives at the ranch in his Cadillac, announces "I am Wilford Hiram. I am mayor," and shakes Andrew Howard's hand so vigorously that one of his rings cuts it. He offers condolences about the crushed rental car and fishes for why federal agents are in town. Andrew gives the cover story that they are an "oddball task force" sent on jobs that may or may not amount to something. Hiram leaves with an offer of whatever "the government of Ballard, Utah" can do. The players privately suspect him of embezzlement tied to the community center (Walkers 05).

docs.title: Walkers 06
docs.text: At Ballard City Hall, the party finds a desk, which Kurt Larson connects to the mayor, piled with New York Post issues that stop about three months earlier and buried under hundreds of Tootsie Roll wrappers. When the Cadillac arrives, Dante asks about records for the junkyard owner Yusuf Ansari. The mayor says the junkyard is in Ballard County but outside the municipality, offers to have a friend at the county records office look it up, nervously chews a candy, and writes the name on the back of an envelope. He says a fire years earlier destroyed most of the geological records. He then escorts the party out and locks the door behind them. Rita has Andrew theorize about Scandinavian "tooth trolls" that feed on sugar (Walkers 06). See sugar clues.

docs.title: Walkers 07 and 08
docs.text: In a private handout in Walkers 07, Rita learns that the skinwalkers cloned Andrew from a tissue sample taken by the ring that cut him on the mayor's hand (replication). In Walkers 08 the party suspects the mayor is one of the creatures, recalling his hard candies; Kurt says, "Yeah, I always knew I didn't like that fucking mayor." Rita later reasons that the skinwalkers probably began by taking over the mayor and others in charge (Walkers 08). See pilot and host biology.

docs.title: Walkers 09
docs.text: In the cavern the party sees the mayor carrying supplies near the tanks of blood and the portal. His fate is never shown (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Hiram's name is spoken only in Walkers 05; the other episodes call him "the mayor."
