docs.title: Willow Greengrass
docs.text:
Willow Greengrass is a member of the Covenant in Auraria, Georgia, who vanished while carrying a sack of peaches through the woods, and whose disappearance, alongside those of two boys, brings the task force to Dahlonega.

Type NPC (missing) Aliases Willow; that cult lady Affiliation Covenant Status Missing (as of Appalachia 09) First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Willow is described through others. Her sister Primenthol Greengrass says she was thin from malnutrition, had no money, no enemies, no suitors and no friends outside the Covenant, and had little "agency" ("she had that forehead") (Appalachia 02). The cold open of the arc shows a young woman in an ankle-length dress hauling a sack of peaches through the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest; something hairy and inhuman scuttles between the trees and a growl drags her off-screen. The scene does not name her, but the peaches match the sack later found in the woods near Auraria (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: Background
docs.text: Prim says their mother joined the Covenant when the girls were small and both were renamed at about age three. Prim left, finished school and returned about a month before the disappearance to coax Willow out. Their mother has since died (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: The disappearance
docs.text: The FBI dossier said an adult woman had disappeared "yesterday" when it was handed over on Monday, October 4. Andrew noticed that she vanished in Auraria, which was not on their map and was treated in the file as part of Dahlonega. Sheriff Carter Burke thought she had simply left the cult. The only evidence is a bag of peaches found in the middle of the woods, now in the sheriff's evidence locker (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: What the Covenant said
docs.text: On the trail near Auraria the team met the bootlegger Frotter Comstock, who knew only that she had gone missing (Appalachia 02). At the Covenant itself, the young woman Clover told Kurt that Willow had a persistent yeast infection, common in the camp, and that Elijah Ray had sent her to scout peach orchards and she never returned. Willow's friend River said she was upset because her sister kept pressing her to leave, that the two had a big fight a couple of days before she vanished, and that Elijah Ray discouraged contact with family. River did not think Prim was a murderer. She said Willow had been scouting a new orchard when she disappeared (Appalachia 04). Monica Cartwright also asked the team whether they had found "that cult lady" (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: Willow's fate is never resolved in the recorded sessions. She is not mentioned in Appalachia 09 or Walkers 01, and the arc's finale was never recorded. See Unresolved mysteries.

docs.title: Yobiah Whateley
docs.text:
Yobiah Whateley is the shell-shocked, churchgoing father of the twins Abelforth and Wilbur Whateley, whose wife Irene walked into the woods in front of him.

Type NPC Aliases Mr. Whateley; Yobi; Josiah Affiliation Whateley family Status Alive (as of Radford Horror 06) First appearance Radford Horror 01 (as an unnamed husband); named in Radford Horror 02 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Yobiah is about sixty, a big man with boots of roughly size twelve. He is old-fashioned and pious, the family in church every Sunday, and tells the team the family could not afford the Usenet access Abe wanted, which he considers "probably perverts" anyway. He regards the clerk at the Pay n' Stay who talked with Abe as a pervert. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 01 the team hears only that Mrs. Whateley, a neighbor less than a mile from the Luckys, saw something out the kitchen window while making dinner, put down her pan and walked into the night while her husband watched (Radford Horror 01).

In Radford Horror 02 the team finds him in a cookie-cutter house, shell-shocked on the couch and ignoring a glass of water while neighbors fuss. The sheriff comforts him: "I'm sure we'll find her, Yobiah." He tells Kurt Larson that Irene looked "surprised" rather than angry or scared, ignored him and stormed out; he thought she was chasing a coyote, kept eating for about ten minutes, then "it got weird." He regrets not following her. His boots are far too big to match the footprints leading into the woods. (Radford Horror 02)

He tells Huell Kendrick that Abe built a replica Mercury spacesuit for a school presentation and ran out that morning; that Abe's interest in space began at twelve and that losing the family dog broke him; that Wilbur has not spoken since the accident; and that the twins' friends included the Nichols girl, the Augustine girl and her brother, and the McCreadys. He declined Dr. Lori's suggestion of family therapy. (Radford Horror 02)

In Radford Horror 03 the players, reviewing their leads, remember him only as "Yobi and his missing wife," part of a "weird religious family" (Radford Horror 03). In Radford Horror 06 the team finds him unconscious in the master bedroom with a bottle of sleeping pills on the nightstand, his pulse and breathing fine. The next morning he is the one who reports his comatose son missing, and he looks to the team as though he has broken psychologically (Radford Horror 06). The police later find Irene's body, crucified, burned and disemboweled, in the back of the old church (Radford Horror 08); Yobiah is not shown reacting.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • A neighbor, Meg Gunderson, first calls him Josiah. Andre closes Radford Horror 02 by correcting the name to Yobiah, admitting he had not had a name ready and made one up. The table also says "Yobi" and, once, "Yoga" (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: The Young Balding Cop
docs.text:
The Young Balding Cop is a chain-smoking Rhode Island police officer who looks much older than his twenty-two years, drives the agents to the Brooks Pharmacy, and is shot dead the moment he steps out of the car.

Type NPC Aliases The 22-year-old; chain-smoking cop Affiliation Local Rhode Island Police Status Dead (Roulet Estate 03) First appearance Roulet Estate 03 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Andre describes him as probably twenty-two years old and "the oldest-looking 22-year-old you've ever seen in your life", with a full "Friar Tuck" hairline. He has clearly been smoking since he was six. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The morning after the agents find the bodies at the Roulet House, the cop, who has been in the background of the scene, nervously approaches the squad car and tells them their car was spotted in the lot of a Brooks pharmacy in a town about 25 miles away. He offers them a ride. Kurt, Andrew and the Biz sit in the back of the squad car, Huell rides in front, and Diane is sent home with another uniform. (Roulet Estate 03)

After about a mile of silence he asks Huell, "So, aliens, huh?" Zack (as Huell) flips him off, and the cop, genuinely hurt, answers, "Hey, there's no call for that." Kurt smooths it over with a Manipulate Someone roll of 11: "Forgive 'em. It's been kind of a rough morning, you know. Got shot at." (Roulet Estate 03)

At the Brooks Pharmacy, the stolen car sits beside another squad car with two cops frantically gesturing from behind it. As the young cop steps out, a rifle shot hits him in the head, with, in Andre's words, "too much bullet for anti-personnel operations." Kurt pushes the squad car into cover while the others are still locked in the back. Dante retconned that Kurt had searched the body first, and Kurt found the keys on the corpse with an Act Under Pressure roll of 10. A second shot missed, and Kurt let the others out. One of the waiting cops explains that the car's radio does not work while it is moving, which is why no one could warn them. The shooter was the Roulet Intruder. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.text: • Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Yusuf Ansari
docs.text:
Yusuf Ansari is a junkyard owner near Roosevelt, Utah, pressured by police into falsely confessing to crushing the task force's rental car, and later found alive among the bodies after the Roosevelt police station massacre in The Walkers in Skin.

Type NPC Aliases Yusuf; the junkyard owner; the car-crusher man Status Alive and traveling with the team at the end of Walkers 08; shot in the shoulder and missing a little toe First appearance Walkers 05 (mentioned); met in Walkers 06 Played by Andre

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Yusuf is weary and defeated, in a borrowed T-shirt and sweatpants when first met in custody. He lives alone in a trailer with a landline; he looks at Dante with disgust when asked if he has a cell phone, since he cannot afford one. He mentions that the dating market for Sikhs in Utah is "not so good," and he is deeply afraid of immigration trouble (Walkers 06).

docs.title: The false confession
docs.text:
In Walkers 05 a young Roosevelt officer, who says he does not want to go back to "the burger hut," leaks that a local junkyard owner has a car crusher, a magnetic crane, several grand-theft-auto priors and no alibi. Kurt Larson urges him to match the physical evidence before trusting any confession. The officer later phones to say the man has confessed; Andrew tells the others "I think the aliens coerced a guy into confessing."

In Walkers 06 Yusuf is brought out and repeats "No immigration. I crush the car. I'll pay for it." He cannot say what kind of car it was and agrees with everything, including when the Biz asks whether it was "the Buick" or "the Chrysler." Kurt eventually gets him to admit that he did not do it: his crusher does not flatten cars that much, and the police are "always threatening immigration." The police told him that if he confessed it would just be a fine. He says he spent part of the night on the landline complaining to his cousin about the electrical grid for at least thirty minutes, and that Jeopardy was on. When he learns Kurt is CIA, he groans, "Not the CIA. Not again." The police take him back into custody. See the Plymouth Voyager and Roosevelt Police Department.

docs.title: The massacre
docs.text:
In Walkers 08 the party breaks Yusuf out of the cells of the Roosevelt police station, where he lay under a pile of bodies. He was shot through the shoulder blade, leaving him little use of his left arm, and someone cut off his little toe while he was unconscious. Huell patches the wound. Yusuf says the attackers were "just people... like families," naked and armed with shotguns, and that many cars drove away afterward. Andre's voice for him prompts Ezra to remark that he sounds Eastern European. Yusuf asks for a gun, takes a shotgun and follows the party. His refrain is "I hate it here so much." Kurt tells him: "Playing dead, you deserve an Emmy, my man." See skinwalkers.

He does not appear in the finale.

docs.title: Episode guide
docs.text:
This is the guide to every session of PITF, in the order the sessions were played: six case arcs and one non-canon one-shot. Thirty-seven canon sessions and the one-shot were recorded. Five more sessions were played but never recorded; they are listed in place, marked unrecorded, and are known only from what later episodes say about them (see Lost episodes). For the television framing of the campaign, see The show; for dates, see the Timeline.

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
In May 1992 four mismatched agents are assigned to the new Paranatural Incident Task Force and sent to Radford, Virginia, where a teenager has vanished from a locked bedroom and a child says a spaceman took her. The case widens into missing women, missing dogs, a crooked psychiatrist and something blue that flies over the woods. It ends in a burning church with the Radford Moth, a cover story, and armed strangers who clean up behind the team.

Arc page: The Radford Horror

Episode Summary Radford Horror 01 The task force forms in a former D.C. barbershop and drives to Radford to look for Amanda Lucky, last seen by a four-year-old who blames a "spaceman." Radford Horror 02 A second woman has walked into the woods; the team digs into the Whateley family's tragedies, the town's vanishing dogs and Dr. Lori's prescriptions. Radford Horror 03 A day of stakeouts and a tailing white van ends with a blue flying object, armed "campers" and an NSA man whose flashlight sets Kurt on fire. Radford Horror 04 Overnight the team recovers the NSA man's burned remains, the Biz burgles Dr. Lori's office, Phoebe Augustine vanishes, and a body turns up by the interstate. Radford Horror 05 Amanda's autopsy shows she was crucified, sedated and partly eaten; the team works the crime scene, the patient files and a town meeting. Radford Horror 06 A night stakeout brings a kidnapping, Huell carried into the air, a mummified body in the Whateley root cellar, and Wilbur Whateley gone from his bed. Radford Horror 07 Heroin at the Lawson cabin, a chartered plane, and a ruined church where the team nearly dies fighting a car-sized psychic moth. Radford Horror 08 The team escapes the cleanup crew with a stolen poncho and flashlight weapon, closes Radford on a cover story, and is sent to Marblehead.

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
In June 1992 the team goes to Marblehead, Massachusetts, to find an EPA and USGS field team that disappeared after an explosion out at sea. They find a town run by the Sons of Adam, a church whose communion wine is full of worms, and a glowing creature offshore that the faithful take for an angel. The case ends at a nuclear power plant with a tactical nuclear weapon and a story about terrorists. The case opens in the last part of Radford Horror 08.

Arc page: The Summer Service

Episode Summary Summer Service 01 The team learns of the offshore blast and dying fish, finds a severed arm in the surf, and drinks Amos Shaw's fishy communion wine. Summer Service 02 Unrecorded. Known from later episodes: a dive in an experimental submarine to a stealth wreck, the first sight of the humming ring-shaped thing, and Kurt's nerve-agent exposure. Summer Service 03 Huell finds a blood-soaked house, the wine proves to be full of worms, and the lighthouse yields an interrogation site and the scientists' field journal. Summer Service 04 The team sends for Ivermectin, acquires a Davy Crockett through Kurt's old CIA contact, and faces a Board of Selectmen that meets under the seal of the Sons of Adam. Summer Service 05 Arnold Weathers and his dog are found as worm-filled hosts and destroyed; police and church members besiege the hotel and the team escapes by a bathroom window. Summer Service 05.5 Unrecorded. Known from remarks in Summer Service 06: the scientists are found alive, the team steals a car, and the creature comes ashore behind a cult convoy. Summer Service 06 With a mysterious radio contact, the team kills the angel thing at the nuclear plant: Huell fires the nuke and Andrew finishes it with the flashlight weapon.

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
In October 1992, with the Marblehead fallout still before Congress, the team is sent to Dahlonega, Georgia, over two disappearances and a run of Bigfoot sightings. The trail runs past a river cult and a hoaxer in a Chewbacca costume to the Spud Hut plant, where ape-men are mining gold underground. Meanwhile the Biz's side job for the KGB turns into a national scandal about the FBI spying on Bill Clinton. The finale was never recorded. The non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable was played between the first and second sessions of this arc and is listed at that point.

Arc page: The Things in Appalachia

Episode Summary Appalachia 01 Solo scenes cover the Marblehead aftermath and the Biz's new KGB job, then the team drives to Dahlonega and meets the Circle Chasers and Sheriff Burke. Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable Non-canon one-shot. A 72-year-old mentor and her dim alien ward save a werewolf president from an ex-champion, and the ward ends up lost in Wisukonshin. Appalachia 02 Interviews, a boy's shoe and a gutted rabbit high in the trees, and faked Bigfoot prints; that night the Biz plants a camera in room 111. Appalachia 03 Andrew sleepwalks to a cave of human remains, a German boy vanishes on a mine tour, and a pale creature mauls Kurt in a hidden tunnel. Appalachia 04 McManley arrives, the mothers are interviewed, and the team visits the Covenant in Auraria, which drinks from a river below the Spud Hut plant. Appalachia 05 Unrecorded. Known from later episodes: a Spud Hut auditor approaches the team, the blood sample comes back as an ape and human hybrid, and the Biz has a bad night. Appalachia 06 Frotter Comstock's "dead Bigfoot" is an executed mercenary in a stolen Chewbacca costume, traced to his motel and his discarded kit. Appalachia 07 A secret menu, an SHA tracking device, the breaking Clinton surveillance scandal, and a wrecked Spud Hut truck full of dirt. Appalachia 08 Jan Martense leads the team below the plant and leaves them outside a "break room" of ape-men; Kurt ends the fight with a Claymore. Appalachia 09 Trapped underground, the team crosses the gold mines, finds a crack in the air pumping gas, kills Big Bob and climbs out as Jan flees. Appalachia 10 Unrecorded. Known from Walkers 01: the team catches Jan in the woods, Andrew is shot in the face, Jan is crushed by a falling ape, and the plant explodes.

Non-canon one-shot

Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable uses a different game system, with Rita and Dante as new characters, and is not part of the campaign's story. In the recap that opens Appalachia 02, Andre decided retroactively that it was an OVA on the Smith Hotel's cable television, which Andrew half remembers from turning the set on to fall asleep.

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
In the days before the 1992 election the team follows a report of a dead woman seen alive to Sherman Ranch in Utah. The ranch's lights, vanishing cars and upright coyotes give way to something worse in the towns nearby: people are being replaced by skinwalkers. Andrew Howard is among those replaced. The arc ends with the National Guard, a portal under a community center, and Ross Perot winning the presidency.

Arc page: The Walkers in Skin

Episode Summary Walkers 01 An epilogue to Georgia: Bush briefs Andrew, Kurt questions the captured Jan, the Biz goes on Letterman, and Alberta Wilmarth brings a new case. Walkers 02 The team settles into a double-wide on the ranch and meets Alberta, Walt, Robert Bigelow and the people of Ballard. Walkers 03 A dusk electrical event kills and moves the car; the team starts the exhumation request and visits the grave, the substation and the community center site. Walkers 04 On night patrol a coyote walks upright and the rental car vanishes straight up, to be found fused into a street in Roosevelt. Walkers 05 A night event brings shared hallucinations, levitation and a ring of light Bigelow calls the Black Sun; radar finds a vast cavern under the ranch. Walkers 06 Ballard is emptying out, the sheriff flees the state, Huell is bitten, and Andrew gets a note summoning him alone to the school gym. Walkers 07 A naked intruder storms the double-wide, and at the gym Andrew meets his double; the Andrew who walks out of the fire is a replica. Walkers 08 Roosevelt is cut off and its police station massacred, an autopsy finds a "pilot" in place of a brain, and the real Andrew wakes in the morgue. Walkers 08.5 Unrecorded. Known from the recap in Walkers 09: horses around the roadblock, a radio call to the National Guard, the barricade fight, and the police station cleared. Walkers 09 The Guard assaults the community center, the false Howard is exposed and killed, the portal machine is destroyed, and Perot wins the election.

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
On Inauguration Day 1993, with President Perot about to disband the task force, the team wakes hungover and without memories in an abandoned house in Rhode Island, alongside Diane and a monk they seem to have kidnapped. Something that looks like a Grey is shooting at them with a Soviet rifle. The answer is more human than expected, and the arc closes with the team scattered and the Biz in Russian hands.

Arc page: The Roulet Estate

Episode Summary Roulet Estate 01 After flashbacks to Utah and Christmas Eve, the team wakes stranded at 118 Benefit Street, where a grey figure with a sniper rifle wounds Huell. Roulet Estate 02 Two bodies, a stolen car, a hidden attic lair occupied for a year or more, and the discovery that the house's water is drugged. Roulet Estate 03 A hostage siege at a pharmacy unmasks the "alien" as a man in a latex mask; months later the team is disbanded and Perot phones Andrew.

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
In April 1993 Perot calls the former task force back as consultants under a by-the-book new agent, Daniel Webster, to find an FBI team that vanished in Radford. The town has new disappearances, a fenced site owned by the Safe Environment Fund, and traces of more moths. In Russia the Biz is the guest and prisoner of Boris Yeltsin. This is the latest arc, and its story is unfinished as of episode 04.

Arc page: The Radford Horrors

Episode Summary Radford Horrors 01 The Biz is questioned by Yeltsin in Moscow while the others search his apartment and are placed under Webster by the new FBI director, Giuliani. Radford Horrors 02 Back in Radford: an IRS raid, the missing agents' tents, a clash at the Safe Environment Fund fence in which Andrew is shot, and a rabid mouse. Radford Horrors 03 The Biz saves Yeltsin from a convoy ambush; in Radford the team takes rabies shots and investigates an abduction at the Pinball Emporium. Radford Horrors 04 A survivor of a crashed triangular craft says "not aliens, the opposite of aliens"; Andrew wakes Wilbur Whateley, who says the moth was pregnant.

docs.title: Notes on numbering and dates
docs.text:
• Episode numbers follow each arc's own count, so the unrecorded sessions keep their slots: Summer Service 02, Appalachia 05 and Appalachia 10. Two more fell between numbered sessions and are listed as Summer Service 05.5 and Walkers 08.5.
  • The Marblehead case is handed to the team at the end of Radford Horror 08, and Walkers 01 is mostly the epilogue of the Georgia case.
  • The one-shot has no episode number and sits outside every arc.
  • Andre dates the opening of The Radford Horrors to "early April '93." (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable
docs.text:
Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable is a non-canon one-shot in which an elderly would-be mentor and her dim, indestructible alien ward save a werewolf president from a former tournament champion, at a cost of $125,000 in property damage.

Arc None: a standalone one-shot, played between Appalachia 01 and Appalachia 02 Canon status Non-canon. In the fiction of the show it is an OVA seen on a hotel television in October 1992 Setting A small, low-gravity planet that is all one country: the tournament athletes' village, the capital and Wisukonshin Timespan About two days System A Masks-style Powered by the Apocalypse game, not Monster of the Week Players present Rita (Mirabeth), Dante (Derk), Andre (GM), Matt (guest, no character) Previous Appalachia 01 Next Appalachia 02

Non-canon

Nothing on this page happens in the main campaign. None of the task force's agents appear, and the session never mentions the FBI or the task force. The people, places and objects below exist only inside the OVA.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Mirabeth, 72, has adopted the alien prince Derk as her mentee and entered him in the World Martial Arts Tournament, whose grand prize is a few minutes with the Philosopher's Stone. Derk wants it to resurrect his friend Fatty Gibbs. When the tournament is suspended over a doping scandal, the unstable champion Ovain flies off to kill the werewolf president. Mirabeth sees publicity in it and gets Derk into a children's flag contest so that he is standing under the skylight when Ovain arrives. Derk carries Ovain into space, Ovain salutes him and leaves the planet, and Derk comes down in the ocean and ends up lost in Wisukonshin.

docs.title: The mentor and the prince
docs.text:
Mirabeth is a widow who lives thin on Social Security, with two grown daughters who keep the grandchildren away from her. She believed the hero "legacy" had to pass down in the family, but her daughter Anna wanted to be a ballerina, and Mirabeth was thrown out of Anna's ninth birthday party. Her attempts to recruit elsewhere have had her asked to leave a lot of places. Derk is one of several princes of a human-like alien race. His father left him at about age five on a high-gravity planet "for a few months" that became 14 years, during which he ate scorpions. He escaped by accidentally jumping to escape velocity and landed among hillfolk farmers, who fed him horse feed and used him as earth-moving equipment. Mirabeth found him hauling a hill to make room for bean fields. Fatty Gibbs, a kind sumo wrestler who showed him how to buy food that was not horse feed, died of a coronary last year.

The world is one planet and one country, about half the size of the continental United States, with roughly half of Earth's gravity. Aliens or androids attack once or twice a decade, so the tournament is held to cultivate a supply of useful superhumans. Twice in the last 40 years a champion has taken over the world and killed the president, and the current president would not veto a ban.

docs.title: The safety briefing
docs.text:
In a tent of four or five hundred sweaty entrants, Mirabeth has been handing out business cards, and a weasel-man trainer steers his lizard-man protege away from her. Ovain, the winner of last year's tournament, sits with his arms crossed muttering "This year, this year, this year, it's gonna be okay." He took over the world about ten years ago, broke down and was institutionalized, and the tournament is part of his rehabilitation. Derk gives a piggyback to Delta, a small psychic alien who cannot see the stage. Colonel Sparago, the safety officer, has to explain to Derk at length that the audience is not invulnerable, then leads a chant of the two rules (don't kill the audience, don't kill the judges). Derk's version is "Kill the audience. Don't kill the judgers," and Sparago settles for "Close enough."

An official then announces that the tournament is suspended over a doping scandal: one of the judges has been found to be on steroids. Ovain begins to levitate out of his chair. Mirabeth sends Derk over to say hi, and Derk tells him "Hi! Mirabeth says you're weird!" Sparago asks the crowd for marijuana or Xanax, too late. Ovain screams "You did this!" and fires a jet of white fire at Sparago. Derk leaps in front of it. His Defend roll is a bare 7 and he chooses to escalate: the blast scatters back into Ovain's many eyes, and Ovain rockets out through the tent roof.

Sparago's aide Mr. Cartwright explains that Ovain was put into online dating as part of his treatment, that it has gone badly, and that he has been journaling about killing the president again. Mirabeth tries to slap Cartwright, rolls a 4, is ignored and marks Insecure. Sparago remarks that champions usually wait until they have won, which is why sedatives now go in the victory punch.

docs.title: Defending a dog
docs.text:
Mirabeth decides that she and Derk will "defend a dog" as advertising for Derk. She eavesdrops on the pure human martial artists, who plan to work with the police and the Secret Service and expect "all of these other freaks" to be shot; caught, she claims to have lost an earring. The alien faction under Moraniel takes Derk for a lost child and sends him back to his guardian.

Mirabeth learns that children from disadvantaged communities will present logo flags for the tournament to the president, and that a bridge-club friend on the committee owes her a favor. To reach a video phone outside the guarded compound, Derk jumps the wall with Mirabeth on his shoulders and twists an ankle (1 harm). They land by the stand of Miguel, where Derk hands over $100 by mistake and receives 98 hot dog tacos and $2 change. On the call Mirabeth claims Derk is 14, since the age limit is 15, but her roll is a 3: she gets the wait list and the address of a social in the capital, 400 miles south. Derk jumps there in about 15 minutes. Mirabeth speed-walks down the shoulder of I-95 in pumps behind her parasol, which takes a couple of hours.

docs.title: The library and the social
docs.text:
Derk waits in the children's room of the public library, speaking with his hand over his mouth because he has been told to use his "inside voice." He eats just under half the snack table and draws his flag on the butcher paper rolled out over the floor: scorpions, stars and a dog. The staff call child services and Animal Control, who arrive asking about "some kind of shaved baboon." Mirabeth sends Derk out along the emergency exit signs and tears the cape-sized flag off the floor.

At the community-center social a girl named Sarah befriends Derk. Mirabeth picks out the exhausted Addison and her miserable teenage son as the most vulnerable family. While Derk tells the boy that Ovain is coming to kill the president, Mirabeth sells Addison on the oil pyramid, an essential-oil scheme she invents on the spot (Provoke Someone, 10). Addison pays $400 down and leaves with her sobbing son. A spot opens that night. Derk adds hot dog tacos to the flag. At a Motel 6, the news shows Ovain fighting the military at the edge of the capital.

docs.title: The presidential event
docs.text:
At security Derk explains the beep of the detector wand with a metal plate in his head, Mirabeth assists with her godlike beauty, and the sweating guard waves them through without scanning her. The human martial artists have been deputized alongside the Secret Service; one of them, a monk, recognizes Mirabeth and lets it pass (Pierce the Mask, 12). The president praises the flag's hot dogs and taco shells, asks about the giant scorpions, learns that the dog is him, and agrees off the record that turning into a dog is pretty cool. He gives Derk a sticker of the presidential seal and promises the flag "real serious consideration."

Mirabeth identifies the one weak point of the event hall, a glass skylight over a roped-off marble floor. She borrows the guard's wand, tells the rope guards that the president wants some heroes who are "a little less hero-looking," freezes them with Symbol of Authority (8) and stations Derk underneath. Asked to show his kung fu, Derk puts a ninety-degree twist in a quarter.

docs.title: The fight and the aftermath
docs.text:
Ovain comes through the skylight. Derk slams him into the floor by the tail (12), then bear-hugs him so that his ki blast goes into the floor (15), and both fall into the basement. An attempt to bond over fathers misses on a 6, and Ovain's punch to the groin makes "an alarmingly metal sound" (12). As Ovain charges an attack that shakes the building, Derk jumps him back out through the skylight. The roll is a 7, so he panics and ends up in space. Ovain asks telepathically what he is. Derk thinks "I like hot dogs!" as hard as he can and springboards home (10). Ovain calls him a worthy adversary and leaves the planet.

Mirabeth throws a force field around herself and the president and holds it for half an hour; the Secret Service moves them to a safe room. About 18 hours of debriefing follow. Sparago itemizes the damage: $125,000, mostly impact craters, a ruptured gas line, four blocks of West City's financial district evacuated, and permanent harm to the ozone layer. He tells her that Derk needs a sponsor and must learn to bend his knees when he lands, and throws her out. At 2 a.m. Derk, who came down in the ocean, spends his last $2 on a video call from outside a McDonald's in Wisukonshin. Mirabeth takes out her curlers, does her makeup and sets out with the umbrella.

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The session has no cold open, "previously on" or credits; it begins with character creation. During the setup Andre asks Rita for a dub voice, and she replies that she has only "the one old person voice." Midway through the presidential event Andre shows the table "the title of the anime that we are in," which Dante reads out as "Three Point J over Two." The session closes on "that is where we leave off this one-shot." The placement of the story inside the main series came afterwards: see The 1992 OVA framing and the section below.

docs.title: Anime conventions and the main campaign
What it parodies
docs.text:
The one-shot runs on the furniture of fighting anime. Andre later called it "the stupid fucking shonen arc," and Matt greeted Derk's backstory with "That's just the plot of Hunter x Hunter."

  • The tournament arc. There are entrants, judges, sponsors and a grand prize, and the tournament is suspended before a single bout.
  • Ki blasts. Ovain's white fire and charge-up attack are the real thing. When Sparago asks who can channel ki into blasts, Mirabeth tells Derk he can: "It's called a punch."
  • The unstable rival. Ovain is a former world conqueror who blurts "It's just like Father," undone by online dating.
  • The training mentor. The table fielded an elderly mentor and her ward (see Game system).
  • The alien prince raised under high gravity. Derk's strength has the standard origin. He came out of it with a five-year-old's education.
  • The hero's corrupted name. His birth name is "Dirk Half Scion of Cantus," which he remembers as "Derk Sauce."
  • Jumps into space. Derk reaches the capital by jumping and takes the final fight into orbit.
  • The numbered title and the dub. The title is "3.J/2," and Andre asks for dub voices.

docs.title: How it relates to PITF
docs.text:
The connection was made in the recap at the top of the next main-campaign session. Describing the team's night at the Smith Hotel in Dahlonega, which has cable television, Andre said: "I decided, right, retroactively, that the stupid fucking shonen arc we did was an OVA that Huell watched on the hotel's cable TV as he was falling asleep." Zack, who plays Huell Kendrick, pointed out that he had not listened to the one-shot and suggested giving the memory to someone who had been there. Andre agreed that "maybe Andrew could have been watching it," and settled on Andrew Howard half remembering it "from just, like, turning the TV on to help him fall asleep." (Appalachia 02)

That exchange is the whole connection. The one-shot itself contains no link to the main campaign, and no year is given in either session; "1992" comes from the date of the Appalachia case during which the OVA is on television.

The cast overlaps in players only: Rita and Dante play new characters, and Zack and Ezra are absent.

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• Ovain's breakdown followed failed online dating, prescribed as part of his treatment, and he had been journaling about killing the president again.
  • Champions usually go rogue only after winning, which is why sedatives go in the victory punch.
  • The human martial artists hoped to cement themselves as "the stable, responsible heroes" the government could depend on, and were deputized.
  • Mirabeth suspects that "Derk" is a fragment of the name his parents gave him. Sparago shares the suspicion and grants only that her ward "has a nickname."
  • Derk's jumps into space do permanent damage to the ozone layer.

docs.title: Open threads
docs.text:
• The tournament is suspended, and the human martial artists fear it will be cancelled.
  • Derk still wants the Philosopher's Stone for Fatty Gibbs.
  • Ovain has gone "back home." Where that is, and what his father did, are never said.
  • Derk needs a sponsor and insurance. Mirabeth's mentor insurance has lapsed.
  • Mirabeth and Sparago expect to meet at the next tournament.
  • The flag is under "real serious consideration."
  • Mirabeth's old rival in the retirement home is never seen.
  • The Animal Control call to the library "ended in a riot"; the detective knows only that Animal Control "was sick of prank calls."
  • Derk is stranded in Wisukonshin.

docs.title: Memorable quotes
docs.text:
Quote

"Get down, Mr. Doggy!"

Dante (as Derk), leaping in front of the blast

Quote

"You can definitely do that, dear. It's called a punch."

Rita (as Mirabeth), when Sparago asks who can fire ki blasts

Quote

"Dating is hard, but you can't take it out on dogs."

Dante (as Derk), after the tail slam

Quote

"You have been a strange but worthy adversary. I salute you. I am leaving this planet and its Tinder. I'm going back home."

Andre (as Ovain)

Quote

"A natural disaster with legs and a mouth."

Andre (as Colonel Sparago), describing Derk

Quote

"Grandpa, I need you to go pick me up. I don't know where I am. And I'm scared."

Dante (as Derk), the 2 a.m. call

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Andre observed that "it's amazing how Derk being fucking stupid has dominated the tone of this one-shot." Dante admitted that he "pushed all the onus of, like, actual thinking, planning onto Rita."
  • "Mr. Doggy" began as Dante's own confusion about which character was the werewolf; the table made it Derk's, with Rita suggesting that he believes all people in charge are werewolves.
  • "Asteroid" for "steroid" recurs through the briefing.
  • Hot dogs become a unit of account: 98 of them for $100, and an $86 motel room that Derk asks to have converted into hot dogs.
  • Mirabeth's lies accumulate: the earring, the child-psychology credentials, the oil pyramid, Derk's age. Dante puts Derk at "like twenty-one"; Mirabeth makes him 14 or 21 as convenient.
  • Dice: Dante's fight rolls ran 12, 15, 12 and 10, with a 6 on the attempt to talk and a 7 on the jump that put Derk in space. Rita rolled 12 on the monk and 11 on the wall jump after her −1. Her two misses were the slap, which cost her Insecure, and the 3 on the call to her bridge-club friend.
  • Andre looked up rules live ("this is a really wordy game document") and renamed Mr. Briggs to Mr. Cartwright on the spot when nobody had caught the name. He also gave two age limits, 15 for the children's event and 17 for tournament entry.
  • Matt heckled throughout and drew flags of his own for the table, a corgi among them.
  • Noise suppression made Dante and Andre cut out at times, and two passages of the last scene are choppy in the recording.

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Mirabeth and Derk already have protocols (jump straight up as a signal flare, follow the arrows "until you get to a door"). Andre asks Dante to introduce his character "again," and Dante says "there's a reason I was stupid this whole campaign"; no other Philosopher's Fist session is known.
  • The one-shot is retconned into the main series as hotel television in Appalachia 02.
  • Nothing from it carries into the main campaign.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Mirabeth's name is also heard as "Meribeth" (Andre checks the pronunciation with Rita late in the session) and "Mirabel," and Derk's as "Dirk." Dante says the name is "canonically spelled with an E."
  • Dante refers to Derk's playbook as "the Bull," and Rita mentions a "Legacy" move. The game itself is never named at the table; Andre says only that "this is Powered by the Apocalypse, but it's a little bit different."
  • Andre describes the planet as "somewhere between Japan and the US." At the table it is also simply called Earth, its capital is called DC, and its Wisconsin is Wisukonshin.
  • The tournament's schedule is inconsistent: Andre first says it is run every five years, but Ovain is "the winner of last year's tournament" and Mirabeth looks forward to "next year at the tournament."
  • Sparago's aide is first called Mr. Briggs and then Mr. Cartwright. Both surnames also turn up in the main campaign, with Briggs in The Summer Service and Gene Cartwright in The Things in Appalachia; nothing at the table connects them.

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
The Radford Horror is the first arc of PITF: eight episodes in which a newly formed FBI task force is sent to a small Virginia town to find a missing cheerleader and instead finds a spaceman, a plague of vanishing dogs, and something very large living in a ruined church.

Setting Radford, Virginia, with opening scenes in Washington, D.C. Episodes 8, all recorded In-fiction dates May 24th to about May 29th, 1992, with an epilogue running to mid-June Main threat The Radford Moth Players Andre (Keeper), Rita, Dante, Ezra, Zack Next arc The Summer Service

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In spring 1992, with the Soviet Union gone and the Bureau downsizing, four people who are in the way are moved onto a presidential task force that most of their colleagues consider make-work. Andrew Howard is a desk agent who sincerely believes in benevolent aliens. Kurt Larson is a CIA man on loan with a trunk full of stilts and wolf urine. Dick "The Biz" Baxter is a cynical counterintelligence agent with money trouble, and Huell Kendrick is a disgraced cop in the middle of a divorce. Their office is a derelict barbershop and their first file is a single sheet: Amanda Lucky, 17, gone from a locked third-story bedroom, and a four-year-old witness who says a spaceman took her. (Radford Horror 01)

The case turns out to be several cases lying on top of each other. One is entirely human. Amanda's psychiatrist, Dr. Lori, and the pharmacist and romance novelist Derek Augustine were both abusing her, and the disputed painkiller prescriptions lead the agents to them. Her boyfriend Dean Lawson was dealing heroin, and had buried about $40,000 behind his family's cabin. (Radford Horror 02, 05, 07, 08)

A second belongs to the Whateley family. One twin was supposed to have robbed a Radio Shack in a homemade spacesuit and run away three years ago; the other has sat unresponsive in a wheelchair since a car crash. The truth is in a hidden cellar under their garage and in Wilbur's journal. (Radford Horror 02, 06, 08)

The third is the thing itself. It is first a blue streak over the forest, then a silent shape that blots out stars, then something that takes a dog from a yard and a girl from a clearing and leaves white powder and a smell of rot. In the seventh episode the agents finally see it clearly, and it nearly kills all four of them. (Radford Horror 03, 04, 06, 07)

Around all of this moves a fourth party that the arc never explains: a watcher on a rooftop, a white van, a man with an NSA badge and a flashlight that sets people on fire, and at the end soldiers without insignia who burn what is left and take the body away. (Radford Horror 01, 03, 07, 08)

The arc also sets the show's habits. Each session opens on a cold open and a cut to credits, the party splits at every opportunity, and Kurt's car trunk and the Biz's digestion are established as permanent features. See The show and running gags.

docs.title: Episodes
docs.text: Episode Summary Episode 01 Four reassigned agents meet in a barbershop, drive to Radford, and work the Lucky house; a child describes a spaceman and someone is watching from a roof. Episode 02 The Whateley disappearance, the Radio Shack robbery, a file of missing dogs, and a psychiatrist who denies writing a prescription. Episode 03 A barn stakeout, a commandeered car, an armed group in a clearing, a silent object in the sky, and Agent Murphy's flashlight. Episode 04 Murphy's papers, a searched motel, DMT from Rutherford, a burgled office, and Phoebe Augustine taken before dawn. Episode 05 Amanda's autopsy shows crucifixion and sedation; a hair tie and a set of fingerprints tie the cases together. Episode 06 Huell tackles the spaceman and falls out of the sky; a mummified boy is found in the Whateley cellar; Wilbur walks away. Episode 07 Dean Lawson's cash and heroin, a flight over the forest, and the fight in the old church. Episode 08 Escape from the cleanup crew, the official story, Wilbur's journal, and the first scenes of the Marblehead case.

docs.title: How it ended
docs.text:
The agents found Phoebe Augustine alive, crucified above the pulpit of an abandoned church in the forest, with Wilbur Whateley beside her and the creature in the rafters. They burned it with a bottle of Everclear, tore its wings, cut off a leg and put out its eyes, came close to dying themselves, and locked it inside the burning building, where it died. (Radford Horror 07)

They then hid from soldiers with flamethrowers, robbed one of them, and woke in hospital. The sheriff's account made Wilbur a serial killer with cartel connections: he had killed his brother and hidden the body, staged the runaway, and taken the women. Irene Whateley was found in the church, crucified, burned and disemboweled. The body in the cellar was "probably Abelforth," pending tests. Lori and Augustine confessed to abusing Amanda and went to prison. The agents read Wilbur's journal, concluded that the moth had been in his head since it hatched, and let the police version stand. By the time they returned to the church, the creature's body, the gore and the dog collars had been removed. They left Radford with a heat-ray flashlight, a cloak made of shadow, most of Dean's $40,000 and a quantity of heroin, none of it recorded anywhere. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: What it left unresolved
docs.text:
• Who the soldiers and the men in heat suits were, how they knew about the moth, and where they took its body. (Radford Horror 08)
  • Who Agent Murphy was. His badge matched no record, and his papers mentioned servitors, "Menelaus," "acceptable leakage" and a name ending "...ig Bill." (Radford Horror 04, 08)
  • What the creature was and who made it. It called Andrew "Changeling" and said he knew its makers. (Radford Horror 07)
  • Why bullets slow before they reach Andrew, and what his church's "mace" is. See The Masters. (Radford Horror 07, 08)
  • What disemboweled Amanda Lucky and Irene Whateley, and whether the moth left eggs. (Radford Horror 08)
  • Whether Wilbur was ever truly catatonic. (Radford Horror 08)
  • How the fingerprints on file from the Radio Shack robbery, taken to be Abelforth's, reached the Lucky roof when he had been dead in the cellar for years. The sheriff's theory that Wilbur wore the suit would explain it, but nobody says so. (Radford Horror 05, 06, 08)
  • Where Dean Lawson went, and who his suppliers were. (Radford Horror 08)
  • Who searched the agents' motel rooms, and who "Red Dutchford" was. (Radford Horror 04)
  • Mr. King's prophecy that "the next master is coming." (Radford Horror 01)

The task force comes back to the town in The Radford Horrors. Further analysis is on the unresolved mysteries page.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Names drift across the sessions. Mr. Whateley is briefly "Josiah" in Radford Horror 02 before Andre settles on Yobiah. The sheriff is named Frank Roosevelt in the premiere and is simply "the sheriff" afterward. Underhill calls the missing twin "Abelforth Radford" in Radford Horror 05, where Andrew's superior, Big Bill Nelson, is also just "Nelson." The table itself keeps turning Abelforth into "Albert" and Amanda Lucky into "Amanda Palmer."
  • The mountain ski lodge is not named until Radford Horror 06, where it becomes the Alpine Lodge. It is a different place from the Ferry Lodge, the team's second hotel.
  • The arc opens on May 24th, 1992. The date of May 29th for the church fight is Andre's estimate at the table in Radford Horror 08 ("I think it's May 29th now").

See Lost episodes for the campaign's recording gaps and About this wiki for spelling conventions.

docs.title: The Radford Horror, Episode 01
docs.text:
The series premiere: four reassigned agents are thrown together in a derelict Washington barbershop, handed a missing-cheerleader case in Radford, Virginia, and told that the only witness is a four-year-old who saw a spaceman.

Arc The Radford Horror Episode 01 (first session of the campaign) Setting Washington, D.C.; the road south; Radford, Virginia In-fiction date Spring 1992; the task force assembles on May 24th, 1992, and the episode ends the following morning Players present Andre (Keeper), Rita, Dante, Ezra, Zack Previous None Next Radford Horror 02

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: In the post-Soviet reshuffle of spring 1992, Andrew Howard, Kurt Larson, Dick "The Biz" Baxter and Huell Kendrick are each moved onto a new presidential task force that most of the FBI regards as make-work. They set up in a run-down barbershop, discover an arsenal in its basement, and receive their first case: Amanda Lucky, 17, vanished from a locked third-story bedroom in Radford. After a miserable night in a bedbug-ridden motel they meet the wary local sheriff, learn of a second disappearance, and work the Lucky house. By the end of the session the evidence says Amanda climbed out of her window and up to the roof of her own accord, with help, and somebody on the post office roof has been watching the agents through binoculars. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: Four reassignments
docs.text:
Andrew Howard's boss, sitting on his desk like a cool substitute teacher, warns him that leading the task force "has boondoggle written all over it" and advises him to be "the most normal thing in your environment." In a flashback, Andrew's mentor Mr. King tells him that he serves a higher purpose, that "the next master is coming," perhaps next year and perhaps in three or four, and that their organization must open secular minds to "his truth and his laws" against "the forces of silence" (see The Masters). On his way out Andrew learns that colleagues call him "Andrew the Alien," and decides the nickname is rad. (Radford Horror 01)

Kurt Larson, a CIA man on loan to the FBI Counterterrorism Task Force, is downsized by a boss fond of a crocodile-versus-German-Shepherd analogy, and is given a "sweetheart" gig hunting ghosts and little green men for the president until his contract ends. Dick Baxter of Counterintelligence is paged out of the canteen mid-corn-dog and laterally transferred to a unit described to him as handling "technological threats to national security"; his boss recites the chain of command as Andrew Howard, then Big Bill Nelson, then the deputy director, then Bush Sr. Huell Kendrick, in the middle of a divorce, is told that he is not fired and that charges will not be pressed, but that he is off his investigation and his team and bound for a "make-work task force." Dick's coworker Toby, his successor Donner and the other office figures are listed under minor characters. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: The barbershop
docs.text:
On May 24th, 1992, at about 7 a.m., Andrew finds the task force's address: a derelict former Capitol Police building, a barbershop full of document boxes, with a ticket-covered 1961 Lincoln Continental parked in the fire lane as the unit's loan car. Inside is the secretary, Diane, chain-smoking and spinning in a barber chair, as baffled by the posting as anyone. A Tough roll of 7 leaves Andrew desperate for a bathroom that is full of boxes, and he uses a barber sink while Diane retreats upstairs singing "Natural Woman." Dick, who has been staking out the building from across the street for hours, sees it happen. (Radford Horror 01)

The rest of the team arrives around 9 a.m. Clearing the bathroom, Huell (Investigate a Mystery, rolled on Cool and ruled a complete success) finds a medicine cabinet hidden behind the plumbing holding two mason jars labelled "Ephedrine" and "Mandrax," which Diane calls old "stakeout candy." Kurt's opinions on expired Mandrax bring up his past in UTAW. Asked what the unit does, Andrew answers, "We're hunting aliens." Kurt then turns to the keypad-locked steel door to the basement: after a hopeful 0-0-0 fails, he fetches Luminol and a blacklight from his minivan, sees 0, 1, 4 and 5 glowing, and works through combinations until the three-digit code turns out to be 4-5-1. He cartwheels down the stairs gun in hand (Act Under Pressure, a 10 on the dice plus 2 Cool) into a steel-walled panic room stocked with Vietnam-era arms: M16s, a napalm launcher, a box of hand grenades, what Kurt takes for an RPG, and a couple of landmines. When Diane notices a landmine, Andrew gives her a speech about benevolent aliens guiding humanity, and she resolves to trust "the institution and you personally." (Radford Horror 01)

A courier delivers the first case file. Radford is a hotspot on the Atolean Paranatural Index, which ranks places by UFO and cryptid sightings and disappearances per capita, and Amanda Lucky vanished two days earlier from a third-story bedroom locked from the inside. An insomniac four-year-old says a spaceman took her, and an artist's sketch is attached. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: The road to Radford
docs.text:
The team drives four hours and sixteen minutes in the Lincoln, which has no air conditioning and a radio that drifts to static. Kurt drives and serves cucumber sandwiches and juice boxes packed by his wife; Dick and Huell play War and drink in the back. At a gas stop in Harrisonburg, Dick's Act Under Pressure roll of 7 offers him a hard choice in the toilet (he can finish, but something will tear), which he declines, beginning the campaign's longest-running bodily saga. (Radford Horror 01)

Radford proves "offensively quaint": population 16,000, colonial revival kitsch, a river and train tracks. The Ferry Lodge is booked solid by an oral surgeons' convention, so the agents take four rooms at $26 each, cash only, at the Pay n' Stay across the street. Its clerk, an Art Bell listener surrounded by UFO posters, warns of missing people, lights in the sky and "people walking around who haven't even been born," and says his father thought the town was cursed because the local armory (the Radford Arsenal) made the guncotton for the atom bomb. Kurt phones the sheriff's office, where Deputy Molly Underhill fetches Sheriff Frank Roosevelt, who sets a 9 a.m. meeting and recommends aluminum foil under the bed feet. Nobody trusts the beds. Dick lies on the shower curtain, rolls a 6 and does not sleep at all; Kurt, in a wetsuit with foil under the bed feet, rolls a 9 and sleeps passably; Huell wakes with a rash across his back; and Andrew, curled up in the tub, sleeps soundly. By 7 a.m. Andrew has spent an hour debating good and bad aliens with the clerk. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: The diner and the watcher
docs.text:
At the Lonely Mountain Diner the waitress Sheila serves breakfast and a superb blackcurrant pie, and blames Radford's disappearances on careless hikers and bears. Stepping out to a payphone, Kurt spots a man in black with binoculars on the post office roof and about forty missing-dog posters. Underhill tells him the sheriff is running late and that she knows of no surveillance operation; Kurt memorizes the plates in the post office lot (Sharp, 13, enough to recognize the cars if he sees them again) and quietly warns the others. A red Miata with a cut muffler roars past, and Sheila names the driver as Dean Lawson, a high-school football player whose parents bought him the car. (Radford Horror 01)

Roosevelt arrives late, sends Underhill to a payphone to verify the agents' credentials with the FBI (Kurt has only his CIA case officer papers, which Underhill takes down too), and asks for no "cowboy bullshit." Dick tries to win him over by calling the case make-work and misses on Manipulate Someone (6, even with +2 Charm). The sheriff's delay has a cause: the evening before, Mrs. Whateley, whose family knows the Luckys and lives a couple of miles from them, stared out of her kitchen window while making dinner, put down her pan and walked off into the night as her husband watched; the woods have been searched since. Roosevelt adds that he recently saw Amanda with a biker who is not her boyfriend, Matt McCready, and at the house he lists her boyfriend Dean Lawson and the Whateley twins as the other young men in her life. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: The Lucky house and the witness
docs.text:
Amanda's third-story bedroom at the Lucky house overhangs a carport, with a two-story drop and no impact marks; the door was locked from inside. Dick's roll of 6 gets nothing useful from the distraught parents, but Huell (an 11 on the dice for a total of 14, hold 2) interviews Liam Lucky alone and establishes that the parents are innocent and that Liam does classified work at the Arsenal. Kurt (Investigate, 13) finds the window unlocked, the drainpipe above it knocked loose, and a hollow bedpost hiding Xanax and Vicodin prescribed by Dr. Lawrence Lori, the town's only therapist, whom Amanda had been seeing for about a year and whom the Luckys believed was helping with her grades and study habits. Andrew (Investigate, 9 plus 1) finds Amanda's diary with every page removed. Kurt climbs the ivy trellis to the roof and finds a bent, scratched metal smokestack where a rope could have been tied. The conclusion is that Amanda left willingly, upward. The parents blame Matt McCready, who lives with his father Ed at a tourist ski lodge in the mountains. (Radford Horror 01)

Across the road, four-year-old Tyler is woken over his mother's objections. Dick gives him an FBI sticker and Kurt a "Viet Cong tooth." Tyler describes a bright light and a spaceman all in white with a helmet, up above the Lucky house, who "kind of just went down"; his parents sent him back to bed, and when he looked again the figure was gone. Roosevelt thinks he dreamed it; Kurt suggests a man in a motorcycle suit. The Luckys confirm that nothing is missing from the room, not even money or a toothbrush, and are surprised to see the diary gutted. The session ends there. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: This is the episode that establishes the campaign as a television show ("If this were a TV show, which let's say it is"). The cold open is a helicopter shot over Jefferson National Forest, stamped "Jefferson National Forest, Virginia, 1992," in which something blue darts over the tree line before a cut to credits. The intro theme plays over double-exposed faces of the agents looking serious in suits, urban decay and cult imagery, and a white-on-black sans-serif title card reads "The Radford Horror." Scenes are introduced with "cut to" and "fade out," and Andre cues music throughout, including music from The Thing in Amanda's bedroom. There is no recap, commercial break or cliffhanger. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• Amanda almost certainly left voluntarily: the window was unlocked, the drainpipe was knocked loose, the roof smokestack is bent and scratched, and the door was locked from inside. Someone on the roof is suspected of helping.
  • Amanda was hiding Xanax and Vicodin (called oxycodone in this episode, and corrected in Radford Horror 02) prescribed by Dr. Lori, whom her parents believed had prescribed nothing.
  • Her diary has been gutted, and her parents did not know. Nothing else is missing from the room.
  • Liam Lucky works on something classified at the Arsenal.
  • An unidentified man in black, who Kurt thinks may be ex-military, is watching the agents, and the sheriff's office says it is not theirs.
  • Mrs. Whateley's disappearance looks different in kind: she saw something from her window and walked away.

(Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: Open threads
docs.text:
• Where Amanda Lucky and Mrs. Whateley are, and whether the two cases are linked.
  • Who the rooftop watcher is; Kurt holds the plates from the post office lot.
  • What Dr. Lori was treating Amanda for.
  • Matt McCready, Dean Lawson and the Whateley twins as suspects; prints from the trellis and roof are pending.
  • What the spaceman was.
  • Who Mr. King's organization and the "forces of silence" are, and what the "next master" means for Andrew.
  • Why some forty dogs are missing.

(Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• The table is new to Monster of the Week: Ezra and Dante ask how rolls work, and Andre reads out the question lists for each move. See game mechanics.
  • During the intro music the table wonders whether Chevy Chase is a guest star, and Andre has them roll for it (a mixed success).
  • Dick rolls three 6s (questioning the Luckys, Manipulate Someone on the sheriff, and his sleep roll), and his digestion becomes a running gag from the Harrisonburg gas station onward.
  • Period dramatic irony is everywhere: Huell decorates his desk with postcards of the World Trade Center and the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building, Kurt says the towers "will stand for a thousand years," and Huell keeps praising O.J. Simpson as a running back.
  • Andrew's use of the barber sink is brought up repeatedly; Kurt solemnly asks whether it indicates a break-in.
  • The bedbug saga: shower curtain, aluminum foil, wetsuit, rash. The oral surgeons become "tooth botherers."
  • The recording is a single mixed audio track with a good deal of crosstalk, so it is not always clear who is speaking.

(Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• This is the series premiere; the characters' histories come out through the reassignment scenes.
  • The dates are consistent: the case file, read on May 24th, says Amanda vanished "two days ago," and Roosevelt, speaking the next morning, says three days. Roosevelt begins his account of Mrs. Whateley with "this morning" but goes on to say she was making dinner and that the woods have been searched "since last night."
  • The task force's name is never spoken in this episode; Huell's boss says it was wanted by "the president's idiot brother."
  • Dante expands UTAW as the "unorthodox tactics and weapons division."
  • Kurt introduces Andrew to the sheriff as "my supervisor, Arnold," and Andrew has to correct the sheriff.
  • Sets up the visits to Dr. Lori, the Whateley house and the McCreadys in Radford Horror 02, and the long-running questions of the rooftop watcher, the missing dogs and Mr. King's prophecy.

(Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: The Radford Horror, Episode 02
docs.text:
The task force works the Whateley disappearance, learns of a boy who robbed a Radio Shack in a homemade spacesuit, maps a plague of vanishing dogs, and finds that both missing women were patients of the same psychiatrist.

Arc The Radford Horror Episode 02 Setting Radford, Virginia In-fiction date Late May 1992, a weekday; from about 11 a.m. to about 4 p.m. on the team's first full day in Radford Players present Andre (Keeper), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita; Kira sat in without a character Previous Radford Horror 01 Next Radford Horror 03

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Picking up straight after the interview with Tyler, the agents put the therapist off and follow the sheriff to the Whateley house, where Irene Whateley walked into the woods the night before. They learn the family's history: one twin, Abe, robbed a Radio Shack in a homemade spacesuit three years ago and vanished, and the other, Wilbur, has been unresponsive since a car crash. At the sheriff's station they find a thick file on missing dogs, all taken from houses that back onto the forest. Dr. Lori admits to treating both missing women but denies writing Amanda Lucky's painkiller prescription, and the pharmacist confides that the paper record of it has disappeared. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: The Whateley house
docs.text:
On the drive, Sheriff Frank Roosevelt gives Kurt Larson the outline: these are the twins Amanda was once involved with, and their mother saw something out of the kitchen window last night and walked into the trees. The house sits in a nicer, cookie-cutter subdivision with a neglected yard. Inside, neighbors fuss around the shell-shocked husband, Yobiah Whateley. (Radford Horror 02)

The Biz walks Irene's route to the tree line fifty feet away (Investigate a Mystery, 8) and finds two sets of footprints of about the same size, one in a heavier shoe, one following the other into the woods until the ground cover swallows the trail after a dozen feet. Yobiah's boots are far too big to match. Kurt interviews him: Irene seemed "surprised," dropped the pan, ignored him and stormed out; he assumed she had gone to scare off a coyote or fighting cats, and waited ten minutes before going to look for her. Since Wilbur's accident she had struggled with depression. (Radford Horror 02)

A neighbor, Meg Gunderson (see minor characters), corners Kurt with gossip. The family was "living the American dream" until their dog went missing, a couple of weeks before Abe's "episode." Abe robbed the store wearing a homemade spacesuit built for a school presentation, and he once dated "that Lucky girl." The table immediately connects this to the spaceman Tyler described. Roosevelt tells Huell Kendrick about Wilbur's crash: fifteen, on a learner's permit, coming down from the mountains in the rain with a high blood-alcohol level. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: Two bedrooms
docs.text:
Abe's room has been kept untouched as a shrine: shuttle poster, UFO painting, shelves of pop science. Andrew Howard, called in as the space buff, finds a hidden book of amateur alien-abduction illustrations. The Biz later finds a receive-only radio on the sill, powers it with batteries from his walkie, and discovers it is tuned to the Art Bell station favored by the Pay n' Stay clerk, whom Yobiah says Abe used to talk to. A roll of 11 on the bookshelf turns up overdue astronomy books, adult ufology texts and a hollowed-out Where the Sidewalk Ends holding about $130, which the Biz leaves in place. Howard concludes that the robbery was probably not about money. (Radford Horror 02)

In the next room Wilbur sits slumped in a wheelchair by the window among pinned butterflies and insects, barely reacting. His father says he has not spoken since the accident and can only carry on an action once someone starts it for him. Both twins' shoes are near the size of the prints. Huell's questioning of Yobiah fills in the day of the robbery (Abe grabbed toast and ran; Wilbur phoned from school to say he never arrived), and the twins' friends: the Nichols girl, the Augustine girl and her brother, and the McCreadys. (Radford Horror 02)

The Biz slips into the parents' bedroom (11, two questions). Nothing is packed and no jewelry is gone, so Irene expected an ordinary night. He also finds Prozac and lithium prescribed by Lawrence Lori, with pills left in the bottles. Outside, Roosevelt says Lori is the only psychiatrist in town and that he is "increasingly thinking you shouldn't go see him." Howard searches the woods for signs of an abduction and misses with a 6. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: The records closet
docs.text:
Roosevelt was on paternity leave during the Radio Shack robbery, so he learns the details with the agents at the sheriff's station. With Huell helping (Help Out, 11), the Biz (8) reconstructs it from the file: Abe threw a cinder block through the window, came in wearing the suit, tried and failed to lift the heavier items (leaving the fingerprints that identified him), and left with lightweight modems, a cellular phone and other portable gear in a garbage bag, then bought a bus ticket to Richmond. None of it ever resurfaced. (Radford Horror 02)

Howard, with his bonus for anything written, rolls a 12 on the missing dogs. A thick folder of complaints goes back a couple of years and has spiked in the last six to eight months, annotated by the sheriff: "What the fuck? Why so many dogs? Perverts???" No dog under about forty pounds has been taken and no remains have been found. Huell marks the cases on a tourist map (8): every house borders the national forest, mostly on the Lucky and Whateley side of town. Roosevelt holds to his pervert theory, is horrified by the Biz's idea of using a shelter dog as bait, and mentions UFO call-ins and complaints about light aircraft flying at night out of Roanoke. Kurt asks Diane to check highway-patrol roadkill figures. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: Dr. Lori
docs.text:
At Dr. Lori's office, a brownstone in the middle of town, Kurt chats up the receptionist about his children and tells her he is a consultant, "ex-CIA," and "mostly desk duty now." Lori says Irene began treatment a year and a half ago for night terrors and insomnia and quit six months ago, unable to bear the lithium tremors and the side effects of the Prozac; he never met her sons. He treated Amanda for about three years for anxiety and depressive tendencies, prescribed only Xanax, and flatly denies the painkillers. He speaks of "the mismatch between the expectations she had created for herself and her true id" and refuses to go further without consent. (Radford Horror 02)

The Biz leans on him (Manipulate Someone, 8) while Huell cleans his nails with a knife. Lori holds out until Kurt points out that Amanda has been gone three days and left in her pajamas with nothing, and then gives up one thing: Amanda said her boyfriend, Dean Lawson, was involved in drugs. Kurt's attempt to read Lori's body language comes to a 4, but Huell's Read a Bad Situation (13) marks Lori as buttoned-down but capable of violence if cornered. With Huell's help the Biz plants a bug (Act Under Pressure, 9); it fails to stick under his chair and rolls into a corner vent, where the audio will be poor and retrieval hard. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: The pharmacy and Arby's
docs.text:
At the pharmacy the pharmacist finds a computer record of Vicodin for Amanda under Lori's name, entered about a year ago, some four months after her other medication began, and filled regularly ever since. The other Vicodin patients on his books are mostly seventeen- and eighteen-year-olds, and Dean Lawson is not among them. Anyone with the password can alter the computer record; prescriptions are phoned in and written in a paper book first. He goes to find the original, comes back saying he cannot talk, and is persuaded by Kurt (Manipulate Someone, 10) to say off the record that the paper entry is missing, "a big problem." (Radford Horror 02)

Lunch at Arby's is a Tough roll for everyone. Kurt, Howard and Huell get through it (8, 9 and 11); the Biz rolls a 5, takes two bites and spends forty-five minutes in the bathroom. At about 4 p.m. the team lists what comes next: the pharmacy's security tapes (kept for only a month), local hikers who might know how someone could live in the woods, the twins' friends, Matt McCready, and above all Dean Lawson. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The cold open returns to the rooftop watcher: a man with close-cropped light brown hair, sunglasses and a dark suit watches something through binoculars, is startled and swears, keys at a small electronic device from his briefcase, runs down a fire escape and speeds off in a white van. Cut to credits. Andre then recaps the previous session in his own voice rather than as a "previously on," and there is no cliffhanger: the episode ends on a to-do list. See The show. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• Two people of similar shoe size walked into the woods from the Whateley kitchen door; neither was Yobiah, and both twins' shoes are close to the size.
  • Abe Whateley owned a homemade spacesuit, stole communications equipment rather than money, and had been talking to the Pay n' Stay clerk and listening to the same station.
  • Large dogs have been vanishing from houses along the forest for a couple of years, at an accelerating rate, with no remains found. The Whateleys' dog was an early case.
  • Irene Whateley and Amanda Lucky were both Dr. Lori's patients.
  • Amanda's painkiller prescription exists in the pharmacy computer under Lori's name, but its paper original is missing and Lori denies writing it.
  • Lori names Dean Lawson as involved in drugs.

(Radford Horror 02)

docs.text:

  • Who entered the prescription and who removed the paper record; the security tapes are kept for only a month.
  • The man in the white van.
  • The Pay n' Stay clerk's connection to Abe; the UFO caller list; the night flights from Roanoke.
  • The bug in the vent, Diane's roadkill check, and the proposed night stakeout in the woods.

(Radford Horror 02)
