docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Andre opens by reminding everyone to mark experience on a roll of 6 or less and by explaining Help Out, which Huell then uses twice with his +3 Cool ("I'm so fucking cool"). See game mechanics.
  • Each agent's extra move comes up: Kurt gets +1 for intimidating with the truth, the Biz +1 when hiding evidence of a crime, Huell +1 on a first interrogation of an uncooperative subject, and Howard +1 on anything involving text.
  • "Perverts" becomes the sheriff's catch-all explanation and a running gag.
  • Dante reveals out of character that Kurt's wife is a former Viet Cong who once tortured him, and that her phone call in the first episode ended with "Come back in honor or not at all, American pig dog."
  • Andre checks anachronisms as he goes (HIPAA, OxyContin, Pokémon) and remarks, during a long stretch of note-taking, "Gotta love a D&D campaign with homework."
  • Ezra shares his theory (Abe living in the woods and eating dogs) while Andre has his headphones off so that he cannot react.
  • Failed rolls that earned experience: Rita's 6 in the woods, Dante's miss reading Lori, and Ezra's 5 at Arby's.

(Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Mr. Whateley's first name wavers: the sheriff calls him Yobiah on arrival, Meg Gunderson calls him Josiah, and Andre closes the session by confirming Yobiah.
  • Amanda's hidden painkiller was oxycodone in Radford Horror 01. Partway through this session the table questions whether that fits 1992, and Andre changes it to Vicodin ("because that was '78"); it is Vicodin from here on.
  • The Luckys said in Radford Horror 01 that Amanda had been seeing Dr. Lori for about a year; Lori himself says about three.
  • Roosevelt is only ever "the sheriff" in this session.
  • Lori first says Irene came to him "about a year ago," and Andre immediately corrects this to a start a year and a half ago and an end six months ago.
  • Sets up the interview with Dean Lawson and the search for the twins' friends in Radford Horror 03, and plants the bug that pays off later in the arc.

(Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: The Radford Horror, Episode 03
docs.text:
A day of split parties and bad rolls ends on a mountain road, where a silent blue-flashing object circles a borrowed car and Kurt runs over a man who says he is from the NSA.

Arc The Radford Horror Episode 03 Setting Radford, Virginia and the mountain road to the ski lodge In-fiction date Late May 1992; the same day as Radford Horror 02, from about 3:30 p.m. into the night Players present Andre (Keeper), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita Previous Radford Horror 02 Next Radford Horror 04

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Listening to the bug in his office, the agents hear Dr. Lori take a heated phone call and rush out. They tail him to a suburban barn where a man is typing a romance novel, and Kurt Larson spends two hours hidden in the hayloft. A white van then tails the team; to turn the tables, Kurt and the Biz commandeer an elderly couple's car at a McDonald's drive-thru and chase the van up the mountain. On the way down, a large silent object shadows their car and flares blue under their flashlights, and at the same moment Kurt hits a man in a black suit who identifies himself as Agent Murphy of the NSA and sets Kurt on fire with a flashlight. Elsewhere on the mountain, Huell Kendrick and Andrew Howard stumble on an armed group in a clearing. The episode ends in a hospital parking lot. (Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: The barn
docs.text:
At Arby's, about 3:30 p.m., the team reviews its leads. From the car outside Dr. Lori's office the Biz listens to the bug (Investigate a Mystery, 10) and hears, muffled by the vent, one side of an angry phone call ("You don't know," "I swear to God"), a slammed handset, pacing and a metallic click. Lori hurries to his car. Huell eases the agents' car out of sight (Act Under Pressure, 13) and Kurt tails him (12) to a wide ranch house with a lit barn in the back yard. (Radford Horror 03)

Kurt goes in on foot. Lori storms out of the barn and peels away; a man follows him to the door, smokes, says "Fuck," and goes back inside, where a typewriter starts up. Andrew, tailing Lori for the first time in his career, rolls a 6 and loses him. To identify the house the others try to rip a chained phone book out of a booth; three weak Tough rolls tear the spine off, and they carry back loose pages while a man mowing his lawn stares. The address belongs to Derek and Maybelline Augustine, the parents of Amanda's friend Phoebe. Deputy Molly Underhill says by phone that the family has a son and a daughter, that she has seen them at church, and that they have never come to police attention. (Radford Horror 03)

When the writer goes up to the house, Kurt picks the barn lock (Act Under Pressure, 9), radios "if you don't hear from me at midnight, I'm dead," switches off his radio and climbs into the hayloft. The writer returns, flips a jazz record and types for two hours. When he leaves for dinner Kurt searches the barn. His first Investigate roll is a 4, but he learns that the manuscript is about a thousand pages of "the shittiest romance novel anyone has ever seen." He copies a notepad of plot notes and dates paired with unfamiliar acronyms, notes condoms in the desk, and on a second roll (7) finds a small hair tie with a pink butterfly in the couch cushions. He reports evidence of an affair, possibly with someone underage. (Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: The failed heist
docs.text: Meanwhile the others return to Lori's office to recover the bug. Huell fails to find a way through the window (Sharp, 6), then talks his way in with a lost-jacket story. The bug is visible down in the vent. His attempt to distract the receptionist by admiring the window is a 5, the miss that levels him up, and she ushers him out and locks the door. By 5:15 p.m. it is, in Rita's words, a "failed heist." An hour spent cruising the woods for dogs and lights finds nothing. (Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: The white van
docs.text:
Collecting Kurt, the team is tailed by a white van, which only Kurt notices (Sharp, 10). After debating a gun at a stoplight, a brake check and Kurt's spike strip, they pick a McDonald's whose drive-thru wraps the building. The van parks at the Radio Shack across the street. Kurt and the Biz walk up to the car ahead in line, which holds a very elderly couple, Howard and his wife. Kurt's Manipulate Someone is an 8 and the Biz's Help Out a 4; the couple only get out after Kurt shows his Vietnam scars, and only settle once Andrew and Huell show them FBI badges. They wait in the agents' car with Andrew and Huell, eating the agents' McDonald's order, and Kurt puts on the old man's hat. (Radford Horror 03)

When the van leaves, Kurt and the Biz follow in the couple's old diesel (Act Under Pressure, 13) up the road to the ski lodge. The van accelerates, the diesel tops out at seventy, and they lose it, keeping only the plate. Reading the road afterwards (the Biz, 8), they can tell only that there are places where the trees are thin enough for a van to have pulled off. Several minutes behind, Andrew and Huell see Dean Lawson's red Miata pull out of the woods where there is no road, and turn to follow it. (Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: The clearing
docs.text: The Miata turns onto a dirt road midway down the mountain. Huell goes in on foot with the Biz's night-vision scope and finds an idling vehicle in a clearing and tense voices speaking Spanish. He snaps a twig, and five or six people with flashlights, one with a shotgun, spread out to look (see Armed group in the woods). Read a Bad Situation (11) and Act Under Pressure (11) get him away. Two of the group reach Andrew at the car with the elderly couple in the back: a muscular teenager in a letterman jacket, who says they are camping, and a thin, twitchy man the teen calls "my uncle Trevor," who reaches into his coat and stops. Andrew bluffs that he is driving his parents down from the lodge (Manipulate Someone, 7), senses he will be shot if he stays, drives around a bend and waits. (Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: The object and Agent Murphy
docs.text:
At dusk above the lodge, Kurt notices stars going out. A large dark object is circling over the diesel. His Investigate roll (9) establishes that it is silent, powered, somewhere between an ultralight and a Cessna in size, complicated in outline, under a couple of hundred feet up, and following them specifically. The Biz tears off the rearview mirror to look up, and both men lean out with flashlights. On the Biz's Act Under Pressure of 12 the object flares a dazzling blue, makes a noise neither has heard before, shows folded, compact shapes, and zips over the tree line. (Radford Horror 03)

In the same instant a man in a black suit, with short dark hair and sunglasses hanging at his neck, steps out of the woods into the road and stares at the car like a deer in the headlights. Andre offers Kurt a choice between swerving while leaning out of the window and simply hitting him, and Kurt hits him at about fifty miles an hour. To Kurt he looks a little like the man who had been following the team, though he cannot be sure. The man cracks the windshield, rolls over the car, and is found alive, vomiting blood and clutching a flashlight and a briefcase. He refuses a hospital, claims to be camping, and finally shows a badge: "I'm Agent Murphy. I'm NSA. You are fucking this up for me. Get back in your car and drive away." When Kurt grabs him (Kick Some Ass, 8, for no harm because Kurt is unarmed), Murphy points the flashlight. There is a blue-purple flash and a rapid electric clacking; Kurt's shirt ignites for 3 harm and both agents are blinded for most of a minute. Kurt bites open a hollow molar and spits a dose of LSD into Murphy's mouth (Act Under Pressure, 10). Murphy runs. The Biz chases him through the woods (Act Under Pressure, 8) while Murphy fires wildly over his shoulder and trees burst into flame; the Biz shouts a warning, fires a warning shot, then shoots to hit and misses with a 4. Murphy drops off a ledge and is gone. In a cutaway the agents do not see, Murphy, with a fractured skull and foaming at the mouth, fires at birds in the trees until the device overheats and he vanishes in a pulse of light. (Radford Horror 03)

Kurt has circles of charred tissue on his chest. The team regroups at the roadside, where old Howard wraps his jacket around Kurt and insists the burns need a hospital at once. The agents return the dented car to its owners with Diane's number for reimbursement, and heads for the hospital. In the car Andrew performs a healing rite (Lay On Hands, 9), healing 2 of Kurt's harm at the cost of a persistent nosebleed, and Huell's first aid (8) heals 2 more. Andrew will not stop talking about spiritual frequencies, and Huell turns up "Baby Got Back" to drown him out. (Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The cold open is set in the woods: a pile of composting leaves and sticks, a heap of dog collars, approaching footsteps, and one more collar thrown on the pile (see Radford's missing dogs). Andre then cuts to credits. The episode has no stated cliffhanger, but closes on the car pulling into the emergency room lot with a burned Kurt in the back seat. See The show. (Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Andre calls it "a roll-heavy episode" in which "we're all having to do things we're bad at." The party splits two, three and at one point four ways.
  • Experience piles up: everyone marks it at the phone booth, Zack levels up on the failed window gambit, and Ezra's track overflows. Ezra rolls double sixes on the flashlight moment.
  • The contents of the car trunk are read out from a shared inventory: stilts, didgeridoos, a jug labelled "Wolf Urine," rollerblades, lawn darts, a black-painted Super Soaker and much more. "Why do you have that?" "Why wouldn't I?"
  • Kurt's LSD tooth is one of four hollow molars, each with a different drug.
  • There are two Howards in one car: Andrew Howard and the old man.
  • The Biz's nuggets come back to him cold at the end of the night. Andre maintains that Arby's is the worst chain in America.
  • When Kurt studies the object overhead, Andre remarks that this is "literally what this is for, for the first time in this campaign": Investigate a Mystery used on an actual paranormal phenomenon.

See running gags and game mechanics. (Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:

  • The white van from the cold open of Radford Horror 02 reappears as a tail.
  • Kurt mentions "the Tulpa thing" as the one time ritual work may have succeeded for him.
  • Kurt ends the episode burned and Andrew with a nosebleed; both carry into Radford Horror 04, as does the question of what is left at the burned roadside.

(Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: The Radford Horror, Episode 04
docs.text:
One long night: the agents recover a dead man's scorched papers, find their motel rooms searched, watch something take a dog from a back yard, and are paged at 4:30 a.m. because a second girl has vanished.

Arc The Radford Horror Episode 04 Setting Radford, Virginia In-fiction date Late May 1992; from about 11 p.m. on the night of Radford Horror 03 to about 6 a.m. the next morning Players present Andre (Keeper), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita; Kira sat in without a character Previous Radford Horror 03 Next Radford Horror 05

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: After Kurt Larson is patched up at the emergency room, the team returns to the mountain road and follows a blood trail to a circle of glassed earth where coyotes are finishing what is left of Agent Murphy. His briefcase yields fragments of unmarked typewritten documents. Back at the Pay n' Stay the rooms have been searched, and the Biz buys DMT from the night clerk, who finally gives his name as Rutherford. Unable to sleep, the Biz watches a dark shape take a dog from a yard and then burgles Dr. Lori's office. Before dawn Phoebe Augustine runs screaming into the woods, and her blood trail ends in a clearing dusted with white powder. At daybreak Deputy Molly Underhill takes the agents aside: a mutilated body, probably Amanda Lucky's, has been found by the interstate. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: The emergency room and the clearing
docs.text:
At about 11 p.m. Kurt is debrided and bandaged at the Radford ER, which returns him to 0 harm and produces about $8,000 in bills. Andrew Howard, still bleeding from the nose, is euphoric because his healing worked for the first time ever. In the waiting room the Biz describes the flashlight weapon and the hovering object, and Andrew quizzes him from a mental list of UFO shapes before proposing that the man in black was an abandoned alien in human disguise. The Biz, who lives in Washington, thinks he was "probably a person." (Radford Horror 04)

Around midnight the team returns to the mountain road. With luminol and a black light Kurt follows the faded blood (Investigate a Mystery, a 6 lifted to a 7 by the +1 Andre grants for the luminol) to a clearing where mildly high coyotes scatter from the remains. A circle of ground has melted to glass; only the back of a suit, the back of a skull and a little brain are left, and the briefcase is a melted wad. A second roll (an 11 on the dice) finds a handful of scorched teeth and, at the edge of the clearing, the wallet with the NSA identification he had shown them, holding no other cards and a little cash. There is no trace of the weapon. Kurt photographs the scene and scrapes about two pounds of remains into a bag. Where the man stepped out of the trees, tire tracks lead into the woods and simply stop, with footprints leading back to the road; Kurt's check for engine grease or other traces comes up empty. (Radford Horror 04)

Kurt puts on a welding mask and Andrew forces the briefcase open (Tough, 8). Inside are a melted wireless telegraph with a Morse key, an incinerated notepad, and typewritten pages on plain paper with no letterhead. The legible fragments, posted by Andre as a handout, include "Salem, Colorado," "annihilation de[vice]," "autonomous political assets," "unwanted scrutiny," "Menelaus," "sequence homologue," "religious ecstasy," "...ig Bill" (which Kurt reads as "Big Bill, probably, maybe"), "unknown servitor act[ivity]" and "acceptable leakage." Kurt says they look nothing like classified NSA documents he has seen; the Biz, recalling a canary trap he once ran, warns that they could be a plant. Kurt decides the sheriff will see none of it. The Biz then cleans the roadside of glass and blood (Act Under Pressure with his concealment bonus, 13), and the remains go into a gas-station cooler. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: The Pay n' Stay
docs.text:
At the motel, Read a Bad Situation rolls from Kurt, Huell Kendrick and Andrew agree: the rooms have been searched. Bathroom windows were pried from outside and suitcases opened, nothing was taken, and only glove prints remain. The Biz, who has given up his room and sleeps in his car, talks to the night clerk. Rutherford holds that the visitors are the Anunnaki, spirits who made the universe in order to harvest it, that they take dogs and people to a pain dimension, and that they can be seen with the right substances. On a Manipulate Someone of 10 he sells the Biz $40 of DMT in a Jack Daniel's bottle with a hole melted in it. (Radford Horror 04)

Rutherford also mentions a guest in a big fishing hat, sunglasses and a heavy coat who checked in that afternoon, registered as "Red Dutchford," drove a brown station wagon, and left a couple of hours before the agents got back. Dr. Lori drives a brown station wagon and loosely fits the description. While Andrew keeps the clerk talking about aliens until 2 a.m., Kurt bump-keys the room (Act Under Pressure, 9, raised to a full success by Andrew's Help). It was never slept in and has been wiped, but he lifts a partial print. Huell, who took no precautions, fails a Tough roll and now has bedbugs. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: The Biz's night out
docs.text:
The Biz drives out with his lights off and his night-vision glasses on, meaning to recover his bug. An Investigate roll of 10 shows him a dark shape skimming the treetops behind the houses that border the woods. It does not glow in night vision, it shrinks as it dives and spreads as it rises, and it dips briefly to the ground in one yard. There he finds a doghouse and a snapped leash (see Radford's missing dogs). He pounds on the back door and slips away as the family comes out. (Radford Horror 04)

He then breaks into Lori's office with one of Kurt's stilts as a pry bar, retrieves the bug from the vent, and takes the back off the locked filing cabinet to photograph the files of everyone the team has met. His roll is a 7, so the cabinet will not go back together. To pass it off as a junkie burglary he steals a prescription pad, throws a brick through the window from outside, clogs the toilet and draws on the stall. He is asleep in his car by 4 a.m. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Phoebe
docs.text:
At 4:30 a.m. every pager goes off. Andrew recognizes the number as the sheriff's station (Sharp, 11) and calls back from the payphone, and Underhill tells him that Phoebe Augustine has been missing from her bed for about an hour. At the Augustine house, where Kurt hid in the barn the day before, police and neighbors are combing the woods. Fatigue rolls leave the Biz and Andrew at -1 for the day. An elderly neighbor heard a scream "like someone seeing something horrible" and saw Phoebe, barefoot in a long T-shirt, run into the dark without answering. (Radford Horror 04)

Kurt tracks her blood with luminol (9) to a clearing about forty feet by thirty, twenty feet short of the river, where the trail stops. Andrew's Investigate roll of 12 finds a dusty, earthy, unhealthy "terrarium" smell and a faint chalky white powder concentrated exactly where the trail ends, and he takes samples. Asking what sort of creature did this, he is reminded of the "Angel of Death" photograph of wing marks in snow: something physically lifted her. More blood at the tree line shows it carried her off to the right, toward the other house the team had visited earlier rather than toward the place where Murphy died. The Biz adds what he saw at 3 a.m. Kurt reasons that the dog was opportunistic but that Phoebe was lured or driven out. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: "Y'all were right"
docs.text: The Biz confesses the DMT and the burglary ("Great initiative," says Kurt), and Kurt's Preparedness roll (7) arranges for a contact, Ralphie, to deliver film-developing gear the next day. Then Underhill takes them aside. A young girl's body, probably Amanda's, has been found by the interstate, with much of the face gone and organs eaten. It is going to Dr. Mauden, the town doctor and medical examiner, who delivered her, and the agents are invited to the autopsy. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The cold open shows the woods beside burning trees: a slumped, smoldering figure, the man who called himself NSA, is approached by a coyote, which begins to eat him. Cut to credits. Play then continues directly from the previous session with no recap. Andre ends on a deliberate cliffhanger ("I have an opportunity to end on a cliffhanger, so I'm gonna do it"), and the players supply Law & Order stings. See The show. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• The man who called himself NSA is dead, in a ring of glassed earth, and his weapon is gone.
  • His papers, if genuine, speak of servitors, "Menelaus," "autonomous political assets," "acceptable leakage" and someone whose name ends "...ig Bill."
  • The thing in the sky is not a tractor-beam craft. It swoops and physically lifts its prey, takes dogs from yards along the forest, and leaves a chalky white powder and a terrarium smell.
  • Phoebe ran into the woods on her own feet and was then lifted and carried away.
  • Someone searched the agents' rooms, and a guest under a false name with a car like Dr. Lori's rented a room for the afternoon.
  • A body believed to be Amanda Lucky's has been found.

(Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Open threads
docs.text:
• Whether the documents are real, and what Salem, Colorado and Menelaus refer to.
  • Whether "...ig Bill" is the task force's own Big Bill. The first letters are burned away, and Kurt can only guess.
  • The partial print from Dutchford's room; the van's plates; the Ferry Lodge's security cameras.
  • The film of Lori's files, the powder samples and the cooler of remains all await analysis.
  • Whether Phoebe was also Lori's patient, and why Lori visited her father's barn.
  • The Biz's unsmoked DMT; Huell's deferred level-up; Kurt's plan to verify the NSA identity through his Dark Past.

(Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Level-ups are settled at the start: the Biz takes +1 Cool ("he's learning to loosen up a little bit") and Zack defers Huell's. Andre asks that this be done up front in future. See game mechanics.
  • Andre observes that the Biz's bonus for concealing evidence of a crime "by far gets the most use."
  • Rutherford's name came from a random name generator mid-scene.
  • Kurt's miss on the engine-grease check (a 4 on the dice) prompts Dante's "What, that's a level-up now."
  • Andre draws a map of the neighborhood, and Zack enjoys that one of its rectangles is labeled "dog." Rita's list of UFO shapes delights him.
  • Sleep deprivation is ruled as -1 to "any roll that requires use of your brain," which the table takes as Sharp rolls, for the day.
  • Andre says he wrote the 4:30 a.m. pager scene before the players chose their night excursions.
  • Kurt complains that his old unit put bombs on bats, dolphins, dogs, gerbils, rats, cats, frisbees and boomerangs, but never had a heat ray.

See also running gags. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Continues directly from Radford Horror 03: the hit-and-run, the burns, the LSD, Andrew's healing.
  • Andrew sets out his belief in the Masters, ascended extraterrestrials among whom he counts Jesus; the Biz, a lapsed but loyal Catholic, calls it blasphemy.
  • The Pay n' Stay clerk of Radford Horror 01 gets a name, and repeats his warning from that episode in a new form: the aliens are here to punish a civilization that has "known sin" since the atomic bomb.
  • The blood trail behind the Augustine house points toward "the other house that you went to earlier," not toward the place where Murphy died.
  • Sets up the autopsy and the interview with the Augustines in Radford Horror 05.

(Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: The Radford Horror, Episode 05
docs.text:
The autopsy of Amanda Lucky shows that she was drugged, crucified and partly eaten, a butterfly hair tie links her to the Augustine barn, and fingerprints from her roof put the long-missing spaceman robber back in Radford.

Arc The Radford Horror Episode 05 Setting Radford, Virginia In-fiction date Late May 1992; the day after Radford Horror 04's night, from mid-morning to about 6:30 p.m. Players present Andre (Keeper), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita; Kira sat in without a character Previous Radford Horror 04 Next Radford Horror 06

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: At the sheriff's station morgue, Dr. Harvey Mauden examines Amanda Lucky with Kurt Larson directing: she was nailed up without restraints, heavily sedated, and something tore open her abdomen. In her hair is a pink butterfly hair tie matching the one from the Augustine barn. Prints from the Lucky roof match the Radio Shack robbery, so Abelforth Whateley is back. In the woods the agents find blood dragged to the top of a tree and the cracked bones of a dog. The town imposes a curfew, Kurt addresses a church full of frightened residents, and an interview with the Augustines turns up a pharmacist who filled Amanda's opioid prescriptions and flinches at Dr. Lori's name. (Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: The autopsy
docs.text:
Following the sheriff in, the team hears from Molly Underhill by radio that the fingerprints from the Lucky roof are back and that the autopsy is starting. At the station, volunteer deputies have been called in and a secretary is shredding paper. Mauden, an older man with a small gold cross who delivered Amanda as a baby, says a Hail Mary over the body and switches on a tape recorder. Part of the face is gone, which he puts down to coyotes after death. A large ragged wound has opened the abdomen and organs are missing. There are punctures through the wrists and ankles. (Radford Horror 05)

Kurt's first Investigate a Mystery (8) establishes that the nails were pulled through the limbs rather than removed, and that the lividity shows she hung from them: Amanda was crucified (see Crucifixion MO). The belly wound is organic, not from a blade, and has no clear tooth marks. His second roll (10) finds no ligature marks, old needle scars six or seven months healed, and one fresh needle mark from the last couple of days. Mauden puts the death no more than four or five hours back. Kurt thinks that is too little time for coyotes to do so much damage; Mauden agrees it is unusual but notes that a bear would leave claw marks, and confides that the nail wounds make him suspect a spree killer. On the same roll Kurt notices a pink butterfly hair tie in her matted hair, the twin of the one he took from the barn couch. The Biz excuses himself from the room and studies the scene photographs instead. (Radford Horror 05)

Underhill then reports the only database match for the roof prints: the electronics-store break-in, the Radio Shack robbery. An APB goes out for Abelforth, along with the child's sketch of the spaceman. In a huddle about secrecy, Andrew Howard says his boss told him to send anything unusual up the chain of command; the Biz cautions that, for Uncle Sam, "state security matters more than lives until it's a lot of lives," and Kurt points out that so far this is only a human murder. (Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: The highway and the woods
docs.text:
At the highway scene, about a mile from the Lucky house, Samson, a part-time deputy in street clothes with a laminated paper badge, shares his coffee. The Biz (Investigate a Mystery, 10) reads the ground: a trail of blood drops and bare foot smears from the tree line to where she fell, a couple of coyote-sized paw smears, and a ring of spatter about five feet across lying on top of her footprints. No one else's tracks are present. Andre confirms that the cold open was her last run. (Radford Horror 05)

In the woods the Biz (Investigate a Mystery, 9 with Kurt's help) cannot pick the trail up again, but finds a branch spattered with gore and a streak of blood dragged all the way up a tree to its top branch, with no hair and no broken limbs. The agents take their own sample and tell the deputy only that there is a "secondary blood spot." Andrew takes the car round while the Biz, Kurt and Huell bushwhack toward Amanda's neighborhood. On the Biz's Sharp roll of 8 they find, about a quarter mile from her house, a scrap of her dress and the week-old skull and spine of a poodle-like dog, the bones cracked open (see Radford's missing dogs). Kurt keeps the skull. Andrew's theory is that aliens pinned her "like a butterfly" and let her go; the Biz prefers a serial killer and coyotes. (Radford Horror 05)

Back at the station, Mauden reports that the toxicology screen shows trace Xanax and a great deal of opiates, enough to sedate. Amanda could walk only because of an old tolerance, which suggests the other missing people may be held the same way. He takes the blood from the woods for testing. Underhill adds that someone has broken into Lori's office, fouled the toilet and thrown a brick through the window, which she takes for a high-school prank, and that Mr. Augustine is one of the town pharmacists as well as a published romance novelist. The white van's plates turn out to be invalid, and the sheriff puts out a second APB for the van. (Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: Bedbugs, a darkroom and a lodge
docs.text:
Lunch is at the Lonely Mountain Diner, where the waitress asks whether the van is linked to "the guy that was up on the roof" and Huell Kendrick orders a stack of pancakes taller than his head. His bedbug welts are now obvious, and the waitress threatens to burn the place down for the insurance if it gets them again. Huell's clothes are steam-sterilized at the hospital, and the Biz buys him slacks and a "Radford, Virginia, UFO USA" flying-saucer T-shirt at a thrift store. The team moves out of the Pay n' Stay into four adjacent rooms at the lodge at $80 a night. (Radford Horror 05)

A Preparedness roll of 10, made at the station that morning, has put a portable darkroom in Kurt's travel case, and he stays behind at the Pay n' Stay to develop the Biz's film of Dr. Lori's patient files. At the lodge he and the Biz go through the prints while Andrew naps. Amanda's file shows Xanax prescribed with a stated reason, doses later raised with no explanation, extra appointments tapering into no-shows, and no mention of opiates. Kurt suspects drugs traded for sex. Andrew's alternative is that Lori and the pharmacist were in league, that the pharmacist was filling prescriptions in Lori's name behind his back, and that the two fell out over it. The other missing patient's file is unremarkable, and Mr. Augustine is not a patient. (Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: The church meeting
docs.text: At 4:30 p.m., with the Biz and Huell still asleep, Kurt and Andrew speak at a community meeting in the town church, the town hall being closed for black mold. Kurt introduces himself as Special Agent Kurtis and Andrew as his supervisor, and gives advice: the victims were lured out of their houses, so stop relatives from leaving; keep dogs indoors as an alarm; lock windows; sleep in the same room. Andrew visibly restrains himself from mentioning aliens. Afterward he admits he was a desk worker until this task force, and listens in awe to Kurt's stories of toppling a popular despot, of a sale made while posing as an insurance salesman, and of a man killed by the oil on Kurt's hand when they shook. (Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: The Augustines
docs.text:
At the Augustine house, Mr. Augustine and Maybelline describe Phoebe's last ordinary evening. Kurt (Sharp, 9) catches a flicker in the father's eye at Lori's name. With Andrew drinking sweet tea in the kitchen, Kurt claims to have spotted the hair tie in the yard by the barn. Augustine says that Amanda visited a few weeks ago for a school project, that she owns plenty of those clips and that the girls play all over the yard; that he has filled Lori's opioid prescription for her a couple of times; that he knows of the "record error" and cannot discuss it; and that Lori came by the day before, upset about a prescription he said he had not written. Lori gives him "a weird vibe": he "likes jazz too much." Kurt comes away believing that Augustine is truly worried for his daughter and mostly truthful, but holding something back about Lori. (Radford Horror 05)

In Phoebe's room (Investigate a Mystery, 8) one slipper lies by the window, which faces the woods, and the other across the room: she saw something and bolted. Kurt misses on her diary (5) but still learns that Amanda was seeing someone besides Dean Lawson, whom Phoebe disliked. Maybelline tells Andrew that Amanda had seemed "off" on her last visits, that one of the Whateley twins once had a crush on Phoebe, and that Dean's parents are never home and he does not go to church: "That boy needs Jesus." The session ends in the lodge lobby with the plan undecided: a night stakeout from the water tower by the ski lodge, a split party, or a chartered plane from Roanoke. Huell wants no part of the water tower. (Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The cold open is a teaser of a young woman in a bloody, ragged dress running through the woods, screaming for help and clutching her stomach. She staggers across a dirt road, something passes overhead and blocks the moonlight, she drops to her knees, and the show cuts to credits. Andre later confirms that it was a flashback to Amanda Lucky's death. Scene changes are called as television edits ("we cut to an hour later"). There is no cliffhanger. See The show. (Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Level-ups taken at the start: Kurt takes Dark Past, and Huell takes a Crooked move that lets him use Tough in place of Charm. See game mechanics.
  • Dante rolls 10s on the second autopsy roll and on Preparedness for the darkroom, and a 5 on Phoebe's diary. A flat roll of 7 decides how well the thrift store can fit Huell.
  • Kira proposes "Roll to eat pancakes." Andre was going to ask for a Tough roll to finish the stack; Zack asks for a take-home box instead.
  • Zack keeps Huell asleep through the church meeting "just because I think it's in character. To be shitty about it."
  • When Kurt pockets the dog skull, Ezra remarks on Dante's habit of collecting skulls in other games.
  • Table anachronisms: Kurt says "Sometimes you really gotta pull out the rizz," and Ezra points out that rizz did not exist in 1992.
  • Andre forgets end-of-session experience until Rita reminds him; everyone marks one for learning something new about the world.
  • The bedbugs remain a running gag, with the diner as their next potential victim and the Pay n' Stay as "Motel Patient Zero."
  • During the opening recap the table briefly calls the dead girl "Amanda Palmer."

(Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• The cold open is the flashback that explains the body reported at the end of Radford Horror 04.
  • Underhill twice calls the missing twin "Abelforth Radford," a slip for Whateley; Mr. Augustine refers to "the Whateleys" later in the same episode.
  • Andre calls Andrew's boss "Nelson" here. He is the "Big Bill Nelson" of Radford Horror 01, usually just Big Bill.
  • The lodge the team moves into is across the street from the Pay n' Stay. It is a different building from the mountain ski lodge whose water tower the Biz proposes as a lookout.
  • The pink hair tie pays off Kurt's search of the barn in Radford Horror 03, and the developed film pays off the Biz's burglary.
  • Sets up the stakeout and the first meeting with Dean Lawson in Radford Horror 06.

(Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: The Radford Horror, Episode 06
docs.text:
A night stakeout ends with Huell tackling a spaceman, being carried above the trees by something that smells of rot, and falling; in the Whateley cellar the agents find a mummified boy nailed to the wall.

Arc The Radford Horror Episode 06 Setting Radford, Virginia and the Alpine Lodge above it In-fiction date Late May 1992; from dusk on the day of Radford Horror 05 to late the next morning Players present Andre (Keeper), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita; Kira sat in without a character Previous Radford Horror 05 Next Radford Horror 07

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: The team splits for the night: the Biz and Andrew Howard watch from a water tower on the mountain while Kurt Larson and Huell Kendrick cruise the suburbs. From the tower the Biz sees Dr. Lori beaten and bundled into a van. Minutes later a dark shape begins circling behind the Whateley house, and a figure in an astronaut suit jogs into the woods. Huell tackles him and finds a Whateley twin under the helmet; the thing in the sky lifts the boy with Huell clinging to him, and Huell falls and breaks his arm. Searching the house, the agents find a hidden root cellar with a mummified, crucified teenager inside, and Wilbur Whateley, unresponsive for three years, climbs out of his window and vanishes. By morning the kidnapper of Dr. Lori turns out to be Derek Augustine. (Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: The water tower
docs.text:
At the Ferry Lodge, rested and free of their exhaustion penalties, the agents take a call from the sheriff. The school has filed enough truancy reports on Dean Lawson to involve the police, his parents cannot be reached, and the sheriff suggests that this would be a pretext for bringing him in. Andrew asks the sheriff's office to do it, first thing in the morning. Andrew also borrows a squad car. He and the Biz take it up the mountain with binoculars; Kurt and Huell keep the sedan, which holds all the gear and which the men tailing them have already marked. (Radford Horror 06)

In the off-season visitor center of the Alpine Lodge they find Matt McCready, in a leather jacket with a paperback. His uncle owns the lodge and has him on night watch against kids with spray paint. He writes a liability waiver in Sharpie and hands over the key to the water tower ladder. He was Amanda's friend. When he asked Dean when he had last seen her, Dean threatened to shoot him or have him killed; Dean has frightening friends, some of them "real methy," and a family cabin about a mile away, which McCready marks on a tourist map. A week ago Amanda seemed to want to tell him something and never did. He adds that while working on the ski lifts he felt something big and silent pass over him, smelling of compost or "an old closet," and that he no longer goes out there without a shotgun. From the tower the Biz can also see a light on at the Lawson cabin. (Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: The van
docs.text: After two quiet hours on the tower the Biz sees a U-Haul-branded van stop outside Dr. Lori's office. The driver punches a man repeatedly in the head, drags him into the back and drives off. Kurt and Huell give chase in the sedan with Huell at the wheel. His Act Under Pressure is an 8 and they lose the van in the back streets. The Biz's Investigate a Mystery is double sixes for 14, and he calls its route to the freeway, but Huell's second roll of 7 fails to reacquire it. Andrew phones the kidnapping in to the highway patrol. (Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: The spaceman
docs.text:
The Biz then notices movement in the sky over the Whateley and Lucky neighborhood, and the ground team turns back. Through the night-vision scope Kurt sees a large dark shape circling fifty or sixty feet above the woods behind the Whateley house, like two round shapes joined in a Venn diagram, as if looking or waiting for something. They watch for ten minutes. Then Huell, with his naked eye, spots a figure at the tree line: someone in an Apollo 11 astronaut suit jogging into the woods. (Radford Horror 06)

Kurt takes his black-painted Super Soaker, loaded with glow-stick fluid, to mark the craft. Huell runs the spaceman down (Act Under Pressure, 10), tackles him in a clearing and pulls off the helmet. Underneath, Huell recognizes one of the Whateley boys. Something enormous descends and blots out the stars. Kurt sprays it (Kick Some Ass, 8): a glowing yellow line splashes across it, it makes a noise, and something "punches him in the brain," blinding him and dealing 2 harm. Huell puts a knife to the boy's face and demands to know what he is doing (Manipulate Someone with Tough, 11). The boy answers calmly, "You don't have to fight this. It's okay," and something above grabs him and lifts him. Huell hugs him and hangs on (Act Under Pressure, 7) and is carried over the tree line into a smell of rotting wood and black mold. The boy looks him in the eye and says, "It's okay. It's worth it," and Huell loses his grip and falls about fifty feet from the clearing (Tough, 6). He breaks his right arm, takes 4 harm and is knocked out. (Radford Horror 06)

From the tower the Biz and Andrew see the glow line, watch Huell drop, and see the shape dive into the Whateley back yard; they throw the key back to McCready and race down the mountain. Kurt finds Huell at the foot of a tree (Investigate a Mystery, 10) and revives him with smelling salts, and the arm is splinted with one of Kurt's stilts. The shape lifts off again without the astronaut, flashing blue under the streetlights, and Kurt tails it by car (11) for two miles along the tree line and back again before it turns into the forest. He marks its last heading on the tourist map. (Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: The cellar
docs.text:
At the dark Whateley house Kurt finds mud up the wall to an open second-story window, which is not Wilbur's, and the garage door ajar (Investigate a Mystery, 11). At the back of the crammed garage, under a tarp, are rotten cellar doors with a padlock. Nobody answers the front door, so Kurt, calling it hot pursuit, picks the lock; he misses the roll and it takes him ten minutes. Upstairs Yobiah Whateley is alive but insensible on sleeping pills. In the second bedroom the window is open, the radio has been knocked off the sill, and muddy tracks end at the window. In the third, Wilbur lies in bed beside his wheelchair with clean feet and thin legs. Smelling salts draw only a vacant stare and soft crying, and Kurt stops. (Radford Horror 06)

Kurt cuts the padlock with bolt cutters. The cellar is five feet high and hung with ratty tarps. Among them are the discarded pieces of the spacesuit, an old dog skeleton whose bones look as if they had been fed through a paper shredder, papery fibrous shreds, and behind the last tarp a mummified teenager in a NASA T-shirt, nailed to the wall through wrists and ankles with the legs spread, the side of the head stove in. The face is too withered to read; the agents presume it is Abelforth Whateley. The Biz's Investigate roll (10) finds a fibrous root-like growth wrapped around a floor joist, its lower end sawn off, with the same organic smell as the thing in the sky; the body is too dry for the time it has been there. They photograph everything and, after some argument, decide not to tell the sheriff. (Radford Horror 06)

At about 11:30 p.m. the Biz looks in on Wilbur again. The bed is empty; Kurt concludes that he went out of the window as soon as nobody was watching the back yard. Back in the cellar, the Biz hides a live bug behind the loose flag patch of the suit, which turns out to be lovingly handmade. Huell finds a spare length of chain (Sharp, 10) and Kurt relocks the cellar doors with his help, leaving scratches around the padlock. The Biz spends the night in a bush watching the window, and nobody returns. (Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: Morning
docs.text:
During the night Andrew drives Huell to the ER, where he is seen by the doctor who treated his bedbugs earlier that day; he is healed but keeps a -1 on shooting and arm-strength rolls. About four hours after the kidnapping the highway patrol pages Andrew: the van's occupants were found at a motel, one torturing the other with pliers and a blowtorch. The victim is Lawrence Lori. In the morning the sheriff reports three missing persons, Wilbur, Lori and Derek Augustine, and Yobiah is led from his house near catatonic. Later the sheriff learns that Augustine is the man in custody. He believed Lori had taken Phoebe and was trying to force her whereabouts out of him, and says he got the idea from the agents. (Radford Horror 06)

The team leaves the sheriff's search party to follow the craft's last heading. Plotted on the map, every heading they have recorded crosses in the forest near the river, where they find scatterings of the white powder but, on two rolls of snake eyes, no clearing. Dr. Mauden reports that the blood from the tree matches Amanda's, that both samples contain about five percent unidentifiable foreign matter, and that her blood shows markers of severe malnutrition that her body does not. He adds that Wilbur could probably walk, and could even stand for short periods with help: "It was more just there was nobody home." The agents settle on two next steps: the Lawson cabin, and a plane for aerial photographs. (Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: In the cold open a teenager frantically digs in a dark yard, throws three large Ziploc bags of cash into the hole and shovels the dirt back. Cut to credits. Ezra opens the session by asking, "Is there a cold open again?" The episode ends on a plan rather than a cliffhanger. See The show. (Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• The spaceman is a Whateley twin in a handmade suit, and he goes to the thing in the sky willingly.
  • The flying thing lifts people bodily, strikes at the mind when attacked, and smells of rot, mold and compost. The agents begin to think it is alive rather than built.
  • A teenager, presumed to be Abelforth, has been dead and crucified in a hidden cellar under the Whateley garage for what looks like years. His parents appear not to know.
  • Wilbur can walk. Dr. Mauden says his body was always capable of it.
  • Amanda's blood carried about five percent unidentified foreign matter and signs of starvation.
  • Dr. Lori's kidnapper was Derek Augustine, acting on his own suspicion.
  • The craft's headings converge on the forest by the river.

(Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: Open threads
docs.text:
• Which twin was in the suit. With a body in the cellar, Kurt reasons that it was "probably the other kid," Wilbur; Radford Horror 07 and Radford Horror 08 bear this out.
  • How Abelforth's fingerprints came to be on the Lucky roof days ago if he has been dead for years.
  • Whether Wilbur is controlled, possessed or has been feigning.
  • Who buried the cash in the cold open (answered in Radford Horror 07: Dean Lawson, in the yard of his family's cabin).
  • The Lawson cabin, with its light on, and Dean's truancy pickup.
  • Whether the scratched cellar lock and the hidden bug will expose the agents' search.
  • Where the thing lands.

(Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Ezra rolls double sixes to track the van. In the woods the next morning both Dante and Ezra roll snake eyes on the same search. Dante gets a 6 on each of his two lockpicking rolls. After a run of 7s and 8s, Huell's fall is the only one of Zack's rolls low enough to earn experience.
  • Huell uses his new move for the first time, rolling Tough in place of Charm when threatening violence. Zack calls it his "Hoodlum ability," and later in the session wonders aloud whether he was allowed to take it.
  • The tower team's ability to see anything at all is credited to "hand wave binoculars," then "CIA binoculars."
  • Ezra gives the Biz a Columbo voice on the radio.
  • Kira urges the party, repeatedly, to eat the root.
  • The twins' names are mixed up all session ("Albert," "Walter"), Yobiah becomes "Yobi," and Amanda Lucky is once again "Amanda Palmer."
  • When Andre mentions the McDonald's where Kurt "carjacked" the elderly couple, Dante objects that this is "not the preferred nomenclature."
  • Andre's music cues include Psycho, "Tubular Bells" and Laura Palmer's theme.

See running gags and game mechanics. (Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Matt McCready says here that his uncle owns the lodge. Radford Horror 01 calls him "Ed McCready's boy," and Radford Horror 02 has him working at "his folks' place."
  • The mountain ski lodge is named for the first time, as the Alpine Lodge, on McCready's waiver. The team's hotel has been the Ferry Lodge since Radford Horror 01.
  • McCready's account of something big and silent with a compost smell matches what Huell smells when he is carried off.
  • The Radio Shack robbery, the spaceman sketch and the roof fingerprints all converge on the Whateley house.
  • The crucifixion in the cellar matches Amanda's wounds from Radford Horror 05; see Crucifixion MO.
  • Derek Augustine's attack on Lori grows out of Kurt's questions about Lori in Radford Horror 05.
  • The cold open and McCready's map set up the visit to the Lawson cabin in Radford Horror 07.

(Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: The Radford Horror, Episode 07
docs.text:
The agents dig up a teenager's heroin money, bribe a pilot with it, find a ruined church from the air, and walk into the campaign's first real fight: a car-sized blue butterfly that leaves all four of them bleeding outside a burning building.

Arc The Radford Horror Episode 07 Setting Stately Acres, Radford, Roanoke and the forest In-fiction date Late May 1992; the day after Radford Horror 06, from midday to nightfall Players present Andre (Keeper), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita; Ben sat in without a character Previous Radford Horror 06 Next Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Looking for Dean Lawson, the team talks its way past a lonely gate guard, Douglas Douglas, and finds about $40,000 buried behind the Lawson cabin and a briefcase of heroin under a child's bed. Kurt Larson uses the heroin to win over a charter pilot called Freak, and from the air spots a ruined church with a flash of blue in its broken roof. Inside they find Phoebe Augustine crucified but alive, Wilbur Whateley rocking on the floor, and in the rafters the creature. The fight leaves all four agents close to death. The church burns with the creature locked inside, and as the agents lie stabilized in the clearing, soldiers without insignia and men with flamethrowers come out of the trees. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: Stately Acres
docs.text: At midday the sedan reaches the gate of Stately Acres, a seasonal mountain community near the ski lodge and two miles from the clearing where the armed group met. The guard, named on the spot as Douglas Douglas, lives in a portable shack with a bed and some thirty years of vintage pinball machines. Kurt poses as a private investigator hired by Amanda's family; Douglas tells Andrew Howard, "you look the most like a Fed of anyone I've ever seen." He cannot leave his post without being fired, must buy his food from the company, and gets a supply drop every three months. He begs for toilet paper, draws a sign advertising a pinball hall for the agents to hang in town, and volunteers that Dean has been up several times lately carrying a shovel. Dean also kicked one of his cats. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: The Lawson cabin
docs.text:
The Lawson cabin is stone and timber with piled-up mail and recent tire tracks. In the back yard the earth at the tree line has been disturbed. Kurt rolls to see whether he packed a shovel and gets snake eyes, so the Biz steals one from the community tool shed (Act Under Pressure, 11) while Andrew keeps Douglas talking about aliens and pinball (Help Out, 7) and Kurt digs with his hands. Digging turns up Ziploc bags of hundred-dollar bills, about $40,000, and a small tin key. "That's why they call it the business," says the Biz. (Radford Horror 07)

Kurt bump-keys the back door. Footprints in the dust lead to a bedroom preserved as it was when Dean was seven or eight, and an Investigate a Mystery of 12 finds a loose floorboard and a locked Samsonite briefcase that the key fits. It holds four parcels of lightly cut heroin, with room for one or two more. The agents keep the drugs, the cash and the key, and refill the hole. (Radford Horror 07)

In town, the doctor who examined Amanda takes a test tube of the heroin, which Kurt values at about five thousand dollars a parcel, to compare with her blood. Deputy Molly Underhill says by radio that Radford has had a few overdoses, that D.A.R.E. came to the high school after a student ended up in the ER a couple of months ago, and that the sheriff is now dismantling the Whateley house for forensics. Kurt expects them to find the cellar. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: Annabelle
docs.text:
At Roanoke Airport the team is sent to Freak, a sunburned, scarred Vietnam helicopter pilot asleep beside a Cessna painted baby blue with house paint. "I don't fly Feds," he says. Kurt offers heroin; his Manipulate Someone is a 7, so Freak wants proof, and Kurt snorts a bump with him (Tough, 9). The fare is $1,000 from Dean's cash. The plane, "Annabelle," has a disco ball, misfires, and barely clears a pine on takeoff. Andrew prays twice. (Radford Horror 07)

Over Radford, near where the lines on the tourist map intersect, Kurt (Investigate a Mystery, 9) sees a clearing with an overgrown building whose caved-in roof shows a flash of dazzling blue. Circling low, they make it out as an old church. Andrew fails to help with a 4 and is violently airsick. The engine cuts out on the approach to Roanoke and restarts when Kurt kicks a panel. Andre rolled for Freak's upkeep of the plane to see whether it would. On the ground Freak tries more of the heroin, calls it Mexican, and says it is exactly what he bought at a party from a young man who fits Dean's description and who said he got it "from a bunch of Mexicans" (see The cartel). (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: The church
docs.text:
After an hour's hike the agents reach the clearing at evening. The church is more than a century old, its windows boarded, with a new padlock on the door, a pile of dog collars outside (see Radford's missing dogs), and an intact stained-glass window of Christ and the spear of Longinus. Andrew is overwhelmed by dread and the sense of a predator's stare, like that of "a cat on a mouse that it's got pinned between its paws." He prays and draws his pistol. (Radford Horror 07)

Inside, a woman hangs crucified above the pulpit, a naked figure rocks and mutters on the floor, and Kurt sees something move in the shadows of the roof. Huell Kendrick orders the figure to stand. It turns: it is Wilbur, known by the scar on the side of his head. "No, it's okay. It's okay. You don't have to do this." Approaching, Huell reads the room (Read a Bad Situation, 12): a gust of air comes down on him with the smell he remembers from being carried off, the woman is breathing, there are two more crucifixion stations, one cleaned and one slick with gore, and there are syringes, gauze, scalpels and bleach (see Crucifixion MO). Huell tackles Wilbur (Kick Some Ass, 10), who is holding a moth pinned to a board, and Andrew handcuffs him. Wilbur says he has been with it so long, that it is more sentient than they are, that "it has to breed," and that "they're born pregnant" (see Moth life cycle). He tells Andrew, "You, of all people, you have to understand," and "You have to know you're not on the right side." (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: The fight
docs.text:
Kurt's flashlight finds it: a car-sized insect with blue butterfly wings, a long curved razor mouth, sharp mantis-like legs, a stinger and chitinous armor. It drops from the ceiling, and the rolling of its wings washes the room in blue light that reaches into the mind. Kurt resists and shoots (Kick Some Ass, 9), shouting "The accident wasn't your fault," and Wilbur screams as if he had been hit. The creature wounds Kurt badly in the leg and slashes the Biz across the chest, for 3 harm each. As Andrew drags Wilbur clear, a voice in his head calls him "Changeling" and says, "You can help me. You have the understanding." Huell lands a heavy shot (12), then fails to resist with a 3 and, under its control, shoots Andrew. The bullet slows just short of his skin and lodges in his breastbone for 1 harm. (Radford Horror 07)

Andrew rolls Huell's Everclear across the floor to Kurt, who throws it as a Molotov (Kick Some Ass, 10). Fire does double harm to it; the wing curls, burning alcohol rains on Kurt as well, and the roof catches. From there the agents take it apart by hand. Kurt's Investigate (9) picks out thin wings, thin legs and unarmored eyes. The Biz rips a wing with his bare fingers (10). Huell takes off a leg with Kurt's bolt cutters and is pinned under its weight. The Biz, thrown forward and pinned beneath its face, drives his fingers into its eyes (8), and a psychic blow leaves him seizing on the floor. Andrew lays hands on the Biz and then on Kurt, taking 2 harm from each onto himself until he vomits blood; his hammer swing is a 3 and he is thrown into a pew. Kurt pulls the nails and gets Phoebe down. (Radford Horror 07)

The building is now burning. Huell throws Wilbur out of the door, and Kurt bites his amphetamine tooth and carries Phoebe out. Huell goes back to free the Biz from under the creature, and its proboscis drains his stomach, filling all seven of his harm boxes. Kurt drags Huell out, Andrew staggers out and collapses on the steps, the Biz burns a point of Luck to wake, a falling roof beam pins the creature, and the Biz collapses just short of the door. Kurt goes back once more (Protect Someone, 9) and is struck by a burning beam for 2 harm bringing him out. He re-padlocks the door. Something slams against it from inside, and Andrew hears, "Save me, child! You know the ones who made me—" before the voice dissolves into screaming. (Radford Horror 07)

Kurt radios Underhill for a medevac: "Multiple officers down. We got the Phoebe Augustine girl and the Whateley boy." First-aid rolls stabilize everyone. Wilbur, both shoulders dislocated from thrashing and his fingernails gone, is catatonic. Then a twig snaps. Kurt (Read a Bad Situation, 11) sees soldiers without insignia, flanked by figures in metal volcanologist suits carrying flamethrowers (see The cleanup crew). They have not seen him. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: In the cold open a man in a suit finds the burned ground and ash where the agents' assailant on the mountain road exploded. He riffles through the ashes, lights a cigarette, and waves soldiers and men in reflective volcanologist gear deeper into the woods. Cut to credits. The episode closes on a cliffhanger: "in the fiction of the TV show," Andre says, the credits roll as Kurt sees the soldiers and says "Aw heck." Dante's first offer for the line had been "I still love you." See The show. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• The thing in the sky is a living creature: a huge blue butterfly or moth that hypnotizes with its wings, speaks into minds, and feeds through a proboscis.
  • Fire does it double harm; its wings, legs and eyes are fragile.
  • Wilbur is bound to it and feels its injuries as his own. He says it must breed and that its kind are "born pregnant."
  • The victims were held at the church, crucified and sedated. Heroin and medical supplies are on site, and the dog collars are outside.
  • The creature calls Andrew "Changeling" and says he knows the ones who made it.
  • Bullets and impacts slow before they reach Andrew.
  • Dean Lawson was dealing heroin that Freak identifies as Mexican.
  • Someone with soldiers and flamethrowers has been following the trail from the place Murphy died.

(Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Douglas Douglas was named on the spot after Ezra asked for a name, "'cause he's about to become the most important character."
  • Kurt rolls snake eyes on having a shovel. Ezra: "This guy brings stilts but not a shovel."
  • Andre says he "wanted this to be a tense combat encounter" and sums it up afterward: "I do like that you guys just came into this building to arrest someone and then just got blended." By the end every agent has been unstable or unconscious at least once. Dante: "Monster of the Week combat sucks, man. I don't know what you want. It's so hard to do anything without being hurt."
  • For the first time Andre rolled for an NPC, to see how well Freak had maintained his plane. The engine cut out.
  • Offered the chance to spend Luck on his failed roll against the mind control, Zack declined: "I was kinda hoping I'd get hit by it, 'cause it's more interesting."
  • The Biz burned a point of Luck to wake up; Ezra had forgotten that Luck was a mechanic. Rita levelled Andrew up at the end of the session.
  • Andre lets Dante retroactively bring tinfoil, and Kurt lines his welding mask with it.
  • Heroin becomes the party's universal tool: bribe, sedative and conversation piece.

See game mechanics and running gags. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• The cold open returns to the place Murphy died in Radford Horror 03 and 04.
  • The cash buried in the cold open of Radford Horror 06 is dug up in the yard of the Lawson cabin, and Douglas's account of Dean and his shovel identifies the digger. The heroin is separate, under a bedroom floorboard; the recap in Radford Horror 08 swaps the two.
  • The pile of collars from the cold open of Radford Horror 03 is found.
  • The smell Huell remembers from being carried off returns just before the creature drops.
  • Wilbur's "It's okay. You don't have to do this" echoes "You don't have to fight this. It's okay," said to Huell in the woods in Radford Horror 06.
  • Huell fights with the broken arm from his fall; Andre notes that he forgot the -1 on Huell's tackle and lets it stand.
  • The cliffhanger is resolved in Radford Horror 08.

(Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: The Radford Horror, Episode 08
docs.text:
The arc finale: the wounded agents slip past a flamethrower team, Andrew's church-issued "mace" turns out to spray nothingness, the police pin everything on Wilbur Whateley, and the session ends with the first scenes of the next case in Marblehead.

Arc The Radford Horror (finale); the last third opens The Summer Service Episode 08 Setting The woods and hospital at Radford, Virginia; Washington, D.C.; Marblehead, Massachusetts In-fiction date May 29th, 1992 (late afternoon) to about a week later; then from June 15th, 1992 Players present Andre (Keeper), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita; Kira sat in without a character Previous Radford Horror 07 Next Summer Service 01

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Outside the burning church, Kurt Larson gets his team and the two rescued teenagers into the trees before the soldiers arrive. One searcher finds them, and is ambushed and robbed of a heat-ray flashlight and a poncho made of shadow. After a week in hospital the agents hear the official story: Wilbur Whateley is a serial killer linked to a cartel, and Dr. Lori and Derek Augustine have confessed to abusing Amanda Lucky. Wilbur's journal tells a different story, of a larva that hatched and spoke in his head. The church has been scrubbed and the creature's body is gone. Back in Washington, a new file arrives: eight government surveyors have vanished in a Massachusetts seaside town. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Out of the clearing
docs.text:
It is about half past five on May 29th, 1992. Kurt, the only one fully on his feet, waves the others into the woods with military hand signals. Tough checks decide who can walk: Andrew Howard is upright on adrenaline with his nose bleeding, Huell Kendrick is wobbling, and the Biz has blacked out again and has to be dragged. From cover they watch the soldiers gesture at the church while the men in heat suits circle it and break the glass at the back. One notices that the door was chained from outside and orders a search of the surroundings. The Biz comes round enough to limp. Kurt hears flamethrowers: "It takes me back." (Radford Horror 08)

Fifty or sixty feet in, Kurt binds wounds with duct tape and balaclavas (Act Under Pressure, 9, with a hard choice). The team chooses to stop for several minutes and end the blood trail completely, at the risk of being found. Andre rolls for the searchers and one closes on their copse. He carries one of the strange flashlights and wears "the shadow of a poncho," the shape of the garment with no fabric, only darkness. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The ambush
docs.text:
Kurt hides as bait under bloody leaves with a lasso and a duck call in his mouth ("I spent a lot of time in Vietnam pretending to be dirt"), rolling an 11. He coaches the others to break the man's concentration with a "verbal psionic flashbang," and Andrew shouts, "Did you know Jesus is one of the Masters?" Of the four Kick Some Ass rolls only Kurt's 10 succeeds. His Help Out is a 12: he kicks the man in the groin so that his head bends into range. Andrew fires the mace that his church issued him years ago and that he has never used. (Radford Horror 08)

Nothing comes out, and the nothing passes through the man's head, erasing pieces as it goes, so that the agents see sinus, brain and cross-sections of skull. As it leaves the back of his skull his face returns around it, and he drops in a violent seizure. They tie him up, take the flashlight, and strip off the poncho, which gives the searchers another roll; they look in the wrong places. Andrew vomits and asks whether he is hallucinating from blood loss. (Radford Horror 08)

After fifteen minutes of limping toward town with the two barely breathing teenagers, the party collapses by a tree. Deputy Molly Underhill finds them. Kurt, barely coherent, hands her the poncho wrapped in tinfoil, and the flashlight, as secret federal evidence. A stretcher comes down from a helicopter. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The hospital and the official story
docs.text:
They wake in a side room of the Radford ER. Diane has driven down because she was told they would probably die. Andrew needed about three people's worth of blood. When Diane asks for the keys to move the illegally parked car, Andrew admits that it is full of drugs and money, and she is relieved that it is only heroin. The ER doctor, who has now seen them "four times in three days," tells them to make better choices, agrees that the Pay n' Stay was a bad one, and prescribes the Biz "some goddamn vegetables." Everyone recovers 3 harm. The agents agree a cover story: an aerial survey, a crucified girl, an erratic boy, and a fire set by persons unknown. Andrew's inspirational speech about the Masters and Mothman is a Manipulate Someone of 5, and is met by a long silence. (Radford Horror 08)

The sheriff and Underhill bring the police theory. The hidden basement of the Whateley house held a spaceman costume with a journal inside it, and a body that, pending dental and DNA tests, is "probably Abelforth," who never ran away at all. On this theory Wilbur is a serial killer who walked out of the house in the costume to stage his brother's departure. The church stands in the old town, abandoned after a colonial-era flood. Heroin found in it, the dozens of spent rounds and the agents' injuries persuade the sheriff that Wilbur was working with a cartel whose gunmen fought the agents. Mrs. Whateley's body was found crucified at the back of the church, burned and disemboweled. Lori and Augustine have each confessed to a sexual relationship with Amanda and are going to prison; Augustine is also thought to be the one who broke into Lori's office. The kidnapping case is closed. Underhill returns the flashlight and the foil. (Radford Horror 08)

The legible pages of Wilbur's journal, which the players read aloud in turn, record a larva resembling Morpho menelaus found by the old-town church on June 3rd, a voice in his head ("She's talking all the time now"), a hatching on August 15th ("She hatched hungry. The dog is dead"), and entries for April 16th to 18th that line up with Abelforth's disappearance (see Moth life cycle). The agents conclude that the moth worked on Wilbur as it worked on Huell, who now says plainly that he did not shoot Andrew by choice. Andrew remembers the bullet slowing. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Loose ends
docs.text:
Discharged after about a week, the team hikes back to the church. The stained glass has been smashed out and the moth's body is gone; Huell, rolling a 5, finds no trace of it. A humanoid fat stain behind the pews marks where Mrs. Whateley lay. The Biz (Investigate a Mystery, 9) sees that the gore below the crucifixion sites has been cleaned away, and the dog collars have been taken too. By the river Kurt tests the flashlight from behind a welding mask: a blinding ultraviolet beam that burns water. The poncho is nearly weightless, dark and transparent, and passes heat and impact, but it cannot be torn and holds his weight from a tree limb (Sharp, 9); his best guess is that it is armor. (Radford Horror 08)

The agents decide to let the police account stand, though two disembowelments remain unexplained and nobody knows whether Wilbur is feigning his catatonia. They tip the sheriff to Dean Lawson, whose parents have just called to say that they cannot reach him, and whose car has not been seen. They keep the cash and the heroin. A couple of weeks later Kurt's contacts report on the NSA badge: it appears genuine, but nobody of that name exists in the records. "I didn't kill an NSA agent, officially." (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: June 15th: a new file
docs.text:
At the barbershop the air conditioning is broken and it is a hundred degrees inside. Several leads since Radford have fizzled. Andrew's mother has been staying with him for a month, Kurt has had his teeth fixed, and the Biz is about $2,500 behind on his car and facing repossession. A crate arrives for Huell from his old narcotics colleagues: a 25-pound stuffed alien with the note "Ha ha, fuck you, Huell." It becomes the team mascot, OJ, with a tie and a badge. Diane takes some of the drug money, which she calls "the budget," to buy window air conditioners. (Radford Horror 08)

Then the courier brings an envelope for Andrew. In Marblehead, Massachusetts, about a month ago, an unexplained explosion blew out windows and sickened the town. An EPA and USGS field team sent to check for a seabed gas leak has been missing for about four days, eight people in all, and the local police have been suspiciously unhelpful. The town is known for sightings of a tentacled sea monster. The team packs the flashlight, a claymore and a flamethrower, takes two cars, overnights near Hoboken, and checks into the Ram and Arms Inn, where the ancient innkeeper mentions "fellas from the government" who came by about a week ago, offers a choice of Bibles, including the local Sons of Adam Bible, and sends up the missing team's luggage. Kurt's Investigate roll finds their field journal: the blast came from the ocean, there was no gas, and the symptoms resembled mild nerve-agent poisoning. The last entry plans a meeting with the town's leaders about evacuation. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The session starts in mid-action with no cold open for the Radford material. Andre formally says "we will wrap up the Radford Horror," then announces a new title screen and gives the next case a proper cold open: four camouflaged men in an unlit steel boat at night aim a tripod-mounted gun with a thermal scope at something that has "got a human with it." The commander says, "Mr. Miller, you may fire when ready"; the gunner answers, "All right, smile, you son of a bitch"; everything explodes at once, and the show cuts to credits. Dante had just proposed a cold open of his own, in which Amanda Lucky's corpse explodes into a thousand moths. See The show. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.text:

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Resolves the cliffhanger of Radford Horror 07.
  • When the players recap where the drugs came from, they put the heroin in the hole in Dean's yard and the money under the floorboards. Radford Horror 07 has it the other way round: the cash and key were buried in the yard, and the heroin was under the bedroom floorboard.
  • The ER doctor speaks of a patient with severe burns who is "missing three or four pounds of tissue out of his thigh." In Radford Horror 07 Kurt took the burns and the leg wound, and it was Huell's stomach that the creature drained.
  • Andre says that both of Kurt's kids have chicken pox; later in the same episode Dante says "we got three kids."
  • The sheriff first describes Mrs. Whateley's body as burned and disemboweled; back at the church Andre adds that she was found crucified, and says he forgot to mention it.
  • Radford Horror 07 left the moth pinned under a beam in the burning church. Here Kurt tells his wife that his opponent is dead, and the body has been removed by the time the agents return.
  • The cleanup crew's flashlight is the same weapon that Agent Murphy used on the mountain road in Radford Horror 03.
  • The innkeeper of the Ram and Arms Inn, with his "Crypt Keeper haircut" and 6 a.m. fish breakfast, matches the description of Jester, the desk clerk of Summer Service 01. Summer Service 01 strongly implies that they are the same man, but the episodes never state it outright.
  • The flashlight, the poncho, the mace, the drug money and OJ all travel on into The Summer Service, which continues in Summer Service 01.
  • The task force returns to the town in The Radford Horrors.

(Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
The Radford Horrors is the sixth and current canon arc of PITF, in which the disbanded task force is sent back to the town of its first case as consultants to a suspicious new agent, while the Biz sits out the story as Boris Yeltsin's prisoner and adviser in Russia.

Setting Radford, Virginia and Roanoke; Washington, DC; Moscow and Oryol Oblast, Russia Episodes 4 so far (ongoing) In-fiction dates April 1993, "a little less than a year" after the first Radford case Main threat Unresolved: the offspring of the Radford Moth, the Safe Environment Fund and its gray van crew, and in Russia the servitors Preceded by The Roulet Estate

Not to be confused with the first arc, The Radford Horror (singular). Dante called the sequel "an Aliens." (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Three months after Rhode Island, the Paranatural Incident Task Force no longer exists. President Ross Perot reads the file on its first case, which says a giant insect was responsible, fires the FBI Director for standing by it, and installs Rudy Giuliani. Perot's own handpicked team of five career agents has meanwhile vanished in the Radford woods; the arc's first cold open shows them being hunted. Giuliani recalls Andrew Howard, Kurt Larson and Huell Kendrick as consultants under Special Agent Daniel Webster, with two orders: find the missing agents, and "establish an acceptable fact pattern" for the original investigation. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

The arc inverts the team's usual position. They are no longer in charge, and their new boss, Ezra's second character, believes they were George H. W. Bush's political dirty-tricks squad and that "alien stuff" is a cover. Much of the comedy comes from Webster recording everything, counting how many people Kurt has skinned, and writing "Andrew Howard is a vampire?" in his notebook, and much of the tension from his slow recognition that the truth is stranger than his theory. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

Radford itself has changed. Molly Underhill is sheriff, Douglas Douglas owns a pinball arcade, and the woods are being bought and fenced by the Safe Environment Fund, which has armed guards, lawyers and a talent for bleaching crime scenes. More townspeople are missing, including Phoebe Augustine, and each absence is explained by a letter about treatment in Los Angeles. A slime that smells like the dead moth turns up in the trees and above an arcade window, and Wilbur Whateley, woken from catatonia by Andrew, says the moth was pregnant. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

A second storyline follows the Biz, a prisoner in Russia since January and now held in comfort at the Hotel Metropol. Boris Yeltsin, who fears his own officers have been replaced, questions him about every case the team has worked. When the presidential convoy is ambushed on the way to a crash site, the Biz saves Yeltsin's life and loses the sight of an eye. At the site, a dying survivor of a triangular craft says his people are "the opposite of aliens." (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Episodes
docs.text: Episode Summary Radford Horrors 01 The Biz parries Yeltsin's questions at the opera; the others search his apartment and are assigned to Webster and sent back to Radford. Radford Horrors 02 An IRS raid, a fence, a tasering, a bullet that stops short of Andrew, a bleached clearing with moth-scented goo, and a rabid mouse. Radford Horrors 03 The Biz rescues Yeltsin from an ambush; Andrew's fever and dream warning; Elizabeth George is taken from the pinball arcade. Radford Horrors 04 "The opposite of aliens" in Russia; the gray van tape; Andrew wakes Wilbur Whateley; camp beside the missing agents' tents.

docs.title: Where it stands
docs.text:
The arc has not ended. As of Radford Horrors 04, the most recent episode:

  • The team is camped beside the missing agents' tents, waiting for McManley and his RV, with a 24-hour deadline from Giuliani to find the agents dead or alive.
  • A copy of the diner tape showing the gray van raid is hidden in a hollow tree, and two samples of goo await analysis.
  • Wilbur Whateley is awake and frightened in Roanoke.
  • Andrew is on rabies treatment that his body reacts badly to and is managing with blood; Webster has noticed the bag, the strength, the bullet and the blood, and has said nothing.
  • A Bivens lawsuit over the fence is pending against the agents.
  • The Biz is in Russia, blind in one eye, three Luck from Doomed, and in Yeltsin's confidence.

(Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)
