docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Andre dates the arc to "early April '93" in Radford Horrors 01, three months after the Biz was taken in January.
  • The rabies course is four doses over two weeks in Radford Horrors 02 and one every Tuesday for four weeks in Radford Horrors 03. The animal that bit Webster is a mouse in the first and "the rat" from the second onward.
  • The missing arcade worker is introduced as Elizabeth George in Radford Horrors 03; Andre's recap in Radford Horrors 04 calls her Lisbeth.
  • Andrew was shot in the chest at the fence in Radford Horrors 02; the recap in Radford Horrors 04 loosely remembers it as "the face or something."
  • Yeltsin is named in Radford Horrors 01 and Radford Horrors 04 but is only "the president" throughout Radford Horrors 03.

docs.title: The Radford Horrors, Episode 01
docs.text:
While the Biz trades alien intelligence with Boris Yeltsin in a Moscow opera box, the rest of the old task force searches his abandoned apartment and is ordered back to Radford under a new agent and a new FBI Director.

Arc The Radford Horrors Episode 01 Setting Hotel Metropol, Moscow; Washington, DC (a school science fair, Huell's apartment, the Biz's apartment, FBI headquarters); woods near Radford, Virginia (cold open) In-fiction date Early April 1993 Players present Andre (GM), Ezra, Dante, Rita, Zack (joined a little late) Previous Roulet Estate 03 Next Radford Horrors 02

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Dick "The Biz" Baxter has been a prisoner in Russia since January and is now a pampered guest at the Hotel Metropol, where Boris Yeltsin questions him in person about Marblehead, the skinwalkers of Utah, a melted alien weapon and Andrew Howard. In Washington, Andrew, Huell Kendrick and Kurt Larson, summoned back by President Ross Perot, search the Biz's apartment and find his gold, a book cipher and a bug-out briefcase with a Swiss passport. At FBI headquarters the newly appointed Director Rudy Giuliani makes them consultants under Special Agent Daniel Webster and sends them to find a missing FBI team in the town of their first case. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Moscow: the gilded cage
docs.text:
The cold open runs straight into the Biz, lying on a king bed at the Metropol in a terry-cloth robe with a champagne bottle under his arm and stroganoff and blini beside him. He has watched a Russian dub of Los ricos también lloran for about three hours. His guard sits at a little table weeping over the soap and eating the borscht the Biz did not want. (Radford Horrors 01)

The captors who kicked him in January and asked about Bill Clinton are long gone. The new ones ask only about aliens, and know a surprising number of specifics. The Biz has met Yeltsin several times. His strategy, which Ezra laid out for the table, is to exaggerate American seriousness about the paranatural, with big budgets, many teams and himself a compartmentalized foot soldier, and to hide that the United States barely pays attention and that Perot will probably axe the task force. If he seems less valuable, it is "back to the frozen shit bucket and the kicking." A Manipulate Someone 11 means the Russians are "buying exactly what you are selling." He quietly notes the window bars and downspouts and hides bed sheets, but does not actually want to escape, and dreads explaining months AWOL if he is sent home. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: The opera box
docs.text:
An officer with unaccented English announces that the president wants the Biz in his opera box in an hour, "clean and sober and properly dressed," and hands him a Russian-style suit that fits perfectly though nobody measured him. He shaves off his mustache. His back is covered in half-faded bruises and his ribs show. (Radford Horrors 01)

In the Metropol's opera house Yeltsin pats the seat beside him and gets to business. Soviet detectors recorded a surge in the cosmic microwave background last year and triangulated it to the "nuclear incident" at Marblehead. The Biz holds to his earlier story: the military handled it, he was an advisor, he does not know what munitions were used. He does not admit that the team set off a very small nuclear weapon. Yeltsin already knows about the engineered worms and has intelligence about a second organism; the Biz confirms a huge sea creature that chased their car, "a big, confusing grub creature with rings rotating around it." (Radford Horrors 01)

Yeltsin explains why he asks in person, says Russia is "developing a test," and turns to the "people who were not people" at the ranch in Ballard. The Biz describes the skinwalkers: good mimics, not strategic, erratic and violent when confronted, the older ones more convincing than the new. Yeltsin compares them to Koschei the Deathless. Then he unwraps a silk handkerchief around a broken, half-melted device identical to the team's flashlight weapon. Several teams of Russian scientists could not identify it. It was taken from a man wearing very dark, welding-style glasses. The Biz tells him what it is, likens it to a Star Wars blaster, and explains that the glasses keep the user from going blind. (Radford Horrors 01)

"Tell me about Andrew Howard," Yeltsin says. The Biz praises his former boss and leaves out everything supernatural. Asked about Howard's family: "Don't think he ever mentioned them. I never mentioned mine, I might hasten to add." (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Washington: the missing man
docs.text:
Perot has summoned the old team on short notice. Kurt, back a day early, is at a school science fair where his nine-year-old daughter Peggy Browning wins gold with a projectile-stabilization project, and keeps up his cover as a "continuous improvement consultant" with a chatty PTA dad. (Radford Horrors 01)

Andrew, off a plane from New York, visits Huell, who is in a wheelchair with a bandaged foot, skipping physical therapy, in a squalid apartment with Roseanne on. Diane has told Andrew that nobody can reach the Biz. Huell plays reluctant, is desperate to get out, and agrees after fifteen minutes of Roseanne. (Radford Horrors 01)

At the Biz's building the front-office staff say, "Oh, thank God, the police are finally here about Baxter. Is he dead?" Half the room looks disappointed at the answer. Inside the apartment the television and heater are still on, there is rotten meat in the fridge, and there is no body. A loose floorboard hides the Biz's share of the gold, eight or nine thousand dollars in cash in Ziploc bags and his cocaine. Unopened FBI mail shows he was granted six months' personal leave for a "family emergency" and never signed the follow-up paperwork. (Radford Horrors 01)

Andrew's Investigate a Mystery (12) yields two things. A discount Playboy subscription begun days before the disappearance shows the Biz planned to stay. And a copy of Moby-Dick has had its first few hundred pages torn out; pages in the wastebasket have circled and underlined words, and there is a chart of numbers and arrows in the back. Andrew quietly asks Huell whether the Biz could be a double agent. "Of course, I didn't notice when you got replaced with an alien," says Huell. (Radford Horrors 01)

They call Kurt, who arrives in the family minivan. He finds bills for classified ads the Biz placed in three small Washington papers (the Washington City Paper, the Washington Informer and the Georgetown Current) and spam mail with shared return addresses. The circled words so far read "instructions to cause soon submarine lost near," order unknown. Kurt's own Investigate a Mystery (11) turns up a heat vent with stripped screws under the bed, and in it a briefcase holding Swiss francs, a cheap revolver, a change of clothes and a Swiss passport with the Biz's photo under the name Noah Mueller. Kurt concludes that the Biz meant to come back, was corresponding with a third party, and was intercepted. He has Diane pull flight records, the newspapers and any reports of lost submarines. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: FBI headquarters
docs.text:
The next morning, outside the door marked "William Sessions," the three find a stranger staring at them: Special Agent Daniel Webster, "a man who looks about twenty-five percent more like a Fed than Andrew Howard." In the men's room an acquaintance named Todd tells Kurt that Perot fired Director Sessions about three hours ago. (Radford Horrors 01)

The new Director is a balding New York corruption lawyer and old friend of Perot, appointed that morning. Giuliani explains that there has been an incident tied to one of the team's old cases, that people are missing, and that the FBI task force sent to investigate has gone AWOL. Perot found the original classified reports unacceptable; Sessions stood by them and was fired. The old team will go as consultants under Webster's operational authority, "strictly there for informational purposes." They are to find out what happened to the previous team and to "establish an acceptable fact pattern" for the previous investigation. Then he asks what they can tell him about Radford, Virginia. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text:
• Cold open: shot in a found-footage style. FBI agents in yellow-lettered jackets sprint through snowy woods at night as something flying picks them off from above. In a clearing they find naked, emaciated men hanging from tree limbs by their punctured hands, bellies distended and rippling. A dim shape in the brush lifts an agent and drains him "like a pouch of Capri Sun." A female agent aims at it, freezes, bleeds from the nose and, moving like a marionette, turns her pistol on a colleague. A helicopter shot shows muzzle flashes, then silence.
  • No credits: Andre announced, "This time we don't cut to credits," and went straight to the Biz.
  • End credits: the episode cuts to credits on Giuliani's question, and Ezra read out the title, The Radford Horrors. Dante called the sequel "an Aliens."
  • Production value: Andre had everyone put on a recording of a Russian opera in the background for the Yeltsin scene.

(Radford Horrors 01) See also The show.

docs.text:
• Russia traced a cosmic microwave background surge to Marblehead and knows about the worms and a second organism. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Yeltsin does not trust that his own officers are who they appear to be: he fears they have been replaced. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Open threads
docs.text:

  • What Yeltsin's test is.

(Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Ezra had not named his new character. Asked for a name, he said, "Fuck me, I didn't actually come up with one... Daniel—Daniel Webster. And I hope that that's not a real name of somebody." Zack called Webster "the Bean to Howard's Ender." (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Ezra shaved the Biz for the opera: "I don't think I can convincingly roleplay a guy with a mustache." (Radford Horrors 01)
  • "Half Gallon Howard," Zack's nickname for Andrew, kept returning, and Roseanne followed the Biz to Moscow ("Goddamn, you can't escape"). (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Zack had Huell pocket a $20 from the Biz's stash as winnings on a bet that there would be cocaine under the floorboards. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Ezra: "I had completely forgotten that there were ever any other agents involved in any of our—" Andre: "There weren't." (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Zack asked whether Radford had been Mothman. Andre: there was no man element, just moth. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Dice: Ezra found his dice in a drawer in another room and rolled the 11 that sold the Biz's story. Andre briefly thought "we've been doing Investigate a Mystery wrong the whole time," then corrected himself. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Homework: Andre asked each player for a list of the equipment they were taking to Radford. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Follows The Roulet Estate by about three months: Huell's foot, the Biz's disappearance from hospital and the shutdown of the task force. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • The Biz's whole share of the gold is under his floorboard here, although the epilogue of Roulet Estate 03 had the other agents bury it in a park near his home. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Returns to the setting of the first arc, The Radford Horror, whose UFO turned out to be a giant moth.
  • Yeltsin's questions revisit The Summer Service (the worms, the sea creature, the nuclear weapon) and The Walkers in Skin (the skinwalkers, the flashlight weapon).
  • Huell's quip about Andrew being "replaced with an alien" refers to Andrew's duplicate in Utah.
  • Roulet Estate 03 left the Biz handcuffed to a chair in the former Soviet Parliament building. Andre placed that in January; by this episode it is April and he has been moved to the Metropol. The first interrogators, who asked about Bill Clinton, have been replaced by ones who ask only about aliens. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • When Kurt asks Diane about lost submarines, Andre notes that the ones she knows of went missing while the team was at Marblehead in The Summer Service. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • The Director is introduced only as "FBI Director Giuliani", a New York lawyer with a long career in corruption investigation. His first name is first used at the table in Radford Horrors 02.

docs.title: The Radford Horrors, Episode 02
docs.text:
Back in Radford under a suspicious new boss, the team walks into an IRS raid, climbs a fence belonging to the Safe Environment Fund, finds a professionally scrubbed site in the woods, and ends the night getting rabies shots.

Arc The Radford Horrors Episode 02 Setting Radford, Virginia: the Ferry Lodge, the Pay n' Stay, the Lonely Mountain Diner, the sheriff's station, the Sportsman RV Campground, the Safe Environment Fund fenced site and the Radford ER In-fiction date April 1993, "a little less than a year" after the first Radford case; one afternoon, evening and night Players present Andre (GM), Rita, Dante, Zack, Ezra; Ethan made a brief out-of-character comment early on Previous Radford Horrors 01 Next Radford Horrors 03

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Daniel Webster leads Andrew Howard, Kurt Larson and Huell Kendrick back to Radford, convinced they are a political dirty-tricks squad. Their hotel is raided by the IRS as they check in. Sheriff Molly Underhill tells them more people have gone missing, Phoebe Augustine among them, and that the missing FBI task force camped by the river before it vanished. The agents' map leads to woods fenced off by the Safe Environment Fund, whose guards taser Webster and shoot Andrew to no effect. The marked spot has been bleached clean, except for a glob of pearlescent goo that smells like the moth. That night a rabid mouse bites Webster in his motel bed. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Getting there
docs.text:
Andre's recap adds detail to the briefing. President Ross Perot read the team's file on the first Radford case ("What the fuck is this? This says it was like a giant bug."), Director Sessions confirmed "it's a giant bug," and Perot fired him and appointed Rudy Giuliani. The team has half a day to pack. Webster brings body armor, a pump shotgun, a scoped revolver and recording equipment. Huell brings DEET and a police-dog training glove. Andrew brings dried pig blood and a bloodletting kit. Kurt brings a spear gun, his P90, a grenade, a claymore and gallons of pesticide. (Radford Horrors 02)

At airport security the spear gun is flagged: the paperwork is lost and Kurt has no badge. His Act Under Pressure fails, but a Manipulate Someone 9 gets it into the cargo hold after he shows the spear scar in his shoulder. Security swabs Andrew's maroon powder for drugs and is visibly disappointed. On the flight Huell tries to defeat the lavatory smoke alarm with wet toilet paper, rolls a 6, and is chewed out by a flight attendant. Andrew wonders aloud whether the moth they killed left eggs: "what's the caterpillar gonna look like? I hope we see one." (Radford Horrors 02)

From Roanoke they drive two rented Land Rovers. Kurt rides with Webster to get the measure of him. Webster says he did logistics at the State Department in 1978 for the rescue of Ross Perot's employees from Iran; Kurt offers CIA "wet work." Webster's Investigate a Mystery (8) concludes that Kurt is hiding most of his career and has "skinned somebody." (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: The Ferry Lodge raid
docs.text:
On a Read a Bad Situation 14, Kurt spots a white van and two inexperienced watchers outside the remodeled Ferry Lodge, now "under new management." Webster books two rooms and insists on sharing with Kurt. As the keys are handed over, an IRS Criminal Investigations SWAT team storms the lobby. Kurt goes prone, draws, then pulls the pin on a grenade and holds it as a dead man's switch; a Manipulate Someone 11 keeps him from being shot. The desk clerk bolts for the back room, shreds documents and sets the file cabinets alight. Kurt tosses a stapler to fake a grenade, she sprints out, and Andrew catches her on a Protect Someone 11. The IRS leader, eight months into a fraud investigation, shuts the lodge. Kurt puts the pin back ("Kind of a fidget") and drops a caltrop in front of an IRS vehicle on the way out. (Radford Horrors 02)

That leaves the Pay n' Stay. Outside it a homeless man says he was kidnapped in a van by chimpanzees, "John Travolta" and "some ladies" with a mind-control ray, and escaped. The new teenage clerk, Charm, hands over keys chained to big red rulers and admits only to mold. Kurt hoses both rooms with pesticide. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: The diner and the sheriff
docs.text:
At the diner Sheila greets "secret agent man," asks after "the one who blew up the toilet," and calls them local heroes. The old laundromat across the street is now the neon Douglas Pinball Emporium. Andrew rehydrates his powder in hot water and covers for it on a Manipulate Someone 9; Webster writes "Andrew Howard is a vampire?" in his notebook. Huell tastes it, then attempts a big breakfast of about 3,000 calories, rolls two 1s on Tough, fails a second Tough roll, and projectile vomits breakfast and blood across the bathroom stall. (Radford Horrors 02)

Molly Underhill is sheriff now, after a "battlefield promotion": the old sheriff had a heart attack and stepped back. She recaps the first case as the town knows it, with its cartel story, and reports new disappearances. Phoebe Augustine is supposedly at a California rehab "like Narconon," and lawyers have threatened anyone who looks into it. The FBI task force stopped by, then vanished. She hands over the lawyers' number, six missing posters and a map to the agents' campsite, and asks the team to do something about the Safe Environment Fund, which has been buying and fencing the woods. Webster reads the original case file, gets Molly's version in private, and distrusts both the cartel and the convenient church fire. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: The campsite and the fence
docs.text:
At the Sportsman RV Campground the agents cut open the missing team's locked tents. Huell's Investigate a Mystery (11) finds no sign of haste or foul play: five agents, a bag of moldy laundry, and a map of the woods marked with irregular polygons and an illegible scribble beside one boundary. Their car is still in the lot with two shotguns locked in the trunk. Kurt's luminol shows only a nosebleed on a pillow. A radio report a week earlier had said they were "chasing up some weird stuff." (Radford Horrors 02)

They hike toward the scribble at dusk, Huell insisting on walking. A quarter mile short they hit an eight-foot chain-link fence with barbed wire and a privacy wrap printed "Safe Environment Fund / No trespassers." It joins an older fence matching one of the map's polygons, so the new stretch probably went up after the agents vanished. Andrew scrambles up and tears the barbed wire apart with his bare hands, which sets a "solar light" whooping. Kurt struggles over (9); Huell makes it with help but falls and jolts his foot for 1 harm; Webster rolls a 5 and hangs from the wire by his coat until Andrew lifts him down like a child. (Radford Horrors 02)

Armed guards arrive on ATVs. Webster screams "FBI! Get on the ground!" and levels his shotgun; on a Manipulate Someone 5 a guard tasers him for 1 harm and the shotgun goes off wide. Kurt fires a P90 burst into the air and the guards fall back. Andrew's Kick Some Ass 10 puts a round through a guard's leg; the guard shoots him in the chest, and the bullet slows and stops an inch from his body. Webster's Investigate a Mystery (10) confirms that he saw it. Over a captured radio, a voice for the property owners orders the guards to stand down and promises "lawyers and emergency response." (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: The scribble
docs.text: With lawyers following and filming, asking again and again whether there is a warrant, the team reaches the marked spot. Kurt's Investigate a Mystery (10): many people have trampled through, the ground smells of bleach, patches have been dug up, and a tree has recently been cut down and removed entirely. Luminol shows nothing at all, not even wildlife blood. High on a branch is a glob of pearlescent, oil-sheened goo that smells of compost and rot, like the moth but stronger and sourer. Kurt scrapes it down with Huell's crutch. Webster tastes it: eye-wateringly bitter, then cold sweats, nausea, a sweet aftertaste and compulsive salivation. Andrew whispers, "Caterpillar slurry." Samples will go to Donald McManley and to Webster's own forensics contact. The site also holds locked shipping containers and a locked temporary building, which the team leaves alone. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Three in the morning
docs.text: Back at the Pay n' Stay, dead flies litter the beds. Webster leaves his camcorder running in a corner and wedges the door. At about 3 a.m. a foaming, stiff-legged mouse crawls up his stomach. He flicks at it with his gun barrel (9, mixed) and it bites him on the nipple through his shirt for 1 harm. Kurt pins it to the floor with the spear gun on a Kick Some Ass 10. Charm admits that bats in the building give the mice rabies, refunds them, and says she does not sleep there herself. At the ER a doctor says, "Not again. Not you guys." Everyone gets abdominal rabies injections, four doses over two weeks, at $3,000 a head. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: Figures in blue gloves and bunny suits comb woods in a grid while a helicopter circles. The camera pans along a barbed-wire chain-link fence. A worker whistles; a supervisor in a suit walks over, takes a blood-streaked handgun and seals it in a Ziploc in a collection case. The camera pulls out across the fence to reveal the logo "Safe Environment Fund," and the episode cuts to credits. Andre said he would have played the credit music "if Discord hadn't broken it." (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• The first Radford case has two files: the FBI's, with a giant insect, and the sheriff's, with a cartel. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • More townspeople are missing, and inquiries are deflected to a rehab in California and a firm of lawyers. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • The missing agents left their camp calmly and headed for a spot now inside the Fund's fence. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • The Safe Environment Fund has armed guards, alarms, lawyers on call and a cleanup crew. The marked spot had been professionally scrubbed before the team reached it. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Something that smells like the moth left residue in the trees. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Webster watched a bullet stop short of Andrew, and ends the day "doing some recalculations" about his conspiracy theory. (Radford Horrors 02)

  • The homeless man's story of a van, chimpanzees and a mind-control ray.
  • What the Ferry Lodge's new management was hiding.
  • Unchecked leads: the lawyers' number, the fence permits at City Hall, the Whateley boy in Roanoke and the burned church.
  • The team's legal exposure for trespass and a wounded guard. Andre said out of character that they were "legally in the wrong."

(Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• The count of people Webster believes Kurt has skinned rose through the session from one to two ("Two guys, but one event," Zack offered), and Zack later added a third. Andre ruled, "It was a spree skinning and not serial skinning." (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Webster brought his own silverware for fear of poison and records everything on tape, camera and camcorder. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Jokes about Andrew's drink included "white Blade" and "Flavor Aid"; Rita maintained he is not a vampire. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Zack rolled for Ezra's new character, whose sheet Ezra could not find. Zack's own dice were cold (6, a 4 on two 1s, 6) while Dante's were hot. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • The table argued at length about whether the trespass was legal. The players pleaded exigent circumstances. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Out of character, Ezra summed up why Webster's theory was failing: "Nobody's talked about Bill Clinton, nobody's mentioned the Rothschilds... You guys have talked about aliens and moths and woods and, like, shitty hotels." (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Andre's connection lagged badly during the fence scene. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Returns to the people and places of The Radford Horror: Molly, Sheila, the diner, the Pay n' Stay, the Ferry Lodge and the ER, whose doctor remembers the team.
  • Webster knows the Biz was caught photographing Bill Clinton in a hotel room, a callback to the Clinton surveillance scandal. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • When Rita mentions that Andrew has brought "that weird pepper spray" again, Kurt says, "My hand still tingles at night sometimes." (Radford Horrors 02)
  • The trespass leads to the Bivens lawsuit in Radford Horrors 03, and Giuliani's "acceptable fact pattern" order continues to hang over the case.
  • Radford Horrors 01 dates the briefing to "early April '93," and the team flies out at noon the next day, which places the return to Radford in April 1993. Asked how long it had been since the team was last in town, Andre said, "A little less than a year." (Radford Horrors 02)
  • The ER doctor here prescribes four vaccine doses over two weeks. In Radford Horrors 03 the same course becomes one injection every Tuesday for four weeks.

docs.title: The Radford Horrors, Episode 03
docs.text:
The Biz saves the Russian president from a highway ambush at the cost of an eye, while in Radford Andrew reacts badly to rabies treatment and a pinball arcade's night worker is tased and carried off.

Arc The Radford Horrors Episode 03 Setting Moscow and a wheat field on the road to Oryol Oblast; the Radford ER and the Douglas Pinball Emporium, Radford, Virginia In-fiction date April 1993; the night of Radford Horrors 02 and the following day Players present Andre (GM), Ezra, Rita, Dante, Zack Previous Radford Horrors 02 Next Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: In Russia, the Biz is woken before dawn to ride with the president to "an unusual aircraft crash." The convoy is ambushed; the Biz drags the unconscious president into a car, loses the pursuit in a wheat field, and kills a gunman with a knife, burning Luck three times and losing the sight of one eye. In Virginia, Andrew Howard dreams that his "dad" warns him "Don't take it," then runs a 104-degree fever after rabies immunoglobulin. Daniel Webster answers to Director Rudy Giuliani for the fence incident. Sheriff Molly Underhill then brings a fresh disappearance: Elizabeth George, taken from the Douglas Pinball Emporium by people who cleaned up after themselves. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Moscow, three in the morning
docs.text:
The Biz, still a little drunk on room-service vodka, wakes to banging on his door. A colonel throws in laundered clothes and gives him five minutes to be ready to ride with the president. In the lobby the president, in a big black coat with a huge thermos of black tea, calls him "Richard" and lowers his voice: there has been "an unusual aircraft crash in Oryol Oblast," and he wants the Biz to look at it. He will not say what is unusual. (Radford Horrors 03)

The convoy is an armored limousine with two cars ahead and one behind. The Biz rides in the squat rear car between two guards with submachine guns, on his first trip without a bag over his head, and falls asleep. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: The ambush
docs.text:
He wakes with his lip stuck to a guard's lapel as a 1960s Russian car rams the limousine and explodes. His guards bail out. A Read a Bad Situation 10 tells him he is hearing Chechen and Russian voices, that there are several carloads of gunmen, that the limo is damaged but people inside are alive, and that his own driver left the keys in and the engine running. (Radford Horrors 03)

He army-crawls to the limo (Act Under Pressure 11) and finds the president unconscious under a guard who is shielding him. A Manipulate Someone 11 gets the guard to help drag the president "Weekend at Bernie's" style back to the rear car. The next Act Under Pressure comes up 8, and Ezra burns a Luck point to make it a 12: the Biz ducks both men as a bullet passes where their heads were, throws the president in the back and takes the wheel. He reverses half a kilometre under fire, the windshield explodes, and he turns the car around through some fence posts. The guard in the back seat is slumped over the president, bleeding into the footwell, and soon dead. The president is breathing and concussed. (Radford Horrors 03)

A heavy Soviet car with four or five men is gaining and the Biz's engine is leaking. He raises Russian security on the radio, shouts for helicopters, cannot follow the rapid directions he gets back, and tells them, "I'm going into a wheat field. You're gonna have to find me." He kills the lights, which kills the radio too, and swerves off the road. The roll is a 6; a second Luck point turns it into stunt driving that loses the pursuers before the car coasts to a stop. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: The wheat field
docs.text:
The trunk holds the president's medical cooler on dry ice, with blood bags, biologics and anti-nerve-agent drugs, alongside a grenade launcher and automatic weapons. The Biz's first aid roll is a 3: he wraps dry ice in his jacket for the president's head, notes uneven pupils, and needs several tries to find a vein for injectable ibuprofen. (Radford Horrors 03)

Someone is jogging toward the car along the crushed trail through the wet wheat. The Biz arms himself, props the dead guard by the driver's door, carries the president fifty feet into the crop and hides. A Read a Bad Situation 8 shows a man in mismatched, outdated paramilitary gear; the Biz is about 90% sure he is not Russian security. The man kicks the dead guard's head and peers into the back seat. (Radford Horrors 03)

The Biz circles behind him with the guard's knife in his teeth. His Kick Some Ass comes up 6 and he burns Luck a third time. The man sees a reflection and turns as the Biz lunges; the knife goes in between body armor and helmet, and Ezra chooses to inflict terrible harm, cutting an artery in the neck and the tendons of the gun arm. The man gouges the Biz's eye: 1 harm, and that eye is blind. The Biz wrestles the gun away (10), and the man staggers up, faints from blood loss and cracks his head on the car. A helicopter with a spotlight lands. The Biz drops his weapons, waves it down and leads the crew to the president. He has three Luck left before he is Doomed. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: The rabies ward
docs.text:
Andrew dreams of shirtless beach volleyball beside a blood-red ocean under a bright blue sun. Across the net are eight men foaming at the mouth and his "dad": gaunt, pale, in jeans and aviator sunglasses, with a Hollywood smile. Andrew gets creamed. A jet-engine roar builds, and Dad mouths, "Don't take it." He wakes in the ER. (Radford Horrors 03)

Kurt hands the doctor the animal, still on the harpoon in a plastic bag. It will go to Roanoke for testing. Immunoglobulin starts at once: by IV for everyone except Webster, who gets about twenty shots around a nipple swollen to the size of a gumball. (Radford Horrors 03)

Webster is paged and calls from the hallway phone while the others eavesdrop. Giuliani wants to know about "the thing with the fence." A Bivens lawsuit is expected, the FBI is obtaining a retroactive warrant, counsel will decide whether the probable-cause claim holds, and a formal reprimand is possible. The guard who tasered Webster has been fired and says he is hearing impaired and did not believe FBI agents would carry a spear gun. Kurt Larson insists it is sporting goods equipment. Giuliani asks whether Webster has worked out his team's "angle." Webster says he sees nothing of political importance here. "Keep an eye out," says the Director. Four hours with FBI counsel follow. (Radford Horrors 03)

When the vaccine arrives, everyone gets a painful injection in the stomach. Andrew, chilled and sweating since the immunoglobulin, whispers the dream to Kurt: "If I die from this vaccine, just send me to California. They'll figure it out." Kurt, drawing on UTAW's psychic dream exercises, suggests the dad might be a tulpa. A Sharp 10 shows him Andrew is pale, yellow-eyed and worse off than Webster. The fever is 104. The doctor blames an immune reaction and wants six more hours of observation; Andrew, afraid of what the doctors might find, leaves with the team, and Kurt is given a cooler of loaded syringes to manage him. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: The Douglas Pinball Emporium
docs.text:
Molly Underhill arrives with coffee, jokes that they got "Pay n' Stayed," offers her unused mother-in-law suite, and drives them to a possible new case. Douglas Douglas, who greets the team "minus the sports-coat guy," explains that the lawsuit the agents pointed him toward last year paid for his arcade. His overnight security and maintenance worker, Elizabeth George, who has been with him for about six months, was gone at opening. A letter on her door says she is in inpatient psychiatric treatment in Los Angeles. The Flash Gordon machine is open mid-repair, there is blood in the parking lot, and the staff bathroom's hand towels are missing. Kurt recognizes the Los Angeles story from the other disappearances. (Radford Horrors 03)

Kurt's first Investigate a Mystery (10), with luminol under the arcade's black lights, finds a broken Taser tine with blood in the neon carpet, a smear and a single hair on the corner of a machine, a missing first aid kit, no fingerprints and a faint smell of bleach. The porch camera's tape has been swapped for a partly overwritten one from another day. A second roll (8) covers the back lot, which has no camera: a section of fence was cut, a vehicle driven in and out, and the fence reattached. The diner across the street has cameras. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: A long pan down a dark aisle of chiming pinball machines: a muffled struggle, the crack of a Taser, a woman's limp, twitching arm, and a man in a black balaclava carrying her out. "We cut to credits." Andre cut between Russia and Virginia with TV-style "cut away there" transitions. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Memorable quotes

docs.title: The Radford Horrors, Episode 04
docs.text:
A half-destroyed survivor of a crashed craft tells Boris Yeltsin his people are "the opposite of aliens," while in Virginia the team finds footage of a paramilitary crew raiding the arcade and Andrew wakes the catatonic Wilbur Whateley.

Arc The Radford Horrors Episode 04 (the most recent episode) Setting A hospital and the Oryol crash site, Russia; Radford, Virginia; the Roanoke mental hospital In-fiction date April 1993; the day after Radford Horrors 03 Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita Previous Radford Horrors 03 Next None yet

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: The Biz is flown with a bandaged Boris Yeltsin to a triangular craft buried in a Russian farm field, where a bisected survivor answers three questions before passing out. In Radford, Kurt Larson obtains the diner's security tape, which shows a gray van crew removing something non-human from the Douglas Pinball Emporium. The team drives to Roanoke, where Andrew Howard lays a hand on the catatonic Wilbur Whateley and heals him enough to talk about the moth. They end the day camped beside the missing agents' tents, with Daniel Webster quietly adding up everything strange about Andrew. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: The opposite of aliens
docs.text:
The Biz wakes locked in a hospital room on an evacuated floor, four guards with machine guns outside. At dawn a guard he knows from the hotel says, "Mr. Baxter, the President would like to see you." Yeltsin, sutured at the head and torso, thanks him and praises the "impressive stunt driving." The Biz explains that driving drunk was "like training with a weight vest on." Russian intelligence thinks the attack was "opportunistic and fairly half-assed." (Radford Horrors 04)

That night a helicopter carries Yeltsin's hospital bed and the Biz to the crash site, and the Biz helps push the bed through an airlock. Under arc lamps, behind double-walled plastic, sits a partly excavated triangular craft a little smaller than the space shuttle, which annihilated a farmhouse when it came down. In the tent are two beds joined by tubes carrying blood, urine and other fluids. One holds a shirtless Russian soldier. The other holds "about 55% of a guy": one arm gone, nothing below the navel, hairless, with the wrong teeth and jaw and eyes set too far apart. The only thing he reminds the Biz of is the subtle change that came over Andrew Howard after he died, "but much more so." (Radford Horrors 04)

Doctors wake him with a syringe, and Yeltsin asks his questions in Russian, then English. Why are you here? "Survey." Why are your people here, the aliens? "Not aliens. The opposite of aliens." What do you want? "Servitors... need resources." He passes out, and the doctors warn that another dose might kill him. In private, the Biz decides against feigning knowledge. These are not the aliens he has dealt with, he says; he has seen resources go through portals, but it "presented differently," and he has never heard of servitors. Yeltsin notes that the survivor accepts O-negative blood, and asks why that would work on an alien. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: The tape
docs.text:
Kurt volunteers to face the diner waitress, who has a bone to pick about her bathroom. A Manipulate Someone 11, an apology for Huell and the promise of a hundred-dollar tip get him her camera footage. At about 4 or 5 a.m. a gray van pulls up at the emporium. Five men get out, one with a long brown ponytail and the rest with military haircuts. A shadow that is not human moves inside the front window. One man opens the lock, there is a scuffle, three men carry out two bags, others carry equipment, and the van peels away. Kurt's Investigate a Mystery (10) reads them as an organized paramilitary cleanup team, not military, and the ponytailed man as a boss playing soldier. The shadow seemed to be trying to get out as the door opened. (Radford Horrors 04)

The waitress says gray vans began appearing a couple of months ago, around the "right to roam" fuss over the woods and the arrival of the Safe Environment Fund. At the emporium, Kurt's second roll (11) finds the way in: an unlocked, screenless office window on the alley, with a compost smell like the moth's and a second dollop of opalescent slime above it. The Smart-car-sized moth could never have fit. His theory is that a juvenile moth or a thrall got inside, the crew came for it, and Elizabeth George was taken because she saw. (Radford Horrors 04)

Huell phones Donald McManley: "Get down here, we've got goo." McManley asks whether there is a face this time, hears "Not yet," says "Small fucking mercies," and promises to arrive tomorrow in his RV. At Blockbuster Video the clerk Harold lets the team view and copy the tape in the back room. Harold saw a ponytailed man drag a homeless man into a van a month and a half or two months ago. Kurt walks twenty minutes into the woods and hides the copy in a hollow tree. Sheriff Molly Underhill, reached by phone, gives the homeless man a name, Billy Thornton; he cannot be found. (Radford Horrors 04)

Andrew, sweating and light-sensitive, refuses the ibuprofen and steroid syringes from the ER and instead mixes blood into lemon-lime Gatorade in front of Webster ("This is my protein mix... This is meds."). He feels better at once. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Giuliani's deadline
docs.text: Webster reports to Director Rudy Giuliani. He sees no link to "political wetwork," he says, and the team talks openly of "Mothman, Bigfoot, aliens." Giuliani thinks it reckless to run lunatics in the field and wants the missing agents found within 24 hours, dead or alive. Webster passes on what the team suspects: the vans came with the Fund, and the missing people's letters all cite an addiction center in Los Angeles they could not afford. Giuliani already has a man looking at the Fund and assigns a researcher. On a Manipulate Someone 10 he is disappointed but still trusts Webster. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Wilbur
docs.text:
The team drives most of the day to Roanoke and reaches the mental hospital an hour before closing. A nurse warns them: no touching. Wilbur Whateley sits in a wheelchair facing the window in a room decorated with his bugs. Kurt's first approach (9, at -2) earns a flicker in the eye. He then holds the goo sample under Wilbur's nose, and Wilbur's muscles stiffen, his eyes go waxy and his fingers clamp the chair. (Radford Horrors 04)

Andrew uses magic and rolls a 13. He senses that Wilbur is not being controlled now, but that his mind is badly damaged from years of being "ridden shotgun" and of faking catatonia. He chooses to heal one harm and puts a hand on Wilbur's shoulder. Wilbur wakes: "Where's my brother?" He recognizes the agents "from the church." He dreamed of "drowning in blue," and says something was "wearing" him. He found an oversized Morpho menelaus caterpillar in the woods, a species that does not belong in Virginia. Kurt's follow-up roll is a 7, and Wilbur begins to panic at what he must not remember: "like the ocean... like a mother... in the basement... It was pregnant. It needed to breathe... it needed hosts, like a parasitic wasp. Those women--". As the nurse ushers them out he adds, "I found it under a white oak." (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: The campsite
docs.text:
Back in Radford with an hour before the shops close, the agents buy tents and food and pitch camp at the Sportsman RV Campground beside the missing team's tents, which they leave undisturbed as evidence. Kurt's tent goes up on a 13; Huell's, on a 9, stands at a twenty-degree tilt with two rods left over. Over hot dogs Kurt tells Webster the story of the Spaceman: townspeople reported a NASA astronaut, and it turned out that Wilbur's space-enthusiast brother had built an accurate astronaut costume in which people were being kidnapped. A real explanation for a crazy report makes Webster feel better. (Radford Horrors 04)

Webster's Sharp 12 then assembles the rest: Andrew's bag produces more than it could hold, Andrew tore barbed wire and snaps branches that should not snap, Webster is increasingly sure he saw him shot, and he keeps drinking blood. Webster says nothing. Andrew asks how many young a moth has; Kurt, on a Sharp 10, recalls from Animal Planet that the answer is 40 to 500 eggs. Kurt settles down to sleep tied into a tree, a habit from Vietnam, and Andrew takes him by the belt and lifts him up there one-handed while Webster watches. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text:
• Recap: Andre opened with a "previously on" summary of the fence standoff, the rabies treatment and the arcade disappearance.
  • Cold open: a slow pan across frozen Russian countryside in the dark to work lights, tents and "unmistakably a triangular UFO embedded into the ground where a farmhouse used to be," as the army raises a tent over it. "We cut to credits. D-dim."
  • Title: none was given. Zack suggested "Opposite of Aliens."
  • Closing image: Andrew lifting Kurt into the tree.

(Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• The beings behind the crashed craft call themselves "the opposite of aliens," are here on "survey," and say servitors need resources. Their survivor can take human O-negative blood. (Radford Horrors 04)
  • The survivor resembles a stronger version of whatever changed Andrew after his death. (Radford Horrors 04)
  • A paramilitary crew in gray vans is collecting moth-related creatures and cleaning up after them. The same ponytailed man abducted Billy Thornton, which supports his story. (Radford Horrors 04)
  • Wilbur was the moth's thrall, not a killer by choice. The moth was pregnant, used women as hosts "like a parasitic wasp," and began as a caterpillar Wilbur found under a white oak. (Radford Horrors 04)
  • A moth can lay hundreds of eggs. Andrew: "We're gonna be doing this for the rest of our careers." (Radford Horrors 04)
  • Webster now suspects Andrew is something other than human. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Open threads
docs.text:

  • Who employs the gray van crew, and whether it is the Safe Environment Fund.
  • Where Elizabeth George, Phoebe Augustine and the other missing people are, and what the Los Angeles letters conceal.
  • The missing FBI agents and Giuliani's 24-hour deadline.
  • McManley's analysis of the two goo samples.
  • The white oak, "the basement," and how many of the moth's young are alive.
  • Whether Wilbur's recovery lasts.
  • Andrew's condition under rabies treatment.

(Radford Horrors 04)

Andre also confirms that Wilbur is "the spaceman kid" and not his space-obsessed brother. (Radford Horrors 04)
  • The syringes Andrew turns down are the ibuprofen and corticosteroids the ER issued to Kurt in Radford Horrors 03. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
The Roulet Estate is the fifth canon arc of PITF, a three-episode story in which the about-to-be-disbanded task force wakes up stranded at a murdered UFO believer's house in Rhode Island and is hunted by what looks like a grey alien.

Setting The Roulet house, 118 Benefit Street, Exeter, Rhode Island; a Brooks Pharmacy 25 miles away; epilogue in Washington, Quantico, New York, Vorkuta and Moscow Episodes 3 In-fiction dates Flashbacks to November and Christmas Eve 1992; main story on Inauguration Day, January 1993; epilogue in spring 1993 Main threat The Roulet Intruder Preceded by The Walkers in Skin Followed by The Radford Horrors

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The arc opens in the wreckage of the Utah case. Big Bill covers the deaths of 300 to 400 people in Roosevelt and Ballard with a story about a cult compound and a Jonestown-style killing, and the agents spend 53 days on paperwork. On Christmas Eve 1992 Bill brings the news that President-elect Ross Perot believes the Paranatural Incident Task Force is a Bush-era political weapon and will disband it on Inauguration Day. The same evening Andrew Howard receives an anonymous foil-wrapped letter. (Roulet Estate 01)

The letter, from a member of the Keely Network message boards who knew Andrew, says that their friend Margaret Roulet, a UFO enthusiast, had been experiencing "visitations" and then vanished. With it is a pencil sketch of trees and black triangles. After their files are taken away the agents get drunk, decide to find proof of aliens for Perot, and make Diane drive them seven hours to Rhode Island, collecting a hitchhiking monk on the way. They wake with no memory of any of it in a freezing Victorian house with no power, no water and, soon, no car. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

What follows is the campaign's smallest and least official case. The agents have no jurisdiction, no backup and no working phone, and the FBI operator they finally reach has never heard of their unit. A naked, spindly figure with a grey alien's face shoots Huell Kendrick in the shin with a Soviet rifle, escapes into a river and later steals their car. In the basement are two bodies; in the chimneys are climbing notches leading to a hidden attic where someone lived for at least a year, photographing the owners as they slept. The house's water is drugged, which casts doubt on everything the agents and the Roulets saw. (Roulet Estate 02)

The finale is a hostage siege at a pharmacy, ending with the alien unmasked as a man in a foam-latex mask. As far as the agents can tell, the monster of this case is entirely human. The paranatural thread runs instead through Andrew, who survives a rifle shot to the face, loses his healing power and discovers a hunger for human blood. An extended epilogue then scatters the team, and Perot's phone call to Andrew sets up the return to Radford. (Roulet Estate 03)

At the table, Ezra predicted the arc would be the "opposite" of the one before it, with less official capacity and more "Scooby and the Gang," and Dante greeted the mask seam with "Old Man Jenkins!" (Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Episodes
docs.text: Episode Summary Roulet Estate 01 After Utah and a Christmas Eve Secret Santa, the disbanded agents wake hungover in an abandoned Rhode Island house and are shot at by a grey-faced sniper. Roulet Estate 02 Two bodies in the basement, a stolen car, a mansion full of clowns, and a chimney that leads to a stalker's attic. Roulet Estate 03 The pharmacy siege unmasks the alien; the task force is disbanded and each agent gets an epilogue, ending with a call from the President.

docs.title: How it ended
docs.text:
Huell tackled the gunman in the pharmacy and Kurt tied his hands. The Biz was shot through the thigh and Huell through the foot; the young officer who drove the agents there was killed, and a pharmacist and another hostage were wounded. Police pulled the mask off a gaunt drug user who needed beta blockers, the same drug found in the attic lair. He was arrested, and his name was never given. (Roulet Estate 03)

The task force was then disbanded. Big Bill was fired. Huell went on workers' comp, Kurt went to Sri Lanka and then to teach at Quantico, Andrew was put on desk duty in New York with a weekly supply of blood mailed by his doctor, and Diane moved to the FBI's records department. The Biz vanished from the hospital and surfaced in a Russian cell at Vorkuta, from which he was flown to Moscow, where Boris Yeltsin asked him about "the humanists." The arc closes with President Perot telling Andrew, "Something's happened in Virginia." (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: What it left unresolved
docs.text:
• The Roulet case itself is never explained on screen. The gunman's identity and motive, whether he killed the Roulets, and whether the second body is Mr. Roulet are all unconfirmed. (Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)
  • The older Polaroids in the attic show sleeping people who were never identified. (Roulet Estate 02)
  • The streaking light, the blinking eyes and Kurt's lost minute may be the drugged water or may not. Several agents saw the "alien" at once before anyone knew it was a mask. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)
  • Whether the house's UFO sightings really matched the craft seen in Utah, as the drunk agents believed. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • The unknown number on Andrew's pager and the phone call at the bar. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • The "Mystery Government Files" floppy the Biz gave Kurt is never read on screen. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • What Andrew has become, and what his doctor and church are withholding. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Who "the humanists" are. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Kurt's belief that a force "on the other end of a portal" is influencing America. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The owners go unnamed in Roulet Estate 01. Andre first gives the name in the recap of Roulet Estate 02, as "Margaret Roulette… or Roulet."
  • Roulet Estate 01 puts its "Inauguration Day, 1993" card over the agents waking at the house, while the recap in Roulet Estate 02 has them setting out drunk on Inauguration Day. Both episodes have Big Bill losing his job on the day the agents spend at the house.
  • In Roulet Estate 03 the other agents bury the Biz's share of the gold in a park near his home; Radford Horrors 01 finds all of his share under a floorboard in his apartment.

docs.title: The Roulet Estate, Episode 01
docs.text:
The disbanded task force wakes up hungover in an abandoned Rhode Island house with their secretary, a monk they apparently kidnapped, and something thin and grey shooting at them from the woods.

Arc The Roulet Estate Episode 01 Setting Roosevelt, Utah (flashback); the PITF office (flashback); the Roulet house, rural Rhode Island In-fiction date Inauguration Day (20 January) 1993, with flashbacks to November 1992 ("78 days ago") and Christmas Eve 1992 ("Twenty-five days ago") Players present Andre (GM), Rita, Dante, Ezra, Zack Previous Walkers 09 Next Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: After the Utah disaster is buried under a cover story, President-elect Ross Perot decides to disband the Paranatural Incident Task Force on Inauguration Day. On Christmas Eve Andrew Howard receives an anonymous letter wrapped in foil. Weeks later the four agents wake, with no memory of the trip, in a freezing Victorian house in Rhode Island, together with Diane and an orange-robed monk who speaks no language they know. The owners were UFO believers who logged "visitations"; their safe and gun room have been emptied. A naked, spindly, grey-faced figure snipes at the team with a Soviet rifle, the car's battery is gone, and by nightfall the agents are stranded and feel watched. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Seventy-eight days ago: Roosevelt
docs.text:
A card reading "78 days ago" opens on a medical tent at the edge of Roosevelt, Utah. EMTs in respirators treat the agents while hazmat crews carry in more National Guard soldiers covered in white powder. The team has already driven Donald McManley, his interns and the surviving Guardsmen out of the police station in the APC. McManley limps to Andrew's bed with an analysis: the powder is a cocktail of benzodiazepines, sedatives and hypnotics plus something unidentified, and only the rising wind kept it from overdosing the soldiers. The Major is carried in among the casualties. Searchers find no trace of the hazmat troops the agents saw and recover no townsfolk bodies. (Roulet Estate 01)

What survives as evidence is McManley's case of autopsy samples, Andrew's Polaroids of the UFOs, the Guardsmen who watched the autopsies (now being debriefed by national security people) and a Ziploc of powder Kurt Larson kept. The powder proves to be a mild amnesiac, so most soldiers have lost about twenty hours. Big Bill flies in because at least 50 to 60 Guardsmen are dead; his debrief starts apoplectic and moves "down the rage hierarchy." He spins the official story: a radical domestic insurgency, a cult compound under the multimillion-dollar community center, embezzlement to fund an uprising, and a Jonestown-style killing when investigators arrived. Deaths across the two towns total roughly 300 to 400. The agents lie in bed listening to radio reports of the incident and of Perot's victory. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Twenty-five days ago: Christmas Eve
docs.text:
After 53 days of paperwork, Andrew types his last Utah report at the office on a terrible brand-new computer while Diane decorates with money that probably came from the cocaine stash. Kurt fixes the banging basement gas heater, whose unreliable igniter lets gas build up and pop. When Diane plugs in the tree it twinkles for four seconds, the breaker trips and Andrew's report vanishes; Kurt breaks into the neighbors' building, from which the office steals its power, to flip the breaker, and notices they now have cable too. (Roulet Estate 01)

The agents trade holiday plans: Kurt with his family, the Biz to Vegas with a judge friend and "very tepidly" looking into "that other thing," Huell Kendrick alone until he sees his college-age daughter after New Year's, Andrew to his mother in California. Andrew's changed body comes up. He still eats but has an "additional requirement" that Rita calls an iron deficiency, he craves very rare steak, and he was shot about five times in the torso in Utah and walked it off. Huell is not in the loop. Carolers collecting for the Salvation Army leave with Huell's cigarettes and one of the Biz's Georgia gold nuggets. (Roulet Estate 01)

Secret Santa follows. Diane gives watercolor paper for Kurt's daughter, a hand-knit sweater for Andrew, scotch for Huell and shoes for the Biz. She receives a pashmina shawl, a Herman Miller chair stamped "Property of the National Security Agency," scotch and some already-scratched scratch-off tickets. Kurt gives Andrew a fake alien fetus in a jar, Andrew gives Huell a gold Dunhill lighter and cigar cutter, Huell gives the Biz the ID of a just-deceased lookalike, and the Biz gives Kurt a floppy disk marked "Mystery Government Files." (Roulet Estate 01)

Big Bill arrives, eats the cookies and delivers the news. Perot believes the task force is a cover for Bush weaponizing the FBI against political enemies. He has asked Bill to resign, will disband and reassign the team on Inauguration Day, and is forming his own task force for the "insurgency incidents." Bill hands Andrew a padded envelope left by an FBI courier with no return address. Outside in the slush Andrew opens it and finds a second envelope wrapped in aluminum foil, holding a letter and a hand-drawn pencil sketch of some trees. As he starts to read, the episode smash-cuts to "Present day." (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Waking in the house
docs.text:
Andrew wakes on a dusty floor in his suit with a Jameson bottle under his elbow and his first-ever hangover; a Tough roll of 12 keeps his stomach down. Kurt is in an armchair with an empty bottle of peppermint schnapps, the Biz is vomiting into a Stetson that is not his, and Huell is under the couch, face to face with a mummified cat. Andrew's last memory, from just before Inauguration Day, is of officials taking the team's files and the others dragging him and Kurt to a dive bar to get angrily drunk. The foil letter is in his pocket. (Roulet Estate 01)

On the stairs he meets a bald monk in an orange robe. Kurt's Sharp roll of 7 rules out every Asian or Middle Eastern language he knows. The water is off, so Kurt drinks from the toilet tank. Huell hands the monk his unloaded gun to see whether he will shoot; he hands it back. Outside, by the car and a mailbox numbered 118, Andrew stares for a long time at a body-shaped lump under a blanket on the back seat. It is Diane, asleep. She explains that the drunk agents woke her at unprofessional hours and made her drive about seven hours to Rhode Island, stopping five times for Corn Nuts, while talking about finding proof for Ross Perot. Howard was excited that some UFO shapes matched Utah, and she thinks a phone call he took at the bar started it. The agents insisted on picking up the monk, whom she took for a Hare Krishna and who she thinks did not want to come. (Roulet Estate 01)

The monk cooks Spam, reconstituted eggs and thick instant coffee over a campfire. Andrew's most recent page is from a number he does not recognize, the car phone is dead and the car will not start. On a group Sharp check the Biz (a natural 12, for 15) and Kurt (12) spot a classic grey alien face peeking over the roof before it scuttles away. Andrew gets out his Polaroid camera and freezes, starstruck. It begins to snow. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: The search and the sniper
docs.text:
The house is a brick-heavy Victorian with fireplaces in many of its rooms, no attic entrance that the agents can find, a dirt cellar, a barn and power cut off at the street. The library holds a UFO collection and Scientology material. Andrew's Sharp 9, raised to 10 by his bonus for books, tells him the owners were a husband and wife, the wife the bigger believer, and a partly coded notebook logs several months of incidents ending in the fall of 1992: Greys in the woods, lights over the house, lost time, experiments during sleep, and things taken or moved. The living room's VHS rack includes tapes labelled "May '91 visitation," "Lights in the sky, July '92" and "September '92 visitation." Kurt pops the lock of the bedroom safe on an Act Under Pressure 9, but the door jams; levering it with a fire poker (7) opens it and gashes his shin for 1 harm. Inside is only a sheet of wedding photos, with marks where other things used to sit. (Roulet Estate 01)

When Andrew fetches the marked-up map from the car, small whizzing shots pass his head. The monk tackles him behind the car as a window explodes and drags him indoors. Kurt sees a spindly figure running east through the trees. Huell's Act Under Pressure 11 keeps it in sight: naked, unnaturally thin and long-limbed. It picks up a rifle and shoots Huell in the shin for 2 harm, the first damage he has taken; Kurt stops to stabilize him (9). Andrew keeps going, and the creature squares up and shoots him in the face. The shot is worth 2 harm, and between his pendant and his new toughness he takes none; the figure's body language reads as shock. It flees to a river, where the trail ends, and Andrew finds the rifle abandoned near the bank. He keeps the hit from the others, telling Kurt, who has noticed the broken skin on his forehead, that he ran through something. (Roulet Estate 01)

The weapon is a VSS, Soviet-era, well used and well kept. Andrew suspects the Utah cleanup crew lured them here to silence them before reassignment; Kurt counters that a lone shooter is a half-hearted hit and may be staged to look Soviet. The monk gives two thumbs up at the word "Pawtucket" and produces screwdrivers, then panics at the idea of going outside. Pushing the car toward the house, Andrew finds the battery missing. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: The steel door
docs.text: The living room's steel door has a combination lock, like a panic room's, so Kurt spends about 45 minutes bashing through the wooden floor at its foot with a wrought-iron fireplace stand. Andrew steps outside and shouts "Can we just talk?" to no answer, then glimpses a brilliant light streaking low through the trees, gone when he turns to look. The hammering stops: Kurt is staring at the door, dizzy, having lost a minute of time. Andrew finishes the job and squeezes his head and flashlight under the door into a weapons closet with empty racks for about twenty guns, empty ammo boxes and a WWII flamethrower left on the back wall. As evening falls Kurt lifts clean fingerprints from the VSS, feels strongly watched with no possible vantage, and pockets a couple of the labelled tapes while the monk chants in the bathroom. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text:
The episode is told out of order, with more on-screen text than any other in the arc. (Roulet Estate 01)

  • Cold open: under a title card reading "Inauguration Day, 1993," all four agents lie draped over furniture in a dirty abandoned living room in mid-afternoon sun. The Biz crawls three feet to a dusty Stetson and vomits into it. Cut to credits and a title card; Dante suggested "The gang gets unemployed."
  • Flashback cards: "78 days ago" and "Twenty-five days ago."
  • Smash cut: from Andrew starting to read the letter to Andrew waking on the floor, with corner text "Present day."
  • Andre noted at the table that "the time skip skipped over Christmas," which is why Christmas Eve was played as a flashback.

See The show for the framing devices across the campaign.

docs.text:
• The Utah white powder is a sedative and hypnotic cocktail with one unidentified ingredient, and it erases about twenty hours of memory. (Roulet Estate 01)

  • Perot believes the task force is Bush's political weapon and will disband it on Inauguration Day. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • The triangular UFOs that excited Andrew on the drunken night match the craft the agents saw in Utah. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • The owners documented their "visitations" in a coded notebook that stops in fall 1992 and on videotapes dated from May 1991 to September 1992. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • The safe and the gun room were emptied before the agents arrived. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Andrew can take a rifle shot to the face without harm. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Andre handed out Secret Santa assignments in chat. Ezra privately sent Andre the idea for the Biz's gift ("I just made Andre's life a little bit harder"), and Andre ruled it a floppy rather than a CD. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Zack could not recall the names he had given Huell's ex-wife and daughter, and Andre moved on with "we'll put a pin in that." (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Dice: Ezra's natural 12 for 15 on the group Sharp check ("The Biz might be a shitbag, but he is smart"), against Rita's 6 and Zack's 7. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Rules talk: nobody could think of a way to Help Out on the safecracking, so Dante rolled it straight, and Rita explained that Andrew negates 2 harm normally and 3 with the pendant. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Running bits: vomiting, toilet-tank water and the "sacrifice bathroom," "twink" jokes about Andrew's bullet resistance, Kurt asking the monk for Gatorade in every language, and "Always with the flamethrowers." (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Period-accuracy debates covered VHS box sets, pagers, car phones and Spirit Halloween. Andre admitted a "small mistake" about the car phone. Zack's microphone misbehaved ("audio is haunted"). (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Picks up directly from the end of The Walkers in Skin: Roosevelt and Ballard, the APC evacuation, the autopsies and Andrew's Polaroids. Andre says the Utah paperwork is "somehow even worse than the nuclear thing," a nod to the end of The Summer Service. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • The Biz's gold nuggets come from the Georgia case, The Things in Appalachia. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Huell's ex-wife and daughter are mentioned for the first time. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Sets up the toilet-tank water, the tapes, the notebook and the monk, all of which pay off in Roulet Estate 02, and the VSS, which is traced in Roulet Estate 03.
  • The owners are not named in this episode. "Margaret Roulet" is first spoken in the recap of Roulet Estate 02, which also identifies the letter's sender and adds that the sketch showed black triangles.
  • The card over the cold open dates the waking to Inauguration Day, and in Roulet Estate 02 Big Bill is due to be fired "sometime today." Two remarks in this episode sit a little earlier: Andrew remembers the drinking as "right before Inauguration Day," and Andre, asked whether it is after New Year, calls it "early January."

docs.title: The Roulet Estate, Episode 02
docs.text:
Stranded in the snow, the agents dig two bodies out of the basement, lose their car to the grey figure, and climb a chimney into the hidden attic where someone has been living above the owners for a year.

Arc The Roulet Estate Episode 02 Setting The Roulet house, 118 Benefit Street, Exeter, Rhode Island; the clown mansion In-fiction date Inauguration Day (20 January) 1993, into the evening Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Rita, Zack Previous Roulet Estate 01 Next Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Still hungover and without transport, the agents search the house of the missing Margaret Roulet. Kurt Larson digs into a trash pit in the basement, suffers a Vietnam flashback and shoots a buried corpse; the pit holds two bodies, one wearing Margaret's wedding ring. The grey intruder drives off in the agents' car. The team hikes to a neighboring mansion decorated with clowns to phone the FBI, returns, and discovers that every chimney in the house is a climbable passage to a hidden attic lair full of the stolen guns, cash, a peyote slurry and Polaroids of sleeping people. The house's water turns out to be drugged. Local police take over the scene and the monk, revealed as a Finnish Hare Krishna, leaves by taxi for Pawtucket. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Taking stock
docs.text:
Andre's recap fills in why the agents came. Someone from the Keely Network message boards who knew Andrew Howard wrote that their friend Margaret Roulet had been having "visitations" and had then vanished; the sketch enclosed with the letter showed black triangles. On Inauguration Day the agents drunkenly made Diane drive them out, and on the way picked up a hitchhiking monk who wanted to go to Pawtucket, an hour and 21 minutes away by car. Andrew now holds the VSS, which can be wrapped in a garbage bag to protect the prints. (Roulet Estate 02)

Andre puts the Biz as "the closest thing to being in charge." He weighs whether the shooter was a real alien or a man in a suit: its proportions looked unnatural, so at the least it was "a weird guy in a suit." The map puts the nearest significant town about two hours' walk away by the winding dirt road. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: The trash pit
docs.text:
Looking for something to open the chained barn, Kurt finds chain cutters in the basement, along with cleaning supplies, a huge glass jar of cocoa-butter lotion with a hand-shaped scoop taken out, and a chemical smell none of it explains. His Investigate a Mystery (10) tells him something was poured over a buried trash pile to sterilize it, and that under the chemicals there is rot. He digs with a crowbar. (Roulet Estate 02)

Upstairs, Andrew keeps stepping onto the porch to shout abuse at the Greys and throw up. The third time, eyes in the woods blink several times and vanish. He flips them off. (Roulet Estate 02)

Below, veiny hands burst from the dirt and seize Kurt's wrists. He empties his sidearm into the hole and watches a Vietnamese prison guard's face crumple. He comes to curled beside the pit with Andrew shaking him, and says he was "back in Saigon." In the hole is a withered, sleeved hand, now shot several times. Andrew fetches the wedding photos: the ring matches Margaret's. More digging turns up at least parts of two bodies, long buried, their clothing bleached and dissolved by something caustic poured in to control the smell. Kurt points out that until now the agents were trespassing, and that a body makes it FBI business; Huell Kendrick calls it probable cause. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: The car, the barn and the clowns
docs.text:
An engine starts outside. The agents reach the front door in time to see a grey alien driving away in their car, the missing battery evidently reinstalled. The monk sprints after it shouting "Pawtucket!" and gives up after about a hundred feet. (Roulet Estate 02)

The barn, opened with the cutters, holds gardening supplies, hundreds of crushed plastic water bottles and a riding lawnmower, the exact model Kurt has at home, with a top speed of about eight miles an hour and wiring chewed by squirrels. Andre rules that only a perfect 12 on a Sharp roll would let the Biz make it go faster without breaking it or hurting himself, and the mower is left behind. Kurt's plan wins: walk within sight of the road rather than on it. They take the wedding photos, the sketches and Andrew's flashlight Polaroids of the corpses, fill bottles with water, and set out in the late afternoon with Diane and the monk as the snow starts again. Andrew, whose new walking pace is 7 to 8 mph, keeps drifting 50 to 60 feet ahead. (Roulet Estate 02)

A long driveway leads to a second Victorian, the clown mansion, with ivy-covered stone clown statues, a clown-head door knocker and a parked Cadillac. The Biz's Manipulate Someone, rolled to look professional and sober, comes up 8, a mixed success, and the oldest man the agents have ever seen opens the door a crack to say "We don't want any." Asking what would convince him, the Biz learns the man, Bruce, is senile and running on routine, so he flashes his badge very forcefully. A much younger woman in a silk bathrobe covered in clown print shows them to the kitchen phone. (Roulet Estate 02)

Andrew calls Big Bill, who is "supposed to be fired sometime today," and gets no answer. The Biz calls the FBI's DC office as Special Agent Dick Baxter and reports two bodies at 118 Benefit Street, Exeter, shots fired by "entities unknown" and a stolen vehicle. The operator has him in the system but is "not familiar" with the task force, and there is no case on file; she promises local officers, delayed a couple of hours by the snow. Kurt orders a taxi to Pawtucket for the monk out of his own pocket, with a three-hour wait, and sends it to the Roulet house. Huell checks the mansion's crawl space for "probable cause" and finds nothing. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Up the chimney
docs.text:
Back at the house Kurt breaks up furniture and lights a fire, which pours smoke into the room. With a mirror and a flashlight he finds a gap in the side of the flue and climbing notches. Every chimney in the house has been altered the same way, invisibly from outside, with a weather flap on top that traps smoke but lifts as an exit. (Roulet Estate 02)

Kurt and Andrew squeeze up through a gap of about five by six bricks; the Biz and Huell cannot fit. The attic holds the stolen guns, money and valuables, a half-packed briefcase of cash, a cot, a card table with cards and MRE containers, cigarettes, and Polaroids of sleeping people on the walls. Kurt's Investigate a Mystery (12) tells him someone has lived here for at least a year, probably unknown to the owners, entering every major room by chimney even after the owners put locks on the inside of their bedroom doors. The photos show the owners and, in older prints, other people. A cooler holds beta blockers in a tube with the label scraped off and a jar of green slurry with an eyedropper. Andrew's roll (9) finds a butterfly knife crusted with months-old blood in an ornate case by a boarded vent; from his earlier work on FBI serial-killer cases, everything reads as textbook. (Roulet Estate 02)

Kurt sniffs the slurry and the walls close in. A Sharp roll of 8 identifies it as very concentrated and probably containing peyote, and he hands Andrew his sidearm until it passes. The guns include a Kalashnikov and Russian WWII-era pistols, which suggests Mr. Roulet was a collector and that the VSS came from the house, which, as Kurt and the Biz agree, makes a KGB assassin less likely. After photographing everything, the two lower the guns, money, valuables and slurry down the chimney. On the way down Andrew sees the bricks turn into rolling muscle that swallows him; he drops three feet onto Kurt, who talks him down. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: The water, the monk and the police
docs.text:
Andrew realizes the toilet-tank water tastes strange, and the water heater's tastes the same. The house's water has been dosed with a hallucinogen, and they stop drinking it. Andrew mimes the danger to the monk and rolls a natural 12 on Manipulate Someone, 11 after his penalty; the monk drops his bottle in disgust and mutters, and Andre rewards the 12 by letting Andrew finally place the language as Finnish. (Roulet Estate 02)

A chubby local officer, who complains he is supposed to be on holiday break, checks badges and the basement: "Yep, that's two corpses." The agents explain that they came to check on a friend of a friend. Asked for a description for the APB on the car, Andrew hedges with shirtless, pale and bald, then realizes the figure he saw had nipples, which contradicts what he believes about Greys, and shouts it to a passing officer, who gives a slow thumbs-up. The taxi arrives; Kurt gives the monk the team's card and a wad of cash, and the monk shouts something incomprehensible from the cab as it leaves. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The cold open is a single dimly lit shot: a nude man with an unnaturally shaped head, a bed sheet around his shoulders against the cold, sits in a dark dusty space with thin light trickling in from overhead. With long spindly fingers he loads shells into a shotgun one by one, "and we cut to credits." Andre and the players then recap the previous episode aloud. The episode ends on the taxi leaving. (Roulet Estate 02) See also The show.

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:

The episodes agree that Big Bill's firing falls on the day the agents spend at the house.
  • Andrew says "I don't know who is or isn't a Master these days," a reference to the Masters. (Roulet Estate 02)
  • The Biz calls himself "the guy who everyone blames the Bill Clinton thing on," a callback to the Clinton surveillance scandal. (Roulet Estate 02)
  • Kurt wishes for his claymores, last used in Georgia in The Things in Appalachia. When Andre remembers a never-resolved loose end about tainted water, Rita says "That's UTAW's problem," naming Kurt's old unit, UTAW. (Roulet Estate 02)
  • Ezra predicted this arc would follow "the opposite arc of the last one," with less official capacity and more "Scooby and the Gang." (Roulet Estate 02)
