docs.title: The Roulet Estate, Episode 03
docs.text:
The "grey alien" takes a pharmacy hostage, turns out to be a man in a latex mask, and the task force is scattered until the President phones Andrew about Virginia.

Arc The Roulet Estate (finale) Episode 03 Setting The Roulet house and a Brooks Pharmacy, Rhode Island; then Huell's apartment building, Quantico, Vorkuta, Moscow and New York In-fiction date January 1993 (the siege); March 1993 (Huell); April 1993 (Kurt); spring 1993 (the Biz and Andrew) Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Rita, Ezra, Zack Previous Roulet Estate 02 Next Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: The agents' stolen car turns up outside a pharmacy 25 miles from the Roulet house, where the naked grey figure is holding hostages with guns from the Roulet collection. Kurt Larson improvises a smoke screen, the Biz crawls into the ceiling, and Huell Kendrick tackles the gunman; the Biz and Huell are both badly shot. The alien head is a foam-latex mask over a gaunt drug user. During the fight Andrew Howard finds his healing power gone and a craving for human blood in its place. An epilogue then visits each agent after the task force is disbanded: Huell on workers' comp, Kurt teaching at Quantico, the Biz in a Russian labor camp and then in front of Boris Yeltsin, and Andrew on desk duty in New York, where President Ross Perot calls him. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The ride to the pharmacy
docs.text:
With the APB out on the agents' car, the agents wait at the house over police coffee, still hungover and woozy from the drugged water. Diane makes small talk with the local police while Andrew lectures them on whether a Grey could have a belly button; officers have asked to see his ID about four times. A young cop with a Friar Tuck hairline reports that the car has been seen at a Brooks pharmacy about 25 miles away and offers a ride. Kurt, Andrew and the Biz sit in the back; Huell rides up front. Diane gets a lift to the airport from another officer. When the cop asks Huell "So, aliens, huh?" Huell flips him off, and Kurt smooths it over on a Manipulate Someone 11. (Roulet Estate 03)

At the pharmacy the stolen car sits next to a squad car with two officers gesturing frantically behind it. The driver steps out and a rifle shot takes off the top of his head. The others are locked in the back seat, so Kurt searches the body for the keys under fire (Act Under Pressure 10), rolls the squad car into cover beside the other and lets them out. The squad car's radio does not work while it is moving, which is why nobody warned them about the hostage taker. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The siege
docs.text:
Officer Todd, a local, "officially surrenders operational command" to Andrew and briefs him. The naked "alien" shouts in American English, has everyone on the floor, has shot a pharmacist non-fatally and was seen taking pills. He demands a fueled Range Rover with no trackers, no police cars in the lot, and every cop inside naked within ten minutes to be handcuffed to shopping carts, or he starts killing hostages. He claims an RPG; Todd saw a flamethrower, a machine gun and a big old wooden rifle. (Roulet Estate 03)

Kurt proposes a pincer through the locked back service entrance. The gunman shoots out the car's tires, and a businessman hostage runs out with a brick cellphone, a phone number and a warning that nobody is to go behind the building. Kurt scraps the plan and builds a smoke screen instead: a shot-out tire pried off its rim, the Biz's flask of vodka, the Biz's lighter and a bag of stale donuts from the squad car. The roll is a 7, so the smoke is slow and thin. (Roulet Estate 03)

Andrew stalls on the phone, first pretending to have the wrong number and then playing dumb about vehicle brands. The gunman cuts the deadline to two minutes and defines a cop as "anybody with a gun." Andrew redials and tries stripping one-handed while babbling about car dealerships; the roll is a 6 and the gunman hangs up. Kurt strips to his underwear, keeping his pistol, and with the smoke's +2 he and the Biz both reach the building's left side on 11s. Kurt boosts the Biz toward a retracted roof ladder, and the Biz's 13 gets him up cleanly. (Roulet Estate 03)

In the lot, an old woman in a lime-green VW Beetle berates the half-naked Andrew, pokes his nipples and cries rape. When he tries to pull her down, on a failed Manipulate Someone 4, she bites him for 2 harm. Huell takes over with a Kick Some Ass 11: she bites his shoulder for 2 harm, and he punches her unconscious and handcuffs her. The two officers behind their car refuse to cross the lot, and Huell vows to get them fired. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Through the ceiling
docs.text:
Kurt picks the back door slowly (7) and creeps behind the ransacked pharmacy counter, where a hostage silently points him toward the front checkout. The Biz opens the roof door with a credit card, crawls into the drop ceiling and wedges himself in to wait as a fail-safe. From above he sees the gunman clearly: huge black eyes, an oversized head, spindly, naked, circumcised and tattooed. (Roulet Estate 03)

When the gunman starts to move where he would spot Kurt, the Biz fires first. On a Kick Some Ass 7 both sides inflict harm: the Biz hits a shoulder, and the gunman fires his Mosin-Nagant up through the tiles into the Biz's thigh for 3 harm. The Biz crashes to the floor, bleeding badly. Andrew and Huell storm the front. At the sight of a gut-shot hostage's blood Andrew is seized by a craving; on an Act Under Pressure 8 he accepts -2 for the rest of the fight rather than drink. Huell tackles the gunman on a 13, takes a 3-harm shot through the foot that leaves him at 2 health, and pins him anyway. Kurt binds the man's hands with his own underwear (13), adds handcuffs, and stands naked with only his gun. A seam shows around the gunman's neck. (Roulet Estate 03)

Andrew tries to "space heal" the Biz and nothing happens. He ties a tourniquet instead (Protect Someone 9) and compulsively licks the blood from his hands while the Biz watches. Police arrive, and one cuts leg holes in a fluffy winter hat for Kurt. They rip off the prosthetic to reveal a skinny man with blisters at his mouth and matted hair, and Andrew kicks over a card display. The suspect starts to collapse. Kurt guesses beta blockers, like those in the attic lair, and the pharmacist confirms the man had been hunting for them. The Biz and Huell leave by ambulance. Huell keeps most of his foot; neither will walk much for two or three months. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Where they went
docs.text:
After a recess in which Andre asked each player what their character does once the task force is gone, the episode skips "about two months." (Roulet Estate 03)

Huell, March 1993. On workers' comp and in a wheelchair, he guilts his widowed neighbor Mrs. McGann into hauling him up the steps (Manipulate Someone 11). A mustard-stained kid in the elevator asks about his foot. He collects his paycheck, puts his mood at 3 to 4 on a scale of one to suicide, and goes to day-drink and watch Roseanne. (Roulet Estate 03)

Kurt, April 1993. He was sent to Sri Lanka against the LTTE, postponed the assassination of Premadasa, and was recalled after Waco to train American agencies. He lectures young FBI agents at Quantico on silent breach signals with flashlights and IR lasers. In his hotel he calls his wife and kids, spends hours "visualizing the polygon" and watches Roseanne. He privately believes a force "on the other end of a portal" is covertly influencing America and cannot get anyone to listen. (Roulet Estate 03)

The Biz. He vanished from the hospital. An on-screen subtitle places him at the Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp, "abandoned since 1962," two weeks after the interrogations stopped, singing sea shanties and talking to a cockroach. A senior mustached officer looks through the slot, is greeted in polite Russian, and orders, repulsed, "Get this man on a plane." Handcuffed beside a silent FSB officer, the Biz flies first class to Moscow and is shackled to a chair in the former Soviet Parliament building. After an hour Boris Yeltsin walks in, cuts and lights him a Cuban cigar, and asks about "the humanists." (Roulet Estate 03)

Andrew. After a week at home, his doctor and officials of his church tell him his powers are unpredictable in crisis and promise tests. For the first time he senses they do not know what they are talking about, and that he is a "special horse," the test case; they X-rayed him and never showed him the films. He joins the World Trade Center bombing investigation on desk duty. Big Bill has been fired and Andrew was seen as his pet, but he cannot be fired because his misdeeds are buried in classified cover-ups, and colleagues run betting pools on why he still has a job. Diane, now in FBI records, phones to check on everyone and cannot reach Mr. Baxter. "He's probably dead," Andrew mutters afterwards. His doctor mails him human blood weekly, disguised as frozen orange juice. Shirtless in his hotel room, scratching his chest scar while the blood thaws in a Brita pitcher, he wonders whether he died, whether he is an alien hybrid, and whether his dreams are his father. He puts on Roseanne and raises a glass. The phone rings. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text:
• Cold open: a shot from the back seat of the stolen car pans up to the grey alien at the wheel in slushy snow, a black 9mm in his left hand, his right drumming the dash. He tunes in "Radar Love" and hums along as the fuel needle dips into the red. Credits. Andre: "The producers of the show sprang for the rights to another song this time."
  • Subtitles: the epilogue's cuts carry on-screen text, including "Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp (abandoned since 1962)" and translated Russian.
  • Exit shots: Huell's vignette ends on a TV-style exit shot, and the episode cuts to black on Andrew's reply to the President.

(Roulet Estate 03) See also The show.

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• The "grey alien" is a man in a foam-latex mask. His name is never given. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • He needed beta blockers, which ties him to the attic lair at the Roulet house. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Andrew's healing no longer works, and the sight of blood now triggers a hunger for it. See Andrew's Condition. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Andrew's doctor and church have never seen a case like his. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • The task force is disbanded and Big Bill fired. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • The Biz went missing from an American hospital and is in Russian hands. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • The team split the Georgia gold equally. The other agents buried the Biz's share in a park near his home, and the Biz had already prepaid a year's rent in gold to a landlord who would not ask questions. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Roseanne became the table's symbol of rock bottom, and Huell, Kurt and Andrew each end up watching it. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Kurt's state of undress escalated from underwear to underwear-as-restraints to a hat with leg holes. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Dante shouted "Old Man Jenkins!" when the mask seam appeared. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Ezra's dice roller failed and Andre rolled for him; Zack's audio dropped several times. Zack was on a streak of 11s: "I've been rolling good today." (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Andre looked up Ross Perot's voice for the final call; Dante said it sounded like a D&D goblin. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Andre briefly forgot the Biz's name. Ezra: "Richard Baxter, a.k.a. Dick." (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Ezra proposed the Biz's disappearance as overdue "consequences" and left the details to Andre, who told him to have a new character ready but not to jump into using it yet. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Ezra suggested asking the gunman whether a Ford Bronco would do instead of a Range Rover, and Rita delivered the line on the phone as Andrew. Dante supplied the Biz's sea shanty about his frozen bucket. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Picks up from the end of Roulet Estate 02, with the police still at the house; the cold open shows the back seat where Diane slept in Roulet Estate 01, Corn Nuts packets included. The beta blockers and the looted guns from the attic resurface with the gunman.
  • Huell was shot in the shin in Roulet Estate 01 and is shot through the foot here. Andre rules that the first wound had healed, so the foot is the injury that puts him in a wheelchair.
  • Andrew shrugged off a rifle shot to the face in Roulet Estate 01; here his healing touch fails for the first time.
  • Andre sums up Andrew's record as "probably the greatest political scandal in American history, and also a nuclear accident, and also, like, all-out war with a small town," references to the team's earlier cases. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Andre reminds Zack of an earlier conversation in which Huell told McManley that watching Roseanne was rock bottom. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • The epilogue has the other agents bury the Biz's share of the gold in a park near his home. In Radford Horrors 01 the whole of his share is found under a floorboard in his apartment.
  • Perot's call leads into The Radford Horrors; the Biz's disappearance is followed up in Radford Horrors 01, and Ezra's new character there is Daniel Webster.

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
The Summer Service is the second arc of PITF, in which the Paranatural Incident Task Force is sent to a Massachusetts fishing town to find a vanished survey team and finds a church that serves worms in its communion wine, a burning thing in the sea, and somebody else's war.

Setting Marblehead, Massachusetts Episodes Seven sessions: five recorded (01, 03, 04, 05, 06) and two unrecorded (02 and "05.5"). The case opens in the last third of Radford Horror 08. In-fiction dates June 1992; a few days in town, ending as a tropical storm makes landfall Main threat The Sons of Adam and the worms; the angel thing Previous arc The Radford Horror Next arc The Things in Appalachia

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Fresh from Radford, the task force receives a file on eight missing people. An unexplained offshore explosion had blown out windows in Marblehead and sickened residents, and an EPA and Geological Survey field team sent to look for a seabed gas leak had vanished after a couple of days. The agents check into the Ram and Arms Inn, are handed the Sons of Adam Bible, and find the survey team's journal, which describes symptoms like mild nerve-agent poisoning. (Radford Horror 08)

The first day in town produces a severed arm in the surf, a bag of impossibly hard crystal marbles on the desk of the clerk Jester, and an evening service at which the unnaturally fit preacher Amos Shaw serves fishy communion wine. Huell Kendrick drinks his. Separately, Kurt Larson learns that FBI counterintelligence is watching the Biz. (Summer Service 01)

From there the case splits in two. Offshore, in a session that was played but never recorded, the team dives to a sunken stealth vessel and hides from a humming ring of lights. (Summer Service 02) Onshore, Huell stops sleeping and grows visibly fitter, a body's worth of blood turns up in the preacher's house, and Donald McManley puts the wine under a microscope and finds it swimming with worms. Andrew Howard is visited in a dream by a dead gray man who asks whether he can order a nuclear strike. The survey team's trail ends in a lighthouse basement set up for interrogation. (Summer Service 03)

Kurt answers the thing in the water by calling in a favor and receiving a Davy Crockett tactical nuclear launcher, which is bolted to the Biz's Buick. The Biz, for his part, is quietly trading messages with Russian intelligence. The town's Board of Selectmen turns out to be the church under another name: glowing, bloating, and sure that Satan is to blame. (Summer Service 04)

As the storm cuts the town off, the team finds the missing selectman Arnold Weathers and his dog reduced to sacks of worms, and is driven out of its hotel at four in the morning by an armed congregation and the local police. (Summer Service 05) After a second unrecorded session, the finale puts the agents on a flooded freeway between a convoy of the infected and the creature from the sea, with a nameless ally on the radio and one nuclear round. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Episodes
docs.text: Episode Summary Summer Service 01 The team interviews the town, finds a severed arm, steals a marble and attends the nine o'clock service; Kurt catches a counterintelligence agent watching the Biz. Summer Service 02 (unrecorded) A submarine dive to the stealth wreck and a first encounter with the angel thing; Kurt is poisoned by the nerve agent. Played but never recorded; known from the briefing in Summer Service 03. Summer Service 03 Huell finds the murder house, Andrew dreams of the gray man, the wine is found to hold worms, and the lighthouse gives up the scientists' journal. Summer Service 04 Kurt receives a tactical nuke, the Biz decodes a Russian message, and the team meets the Board of Selectmen. Summer Service 05 The fight with Puddles and Arnold Weathers; the church and police besiege the hotel and the team escapes in McManley's RV. Summer Service 05.5 (unrecorded) The scientists are found alive, the team loses its car and steals another, and the chase toward the nuclear plant begins. Played but never recorded; known from remarks in Summer Service 06. Summer Service 06 The radio contact, the death of Jester, the nuclear shot, the death of the angel thing, and the cover story.

docs.title: How it ended
docs.text:
The convoy of infected townspeople broke itself against the defenses of the nuclear plant. Huell fired the Davy Crockett into the angel thing as it rose from the sea; it survived, and Andrew killed it with the flashlight weapon at a range of about twenty feet. Its death released more radiation than the bomb. Jester, who had been driving the team's stolen FBI car in the convoy until it stuck in a dip, bit Huell and died under the wheels of the car the agents were driving. The radio contact left a canister of anti-worm agent on the road, which the agents passed to the National Guard. The Guard sealed the town and began distributing deworming medicine, with the warning that some of the infected would not survive it. Big Bill ordered the affair reported as terrorism. All four agents ended the arc alive in a medical tent, sick or shaken. (Summer Service 06)

The missing scientists were found alive in the unrecorded session before the finale; Kurt later testifies that they had been "kidnapped and held hostage". (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01)

A few months later the EPA and the NRC had been called in to clean up, the team's car and equipment remained impounded, the rest of the government had been given a version in which a cult with a rogue Soviet nuclear device attacked the plant, and Kurt was testifying to a House subcommittee. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Left unresolved
docs.text:

  • What the angel thing was, and what the contact meant by "We didn't mean for it to get out". (Summer Service 06)
  • Who the gray man in Andrew's dream was. (Summer Service 03)
  • What the crystal marbles are for. The Biz identified them as diamonds, and they were found with Jester, Shaw and Arnold Weathers. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05)
  • Who died in Shaw's house. (Summer Service 03)
  • Whose arm was in the surf. (Summer Service 01)
  • What the two sets of town ledgers showed, and what became of Madeline Weathers. (Summer Service 05)
  • The Biz's dealings with Russian intelligence, and the counterintelligence investigation Kurt is hiding from him. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 04)
  • The whisper that woke Andrew before the siege. (Summer Service 05)

More on these at Unresolved mysteries.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Two sessions of this arc were played but never recorded; see Lost episodes.
  • The briefing in Radford Horror 08 dates the explosion "about a month ago"; Briggs, in Summer Service 01, says "about a week and a half ago". (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 01)
  • The innkeeper of the Ram and Arms Inn in Radford Horror 08 and Jester in Summer Service 01 share the "Crypt Keeper haircut" and the 6 a.m. fish breakfast. The episodes strongly imply that they are the same man, but never state it outright. (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 01)
  • The Ram and Arms Inn and the Sons of Adam are named when the case opens; from then on they are usually just "the hotel" and "the church". (Radford Horror 08)
  • The warhead's yield is 0.2 kilotons according to its manual and "half a kiloton" when Andre restates it in the finale. (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 06)
  • The submarine in the finale's cold open is the USS Oklahoma City. Big Bill later says "we lost one of our submarines", without naming it. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The Summer Service, Episode 01
docs.text:
The task force spends its first full day in Marblehead chasing a vanished survey team, pulls a severed arm out of the surf, and sits through a sermon and a cup of fishy communion wine at the town's ocean-obsessed church.

Arc The Summer Service Episode 01 (arc opener) Setting Marblehead, Massachusetts In-fiction date June 1992; one day, from morning until after the nine o'clock evening service Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Rita, Ezra, Zack; Kira (guest) sitting in Previous Radford Horror 08 Next Summer Service 02 (unrecorded)

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: The Paranatural Incident Task Force is in Marblehead to find a previous team of investigators, known to locals as "the scientists", who looked into illnesses after an offshore explosion and then stopped reporting. Working from that team's contact list, the agents learn that the blast came from the sea at 3 a.m., that fish have been dying ever since, and that a six-year-old who collapsed on the beach showed symptoms closer to a stimulant overdose than to gas poisoning. They find a severed arm in a black turtleneck sleeve floating among the dead fish, the Biz steals a strange crystal sphere from the motel clerk, and the whole team attends the nine o'clock service of preacher Amos Shaw. Afterwards Kurt catches an FBI counterintelligence agent who has been watching the Biz, and keeps it to himself. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Field notes and the hallway payphone
docs.text:
In their room at the bed-and-breakfast on Gregory Street, the team goes through the previous team's field notes. The missing investigators interviewed locals who fell ill after the explosion, judged the symptoms inconsistent with natural gas poisoning, and wrote in their last entry that they were going to meet town leaders. Their contact list names the Cartwright family, Ma Gramoire, "Lana Scott" and Denver O'Donnell. Huell Kendrick resolves to keep better notes this time. (Summer Service 01)

The rooms have no phones, and the hallway payphone is occupied by a gossiping teenage girl. Kurt Larson sits down beside her and clips his toenails. His Manipulate Someone comes up 9, a mixed success: she will only leave if he shows he means it, so he squeezes a toe as though it were infected. Her mother opens the door, freezes, drags the girl inside and deadbolts it. A stranger on the line asks, "Marion? Marion, are you there?" (Summer Service 01)

Posing as an FBI consultant, Kurt calls the Scott number. Irene Scott answers "Scott Insurance, we do boats and cars" and says her daughter spent a couple of hours on a ventilator in Salem and is back at school; the scientists drew blood, promised to follow up and vanished. Ma Gramoire hangs up the moment she hears "FBI". (Summer Service 01)

Meanwhile Andrew Howard speed-reads the motel Bible. Rita's 11 is a full success. Alongside the ordinary text, the book sends Jesus to a sunken continent between India and Madagascar, which Andrew recognises as Lemuria; says Eden was taken beneath the waves; promises a physical return to Eden on Judgment Day; and rails against continental drift. The tone around Revelation has what the table calls Jonestown vibes. Andrew's verdict: "I think they might sacrifice people to a sea monster." (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Briggs and the arm in the surf
docs.text:
Playing tourists, the agents pass the front desk, where the clerk with the "Crypt Keeper haircut" now wears a name tag reading "Jester", and walk to the old working docks. There Andrew finds Briggs, a drunk fisherman and veteran with a prosthetic foot, dozing beside a barely floating boat and calling everyone "officer". Kurt shows his own bullet wounds and the two bond as veterans. Briggs blames "the goddamn Russians" for a 3 a.m. bombing about a week and a half ago that blew out every window near the shore and put glass in his groin. Since then there have been dead fish, weird weather, headaches and bad moods. He describes the church as against alcohol, given to sea baptisms of about forty white-clad people at a time and to speaking in tongues, and possibly older than the colony. He vouches for the cemetery keeper, O'Donnell, recommends the fort, warns them off local seafood, and points out the wealthy island across the bay. (Summer Service 01)

Walking the beach past broken and taped windows, Kurt rolls a 12 on Investigate a Mystery. The blast came from out in the harbor and moved inland, and at the center of the damage something black is bobbing among the dead fish. It is a bloated, fish-eaten human arm, fingers to past the elbow, in a soaked black turtleneck sleeve and black glove, the bone violently splintered. Huell buys a trash bag at Harvard's Bait Shop, and the team decides not to remove the glove in case the hand comes apart. (Summer Service 01)

From a payphone Andrew tells Diane he has found an arm. She promises forensics and recalls that the brief called the local police hostile. The arm goes into a cooler with ice and duct tape; Kurt's Preparedness roll (10) turns up Tiger Balm for under everyone's noses. The cooler rides in the trunk of the Biz's car with the windows down. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: The marbles and the Scotts
docs.text:
Back at the motel to shower, the Biz (Sharp, 9) notices that Jester is arguing in the back room and has left an open bag on the desk. Inside are about a dozen clear crystal marbles, slightly smaller than ordinary marbles, warmer than glass, very light and so hard that his new carbon-steel pocket knife blunts on one without leaving a mark. He licks one, then palms it and hides it even from his teammates. Kurt (Sharp, 11) catches three words of the argument: "weather", "quarantine", "unbeliever". Jester returns, snatches the bag, and tells Huell, who covers by asking for a toothbrush, that this is a "bed-and-breakfast, not a bed-and-toothbrush." (Summer Service 01)

At the Scott home, Irene and her husband Douglas introduce Lena, about six, who shouts "Strangers!", climbs into Andrew's lap and demands coffee. The day after the blast she wandered from a school trip at the fort down to the beach and was found unconscious, with breathing trouble, vomiting, a racing pulse, pinhole pupils, trembling, compulsive movements and sweating. She improved within eight hours. The Biz quietly shows her his marble; she is not interested. Outside, Kurt says the symptoms match a stimulant or amphetamine overdose. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Waiting for nine o'clock
docs.text: The team scouts the colonial church and decides to attend the evening service before approaching the priest. Andrew is paged by Dr. Khan of the Radford ER, whose lab has lost the blood samples from his clotting test. At McDonald's, where the Happy Meal toys are Halloween-themed in June, Diane reports that a forensics team under Donald McManley arrives in the morning. McManley is good but abrasive and has already called the team "flatfoots". Diane, unwilling to say the word aloud, asks whether this is "another M-O-T-H situation"; Andrew says it is a sea monster the locals are feeding, or trying not to feed. Kurt fails a Tough roll with a 3. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: The service and the man on the roof
docs.text:
The congregation mixes business leaders and fishermen. The Biz's 13 on Sharp sizes up the preacher: about sixty, but muscular, glowing and light on his feet, in homemade white vestments. Shaw reads Revelation 13 and preaches that angels are terrifying monsters built by God to wipe out sin, that good is not nice, and that the world comes from water and returns to it. Communion is wine only, and it tastes fishy. Huell drinks all of his and gets an upset stomach; Kurt sips, pretends to finish, and feels sweaty and off. Andrew and the Biz decline. Shaw introduces himself as "Mr. Shaw", assumes Andrew is government, scolds the Biz for swearing in "God's house", and calls the wine "a local variety". Kurt (Sharp, 7) sees a flicker of reaction he cannot read, and feels an iron grip in the handshake. (Summer Service 01)

Outside, Kurt spots a man with binoculars on the roof of a closed general store and reaches the fire escape on an Act Under Pressure 11. The man greets him by name and shows FBI counterintelligence credentials: "Richard", the Biz, has been a person of interest for a couple of weeks because his money problems make him vulnerable to leverage. Kurt threatens him, says the unit is his to handle, and lets him go. He tells the team only that it was "skeletons in my closet". Back at the motel, Jester is frantically searching his desk. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• The case began in the last third of Radford Horror 08, where the team received the Marblehead file, checked into the Ram and Arms Inn, took the Sons of Adam Bible and found the survey team's journal. The inn and the church are named there; in this episode they are simply "the motel" and "the church". (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 01)
  • Callbacks to Radford: the fight with the moth, Andrew's nosebleed, Kurt's leg injury, and the rooftop watcher Kurt hit with a car. (Summer Service 01)
  • The briefing in Radford Horror 08 puts the explosion "about a month ago"; Briggs here puts it "about a week and a half ago". (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 01)
  • The survey team's contact list reads "Lana Scott"; the Scotts call their daughter Lena. (Summer Service 01)
  • The next session, Summer Service 02, was never recorded, so McManley's arrival is never seen. The counterintelligence thread returns in Summer Service 03.

docs.title: The Summer Service, Episode 02
docs.text:
The second session of The Summer Service was played but never recorded; it covered the team's second day in Marblehead, including a dive in an experimental submarine to a sunken stealth vessel and the first sighting of the thing later called the angel.

Arc The Summer Service Episode 02 (unrecorded) Setting Marblehead, Massachusetts, and the sea floor off the shelf In-fiction date June 1992; the day after Summer Service 01 Previous Summer Service 01 Next Summer Service 03

Unrecorded session

This session was played but never recorded. No quotes or roll results survive. Everything below is what later episodes establish about it, chiefly Summer Service 03, which opens the same night with "you guys had just come back to the hotel after your adventures for the day".

docs.title: The dive
docs.text:
Andrew Howard and Kurt Larson describe the dive to Big Bill by phone the next morning. (Summer Service 03)

  • The team "went down in an experimental submarine with some college kids". One of them, a young woman, had found a dead body on the sea floor during her research and took the agents over the shelf to see it. Asked whether it was one of the missing researchers, Andrew answers, "Don't know. Body was gone when we got down there."
  • The body had been lying under a sunken vessel. Kurt describes a hull built to minimize its radar signature, with no 90-degree angles and a sawtooth shape on its flat parts, carrying an unusual turret with big capacitors. He reads the turret as a directed-energy weapon or a rail gun, and Big Bill is reminded of Reagan's Star Wars proposals.
  • The wreck had "a chunk taken out of it. Like, it got eaten." The missing section was the part that had covered the body.
  • While the team was at the wreck a second vessel arrived, fully underwater, "covered in lights" and shaped like a gyroscope. It hummed at a pitch that threatened to break their submarine apart. The sub lost power; the team left everything switched off and was not found. The thing moved as though it were searching for something and then went elsewhere. This is the first appearance of the angel thing, which Kurt calls "that glowy ring fuck thing that scared the shit out of me underwater" and "the spinning death wheel under the water that eats ships for dinner".

(Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Illness and exposure
docs.text:
• Kurt was poisoned by the nerve agent in the water. He later tells Ma Gramoire, "I just got my hands wet." The Biz was not poisoned. Lab results on "whatever got you guys" reach the team through Diane the next morning.
  • Kurt also has adult chicken pox, which he says his kids gave him. He "took some steps" to look after himself during the session, for which Andre gives him +1 forward on his first roll of the next one.
  • Huell Kendrick, who drank a full cup of communion wine in Summer Service 01, had been awake for 48 hours by the end of the day.

(Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Other developments
docs.text:
• By the next episode the whole team knows that the crystal marbles are diamonds. In Summer Service 01 the Biz had hidden his marble from the others; Andre confirms that "Ezra told you guys the marbles are diamonds".
  • Donald McManley, expected "in the morning" at the end of Summer Service 01, is in town with his mobile lab when Summer Service 03 begins.
  • Big Bill says he and Kurt "talked very briefly last night", and reckons the team has been in town "day and a half? Two days?"
  • The session ended with the team back at the hotel and going to bed.

(Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Later references
docs.text:
• In the finale, the voice on the radio asks whether the agents know about his side's "advanced team". Andrew asks if it was "dead in the bottom of the ocean", and Kurt identifies it as "the boat with a bite taken out of it". (Summer Service 06)
  • The encounter with the ring is why Kurt phones an old contact for something big enough to kill it. What arrives is the M28 Davy Crockett. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04)
  • Andrew's report of the wreck leads Big Bill to have a Los Angeles-class attack submarine retasked to the area. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Never established
docs.text:
• Which of the four agents were aboard the submarine. Andrew and Kurt describe the dive first-hand.
  • Who the college researchers were and how the team met them.
  • What became of the severed arm from Summer Service 01, and whether the Cartwrights or Denver O'Donnell were ever interviewed. None of them comes up again.

docs.title: The Summer Service, Episode 03
docs.text:
A sleepless Huell walks into a blood-soaked house, Andrew is warned off the water by a dead man in a dream, the communion wine turns out to be full of worms, and the trail of the missing scientists ends in a lighthouse basement.

Arc The Summer Service Episode 03 Setting Marblehead, Massachusetts In-fiction date Summer 1992; from about 10:30 p.m. on the team's second day through the following day Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita; Kira (guest) at the table without a character Previous Summer Service 02 (unrecorded) Next Summer Service 04

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Picking up the night after the unrecorded submarine dive, the session finds Kurt sick with chicken pox and nerve agent and Huell awake for 48 hours and visibly fitter. Huell's walk for fries leads him to the wrecked, bloody home of preacher Amos Shaw. Andrew dreams of a gray-skinned dead man who asks whether he can order a nuclear strike. In the morning the lab reports a synthetic toxin close to VX, Big Bill takes the case toward the Oval Office, and Donald McManley finds worms swimming in the communion wine. A tip from Ma Gramoire sends the team to the town's lighthouse, where they find a glass-melting blast scar, a transmitting police radio, an interrogation site, and the missing scientists' field journal. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: The murder house
docs.text:
Back at the hotel after the dive, Kurt is feverish and freezing. His Tough roll, with +1 forward for looking after himself in the unrecorded previous session, comes up 8: no penalty, but a bad night. Huell cannot sleep at all. He is full of nervous energy and hungry, and Andre gives him +1 Tough for the episode. On his way out to McDonald's he passes a haunted-looking Jester, who gives him an appraising nod. (Summer Service 03)

Huell passes a house whose door has stood open for days with mail piling up, and knocks. Inside the house a lamp is tipped over, furniture is knocked askew, there are holes in the drywall, and a burner is still lit under a pan with its bottom melted out. His Read a Bad Situation (10) tells him nobody present means him harm. In the kitchen (Investigate a Mystery, 9) he finds bloody gauze and tweezers and a blood smear running from the stairs. Upstairs a long, bloody gouge runs through the hallway wall, and the bathroom door has been burst outward from inside. The bathroom is wrecked, with blood in the tub and sink and rags of skin on the taps. In the untouched bedroom (Investigate a Mystery, 12) are biblical scholarship, fringe books on Lemuria, clerical garments like those at the church, and a grocery bag holding about ten pounds of crystal spheres like Jester's. Huell calls the FBI switchboard from a payphone; the operator warns of a chemical-weapon exposure alert on Marblehead and pages the team. (Summer Service 03)

McManley arrives with his mobile home lab. He finds a full body's worth of blood loss, three or four days old. Andrew checks the porch mail: it is all addressed to Amos Shaw. Since Andrew met Shaw alive inside that window, the victim is someone else. McManley bags the spheres without knowing what they are and decides not to tell the local police. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: The gray man
docs.text:
An hour before the page, Andrew lies paralyzed while pool-water light swirls on his ceiling. A nude, gray-skinned man with a swollen, seamed skull and large bloodshot eyes squats at the foot of the bed. He apologizes for what is going to happen, tells Andrew again and again to stay away from the water, says "they damaged it" and "it can't cool itself anymore", and asks whether Andrew can order a nuclear strike. He says he wishes he were not dead, asks Andrew to hug his mom for him, kisses him on the lips and vanishes. Andre introduces a new mechanic, dread: Rita rolls 7 and Andrew takes 5. He does not tell the others about the dream. (Summer Service 03)

On the drive back Andrew studies Huell (Investigate a Mystery, 7) and sees that he is more muscular, that his hairline has come forward, and that he has a little of the same youthful glow as Shaw and Jester. Huell jokes that the priest slipped him methamphetamine. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Washington gets involved
docs.text:
At 6:30 a.m. Kurt's rash has spread up his neck and arms, and he duct-tapes his hand inside a thermos of warm coffee. Diane pages: the CDC, FEMA and the NCEH are calling, the governor may call out the National Guard and close the beaches, and the toxin is "not VX exactly" but close, resembles jellyfish toxin and seems synthetic. Andrew tells her he now suspects an alien submarine rather than a sea monster. The radio reports a tropical depression moving in. (Summer Service 03)

Kurt phones an old weapons contact and asks for something big enough to kill the "glowy ring". Andre runs it as a Preparedness check at -1 forward "because it's such a big ask"; the 10 drops to 9, a mixed success: a deniable weapon with its serial numbers filed off will arrive "in a day or two". The Biz privately messages Andre a plan and rolls Charm, 8; the result is deferred. (Summer Service 03)

Andrew then briefs Big Bill Nelson, head of the Foreign Influence Task Force: the submarine dive, the stealth wreck with its capacitor turret, the bite taken out of it, the humming ring of lights, the cult, the spherical diamonds and the wine. Big Bill treats it as counterintelligence, says he will go to the Oval Office and try for a Navy submarine survey, and orders the team to find the missing scientists before the Guard arrives. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Worms
docs.text:
The team splits. Andrew attends the 7 a.m. service at the church, where his Sharp 9 shows that many congregants share the glow. Shaw is absent. A new priest, opalescent, translucent and slightly bloated like a drowned body, preaches against doubt. Andrew holds the wine in his mouth, but his Manipulate Someone fails on a 6 and the priest knows he did not swallow. He spits it into an empty Crystal Pepsi bottle outside and walks it past a student protest against the Seabrook nuclear plant at town hall to McManley at the post office next door. Under the microscope the wine is swimming with worms like tapeworms or nematodes. McManley prescribes ivermectin from a large-animal vet. The congregation drinks the wine three times a day. (Summer Service 03)

Kurt, Huell and the Biz visit Ma Gramoire, a 4'7" woman with a cane who will talk to the government only when it brings back her National Guard son Jordan. Kurt's Manipulate Someone (7) succeeds only if he acts at once, so he calls Big Bill's office from her phone and has Jordan requested for the deployment. Over grilled cheese and absinthe she says she was poisoned by dipping a toe in the sea, that the scientists got nowhere with the Board of Selectmen, and that they were going to check the town's only lighthouse. Kurt leaves drunk. Outside town hall the Biz flicks a cigarette into a protester's eye (Kick Some Ass, 10). Andrew greets the car with the news: "Guys, we have worms!" (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: The lighthouse
docs.text:
At the taped-off lighthouse, Lena Scott runs up and hugs Andrew; the agents warn her parents about the water and the coming soldiers, and the family leaves. Kurt, at -1 forward from the absinthe, picks the gate lock on an Act Under Pressure 11. Behind the building the Biz rolls 14 on Investigate a Mystery: a crater, a scorched wall, and rock melted to volcanic glass, plus a smeared bloody fingerprint on the door post as if someone had been pulled away. Inside, every piece of glass is broken. Huell spots a police walkie-talkie with its button taped down and signals silence; Kurt hides it under blankets in the car. (Summer Service 03)

A second 14 from the Biz finds a hidden trapdoor with blood on its edge. In the basement Kurt (11) finds blood-stained ropes cut into short lengths, two teeth, two bloodied chairs set for interrogation, and an EPA field journal. Luminol shows a bleach trail from the trapdoor to where a car would park: someone was beaten here and taken to a third location, probably by police. The journal records the nerve-agent conclusion, unknown "taxidermy mash-up" fish, and normal-looking fish hollowed out by worms yet still alive, drawn as bags of worms. The scientists were threatened by the mayor and senior officials, and a local sent them to the lighthouse. That is the last entry. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: Andre narrates a teaser: Jester carries a tray of food at night to an ornate, chained house overlooking the sea and calls through the door, "Arnold? Buddy, you feelin' any better? I brought you some food." A wet, dog-like growl answers. The tray is yanked through the mail slot, the door and chains bounce, and the camera zooms in on the door before a cut to black and the credits. The occupant is Arnold Weathers and the house is his. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: The Summer Service, Episode 04
docs.text:
With a tropical storm closing in, Kurt takes delivery of a tactical nuclear weapon, the Biz decodes a message from Russian intelligence, and the team walks into a meeting of Marblehead's glowing, bloated Board of Selectmen without a plan.

Arc The Summer Service Episode 04 Setting Marblehead, Massachusetts In-fiction date Summer 1992; one stormy day, from leaving the lighthouse to the 6:30 p.m. selectmen's meeting Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Rita, Zack; Kira (guest) speaking mostly out of character Previous Summer Service 03 Next Summer Service 05

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: The team leaves the lighthouse as the weather turns. Kurt, sicker by the hour, collects the weapon his old CIA contact has sent: an M28 Davy Crockett with one nuclear round, which he and Huell bolt onto the Biz's Buick. The Biz buys a copy of Moby-Dick and secretly decodes a Russian message about lost submarines. That evening Jester escorts the agents to the Board of Selectmen, which meets under a seal reading "Sons of Adam". The mayor blames Satan for everything, and the session ends with the agents standing in the room debating whom to arrest. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Out of the lighthouse
docs.text:
Andre opens with a recap that names Kurt's contact: Carter, a former CIA fixer who claims Iran-Contra was his idea and is now an arms dealer. Kurt worked with him for about five years and once saved his life, but does not know whether Carter is his first or last name; Dante offers that his first name is Jimmy. At Andre's out-of-character offer, Dante burns one of Kurt's Luck points for "a really good weapon that is potentially more inconvenient and dangerous." (Summer Service 04)

Outside the lighthouse, Andrew Howard rolls Sharp, 8: the sky has gone yellow-gray, a cold wind and rain are coming in, and the tail of a squad car is driving away. Kurt puts the walkie-talkie back in the car so the team can talk. The rain makes him worse, with fever, joint pain and an itch spreading round his ribs. His umbrella is at the hotel (preparedness roll, 8), so Andrew produces a flimsy collapsible one from his satchel. The agents agree the lighthouse is "an active trap" and leave. Andre lays out the arrest rules: a good-faith case before a judge, and 48 hours to charge. (Summer Service 04)

Andre rolls a luck check for a large-animal vet and gets 7: the nearest is in Salem. From a payphone Andrew reports to Big Bill, who says a Los Angeles-class attack submarine has been retasked and will arrive within hours, while the National Guard is delayed by washed-out roads until tomorrow. Andrew tells him about the worms; Kurt grabs the phone to warn that the Guard must not eat anything in town. Big Bill's instruction is to keep Larson alive. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Little Feller
docs.text:
Kurt is paged by a courier, who is waiting in a military-surplus armored truck beside McManley's RV at the post office with a crate seven feet long. Carter sends his love, says this is the last one, and considers the two of them even. Inside are metal tubes, a range table and a manual for the Davy Crockett (Andre reads the cover as "M29"; Dante corrects it to M28): range 1.25 miles, yield 0.2 kilotons, every part stamped "decommission", with an aftermarket rangefinder welded on and its numbers rewritten in Sharpie. Kurt explains to the others that it is a tactical nuke, because "that thing underwater gave me the spooks." Andrew: "I'm sorry, you have a nuke?" The Biz, who spent his career on nuclear-security intelligence, is privately appalled and smokes in silence. Andre notes that without the Luck point the delivery would have been a Scorpion, a shoulder-fired rocket launcher. (Summer Service 04)

Kurt and Huell spend three or four hours at a disused gas station mounting the launcher on the Biz's 1986 Buick Regal, two tripod legs on the trunk and a third through a hole cut in the roof. The car is left behind the station under a tarp. The warhead, about 60 pounds, goes back to the hotel wrapped in a poncho and five trash bags. Jester warns them not to leave "whatever that is" in the room; Kurt says it is laundry, and Jester points him to the washing machine downstairs. (Summer Service 04)

In a scene added after the fact at Dante's suggestion, the team persuades a reluctant Donald McManley (Manipulate Someone, 13) to lend his "useless" assistant Henry, who is sent to Salem for ivermectin on a Vespa, in the storm, with Kurt's concealed carry permit as his credentials. Andrew buys "I heart Marblehead" ponchos and a souvenir ornament for his mother; the Biz buys welding goggles and a box of earplugs. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: The sweepstakes line
docs.text: The Biz's secret plan from the previous session needs a 1980 reprint of Moby-Dick. He finds one at the Readful Things bookstore, where the clerk has the glow and a fishy, open-mouthed face and tracks him with her head. Hours later he sends the others away and walks to a distant payphone. A recorded voice advertises a promotional sweepstakes and reads out lists of numbers. Ten minutes with the book cipher gives a message from Russian intelligence: "Two secret[?] submarine lost near Massachusetts. Cause unknown. Instructions to follow soon." The Biz concludes the Russians are probably not behind the events in Marblehead and tells no one. Andre delivered the message with the other players out of the room. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Dinner and the board
docs.text:
Jester tells Andrew that the selectmen meet at 6:30 and that dress is formal. In suits, the team eats at McDonald's, where storefronts are being boarded up. Esteban, behind the counter, has been told by his girlfriend that he smells like beans. Kurt's Investigate (11) confirms it, and Esteban works out that his uncle, a church member who volunteers to do the laundry, is putting bean juice in the wash "to keep me a virgin." He thanks the agents with fries. (Summer Service 04)

Jester, in a suit thirty years out of date, leads them to the town hall. The second-floor room has eleven chairs with name plaques in a circle and a wall seal reading "Sons of Adam", showing Jesus amid parted waters. Jester takes one of the two unoccupied chairs, marked "J. Evans, businessman". The one left empty belongs to Arnold Weathers. Present are the mayor, whom Andrew recognises as the man who preached in the priest's place the day before; the priest himself, Amos Shaw, alive, smiling amiably and beginning to bloat, although his house "looked like somebody exploded in it"; and the Chief of Police, who glares at Jester. (Summer Service 04)

Huell's Investigate a Mystery (9) shows that everyone in the room has the glow, the agents included, and that the mayor, the chief and several others are bloated with near-translucent skin. As far as Jester is concerned, the agents called the meeting. Asked about the scientists, the mayor says they left town suddenly just over a week ago, having talked of going back to Washington for more resources, and that the tone of their questioning "was not very well received here". Asked what causes the illnesses, he answers "Satan": the second coming is near, and the dead fish are a blight curable only by prayer. Huell's Read a Bad Situation picks out the nervous glances at Weathers's chair and the banker Horace Cromwell, the most bloated man in the room, who says "I'm fine" while his neck swallows twice. When Kurt raises the melted shoreline, the chief goes very still; the mayor suggests lightning or dynamite fishing and tells "Jimmy" to look into it. Andre calls the session there. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: In pouring rain, a woman of about ninety jogs circles around her block. Her daughter runs out with a jacket over her head. The old woman says "Pastor says God is coming," promises "I'm not going to let you go to hell. You'll come with me," kisses her and runs on. Cut to credits. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• The glow is an early stage of the town sickness; bloating and translucent skin come later. The town's leaders are furthest along, and the agents now glow too.
  • The Board of Selectmen is a church body. Jester is a selectman.
  • The mayor's claim that the scientists left of their own accord contradicts the evidence from the lighthouse.
  • Russian intelligence has lost submarines off Massachusetts and does not know why.

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• The weapon is the one Kurt ordered in Summer Service 03, and the Biz's secret plan and Charm roll from that episode pay off here as his call to the sweepstakes line.
  • In Summer Service 03 the blood-soaked house turned out to be Amos Shaw's and an unfamiliar, bloated preacher had taken his pulpit. Here Andre confirms that "the mayor was the replacement priest" and that the actual priest is alive and sitting on the board. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04)
  • The mayor's account of the scientists leaving for Washington contradicts their field journal, found in Summer Service 03, which says the board threatened them and that they were heading to the lighthouse. Andre confirms that "just over a week ago" does match when they disappeared. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04)
  • The Navy submarine Big Bill sends is seen in the cold open of Summer Service 06.
  • The empty chair is explained in Summer Service 05, and the Davy Crockett is fired in Summer Service 06.

docs.title: The Summer Service, Episode 05.5
docs.text:
A session of The Summer Service was played between the hotel siege and the finale but never recorded; in it the team found the missing scientists alive, lost its FBI car, stole another, and ended up behind a convoy of the infected on a flooded freeway with the angel thing coming ashore after them.

Arc The Summer Service Episode 05.5 (unrecorded) Setting Marblehead, Massachusetts, and the freeway toward the nuclear plant In-fiction date Summer 1992; between the pre-dawn escape from the hotel and the afternoon of the finale Previous Summer Service 05 Next Summer Service 06

Unrecorded session

This session was played but never recorded. It has no number of its own; "05.5" marks its place between Summer Service 05 and Summer Service 06. No quotes or roll results survive, and Summer Service 06 gives no recap. Everything below is what that episode establishes in passing.

docs.title: Where the recordings break off and resume
docs.text:
Summer Service 05 ends before dawn on the road toward Salem. The team has escaped the hotel in Donald McManley's RV, switched to the Biz's Buick behind the abandoned gas station, and picked up McManley's assistant with the ivermectin; the players put off deciding whether to take it. (Summer Service 05)

Summer Service 06 opens in the afternoon, in the storm, on the flooded freeway. The team is in a stolen car behind a slow convoy of the infected, and the angel thing is "making its way towards you, trenching out the ground". (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: What Summer Service 06 establishes
docs.text:
• The scientists were found alive. Andrew Howard tells the radio contact, "we found our research guys. They were alive." Testifying to a House subcommittee a few months later, Kurt adds that the survey team "had been kidnapped and held hostage up until that point". (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01)
  • The team lost its FBI car. It turns up near the back of the convoy with Jester at the wheel and Kurt Larson's gear still inside. Andrew's account is simply, "they carjacked us."
  • The team stole a car. Andre reminds the players "that you stole this car", and that they are glad they "didn't take the Biz's Buick" into wheel-well-high water. The Davy Crockett, mounted on the Buick in Summer Service 04, is with them in the stolen car.
  • The infected formed a convoy heading for the nuclear power plant, and the team followed it.
  • The angel thing came ashore. The creature left the sea and came up the freeway after the team. The team set off a claymore on a truck; Kurt says they were "trying to slow down whatever the hell it is". The sonar operator in the finale's cold open hears this as a small explosion, "maybe like a grenade", just after the creature "went on land".
  • Huell took a dewormer. Early in the finale Andre tells Zack that "the deworming agent is kicking in" for Huell Kendrick, and the worm bonus comes off his sheet.
  • The team had fought worm bags. Asked whether they have fought those things, Kurt answers, "Yeah, pretty gnarly."
  • The lab techs stayed behind. Dante checks that "we left the lab tech guys there, right, with the RV", and Andre confirms it.
  • The Guard had been called. The National Guard sergeant on the radio is looking for "the FBI agents who called us out".

(Summer Service 06)

The radio contact opens the finale by apologizing for "my commanding officer's rudeness earlier". The only such exchange in a recorded episode is the voice that says "We're the goddamn Marines. Get off the line" in Summer Service 05; whether the two sides spoke again in the unrecorded session is not established. (Summer Service 05, Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Never established
docs.text:
• Where the scientists were found, and what they told the team.
  • How the FBI car was lost, and why the team was using it rather than the Buick.
  • Whether Kurt and Andrew took the ivermectin along with Huell.
  • What became of Madeline Weathers, and whether she burned the church.
  • What the two sets of financial books showed.
  • What McManley's assistant killed on the road from Salem.

docs.text:

  • The scientists' captivity comes up again in Kurt's testimony at the start of the next arc. (Appalachia 01)
  • See Lost episodes for the campaign's other unrecorded sessions.

docs.title: The Summer Service, Episode 05
docs.text:
The missing selectman turns up in his own bathtub, the team fights a worm-riddled Doberman that will not stay dead, and at four in the morning the church and the police come for the agents at their hotel.

Arc The Summer Service Episode 05 Setting Marblehead, Massachusetts In-fiction date Summer 1992; from the evening of the selectmen's meeting to before dawn the next day Players present Andre (GM), Rita, Dante, Zack, Ezra; Kira and Ben (guests) at the table without characters Previous Summer Service 04 Next Summer Service 05.5 (unrecorded)

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Leaving the hostile selectmen's meeting, the agents are approached by Madeline Weathers, whose uncle Arnold has been missing for days. At his padlocked house on the island they fight his dog Puddles, now a bloated, hairless host for the worms, and then Arnold himself, who bursts apart in the bathroom. The team learns what kills the worms, takes away two sets of town ledgers and a shoebox of marbles, and limps back to the hotel. Before dawn, armed church members and police surround the building. The agents escape through a bathroom window with the nuclear warhead and flee in Donald McManley's RV, and the assistant sent for ivermectin finally returns, covered in gore. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: The niece
docs.text:
The meeting at the town hall winds down in silence, and the team decides not to start a fight. A man at the back of the room with what Andre calls "big Edgar suit energy" unnerves everyone. McManley radios that his RV has no hot water, that he is taking a room at the team's hotel, and that the assistant they borrowed is not answering. (Summer Service 05)

In the parking lot a young woman in a raincoat asks Andrew Howard whether he is a cop and then for his "position on Jesus Christ". Andrew tells her Jesus was an all-powerful alien. Madeline Weathers says she just wants "somebody normal". Her uncle missed an appointment four days ago, his gate is padlocked, the police did nothing, and she blames "that fucking church". Ma Gramoire told her the agents were in town. (Summer Service 05)

Andrew's Read a Bad Situation (10) shows the suited man standing motionless in the rain and headlights following at a distance. Madeline's Beetle runs a red light. Huell Kendrick, driving because Kurt is sick and drunk, rolls Act Under Pressure three times: a 5 loses both her and the tail, a 7 finds her again, and a 14 carries the car across a one-way street, hydroplaning past an elderly couple in a station wagon. They cross a flooded bridge to the island. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Puddles
docs.text:
Arnold Weathers' house stands behind an eight-foot wall. The gate and the oak front door are both padlocked from outside; Kurt picks them. The mail goes back about a week, longer than Madeline's four days, and there is an empty dog bowl. Andrew stays outside with Madeline while Huell, the Biz and Kurt go in to a stench of blood, feces and vomit and clumps of black hair. (Summer Service 05)

Huell's flashlight finds a bloated, hairless white Doberman streaming fluid. His Kick Some Ass (11) puts a bullet through its forehead to no effect, and it bites his neck and shoulder and drags him. Kurt shoots its leg (8) and it turns on his forearm. The Biz's panicked burst totals 4 and hits only vases and windows. Andrew runs in, shouts "Hold it away from you!" and uses his holy weapon, which he thinks of as pepper spray. He rolls a 6 and then a 2 to avoid Kurt's arm. The spray of nothingness beheads the dog and passes through Kurt's hand. Kurt takes 3 harm and drops to his knees. (Summer Service 05)

Huell (Read a Bad Situation, 14) sees worms riddling the dog's neck and its eyes still moving under closed lids. His first aid (13) brings Kurt back from the edge. When the door is reopened the body is gone and only the head remains. Andrew bags it; Kurt stays on the porch with a claymore aimed at the door. (Summer Service 05)

In the kitchen Andrew opens the pantry and finds the headless dog standing upright with worms poking from its neck. He fires Kurt's flashlight weapon on a mixed 9: the dog ignites and vomits a stream of worms, but the reflection off the cans blinds Andrew and the Biz for a minute. Huell takes the light with his eyes shut and finishes it, and the burning carcass falls on him. All four roll to process what they have seen; nobody gets a full success, and each takes 5 dread. During the cleanup a voice breaks in on the radio: "We're the goddamn Marines. Get off the line." (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Arnold
docs.text:
A trail of dark fluid leads upstairs to the bathroom. When Andrew turns on the light, Arnold lunges out of a tub of black liquid: bloated, hairless and soft, with broken handcuffs cut into his wrists. He is trying to flee, not attack. Andrew body-blocks him (10) and Arnold ruptures into worms on top of him. Huell kicks off his jaw, stomps his knee, and the head comes off on the sink as the body collapses. They shut the door on the moaning. (Summer Service 05)

Kurt calls the FBI from the house phone. Big Bill cannot be reached. The National Guard is stuck about forty miles out, and a shipment of illegal M16s bound for a Marblehead citizen has been intercepted. Kurt reports that the church is infecting people deliberately. In the bedroom Huell finds two nearly identical sets of the town's financial books and a shoebox of clear marbles. Kurt's kitchen experiments show that vodka, heat and heavy salt kill the worms and that communion wine does not. (Summer Service 05)

Andrew shows Madeline the head; she recognizes Puddles and screams. She vows to burn the church. Kurt, on a mixed Manipulate Someone, shows her his grenades and asks her to wait, because the kidnapped scientists may be inside, and she makes him promise that "all of those motherfuckers are going to pay". The team leaves her at home with pager numbers, a joint, Molotov instructions, Huell's favorite knife Muriel, and a bug the Biz plants in her house. Andrew lays on hands (8): Huell, two harm from death, heals 2, and Andrew takes 2 and a nosebleed. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: The siege
docs.text:
At the hotel, Jester is gone from the desk; McManley says he took a call and practically ran out. Andrew hands the living head to an assistant at the RV. McManley, in floral pajamas and a nightcap, examines it ("it's really bad") and goes to bed with a shotgun. Kurt tells the Biz his theory that the glowing thing and the nerve agent belong to a separate faction that tried to contain the worms. Huell, who no longer sleeps and healed fully within an hour, cuts his own arm open under a tourniquet: the worms in his flesh burrow away from the air, and his blood is darker than it should be. The radio names the storm "Andrew 2". (Summer Service 05)

About 4 a.m. a voice whispers "Wake up and get your gun" in Andrew's ear; he credits the ghost of his alien dad. The Biz (Read a Bad Situation, 11) sees a police car pull up and silent, armed church members gathering in the rain with their lights off. Huell, out at McDonald's, radios a warning and calls the FBI from a payphone: "I think the local police are trying to form a posse to murder us." No helicopter can fly in the storm. (Summer Service 05)

Andrew kicks in a guest's door (12) to scout the back, then drops a toilet tank lid on the watcher under the bathroom window and falls on him (10). The team passes the sixty-pound warhead down through the window (Kurt 10, the Biz 13) as police climb the stairs. Huell fires at the sidewalk as a diversion and slips away on a 15. Kurt leads the rest unseen to the RV (Act Under Pressure, 11), and McManley drives out on two wheels in the gusts. (Summer Service 05)

They ditch the RV behind the abandoned gas station and take the modified Buick, which has several inches of rainwater on the floor. A radio call from the Salem direction turns out to be the missing assistant: "I just killed a guy, I think. Or something." They find him on a blood-soaked Vespa with a gore-covered umbrella. He hands over the ivermectin and climbs in. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: There is no cold open. The episode picks up mid-scene at the end of the selectmen's meeting and ends as the assistant climbs into the car. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:

  • The assistant who returns from Salem is Henry, lent by McManley in Summer Service 04. His name is not used in this episode.
  • Andrew's holy weapon is the canister of mace he first used in Radford Horror 08, where "nothing comes out" and the nothing passed through a man's head. He still thinks of it as pepper spray.

  • An unrecorded session, Summer Service 05.5, was played between this episode and the finale, which opens with the team already facing the angel thing on the flooded freeway.

docs.title: The Summer Service, Episode 06
docs.text:
In the arc finale, a cheerful voice on the radio helps the team plan a nuclear strike, Jester gets his reckoning, Huell fires the Davy Crockett at the angel thing, and a flashlight finishes what the bomb could not.

Arc The Summer Service Episode 06 (arc finale) Setting The flooded freeway and marsh outside Marblehead, Massachusetts; the nuclear power plant; the National Guard checkpoint In-fiction date Summer 1992, during the tropical storm; mid to late afternoon into evening Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita; Kira and Ben (guests) at the table without characters Previous Summer Service 05.5 (unrecorded) Next Appalachia 01

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: On a flooded freeway behind a convoy of the infected, the team is contacted by an unnamed radio operator whose own people died on the stealth wreck and who has a poison for the worms but no way to kill the creature. Kurt offers the Davy Crockett. On the way to a firing position the agents retake their stolen car from Jester and kill him. The convoy is cut down at the plant fence, the angel thing rises from the sea, and Huell hits it with the warhead. It survives and comes for them. Andrew burns it down with the flashlight weapon twenty feet from the car. The agents hand a canister of anti-worm agent to the National Guard, and Big Bill orders the story told as terrorism. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The voice on the radio
docs.text:
The episode opens mid-chase, following the unrecorded Summer Service 05.5. The glowing creature, which has been trenching the ground toward the team's car, freezes, lets out a long fluting cry and turns back to the sea. The radio crackles and a stranger's voice asks whether the earlier explosion was theirs. It was the claymore the team set off on a truck. "Well, you pissed it off," he says. (Summer Service 06)

Asked who he is, the voice says some things have to remain a mystery, apologizes for his commanding officer's rudeness, and explains that he is only allowed to tell them things they already know. Kurt summarizes the worms and the glowing thing, to the man's delight. His side has an agent for the worms and a "Casaba", a weapon that cannot be fired from the ground and cannot be flown in the storm. Kurt asks, "Can you keep a secret?" and reveals the Davy Crockett. The contact does not know the name ("It might be different where I'm from") but is overjoyed. (Summer Service 06)

The plan: the creature is heading for the nuclear power plant. Let the convoy hit the plant's defenses, wait for the creature to come out, and take a long shot. The contact will call out its position; at the moment it is chasing an American submarine. His anti-worm agent is a liquid poison developed from worm samples; some of it can be dumped in the ocean to deal with the contaminated fish, but he does not see how to get it into the townspeople, and says without embarrassment that "we're gonna have to kill all these people." When Andrew asks whether the "advanced team" was lying dead at the bottom of the ocean, in what Kurt calls "the boat with a bite taken out of it", the contact confirms it and apologizes for the nerve agent: "We had to bring something broad-spectrum because we weren't sure what it was gonna make. And then, you know, we got blown up, so it leaked everywhere." He warns that the convoy has about eight worm bags and that the team should not engage until the plant's defenses have worn it down. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Toothbrush Man
docs.text:
The Biz (Sharp, 10) spots the team's own stolen FBI car near the back of the convoy during a lightning flash. A National Guard sergeant, who gives his name as both Jefferson and Johnson, broadcasts that the Guard has taken command at Marblehead and wants a consult from the FBI agents; Kurt answers, but the team's radios are too weak to be heard. (Summer Service 06)

Lying in the back seat at -1 to everything, Kurt teaches the others to fire the launcher (Act Under Pressure, 10). The Biz "kinda gets it" on a 9; Andrew panics on a 6. Huell's deworming takes hold: he loses his luster, gets a pounding headache and feels four sleepless days at once, and Zack removes the worm bonus from his sheet. (Summer Service 06)

The FBI car has dropped behind the convoy, stuck in a water-filled dip, and its lone driver gets out to hunt through the trunk for something to put under the wheels. Andrew: "Look, they carjacked us. That's a carjacker. We're a law enforcement. Let's kill a guy." Kurt: "We'll kill a guy. We're the cops." As the team pulls up behind him, the man turns out to be Jester. Huell's shot with the flashlight weapon goes wide on a 5 and sets one of the FBI car's tires alight. Jester screams "It's you, Toothbrush Man!", dives through the window and sinks his teeth into Huell's neck. Andrew swerves toward the stuck car to scrape him off (9, mixed), Huell leans out on a Help Out of 13, and Jester is slammed against the other car's windshield and dragged off. Andrew parks on him and backs over him; he is left spewing blood, bile and worms. Andrew vomits on him, and burns the escaping worms with the flashlight as the team leaves. Huell reaches level four. The team recovers Kurt's gear, and the Biz's welding goggles and earplugs. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The shot
docs.text:
Andrew bogs the car on a 6, and Huell frees it with Kurt's steel plate (Act Under Pressure, 9), which takes a while. By then the convoy is massing at the fence, a mile from shore across the marsh. Kurt asks who wants to cause a nuclear incident. Huell and the Biz settle it by rock-paper-scissors, sent privately to Andre: paper beats rock. (Summer Service 06)

The convoy rams the fence. The ground beyond drops six inches and bursts dozens of tires, and pop-up machine guns shred the vehicles. A handful of howling infected run through the fire into the facility. A light rises out of the ocean. Kurt bites down on his amphetamine tooth to clear his penalty and coaches Huell's stance for +1. Huell rolls 6, plus 1 for 7, a mixed result, and Zack burns a Luck point to make it a success. Huell slips, remembers the advice, and puts the W54 into the light. (Summer Service 06)

The flash is blinding even through goggles. Distant trees ignite, the shockwave flattens everyone, the fence falls and the guns go silent. A pillar of fire rises, and the creature screams, survives, and comes straight for them, brighter than before. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The flashlight
docs.text:
Andrew rolls a 4 and sticks the car at once, with about twenty seconds left. The team piles into an abandoned convoy car as the creature strips a molten line through the first one and circles. Paint blisters, tires burst and the upholstery catches. Andrew leans out with the flashlight (Kick Some Ass, 8): a solid hit that burns his hand and starts to melt the weapon's case. The creature charges, spirals into the earth twenty feet away, sprouts the legs of every kind of animal, and dies as a white-hot pillar of flame in a crater. (Summer Service 06)

Kurt declines to collect samples. His Sharp 11 catches the Geiger counter in the abandoned trunk going wild: the radiation spiked when the creature died, not when the bomb went off. The contact whoops, tells them to get away and find iodine, and promises "a little present on the road"; the rest of the agent will go into the ocean. He signs off with "Sorry about this, by the way. We didn't mean for it to get out, you know." The present is a big metal spray canister full of liquid, left in the middle of the freeway. The team leaves its contaminated gear and drives off in a lifted Ford Pinto with painted flames. Kurt and Huell pass out; Huell visibly loses the muscle and hair the worms gave him and runs a high fever. Andrew hangs his head out of the window. The Biz drives. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Terrorists
docs.text:
At the Guard checkpoint the agents hand the canister to an older officer, who sends it to a chemist. Andrew phones Big Bill, who is fifteen miles away behind four feet of water, waiting for a boat. Big Bill has heard that the attack on the plant is under control and that a submarine was lost. He orders that the task force's real purpose stay out of it: the story is terrorists. (Summer Service 06)

Andrew and Kurt tell the officer about a religious terrorist group that seeded a parasite through the local food supply and attacked the plant. The officer reports strange murals at the town hall, a few guards killed, medics seeing "profoundly wild things", and deworming medicine going out; some people will not pull through. On his way out he mentions that someone used a tactical nuke. The team feigns surprise. Huell vomits dying worms, and he and Kurt fall asleep over chicken soup in the medical tent. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: Two intercut scenes with on-screen captions. "A few hours ago": a phone rings in a dark bedroom, and Big Bill tells his wife, "I have to go into work. The Protestants are trying to kill my detectives." "A few seconds from now": aboard the USS Oklahoma City, sonar operator Davy reports that the bogey went on land, then a small explosion, then "the craziest sound I've ever heard". It comes back at 60 to 70 knots. The captain orders full about and everything conventional fired. The last word before the credits is the sonar operator's whisper: "80 knots". (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• The stealth wreck's dead crew were the contact's "advanced team", and the nerve agent in the water was theirs.
  • The contact's side knew about the worms, has a poison for them, and expects to kill the infected.
  • The contact's parting apology, "We didn't mean for it to get out", implies that his side is responsible for the outbreak.
  • The angel thing survived a nuclear warhead and was killed by the flashlight. Its death, not the bomb, caused the radiation spike.
  • Infected townspeople got inside the plant.
  • The dewormer strips Huell of everything the worms gave him.
  • Officially, Marblehead was a terrorist attack.

(Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• The toothbrush grudge from the first session pays off in Jester's last words and Huell's one-liners. Ezra names the result "Pretzel Man".
  • Rock-paper-scissors for the right to fire a nuclear weapon, submitted secretly to the GM.
  • Zack burns a Luck point on the shot and describes Huell sneezing at the right moment. Dante reveals Kurt's amphetamine tooth, refilled "between missions". Rita rolls a 6 and a 4 on driving and bogs the car twice.
  • Zack, on the creature's death: "Anyone see the panda? That was cool."
  • Andre turns off his noise cancellation to perform the creature's cry; the software also eats Zack's Geiger-counter noises.
  • Kurt gives the unofficial motto of UTAW, "anything done in defense of the American people is legal"; Andre first hears it as "Utah's motto".
