(Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Andre gives the warhead's yield as "half a kiloton" here; the manual in Summer Service 04 says 0.2 kilotons.

  • The contact's "advanced team" explains the wreck seen in the unrecorded Summer Service 02 and the poisonings investigated since Radford Horror 08.

  • The gray man's question in Summer Service 03, whether Andrew could order a nuclear strike, is answered here.
  • Jester's "bed-and-toothbrush" line and the stolen marble are from Summer Service 01; Huell tells him, "Guess what? We took your marble."
  • The flashlight weapon came from The Radford Horror. In Summer Service 05 it is Kurt's; here Andrew carries it.
  • The aftermath is picked up a few months later: the radiological cleanup, the impounded car, the official story of a cult with a rogue nuclear device, and a congressional hearing. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
The Things in Appalachia is the third arc of PITF, in which the task force goes to the north Georgia gold country to investigate disappearances and Bigfoot sightings and uncovers an illegal gold mine worked by ape-men beneath a potato restaurant chain's distribution plant.

Setting Dahlonega and Auraria, Georgia, with opening scenes in Washington, D.C. Episodes 10 sessions: 8 recorded, 2 unrecorded (05 and 10) In-fiction dates October 3 to about October 7, 1992 Main threat The Ape-Men and their keeper, Jan Martense Previous arc The Summer Service Next arc The Walkers in Skin

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
A few months after Marblehead, the Paranatural Incident Task Force is handed a thin dossier: a missing boy, a missing woman and a run of Bigfoot sightings around Dahlonega, a gold-rush tourist town. The agents arrive to find the best hotel full of dental oncologists, a religious community called the Covenant living in a ghost town, a band of teenage monster hunters, and a potato restaurant, the Spud Hut, whose trucks never stop running. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)

The case splits into three strands that take the whole arc to braid together. The first is a real predator: something pale and fast that climbs, hangs its leavings in trees, lures a man into a cave, takes a boy from a mine tour and mauls Kurt Larson in a hidden modern tunnel. The second is a hoax: clean giant footprints, a "Chewbacca" collected by a black sedan, and finally a dead ex-serviceman in a stolen costume, shot in the back of the head. The third is the Spud Hut itself, with its hundred-item menu, its savant counter man, its cipher of a secret menu, and its trucks hauling sacks of dirt. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 06, Appalachia 07)

Running underneath is a private plot. The Biz, on instructions from a KGB front, plants a camera in the hotel room next to the team's. The room's occupant turns out to matter a great deal: by the seventh session, state police are accusing the FBI of spying on presidential candidate Bill Clinton, and the team is hiding from reporters while it works. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 07)

The strands meet under the Spud Hut plant. Its manager, Jan Martense, has spent a year and a half working ape-men in the old mines on ketamine, and his conspiracy staged the Bigfoot hoax to discredit sightings of the ones that escaped. He leaves the team to die on a sealed underground level. They get out through the mines, past a crack in the air that somebody else is using to pump gas into the tunnels. (Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09)

Two sessions of the arc, including its finale, were played but never recorded, and several early threads (the Covenant, its river, the baptism of a vacuum salesman) are not picked up again in the recorded episodes. See lost episodes.

docs.title: Episodes
docs.text: Episode Summary Appalachia 01 Solo scenes after Marblehead, a secret KGB errand for the Biz, and the drive to Dahlonega. Appalachia 02 A shoe and a rabbit pelt in the treetops, the first Spud Hut dinner, fake footprints, and a camera in room 111. Appalachia 03 Andrew sleepwalks to a cave of remains; a boy vanishes on a mine tour; a pale creature mauls Kurt underground. Appalachia 04 McManley arrives, Sheriff Burke demands answers, and the team visits the Covenant in Auraria. Appalachia 05 (unrecorded) The evening after Auraria: a Spud Hut auditor, a hybrid blood result, and the Biz's private night. Appalachia 06 The "dead Bigfoot" is an executed man in a stolen Chewbacca costume, traced to a motel dumpster. Appalachia 07 A cipher menu, a tracking tag in bloody vomit, the Clinton accusation, and a wrecked truck full of dirt. Appalachia 08 Inside the Spud Hut plant, Jan Martense leaves the team at the door of a room full of ape-men. Appalachia 09 Clive explains the gold mine; ketamine Combos, a crack in the air, Big Bob, and escape to the woods. Appalachia 10 (unrecorded) The finale: Andrew shot in the face; Jan shot, crushed by an ape-man and captured; the plant explodes.

docs.title: How it ended
docs.text:
The recorded story stops with the team hurt and loaded with gold in the woods outside the plant, and Jan driving away in a red pickup with a large animal crate. (Appalachia 09)

Unrecorded session

The finale, Appalachia 10, was played but never recorded. What follows is what the characters say about it in Walkers 01.

The same day, the team caught up with Jan. He shot Andrew Howard in the face; Andrew survived and left hospital in about half the expected time. Kurt shot Jan, the Biz put a shotgun blast into him, and a falling ape-man broke his skull. He was taken alive and ended up in the CIA's Black Site Omaha. The Spud Hut facility exploded shortly after he fled it, which Kurt puts down to the gas that an unknown party piped into the mines. (Walkers 01)

A month later the Clinton surveillance scandal was still running. The official line blamed "Jan Martense, the illegal gold miner", but the state police had the Biz's night-vision goggles from a rose bush, and he went on Late Night with David Letterman as "the most hated cop in America". At Omaha, Jan told Kurt that his ape-men were his own sons by an ape woman he called Shelly, whom he took five years earlier from the van of a man with NSA identification he had run over. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text:
• Who opened the crack in the air and piped gas into the mine, and why.
  • What Shelly was, and why a man with NSA identification had her.
  • The fates of Willow Greengrass, Gene Cartwright and Frederick, which are never confirmed on a surviving recording.
  • The identity of the man whose lighter was marked "HF", and why Andrew walked to his remains in his sleep.
  • What happened to Jeremy at his baptism, the Covenant's land dispute, and the Spud Hut runoff in its river.
  • What became of the surviving ape-men, Sheriff Burke and the gold.
  • Who shot Troy Cleaver. Kurt assumes it was Jan, and Jan does not deny it.
  • Exactly what the Biz did on the night before Appalachia 06, which was played in an unrecorded session and partly in private between Ezra and Andre.
  • Whether the cryptogram secret menu was ever decoded.

See also unresolved mysteries.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Episodes 04 and 07 survive only as single mixed audio tracks, so it is not always clear who is speaking in them.
  • The in-fiction calendar drifts. In Appalachia 01 the solo scenes fall on Sunday, October 3, the team is briefed in Washington on Monday the 4th, and it reaches Dahlonega at 7 p.m. on Tuesday the 5th, which makes Appalachia 02 Wednesday the 6th and Appalachia 03 and 04 Thursday the 7th; in Appalachia 04 Andre believes it is Wednesday; in Appalachia 07 he says the team arrived on October 4 and that it is now the 7th.
  • The local newspaper is the Dahlonega Times in Appalachia 01 and the Gold Bug in Appalachia 06. The Bigfoot photograph is credited to "Charlie" Briggs in Appalachia 02, but the photographer the team reaches in Appalachia 06 is Derek Edwards.
  • Jan says in Appalachia 08 that he grew up in East Germany, but the players call him Polish from then on. His name is heard as both "Jan" and "Yan"; Andre's explanation in Appalachia 09 is that people in town do not say it correctly.
  • The Claymore's toll is one ape-man dead in Andre's count at the end of Appalachia 08 and two in the recap that opens Appalachia 09.

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia, Episode 01
docs.text:
A few months after Marblehead, the task force is sent to Dahlonega, Georgia, to look into two disappearances and a rash of Bigfoot sightings, while the Biz quietly takes a job from the KGB.

Arc The Things in Appalachia Episode 01 Setting Washington, D.C.; the drive south; Dahlonega, Georgia In-fiction date Sunday October 3 to Wednesday October 6, 1992 Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita; Kira sitting in Previous Summer Service 06 Next Appalachia 02

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: The arc opens with a woman being dragged away in the Georgia woods, then catches up with each agent in the aftermath of Marblehead. Kurt Larson testifies to a House subcommittee, the Biz accepts a secret errand from a KGB front, Huell Kendrick coaxes a shattered Donald McManley back to work, and Andrew Howard asks his church's doctor about the nosebleeds that follow his healing. A new dossier then sends the team to Dahlonega, where they check into the Smith Hotel, meet a trailer full of young Bigfoot hunters, and get the case file from Sheriff Carter Burke. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: After Marblehead
docs.text: A few months have passed since the end of The Summer Service. The EPA and the NRC have cleaned up the radiological mess left by the sea creature and the Davy Crockett, and have refused to return the team's car and equipment. Three versions of Marblehead now exist: the code-word classified report held by Big Bill, the version given to the rest of the government (an extremist cult with a nerve agent and a rogue ex-Soviet nuclear device botched an attack on the power plant, with the worms played down), and a different version again for the public. The rest of the FBI has stopped bullying the task force; the office is stocked with joke copies and posters of E.T., Alien and Close Encounters, plus a VHS player and a small CRT television. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Four Sunday scenes
docs.text:
On Sunday, October 3, Kurt testifies to a House subcommittee in an old service suit he never broke in, flanked by Big Bill and his CIA boss, a man in a nautilus-print tie. Congressman Bradley asks about the worms in the communion wine and the church leaders who later died of infection. Kurt sidesteps without lying: the team was in town only three days, he was feverish with chicken pox and poisoned by nerve gas, and the cult acted from no conventional motive. Asked where the team's worm cure came from, he offers only speculation. When Bradley raises a gap in the testimony just before the power plant attack, and asks whether Kurt was at a road stop off a highway, Big Bill has both questions struck on national-security grounds and Bradley ends the session. (Appalachia 01)

The Biz receives a sweepstakes invitation he recognises as a KGB front. From a payphone he calls the "Canada maple syrup sweepstakes line" and decodes the numbers with Moby-Dick as the codebook. The message promises information on the "Massachusetts matter" and $10,000 for a favor, and says he will soon be sent to "George I A" (the word Georgia is not in the novel). Distrusting the old dead drop, a loose paving stone under a park bench, he pays a homeless man about $50 to fetch the package. It holds a covert microphone and a compact film camera and flash-paper instructions: plant the camera in room 111 of the Smith Hotel in Dahlonega before midnight in two days, retrieve it 24 hours later, and mail the undeveloped film. He tells nobody. (Appalachia 01)

Huell, haggard after weeks of illness as the dead worms left his body, is sent by Big Bill to check on McManley, who is on leave and close to being fired. McManley answers his cottage door with a shotgun and a cigarette. The house is clean but full of terrariums, with foil on the windows and a fat tegu named Cartwright; in the bathroom Huell finds a second, dusty toothbrush and razor and several bottles of ivermectin. McManley describes what he saw at Marblehead and spirals into an existential crisis. Huell's Manipulate Someone roll, at -1 forward because McManley hates him, comes up 3, and Zack spends a Luck point after the roll to turn it around. Commiserating over Roseanne works: McManley promises to return on Monday, says he should call Keith, and drags his television to the curb. (Appalachia 01)

Andrew visits Dr. Arthur, his childhood doctor and a fellow member of his church, for a blood draw to check for a clotting disorder. He admits he has performed ritual healing twice, with a nosebleed each time. Dr. Arthur explains that higher powers act through the healer, warns him about backlash and about outsiders, offers a meditation seminar, and recommends tampons for the nosebleeds. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: The dossier
docs.text:
On Monday the team is watching Close Encounters at the improved PITF office when Diane brings up a dossier: a child missing for about a week, another child who says he saw Bigfoot, a woman missing since the day before, four or five sightings that week, and a Dahlonega Times clipping with a grainy photograph. Huell's Investigate a Mystery (10) finds the photo could be a man in an ape suit. Below the fold, Bill Clinton is due to give a campaign speech in Atlanta. A nearly new 1991 Ford Explorer replaces the impounded car. (Appalachia 01)

The team finishes the film and leaves on Tuesday. Everyone rolls Act Under Pressure to see how late they get away; Andrew's 6 is the lowest, Kurt physically drags him out, and they depart at 8:45 a.m. On the road Andrew lectures on Bigfoot hunting, and on rereading the dossier he notices that the woman vanished in Auraria, a place not on their map, and that an unexplained article about religious vision ceremonies is tucked in the back. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Dahlonega
docs.text:
They reach Dahlonega around 7 p.m. and choose the stately Smith Hotel over the de-branded Express & Suites. A dental oncologists' conference has left only rooms 109 and 110, next to the Biz's target. The desk clerk describes the hotel's stable and mineshaft exhibit and the religious community that took over the Auraria ghost town about ten years ago: long dresses, tents, no electricity, morning glories everywhere, talk of the end of the world. He advises against staying there after dark and mentions that he turned away some teenage "UFO people" with a trailer and a dog. (Appalachia 01)

Dinner is at the local McDonald's, where the counter kid, Eric, recommends Stigley's Pub and the original Spud Hut. Kurt sweeps his room for bugs and finds none. At breakfast Huell's Read a Bad Situation (8) catches a dental oncologist digging through the scrambled eggs with his bare hands; the Auraria peach preserves are rich and slightly fermented. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Hunters and the sheriff
docs.text:
On the way to the sheriff's station the team stops at a silver trailer painted with a crop circle. The young Bigfoot hunters (Sloth, Eddie, Vanessa, Delilah and the dog Harvey) have triangulated the sightings: recent ones in town, older ones near Auraria around the time the boy vanished, and a search zone in between. Kurt takes their BBS card, gives them his pager number and marks the zone on his map. (Appalachia 01)

Sheriff Burke emerges after about twenty minutes in the restroom and treats Andrew as the lead. The manhunt for the boy found little, and Burke thinks the woman simply left her community. He supplies the names: missing woman Willow Greengrass, her sister Primenthol Greengrass (an ex-member turned podiatrist, back in town about a month), missing boy Gene Cartwright, aged seven, and five-year-old witness Edward Nick. The only evidence in Willow's case is a bag of peaches found in the woods. Outside, the team decides to bring McManley down to examine it. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The episode opens in the show's television style, with an on-screen caption: "Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest, 70 miles north of Atlanta". A young woman in an ankle-length dress hauls a sack of peaches through the trees; something hairy scuttles nearby, she picks up a rock, and a growl behind her drags her off-screen screaming. Hard cut to credits. The first act is then a run of solo "cut to" scenes, one per agent. The Biz's KGB call was played with the other players briefly removed from the call, so that Ezra received the message privately. The session stops partway through the morning of October 6 for lack of time. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• Marblehead has three official versions; the worms' existence is public but their nature is classified.
  • Andrew's healing is, according to Dr. Arthur, higher powers acting through the healer, and it carries bodily backlash.
  • The KGB holds information on the "Massachusetts matter" and wants room 111 of the Smith Hotel filmed.
  • Willow Greengrass vanished in Auraria, not Dahlonega, and the dossier blurs this.
  • The newspaper Bigfoot photo could be a man in a suit; Burke thinks the recent sightings look fake, while older ones near Auraria coincide with Gene's disappearance.

(Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Open threads
docs.text:
• What took the woman in the cold open, and where Willow and Gene are.
  • Why the KGB wants room 111 watched; on arrival Andre tells Ezra the Biz has 24 hours left to plant the camera, and the episode ends with the job still to do.

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Follows directly from the fallout of Summer Service 06: the radiological cleanup, the impounded car, Huell's worm infection, Kurt's chicken pox and nerve-gas poisoning, and McManley's trauma.
  • Huell calls Marblehead his second "bug mission"; the first was the moth-winged dog of The Radford Horror.
  • Sets up McManley's arrival in Georgia, the visit to Auraria, the Biz's room 111 job, and the Spud Hut plant outside town.
  • The dates are stated at the table: the solo scenes fall on Sunday, October 3, 1992; the briefing on Monday, October 4; the drive and the 7 p.m. arrival in Dahlonega on Tuesday, October 5; and the meetings with the hunters and the sheriff on the morning of Wednesday, October 6. The dossier read on October 4 says the woman disappeared "yesterday".

(Appalachia 01)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia, Episode 02
docs.text:
The team spends a long Wednesday on the Dahlonega disappearances, finding a child's shoe and a gutted rabbit hung high in trees, evidence of a Bigfoot hoaxer, and a hotel room staged for somebody else's scandal.

Arc The Things in Appalachia Episode 02 Setting Dahlonega, Georgia; Auraria and the woods nearby In-fiction date Wednesday, October 6, 1992, morning to night Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita Previous Appalachia 01 Next Appalachia 03

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: After a cold open in which a Spud Hut plant worker is lured into a cave, the agents interview five-year-old witness Edward Nick and search the field where Gene Cartwright was taken, recovering his shoe from a treetop with pale hair in the laces. They hear the story of the Covenant from Primenthol Greengrass, eat at the original Spud Hut, meet a bootlegger and the Circle Chasers in the woods near Auraria, and find both faked giant footprints and a real kill. That night the Biz plants his camera in room 111. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: The witness
docs.text: It is Wednesday morning outside the sheriff's office, and Andrew has just called Donald McManley from the payphone. The team decides to question the child witness first. At trailer 513 of the trailer park, Edward's mother lets them in after Kurt Larson announces "We're with the Federales." Edward watches Looney Tunes without turning round, but gives Andrew Howard a Transformers toy, a juice box and a scribbled drawing of a crouched hairy figure. He says "He was fast" and pantomimes something scrabbling on all fours. His mother blames a Bigfoot book from an aunt for the "Bigfoot nonsense" and points the agents to the bent tree at the wood line, where Gene was when the screaming started. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: The shoe in the tree
docs.text:
In the field Kurt orders an inverted-wedge search. The manhunt has trampled the scene, so Investigate a Mystery is at -1; Ezra's roll, restored to 11 by Dante's assist, earns two questions. The first leads the Biz to notice something dangling from a high branch. Huell Kendrick climbs on a mixed Act Under Pressure result (9), chooses to risk the sketchy limb, scrambles back as it cracks, and brings down a child's shoe with a tuft of pale, soft hair, roots intact, caught in the laces. Kurt and Huell conclude the boy is dead. Sheriff Burke later confirms by phone that Gene's shoes were red with white soles and admits his deputies should have looked up. (Appalachia 02)

Over tuna green bean casserole, Edward's father comes home in gray Spud Hut coveralls, exhausted. A co-worker, Aaron, stepped out for a smoke break in the middle of the shift and never came back. Kurt asks him to call if Aaron does not turn up. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Prim and the Covenant
docs.text: The team finds Prim Greengrass in room 11 of the bedbug-prone Hotel and Suites, the hotel the team passed over. Her mother joined the Covenant when the sisters were small and both were renamed. Prim left, graduated, and came back about a month ago to coax Willow out, bringing her six-foot party subs against malnutrition. She describes the leader, Elijah Ray, who moved the congregation to Auraria after a prophetic dream and a television report of a shooting star, the red-clay baptisms, and the vision-quest peach drink, and warns the agents never to take a vision quest. Willow had no enemies, suitors, money or outside friends, and Prim is sure she would have come to her. Prim also takes Andrew into the bathroom to learn his embarrassing middle name, which is never revealed at the table. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: The original Spud Hut
docs.text: At the original Spud Hut, a hut under a huge neon potato, the counter worker recites about a hundred specials from memory while the line behind nearly riots. Kurt drops a handful of matchsticks and the worker instantly says there are 43. Told to get out and use his gift, he answers that the Spud Hut changed his life. The food arrives within a minute. Afterwards he locks up and walks across the lot into the woods. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: The woods near Auraria
docs.text:
Auraria is a ghost town with one pre-Civil War church, glowing white tents, robed members who ignore the agents, and closed morning glories everywhere. The team leaves the members alone and takes the trail toward the Circle Chasers' search area. They meet Frotter Comstock, a bootlegger hauling chemistry gear, who services the Covenant's still and keeps methanol out of their ritual drink. A couple of weeks ago something skulked around his ridge homestead; he saw only a pair of eyes. (Appalachia 02)

Further on, the Biz's Investigate a Mystery earns one question, "What is being concealed here?", and turns up a pair of suspiciously clean giant footprints, twice the size of a human foot, with the edge of a sneaker print and a cigarette butt beside them. Kurt photographs them and leans toward a hoax. An unearthly howl scatters the birds, and the Circle Chasers arrive; Harvey leaps on Andrew and licks his face. They show a three-second clip in which a gray, man-sized blur snatches a rabbit from the trail. Kurt notes their footwear to rule them out as the fakers. About a hundred feet from the snatch site, blood drips onto Andrew from a tree. Huell climbs again with a boost from Andrew, slips, catches himself under both arms and takes 1 harm, and comes down with a white rabbit's pelt, stringy meat still stuck inside and its internals gone. The answer to "Where did it go?" is that the creature is very comfortable moving vertically. Plotted on the map, the sightings make a line that points toward town. On the way back to the road, about forty Spud Hut trucks roll past. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Room 111
docs.text: Back at the Smith Hotel, the Biz is considering the lock of room 111 when the desk clerk reports the room as suspicious: booked under one name, paid with a card in another, with a $100 bribe for silence from an armed, rude, military-looking Midwesterner. He lends the Biz the master key. Inside is a delivered basket of wine and chocolates. The Biz hides the camera beside the VCR, facing the bed, sticks the microphone to the bedside drawer, and leaves no prints (Act Under Pressure 10). He concludes it is a setup, though not one aimed at him. The rabbit pelt goes in the mini fridge and the team turns in. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: Andre forgot to start the recording, so the file opens in the middle of his recap. The cold open has no player characters: a worker at the Spud Hut distribution center is locked out on a smoke break, follows baby-like sobbing into a rocky fissure, finds an ancient pickaxe in the sand, and is attacked by a glinting-eyed figure perched in the crevice. Andre calls for a "slow Hitchcock zoom" and then "we cut to credits". At the top of the session the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable is declared an OVA that Huell watched on the hotel's cable television while falling asleep. The room 111 scene was played with the other players out of the call. See the show. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• Whatever took Gene climbs: his shoe was hung high in a tree with pale hair in the laces, and the rabbit was ripped apart and left in a treetop.
  • Edward's sighting was three days ago, and the thing he saw moved fast on all fours.
  • Someone is staging Bigfoot evidence: clean giant prints beside a sneaker print and a cigarette butt.
  • The Covenant's peach drink gives visions; it contains a hallucinogenic fungus and risks methanol contamination. See Covenant beliefs.
  • Room 111 is staged for a sexual encounter and was booked by an armed, military-looking man.

(Appalachia 02)

docs.text:

  • Huell is one harm from dying.

(Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:

docs.text:

  • Kurt recalls the earlier case of a child who saw a spaceman, a reference to The Radford Horror; "last time religion was worms" refers to The Summer Service.
  • Appalachia 01 describes the town's other hotel, the "Express & Suites", as a former Holiday Inn; here Andre calls it the "Hotel and Suites" and a former Best Western.
  • The Biz plants the camera he was given by the KGB front in Appalachia 01, on the night of his deadline. His instructions were to retrieve it 24 hours later and mail the film.
  • Sets up McManley's arrival, the cave behind the Spud Hut plant, and the Bigfoot hoaxer.

(Appalachia 02)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia, Episode 03
docs.text:
Andrew wakes in the woods holding a dead man's lighter, the team finds the cave where the man was torn apart, and a search for a boy lost on a gold mine tour ends with a pale creature mauling Kurt in a hidden modern tunnel.

Arc The Things in Appalachia Episode 03 Setting Dahlonega, Georgia: the Smith Hotel, the woods, the Consolidated Gold Mine In-fiction date Thursday, October 7, 1992, from about 3 a.m. to about 3 p.m. (the night and day after Appalachia 02) Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita Previous Appalachia 02 Next Appalachia 04

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Andrew Howard sleepwalks miles from the hotel and wakes with a stranger's bloody lighter in his hand. Retracing his trail the next morning, the team finds a blood-splattered cave with a man's face stuck to the wall. When a German boy vanishes on a mine tour, the sheriff enlists the agents; they fall into a hidden modern tunnel beneath the tourist mine, where something pale, furry and enormously strong attacks Kurt Larson and flees. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: The sleepwalk
docs.text:
The team goes to bed at the Smith Hotel; Huell Kendrick and Andrew fall asleep to The Golden Girls. Smash cut: Andrew wakes in the woods in sweat-soaked pajamas, his feet bloody, clutching a bloody steel cigarette lighter he has never seen. The blood on his feet is his own; the blood on the lighter is not. Back in the room, Huell wakes to a banging window and an empty bed, sees no reason for suspicion, and goes back to sleep. (Appalachia 03)

Andrew heads for a bright patch of sky. He crosses his own earlier trail at some broken plants, wraps his feet in his pajama top, falls into a ravine on a 6 (1 harm), and pushes through Russian olive thickets before emerging on a dark street. A Manipulate Someone roll of 9 stops a cab; the driver assumes "girl trouble", lays down a towel and drives him home for nothing. In the hotel hallway a curly-haired blonde woman in a bathrobe asks if he is all right before a suited man with a military haircut steers her back into the next-door room and glares at him. The night clerk says the room is booked under one name, occupied under another and paid for under a third. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: The death cave
docs.text:
In the morning Kurt questions Andrew about sleepwalking and drugs and concludes, "This kid's a square." Andrew's Investigate a Mystery (9, at -2 forward) picks up two lines of his own blood, and after an hour and a half the team reaches a crevice in the rock near a road. The Biz is too stocky to fit and stands guard. Inside is a sandy chamber splattered with blood: an old bloody pickaxe, skin, bones, hair, scraps of gray cloth, a cigarette pack, and a man's folded face stuck to the wall, which Andrew bags. Kurt's roll (8) finds no powder marks or chemical smell. The man was shredded and slung against the walls, his bones split open with tooth marks and his muscle, organs and fat gone. (Appalachia 03)

Andrew's trail runs on to a freeway where white Spud Hut box trucks pass in convoy; Kurt reasons he must have been sprinting. On the walk Andrew says his mother once tied him in a sleeping bag for about a week when he "kept lashing out". Kurt holds his face and recites the names of the psychic-spy programs he knows from the CIA, and gets only confusion. Back in town the lighter proves to be stainless steel with "HF" written in Sharpie on the bottom. While stowing the evidence in the mini fridge, Huell glimpses a laughing man in a cowboy hat and dark sunglasses entering the next-door room and finds him familiar for a split second. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: The mine search
docs.text:
At the sheriff's station the department is mobilising: a German boy, Frederick, vanished on a gold mine tour about an hour and a half earlier. Hearing that Kurt has caving experience, the sheriff enlists the team and puts him in charge of their safety. At the Consolidated Gold Mine the sheriff takes the left fork and sends the agents right. They mark the walls with glow-stick arrows and call for Frederick in German. (Appalachia 03)

Kurt's Investigate a Mystery comes up 9 and he takes the full success at a cost: a boarded floor gives way. Kurt (12) and the Biz (11) land unhurt; Andrew (8) and Huell (7) take 1 harm each. They are in a newer, electric-era tunnel with fresh cave-ins at both ends, a work light in the rubble and vehicle tracks. Kurt's answers: a new mineshaft is being concealed, and many people and vehicles went toward the blocked end. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: The thing in the tunnel
docs.text:
Andrew squeezes through a gap and helps the rest into a dark tunnel. Far ahead a small red light blinks. Kurt orders lights off and the team advances as a human chain; on point (13) he catches himself at the lip of a pit and gets everyone across. The light pulses, something growls, and the light moves. The team forms a four-man stack and switches on flashlights. A white blur charges. Kurt's Kick Some Ass (8) puts a bullet in it, but it hurls him into Andrew and the wall, tears a long cut up his back and strains his bicep tendon (2 harm), then flees moaning and screaming. All anyone saw was that it was pale, furry, fast and had arms. (Appalachia 03)

Andrew puts his bracelet on Kurt and Lays on Hands (8, mixed): Kurt's harm is healed, but Andrew takes it as a massive nosebleed and is left unstable. The creature's blood trail leads to a vertical elevator shaft with no way up; at the bottom lies a single child's tennis shoe. The pit turns out to be a freshly dug shaft, from which Kurt pulls a small gold nugget. Climbing out, Kurt reinjures his elbow, and Huell's first aid (10) stabilises Andrew. As the Biz climbs out last, the tunnel collapses behind him. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Debrief
docs.text:
The team tells the searchers Frederick is probably dead and hands over the shoe; a German woman from the tour group screams in tears. They mention illegal mining but withhold the creature. The tour guide, who owns the mine, doubts anyone could keep such a thing secret; Andrew suggests a cult, and the sheriff's face darkens. On the map, the hidden tunnel's estimated exit lies near both the death cave and the Spud Hut distribution center. (Appalachia 03)

Donald McManley radios that he is arriving with the mobile lab, delighted by "a face in a bag", and relays Big Bill's order: after Ruby Ridge and "that thing in Marblehead", this case goes strictly by the book. The team agrees to leave Andrew's sleepwalking out of the account of how the lighter was found. From the mine's payphone Andrew calls the distribution center, where Stacy confirms that Aaron Richters did not clock out yesterday or come in today, and offers to connect him to Jan, who runs the plant. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The cold open follows a mine tour. A bearded guide in suspenders explains that all the town's mines connect to each other and to natural caves. A boy in overalls with a Game Boy hears giggling down a roped-off passage; "camera slowly zooms into the black". The guide finds the rope poles tipped over and the Game Boy still bleeping on the floor. "Cut to credits." Andre narrates camera moves throughout the session ("camera tracks in on Andrew Howard's face", "smash cut"). There is no recap. See the show. (Appalachia 03)

docs.text:
• Picks up the same night as the end of Appalachia 02, after the Biz planted his camera in room 111; the guests Andrew and Huell see are the room's occupants. The pickaxe and gray cloth in the cave match that episode's cold open, and Stacy's report that Aaron Richters never clocked out follows up Edward Nick Sr.'s account of his missing co-worker.
  • The tennis shoe is a different shoe from the one found in the field.
  • "That thing in Marblehead" is the end of The Summer Service.

(Appalachia 03)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia, Episode 04
docs.text:
With McManley in town and five people now missing, the team is called to account by Sheriff Burke, hears about a "Chewbacca" picked up by a black sedan, and finally visits the Covenant in Auraria.

Arc The Things in Appalachia Episode 04 Setting Dahlonega, Georgia and Auraria In-fiction date Thursday, October 7, 1992, from about 3 p.m. to dinner time (the same afternoon Appalachia 03 ended) Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita Previous Appalachia 03 Next Appalachia 05 (unrecorded)

Uncertain

The recording of this session is a single mixed audio track, so it is not always clear who is speaking. Quotes below are attributed only where the speaker is clear.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Donald McManley arrives with his mobile lab and takes charge of the evidence. Sheriff Carter Burke demands to know why the FBI turned up before anyone knew there was a pattern. The agents interview Frederick's mother through a translator and Gene's mother, Monica Cartwright, in person, then drive to Auraria, where the Covenant turns out to be poor, sick from its river, and fighting an eviction. Andrew Howard talks his way in to see a new recruit who is to be baptised that evening, the same man the cold open shows vanishing into red mud. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: McManley arrives
docs.text:
At about 3 p.m. the team is outside the hotel as McManley's RV pulls in. He complains that the town has no RV hookups. Huell Kendrick hands him the face in the bag; the team adds a bag of recovered remains, the two boys' shoes, and a small sample of blood from the mineshaft where Kurt Larson shot the creature. McManley grumbles that Kurt could have used a higher caliber and tells him to ice his elbow. (Appalachia 04)

The agents trade theories. The Biz and Huell float a yeti or werewolf. Kurt argues that it is an animal, not strictly human, and that the red light on it was inorganic, a recording or tracking device, which means people are involved. McManley proposes a huge man on meth and PCP; Kurt replies that such a man could throw him but could not be that fast. In the lot, a van and a shiny black Ford truck have a fender bender, and a suited man with a clipboard swaps details with a woman in a forest-ranger uniform. The team watches and does not approach. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Man-to-man with Burke
docs.text:
Andrew phones Burke from the payphone outside the hotel. Burke reports that Aaron Richters has been reported missing by the distribution center, and orders the team to the station. In his office Burke lays it out: five people missing in two days, and the FBI arrived before it was clear there were even two. Andrew admits they do not know what is going on. Kurt describes the task force as an oversensitive early warning system that happens to be right this time, and suggests a curfew and a "truth-adjacent" cover story about a fatal tick-borne disease. Burke says he has asked the state police for help, asks the agents to call them too, and names the strongest man in town, a bodybuilder called Walter Sellers. (Appalachia 04)

Burke's own translator is two days away, so at the team's suggestion he sets up an elderly speakerphone and an FBI translator interprets by telephone for Frederick's mother, who speaks only German. She heard a clatter, no scream, and turned the corner to find him gone and his game on the floor. Kurt explains why the search paused: the shoe points toward an exit, and the cave-in is being excavated. (Appalachia 04)

Meanwhile the Biz returns a page from Jeff "Apple" Appleby, an old drinking buddy and newly appointed federal judge, who wants him in Las Vegas to celebrate. Andrew confirms the case will not wrap by Friday. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Monica Cartwright
docs.text: At her trailer, among wine bottles and a broken air conditioner, Monica recounts Gene vanishing while playing with "the Nick boy". She repeats a sighting of drunk off-season hunters in gray jumpsuits and sunglasses, in a Jeep with a big cage and shotguns. She adds that about a month ago a naked, hairy figure that looked exactly like Chewbacca stood at the end of her driveway with a backpack and then got into the back of a black sedan; Burke dismissed it because she had been drinking. She tells the agents not to come back without her son. Outside, they agree that Gene is almost certainly dead. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Auraria
docs.text:
In Auraria the Covenant members stare. A shy young woman, Clover, says Willow had been sent by Elijah Ray to scout peach orchards and never came back with her samples, that she would not have abandoned the peaches, and that she had been fighting a little with her sister. She also says members get infections every few months from bathing in the river, which carries "a lot of runoff from the Spud Hut plant". Kurt leaves a stack of women's shelter cards; her answer to every concern is that they are getting a boiler. (Appalachia 04)

Mother Dahlia Riversand intercepts the team and installs them in the community center. Kurt's Investigate a Mystery (7, a partial hit) reads a community on the edge of economic viability: rough outhouses, many stills, frantic canning and quilting. Willow's friend River confirms the fight with Prim but does not think Prim is a murderer. Dahlia and River explain the land dispute: about a year ago "corporate goons" arrived with paperwork claiming the land. The orchard deal and the preserve sales are meant to pay for a lawyer. The eviction letters, of which Dahlia has only copies, name a law firm, Jackson and Lee's, and no client. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Jeremy
docs.text:
Dahlia invites the team to that evening's baptism of a door-to-door vacuum salesman. Rita's Manipulate Someone (8) has Andrew play lost and haunted in a private aside; Dahlia tells him the devil is standing right behind him and lets him alone speak to the recruit through a tent wall. Jeremy assumes the FBI has come about "those deaths" and swears he did not know the vacuum cleaners were deadly. He is a Quaalude addict who lost his family and job, broke down near Auraria, and trusts the Covenant to run his life better than he has. (Appalachia 04)

While Andrew is away, Kurt and Huell needle a stony Covenant man with talk of cheeseburgers and stuffed-crust pizza until he storms off reciting Latin. Dahlia explains that the river water has been boiled and treated with chlorine tablets for about a year, since intestinal trouble began. The team leaves without stopping the baptism, and resolves to test the river and look harder at Spud Hut, after one more dinner there. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: White on-screen text reads "Dahlonega, Georgia". In a gas-lit tent a sweating vacuum cleaner salesman in a brown suit changes into a thin white robe and follows a candlelit path to a red-clay river, where four women in white kneel in the mud. An older man with high cheekbones kisses his forehead and hands him a jar of dark liquid with peaches floating in it. He drinks; the sound goes muffled and the camera tilts into Dutch angles. The old man chants in Latin and plunges him into the mud, and he disappears beneath the surface. The session has no recap and ends on Andre's remark, after a Hannibal Lecter joke about Spud Hut, "That is kind of a plot point of the show." See the show. (Appalachia 04)

docs.text:

  • A hairy "Chewbacca" figure was collected by a black sedan about a month ago, which points to human handlers or a costume.
  • Men in gray jumpsuits with a caged Jeep and shotguns were seen in the woods.
  • The Covenant's river carries runoff from the Spud Hut plant, and members have been sick for about a year.
  • Someone has spent a year trying to evict the Covenant through the law firm Jackson and Lee's.
  • The Covenant's baptism uses a peach drink and immersion in red clay.

(Appalachia 04)

(Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• "We're getting a boiler" became the Covenant's answer to every hygiene question, with the date slipping each time. See running gags.
  • The table groaned at another Spud Hut dinner while agreeing to it; Appleby's advice was "Don't eat the shrimp scampi."
  • Zack suggested the salesman sold Kirby vacuums, and Andre briefly retconned the brand before Dahlia named it as something like "Con-A-Wear".
  • Andre said the task force has handled about ten cases, most of them duds.
  • Ezra observed that Andre's NPC names usually carry a joke or a meaning and plainly do not come from a name generator.
  • Asked the day of the week during the Appleby call, someone at the table (probably Andre) says "I believe it's Wednesday". By the count kept in Appalachia 02 and Appalachia 03 it is Thursday.
  • Dice: Dante rolled a 7 on Investigate a Mystery despite his +3.

(Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Continues directly from Appalachia 03: the face, the blood sample, Kurt's elbow, Frederick.
  • Monica's "Chewbacca" and the men in gray jumpsuits follow up the staged footprints of Appalachia 02 and set up the body in the Chewbacca costume in Appalachia 06. Gray jumpsuits are also what the Spud Hut plant workers wear in Appalachia 02.
  • The cold open shows the baptism Dahlia invites the team to, which is to take place that evening.
  • The next session, Appalachia 05, was played but never recorded. Appalachia 06 picks up the following morning and does not say what became of Jeremy's baptism or the planned Spud Hut dinner.

(Appalachia 04)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia, Episode 05
docs.text:
The fifth session of the arc was played but never recorded; it covered the evening and night after the team left Auraria, and its events are known only from what later episodes say on the recording.

Arc The Things in Appalachia Episode 05 (unrecorded) Setting Dahlonega, Georgia In-fiction date The evening and night of Thursday, October 7, 1992, between the end of Appalachia 04 and the morning that opens Appalachia 06 Previous Appalachia 04 Next Appalachia 06

Unrecorded session

This session was played but never recorded. Nothing on this page was heard directly; every statement below comes from a later episode and is cited to it. See lost episodes.

docs.title: What later episodes establish
docs.text: Appalachia 04 ends at dinner time, with the team leaving Auraria and planning one more meal at the Spud Hut. The recording of Appalachia 06 begins partway through Andre's recap of this session and then opens on the following morning at the Smith Hotel. (Appalachia 04, Appalachia 06)

docs.title: The Biz's night
docs.text:
The Biz had a storyline of his own that night, which Andre calls "your nonsense" and Ezra calls "my thing". Andre recaps the only parts the other characters saw: when Huell Kendrick woke in the morning the Biz wandered in wearing slept-in clothes, not having slept in the room; the door of the hotel room next to theirs, room 111, had been broken down; and the Biz had a badly twisted ankle. Ezra, in character, insists that everything was normal. (Appalachia 06)

The cold open of Appalachia 06 shows the aftermath: state police have taped off the bushes outside the hotel, and one of them pulls out a night-vision headset and has it bagged for "the Secret Service fellows". Later the same day Ezra asks Andre, "Did I ever retrieve the thing?", is told he did not, and the two settle the rest privately. After a day of hiking, the Biz's ankle has swollen up badly by evening. (Appalachia 06)

Later episodes fill in what the police think happened. In Appalachia 07 the state police call a press conference about Bill Clinton, whom nobody in town knew was in Dahlonega. In Appalachia 08 the players sum up the story so far: surveillance equipment found in a bush is believed to have been used to spy on Clinton, and the police have fingerprints. In Appalachia 09 the Biz complains that he cannot find his night-vision goggles. See Clinton surveillance scandal. (Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09)

docs.title: The Spud Hut auditor
docs.text: By Appalachia 06 the team has met a financial auditor from Spud Hut corporate. Kurt Larson calls him "the Spud Hut guy that came to interview us" and "the one that was following us", and has a number to reach him on. When the auditor balks at being shown a photograph of a corpse, the Biz reminds him, "Look, you wanted to help the FBI." He does not appear in Appalachia 04, so the meeting took place in this session. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Frotter's bear
docs.text: Frotter Comstock asked the agents to come and shoot a bear on his property, and they would not. He opens the next morning by declaring his "disappointment that y'all wouldn't come down and shoot that bear for me", and at his homestead he points out "the bear incident": a large streak of gore on the ground beside one of his shacks. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: The hybrid
docs.text: In Appalachia 04 Donald McManley has only just been handed the blood from the mineshaft and is still proposing a large man on drugs. In Appalachia 06 Kurt wants the gore at Frotter's compared with "the human hybrid tissue" and asks for another blood sample to be cross-checked "against the ape-man", and nobody at the table questions either phrase. McManley's finding that the mineshaft creature is part human was therefore delivered in this session. See Ape-Men. (Appalachia 04, Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Left unanswered
docs.text:
The recorded episodes never return to several things that Appalachia 04 set up for this evening:

  • Whether the team ate at the Spud Hut again or tested the Covenant's river.
  • Whether anyone attended Jeremy's baptism, and what became of him.
  • Whether Elijah Ray was ever met.
  • Who the suited man and the forest ranger in the hotel parking lot were.
  • What came of the eviction letters from Jackson and Lee's, and of Kurt's promised follow-ups with the state police.
  • Exactly what the Biz did during the night, which was played privately between Andre and Ezra.

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Follows the dinner-time ending of Appalachia 04. The Biz planted a camera in room 111 in Appalachia 02 with instructions to collect it 24 hours later, and no recorded episode shows him doing so.
  • Leads into the cold open of Appalachia 06, where the goggles are found, and into Frotter's report of a "dead Bigfoot" on his land.
  • The auditor returns for lunch at the Spud Hut in Appalachia 06.
  • The night at the hotel becomes the Clinton surveillance scandal of Appalachia 07 and Appalachia 08.

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia, Episode 06
docs.text:
A "dead Bigfoot" on Frotter Comstock's land turns out to be an executed ex-military man in a stolen Chewbacca costume, and the team traces him from a dry cleaner to a motel dumpster.

Arc The Things in Appalachia Episode 06 Setting Dahlonega, Georgia and Comstock's property near Auraria In-fiction date October 1992; one day, morning to evening Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita Previous Appalachia 05 (unrecorded) Next Appalachia 07

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: The morning after the Biz's unseen night, Frotter Comstock reports a dead Bigfoot. It is a man in an expensive Chewbacca costume, shot in the back of the head, with fake footprint evidence nearby and signs that someone cleaned up afterwards. The team follows the costume to the photographer it was stolen from, to the dry cleaner it was stolen out of, and to the Motel and Suites, where the dead man's discarded belongings include a false-lined briefcase holding about $10,000. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Breakfast
docs.text: The recording begins in the middle of a recap of the unrecorded Appalachia 05: the Biz came in wearing slept-in clothes, the hotel door next to the team's was broken down, and he has a badly twisted ankle. At the continental breakfast, Frotter Comstock arrives with the sheriff, complaining that the agents would not come and shoot "that bear" for him. He reports a dead Bigfoot on his land and refuses to touch it for fear of disease. Kurt Larson tells the sheriff to make sure nobody interferes with it: "CIA standard procedure." (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: The body in the copse
docs.text:
Frotter's outbuildings have been hastily wrapped in blue tarps, and a large streak of gore by one shack is introduced as "the bear incident". The body lies in a copse of trees at the base of the hill below. Andrew Howard's Investigate a Mystery (12) establishes that it is a man in a costume soaked in real blood, with a wound like a gangland execution he once saw in an Academy photograph. When Andrew announces that the man was "capped", the sheriff rebukes him: "Son, a man is dead." (Appalachia 06)

Kurt checks for body armor and finds none, which rules out his old unit, UTAW. Under the mask is a white man of 25 to 35 with a military haircut; every tag has been cut from his clothes and his pockets are empty. He has faded anchor and trident tattoos, and Kurt's Sharp roll (11) identifies the trident as a Navy SEAL emblem. The man was shot standing, from directly behind, and was not moved. A second roll (11) puts the weapon at roughly a .357 Magnum at point-blank range. (Appalachia 06)

The Biz's Investigate a Mystery (12) finds ATV tracks that stop near the body and continue down toward the freeway, a snapped plaster-of-Paris toe matching fake Bigfoot prints in the mud, and partial human prints. The molds themselves are gone: someone tidied up after the killing. Frotter whispers to Andrew that he will allow a search of the property if they leave the buildings alone, and gets an ambiguous wink. After a table debate about warrants, Kurt goes into a building anyway and finds Frotter trying to brew beer with marijuana in place of hops. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Following the costume
docs.text:
McManley collects the body in his RV, later noting that the costume's bandolier had been removed and mud rubbed into the fur. At the Gold Bug newspaper, a pinched older woman identifies the Bigfoot photographer as Derek Edwards. By phone Derek says his pictures came from motion-sensor cameras, and that his own Chewbacca costume, bought for cash at a convention, was stolen from Apollo's dry cleaners eight months ago. (Appalachia 06)

Kurt calls the Spud Hut corporate auditor who has been tailing the team, and he buys them lunch at the Spud Hut. The counter savant recognises the dead man's photograph: he came in three times, 4, 9 and 25 days ago, paid cash, wore a holster, and arrived by ATV. Once he was there at the same time as a man in a business suit, though they did not speak. The auditor says the man is not on the plant's employee list. (Appalachia 06)

The scene photographs are developed in the hotel bathroom. The Biz volunteers, Andre passes Ezra private information, and the Biz emerges shaken and absent-minded. The photos and tattoos are faxed to the FBI from the police station. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Apollo's and the Motel and Suites
docs.text:
At Apollo's, the owner admits the storage-room latch had been broken for months. He recognises the dead man as an out-of-town drifter who used to stand watching, sometimes talking on a walkie-talkie, and who was probably staying at the Motel and Suites. There, a weary clerk behind bulletproof glass confirms the man registered as "John Doe", paid cash, was collected once or twice by a helmeted man on an ATV, and had a female caller. His things were thrown out the day before. The clerk warns the agents not to open the green garbage bag. (Appalachia 06)

McManley sends three teenage interns to work the dumpster. Snakeskin cowboy boots identify the right bag, and Kurt's Investigate a Mystery (10) turns up a briefcase with a false lining, a slot for a high-caliber handgun and about $10,000 in bank-banded notes; a coil of animal hair in one boot and a walkie-talkie in the other; and plastic bags and duct tape. There is nothing identifying. Kurt notes the walkie-talkie's frequency and reads the man as a mercenary, not a spook, possibly sent to kill someone and double-crossed with his own gun. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Where things stand
docs.text: Kurt's working theory is that someone hired the former SEAL to fake Bigfoot, perhaps to keep people off Spud Hut property; that a real ape-man hybrid exists separately and the two are unrelated; and that there is also a bear. He wants the gore smear at Frotter's tested against the hybrid tissue. Asked to convey how bad the Biz's day is, Ezra declines. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: "We open on a slow zoom on the hotel." Caution tape surrounds the bushes outside the Smith Hotel while tired state police take prints and swabs. An officer emerges with a night-vision headset: "Bag it and tag it, the Secret Service fellows I want to take a look at that." Andre later confirms that the "thing" the Biz needs to retrieve relates to this scene. Ezra was taken aside twice for private information, so part of the Biz's story is off the record. See the show. (Appalachia 06)

  • Derek Edwards is the newspaper photographer; Appalachia 02 gave the photo credit as "Charlie" Briggs, and Appalachia 01 called the paper the Dahlonega Times, not the Gold Bug. Andre also introduces the Gold Bug as "the official newspaper of Auraria, Georgia".

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia, Episode 07
docs.text:
Over one evening the team gets a secret menu in cipher, a tracking tag pulled out of bloody vomit, a furious call about a presidential candidate, and a wrecked Spud Hut truck full of dirt.

Arc The Things in Appalachia Episode 07 Setting Dahlonega, Georgia: the Spud Hut, the hotel, the freeway crash site In-fiction date October 7, 1992, sunset into the night Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita Previous Appalachia 06 Next Appalachia 08

Recording

This session survives only as a single mixed audio track, so it is not always clear who is speaking. Lines whose speaker is uncertain are marked (?) below.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Dinner at the Spud Hut brings a drunk dealer in dangerous chemistry sets, a secret menu written as a cryptogram, and the Circle Chasers, who have found a blinking tracking device marked "Inventory Control, SHA Tracking". Then the news breaks that state police are accusing the FBI of spying on Bill Clinton in Dahlonega, and Big Bill tears into Andrew Howard by phone. The night ends at a crashed Spud Hut truck whose driver has been taken and whose potato sacks hold dirt. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Dinner and the secret menu
docs.text:
After a stop at the hotel to sit down and change socks, the team returns to the Spud Hut for the second time that day, partly to recruit the counter man with the remarkable memory. In line they meet Eduardo Hooper, a drunk man in a cowboy hat and bolo tie who sells 1960s chemistry sets with uranium in them and who whispers an order for the "special taco taco spud". Kurt Larson takes his card as an off-the-books source. (Appalachia 07)

The Biz orders the same thing and asks about the rest of the secret menu. The counter man unlocks a briefcase with two keys and hands over a sheet of symbols, explaining, "I designed the cryptogram myself." Huell Kendrick orders margarita spuds, potato skins filled with margarita. Kurt tries to buy one using three IDs in three different names; his Manipulate Someone comes up 9, and the clerk gives way only after Kurt shows photographs of his grown children and Andrew offers his own ID in support. Kurt immediately hands the drink to the Circle Chasers girl who had been refused one for lack of ID. The Biz's taco taco spud turns out to be a superbly cooked octopus. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: The Circle Chasers' find
docs.text:
The Circle Chasers' RV bursts into the lot. Harvey knocks Andrew over, and on a roll of 13 Andrew scoops the Great Dane up and cradles it like a baby. Vanessa gasps, "Bear vomit." Huell pays for everyone's dinner out of the cash from the dead man's briefcase. (Appalachia 07)

After closing, under the potato-colored light of the sign, the teenagers take the team into their blacklit RV and produce a Ziploc bag holding a blinking red light. They had gone to look at a reported "squatch" lying among trees, found vomit full of blood with the light in it, and been chased off by a bear "with, like, half a face". Kurt says it was not a bear and warns them to stay away. The Biz, drunk, rolls Investigate a Mystery at -1 for a 9: the device is electronic, on a ragged leather band, and etched "Inventory Control, SHA Tracking, SS994-0851". Kurt dislikes the word "inventory", and the team stores it in an emptied corn-nuts cup as a makeshift Faraday cage. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: The Clinton story
docs.text:
As they reach McManley's RV every pager goes off. McManley asks whether they have seen the news: a state police official has told a press conference that the FBI is in Dahlonega surveilling presidential candidate Bill Clinton, and reporters are expected within about five hours. Kurt does not know who Clinton is, and Andre insists that in October 1992 he would. (Appalachia 07)

Andrew phones Big Bill from the hotel lobby. Bill points out that there are only four FBI officers in Georgia and demands a detailed inventory of everything the team has done and every piece of equipment it has used over the last 50 hours; Andrew offers an itinerary. Andrew babbles about bears and potatoes and then blurts out the body count: two children, the exploded man in the cave, the executed man in the Chewbacca costume, and one man missing. Bill tells him not to talk to anybody, says he will go to the President and come down himself, and ends, "Howard, don't fuck this up." The teenage desk clerk, Tully, overhears; asked for a fax machine, Tully offers to call their mother, who has one, and Andrew declines. (Appalachia 07)

Comparing notes, the Biz suggests the story is a fake Watergate-type smear. Kurt wonders whether someone is misusing the contents of their old irradiated car to frame an off-the-books team. Since Andrew is forbidden to speak to townspeople or reporters and looks unmistakably like a policeman, the team sets about disguising him. Kurt's Preparedness roll (12) means his backup escape kit is complete, the original having been irradiated: makeup, prosthetics, wigs and whole outfits. Andrew gets a weight on the back of his neck to make him slouch, platform shoes and a convincing fake mustache, and Kurt hands out Hawaiian shirts all round as "the real urban camo". Andre rolls Andrew's Manipulate Someone (at -1) himself and keeps the result secret. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: The truck
docs.text:
The sheriff radios about a truck accident with a great deal of blood. At the scene, cruisers block the freeway and Spud Hut trucks queue behind them. The truck, marked SHGRDC with an SHA logo matching the tracking device, lies on its side at the bottom of a hill. The cab is bloody on every surface, with no body, eight gunshots through the cabin, a rear window broken inward and a windshield broken outward. On top, the vinyl roof is ripped as if by fingers. Kurt reasons that something came in through the back window, mauled the driver and left through the front with what remained. (Appalachia 07)

In the spilled trailer, the sheriff slits a sack labelled "Potatoes" and dirt pours out. Another holds a whole octopus floating in liquid. Huell asks McManley to analyse the dirt. The sheriff passes on gossip from a friend in the state police: the Secret Service tipped them off, and the prints on a piece of surveillance equipment matched an employee in the FBI database. The sheriff proposes visiting the Spud Hut plant first thing in the morning. Andrew's itinerary for Big Bill is to be faxed from the sheriff's station, and Kurt sends the cryptogram to the NSA, the "Puzzle Palace", without telling them it is a menu. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: A heavyset Spud Hut driver in a gray jumpsuit drives at sunset to "Radar Love", a mustard-stained photograph taped to the dash. He hears a clang and ripping from behind the cab, then breaking glass and a growl. He reaches for the Glock under his seat and misses. The truck swerves through a barricade amid screams and gunshots and stops among trees with the song still playing quietly. Cut to credits. Andre then asks the table to recall where they left off. See the show. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• The Spud Hut menu keeps growing: margarita spuds, the octopus, a burger spud with a patty of crumbled bacon. The team's count of Spud Hut visits is now an embarrassment for the itinerary. See running gags.
  • Andrew's satchel is described as magical storage whose contents he forgets; the verdict at the table was "Howard basically has magical dementia."
  • Zack called "nose goes" on who was spying on Clinton; Andrew, who does not know the game, lost.
  • Andre scolded the table for forgetting that it is October 1992 and an election is about to happen: not knowing Clinton "would be like not knowing who Kamala Harris is".
  • Dice: Andrew 13 to catch the dog, Kurt 9 on Manipulate Someone and 12 on Preparedness, the Biz 9 on a drunk Investigate a Mystery, and a hidden Manipulate Someone roll for Andrew's disguise.

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• Follows the dumpster search of Appalachia 06.
  • The surveillance equipment in the news story follows from the night-vision headset that state police bagged for the Secret Service in the cold open of Appalachia 06. Nobody at the table makes the connection aloud in this episode.
  • The tracking device accounts for the blinking red light seen on the creature in the tunnel in Appalachia 03.
  • Andre says here that the team arrived on October 4 and that it is now the 7th. In Appalachia 01 the team was still at the office in Washington on Monday, October 4, and the date had become the 5th by the time they were in Georgia.
  • Sets up the plant visit in Appalachia 08.

(Appalachia 07)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia, Episode 08
docs.text:
The team finally enters the Spud Hut plant, where Jan Martense walks them four stories underground, leaves them outside a "break room" full of ape-men, and takes the elevator back up.

Arc The Things in Appalachia Episode 08 Setting Spud Hut Georgia Regional Distribution Center, Dahlonega, Georgia In-fiction date October 1992, a workday, directly after the truck wreck of Appalachia 07 Players present Andre (GM), Dante, Ezra, Zack, Rita Previous Appalachia 07 Next Appalachia 09

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Hiding from reporters over the Clinton surveillance story, the team follows the sheriff to the Spud Hut plant and bluffs its way inside, though not before Andrew Howard is recognised on live television. Plant manager Jan Martense leads them down to the Special Projects level, sends them to wait in a room with the door code 441, and leaves. The room holds five ape-men. The fight ends when Kurt Larson sets off a Claymore mine in the corridor. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Outside the plant
docs.text:
With McManley called to process the truck cab, the team follows the sheriff to the plant. The Spud Hut trucks that had been everywhere are gone from the road. In the lot are a Fox 5 Atlanta van and the car of the investigator who has been looking into Spud Hut, chain-smoking out of his window. Kurt swears him to secrecy and tells him the wrecked truck carried only dirt, "not one potato". The investigator guesses, "Gold mining?" He warns that the plant's executive is high-strung and European: "I think he's Polish or Irish or something." (Appalachia 08)

The team decides to pose as reporters being escorted by the sheriff. Andre rules that he will make Kurt's Manipulate Someone roll himself and keep the result hidden. Andrew's unmistakable look would cost a -1, so the sheriff swears him in as a deputy and dresses him in the spare uniform of an absent deputy called String Bean; Kurt's fake European accent (Act Under Pressure, 12) adds +1. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: "Thank you for your time"
docs.text:
At the door the Fox 5 crew recognises "Andrew Howard with the FBI" and asks him, live, about the "Bill Clinton wiretap" and whether this is the next Watergate. Andrew says "Nothing," then "Thank you for your time," and power-walks away. The sheriff talks the receptionist, Charlene, into unlocking the door. On the threshold Andrew turns back, sweating, to add "Thank you for your time again." Andre adds that the clip of Andrew, sweating, turning back to say it again goes on to be replayed on the news about every ten minutes. (Appalachia 08)

Inside, Charlene asks for identification, and Kurt fumbles past an ID marked "Brazil" before finding a real one. Andrew's pager goes off with Big Bill's number, but all the phones are down. She leads them through corridors of workers hauling potato sacks, explains a fishy smell as the "new special taco sauce", and tells the Biz not to touch the sacks: Spud Hut potatoes are "never touched by human hands". (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Jan Martense
docs.text:
Jan is very tall, gaunt and sweaty, in an ill-fitting suit. Kurt introduces himself as CIA "assisting the FBI"; Jan says he grew up in East Germany and understands such arrangements. In the cargo elevator he asks whether they were spying on the presidential candidate. He calls the driver's death a "tragic accident". Told that the truck carried only soil, he promises to check every outgoing truck against its manifest and says he will not tolerate chicanery. Kurt's Read a Bad Situation (9) is ambiguous: Jan is a little squirrelly, but he is also a corporate manager talking to the CIA. The Biz's pager shows Big Bill's number just before it loses signal as the elevator descends. (Appalachia 08)

Jan keys the steel doors marked "Special Projects", takes them down a second elevator, and says, "Down here we do the toppings." Then he abruptly needs to "make an arrangement" on the internal phones, the external lines being out. He sends them to wait five minutes in a room down the hall, code 441, with chairs and a drinks machine, and rides the elevator back up to ground level. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: The break room
docs.text:
Kurt enters the code, props the dark room's door with his shoe and watches the elevator rise. The others wander the open floor. A group Read a Bad Situation (Kurt 9, Huell 8, Andrew 9, the Biz 11) turns up medical equipment, animal-handling equipment and shovels stashed where they should not be. The Biz, with an 11, is the only one to hear the door squeak; he turns to see a huge, pale, hairy arm probing out, with reflective eyes behind it, and shrieks. Shrieking and the rattle of cages erupt inside the room. (Appalachia 08)

Kurt decides to shoot his shoe out of the gap. Andrew, delighted at the chance of meeting a cryptid, takes the handle; every light goes out. On a 9 he gets the door open, Kurt shoots the shoe inside, and Andrew slams the door on a long-nailed hand. The door then bursts open into his forehead. His protection cancels the harm, but he is dazed, and several figures come out. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Ear pro
docs.text:
Kurt's flashlight shows five pale, hairy, hunched, partly human apes. One picks Andrew up and throws him through the drop ceiling into the pipes; he fails to grab hold (5), falls back into its grip and is juggled. Another punches Kurt's dog whistle into his throat. Huell Kendrick rolls Kick Some Ass for 10 and shoots one through the neck by the light of Andrew's camera flash; it staggers into him and slams his head into a cinder-block wall (2 harm, stunned). (Appalachia 08)

With four creatures closing on him, Kurt makes a preparedness roll (7, raised to 10) and produces a Claymore from his belt. He sets it down, jumps back and yells "Ear pro!" The stunned Huell cannot react; the Biz (8) drops and covers; Andrew (10) happens to be thrown back to the ceiling, above the blast. The creature juggling him becomes a mist of gore and bone. Huell takes fragments and a ruptured eardrum, ending at 3 harm and semi-conscious; the Biz takes 1. Everyone is deafened, and the door frame and opposite wall are gone. The sheriff, who has been screaming continuously since the hand first appeared and who dived through the "break room" door when he saw the Claymore, peeks back out. (Appalachia 08)

Andre's tally at the end of the session is one creature dead, the one that was juggling Andrew, and three hurt: at least two badly injured by the blast, plus the one Huell shot through the neck. The four survivors have fled into the rest of the floor. Dante asks whether two are dead and Andre corrects him: "One's dead." About a minute and a half has passed since Jan's elevator went up. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The camera glides down a steel corridor to double doors marked "Special Projects" with a keypad, tips down through a floor grate past pipes and hissing steam, and enters a nearly dark room of rattling steel cages. Hooting and shrieking build to a peak, then stop as a dozen shining eyes turn toward the camera. "We cut to credits." There is no "previously on"; the players recap the truck wreck themselves. The session ends on a cliffhanger. See the show. (Appalachia 08)
