docs.title: The Walkers in Skin, Episode 07
docs.text:
A naked giant breaks into the double-wide, Bigelow's recordings and staff vanish, and Andrew Howard walks into the school gym at 1 a.m. to meet himself. The Andrew who walks out is not the same one.

Arc The Walkers in Skin Episode 07 Setting Sherman Ranch; Ballard High School In-fiction date The night of November 2–3, 1992 (Election Day), from sunset to about 5 a.m. Players present Andre (GM), Rita, Dante, Ezra, Zack Previous Walkers 06 Next Walkers 08

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: An intruder with a shotgun and a key lets himself into the guest double-wide; Andrew Howard ends the fight by driving something out of him with light. At the big house, Robert Bigelow finds every recording and three employees gone, and arms everyone. Andrew keeps his 1 a.m. appointment at the gym, where upright horses usher him in to meet his own double. He fights, sets off a grenade, and loses. A replica takes his place and tells the team a tidied story. In the burning school Huell Kendrick faces a pack of upright coyotes and finds bodies wrapped in plastic falling from the ceiling. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: The two Andrews
docs.text:
Which Andrew is which

Rita plays the real Andrew Howard up to the end of the gym fight. Andre ejects Dante, Ezra and Zack from the call for the whole of that scene. When the double's tendrils enter Andrew's mouth and "everything goes black", Andre gives Rita a written handout and tells her, "you are not in Andrew Howard's body. You are in a replica." From that moment she plays the replica, which is the same double Andrew fought in the gym ("You are the one that barfed in his mouth"), and which passes itself off to the team as Andrew. The other players are brought back only afterwards. Neither they nor their characters are told of the swap in this episode; Rita remarks at the table, "I think they have suspicions." She keeps playing the replica through Walkers 08 and the unrecorded Walkers 08.5, and the real Andrew returns in Walkers 09. (Walkers 07)

Andre told Rita that the faction clones people from tissue samples (Andrew's came from the cut left by the mayor's ring in Walkers 05, Huell's from the bite in Walkers 06); that a clone of Huell exists but has not yet replaced him; that this copy was made in a hurry and "wrong", has leukemia, and deteriorates the longer it lasts; that it starts at four harm from the grenade and must explain its injuries; and that the faction has suborned about 60% of the town and is close to dropping its pretenses. What will happen to the real Andrew is left unsaid: "You would assume the plan is to kill him." See Replication. In the Plot below, "Andrew" in quotation marks is the replica. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: A rough nap
docs.text:
The team naps at about 6 p.m., with Huell's bitten hand swelling. Around 11 p.m. the Biz wakes on edge (Read a Bad Situation, 9) to scratching at the front door. Through the peephole he sees a low mass, not human height, which skitters around the house when he opens up. Then hinges squeak in the mud room at the back. The laundry-room door opens by millimeters and a wide, bald head pokes out two feet off the floor. (Walkers 07)

The intruder is a naked giant, nearly seven feet tall, with an over-under shotgun. He throws Huell into the Biz. Andrew, in striped pajamas, tackles him from behind (Protect Someone, 12) so that one barrel goes into the ceiling, and is slammed through the drywall. Kurt Larson forces the second barrel into the wall and is caught in a chokehold. The Biz loops his belt around the man's neck (a 5) and has a chunk bitten out of his cheek. Shots to both feet from Kurt's P90 and Huell's pistol produce no sign of pain. (Walkers 07)

Andrew will not risk a head shot with the Biz in the way. He uses Cast Out Evil instead, and rolls a 12. With his hands on the man's face, a black-light glow passes through the body and bluish-white light streams from the eyes and mouth. The man goes limp. Andrew does not understand what he did. Huell's first aid (a 15) stabilizes the body, which breathes but has fixed pupils and no muscle tone. A key is still in the back door. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: Protocol blue
docs.text: Walt "Coyote" Murphy arrives at 11:15, looks at the naked man, and says, "Is that... you?" The phones are down. He drives the body to the emergency room in Roosevelt without stopping in Ballard. At the big house Bigelow is raging: every hard drive and tape (Bigelow's recordings) is gone, the barn is cleared out, three employees are missing, and whoever did it had keys to everything. Told about the missing students and the departed sheriff, he declares "protocol blue", opens "the big cabinet", hands out SPAS-12s and M16s, and asks the team to stay. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: The gym
docs.text:
Andrew dresses in his FBI suit and takes his camera, pepper spray, pistol, bag and pendant. He refuses backup. Huell drives him in, straightens his tie ("You kids have fun"), and parks out of sight. (Walkers 07)

The gym's latch is taped over, as the note promised. Andrew knocks. Two horses standing on their hind legs are inside; one politely gestures him in. On a stool sits Andrew Howard, who waves, trots over and shakes his hand. Armed townspeople file in behind. The double offers the easy way or the hard way. The easy way is a kiss: his mouth stretches wide and fine gray tendrils extend from his throat. The hard way is the click of a shotgun. (Walkers 07)

Andrew pepper-sprays him (Kick Some Ass, 9). For a moment the double's head is simply erased, showing cross-sections in colors that do not belong inside a human head, and he collapses in a seizure. A horse brings its hoof down on the back of Andrew's neck and someone shoots him in the stomach with a shotgun. Using his What I Need When I Need It move, he pulls a grenade from his bag and pulls the pin; his Act Under Pressure is an 8, and it slips from his hand. A horse throws itself on it. The blast drives a piece of horse into his back. He casts out whatever is in the horse stamping him (a 14) and it goes limp, pinning him. The double, missing part of a shoulder, crawls over it. Sickly-sweet vomit drips onto Andrew's face, the tendrils enter his mouth, and everything goes black. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: Coyotes in the hallway
docs.text:
From the car, Huell hears the explosion and finds the gym in flames. "Andrew" staggers out bloodied and says townsfolk tried to kidnap him and he used a grenade. Huell patches him up (a 13) and goes in. The gym is chairs, limbs and pieces of horse (Investigate a Mystery, 10); the attackers have retreated deeper into the school. Part of the ceiling comes down, dropping a spiral bundle of melted plastic that lands with a wet splash. (Walkers 07)

In the hallway ten or twelve coyotes stand staring, then advance in step. Warning shots do nothing. Huell kills one; another clamps onto his arm; the pack rises onto its hind legs. "Andrew" arrives, fires (a 13), and routs them. Huell unrolls the bundle: a putrefied corpse packed in white powder. More fall. No fire truck ever comes. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: Until sunup
docs.text: Back at the ranch "Andrew" tells Kurt and the Biz about townsfolk, horses and a grenade, leaves out his double, and guesses "a religious cult thing again". Kurt recognizes the smell of a mass grave on Huell and concludes this has been going on for months. The dead coyote, oddly clean and groomed, goes into Bigelow's beer cooler for McManley. "Andrew" takes first watch with the Ponytail Lady. Midnight passes into Election Day. At about 5 a.m. Walt returns: the intruder died on the heart-lung machine. The plan is to drive out at sunrise with radios and call in the National Guard. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: A dim room of stock tanks filled with dark liquid, hoses and wires, with distant voices and squeaking shoes. Huell's face rises from the last tank and opens bloodshot eyes. Cut to credits. This is Skinwalker Huell. Andre follows with a recap of the previous session. After the gym scene the episode cuts back in time to Huell waiting in the car, and later "to the following morning". (Walkers 07)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin, Episode 08.5
docs.text:
A session of The Walkers in Skin that was played but never recorded, in which the team finds horses, calls in the National Guard and retakes the Roosevelt police station.

Arc The Walkers in Skin Episode "08.5" (played between episodes 08 and 09) Setting Ballard and Roosevelt, Utah In-fiction date November 1992, between the morning of Walkers 08 and the evening of Walkers 09 Previous Walkers 08 Next Walkers 09

Unrecorded session

This session was played but never recorded. No recording of it exists, so there are no quotes and no dice results. What happened in it is known only from Walkers 09: Andre's recap at the start of that episode, and things the players and their characters say later in it. See Lost episodes.

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Walkers 08 ended with the team cut off: phones and power out, every car in Roosevelt stolen, and the only road held by armed impostors at the bridge blockade. Walkers 09 opens with the team riding in a National Guard convoy toward the community center. This session covered everything in between. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Andre's recap
docs.text:
At the start of Walkers 09, Andre recaps the session in order. (Walkers 09)

  • The team "went and got some horses" so that they could get around the roadblock.
  • They took a generator to the radio station and called the National Guard.
  • They met the Guard, on horseback, outside town.
  • They rode back and fought their way through "the road barricade in between Ballard and Roosevelt".
  • They breached and cleared the Roosevelt police station.
  • The session ended with a plan to go back to the community center "to find out what's going on".

docs.title: Details mentioned during Walkers 09
docs.text:
• The X marks. The team marked themselves with X's so that they could be told from copies. When Zack asks, "Did we put X's on ourselves?", the whole table confirms it. (Walkers 09)
  • The Guard. The detachment is led by the major and travels in Humvees and APCs. The team had warned the Guard about the ranch phenomenon only in passing: Rita recalls "an offhand comment" that they should keep the horses, and the major still needs the lifting of vehicles explained to him in the finale. (Walkers 09)
  • Riders. People from Bigelow's ranch ride with the convoy on horseback, Walt "Coyote" Murphy among them. Huell Kendrick and "Andrew" shared a horse ("We rode a horse together, Howard"), and "Andrew" rode in the major's Humvee for "the confrontation". (Walkers 09)
  • The police station. Something escaped through a window while the team was clearing the station. In the finale Kurt works out what it was: "Oh, you're what escaped through the window." Donald McManley, his interns and a handful of Guardsmen were left at the station, where the Guardsmen helped with autopsies; the team collects them at the end of the finale. (Walkers 09)
  • Injuries. Huell came out of the session badly hurt. In the finale Zack finds he is unstable and one harm from dying because of "injuries last time". (Walkers 09)

docs.title: The two Andrews
docs.text:
The Andrew who rode with the team in this session was the replica that Rita had been secretly playing since the end of the gym scene in Walkers 07. It wore an X like everyone else, and at the start of the finale the other characters still trust it. By then its bruises have worsened and its skin has an unhealthy cast. (Walkers 07, Walkers 09)

The real Andrew, who revived in the police station morgue at the end of Walkers 08, was absent throughout. By his own account in the finale he woke to find the station "full of cops", knew they were not real ones, and broke out; he was the thing that escaped through the window. He then spent an afternoon explaining his situation to Nancy the goose. Andre puts his absence from the team at about two days. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Not established
docs.text:
• Where the horses came from. In Walkers 03 Walt says the ranch keeps none: "Strictly ATVs." (Walkers 03)
  • Which barricade the team broke. Andre's recap places it between Ballard and Roosevelt; the blockade seen in Walkers 08 was at a bridge on the road out of Roosevelt toward Bridgeland. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)
  • How the fights at the barricade and the station went, and what became of Yusuf Ansari, who was last seen wounded at the station in Walkers 08. (Walkers 08)
  • Who took the battery from Huell's walkie-talkie, which he finds missing at the start of Walkers 09. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
• The radio station was spotted on the map of Ballard in Walkers 08, and the team left that episode planning to collect Bigelow's people and try it. (Walkers 08)
  • The National Guard had been on standby since Kurt's call to Big Bill in Walkers 06. (Walkers 06)
  • The impostor police seen walking toward the station at the end of Walkers 08 are the "cops" the real Andrew woke among. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)
  • The session leads directly into the convoy scene that opens Walkers 09. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin, Episode 08
docs.text:
The team finds Roosevelt carless, powerless and policed by the dead, McManley's autopsy shows what the townspeople have become, and the only road out is blockaded. Throughout, the Andrew Howard riding with them is a copy.

Arc The Walkers in Skin Episode 08 Setting Sherman Ranch; the Ballard road; Roosevelt, Utah In-fiction date Early November 1992, the morning after the gym fire, about 9 a.m. into the afternoon Players present Andre (GM), Rita, Dante, Ezra, Zack; Ben listening to the closing scene Previous Walkers 07 Next Walkers 08.5 (unrecorded)

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: Donald McManley is ambushed on the road by townspeople, two of them children. In Roosevelt every car has been stolen or sabotaged and every officer in the police station has been shot; Yusuf Ansari survives under the bodies. After a firefight with a three-man cleanup crew, McManley opens a skull and finds a pilot: the people of Ballard are manufactured vehicles. The road out is held by two dozen armed impostors in police uniforms. After the other players log off, a private scene shows the real Andrew Howard waking, changed, at the bottom of the morgue pile. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: The two Andrews
docs.text:
Which Andrew is which

For the whole of the team's story in this episode Rita plays the replica that took Andrew's place at the end of the gym scene in Walkers 07: a clone made by the skinwalkers which has his memories (Andrew, as Andre puts it, was "brain-downloaded and then cloned"). Dante, Ezra and Zack have not been told, and neither have their characters. Rita plays the replica as she would play Andrew: sunny, fussy about Bureau protocol, photographing everything. The real Andrew appears only in the closing scene, played after the other three have left the call. (Walkers 08)

The copy shows through in the dice and the fiction. It rolls a 3 in the firefight, panics, shoots out one of Betsy's windows and is wounded; Andre notes that whatever made Andrew tough "is not kicking in as much" ("Since apparently I can be shot now"). Its Lay on Hands on the Biz does nothing at all. It is the one who takes the organ from the autopsy and keeps hold of it. After the session Rita explained what the replica had been doing for its faction: it stole the sugar from the station break room, "because that's all I can eat", and got hold of the Biz's blood so that a copy of him could be started, though the faction cannot replace him without his memories. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: The ambush
docs.text:
At about 9 a.m. the team is eating pancakes at Bigelow's armed compound. The phones are down and the walkie-talkies cannot reach Salt Lake City. Kurt Larson spots a small radio station on the map of Ballard. McManley, due at ten, radios at 11:30: a shootout on the Roosevelt road, bodies, send help. (Walkers 08)

They drive Betsy past the burned school. McManley's Suburban lies on its side behind a spike strip. Around it are four dead townspeople: a matronly woman with a shotgun, an older man with a handgun, and two children with kitchen knives. They fired without a word, and he did not see that two were children until it was over. One of his two interns is shot in the leg. The spike strip came from an empty Roosevelt cruiser whose radio is silent. "Andrew" wants to call it in and leave the scene undisturbed; Kurt and the Biz overrule him. McManley, offered a meditation technique: "If you touch me, I will break your goddamn arms." He also brings the election news: the count is unfinished, with Perot ahead. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Roosevelt
docs.text:
The traffic lights are out and there is not a car on the street. Kurt's Read a Bad Situation (10) finds no hidden danger, only one way out: the road. A confused local says his car was stolen and nobody answers at the station. At a repair shop the mechanics report every drivable car taken and the rest sabotaged by hand, with batteries gone, belts cut and sugar in the tanks. Someone wants nobody to leave. (Walkers 08)

At the station, Huell Kendrick throws a brick through the glass door while Kurt is still picking the lock ("I'm the FB-fucking-I"). The Biz fails the entry roll with a 3 and slices his foot. Inside, every officer of the Roosevelt Police Department is dead, and each is missing a small part taken after death: a finger, a toe, an ear. In the cells Kurt finds Yusuf alive under a heap of bodies, shot through the shoulder and missing a toe. He describes naked people, "like families", with shotguns and a machine gun, and then many cars driving away. The armory is stripped. Kurt shoots open the morgue: dozens of decaying bodies in plastic and rock salt, which is where the bodies from the Ballard school ceiling went. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: The cleanup crew
docs.text: Three men in gray maintenance uniforms (the Utah cleanup crew) are found inspecting the team's cars. They say they need the substation keys. Told they will be searched, one draws. Kurt (a flat 10) wounds him; "Andrew" panics on his 3; Huell is grazed; the Biz, also grazed, kills the gunman with a head shot. Kurt rams the two who run against the gate with Betsy. They will not speak. The Biz's Manipulate Someone question shows that "the facade of acting like a person has completely dropped away". Their bags hold guns, plastic sheeting and bungee cords. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: "This is a vehicle"
docs.text:
McManley autopsies the dead gunman on the conference table. There is no stomach, about eight feet of malformed intestine, and a small fatty liver. Inside the skull is a brain-like organ, iridescent purple and green, with sucker-tipped tendrils and a passage down to the sinuses; the body's own brain is a shrunken lump at the top of the spine. "This is not a person. This is a vehicle. Somebody made this. And whatever you killed inside of it was its pilot." The pilot feeds from the host's blood and can digest only simple sugars and starches. The body is anatomically childlike, "a 200-pound baby", and an ordinary person could not be occupied this way; the raw material might be a tissue sample. "Andrew" asks to keep the organ in its Tupperware. See Pilot and host biology. (Walkers 08)

Back at the cells the two prisoners are slumped and empty. Kurt (a 10) sees movement in the drop ceiling; a flashlight through an eye shows light at the back of the mouth. Their pilots have left. Two of the ambush bodies, a child and an adult, still hold dead ones. McManley: "I think I shot something a lot worse." The team concludes the mayor of Ballard was taken months ago, which explains the sugar clues. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: The bridge
docs.text: The hospital has a generator it cannot spare and no ambulance. The Guard is 141 miles away in Salt Lake City; Bridgeland is 23. As the two-car convoy leaves, uniformed figures who have trouble walking are approaching the station. At the bridge on the only road, a dozen cars form a blockade manned by twenty to twenty-five people in stolen police uniforms and body armor, who turn a FedEx truck around. Kurt scouts it unseen (an 11). The team turns back toward Ballard to collect Bigelow's guards, try the radio station, or look for a road east to Vernal. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: The other Andrew Howard
docs.text: After Dante, Ezra and Zack log off, with Ben listening in, Andre cuts to "the other Andrew Howard". The real Andrew is dead, shot through the heart, and it is agonizing. Then the non-human parts of his biology assert themselves and he spasms back to life. He wakes naked, wrapped in plastic and duct tape, at the bottom of the corpse pile in the Roosevelt police station morgue, with two heartbeats. Rita rebuilds him from the Divine playbook into the Monstrous: Lay on Hands and Cast Out Evil are gone, What I Need When I Need It stays, and he gains a ranged "life drain" attack and a curse, Feed, that needs regular blood. Andre: "They killed you. It just didn't stick." (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: The episode has no cold open, recap or credits: it begins with the 9 a.m. pancakes and ends on the private "cut to the other Andrew Howard" scene. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin, Episode 09
docs.text:
The arc finale: a National Guard convoy, a homemade killdozer and three agents on horseback assault the community center, the real Andrew Howard comes sprinting back, and the team shuts a portal in a cavern under Utah.

Arc The Walkers in Skin Episode 09 (finale) Setting Ballard, Sherman Ranch, the community center and the cavern In-fiction date One evening in early November 1992, sunset into night; the election result is announced at the end Players present Andre (GM), Rita, Dante, Ezra, Zack Previous Walkers 08.5 (unrecorded) Next Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Synopsis
docs.text: The convoy drives through dead Ballard toward the community center, picking up a patriot in an armored bulldozer on the way. The ranch farmhouse floats into the sky and is launched toward Roosevelt. In the fight at the fence a naked, bloody Andrew Howard runs in at thirty-five miles an hour, insisting he is the real one. He is. The replica that Rita has secretly played since Walkers 07 is exposed, and she takes back the original, now the Monstrous. Below the building the skinwalkers are evacuating through a portal powered by a dead angel. The team wrecks it. Outside, white powder is falling, black triangles are overhead, and people in hazmat suits are collecting the bodies. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: The two Andrews
docs.text:
Which Andrew is which

Rita begins this episode still playing the replica that took Andrew's place at the end of the gym scene in Walkers 07. It is the Andrew who rides with the major and wears the team's Sharpie X. When the real Andrew arrives in the middle of the battle, Andre voices him at first, so that for a few minutes Rita's replica and Andre's real Andrew argue over which is which. Once the replica has refused to open its mouth, shot Kurt and shown its tendrils, Andre ends the secret: "Now that the game is up, Rita, let's swap back who we're controlling." From then on Rita plays the real Andrew and Andre plays the replica until its death in the cavern. Up to that moment Dante, Ezra and Zack play their characters as trusting the Andrew with the X: Huell pulls him onto his own horse and helps him shoot at the real one. (Walkers 09)

By this episode the replica looks ill. Andre describes worsening bruises on its arms and an unhealthy cast to its skin, and reminds Zack that this Andrew "has been a lot less bulletproof than you've known him to be". (Walkers 09)

The real Andrew's account: he lost time after pulling the pin on the grenade in the school gym, was shot point-blank in the chest, and woke under a pile of bodies in the police station morgue, which was full of false police. He broke out, and Kurt realizes he was what had escaped through the station window. He has been gone about two days and spent the afternoon explaining himself to Nancy the goose. He says he was dead and "there was no God up there". Since waking he runs at about 35 miles an hour and shrugs off small-arms fire, and he looks subtly inhuman and perhaps slightly taller. His death and revival were shown in the closing scene of Walkers 08. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: The convoy
docs.text:
At dusk the Guard's Humvees and APCs roll through lightless Ballard, followed by Betsy and Bigelow's people on horseback. Kurt Larson, the Biz and Huell Kendrick are on horses too, since horses are nonferrous. "Andrew" (the replica; see above) rides with the major. Huell finds the battery missing from his walkie-talkie; asked why, Andre says only, "You don't know." Kurt warns the major to bail out if a vehicle starts to rise. (Walkers 09)

A dust plume behind them turns out to be a killdozer: an armored bulldozer with machine guns, pipe bombs and a flamethrower, finished that morning by Ned Simpson, a feed-store worker who has spent six months welding it and believes he is fighting "the communist menace". Kurt: "in the CIA, this is what we call an asset." The major lets him join. (Walkers 09)

The substation is arcing so violently that it has set fires on both sides of the road. Near the ranch a cloud crosses the sun. Kurt's Read a Bad Situation (a 10) shows that it is the farmhouse, floating inside a halo of barbed wire, roof panels and horseshoes. As the sun sets a purple glow builds over the ranch; the house vanishes in a vapor cone, launched toward Roosevelt, and the glow snaps into a burning white ring a kilometer across. Invisible waves shove the vehicles, and everyone loses a second or two at a time. The major halts, orders body armor and horses, and sends Walt "Coyote" Murphy back with his illegal RPG and two Guardsmen to destroy the substation, at Kurt's suggestion. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: The killdozer charge
docs.text: A megaphone appeal ("This is the National Guard, please, sir--") is answered with gunfire. Ned drives into the fence and the heap of cars behind it, most of Roosevelt's. The naked defenders are poor tacticians and utterly fearless. The opening Kick Some Ass rolls are 7, 7 and 5, and everyone takes harm. Kurt sweeps climbers off the killdozer with the flame light (an 11). (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Two Howards
docs.text:
Huell's Investigate a Mystery is a 12. A naked, blood-covered Andrew Howard with a gaping chest wound and a miserable face is sprinting toward them from the direction of Coyote's team. The Howard beside Huell wears the X, so Huell pulls him onto his horse and they both shoot the runner, who drops, rolls and keeps coming. (Walkers 09)

A naked copy of Huell, Skinwalker Huell, drags the original off his horse, tendrils coming from its mouth. Huell frees himself on an exact 10, after one tendril has been in his mouth long enough for him to smell his childhood bedroom. His horse tramples the copy and crushes its head. (Walkers 09)

The runner catches up, shouting that he was shot, woke under dead naked people and found no God, and that Huell should check whether the other one can eat solid food. He jumps onto the horse and forces a hand into the X Howard's mouth. Kurt puts the P90 to his head (Manipulate Someone, 9) and he backs off, the first "skinwalker" to talk or show any self-preservation. Kurt cuffs him, then asks the X Howard to open his mouth. "I don't wanna." Rita rolls an 11 to shoot Kurt in the leg, and the replica bolts. Huell rides him down (a 12). When Huell pushes fingers into his mouth, a gray tendril enters Huell's and pulls out a memory of his father, Thomas Kendrick, eating a plate of bacon. (Walkers 09)

Andre announces the swap: Rita now plays the real Andrew and Andre the replica. The real Andrew eats freeze-dried macaroni and cheese and keeps it down; Kurt uncuffs him and sends word to the major that the other Howard is not to be trusted. Huell, one harm from death, faints. Nancy the goose arrives, having followed Andrew's trail. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: The Ballroom
docs.text:
As vehicles begin to lift, the team goes in by the unguarded back door. A locked door marked "Ballroom" opens onto a shaft several hundred feet deep, with scaffolding, stairs and heavy electrical conduit. Outside it has gone quiet. White powder is falling like snow, and a silent black triangle passes over; another breaks apart as if shredded by something invisible. Kurt breathes a little powder and is dizzy (Tough, 10). (Walkers 09)

At the bottom is a vast lit cavern. Naked skinwalkers carry tanks of blood, with things writhing in them, toward a machine the size of half a dozen semi-trailers. It is built into the corpse of a glowing grub-angel like the one the team fought at Marblehead, and it holds open a twenty-foot portal onto a burned landscape under a smoky sky. It is an evacuation. The team marks their brows with Sharpie, strips, and walks in among them (Huell leads, an 11). They see the duplicate limping about and the mayor, Wilford Hiram, carrying supplies. A maimed old farmer vomits his brain into a tank and dies. In a pile of the dead's belongings Andrew finds his suit, his bag, and his pendant in a Ziploc marked "Hazardous!!!". (Walkers 09)

Then the cavern's power fails, presumably the work of Coyote's team at the substation. The portal spasms, something screams in an unknown language, and the crowd rushes it. Kurt throws grenades into the crowd and through the opening. Huell (a 10) lands one deep in the machinery and the portal winks out, stranding fifty or sixty skinwalkers in the dark. The flame light fires its last charges and melts. (Walkers 09)

The duplicate attacks: "You trapped us here." Return fire cannot hurt the real Andrew, who shoots his copy in the back, and the pilot wriggles out of its mouth and scurries away. The ceiling starts to come down. Huell (a 14) leads the sprint up the stairs. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Cleanup
docs.text: Everyone outside is unconscious. Black craft swoop overhead, the killdozer hangs in a tree, and the community center slides into a sinkhole. Dozens of people in hazmat suits (hazmat cleanup teams) are clearing bodies. Andrew takes a few dozen blurry Polaroids. Kurt commandeers a Humvee from a panicking medic ("I'm the chain of command. We're moving.") and drives off, still naked. At the wrecked substation they right Coyote's overturned APC and find him and the Guardsmen alive. The APC's radio now reaches Salt Lake City, and Kurt puts on record that a cover-up they did not cause is under way. They collect McManley and his interns from the police station and drive for a hospital. On the radio, Ross Perot has won the election. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Cold open and framing
docs.text: Andre first recaps the previous session, Walkers 08.5, which was never recorded. The cold open is a high shot of the community center, with hundreds of cars piled inside its fence and armed, mostly naked townspeople hauling supplies. It pans down to a wet, sullen, naked Huell beside an ice cream van and a bulldozer, eating Twizzlers. Cut to credits. Andre notes that an earlier cold open showed this Huell's face rising from a vat. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Revelations
docs.text:
• The Andrew with the team was a copy. The original died, came back changed, and is now fast and close to bulletproof. (Walkers 09)
  • Skinwalker tendrils read memories. (Walkers 09)
  • The cavern under the ranch held a portal machine built into a dead angel like Marblehead's. The portal resembles the one in Georgia but opens somewhere else. (Walkers 09)
  • The skinwalkers were leaving, carrying their pilots in tanks of blood to a burned world. (Walkers 09)
  • A third party with black aircraft, hazmat crews and a sedating powder cleans up afterwards. (Walkers 09)
  • Perot is president-elect. See Alternate history. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Table notes
docs.text:
• Huell twice holds a gun on Andrew for an identity test about cigar-shaped craft, and Rita reads real UFO sightings aloud. (Walkers 09)
  • Zack, after the memory probe: "I'm getting Ratatouille'd." (Walkers 09)
  • Zack's dice run hot, with several 12s and a 14. See Game mechanics. (Walkers 09)
  • The party infiltrates the cavern naked, and Kurt hands Andrew a pair of bloody underwear. Andre: "It's an erotically charged campaign." (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Continuity
docs.text:
Unrecorded session

The horses, the National Guard, the Sharpie X marks and the cleared police station all come from Walkers 08.5, a session that was played but never recorded. It is known only from Andre's recap at the start of this episode and from remarks made during it.

  • The swap closes the storyline begun in Walkers 07, where the real Andrew fell in the gym and the replica took his place, and continued through Walkers 08, whose closing scene showed the real Andrew reviving in the morgue. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08)
  • The naked Huell of the cold open is the copy whose face rose from a tank in the cold open of Walkers 07, grown after the bite in Walkers 06. (Walkers 06, Walkers 07)
  • The white ring is the one seen on the security footage of Andrew's levitation; the car heap answers the stolen cars of Walkers 08; the National Guard was put on standby in Walkers 06. (Walkers 06, Walkers 08)
  • Shelly Wilmarth's exhumation, the reason the team came to Utah, is not mentioned in the finale. (Walkers 09)
  • The next arc, The Roulet Estate, follows. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Radford, Virginia

docs.title: Abe's radio
docs.text:
Abe's radio is a small receive-only AM/FM Circuit City radio on the windowsill of Abelforth Whateley's preserved bedroom, tuned to the same late-night station as the Pay n' Stay clerk's Art Bell show.

Type Item (consumer electronics) Aliases Circuit City radio; the AM/FM radio Holder Left in place at the Whateley house First appearance Radford Horror 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The radio is a small, receive-only AM/FM set from Circuit City with dead batteries, sitting on the sill of Abe's room. The room has been left more or less as it was since Abe vanished three years earlier, with shuttle posters, a UFO painting and shelves of space books (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: It can only receive and cannot transmit. With AA batteries borrowed from his walkie-talkie, the Biz plays it and finds it tuned to the same station that the Pay n' Stay clerk listens to, which carries Art Bell later at night. He notes the frequency and puts the original batteries back (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Pay n' Stay link. In Radford Horror 01 the clerk, Rutherford, has UFO posters, an abduction book and Art Bell playing on the radio (Radford Horror 01). In Radford Horror 02, Abe's father, Yobiah, says Abe talked to "that weirdo down at the Pay n' Stay" and wanted Usenet; he calls Usenet "probably perverts." Together with the radio, this points to Abe having shared his UFO interest with the motel clerk (Radford Horror 02).
  • What the team concludes. After finding about $130 hidden in a hollowed-out copy of Where the Sidewalk Ends, the Biz briefs Andrew on the money, the radio and the radio station. Andrew concludes that Abe's robbery was probably not for money. The gear Abe took in the robbery (lightweight modems, a cellular phone and other portable items) was communications equipment (Radford Horror 02).
  • Open thread. The Biz writes down the frequency, but it is never stated aloud, and the radio does not come up again in later episodes.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The Biz returns the batteries to his walkie-talkie, leaving the radio as he found it (Radford Horror 02).
  • Art Bell and Usenet are among the early-1990s period references in Radford Horror 02.

docs.title: The Agents' Car
docs.text:
The Agents' Car is the vehicle in which Diane drove the task force to Rhode Island; it loses its battery, is stolen by the Roulet Intruder, and is eventually recovered at a pharmacy parking lot.

Type Item (vehicle) Aliases stolen car; car and car phone Holder The task force, then the Roulet Intruder First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The car carries a car phone and a marked-up map of the area. Diane slept in the back seat under a blanket, and the car is littered with the packages of the Corn Nuts she was made to stop for on the drive (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Roulet Estate 01. The hungover agents find the car in the driveway of the Roulet House. Andrew first mistakes the blanketed shape in the back seat for a body, but it is Diane. The car will not start and the phone does not work. During the sniper's attack a car window is shot out. Afterward the agents push the car closer to the house, and when they raise the hood they find the battery missing (Roulet Estate 01).

Roulet Estate 02. While the agents are in the basement, an engine starts outside. They reach the front door in time to see a grey alien driving their car around the corner of the driveway. The monk sprints after it shouting "Pawtucket!" and gives up after about a hundred feet. The players assume the thief put the battery back; the episodes never explain why he removed it. Later a local officer asks for a description of the shooter and the car so that an APB can go out (Roulet Estate 02).

Roulet Estate 03. The episode opens with a cold open shot from the back seat as the gunman, in a grey alien head and holding a 9mm pistol, drives the car through slush, humming along to "Radar Love" with the fuel gauge in the red. After the agents learn from a young officer that it has been spotted, they find it parked in the lot of a Brooks pharmacy beside a squad car. The gunman's shots into the lot hit the tires of the police car the agents push toward cover; Kurt pries a flat tire off its rim, douses it with vodka from the Biz's flask and sets it alight, adding a bag of stale donuts from the squad car, to make a smoke screen (Roulet Estate 03).

Type Item (evidence) Aliases VHS; obituary Holder Andrew Howard First appearance Walkers 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Alberta arrives at Andrew's apartment in Washington, D.C. holding a big box of documents and tapes, having eaten nothing but corn nuts for three days on the road. She shows him her mother Shelly Wilmarth's yearbook photo, a family photo from a big reunion five or six years earlier, an obituary clipping, and a VHS copy of local news footage of a protest about the community center (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The box is evidence rather than anything paranormal in itself. The obituary says Shelly died in the winter of 1990, and Alberta says she died two years earlier, of a heart attack while out with the cattle on the family ranch. Yet the tape, paused just before a cut, seems to show her alive. Alberta also says the tenant of the ranch (the "space guy", later identified as Robert Bigelow) has seen Shelly walking around the edges of the property at night. In her pitch Andre (as Alberta) insists that "she's not a ghost" and "She's just alive again." (Walkers 01)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The pitch. Rita (as Andrew) rules out a secret twin, since Alberta has only brothers, and says doppelgangers copy children rather than older women; then, hearing that Shelly died alone, he puts "doppelganger" back on the list and delivers a long lecture. Alberta describes the ranch as plagued by boiled cattle, missing pets, UFO lights and Navy radiation investigators, and leaves (Walkers 01). Andrew heats her some leftover chicken and noodles.

Follow-up. Big Bill tells Andrew the task force is welcome to look into it and that the FBI will pay for the plane tickets, and the team flies to Utah. In a recap for the Biz's player, Walkers 03 restates that the client said her mother had died on the ranch and then showed up in TV coverage of a protest in town. The team's goal becomes the exhumation. In Walkers 05 Rita asks when Shelly died, and Andre answers about two months ago, which makes the TV appearance a few weeks old and possibly part of an escalation. That disagrees with Alberta's two years in Walkers 01.

Where the footage matters. The tape shows the protest outside the community center, the same project that Maggie later says was built on bulldozed Pueblo ruins despite a protest (Walkers 03).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 01
  • Walkers 03 (recap of its premise)
  • Walkers 05 (the timeline of the mother's death)

docs.title: Foam-Latex Alien Mask
docs.text:
The Foam-Latex Alien Mask is the grey-alien prosthetic head, with huge black eyes and an oversized skull, worn by the Brooks pharmacy gunman, whose unmasking shows the "alien" to be a human in costume.

Type Item (costume) Aliases mask; prosthetic Holder The pharmacy gunman, then the police First appearance Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The mask is a foam-latex head with huge oval black eyes and an oversized cranium, worn over the head and ending in a seam at the neck. Together with the gunman's spindly build and long fingers it makes him pass for a classic grey (Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
During the Brooks pharmacy siege, the Biz sees the gunman from the drop ceiling with large oval black eyes, an unnaturally large head and a naked, tattooed body. After Huell tackles him, Kurt ties his hands with his own underwear and sees a seam around his neck where the mask ends (Roulet Estate 03).

Police tear the mask off rather than removing it carefully. Underneath is a skinny man with herpes blisters around his mouth and meth-head hair. Andrew, an avowed believer in Greys, kicks over a card display stand in anger. Dante (as Kurt) says, "Fuck! I fucking knew a Grey wouldn't be circumcised." The Biz had already noticed from the ceiling that the gunman was circumcised and tattooed (Roulet Estate 03).

The earlier "alien" at the Roulet House was seen only briefly, and the episodes never say outright that it wore this mask. The players treat the pharmacy gunman as the same person, on the strength of the shared beta blockers.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Amanda's diary
docs.text:
Amanda's diary is the diary of Amanda Lucky, found in her bedroom with every page removed, a fact her parents did not know.

Type Item (diary) Aliases the gutted diary Holder Last seen in Amanda's bedroom at the Lucky house; the missing pages are unaccounted for First appearance Radford Horror 01 Appearances Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 05

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The diary is described only as a shell: its cover remains but all its pages have been removed (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The diary has no supernatural properties. It matters as a clue that Amanda, or someone else, took pains to remove her own record.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Discovery. In the Lucky house, Andrew (Investigate a Mystery, 9 with a +1) finds the diary with its pages removed. Alongside it, Kurt finds a hollow bedpost holding Xanax and Vicodin prescribed to Amanda by Dr. Lori (see Amanda's prescriptions) and a loosened drainpipe above the window. The team deduces that she left voluntarily, climbing up onto the roof (Radford Horror 01).
  • The parents. Before leaving, Kurt asks Amanda's parents whether anything is missing. They say no money or toothbrush is gone, and they are surprised to hear the diary has been vandalized, since they knew she used it (Radford Horror 01).
  • Phoebe's diary. In Radford Horror 05, Kurt searches Phoebe Augustine's room and skims her diary. It is a separate, intact diary; it tells him that Amanda was seeing someone besides Dean Lawson and that the diary's writer did not like Dean (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: • Who removed the pages, and why.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 01
  • Radford Horror 05 (Phoebe's diary)

docs.title: Amanda's prescriptions
docs.text:
Amanda's prescriptions are the hidden stash of Xanax and opioid pills found in a hollow bedpost in Amanda Lucky's bedroom, labeled with Dr. Lawrence Lori's name, whose Vicodin record was later found altered in the pharmacy computer, with its paper copy missing.

Type Item (medication, evidence) Aliases pill stash; Vicodin and Xanax bottles; Amanda's prescription bottles Holder Found in the Lucky house; bagged as evidence and shared with Sheriff Roosevelt First appearance Radford Horror 01 Appearances Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 05

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In the pink Lisa Frank bedroom, a hollow bedpost on the four-poster bed holds bottles of Xanax and an opioid, labeled with Amanda's name and with Dr. Lawrence Lori as prescriber (Radford Horror 01). Kurt finds them with an Investigate a Mystery roll of 13 and shares the pills with Sheriff Roosevelt, asking him to dust the trellis and roof (Radford Horror 01).

In Radford Horror 01 Andre names the opioid as oxycodone. During Radford Horror 02 the table works out that oxycodone was not yet on the market in this era, and Andre revises it: "it was Vicodin then." From that point the bottles are Vicodin, and the pharmacy record concerns Vicodin (Radford Horror 01; Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• Xanax. Prescribed to Amanda for about three years for anxiety and severe depressive tendencies, according to Lori (Radford Horror 02). His files show the dose was later raised without explanation (Radford Horror 05).
  • Vicodin. Lori flatly denies prescribing it and suggests forgery or a pharmacy error (Radford Horror 02).
  • Autopsy. Amanda's toxicology shows trace Xanax and a lot of opiates, enough to chemically sedate a person. The team's theory is that she was drugged and held, and could walk only because of old tolerance, so other missing people may be held the same way (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Discovery. Amanda's parents believed Lori had prescribed nothing; they say he helped with her grades. The stash is the first lead to Lori (Radford Horror 01).
  • Lori's side. In his office, Lori says he prescribed only Xanax, refuses to elaborate without consent or a deposition, offers prescription receipts, and under pressure names Dean Lawson as drug-involved (Radford Horror 02). See Dr. Lori's office.
  • The pharmacy. The Radford pharmacy has a computer record of Vicodin for Amanda under Lori, entered about a year earlier and started about four months after the Xanax. Prescriptions are phoned in, logged on paper, then entered in the computer, and anyone with the password can alter the record. The pharmacist finds that the paper original is missing, "a big problem" (Radford Horror 02). The pharmacist adds that the Vicodin prescriptions he fills, apparently all from Lori, mostly go to 17- and 18-year-olds.
  • Photos of the patient files. The Biz photographs Lori's files for Amanda; Kurt later develops them. They show Xanax prescribed with a stated reason, doses raised without explanation, extra appointments that taper into no-shows, and no mention of opiates. The Biz had also stolen a prescription pad from Lori's office (Radford Horror 05). See Dr. Lori's patient files.
  • Theories. After learning that Derek Augustine is a pharmacist who filled Lori's opioid prescriptions for Amanda, a couple of times assuming wisdom teeth, Kurt suspects an affair (drugs in exchange for sex), and Andrew proposes that Lori and the pharmacist were partners who fell out; the missing item was Lori's hard-copy validation. Augustine claims ignorance of the "record error" (Radford Horror 05). Lori's side is that he never wrote the script.
  • Resolution. In Radford Horror 08 the sheriff says Lori and Augustine confessed to abusing Amanda and are going to prison, which would account for the drugs in the official account. The team does not argue (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Who altered the pharmacy record and removed the paper log.
  • Whether Lori wrote the Vicodin prescriptions.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 01
  • Radford Horror 02
  • Radford Horror 05

docs.title: Andrew's pendant
docs.text:
Andrew's pendant is the protective religious necklace worn by Andrew Howard, a small metal piece that absorbs harm and repels attackers, and which he never takes off.

Type Item (protective device) Aliases Force field; protective medallion; Andrew's necklace; religious pendant Holder Andrew Howard Origin A gift from Andrew's mother "and the guy" (Rita, Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The table uses several names for the object, depending on who is speaking: "pendant" and "force field" in Walkers 04 and 05, "protective thing" and "little medallion" in Walkers 07, and "religious pendant" in Walkers 09. All of them refer to the same small metal necklace, which Andrew never takes off ("I never take that off", Rita, Walkers 05).

In Walkers 09, searching for it, Rita says she wants "the pendant that my mom and the guy gave me". The episodes never say who "the guy" is. Andrew's mother belongs to his church, the Aetherius Society, but the pendant is never tied to it explicitly.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• Kinetic protection. In Walkers 04 Andre rules that the pendant "technically" protects Andrew from kinetic damage, and describes him gently levitating a tenth of a millimeter above the Jeep seat, floating a little over every bump (Walkers 04).
  • Absorbs falls. In Walkers 05 a hatch he is prying open bends sharply upward and he hits the pavement, but Andre says he takes no harm "because you're force field". Later in the episode he falls from the ceiling onto his shoulder with the same result, and wakes furious that he "almost got abducted" (Walkers 05).
  • Repels the goose. When Nancy the goose drops onto Andrew's head from above a doorway, Andre rules that his force field repulses her first strike. She then mauls him anyway once he is on his back, and Kurt pries her off with the stilts (Walkers 04).
  • Negates harm. In Roulet Estate 01 Rita asks whether the pendant "did pendant things" when Andrew was shot in the face, and Andre confirms it did. She explains that Andrew can negate 2 harm without the pendant and 3 with it: "I have two different things that let me negate one harm" (Roulet Estate 01).

The source of the effect is never explained.

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
The pendant first shows its effect in Walkers 04, where it keeps Nancy from landing her first attack (Walkers 04). In Walkers 05 it saves Andrew from two falls (Walkers 05). In Walkers 07 he dresses in his FBI outfit and takes his sidearm, "your little medallion" and his other gear before driving to Ballard High School (Walkers 07). In the gym he is replaced by a duplicate (see Andrew Howard (duplicate)).

In Walkers 09 the real Andrew wants his things back; Andre notes that the other Andrew had neither the bag nor the pendant. At the pile of stolen possessions near the portal, Rita rolls Sharp and Andrew finds a ruined suit, a fanny pack and a little necklace inside a Ziploc bag labeled "Hazardous!!!" with several exclamation points. Rita says she mostly wants the "religious pendant" back because it was "harder to replace" (Walkers 09). See also Andrew's satchel.

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text: Andrew wears it through the Roulet case, and it is part of the table's accounting of how he survives being shot (Roulet Estate 01). See Andrew's Condition.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 04
  • Walkers 05
  • Walkers 07
  • Walkers 09
  • Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Andrew's satchel
docs.text:
Andrew's satchel is the beat-up leather bag carried by Andrew Howard, which holds all of his possessions and, as the campaign goes on, visibly more than it should.

Type Item (magical storage) Aliases Magic bag; the bag of many wonders; the magic satchel; fanny pack, man purse and nutbag (table jokes); Andrew's bag; hammerspace pocket Holder Andrew Howard First appearance Radford Horror 07

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The satchel is a 20-inch leather bag (Appalachia 09). In Radford Horrors 01, Rita corrects Andre's repeated "fanny pack" with "it's a leather satchel", and the table runs through "man purse", "fanny purse" and Dante's "nutbag" before Rita settles on "technically the bag of many wonders" (Radford Horrors 01). Andre himself still calls it a fanny pack in Appalachia 09 and Walkers 07. The Walkers in Skin appearances are also covered on What I Need When I Need It bag.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The bag is the expression of Andrew's playbook ability, "What I Need When I Need It". As Rita explains it in Walkers 07, Andrew can retrieve any small, one-handed object that he owns or could feasibly own from a magical space that nobody else can reach, with no roll, as long as he reaches into the bag and believes he has the item there; Andre allows it (Walkers 07). In Appalachia 07 Rita adds that Howard himself does not know the bag is magic. He only knows that he leaves things in it and forgets them, which prompts a table joke that "Howard basically has magical dementia" (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text: In Radford Horror 07, before the trip to the church, Rita notes that Andrew takes his satchel of the things he normally wanders around with, and "also the satchel is the thing he can pull anything he owns out of". He packs some of the team's cash in it, and offers it as extra room for the team's supplies. In the church fight he digs through it for a hammer and swings it at the creature (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: In Appalachia 07 Andrew finds a quarter for a payphone by rooting through the satchel instead of his pockets (Appalachia 07). In Appalachia 09, in the Dahlonega mines, the team finds bear suits, shotguns, pepper spray, air horns and goalie masks in a room of the mines; Andrew packs as much of it as will fit in his bag, and later fits about six gold bars in it (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text: In Walkers 01 Andrew digs through his satchel in the Oval Office waiting room to give his hands something to do and finds a handful of Yeti fur he forgot to turn in; Dante notes that it should not have made it past White House security, but "it's a magic bag" (Walkers 01). In Walkers 07 Andrew packs his camera, pepper spray, pistol and "little satchel of odds and ends" for a date. In the Ballard High School gym he pulls a live grenade from it, believing it came from Kurt or the Biz (Walkers 07). Later in the same episode, when Dante asks about claymores, Andre says the only reason Andrew had one was his "bullshit hammerspace pocket" (Walkers 07). See Claymore mine.

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text: In Radford Horrors 04, camping in the woods, Rita wonders how long it will take Daniel Webster to notice that something is wrong with the bag. Andre has Ezra roll Sharp, and on a 12 Webster pieces together that a winter hat, fire-starting gear, a flashlight, blood bags, a camera, evidence bags, a walkie-talkie and a blank VHS tape have all come out of a bag that cannot hold them. He also connects this to Andrew's casual superhuman strength and to the fact that he keeps drinking blood. Webster decides not to confront him (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 07
  • Appalachia 07, Appalachia 09
  • Walkers 01, Walkers 07
  • Radford Horrors 04
  • Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Anonymous note
docs.text:
The anonymous note, also called the "angels" note, is an unsigned message left in Andrew Howard's bed in Ballard that lures him alone to the high school gym at 1 a.m. (Walkers 06)

Type Item (written message) Aliases the "angels" note Author Never identified Holder Andrew Howard First appearance Walkers 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Andre reads the note aloud to the table in Walkers 06: "Something bad is happening in this town. Some of your friends aren't who you think. I know you aren't one of them; you have angels. I have a list of them. I've seen things. I can show it to you. Come to the school gym at 1 a.m. The lock is taped over so the kids can weed in there. Don't bring the others. I won't come in if you bring the others." (Walkers 06)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Walkers 06 Andrew shows the note to the team. Kurt and Huell both deny writing it, and Huell, who has just come back from a meeting in Ballard where nobody turned up, offers Andrew the P90. Andrew declines it. Rita's Andrew insists that angels are real but not understood, "something else that we call angels because we don't really comprehend what their physical bodies are," while Ezra's Biz cannot bear to hear that they are not. Andrew decides to go. Kurt suggests the team drive him part of the way and wait within earshot, and Andrew agrees to walk the last stretch. (Walkers 06)

In Walkers 07 Andrew checks his wallet and keys, takes his camera, pepper spray, pistol, satchel and medallion, and goes to Ballard High School with Huell Kendrick parked a few blocks away as a "chaperone." Andre sends the other players out of the scene. A line of yellow light shows under the gym door and the latch is taped over, as the note promised. Inside, Andrew finds no informant. Two horses standing on their hind legs flank the door, and a man sitting on a stool turns out to be Andrew Howard himself. Armed townspeople file in behind the double, who says "We can do this the easy way or the hard way." Andrew guesses at once that they intend to replace him. (Walkers 07)

The note thus worked as a trap, but no episode says who wrote it. When Andrew returns to the team, the Walkers 07 recap simply lists it among the earlier events. (Walkers 07)

Table talk

Rita played the real Andrew through the gym scene in Walkers 07. When the scene ends, Andre has the duplicate take Andrew's place, and Rita plays the duplicate from the team's return onward, without the other players knowing. The genuine Andrew is not seen again until the end of Walkers 08, when Andre cuts to him waking at the bottom of the morgue pile.

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text:
• Who wrote the note, and whether the "list" it mentions ever existed.
  • Whether the "angels" line was bait invented by the double's faction or refers to something real about Andrew; no later episode picks it up.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 06
  • Walkers 07

docs.title: Anti-worm agent canister
docs.text:
The anti-worm agent canister is a half-empty metal spray canister of liquid poison that the radio contact left on the freeway outside Marblehead, which the team handed to the National Guard as a "worm cure".

Type Item Aliases worm cure Holder Handed to the National Guard, who sent it to a chemist First appearance Summer Service 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A large metal spray canister full of liquid, found sitting in the middle of the freeway after the creature died. The radio contact had promised to "leave you guys a little present on the road". It felt about half empty. The label read VX (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The contact described the agent as "just a poison" for the worms, developed from samples recovered after his advanced team was destroyed. He proposed dumping some of it in the ocean to deal with contaminated fish. Kurt suggested crop-dusting it after the storm, and the contact said it would not kill anything else, "probably". He also said plainly that his side would have to kill all the infected townspeople, and that it was better to do so once they no longer had special support. When Kurt asked whether it was a treatment or only a poison, the contact answered only that they had developed a toxic agent for the worms (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: History
docs.text: At the Marblehead checkpoint Kurt told a National Guard lieutenant that the canister was a worm cure that should kill the worms but not human tissue, and offered it for the Guard to disperse. The lieutenant had it taken to the chemist. Kurt said the team had been intercepting a splinter group of bioterrorists. After Andrew's call to Big Bill, the lieutenant questioned the team about the canister. Rita and Dante said it was an antidote found in their investigation and that its maker was unclear, though Andrew guessed the terrorists. The lieutenant said the Guard was already distributing deworming medicine and asked how the cure related to the synthetic nerve agent, which the team could not yet explain. The team's own treatment had been ivermectin (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 06

docs.title: Atolean Paranatural Index
docs.text:
The Atolean Paranatural Index is a ranking of places by UFO and cryptid sightings and disappearances per capita, which turned up in the background reading for the Paranatural Incident Task Force and marks Radford, Virginia as a hotspot.

Type Item (document, ranking) Holder The task force, as part of the Radford case file First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The index appears in a single episode. It looks at UFO and cryptid sightings per capita and disappearances per capita, and it includes a list of hotspot cities. The first case file, delivered to the barbershop headquarters in D.C. by an FBI courier, explains that the index came up during the background reading for the task force, that Radford is on the hotspot list, and that the report of Amanda Lucky's disappearance, with an artist's sketch of the spaceman a four-year-old described, triggered the guidelines the president had set out for the task force (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
With the file in hand, the team has about two hours before the four-hour, sixteen-minute drive to Radford, and is told to get a motel there (Radford Horror 01).

Local color supports the ranking. On arrival, a "Population 16,000" sign greets the team, and the Pay n' Stay clerk warns of missing people, lights in the sky and "people walking around who haven't even been born." He adds that his father thought the town was cursed because the local armory made guncotton for the atom bomb (Radford Horror 01). See Radford Arsenal.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The episodes never explain who compiles the index, what "Atolean" refers to, or whether other places in the campaign appear on it.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Attic Polaroids
docs.text:
The Attic Polaroids are a collection of instant photographs of sleeping people pinned to the walls of the hidden attic lair in the Roulet House.

Type Item (photographs) Aliases Polaroids of sleeping victims Location Hidden Attic Lair, Roulet House First appearance Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A bundle of Polaroids, mostly of people sleeping, is stuck up on the walls of the lair. Many appear to show the Roulets themselves; others look like older photographs of different people the agents cannot identify (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Together with a cot, cigarettes, MRE containers and a card table, the photos tell Kurt and Andrew that someone had lived in the attic for at least a year, probably without the owners' knowledge. Since every major room has a chimney, he could enter any of them, and the owners had fitted interior locks to their bedroom doors. Andrew, who had helped on FBI serial-killer investigations before joining the task force, finds the whole lair "the most serial killer-y serial killer shit" he has ever seen. Andre leaves it unclear whether the same person is also a grey alien (Roulet Estate 02).

In Roulet Estate 01 Andrew had explained that the Greys go after people who are unconscious and sleeping and give them things so that they do not remember, and the photos fit that pattern. The episodes never establish whether the Roulets' "visitations" were really the intruder drugging and watching the household (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text: Kurt and Andrew take crime-scene photos of the lair, then bag the guns, money, valuables and green slurry and lower them down the chimney. The agents never identify the people in the older photos (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Bag of Peaches
docs.text:
The Bag of Peaches is the sack of peaches found in the middle of the woods near Auraria, the only physical evidence of Willow Greengrass's disappearance, which Sheriff Burke kept in his station's evidence locker.

Type Item Aliases peach evidence; Willow's sack of peaches Holder Dahlonega Sheriff's Station evidence locker First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: An ordinary sack of peaches. Sheriff Burke pointed it out through the bars of the evidence locker and described it as "just sitting out in the middle of" the woods. He said his department had not gotten much off it that was unexpected (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Nothing unusual is established about the bag itself. It matters because of what surrounds it: peaches are tied to Auraria and the Covenant, whose members sell peach preserves and a fermented peach drink. The cold open of Appalachia 01 shows a young woman in an ankle-length dress hauling a large sack of peaches through the forest before something drags her off-screen, though the scene does not name her. The episodes do not state outright that the woman is Willow or that the sack in the locker is the one she dropped.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Appalachia 01, Sheriff Carter Burke described the case-file subjects: missing woman Willow Greengrass, missing boy Gene Cartwright and witness Edward Nick. He believed Willow had simply left the cult. He then showed the bag in the evidence locker and invited the FBI to bring its own forensics person to examine it, since his small department lacked full facilities. The team said they had a forensics man, Dr. McManley, but that it would be a while before he could help (Appalachia 01).

In Appalachia 02, Willow's sister Primenthol Greengrass told the team that the police had found the sack she was carrying in the middle of the woods, with no sign of her. In Appalachia 04 a Covenant member confirmed that the peaches had been found and said Willow "wouldn't have left those"; Elijah Ray had sent her out to scout peach orchards, and she was on her way back with samples (Appalachia 04). The episodes do not show the bag being tested.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 01
  • Appalachia 02 (mentioned)
  • Appalachia 04 (mentioned)

docs.title: Beta Blockers
docs.text:
Beta Blockers are a prescription medication that links the Roulet Intruder's attic lair to the Brooks pharmacy siege.

Type Item (medication) Holder The Roulet Intruder First appearance Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In the lair, Kurt finds a cooler holding a prescription tube with the label scraped off. He identifies the contents as beta blockers (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The agents do not learn why the occupant needed the drug. In Roulet Estate 03 the pharmacy's dispensing area has been ransacked, with pill bottles scattered across the floor. When the gunman begins to crumple as police lead him out of the squad car, Dante (as Kurt) says, "I think it needs beta blockers," citing the ones found in the attic lair. The pharmacist confirms that the man had been looking for them in the back and could not find the supply before the situation escalated. Police have a pharmacist fetch some so that the prisoner does not die in the squad car (Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: History
docs.text: The beta blockers and the raid on the Brooks pharmacy are the main evidence connecting the masked man to the person who lived in the hidden attic lair. The episodes do not say why he depended on the drug or whether it was prescribed to him (Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Roulet Estate 02
  • Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Betsy
docs.text:
Betsy is the elderly, putt-putting squad car that Roosevelt's police department lends the task force after their rental van is destroyed, and which becomes the team's vehicle for the rest of the Ballard case. (Walkers 04)

Type Item (vehicle) Aliases loaner squad car; the PCs' old car Holder The task force (on loan from the Roosevelt Police Department) First appearance Walkers 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Betsy is an old, classic-looking car done up as a police car. The officer who brings it says "She's been with the department a long time" and that it does not matter if she gets dirty. It makes cartoon putt-putt noises, seats about five and has a trunk. No make or model is given. (Walkers 04, Walkers 08) In Walkers 08 the table decides that Betsy is an old retired vehicle that the town uses for school plays. (Walkers 08)

The trunk holds musical-theater costumes, which Roosevelt's officers identify as costumes from a school production of Cats, and a pair of stilts. (Walkers 04) The car smells of the costumes and, in Rita's phrase, "reeks of high school sadness." (Walkers 05) In Walkers 08 Zack asks to make it canon that Betsy has a novelty horn. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Loan. After the team's Plymouth Voyager is found crushed on the road, Officer Hernandez of the Roosevelt Police Department accepts Andrew Howard's FBI identification, waives the tickets and offers Betsy ("We can give you Betsy"). After about an hour he delivers it, while five officers strain to lever the wreck off the road. The team drives back to Ballard in Betsy. (Walkers 04)

Stilts. Kurt Larson claims the stilts in the trunk as replacements for his Vietnam-era pair, which were lost with the Voyager. Back at the ranch he uses them to open the door and to pry the goose Nancy off Howard's head. (Walkers 04)

Chained down. In Walkers 05 the party drives Betsy to Roosevelt, where an officer runs up and asks if they are the ones assigned to Betsy. That night Dante's Kurt proposes chaining Betsy to the ground. The team pounds four posts and chains the car to them, which takes a couple of hours in the cold, so that the ranch cameras will have something to record. By morning the house has shifted a few inches and is noticeably warm, but Betsy is fine and not warm, which Kurt reads as meaning it was probably not targeted. (Walkers 05) This is tied to the vanishing car incident.

Cemetery trip. In Walkers 06 the ground-penetrating radar is loaded into Betsy for the trip to the cemetery. Later, when a rattling noise comes from outside, Rita's Andrew worries that someone is stealing Betsy; it is the goose. (Walkers 06)

Gym night. In Walkers 07 Huell drives Andrew to the high school in Betsy, and afterward Huell carries a dead coyote back and puts it in the trunk. (Walkers 07)

Ballard breakout. In Walkers 08, with the rental gone, the team piles into Betsy to find a man whose Suburban lies on its side across the road into Ballard. Because Betsy seats only about five, the team splits between Betsy and a police cruiser when it needs to carry bodies. Rita objects to putting a body in the car: "Betsy's already been embarrassed enough being stuffed full of Cats costumes." Betsy is the vehicle that approaches strangers, so as not to show them the bodies. In the firefight at the ambush, Rita's Andrew rolls a 3, panics and shatters one of Betsy's windows. Kurt then rams two fleeing men from behind with Betsy at about 20 miles an hour, knocking them into a wrought-iron gate. (Walkers 08)

Convoy. In Walkers 09 Betsy is among the vehicles of the National Guard convoy, which includes Humvees, APCs, an armored bulldozer, a police car and "one elderly vehicle, Betsy," that the major takes off-road around the arcing substation. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• In Walkers 07 Zack's Huell, who cannot remember the goose's name, insists on calling her "Betsy," a joke Zack calls "dumb"; the goose is Nancy. (Walkers 07)
  • Kurt's submachine gun is also called "Bessie" (Kurt's P90).
  • Ezra's Biz remarks in Walkers 04 that every car he has driven in Utah has been turned into a pancake. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Bigelow's recordings
docs.text:
Bigelow's recordings are the tape reels, VHS tapes and hard drives on which Robert Bigelow's staff log instrument data and camera footage from the Sherman Ranch, including the footage of the car lifting and the white ring. All of them were stolen in a single night. (Walkers 07)

Type Item (data records) Aliases tape reels; sky camera video; camera footage tape; stolen recordings and drives Holder Bigelow's research operation (until stolen) First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Instrument reels. In Walkers 02 Bigelow's team says it records everything onto "big tape reels." The data show many unexplained heat signatures and electromagnetic or electrical events, plus the exploded sheep, all confined to the ranch and about half a mile around, with nothing in town. Bigelow dismisses the nearby substation as unrelated and offers the party the data sets. (Walkers 02)

Camera footage. The big house has a bank of monitors fed by cameras across the ranch. The guest house is not covered, though one camera on the big house catches part of it. (Walkers 04) The ranch also has a visible-spectrum sky camera and a thermal camera. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• The lifted car. In Walkers 04 a staffer at the big house cues up a cassette of the night the team's rental vanished. A slightly different patch of grey seems to rise beside the house, but it would not convince anyone who was not already looking. There is no radar return, though some of the electromagnetic meters "went nuts." This is the vanishing car incident; see also Plymouth Voyager. (Walkers 04)
  • The white ring. In Walkers 05 a white light wakes Bigelow, and the party finds his staff reviewing the sky camera's VHS tape in the big house. In motion it shows a very bright white ring with a slightly purple glow, oscillating and vibrating for a few seconds before dissipating. The thermal feed was whited out, and most of the ranch's electronics broke. Bigelow calls it one of the most clear-cut events they have had, with "a definite nonlinear trajectory" on many graphs, and says "We may be on the verge of making contact." He reads the ring in Black Sun terms. Kurt persuades him to set up a big ring of cameras around the party's house. (Walkers 05) See the white ring.
  • Camera test. The party chains Betsy down in front of the ranch's cameras so that the footage will have something to show. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Walkers 07, Bigelow rages that somebody "broke in and stole all our hard drives, all our tapes, all of our recordings, and three of my fucking employees." The barn has been cleared out as well, and whoever did it had keys to the whole place. The party notes that the intruder who broke into their own house also had a key. Bigelow declares "protocol blue" and has his remaining security staff arm up. (Walkers 07)

No episode says who took the recordings or what became of them. The theft happens on the same night the skinwalker faction replaces Andrew Howard, but the connection is never stated; see skinwalkers.

docs.title: The Biz's Buick Regal
docs.text:
The Biz's Buick Regal is the 1986 Buick that Dick "The Biz" Baxter drives in The Summer Service, first as the carrier of a severed arm and later as a roof-cut mount for the Davy Crockett.

Type Item (vehicle) Aliases 1986 Buick Regal; the Biz's car; mobile artillery; modified vehicle Holder The Biz (owner) First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: An ordinary mid-80s sedan with a long, flat trunk. The Biz has money problems and car payments, and he jokes about letting the car be repossessed (Summer Service 01). The make and model are not given until Summer Service 04, when Ezra settles on a 1986 Buick Regal after Andre suggests an '89 and a joke about a Pinto (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: In Summer Service 04 the team modifies it into an improvised fighting vehicle. Two legs of the Davy Crockett tripod sit on the trunk and a third goes through a hole cut in the roof. The roof hole later leaks, leaving several inches of water on the floor in the storm (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• The arm's hearse. After the team finds the severed arm on the beach, it is bagged and sealed in a cooler with ice and put in the Biz's trunk with the windows down. The smell soaks into the car, and the repossession jokes become a running gag (Summer Service 01).
  • Mobile artillery. When Carter's crate arrives at the post office, Kurt asks whether the Biz's car has been repossessed yet; it is still on the side of the road, and he commandeers it as an improvised fighting vehicle. The Biz tells him he is done with it. Kurt and Huell spend three to four hours mounting the weapon on it at a disused gas station on the edge of town (see Abandoned gas station). The Buick is then hidden under a tarp behind the station, while the roughly 60 lb W54 warhead goes back to the hotel (Summer Service 04).
  • The hotel siege. During the storm the team abandons the RV behind the gas station and takes back the modified car with the Davy Crockett on it. Its leaking roof soaks the floor, and the car smells terrible (Summer Service 05).
  • The finale. In Summer Service 06 the team drives a car they commandeered, and Kurt teaches them to fire the weapon from its back seat. Andre narrates that the team is glad it did not take the Biz's Buick through the flooded roads. The team's own FBI car is spotted among the infected convoy (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • When the Biz spots the FBI car in the convoy, Andre first calls it "the Lincoln" and then corrects himself, which confuses Ezra, who thought his car was a Buick. Dante remarks he is glad they took the Davy Crockett off it. Andre clarifies that the car in the convoy is the FBI car, not the Biz's, and Ezra concludes it is "not the one that had it". No episode shows how the weapon moved from the Buick to the team's other vehicles; it happened between Summer Service 05 and 06, which includes the unrecorded Summer Service 05.5.
