docs.title: Bug-out briefcase
docs.text:
The bug-out briefcase is an escape kit hidden in a heat vent under Dick "The Biz" Baxter's bed, holding cash, Swiss francs, a cheap revolver, a change of clothes and a Swiss passport in the name of "Noah Mueller."

Type Item (escape kit) Aliases Noah Mueller passport; Swiss francs; the bug-out bag Holder Dick "The Biz" Baxter; found by the team in his apartment First appearance Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Kurtis Larson finds the case with a successful Investigate a Mystery roll (11), after searching for false bottoms, loose bricks, floorboards, wallpaper and vents. The heat vent under the Biz's bed had stripped screws. Inside are (Radford Horrors 01):

  • a few hundred US dollars,
  • a much larger sum in Swiss francs,
  • a cheap revolver,
  • a change of clothes,
  • a Swiss passport with the Biz's photo under the name Noah Mueller.

The name Noah Mueller is of uncertain spelling.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The kit is not supernatural. It serves as a clue to the Biz's intentions and as a "secret identity" trope: it shows he had a Swiss alias and money ready to disappear.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Discovery. In the early part of the Radford Horrors, Andrew Howard and Huell, joined by Kurt, search the Biz's neglected apartment after he vanishes. The place has dust, cobwebs, a taped-up leather recliner, a heater running, a TV on Animal Planet, rotten fridge meat, and shelves of war memoirs, technical manuals, hard-boiled novels and Russian books. Under a loose floorboard the team finds his share of the gold, about $8,000 to $9,000 in Ziplocs, and cocaine. The Biz had also requested six months of personal leave for a "family emergency," a discount Playboy subscription began days before he vanished, and a Moby-Dick with its first pages torn out hides a cipher (see Moby-Dick book cipher) (Radford Horrors 01).
  • Kurt's reading. Dante (as Kurt) remarks, "Well, I'm guessing this is his bug-out bag. Totally normal thing to own." Kurt concludes that the Biz had other plans, meant to return, was in touch with a third party and was intercepted, since the Swiss francs were left behind. Asked whether the Biz is a double agent, Kurt answers that "there are degrees of double agent."
  • Aftermath. The Biz had in fact been taken to Russia, where he is held at the Hotel Metropol and brought before Boris Yeltsin (see Radford Horrors 01; Hotel Metropol). Kurt reads the kit as intended for Switzerland, but the episodes never confirm where the Biz meant to go.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Why the Biz needed an identity as a Swiss citizen, and who he was corresponding with via classified ads in the Washington City Paper, the Washington Informer and the Georgetown Current.
  • Whether the Biz ever recovers the kit.

docs.text: • Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Chewbacca Costume
docs.text:
The Chewbacca Costume is the expensive Chewbacca-style costume, stolen from Apollo's dry cleaners, in which an ex-military hoaxer was found executed on Frotter Comstock's land.

Type Item Aliases Bigfoot costume Owner Derek Edwards (originally) Last known holder Evidence (the body in it was examined by McManley) First appearance Appalachia 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The costume was bought for cash at Comic-Con by the amateur photographer Derek Edwards, who said it "smelled pretty strongly like fat nerd." On the corpse it was soaked in what looked like real blood. The bandolier had been removed and mud rubbed into the fur in an attempt to make it look less like Chewbacca, though Andre noted it was "pretty clearly Chewbacca" (Appalachia 06).

It was stolen from Apollo's dry cleaners about eight months before the body turned up, according to Derek (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The costume has no special properties. It worked as a convincing Bigfoot disguise from a distance, and was used with plaster-of-Paris footprint molds. Someone cleaned up the fake prints after the killing, leaving a snapped-off plaster toe and a few nice fake prints in the mud (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Discovery. Frotter Comstock reported a dead Bigfoot on his land. The team found a man in the costume at the base of a hill below Comstock's buildings, shot in the back of the head while standing, which Kurt judged to be about a .357 Magnum. Underneath were plain clothes with every tag cut out. Tattoos of an anchor on his bicep and a trident on his calf led Kurt to identify the man as a former Navy SEAL (Appalachia 06). Andrew announced the man was "capped"; the sheriff scolded him that every death, even in a Chewbacca costume, deserves gravity.

The theft. Derek, whom the team reached through the Gold Bug newspaper and met at the Spud Hut, said his costume had been stolen from the dry cleaners. The dry cleaner's owner admitted the storage-area latch had been broken for a couple of months, that several items vanished, and recognized the dead man as an out-of-town drifter he had seen hanging around (Appalachia 06). The man registered at the Motel and Suites as "John Doe"; he is later called Troy Cleaver.

Aftermath. The costume came up in Andrew's report to Big Bill: "We're not surveilling Bill Clinton. We're surveilling dead Chewbacca." (Appalachia 07)

The explanation. In Appalachia 09, the worker Clive said the conspiracy included a mercenary who melted the gold down. Kurt said he was pretty sure Jan had killed the mercenary, since a dead man in a Bigfoot costume with ex-military tattoos had been found in the forest. Clive confirmed that the dead man was the mercenary ("God damn it, he did the Bigfoot thing"). He said he did not know where the mercenary got the costume and that he had told him it was stupid because people would know it was Chewbacca. Clive added that the fake Bigfoot sightings were meant to discredit people who had seen workers that escaped, and that Jan Martense had told him the mercenary took care of the problem. See The Bigfoot Hoax. When Kurt later questioned Jan at Black Site Omaha, he said he assumed Jan had taken care of the mercenary in the woods, and Jan did not deny it (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Child's Tennis Shoe
docs.text:
The Child's Tennis Shoe is the German-looking child's shoe found at the bottom of the hidden elevator shaft beneath the Consolidated Gold Mine, the only trace of missing boy Frederick.

Type Item Aliases German shoe; Frederick's shoe Holder Handed to the search party and the sheriff's deputies First appearance Appalachia 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A single child's tennis shoe. Andre called it "German-looking" and joked that it was Deichmann brand; the players riffed on lederhosen and elf shoes. It is a different shoe from the red, white-soled one found in the field earlier, as Rita checked (Appalachia 03). See Gene's Shoe.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: None are established. It suggests that the missing German boy Frederick had been in or near the old elevator shaft.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Discovery. Following the wounded creature's streaky red blood trail, the team reached a vertical shaft with coiled cables, an old elevator with no way up. At the bottom lay the single shoe, which they took (Appalachia 03). The shaft is part of the Hidden Modern Tunnel below the Consolidated Gold Mine.

Handover. Out of the mine, Huell said bluntly, "Kid's dead, though. Here's the shoe," and a German woman from the tour group burst into tears. Kurt told the searchers there was a slim chance that, if someone had taken the boy, they had brought him to the surface by a route the team could not follow from below, and gave them the shoe (Appalachia 03).

Later. In Appalachia 04 the sheriff said the latest missing child had only one parent, who spoke almost only German, and that a translator was two days away. The shoe itself is not mentioned again. In Appalachia 09 the worker Clive was dismayed to hear that children had gone missing in the mines, but the episodes never say whether Frederick was one of the people taken by the ape-man operation.

docs.title: Church mace
docs.text:
The church mace is a canister issued to Andrew Howard by his church, which looks like a can of pepper spray but sprays a "nothing" that passes through matter, erasing or severing whatever is in its path and leaving its victims in a violent seizure.

Type Item (weapon) Aliases Andrew's pepper spray; the absence; Andrew's mace; the mace; the nothing; the void; Andrew's holy weapon; the absence beam Holder Andrew Howard Origin Given to Andrew by his church, the Aetherius Society First appearance Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 08 Andre rules that the "mace" was given to Andrew by his church, and Rita adds that it has been his self-defense weapon for years and that he has never used it before. It is a canister rather than a club, and its contents are not a chemical: Zack remarks that ordinary pepper spray "is made of stuff", while Andre says Andrew's "is void". What comes out is called "nothing" or "nothingness" (Radford Horror 08).

Andrew carries it with his usual gear, alongside his camera, pistol and satchel (Walkers 07). He treats it as ordinary pepper spray and tends to forget in the moment that it is not: "Shit, I forgot this wasn't pepper spray," Rita says in Summer Service 05 (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• Erases matter, then restores it. When the nothing passes through a body, the matter in its path vanishes, so onlookers can see sinus cavity, brain, pulsing blood vessels and cross-sections of skull. As the nothing exits the back of the skull, the face returns around it (Radford Horror 08). In Walkers 07 a man's head is erased for a fraction of a second, showing cross-sections of colors that do not belong in a human head and leaving the bits of his face that remain looking "extremely surprised" (Walkers 07).
  • Causes seizures. The men hit in the head in Radford Horror 08 and Walkers 07 both drop into a grand mal seizure once the matter returns (Radford Horror 08, Walkers 07).
  • Severs. In Summer Service 05 Andre rules it a three-harm weapon; it takes a dog's head off and passes through Kurt's hand (Summer Service 05). In Appalachia 09 it cleanly cuts off an ape-man's arm (Appalachia 09).
  • Resembles the crack in the air. When the team studies the crack in the air, Rita asks how similar it is to "my pepper spray, where it's just, like, an absence?" and Andre describes metal visible through it with a hard edge (Appalachia 09).
  • Unexplained. Nobody at the table learns how it works. In Radford Horror 08 Ezra and Dante first wonder whether the man's reaction was a side effect of his cloaking gear, and conclude only that the canister itself is strange (Radford Horror 08). In Walkers 07 Dante says that the table does not know what is going on with the pepper spray but has "seen it melt through a man" (Walkers 07).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text: After the church fight in Radford Horror 08, the team hides in the woods from men in camouflage and "volcanologist" gear. Kurt sets himself up as hidden bait under bloody leaves and kicks the searcher in the groin to bring his head down into range. Andrew, who had been planning to pepper spray him, shouts "Did you know Jesus is one of the Masters?" as a distraction, a line Rita proposes as the kind of weirdness Andrew would use, and fires the mace. The man is left convulsing; the team ties him up and takes his flashlight and a "shadow poncho" (Radford Horror 08). See Flashlight weapon.

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text: In Summer Service 05 Andrew goes for his pepper spray against the worm-ridden Doberman in Arnold Weathers' house after it has savaged Huell and Kurt, shouting "Hold it away from you!" He rolls a 6 on Kick Some Ass and then a 2 to avoid hitting Kurt, so both are caught in the spray. The nothing takes the dog's head off, but also goes through Kurt's hand, costing him about ten percent of his blood volume and three harm (Summer Service 05). The dog's head stays alive, with open eyes and a moving jaw, and the team bags it for McManley's RV; see Puddles.

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: In Appalachia 09 the team, some of them in bear suits, is pursued through the Dahlonega mines by Big Bob, a huge, fast ape-man that survives shotgun fire. It picks Huell up and holds him over its head. Rita rolls a 10 on Kick Some Ass and uses the spray's "absence" to cut off the arm holding Huell. The beam passes through, Huell drops onto Andrew for one harm, and the ape looks at its spurting stump before toppling backwards, ending the fight. Andrew pries the severed hand off Huell and keeps it as a trophy (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
Early in Walkers 07, when a monster is choking Kurt and Huell in a hallway with Andrew on its back, Rita asks whether Andrew has an angle to "pepper spray, sever the arm". The table jokes that the spray is deadlier than a gun, but Rita instead rolls Cast Out Evil and the spray is not used (Walkers 07).

Later in the episode Andrew, led into a gym by people who want to replace him, asks what "the hard way" is. The man who has been talking tries to kiss him with tendrils coming out of his throat, and Andrew sprays him in the face as he would a mugger (Kick Some Ass, 9). The man's head is erased for a moment and he drops into a seizure, but the fight goes badly for Andrew, who is kicked by a horse and shot with a shotgun (Walkers 07). See Andrew Howard (duplicate).

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text: In Radford Horrors 02, as the others plan what to tell a contact, Rita jokes that Howard, if he overheard, would say, "Oh, I guess I should warn you guys, I did bring that weird pepper spray" (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The canister goes by several names at the table. In Radford Horror 08 the players use "mace" and "pepper spray" interchangeably; in Summer Service 05 Andre calls it Andrew's "holy weapon", which the table had just re-themed on his sheet, while Rita calls it his pepper spray; and from Appalachia 09 onward the table speaks only of his pepper spray and its "absence". Its effects are the same under every name (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 09).
  • The bear-suited gang in Appalachia 09 also carries ordinary pepper spray among its gear (Appalachia 09).
  • Dante jokes in Walkers 02 that "you can't even pepper spray" geese, since they are "immune to capsaicin" (Walkers 02).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 08 (as the "mace")
  • Summer Service 05 (as the "holy weapon")
  • Appalachia 09
  • Walkers 07
  • Radford Horrors 02 (mentioned)

docs.title: Claymore Mine
docs.text:
The Claymore mine is a directional anti-personnel mine carried by Kurt Larson. He uses it to kill an ape-man and drive off the rest during the ambush on the Special Projects level beneath the Spud Hut plant.

Type Item (explosive) Aliases Claymore; "Claymores for Bigfoot" Holder Kurt Larson (played by Dante) Status Used; Kurt has room for only one First appearance Appalachia 03 (mentioned); used in Appalachia 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Kurt carries the mine on his back belt "like a fanny pack", where it takes up his single equipment slot. Rita points out that he had also wandered around with Claymores "in the last mystery". (Appalachia 08) In Appalachia 03, Kurt already jokes, "I really hate being on American soil. This is dumb. We just Claymore all the ends we couldn't clear."

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• Directional blast that kills or vaporizes creatures in front of it, with a pressure wave and fragments that can reach allies nearby.
  • Loud enough to deafen the whole team. Kurt warns them by shouting "Ear pro!" and covering his own ears.
  • Andre allowed Dante a preparedness roll to have it on hand. Dante rolled a 7, which his Sharp stat raised to a 10. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: The Special Projects ambush
docs.text:
Five ape-men attack the team. One juggles Andrew Howard while another punches Kurt's dog whistle into his throat. Once Kurt dislodges it, four of the creatures are closing on him. He produces the mine, shoves it down in front of him, jumps backward and yells "Ear pro!". The other PCs resolve their reactions first: Huell Kendrick, stunned, fails automatically; Andrew is thrown back up to the ceiling and so is above the blast; and Dick "The Biz" Baxter drops and covers his ears on military reflex. (Appalachia 08)

The mine detonates. The creature juggling Andrew becomes a mist of gore and bone fragments, and Andrew drops into the remains and bumps his head on the concrete. Huell is hit by ricocheting fragments and a pressure wave, ruptures an eardrum, and is left semi-conscious at three harm. The Biz takes one harm. Everyone is temporarily deafened, and the door frame and the wall opposite it are destroyed. Sheriff Carter Burke, who dived through the "break room" door when he saw the mine, peeks back out afterward. The surviving creatures flee into other parts of the floor. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: At the start of Appalachia 09, Andre remarks that the "break room" Jan Martense sent the party to "was never a break room. It was just a door", and that the shrapnel from the Claymore has blown the door away completely. Later, when about ten ape-men block the only exit, Zack asks whether Kurt brought a second Claymore. Andre rules that a second mine cannot fit in his equipment slot. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The tally of dead creatures varies. At the end of Appalachia 08, Andre says one is dead and at least two badly injured, though Dante counts two dead after adding a creature Zack had shot earlier. Andre's recap at the start of Appalachia 09 says the Claymore "evaporated two of the Yetis".
  • Dante argued that a Claymore and gunshots could not go unheard even four stories down, which raised the team's worry about the news crew upstairs. (Appalachia 08)
  • Kurt's line "Claymores for Bigfoot" comes in the next episode, when Dante compares them to garlic for Dracula. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 03 (mentioned)
  • Appalachia 08
  • Appalachia 09

docs.title: Communion wine
docs.text:
The communion wine is the fishy "local variety" of sacramental wine served by the Sons of Adam church in Marblehead, which turns out to be swimming with the worm parasite.

Type Item Aliases Blood of the Lamb; the wine Holder The Sons of Adam church, served at the colonial church First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: At the church service the only communion offered is wine, not wafer and wine. The priest hands over a small cup with the words "Blood of the Lamb", and the congregation nods in reply. The wine has a distinctly fishy note, and Andre likens it to the bad prison wine Kurt has had before. Asked afterward whether the church makes it, Amos Shaw answers, "It's a local variety" (Summer Service 01). The congregation takes communion three times a day (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
McManley examined a sample under a microscope in his RV lab and found it swimming with worms resembling tapeworms or nematodes. He told Andrew to find a horse doctor for ivermectin and to avoid the wine, then said he would call the CDC (Summer Service 03).

Drinkers gain vigor, muscle and hair regrowth and a youthful look. The advanced stage is a translucent, bloated pallor, as seen in the new priest (The glow). Fish in the missing scientists' journal were hollowed out by similar worms yet still alive (Summer Service 03). The worms survive in the wine, though Andre rules that vodka, heat and heavy salt hurt them (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• The service. Huell and Kurt take the wine while Andrew and the Biz stay out of the line. Huell drinks all of it and ends up with a mildly upset stomach. Kurt pretends to finish it and feels sweaty and off. Kurt's Sharp roll (7) catches a flicker of reaction from Shaw when he mentions the flavor (Summer Service 01).
  • The sample. Andrew goes back to a 7 a.m. service to obtain a sample. He holds the wine in his mouth, but his Manipulate Someone roll (6) fails, and the priest does not believe he swallowed. Outside, he spits it into an empty Crystal Pepsi bottle and delivers it to McManley (Summer Service 03).
  • Effects. Huell, Kurt and Andrew fear they are infected, and Huell's muscle and hairline change visibly. The cure, ivermectin, later removes Huell's worm strength (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 06).
  • Kitchen tests. In Summer Service 05, after Kurt notes that the worms survive being delivered in communion wine, Andre says they do not like alcohol, and Kurt wonders whether that explains why Ma Gramoire is fine (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Summer Service 01
  • Summer Service 03
  • Summer Service 05

docs.title: Covenant Peach Preserves
docs.text:
The Covenant Peach Preserves are the fermented peach jam and the hallucinogenic, fungus-laced peach drink produced by the Covenant, the religious community living in the ghost town of Auraria, Georgia.

Type Item (food, drug) Aliases Auraria peach preserves; peach liquid; Covenant peach drink; hallucinogenic peach Maker The Covenant Sold at The Smith Hotel (continental breakfast and gift shop); a stand in Auraria First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The Covenant makes two peach products. The first is an ordinary jam: ripe, slightly fermented peaches with a rich, malty flavor, good on toast. The second is a different, hallucinogenic variety, a dark liquid with whole peaches floating in it, which the team hears about as "the peach drink" and "their peach wine". (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 04) Peaches are a signature of the Covenant, and the sign at Auraria reads "Welcome to the Covenant. Try our peaches." (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• The peach drink is a ritual beverage that gives visions. Primenthol Greengrass, a former Covenant member, warns the team that "if they offer you a vision quest, don't take it," and says the peaches are not the only ingredient: they are hallucinogenic "if you grow the right funguses." (Appalachia 02)
  • The drink is made with natural yeast, which carries a risk of methanol contamination. Frotter Comstock, met near Auraria, explains that he had been helping the community with a "methanol problem with their ritual beverage". (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: The hotel breakfast
docs.text: The clerk at the Smith Hotel lists peach jam among the breakfast offerings. He says the "religious folks" of Auraria make excellent peach preserves, served with the continental breakfast and sold by the jar in the gift shop. The team finds the preserves very good, with a rich, fermented flavor. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Willow's peaches
docs.text: The only physical evidence in the disappearance of Willow Greengrass is a sack of peaches found in the woods, which Sheriff Carter Burke keeps in the evidence locker; see Bag of Peaches. The cold open shows a young woman hauling a sack of peaches through the forest before something drags her off. (Appalachia 01) In Appalachia 02 the team learns of the hallucinogenic drink from Prim. Whether it has anything to do with Willow's disappearance is never pursued.

docs.title: The baptism and the preserve stand
docs.text:
The cold open of Appalachia 04 shows a vacuum-cleaner salesman, later identified as Jeremy, being handed a jar of dark liquid with peaches floating in it by an older man with high cheekbones at a red-clay river baptism. After he drinks it, the sound muffles and the camera grows unsteady. The Covenant later offers to get the team into a baptism "this evening". The team does not attend. (Appalachia 04)

In Auraria the team sees many stills, people frantically canning in hot tents, and a stand selling preserves and quilts. The elders explain that the orchard deal and the preserve sales are meant to fund a lawyer against the land dispute. Willow had been sent by Elijah Ray to scout peach orchards. The baptism rite combines the peach liquid, Latin chanting and immersion in red clay; see Covenant Beliefs. (Appalachia 04)

Back at the sheriff's office, the players note that the hallucinogenic product has only been mentioned in passing, by Willow's sister. Andre confirms there are two preserves: the ordinary jam the team has eaten, and "another thing". (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• During the visit to Auraria, a player muses that the huge attacker might be "the clay god". (Appalachia 04)
  • Dante jokes that the cold open of Appalachia 04 plays like a scary Smucker's ad. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Cryptogram Secret Menu
docs.text:
The Cryptogram Secret Menu is a handwritten sheet of cipher symbols that the counter worker at the original Spud Hut keeps in a briefcase locked with two keys and hands to the team as "the menu".

Type Item (document, cipher) Aliases secret menu Creator The Spud Hut counter worker (see Spud Hut Counter Savant) Holder The team; the players decide to send it to the NSA Status Slated to go to the NSA as an unexplained puzzle; never decoded on air First appearance Appalachia 07

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The menu is a single sheet of paper covered in handwritten cryptic symbols, which Andre describes as "like some Zodiac Killer shit". (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The cryptogram stands in for a secret menu at a chain whose ordinary Spud Hut menu already covers nearly every cuisine. Whispered orders appear to belong to the same hidden layer: Eduardo Hooper quietly orders the "special taco taco spud" and says, "If anyone asks, I did not tell you about the secret menu." (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
On the team's second visit to the Spud Hut, the Biz orders the taco taco spud and asks whether there is more to the secret menu. The counter worker unlocks his briefcase with two keys, takes out the sheet and hands it over: "That is the menu." Asked about the symbols, he adds, "I designed the cryptogram myself." Zack suggests photographing it for "the crypto boys" back home. When Eddie Jones later asks about the highest-protein item, the counter worker refuses to discuss the secret menu in front of outsiders. (Appalachia 07)

Near the end of the episode the players debate where to send the page. Ezra proposes the state police, while Dante prefers Kurt's old employers, calling it a "Zodiac Killer misdirect" that is more useful to the team than leaving it at the next dead body. Andre notes that the CIA calls the NSA the "Puzzle Palace", and the team agrees to send it there without telling the codebreakers it is a menu. (Appalachia 07)

The episodes never reveal what the cryptogram says.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Zack hopes the NSA will crack it "after, like, a thousand hours, only to find out it's a fucking menu". Dante adds that if they work out the word "spud", "the goose is cooked". (Appalachia 07)
  • Ezra says "the idea of an actually secret menu is extremely funny to me." (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Crystal marbles
docs.text:
The crystal marbles are perfectly spherical, clear, warm and extremely hard spheres hoarded by several members of the Marblehead church, one of which the Biz pockets and insists is a diamond.

Type Item Aliases crystal spheres; diamonds; the marble; shoebox of clear marbles Holder Jester, Amos Shaw and Arnold Weathers each held a stash; the Biz holds one First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The spheres are clear, a little smaller than an ordinary marble, and sparkle intensely with the chromatic scatter of high-quality quartz or other gemstones. They feel warmer than glass, very smooth and surprisingly light, "like plastic" in the Biz's pocket (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: They are extremely hard. When the Biz drags his new carbon-steel pocket knife along one, the blade visibly blunts and the sphere is not marked (Summer Service 01). The Biz announces to the group that the spheres are diamonds, and Rita's Andrew repeats the word to Big Bill, calling them "weird, perfectly spherical diamonds" (Summer Service 03). The episodes never establish what they are, or whether they are payment to the congregation, a by-product of the worm infection, or something else. In Summer Service 05 Dante jokes, "Synthetic or no, we're obliterating the diamond market." (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Jester's bag. At the inn's front desk the Biz finds an open bag of about a dozen marbles that Jester left behind while arguing in the back room, in which the words "weather", "quarantine" and "unbeliever" are audible. Jester returns and snatches the bag back, but the Biz has palmed one (Manipulate Someone, 7). Later he shows it to a little girl at the Scott house, who is uninterested and asks for coffee. At day's end Jester is frantically rooting around his desk (Summer Service 01).
  • Shaw's nightstand. In the "murder house" Huell finds roughly ten pounds of clear spheres in an improvised plastic grocery bag in Amos Shaw's nightstand. He leaves them in place and keeps quiet that the Biz called them diamonds, and McManley bags them as evidence (Summer Service 03). See Amos Shaw's house.
  • The Biz's temptation. The Biz considers buying a new car with a diamond, then reconsiders (Summer Service 03).
  • Before the selectmen's meeting. Ezra jokes that Jester "did lose a very valuable diamond recently" (Summer Service 04).
  • Arnold's shoebox. In Arnold Weathers' house, Huell finds two sets of the town's financial books (Two sets of financial books) and a shoebox in a closet absolutely full of clear marbles. He takes both back downstairs and hands the marbles to the Biz (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: M28 Davy Crockett
docs.text:
The M28 Davy Crockett is a decommissioned man-portable tactical nuclear recoilless rifle with a W54 warhead, supplied to Kurt by his arms-dealer contact Carter and fired by Huell at the glowing creature in The Summer Service finale.

Type Item (weapon) Aliases Davy Crockett; W54 warhead; the nuke; the bomb; Little Feller II; M29; Kurt's heavy weapon Holder Kurt Larson, later fired by Huell Kendrick First appearance Summer Service 03 (requested); delivered in Summer Service 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The launcher arrives in a crate about seven feet by four feet by four feet, packed with metal tubes and smaller boxes and topped by two booklets, a range table and a manual. Every part is stamped "decommission". Carter has welded an aftermarket coincidence rangefinder to the side of the tube, filing off the numbers and rewriting them in Sharpie to match the weapon. The weapon is a tube that should be mounted on its tripod, with a charge cylinder, a firing rod, a screw-on projectile and a 72-foot firing cord. It can be shoulder-fired but weighs over a hundred pounds (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• The manual gives a maximum range of 1.25 miles and a yield of 0.2 kiloton (Summer Service 04).
  • The W54 warhead weighs roughly 60 lb, "surprisingly light", and is man-carriable (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05).
  • In the finale Andre corrects the players' guess of half a megaton to half a kiloton. Firing it kicks hard, and a wide, braced stance matters (Summer Service 06).
  • Andre gives the real weapon's code name as "Little Feller II" (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Ordering it. After the dive, Kurt phones an old contact from experimental weaponry for something big enough to kill the "glowy ring". The Preparedness roll is a 10 at -1 forward, so a 9, a mixed success. The contact promises a deniable weapon in a day or two with the serial numbers filed off (Summer Service 03). In Summer Service 04 Andre reveals that the contact is Carter, a former CIA fixer who left the agency at the same time as Kurt after Iran-Contra and became an overseas arms dealer. Dante burns a Luck point so that Kurt gets "a really good weapon"; without that burn he would have received a Scorpion (Summer Service 04).
  • Delivery. A courier in a military-surplus armored truck delivers the crate beside the RV at the post office. He says Carter sends his love, that this is the last one, and that afterward they are even. Kurt tells the others what it is: a tactical nuke. The warhead is wrapped in Kurt's poncho and bagged, and stored in his room at the inn, where Jester warns them not to leave "whatever that is" (Summer Service 04).
  • Mobile artillery. Kurt and Huell spend three to four hours mounting it on the Biz's Buick (Summer Service 04).
  • The siege. The team passes the 60 lb warhead down through the bathroom window while police climb the stairs, and the weapon rides in the modified car afterward (Summer Service 05).
  • The finale. Kurt tells the radio contact that the team has "a W54 and the means to launch it". The contact does not recognize the model name, saying, "It might be different where I'm from." Kurt teaches the team to fire it from the back seat of a commandeered car. Huell and the Biz play rock-paper-scissors for the honor, and Huell's paper beats the Biz's rock. Huell rolls a 7 and Zack burns a Luck point to turn it into a success. Huell starts to slip backward but braces his foot as Kurt advised. The blast knocks everyone flat, topples part of the fence of the nuclear power plant and ignites distant trees. The creature survives and is later killed by Andrew's flashlight (Summer Service 06).
  • Aftermath. Whatever remained of the launcher was left behind. A Guard officer later remarks that someone used a tactical nuke at the plant and that it will be hard to keep out of the news (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Summer Service 06 Andre cannot remember the designation and says it is "the M28 or M29"; Dante replies that those are the launcher and that what it launches is the W54. In Summer Service 04 Dante calls it the M28 Davy Crockett after looking through the manual.

docs.title: Dead Man's Briefcase
docs.text:
The Dead Man's Briefcase is a false-lined case holding about $10,000 in banded cash and a slot for a high-caliber handgun. The team pulls it from the Motel and Suites dumpster after the death of the man in the Chewbacca costume.

Type Item (container, evidence) Original owner The man registered as "John Doe", later named Troy Cleaver Found at Motel and Suites, dumpster Holder The task force (the cash is spent in Appalachia 07) First appearance Appalachia 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The briefcase is nominally empty, but its lining separates easily when the team pokes at it. Behind the lining are a slot shaped for a high-caliber handgun and about $10,000 in hundreds and twenties, wrapped in paper bands like those a bank uses for a withdrawal. Some of the bills are visibly more worn than others, and the bands carry no dates. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The case itself has no identifying marks. In the same trash bag the team finds a thick coil of animal hair tucked in one snakeskin boot, a walkie-talkie in the toe of the other, plastic bags and duct tape. Nothing in the bag identifies its owner. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: The dumpster
docs.text:
The dead man had registered at the Motel and Suites as "John Doe" and paid in cash. The clerk says his things were thrown out after he stopped renewing his room, and warns the team not to open a green garbage bag full of soiled linens. About a dozen bags are in the dumpster, and the snakeskin cowboy boots, which the clerk remembers throwing out, identify the right one. Kurt rolls Investigate a Mystery for a 10 with bonuses, a full success, and uses it to ask what is being concealed. (Appalachia 06)

Kurt notes the walkie-talkie's frequency in case anyone tries to contact the dead man. Andre rules that the contents read as "not spook, but maybe mercenary" to Kurt. Dante theorizes that the man was sent to kill someone and was double-crossed, or perhaps was paid with this cash for a contract. The interns dust the items for fingerprints, and the clerk lets the team take his own prints for exclusion. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: The ten grand
docs.text: At the Spud Hut in Appalachia 07, Huell pays for dinner for everyone, including the Circle Chasers, with the line: "Sure, we found ten grand in a garbage can. Fuck it, it's on me, boys." (Appalachia 07) The episodes never say how much of the cash was spent or what became of the gun slot.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Kurt's remark that wearing no vest under a Chewbacca costume is "a rookie mistake" accompanies the search. (Appalachia 06)
  • The fingerprints, the walkie-talkie frequency and the dead man's room all remain open leads at the end of Appalachia 06; the clerk has already rented the room to someone else. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:

docs.title: Dean Lawson's heroin and cash
docs.text:
Dean Lawson's heroin and cash is the buried $40,000 and the briefcase of four heroin parcels that the task force dug up at the Lawson cabin outside Radford, then kept and spent.

Type Item (contraband and money) Aliases $40,000 cash; Samsonite briefcase; drug money; small tin key; "the budget" Holder The task force (originally Dean Lawson) Status Kept by the team; some heroin carried along on the drive to Marblehead First appearance Radford Horror 06 (the cabin is mentioned)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The cash was several Ziploc bags of hundred-dollar bills, about $40,000 in all, buried near the back of the cabin together with a small key (Radford Horror 07). Kurt wondered who would make a key out of tin; Andre confirmed that it was tin. The key opened a locked Samsonite briefcase hidden under a loose floorboard beneath the bed in the cabin's unchanged child's room. Inside were four parcels of slightly cut South American heroin, with room for five or six; Andre put their value at $10,000 to $20,000 (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The stash was evidence of Dean's role in the local drug trade. Kurt tasted the heroin and asked the town doctor, Dr. Harvey Mauden, to compare it with the substance found in Amanda's blood. The doctor, who had once worked at an addiction clinic, was stunned by the quantity, estimated it at about $5,000 worth, and kept a test-tube sample to send to a friend (Radford Horror 07). The pilot Freak called it Mexican heroin and said he had bought the same stuff from a young man at a party; when Kurt described Dean, Freak agreed it sounded like him (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: Discovery
docs.text:
Douglas Douglas, the guard at the cabin community, told the team he had seen Dean carrying a shovel to the family cabin several times. The Biz stole a shovel from the community tool shed while Andrew kept Douglas talking about pinball. After digging up the cash and key, Kurt bump-keyed the back door and the team found the briefcase. Kurt put the board and briefcase back, took the drugs, cash and key, and refilled the hole (Radford Horror 07). The Biz's reaction to the money was "That's why they call it the business."

The cabin had earlier been pointed out on a tourist map by McCready, who put it about a mile from the lodge (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: Use in Radford
docs.text: The team used the contraband as a tool throughout the case. Kurt offered heroin to Freak, snorted a bump to show it was safe, and paid him $1,000 of the cash for the flight over the woods. During the fight with Wilbur Whateley, Andrew tried to sedate him with heroin and syringes from the church (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text:
After the team woke in the Radford ER, Andrew told Diane the car was full of drugs and money, and she was relieved it was only heroin. The Biz bet drug money on a baseball game (the Cubs did not win). The team decided to tip off the sheriff about Dean, though Dean's parents could not reach him and his car was missing. They kept the cash and heroin, and Kurt rode out of Radford with his feet on the drugs. At headquarters the stash sat in the weapon lockup, and Diane took some of the drug money, which the team came to call "the budget", to buy window air-conditioning units (Radford Horror 08). Kurt packed some of the heroin for the drive to Marblehead (Radford Horror 08).

Quote

"There's no feeling in the world like gambling with drug money." (Dante (as Kurt), Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Radford Horror 08, Dante misremembers the hiding places, saying the heroin was buried in the yard and the money was in the floorboards. Radford Horror 07 shows the reverse: the cash was buried in the yard and the heroin was under the bedroom floorboard.

docs.title: Diner security tape
docs.text:
The diner security tape is a VHS recording from the Lonely Mountain Diner's camera that shows a gray van crew raiding the Douglas Pinball Emporium, and that Kurt copied and hid in a hollow tree.

Type Item (evidence) Aliases VHS tape Holder Kurt (original, on loan from the diner); a copy is hidden in the woods Status Original borrowed from the diner; backup copy hidden in a hollow tree First appearance Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The tape comes from the camera at the Lonely Mountain Diner, across from the Douglas Pinball Emporium. The diner waitress (Sheila) said the camera had been "on the fritz lately," but she got it working and found the footage (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
The diner closed at 1 a.m., and the waitress put the raid at around 4 or 5 a.m. The grainy footage shows a gray van pulling into the lot and five men getting out: one with a long brown ponytail, the rest with military haircuts, some with their faces covered. A non-human shadow moves inside the emporium's window. One man opens the lock, possibly with a bump key, and the men rush in. After a scuffle, three of them carry out two bags, and two minutes later the others carry out assorted equipment before the van peels out (Radford Horrors 04).

Kurt's Investigate a Mystery roll (10) on the question "What is being concealed here?" concluded that the crew was an organized cleanup team used to working together. The ponytailed man moved like an action-movie character rather than a fighter, and Andre said he looked like a LARPer, probably a boss playing soldier. The shadow was not human and seemed to be trying to get out as the door was opened (Radford Horrors 04). The crew matches the gray van crew.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Kurt won the waitress over with a Manipulate Someone roll (11), an apology for the mess Huell had made of her bathroom the day before, and a promised hundred-dollar tip. She let him take the tape on condition that it be replaced or returned before the team left town. Kurt wanted it copied right away because magnetic media is not stable. At Blockbuster Video, Andrew showed his badge and the clerk Harold let the team use the back-room VHS TV; they photographed the screen and made a copy of the tape. Kurt then walked twenty minutes into the woods and hid the copy in an evidence bag inside a hollow tree, deliberately avoiding any fixed location that could be wiped (Radford Horrors 04).

Harold told the team that a month and a half to two months earlier, while closing up, he had seen a homeless man dragged into a van with a ponytailed man nearby, which fit the account of Billy Thornton. The episode leaves open who employs the crew and what the shadow in the window was (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: EPA field journal
docs.text:
The EPA field journal is an EPA-branded notebook of cryptic shorthand, left behind by the missing survey scientists and found under a shelf in the lighthouse basement.

Type Item (document) Aliases field notebook Holder Found by the team at the lighthouse First appearance Summer Service 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A small field notebook with EPA branding, written largely in cryptic shorthand. It lay under a shelf in the lighthouse's hidden storage basement, which is reached through a trapdoor and a slide-down ladder. Kurt found it along with rope cut into two- or three-foot lengths and stained with blood, two teeth (a canine and an incisor) and a pair of chairs set out in the middle of the room, also bloodied. The replacement bulbs and mirrors for the lighthouse were smashed in their boxes. Kurt made the discovery with an Investigate a Mystery roll of 11 (9 +3 -1), and luminol later showed a bleach-cleaned trail of blood from the trapdoor to the front door and out to where a car would park (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• The nerve-agent conclusion. The scientists concluded that the cases of poisoning were caused by a nerve agent (Synthetic nerve agent).
  • The fish. Several days were spent surveying local fish. Some were unknown species, distorted versions of known fish or "taxidermy mashups" with parts of one attached to another. Others looked normal but were packed with worms that had replaced their vital organs, and unlike the other fish they were not dead.
  • Threats. At a town council meeting the scientists were threatened by the senior town officials and the mayor.
  • The last entry. A local told them to check out the lighthouse, and that is where the notebook ends.

All of the above is from (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The team reads the journal at the end of the episode, after climbing out of the basement. The blood, the chairs and the cleaned trail lead the team to conclude that somebody was beaten up in a chair and then dragged out to a third location, most likely by the police given the taped-down radio at the door (Police walkie-talkie) (Summer Service 03).

The journal is a separate document from the earlier Survey team's field notes that the team found at the inn.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 03

docs.title: Flame light
docs.text:
The flame light is the fiery flashlight weapon that Kurt Larson uses in the final battle at the Roosevelt community center and in the cavern; it sears whatever it is aimed at and finally melts itself from overuse. (Walkers 09)

Type Item (weapon) Aliases flashlight weapon; "the flashlight that kills everything" Holder Kurt Larson Status Destroyed (melted) in Walkers 09 First appearance Walkers 09 (under this name)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The flame light is a flashlight that works as a weapon: it sears its targets, makes a loud clacking sound when used, has a limited number of charges, and overheats until it melts. Kurt also carries an ordinary flashlight, and before the battle Andre warns Dante to be sure he has "the right flashlight" before signalling the major's Humvee. (Walkers 09) The weapon matches the flashlight weapon that the team has used since the Radford case, which Dante recalls in Walkers 01 as the "magic flashlight that burns things." (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• Searing attack, rolled as Kick Some Ass (Dante rolls an 11 with it).
  • Limited charges.
  • Overheats and melts itself after its last charges. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
During the charge on the community center, naked skinwalkers swarm Ned Simpson's killdozer, and the party shoots two of four climbers off it. Kurt sweeps the machine with the flame light and sets the other two on fire; despite their indifference to pain, having "what little clothes and skin they do have suddenly set on fire" drives them off. (Walkers 09)

Later, in the cavern, after Huell's thrown grenade lands in the portal's support machinery and the portal winks out, the party is left in the dark with 50 or 60 skinwalkers. At Zack's prompting, Dante's Kurt sprays the crowd with "the flashlight that kills everything," setting fires. It gets hotter and hotter in his hand; he sets it down and walks away, and it glows and melts itself. Andre explains that it "only had so many charges." (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 09

docs.title: Flashlight weapon
docs.text:
The flashlight weapon is a flashlight-shaped beam device of unknown origin that fires a blinding blue-purple flash, sets targets alight and burns even water; the team first meets it in the hands of Agent Murphy and later carries one of their own.

Type Item (weapon, probably alien technology) Aliases Murphy's flashlight device; the purple-flash weapon; heat-ray flashlight; alien flashlight; flashlight laser; flamethrower flashlight; the flame light (Walkers 09); the flashlight that kills everything Holder Agent Murphy (first); the soldiers and "volcanologists" hunting the team; Kurt Larson; Andrew Howard; a broken copy with Boris Yeltsin First appearance Radford Horror 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Murphy's device looks like an ordinary flashlight until it is switched on. When fired it makes a rapid electric "clack-clack-clack" and a pulse of intensely bright blue-purple light (Radford Horror 03). Later episodes call it a laser, a heat ray and a flamethrower. In Summer Service 06 Andre notes that nobody knows what powers the team's copy or how many shots it holds (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• Burns. Each hit does 3 harm. In Radford Horror 03 the flash sets Kurt's shirt on fire, and Murphy sets trees ablaze as he flees (Radford Horror 03).
  • Blinds. The flash leaves anyone nearby unable to see, and a user needs very dark, welding-style glasses to avoid blinding himself. Kurt wears a welding mask when he tests the captured device in Radford Horror 08, and the light still leaves dots in his vision (Radford Horror 08; Radford Horrors 01). In the Marblehead pantry in Summer Service 05, the beam bouncing off metal cans blinds Andrew and the Biz, the Biz for about a minute (Summer Service 05).
  • Burns water. In Radford Horror 08 Kurt aims the captured device at the river. A patch of water explodes into steam, with an unnatural ultraviolet glow around the edge of the mask, and Andre describes the heat breaking the water into hydrogen and oxygen that burn and recombine: "It is so hot that it is literally burning the water" (Radford Horror 08).
  • Overheats. In Radford Horror 03 Murphy's device overheats and he vanishes in a pulse of light. In Summer Service 06 the plastic case begins to melt in Andrew's hand, and in Walkers 09 the "flame light" melts itself after its last charges (Radford Horror 03; Summer Service 06; Walkers 09).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 03, Murphy is hit by the team's car and found alive on the highway, vomiting blood, clutching a flashlight and a briefcase. He shows a badge: "I'm Agent Murphy. I'm NSA. You are fucking this up for me. Get back in your car and drive away." When Kurt grabs him, Murphy points the device. Kurt's shirt ignites for 3 harm and both Kurt and the Biz are blinded. Murphy burns trees as he flees into the woods. The team does not see his end: the narration cuts to him, panicking and firing at birds, until the device overheats and he vanishes in a pulse of light (Radford Horror 03).

In Radford Horror 04 the team finds a circle of ground melted to glass with almost nothing left of Murphy but the back of a suit, part of a skull and a little brain. There is no trace of the weapon, which Kurt assumes exploded. Kurt grumbles that UTAW tried bombs on bats, dolphins, dogs and boomerangs, but never produced a heat ray: "You know what I could have done to Castro with that heat ray?" (Radford Horror 04).

At the end of Radford Horror 07, soldiers without insignia and people in metal "volcanologist" suits with flamethrowers approach the team, and Andre points out that they carry "those flashlights", which Dante identifies as the one that set Kurt on fire (Radford Horror 07). See Cleanup crew.

In Radford Horror 08 the team ambushes one of the searchers and takes his flashlight, which comes free, along with his shadow poncho. Kurt wraps the poncho in foil and hands both it and the flashlight to Molly Underhill as "special federal evidence" before the team passes out. Molly returns the flashlight and foil in the hospital, and Kurt, who says he likes the flashlight, tests it at the river (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
In Summer Service 05 Kurt remembers midway through the Doberman fight that he has "a flashlight that burns things". Later he calls it the "flamethrower flashlight" and plans to have it out when the team clears the house. In the pantry Andrew fires it at the worm-ridden dog: the beam incinerates the worms in the air, sets the dog on fire for 4 harm, and blinds him and the Biz. Huell, who had looked away, can still see (Summer Service 05).

In Summer Service 06 the device is passed around the team. Huell's shot at a screaming man on the road goes wide over a bump and burns out a tire. Andrew burns the fleeing worms twice. In the finale he reaches out of the shelter of the car roof and hits the angel thing (Kick Some Ass, 8), burning his hand as the plastic case begins to melt. The creature spirals off, crashes into the earth and burns as a pillar of flame (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text: In Walkers 09 the device, now called the "flame light", is Kurt's weapon again. He sweeps the killdozer with it and sears off the two remaining attackers clinging to it (an 11). At the portal, when Zack asks whether they still have "the flashlight that kills everything", Andre confirms it, and Kurt sprays the crowd until it grows too hot to hold. He sets it down and it melts itself, its charges spent (Walkers 09). See also Flame light.

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text: In Radford Horrors 01, Boris Yeltsin unwraps a broken, half-melted object from a silk handkerchief and asks Dick "The Biz" Baxter, his prisoner in Moscow, whether he recognizes it. It is identical in design to the team's flashlight weapon. Yeltsin says he has had scientists working on it, and sent them to Siberia when they failed, and that the man it was taken from wore very dark sunglasses "like welding glasses". The Biz describes it as a heat weapon and explains that the glasses were so the user would not blind himself (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Who made the devices, and whether Murphy, the soldiers in Radford Horror 07 and the man Yeltsin's copy came from belong to the same group.
  • What powers them and how many shots they hold.

docs.title: Foil-Wrapped Letter
docs.text:
The Foil-Wrapped Letter is an anonymous letter and pencil sketch of trees, sent in a foil-lined envelope by a Keely Network contact, that sends the task force to Exeter, Rhode Island.

Type Item (document) Aliases the letter; tree sketch; Keely Network letter Holder Andrew Howard First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A postcard-sized envelope wrapped in aluminum foil comes inside a padded envelope. It holds a letter and a hand-drawn pencil sketch of some trees. The text of the letter is never read out; according to Andrew it describes a classic case of two people being abused by the Greys (Roulet Estate 01).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
On Christmas Eve 1992, Big Bill gives Andrew a padded envelope with his name scrawled on it and no return address, which an FBI courier asked him to drop off. Rita (as Andrew) asks the others, "Hey, guys, you think this might kill me?" before opening it. Andrew peels back the foil in the slush outside the office, and as he starts to read, the scene smash-cuts to the hungover agents waking in the Rhode Island house (Roulet Estate 01).

Andrew wakes with the letter and has no memory of how the team got to the house. He circulates it among the others and later uses the marked-up map in the car to check that they are at the address on it. Diane says she was woken at unprofessional hours and told to drive them to Rhode Island, and that they kept talking about finding proof for Ross Perot. In the library Andrew tells Kurt that, "just like the letter said," they have "a classic case of two people being abused by the Greys" (Roulet Estate 01).

In Roulet Estate 02, Andre's recap explains that someone from the Keely Network message boards who knew Andrew had written that their friend Margaret Roulet had been experiencing "visitations" and then vanished. The sender is never identified (Roulet Estate 02).

Diane remembers that Andrew was very excited about the shape of the UFOs, which matched what the team had seen before, and she believes he took a phone call at the bar that set the whole trip off, though she does not know what it said. Andre clarifies in the recap that the black triangles were in the sketch (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:

  • Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Folded Face
docs.text:
The Folded Face is the peeled-off face of a dead man, found stuck to the wall of a blood-splattered cave outside Dahlonega. Andrew Howard bags it as evidence, and the team later hands it over to Dr. McManley.

Type Item (human remains, evidence) Aliases face in a bag; the face in the bag Belonged to Dead Man in the Cave Found at The Death Cave Holder Donald McManley First appearance Appalachia 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A man's face, folded and stuck to the cave wall with blood. Huell studies it and judges the man to be a middle-aged smoker who looks older than his hair color implies. Nobody on the team recognizes him. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The face has no supernatural properties. The scene around it suggests that the man was shredded and smashed against the walls, "almost like when gators have been at a body for a while", with split bones, tooth marks, and muscle, organs and fat missing. Dante checks for powder marks and the smell of smoke or incendiaries and finds none, so this was not an explosion. (Appalachia 03) A glob of dark hair and fat stuck to the HF Lighter found in Andrew's hand looks roughly right for this face. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: The cave
docs.text: Following his own blood trail, Andrew leads the team to a cave beside a road. Its interior is splattered with blood, and there is a very old pickaxe on the ground. Kurt notices a lump of skin on the wall, and after a moment realizes that it is a folded face. Andrew seals it in a bag and tosses it to Huell. The team photographs the scene and marks it with FBI pink flags. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: The mini fridge
docs.text: Back at the Smith Hotel, the team stashes the face and the other evidence in the hotel mini fridge. When the team reaches McManley, he is thrilled by the news. "Oh, oh, tell me you have a body," he says, and when Andrew offers "a face in a bag", he answers, "Like Christmas." He then asks about RV hookups. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Handed to McManley
docs.text:
When McManley's RV pulls into the hotel lot, Huell hands him the face. McManley holds it up and says, "Kinky. Alright. We'll get this analyzed." Andrew protests that it was only put in a bag, and McManley replies, "It's an expression, son." (Appalachia 04) Dick Baxter later brags about the face in the bag while softening a call to his friend Appleby, a federal judge, and promises, "I'll see if I can sneak you a chunk." (Appalachia 04)

The episodes do not report any result of McManley's analysis.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 03
  • Appalachia 04

docs.title: Gene's Shoe
docs.text:
Gene's Shoe is the red, white-soled child's shoe of the missing boy Gene Cartwright, found hanging high in a tree with a tuft of pale hair caught in its laces.

Type Item (evidence) Aliases the shoe; pale hair Owner Gene Cartwright Found at The Field and Bent Tree Holder Donald McManley (from Appalachia 04) First appearance Appalachia 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A child's shoe, red with a white sole. Sheriff Carter Burke confirms over the phone that the missing boy's shoes were red with white soles. Caught in the laces is a tuft of pale hair that feels like soft body hair, with the ends still on it. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The pale hair is the clue that makes the shoe relevant to the question of what sort of creature is involved. The players read the shoe and hair together as pointing to something that can climb, and that may have returned to hang its prey in the tree. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: The field
docs.text:
In Appalachia 02, the team searches the field near the tree where Gene, aged seven or eight, disappeared while playing with the neighborhood children. The volunteer search has trampled the scene. Dick Baxter asks "What sort of creature is it?" and, on an 11, notices something dangling from a high branch. Huell climbs the tree, tears and muddies his suit on the way down, and retrieves the shoe. Kurt says, "I don't mean to be blunt, but shoe in a tree, that kid is dead." (Appalachia 02)

The team bags the shoe and hair and stashes them in the trunk of the Ford Explorer. Kurt phones Sheriff Burke, who confirms the shoe's color, admits his deputies should have looked up, apologizes for the volunteers trampling the scene, and asks to see the shoe once forensics is done. (Appalachia 02)

Edward Nick, a neighbor's boy who was playing with Gene, says Bigfoot took him; Rita points out that this does not explain how the shoe got into the tree. Later the team finds a white rabbit's pelt, ripped apart with its insides gone, high in another tree, and Kurt wonders whether the shoe was hung in the first tree afterward, by a creature returning to hang its prey. See White Rabbit Pelt. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Handed to McManley
docs.text: In Appalachia 04, the bag of recovered pieces the team gives McManley includes Gene's shoe and the shoe of the other missing boy. That second shoe, found in the tunnels, is a separate item: see Child's Tennis Shoe. Elsewhere in the episode, Dante argues that a shoe in a tree is as good as a body for presuming Gene dead. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Gene's family lives in trailer 920 and the Nick family in 513. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 02
  • Appalachia 04

docs.title: Gold Bars
docs.text:
The Gold Bars are the hundreds of pounds of cast gold stacked on a kitchen table in a room beneath Dahlonega. They are the product of Jan's Conspiracy and its ape-man mining shifts. Half of the stockpile is already missing when the party arrives, and the party, Clive and the sheriff pocket some of the rest.

Type Item (treasure) Found at The gold room in The Dahlonega Gold Mines Producer Jan's Conspiracy Holders The party, Clive and Sheriff Carter Burke (what they carried out) First appearance Appalachia 09

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The gold has been melted down and cast into bars. When Clive opens the door, the table is "mostly full of gold", amounting to "hundreds of pounds", and "like, half of it" is missing. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Andre handled the gold as a physical burden. A reasonable amount, such as a couple of small bars in the pockets, costs nothing, but an unreasonable amount gives -1 forward to physical rolls until it is dropped. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: The operation's output
docs.text: Clive explains that there is a lot of gold left under Dahlonega and that the ape-men are a good workforce for digging it, since they do not talk to anyone. Dante sums it up: "Apes mine gold. Tell nobody, 'cause ape." Clive says a mercenary did the melting. He was promised a third of the gold, and says Jan wanted at least $100 million, or it was not worth doing. Ezra tells him he was never going to see that third. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: The party takes its share
docs.text:
When Clive shows the team the gold room, he curses Jan for the missing half, then asks to take some himself after "a year and a half" of work. The party agrees, under the banner of "civil forfeiture". Huell and the Biz take unreasonable amounts and clink as they walk. Kurt takes a reasonable amount, "mostly for my wife and kids". Andrew finds more room in his bag than expected, and the Biz mentions needing a new pair of night-vision goggles. The sheriff announces, "I'm taking some, and we're gonna figure out the legality of this later." Dante and Rita reassure him that his department, not he, is keeping it. (Appalachia 09)

At the end of the episode, the party emerges from a ladder in the woods outside the Spud Hut plant, and the sheriff wraps his arms around a tree and sways gently. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Jan's plan
docs.text:
In the epilogue, Jan, held at the CIA's Black Site Omaha, tells Kurt that his plan had been to melt the gold down, take it to a dealer and work out the laundering later through acquaintances who set up businesses for that purpose. (Walkers 01)

Unrecorded session

The finale of the arc, Appalachia 10, was never recorded. The fate of the bars after Appalachia 09 is not shown on air.

docs.title: Green Slurry
docs.text:
Green Slurry is a homemade, highly concentrated peyote preparation, kept in a jar with an eyedropper in the hidden attic lair of the Roulet House.

Type Item (drug) Aliases peyote slurry Holder The task force (taken from the lair) First appearance Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The slurry is in a homemade-looking jar with a lid in the hidden attic lair, alongside a cooler holding beta blockers. An eyedropper with it suggests to Kurt that the occupant has been gradually taking some out to use (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Kurt cracks the jar and sniffs it. The smell is oddly familiar; the walls seem to close in and something moves at the edge of his vision. A Sharp roll (5 + 3 = 8) is not enough to identify the mixture exactly, but he can tell that it is very concentrated and probably contains peyote. He hands his sidearm to Andrew until he has caught his breath (Roulet Estate 02).

The house's water also gives the agents hallucinations (see The Drugged Water), but no one in the episodes connects it to the slurry (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text: Kurt and Andrew bring the jar down the chimney with the looted guns, money and valuables, so that the intruder has fewer resources if he returns. Kurt plans to have it analyzed. Its purpose, and whether the Roulets' "visitations" were drug trips, are never established (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Ground-penetrating radar
docs.text:
The ground-penetrating radar (GPR) is a push-mower-sized radar unit that the task force rents from the equipment dealer Drebin and uses to scan the ground under the Sherman Ranch and the grave of Shelly Wilmarth. (Walkers 04, Walkers 05)

Type Item (equipment) Aliases GPR; the radar; ground radar Holder Rented by the task force; operated mostly by Kurt Larson Cost $800 rental ("a friend rate") First appearance Walkers 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The GPR looks like a push lawnmower with a screen on the handles. Drebin's instructions are that the voltmeter must read above 60 or the batteries need replacing, and that the display is switched on by tilting it forward and back. In Walkers 06 Andre adds that two big car batteries power it, and that it is a little heavier than a push lawnmower. Its display is "extremely cryptic," and Andre rules that reading it takes a Sharp roll every time. (Walkers 05, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Drebin explains that the signal shows irregularities in depth as fluctuations in the lines, so that "empty coffin, you're gonna see a void. Full coffin, you're not gonna see a void." It shows only the shallow signal well. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Sourcing. In Walkers 04, as a backup plan in case the exhumation order falls through, Dante's Kurt goes to the big house to phone around for ground radar or sonar. Zack suggests a contact, and Ezra's Biz uses Fixer (Charm, a 12) to recall a friend of his ex-wife's brother in Salt Lake City who sells equipment for finding wrecked cars in lakes. After about an hour on the phone the Biz reaches him, and he agrees to rent a ground-penetrating radar for about $800 the next day. (Walkers 04)

Delivery. In Walkers 05 Drebin delivers the unit and demonstrates it on the ranch's septic tank, which shows a void about ten feet down. He then points out a very large signal about 70 feet down ("it's like a cave") and loses interest. He clutches his pet iguana, says he will be back in 24 hours to collect the unit, and leaves. While they wait, Kurt (Sharp 13, counted as 12) and Andrew experiment with it, concluding that the cavern extends under the whole area at depth and that nowhere on the property is closer to the surface; this is the first sign of the cavern. Andrew buries a Cats costume as a calibration, and it barely shows at the very top of the display. The radar is also part of the cover story Dante's Kurt and Andrew give to the mayor, Wilford Hiram: a non-invasive check that Shelly Wilmarth's casket is in fact full. (Walkers 05)

Cemetery. In Walkers 06 the party loads the radar into Betsy and goes to the churchyard cemetery. The machine will not start. Flipped over, it shows several bundles of wires on its underside that look chewed, although the underside cannot be reached while the unit stands upright, as it had been left. The table jokes about the goose, ape men and squirrels. Zack's Huell passes the Sharp roll that Andre sets at minus three and repairs it. Pushed over the grave and compared with neighbouring plots, the radar convinces the party that something solid is in the coffin, with about 85 percent confidence. The exhumation order is not yet approved, so this serves as a backup, and they plan to dig the next day. (Walkers 06) See the exhumation of Shelly Wilmarth.

The cause of the chewed wires is never established.

docs.text:

  • Walkers 05
  • Walkers 06

docs.title: HF Lighter
docs.text:
The HF Lighter is a bloody stainless-steel lighter, marked "HF" in Sharpie, that Andrew Howard finds clutched in his own hand after waking in the woods outside Dahlonega.

Type Item (evidence) Aliases bloody steel lighter Found by Andrew Howard Probable owner Dead Man in the Cave First appearance Appalachia 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The lighter is stainless steel, a little more upscale than a gas-station lighter, with no engraving. Under the blood on its bottom, the initials "HF" are written in Sharpie. Dark hair and fat stuck to its side look roughly right for the folded face. Kurt examines it in gloves. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The blood on the lighter is not Andrew's: the cuts on his feet are his own, but the lighter's blood is not. (Appalachia 03) Zack observes from the dead man's face that he looked like a smoker, which the team takes to fit the lighter and the cigarette pack found in the cave. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Andrew wakes in the woods in sweat-soaked pajamas, bleeding from the feet and clutching a lighter he has never seen. He walks for hours and gets back to the Smith Hotel. Before rinsing off, he bags the lighter and as much of the blood on his hand as he can. (Appalachia 03)

The next day, Dante points out that the team has not yet looked at the lighter, and examines it for a name. The team follows Andrew's blood trail to a crevice, which leads them to the bloody chamber and the man's face. (Appalachia 03) Everything, including the lighter, goes into the hotel mini fridge. Andrew asks how the team will explain the lighter when it has to be recorded. Dante says they will treat it as circumstantial evidence from the crime scene he found, and leave out that he was sleepwalking. (Appalachia 03) Kurt tells Sheriff Carter Burke about the lighter and the blood, and the sheriff puts the matter aside until after the search for the missing German boy, Frederick. (Appalachia 03)

Later in the episode, Andrew phones the Spud Hut distribution center about a missing worker, Aaron Richters, but notes that his initials do not match the lighter's. The team concludes that the dead man might have borrowed a friend's lighter. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes never explain the initials "HF", nor how the lighter came to be in Andrew's hand.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Appalachia 03

docs.title: Ivermectin
docs.text:
Ivermectin is the veterinary dewormer that McManley recommends against the Marblehead worm infection, which Henry fetches from Salem and which strips Huell of his worm-given strength.

Type Item (medicine) Aliases worm pills; worm medicine Holder McManley's assistant Henry fetched it; Huell is the notable patient First appearance Summer Service 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: An antiparasitic normally bought from a large-animal vet, a "horse doctor". Dante points out that it is also used in fish farming, which gives it a slight reason to be in Marblehead (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: McManley recommends it against the worms in the communion wine (Summer Service 03). In the finale, deworming ends the infected's enhancements but is hard on the body. Huell loses his worm "luster", gets a pounding headache and later visibly loses muscle and hair, regains wrinkles, runs a high fever and vomits dying worms. Zack removes the worm bonus from Huell's sheet. Andre also says that some of the infected will not pull through the treatment (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• The recommendation. McManley tells Andrew to find a horse doctor, get ivermectin into his body as soon as possible, and keep away from the wine. Huell is torn: he likes his hairline and fitness, but Zack wonders whether he will end up a zombie or a "super tough worm guy" (Summer Service 03).
  • Henry's errand. After the Biz wins McManley over (Manipulate Someone, 13), McManley lends the team his assistant Henry. Henry is sent to Salem for ivermectin or any other broad-spectrum parasite killer, armed with Huell's concealed carry permit as FBI cover, and Vespas off into the rain (Summer Service 04).
  • Advice to Madeline. Kurt tells Madeline Weathers to get antiparasitics, even if she has to lie to a horse doctor about having a pony (Summer Service 05).
  • Delivery. On the road toward Salem, Henry sits on his blood-soaked Vespa holding a pharmacy bag. He climbs into the team's vehicle and says, "Here's your worm pills. I'm going to bed." The players stop the session before anyone takes the pills, and Kira points out that killing a host's parasites all at once can make the host very ill (Summer Service 05).
  • Effect on Huell. By the finale the deworming is already taking hold in Huell. The pills are taken off-screen, between Summer Service 05 and the finale, during the unrecorded Summer Service 05.5. Andre has the National Guard distributing deworming medicine across Marblehead (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Dante's Kurt jokes about getting "some of that suppressed COVID cure" in Summer Service 05. When Andre suggests filling a Super Soaker with dissolved ivermectin in Summer Service 06, Zack answers, "Not COVID."
