docs.title: Ketamine
docs.text:
Ketamine is the sedative that the handlers in Jan's Conspiracy use to keep the ape-men of the Dahlonega gold mines docile and focused, and that Kurt Larson turns against them to get the party past a mining shift.

Type Item (drug) Holder Clive (the handler's stock); Kurt Larson (a share) Used by The ape-men's handlers; Kurt First appearance Appalachia 09

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Clive keeps ketamine as a powder, which the operation normally mixes into the ape-men's food. He carries it with a clicker and a shotgun. When he is asked to drug the shift on the spot, he explains, "The ketamine's usually in the food. I just have the powder." (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• The ape-men are kept addicted to it. Clive says that without it "they kill each other, they tear up the enclosures, and they don't focus". They like food and ketamine and dislike loud noises. (Appalachia 09)
  • It is used together with clicker training, positive and negative reinforcement, and demonstration. (Appalachia 09)
  • It numbs pain. During the run from Big Bob, Dante says, "thank god I'm on ketamine and I don't feel that shit." (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Clive's stock
docs.text: After meeting Clive in the kennel security office, the party learns that the operation has run for a year and a half and that the ape-men arrive looking about six and are full-grown in about two months. Clive offers the party some ketamine. Kurt says he has "sworn off" it, and the others decline. Clive adds that there is a finite amount of ketamine a person can buy from large-animal vets before they get suspicious. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: The Combos plan
docs.text:
The party plans to drug the next shift and then leave through the mines by way of the gold room. Clive has already fed the shift their treats and has only the powder. Preparedness rolls turn up snacks: Andrew has Corn Nuts, and Kurt, on a mixed success, has Combos. They hollow out the Combos and pack them with a ketamine paste, while the sheriff keeps watch. (Appalachia 09)

Facing the mining shift, Kurt walks out, eats a spiked Combo and mimes ecstasy, getting high himself. His Manipulate Someone roll is an 11. The ape-men advance aggressively, see his face relax as the drug hits, and "immediately get it". They spoon ketamine into their mouths, one pulls him into an affectionate shove, and another gently hands him a jackhammer. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Epilogue
docs.text: In the epilogue, Kurt tells Jan that the ketamine and shotguns made it "not a good night", and asks where Jan got it. Jan answers, "One of the high schoolers sells it to me." Kurt also jokes about giving ketamine to a nuisance named Chester. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Kurt says ketamine "might be the only drug I have a problem with", and later, running from Big Bob, "Racehorses take this stuff. I'm like a racehorse." (Appalachia 09)
  • Dante's performance for the ape-men: "Mmm, mmm, mmm, fellas, you have gotta try this stuff. Oh my god. That is some good ketamine." (Appalachia 09)
  • Earlier in the episode, Dante mentions that Kurt's CIA days included failed attempts with "ketamine teeth". (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 09
  • Walkers 01 (mentioned)

docs.title: Killdozer
docs.text:
The killdozer is Ned Simpson's home-welded armored bulldozer, fitted with machine guns, pipe bombs and a flamethrower, which joins the National Guard convoy and leads the charge on the Roosevelt community center. (Walkers 09)

Type Item (vehicle) Aliases armored bulldozer Holder Ned Simpson Status Last seen stuck in a tree First appearance Walkers 09

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Ned, a feed-store worker, tells Kurt he finished the machine that morning: "As soon as the power went out, I knew today was the day." He says it carries machine guns, "a bunch of pipe bombs in the back" and a flamethrower. When the convoy is loading up, Andre describes the cab as looking "like a Soyuz capsule." (Walkers 09)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Dust behind the convoy reveals the killdozer closing in as the party rides back through abandoned Ballard. Ned believes the collapse is a ruse and calls on every patriot to "take up arms and/or bulldozers and fight the communist menace." Dante's Kurt calls him "an asset" and slows down to talk to him. Kurt pitches Ned to the major, who, after a long look through the window, says "Fine" and slows the convoy to 20 miles an hour. (Walkers 09)

When a strange field halts the convoy and the major orders heavy equipment carried and civilians left behind, Ned flatly refuses to leave the killdozer ("I did not spend six months welding this thing"). The group stuffs it with grenades, radio equipment and heavy supplies, and he gives a big thumbs-up. (Walkers 09)

At the community center the killdozer charges a fence with cars piled up behind it, probably most of the cars from Roosevelt. The naked defenders swarm it, and Kurt burns off climbers with the flame light. On its second pass around the parking lot it is crushing people, and as the invisible waves come through it levitates for a few seconds at a time. Kurt warns Ned that the dozer keeps levitating; Ned answers only with "Die, commie freaks!" interspersed with machine-gun fire. (Walkers 09)

At the end, with everyone outside unconscious and black craft overhead, the killdozer is stuck in a tree, which Andre says is "struggling a little bit" to support it. Ned's fate is never shown. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• When Andrew asks what the bulldozer is, Dante's Kurt answers "Civilian assistance." (Walkers 09)
  • Dante summed up the session as "Got the real Andrew back, fucking killdozered a community center." (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 09

docs.title: Kurt's P90
docs.text:
Kurt's P90 is the FN P90 submachine gun, nicknamed "Bessie," that Kurt Larson acquires before the Utah trip and carries throughout the Ballard case, where it is coveted, repeatedly dropped, lent out and finally carried into the last battle. (Walkers 01)

Type Item (firearm) Aliases P90; FN P90; Bessie; "space gun" Holder Kurt Larson (briefly lent to Huell Kendrick) First appearance Walkers 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A compact FN P90 submachine gun. Walt calls it "a space gun" and it looks to him like a toy. Dante's Kurt says it "fits into a handbag" and fires "real little bullets." Zack's Huell calls it a bullpup. (Walkers 04, Walkers 06)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Acquisition. In Walkers 01, during downtime, Dante announces that he wants "a fucking P90," complaining that the standard sidearm and "this revolver" can "go fuck itself." Andre asks when the P90 came out (Dante says around 1986) and confirms that Kurt has sourced one. Kurt then looks for a holster he likes, since the P90 rubs his armpit. (Walkers 01)

Travel. The team chooses to fly to Utah. Kurt leaves his claymores behind but, because he has a license for it, keeps the P90. (Walkers 02)

Walt's envy. Walt "Coyote" Murphy falls in love with the P90 when he arrives for his sheep patrol, asking to hold it and wishing aloud that he could shoot Nerf darts out of it. Dante's Kurt asks him: "You ever just sat there holding down the trigger and liquefied a whole pumpkin?" Walt replies that he hasn't, and that this "might be a shortcoming." (Walkers 04)

The night event. During the disturbance in Walkers 05, Kurt wakes believing he is in Saigon, with the P90 in hand ("Your pizza's here, ma'am," Dante jokes). He drops the P90 more than once; Huell keeps handing it back ("you dropped your P90 again"), and Kurt resolves to put the strap on. (Walkers 05)

Loan to Huell. In Walkers 06 Huell asks "Can I buy your P90?" and Kurt lends it with the words "just treat Bessie right." Huell takes it to his solo scene at the Ballard grocery store and keeps a hand on it as he enters the back break room. He returns after a little over an hour with a bloody bandage around his hand and gives the gun back, and Kurt asks whether it has been used. Huell later offers it to Andrew before the gym meeting, and Andrew declines. (Walkers 06)

The intruder. In Walkers 07, Kurt shoots the naked intruder in the double-wide in the foot with a short burst from the P90 (Kick Some Ass, an 8). It does 2 harm and the intruder shows no reaction, then chokes Kurt. (Walkers 07)

Final battle. In Walkers 09 Kurt strips the metal from himself before the convoy moves in, but keeps the P90 in hand while the holster on his back comes off. In the cavern he later puts it to the head of the captured runner who turns out to be the real Howard, a Manipulate Someone roll. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • "Bessie" is Dante's name for the gun; the loaner car is Betsy.

docs.title: 1961 Lincoln Continental
docs.text:
The 1961 Lincoln Continental is the black, ticket-covered Continental hardtop that the FBI lent to the task force as its road-trip car on the way to Radford.

Type Item (vehicle) Aliases the Lincoln, the Continental Holder The task force (agency loan car) First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The car is a black 1961 Lincoln Continental hardtop, an agency loan found parked in a fire lane and completely covered in parking tickets. It has no working air conditioning, which matters in a black car in a humid D.C. May, and the radio's tuning knob is loose enough that vibration twists the dial to a new station roughly every 90 seconds, leaving mostly static between stations (Radford Horror 01). Gas reimbursements for the car are auto-approved.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The car has no special abilities. Its trunk is enormous, but Kurt's travel case takes up roughly 75 percent of it, and the suspension visibly sags when the case goes in (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
On May 24th, 1992, at about 7 a.m., Andrew found the task force's address: a derelict barbershop in a black D.C. neighborhood. Parked outside, in front of a Crown Victoria full of document boxes, was the Lincoln. An FBI agent on site explained that the building had belonged to the Capitol Police, who sold it to the FBI rather than pay to remove the asbestos, and told Andrew the Lincoln was the task force's car. Andrew gathered up the parking tickets to hand to the secretary, Diane, who started calling the FBI to sort them out (Radford Horror 01). The building is the D.C. barbershop.

With two hours to spare, the team packed and drove to Radford in it. Kurt drove while the Biz and Huell sat in back, played War and drank. Kurt passed back cucumber sandwiches and juice boxes his wife had packed, and Huell asked for Ecto Cooler (Radford Horror 01). A meter maid was heard writing another ticket for the Continental while Andrew briefed the team at the barbershop.

The Lincoln is not named again in the Radford arc, but in Radford Horror 08 the team's car is described as illegally parked and ticketed outside the Radford ER, and Andrew told Diane it was full of cash and heroin (Radford Horror 08). See Dean Lawson's heroin and cash.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Summer Service 06, Andre briefly called a car in a convoy "the Lincoln" before correcting himself and saying it was the FBI car, not the Biz's Buick (Summer Service 06). See The Biz's Buick Regal.

docs.title: Dr. Lori's patient files
docs.text:
Dr. Lori's patient files are the psychiatrist's paper records, which the Biz photographed during a burglary of his office and which Kurt later developed into evidence about Amanda Lucky's prescriptions.

Type Item (evidence; film and photographs) Aliases file photos; film Holder The Biz (photographed); Kurt (developed) Status Developed and examined in Radford Horror 05 First appearance Radford Horror 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The originals were the patient files kept in a locked filing cabinet in Dr. Lori's office. The Biz photographed them on film, which in 1992 had to be developed before anyone could read it (Radford Horror 04). The files belonged to Dr. Lawrence Lori's patients, including Amanda Lucky.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Developed, the photographs show that Amanda's file begins with a couple of ordinary interviews, then a Xanax prescription with notes explaining why it was prescribed. Later notes raise the dose several times with no explanation. Roughly halfway through the log, extra appointment dates appear alongside the weekly session, and near the end they taper off into several meetings marked "no show." The file says nothing about prescribing opiates. The file for the other missing woman is routine, with medical justification for everything in it, and there is no file at all for Mr. Augustine (Radford Horror 05).

The autopsy and tox screen, meanwhile, found trace amounts of Xanax and a large quantity of opiates in Amanda's blood, so there was a gap between what the files recorded and what was in her system. The team also knew that the hard copy a doctor sends to the pharmacy to validate a prescription was missing (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The Biz broke into Lori's office to retrieve his transmitter from the vent (see the bug in Dr. Lori's vent). Using one of Kurt's stilts as a pry bar, he decided to take the back off the filing cabinet rather than damage the lock, and photographed the files on everyone known so far. His Act Under Pressure roll came up 7, so the cabinet would not go back together and Lori would eventually notice. To disguise the break-in as a junkie burglary, he stole a prescription pad, threw a brick through the window on his way out, clogged the toilet and drew on the bathroom stall with a Sharpie (Radford Horror 04).

In Radford Horror 05, Kurt rolled Preparedness and found that his travel case held a portable darkroom: a small bottle of chemicals, a red bulb and some plastic baggies, good for developing a roll in about 45 minutes. He developed the film at the Pay n' Stay (Radford Horror 05). The team then argued over theories. Kurt suggested an affair, with drugs given in exchange for sex. Andrew proposed that Lori and the pharmacist, Derek Augustine, had been working together, and that Augustine had been getting prescriptions written in Lori's name on the side before the two fell out (Radford Horror 05).

In the recap in Radford Horror 08, Andre reported that Lori and Derek Augustine had both confessed to an inappropriate sexual relationship with Amanda. Authorities also believed Augustine had broken into Lori's office, because of the feces left in the toilet (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The bug in Dr. Lori's vent
docs.text:
The bug in Dr. Lori's vent is a small radio transmitter and microphone that the Biz planted in the psychiatrist's office, which rolled into a vent on a mixed roll and later picked up Lori's heated phone call.

Type Item (surveillance device) Aliases the bug; listening device Holder The Biz (owner) Status Retrieved by the Biz in Radford Horror 04 First appearance Radford Horror 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The bug is a plain radio transmitter with a microphone. The Biz meant to stick it under a chair in Dr. Lori's office, in a nondescript brownstone near the middle of Radford (Radford Horror 02). It is not expensive, but as Andre pointed out in Radford Horror 03, replacing one would mean going back to "a real city" (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Because the bug ended up in a corner vent rather than under the desk, the audio was poor and words were hard to make out (Radford Horror 02). The Biz listened from a car outside (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Planting
docs.text: During the team's visit to Dr. Lawrence Lori, the Biz tried to plant the bug under his chair. Huell helped by sneezing (a Help Out roll of 12 on Cool), and the Biz rolled a 9 on Act Under Pressure, counting his bonus for concealing evidence of a crime. A mixed success gave Andre a worse outcome: the bug failed to stick and rolled into a small vent in the corner (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: The heated call
docs.text: In Radford Horror 03 the Biz listened in (Investigate a Mystery, 10). He caught only snippets of one side of a heated phone call, including "You don't know" and "I swear to God." After a handset slam, pacing and a metallic click, Lori hurried out to his car. The team followed him to a meeting at the Augustine barn (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Failed retrieval
docs.text: The rest of the team returned to the clinic to get the bug back. Huell inspected the window (Sharp, 6): only a crowbar would open it without damage. He faked a lost jacket, and the receptionist walked him to the office and watched him. The bug was visibly down in the vent. Huell's pretext of asking what kind of window it was, because he was thinking of replacing his own, rolled a 5 on Manipulate Someone. The receptionist stepped between him and the window, ushered him out and locked the door. The team dropped the break-in and discussed getting a warrant (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Retrieval
docs.text: At night in Radford Horror 04, the Biz broke in himself, wedging one of Kurt's stilts into the window to force it, and took the top off the furnace vent to retrieve the bug. He then photographed the office's files, which became Dr. Lori's patient files (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Minor items and artifacts: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: Minor items of The Things in Appalachia: smaller props, tools, vehicles and pieces of evidence. Larger objects have their own pages, such as the Chewbacca Costume, the SHA Tracking Device and the Claymore Mine.

docs.title: 1991 Ford Explorer
docs.text: The Explorer is the team's near-new replacement vehicle, used after the EPA and NRC hold their old car and equipment following Marblehead. It has four-wheel drive, power windows and a working air conditioner and radio. In Appalachia 02 the team keeps Gene Cartwright's shoe in its trunk until McManley arrives, while the old car, with the team's night vision, is still held for decontamination. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Ancient Pickaxe
docs.text: In the second cold open, a Spud Hut worker finds an ancient pickaxe in the sand of a rocky fissure and raises it as a weapon just before he is attacked. In Appalachia 03 the team finds an old, bloody pickaxe in the Death Cave among skin, bones and a folded face. The players assume it is the same tool. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Animal Crate
docs.text: The animal crate is a large crate that Jan Martense wheels from a service lift to a red pickup in the cold open of Appalachia 09. Its contents are never revealed. In Appalachia 09, Dante guesses that Jan took a sample with the crate and left. See Hidden Ape-man. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Animal Hair Coil
docs.text: One of the dead drifter's snakeskin cowboy boots holds a coil of animal hair, alongside plastic bags and duct tape. Kurt reads the hair as material for faking Bigfoot evidence and the bags and tape as possible body-disposal gear. See Snakeskin Cowboy Boots and The Bigfoot Hoax. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Anti-suicide Playing Cards
docs.text: At the Omaha black site, ordinary playing cards are banned, so Kurt shows Jan Martense how to make improvised cards from bits of napkin and coasters. He promises to ask the desk guard for proper anti-suicide cards and keeps the promise. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Bear Suits and Shotguns
docs.text: The handlers in the Spud Hut basement keep bear suits, 12-gauge shotguns, pepper spray, air horns and goalie face masks in a gear room. The party takes them as armor and weapons; the bear suits give 1 armor. Clive wears the upper half of a suit and a face shield. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Bigfoot T-shirt
docs.text: Andrew's souvenir "Bigfoot-sized nuggets" shirt is given to him at the Consolidated Gold Mine after his own shirt is soaked in blood. He wears it under his suit in Appalachia 04 and again in Appalachia 06, where every NPC still clocks him as a cop and he says, "I love this T-shirt." By the ninth episode it is bloodstained again. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Case Dossier
docs.text: The Dahlonega dossier is a hastily assembled file that Diane delivers: a child missing about a week, another child claiming a Bigfoot sighting, a woman missing since the day before, four or five sightings, and the Dahlonega Times clipping. Andrew notices the woman vanished in Auraria, not Dahlonega, and finds an unexplained article about religious vision ceremonies tucked in the back. See Diane. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Circle Chasers' VHS Footage
docs.text: The Circle Chasers' tape is a three-second clip in which a rabbit freezes in the trail and a gray, man-sized blur grabs it. The teens promise a copy in exchange for a blank VHS. See Rabbit Thing. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Clinton Polaroids
docs.text: The Clinton Polaroids are the photographs at the center of the surveillance scandal. On his show, David Letterman reveals that they were taken with a Russian camera, which is news to the Biz. See the Clinton Surveillance Scandal. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Creature Blood Sample
docs.text: After Kurt shoots the pale creature in the hidden mineshaft, the team collects a small ring-bagged blood sample, among the evidence handed to McManley. McManley complains the round was too small a caliber. Dante notes a blinking red light on it and wonders whether it is a bioweapon. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Creature Remains
docs.text: The Claymore blast beneath Spud Hut leaves gore and bone fragments in the hallway. Dante concludes that Spud Hut is cloning an army of chimp-men, and Rita suggests they are replacing human labor in the mine. The Claymore itself is described at Claymore Mine. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Dog Whistle
docs.text: Kurt blows a dog whistle at the creatures in the break room as an improvised light-and-sound weapon. One creature punches it into his throat, and the shriek agitates the others. Kurt clears it before the creatures close in. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Eviction Letters
docs.text: Mother Dahlia Riversand shows the team copies of the Covenant's eviction letters, kept for a lawyer. They name only the law firm Jackson and Lee's, not its client, and Kurt takes notes. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Flash-paper Instructions
docs.text: The Biz's dead-drop bag holds thin burn-after-reading flash paper telling him to install the camera in room 111 of the Smith Hotel before midnight, retrieve it 24 hours later and mail the undeveloped film to an address to be supplied. The rest of the team is not told. See Room 111. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Forklift
docs.text: Kurt hotwires a forklift in the Spud Hut basement (Act Under Pressure 7, with a penalty because he must keep a hand in the wiring) and uses it to ram a flimsy door and the elevator's security grate. He later raises the tines to stand on them. The braided cable that would release the elevator's shutter stays twenty-five feet out of reach. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Frederick's Game Boy
docs.text: The gray Game Boy that the German boy Frederick was playing in the Consolidated Gold Mine is found bleeping on the floor when he vanishes, one of the few traces left. His mother later says he was playing his video game when she heard a clatter. See Frederick. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Frequencies Bracelet
docs.text: Andrew wears a bracelet from his doctor that he says is "more just frequencies." He puts it on Kurt as a focus and uses Lay on Hands, which heals Kurt's 2 harm but gives Andrew a massive nosebleed. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Gold Nugget
docs.text: Kurt lifts a small gold nugget from the freshly dug 10-to-15-foot shaft bridged by two-by-fours in the hidden tunnel. It is kept and photographed as evidence. See Gold Bars. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Green Garbage Bag
docs.text: The Motel and Suites clerk warns the team never to open the green garbage bag in the dumpster, which holds linens from a porn shoot booked under the name Jenny Maxine. It is left unopened. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Hooper's Business Card
docs.text: Eduardo Hooper hands Kurt a business card as a contact for "dangerous" 1960s chemistry sets, including ones with uranium, which he sells from a storage facility. The Biz already has one. See Eduardo Hooper. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Hotel Master Key
docs.text: The Smith Hotel desk clerk lends the Biz a master key that opens any room, to be returned afterward. The Biz uses it to enter room 111 and plant the spy camera and microphone. See Smith Hotel Desk Clerk. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Huell's Dragon Knife
docs.text: Huell replaces his knife with an embarrassingly large one, engraved with a dragon on the hilt and marked "Nippon Steel." (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Hunters' BBS Card
docs.text: The Circle Chasers give Kurt a card with the number of their bulletin board system in exchange for his pager number. See The Circle Chasers. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Ivermectin Bottles
docs.text: Huell finds three or four ivermectin bottles in McManley's bathroom, all but one used, left from the worm infection after Marblehead. The drug is described at Ivermectin. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Kurt's Escape Kit
docs.text: Kurt's escape kit holds makeup, prosthetics, wigs, sunglasses, several outfits and forged credentials from several countries, including fake press IDs for four countries and a "Brazil" ID. His original kit was irradiated with the old car, so he fetches his complete backup from home, rolling 12 on Preparedness. He uses it to disguise Andrew and hands out Hawaiian shirts as "urban camo." (Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Kurt's Shoe
docs.text: At Spud Hut Corporate, Kurt props the "break room" door open with his shoe. When the arm reaches out, the door sticks on the shoe, and Kurt shoots it through the gap. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Luminol and UV Light
docs.text: Kurt passes a Preparedness roll (Sharp) to have his forensic kit of luminol and a UV light when the team's night vision is stuck in the decontaminated car. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Newspaper Bigfoot Photo
docs.text: The Dahlonega Times photograph is a blurry, Patterson-Gimlin-style shot credited to Charlie Briggs. Huell's Investigate a Mystery (10) says it could be a man in an ape suit, and Kurt rates it about 50th percentile for faking. See The Bigfoot Hoax. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Plaster Bigfoot Molds
docs.text: At Comstock's land, Ezra's roll finds a snapped plaster-of-Paris toe and fake Bigfoot prints in the mud. The molds themselves are missing, so someone cleaned up after the killing. Earlier, the team found two suspiciously clean giant footprints, a sneaker edge and a cigarette butt near the circle site. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Severed Ape Hand
docs.text: Andrew pries the severed hand of Big Bob off Huell and keeps it as a trophy. Kurt warns it is bad luck. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Snakeskin Cowboy Boots
docs.text: The dead drifter's snakeskin cowboy boots identify his bag in the Motel and Suites dumpster. One holds a coil of animal hair and the other a walkie-talkie. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: String Bean's Uniform
docs.text: A spare uniform belonging to the absent deputy String Bean is lent to Andrew as part of his disguise at Spud Hut Corporate. It is ruined in the fight below. See String Bean. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Walkie-talkie
docs.text: The walkie-talkie is the dead drifter's radio, hidden in a snakeskin boot. Kurt records its frequency to catch any contact with the man's associates. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Women's Shelter Cards
docs.text: Kurt carries a stack of women's-shelter hotline cards and presses them on Covenant women, including Clover, River and Jeremy. Clover is unmoved ("We're getting a boiler"). (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Yeti Fur
docs.text: Andrew digs up a handful of white Yeti fur he forgot to turn in, and a clump of it, still slightly bloody, falls to the floor of the Oval Office. See Andrew's Satchel. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Minor items and artifacts: Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable (non-canon one-shot)
docs.text:
Non-canon

These items appear only in Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, a non-canon one-shot presented as an in-universe anime OVA. Nothing here is part of the main campaign's continuity.

Minor items of the one-shot, in alphabetical order.

docs.title: Mirabeth's Business Cards
docs.text: Cards that Mirabeth presses on other trainers' fighters in the briefing tent as part of her poaching, and on Addison at the social. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Presidential Seal Sticker
docs.text: A token the werewolf president gives Derk to "show that you met me," after praising his flag and saying privately that turning into a dog is pretty cool. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The $100 Bill and the $2
docs.text: The cash for Derk's hot dogs at Miguel's stand. Mirabeth hands Derk the money so that he can pay, and he hands over $100 for hot dogs that cost a dollar each. The honest vendor returns 98 hot dogs plus $2. The $2 later pays for the video call Derk makes to Mirabeth at 2 a.m. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The Bent Quarter
docs.text: A roped-area guard asks Derk to show his kung fu and hands him a quarter. Derk bends it between two fingers ("Iron fist"), putting a ninety-degree twist in it. He still has the coin at the end of the one-shot, having straightened it out. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Video Phones
docs.text: Street-corner video phones with a map application that shows satellite photography. This world has no cell phones, so Mirabeth uses one to call her bridge-club friend, and she has an in-home one on which she takes Derk's late-night call. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Minor items and artifacts: Radford (The Radford Horror and The Radford Horrors)
docs.text: This page lists the minor objects, evidence and gear of the two Radford arcs.

docs.title: Alien-abduction illustration book
docs.text: Andrew finds a book of amateur drawings, many of naked women, hidden under Abe's bed at the Whateley house. (Radford Horror 02) See Abelforth Whateley and Whateley house.

docs.title: Andrew's blood supply
docs.text: Andrew carries a maroon powder of dried pig blood, which he passes off as a "protein mix"; airport security swabs it in Radford Horrors 02. In Radford Horrors 04 the cover story is a Gatorade-and-blood slurry. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04) See Andrew's Condition and Airport security agents.

docs.title: Annabelle
docs.text: Annabelle is Freak's plane, a baby-blue, house-painted Cessna with a disco ball and black lights. Its fuel line is dirty, and the fix is a kick to a panel. (Radford Horror 07) See Freak.

docs.title: Autopsy blood samples
docs.text: Amanda's autopsy blood contains about 5 percent unidentified foreign matter, and the samples are sent for an analysis that takes weeks. (Radford Horror 06) See Amanda Lucky and Dr. Harvey Mauden.

docs.title: Barn notepad
docs.text: A notepad in Derek Augustine's converted barn holds plot notes and dates labeled with acronyms. Kurt copies the notes and takes discarded manuscript pages. (Radford Horror 03) See Augustine house and barn.

docs.title: Black Super Soaker
docs.text: Kurt's spray-painted Super Soaker is filled with glow-stick fluid and is used to mark the craft. (Radford Horror 06) See The Radford Moth.

docs.title: Brown station wagon
docs.text: A witness says the fishing-hat man, Red Dutchford, arrived in a station wagon, and the players recall that Dr. Lori drove one too. (Radford Horror 04) See Red Dutchford and Dr. Lawrence Lori.

docs.title: Convoy weapons
docs.text: During the Moscow convoy ambush the Biz takes weapons from the trunk, including a grenade launcher and an AK. (Radford Horrors 03) See Convoy ambushers.

docs.title: DMT pipe
docs.text: The DMT pipe is a Jack Daniel's bottle fashioned into a pipe, obtained from Rutherford, who sells the contents as "Dimitri"; he says it is heated with a lighter and inhaled. (Radford Horror 04) See Rutherford.

docs.title: Dog map
docs.text: Huell's tourist map from the Pay n' Stay is marked in Sharpie with every missing-dog house bordering the woods. (Radford Horror 02) See Radford's missing dogs.

docs.title: Dog skull
docs.text: A week-old, poodle-like skull, cracked and gouged, is found with its spine in the woods. Kurt keeps the skull. (Radford Horror 05) See Kurt's cooler.

docs.title: Elderly couple's diesel car
docs.text: The team commandeers the elderly couple's old diesel sedan, an "old lady Benz" that tops out at 70 miles per hour. It ends the chase with a dented hood, a cracked windshield and a torn-off rearview mirror. (Radford Horror 03) See Howard and his wife.

docs.title: Ephedrine and Mandrax jars
docs.text: Half-gallon jars of ephedrine and Mandrax with white duct-tape labels, one half full and one quarter full, are found in a hidden cabinet in the barbershop. They are "stakeout candy" and are left behind. (Radford Horror 01) See D.C. barbershop.

docs.title: Everclear
docs.text: Huell brings Everclear, which becomes the Molotov that burns the creature at the church. (Radford Horror 07) See Old-town church.

docs.title: Field medical kit
docs.text: The ER doctor gives Kurt a cooler of loaded syringes, iodine swabs and gloves to treat Andrew. (Radford Horrors 03) See Rabies treatment protocol.

docs.title: Flash Gordon pinball machine
docs.text: The Flash Gordon machine is popular but fragile, and Elizabeth George was repairing it when she was taken. (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04) See Douglas Pinball Emporium and Elizabeth George.

docs.title: Hollowed-out Where the Sidewalk Ends
docs.text: A hollowed-out copy of Where the Sidewalk Ends in Abe's room holds $120 to $130. Ezra (as the Biz) declines to touch it, notes which book it is and leaves the cash in place. (Radford Horror 02) See Radio Shack spacesuit robbery.

docs.title: Irene's Prozac and lithium
docs.text: Expired Prozac and lithium prescriptions written by Dr. Lori, with leftover pills, are found in the Whateley house. (Radford Horror 02) See Irene Whateley.

docs.title: Kurt's cooler
docs.text: Kurt keeps an ice cooler holding the NSA man's remains, the dog skull and a couple of beers. In Radford Horror 08 it still holds the NSA man's skull; his badge looks genuine, but no one in the records has that name. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 08) See Agent Murphy.

docs.title: Kurt's grenade
docs.text: Kurt pulls a grenade as a dead man's switch during the IRS raid and re-pins it, bending the pin. He then uses it as a "fidget". (Radford Horrors 02) See IRS Criminal Investigations.

docs.title: Kurt's hollow teeth
docs.text: Kurt has hollow molars that hold drugs. One holds LSD, which he bites and spits at Murphy; another holds a stimulant, giving +1 forward and a temporary -1 harm, with two molars left. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 07) See Kurt Larson.

docs.title: Letter on Elizabeth's door
docs.text: A letter left in place by Douglas on Elizabeth George's door states that she is in inpatient psychiatric treatment in Los Angeles. (Radford Horrors 03) See LA treatment cover story.

docs.title: Live radio bug
docs.text: The Biz's transmitter is hidden behind the flag patch of the handmade spacesuit and tuned in by radio. It is silent overnight. (Radford Horror 06) See Spaceman suit.

docs.title: Marcus Heat novels
docs.text: Marcus Heat is the pen name of Derek Augustine, and his romance novels are something Howard wants to find. (Radford Horror 05) See Derek Augustine.

docs.title: Missing posters and lawyers' number
docs.text: Molly gives the team six missing-person posters with a lawyers' phone number written on the file. (Radford Horrors 02) See The scary lawyers.

docs.title: Missing-dog folder
docs.text: The sheriff's folder of large-dog complaints, annotated "Perverts???", goes back a couple of years and spikes over the previous six to eight months. (Radford Horror 02) See Radford's missing dogs.

docs.title: Night-vision and bugging gear
docs.text: The Biz's stakeout kit includes a monocular night-vision scope and a small spy camera in his overnight bag; Huell carries the scope and returns it greasy. The scope is later shared around the ground team. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 06) See Dick Baxter.

docs.title: Partial fingerprint
docs.text: A partial fingerprint is lifted from Dutchford's wiped room, to be compared with prints from Lori's office. (Radford Horror 04) See Red Dutchford.

docs.title: Pay n' Stay tourist map
docs.text: The Pay n' Stay's tourist map is marked with the Lawson cabin and the bearings of the craft's flight lines. In Radford Horror 07 the intersecting lines are used to find the church and give coordinates. (Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07) See Pay n' Stay.

docs.title: Pesticide
docs.text: Kurt's pesticide is juvenile hormone plus nicotine, in gallons, and he sprays it in both motel rooms during the rodent crisis. Mammals are unaffected. (Radford Horrors 02) See Pay n' Stay.

docs.title: Polaroid of Phoebe's night dress
docs.text: A Polaroid of Phoebe's night dress is given to Kurt for the APB. (Radford Horror 05) See Phoebe Augustine.

docs.title: Prescription pad
docs.text: The Biz steals a prescription pad from Dr. Lori's office to fake a junkie break-in. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05) See Dr. Lori's office.

docs.title: President's medical cooler
docs.text: The Russian president's medical cooler in the convoy trunk holds dry ice, blood bags, biologics and anti-nerve-agent drugs with Russian labels. It is used to carry the ibuprofen. (Radford Horrors 03) See Boris Yeltsin.

docs.title: Radford case files
docs.text: The first case folder, with the spaceman sketch, is delivered to Andrew by a courier. By 1993 the FBI and local versions of the case disagree. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horrors 02) See FBI courier.

docs.title: Radio Shack case file
docs.text: The paper file on Abe's break-in describes a cinder-block break-in, the spacesuit, fingerprints from heavy gear, stolen modems and a cell phone, and a bus ticket to Richmond. (Radford Horror 02) See Radio Shack spacesuit robbery.

docs.title: Rooftop man's device
docs.text: The rooftop watcher carries a briefcase with a flashlight and a small electronic device, which he keys in the cold open before a white van appears. (Radford Horror 02) See Rooftop watcher.

docs.title: Russian-style suit
docs.text: The Biz receives an expensive, fitted suit with a longer coat, which fits perfectly, for the opera. (Radford Horrors 01) See Russian officer.

docs.title: Swapped security tape
docs.text: The Pinball Emporium's porch camera tape is replaced by the kidnappers, so the original footage is gone. (Radford Horrors 03) See Douglas Pinball Emporium and Diner security tape.

docs.title: Taser tine
docs.text: Kurt finds a broken Taser prong with blood in the carpet at the emporium, evidence along with missing towels and a first-aid kit. (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04) See Gray van crew.

docs.title: The Biz's gold, cash and cocaine
docs.text: The Biz leaves behind a full gold share, about two-thirds of the original find, about $8,000 to $9,000 in Ziplocs and cocaine, all hidden under a floorboard of his apartment. The Roulet Estate 03 epilogue had instead had the other agents bury his share in a park near his home. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01) See The Biz's apartment.

docs.title: Tinfoil welding mask
docs.text: Kurt's tinfoil-lined welding mask is his improvised mind shield, logged with balaclavas, night vision, a dog whistle and bolt cutters before the climax. (Radford Horror 07) See Old-town church.

docs.title: U-Haul-branded van
docs.text: A U-Haul-branded van, smaller than the earlier white van, is the vehicle Derek Augustine uses to abduct Dr. Lori. (Radford Horror 06) See Derek Augustine.

docs.title: Unopened FBI mail
docs.text: Unopened FBI mail in the Biz's apartment includes leave-of-absence paperwork for a family emergency, apparently a cover. (Radford Horrors 01) See Apartment office staff.

docs.title: Webster's recording gear
docs.text: Webster records everything, with a tape recorder, camera and camcorder that he leaves running overnight. (Radford Horrors 02) See Daniel Webster.

docs.title: Window AC units
docs.text: Two window air conditioners are bought for the office with drug money, and they flicker the lights. (Radford Horror 08) See Dean Lawson's heroin and cash.

docs.title: Wolf piss
docs.text: Wolf urine is Huell's prized cargo, and the reason is never stated. (Radford Horror 08) See Huell Kendrick.

docs.title: Woods blood sample and dress scrap
docs.text: Blood from the woods is given to Dr. Mauden for a toxicology match and a species test, along with a dress scrap from a branch. (Radford Horror 05) See Dr. Harvey Mauden.

docs.title: WTC and Oklahoma City postcards
docs.text: Huell's ironic decor includes postcards of the World Trade Center and the Alfred P. Murrah Federal Building. (Radford Horror 01) See Huell Kendrick.

docs.title: Minor items and artifacts: The Roulet Estate
docs.text: Minor items of The Roulet Estate, in alphabetical order. Larger objects of the arc have their own pages, including the Foil-Wrapped Letter, the VSS Rifle, the Wedding Photos, the Visitation Tapes, the Green Slurry, the Beta Blockers, the Attic Polaroids, the Mosin-Nagant, the Foam-Latex Alien Mask and The Agents' Car.

docs.title: Andrew's Pager
docs.text: Andrew Howard's pager, which shows the last page he received. That page came from a number he does not recognize, and it is never traced. It fits with Diane's account that Andrew took a call at the bar before the trip. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Andrew's Polaroid Camera
docs.text: A Polaroid camera that Andrew pulls from his satchel when the Grey appears on the roof, kept alongside three treasured Polaroids of the UFOs over Ballard. He is too starstruck to use it on the Grey, but in Roulet Estate 02 he takes flashlight Polaroids of the corpse parts brought up from the basement and of the hidden attic lair. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02) See also Andrew's satchel.

docs.title: Black 9mm Pistol
docs.text: The pistol clutched in the intruder's left hand against the steering wheel in the cold open of Roulet Estate 03. The intruder sits in the agents' stolen car, humming along to "Radar Love" and tapping his fingers on the dashboard as the fuel needle dips into the red. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Brick Cellphone
docs.text: The big cellular phone that the businessman hostage carries out of the Brooks pharmacy so that the agents can call the gunman. The number is 401-998-3147. Andrew Howard stalls by pretending to have dialed a wrong number, then calls as Special Agent Howard and plays dumb about vehicle brands, until the gunman cuts his deadline to two minutes. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Briefcase of Cash
docs.text: A briefcase of money found in the hidden attic lair, looking as though it was being packed and then abruptly abandoned. The agents bag the cash along with the guns and valuables and carry it down the chimney so the intruder cannot use it. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Butterfly Knife
docs.text: A butterfly knife crusted with blood, in an ornate case beside a boarded-over attic vent in the lair. Andre tells Andrew the blood is months old, and the find, with the photos on the walls, strikes him as the most serial-killer material he has ever seen. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Cocoa-Butter Jar
docs.text: A huge glass jar of cocoa-butter lotion among the cleaning supplies in the basement, with a hand-shaped scoop taken out of it. The agents joke that someone has psoriasis. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Dunhill Lighter and Cigar Cutter
docs.text: A Dunhill lighter and cigar cutter that Andrew Howard found at a pawn shop or thrift store as his Secret Santa gift to Huell Kendrick at the Christmas Eve party. (Roulet Estate 01) See also Christmas Eve Secret Santa.

docs.title: Dusty Stetson
docs.text: A dusty Stetson hat. In the cold open of Roulet Estate 01 the Biz crawls three feet across the floor of the abandoned living room and vomits into it. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Fake Alien Fetus Jar
docs.text: Kurt Larson's Secret Santa gift to Andrew, from a flea market: a fake alien fetus, a monkey sewn to an octopus, in a jar with a visibly bulging lid and a distinct coleslaw odor. Rita (as Andrew) shakes it and remarks, "Baby's fermenting." Diane says it is the grossest thing she has ever seen and tells the agents they are the weirdest cops. (Roulet Estate 01) See also Christmas Eve Secret Santa.

docs.title: Fake ID
docs.text: Huell Kendrick's Secret Santa gift to the Biz: the identification of a recently deceased man who looks something like him. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Frozen Blood Shipments
docs.text: Human blood mailed weekly to Andrew in dry ice, disguised as frozen orange juice. In the epilogue Andrew thaws it in a Brita pitcher in his New York hotel and, after watching Roseanne, raises a glass of it to his lips. The shipments come from his doctor. (Roulet Estate 03) See also Andrew's Doctor and Andrew's Condition.

docs.title: Herman Miller NSA Chair
docs.text: A Herman Miller chair stamped "Property of the National Security Agency," which Kurt steals as his gift for Diane. He admits it is a little used but points out that new it costs about eight grand. Diane says she will set her old chair on fire at the curb, and Kurt agrees they will have to "for the bugs." (Roulet Estate 01) See also Unnamed NSA Agent.

docs.title: Marked-Up Map
docs.text: A marked-up map found in the agents' car. Together with Diane's testimony, it convinces Andrew that the agents are at the right address. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Mr. Roulet's Gun Collection
docs.text: The firearms collection looted from the weapons closet and stored in the attic lair, including a Kalashnikov and Russian World War II pistols, many of them loaded. The agents reason that it explains why the intruder shoots a VSS, and they bag the guns and lower them down the chimney into the house. (Roulet Estate 02) See also Mr. Roulet.

docs.title: Mystery Government Files Floppy
docs.text: A floppy disk labelled in Sharpie "Mystery Government Files," the Biz's Secret Santa gift to Kurt. The label sets off Kurt's "schizophrenic detector," and the disk is never read on screen. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Riding Lawnmower
docs.text: A riding mower in the Roulet barn, the exact model Kurt owns at home, with a top speed of about 8 mph. Squirrels have chewed some of the wiring, but Kurt gets it started. The Biz asks about modifying it, and Andre rules that only a perfect 12 on a Sharp check would do it without breaking the mower or hurting himself. Ezra suggests sending it off as a decoy with a brick on the pedal and a scarecrow aboard. The agents reject it as transport because it is loud, can only go on the road and cannot carry everyone. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: The Biz's Flask and Lighter
docs.text: The vodka flask and lighter that supply Kurt's smoke screen at the Brooks pharmacy. With a shot-out tire and a bag of stale donuts from the squad car, he builds a smoke bomb: the Biz's vodka goes on the tire, which is lit with his lighter. The smoke comes out slowly and thickens gradually. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The Georgia Gold
docs.text: The gold nuggets that the Biz brought back from Georgia during The Things in Appalachia. He gives one to the Salvation Army carolers in Roulet Estate 01, and complains that no one will accept nuggets as currency. In Roulet Estate 03 the table establishes that the team split the gold equally and that, after the Biz vanished, the other agents buried his share in a park near his house and left him a cryptic message. In Radford Horrors 01 his whole share is instead found under a floorboard in his apartment. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01) See also The Biz's Apartment and Buried Gold.

docs.title: The Roulets' Notebook
docs.text: A partly coded notebook found in the house's library, among UFO and Scientology material. It logs months of incidents ending in fall 1992: lights flying over the house, lost time, figures in the woods, the feeling of being watched, objects moved or taken. After a successful roll Andrew concludes that the owners were a husband and wife, and that the wife was more of a true believer. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Utah White Powder
docs.text: The powder that covered the Guardsmen in Roosevelt, Utah, during The Walkers in Skin. In the flashback to the medical tent, McManley reports that it is a cocktail of benzos plus something still unidentified, sedatives and hypnotics, which turns out to be a mild amnesiac that erased about twenty hours of memory for most of the soldiers. Kurt keeps a Ziploc baggy of it. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: WWII Flamethrower
docs.text: The one weapon left in the looted weapons closet, seen by Andrew when he squeezes his head and flashlight under the steel door: a World War II-era flamethrower on the rear wall. In Roulet Estate 03 a police officer reports that the pharmacy gunman has a flamethrower, a machine gun and a big rifle; it is never said whether this is the same flamethrower. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 03) See also The Weapons Closet.

docs.title: Yeltsin's Cuban Cigar
docs.text: The cigar that Boris Yeltsin cuts and lights, with a small silver lighter, for the shackled Biz before asking about the humanists. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Minor items and artifacts: The Summer Service
docs.text: These are the smaller objects of the Marblehead case: gadgets, weapons, souvenirs and clues. Bigger items have their own pages, including the M28 Davy Crockett, the crystal marbles, ivermectin and the severed arm.

docs.title: The Biz's pocket knife
docs.text: A new carbon-steel folding knife that the Biz buys in Summer Service 01, after his tussle with the moth. He tests it on one of the crystal marbles, the blade blunts without leaving a mark, and he decides to steal the marble. See Crystal marbles. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Bug
docs.text: A listening device that the Biz plants in Madeline's house before the team leaves her there. See Madeline's house. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Casaba
docs.text: A weapon that the radio voice of the covert group says it has. He explains that it cannot be fired from the ground because it would kill the shooter and that the wind speeds are too high to fly it, so the team has to deal with the creature itself. It is never used. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Claymore
docs.text: Kurt's directional mine. He sets one on Arnold Weathers' porch aimed at the door, and in Summer Service 05 he also sets one at his hotel room door, telling the others to knock before entering. A Claymore set off on a truck in an unrecorded session is, in Andre's words, presumably the explosion that the radio voice in Summer Service 06 says "pissed it off." Compare Claymore Mine from the Things in Appalachia. (Summer Service 05; Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Experimental submarine
docs.text: The small research submarine used for the dive in the unrecorded Summer Service 02. According to Andrew's account to Big Bill in Summer Service 03, the team went down with a college researcher to see a dead body she had found, but the body was gone. While they searched, a vessel covered in lights returned, and the team shut off all power and lights and went undetected. Andrew says the vessel "hummed," and asks whether such a hum could break apart the sub they were in. See The stealth wreck and College researcher. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Fish-in-bikini ornament
docs.text: A souvenir that Andrew buys in Marblehead for his mother, a fish in a bikini staring saucily at the viewer on a bed of dancing crabs. Andre calls it "a pretty slutty fish." Andrew keeps it on his nightstand, where it is the first thing he sees when the voice wakes him, and Ezra later tells him to "make peace with your fish god." (Summer Service 04; Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Ford Pinto
docs.text: The getaway car that the team steals in the finale: a Ford Pinto with a lift kit and flames painted on the side, which Dante jokes juxtaposes well with the molten swipes the creature has taken out of it. See The nuclear power plant. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Geiger counter
docs.text: Part of the team's gear in the trunk of their car. As they leave, it is going wild, and Andre says that it barely registered when the nuke was fired and began going off only when the creature died. The team leaves it behind with the rest of their radioactive gear. See Stolen FBI car. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Hand grenades
docs.text: Kurt decides in Summer Service 04 to carry two hand grenades in his fanny pack, convinced that there is a conspiracy in town, and he makes room by dumping his interagency loan paperwork. He brings them to the town hall because he trusts no one there. In Summer Service 05 Madeline asks for a grenade and is refused. (Summer Service 04; Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Hydraulic tripod gun
docs.text: Also called the boat gun. An exotic oval-barreled gun on a tripod, bolted to the deck and built around hydraulic recoil absorbers, with a thermal scope on its side. It is used by the crew in the cold open of Radford Horror 08. See Boat crew. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Kurt's gear
docs.text: Also called the caltrops, steel plate, flamethrower and amphetamine tooth. Before the nuke shot in the finale, the team unloads the old car into the new one, including Kurt's caltrops, steel plate and flamethrower. Kurt pops his amphetamine tooth to clear the -1 that his chicken pox has been giving him, and he uses it again later on the drive home. Dante explains that Kurt has to have his teeth redone between missions, because he used both his LSD and amphetamine teeth. (Radford Horror 08; Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Lighthouse basement evidence
docs.text: Also called the ropes, teeth and chairs. In the basement below the lighthouse the team finds blood-stained ropes cut to lengths of two or three feet, two teeth (a canine and an incisor), a field notebook with EPA branding, and two bloody chairs set out in the middle of the room, along with smashed bulbs and mirrors. It suggests that one of the missing scientists was beaten there. See The lighthouse. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Molotov cocktail
docs.text: Kurt teaches Madeline to make one before the team leaves her house, explaining that guns are not that effective against what is out there. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Muriel
docs.text: Huell's favorite knife, which Zack names on the spot after Huell's wife. He gives it to Madeline when the team leaves her. See Madeline Weathers. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Rice jar of worms
docs.text: Also called the mason jar. Huell empties a rice jar from the pantry to collect samples of the worms from the bathroom. A line about it later becomes a table joke from Zack: "their god's definitely real, I have a mason jar full of it right here." See The worms. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Spy radio
docs.text: A bugged radio that the team finds in their car before Summer Service 03. It leads them to avoid using the car radio and to proceed with caution. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Statesman's Journal
docs.text: The Salem newspaper that the Biz buys at Readful Things as cover. Its front page carries the nuclear plant protests and the fish die-off. See Seabrook nuclear plant. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Stolen FBI car
docs.text: The team's FBI car, which Rita says Jester carjacked from them. In the finale the Biz spots it one row from the rear of the convoy and is about eighty percent sure it is theirs. Its tire burns out during the chase, and the team abandons it. See Jester. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Toilet tank lid
docs.text: Andrew's improvised weapon against the man in the alley outside the hotel bathroom window. He drops from the window holding it, hits the man on the head and badly twists his own ankle. See Toilet guy. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Welding goggles and earplugs
docs.text: The Biz buys four pairs of welding goggles and a box of earplugs in Summer Service 04. In the finale he explains he had a bad feeling about looking directly at a nuke, even a little one, and the team brings them along. During the Davy Crockett shot something extremely bright happens, even through the goggles, and the person firing is briefly struck blind by stars in their eyes. (Summer Service 04; Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Minor items and artifacts: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text: This page lists the minor objects of The Walkers in Skin; larger items include Betsy, the Plymouth Voyager and the ground-penetrating radar.

docs.title: Ambushers' shotguns
docs.text: Guns taken from the roadside ambush in Walkers 08. Kurt orders the weapons confiscated, one shotgun goes to Yusuf, who has said he wants a gun, and another is used to open the lock of the morgue cabinet. See the roadside ambushers. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Ape gold
docs.text: Gold taken from the party's previous investigation, which Andre describes as one large sock full of gold sitting at the D.C. office. In Walkers 06 the Biz raises it as a way to pay the $10,000 fine offered for the Voyager. See Jan's Conspiracy. (Walkers 03, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Best of Queen tape
docs.text: Kurt's Best of Queen cassette, which comes through the wreck of the Voyager physically intact but plays only static. Queen is also the "music" that Sheriff McDermish mistakenly reports as a noise complaint in Walkers 03. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Bone saw
docs.text: A saw that Kurt fetches from the morgue cabinet at the Roosevelt police station so that McManley can carry out an autopsy. See the Roosevelt police station. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Car phone request
docs.text: A request for a car phone, filed with the Bureau and still pending in Walkers 03. In Walkers 08 the lack of one hurts: with the rental destroyed, the team has no car phone or satellite phone, and their walkie-talkies cannot reach Salt Lake City. (Walkers 03, Walkers 08)

docs.title: Cats costumes
docs.text: School fundraiser costumes that are in the trunk of the loaner squad car Betsy, and which Walt identifies as Cats costumes from Roosevelt's drama department (they "sewed a butthole onto each one"). Huell buries one to calibrate the ground-penetrating radar, and the costumes are still in the car in Walkers 07 and 08. See the Roosevelt high school drama department. (Walkers 04, Walkers 05, Walkers 07, Walkers 08)

docs.title: Ceramic frog
docs.text: A ceramic frog that hides the keys to the ranch's guest double-wide in Walkers 02. In the cold open of Walkers 06, a ceramic frog hides the spare key to Doug's trailer. (Walkers 02, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Cocaine in shoe heel
docs.text: Kurt's stash, hidden in the heel of a shoe. During the night event it is used as a dental anesthetic for the Biz, and Kurt takes some himself. See the night event. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Dead coyote
docs.text: A coyote shot at the school and kept in Bigelow's emptied porch beer cooler, with ice and bricks on the lid, for McManley to examine. Kurt finds it clean and groomed, with no ticks or wounds apart from the bullet, and jokes that the Mormons are training coyotes. See upright coyotes. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: Drinking fountain test kits
docs.text: FBI kits for testing the water from Ballard's fountains. Gardner asks for another kit over the intercom. See Ballard water contamination. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: FBI case file
docs.text: Gardner's copy of the earlier local reports on the ranch, covering lost time, the Ranger's shooting and the mutilations. The party is meant to check it back in, and has not read it yet when it is handed over. See livestock mutilations. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: French Toast Castle
docs.text: The Good Hills Diner's eight-inch tower of French toast, held together with toothpicks and drowned in syrup. Andrew eats only an embarrassingly small portion and is warned it will ruin his day. The leftovers, taken in a to-go box, are used as bait for the goose, who eats them. See Good Hills Diner and Nancy the goose. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Gold fillings
docs.text: Replacement fillings for the Biz, who loses every filling in the night event. The Roosevelt dentist has only gold on hand, which is non-magnetic. The Biz notes the fit with his nickname and his watch. See the Roosevelt dentist. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Goosebumps books
docs.text: The reading of the teenage intruders in the barn: Welcome to Dead House, Monster Blood and Stay Out of the Basement. They belong to Harrison. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Grenade
docs.text: A grenade produced from Andrew's bag in the gym. It kills horses and townsfolk and wounds both Andrew and his double. The duplicate later describes it to the others as "leverage that went off." See Andrew's bag and Ballard High School. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: Hooster's package
docs.text: A flat-rate package of gadgets that the Biz orders from Hooster: a net gun, thermite and a bomb collar, for use against the goose. In Walkers 05 Dante recalls that the order has been placed. (Walkers 04, Walkers 05)

docs.title: Howard's camera and photographs
docs.text: Andrew's habit of photographing every scene. In Walkers 03 he records the sky, scorch marks, tire tracks, the substation, fences and the community center site. In Walkers 07 the lens is smashed in the gym. In Walkers 08 he photographs the ambush scene, the dead officers and the prisoners, and in Walkers 09 the real Howard takes dozens of blurry Polaroids of the hazmat crews and the black craft. (Walkers 03, Walkers 07, Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Howard's Fossil watch
docs.text: Andrew's 1990s Fossil high-beat mechanical watch, with glow-in-the-dark hands. It keeps working through the dusk event, unlike the battery and digital watches of his companions. See the dusk event. (Walkers 03)

docs.title: Howard's jacket
docs.text: Andrew's jacket, stolen and worn by the goose. Walt says that letting the goose take it "shows weak," and Andrew remarks that she is "in a lovely jacket now." See Nancy the goose. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Huell's walkie-talkie
docs.text: A police-model handset, probably a Motorola, whose proprietary battery has gone missing. In Walkers 09 Andre tells Huell that the battery is missing, and the table discusses where a replacement could be found. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Joke pen
docs.text: A pen from the front desk of the Roosevelt police station that Huell gives to Yusuf. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Kurt's shovel
docs.text: A shovel that Kurt brings along for the exhumation; it was previously used on Chester. See the exhumation of Shelly Wilmarth. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Kurt's stilts
docs.text: Kurt's Vietnam-era pair, carrying shrapnel, is lost with the Voyager and later recovered from the wreck. A spare pair turns up in the trunk of Betsy, and the party uses them to open a door and pry at the goose. (Walkers 04, Walkers 05)

docs.title: Kurt's watch
docs.text: A small gear-driven battery watch that stops at the dusk event. In Walkers 06 Kurt takes it apart and holds the pieces out to the beam, which sends them rocketing upward. See the beam. (Walkers 03, Walkers 06)

docs.title: LSD tooth
docs.text: Kurt's dental capsule, which shifts his cognition when he bites it during the night event. See the night event. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Mud room key
docs.text: The key that the naked intruder used on the ranch's back door. Andrew keeps it, and it suggests that someone holds keys to the estate. See the naked intruder. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: Plastic FBI badge
docs.text: The Biz's toy badge, which he uses to apply pressure to the people he questions. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Remington Model 870
docs.text: The sheriff's Vietnam-era shotgun, which Sheriff McDermish gives to Kurt before fleeing Ballard. It is listed among the party's weapons in Walkers 07. (Walkers 06, Walkers 07)

docs.title: Roosevelt police cruiser
docs.text: An abandoned cruiser, in better condition than Betsy, parked in the rocks by the ambush site. It is the source of the spike strip, and the party uses it to carry the ambush bodies. Its radio hears nothing on any preset channel. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Sheriff's names list
docs.text: A Post-it note listing absent families and their addresses, which Sheriff McDermish hands to Kurt. See disappearances in Ballard. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Spike strip
docs.text: A spike strip taken from the roadside ambush. It came from the empty Roosevelt police cruiser parked in the rocks, and Kurt orders it confiscated. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: The Biz's Casio
docs.text: The Biz's cheap digital watch, whose seven-segment display is left permanently scrambled by the dusk event. See the dusk event. (Walkers 03)

docs.title: Missing agents' map
docs.text:
The missing agents' map is a map of the woods around Radford, found in the missing FBI team's abandoned camp, marked with irregular polygons and one illegible scribble.

Type Item (map) Holder Huell Kendrick Status Led the team to the Safe Environment Fund fence First appearance Radford Horrors 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The map shows the woods with a number of irregular polygons drawn over it and an illegible scribble beside the boundary of one of them. It was found in the administrative tent of the missing FBI task force at their campsite at the Sportsman RV Campground (Radford Horrors 02). It is separate from the ordinary tourist map the team had of the area.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The team treated the scribble as the place the missing agents had been heading. The team's own route did not correspond to the polygons at first, but following the new fence they came to an older fence that lined up with one face of a polygon on the map. They reasoned that the newer fence went up after the agents vanished, so the agents had probably gone straight to the scribble (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Huell cut open the locked tents and made an Investigate a Mystery roll (11). He found no sign that the agents had left in a hurry, a bag of molding laundry by the clothesline, and accommodations for five agents (two tents, with three cots and two, plus an administrative tent). In the administrative tent he found the map and took it; Andre described it appearing on screen and being put away in the manner of Resident Evil. The agents' car was still in the lot with two shotguns locked in the trunk, and Kurt's luminol found only a nosebleed's worth of blood on a pillow. A radioed report a week earlier had said they were "chasing up some weird stuff" (Radford Horrors 02).

Following the map toward the scribble, the team met an eight-foot chain-link fence topped with barbed wire and wrapped in a printed polymer sheet bearing the Safe Environment Fund logo, with solar lights staked in the trees. The team climbed it, and guards on ATVs confronted them. Webster was tased, Andrew shot a guard in the leg, and the bullet the guard fired at him stopped an inch from his chest (Radford Horrors 02).

At the scribble itself, Kurt found a smell of bleach, patches of dug-up ground and a tree that had been cut down and removed that day. Luminol showed nothing, and Andre told the players that whoever did this was no amateur and that a shootout had probably happened there. The team took samples of the cleaned areas and of the pearlescent goo on a high branch. See also the SEF fenced site and the Safe Environment Fund (Radford Horrors 02).

The fallout was the Bivens lawsuit. In Radford Horrors 03, FBI Director Rudy Giuliani phoned Webster about the fence. He said a Bivens suit was expected, that the FBI was seeking a retroactive warrant to cover the search, and that a formal reprimand was possible if the probable cause claim could not be defended. He added that it would be a different story had the team actually found the missing agents (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The missing agents' fate is not resolved by anything on the map; it only shows where they were headed.

docs.title: Mosin-Nagant
docs.text:
The Mosin-Nagant is the heavy wooden rifle that the masked Brooks pharmacy gunman uses to kill a police officer and wound the Biz and Huell.

Type Item (firearm) Aliases big wooden rifle Holder The pharmacy gunman, then the police First appearance Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Officer Todd tells the agents that the gunman has a flamethrower, a machine gun and "some kind of big rifle. Like one of them big old-fashioned wooden rifles, like the real heavy ones." The gunman also claims to have a rocket-propelled grenade, which Todd did not see. Andre names the rifle as a Mosin-Nagant when the Biz is shot (Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: As the agents arrive at the pharmacy, a shot takes off a large part of a police officer's head, which looks to the veterans among them like "too much bullet for anti-personnel operations". A second shot, fired as Kurt searches the body for the squad car's keys, hits the ground near him. In the ceiling above the pharmacy, the Biz shoots the gunman in the shoulder. The gunman fires the Mosin-Nagant up through the ceiling and hits the Biz's thigh for 3 harm, dropping him to the tile floor. When Huell tackles the gunman, another shot goes through Huell's foot for 3 harm and leaves him on 2 health (Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The episodes never say where the rifle came from. The agents had found a Kalashnikov and WWII Russian pistols in the attic lair, apparently from the gun collection emptied out of the weapons closet, and the masked man is assumed to be the lair's occupant (Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03). Huell knocks the gun out of his hands as he tackles him, ending the siege (Roulet Estate 03).

The VSS rifle from the earlier episodes is the other firearm the intruder is seen using.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Murphy's briefcase and documents
docs.text:
Murphy's briefcase and documents are the briefcase, fragmentary papers, wireless telegraph and NSA identification belonging to the man who called himself Agent Murphy.

Type Item (documents and props) Aliases burned papers; NSA badge; Morse telegraph Holder Agent Murphy, then the task force Status Papers and badge examined; the badge appears genuine but matches no one in the records First appearance Radford Horror 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
When the team first met Murphy on the mountain road he was clutching a flashlight-like device, and he pulled out a badge: "I'm Agent Murphy. I'm NSA. You are fucking this up for me. Get back in your car and drive away." (Andre (as Agent Murphy), Radford Horror 03). His weapon is described on the flashlight weapon page.

At the end of Radford Horror 03, in a scene the characters did not witness, the device overheated and Murphy vanished in a pulse of light. In Radford Horror 04 the team followed his blood trail to a clearing where mildly high coyotes were eating his remains: the back of a suit, the back of a skull and a little brain, on a circle of ground melted to glass. His briefcase lay beside him as a melted wad of plastic and metal, and his wallet, with an NSA ID and a little cash, was the only other possession left (Radford Horror 04).

Kurt put on a welding mask from the trunk ("Once immolated, twice shy"), and Andrew forced the warped briefcase open with a foot on the latch (Tough, 8). The scorched papers scattered everywhere, and Kurt called it "fifty-two-card pickup" (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
The contents were a melted wireless telegraph with a hand key for Morse code, and loose, badly burned typewritten pages on plain printer paper with no letterhead. Kurt checked the papers with a black light for hidden messages and found none. Andre handed the players the legible fragments, and the players read them aloud. They include "...hind Salem, Colorado"; "abstract annihilation de..."; "autonomous political assets"; "unwanted scrutiny"; "Sequence homologue"; "homologue bias"; "religious ecstasy"; "...ig Bill"; "samples"; "Unknown servitor act..."; "Acceptable leakage"; "Menelaus"; and "...tiary objective" (Radford Horror 04).

The players read "...ig Bill" as probably Big Bill and tied "servitor" and "Menelaus" to the Radford Moth (whose Latin name is Morpho menelaus) and to servitors. Kurt said the pages looked unlike any classified NSA documents he had seen. The Biz speculated that they might be deliberately planted fake data used to trace leaks, although Kurt noted that a man who fought so hard to keep them seemed unlikely to be carrying decoys (Radford Horror 04). The episodes never settle whether the documents are genuine.

docs.title: The badge
docs.text: In Radford Horror 08, Kurt used his illegal contact to check the NSA badge (Manipulate Someone, 9). The result came back weeks later, after the team returned to D.C.: the badge was not a counterfeit, but no one with that name existed in the records, and if it was a forgery it was the best the examiners had ever seen. Kurt's reaction was "I didn't kill an NSA agent, officially." He planned to pull the teeth from the skull in his cooler, keeping them for identification, and dissolve the rest in acid (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The Biz's Night-vision Goggles
docs.text:
The Biz's Night-vision Goggles are Dick Baxter's night-vision monocular, a PVS-7. State police find it in the bushes outside the Smith Hotel, and it feeds the surveillance scandal that makes the Biz "the most hated cop in America".

Type Item (equipment) Aliases night vision headset; PVS-7 monocular Owner Dick "The Biz" Baxter (played by Ezra) Value Roughly $4,500, according to Ezra Found by Georgia State Police First appearance Appalachia 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The goggles are a night-vision headset or monocular. In the Walkers 01 epilogue, Ezra names the model as a PVS-7 and puts its price at roughly $4,500, "pretty nice used car money" in the nineties. The Biz says that the last time he saw them they were in a case in the trunk of his car. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: The cold open
docs.text: Appalachia 06 opens with a slow zoom on the Smith Hotel: caution tape stretched around the bushes outside, and tired state police officers taking prints and swabs. One of them emerges from the bushes holding a night-vision headset and orders, "Bag it and tag it, the Secret Service fellows I want to take a look at that." Later in the episode, Andre has to remind the players what the scene showed. Dante recalls thinking that the goggles "could belong to anybody". (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: The surveillance scandal
docs.text: In the following episodes, the team hides from the press because FBI agents are suspected of spying on Bill Clinton. In Appalachia 07, a contact with a friend at the state police reports that investigators recovered something with prints that match an FBI agent, after a tip-off from the Secret Service. In Appalachia 08, the players piece together that goggles found in a bush were used to spy on Clinton, and a reporter asks Andrew on live TV about "the Bill Clinton wiretap". See the Clinton Surveillance Scandal. (Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08)

docs.title: The mines
docs.text: In Appalachia 09, the Biz complains that he cannot find his night-vision goggles, which would be useful in a mine. When the party divides the gold, he says he has "a new pair of night vision goggles to buy". (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: The epilogue
docs.text: On Late Night with David Letterman in Walkers 01, the Biz is introduced as "the most hated cop in America". Asked about the goggles, he says, "Well, I'd like them back," and that they are "really expensive". He confirms they were his and not the FBI's, and that he owns them for "spying on people". Letterman notes that the state police say they found the goggles in a rose bush and asks how they got there. Letterman also says that Jan Martense, "the illegal gold miner for the food company", had been surveilling Clinton. The Biz offers two possibilities: they were lost during his own surveillance work, or they were stolen from his car trunk. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes never show how the goggles ended up in the hotel bushes, or whether Jan Martense had anything to do with their disappearance.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The cold open of Appalachia 06 was meant as a clue, but the players focused on the officer's way of drinking coffee instead. (Appalachia 06)
