docs.title: OJ the stuffed alien
docs.text:
OJ the stuffed alien is a 25-pound plush alien, sent to Huell as a prank by his former narcotics colleagues, which became the task force's mascot.

Type Item (mascot) Aliases OJ; mascot Holder The task force (Huell gave it to Andrew) First appearance Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text: OJ is an enormous 25-pound stuffed alien that must have cost several hundred dollars. The team dressed it in a tie, and Kira's contribution at the table was a little badge (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: History
docs.text: Back at headquarters on June 15th, 1992, after the team's recovery in Radford, a courier wheeled in a crate addressed to Huell Kendrick. Inside was the plush alien with the note "Ha ha, fuck you, Huell," in the handwriting of his old coworkers from narcotics, who had evidently learned of his new assignment. Huell gave it to Andrew as the new team mascot. Diane insisted that a mascot needed a name. Kurt suggested Willie Pete, slang for white phosphorus, after a dog he claimed to have had in Vietnam; Andre floated Kevin and asked what rhymes with alien, and the team finally settled on OJ. The team propped OJ up next to their desks upstairs (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The naming scene includes a "what rhymes with alien" gag, and Andre remarked that "OJ the alien" has "even some assonance" (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Pearlescent goo
docs.text:
Pearlescent goo is a bitter, compost-scented slime that the team found on a tree in the Safe Environment Fund's fenced site and again above the window of the Douglas Pinball Emporium's office.

Type Item (physical sample) Aliases caterpillar slurry; opalescent slime; goo samples Holder Kurt (samples), then Donald McManley for analysis First appearance Radford Horrors 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The goo is glistening and pearlescent, a little thicker than snot, and it smells rotten and compost-like, the same smell the team associated with the Radford Moth (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
Daniel Webster tasted the first sample. It was eye-wateringly bitter and he immediately felt unwell, followed by a weird sweet aftertaste that made him salivate compulsively (Radford Horrors 02).

In Radford Horrors 04, Kurt held a sample under the nose of the catatonic Wilbur Whateley at the Roanoke mental hospital. Wilbur's muscles stiffened under his clothes, his eyes took on a waxy look and his fingers clutched the handles of his wheelchair, though he did not respond at that moment (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: The tree in the SEF site
docs.text: At the cleaned scribble inside the Safe Environment Fund fenced site, Kurt noticed something shiny on a high branch and used Huell's crutch to scrape it down: a big glob of glisteny, pearlescent snot stuck to the crutch. Kurt took a sample, which he thought might be a chemical agent, and wanted to get it to McManley. Andrew whispered "Caterpillar slurry," and kept repeating it until the lawyers arrived. Earlier in the episode Andrew had wondered aloud whether the dead moth had left eggs or young (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The emporium window
docs.text:
At the Douglas Pinball Emporium in Radford Horrors 04, Kurt's Investigate a Mystery roll (11) showed that the office window opening onto the alley was a likely route in. It had the same rotten compost smell as the moth, although the Smart car-sized moth could not have fit through it. Searching the alley, he found another dollop of the slime above the window and took a sample. Kurt's working theory was that the cleanup crew was sent because something alien, perhaps a juvenile moth, had been in the building; see the diner security tape and the emporium intruder (Radford Horrors 04).

Huell phoned McManley from a payphone: "Get down here, we've got goo." McManley asked, "Is there a face this time?" Huell answered, "Not yet," and McManley agreed to come, though not until the next day. The phrase appears to refer back to the folded face of the Appalachia case. With two goo samples in hand, Kurt looked forward to McManley's analysis (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Derk's Flag
docs.text:
Non-canon

Derk's Flag belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Derk's Flag is the cape-sized butcher-paper flag that Derk draws on the floor of the Public Library for the Flag Contest.

Type Item Holder Derk, then the werewolf president First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A tattered butcher-paper flag, large enough to be worn as a cape, marked with bugs and wet handprints and knee prints. It shows scorpions (the president reads them as "giant scorpions attacking the earth"), the stars as seen from space, a corgi-like dog that is the president and, added later, hot dogs in taco shells. The taco dogs are better drawn than anything else on it, but the composition is incoherent, and laying the colors over the black of space makes them look odd. Derk says he should have drawn only hot dogs. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Derk draws it over about an hour and a half in the library's children's room (a Superior roll of 6) while parked among toddlers. Mirabeth tears it off the floor as she rescues him. Outside the community center she shows it to Derk as his art and has him draw something smaller. He never draws a better flag, and he simply adds the taco dogs to the same one. (Philosopher's Fist)

At the Presidential Event Hall, Derk presents it to the werewolf president, who praises the hot dog as a patriotic food and the taco shell as "multiculturalism," learns that the dog is himself, and promises "real serious consideration." He gives Derk a presidential-seal sticker to "show that you met me." During the fight, Derk stands up for the president against Ovain with "Hey, be nice to him! He liked my flag!" (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Andre remarked that Derk "for sure just drew a corgi," the only kind of dog he knows. Matt agreed ("Oh, that's a corgi, I promise"), and Andre said he had not yet seen Matt's flags on the table's Discord.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Detector Wand
docs.text:
Non-canon

The Detector Wand belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Detector Wand is the guards' handheld superhuman and metal detector at the Presidential Event Hall.

Type Item Aliases Superhuman and metal detector Holder The wand guard, then Mirabeth First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A handheld wand about the size of a billy club, but flat and rectangular with rounded corners. It has a single LED on the back that lights up and an external battery pack. A trigger activates it. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: It detects both concealed weapons and metal and superhuman abilities, and the one LED serves for all of them. Neither Derk nor Mirabeth knows how it tells them apart. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
At security the older, chubby, profusely sweating guard waves the wand over Derk and it goes off. Derk says, "Mama says there's a metal plate in my head from when I went down," reasoning that with only one LED the alarm can be blamed on metal. The wand goes off again, and Mirabeth helps with her godlike beauty (Savior 7) while Derk rolls a 6. The guard taps Derk's head, which makes a "tink, tank" sound, and Derk adds, "Rocks are good for your bones." The guard lets them through, saying that next time they need a waiver, and Mirabeth fakes an intimate moment with him. He tells her, "It's my job, man," and moves down the line without scanning her. (Philosopher's Fist)

Inside the hall, she finds him by the snack table and sweet-talks him into showing her the wand, then walks off with it. A roll of Mundane persuades him to let her borrow it, and he is left standing there looking nervous. She uses it to convince the guards at the roped-off floor that Derk is there to protect the president. Afterward Colonel Sparago accuses her of using "sexual wiles" on a man who has been struggling in life. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Mirabeth's Parasol
docs.text:
Non-canon

Mirabeth's Parasol belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Mirabeth's Parasol is the clear collapsible umbrella that Mirabeth carries as part of her gear.

Type Item Aliases Umbrella Holder Mirabeth First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A clear, collapsible umbrella with aerodynamic stabilizer fins, which keep it at a fixed orientation, and a single windshield wiper attached to the middle spoke. Twisting the spoke turns the wiper against the umbrella. It collapses into her hip bag. Andre pitched the idea to Rita during the trip to the capital, and she accepted it. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: It works as a bug shield at speed. On her trip to the Capital, Mirabeth uses her legendary speed as a dignified power-walk down the shoulder of I-95 in pumps, holding the open parasol in front of her and going up and over any car in her way. She says she has "really perfected the art of this over the decades." Dante called the result "Fucking speedster Mary Poppins." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text: Besides the I-95 trip, the parasol appears in the final scene: after her debriefing and Derk's 2 a.m. call, Mirabeth sighs, pulls out the umbrella and sets out to fetch him from Wisukonshin. Andre pictures her with the umbrella out in front of her and the windshield wiper running. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The Oil Pyramid
docs.text:
Non-canon

The Oil Pyramid belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Oil Pyramid is the essential-oil multi-level-marketing scheme that Mirabeth invents on the spot at the pre-event social.

Type Item (fictional product) Aliases Oil pyramid kit; the essential-oil MLM Holder Mirabeth (the seller); Addison (the buyer) First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: There is no actual product. Rita says Mirabeth is "entirely pulling out of my butt an essential oil MLM," and Andre, as Addison, calls it "the oil pyramid kit." Mirabeth hands Addison a business card with the pitch. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
At the community-center social (The Flag Contest), Mirabeth uses an Assess the Situation roll of 9 to find the people most vulnerable to her: Addison, an exhausted, poor mother, and her miserable teenage son, whose flag she is critiquing line by line. While Derk tells the boy that Ovain is coming to kill the president, Mirabeth draws Addison aside and pitches the scheme. She guilt-trips her about her son's stress, and the pitch lands on the point that "the oil pyramid really kind of provides financial stability to working moms." Mirabeth rolls a 10 on Provoke Someone, and Addison pays a $400 down payment. (Philosopher's Fist)

Then her son runs over sobbing, "Mommy, I don't wanna get killed with the president." Having heard about the threat, Addison hurries him to the car, saying she will call Mirabeth about the oils. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• It is one of Mirabeth's growing string of lies, alongside the lost earring, her "child psychology" credentials and the claim that Derk is 14.
  • Dante joked that the $400 made back Derk's hot dog money "plus interest."

docs.title: Philosopher's Stone
docs.text:
Non-canon

The Philosopher's Stone belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Philosopher's Stone is the grand prize of the World Martial Arts Tournament and the reason Derk enters.

Type Item Holder The tournament, as its prize First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The stone never appears in the one-shot; it is described only as the tournament's grand prize. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The winner gets access to it for a couple of minutes. It is usually used in a high-efficiency hospital setting, because tournament fighters are very death- and injury-prone. Andre tells Dante that it can be used to resurrect Fatty Gibbs. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text: Derk's friend Fatty Gibbs, a sweet sumo wrestler, died of a coronary artery problem earlier last year. Derk wants the stone to bring him back, and that is why he agreed to enter. The tournament is suspended after a doping scandal and may be canceled, so the prize is out of reach as the one-shot ends, and Derk is lost in Wisukonshin. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.text: • Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Pilot organ in Tupperware
docs.text:
The pilot organ in Tupperware is the iridescent, brain-like organ that Donald McManley cuts from the skull of a dead skinwalker host at the Roosevelt police station, and which the duplicate Andrew Howard takes charge of in a plastic food container. (Walkers 08)

Type Item (biological specimen) Aliases the organ; the brain Holder The duplicate Andrew Howard First appearance Walkers 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The organ looks at first like a brain, with swirls of purple and green iridescence, "like gasoline" in Zack's words. Long tendrils hang limply from the bottom, and McManley points out small suckers on them. It sits in a cavity carved out of the skull, which is thinner than normal, and light shines up through the mouth because a path runs from the back of the sinuses straight into the skull cavity. The host's own brain is a raw, irritated lump at the top of the spinal column, perhaps a twentieth or thirtieth of normal size. (Walkers 08) It is the "pilot" of the host body; see pilot and host biology and skinwalkers.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
McManley guesses that the pilots latch onto the blood vessels coming off the host's brain and feed from its blood supply, and that without much of a digestive tract they can only digest simple foods such as starches and sugars. This fits the sugar that has been disappearing around Ballard. He rules out the idea that a pilot could take over an ordinary person, since there would not be room. Of the host he says: "This is not a person. This is a vehicle. Somebody made this. And whatever you killed inside of it was its pilot." Anatomically the body is that of a child in an adult's size, "like a 200-pound baby." (Walkers 08)

Later, the prisoners in the cell are found slumped and empty-headed. Dante's Kurt concludes that "whatever was in these guys' head instead of a brain just scuttled into the ceiling tiles." The team plans to check the ambush bodies by shining a flashlight through an eye into the mouth to see whether a pilot is still inside. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
During the autopsy of the dead gunman, McManley, who is using break-room Tupperware as bins for the organs he removes, finds no stomach, about eight feet of malformed intestine, and a small fatty liver. When he opens the skull he lifts out the organ. Kurt's reaction is "What in the Goosebumps fuck is that?" McManley says he will put it in a Tupperware "because that's where we are right now." (Walkers 08)

Rita's Andrew asks to hold it, and McManley hands him the Tupperware. Andrew stays fascinated by it throughout the autopsy, and he takes the box back from McManley to point at the suckers. (Walkers 08)

Andrew is, in fact, the duplicate. At the end of the session Rita tells the table that she had been acting subtly on her faction's behalf, stealing the sugar from the break room and deliberately getting hold of the Biz's blood so the faction could begin preparing a copy of him. The other characters do not know. See Andrew Howard (duplicate). (Walkers 08)

The episodes do not show what became of the Tupperware afterward.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 08

docs.title: Pink butterfly hair tie
docs.text:
The pink butterfly hair tie is a small hair tie with a pink butterfly, found in the couch of the Augustine barn, that matches one found in Amanda Lucky's blood-matted hair.

Type Item (physical evidence) Aliases butterfly clip; hairband Holder Kurt (the barn one); Dr. Mauden (the one from the body) First appearance Radford Horror 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The hair tie is small, hard and plastic, with a pink butterfly on it. Kurt called it a "hair tie" and Andre's narration also calls it a "hairband" (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 03, Kurt broke into the barn behind the Augustine house, where Derek Augustine writes. He found a desk with a typewriter, a notepad of plot notes for a romance novel with dates paired with acronyms he did not recognize, condoms in the desk drawer, aspirin and cigarettes. A second Investigate a Mystery roll (7) in the couch cushions turned up the hair tie, which Kurt took along with wadded drafts from the trash (Radford Horror 03).

In Radford Horror 05, during the autopsy of Amanda Lucky with Dr. Harvey Mauden, Andre described a single pink butterfly hair tie stuck in her blood-matted hair. The players recognized it as matching the one from the barn couch, and Mauden tagged and bagged it with the remains of her dress. Kurt later cited it when naming Dr. Lori as suspect, since Lori's patients kept disappearing and the team had found the same butterfly clip where Lori had gone (Radford Horror 05).

When the team interviewed the Augustines, Kurt told Derek that he had noticed a similar pink clip on the ground in the yard by the barn, concealing the break-in. Derek replied that Amanda had come over to see his daughter Phoebe a few weeks earlier for a school project, and that Phoebe had a bunch of such clips, so one could easily have fallen off while the girls played in the backyard. Rita's character, Andrew, noted that the hair tie may simply have been from a multipack (Radford Horror 05).

In the recap in Radford Horror 08, Andre reported that Derek and Dr. Lori had both confessed to an inappropriate sexual relationship with Amanda (Radford Horror 08). The episodes never state whether the hair tie was actually Amanda's from the barn or Phoebe's, although the confession places Amanda in Derek's circle.

docs.title: Plymouth Voyager
docs.text:
The Plymouth Voyager is the wood-panelled 1990 rental minivan that the task force collects in Salt Lake City, which stalls at dusk at the Sherman Ranch, is lifted away overnight, and turns up wrecked and magnetized in Roosevelt. (Walkers 02, Walkers 04)

Type Item (vehicle) Aliases the van; rental car; wrecked rental car Holder Andrew Howard (booked in his name) Status Destroyed (Walkers 04) First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Andrew Howard books the rental. Andre lists a Ford Escort, a Toyota Camry, a Plymouth Voyager and two Jeep Cherokees; Rita asks for the closest thing to a minivan, and the team gets a 1990 Voyager, recognizable by its "plastic wood." It is found in a parking lot in Salt Lake City around noon, with Howard holding the keys. (Walkers 02) The table jokes about the Plymouth Voyager III concept car and the Gigahorse, and Dante recalls the van the team rolled in Texas. (Walkers 02) The rental company later complains to the team about the car. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The dusk event. In Walkers 03, at dusk on October 30, 1992, the Voyager dies about 50 feet from the ranch gate and every electronic device in it goes dead; only Andrew's pager still works. The sky pulses, and the team retreats into the car, which they call a Faraday cage. The car moves six inches sideways, there is a popping noise, the engine restarts, and the sky stops flickering. Scorch marks are later found inside the engine body. (Walkers 03) See the dusk event.

The disappearance. In Walkers 04 the Voyager's alarm and lights go off with nothing visible nearby. By morning the van is gone: one set of tire tracks leads to the parking spot and none lead away. Huell's Investigate a Mystery (10) shows it most likely went straight up, and the ground where it stood is at about 200 degrees. The ranch footage shows only an unconvincing patch of grey rising (see Bigelow's recordings). (Walkers 04) See the vanishing car incident.

The wreck. Traffic is backed up on East Lagoon Street in Roosevelt, where the Voyager is pancaked about a foot thick, fused into a slight crater in the roadway. Huell's second Investigate a Mystery (6) fails, and Kurt infers the flattening came from a drop. The map in the glove compartment and Kurt's Vietnam-era stilts are lost. The Roosevelt police arrange a flatbed and the loaner Betsy, and Huell's Help Out (double sixes, 15) lets him lift the wreck free of the asphalt with his back, although 10 to 20 percent of the car stays fused in the road. (Walkers 04)

Examination. By Walkers 05 the wreck has been towed to the Roosevelt police garage, where it stands on its side against a wall. From the glove box the officers have recovered the license and registration and a Best of Queen tape. Kurt finds the car magnetic, which it was not when parked. His examination suggests all of the damage came from impact with the ground at terminal velocity, and that it landed upside down. The upholstery is slightly melted, and an officer remarks that the car "kinda smells like coyote pee." Rita's Andrew offers "UFO" and concludes that "Car got abducted. They didn't want it, though." The officer instead suggests a local junkyard owner with a car crusher and a magnetic crane, which sends the team to Yusuf Ansari in later episodes. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The table's running gag is lost rentals: "we are not being very good with rentals lately," and Ezra's Biz notes that every car he has driven in the state has been turned into a pancake. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Police walkie-talkie
docs.text:
The police walkie-talkie is a police-style radio with its transmit button taped down, left on a table just inside the lighthouse door, which the team treats as a bug or trap.

Type Item Holder Kurt, who hid it in the team's car and later returned it to the lighthouse First appearance Summer Service 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Kurt finally gets the chain on the lighthouse door open after a slow lock-picking effort. Huell reads a bad situation (10) and finds the building empty, but notices that someone has left a walkie-talkie with the button taped down on a little side table next to the door. He signals everyone to be silent. A further question confirms it is a police-style radio, the kind used by local departments. Every piece of glass inside the building is broken (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The team takes it for a bug or trap that would let someone listen to everything said at the door, and it deepens their suspicion of the town police. Kurt carries it out rather than disabling it (Summer Service 03). See Marblehead police.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Kurt carries the radio out and buries it under the blankets in the car (Summer Service 03).
  • Leaving the lighthouse in Summer Service 04, Kurt retrieves the walkie-talkie from the car and puts it back where it was, closing the door so the team can talk freely. As they step out, an observant team member catches the tail end of a squad car driving away (Summer Service 04).
  • The episodes never reveal who was listening.

Not the car bug

The team had separately found a spy radio hidden in their own car before Summer Service 03. The players treat the two as different bugs.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Summer Service 03
  • Summer Service 04

docs.title: The severed arm
docs.text:
The severed arm is a bloated human forearm in a black turtleneck sleeve and glove, found among dead fish on the Marblehead beach at the start of The Summer Service.

Type Item (remains) Aliases the arm Holder The task force, in a cooler in the trunk of the Biz's car First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Church bells strike three as the team walks the beach past broken, freshly repaired and taped-up windows. Kurt rolls Investigate a Mystery (12), works out that the blast came from the harbor and moved inland, and finds the center of the damage. Something black is bobbing among the dead fish. It is a bloated, fish-eaten human arm in a soaking wet black turtleneck sleeve and black glove, with a violently splintered bone, running from the middle finger to past the elbow (Summer Service 01). See the beach and harbor.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Bagging it. Huell asks the woman at Harvard's Bait Shop for a large trash bag. The smell lessens but does not go away. The team decides not to remove the glove, since the hand might come apart, and leaves the arm for a medical examiner (Summer Service 01).
  • Calling it in. From a payphone Andrew tells Diane he has found an arm. She offers to send forensics and recalls that the brief said local police were hostile. Later she arranges for a forensics team to arrive the next morning and tells the team to keep the arm on ice (Summer Service 01).
  • The cooler. The team buys a cooler and ice at a beach store and duct-tapes it shut. Kurt rolls Sharp for Preparedness (10) and finds Tiger Balm in his kit, which everyone rubs under their noses. The cooler goes into the trunk of the Biz's Buick with the windows down. A young woman tells Kurt he smells (Summer Service 01).
  • Running gag. The smell soaks into the Biz's car, fueling repossession jokes. A small boy stops to stare at the team, holds his nose and starts crying. In Summer Service 03 Rita jokes that the Biz's car, supposedly already repossessed, is "why he put the severed arm in it" (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The owner is never identified, and the arm's later whereabouts are never stated. The black turtleneck and glove could suggest one of the missing earlier survey team, but no episode says so.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Summer Service 01
  • Summer Service 03 (mentioned)

docs.title: SHA Tracking Device
docs.text:
The SHA Tracking Device is a blinking red electronic tag on a ragged leather band, etched "Inventory Control, SHA Tracking, SS994-0851". A blinking red light is first glimpsed in the hidden tunnel, and the Circle Chasers later recover the tag from bear vomit.

Type Item (electronic tag) Aliases blinking red light; SS994-0851 Maker Spud Hut (Spud Hut America, "SHA") Found by The Circle Chasers Holder Donald McManley First appearance Appalachia 03 (as a blinking red light)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: An electronic device with extra circuitry attached to a ragged leather band. It is still blinking red when the team examines it, and is etched "Inventory Control, SHA Tracking, SS994-0851". (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• The device is still blinking, so the players presume it is active. Dante and Ezra both dislike the word "inventory", since it implies that Spud Hut tags living creatures as stock. (Appalachia 07)
  • At the wrecked truck, the logo reads "S-H-A", Spud Hut America, and Zack asks whether it is "like in that tracking number we found earlier". Andre answers, "Maybe." (Appalachia 07)
  • The ape-men on the later mining shift wear tracking bands on their arms, with blinking red lights. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: The red light in the tunnel
docs.text:
In Appalachia 03, the team follows a hidden modern tunnel and sees a small red light blink in the darkness far down the passage. Kurt later describes the creature that attacked them as having a blinking red light, and wonders if it is a bioweapon. (Appalachia 03)

In Appalachia 04, Kurt argues that the glowing red light attached to the creature suggests that "there are people involved", since it could be a recording device or a tracking device. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Bear vomit
docs.text:
In Appalachia 07, the Circle Chasers tell the team that while checking a recent Bigfoot sighting they found bear vomit full of blood and a blinking light, and were then chased by a bear "with, like, half a face"; see Half-faced Bear. In their RV, they produce the light in a Ziploc bag. Ezra's Dick Baxter examines it with an Investigate a Mystery roll of 9, and learns that it is electronic equipment attached to a leather band bearing the etched inscription. (Appalachia 07)

The team stores the device in an emptied corn nuts cup as a makeshift Faraday cage, after the players float a soda can, tinfoil and one of the coolers used for body parts. They then take it to McManley. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes do not report what McManley found out about the device.

docs.title: Shadow poncho
docs.text:
The shadow poncho is a nearly weightless, dark, see-through garment of surprising strength that the team took from a stranger they captured in the woods after the Radford church fire.

Type Item (cloak; apparently alien technology) Aliases cloak; "the shadow of a poncho" Holder Kurt Larson First appearance Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The garment covers the area a poncho would cover, but instead of fabric there is only darkness: Andre described it as "the shadow of a poncho." Seen through, things look darker, and it can barely be felt when touched. The material is "profoundly strange." It packs down to almost nothing, like wadding up tissue paper (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Kurt tested it after the team returned to the church. It is very light and whispery like spider web, yet on a Sharp roll (9) Andre ruled that it was extremely strong: it would not break however hard he pulled, and hooked over a tree limb it held his entire weight. Kurt's best guess was armor, possibly synthetic spider silk, synthetic moth silk or actual alien moth silk. The players had at first wondered whether it was a cloaking device, but Andre said it gave no such impression (Radford Horror 08). The episodes never establish any connection to the Radford Moth beyond Kurt's guess.

docs.title: Taken from the stranger
docs.text: After the church fight, armed strangers (special forces men and "volcanologists" in heat suits) arrived at the old-town church with flamethrowers and heat-ray flashlights. The injured team hid in the woods. One searcher who wore the poncho and carried a strange flashlight came close. Kurt lay hidden under bloody leaves as bait with a lasso, kicked the man in the groin to bring his head forward, and Andrew fired his church-issued mace, whose "nothing" passed through the man's head. The man dropped into a seizure and was tied up. Andre offered the players a choice between taking the weapon and the poncho; they took the flashlight at no cost and stripped off the poncho at the risk of drawing attention, but the other searchers were looking in the wrong places. The man's identity and fate are never learned. See the cleanup crew and the flashlight weapon.

docs.title: Handed to Molly
docs.text:
Kurt wrapped the poncho in tinfoil and, when Deputy Molly Underhill found the team, handed it over as "special federal evidence" to hide and tell no one about. Molly pocketed it, and in the hospital she returned the flashlight and the aluminum foil. Kurt tested the poncho afterward (Radford Horror 08).

Quote

"Don't tell nobody. Don't give it to nobody. Don't eat it." (Dante (as Kurt), Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Radford Horrors 04, Kurt sleeps tied to a tree in "a poncho and thermal netting," a habit from his camping; the episode does not say whether this is the shadow poncho (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 08
  • Radford Horrors 04 (a poncho of unstated type)

docs.title: Sons of Adam Bible
docs.text:
The Sons of Adam Bible is the thick, self-published Bible of the Marblehead church, with added Lemuria and Eden material, which the team is offered by the innkeeper at the end of The Radford Horror.

Type Item (book) Aliases motel Bible; local Bible Holder Handed out by the innkeeper of the Ram and Arms Inn; read by Andrew First appearance Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A clearly self-published Bible, a good deal thicker than a standard one, with extra material and an illustration of Jesus parting the water inside the front cover (Radford Horror 08). At check-in the innkeeper offers three choices: King James, Gideon's, or "the local flavor, which I highly recommend, the Sons of Adam Bible". The team takes the local one, and the innkeeper invites them to attend some of the Sons of Adam church's services (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
In Summer Service 01, Andrew speed-reads it "with a sick intensity". Andre grants +1 forward for extracting information from text and calls it Read a Bad Situation, although Zack thinks Investigate a Mystery fits better. Rita rolls an 11. She asks what sort of creature is involved and what is being concealed. The answers:

  • Most of the normal scripture is present, mixed with added text that sends Jesus to a sunken continent between India and Madagascar. The continent is Lemuria, though the text never names it.
  • The Garden of Eden was taken beneath the waves to protect it, and on Judgment Day everyone returns physically to Eden.
  • The text includes noticeably worse-written diatribes against continental drift ("the firmament does not shift").
  • It has a hysterical, millenarian tone around Revelation, with Jonestown overtones.

(Summer Service 01). Andrew recognizes the Lemuria allusions from his fringe reading. When he finishes, he slaps the covers shut and gives his verdict:

Quote

"I think they might sacrifice people to a sea monster." (Andre, narrating Andrew)

The theology behind it is covered under Second coming and eschaton.

docs.title: History
docs.text: The Bible is given out at the Ram and Arms Inn, and in The Summer Service the players call it the motel Bible. It is Andrew's first real window into the church's beliefs, before he hears Amos Shaw preach about angels as terrifying monsters constructed by God to wipe out sin (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:

  • Summer Service 01

docs.title: Spaceman suit
docs.text:
The spaceman suit is the homemade, Mercury-and-Apollo-style spacesuit worn in the Radford Radio Shack robbery and later seen on a figure running into the woods; the team found it discarded in the Whateley cellar.

Type Item (costume) Aliases Abe's spacesuit; Mercury replica; handmade Apollo 11 spacesuit; spaceman costume Holder Abelforth Whateley (maker and original wearer); later the police First appearance Radford Horror 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In Radford Horror 02, Irene Whateley and the sheriff describe Abe's homemade replica of a Mercury spacesuit, which he made for a school presentation (Radford Horror 02). In Radford Horror 06, the suit that the team sees is an Apollo 11 astronaut suit with an Apollo command cap (Radford Horror 06). Up close, it is handmade, hand-sewn with obvious love and care, with an American flag patch (Radford Horror 06). The differing descriptions of its style are never reconciled, and the players treat it as one suit.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The suit is bulky: during the robbery the wearer could not lift the heavier merchandise, which is how the fingerprints came to be on file (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: The Radio Shack robbery
docs.text: At the sheriff's station, the Biz searched the records, helped by Huell, and rolled an 8 on Investigate a Mystery. The file showed that Abe had thrown a cinder block through the Radio Shack window and entered in a spaceman suit. He tried to steal heavier items but could not lift them, then left with lightweight modems, a cellular phone and other portable goods in a garbage bag, and bought a bus ticket to Richmond. The sheriff had not known about the suit, and said it "does give a different color to the conversation we had earlier" (Radford Horror 02). See Radio Shack spacesuit robbery. In Radford Horror 05, Deputy Molly Underhill reported that the fingerprints dusted on the roof of the first crime scene had been run and matched the robbery, the only other incident involving a spaceman. She concluded that Abelforth was probably back in town and put out an APB (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: The spaceman in the woods
docs.text: In Radford Horror 06, the team saw an Apollo 11 astronaut jogging into the woods. When they caught him, the helmet came off to reveal a Whateley boy under an Apollo command cap. As something above grabbed him and lifted him away, he said "You don't have to fight this" and "It's okay. It's worth it" (Radford Horror 06). See The Spaceman.

docs.title: The cellar
docs.text: Later that night, the team entered the Whateley house and found discarded spacesuit pieces piled in an unfinished cellar, next to a pair of human feet. The suit was the only thing in the room that appeared recently disturbed. The Biz hid his bug behind the loose American flag patch of the suit, intending to learn if anyone came back for it (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: Police theory
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 08, the team was told the police theory: investigators had found a hidden basement holding a spaceman costume with a journal inside, and the cadaver of what was probably Abelforth. They believed Wilbur had come downstairs as his brother, pretended to leave, climbed back into his window, removed the costume and come down again as himself, so that both boys seemed to have left. The journal is described on the Wilbur's journal page (Radford Horror 08).

Disputed

The police theory pins the killings on Wilbur Whateley as a serial killer, which the team did not fully accept. The episodes do not settle who wore the suit on each occasion.

docs.title: Kurt's spear gun
docs.text:
Kurt's spear gun is a single-shot, cabled harpoon gun that Kurt carries as "sporting goods equipment." It killed the rabid mouse, alarmed airport security and became a talking point in the lawsuit that followed the SEF fence incident.

Type Item (weapon) Aliases harpoon; "sporting goods equipment" Holder Kurt Larson First appearance Radford Horrors 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The spear gun is a pressurized, single-shot weapon whose spears are attached to spools of wire cable. Kurt says the cable is shark-resistant, with good tensile strength, and defends the gun's "penetration capability." Once a spear is fired, the spool must be detached or another spear loaded and the gun re-pressurized, which Kurt admitted makes it a poor choice for anything like taking over a plane. He sleeps with it (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Kurt brought the spear gun to the Radford woods alongside his P90, a grenade, caltrops and about 30 gallons of pesticide. Daniel Webster, who asked why Kurt would bring a spear gun rather than a rifle, grew increasingly convinced Kurt would shoot him with it to make a point. Kurt, for his part, reflected that he regretted never having brought a spear gun into an interrogation room, since it clearly "has presence" (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Airport security
docs.text: At the airport, the spear gun was held up because the weapons-transport paperwork had been misplaced and Kurt had no FBI badge. His Act Under Pressure roll to find a coworker to vouch for him failed (3, or 5 with a bonus), and the airport was in chaos because of a strike. A Manipulate Someone roll (9, mixed) succeeded when he pulled down his collar to show where a Vietnamese spear had pierced his shoulder: "I bled for this country. I continue to bleed for this country." The screener told him to pack the spear separately (Radford Horrors 02). On the plane, Kurt complained to Andrew about how hard it would be to hijack a plane with a spear gun.

docs.title: The rabid mouse
docs.text:
At the Pay n' Stay at about 3 a.m., a foaming, stiff-legged mouse crawled up Webster's stomach and bit him on the nipple. Kurt woke, aimed and fired in one motion, and a Kick Some Ass roll speared the mouse through the torso, nailing it to the floor. Andrew pulled the spear out of the floor, and the clerk, Charm, admitted the motel had been promised the rodents were exterminated (Radford Horrors 02). See the rabid mouse.

In Radford Horrors 03, the team shared a hospital room for rabies treatment. When the doctor said "All right, give me the rat," Kurt extended the harpoon with the mouse still on it, wrapped in a plastic bag. It was to be tested in Roanoke, since the local hospital lacked the supplies; the team would need a four-vaccine series unless the result came back negative (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The lawsuit
docs.text:
The lawyers for the Safe Environment Fund raised the spear gun in the dispute that became the Bivens lawsuit. The guard who had tased Webster claimed he did not believe the FBI would be carrying one, which was why he fired, and also had a hearing impairment. Webster pointed out that Kurt had not shot anyone with it. Andrew objected that it was technically a harpoon, not a spear gun (Radford Horrors 03).

Quote

"If they ask, I had a piece of sporting goods equipment on me. Not a weapon: sporting goods equipment, purchased from a sporting goods store." (Dante (as Kurt), Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Spud Hut Menu
docs.text:
The Spud Hut Menu is the roughly 100 numbered stuffed-potato "specials" served at the original Spud Hut in Dahlonega, covering nearly every cuisine and recited from memory by the counter worker.

Type Item (menu) Aliases specials menu; margarita spud; octopus spud; taco taco spud Offered by Spud Hut Recited by Spud Hut Counter Savant First appearance Appalachia 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The Spud Hut has no indoor dining room and no menu board. Customers order at a window, and the counter worker offers to "hear the specials" and then recites roughly 100 numbered dishes from memory. Andre read the whole list aloud at the table, to the point that the players stopped him only by asking for it to be posted. Afterward he admitted, "I should have prepared five hundred." The specials include a Cobb salad spud (the first on the list), peach pie à la mode, poutine, escargot, banh mi and s'mores, with the curry chicken spud at number 23. Dante complains that there is no fish and chips spud. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• Every dish is a stuffed or topped potato, a "spud", in small, medium or large. The potatoes arrive within a minute, and Andre rates them from an A to a C-plus depending on the spud. (Appalachia 02)
  • Customers who order one of everything and finish it eat free; those who cannot finish pay about $5,000. The worker adds that the 100 specials are only part of "the full menu". (Appalachia 02)
  • Appalachia 06 adds more items: Viennese beef, a "non-authentic" au gratin, jambalaya, tikka masala, huevos rancheros (number 48), chicken fajita (number 39), French dip, Monte Cristo and spinach and artichoke spuds. The "first three prime spuds" are the peach pie à la mode, BLT and taco supreme. (Appalachia 06)
  • The Spud Hut has a liquor license. In Appalachia 07 the margarita spud is a potato skin with a slit in the top, full of margarita; the bacon burger spud has a patty "made entirely of crumbled bacon"; and the "special taco taco spud" comes with a whole octopus on top. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: First visit
docs.text: In Appalachia 02, the team reaches the window before closing. The counter worker recites the specials while the line behind them nearly riots. Zack tells the staff, "Sir, sir, I am an officer. Do not touch me. I am listening to the menu." Dante drops a pile of matchsticks and asks how many there are, and the worker answers "forty-three" and is exactly right. The team orders Southwestern, poutine, BLT and chicken Parmesan spuds. The worker then closes the window and walks into the woods. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Appalachia 06
docs.text: In Appalachia 06, the worker recites the specials again and recommends the huevos rancheros spud to Andrew, who orders the chicken fajita with the peppers picked out. The Biz switches his order from tikka masala to French dip. Dante tells the worker, "You will be hearing from Langley." (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: The secret layer
docs.text:
In Appalachia 07, the team returns for dinner, with the players wanting to recruit the counter worker. Huell and the Biz each get margarita spuds, and Kurt buys one with several fake IDs and photos of his kids. The Biz eats his first octopus and judges it phenomenally cooked: "Surf and turf, what's not to like?" Delilah of the Circle Chasers devours four chicken pot pie spuds. The octopus spud and the whispered "taco taco spud" tie into the Cryptogram Secret Menu. (Appalachia 07)

A whole octopus later turns up in a "Potatoes" sack on the wrecked Spud Hut Truck.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The 100-item menu is a running table joke. Zack explains why nobody stopped Andre: "stopping you would be like losing." (Appalachia 02)
  • Zack compares the specials to the McRib, which comes back every so often with another hundred options. Dante suggests the equivalent would be a "Carno Spud", a potato made entirely of meat. (Appalachia 02)
  • When Dante tries to jump in with an order, Andre tells him, "You don't know how long this menu goes on, motherfucker. Don't commit to things you don't understand." (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 02
  • Appalachia 06
  • Appalachia 07

docs.title: Spud Hut Truck
docs.text:
The Spud Hut Truck is a Georgia Regional Distribution Center delivery truck that crashes off the freeway after its driver is attacked in the cold open of Appalachia 07. Its sacks marked "Potatoes" turn out to hold dirt and, in one case, an octopus.

Type Item (vehicle and cargo) Aliases truck dirt cargo Owner Spud Hut (marked S-H-G-R-D-C and S-H-A) Location Freeway Crash Site Attacker Thing That Attacked the Spud Hut Truck First appearance Appalachia 07

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The truck carries the banner "S-H-G-R-D-C", which people say as "Shugrid" and which stands for the Spud Hut Georgia Regional Distribution Center, with a big "S-H-A" (Spud Hut America) logo beneath it. Huell points out that "SHA" matches the SHA Tracking Device. In the cold open, a photo of a blonde-haired woman with golden-retriever curls is taped to the dashboard, with a mustard stain on it, and the driver keeps a Glock under his seat. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• The back of the truck has spilled open, and the bags marked "Potatoes" contain dirt. Zack asks McManley to analyze it; McManley says he can tell the team how much clay it contains, and "some stuff. Don't expect a fucking map." One bag holds a whole octopus floating in liquid. (Appalachia 07)
  • In Appalachia 08, Kurt tells a Spud Hut investigator that the truck held "not one potato", only dirt, and the investigator guesses "Gold mining?". He tells Jan Martense the same thing, and Jan promises to check every outgoing truck against its manifest. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: The cold open
docs.text: At sunset, an overweight driver in a gray jumpsuit drives down the freeway listening to "Radar Love" and picking at a congealing hamburger. He hears a clang and a ripping noise behind him, turns on his blinker and turns the radio down. Glass breaks behind him and something growls in the cab. He grabs for the Glock under his seat and misses, there is a blur of motion and he screams. The truck swerves through a barricade and an embankment, and stops among the trees with the song still playing quietly. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: The crash site
docs.text:
The team arrives to find the sheriff, emergency workers and queued Spud Hut trucks on the freeway. The cab is on its side and soaked in blood: no body, no face, no direction to the spatter, and far too much blood for the driver to be alive. Dashboard instruments are broken, and there are eight gunshots through the cabin. The back window broke before the crash and the windshield broke outward after it. The vinyl roof is ripped as if by fingers. Kurt reasons that something crawled through the rear window, mauled the driver and left through the front with what was left of him. The sheriff admits it is odd that there are so few pieces, and Kurt calls the scene "weirdly meticulous for what a mess it was". (Appalachia 07)

The sheriff slits one of the bags and the dirt spills out. The team realizes that they have avoided Spud Hut Corporate "like the plague" for three months, and the sheriff proposes visiting first thing in the morning. (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: In Appalachia 08, the team drives to the Spud Hut plant and notices that no Spud Hut trucks are on the road, though they had been omnipresent before. Jan calls the driver's death a "tragic accident" and says the company is tracing the driver's path that day. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The driver's body is never found, the episodes never report McManley's result for the dirt, and the woman in the dashboard photo is never identified.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 07
  • Appalachia 08

docs.title: Spy Camera and Microphone
docs.text:
The Spy Camera and Microphone are a covert recording microphone and a compact hidden film camera that Dick "The Biz" Baxter collected from a KGB dead drop and planted in room 111 of the Smith Hotel in Dahlonega, Georgia.

Type Item (surveillance gear) Aliases KGB camera; covert microphone and hidden camera; the Biz's spy camera Holder Dick "The Biz" Baxter Origin KGB dead drop First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The gear arrived in a taped paper bag. Andre describes a "brand new covert recording microphone" and a small, compact film camera intended to be hidden in vents or behind drywall (Appalachia 01). When the Biz installs them, the camera turns out to be a nondescript black box with a small hole in it and a motion sensor. The microphone has a sticky backing (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• The camera is motion-activated and loaded with film, so its pictures cannot be seen until the film is developed (Appalachia 02).
  • The Biz can rig it with a timer pin to shoot without him holding it (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Collection
docs.text:
In Appalachia 01 the Biz receives a sweepstakes invitation that he recognizes as a KGB front. He decodes the message using Moby Dick as a codebook. It promises information on the Massachusetts matter in return for a favor, tells him to collect equipment at his old drop spot before leaving for "George I A", and offers $10,000 (Appalachia 01).

The old drop is a loose paving stone under a park bench near his former home. Suspicious of it, he pays a homeless man about $50 to fetch the package. The man returns with the taped bag, unopened. Inside are the microphone, the camera and a sheet of thin paper, to be burned or eaten, with instructions: within two days, install the camera in room 111 of the Smith Hotel before midnight; retrieve it 24 hours later; and mail the undeveloped film to an address to be supplied the next day. The rest of the team is not told (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: Planting in room 111
docs.text:
In Appalachia 02 the Biz enters room 111, where someone has left a basket of wine and chocolates. He tucks the camera in among the cables beside the VCR under the TV and angles it toward the bed. He sticks the microphone to the bedside drawer, which holds a Gideon Bible, a box of condoms and lubricant. He tells the table he suspects a setup, though not one aimed at himself. When the desk clerk describes the man who booked the room as sounding Midwestern, the Biz concludes "That is him" (Ezra, as Dick "The Biz" Baxter, Appalachia 02).

In Appalachia 06 Ezra asks whether the Biz ever retrieved "the thing", and Andre confirms he had not. That episode's cold open shows state police searching the hotel's grounds.

docs.title: Photographing the crack
docs.text: In Appalachia 09 Andrew's camera is smashed in the ape-man fight. A Preparedness roll establishes that the Biz carries a spy camera, mostly full of developed pictures with room for a few more. He rigs the timer pin and photographs the crack in the air deep in the mine, including a shot through it. His fingers feel electrified and freezing near the rift, but he gets the picture (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: The Clinton photos
docs.text: In Walkers 01, the epilogue to the arc, David Letterman tells the Biz that the Polaroids in the Clinton affair were taken with a Russian camera, which is news to the Biz. The Biz replies that Jan is Polish and the Poles were part of the USSR (Walkers 01). The episodes never state outright that this is the room 111 camera, but the KGB handed the Biz a camera for a job in that hotel; see the Clinton surveillance scandal.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • It is never established whether the camera in the mine is the same unit as the room 111 camera, or whether the room 111 film was ever developed or mailed. Appalachia 09 calls it only the Biz's spy camera.

docs.title: Survey team's field notes
docs.text:
The survey team's field notes are the journal and contact list that the missing EPA/USGS survey team left behind at their lodgings in Marblehead, Massachusetts, and which the task force uses to start its investigation of the town.

Type Item (document) Aliases Survey field journal; previous team's field notes; field journal Holder The task force Origin Left among the survey team's belongings at the Ram and Arms Inn First appearance Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The notes are a field journal, mostly empty but with a few entries, kept by the previous team of investigators, together with a list of local contacts and their phone numbers. The team were an EPA/USGS survey party sent to check Marblehead after the explosion (see EPA/USGS survey team). The journal turns up among the team's abandoned belongings: suitcases, clothes, IDs, technical manuals, chemical sampling equipment and several wallets. (Radford Horror 08)

Not the lighthouse notebook

A second, EPA-branded notebook is found later in the lighthouse basement. It is a separate item; see EPA field journal.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
• The explosion came from the ocean. The team tested some of the locals for gas poisoning and found no sign of carbon monoxide or methane. What they found instead was closer to mild nerve agent poisoning, with shakes, lightheadedness, digestive trouble, headache, restlessness and dizziness. (Radford Horror 08) This is the first hint of the synthetic nerve agent.
  • The last entry says the team wanted to talk to the town leadership about possibly evacuating the town until the cause was known. No later entries follow. (Radford Horror 08)
  • The contact list names the Cartwright family, Ma Gramoire, Lana (Lena) Scott and Denver O'Donnell, each with a phone number. Andre gives the name as "Lana Scott"; Dante calls her Lena. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The innkeeper at the Ram and Arms agrees to send the survey team's belongings up once the task force explains that they are from the government. Dante helps him haul up a large cardboard box, and the group unpack it in Andrew's room. A successful Investigate a Mystery roll ("what happened here") turns up the journal, and the episode ends on its contents. (Radford Horror 08)

At the start of Summer Service 01 the team go over the notes in their motel room. Andre summarizes them for Zack: the team interviewed people who had symptoms after the explosion, found the symptoms inconsistent with natural gas poisoning, and planned to meet town leaders. Zack, whose character Huell lost his own notes in an earlier case, says he wants to keep better notes this time. Dante proposes working the contact list first, and the list becomes the task force's first set of leads. Kurt phones Ma Gramoire, who hangs up as soon as he mentions the FBI. (Summer Service 01)

The second notebook, found in the lighthouse in Summer Service 03, completes the story: it records that the team went before the Board of Selectmen, were threatened by senior town officials and the mayor, and then set out for the lighthouse on a local's advice. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The two briefings of the same journal differ on one point: Radford Horror 08 has the team planning to raise an evacuation with the town leaders, while Summer Service 01 only says they were going to meet the leaders to find out what was going on.
  • The timeline of the explosion differs between episodes; see The Marblehead explosion.

docs.title: Triangular craft
docs.text:
The triangular craft is a crashed triangular aircraft embedded in the site of a destroyed farmhouse in Oryol Oblast, Russia, which Boris Yeltsin asked the Biz to examine.

Type Item (crashed craft) Aliases UFO; "unusual aircraft crash" Location Oryol crash site, Russia Status Partly excavated under a tent and guarded by the Russian military First appearance Radford Horrors 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The craft is a triangular object a little smaller than the space shuttle. It annihilated a farmhouse on landing and is embedded in the ground where the house stood. It is badly wrecked, but the triangular shape is still recognizable. It is partly excavated, visible through a clear double-walled plastic curtain under high-intensity arc lamps, inside a tent room (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Andre describes no controls or markings on the craft itself. What the Biz saw inside the tent was its occupant: the crash survivor, a bisected non-human being kept alive in a hospital bed and hooked by tubes to a Russian soldier. See that page for the survivor's behavior and what it told Yeltsin (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Radford Horrors 03, Boris Yeltsin, calling the Biz "Richard," met him on the stairs of the Hotel Metropol in the rain and told him, lowering his voice, that there had been "an unusual aircraft crash in Oryol Oblast" and that he wanted the Biz to take a look at it with him. Dante joked, "Somewhere Andrew is tingling." The convoy was ambushed on the way by Chechen and Russian attackers, and the craft was not reached in this episode (Radford Horrors 03). See convoy ambushers.

In Radford Horrors 04, the cold open showed the buried craft under work lights. After a night in a hospital room, the Biz was taken at dawn to see the wounded president, then flown by helicopter with Yeltsin's hospital bed to a field near the site. After roughly forty minutes waiting on a folding chair in a tent while the Russians planned how to move the bed in without uncleared eyes seeing, he helped push the bed into the craft room. Yeltsin had the doctors wake the survivor with a syringe. Asked in Russian and then English why it was there, it said "Survey," and answered that its people were "not aliens, the opposite of aliens," adding "Servitors... need resources" before losing consciousness. In private, the Biz told Yeltsin that these were not the same aliens the Biz had dealt with, that he had seen resources go through portals before but that it "presented differently," and that he had not heard of servitors (Radford Horrors 04). See servitors and Dick "The Biz" Baxter.

What remains unknown

The episodes do not say what the craft is made of, how it crashed, or what became of it after the Biz's visit. Zack joked that the episode could have been titled "Opposite of Aliens."

docs.title: Two sets of financial books
docs.text:
The two sets of financial books are a pair of nearly identical sets of town accounts that Huell finds in Arnold Weathers's upstairs bedroom, beside a shoebox of clear marbles.

Type Item (documents) Aliases Town books Holder The task force (as of the end of Summer Service 05) Origin Arnold Weathers' bedroom, Arnold Weathers' house First appearance Summer Service 05

docs.title: Description
docs.text: After the team has dealt with Puddles and Arnold, Zack's character Huell searches the upstairs bedroom and rolls a 9 on Investigate a Mystery. Andre has him ask "what happened here," and he finds a set of financial books for the town. Searching longer, he finds a second set. In the dark the two look almost identical, but not quite. Further on he finds a shoebox in the closet "absolutely full" of the clear marbles. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The books are never opened on screen, so the differences between the two sets, and whatever they conceal, are never established. The team has no chance to read them before the session ends. Arnold held a seat on the Board of Selectmen, and at the meeting in Summer Service 04 his empty chair was a point of nervous alarm for the other members. The players treat the books and marbles together as evidence tying Arnold to the town leadership's secrets. (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Huell hands the marbles to the Biz and the team carries the two sets of books and the marbles back downstairs. Dante jokes that, synthetic or not, the marbles will let them obliterate the diamond market. Later in the session, while the group argues over the ivermectin, Andre notes that the team successfully brought the books along because they have not yet had a chance to look at them. (Summer Service 05)

The books do not come up again in the recorded episodes, and it is never established what the team did with them.

docs.title: Visitation Tapes
docs.text:
The Visitation Tapes are the Roulets' labelled VHS tapes, kept in a huge rack in the living room of the Roulet House, some of which are labelled as records of alien visitations.

Type Item (video tapes) Aliases VHS tapes Holder Kurt Larson (a couple of the tapes) First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The living room of the Roulet House holds a television and a huge VHS rack. Some tapes are home movies. Others are labelled by hand, including "September '92 visitation", "May '91 visitation" and "Lights in the sky, July '92" (Roulet Estate 01).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: Kurt reads the labels hoping to compare the dates with the owners' partly coded notebook in the library, which logs sightings of Greys and lights over the house ending in the fall of 1992 (Roulet Estate 01).

docs.title: History
docs.text: At the end of Roulet Estate 01, Kurt takes a couple of the labelled tapes with him as evidence. In the recap at the start of Roulet Estate 02, Andre says the agents found VHS tapes but have not watched them, and no one watches them in the episode. There is no power in the house in any case (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02). Their contents are never revealed.

docs.title: VSS Rifle
docs.text:
The VSS Rifle is a Soviet-era suppressed rifle that the Roulet Intruder uses to shoot Huell and Andrew and then drops by the river, where Andrew picks it up.

Type Item (firearm) Aliases VSS Holder Andrew Howard (as evidence) First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The VSS is a Soviet-era rifle, fairly well used but well taken care of, loaded with normal nine-millimeter rounds. It has a serial number, which Kurt makes a note of. It is a specialized weapon; as Andre puts it, "the VSS is nobody's everyday carry" (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Roulet Estate 01. While Andrew is outside studying the map in the car, an odd whizzing noise passes his head and a car window explodes; the monk tackles him and drags him behind the car. Huell and Andrew chase a naked, unnaturally thin figure through the woods. It picks up a sniper rifle and shoots Huell in the shin (2 harm), then squares up and shoots Andrew in the face. Andrew negates the harm, and from the figure's body language it is startled. It flees to a river, and Andrew finds the rifle dropped near the bank and takes it. Back at the house Kurt dusts the rifle and takes samples of the prints, wanting the evidence collected before the team has to fire the rifle themselves (Roulet Estate 01).

Andrew suspects the people who did the cleanup in Utah are tying up loose ends. Kurt answers that one shooter is a half-assed effort rather than a fire team, and wonders whether the attack was meant to look like a Soviet assassination (Roulet Estate 01).

Roulet Estate 02. The agents wrap the rifle in a garbage bag to protect the prints, having no equipment to run them. When they find a Kalashnikov and WWII Russian pistols in the attic lair, Andre says the gentleman of the house seems to have been a firearms collector. The players take it that the VSS was probably stolen from such a collection, which makes a KGB plot less likely (Roulet Estate 02). The serial number and fingerprints are never traced on screen.

docs.title: Wedding Photos
docs.text:
The Wedding Photos are a sheet of old wedding photographs, the only thing left in the bedroom safe of the Roulet House, which let the agents identify Margaret Roulet's body by her ring.

Type Item (photographs) Holder The task force First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The sheet shows wedding photos that look to be from the 1950s or 1960s, probably taken in Arizona, of a curly-haired woman and a man with close-cropped military hair. Marks in the safe show where other items once sat (Roulet Estate 01).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Kurt cracks the safe in the bedroom with an Act Under Pressure roll, forcing it with a fire poker. The poker whips back and cuts his shin for 1 harm, but the safe opens. The photos are the only contents (Roulet Estate 01).

In Roulet Estate 02, after Kurt empties his gun into the basement trash pit and the others find a withered, sleeved hand there, Andrew goes to fetch the photos. Consulting them, the agents see that the ring on the hand is the same wedding ring as in the pictures, which Andre confirms identifies the body as that of Margaret Roulet. The agents take the photos with them as evidence when they go for help (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: What I Need When I Need It bag
docs.text:
The What I Need When I Need It bag is the satchel or fanny pack through which Andrew Howard uses his Divine playbook ability of the same name, pulling out any small object he could plausibly own. (Walkers 07)

Type Item (magic container) Aliases Andrew's bag; satchel; fanny pack; hammerspace pocket Holder Andrew Howard Related page Andrew's satchel, the same bag in earlier arcs First appearance Walkers 07 (under this name)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Rita's Andrew calls it his "little satchel of odds and ends" when he dresses for the gym, and Andre refers to it as a fanny pack when Andrew reaches into it. The ability behind it, What I Need When I Need It, lets Andrew retrieve "any small object that I own or could feasibly own," held in one hand, from a magical space that nobody else can reach, with no roll. Rita treats it as working only if Andrew reaches into the bag and only if he plausibly thinks he has the item. Andre calls it a "bullshit hammerspace pocket" and "magic bag." (Walkers 07)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Earlier uses. Andre explains in Walkers 07 that the claymore Andrew once had came out of the bag, and that the team's own claymores did not come with them to Utah because they flew. See Andrew's satchel for the item's earlier history. (Walkers 07)

The gym grenade. On the night of the gym meeting, Andrew takes his camera, pepper spray, pistol, satchel and protective medallion. When the double and its allies close in, Rita says Andrew digs "for a grenade or other explosive device that I believe I have from Kurt and Biz," and Andre has him find one in his fanny pack. He pulls the pin, the grenade slips from his hand as he runs, a horse throws itself on it, and a piece of horse flung by the blast knocks him down for 3 harm. (Walkers 07) This was also the occasion on which the real Andrew was replaced; see Andrew Howard (duplicate).

Playbook change. At the end of Walkers 08 the genuine Andrew wakes at the bottom of the morgue pile as the Monstrous, and Rita rebuilds him (see Andrew Howard (the Monstrous)). She asks to keep What I Need When I Need It, "mostly because it's tied to an item. So it wasn't really, like, his power," and gives up Lay on Hands and Cast Out Evil. Andre agrees, and Rita takes a move from another playbook so that the ability survives. (Walkers 08)

Recovery. In Walkers 09, in the cavern, Andre notes that "the other Andrew did not have the bag and also did not have the pendant." Andrew searches the pile of dead people's belongings (Act Under Pressure, 10) and finds a ruined suit, a fanny pack, and his necklace in a Ziploc bag labeled "Hazardous!!!". The suit is missing because the duplicate is wearing it. Andrew takes the fanny pack and the pendant, which is the item described at Andrew's pendant. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Walkers 08, while Rita is playing the duplicate, she has him take a hanky "out of his bag" in the car. The duplicate is later said not to have had the bag, so the episodes do not agree on whether he carried a bag of his own. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: White powder
docs.text:
White powder is the faint chalky residue, accompanied by a "terrarium" smell, that Andrew Howard collected at the clearing where the blood trail of the Radford creature ended.

Type Item / evidence Aliases chalky powder; strange powder and root growth Holder Andrew Howard (collected samples); the task force Status Collected; no analysis result is ever reported First appearance Radford Horror 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Kurt loses the blood trail at a clearing near the river bank, about forty feet wide and thirty feet deep. Kurt looks up and sees no broken branches overhead, and Andre rules that a pretty big aircraft could land there without disrupting anything. Andrew rolls Investigate a Mystery (a 12 plus Sharp) and learns that there is no dog smell, but a dusty, earthy, unhealthy "terrarium" smell, and a very faint dusting of white powder with a chalky texture, concentrated exactly where the trail was lost (Radford Horror 04). Andrew collects some of it.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• The powder marks the place where the creature's trail ended, and the team later describes the spot as the clearing where a girl went missing. The task force connects it with the Radford Moth (Radford Horror 04).
  • In Radford Horror 06 the team plots the craft's recorded headings on a map. They converge near the river, where Andre describes "saltings" of the same weird powder, though the team spots nothing else (Radford Horror 06).
  • In the hidden cellar of the Whateley house, the Biz finds a fibrous, root-like growth wrapped around a floor joist, its lower end sawed off, smelling overwhelmingly of the same organic smell. The Biz proposes cutting off a sample for analysis (Radford Horror 06). Whether the root and powder are formally linked is never stated; the shared smell is what connects them.

docs.title: History
docs.text: Andrew gathered the powder in Radford Horror 04. When the team prepares evidence for handover in Radford Horror 05, Andrew lists "the chalky powder that we found at the abduction site" alongside the stolen skull and film waiting to be developed (Radford Horror 05). No lab result for the powder or the root is ever given.

docs.title: White Rabbit Pelt
docs.text:
The White Rabbit Pelt is the gutted skin of a white rabbit that Huell Kendrick retrieved from a treetop near the spot where the Circle Chasers filmed a rabbit being snatched.

Type Item (evidence) Aliases rabbit pelt Holder The task force (kept in the Smith Hotel mini fridge) First appearance Appalachia 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The pelt is a white rabbit's skin with stringy meat and blood stuck to the inside and all of the internal organs gone. On a superficial inspection it looks ripped open rather than cut or chewed (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Properties
docs.text: The pelt answered the team's question "Where did it go?" It had been carried up a tree about 100 feet from the snatch, and Andre tells the players that the creature is "very comfortable moving vertically". Kurt Larson pointed out that Gene's shoe, found in another tree, might likewise have been hung there after the incident rather than during it, and suggested the creature may return to hang its prey. Andrew's Rita-voiced verdict was that it could still be a werewolf (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Appalachia 02 the Circle Chasers show the team a three-second VHS clip in which a flashlight darts across a trail and a rabbit is taken. The team goes to the rabbit site (see Woods Trail and Rabbit Site) to look for a blood trail. After about half an hour of searching, blood drips onto Andrew from a tree about 100 feet from where the rabbit was taken.

Zack volunteers Huell to climb. Andrew's Help Out gives Huell a +1 but exposes Andrew to danger. Huell slips, catches himself on the branch below and is racked under both arms, taking 1 harm and a cylindrical bruise along each arm. He comes down with the pelt. Kurt suggests bagging it for Donald McManley, and the team marks the map with Comstock's ridge, the road spot and the rabbit site to start building a range. That night the pelt goes into the hotel mini fridge so it will not decompose (Appalachia 02).

In Appalachia 03, when Kurt compares the map against the tunnel exit and the Spud Hut distribution center, Andre says "the rabbit thing" is nowhere near either. The pelt is not mentioned again.

docs.title: Wilbur's journal
docs.text:
Wilbur's journal is the notebook of Wilbur Whateley recording how he found and raised a monstrous moth larva, handed to the task force by the sheriff at the end of the Radford case.

Type Item / document Holder The task force (given by the sheriff) Status Only the legible pages survive; later pages were removed First appearance Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Sheriff Frank Roosevelt explains that deputies found a hidden basement under the Whateley residence containing a spaceman costume, and that the journal was inside the costume (see Spaceman suit). He gives the team a plastic bag of pages, saying a lot of the later pages had been removed and that these were the legible ones (Radford Horror 08). The pages are dated June 3rd through August 15th, plus April 16th through 18th. The year is never stated.

docs.title: Contents
docs.text:
The players read the entries aloud at the table (Radford Horror 08):

  • June 3rd: Wilbur finds a larva in the woods by the church in the old town. It resembles a Morpho menelaus larva but is much larger, with anatomical abnormalities. He saves it from the specimen jar and stashes it in the basement.
  • June 10th: Amanda Lucky and Phoebe Augustine visit and hike the river. Wilbur writes that he does not think Amanda knows, but feels Phoebe might. The larva refuses leaves but loves beef.
  • June 14th and 21st: The cocoon is huge. Wilbur keeps thinking he hears someone talking to him, and recalls that people can pick up radio on their fillings, something Abelforth always tells him about.
  • July 30th: "She's talking all the time now," and he can hardly tell her voice from his own.
  • August 15th: "She hatched hungry. The dog is dead." The later lines repeat that she is beautiful and that she is his.
  • April 16th to 18th: Abe will not stop looking for the dog, and Wilbur fears he will find her, so he decides to move her to the old church. On the 17th he writes, "I did something. I need to figure out how to get away with it." On the 18th: "She's helping me. She's taking it away. I don't have to feel any of it."

Andre confirms that the team can work out that Abelforth's disappearance lines up with April 17th.

docs.title: History
docs.text: The sheriff presented the police theory that Wilbur killed his brother and staged both boys' departure, making him a serial killer. The players read the journal as evidence that the Radford Moth was influencing Wilbur, with Kurt comparing it to the way it tried to affect his own mind, and Huell admits he did not shoot Andrew on purpose. See also Moth life cycle (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Radford, Virginia
docs.text: Page Alpine Lodge Alpine Lodge is a tourist ski lodge in the mountains above Radford, Virginia, home to the teenager Matt McCready and the site of the water tower that the task force uses for its night stakeout in The Radford Horror. The Biz's apartment The Biz's apartment is Dick "The Biz" Baxter's dust-covered Washington, D.C. Highway crime scene The highway crime scene is the roadside by the interstate into Radford, Virginia, where the mutilated body of Amanda Lucky is found at the end of Radford Horror 04. Hotel Metropol The Hotel Metropol is a luxury hotel in Moscow where Dick "The Biz" Baxter is held in comfortable captivity during The Radford Horrors. Mountain road hit-and-run site The mountain road hit-and-run site is a stretch of winding mountain road below the Radford ski lodge where the team is shadowed by an unknown flying craft in Radford Horror 03 and Kurt Larson's car hits Agent Murphy. Old-town church The old-town church is a century-old stone-and-wood church standing in a clearing deep in the woods near Radford, Virginia. Oryol crash site The Oryol crash site is a farm site in Oryol Oblast, Russia, where a triangular craft has crashed into and destroyed a farmhouse. Radford pharmacy The Radford pharmacy is the town drugstore in Radford, Virginia where the team learns that a Vicodin record under Dr. Radford, Virginia Radford, Virginia is a quaint small town of about 16,000 in the woods of southwest Virginia, a paranatural hotspot and the setting of both Radford arcs: The Radford Horror (1992) and The Radford Horrors (1993).
