docs.title: Abandoned gas station
docs.text:
The abandoned gas station is a disused filling station on the edge of Marblehead where the task force turns the Biz's Buick into a mobile nuclear artillery piece and later hides both the car and McManley's RV from the town.

Type Location (derelict building and lot) Aliases Disused gas station; the defunct gas station Region Edge of Marblehead, Massachusetts First appearance Summer Service 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The station is disused and sits at the edge of town. Its lot has enough shelter from the rain to work on a car for hours, and room to park behind the building, out of sight of the road (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Summer Service 04
docs.text:
After the courier delivers a crate from Carter outside the post office, Kurt and Huell spend three to four hours at the station mounting the M28 Davy Crockett on the Biz's 1986 Buick Regal. Two tripod legs rest on the long flat trunk and a third goes through a hole cut in the roof. Zack (as Huell) helps with the work, joking that he is "jacked" because of the worms. The other team members run errands (ponchos, trash bags, welding goggles and earplugs) and then meet at the station, where they find "the most conspicuous vehicle any of you have ever seen" (Summer Service 04).

Rather than leave the Buick in view, the team parks it behind the station under a tarp, which Andre allows the players to retcon as having been bought at the hardware store. The roughly sixty-pound W54 warhead goes back to the hotel with the team (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Summer Service 05
docs.text:
After the 4 a.m. siege at the hotel, the group considers ditching McManley's RV, which is large, recognizable and handles badly, and retaking the smaller modified car with the Davy Crockett on it. Andre suggests hiding the RV behind the gas station, where the car was left. They abandon the RV there and take the Buick, whose roof hole has been leaking rain so that it has several inches of water on the floor and smells of "hand". They then drive out to meet McManley's borrowed assistant, who is waiting at an intercept point on the freeway on his Vespa, gore-covered, with a pharmacy bag of Ivermectin. He climbs into the cramped car and says, "I hate it here. It sucks so bad." The session ends with the team undecided about taking the drug (Summer Service 05). See McManley's RV.

Unrecorded session

The unrecorded session Summer Service 05.5 falls between Summer Service 05 and the finale. By the finale the Davy Crockett has been taken off the Buick, which Kurt says he is glad of, and the team fires it at the nuclear plant instead (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Alpine Lodge
docs.text:
Alpine Lodge is a tourist ski lodge in the mountains above Radford, Virginia, home to the teenager Matt McCready and the site of the water tower that the task force uses for its night stakeout in The Radford Horror.

Type Location (ski resort) Aliases Ski lodge; McCready ski lodge; the water tower; Make-Out Peak Region Mountains above Radford, Virginia, outside town Operators The McCready family First appearance Radford Horror 01 (as an unnamed "tourist lodge up in the mountains")

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The lodge is a tourist ski resort reached by a narrow, winding road with ski-lodge signs. It has a parking lot behind the main buildings, internal streets leading to nicer cabins, and access roads up to the ski lifts (Radford Horror 03). Out of season, a teenager keeps watch in the office at night because kids from town have been spray-painting the property. The lodge gets UFO hunters every year and keeps a rack of UFO merchandise in the gift shop (Radford Horror 06). The mountain is nicknamed "Make-Out Peak," and its view over the whole area makes it a candidate vantage point (Radford Horror 05).

Not the Ferry Lodge

The ski lodge is a different place from the Ferry Lodge in town where the team stays. The players sometimes call both "the lodge," and the Ferry Lodge is what is meant by "the lodge" in most of the team's planning (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The water tower: a curved, snow-shedding top roughly 20 feet above the tree line and 35 to 40 feet off the ground, with a 10-inch hatch in the middle. Light pollution is enough for watchers to pick out shapes moving against the horizon (Radford Horror 06).
  • The office: where the team meets Matt McCready (Radford Horror 06).
  • Cabins and lift roads: where the team loses a car it is tailing (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 01: Amanda Lucky's parents point the finger at Matt McCready, whom they say lives with his father Ed at a tourist lodge in the mountains (Radford Horror 01).
  • Radford Horror 03: The team follows a speeding car up the mountain past the ski lodge but loses it. It is not in the lodge lot and could be somewhere in the complex, on the cabin or lift roads (Radford Horror 03).
  • Radford Horror 05: The Biz suggests using the lodge's water tower for night observation, and the plan is carried over to the next session (Radford Horror 05).
  • Radford Horror 06: The Biz and Andrew take a squad car up to the lodge and find Matt on night watch. He has them sign a Sharpie waiver, lends them the key to the locked ladder, and says Dean Lawson was his first thought when Amanda went missing. He marks the Lawson family cabin on a tourist map about a mile from the lodge. He also says that while maintaining the ski lifts he felt something big and silent pass over him, smelling like compost or "an old closet," and that he no longer goes out there without a shotgun. From the tower the Biz and Andrew watch the craft carry off the Whateley twin and drop Huell, and they toss the key back to McCready, who catches it mid-joint. The team's cover story the next morning is that Huell fell off the water tower (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Matt McCready is the lodge's night watchman. Radford Horror 01 has Amanda's parents say he lives with his father Ed at the lodge, while in Radford Horror 06 Matt says his uncle owns the place and he helps out. The episodes do not reconcile the two (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: Amos Shaw's house
docs.text:
Amos Shaw's house is the priest's home in Marblehead, which Huell finds standing open with its bathroom wrecked and soaked in blood, a shelf of Lemuria books and ten pounds of crystal spheres in the nightstand.

Type Location (private house; crime scene) Aliases The murder house; the priest's house Region Marblehead, on Huell's route to the McDonald's, near a payphone Owner Amos Shaw First appearance Summer Service 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The house is on Huell's route to McDonald's and is near a payphone. Its door has stood open for days and the mail has piled up around the front door. Crucifixes hang throughout, and the decor is that of a bachelor, suggesting a single resident (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Living room and kitchen. A lamp is tipped over onto the floor, the couch is knocked out of place, fixtures are toppled and there are holes in the drywall. A burner is lit under a pan whose bottom has melted out. Next to the pan are medical tweezers, a roll of gauze with bloody fingerprints and other debris of someone treating an injury. A smear of blood leads from the base of the stairs into the kitchen and ends.
  • Upstairs hall. A long gouge runs through the wall as if a crowbar had been shoved in and dragged, with blood along its length.
  • Bathroom. The door has been burst outward from inside, its hinges partly torn from the wall. Blood fills the tub and sink, rags of skin hang on the taps, the mirror is broken and half pulled off the wall, a wrenched tub pipe drips into the carpet and the window is smashed.
  • Bedroom. Untouched. It holds a shelf of academic biblical books beside fringe material on Lemuria, clerical garments in the closet like those worn at the church (some missing), and in the nightstand an improvised plastic grocery bag of about ten pounds of clear crystal spheres like those Jester carries.

docs.title: Summer Service 03
docs.text:
Late at night, Huell, restless after about forty-eight hours without sleep, knocks on the door (the GM insists he do so in character) and it swings open. He turns off the burner, then rolls Read a Bad Situation, which tells him that nobody present means him harm. He investigates the kitchen and bedroom, then calls the FBI switchboard from a payphone and has the team paged (Summer Service 03).

Donald McManley arrives in his mobile-home lab. He reports that the amount of blood is about a human body's worth, mostly lost in the bathroom, so the victim is dead, and because the bathroom door was broken outward a second party may have been present. He accepts Huell's "wellness check" story, bags the marbles, has his tech print the house overnight and means to keep the local police out of it. The mail on the porch is all addressed to Amos Shaw. McManley reasons that the blood is three or four days old and that Andrew met Shaw alive within that window, so the victim is someone else (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Summer Service 04
docs.text: At the selectmen's meeting Shaw is present and smiling, with early signs of the bloating seen in other members. Dante (as Kurt) refers to him as the man "whose house looked like somebody fucking exploded in it". The team discusses arresting him for murder or searching the house again, but does not resolve it (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Shaw is missing from the 7 a.m. service in Summer Service 03, where the mayor preaches in his place, but is alive and at the table in Summer Service 04. The identity of the person who died in the house is never given. See Amos Shaw.

docs.title: Arnold Weathers' house
docs.text:
Arnold Weathers' house is a walled, chained-and-padlocked seaside house on the island across the bay in Marblehead, where the task force fights the infected Doberman Puddles and then finds and destroys Arnold himself.

Type Location (private house) Aliases Arnold's house; the chained house Region The island across the bay, Marblehead Owner Arnold Weathers First appearance Summer Service 03 (cold open)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In the cold open of Summer Service 03 the house is an ornate old building overlooking the sea, with a chained gate and a chained front door (Summer Service 03). In Summer Service 05 the team sees it for the first time as an estate behind an eight-foot privacy wall, with a padlocked gate hidden from the road. The decor is late 1970s, and the GM prices the house at roughly $700,000 to $800,000 "in 1992 money". The telephone still works (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Courtyard and yard. Neglected. The mail pile goes back about a week, longer than the four days Madeline claims. There is an empty dog bowl but no dog.
  • Entry and living room. Clumps of black hair around the entry; late-1970s furnishings; smears on the ceiling; a fresh, viscous "nest" on the couch.
  • Kitchen and pantry. The kitchen is clean and abandoned. A lattice-doored pantry conceals the headless dog's body, which is burned here.
  • Library. Closed; not entered.
  • Upstairs hall and bathroom. A trail of dark, decomposed-smelling fluid leads to a tub of black liquid.
  • Bedroom. Holds two near-identical sets of the town's financial books and a shoebox full of clear marbles.

(Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Summer Service 03
docs.text: Jester carries a tray of food at night to the chained house, unlocks the gate, steps in and locks it behind him. At the front door he calls, "Arnold? Buddy, you feelin' any better? I brought you some food." A wet, drooling, dog-like growl answers and something thumps the door. He slides the tray through the mail slot; it is yanked inside, the growl turns to crazed barking and the door and chains bounce. This is the cold open (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Summer Service 05
docs.text:
Madeline, who says her uncle has been out of contact for four days, leads the team across the flooded bridge. Kurt picks the gate lock and the front-door padlock, and Madeline opens the door itself with her key. Inside:

  • Puddles. Huell's flashlight reveals a bloated, hairless white Doberman streaming fluid, its collar cutting into its neck. A bullet through the forehead does nothing. It bites Huell and then Kurt. Andrew's void spray beheads it but also passes through Kurt's hand. The head stays alive; the headless body later stands up in the pantry and is burned. See Puddles.
  • Arnold. Upstairs, Arnold lunges from the tub: bloated, hairless and soft, with broken handcuffs cut into his wrists. He is trying to flee, not to attack. Andrew body-blocks him and he ruptures into worms; Huell kicks off his jaw and a strip of face, then stomps his knee until the head comes off against the sink and the body collapses into worms. The team shuts the bathroom door; moaning continues behind it.
  • Aftermath. Kurt phones the FBI from the house phone, Huell collects worms in an emptied rice jar and finds the ledgers and marbles, and Kurt tests the worms in the kitchen: vodka, heat and heavy salt kill them, and communion wine does not. Madeline recognises the dog's head as Puddles and learns that her uncle will not recover. The team leaves a pantry burned to charcoal (Summer Service 05).

See Arnold Weathers and The worms.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Arnold Weathers, his Doberman Puddles, and until the end of the night whatever worms they carried. Madeline Weathers is his niece and lives elsewhere.

docs.title: Augustine house and barn
docs.text:
The Augustine house and barn is the Radford family home, bordering the woods and a river clearing, where Phoebe Augustine vanishes from her bed, and whose locked backyard barn is her father Derek's writing office.

Type Location (suburban house and converted barn) Aliases The barn; Augustine household and barn; Augustine house and river clearing Region Suburban Radford, Virginia, at the edge of the woods Residents Derek Augustine, Maybelline Augustine, Phoebe Augustine, and a son of about eleven First appearance Radford Horror 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The house is a wide, upper-middle-class ranch house with a semicircular driveway and a large green backyard, with thin trees along a neighboring yard (Radford Horror 03). The barn at the back has been converted to an office. It has frosted aftermarket windows, a desk and typewriter, a record player (light jazz), a couch, a mini fridge and a lamp, but no air conditioning, phone or calendar. A hayloft with no ladder holds boxes of paper, an old vacuum and Christmas decorations (Radford Horror 03). Phoebe's bedroom is full of horse things, with no UFO items, and its window faces the woods at the end of the street (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The barn: Derek's writing space, usually locked. The writer inside is drafting a romance novel Andre describes as "the shittiest romance novel that anyone has ever seen," about a thousand pages deep (Radford Horror 03). Derek writes under the pen name Marcus Heat (Radford Horror 05).
  • Phoebe's bedroom: with an unmade bed, one slipper by the window and the other across the room (Radford Horror 05).
  • The woods and river clearing behind the house: a roughly 40 by 30 foot clearing where Phoebe's blood trail ends about 20 feet short of the water, with white powder (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Radford Horror 03
docs.text: Kurt tails Dr. Lori to the house. Lori storms out of the barn after a furious meeting, and an unrecognized man follows to the door, smokes, says "Fuck," and goes back in; a typewriter starts. The team learns the house belongs to Derek and Maybelline Augustine, the family of Amanda's friend Phoebe, and Deputy Molly Underhill says the family has never crossed law enforcement's radar (Radford Horror 03). Kurt picks the barn lock and spends over two hours in the hayloft. When the writer leaves for dinner, Kurt searches the barn, finding a notepad of plot notes with dates paired with acronyms (which he copies by graphite trace), unused condoms, aspirin and cigarettes, and no pill bottles. In the couch cushions he finds a small pink butterfly hair tie, and takes it with wadded drafts from the trash. Kurt suspects an affair, possibly with a minor (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: Radford Horror 04
docs.text: At 4:30 a.m. the team's pagers go off: Phoebe is missing from her bed, gone about an hour. Police and neighbors comb the woods. The blood trail Kurt follows with luminol ends at the riverside clearing, and the search turns up the white powder. A witness says Phoebe was wearing only a long T-shirt and already had cuts on her feet from the brambles (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Radford Horror 05
docs.text: The team interviews the Augustines while a part-time deputy sits with them. Derek's eye flickers at Dr. Lori's name; he says the pink clip must have fallen off when Amanda visited a few weeks earlier, and that Lori gives him "a weird vibe" because "he likes jazz too much." Kurt searches Phoebe's room and learns Amanda was seeing someone besides Dean Lawson; Maybelline says one Whateley twin had a crush on Phoebe. Kurt notes that the clip in Amanda's hair matches the one from the barn (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• Derek Augustine: pharmacist and romance novelist (Radford Horror 05).
  • Maybelline Augustine: Phoebe's mother, who gossips about Dean Lawson (Radford Horror 05).
  • Phoebe Augustine: the missing "horse girl," a friend of Amanda (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Auraria, Georgia
docs.text:
Auraria, Georgia is an abandoned gold-rush ghost town in the mountains near Dahlonega, taken over about ten years before the arc by the religious community known as the Covenant.

Type Location, ghost town Aliases Auraria; the Covenant site Region North Georgia, a 15 to 20 minute drive from Dahlonega Occupants The Covenant First appearance Appalachia 01 (mentioned)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Auraria ("gold in Latin") is a gold-rush ghost town. Its pre-Civil War church is the only good building, lightly modernized, and white tents glow around it. A sign reads "Welcome to the Covenant. Try our peaches," and closed-up morning glories grow everywhere (Appalachia 02).

By the time of Appalachia 04 the party had walked the town. The Covenant has no electricity or phones. Members live in tents, the old church and the community center, and the site has handmade rough-wood outhouses, many stills, a stand selling preserves and quilts, and a farm truck. Members bathe in the river. As Kurt walked through, he judged the community to be on the edge of economic viability, with frantic canning and quilting in hot tents.

The Smith Hotel desk clerk described the residents' long dresses, tents and end-of-the-world talk, and said he would not stay there after dark (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The pre-Civil War church.
  • The community center, the only other building in town, used for the party's interviews with River and Mother Dahlia Riversand (Appalachia 04).
  • The preparation tent and the river, used for red-clay baptisms. A Covenant member said runoff from the Spud Hut plant ran into the river.
  • A hiking trail about ten minutes from town that leads to the Circle Chasers' footprint site and the rabbit-snatch site; see the woods trail and The Field and Bent Tree.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Appalachia 01. The missing Willow Greengrass was a Covenant member who vanished near Auraria; the team's dossier mentioned Auraria, which was not on their map, and included an article about religious vision ceremonies. Older Bigfoot sightings clustered near the town (Appalachia 01).

Appalachia 02. The party drove to Auraria and pulled up at dusk to find robed members paying them little mind, then took the trail toward the Chasers' circle without approaching them (Appalachia 02).

Appalachia 04. The party interviewed Covenant members. Clover said Willow had been sent by Elijah Ray to scout peach orchards and had fought with her sister. River and Mother Dahlia Riversand explained a land dispute: "corporate goons" had arrived about a year earlier with paperwork threatening eviction, and the Covenant was selling preserves to pay a lawyer. See The Land Dispute. Dahlia produced copies of eviction letters naming only a law firm, Jackson and Lee's. Rita's Andrew spoke with the door-to-door salesman Jeremy through a tent wall, and the team left without meeting the Reverend (Appalachia 04).

Appalachia 06. Frotter Comstock's property lies outside Auraria; see Comstock's Property. The Gold Bug, the town's official newspaper, has its shop front here, and a staff member told the party it would be "hard to keep a Bigfoot costume secret in this town" (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The Covenant, led by Elijah Ray, with Mother Dahlia Riversand as elder. Their beliefs are covered on Covenant Beliefs, and they make Covenant Peach Preserves.

docs.title: The bar
docs.text:
The bar is an unnamed Ballard, Utah bar across the street from the courthouse, with darts, a slightly broken pool table and a cassette jukebox, where the team meets the bartender Maggie.

Type Location (bar) Aliases Ballard bar; Maggie's bar Region Ballard, Utah Inhabitants Maggie First appearance Walkers 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The bar sits across the street from the closed courthouse, a building that was clearly once a church. It is nervously quiet, with very quiet jazz playing, a dartboard, a slightly broken pool table and a cassette jukebox that Maggie tries to fix. The bar has the energy of "please don't give the government an excuse to shut us down": the nosy Mormon majority of Ballard barely tolerates it, and Maggie is fiercely protective of its license (Walkers 03).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Sheriff McDermish took the team there for a beer after they told him they wanted an exhumation done. The party spent about two hours in the bar (Walkers 03).

  • Howard and the shot. Maggie suspected Andrew Howard of being "another Mormon fed", demanded ID and made him drink a free vodka-Coke shot, then softened and gave him a root beer float. She later put half-gallon milkshakes on the house, and the Biz teased Andrew as "Half-Gallon Howard".
  • Darts. Huell rolled a 7 and spent a Luck point to beat the Biz, who handed over $20.
  • Recognition. Maggie recognized the Biz as the man who "spied on Bill Clinton" and Huell as the man on the couch who "looked like a hostage", though an armed one.
  • Gossip. She told the team that Deborah Wells was building the community center half a county from the community, that Pueblo ruins were bulldozed for it, and that she once saw what she thought was ball lightning on the ranch's back road. Ballard had about thirty blackouts a year and nothing in town worked.
  • The water. A drunk Huell told her the town water had semen in it. The party half-confirmed it, and she reasoned it must be bulk-bought animal semen with a paper trail. See Ballard water contamination.
  • The sheriff. He swapped Vietnam stories with Kurt and described in detail the lasting effects of being shot in the rear, until Maggie said she would need a rule on the wall about it, before leaving to be with his son and a game of Monopoly.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 03

docs.title: Ballard City Hall
docs.text:
Ballard City Hall is a converted double-wide in Ballard, Utah, with dusty offices, bedrooms stacked with file boxes, the mayor's candy-strewn desk and a padlocked refrigerator of sugar, found abandoned in The Walkers in Skin.

Type Location (government building) Aliases City Hall; the Ballard courthouse Region Ballard, Utah Affiliation Ballard town government First appearance Walkers 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A double-wide converted to offices, with the lights on and the shades drawn. Inside were dust on everything, fans running, a radio playing the news, and no cars outside. Nobody had been there for days to a week. The kitchenette was stripped, the bedrooms were stacked with file boxes, and there was a padlocked refrigerator (Walkers 06).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The sugar fridge. Huell Kendrick found a key ring in a desk and opened the fridge to find plastic bags of coarse white granules stacked floor to ceiling. Kurt tipped a sample into a vial, and Andrew photographed the bags. It was just sugar. See Sugar clues.
  • The mayor's desk. Piled with New York Post newspapers that stop abruptly about three months earlier, buried under hundreds of Tootsie Roll wrappers.
  • Deborah Wells's desk. The other heavily used desk, belonging to the city treasurer and school superintendent.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The party tried the door after the answering machine said the office was out to lunch. Kurt's first lockpick snapped in the lock; a second cleared the broken tip and he shouldered the thin door open. While they searched, the mayor's Cadillac arrived. The party claimed the door was open and they had come for records on Yusuf. The mayor chewed lemon candies nervously, said the junkyard was outside the municipality, mentioned that a fire a few years earlier had destroyed the geological records, offered to call a friend at the county records office, took the ranch's number and locked up (Walkers 06).

Walkers 07 recalls the sugar fridge and the mayor's candies, and in Walkers 08 the team uses them to conclude he was replaced a couple of months earlier.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Andre calls the building "the courthouse" throughout the visit and confirms to Zack, "Yes, this is the Ballard Courthouse", while the players call it City Hall. This conflicts with Walkers 03, where the courthouse across from the bar is a closed former church. The show never reconciles the two.

docs.text:

  • Walkers 07 (recap)
  • Walkers 08 (mentioned)

docs.title: Ballard general store
docs.text:
The Ballard general store is the town grocery and gossip hub of Ballard, Utah, where the team shops in Walkers 02 and where Huell's solo meeting goes wrong in Walkers 06.

Type Location (shop) Aliases Ballard grocery store Region Ballard, Utah First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A full grocery with baloney, Spam, white bread, tortillas, American cheese, pasta, mayo, mustard, Ball Park franks and potatoes. It is open nine to five, Monday through Saturday (Walkers 02). Andre calls it "a general store" when the team drives into town, and the clerk tells them "it's a grocery store"; Walkers 06 calls it the grocery store, and it has an alley beside it and a back break room with Go Fish cards, magazines, a decanter of Tang and a nicotine-stained door.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• The beehive clerk (Walkers 02). A middle-aged, lifelong resident with an enormous beehive hairdo. She greeted the team with "Y'all are new, right?", insisted Ballard was normal ("The ranch is weird, but that's the county"), resented the community center, blamed the mayor and "the goddamn busybody" Deborah Wells, and would prefer a clinic. She misses Reagan and traded Rod Serling jokes with Kurt. She mentioned Edward Douglas, a local man who shot half his foot off and drove an hour for treatment.
  • The listless clerk (Walkers 06). The only person on duty, who said the rest of the rotation (a weekend girl, a janitor and a stock boy) was not due. The episodes do not say whether she is the beehive clerk.

docs.title: The grocery run (Walkers 02)
docs.text: The team bought bologna, white bread, mayo, American cheese, cheap beer and Ball Park franks for $35.25. Howard awkwardly questioned the clerk while the others watched. The team told her to drink only bottled or well water because of the contaminated supply, saying "We're from the government"; see Ballard water contamination. Dante (as Kurt) remarked to the Biz that "Andrew has no game" (Walkers 02).

docs.title: Huell's failed meeting (Walkers 06)
docs.text: After an unknown caller phoned about "your colleague" and told Huell Kendrick to come alone to the store and let himself into the little room in back, Huell went alone. In the alley beside the store a "homeless" man asked for a dollar, lunged and bit Huell's wrist, shouted "Pig!" and ran off with the dollar. The clerk bandaged him and said "we don't got homeless in Ballard". Huell waited in the break room with a hand on the P90, found nothing, and returned to the guest house, over an hour later, with a bloody bandage on his hand. See The "homeless" man. The recap of Walkers 07 says the bite later gave the faction Huell's tissue. See Replication.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The "general store" of Walkers 02 and the "grocery store" of Walkers 06 are treated as one shop; the clerk's own words in Walkers 02 use both terms. Stewart's, the grocery in Roosevelt, is a different shop.

docs.text:

  • Walkers 07 (recap)

docs.title: Ballard High School
docs.text:
Ballard High School is the small county high school in Ballard, Utah, a school of about sixty students with a bad smell hanging over it. Its gym is where Andrew Howard is replaced by a duplicate, where plastic-wrapped corpses are hidden in the ceiling, and where a grenade starts the fire that destroys the building.

Type Location (school) Aliases The gym; school gym; Ballard schools Region Ballard, Utah Status Burned nearly to the ground (as of Walkers 08) First appearance Walkers 03 (mentioned); Walkers 04 (described)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The school draws students from the whole county, yet has only about sixty. The teenager Harrison tells the task force that this semester the smell has been "fucking eye-watering", and that the students sing a crude anthem to the tune of "We Are the Champions" (Walkers 04). The gym is an ordinary school gym, with lockers down one hallway and offices down another (Walkers 07).

docs.title: The gym
docs.text: An anonymous note tells Andrew to come to the school gym at 1 a.m., adding that the lock is taped over so the kids can smoke weed there (Walkers 06). On the night, a thin line of yellow light shows under the door, the latch is taped, and two stools stand in the middle of the floor (Walkers 07). After the fight the sprinklers are running, chairs are scattered, and a dead horse lies by the door. Part of the ceiling later gives way and drops the stored bodies (Walkers 07).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Warning signs. Before the task force reaches the school, locals describe its decline. The bartender Maggie mentions a smell at the high school, four new school computers that never worked, and the way people who might earn a college degree keep disappearing (Walkers 03). The Ballard sheriff later reports that a county spot-check found over half the students absent, while the school says its own numbers show no absences and calls the discrepancy "an oversight"; most of the absent students are Mormon (Walkers 06). See Disappearances in Ballard.

The night of the gym. Andrew goes in alone; Huell drops him three blocks away and later parks a block from the school. Inside, two upright horses flank Andrew, and he finds a second Andrew Howard sitting on a stool. The double says, "We can do this the easy way or the hard way", and Andrew pepper-sprays it. Armed locals then come into the room. Andrew pulls out a grenade, drops it, and one of the horses throws itself onto it. The horses beat him down, and the badly injured double crawls on top of him and forces tendrils into his mouth (Walkers 07). See Replication.

Andre had removed every other player from the scene before Andrew entered the gym. When the scene ends he gives Rita a private handout and tells her she is now "in a replica". From this point Rita plays the duplicate, not the original (Walkers 07).

The fire. Huell sees flickering light, hears an explosion, finds the gym in flames, and meets "Andrew" (the duplicate) staggering out bloodied while a burning horse runs across the parking lot. Inside he finds blast damage and the remains of the horses, and a pack of coyotes standing stock-still in a hallway. When part of the ceiling falls, a spiral bundle of melted plastic drops out, and more bundles follow: putrefied corpses packed in white powder, about six in all. No fire truck ever comes (Walkers 07). See Plastic-wrapped bodies.

Aftermath. Driving through town the next morning, the team sees that the school is "pretty much burned to the ground" (Walkers 08). In the Roosevelt police morgue they find dozens of salted bodies, and Andre says they have found "where the bodies from the library ceiling went" (Walkers 08). The real Andrew wakes among them. In Walkers 09 he says he was shot in the chest, woke up under a pile of dead naked people, and thinks he was dead. See Roosevelt police station.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The gym is held by the Skinwalker faction: armed townspeople, the horses, and the coyotes. The stored corpses are earlier victims of the skinwalkers.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Andre's "library ceiling" in Walkers 08 is almost certainly a slip for the gym ceiling, where the bodies were seen in Walkers 07.

docs.title: Ballard, Utah
docs.text:
Ballard, Utah is the small, mostly Mormon desert farming town beside Sherman Ranch where the task force investigates in The Walkers in Skin, a town where nothing works and whose people are quietly replaced by skinwalkers until it stands empty and its school burns.

Type Location (town) Aliases Ballard Region Utah, southeast of Salt Lake City Government Ballard town government (Mayor Wilford Hiram) Status Abandoned and dark (as of Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Ballard sits in red-rock desert. Andre describes it as a town of a few hundred people, "500 people... maybe a thousand", yet surprisingly complete: a high school, a courthouse in a converted former church, a general store, a church, a diner, a bar, and mostly double-wides with a few wooden buildings. Even the sheriff's station is a double-wide (Walkers 02, Walkers 03). The locals mention often that most of the town is Mormon, which matters later when the missing are counted (Walkers 03, Walkers 06).

Everything in town is slightly broken. A general-store customer tells the team "The ranch is weird, but that's the county" (Walkers 02). The bartender Maggie lists about thirty blackouts a year, four new school computers that never worked, and a smell at the high school (Walkers 03).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Ballard High School, including the gym.
  • Ballard General Store, the grocery and gossip hub where the "homeless" man bites Huell.
  • The bar, Maggie's quiet bar with darts and a broken cassette jukebox.
  • Ballard City Hall, a double-wide with a fridge full of sugar.
  • Churchyard cemetery, where Shelly Wilmarth is buried.
  • The sheriff's double-wide, a station and home with a Monopoly game on a card table (Walkers 03).
  • The community center and substation, a few miles out.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Arrival. The team meets the town through its gossip. A general-store woman blames Mayor Hiram and "the goddamn busybody" Deborah Wells for the community center, and mentions a man who drove an hour for treatment after shooting off half his foot (Walkers 02). Bigelow knows that Ballard's water contains live sperm and high arsenic (Walkers 02); see Ballard water contamination.

First oddities. Sheriff McDermish agrees to file the exhumation paperwork but warns the judge may stall it (Walkers 03). Maggie says the people who might earn a college degree keep disappearing, and that Wells's community center was built on bulldozed Pueblo ruins despite a protest (Walkers 03). Walt Murphy grumbles about the Mormon-dominated council (Walkers 04). Mayor Hiram visits the team in Roosevelt, crunching lemon candies (Walkers 05).

Emptying out. By Walkers 06 City Hall has been abandoned for days or a week, the grocery has a single clerk, the diner has three patrons instead of ten to fifteen, and traffic has stopped. The sheriff reports over half the school absent and houses empty, then flees the state. A "homeless" man bites Huell, though the clerk says Ballard has no homeless (Walkers 06). See Disappearances in Ballard and Sugar clues.

The night of the gym. The phones go down and the town is eerily quiet; the gym fight ends in a fire (Walkers 07). In a private exchange with Rita, who is now playing the duplicate Andrew, Andre says the Skinwalker faction has "suborned about 60%" of the town (Walkers 07).

A dead town. As the team drives through town the next morning, the school is pretty much burned to the ground, nobody is out, and there is a bad mood in the air (Walkers 08). The team finds the mayor was taken over months ago, and concludes Ballard is "a dead town" while Roosevelt is mid-replacement. The only road out is blocked at the bridge. Dante proposes using Ballard's radio station and its backup generator; according to the recap that opens Walkers 09, the team later carried a generator there and called the National Guard (Walkers 08, Walkers 09).

Finale. In Walkers 09 the convoy drives back through totally abandoned Ballard toward the ranch and the community center. The community center collapses into a sinkhole over the stranded skinwalkers, and the ranch farmhouse is launched toward Roosevelt.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Mayor Wilford Hiram, treasurer and school superintendent Deborah Wells, Sheriff McDermish and his son Bud, the bartender Maggie, and the ordinary townspeople who are gradually replaced. See Skinwalker faction.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Walkers 02 Andre calls the trip from Salt Lake City to the ranch "almost a three-hour drive", but in Walkers 06 he places Ballard "an hour's drive" southeast of the city. The episodes never reconcile the two.

docs.title: The beach and harbor
docs.text:
The beach and harbor is the Marblehead shoreline near the center of the offshore blast, littered with dead fish and lined with taped windows, where Kurt spots and the team recovers a severed arm.

Type Location (shoreline) Region Marblehead, Massachusetts First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The old working docks sit near the beach: weathered buildings that each look "10 percent like a lighthouse", with yachts, fishing boats and lobster boats crowded in the harbor. Along the beach are broken windows, freshly repaired windows and windows covered with tape, all from the explosion a week and a half before. Dead fish lie along the shore (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The docks. Briggs, the drunk, one-footed fisherman, lives on a barely floating boat here, asleep in a lawn chair beside it when Andrew finds him.
  • Harvard's Bait Shop and a beach supply store. Huell buys a trash bag for $1 (paying $5 and taking no change) at the bait shop, whose owner's cousin draws axolotls; the team buys a cooler, ice and duct tape at the beach store.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
At about three o'clock, after church bells strike three, the team walks the beach. Dante's Kurt rolls a 12 on Investigate a Mystery and establishes that the blast came from out in the harbor and moved inland. He finds the center of the damage and sees something black bobbing among the dead fish (Summer Service 01).

It is a bloated, fish-eaten human arm in a soaked black turtleneck sleeve and black glove, running from the fingers to past the elbow, with the bone violently splintered. See The severed arm. Huell bags it, the smell lessens but does not go away, and the team leaves the glove on in case the hand comes apart. Andrew phones Diane ("I found an arm... Ocean."), who promises forensics (Summer Service 01).

Kurt's Tiger Balm, a cooler rinsed at a beach foot faucet and the open windows of the Biz's car turn the arm into a running gag for the rest of the day. A little boy cries when Andrew blames the smell on the Biz. The beach is also where Lena Scott, who loves it, wandered off from a school field trip the day after the blast and was found unconscious (Summer Service 01); see Lena Scott.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Briggs is the only named resident. Briggs reports dead fish, odd weather, headaches and bad moods since the blast. For a separate stretch of glassed coast found in later sessions, see Melted shoreline.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 01

docs.title: The big house
docs.text:
The big house is the main house and equipment barn of Sherman Ranch, rented by the billionaire Robert Bigelow as the base of his research operation: a place of camera monitors, staff quarters, a roof where an eye appears, and a porch cooler that ends up holding a dead coyote.

Type Location (house and barn) Aliases Bigelow's house; big house and barn; the barn Region Sherman Ranch, near Ballard, Utah Holder Robert Bigelow (tenant); the ranch belongs to Alberta Wilmarth First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Alberta rents the big house to Bigelow, so she offers the task force the smaller guest double-wide instead (Walkers 02). Bigelow's rules, relayed by Walt Murphy, are that the big house and the barn beside it are off-limits (Walkers 02). The bedroom windows of the double-wide face it.

Inside, a bank of TVs shows the ranch cameras, though only one camera on the big house can even partly see the guest house, and a woman on the staff can cue the tapes (Walkers 04). Staff sleep upstairs, and VHS tapes play on monitor screens (Walkers 05). The porch has a beer cooler (Walkers 07). The barn holds banks of instruments for the research and has a loose chain on its door (Walkers 04).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The porch. Bigelow receives the team here, serving sweet tea and buttered bread while a blonde security guard (Ponytail Lady) asks them to leave weapons at the door (Walkers 02). Walt gives out brownies and cold soup here (Walkers 03).
  • The camera room. The team watches footage here of the vanished rental car and of the night event (Walkers 04, Walkers 05).
  • The roof. On the evening before the night event, while the team is out in the yard, a single eye watches from the roof of the house; as they back away, at about fifty feet, the goose drops down from the roof (Walkers 05).
  • The barn. Two stoned teenagers hide behind the equipment (Walkers 04); it is later emptied of recordings (Walkers 07).
  • The big cabinet. Bigelow's armoury of SPAS-12 shotguns and M16 rifles (Walkers 07).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Instruments and data. Bigelow's team records electromagnetic, electrostatic, radio, thermal and acoustic data on large tape reels; he reports that all the anomalies are confined to the ranch and about half a mile around (Walkers 02). See Bigelow's recordings.

The cameras. Kurt asks to compare the records with the substation "pop" and the shift of the car; a curt doorman turns him away (Walkers 04). The team later gets the tape: a patch of slightly different gray seems to be where the car was, and the EM meters spike at the times of the pop and the car shift, though the data are noisy. The team parks Betsy in front of the cameras (Walkers 04) and, in Walkers 05, chains it to four posts there.

The night event. After the night event, Bigelow shows the party a frozen sky-camera frame and asks about the Black Sun; the video shows a bright white ring (see The white ring and Black Sun). He agrees to ring the guest house with cameras and arranges a dentist in Roosevelt (Walkers 05).

The break-in. After the naked intruder's attack on the guest house, Bigelow says someone broke in and stole all his hard drives, tapes and recordings, and three of his employees. The barn's contents are gone too, and whoever it was had keys to everything. He declares "protocol blue", unlocks the big cabinet, and sets a ground-floor defensive perimeter. The team finds a beer cooler on the porch and uses it, weighted with bricks, to store the dead coyote from the gym. At the close of the episode the team's plan is to drive out at sunrise with radios and summon the National Guard (Walkers 07).

The morning after. In Walkers 08 one of Bigelow's enforcers makes pancakes in the kitchen at about 9 a.m., while his people carry SPAS-12s and M16s and the phones are dead. The episode does not name the building, but later in the episode Andre suggests going "back to the ranch" for the rest of Bigelow's security force. The later fate of the ranch is told at Sherman Ranch.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Robert Bigelow and his research staff and security, including the blonde guard; the ranch hand Walt Murphy (nicknamed "Coyote"); and, for a time, the task force as backup (Walkers 07).

docs.title: The Biz's apartment
docs.text:
The Biz's apartment is Dick "The Biz" Baxter's dust-covered Washington, D.C. apartment, which Andrew, Huell and Kurt search in The Radford Horrors to find out what happened to him; it hides gold, cash, cocaine, a cipher book and a bug-out briefcase.

Type Location (apartment) Aliases None Region Washington, D.C. Resident Dick "The Biz" Baxter First appearance Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The apartment is in a complex with a front office. The mail slot is jammed and a post-office notice is stuck on the door. Inside are dust and cobwebs, a tape-patched brown leather recliner, a TV left on Animal Planet, a heater running, an ashtray of old butts, war memoirs, technical manuals, shelves of hard-boiled detective novels, Russian novels and books on Russian politics. The refrigerator holds rotten meat, and the phone is disconnected. There is no body (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The desk: spam mail the Biz kept, including sweepstakes and jelly-of-the-month clubs.
  • The loose floorboard under the rug: the Biz's full share of the gold (about two-thirds of the original find), roughly $8,000 to $9,000 in Ziplocs and rubber bands, and his cocaine.
  • The heat vent under the bed: stripped screws mark it; inside is a bug-out briefcase with a few hundred US dollars, a much larger sum in Swiss francs, a cheap revolver, a change of clothes and a Swiss passport with the Biz's photo under the name Noah Mueller.

(All from Radford Horrors 01.)

The gold under the floorboard disagrees with the epilogue of Roulet Estate 03, in which the other agents bury the Biz's share in a park near his home and leave him a cryptic message.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Andrew Howard, newly back from New York, picks up Huell from his squalid apartment, because Diane has called and cannot reach the Biz, who left the hospital months before. At the Biz's building, the front-office staff say, "Oh, thank God, the police are finally here about Baxter. Is he dead?" and half the room looks disappointed, and Huell guesses they have a betting pool on whether he is dead. Andrew's aura gets the manager to hand over the emergency key without ID (Radford Horrors 01).

Andrew's Investigate a Mystery roll (12) finds that a discount Playboy subscription began days before the Biz vanished, showing he planned to stay, and that a copy of Moby-Dick has its first few hundred pages removed. The discarded pages in the wastebasket have circled and underlined words, and a chart of numbers and arrows sits in the back; see the Moby-Dick book cipher. Unopened FBI mail shows the Biz was granted a six-month personal leave for a "family emergency" but never signed the follow-up paperwork (Radford Horrors 01).

Andrew privately asks Huell whether the Biz could be a double agent; Huell answers, "I didn't notice when you got replaced with an alien." Andrew phones Kurt, who arrives in the family minivan to the smell of "four-month-old ham." Kurt reassembles the torn pages and goes through the spam, finding bills for classified ads the Biz placed in the Washington City Paper, the Washington Informer and the Georgetown Current. The circled words read "instructions to cause soon submarine lost near" (order unknown, set incomplete). Kurt's Investigate a Mystery roll (11) finds the bug-out briefcase and he concludes the Biz meant to return, was corresponding with a third party and was intercepted. Diane is asked to narrow the disappearance window, pull international flights and check on missing submarines; she knows only of those lost at Marblehead (Radford Horrors 01).

Meanwhile in Moscow

The episode intercuts the search with the Biz's own scenes: he is a captive in the Hotel Metropol in Moscow, held since January (Radford Horrors 01). The searchers do not know this.
