docs.text: • Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Black Site Omaha
docs.text:
Black Site Omaha is a CIA prison five stories under the sea, beneath a naval research base, where Jan Martense is held after the Dahlonega case.

Type Location, black site Aliases Omaha Operator CIA Region Beneath a naval research base Notable inmate Jan Martense First appearance Walkers 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Kurt Larson reaches Omaha by passing through a naval research base and a keycode door and riding an elevator five stories below the ocean. Inside are steel corridors, a medical wing, and steel interview rooms where prisoners are held in plastic restraints with rounded edges. Visits are cleared in four-hour blocks (Walkers 01).

Playing cards are banned, so Kurt bribes the desk guard with ordinary cigarettes (he stresses they are not poisoned or hallucinogenic) and later keeps a promise to ask for anti-suicide playing cards for Jan.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
In the epilogue to The Things in Appalachia, Kurt interviews Jan in a steel room. Jan wears a gray jumpsuit and plastic handcuffs, cuffed to a plastic chair, with stitches and bruising. In the climax he was shot and then crushed by a falling ape, which broke his skull. They agree to a quid pro quo, and Kurt teaches him to make improvised playing cards from napkins and coasters. Jan tells how, about five years earlier, he drunkenly struck and killed a man in a black suit on a Georgia highway, found NSA identification on him, and found an ape woman, whom he named Shelly, in the man's van. He began the breeding and mining that became Jan's Conspiracy (Walkers 01). See also the dead NSA man.

Jan could not say why the Spud Hut facility exploded. Kurt, who suspects the explosion was deliberate, keeps the portal secret from him, since Jan appears not to know of it. Ordered not to attend David Letterman's taping, Kurt sees the Biz sweating on a TV while he waits.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• Jan Martense, held prisoner.
  • An unnamed desk guard, who accepts cigarettes and clears visits.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 01

docs.title: The Break Room (code 441)
docs.text:
The Break Room (code 441) is a fake break room on the Special Projects level beneath the Spud Hut plant in Dahlonega, which in fact held the ape-creatures that ambushed the party.

Type Location, holding room Aliases The break room Region Special Projects level, four stories underground at the Spud Hut plant Inhabitants Ape-men First appearance Appalachia 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The room lies behind a hefty, windowless steel door that opens into the hallway and is keyed with code 441. Jan told the party it held chairs and a drinks machine. It was actually a dark room of rattling steel cages, which Dante's character called a "werewolf feeding pen" disguised as a break room. Veterinary equipment, gurneys with thick leather straps and mining equipment were stashed nearby (Appalachia 08; Appalachia 09).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The room appears first in the cold open of Appalachia 08. The camera glides to the double steel doors marked "Special Projects," drops through a floor grate, and enters a dark room of cages. Distant hooting and shrieking build, then stop as a dozen eyes turn toward the camera (Appalachia 08).

In the session itself, Jan Martense took the party down a second elevator ("Down here we do the toppings"), gave them the code, told them to wait five minutes, and rode back up on the excuse of an internal call. Kurt Larson opened the door and propped it with his shoe. While the others explored the floor, Dick "The Biz" Baxter heard the door squeak and saw a huge pale arm probe out. The party then fought five pale, hairy, long-nailed creatures. One threw Andrew Howard through the drop ceiling and juggled him, another punched a dog whistle into Kurt's throat, and Kurt ended the fight with a Claymore mine (see Claymore Mine). The blast destroyed the door frame and the opposite wall. The sheriff, Carter Burke, dived through the door into the room when he saw the mine (Appalachia 08).

The session closed on a table joke from Dante: "Who left the ape-men in the break room? Lenny."

In Appalachia 09 Andre remarked that "it was never a break room. It was just a door", a door onto the cage room that Jan had passed off as one, and that Claymore shrapnel had blown the door away completely. Clive explained that the creatures were "rejects," ape-men whose temperament did not take to training; Jan was too "sensitive" to dispose of them.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Five untrainable ape-men, caged here and kept near the kennel (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The two episodes give different casualty counts. At the end of Appalachia 08, Andre said one creature was dead, two were badly injured and the rest had fled. In Appalachia 09, Andre's recap says the Claymore killed two, and the party tells Clive that two are dead and three are missing.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 08
  • Appalachia 09 (aftermath)

docs.title: Bridge blockade
docs.text:
The bridge blockade is the barricade at a creek bridge on the only road out of the Ballard and Roosevelt area, held by twenty to twenty-five armed skinwalkers in stolen police uniforms, which keeps the task force and the towns' residents from reaching the outside world.

Type Location (roadblock) Aliases The bridge; the blockade; fake police at the bridge Region Road out of Roosevelt, Utah toward Bridgeland Held by Skinwalker faction Status Broken through with the National Guard (as told in the recap of Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A bridge over a creek carries the only road out. A barrier of about a dozen cars, a few of them overturned, plus an ambulance, cars with police lights, and some horses, blocks it. About twenty to twenty-five heavily armed people man it, most dressed as cops in what looks like uniforms and body armor taken from the police station. The next town, Bridgeland, is 23 miles away, and Salt Lake City is 141 (Walkers 08). The creek could be crossed by car off-road, but only with difficulty, and climbing the far embankment would be a last resort.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Scouting. After finding Roosevelt's police dead and its cars gone, the team drives a couple of miles toward Bridgeland in a two-car convoy with Betsy in front. Kurt parks well back and creeps up on foot, rolling an 11 on Act Under Pressure, and sees the blockade diverting traffic and turning people back (Walkers 08). As the team leaves, the blockade turns around a FedEx truck.

Conclusions. From this the players conclude that the world beyond the town is probably normal, that Ballard is "a dead town", and that Roosevelt is being replaced person by person, starting with the police. They reason that the cops' cars must be tied up at the blockade. They consider fetching the rest of Bigelow's security force from the ranch, using Ballard's radio station, or trying the road east toward Vernal, and drive back toward Ballard (Walkers 08).

Unrecorded session

The session between Walkers 08 and Walkers 09 was never recorded. In the recap that opens Walkers 09, Andre says the team got horses to get around the roadblock, took a generator to the radio station and called the National Guard, met the Guard on horseback outside town, and fought through the road barricade between Ballard and Roosevelt before breaching and clearing the police station. The recap does not describe the fight, and it does not say whether this barricade is the same as the bridge. See Lost episodes.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Armed skinwalkers in police uniforms: the same faction that massacred the Roosevelt police. The blockaders are not fought on-screen in a recorded session.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 08
  • Walkers 09 (recap only)

docs.title: Brooks Pharmacy
docs.text:
The Brooks Pharmacy is a one-story strip-mall pharmacy in a town about 25 miles from Exeter, Rhode Island, where a masked gunman takes hostages in the finale of The Roulet Estate.

Type Location (shop) Aliases The Brooks Region A town about 25 miles from Exeter, Rhode Island First appearance Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The store has wraparound laminated-glass windows, one of them riddled with bullet holes, and a door on the corner set at about 45 degrees; Rita compares it to a CVS. A service entrance at the back is kept locked by someone named Markeith. An access ladder for roof maintenance, currently retracted and six or seven feet up, leads to a roof door and a cramped crawl space full of air-conditioning equipment above a drop ceiling. Inside, the pharmacy area has been trashed, with plastic tubs and pill bottles scattered across the floor, and a checkout counter stands near the front. A parking lot lies in front, with snow on the ground. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
• The arrival. A local cop reports that the agents' stolen car has been spotted at the Brooks. When the agents arrive, it is parked beside a squad car with two cops hiding behind it. The young balding cop is shot dead as he steps out of the car. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • The briefing. Officer Todd surrenders command to Andrew and relays the gunman's demands: a fueled Range Rover with no trackers, no police cars in the lot, and all cops inside within ten minutes, naked, to be handcuffed to shopping carts. A businessman hostage runs out carrying a brick-sized cellular phone and recites a number, 401-998-3147, for the agents to call. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • The plan. Shots from the store flatten the tires of the car the agents are pushing, so Kurt strips a popped tire, soaks it in a flask's worth of vodka and stuffs in a bag of crusty donuts from the squad car to make a smoke screen. Andrew stalls the gunman on the phone, asking whether a Ford Bronco will work, and takes off his shirt after being told to strip, which draws the old woman in the VW Beetle. The Biz climbs the ladder, picks the roof door lock with a credit card and creeps through the drop ceiling. Kurt picks the back door and creeps toward the counter, where a hostage's gaze tells him where the gunman is. Andre estimates 20 or 30 hostages from the shapes in the window and the crowd outside. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • The fight. The Biz shoots first through the ceiling and is hit in the thigh by a Mosin-Nagant round, falling to the tile. Huell tackles the gunman and takes a shot through the foot. Kurt binds him. Police remove the alien mask, and the man, revealed as the Roulet Intruder, is given beta blockers when he begins to collapse. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The pharmacist (shot non-fatally), a businessman, a customer with a gut wound, and the other hostages. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: The cavern
docs.text:
The cavern is the vast underground cave beneath Sherman Ranch, first found by ground-penetrating radar and later revealed, under the community center, to hold the portal machine and the evacuating skinwalkers before it collapses in the finale.

Type Location (cave) Aliases The cave; Ballroom shaft Region Beneath Sherman Ranch and the community center, Utah Status Collapsed (as of Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 05

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
As first found. On the day after the night event, the dealer Drebin demonstrates the ground-penetrating radar and spots a big signal 70 feet down: "No, it's like a cave." Dante (as Kurt) rolls double fives plus three on a Sharp check, a 12, and learns that the cave seems to extend under the whole area, deeply buried, with no shallower gradient anywhere on the property (Walkers 05).

As entered. The way down is from the community center, through an unguarded back door into a hallway with dirt on the floor. Behind a lock marked "Ballroom" is a huge hole with scaffolding around its edge, a bundle of high-powered electrical conduit and shaky stairs, a few hundred feet deep. At the bottom is a huge cave lit by work lights (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text: At the far end of the cavern stands a machine the size of about half a dozen semi-trailers, built into the corpse of a creature like the glowing, insect-limbed grub-angel the team fought earlier in the campaign (The Summer Service). See Grub-angel power core. The machine generates a portal about 20 feet across, through which people pour and tanks are carried (Walkers 09).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Secrecy. Alberta Wilmarth guesses a natural gas bed when Kurt phones her, worries about mineral rights, and asks the team to tell no one (Walkers 05). In Walkers 06 Kurt asks the town for geological survey data to find an entrance, but is told that a fire years ago destroyed most of the records and that the area is "not very geologically active".

The evacuation. In Walkers 09 the team strips off its metal and clothing, marks itself with Sharpie, and sneaks down. Naked skinwalkers carry tanks of blood with things swimming inside toward the machine; the mayor carries supplies; an elderly farmer with one arm missing and a chunk of his torso blown out vomits his brain into a tank and dies; skinwalkers stop silently to entangle tendrils. Through the portal is a burned, blasted landscape under a smoky sky, with emergency lights set up in a trail that the carriers follow.

Collapse. The cavern's power fails, the portal spasms, and a diffuse scream in an unknown language sounds as people rush it. In the dark the team pulls pins and throws grenades into the crowd. Zack (as Huell) lands one far off in the support machinery and the portal winks out, stranding some 50 or 60 skinwalkers in the dark. Kurt's flame light melts itself. The duplicate Andrew attacks the team and is shot by the real Andrew, and a brain-creature wriggles out of his mouth. The ceiling collapses as the team flees up the stairs, and the community center slides into a sinkhole (Walkers 09).

docs.title: What lies unknown
docs.text: Who built the shaft and machinery, where the portal leads, and what became of those who went through are never explained. Zack asks whether the far side resembles the room with the portal in Georgia (The Things in Appalachia), and Andre says it does not (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The radar signal is placed 70 feet down in Walkers 05, while the Ballroom shaft in Walkers 09 is a few hundred feet deep. The episodes do not reconcile the two figures.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 05
  • Walkers 06
  • Walkers 09

docs.title: Churchyard cemetery
docs.text:
The churchyard cemetery is the fenced graveyard in Ballard, Utah where Shelly Wilmarth lies under an expensive black granite slab, the target of the task force's exhumation plan in The Walkers in Skin.

Type Location (cemetery) Aliases The cemetery; Shelly Wilmarth's grave; black granite slab Region Ballard, Utah First appearance Walkers 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The churchyard is fenced and locked with a cheap '90s Master Lock. The gate opens with "the loudest squeal you have ever heard", and the grass is well maintained (Walkers 03).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text: Shelly Wilmarth's grave. A big black granite slab lies over the grave. It is undisturbed and clean, with trimmed grass around it and some trampled grass suggesting a recent visitor (Walkers 03).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The first search. After about two hours in the bar, the team goes to the churchyard. Kurt picks the lock, and after about half an hour of searching they find the grave. Kurt notes that they could steal the body if the exhumation is denied (Walkers 03).

The court order. The sheriff files the paperwork, but the judge, who objects for religious reasons, will not budge for Andrew. The task force's boss Big Bill talks to the judge for about twenty minutes, and the exhumation is set for the day after tomorrow (Walkers 04). As a backup plan, the team rents ground-penetrating radar to check the casket first (Walkers 04, Walkers 05). See Exhumation of Shelly Wilmarth.

The radar test. In Walkers 06 the team takes the radar to the cemetery. At first it will not turn on, and its wires look chewed. Zack (as Huell) repairs it with aluminum-foil gum wrappers on a roll of double sixes. Pushed over the grave and compared against neighbouring graves, it shows something solid in the coffin, and the team is about 85 percent confident of it.

The exhumation order. At the start of Walkers 07, Andre notes that the team has the exhumation order for the next morning. The grave is never opened in any recorded episode.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Walkers 01 Alberta says her mother died two years earlier and shows an obituary reading winter 1990, while in Walkers 05 Andre says Shelly died "about, I think, like two months ago". The episodes never reconcile the two.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 03
  • Walkers 04
  • Walkers 05
  • Walkers 06
  • Walkers 07

docs.title: The Clown Mansion
docs.text:
The Clown Mansion is the Victorian house down the road from the Roulet estate, decorated with ivy-covered clown statues, where the agents use the kitchen phone to call the FBI.

Type Location (residence) Aliases Clown house Region Near Exeter, Rhode Island; about 30 minutes' walk from the Roulet House First appearance Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The mansion stands at the end of a long, winding driveway beyond a mailbox: a second large Victorian, with ivy-covered stone clown statues arranged around the driveway, a large clown head for a door knocker and a Cadillac parked outside. The table dislikes it. Zack says "Nose goes" to avoid knocking, Dante says "Hate that" about the knocker, and and Zack later calls the place the "clown dungeon". (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
With their car stolen, the agents hike down the dirt road in the afternoon snow looking for a phone or a car. At the clown mansion, Ezra (as the Biz) knocks and rolls Manipulate Someone, getting an 8, a mixed success. After a long wait, an ancient man opens the door a crack and says, "We don't want any." Andre rules that the man is quite senile and has settled into a rhythm in which he can function without understanding what is going on. The Biz flashes his badge forcefully, and the man says, "Okay, you can come in," and wanders backwards. A much younger woman, called to the door by "Who is it, Bruce?", ushers them to the kitchen phone: "Look like you're all freezing." (Roulet Estate 02)

Andrew calls Big Bill, who does not pick up. The Biz then calls the FBI's DC office, giving his name and badge number as Special Agent Dick Baxter, and reports two dead bodies at 118 Benefit Street, a stolen vehicle and shots fired by "entities unknown". The operator does not know his task force and finds no case on file, but promises a local unit to secure the scene and backup later; snow may delay it a couple of hours. Meanwhile Kurt watches the Cadillac from the window to make sure nobody tampers with it. As they leave, the agents notice that the younger woman's silk bathrobe is covered in a clown print. (Roulet Estate 02)

While using the phone, Dante also books a taxi to Pawtucket for the monk with his own money. It is sent to the Roulet house, and the monk walks back there with the agents to wait for it. See The Finnish Hare Krishna Monk. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• Bruce, an ancient, senile man.
  • An unnamed younger woman in a clown-print robe. The agents wonder whether she is Bruce's wife or daughter, and the episodes do not say.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: The colonial church
docs.text:
The colonial church is the small, very old, well-kept church in Marblehead where the Sons of Adam hold several services a day and serve worm-filled communion wine.

Type Location (church) Aliases The church Region Marblehead, Massachusetts Affiliation Sons of Adam First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The church is "colonial old": small, well maintained and fitted with an old, slightly out-of-tune organ. The preacher wears a ceremonial robe. The congregation is a mix of the town's business leadership and "salt-of-the-earth" fishermen. Communion is a small cup of wine and nothing else (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03).

Services are frequent. The team scouts the church after missing the 3 o'clock service and returns for the evening service at nine, in Summer Service 01. Summer Service 03 attends a 7 a.m. service, and Andre says the church holds three a day (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Summer Service 01
docs.text: The team plans to attend first, pretend interest or conversion, and talk to the priest later ("we shouldn't be trying to speedrun the human sacrifice"). At the 9 p.m. service the preacher, Amos Shaw, preaches that angels are terrifying monsters, that good is not nice and that the world comes from water and returns to it. Huell and Kurt take the wine, which tastes fishy, like bad Pruno; Kurt only pretends to finish his. Afterward Shaw introduces himself as "Mr. Shaw", not "Father", and scolds the Biz for swearing in "God's house" (Summer Service 01). Outside, Kurt spots an FBI counterintelligence agent on a nearby rooftop.

docs.title: Summer Service 03
docs.text: Andrew attends the 7 a.m. service alone, because he looks "too much like a Fed" for the visit to Ma Gramoire. Shaw is gone. A new priest, opalescent, translucent and slightly bloated like a drowned man, preaches against doubt and the secular world and says "Blood of Christ" while examining Andrew. Andrew holds the wine in his mouth, fails to bluff the priest (Manipulate Someone 6) and spits it into an empty bottle outside. McManley later finds worms in it (Summer Service 03). See Communion wine.

docs.title: Summer Service 05
docs.text: The church is not entered, but it hangs over the whole session. Madeline Weathers blames "that fucking church" for her uncle's disappearance and vows to burn it. At 4 a.m. silent, armed church members gather in the rain around the hotel (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Amos Shaw; the replacement priest, revealed in Summer Service 04 to be the Mayor of Marblehead; Jester; and the congregation.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Summer Service 01
  • Summer Service 03
  • Summer Service 05

docs.title: Community center
docs.text:
The community center is the fenced cinder-block construction project, pushed by Deborah Wells and Mayor Wilford Hiram on bulldozed Pueblo ruins within sight of Sherman Ranch, which proves to be the skinwalkers' stronghold above the "Ballroom" shaft and collapses into a sinkhole in the finale.

Type Location (construction site) Aliases Community center site; community center project; rural community center Region Desert outside Ballard, Utah Held by Skinwalker faction Status Collapsed into a sinkhole (as of Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
From the ranch, Walt Murphy points out the building going up beside a gray substation built just for it, about four miles from the only part of the county where anything strange happens. The town says it will swallow the ranch area, but Alberta, Walt says, will never sell (Walkers 02).

Up close it is most of a cinder-block building, ringed by a heavy chain-link fence topped with barbed wire, with bulldozers and a backhoe parked outside and work lights on. Mean graffiti over the construction logos on the fence accuses the builders of "cultural genocide". It stands at the end of a dirt road in empty desert, and the guest house is visible from it (Walkers 03).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The hollow hallway. An unguarded back door opens onto an ordinary hallway with dirt on the floor and a hollow-sounding floor (Walkers 09).
  • The Ballroom. A locked door in the hallway opens onto a shaft a few hundred feet deep that leads to the cavern.
  • The fenced yard. Behind a fence that has been knocked down in several places, most of Roosevelt's cars are piled up (Walkers 09).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Suspicion. Maggie says the center is being built far from the community, pushed by Deborah Wells, over Pueblo ruins that were bulldozed despite a protest (Walkers 03). Rita (as Andrew) photographs the site, and the team decides not to break in yet. Kurt concludes the ranch is the likely reason for the location. After meeting the mayor, Andrew and Kurt wonder whether it is a "community center scam", or a church community center moved to mine a gas reserve (Walkers 05).

The assault. In Walkers 09 a convoy of Guardsmen, the task force, ranch hands on horseback and Ned Simpson's killdozer approaches from behind a hill. The APC with the megaphone is answered with gunfire. The naked defenders are tactically poor but show no fear of death, and they swarm the killdozer; Kurt sears the last two climbers off with the flame light. Hoarded supplies and cars are stored here.

The collapse. After the team destroys the portal machine in the cavern below, the community center slides into a sinkhole while the survivors above lie unconscious from the falling white powder. Dozens of people in hazmat suits then load up bodies as black aircraft circle overhead (Walkers 09). See Hazmat cleanup teams.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The skinwalker faction (copies of the people of Roosevelt and Ballard, including the mayor), who haul supplies into the center and defend it with guns (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 02
  • Walkers 03
  • Walkers 05
  • Walkers 09

docs.title: Comstock's Property
docs.text:
Comstock's Property is the ridge homestead of bootlegger Frotter Comstock outside Auraria, Georgia, where something skulked in the dark and where the body in the Chewbacca costume was later found.

Type Location, homestead Aliases Frotter's land; ridge homestead; Comstock's ridge homestead Region A ridge outside Auraria, North Georgia Owner Frotter Comstock First appearance Appalachia 02 (mentioned); first visited in Appalachia 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The property sits up on the ridge, a hillside with outbuildings that Frotter had hastily wrapped in blue weather tarps before fetching the sheriff. The buildings house his moonshine work and a marijuana-beer experiment. A large streak of gore beside one shack is introduced as "the bear incident." Below lies a leaf-strewn copse of scrubby land, reached by climbing down, beside a walking path with ATV tracks (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Appalachia 02. The party met Frotter on the woods trail near Auraria. He told them that a couple of weeks earlier something had skulked around his ridge homestead and that he saw only a pair of eyes in the dark, "tall, but not unusually so," which ran off. The team marked his ridge, the road spot and the rabbit-snatch site on a map, and the line through them pointed toward town (Appalachia 02). See Woods Trail and Rabbit Site.

Appalachia 06. Frotter arrived at the team's hotel with the sheriff, reporting a dead Bigfoot on his land and refusing to touch it. At the property the "squatch" lay about 50 feet below the buildings. Andrew Howard rolled a 12 to investigate and learned it was a man in an expensive Chewbacca costume soaked in real blood, shot dead-center from behind in what looked like a gangland execution. See Chewbacca Costume and Troy Cleaver.

The body was a white male of 25 to 35 with a military haircut and every clothing tag cut out. Kurt Larson read faded anchor and trident tattoos as Navy SEAL emblems. Blood pooling showed the body had not been moved. ATV tracks stopped near the body and continued down the mountain toward the freeway, and the Biz found a snapped plaster-of-Paris toe matching fake Bigfoot prints, with the molds missing. See The Bigfoot Hoax.

Kurt stuck his head into one outbuilding for twenty seconds and concluded that Frotter was trying to brew beer with marijuana instead of hops; the firearms in view were almost all shotguns and small-caliber pistols. Kurt judged the murder weapon to be roughly a .357 Magnum at point-blank range and did not think Frotter was the killer. Frotter whispered an offer to allow a search of the land if the agents did not get a warrant for the buildings, and Andrew answered with a wink and "I understand what you're saying," which Rita noted was not actually an agreement. The sheriff drove Frotter away to the station, and the team left the body for McManley to collect and went on to the dry cleaner where the costume had been stolen (Appalachia 06).

Later in Appalachia 06, Kurt asked that a sample of the gore smear Frotter blamed on a bear be tested against the other tissue the team had gathered. The result is never given (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Frotter Comstock, a bearded 50-something bootlegger who services the Covenant's still and loves the Spud Hut.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 02
  • Appalachia 06

docs.title: Consolidated Gold Mine
docs.text:
The Consolidated Gold Mine is a tourist gold mine in Dahlonega, Georgia, where the German boy Frederick vanished and below which the party found a hidden modern tunnel.

Type Location, tourist attraction and mine Aliases American gold tunnels (the name used for the scene of Frederick's disappearance) Region Dahlonega, Georgia Owner The bearded tour guide, whose family owns the land around the mine First appearance Appalachia 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The surface is an old wooden building with pickaxes by the door and kitschy decor, with an animatronic prospector on a truck outside. A big staircase leads down, tourist maps sit at the front desk, and the lobby has a payphone and phone book. The tunnels are safe for about 150 feet. Beyond that lie unreinforced branches, cave-ins and mine gas, part of tens of miles of connected workings (Appalachia 03). See The Dahlonega Gold Mines.

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The tour tunnels, where a tour guide shows gold glints in the rock and says that all the town's mines connect to each other and to natural caves. In the cold open he warns that sealed shafts are deadly ("we've lost a couple people").
  • The Hidden Modern Tunnel: a newer, electric-era passage below, with work lights, tools, motor-vehicle tracks and both ends caved in. Its features include a freshly dug 10-to-15-foot shaft yielding a gold nugget, a pit bridged by two-by-fours, and an old elevator shaft with coiled cables.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Appalachia 03. Frederick, a young German boy in overalls with a gray Game Boy, wandered off the tour after hearing giggling, leaving his game behind. The team arrived at the mine as the sheriff was mobilising a search. After Kurt Larson claimed spelunking experience, the tour guide made the party responsible for the searchers' safety. The team marked the walls with glow-stick arrows and called for Frederick in German. In the lower tunnel they found the cave-ins and vehicle tracks and squeezed through into the hidden tunnel, where a small red light blinked ahead.

A pale, furry, fast creature with arms charged out of the dark, slammed Kurt into Andrew Howard and the wall and tore a long cut up his back, then fled screaming along a streaky red blood trail to the elevator shaft. At the bottom lay a single German-looking child's tennis shoe, a different one from the shoe found earlier in a field; see Child's Tennis Shoe. As the Biz climbed out last, the tunnel collapsed behind them, so Kurt estimated its position by pace-counting. Back at the surface Kurt cross-checked his pace-count against the tourist map, which showed only a few branches, and concluded with some doubt that no known tunnel matched where the shaft would lead (Appalachia 03).

The team handed over the shoe and said Frederick was probably dead. They told the searchers about the illegal mining but held back the creature. Frederick's mother, a German woman from the tour group, screamed in tears. Rescuers would need days to dig out the cave-in. At the debrief the tour guide, who owns the mine, doubted anyone could keep secret mining hidden ("like building the Batcave"); Andrew suggested a cult and the sheriff's face darkened.

Appalachia 04. Frederick's mother, who spoke only German, told an FBI translator over the station speakerphone that her son was playing his video game in the "American gold tunnels," that she heard a clatter and no scream, and that he was gone with the game left behind. She asked why the search had stopped, and Kurt cited the shoe pointing toward an exit, the partial cave-in being excavated, and signs of recent activity and vehicles (Appalachia 04).

The hidden tunnel was later understood as part of the ape-men's workings; see Jan's Conspiracy.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The bearded tour guide and owner, who wears suspenders and has a long white beard. The cave creature the party met was not identified in these two sessions; see Ape-Men.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:

  • Appalachia 04

docs.title: The Dahlonega Gold Mines
docs.text:
The Dahlonega Gold Mines are tens of miles of interconnected gold workings and natural caves beneath Dahlonega, Georgia, where ape-men secretly dug gold for Jan's Conspiracy.

Type Location, mine network Aliases The mines; the tunnels; interconnected mines Region Beneath Dahlonega, Georgia Operators Jan's Conspiracy (secret workings); tourist mines such as the Consolidated Gold Mine First appearance Appalachia 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In the cold open of Appalachia 03 a tour guide explains that all of the town's mines connect to each other and to natural caves, and that sealed shafts are deadly. The sheriff later briefs the party on unreinforced tunnels, mine gas and "tens of miles" of connected workings (Appalachia 03).

Beneath the tourist routes lies a newer, electric-era network; see Hidden Modern Tunnel. By the finale the party had learned the layout of the secret workings below the Spud Hut plant: a mine elevator, a shift elevator, a gold room, a side tunnel containing a portal, narrowing winding passages, and a ladder shaft. The air smells like a zoo, strongest deeper in (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The shift elevator and mine elevator. The elevators carry the ape-men down to work; the mine elevator was already at the bottom and empty when the party arrived.
  • The gold room. A kitchen table stacked with hundreds of pounds of cast gold bars, about half already taken by Jan. See Gold Bars.
  • The crack in the air. A hard-edged cut in space lit by rippling light like pool caustics, with a metal pipe passing through it and gas hissing out. See The Crack in the Air.
  • The ladder shaft. An unguarded exit that comes out under a tarp in the woods outside the plant.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Appalachia 03. The party searched for the missing boy Frederick and found the hidden modern tunnel, where a pale creature mauled Kurt (Appalachia 03). See Consolidated Gold Mine.

Appalachia 08. Kurt told the investigator outside Spud Hut that the dirt truck carried "not one potato" and that there had been recent activity in the tunnels; the investigator guessed gold mining (Appalachia 08). The team theorised that the ape-creatures might be mine labor.

Appalachia 09. Led by the handler Clive, the party crossed the workings. The ape-men worked as a "shift" in hi-vis vests, safety helmets and pickaxes, with blinking red tracking armbands, and were kept addicted to ketamine. The operation had run a year and a half. Kurt walked out among a group of drugged ape-men to cross, the party fled the huge ape-man Big Bob, and a ladder led out (Appalachia 09). Clive said the handlers lit only the routes they wanted, relying on the ape-men's fear of dark tunnels. Kurt feared someone would blow the mine up with hydrogen from the portal's pipe.

Unrecorded session

The finale, Appalachia 10, was never recorded. In the epilogue in Walkers 01, Kurt says the party survived the mines with ketamine and shotguns, and that the Spud Hut facility exploded shortly after Jan fled. His explanation to Jan is that an outside force filled the mines with explosive gas and ignited it.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The ape-men and their handler Clive. About 25 ape-men worked the mines, according to Clive, plus the loose "rejects" from the break room.

  • Appalachia 09

docs.title: Dahlonega Sheriff's Station
docs.text:
The Dahlonega Sheriff's Station is the small headquarters of Sheriff Carter Burke in Dahlonega, with an evidence locker holding the missing woman's peaches, an office hung with animal heads and guns, and a break room with the only phone line.

Type Location, police station Aliases Sheriff's station; sheriff's office Region Dahlonega, Georgia Occupants Dahlonega Sheriff's Department First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The station is small. An older woman works the front desk. Burke's office has animal heads and guns on the wall (Appalachia 04). The break room is the only room with a phone line, and Burke uses a 1980s speakerphone there. The evidence locker holds the case's only physical evidence in the opening sessions (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Appalachia 01. The team arrived after a ten-hour drive. The older woman at the front desk said Burke was in the restroom with IBS, and he emerged about twenty minutes later. He called Andrew "Detective Howard," and showed through the bars of the evidence locker the one piece of evidence in Willow Greengrass's case, a bag of peaches found in the woods; see Bag of Peaches. He offered the FBI its own forensic examination of it, and the team decided to bring in Donald McManley (Appalachia 01).

Appalachia 03. The station was mobilising a search for the missing German boy Frederick when the team arrived. When Kurt reported a lighter with initials and a fair amount of blood in the forest, the sheriff said they would address it after the search ("That's too many people going missing") (Appalachia 03).

Appalachia 04. Burke called the team in for a "man-to-man": five missing people in two days, and the FBI had arrived before it was clear there were even two. He demanded to know what they knew, asked them not to affect his tourism, and bristled when told the peach product was hallucinogenic. Kurt suggested a curfew and a cover story about a fatal tick-borne disease. Burke cleared the break room for a speakerphone call with Frederick's mother and an FBI translator (Appalachia 04).

Appalachia 07. The team planned to fax their itinerary to Big Bill from the station, listing the places they had been and "the embarrassing number of times we have gone to Spud Hut," and leaving out the Biz's sleep-sprinting and Andrew's nightmare (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Sheriff Burke, his deputies, and the unnamed older receptionist.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 01
  • Appalachia 03
  • Appalachia 04
  • Appalachia 07

docs.title: Dahlonega Trailer Park
docs.text:
The Dahlonega Trailer Park is an upscale double-wide park in Dahlonega, home of the Nick and Cartwright families, backing onto the large field where the boy Gene Cartwright was abducted.

Type Location, residential park Aliases Nick trailer (513); Cartwright trailer (920) Region Dahlonega, Georgia Residents The Nick family (trailer 513); Monica Cartwright and Gene Cartwright (trailer 920) First appearance Appalachia 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The park is described as fairly upscale, a double-wide park with a couple dozen kids playing in a large overgrown field behind it. A rock shaped like a man's head, "Injun Rock," points toward the bent tree where Gene was taken; see The Field and Bent Tree (Appalachia 02). The Nicks live at number 513 and the Cartwrights at 920. Edward Nick Sr. remarked that his family stayed at the Smith Hotel "when the trailer park went down about five years ago"; the episodes never say what happened.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The Nick trailer. The morning after their drive, the party reached trailer 513, where Kurt got in by saying "We're with the Federales." Edward Nick, a boy of about five or six, watched cartoons, gave Andrew Howard a Transformers toy and a juice box, and handed over a drawing of a crouched hairy figure. He said "He was fast." He first said he saw it yesterday, but his mother corrected him: three days earlier. His mother directed the party to the bent tree and mentioned the Cartwrights, out-of-season hunters and the Covenant in Auraria. She offered tuna green bean casserole, and Edward Nick Sr. arrived at dinner in gray Spud Hut coveralls to report that his coworker Aaron Richters had left on a smoke break and never come back (Appalachia 02).

In the field behind, the party found Gene's Shoe in a high branch, with a tuft of pale, soft hair caught in the laces. Kurt and Huell concluded the boy was dead.

The Cartwright trailer. In Appalachia 04 the team chose to interview "dead kid mom" Monica Cartwright before visiting the Covenant. She was drinking warm white wine among bottles on the couch and sprayed a broken air conditioner with WD-40. She said Gene vanished while playing with "the Nick boy," who screamed. She reported seeing drunk off-season hunters in gray jumpsuits and sunglasses in a Jeep with a big cage and shotguns, and said that a month earlier a naked, hairy figure resembling Chewbacca had stood at her driveway with a big backpack, then climbed into a black sedan. Sheriff Burke had dismissed this because she was drunk. She told the team not to come back without her son (Appalachia 04). The Nick boy's surname is heard as both "Nick" and "Nichols."

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The Nick family: Mrs. Nick, Edward Nick Sr. (a Spud Hut worker) and Edward. Monica Cartwright and the missing Gene.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 02
  • Appalachia 04

docs.title: Dahlonega, Georgia
docs.text:
Dahlonega, Georgia is a gold-rush tourist town of a few thousand people, officially the "wine tasting room capital of Georgia" according to the state senate, home of the Spud Hut and the base for the party throughout The Things in Appalachia.

Type Location, town Aliases Dahlonega Region North Georgia mountains (Appalachia) Notable institutions Dahlonega Sheriff's Station, Smith Hotel, the Spud Hut First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A former gold-rush center, Dahlonega is a small mountain town of roughly six by seven streets, with a gold mining museum, a McDonald's, a food mart, Stigley's Pub and an Express & Suites motel; there is no Walmart. The town's tourist industry is built on its mines. The Smith Hotel desk clerk delivers a tour-guide spiel about the wine tasting and the gold mining museum (Appalachia 01). Underground Gold Mine Tours advertises itself as one mile from downtown, and the town has a newsstand and a second hotel, the Hotel and Suites, which used to be a Best Western (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Dahlonega Sheriff's Station, Sheriff Carter Burke's base.
  • Smith Hotel (including room 111) and the Motel and Suites.
  • The original Spud Hut and the Spud Hut Regional Distribution Center, the town's main employer.
  • The Consolidated Gold Mine and the wider Dahlonega Gold Mines.
  • The Dahlonega Trailer Park and the Death Cave on the edge of town.
  • Auraria, a short drive away, home of the Covenant.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
October 1992. The team arrives to investigate a missing woman, Willow Greengrass, and reported Bigfoot sightings, and meets the Circle Chasers, Sheriff Burke and the local color (Appalachia 01). Over the arc the disappearances mount, with Willow, Edward Nick, Gene Cartwright, Aaron Richters and Frederick all vanishing. The sheriff laments "too many people going missing" (Appalachia 03).

The Clinton scandal. Presidential candidate Bill Clinton was campaigning in Dahlonega, and a Georgia State Police press conference alleged that the FBI was in town surveilling him (Appalachia 07). Reporters gathered in town, and a Fox 5 crew recognized Andrew Howard live on television (Appalachia 08). See Clinton Surveillance Scandal and Fox 5 Atlanta.

The finale. In Appalachia 09 the party crossed the mines beneath the town, ending at a ladder exit under a tarp in the woods outside the Spud Hut plant (Appalachia 09). The final session was never recorded; the epilogue in Walkers 01 says the Spud Hut facility exploded shortly after Jan fled.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Sheriff Burke, the Circle Chasers, the Covenant of nearby Auraria, Jan Martense and the Spud Hut staff, and the Smith Hotel clerk. The Spud Hut's perfect-recall counter worker appears as the Spud Hut Counter Savant.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The Smith Hotel clerk gives the population as about 4,000 in Appalachia 01; in Appalachia 03 Andre says the real-life figure at the time was about 4,500.

docs.title: The Death Cave
docs.text:
The Death Cave is a blood-splattered crevice cave near a busy freeway outside Dahlonega, where the party found a man's folded face, scattered remains and a bloody pickaxe.

Type Location, cave Aliases Crevice cave; the cave Region Near the freeway and the Spud Hut Regional Distribution Center, outside Dahlonega Victim The Dead Man in the Cave First appearance Appalachia 02 (cold open)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The cave is a crevice in rock near a road, with bloody smears showing that someone went in and out. Inside is a sandy chamber reached by a tight squeeze, a worry for the Biz. The chamber is splattered with blood. Kurt found no powder marks or chemical smell and judged that the man was shredded and slung against the walls "like gators have been at a body," with bones split open, tooth marks, and muscle, organs and fat missing (Appalachia 03).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Appalachia 02, cold open. A Spud Hut distribution-center worker on a smoke break was locked out when his propping rock scraped away. He followed baby-like sobbing into a rocky fissure near the plant, found an ancient pickaxe in the sand, raised it, and was attacked by a glinting-eyed, humanlike figure perched in the crevice. The scene ended in darkness and screams. The man is not named; the sobbing that drew him in suggests the creature lures victims with a baby-like cry (Appalachia 02).

Appalachia 03. Andrew Howard woke in the woods at about 3 a.m. in sweat-soaked pajamas, with bloody feet, holding a steel cigarette lighter he had never seen. The party retraced his route the next morning, followed his blood trail, and reached the cave after about 1.5 hours. Andrew squeezed in first, followed by Kurt and Huell. The party found an old bloody pickaxe, skin, bones, hair, gray cloth scraps, a cigarette pack and a man's folded face stuck to the wall. Andrew bagged the face; see Folded Face. The face belonged to a middle-aged smoker with a salt-and-pepper beard whom nobody recognized. The lighter, marked "HF" in Sharpie, held hair and fat matching the face; see HF Lighter. The cave held gray cloth shreds but no wallet. The party photographed the scene with the film camera and planted pink flags (Appalachia 03).

The blood trail ran on to the freeway, where white Spud Hut box trucks drove past toward town. The party hoped the lighter's initials would help narrow down who the dead man was. The missing Spud Hut employee Aaron Richters does not fit "HF," and the man is never identified.

Appalachia 07. Andrew Howard blurted the body count to Big Bill, including "the exploded man in the cave," and Dante's character later contrasted the cave's many fragments with the "weirdly meticulous" killing of a truck driver (Appalachia 07). See Thing That Attacked the Spud Hut Truck.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: None found. The creature that attacked in the cold open is never clearly seen, and the episodes do not connect it to the pale furry creature the party met in the mines.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 02
  • Appalachia 03
  • Appalachia 07

docs.title: Douglas Pinball Emporium
docs.text:
The Douglas Pinball Emporium is a neon-lit pinball arcade in Radford, Virginia, set in a former laundromat across the street from the Lonely Mountain Diner. It is the scene of the abduction of overnight worker Elizabeth George and of a gray-van raid in The Radford Horrors.

Type Location (arcade) Aliases The arcade; Pinball Emporium Region Radford, Virginia Owner Douglas Douglas First appearance Radford Horrors 02 (seen from the diner; first entered in Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The arcade occupies the former laundromat, now painted black and topped with a neon "Douglas Pinball Emporium" sign (Radford Horrors 02). Inside are neon carpet and black lights, a staff bathroom, a break room or lounge with an attached security office, and a front porch with a rain overhang and a dome camera. A heavy back maintenance door has no camera at all. A fence at the back of the lot has been cut and rejoined (Radford Horrors 03).

Further details emerge in the next episode. The front windows have been fixed after an earlier break-in. A man-sized office window onto a side alley is unlocked and has no screen. The loading dock is padlocked and there is a back service door. Neighbors are the post office and a failed tourist shop, and across the street are the diner, a small library and a gas station (Radford Horrors 04).

The arcade is about six months old: Elizabeth George has worked there "pretty much since the place started." Douglas Douglas says the lawsuit he won over his earlier job at the mountain vacation-home community, where he was kept from leaving and the team lent him toilet paper and the Department of Labor phone number, paid for it (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The Flash Gordon machine. Left opened up on the floor mid-repair by Elizabeth George, who was working on it when she vanished (Radford Horrors 03).
  • Staff bathroom and break room. The hand towels were missing from the bathroom and the first-aid kit from the break room (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04).
  • The front porch camera. Its tape had been replaced with a partly overwritten tape from another day (Radford Horrors 03).
  • The office window. The route the intruder used, marked by a rotten compost smell like the Radford Moth and a dollop of opalescent slime above the sill (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Elizabeth George's disappearance
docs.text:
The Radford Horrors 03 opens with a cold open along a dark aisle of chiming pinball machines: a struggle, a Taser crack, a woman's limp arm, and a man in a black balaclava carrying her out (Radford Horrors 03). Sheriff Molly Underhill then drives the team to the arcade. Douglas reports that his overnight security and maintenance worker was gone at opening, and that a letter on her door says she is in inpatient psychiatric treatment in Los Angeles (Radford Horrors 03).

Kurt Larson luminols the floor and finds a broken Taser tine with blood in the carpet, a blood smear and a single head hair on a machine corner, no fingerprints, and a faint bleach smell. There is also a bloodstain in the parking lot. Kurt finds that a section of the back fence was cut, a vehicle driven through, and the fence reattached (Radford Horrors 03).

Kurt recalls that other missing Radford people were officially said to be in drug or psychiatric facilities in Los Angeles, and the team treats the letter as the same cover story (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The gray van raid
docs.text:
In Radford Horrors 04, Kurt wins over the diner waitress Sheila and she repairs her "on the fritz" camera. It shows a gray van arriving at about 4 to 5 a.m. Five men get out, one with a long brown ponytail and the rest with military haircuts, some with covered faces. A non-human shadow moves in the emporium window, and one man opens the lock, possibly with a bump key. After a scuffle, three men carry out two bags, others carry out equipment, and the van speeds away (Radford Horrors 04). See Diner security tape. The waitress adds that gray vans began appearing a couple of months earlier, around the "right to roam" dispute over the woods and possibly tied to the Safe Environment Fund (Radford Horrors 04).

Back at the emporium, Kurt finds that the shadow stood at the left of the front window, where the floor had been recently cleaned. He concludes the office window was the way in, and that the emporium intruder was a smaller moth-related being, since the full-size moth could not have fitted through. His working theory is that a juvenile moth or a thrall was in the arcade, that the gray van crew came for it, and that Elizabeth, repairing the machine, was caught in the crossfire and taken to hide evidence. Zack floats the idea of a hidden recording device inside the machine (Radford Horrors 04).

It is never established in the recorded episodes what became of Elizabeth.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• Douglas Douglas, owner.
  • Elizabeth George, overnight security and maintenance worker, taken from the arcade.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• In Radford Horrors 03 Andre stumbles over the worker's name ("Lizbeth Geor... Sorry, Elizabeth George"), and in Radford Horrors 04 she is called "Lisbeth George"; the name is spelled variously.
  • Douglas Douglas, whose guard shack is filled with vintage pinball machines, first appears at Stately Acres (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horrors 02 (the neon sign, seen from the diner)
  • Radford Horrors 03
  • Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Dr. Lori's office
docs.text:
Dr. Lori's office is the brownstone practice of Radford's only psychiatrist, Dr. Lawrence Lori. It is where Dick "The Biz" Baxter plants a listening bug that rolls into a vent, and where he later burgles the files.

Type Location (medical office) Aliases Lori's clinic; Dr. Lori's practice; the brownstone office Region Radford, Virginia Operator Dr. Lawrence Lori First appearance Radford Horror 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The practice is a nondescript brownstone in mid-town. It has a waiting room with a receptionist who offers lemon candies, a desk with chairs, a couch and a chair at the back, and a fireplace. A vent in the corner is where the bug ends up. The office has a small window that Huell judges only a crowbar would open, and a locked filing cabinet. It has an alarm (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: The interview and the bug
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 02 the team visits after learning that Dr. Lori prescribed Prozac and lithium to Irene Whateley. The sheriff has told them he is "increasingly thinking you shouldn't go see him" because of Amanda's Xanax stash. Kurt waits about fifteen minutes while the receptionist pages Lori, and chats with her about his family and music. When Kurt describes himself as "ex-CIA, mostly desk duty now," Andrew Howard steps in to correct for operational security (Radford Horror 02).

Lori emerges with a nervous teenage patient and takes the team to his office. He says Irene began treatment a year and a half earlier and quit six months ago over side effects. He never met her sons, and says the family sent Wilbur Whateley to military school before the crash. Under pressure from the Biz, with Huell Kendrick menacing in silence, he gives up that Amanda Lucky said her boyfriend Dean Lawson was involved in drugs (Radford Horror 02).

Before leaving, the Biz plants a bug (Act Under Pressure, 9, after Huell's Help Out). It fails to stick under his chair and rolls into the corner vent, so the audio is poor and retrieval will be hard (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: The bug in use
docs.text: In Radford Horror 03 the Biz listens from the car and hears Lori in a heated one-sided phone call ("You don't know," "I swear to God"), then a handset slam, pacing and a metallic click before Lori rushes to his car. The team follows him to the Augustine house and barn. Later Huell tries to retrieve the bug with a lost-jacket pretext. The bug is visibly down in the vent, but the receptionist steps between him and the window and ushers him out, and the team drops the break-in plan (Radford Horror 03).

docs.title: The burglary
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 04, unable to sleep, the Biz breaks into the office with gloves and one of Kurt's stilts as a pry bar. He retrieves the bug from the furnace vent and photographs the files on everyone known so far, taking the back off the locked cabinet (a roll of 7, so the cabinet will not go back together). To make it look like a junkie burglary, he steals a prescription pad, throws a brick through the window from outside (setting off the alarm), clogs the toilet and draws on the stall with a Sharpie (Radford Horror 04). He confesses to the team later, and Kurt answers "Great initiative" (Radford Horror 04).

The film is developed in Kurt's portable darkroom at the Pay n' Stay and shows Lori's file on Amanda (Xanax with doses later raised without explanation, extra appointments tapering into "no shows") and a routine file for her mother (Radford Horror 05). Deputy Molly Underhill tells the team the break-in (dog feces in the toilet, brick through the window) is thought to be a high-school prank (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: In Radford Horror 08, while briefing the team on the arrests of Lori and Derek Augustine, the sheriff's office says it suspects Derek of the break-in because animal feces were left in Lori's toilet. Kurt Larson agrees that it fits Derek's pattern of escalation, and the Biz's role in the burglary is not mentioned (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• Dr. Lawrence Lori, psychiatrist.
  • An unnamed receptionist, who stonewalls Huell in Radford Horror 03.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 02
  • Radford Horror 03
  • Radford Horror 04
  • Radford Horror 05 (aftermath of the burglary)

docs.title: Ferry Lodge
docs.text:
The Ferry Lodge is a rustic pine-log hotel in Radford, Virginia, across the street from the Pay n' Stay. It is full on the team's first night in town, becomes their base partway through The Radford Horror, and returns remodeled and under new management in The Radford Horrors, where the IRS raids it.

Type Location (hotel) Aliases The lodge Region Radford, Virginia First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In the first arc the lodge is a big, nice, rustic pine-log hotel. Andre spells the name out as "F-E-R-Y" (Radford Horror 01). The rooms the team takes cost $80 a night, reimbursable, and are four adjacent second-floor rooms with thick timber walls, Indian blankets, stag heads, a pine smell and old TVs with cable and pay-per-view. The lobby has cucumber-and-hibiscus water and a tree-ring table, and a lobby phone (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06). It is a separate place from the mountain ski lodge, the Alpine Lodge, where the team later uses the water tower (Radford Horror 06).

In the second arc the lodge has been remodeled "under new management": a bank of payphones, new windows, brighter lights, hot tubs, a pool and a mud-mask spa. It is half empty. The clerk pitches an "Alpine Relaxation Package" (Radford Horrors 02). Sheriff Molly Underhill says the new management arrived four or five months earlier and are "snooty" and secretive, hiring no locals (Radford Horrors 02); the diner waitress agrees (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
On their first night in Radford, Dick "The Biz" Baxter spots the lodge. It is full because of an oral surgeons' convention, and the clerk offers one single bed and points to the Pay n' Stay across the street (Radford Horror 01). The team later notes that the lodge has cameras (Radford Horror 04).

Around 1 p.m. in Radford Horror 05 the team moves from the Pay n' Stay to the lodge, after the bedbug trouble. Kurt and the Biz carry in a cooler holding the NSA agent's remains, the dog skull and a couple of beers. Kurt sets tell-tales in his room and keeps his pager on him. An orthodontist conference has nearly emptied the lobby by afternoon, and the team regroups there in the evening to discuss stakeout options (Radford Horror 05).

In Radford Horror 06 Andrew Howard takes a page from the sheriff on the lobby phone about Dean Lawson's truancy, which becomes a pretext to bring Dean in.

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
On arrival Kurt notes the lodge lot is half empty. A Read a Bad Situation roll shows a nondescript white van and two street-corner "inexperienced field agents" watching the lodge. The van drives off when approached and circles back (Radford Horrors 02). Daniel Webster books two doubles, insisting on bunking with Kurt (Radford Horrors 02).

As the keys are handed over, IRS Criminal Investigations SWAT storms in. Kurt goes prone and draws, then pulls the pin on a grenade and holds it as a dead man's switch, and a Manipulate Someone roll of 11 keeps him from being shot. The clerk runs to the back room, shreds documents and sets the file cabinets on fire. Andrew catches her and passes her to Webster. The IRS leader, who had run an eight-month fraud investigation, is furious and shuts the lodge, and the team is escorted out (Radford Horrors 02). Kurt and Andrew later confirm with an IRS agent that the white van and the corner watchers were IRS (Radford Horrors 02). See IRS Criminal Investigations.

Later, on the diner's camera, the waitress says many gray vans gathered around the lodge during "the raid" (Radford Horrors 04). The woods past the lodge are where Billy Thornton goes to use heroin, and where Kurt hides the backup tape in a hollow tree twenty minutes' walk away (Radford Horrors 04).

The waitress is referring to the IRS raid, and says she never saw that kind of van around town before; whether the gray vans seen at the Douglas Pinball Emporium were among them is never established.

docs.text:
• The oral surgeons' convention and later the orthodontist conference (first arc).
  • The new management and a clerk who flickers when Webster says "FBI" (second arc).

docs.title: The Field and Bent Tree
docs.text:
The Field and Bent Tree is the overgrown field behind the Dahlonega trailer park where Gene Cartwright, a boy of about seven, was taken, and where the team found his shoe hung high in a tree.

Type Location Aliases Injun Rock (the head-shaped rock used as a landmark) Region Dahlonega, Georgia First appearance Appalachia 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The field lies behind the double-wide park where the Nick family lives, and a couple dozen kids play there. When the team arrived it was knee-high grass, thick with mosquitoes and biting flies, ringed with police tape and trampled by the volunteers of the manhunt (Appalachia 02).

Edward Nick's mother directed the team to the spot by landmark. From her window, a big rock that looks like a man's head, which she calls "Injun Rock," has a nose that points toward a bent tree at the wood line. Edward had been right by that tree when the family heard the screaming (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Injun Rock. The head-shaped rock; following its nose leads to the bent tree.
  • The bent tree. Gene's red, white-soled shoe was hung high in its branches, with a tuft of pale, soft, body-like hair (ends intact) caught in the laces.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Kurt proposed an inverted-wedge search formation, with the people in the back rechecking the footsteps of those in front. Because the volunteers had trampled the ground, Investigate a Mystery was at -1; the Biz still rolled well enough, with a boost from Kurt, to ask two questions. His first, "What sort of creature is it?", revealed something dangling from a high branch. Huell climbed the sketchy limb (Act Under Pressure, a mixed result), passed the roll to avoid falling as the branch cracked, and ruined his suit retrieving the shoe. Kurt and Huell concluded the boy was dead (Appalachia 02).

The Biz's second question, "Where did it go?", was answered by Edward's account, relayed by his mother: something appeared from nowhere, grabbed him and ran into the woods. Andrew pointed out that this did not explain a shoe in a tree. The shoe and hair were bagged for McManley. Kurt phoned Sheriff Burke, who confirmed that the missing boy's shoe was red with a white sole, and who added that he needed to talk to his deputies about looking up when surveying a scene (Appalachia 02). See Gene's Shoe.

A different child's shoe, German in style, was later found in the hidden modern tunnel; see Child's Tennis Shoe.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: None. The surrounding trailer park is covered at Dahlonega Trailer Park. Edward Nick and the missing Gene Cartwright lived there.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Appalachia 02

docs.title: Flooded freeway and marsh
docs.text:
The flooded freeway and marsh is the stretch of storm-drowned road and wetland leading to the Marblehead-area nuclear power plant, where Jester dies, Huell fires the Davy Crockett and the angel thing burns out in a radioactive crater.

Type Location (highway and wetland) Region Outside Marblehead, Massachusetts, about a mile from the shore and the nuclear power plant fence First appearance Summer Service 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In the finale the rain is so heavy that the time of day is hard to judge, though the party calls it mid to late afternoon. Roads are flooded to the wheel wells, convoy cars flood out and are abandoned, and for the last quarter mile to the plant fence the Guard convoy has to leave the freeway and cross marsh. The party's car cannot follow (Summer Service 06). The weather is the aftermath of Tropical Storm Andrew 2.

docs.title: Summer Service 06
docs.text:
• The angel thing turns back. The glowing angel thing, trenching the ground toward the team, stops, lets out a long fluting cry and returns to the sea. A mystery voice on the pocket radio, the radio contact, tells Kurt that the earlier explosion (a claymore the team set off on a truck) "pissed it off". The radio contact says they have something for it but it must be fired from the air, and the storm has grounded that option. The plan is to let the convoy engage plant security so the creature comes out to help, then take a long shot with the Davy Crockett.
  • Jester. The team sees its own stolen FBI car lagging in a water-filled depression with one occupant. They decide to jump it ("We're the cops"). The driver is Jester, who screams "It's you, Toothbrush Man!" and bites Huell's neck through the window. Andrew swerves to scrape him off against the stuck car, Huell leans out, Jester slams into its windshield, and Andrew backs the team's car over him; he dies spewing blood, bile and worms.
  • Lesson and shot. In the back seat Kurt teaches the others to fire the Davy Crockett. Andrew bogs the car in the mud, and Huell frees it with Kurt's steel plate. The convoy rams the fence, the ground drops six inches and pops dozens of tires, and pop-up machine guns shred it. A light rises from the ocean. Huell wins rock-paper-scissors for the honour of firing, burns a Luck point to turn a mixed result into a success and fires the W54 warhead into the light.
  • The creature dies. The shockwave flattens the fence and silences the guns, and a pillar of fire rises, but the creature survives and comes straight for the team. It strips a line through an abandoned car and circles. Andrew leans out with the flashlight weapon, lands a solid hit, burns his hand, and the creature spirals into the earth about twenty feet from the car. As it dies it sprouts legs from every kind of animal (Zack saw a panda) and ends as a white-hot pillar of flame in a crater.
  • Radiation. Kurt rolls Sharp 11 and notices the Geiger counter in the abandoned car's trunk going wild. The radiation spiked when the creature died, not at the nuke. The team abandons its radioactive gear, including the Geiger counter, and takes a Ford Pinto with a lift kit and painted flames, one of the cars that made it through the flooding, to drive off. Near the crater the contact leaves "a little present on the road", a half-empty metal canister, the anti-worm agent canister.

(Summer Service 06)

Quote

"Eh, fuck samples, we're not scientists." Dante (as Kurt), declining to take samples from the crater. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The crater. Where the creature died. Gear left near it is radioactive.
  • The fence and plant approach. Covered on the nuclear power plant page.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 06

docs.title: Freeway Crash Site
docs.text:
The Freeway Crash Site is the stretch of freeway outside Dahlonega, Georgia, where a Spud Hut truck went through the guardrail, leaving a cab drenched in blood and no driver.

Type Location Aliases truck wreck site; the freeway Region Dahlonega, Georgia First appearance Appalachia 03 (the freeway); Appalachia 07 (the crash)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The freeway is a busy road carrying a near-constant stream of white Spud Hut box trucks marked for the Georgia Regional Distribution Center. The team first saw it when following Andrew's blood trail from the death cave: three trucks passed toward town, then five more as they walked it back, and the blood ended at broken beer bottles (Appalachia 03).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The crash. In the cold open of Appalachia 07, a heavyset Spud Hut driver in a gray jumpsuit was driving at sunset to "Radar Love" when something clanged and ripped behind his cab. Glass broke and a growl came from the rear; he reached for a Glock under the seat, missed, and screamed. The truck smashed through a barricade and embankment, and came to rest among trees with the song still playing quietly (Appalachia 07).

The scene. Late that evening the sheriff asked the team to bring their forensics man. Sheriff's cars blocked the freeway with Spud Hut trucks queued behind them, honking. The truck lay on its side at the bottom of a hill and was marked "S-H-G-R-D-C" with an "S-H-A" (Spud Hut America) logo, which Huell linked to the "SHA" on the SHA tracking device (Appalachia 07).

The sheriff showed the cab:

  • Blood on every surface, including the photo of a blonde taped to the dash, but no body and no face, and far too much blood to survive.
  • Eight gunshots through the cabin and broken instruments.
  • The rear window broken inward and the windshield broken outward.
  • The vinyl roof ripped as if by fingers.

Kurt reasoned that something crawled in through the rear window, mauled the driver and left through the front with what remained. He called it "weirdly meticulous for what a mess it was," and the group noted that there had been many more fragments in the cave. In the spilled load the sheriff slit a bag labelled "Potatoes" and dirt poured out; another bag held a whole octopus floating in liquid (Appalachia 07). See Spud Hut Truck and the thing that attacked the truck.

Aftermath. The next session opened with the players recapping the clawed cab and the dirt cargo. They followed the sheriff to Spud Hut Corporate and noted that Spud Hut trucks, previously omnipresent, were absent from the road (Appalachia 08). A related earlier lead: the Biz found ATV tracks near the Chewbacca-costume body that ran down the mountain toward the freeway (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: None. The driver was presumed dead and his body was never found.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 03
  • Appalachia 07
  • Appalachia 08

docs.title: National Guard checkpoint
docs.text:
The National Guard checkpoint is the roadblock, command tent and medical tent at the entrance to Marblehead where the National Guard seals the town and the task force gives its cover story and falls asleep at the end of The Summer Service.

Type Location (military checkpoint and field camp) Aliases Guard checkpoint and tents Region Entrance to Marblehead, Massachusetts Controlled by National Guard First appearance Summer Service 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The checkpoint blocks the road into Marblehead. Behind it stand a command tent with a telephone and a medical tent. Evacuees are being diverted to a hotel outside the town (Summer Service 06). Earlier in the session a Guard sergeant, who gives his name as "Jefferson" and then "Johnson" within the same broadcast, announces on all frequencies that the Guard has arrived and taken command (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The checkpoint. A young lieutenant first turns the team away. When they say they are the FBI agents the Guard wanted, he sends them to an older officer (see Older Guard officer).
  • The command tent. Andrew phones Big Bill from here. The officer debriefs the team.
  • The medical tent. The team is sent here for antivirals and hot soup. Huell and Kurt collapse into chicken-soup slumber.

docs.title: Summer Service 06
docs.text:
After the nuclear shot, the team drives a Pinto back to Marblehead: Kurt and Huell sleep in the back seat, Huell visibly losing muscle and hair as the worms die and running a fever, Andrew hangs his head out of the window and the Biz drives. A young lieutenant at the checkpoint turns them away, then passes them to an older officer in a lieutenant's uniform. They hand over the anti-worm canister, which is sent to a chemist, and Kurt says they have been intercepting a splinter group of bioterrorists (Summer Service 06).

Andrew calls Big Bill Nelson, who is about fifteen miles away, stuck behind roads four feet underwater and waiting for a boat. Big Bill has heard that the nuclear attack is under control and that a submarine was lost. He tells Andrew to give the military the conventional facts and to keep the real purpose of the task force for the report, "with appropriate classification". Andrew asks, "Terrorists, right?" and Big Bill confirms: "Terrorists" (Summer Service 06). See Terrorist cover story.

In the debrief, Andrew and Kurt describe a religious terrorist group, citing City Hall's murals and its literature on returning to the ocean, that tried to take down the plant after seeding the food supply with a parasite. The officer says the attack failed but killed a few guards, medics report "profoundly wild things" and the military is distributing deworming medicine, though some will not pull through. He sends them to the medical tent and, on leaving, mentions that "someone used a tactical nuke" at the plant and that it will be hard to keep out of the news. The team feigns surprise; Zack (as Huell) says, "That scoundrel. What?" (Summer Service 06).

The team ends the arc asleep in the medical tent; Andre ends the session a little early, noting that the players' choice to use the nuke and skip the facility shortened the climax (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The young lieutenant, the older officer, the Guard's medics and soldiers; the four agents as patients.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 06

docs.title: Guest double-wide
docs.text:
The guest double-wide is the small house on Sherman Ranch that Alberta Wilmarth lends the task force as lodging, besieged by the goose, shifted by the night event, and broken into by a naked intruder.

Type Location (lodging) Aliases The little house; grandma cottage; guest house; the cabin; the trailer Region Sherman Ranch, near Ballard, Utah Holder Alberta Wilmarth (owner); the task force (guests) First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Because the big house is rented to the billionaire, Alberta offers the "grandma cottage" and promises to warn security so the team is not shot (Walkers 02). Walt lets the team in with keys hidden under a ceramic frog. The air conditioner is at the back and its door must be kept open to work; the back door does not lock but has a deadbolt on the inside; and the toilet gurgles for a long time before it flushes, and then only weakly. Walt's house rules are to keep the headlights on when driving at night and to stay out of the big house and barn. Of the bedrooms, one is a child's room with colorful cartoon animals on the wallpaper and a toddler-sized bed. The bedroom windows face the big house, while the big living-room window faces away from the ranch (Walkers 02). Later episodes add twin mattresses, a Bakelite rotary phone and a washing machine with no dryer (Walkers 04).

Walkers 02 says the house has four bedrooms. In Walkers 07 Andre describes it as having two bedrooms, one of which the team is not using, plus a living room with a kitchen area and a laundry room and mud room at the back where the back door is. The episodes do not reconcile the counts (Walkers 07).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The goose. Nancy, the ranch's enormous goose, besieges the house from the first day. When the team flees to the car, she bites Huell's nose so hard it bleeds and swells shut. When the team gets back that night a goose-shaped silhouette hustles at them out of the dark and rattles the doorknob from the other side (Walkers 03). In Walkers 04 the team traps her inside, then runs "Operation Get Goose Out" with Kurt on stilts. She escapes, leaving the house trashed and goose dung on Huell's pillow.

Calls and planning. The house has a working phone, from which Huell calls McManley (Walkers 03, Walkers 04). Andrew spends hours seeking the exhumation order, and the Biz arranges the radar (Walkers 04).

The night event. After a long day the team sleeps inside when the night event strikes. Huell's world pivots 90 degrees, Kurt wakes in Saigon, the Biz loses every filling and bleeds from the mouth, and Andrew is found screaming inside the refrigerator, from which he floats to the ceiling. The silverware is piled on the couch, belongings are scattered, and the house has shifted a few inches so that its stairs no longer line up with the front porch (Walkers 05).

The break-in. About 11 p.m. on the night of Walkers 07, the Biz wakes and sees something low through the peephole. A naked giant, about 6'7" to 6'8", enters through the mud-room back door with a key and carries an over-under shotgun. He fights the team, and Andrew's Cast Out Evil leaves him limp. He later dies in Roosevelt. See Naked intruder.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The task force: Andrew Howard, Kurt Larson, Dick "The Biz" Baxter and Huell Kendrick, plus an unwelcome goose.
