docs.title: Hidden Attic Lair
docs.text:
The Hidden Attic Lair is a secret den above the Roulet house, reached through the chimneys, where the Roulet Intruder lived for at least a year.

Type Location (hidden room) Aliases The hideout; chimney attic Region Inside the Roulet House, Exeter, Rhode Island First appearance Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The lair is reached by a gap of about five by six removed bricks in the side of a chimney. Climbing notches are cut inside the flue, and each chimney's weather flap on top traps smoke but can lift to serve as an exit. Every chimney in the house has been modified this way, invisible from outside. See Chimney Passages. Only Kurt and Andrew fit; Huell and the Biz cannot. (Roulet Estate 02)

Inside the attic are:

  • a cot, garbage bags, a card table with cards and MRE containers, and cigarettes;
  • looted guns, including a Kalashnikov and Russian WWII-era pistols, many loaded, plus money and valuables;
  • Polaroids of sleeping people on the walls, including the owners and older photos of other people;
  • a cooler with beta blockers in a prescription tube with the label scraped off, and a homemade jar of green slurry with an eyedropper;
  • a blood-crusted butterfly knife in an ornate case beside a boarded attic vent;
  • a briefcase of money that looks as though it was abandoned partway through packing. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The cold open of Roulet Estate 02 shows a nude man with an oddly shaped head loading shotgun shells one by one in a dark, dusty space with thin light trickling in, evidently this attic. Kurt lights a fire in a fireplace; it spews smoke, and with a mirror and flashlight he sees a gap in the chimney side and climbing notches. He and Andrew climb up. Kurt rolls a 12 on Investigate a Mystery and learns that someone has probably lived there for at least a year, unknown to the owners, entering every major room by chimney; the agents recall that locks had been installed on the inside of the bedroom doors. The photos give Andrew a strong serial-killer impression. Kurt sniffs the slurry, hallucinates, and hands his sidearm to Andrew. (Roulet Estate 02)

The agents photograph everything, bag the guns, money, valuables and slurry and lower them down the chimney to deny the intruder resources. On the way down Andrew hallucinates that the bricks around him are turning into rolling muscle and swallowing him, and he drops three feet onto Kurt. (Roulet Estate 02)

In Roulet Estate 03, the beta blockers resurface when the pharmacy gunman begins to collapse, and Kurt links them to the lair. See The Roulet Intruder. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The Roulet Intruder.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Roulet Estate 02
  • Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Hidden Modern Tunnel
docs.text:
The Hidden Modern Tunnel is an electric-era mineshaft hidden beneath the tourist Consolidated Gold Mine in Dahlonega, Georgia, with work lights, vehicle tracks, an old elevator shaft and a freshly dug gold pit.

Type Location Aliases secret mineshaft Region Beneath Consolidated Gold Mine, Dahlonega First appearance Appalachia 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The tunnel sits below the old tour tunnels and is far newer. Andre described it as a "new-ass mineshaft" dug since electricity: both ends of the section the team landed in had fresh cave-ins, with an electric work light sticking out of the rubble, and there were signs of motor vehicles having been driven toward the blocked ends. Further in were more electric lights and tools, a gap in the floor that Kurt nearly fell into, and a vertical shaft with coiled cables where an elevator had once run, now with no way up (Appalachia 03).

Dahlonega's mines interconnect with each other and with natural caves. Before the team went down, the sheriff warned them that the workings run for tens of miles, that the old branches are not reinforced, and that it is easy to get lost (Appalachia 03).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Collapsed floor. A reinforced, boarded section of the old tunnel gave way under the team. Kurt and the Biz landed unhurt; Andrew and Huell each took 1 harm from falling rocks and timbers.
  • Work-light tunnel. One end was fully blocked; the other could be wriggled through. Andrew rolled well to get through and help the others across. A small red light blinked far ahead.
  • The gold pit. The gap in the floor that Kurt, on point, caught himself at is a freshly excavated shaft 10 to 15 feet deep, bridged by a couple of two-by-fours. When the team returned, Kurt was lowered on a rope and pulled a small gold nugget from the floor. He kept it as evidence.
  • Elevator shaft. At the bottom lay a single German-looking child's shoe, taken as evidence. See Child's Tennis Shoe.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The team entered during the search for Frederick, the German boy who vanished from a mine tour. In the dark, a white blur charged them. Kurt fired and was hurled into Andrew and the wall; a second hand tore a long cut up his back and badly strained a bicep tendon (2 harm). The creature fled down the tunnel with a moaning scream. Andrew healed Kurt with Lay on Hands but took the harm as a massive nosebleed (Appalachia 03). See Frederick.

The team followed the creature's blood trail to the elevator shaft, found the shoe, and went back to the pit. Climbing out, Kurt ran a rope and reinjured his elbow, and as the Biz came up last the tunnel caved in behind him. It could not be revisited without shovels, and the search party estimated that digging down would take days (Appalachia 03).

Kurt checked a tourist map: no known tunnel matched, so the shaft probably ended in another tunnel nearer the surface. Taking the likely exit point as the land above the cave system, the map put it near both the death cave and the Spud Hut Regional Distribution Center. The mine's tour-guide proprietor said he doubted anyone could keep a mine secret, since it would take too many laborers. Andrew suggested a cult could, and the sheriff's face darkened (Appalachia 03).

In the final recorded session a worker named Clive told the team that the Spud Hut operation used bred ape-men to dig gold under Dahlonega, and the team was taken through the mines to a gold room. The Dahlonega Gold Mines page covers that network. It is never stated outright that the tunnel in Appalachia 03 is part of it, but the nugget, the vehicle tracks and the creature that attacked the team all fit (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: Nobody says who dug the shaft when the team explored it; the final session points to Jan Martense and his conspiracy.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Appalachia 03

docs.title: Highway crime scene
docs.text:
The highway crime scene is the roadside by the interstate into Radford, Virginia, where the mutilated body of Amanda Lucky is found at the end of Radford Horror 04.

Type Location (roadside crime scene) Aliases The interstate Region Radford, Virginia First appearance Radford Horror 04 (mentioned); first visited in Radford Horror 05

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The scene is on the highway into town, beside thick woods with few streetlights and a shadowed pool of blood. It is about a mile from the Lucky house and near both the Pay n' Stay and the Ferry Lodge (Radford Horror 05). In the photos Amanda lies collapsed 10 to 15 feet from the tree line, a mile from home, in a nightgown with no pockets (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Discovery of the body
docs.text: At the end of Radford Horror 04, Deputy Molly Underhill takes the team aside. A young girl's body, probably Amanda's, has been found by the interstate, badly mutilated: much of the face gone and organs eaten, which the examiner attributes to animals after death. Molly says, "y'all were right." The body goes to Dr. Harvey Mauden, who delivered Amanda, and the team is invited to the autopsy (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: The team's examination
docs.text:
Radford Horror 05 opens on a young woman in a bloody, ragged dress running through the woods, clutching a stomach wound, until something passes overhead and blocks the moonlight. Andre tells the players this is the same person whose body they then see at the autopsy, "presumably a flashback" (Radford Horror 05).

At the autopsy at the sheriff's station, Dr. Mauden concludes that the nails through Amanda's wrists and ankles were pulled through rather than removed, and the team concludes she was crucified but not restrained. See Amanda Lucky for details (Radford Horror 05).

At the scene a part-time deputy in street clothes, with a laminated paper "badge," offers coffee and says things were quiet "except for the dogs." Dick "The Biz" Baxter rolls a 10 to Investigate a Mystery and finds a trail of blood drops and foot smears from the tree line to the body, lost about 10 meters into the woods. One or two coyote-sized paw smears lie in the blood, and a diffuse ring of spatter about five feet across sits on top of Amanda's own bare footprints. No other tracks are present and nothing suggests pursuit. The droplets shrink the farther back they go (Radford Horror 05).

The Biz and Andrew Howard trade theories. Howard suggests that the people who took Amanda experimented on her and let her go, and jokes about a werewolf. The Biz favors a serial killer plus coyotes after the fact (Radford Horror 05).

The team later retraces Amanda's route through the woods nearer her home, covered on the page for Jefferson National Forest. About a quarter mile from the Lucky house they find a scrap of her dress on a branch and the skull and spine of a large dog (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 04
  • Radford Horror 05

docs.title: Hotel Metropol
docs.text:
The Hotel Metropol is a luxury hotel in Moscow where Dick "The Biz" Baxter is held in comfortable captivity during The Radford Horrors. Its opera house is where President Boris Yeltsin questions him in a reserved box.

Type Location (hotel and opera house) Aliases Metropol; Moscow hotel; Metropol opera house Region Moscow, Russia Holder / occupant The Biz, under guard First appearance Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The hotel has aftermarket bars on the windows, a survivable drop outside, and downspouts the Biz notices when he scouts it. It contains an opera house with upper-level reserved boxes, one of which Yeltsin uses (Radford Horrors 01).

Radford Horrors 03 does not repeat the hotel's name, but the Biz is still held in the same room with the same guards: three guards rotate through eight-hour shifts, one a hard-ass and two pleasant, and room service brings vodka. A sleepy bellboy staffs the lobby (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The Biz's captivity
docs.text:
The Biz is introduced in Radford Horrors 01 lying on a king bed in a terry-cloth robe with champagne, stroganoff and blini. He has watched Russian-dubbed Los ricos también lloran (The Rich Also Cry) for about three hours. His guard sits crying at a little table, eating the borscht the Biz would not eat (Radford Horrors 01).

The story has jumped from January to April. His January captors, who beat him and asked about Bill Clinton, are gone. The new, friendlier captors ask only about aliens and seem to know many specifics. The Biz quietly scouts the hotel, hides bed sheets and chats up the guards, but does not actually want to escape, since he fears having to explain months AWOL if sent home (Radford Horrors 01). See The Biz's guards.

docs.title: Yeltsin at the opera
docs.text:
An officer with clean, unaccented English tells the Biz that the president wants him in his opera box in an hour, "clean and sober and properly dressed," and hands him a Russian-style suit. The Biz is seated beside Yeltsin during an opera he guesses to be a comedy about Tsarist-era royals (Radford Horrors 01).

Yeltsin tells him the Metropol is now inferior in creature comforts to the remodeled Baltschug Kempinski, "but you cannot beat an in-house opera." He explains the cosmic microwave background and says Soviet detectors spiked the previous year and were triangulated to the Marblehead nuclear incident. He asks about the weaponized worms and a second organism, the people who were not people at the Ballard, Utah ranch (the Biz explains skinwalkers), and a broken, half-melted device identical to the team's "flashlight" laser weapon. He closes by asking about Andrew Howard, and the Biz leaves out Howard's supernatural abilities (Radford Horrors 01).

Back in his room, the Biz finds Roseanne still on and feels less likely to be killed (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: The night drive
docs.text: In Radford Horrors 03 the Biz, still a bit drunk on room-service vodka, is woken by banging. An officer throws in laundered clothes and says he must be ready in five minutes. In the lobby, at about 3 to 3:30 a.m., Yeltsin calls him "Richard" and says there has been "an unusual aircraft crash in Oryol Oblast" he wants him to see. The convoy then leaves for the Oryol crash site and is ambushed (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• Dick "The Biz" Baxter, held.
  • The Biz's guards, including one the Biz befriends over soap operas and borscht.
  • Boris Yeltsin, a visitor.

docs.title: The island across the bay
docs.text:
The island across the bay is the wealthy part of Marblehead, home to Castle Rock and a bird sanctuary, reached by a bridge that floods during the storm; Arnold Weathers lives there.

Type Location (residential district) Aliases Bird sanctuary island; "the island" Region Across Marblehead Bay, Massachusetts First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In Summer Service 01, Kurt asks a local about the island he can see across the water. The local replies that it is not really an island, since a highway connects it to town, and Dante jokes that it is a "man-made peninsula". It is the nice part of town, with Castle Rock (worth seeing for tourists), lobster fishing boats and a bird sanctuary (Summer Service 01).

By Summer Service 05 the connection is a bridge that the storm has all but washed out: wind whips the ocean across the pavement, and cars are up to mid-wheel in seawater for much of the crossing. The homes beyond are rich, with high walls and privacy (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Arnold Weathers' house, an eight-foot-walled estate with a padlocked gate.
  • Castle Rock and the bird sanctuary, named but not visited.

docs.title: Summer Service 05
docs.text: Summer Service 05 is the only visit. During the storm, Madeline Weathers leads the team in a Volkswagen Beetle across the flooded bridge. Huell drives the team's car, shakes a tail by driving through the storm, narrowly misses an elderly couple's station wagon and hydroplanes across a one-way street. On the island they find Arnold's house padlocked and silent, and later destroy him and the infected dog Puddles there (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Wealthy residents and Arnold Weathers.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Summer Service 03, Ma Gramoire's slightly broken-down house is described as being "on the main island", which appears to mean the main part of town rather than this district.

docs.title: Jefferson National Forest
docs.text:
Jefferson National Forest is the dense Virginia woodland that surrounds Radford, where Irene Whateley walks out of her kitchen, the town's dogs disappear, Amanda Lucky dies, and the craft of The Radford Moth is chased in The Radford Horror.

Type Location (national forest) Aliases The woods; river forest Region Virginia, around Radford First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The forest is shadowy and thick with underbrush. Near the town the canopy is light but the undergrowth is unforgiving, dense ground cover hides tracks after about a dozen feet, and many houses sit in small enclaves surrounded by woods: walk one way and civilization is a mile off, walk another and the forest runs on for miles (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 05). When the team searches from the highway scene, Andre says that walking straight on would take them deep into Jefferson National Forest, while walking forty-five degrees left would lead to Amanda's neighborhood (Radford Horror 05). On the route to town the team drives through the Monongahela and Jefferson National Forests, where it grows dark early under the tree cover (Radford Horror 01).

The tourist map the team uses marks the missing dogs: every house borders the woods, concentrated on the side of town where the Luckys and Whateleys live (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The woods behind the Whateley house. The route Irene took, a clearing where Huell Kendrick tackles the astronaut, and where the craft hovered (Whateley house) (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 06).
  • The blood tree. A low branch spattered with gore and a streak of blood dragged to the top branch of a tree, with no hair and no broken limbs (Radford Horror 05).
  • The dog skeleton site. A quarter mile from the Lucky house, the team finds a scrap of Amanda's dress on a branch and the skull and spine of a poodle-like dog, about a week old, bones cracked open and flesh gouged away. Kurt keeps the skull (Radford Horror 05).
  • The convergence near the river. Every recorded craft heading crosses in the forest near the river, where the team finds salt-like patches of strange powder but no clearing yet (Radford Horror 06).
  • The old-town church. An hour's hike into the woods, the old-town church lies in a clearing in the forest (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: Opening images
docs.text: The first cold open is a helicopter shot over Jefferson National Forest in 1992, speeding up as the dark gaps between the trees deepen, with something blue darting over the tree line (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: Irene's disappearance and the missing dogs
docs.text:
Irene Whateley was seen at her kitchen sink, dropped her pan, and walked straight into the woods about fifty feet away. Dick "The Biz" Baxter reads two sets of footprints, one with a heavier shoe, leading deeper into the woods before the trail is lost after about a dozen feet (Radford Horror 02).

Andrew Howard finds a thick sheriff's folder of dog complaints going back a couple of years, spiking in the last six to eight months. No dog under about 40 pounds has been taken, and no remains have ever been found (Radford Horror 02). See Radford's missing dogs. The team debates predators, perverts and dog fighting, and the Biz floats an out-of-character theory that Abe is living in the woods eating dogs (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Amanda's last run and the search
docs.text: The cold open of Radford Horror 05 shows a woman in a bloody dress running through the woods and across a dirt road, with something passing overhead. After the autopsy the team bushwhacks through the woods. They find the blood tree and the dog skeleton, and the Biz reads the trail of blood and coyote-sized paw smears at the roadside (Radford Horror 05). The autopsy doctor later tells them the blood from the tree matches Amanda's tox report, and that both blood samples contain about five percent unidentifiable foreign matter (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: The craft chase
docs.text: In Radford Horror 06, with the Biz and Howard watching from the water tower at the Alpine Lodge, Kurt Larson and Huell watch from the ground. Through Kurt's night vision scope they see a large dark shape circling 50 to 60 feet over the woods, two round shapes joined like a Venn diagram. Huell chases a figure in an Apollo 11 spacesuit into the woods and tackles him in a clearing; he turns out to be one of the Whateley boys. Something enormous descends over them. Kurt hits it with a Super Soaker filled with glow-stick fluid, which marks it for the watchers, and is blinded by a stab of pain that deals him 2 harm. The craft lifts the Whateley boy and Huell, who hangs on, above the tree line; the boy tells him "It's okay. It's worth it," and Huell loses his grip, falls through the trees and breaks an arm (Radford Horror 06). See also the Spaceman.

docs.title: Lawson cabin
docs.text:
The Lawson cabin is the Lawson family's stone-and-timber cabin in the Stately Acres community near Radford's ski lodge, where Dean Lawson buried $40,000 in cash and hid a briefcase of heroin in The Radford Horror.

Type Location (private cabin) Aliases The cabin; Lawson family cabin Region Stately Acres, near Radford Owner The Lawson family First appearance Radford Horror 06 (mentioned)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The cabin is stacked stone and heavy timber with a big Lawson sign at the turnoff, a dusty porch, piled mail and an empty garbage bin. The backyard has a fire pit, log benches and a swing. Inside it is swanky: a giant CRT TV and VHS player, leather recliners and original art. The back door's locks are weak, and footprints in the dust lead to the kitchen and to a back bedroom that is Dean's unchanged childhood room from when he was about seven or eight (Radford Horror 07). Little used, but with recent tracks, it sits about a mile from the Alpine Lodge by the account of Matt McCready (Radford Horror 06). Cameras cover only the guard shack at the community entrance (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: First mentions
docs.text: Matt McCready tells the team that Dean has scary, "methy" friends and a family cabin about a mile from the ski lodge, which he marks with an X on a tourist map (Radford Horror 06). From the water tower, Dick "The Biz" Baxter notices a light on at the cabin (Radford Horror 06). The team lists finding Dean at his house in town and at the cabin as a next step (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: The search
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 07 the team stops at the Stately Acres gate, where the guard Douglas Douglas says Dean has been seen several times carrying a shovel to the family cabin, adding, "Burying bodies? I don't know." He says he hates the Lawson kid, who "kicked one of my cats." He allows them to look around as long as he is not fired (Radford Horror 07).

At the cabin, Kurt Larson hops the back gate and finds a fire pit, disturbed earth at the tree line, cigarette butts in a child's plastic bowl and fresh fingerprints on the back doorknob. His own shovel breaks (snake eyes), so the Biz steals a fiberglass-handled shovel from the community tool shed while Andrew Howard keeps Douglas talking about aliens (Radford Horror 07).

Digging turns up several Ziploc bags of hundred-dollar bills, about $40,000, and a small key. Kurt then bump-keys the back door and, after an Investigate a Mystery roll of 12, finds a loose floorboard under the child's bed hiding a locked Samsonite briefcase. The key fits, and inside are four parcels of slightly cut South American heroin, with room for five or six. Kurt tastes it, puts the board and briefcase back in place and keeps the drugs, cash and key; he refills the hole (Radford Horror 07). See Dean Lawson's heroin and cash.

The team later offers some of the heroin to the pilot Freak to get him to fly them, and pays him $1,000 from the cash, before heading to the old-town church (Radford Horror 07). Deputy Molly Underhill radios that the sheriff is having the Whateley house dismantled for a forensic examination, which Kurt fears will expose "the garage" (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: • Dean Lawson, who is not found at the cabin.

docs.title: The lighthouse
docs.text:
The lighthouse is Marblehead's tourist lighthouse, a site with a blast crater, a scorched and glassed wall and a hidden basement where the missing EPA scientists were interrogated.

Type Location (historic lighthouse and tourist site) Region Coastal rocks, Marblehead, Massachusetts First appearance Summer Service 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The lighthouse is a historic tourist attraction on rocks at the coast. A paved path with brass signs leads to a wrought-iron gate set between two outcroppings, closed with police tape and a Master Lock and chain. The front door is padlocked and taped (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The crater. Behind the lighthouse a crater has taken out a railing of the viewing platform. The back wall is scorched, with bubbled paint, drips of volcanic glass and spiky glass filaments on the nails, and the crater rock is melted to glass. A smeared bloody fingerprint on the door post looks as if someone grabbed it and was pulled away.
  • The ground floor. A little-used cot, a vanity and a dish shelf, with every piece of glass shattered. A police-style walkie-talkie sits on a side table with its button taped down.
  • The hidden basement. A trapdoor with a slide-down ladder leads to a storage basement: blood-stained ropes cut into two- to three-foot lengths, two teeth (a canine and an incisor), two bloodied chairs set for interrogation, smashed replacement bulbs and mirrors, and an EPA field notebook. Luminol shows cleaned-up blood and a bleach trail from the trapdoor to the front door and out to where a car would park.

(Summer Service 03) The glassing is discussed on the Melted shoreline page.

docs.title: Summer Service 03
docs.text: Ma Gramoire tells Kurt that the missing scientists said they were going to check out the lighthouse ("There's only the one lighthouse in town"). Kurt, drunk on her absinthe (-1 forward), picks the gate lock, and the Biz, now the party's investigator, finds the fingerprint (14) and the trapdoor (14). Huell reads the room and spots the walkie-talkie; Kurt hides it in the car under blankets. Lena Scott and her parents arrive at the gate and ask whether the lighthouse is reopening; Andrew tells them not to follow, Kurt warns them to stay out of the water and not to eat the fish, and they leave. The basement shows someone was beaten in a chair and taken to a third location, probably by police. The field journal records the nerve-agent conclusion, the strange fish and threats from the mayor and senior officials; its last entry is about the lighthouse (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Summer Service 04
docs.text: The party leaves the lighthouse at the start of the session as the storm sets in. Andrew, who stood guard outside, catches the end of a squad car driving away. Because of that, and because their out-of-town car may have been noticed, Dante (as Kurt) calls the lighthouse "an active trap" and the team decides to get away from it. The walkie-talkie is returned to the car so they can speak aloud (Summer Service 04). Later, when Kurt asks about the melted shoreline, the Chief of Police goes very still, and Kurt says he saw it from a boat near the lighthouse (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Summer Service 05
docs.text: The lighthouse is mentioned only as a joke hiding place (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: None. The missing scientists were held and questioned here, and the police are implied to have removed them, but no one is present when the team visits.

docs.title: Lonely Mountain Diner
docs.text:
The Lonely Mountain Diner is Sheila's diner in Radford, Virginia, a friendly 1950s-style vinyl diner with superb blackcurrant pie. The team uses it for meetings and meals across both Radford arcs, and in Radford Horrors 04 its security camera supplies footage of the gray van raid.

Type Location (diner) Aliases The diner; Sheila's diner Region Radford, Virginia Staff Sheila, waitress First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In the first arc the diner is friendly and serves blackcurrant pie (with peach ice cream and cheddar); the only drinks on offer are Pepsi and water. It has a kitchen phone with a broken mic, a payphone around the corner and a kitchen back exit. The roof of the post office is not visible from inside (Radford Horror 01). It is a 1950s vinyl diner with a friendly waitress and a discontinued "heart attack special" (Radford Horror 05).

In the second arc it stands across the street from the neon Douglas Pinball Emporium, in a row that includes a small library and a gas station. It closes at 1 a.m., and every other nearby business closes earlier (Radford Horrors 04). Its menu includes a big breakfast of two sausage patties, four bacon, three eggs over medium, half-pound hash browns, two biscuits with gravy and fruit salad, plus a Monte Cristo and pie (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
Sheriff Frank Roosevelt proposes meeting the team here at 9 a.m. In Radford Horror 01 Sheila serves breakfast while Roosevelt is late, and blames the disappearances on careless hikers, the woods and bears. Kurt goes out to the payphone and spots a man in black with binoculars on the post office roof, and about forty missing-dog posters. He memorizes plates in the post office lot. Sheila checks the window and sees the man but does not know him ("So this isn't like a clock tower situation?"). A red Miata with a cut muffler roars past, and she names the driver as Dean Lawson (Radford Horror 01). See Rooftop watcher.

In Radford Horror 05 the team has lunch there at about 11:45 a.m. The waitress asks whether the van is linked to "the guy on the roof." Huell Kendrick orders a pyramid stack of pancakes taller than his head. Overhearing his obvious bedbug bites, the waitress threatens to burn the diner down for the insurance if it gets bedbugs again, blaming the Pay n' Stay as "Motel Patient Zero" (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
When the team returns, Sheila greets them as "secret agent man," asks about "the one who blew up the toilet" (the Biz) and about Huell's foot, and calls them local heroes for saving "that lady." The former laundromat across the street is now the Emporium (Radford Horrors 02). At that diner Andrew drinks blood in front of Daniel Webster and passes it off as a protein mix, and Huell tries some, eats a big breakfast and vomits all over the diner's bathroom (Radford Horrors 02). The incident is recapped at the start of Radford Horrors 04.

After the Emporium abduction, the team notes that the diner across the street has cameras (Radford Horrors 03). In Radford Horrors 04 Kurt Larson apologizes for Huell's mess, promises a hundred-dollar tip and asks for the footage. The waitress repairs her "on the fritz" camera and finds the gray van raid, which she says came amid a couple of months of gray vans arriving around the woods dispute, possibly tied to the Safe Environment Fund. Kurt takes the tape and promises to return it (Radford Horrors 04). See Diner security tape.

She also tells the team that Billy Thornton, the "homeless" man, hangs around the Pay n' Stay (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.text: • Sheila, the waitress.

docs.title: Lucky house
docs.text:
The Lucky house is the Radford, Virginia home of Liam Lucky and his family, and the first crime scene of The Radford Horror: the locked third-story pink bedroom from which Amanda Lucky vanished.

Type Location (private home, crime scene) Aliases Lucky residence Region Radford, Virginia Inhabitants Liam Lucky and Sarah Lucky; formerly Amanda Lucky First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The house is three stories tall. The third story extends about fifteen feet over a carport on two round wooden posts, with a two-story drop below and no impact marks. An ivy trellis runs up the back to the roof, where a bent metal smokestack stands. The doors have good locks. The décor is very Catholic, with shrines and an oak crucifixion carving, about six feet tall, in place of a TV (Radford Horror 01).

Amanda's bedroom is a pink "Lisa Frank" room with a four-poster bed (one bedpost hollow), a vanity and a bookshelf. Police tape is up (Radford Horror 01). It was locked from the inside, and prints show only Amanda and her family (Radford Horror 01).

Across a wide road and a deep yard, about 100 feet away, stands the trailer of the boy Tyler (Radford Horror 01). The Whateley house is less than a mile away (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: The first crime scene
docs.text:
Sheriff Frank Roosevelt takes the team to the house after breakfast at the Lonely Mountain Diner. He describes Amanda as a 17-year-old cheerleader who was arrested for intoxication and is linked to Dean Lawson, Matt McCready and, in middle school, the Whateley twins (Radford Horror 01).

The team's investigation produces several findings (Radford Horror 01):

  • Huell Kendrick interviews Liam Lucky separately. Both parents are innocent and were asleep, and Amanda is an only child. Liam works on something classified at the Radford Arsenal.
  • Kurt Larson finds the drainpipe above the window knocked loose and the hollow bedpost hiding Xanax and Vicodin prescribed by Dr. Lori. See Amanda's prescriptions.
  • Andrew Howard finds Amanda's diary with its pages removed.
  • The team deduces that Amanda left voluntarily, upward to the roof. Kurt climbs the trellis and finds the bent smokestack with scratch marks consistent with a rope tied there.
  • The parents say Amanda saw a therapist for a year "for her grades," and blame Matt McCready, who lives with his father at a tourist ski lodge. They are surprised the diary was gutted, and report no missing money, toothbrush or suitcase.

Across the road Tyler describes a light and a spaceman all in white with a helmet, above the Lucky house, who "just went down." Roosevelt thinks he dreamed it, and Kurt proposes a man in a motorcycle suit and helmet (Radford Horror 01). See The Spaceman.

docs.title: After Amanda's death
docs.text: The highway crime scene where Amanda's body is found lies about a mile from the house. During the bushwhack through the woods in Radford Horror 05, the team finds a scrap of her dress and the remains of a dog about a quarter mile from the house. Kurt later searches Amanda's room again and finds one bedroom slipper by the window and the other across the room, suggesting that she went to the window, saw something and ran from it so fast that she left her slippers behind (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• Liam Lucky and Sarah Lucky, Amanda's parents.
  • Amanda Lucky.

docs.text:

  • Radford Horror 05

docs.title: Marblehead town hall
docs.text:
Marblehead town hall is the town's City Hall, the site of a student protest over the fish kill and of the second-floor selectmen's meeting room, with its eleven chairs, a Sons of Adam seal and church murals.

Type Location (civic building) Aliases City Hall; the selectmen's meeting room Region Marblehead, Massachusetts, beside the post office Used by Marblehead Board of Selectmen First appearance Summer Service 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The post office stands next to City Hall; McManley parks his mobile-home lab there (Summer Service 03). Upstairs, the second-floor meeting room is built for the board: eleven chairs with name plaques in a circle, and on the rear wall a seal reading "Sons of Adam" showing Jesus amid parted waters (Summer Service 04). Stairs lead down to a parking lot (Summer Service 05). In the finale, the Guard officer mentions "some real weird murals in City Hall" (Summer Service 06); the episodes never show or describe them.

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The selectmen's room. The seats include "J. Evans, businessman" (Jester), the mayor, Amos Shaw, the Chief of Police and banker Horace Cromwell. The plaque of Arnold Weathers is empty, and the councilmen glance nervously at his chair (Summer Service 04).
  • The steps and lot. Protest and parking area.

docs.title: Summer Service 03
docs.text: Andrew walks past a protest of college students outside City Hall, chanting "No more dead fish! No fish for science!", "No Nukes" and "Close Seabrook!" On the way to pick him up, Huell tells the Biz to flick a cigarette at a protester, and it hits a college kid in the eye (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Summer Service 04
docs.text: Jester invites the team to the 6:30 selectmen's meeting, where the dress code is formal. The team arrives in suits and finds a second-floor room with eleven chairs. The Biz sits backwards on a chair, and the chief of police refuses Kurt's request to smoke. The mayor, who preached in Shaw's place in Summer Service 03, is bloated and near-translucent, and so are the chief and several others; Shaw has begun to bloat and Cromwell looks the worst, swallowing twice when Huell asks if he is all right. Everyone in the room has the glow, including the team. When the team asks about the scientists, the mayor says they left just over a week ago and that "some of the tone of their questioning was not very well received", since they accused the town of poisoning the fish with agricultural runoff. Asked about the sickness, the board answers "Satan", and the mayor says that as "game day" nears the devil will be forced to work in the open. Dante (as Kurt) asks about the melted shoreline, and the chief of police's expression goes very still. The session ends with the party in the room with no plan, weighing arrests of the priest, the chief, or everyone (Summer Service 04). See Second coming and eschaton.

docs.title: Summer Service 05
docs.text: The meeting winds down in awkward silence and a silent man in a suit at the back unnerves everyone. Outside, in the rain, Madeline Weathers approaches Andrew in the parking lot (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Summer Service 06
docs.text: The team describes the City Hall murals to the Guard officer as evidence of a religious terrorist group (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The selectmen, the mayor, Jester and the Chief of Police.

docs.text:
• Summer Service 03
  • Summer Service 04
  • Summer Service 05
  • Summer Service 06

docs.title: Marblehead, Massachusetts
docs.text:
Marblehead, Massachusetts is the small colonial coastal town near Salem that is the setting of The Summer Service: a place struck by an offshore explosion, then by a storm, a worm-borne sickness and a cult-run town government, before the National Guard seals it off.

Type Location (town) Aliases Marblehead Region Massachusetts coast, a couple of miles from Salem Governed by A Board of Selectmen dominated by the Sons of Adam Status Sealed by the National Guard as of Summer Service 06 First appearance Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The task force's file describes a preserved colonial seaside town, a couple of miles from Salem, with sea-monster lore, including a tentacled worm monster said to drag people under (Radford Horror 08). In Summer Service 01, Rita looks it up and finds it is about three miles long. The town has one church, one high school, one elementary school, one grocery store, one CVS, one cemetery, a historic district, a fort, a town hall, swampy areas, a radio tower to the north and a crowded harbor of yachts, fishing boats and lobster boats. Andre compares its size with Socorro, New Mexico. It was once enthusiastic about Prohibition (Summer Service 01).

Real Marblehead is run by selectmen, a fact Andre points out; in the campaign the board is a church-linked body with an eleven-seat meeting room (Summer Service 04). Locals are touchy about fish, and Briggs tells the team to "stick to good old Mickey D's" (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Ram and Arms Inn, the team's lodging, a decrepit hotel overlooking the old fort (called a motel or bed-and-breakfast on Gregory Street in Summer Service 01).
  • The beach and harbor and the old working docks.
  • The colonial church.
  • Marblehead town hall and the post office, where McManley parks his lab (see McManley's RV).
  • Amos Shaw's house.
  • The lighthouse.
  • The island across the bay and Arnold Weathers' house.
  • McDonald's, the only food the team trusts.
  • Abandoned gas station.
  • Readful Things, a bookstore with several editions of Moby-Dick and a glowing clerk; Harvard's Bait Shop; a hardware store; the Scott home (Scott Insurance, Boat Specialty) (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 04).
  • National Guard checkpoint at the town entrance, and the nuclear power plant and flooded freeway and marsh outside it.
  • Salem, the nearest big city, with the hospital, the pharmacy for ivermectin and a Whole Foods.

docs.title: Before the arc
docs.text: An unexplained offshore explosion blows out windows in town and sickens residents. The case file in Radford Horror 08 says it happened about a month earlier and that an EPA/USGS field team sent to check for a seabed gas leak has gone missing (Radford Horror 08). In Summer Service 01, Briggs says the fish have been washing up dead for a week and a half since the blast, which fits poorly with the case file's month; the episodes do not reconcile the two (Summer Service 01). See The Marblehead explosion and EPA/USGS survey team.

docs.title: Radford Horror 08
docs.text: The team drives from Hoboken through Stamford, Bridgeport, Boston, Revere and Swampscott and checks in at the Ram and Arms Inn. The innkeeper mentions "fellas from the government" a week earlier, hands over the missing team's belongings and the team finds their field journal (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Summer Service 01
docs.text: The team interviews the sick, finds a severed arm on the beach, attends the church service and meets the preacher Shaw (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Summer Service 03
docs.text: Huell finds Shaw's wrecked house. Andrew dreams of a dead gray man warning him off the water. The team learns the poison is a synthetic nerve agent close to VX, discovers the worms in the communion wine, and finds the lighthouse basement. A tropical depression arrives and Diane reports that the CDC, FEMA and the NCEH are calling; the town is under a chemical-weapon alert (Summer Service 03). The unrecorded Summer Service 02 involved a dive in an experimental submarine that found a stealth wreck and a lit vessel; this is known only from the team's recaps in Summer Service 03 (Summer Service 03); see The stealth wreck.

docs.title: Summer Service 04
docs.text: In the storm, shopkeepers board their windows, a nuclear weapon is delivered and the selectmen's meeting reveals that the town's government is the church (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Summer Service 05
docs.text: Tropical Storm Andrew 2 floods the bridge to the island and washes out roads. The team destroys the infected Arnold Weathers and his dog, and escapes a 4 a.m. attack by the congregation and the police (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Summer Service 06
docs.text: The Guard arrives in force. The team fires the Davy Crockett at the angel thing near the nuclear plant, and the Guard seals the town. Murals in City Hall, the church literature, a cover story of "terrorists" and a medical effort of mass deworming follow (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Later mentions
docs.text: In Radford Horrors 01, Yeltsin tells the Biz that Soviet detectors recorded a cosmic microwave background surge "last year" traced to Marblehead, and the Biz sticks to a story that the military handled it. Dante (as Kurt) refers to "the angel we nuked" there. Diane also knows of submarines that went missing while the team was at Marblehead (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Amos Shaw, the Mayor, the Chief of Police, Jester, Ma Gramoire, Briggs, the Scott family, Esteban, Madeline and Arnold Weathers, plus the Marblehead police and the congregation.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• A McDonald's here sells Halloween Happy Meal toys in June 1992.
  • The storm's name, "Andrew 2", doubles as a gag on Andrew Howard's name.

docs.title: McDonald's
docs.text:
The McDonald's in Marblehead is the task force's recurring refuge and its only trusted source of food, where the Happy Meal toys are Halloween-themed in June and where Esteban works.

Type Location (fast-food restaurant) Region Marblehead, Massachusetts First appearance Summer Service 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The team treats the chain as the one safe food in a town that serves fish at every opportunity and drinks worm-filled wine. Briggs tells them to "stick to good old Mickey D's" (Summer Service 01); in Summer Service 05 Ezra calls it "the safe food that we can actually eat in this town", and in Summer Service 03 Andre announces, "For the sake of immersion, I have just eaten some McDonald's" (Summer Service 05, Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Summer Service 01
docs.text: After visiting the Scott family, the team waits out several hours at the restaurant before the evening church service. Andre first says they spend four hours there, then that about three have passed when Diane pages them. The Happy Meal toys are Halloween-themed in June 1992, when May's were Cabbage Patch Kids, and the team wonders whether the theme is local or whether Radford had it too. Two surly teenagers hold an intense booth conversation. Diane pages with news that McManley is on the way (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Summer Service 03
docs.text: Restless after two days awake, Huell walks to McDonald's at about 10:30 p.m. and finds Amos Shaw's open house on the way. He is standing on the curb with fries when the team and McManley arrive (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Summer Service 04
docs.text: Before the selectmen's meeting the team dines at the restaurant in formal wear while storefronts are boarded. Esteban is working: his mother is in the hospital, his girlfriend says he smells like beans, and he cannot smell it himself. An investigation roll confirms that he smells strongly of beans, and so does a shirt from his home. Esteban works out that his uncle, who volunteers to take the laundry to the laundromat and is a church member, has been adding bean juice to the wash, apparently "to keep me a virgin". The team's advice is absurd (Andrew: borrow the girlfriend's shower and come out in a towel; Huell: "Take the biggest knife in your kitchen"), and Esteban thanks them with a basket of fries with extra salt. Kurt eats his own tuna and noodles instead. Huell orders a Quarter Pounder with no ketchup and a Diet Coke (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Summer Service 05
docs.text: Overnight, Huell goes to McDonald's twice. A teenage girl covering the shift says Esteban "figured it out", and that it was his uncle. The RV later picks Huell up there. When Andre quips that the players should have negotiated a sponsorship deal, Dante answers, "We just really want you to associate the taste of McDonald's with worm parasites." (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Esteban and his co-workers.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Dante's Innsmouth joke in Summer Service 01: "Even got McDonald's in Innsmouth."

docs.title: McManley's RV
docs.text:
McManley's RV is the mobile-home forensics lab of Dr. Donald McManley, the FBI examiner who follows the task force from Marblehead to Dahlonega.

Type Location (vehicle, mobile lab) Aliases The wagon; the mobile lab; McManley's lab; the mobile crime lab Region Marblehead, Massachusetts; later Dahlonega, Georgia Holder Dr. Donald McManley and his interns First appearance Summer Service 03 Last appearance Appalachia 07

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The RV is a large mobile home fitted out as a crime lab and used by McManley as both workplace and lodging. It carries a microscope, a generator and a rotating crew of nervous interns. In Marblehead it has no hot water, and McManley moves into the team's hotel for a night (Summer Service 05). In Georgia he complains that the town has no RV hookups and plans to rent rooms and run a generator on diesel (Appalachia 04). In the rain at Marblehead the RV is described as top-heavy; it goes up on two wheels in the gusts when he drives it off (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
In Summer Service 03 the RV is first parked outside Amos Shaw's house after the team calls the FBI for a forensic examiner. McManley reports from inside that a full body's worth of blood has been lost, mostly in the bathroom, and bags the marbles Huell left behind (Summer Service 03). He then parks beside the Marblehead post office, next to City Hall, which becomes his base and the team's mailing point. There he puts the team's sample of communion wine under the microscope and finds it swimming with worms like tapeworms or nematodes. He tells Andrew to get ivermectin and says he will call the CDC (Summer Service 03).

In Summer Service 04 the RV, still parked outside the post office as McManley's base of operations, is the delivery point for the armored-truck crate that contains the M28 Davy Crockett. The courier meets Kurt beside it. McManley is reluctant to spare anyone ("just drive to Salem"), but the team talks him into lending his assistant Henry to fetch the ivermectin from Salem. Henry unloads a small Vespa from the back of the RV and rides off in the rain (Summer Service 04).

In Summer Service 05 the siege begins at the hotel. At about 4 a.m. a police car and silent armed church members gather outside. The dog head is handed to an assistant in the RV, and McManley examines it in floral pajamas before going to bed with a shotgun. During the siege Kurt leads the group to the RV unseen. They find the assistant asleep inside with a garbage can and cinder block over the dog head, and McManley drives the RV off. It picks up Huell at the McDonald's, and the team decides to ditch it, as big, recognizable and poor in the wind, behind the abandoned gas station and take back the Biz's modified car. When Henry finally returns on his Vespa with the medicine, Andre says he climbs into "the cramped-ass RV", and Dante corrects him: "Cramped-ass car" (Summer Service 05).

In Summer Service 06 the team tries to raise the lab technicians left behind with the RV on the radio and cannot get a hold of them. Their fate is never resolved (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
The RV reappears in Georgia as the base for McManley's forensic work. In Appalachia 03 he radios that he is arriving with the mobile crime lab, delighted by the "face in a bag" and asking about RV hookups. He relays Big Bill's orders that, because of Ruby Ridge and "that thing in Marblehead", the cult-linked case must go strictly by the book (Appalachia 03).

In Appalachia 04 the RV pulls up outside the Smith Hotel. McManley takes the face, the remains bag, shoes and a blood sample, and is appalled by the giant potato sign of the Spud Hut (Appalachia 04).

In Appalachia 06 the team drives to the trailer to deliver the body of the man in the Chewbacca costume. McManley later notes that the bandolier had been removed and mud rubbed into the fur, and heads out in his motor home. Two interns look for somewhere to wash up and ride a moped back to the RV (Appalachia 06).

In Appalachia 07 the RV is parked at the hotel, crowded with interns. The team brings the SHA tracking device and a dirt sample to McManley, who also brings news of the Clinton surveillance affair (see Clinton Surveillance Scandal). Later McManley and two interns pile into the team's car for the drive to the truck site, and the drunk Biz grills the more nervous intern about who was photographing Bill Clinton (Appalachia 07). This is the last time the RV appears in the recorded episodes.

Not the Circle Chasers' RV

Appalachia 07 also features a blacklit RV belonging to the teenage Bigfoot hunters of the Circle Chasers. It is a different vehicle.

docs.text:

  • Unnamed interns and lab technicians, including the assistant who sleeps in the RV during the siege in Summer Service 05
