docs.title: Minor locations: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: Minor locations of The Things in Appalachia, the smaller places visited or mentioned in Georgia. Major sites such as Dahlonega, Auraria and the Smith Hotel have their own pages.

docs.title: Apollo's Dry Cleaners
docs.text: Apollo's is a small-town dry cleaner "down on Second" in Dahlonega, with a rack storage area behind double doors whose latch had been broken for months. Derek Edwards's Chewbacca costume was stolen from there eight months before the arc, and the owner paid Derek $100. The owner recognizes the dead drifter as a man who loitered in the area. The cleaner closes for the night while the team is still questioning the owner. See Apollo's Dry Cleaners Owner. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest
docs.text: The national forest, captioned as seventy miles north of Atlanta, is the setting of the arc's first cold open. A young woman in an ankle-length dress carries a sack of peaches through the trees until something hairy and inhuman drags her screaming off camera. Peaches, an Auraria-style dress and a missing woman suggest Willow Greengrass, but the episode never says the woman is her. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Circle Chasers' RV
docs.text: The Circle Chasers' vehicle is a streamlined silver trailer with a crop circle painted on its side, parked by the road outside Dahlonega when the team first meets the group. By the seventh episode it sits in the Spud Hut lot: blacklit, with guitars, amps and pedals, chewed dog toys, a smell of patchouli and weed, and a wall of firearms. Inside, the teens show the team the blinking tracking device from the bear vomit. See The Circle Chasers. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Community Center
docs.text: The community center is the only other building in Auraria besides the old church. The Covenant's Mother Dahlia Riversand sets the team up there to interview River, and the stony Covenant man storms off from it after Kurt and Huell mention cheeseburgers. See The Covenant. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Dahlonega McDonald's
docs.text: The Dahlonega McDonald's is a near-empty restaurant where the team eats on their first evening in Dahlonega, at about 8 p.m. The worker Eric fears it will close. See Eric. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Dr. Arthur's Office
docs.text: Dr. Arthur's clinic is in his own home, with four beaded curtains, an incense haze and a chest freezer for blood draws. Andrew visits for a clotting-disorder blood test and overdue shots, including MMR, and gets a talk on ritual healing. See Dr. Arthur. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Gold Room
docs.text: The gold room is an underground chamber below the Dahlonega mines with a kitchen table stacked with hundreds of pounds of cast gold bars, about half already gone. The party takes bars under the banner of "civil forfeiture." See Gold Bars and The Dahlonega Gold Mines. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Hotel and Suites
docs.text: Also called the former Best Western, this is the bedbug-prone hotel where Primenthol Greengrass stays, with bedbug traps at the foot of the bed and one chair. It is distinct from the de-branded ex-Holiday Inn used by the dead drifter, which is the Motel and Suites. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Ladder Shaft
docs.text: The ladder shaft is the unguarded, tarp-covered exit from the mines to the woods outside the Spud Hut plant. Clive leads the party there, and Andrew and Huell both aggravate their injuries climbing it. Kurt and the Biz realize it explains how the ape-men escaped, since the handlers relied on the ape-men's fear of dark tunnels. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Lake
docs.text: The lake, unnamed at the table, is where Jan Martense says he sank the car, with the dead NSA man in the passenger seat. Kurt gets the lake's name from Jan. See Jan Martense. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Letterman Studio
docs.text: The New York studio where Late Night with David Letterman tapes. The Biz sits on Letterman's overstuffed couch, staring waxily and sweating through his makeup. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: McManley's Cottage
docs.text: Donald McManley's home is a quaint rose-bush cottage with many locks. Inside it is clean but stale, with reptile terrariums, foil-covered windows, takeout bags and the television tuned to Saturday Night Live. McManley answers the door with a shotgun and cigarette. Huell finds ivermectin bottles in the bathroom and leaves with McManley's promise to return to work. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Old Drop Spot
docs.text: The Biz's old dead drop is a park bench near his old house in Washington, with a loose paving stone concealing a gap. He distrusts it and sends a homeless man to retrieve the taped paper bag, which holds a microphone, a hidden film camera and flash-paper instructions. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Oval Office
docs.text: The Oval Office is where George H. W. Bush debriefs Andrew on Georgia, after Andrew has waited an hour and a half while the president's secretary types angrily. He drops a clump of slightly bloody Yeti fur on the carpet when finally called in. See George H. W. Bush. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Preparation Tent and River
docs.text: A gas-lit tent near the Covenant's red-clay river is where vacuum salesman Jeremy prepares for his baptism. The arc's fourth cold open follows him down a candlelit path to the river, where four women in white kneel in the mud, and an older man with high cheekbones chants in Latin and plunges him beneath the surface. Mother Dahlia Riversand later invites the team to attend the baptism "this evening," and they leave without stopping it. See Covenant Beliefs. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Woods and Ravines
docs.text: The woods and ravines outside Dahlonega are Andrew's route when he sleepwalks from the Smith Hotel: an unused trail, broken stalky plants, Russian olive thickets, a ravine where he hits his head and a street in a dark neighborhood where he finally emerges. The next morning, retracing his blood trail, the team follows it to the Death Cave. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Minor locations: Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable (non-canon one-shot)
docs.text:
Non-canon

These places appear only in Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, a non-canon one-shot presented as an in-universe anime OVA. Nothing here is part of the main campaign's continuity.

Minor locations of the one-shot that do not have their own pages, in alphabetical order. The major sites are the Athletes' Village, The Capital (DC), the Presidential Event Hall, the Public Library and Wisukonshin.

docs.title: Community Center
docs.text: The venue of the pre-event social for disadvantaged children and their guardians, ten blocks from the Public Library. Here Derk is insulted by a bully and befriended by Sarah, and Mirabeth sells Addison an invented essential-oil business. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: I-95
docs.text: The highway whose shoulder Mirabeth speed-walks along in pumps to reach the capital, about 400 miles from the athletes' village. She keeps up a dignified power-walk behind her finned parasol and goes up and over any car in her way. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Miguel's Hot Dog Taco Stand
docs.text: A street stand about a quarter mile outside the athletes' compound, where Miguel sells hot dogs in taco shells with spicy cheese, tomatoes and pico de gallo. Derk and Mirabeth land beside it after leaping the compound wall, and Derk eats 98 hot dog tacos. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Mirabeth's Home
docs.text: Mirabeth's home, equipped with an in-home video phone. After her debriefing she speeds home, and Derk mostly knows where it is. It is where she takes Derk's 2 a.m. call asking to be picked up, and she sets out from here, after removing her curlers and doing her makeup, to rescue him. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Motel 6
docs.text: The leads' $86 joint suite in the capital, one of the relatively clean ones, where they stay after a spot opens up for Derk. The television news there shows Ovain fighting the military at the capital's edge the night before the presidential event. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: West City
docs.text: A financial district where four blocks are evacuated after a gas-line rupture. After the Ovain fight, Colonel Sparago lists the rupture among the damage he attributes to Derk. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Minor locations: Radford (The Radford Horror and The Radford Horrors)
docs.text: This page lists the minor places visited or mentioned in the two Radford arcs, from fast-food stops to a flooded colonial settlement.

docs.title: Arby's
docs.text: The Radford Arby's is the team's regroup spot and the starting point of Radford Horror 03, where Andre remarks that it "might be the worst chain in America". (Radford Horror 03) See Running gags.

docs.title: Ballard, Utah ranch
docs.text: The ranch in Ballard, Utah is mentioned in Moscow, where the Biz explains skinwalkers to Yeltsin: they mimic well but are not strategic, they turn erratic and violent when confronted, and the older ones are more convincing than new ones. It is the site of the Utah case, covered in Sherman Ranch and Ballard, Utah. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Blockbuster Video
docs.text: The back employee room of a Blockbuster Video, with a tiny VHS TV, is where the team views the diner's raid tape and has it copied by Harold. (Radford Horrors 04) See Harold and Diner security tape.

docs.title: Dirt road and clearing
docs.text: The dirt road midway down the mountain leads to a clearing where an armed group is camped: five or six Spanish-speaking people with flashlights, at least one shotgun and an idling vehicle. Dean Lawson's Miata came from the same area. (Radford Horror 03) See Armed group in the woods and Mountain road hit-and-run site.

docs.title: Dog's backyard
docs.text: A suburban backyard, a few blocks from the Augustines, holds a doghouse with a snapped leash where a dog was taken at about 3 a.m. It is where the team finds the white powder. (Radford Horror 04) See White powder and Radford's missing dogs.

docs.title: FBI headquarters
docs.text: The FBI building in Washington is where the team is reassigned, with a smoky canteen, crowded elevators and winding corridors. In 1993 it is tense after Sessions's firing: the team waits outside the Director's office, Todd talks to Kurtis in the men's room, and Giuliani briefs the team in the Director's office. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horrors 01) See FBI and Rudy Giuliani.

docs.title: Hoboken motel
docs.text: A motel in Jersey City, in the vicinity of Hoboken, is the non-horrifying but expensive overnight stop on the drive to Marblehead. (Radford Horror 08) See Marblehead.

docs.title: Huell's apartment
docs.text: Huell's flat is squalid: Roseanne is on, takeout covers the area around the TV, phone books sit on chairs, the microwave is full of dishes and there is a melted Pop-Tart in the toaster. Huell convalesces here after his leg injury. (Radford Horrors 01) See Huell Kendrick.

docs.title: McDonald's drive-thru
docs.text: The Radford McDonald's has a drive-thru wrapping three sides of the building, with the town's only Radio Shack across the street. The team commandeers the elderly couple's car here, and the drive-thru voice offers to dino-size the order for $11.95. It is also a stakeout food stop and the scene of the earlier carjacking. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 06) See Howard and his wife.

docs.title: Post office
docs.text: The roof of the Radford post office is used by an unknown watcher, and its parking lot holds the plates Kurt memorizes. The Marblehead post office also appears in The Summer Service, where McManley's mobile lab is parked. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04) See Rooftop watcher.

docs.title: Quest Coffee
docs.text: Quest Coffee is the upstart coffee shop in Radford. When Kurt jokes about artisanal coffee shops, the sheriff names the only two coffee places in town: the diner and Quest Coffee. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: Radford church
docs.text: The Radford church hosts the town's community meeting at 4:30 p.m., with the sheriff, the FBI and the priest speaking in that order; the town hall is out because of a roof leak and black mold. Molly briefs the team in the back break room beforehand. It is not the old-town church of the climax. (Radford Horror 05) See Old-town church.

docs.title: Radford family-medicine clinic
docs.text: The family-medicine clinic is the doctor's office in town, where the team takes the heroin sample for testing. (Radford Horror 07) See Dean Lawson's heroin and cash.

docs.title: Radford old town and mill
docs.text: The colonial old town is a flooded, abandoned settlement with stone foundations around the church. A mill a quarter mile to the west survives, overgrown, and the team does not find the heroin there. (Radford Horror 08) See Radford old town flood and Old-town church.

docs.title: Radford Sheriff's station
docs.text: The small station has a broom-closet records archive of shelves, boxes and filing cabinets, where Andrew finds the Radio Shack file and the missing-dog folder. Its small morgue, with nitrile gloves, linen aprons and a Vicks tray, is used for Amanda's autopsy. In 1993 the station is lit up at night, and Molly keeps files and the posters there. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horrors 02) See Radford Sheriff's Department.

docs.title: Radio Shack
docs.text: The Radford Radio Shack was the site of Abe's spacesuit break-in three years before the story. The robbery file describes a cinder-block break-in, the spacesuit, fingerprints from heavy gear, stolen modems and a cell phone, and a bus ticket to Richmond. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03) See Radio Shack spacesuit robbery.

docs.title: River near the church
docs.text: The river near the old-town church is where the team tests the heat-ray flashlight. (Radford Horror 08) See Flashlight weapon.

docs.title: Roanoke Airport
docs.text: Roanoke Airport is the nearest airport, about 45 minutes from Radford by road. It is a small regional airport with 737s and private traffic, ringed by mountains; Freak's Cessna is parked in a corner. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 07) See Freak and Annabelle.

docs.title: Roanoke hospital
docs.text: The hospital in Roanoke runs the DFA test on the rabid rat that bit Webster and supplies the HDCV vaccine. (Radford Horrors 03) See Rabid mouse.

docs.title: Salem, Virginia
docs.text: Salem is the town of the ultralight owner, off to the right of the team's search area. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Science fair gymnasium
docs.text: The school gym, with foam boards, potato batteries and a volcano, is where Kurtis meets Toby Garland. (Radford Horrors 01) See Peggy Browning.

docs.title: State police headquarters
docs.text: State police headquarters holds Derek Augustine after the rescue of Dr. Lori. (Radford Horror 06) See Derek Augustine.

docs.title: Tyler's trailer
docs.text: Tyler's trailer sits about 100 feet from the Lucky house, across a wide road and deep yard. The living room is where Tyler is interviewed. (Radford Horror 01) See Tyler and Lucky house.

docs.title: Underhill's mother-in-law suite
docs.text: The rear suite of the sheriff's home is offered to the team, and accepted, as lodging after the Pay n' Stay. (Radford Horrors 03) See Molly Underhill and Pay n' Stay.

docs.title: Minor locations: The Roulet Estate
docs.text: Minor locations of The Roulet Estate, in alphabetical order. The main sites have their own pages: The Roulet House, Roulet Basement, Hidden Attic Lair, The Clown Mansion, The Weapons Closet, Brooks Pharmacy and Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp.

docs.title: Andrew's New York Hotel
docs.text: The hotel room where Andrew Howard lives during his desk posting in New York. Shirtless, he thaws the weekly shipment of human blood in a Brita pitcher, wonders whether he died and what he has become, and watches Roseanne by the light of the TV. The epilogue ends here when the phone rings and the President says, "Something's happened in Virginia." (Roulet Estate 03) See also Frozen Blood Shipments.

docs.title: Ballard
docs.text: The Utah town that was one of the two disaster sites of The Walkers in Skin; see Ballard, Utah. In Roulet Estate 01 it appears only as the setting of the three treasured Polaroids of UFOs that Andrew keeps in his satchel alongside his camera. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Exeter, Rhode Island
docs.text: The rural town where the Roulet house stands, at 118 Benefit Street. The nearest significant town is about a two-hour walk down a winding dirt road, or about an hour of hiking as the crow flies, and snow and cold close in over the course of the arc. The pharmacy where the stolen car turns up is in a town about 25 miles away. (Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03) See also The Roulet House.

docs.title: Former Soviet Parliament Building
docs.text: The Moscow building where the Biz is shackled to a chair in a small meeting room after his flight from Vorkuta. Boris Yeltsin finally walks in, offers a Cuban cigar and asks about the humanists. A silent FSB officer stares at the Biz. (Roulet Estate 03) See also The Humanists.

docs.title: Huell's Apartment Building
docs.text: The filthy apartment and building where Huell Kendrick recovers in March 1993, on disability and in a wheelchair, with two steps up to the elevator landing and communal mailboxes. He is nearly broke and spends his days drinking and watching Roseanne. His neighbor Mrs. McGann hauls the chair up the steps, and the elevator kid asks about his foot. The apartment returns in Radford Horrors 01. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Pawtucket
docs.text: The monk's destination, 1 hour 21 minutes away by car and nine hours on foot. "Pawtucket" is the one word the monk and the agents share, and it becomes a running gag as the agents keep trying to get the half-kidnapped man there. He eventually leaves by taxi. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02) See also The Finnish Hare Krishna Monk.

docs.title: Quantico
docs.text: The FBI training base in Virginia where Kurt Larson lectures young agents in April 1993. His subject is silent breach technique, including a flashlight tip used to signal which corner to take, an infrared laser matched to night vision, and the fact that red dots do not work with headsets. In the evenings he calls his wife and kids from a hotel and spends a couple of hours "visualizing the polygon." (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Roosevelt Medical Tent
docs.text: A flashback setting at the edge of Roosevelt, Utah, 78 days before the present; see Roosevelt, Utah. EMTs in respirators treat the agents while hazmat crews bring in more National Guardsmen covered in white powder. McManley limps to Andrew's bed to report that the powder is a cocktail of benzos and sedatives, and the Major is carried in among the casualties. (Roulet Estate 01) See also Utah White Powder.

docs.title: Roulet Barn
docs.text: A barn behind the Roulet house, chained with a bike lock that the agents cut with bolt cutters. It holds a riding lawnmower, gardening supplies and a huge pile of crushed plastic water bottles. (Roulet Estate 02) See also Riding Lawnmower.

docs.title: The Biz's Apartment and Buried Gold
docs.text: The Biz's apartment, which the table establishes he prepaid for a year in January, in gold, to a slightly seedy landlord who would not ask questions, and the park near his house where the other agents buried his share of the gold after he vanished, leaving him a cryptic message. After Andrew mutters "He's probably dead," he plans to go knock on the apartment door and ask the landlord whether he has been seen. (Roulet Estate 03) See also The Georgia Gold.

docs.title: The Dive Bar
docs.text: The bar where the agents drank angrily after officials came to take their files, shortly before Inauguration Day. Andrew's last memory is of being dragged there, and Diane later says they had been driving for seven hours. Its location is never given. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: World Trade Center
docs.text: The site of Andrew's desk posting on the February 1993 bombing investigation. He analyzes photographs of the bomb in an office there, and a 747 passes outside the window. (Roulet Estate 03) See also February 1993 WTC Bombing.

docs.title: Minor locations: The Summer Service
docs.text: These are the smaller places visited or mentioned during the Marblehead case. The larger sites have their own pages, including Marblehead, the lighthouse and Marblehead town hall.

docs.title: The cemetery
docs.text: The town's only graveyard, kept by O'Donnell. Briggs calls it "a nice graveyard" and, asked whether it belongs to the church, says he does not think so. The team never visits. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: The fort
docs.text: Also called the old fort. A military fort on the coastline that the Ram and Arms Inn looks out on, as Andre describes when the team arrives at the end of Radford Horror 08. Briggs tells tourists the fort is "pretty cool," and Irene Scott's daughter wandered away from a school field trip there before she was found unconscious on the beach. See Ram and Arms Inn. (Radford Horror 08; Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Gramoire Residence
docs.text: Ma Gramoire's slightly broken-down house on the main island, with "Gramoire Residence" over the door. Kurt, Huell and the Biz visit in Summer Service 03, where she receives them with a cane, a sharp tongue, a grilled cheese sandwich and absinthe over ice. Kurt uses her phone to call Big Bill. See Ma Gramoire. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Harvard's Bait Shop
docs.text: The shop where Huell buys a trash bag to hold the severed arm. The owner's cousin draws the axolotls in the shop. Bagging the arm lessens the smell but does not remove it. See The severed arm and the shop owner. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Madeline's house
docs.text: The house of Madeline Weathers, where the team escorts her after the visit to her uncle's walled house. Before they leave, the Biz plants a bug, the team gives her pager numbers, and Kurt gives her a joint and teaches her to make a Molotov cocktail. Huell gives her his knife. See Madeline Weathers and Arnold Weathers' house. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: The old docks
docs.text: The weathered working docks of Marblehead, where Andrew finds Briggs dozing in a lawn chair beside a rickety fishing boat and the team questions him. Briggs blames "the goddamn Russians" for the bombing. See Briggs. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Readful Things
docs.text: An independent bookstore where the Biz buys the 1980 reprint of Moby Dick that he needs for his secret instructions. The clerk has the glow and watches him closely, and he also buys a newspaper there as cover. See Moby-Dick book cipher and the Readful Things clerk. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Salem
docs.text: The nearest city to Marblehead, a couple of miles away; Andre notes the team could walk there. A doctor in Salem drained the infected glass cut that Briggs took in the explosion, and Irene Scott's daughter was taken to the big hospital there, where she was on a ventilator for a couple of hours. In Summer Service 04 a luck roll puts a large-animal vet in Salem, and Henry goes there for the ivermectin; in Summer Service 05 the signal from his radio comes from the Salem direction. Madeline Weathers says she gets her food from the Whole Foods in Salem. See also Ivermectin. (Radford Horror 08; Summer Service 01; Summer Service 04; Summer Service 05)

docs.title: The Scott home
docs.text: A small suburban house near the commercial district, which is also the office of Scott Insurance. Irene checks the team's ID and offers coffee and snacks, and Douglas arrives with his young daughter Lena, who crawls into Andrew's lap and asks for coffee. See Scott Insurance, Douglas Scott and Lena Scott. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Seabrook nuclear plant
docs.text: Also called Seabrook. The nuclear power station that Andre says has "just opened," which the college protesters blame for the fish die-off. The front page of the Salem Statesman's Journal covers the plant protests alongside the die-off. See College protesters and The nuclear power plant. (Summer Service 03; Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Minor locations: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text: This page lists the minor places visited or mentioned in The Walkers in Skin; the main settings are Ballard, Roosevelt and the Sherman Ranch.

docs.title: Ambush site
docs.text: A stretch of the only road between Ballard and Roosevelt, where a spike strip rolls McManley's Suburban. Four townspeople attack him there, and the party later finds an empty Roosevelt police cruiser parked in the rocks nearby, the source of the spike strip, whose radio is silent on every channel. See the roadside ambushers. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Andrew's apartment
docs.text: Andrew's home in Washington, D.C. Alberta Wilmarth turns up there at the end of Walkers 01, holding a box of documents and tapes, and asks the FBI to force the church to exhume her mother. The apartment also features in a dream Andrew recalls in Walkers 06, in which he takes out the trash and finds his naked self eating garbage. See Alberta's box. (Walkers 01, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Ballard courthouse
docs.text: A former church in Ballard that serves as the courthouse. It is closed after hours when the party drives into town in Walkers 03, and a bar across the street is open. A traditionalist judge sits here, and Big Bill later talks a religious judge into issuing the exhumation order. In Walkers 06 the courthouse is instead described as another double-wide; see Ballard City Hall. (Walkers 03)

docs.title: Ballard radio station
docs.text: A small radio station on the east side of Ballard, which Kurt spots on a town map as a possible backup source of communication. The party carries a generator there to broadcast to the National Guard, an event known from the recap at the start of Walkers 09. See the National Guard. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Bridgeland
docs.text: The next town past the bridge blockade, 23 miles from Roosevelt. In Walkers 08 the party votes to drive for it in a two-car convoy, before turning back at the blockade. The players first say "Ragland"; Andre gives the name as Bridgeland. See the bridge blockade. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: Doug's trailer
docs.text: A trailer in the desert whose key is hidden under a ceramic frog. It has a cross and a mirror in the entryway, cabinets full of hundreds of Jell-O packages, and plates of Jell-O in the fridge with rotting food shoved behind. It also holds a figure wrapped in garbage bags. The trailer appears only in cold opens, and its location is never given. See Doug and sugar clues. (Walkers 04, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Duchesne
docs.text: The town from which the tow truck comes to recover the wrecked rental van in Roosevelt. It is named only in passing. See the Plymouth Voyager. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: East Lagoon Street
docs.text: The Roosevelt street where the vanished Plymouth Voyager reappears, flattened and fused into the asphalt, with 10 to 20 percent of the car stuck in the road even after Huell lifts the wreck free. Andrew responds to the news with "It got unabducted." See the vanishing car. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Good Hills Diner
docs.text: A busy diner in Roosevelt, recommended by Officer Hernandez. It serves the eight-inch French Toast Castle, two-pound biscuits and gravy, and funeral potatoes. The party breakfasts here in Walkers 04, with a glum waiter who mixes up the order. See French Toast Castle. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Pig pen
docs.text: Alberta's pig pen on the ranch. She tends it in Walkers 02, and Walt says the pigs are nice "except for the screaming." In Walkers 04 a carbonized crow falls into it. See the burned crow. (Walkers 02, Walkers 04)

docs.title: Roosevelt hospital
docs.text: A small hospital in Roosevelt. In Walkers 07 it is where the naked intruder dies after being driven there. In Walkers 08, with the ambulance and its radio stolen, the doctors are keeping the generator running for a single ventilator patient. See the naked intruder. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08)

docs.title: Salt Lake City
docs.text: The state capital, where the party lands and where the FBI field office is. It is also the base of the Utah National Guard, 141 miles from Roosevelt, and the home of the dealer who rents the party a ground-penetrating radar for $800. In Walkers 08 the radios cannot reach it. See the FBI Salt Lake City field office. (Walkers 02, Walkers 04, Walkers 08)

docs.title: Sheriff's double-wide
docs.text: Sheriff McDermish's station and home, a trailer with a card table, a Monopoly game under way and a porch where he chain-smokes. Bud answers the door in Walkers 03. In Walkers 06 it is the place where the sheriff gives Kurt his Remington 870 and a list of absent families, before leaving town. See Ballard Sheriff's Office. (Walkers 03, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Stewart's
docs.text: A grocery store in Roosevelt with house egg-based ice cream, in hazelnut and French vanilla. The party shops here before the night event, and the elderly cashier gives Andrew his nickname "Half-Gallon Howard." See the checkout lady and Dollar Tree. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Stock-tank room
docs.text: A dim room of tanks of dark liquid, hoses and wires, with distant voices and squeaking shoes, seen only in the cold open of Walkers 07. Huell's face rises from the last tank and opens bloodshot eyes. The scene hints that a copy of Huell exists; see Skinwalker Huell. (Walkers 07)

docs.title: Vernal
docs.text: A larger town east of Ballard, considered by the party in Walkers 08 as another way out of the area. They never go there. (Walkers 08)

docs.title: World beyond the portal
docs.text: A burned, blasted landscape under a smoky sky, with a trail of emergency lights, glimpsed through the portal in the cavern. The party sees no machinery on the far side, and the portal resembles the one in Georgia but does not exit there. It looks like an evacuation destination for the skinwalkers' tanks of blood. See the portal and the cavern. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Yusuf's junkyard
docs.text: A junkyard with a car crusher and a magnetic crane, owned by Yusuf Ansari. The mayor says it lies in Ballard County outside the municipal limits, which is why he cannot help. The Roosevelt police arrested Yusuf after he confessed to crushing the Voyager; the party doubts the confession. (Walkers 05, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Motel and Suites
docs.text:
The Motel and Suites is a seedy, de-branded former Holiday Inn in Dahlonega, Georgia, where the man in the Chewbacca costume stayed as "John Doe" and where the team searched the dumpster.

Type Location Aliases Express & Suites; former Holiday Inn Region Dahlonega, Georgia First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The motel lost its Holiday Inn franchise. The "Holiday Inn" part of the old sign has been chiseled off, and the air conditioners rattle out of phase, which Zack said sounded like cicadas. The front office is behind bulletproof glass with a slot for passing things through. A nicer place "up the hill" is where better guests stay (Appalachia 06).

When the team first arrived in town in Appalachia 01, the sign read only "Express & Suites"; it had clearly been a Holiday Inn until the franchise was lost. The team chose the Smith Hotel instead.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The dumpster search. Apollo's dry cleaners had pointed the team here: its owner recognized the dead man's photo as an out-of-town drifter who stood around watching, sometimes on a walkie-talkie, and believed he was staying at the Motel and Suites. The clerk confirmed the man registered as "John Doe," had been seen with a walkie-talkie a couple of times, and was picked up on an ATV once or twice by another man. His belongings were thrown out after he stopped renewing (Appalachia 06).

The clerk warned them off a green garbage bag, which held linens from a pornographic shoot of a scatological sort. The dumpster held about a dozen bags. Kurt phoned McManley, who sent three teenage interns about half an hour later to help sort the trash. Snakeskin cowboy boots, which the clerk remembered taking from the room, identified the right bag (Appalachia 06).

The haul: a briefcase with a false lining and a slot for a high-caliber handgun, about $10,000 in bank-banded hundreds and twenties, a thick coil of animal hair in one boot and a walkie-talkie in the other, plus plastic bags and duct tape. Nothing identified the man. See Dead Man's Briefcase. Kurt's read, confirmed by Andre as an intuitive impression, was that the man was a mercenary rather than a spook, perhaps sent to kill someone and double-crossed. The dead man's room had already been rented to a family (Appalachia 06). He was later identified as Troy Cleaver (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The unnamed clerk, who had worked there a few months and said such messes happen conservatively four times a year. He gave Andrew a fatherly pat through the slot and a pep talk about being in the right line of work (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 01
  • Appalachia 06

docs.title: Mountain road hit-and-run site
docs.text:
The mountain road hit-and-run site is a stretch of winding mountain road below the Radford ski lodge where the team is shadowed by an unknown flying craft in Radford Horror 03 and Kurt Larson's car hits Agent Murphy. A nearby clearing is where the burned man's remains are found in Radford Horror 04.

Type Location (road and forest clearing) Aliases Mountain highway stretch; the clearing; hit-and-run site and clearing; mountain road Region Mountains near Radford, Virginia, below Alpine Lodge First appearance Radford Horror 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The road is a winding mountain highway with ski lodge signs. The ski lodge has a parking lot, buildings, cabin roads and ski-lift access roads (Radford Horror 03). Midway down the mountain a dirt road leads off to a clearing where an armed group meets. After Murphy's flashlight weapon is fired, the trees beside the road are left burning (Radford Horror 03).

In Radford Horror 04 a clearing in the woods is where the burned man's remains lie. A circle of ground is melted to glass, and tire tracks lead into the trees and simply end (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: The hit-and-run
docs.text:
At dusk in Radford Horror 03, Kurt notices stars going out above the lodge. A large dark silent object circles over the car, between an ultralight and a Cessna in size, under a couple of hundred feet up, and powered. It seems to follow them specifically. Dick "The Biz" Baxter leans out with a flashlight (he has torn off the rearview mirror to look up) and rolls a 12: the object flares a dazzling "evanescent" blue, makes a noise they have never heard, shows folded compact shapes, and zips over the tree line (Radford Horror 03).

At that moment a man in a black suit steps out 10 to 15 feet ahead. Kurt brakes rather than swerves and hits him at about 50 mph. The man cracks the windshield, rolls over the car and falls behind. The Biz thinks aliens just blew up the windshield (Radford Horror 03).

Meanwhile, Huell Kendrick finds an idling vehicle in a clearing and overhears tense Spanish, then five or six people with flashlights (one with a shotgun) spread out. Andrew Howard is questioned by two of them at the car and drives off after sensing he'll be shot. See Armed group in the woods (Radford Horror 03).

Kurt and the Biz find the struck man alive, vomiting blood, clutching a flashlight and a briefcase. He shows a badge: "I'm Agent Murphy. I'm NSA. You are fucking this up for me." When Kurt grabs him, Murphy points the flashlight: a blue-purple flash and a rapid electric clacking set Kurt's shirt on fire (3 harm) and blind both agents for 30 to 45 seconds. Kurt spits his "LSD tooth" dose into Murphy's mouth, and Murphy flees. When the Biz chases, Murphy fires behind him and trees burst into flame, and he drops off a ledge (Radford Horror 03).

In a scene the party does not witness, Andre cuts to a delirious Murphy (skull fracture, one eye partly out, foaming blood) shooting at birds until the device overheats and he vanishes in a pulse of light (Radford Horror 03). The pulse is the device burning him and the ground around him; the team finds what is left at the clearing later that night (see below).

docs.title: The clearing
docs.text:
The cold open of Radford Horror 04 shows a slumped, partly smoldering figure beside burning trees, approached by a coyote that begins to eat him. After Kurt is treated at the ER, the team returns around midnight. Broken glass and blood remain. Kurt luminols the faded blood and follows it to a clearing, where mildly high coyotes are eating the remains and scamper off. A circle of ground is melted to glass; only the back of the suit, the back of the skull and a little brain remain, and the briefcase is a melted wad. Kurt finds scorched teeth and the NSA ID (Radford Horror 04). The two scenes follow one another: the overheating device consumes Murphy in the pulse of light at the end of Radford Horror 03, and Radford Horror 04 opens on his half-burned remains on the glassed ground it left behind (Radford Horror 03; Radford Horror 04).

Where the man stepped from the woods, tire tracks lead into the trees and simply end, and footprints lead back to the road. Kurt cannot say how the car was removed (Radford Horror 04). See Murphy's briefcase and documents.

The Biz then cleans the scene: he removes the glass and blood and walks down the thin burned trees so they are out of sight (Act Under Pressure 13) (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 03
  • Radford Horror 04

docs.title: The nuclear power plant
docs.text:
The nuclear power plant is a fortified coastal reactor facility near Marblehead, Massachusetts, and the target of the infected convoy in the climax of The Summer Service.

Type Location Region Marblehead area, Massachusetts, on the coast Status Fence knocked down and machine guns silenced by the nuclear blast; infected people were inside and fighting continued (as of Summer Service 06) First appearance Summer Service 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The plant lies beyond a flooded freeway and a stretch of marshland, ringed by a perimeter fence. When Kurt worries about firing a nuclear device near it, the radio contact replies, "Oh, those things are way overbuilt. It'll be fine. They're designed for you to fly a 747 into 'em." Kurt doubts his claim to have "done this before" (Summer Service 06).

The episodes never name the plant or the real-world facility it might be modeled on.

docs.title: Defenses
docs.text: Just beyond the fence the ground drops about six inches when something heavy crosses it, which popped dozens of tires on the convoy's vehicles. Machine-gun turrets then cut the convoy down from behind the rain and fog. A handful of howling infected ran through the gunfire and got inside, and one gun jammed with a horrible mechanical sound (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
• The plan. After the glowing angel thing turned back toward the sea, the radio contact and Kurt agreed the creature was heading for the plant, where the convoy of worm-infected townspeople was going. The idea was to let the convoy engage plant security, which would force the creature out of the water to help them, and then to take a shot at it from a vantage point (Summer Service 06).
  • The convoy attack. The team followed the convoy along the freeway, then watched it leave the road for the last quarter mile through marsh. From about a mile away they saw the convoy ram the fence, lose its tires to the sunken ground and get shredded by the machine guns (Summer Service 06).
  • The nuclear shot. As a light rose out of the ocean, Huell fired the Davy Crockett. The shockwave knocked the team flat, toppled the fence and silenced the guns, and trees in the distance burst into flame. The creature survived and came straight for the team (Summer Service 06).
  • Aftermath. Gunfire could still be heard from the plant as the team left. At the Marblehead checkpoint a National Guard lieutenant told Andrew that the attack had failed but killed a few guards. The older officer in charge later remarked that someone had used a tactical nuke there, which would be very hard to keep out of the news. The team agreed to tell the authorities that terrorists were responsible (Terrorist cover story) (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Plant security and the infected who breached it. It is never shown how many infected survived inside.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 06

docs.title: Old-town church
docs.text:
The old-town church is a century-old stone-and-wood church standing in a clearing deep in the woods near Radford, Virginia. It is where the crucifixions of The Radford Horror take place, where the team fights the Radford Moth, and which burns down during the fight and is then cleaned of evidence.

Type Location (abandoned church) Aliases The abandoned church; burned church; church in the clearing; burned-out church Region Woods near Radford, Virginia, by the river First appearance Radford Horror 07

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The church is a stone-and-wood colonial building, at least a hundred years old, in an overgrown clearing of about twenty by thirty feet, an hour's hike into the woods (Radford Horror 07). Its windows are boarded with plywood, its roof has partly caved in and shows a blue glow through the gap, it has a new padlock, and a pile of dog collars sits outside. The rear stained glass of Christ with Longinus's spear is intact. Inside are cleared pews and a pulpit with a crucifixion station plus two more, with medical supplies and heroin. The back rooms are unexplored (Radford Horror 07).

In Radford Horror 08 the church is placed in an abandoned colonial "old town" built near the river, which has since flooded and been abandoned. The church survived the flood. Stone foundations remain, and a quarter mile west an overgrown mill survives, where no heroin was found (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The crucifixion site and the fight
docs.text:
Having spotted the building from Freak's plane, the team hikes in at evening. Andrew Howard is overcome with dread and the sense of being watched by a clinical intelligence, like "the stare of a cat on a mouse that it's got pinned between its paws." Inside, a woman is crucified above the pulpit, a naked scarred boy rocks and mutters, and there is motion in the rafters. The boy is Wilbur Whateley (Radford Horror 07). The woman is Phoebe Augustine (Radford Horror 07).

Wilbur tells Andrew "it has to breed. They're born pregnant." A car-sized blue butterfly creature drops from the ceiling, its rolling wings washing the room in blue light and touching the minds of the agents. Kurt counters it with fire (an Everclear Molotov, doubled for its weakness), the Biz rips its wing and gouges its eyes, and Huell cuts off a leg with bolt cutters. The roof catches fire, and the party evacuates Wilbur, Phoebe and the wounded as the building burns. Kurt re-padlocks the door, and something slams against it from inside. Andrew hears "Save me, child! You know the ones who made me—" dissolving into screaming and silence (Radford Horror 07).

At the end of the episode, soldiers without insignia and "volcanologists" in metal suits with flamethrowers approach (Radford Horror 07). The next episode opens in late afternoon on May 29th, 1992, with the church an inferno. Special forces gesture at it while volcanologist men circle it and break glass at the back (Radford Horror 08). See The cleanup crew.

docs.title: The cover-up
docs.text:
The sheriff presents the police theory in Radford Horror 08: a hidden basement with a spaceman costume containing a journal, a cadaver likely Abelforth Whateley, Wilbur as a serial killer, a cartel link through the heroin found in the church, and Mrs. Whateley's body, crucified, burned and disemboweled, at the back of the church. See The cartel (Radford Horror 08).

When the team returns after discharge, the church is behind police tape and mostly burned. The stained glass window has been smashed out, the moth corpse is gone, and the gore and the dog collars have been cleaned away. A humanoid fat stain marks where Mrs. Whateley lay. The Biz learns that evidence was deliberately removed, and Huell finds no remains of the moth (Radford Horror 08). Kurt tests the strange flashlight by the nearby river with a welding mask (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The second arc
docs.text: A little less than a year later, Sheriff Molly Underhill tells the team that the people found at the church were almost dead and that cartel members were apparently there too. Daniel Webster distrusts the cartel explanation and the conveniently timed church fire (Radford Horrors 02). Andrew wants to return to the burned-out church, but the team never visits it in the recorded sessions (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: • Wilbur Whateley and the Radford Moth, at the time of the fight.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 07
  • Radford Horror 08
  • Radford Horrors 02

docs.title: Original Spud Hut
docs.text:
The Original Spud Hut is the walk-up stuffed-potato restaurant in Dahlonega, Georgia, under a giant neon potato, where the team ate again and again while investigating the town.

Type Location Aliases Spud Hut (Dahlonega); Spud Hut restaurant; Spud Hut drive-thru Region Dahlonega, Georgia Affiliation Spud Hut First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In Appalachia 01 the team saw only the dark neon sign, an unlit potato above a lot with room for about 40 cars, after a McDonald's counter kid named Eric recommended the original Spud Hut and complained that the only other local option was the big Spud Hut plant on the edge of town. In Appalachia 02 a woman they questioned told them the original Spud Hut is in this town, not in Idaho as people assume, and is "sixty or seventy years old now."

When the team ate there in Appalachia 02, Andre described a hut about the size of a small burger joint, with an awning, a couple of benches and an order window but no inside to the restaurant. The neon potato is significantly wider than the building and casts a dim, potato-colored light over several blocks. Andre made it canon that the bathrooms are in a separate building across the parking lot, and that the worker's kitchen is a corridor about two feet by five. Spuds cost $5 each, which Ezra called expensive for 1992. Food arrived within a minute or so and Andre rated the spuds from an A to a C-plus (Appalachia 02).

Drive-thru versus walk-up

In Appalachia 03 the team "pulls up under the big Spud Hut sign," orders at the front and is told to wait by the second window, which reads more like a drive-thru than the walk-up hut with benches in Appalachia 02. The episodes treat it as the same restaurant and never address the difference.

docs.title: The menu and staff
docs.text:
The counter worker recites roughly 100 specials from memory with no menu board. When Kurt dropped a pile of matchsticks, he said the number was 43 instantly, and when Kurt urged him to get out and use his mind, he answered, "I can't leave the Spud Hut. The Spud Hut changed my life." He then locked up and walked off across the parking lot into the woods (Appalachia 02). In Appalachia 06 a savant counter kid who had worked there 793 days said "Spud Hut saved my life" and called a coin flip correctly. See Spud Hut Counter Savant.

The numbered menu is covered at Spud Hut Menu. In Appalachia 02 the team ordered Southwestern, poutine, BLT and chicken Parmesan spuds; at lunch on another day they ordered Greek, spaghetti and meatball, Reuben and spinach and artichoke spuds (Appalachia 03). Andre also established that the restaurant has a liquor license, and it keeps a locked, encrypted secret menu (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
• Appalachia 02. The counter savant, a hundred specials and a challenge: finish one of each and it is free; otherwise the bill is about $5,000. Kurt told the worker to leave; he answered with the "changed my life" line (Appalachia 02).
  • Appalachia 03. Lunch after the cave and the freeway, $25 for four (Appalachia 03).
  • Appalachia 06. Lunch with the photographer Derek Edwards and the Spud Hut corporate auditor, who had been following the team. The savant told them the dead hoaxer had come in on three occasions (4, 9 and 25 days earlier), carried a holster and a wallet containing only cash, and arrived by ATV. Once he was there at the same time as a man in a business suit, though the two did not speak (Appalachia 06).
  • Appalachia 07. Dinner. They met the drunk Eduardo Hooper, the Circle Chasers arrived, and the counter man produced the handwritten cryptogram from a two-key briefcase. The Chasers' Great Dane, Harvey, knocked Andrew over; the Chasers described bear vomit and a blinking light that became the SHA tracking device. The hut closed but left the giant potato lit for a couple of hours, so the group stood in potato-colored light ("potato noir") (Appalachia 07).

After the arc, Kurt arranged for the savant teen from Spud Hut to get a job at the CIA (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The savant counter worker, covered above. See also Eduardo Hooper and the Circle Chasers.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 01
  • Appalachia 02
  • Appalachia 03
  • Appalachia 06
  • Appalachia 07

docs.title: Oryol crash site
docs.text:
The Oryol crash site is a farm site in Oryol Oblast, Russia, where a triangular craft has crashed into and destroyed a farmhouse. The Russian army has put up a tent over it, and in Radford Horrors 04 Dick "The Biz" Baxter accompanies President Boris Yeltsin there.

Type Location (crash site) Aliases Russian crash site; Oryol Oblast; Russia crash site Region Oryol Oblast, Russia Controlled by Russian government First appearance Radford Horrors 03 (named as destination)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
A tent covers the partly excavated triangular craft beside the destroyed farmhouse; the helicopter lands in a fallow field nearby (Radford Horrors 04). The cold open of Radford Horrors 04 pans over frozen countryside in the dark to work lights and the buried triangular craft, where the farmhouse used to be, as the army erects a tent (Radford Horrors 04).

Behind a double-walled plastic curtain under arc lamps lies the craft, a little smaller than the space shuttle, which annihilated the farmhouse. The tent is entered through an airlock (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: The destination
docs.text: In Radford Horrors 03 Yeltsin wakes the Biz and tells him in the hotel lobby that there has been "an unusual aircraft crash in Oryol Oblast" he wants him to see. The convoy is ambushed on the road before it can reach the site, and the Biz saves the president (Radford Horrors 03). See Hotel Metropol and Convoy ambushers.

docs.title: The visit
docs.text:
After a night in a guarded hospital room, the Biz is taken to see the president, who is sutured but gracious. The Biz then rides a helicopter with Yeltsin's hospital bed through the night to the crash site, takes a jeep to the tent, and after about forty minutes on a folding chair helps push the bed through the airlock into the craft room (Radford Horrors 04).

Inside the tent are a shirtless Russian soldier in one bed and "about 55% of a guy" in the other, with one arm missing and everything below the navel gone, the two connected by tubes exchanging blood, urine and other fluids. The being is hairless, with wrong teeth and jaw, wide-set eyes and pale, mottled skin. It reminds the Biz, much more so, of the subtle change over Andrew Howard since he died (Radford Horrors 04). See Crash survivor.

Yeltsin has doctors wake the being with a syringe. Asked why it is here, it answers "Survey." Asked about its people, it says "Not aliens. The opposite of aliens," and then "Servitors... need resources." Doctors warn that pushing further is very risky, so Yeltsin ends it. In private, Yeltsin asks the Biz for insights and notes that the being accepts O-negative blood (Radford Horrors 04). See Servitors.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The episodes do not explain what servitors are, what resources they need, or what Yeltsin does next (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horrors 03
  • Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Pay n' Stay
docs.text:
The Pay n' Stay (formally the Econo-Thrift Pay n' Stay) is the run-down cash-only motel in Radford, Virginia, across the street from the Ferry Lodge, where the task force stays on both of its Radford cases and which becomes a running joke for its bedbugs, mold, bats and rabid mice.

Type Location (motel) Aliases Econo-Thrift Pay n' Stay; Econo Thrift Pay n' Stay; the motel Region Radford, Virginia Staff Rutherford (night clerk, first arc); Charm (clerk, second arc) First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In the first arc the motel has a half-lit sign, a gas station behind it and an open-window front office. Rooms cost $26 a night, cash only, and are avocado-brown with 4-inch black-and-white 1950s TVs with three channels, peeling wallpaper, a nicotine-stained mirror, carpet that extends into the bathrooms, and bedbugs. There is no continental breakfast; coffee costs 50 cents (Radford Horror 01). The doors are thin, and someone once died of heroin in a bathtub, according to a joke (Radford Horror 05). Its payphone is by the front desk (Radford Horror 04).

In the second arc the motel is within 1,000 feet of a school, which cost the old UFO-fan manager his job. Mold, bedbugs, bats and rabid mice are all present. The bed sheets are washed this time, and keys are on huge red rulers (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
On arrival, the group finds the nearby Ferry Lodge full and the clerk points them across the street. From across the street the motel looks "real, real old and not particularly well-maintained." The group pays for a second night in three rooms ($78) (Radford Horror 01). Dick sleeps on the shower curtain to avoid bedbugs, Kurt in a wetsuit, Andrew Howard in the tub, and Huell gets a rash (Radford Horror 01).

The motel's owner listens to a UFO radio station (the Art Bell station), and the Biz finds the radio in the room of the missing Abelforth Whateley tuned to the same one. The motel also supplies the tourist map that the team later uses to chart the missing dogs and the craft's headings (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 06). See Abe's radio.

In Radford Horror 04 the rooms have been searched. Bathroom windows were pried open from outside and suitcases opened, with nothing taken. The Biz chats up the night clerk Rutherford and buys $40 of DMT from him. He also learns of a guest in a fishing hat, Red Dutchford, who checked in under that name and left that evening. Kurt bump-keys the man's room and finds it wiped (Radford Horror 04). Huell takes no precautions against the bedbugs and ends up with a rash (Radford Horror 04).

In Radford Horror 05 Kurt develops the burglary film here in his portable darkroom and scalds Huell's sheets. The team then moves to the Ferry Lodge around 1 p.m. (Radford Horror 05). The diner waitress blames the motel as "Motel Patient Zero" for the bedbugs (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
After the IRS shuts the Ferry Lodge, the team checks into the motel. A homeless man there says he was kidnapped in a van with chimpanzees and molested by "John Travolta" (Radford Horrors 02). See Billy Thornton. The new clerk, the teen Charm, gives them two doubles. Kurt hoses both rooms with pesticide. Charm says a three-day chlorine tent killed the bedbugs, but hides "something"; she admits only to mold (Radford Horrors 02).

At about 3 a.m. a foaming, stiff-legged mouse climbs up Daniel Webster's stomach. He flicks it off with his gun barrel and it bites him through his shirt. Kurt spears it to the floor with his spear gun. Charm admits a rodent problem, saying a bat infestation gives the mice rabies. She refunds them and says she doesn't sleep there. The team ends the session at the Radford ER, where all receive rabies shots (Radford Horrors 02). See Rabid mouse.

Afterward, "Pay n' Stayed" becomes the local joke for catching something there; Sheriff Molly Underhill greets the team with "I heard you got Pay n' Stayed" (Radford Horrors 03). In Radford Horrors 04 the homeless man, Billy Thornton, is again said to haunt the motel; a teenage staffer in hip waders says he goes to the woods past the Ferry Lodge to use heroin (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.text:

  • Charm, the teen clerk of the second arc.
  • Billy Thornton, who haunts the motel.

docs.title: Athletes' Village
docs.text:
Non-canon

The Athletes' Village belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Athletes' Village is the walled beachside compound where entrants to the World Martial Arts Tournament are housed and briefed.

Type Location Aliases The briefing tent (its main gathering place) Region Beach, about 400 miles north of the Capital First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Andre describes it as something like an Olympic village, but a lot less nice: a bunch of huts in a big field by the beach, with running water, cots, tiny dorm rooms and very basic supplies. Because tryouts are open, four or five hundred people are staying there, many of them hillfolk who rarely shower. A big tent is put up every year for the mandatory safety briefing; its air conditioning makes a "wow, whoa" noise and cannot cope with the crowd. Entrants are not allowed to leave, and the perimeter has a high wall with guards about every hundred feet, which "is not unbreakable, but it's not quietly breakable." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The briefing tent
docs.text: Mirabeth and Derk walk into the tent among the crowd. Mirabeth hands out business cards, and an elderly weasel-man trainer shields his enormous lizard-man protege from her poaching. Colonel Sparago opens the briefing, quizzes Derk on the two rules (do not kill the audience or the judges) and is interrupted by the news of the doping scandal. Then Ovain panics, blasts Sparago, is deflected by Derk and rockets through the tent roof. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Leaving the village
docs.text: With entrants forbidden to leave, Derk jumps the wall with Mirabeth on his shoulders and lands about a quarter mile away beside Miguel's hot dog taco stand, where he eats 98 hot dogs. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The Capital (DC)
docs.text:
Non-canon

The Capital belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Capital, called DC, is the seat of government of the world of Philosopher's Fist and the setting for most of the one-shot.

Type Location (city) Aliases DC Region About 400 miles south of the Athletes' Village, along the coast First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Andre calls it a relatively nice city. The planet is one country, so this is the capital of the whole world. There are no cell phones, but there are video phones on practically every street corner, with a map application that shows satellite photography of the area. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Getting there
docs.text: After learning of the pre-event social, Derk jumps the distance in about fifteen minutes. Mirabeth speed-walks the shoulder of I-95 in pumps behind her parasol, going over any car in her way, and arrives in a couple of hours. Derk's re-entry roll is an 11, docked to 10, and he lands outside the library beside a wishing-well fountain, where he washes off the bugs. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Notable places
docs.text:
• Public Library: the children's room where Derk draws his flag.
  • Community center: ten blocks from the library, venue of the pre-event social for disadvantaged children (The Flag Contest).
  • Motel 6: $86 for a joint suite, one of the relatively clean ones. The leads stay the night after a spot opens, and the TV news shows Ovain fighting the nation's military at the edge of the capital. Mirabeth, who sleeps with the TV on, comes across it on the way to "this universe's equivalent of Jeopardy!"
  • Presidential Event Hall: site of the fight with Ovain.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text: Across about two days the leads attend the social, sell an oil pyramid scheme, pass security at the event hall and fight Ovain. Afterward Mirabeth endures about eighteen hours of debriefing, and Colonel Sparago lists the damage, including a ruptured gas line and four financial-district blocks of West City evacuated. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Presidential Event Hall
docs.text:
Non-canon

The Presidential Event Hall belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Presidential Event Hall is the stone-walled hall in the Capital where the werewolf president receives the children's flag designs and where Ovain attacks.

Type Location (building) Region The Capital First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The hall has sturdy, heavy stone walls and a banquet table with canapes (some of them little wonton-wrapper lobster rolls that remind Derk of scorpion). Guests are arranged in a ring around the room, with the president going down the line. In the dead center is a roped-off marble area with an elaborate geometric floor pattern, beneath a stained-glass skylight. The skylight is the room's one weak point. The roped-off area is not in use for the event; it holds maintenance signs and tarps and is guarded to prevent anyone cutting through to the president. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Security. At the door a guard sweeps each guest with the detector wand. He waves Derk through after the "metal plate" story and never scans Mirabeth. Derk is offered controlled substances four times in the hour afterward and declines each. The Pure Human Martial Artists have been deputized among the Secret Service. (Philosopher's Fist)

The flag. Derk presents his flag to the werewolf president, who praises it and gives him a presidential-seal sticker. (Philosopher's Fist)

The plan. Mirabeth, assessing the room with Derk's input, works out the skylight weakness. She borrows the guard's wand, tells the guards at the rope that the president wants "inconspicuous" heroes, and stations Derk under the skylight. When one guard asks him to prove he can do kung fu, he bends a quarter. (Philosopher's Fist)

The fight. Ovain crashes through the skylight shouting "You goddamn dog man! You're not taking this room!" Derk slams him down by the tail, bear-hugs him so that a ki jet hits the floor, and both fall into the basement. When Ovain starts charging a building-shaking attack, Derk jumps him out through the skylight into space. All the windows blow out, people are thrown to the ground, alarms go off and the hall is left with a flaming hole in the floor running up through the skylight. (Philosopher's Fist)

Aftermath. Mirabeth raises a Divine Armor force field around herself and the president for about thirty minutes, and the Secret Service moves them to a safe room for several hours. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.text: • Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Public Library
docs.text:
Non-canon

The Public Library belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Public Library is the library in the Capital whose downstairs children's room is where Derk draws his flag.

Type Location (building) Region The Capital First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Mirabeth picks the library from the video phone's satellite map as a place where Derk can draw while she travels. The children's room is downstairs. Butcher paper is unrolled over the floor, and a table holds ham-and-cheese sandwiches, a few PB&Js and a pile of juice boxes. A large wishing-well fountain with coins in the bottom stands outside. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Derk lands outside the library after his jump from the Athletes' Village, cracking the paving stones, and washes in the fountain. A librarian asks him to use his "inside voice," so he answers with his hand over his mouth, and the staff sit him down in the children's room next to a group of toddlers. He eats just under half the snack table and, according to the staff, apparently mistakes a snow globe for a juice box. Over the next hour and a half he draws scorpions, the stars seen from space and a dog on the floor paper, a Superior roll of 6. (Philosopher's Fist)

The staff, who found him unsupervised and unable to explain himself, call child services and Animal Control. When Mirabeth arrives about an hour later, the front desk is empty, the toddlers are crying in a corner and every member of the staff is staring at Derk. She sends Derk off along the emergency exit signs at speed and tears the cape-sized paper off the floor, which becomes Derk's Flag. She walks past Animal Control and out the front door while police sirens approach. Later a detective asks her about the incident and says the Animal Control call ended in a riot, adding that the agency was sick of prank calls. What happened in the riot is never explained. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Wisukonshin
docs.text:
Non-canon

Wisukonshin belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Wisukonshin is this world's version of Wisconsin, where Derk lands lost at the end of the one-shot.

Type Location (region) Aliases Wisconsin Region Far from the Capital First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Andre identifies it as "the world's version of Wisconsin." All Derk can report is trees, roads, a sign he reads as "Forester" or "Farm Mister" (he knows the F, the R and the word "mister" by shape), and a McDonald's. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text: After the fight in the Presidential Event Hall, Derk's aim is off and he re-enters over the ocean, then hops about looking for landmarks. At 2 a.m. he spends his last $2 on a video call to Mirabeth: "Grandpa, I need you to go pick me up. I don't know where I am. And I'm scared." Mirabeth tells him to ask someone in the McDonald's where he is, and he comes back with the answer, Wisukonshin. He looks so sad that the workers give him a package of nuts to tide him over. Mirabeth removes her curlers, puts on makeup and sets out with her umbrella to rescue him. Andre closes with "that is where we leave off this one-shot." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.text: • The name is only spoken aloud in the session, so its spelling here is of uncertain form.

docs.title: PITF office
docs.text:
The PITF office is the Washington, D.C. headquarters of the Paranatural Incident Task Force: a run-down former barbershop on three floors, with a Vietnam-era armory in its steel-walled basement, where Diane keeps the desks running and the team files its reports between cases.

Type Location (headquarters) Aliases The office; task force HQ; headquarters; the barbershop; D.C. barbershop; home base; the basement arsenal Region Washington, D.C., five or six miles south of FBI headquarters, toward the edge of the city Inhabitants Diane, the task force; Big Bill visits First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
When Andrew Howard first arrives on May 24, 1992, the address is a derelict barbershop in a Black neighborhood that has not been used in a couple of years, with water damage and a maze of document boxes. An FBI agent carrying boxes out to a Crown Vic explains that the building used to belong to the Capitol Police, who sold it to the FBI rather than pay to remove the asbestos, and that the FBI had been using it for document storage. A Safeway is down the street (Radford Horror 01).

The building has three floors (Radford Horror 01):

  • Ground floor. The barbershop itself, with barber chairs, washbasins, a little sports radio and a public bathroom.
  • Upstairs. A couple of rooms and a bathroom. A telephone hangs on the wall behind the boxes, next to a desk with a surprisingly nice IBM PC, the first color-screen computer Andrew has seen, and a modem.
  • Basement. A steel door with a keypad lock, built nothing like the rest of the building; see below.

By October 1992 the office has been improved. In Appalachia 01 it has four window air conditioners, a roof that no longer leaks, a front desk downstairs in front of the barber fixtures with a bell to call for Diane, a VHS player and a small CRT television, and a pile of E.T., Alien and Close Encounters tapes and posters sent by people who thought they were funny. Diane buys supplies from what she calls the "petty cash", which is actually drug money, and the alien mascot OJ keeps watch (Appalachia 01). See OJ the stuffed alien.

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The basement arsenal. Behind the keypad door is a steel-walled panic room. Kurt Larson guesses 0-0-0, then fetches luminol and a blacklight, finds which keys glow and cracks the code as 4-5-1. Inside are Vietnam-era arms: M16s, a napalm launcher, a box of hand grenades, a disassembled RPG and landmines. Kurt shakes a landmine to test it and mentions that "Todd used to buy them" (Radford Horror 01). By Radford Horror 08 the lockup holds flamethrowers, machine guns, landmines, claymores and an alien weapon (Radford Horror 08). The basement also has a gas heater, which is unreliable (Roulet Estate 01).
  • The downstairs bathroom. Full of document boxes to the ceiling on the first day. While it is being cleared, a medicine cabinet turns up, taken off the wall and tucked behind the plumbing, holding two half-gallon jars labeled "Ephedrine" and "Mandrax", which Diane calls old "stakeout candy" (Radford Horror 01).
  • The fire lane out front. A 1961 Lincoln Continental covered in parking tickets sits here on the first day and becomes the team's loaner car; see 1961 Lincoln Continental (Radford Horror 01). In Appalachia 01 a nearly new 1991 Ford Explorer is parked in its place (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
On May 24, 1992, at about 7 a.m., Andrew finds the address. Inside he meets Diane, who has big dated hair and is chain-smoking and spinning slowly in one of the barber chairs. She has been told to report here for a task force assignment and cannot tell whether the place is "a barbershop or maybe a slum". Andrew hands her the Lincoln's parking tickets and she goes off to find a phone to call the FBI about them. Andrew hauls boxes and, with the bathroom still full of them, pees in a barber sink while Diane sings "Natural Woman" (Radford Horror 01).

The rest of the team arrives around 9 a.m.; Dick "The Biz" Baxter has been watching the building from across the street for hours. Huell Kendrick tapes a World Trade Center postcard to his spot, and Kurt says the towers "will stand for a thousand years". Kurt opens the basement arsenal. Andrew gives Diane a speech about benevolent aliens guiding humanity, and she resolves to trust "the institution and you personally" (Radford Horror 01).

On June 15, 1992, the air conditioning is broken, it is about 100 degrees inside, and the work order will not bring anyone for days. Kurt gets the unit blowing weakly with a grinding noise. Diane takes some of the drug money from Radford, which she calls "the budget", to buy window units, and installs two that take the edge off the heat but make the lights flicker. The desks and chairs requisitioned after Radford have finally arrived, and the roof leaks, with another work order pending. The seized heroin goes into the trunk of the Biz's car for the Marblehead trip, and Kurt sets up hourly check-ins with Diane before the team leaves (Radford Horror 08). See Marblehead.

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: In Appalachia 01 the team has been treated with more respect since Marblehead, and the rest of the FBI has stopped bullying it. On Monday, October 4, 1992, they watch Close Encounters in the office, Andrew shivering from vaccine side effects. Their own car is being held for radiological contamination, which is why the Explorer is out front. Diane brings up the dossier that sends them to Dahlonega, Georgia (Appalachia 01). See Dahlonega.

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text: In Walkers 01, shortly before the 1992 election and after the team's trip to New York, Andrew is stuck at the office with two reports left, doing the paperwork alone while the others kill time. The Biz recovers from his heart attack and practices magic tricks, Kurt hunts for a holster for his P90, and Huell collects pogs. Diane asks how to deal with "crazy people" who come by, including a woman whose dead mother is haunting her, and the group settles on a tip box; Diane then announces she is off to Wally World for crafts supplies. Chester, a recurring nuisance, is "getting really aggressive", and Huell has used Kurt's shovel on him. That evening Alberta Wilmarth knocks on Andrew's door, not the office's, to ask him to force the Mormon church to exhume her mother. The next morning Big Bill tells Andrew over the phone that it is his task force and the FBI will pay for the plane tickets to Utah (Walkers 01).

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text:
Roulet Estate 01 includes a flashback card reading "Twenty-five days ago", set on Christmas Eve 1992. After fifty-three days of paperwork, Andrew is typing his last report on the Utah disaster on a terrible brand-new computer. Diane has decorated the office, probably with money from the cocaine stash. The evening runs as follows (Roulet Estate 01):

  • The heater. Kurt, avoiding paperwork and acting on dad instinct, goes to fix the banging basement gas heater. Its igniter is unreliable, so gas builds up and pops when it lights.
  • Stolen power and cable. Diane plugs in the Christmas tree, which twinkles for four seconds before the breaker trips and Andrew's report vanishes. Kurt breaks into the neighbors' building to flip their breaker, restores power and notices that the neighbors now have cable, which the team takes too.
  • Holiday plans. Kurt is staying with his family, the Biz is going to Las Vegas, Huell will be home alone until he sees his daughter after New Year's, and Andrew will visit his mother.
  • Carolers. Salvation Army carolers collect at the door; Huell donates what is left of his cigarettes and the Biz a gold nugget from Georgia.
  • Secret Santa. The gifts include a hand-knit sweater from Diane for Andrew, a fake alien fetus in a jar from Kurt for Andrew, a gold Dunhill lighter and cigar cutter from Andrew for Huell, and a floppy disk marked "Mystery Government Files" from the Biz for Kurt.
  • Big Bill's news. Big Bill arrives, eats biscochitos and half a gingerbread man, and tells the team that the President-elect, Ross Perot, believes the task force is a cover for Bush weaponizing the FBI against his political enemies. Perot asked him to resign and will disband and reassign the task force on Inauguration Day. He also hands Andrew a padded envelope with no return address that an FBI courier left for him. Andrew opens it outside in the slush and finds a foil-wrapped letter and a pencil sketch of trees, which open the Roulet case (see Foil-Wrapped Letter).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Dante jokes that the task force's abbreviation is "Pitfa" (Radford Horror 08).
  • Kurt's luminol-and-blacklight trick for the keypad is a rare case of his gear paying off right away (Radford Horror 01).
