docs.title: Radford Arsenal
docs.text:
The Radford Arsenal is the military plant in Radford, Virginia, where Liam Lucky does classified work and which local legend blames for cursing the town.

Type Location (military facility) Aliases The Arsenal; the armory Region Radford, Virginia Employees Liam Lucky First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The Arsenal is never seen. It is mentioned only as the local military facility in a town Andre describes as "offensively quaint": a "Population 16,000" sign, colonial-revival kitsch, train tracks and a river that make it look like a model railroad town (Radford Horror 01). No scene takes place there.

docs.title: Liam Lucky's classified work
docs.text: When Huell Kendrick talks to Liam Lucky apart from his wife, Liam makes a slightly odd mention of his job. Pressed, he says he works for the Arsenal on something classified that he cannot discuss (Radford Horror 01). The team does not link his work to Amanda's disappearance. See Lucky house.

docs.title: The armory curse
docs.text: The clerk at the Pay n' Stay, later named Rutherford, warns the team that people go missing, that there are lights in the sky, and that there are "people walking around this place [who] haven't even been born." He adds that his father believed the town was cursed "because the armory down there made the guncotton for the atom bomb" (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The nature of Liam's classified project, and whether the Arsenal has any real connection to the Radford phenomena, are never resolved. The Arsenal does not come up in The Radford Horrors.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The word "armory" also describes the basement arsenal of the task force's barbershop headquarters, which is Kurt Larson's "armory" from character creation. It is a different thing from the Radford Arsenal (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Radford ER
docs.text:
Radford ER (also called the Radford County emergency room, or simply the hospital) is the small local emergency room in Radford, Virginia where the task force keeps ending up, treated for burns, bedbugs, broken bones, bullet wounds and rabies exposure.

Type Location (hospital) Aliases Radford County ER; Radford County emergency room; Radford local hospital; the hospital Region Radford, Virginia First appearance Radford Horror 03 (arrival only) Other appearances Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 08, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The ER is described as small and quiet, a place of drug seekers and one man who shot his own foot (Radford Horror 04). It has a waiting room, a side room that can be crammed with extra beds, and a hallway pay phone (Radford Horrors 03). It is not equipped for everything: in 1993 it has no way to run a DFA test for rabies, so samples and patients go to Roanoke, which also supplies the HDCV vaccine (Radford Horrors 03).

The staff are never named. The recurring ER doctor is a tired, exasperated man who comes to know the team on sight. On the first visit, a nurse tells the burned Kurt to sit down while she fetches the doctor (Radford Horror 04).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 03. The episode ends with the team pulling into the ER parking lot with a seriously burned Kurt in the back seat, after the encounter with Agent Murphy (Radford Horror 03).
  • Radford Horror 04. About 11 p.m., Kurt is wheeled back and debrided, cleaned and bandaged, taking him back to 0 harm and running up roughly $8,000 in bills. Andrew Howard, who healed Kurt for the first time ever, arrives with a nosebleed and a "spiritual high," and a doctor brings him gauze and an ice pack and mentions that Kurt also needs a dentist. In the waiting room the Biz briefs Andrew and Huell on the hit-and-run and the flashlight weapon (Radford Horror 04).
  • Bedbugs. After a night at the Pay n' Stay, Huell's bedbug bites become obvious and he gets hydrocortisone at the hospital; his clothes are steam-sterilized and he wears scrubs, then borrowed clothes (Radford Horror 05).
  • Radford Horror 06. Later the same day, Huell comes back with a broken right arm (ulna) after the Whateley house fight. The same doctor from the bedbug visit treats him: "Twice in a day, you are not having a good life, my friend." Huell is healed to full, though his right arm stays cumbersome (-1 to shooting and arm-strength rolls). The doctor jokes about frequent flyer miles and radiation allergies (Radford Horror 06).
  • Radford Horror 08. After the burning church, the team wakes in the Radford County ER, four beds shoved into a side room. Diane has driven out; Andrew needed about three people's worth of blood. The doctor lectures them that he has seen them four times in three days and agrees with Huell's remark that the Pay n' Stay is a poor life choice, reports that the Biz had severe burns, three to four pounds of thigh tissue missing and badly impacted bowels, and offers to say they are still unconscious if they need time before the sheriff and deputy question them. Andre estimates a stay of about a week, during which the doctor brings the Biz kale salad, and the team plans a cover story, gets medical records, watches baseball and calls home (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
• Radford Horrors 02. After the motel attack by the rabid mouse, the team goes to the ER at the end of the session. The doctor greets them with "Not again. Not you guys." and orders rabies shots for everyone: a series of four stomach injections over two weeks, at $3,000 a head. Dante's Kurt complains that it is "not coming out of my coke budget" (Radford Horrors 02).
  • Radford Horrors 03. Andrew wakes from a dream of his "dad" (see Andrew's alien dad) in the ER. The team shares one patient room. The doctor takes the rat, still on Kurt's harpoon in a plastic bag, for testing in Roanoke; rabies immunoglobulin starts at once, by IV for most of the team and by about 20 shots around Webster's swollen nipple. Webster is paged to the hallway pay phone, where FBI Director Rudy Giuliani asks about the fence incident (see Bivens lawsuit). Andrew reacts badly to the treatment and worries he is a "rabies construct" (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• The unnamed ER doctor, who gradually goes from clinical to resigned.
  • Patients on visits: the task force, in rotating combinations of Kurt Larson, Huell Kendrick, Dick Baxter, Andrew Howard and, in 1993, Daniel Webster.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The doctor's "four times in three days" scolding is one of the campaign's recurring hospital gags (Radford Horror 08).
  • Andre's audio briefly cut out during the hospital scene in Radford Horrors 03; this was a recording glitch, not part of the story (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: Radford pharmacy
docs.text:
The Radford pharmacy is the town drugstore in Radford, Virginia where the team learns that a Vicodin record under Dr. Lawrence Lori's name has been entered for Amanda Lucky, and that the paper original is missing.

Type Location (shop) Aliases the pharmacy; the town pharmacy Region Radford, Virginia First appearance Radford Horror 02 Inhabitants An unnamed pharmacist, his boss, teenage stock staff

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The pharmacy is a town drugstore with a counter, a computer, a records cabinet in back, security cameras whose footage is kept for a month, and a payphone outside, with a line of customers usually waiting (Radford Horror 02). The chain or brand is never given; Ezra jokes that it is a Walgreens or a grocery-store pharmacy.

docs.title: The visit (Radford Horror 02)
docs.text:
After Dr. Lori tells the team he prescribed Amanda only Xanax, denies ever prescribing Vicodin, and suggests forgery or a pharmacy error, the team visits the pharmacy (Radford Horror 02).

  • The pharmacist confirms the computer holds a record of Vicodin for Amanda under Dr. Lori. It was entered about a year earlier, was filled regularly, and began about four months after the Xanax.
  • Anyone with the password can alter records. Prescriptions are phoned in, written in a paper log, and then entered into the computer.
  • The pharmacist says he would never let Dean Lawson near the store. He says Matt McCready works at his parents' place, and rules out the Whateley boys and the Nichols girl as well. The Vicodin prescriptions he fills, apparently all from Lori, mostly go to 17- and 18-year-olds, a year or two older than the teenagers the team has been asking about.
  • Huell asks, "Supposing I wanted to fraudulently fill a prescription, how might I go about doing that?"
  • After checking with his boss, the pharmacist goes to look for the paper original, returns, and says he cannot talk. Kurt (Manipulate Someone, 10) gets him to confide off the record that the paper record is missing, "a big problem." Kurt gives him the number of the team's hotel and asks him to keep them posted.

Afterward the team lists the pharmacy's security tapes as a follow-up (Radford Horror 02). See also Amanda's prescriptions.

docs.title: Later developments
docs.text: In Radford Horror 05 a member of the sheriff's department tells the team that Derek Augustine, the father of Phoebe Augustine, is "one of the pharmacists" and a published romance novelist. Kurt makes him his prime suspect for the stolen paperwork. Augustine says he filled Lori's prescription for Amanda a couple of times, assuming it was for something like a wisdom tooth, and claims to know nothing beyond the "record error" the pharmacy is looking into. He adds that Dr. Lori came to see him the day before, upset about a prescription he had not written (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The pharmacy has more than one pharmacist. The episodes never establish whether the man at the counter in Radford Horror 02, who is not named, is Augustine or a colleague.
  • Huell's line "Supposing I wanted to fraudulently fill a prescription, how might I go about doing that?" prompts the pharmacist to ask whether he needs his lawyer (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Radford, Virginia
docs.text:
Radford, Virginia is a quaint small town of about 16,000 in the woods of southwest Virginia, a paranatural hotspot and the setting of both Radford arcs: The Radford Horror (1992) and The Radford Horrors (1993).

Type Town Aliases Radford Region Southwest Virginia, near Roanoke and Salem, bordering Jefferson National Forest Population About 16,000 (including the surrounding area) First appearance Radford Horror 01 Arcs The Radford Horror; The Radford Horrors

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
On their first trip from Washington, D.C., after a four-hour, sixteen-minute drive, the team passes signs for Roanoke and Salem, then pulls off for Radford, where a sign reads "Population 16,000." Andre describes the town as "almost offensively quaint": colonial revival kitsch, train tracks and a river, and an old main street with Old West facades (Radford Horror 01). A local credits the town's unexpectedly educated population to the university and its college. The sheriff explains that the 16,000 includes the surrounding metro area (Radford Horror 02). The town borders a national forest, and the woods are a recurring focus of the story.

Roanoke is the nearest city. Its airport, about 45 minutes from Radford, is where the light aircraft that sometimes wake the town at night are flown from (Radford Horror 02; Radford Horror 07), and in 1993 its hospitals do the testing and psychiatric care that Radford cannot (Radford Horrors 03; Radford Horrors 04). The sheriff's department fields a fair number of "quack" call-ins about UFOs, and the town sells "Radford, Virginia, UFO USA" flying-saucer T-shirts at its thrift store (Radford Horror 05). Much of the land around Radford is privately owned and had long been open to hikers and hunters, until in 1993 a company, the Safe Environment Fund, bought up large tracts, fenced them and began bringing in construction equipment (Radford Horrors 02).

The first case file ranks Radford as a hotspot on the Atolean Paranatural Index (Radford Horror 01).

The Pay n' Stay clerk in the first arc warns that the town has missing people, lights in the sky, and "people walking around who haven't even been born," and says his father believed the town was cursed because the local armory made the guncotton for the atom bomb (Radford Horror 01; see Radford Arsenal).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Lodging: Ferry Lodge and the Pay n' Stay face each other across the street; the team later moves into the lodge in 1992 and, in 1993, finds the lodge upgraded.
  • Eating: Lonely Mountain Diner, where Sheila waits tables; Arby's; a McDonald's; Quest Coffee, a rival coffee shop; and later a Blockbuster Video where clerk Harold works.
  • Law and medicine: the Radford Sheriff's Department with its small morgue, the Radford ER, Dr. Lori's office, the Radford pharmacy, and a family-medicine clinic run by Dr. Harvey Mauden.
  • Homes: the Lucky house, the Whateley house, the Augustine house and barn, and the Lawson cabin in Stately Acres.
  • The woods: Jefferson National Forest, the Alpine Lodge water tower, the mountain road site, the highway crime scene and the old-town church.
  • 1993 additions: the Douglas Pinball Emporium, the Safe Environment Fund fenced site and the Sportsman RV Campground.

docs.title: The Radford Horror (1992)
docs.text:
The task force arrives on a case file reporting that 17-year-old Amanda Lucky vanished from a locked third-story bedroom and that an insomniac four-year-old saw a spaceman. A neighbor, Mrs. Whateley, had also walked off into the night (Radford Horror 01). Local dogs are disappearing, a man watches from the post office roof, and the team learns that the Whateley family's son Abe had once robbed a store in a homemade spacesuit (Radford Horror 02; see Radford Moth and Radford's missing dogs).

Over the next episodes Kurt is badly burned in an encounter with Agent Murphy on a mountain road (Radford Horror 03), Amanda's crucified body is found beside the highway (Radford Horror 05), and the team raids the Whateley house cellar (Radford Horror 06). The finale takes place in an abandoned church in the woods, where the team fights the car-sized blue moth creature and rescues Phoebe Augustine and Wilbur Whateley; the church burns, and the team is rescued by Deputy Molly Underhill (Radford Horror 07; Radford Horror 08). The police close the case with Dr. Lori and Derek Augustine imprisoned for abusing Amanda, Wilbur suspected as a serial killer, and a cartel link guessed from the heroin; the team lets the story stand (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The Radford Horrors (1993)
docs.text:
By early 1993 more people have gone missing in Radford, and a separate FBI task force sent to look has vanished. The team returns in April 1993, about a year after the first case, with new boss Daniel Webster, but without the Biz, who is held in Russia (Radford Horrors 02). Molly Underhill is now sheriff. The Ferry Lodge has been upgraded and is raided by IRS agents; the Pay n' Stay has a new teenage clerk; the Safe Environment Fund has fenced the woods; and a gray van crew is cleaning up after something at the Pinball Emporium (Radford Horrors 02; Radford Horrors 03; Radford Horrors 04). The team wakes Wilbur Whateley at a Roanoke mental hospital and camps beside the missing agents' tents (Radford Horrors 04).

The Radford Horrors 01 opens with a cold open of FBI agents chased through snowy woods by a flying thing, then moves to Moscow and Washington before turning toward Radford (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Sheriff Frank Roosevelt, Molly Underhill, the Whateley family (Abelforth, Wilbur, Yobiah and Irene), Dr. Lawrence Lori, the Augustines (Derek, Maybelline and Phoebe), Dean Lawson, Matt McCready, Douglas Douglas, Charm, and Billy Thornton. More are listed on Minor characters: Radford.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The first arc is set in spring 1992 (the task force first assembles on May 24, 1992); the return arc begins in early April 1993 (Radford Horror 01; Radford Horrors 01).
  • Dante, cutting off a table discussion about where to find a clue, dismisses the town with "They don't have shit in Radford" (Radford Horror 05).

docs.text:

docs.title: Ram and Arms Inn
docs.text:
The Ram and Arms Inn is a decrepit old hotel, in practice a bed-and-breakfast, on Gregory Street in Marblehead, Massachusetts, where the task force lodges throughout The Summer Service.

Type Location Aliases the hotel; the motel; B&B Region Marblehead, Massachusetts Inhabitants Jester (front desk); an ancient innkeeper First appearance Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The inn is a plain but clean old hotel with a view of the old military fort, a ram's-head coat of arms over the door and a narrow wooden staircase. The rooms are small, little more than a twin bed and a chair, with a nice window view (Radford Horror 08). They have no phones or televisions, only a phone at the end of the hall. The inn stands on Gregory Street, close to the beach, and guests are served a fish breakfast at 6 a.m. (Summer Service 01). The building has two stories, good water pressure, a hallway bathroom whose window opens onto an alley, and a small washing machine downstairs (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05). Every guest is offered a Bible, including the Sons of Adam Bible (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
• Check-in. At the end of Radford Horror 08 the team arrives and an ancient innkeeper offers four single rooms and the 6 a.m. hot fish breakfast. He says business has been quiet "except for those fellas from the government" about a week earlier, and he is keeping their belongings in a box in the back. This is the EPA/USGS survey team. The innkeeper carries the box up to the team's rooms (Radford Horror 08). See Ram and Arms innkeeper.
  • Summer Service 01. The team goes through the previous team's belongings and Andrew speed-reads the Bible. Kurt makes calls from the hallway phone once a teenage girl has finished with it. At the desk the Biz finds Jester's bag of crystal marbles. When Huell asks for a toothbrush, Jester tells him the inn is "a bed-and-breakfast. Not a bed-and-toothbrush." The day ends with Jester frantically rooting around his desk (Summer Service 01).
  • Summer Service 03. After the dive, Kurt sleeps badly in feverish chills. Jester looks haunted and gives Huell an appraising nod. When McManley says he hears the hotel serves a fish breakfast, Andrew warns, "Don't eat the fish here. The water is tainted" (Summer Service 03).
  • Summer Service 04. Jester, who is also a selectman, tells the team, "You better not be planning to leave whatever that is in the room." The roughly 60 lb W54 warhead of the Davy Crockett is wrapped in Kurt's poncho and stored in his room (Summer Service 04).
  • Summer Service 05, the siege. During the tropical storm, McManley takes a room because his RV has run out of hot water. Jester is not at the desk; McManley says he took a call in the back and practically ran out the door. In the middle of the night Andrew feels a voice at his ear telling him to get his gun. Church members gather outside in the rain and a police car pulls up. Andrew kicks in a guest's door to scout the back, then drops a toilet tank lid onto a watcher below the bathroom window and lands on him. The team passes the Davy Crockett down through that window and sneaks past the remaining watchers to the RV (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Jester works the front desk and is a member of the Sons of Adam.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 08 is the only episode in which the inn is named. In The Summer Service it is "the hotel", "the motel" or a bed-and-breakfast.
  • The innkeeper of Radford Horror 08 is a very old man with a "Crypt Keeper" haircut, and Summer Service 01 introduces Jester as the man with the Crypt Keeper haircut who "now" wears a name tag. The episodes strongly imply that they are the same man, but never state it outright.

docs.title: Roanoke mental hospital
docs.text:
The Roanoke mental hospital is the psychiatric facility in Roanoke, Virginia, where Wilbur Whateley is held, catatonic, after the events of The Radford Horror, and where Andrew Howard wakes him in The Radford Horrors.

Type Location (psychiatric hospital) Aliases the Roanoke hospital; mental hospital in Roanoke Region Roanoke, Virginia, most of a day's drive from Radford, Virginia Notable inhabitant Wilbur Whateley First appearance Mentioned in Radford Horrors 02; visited in Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The hospital appears in one scene. The woman at the front desk tells the team the hospital closes in an hour, and warns that Wilbur is catatonic and that visitors must observe a "no touching" rule. Wilbur sits in a wheelchair staring out a window, in a room decorated with his bugs, with a Jeopardy! marathon on the TV (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Before the visit
docs.text: At the end of the first Radford case the police theory makes Wilbur a serial killer who impersonated his brother's departure (see Radford Horror 08); he is catatonic after the church fire. In Radford Horrors 02, the sheriff tells the team that Wilbur is in custody at a mental hospital in Roanoke, "back to it," either catatonic or pretending to be (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The visit (Radford Horrors 04)
docs.text:
The team spends most of a day driving to Roanoke, eating at a Taco Bell by the airport, and reaches the hospital with an hour before closing (Radford Horrors 04).

  • Kurt tries to talk to Wilbur (Manipulate Someone with -2 forward, 9) and gets only a flicker in his eye. He then holds a sample of the moth's pearlescent goo (see Pearlescent goo) under Wilbur's nose; Wilbur's muscles stiffen, his eyes go waxy, and his fingers grip the wheelchair handles.
  • Andrew uses his Use Magic move (Weird +3, a 13) and chooses to "heal one harm." He lays a hand on Wilbur's shoulder despite the "no touching" rule and senses that Wilbur is not currently controlled but has a badly damaged mind from years of being "ridden shotgun" and of faking catatonia. The "crooked mental knots" loosen and Wilbur wakes, asking, "Where's my brother?"
  • Wilbur recognizes the team "from the church." He says he dreamed of "drowning in blue," that something was "wearing" him, that there was a fire, and that he found an oversized Morpho menelaus caterpillar in the woods that did not belong in Virginia and may have killed the dog.
  • Pressed further, Wilbur panics and says it was "like the ocean" and "like a mother," that it was "in the basement," that "it was pregnant. It needed to breathe," and that "it needed hosts, like a parasitic wasp. Those women—" As the nurse escorts the team out, he adds, "I found it under a white oak."

The nurse is stunned that Wilbur woke at all. On the drive back, Webster asks whether they have just tortured a mental patient; Kurt answers that they may have woken a man from a years-long catatonia (Radford Horrors 04). At the table, Dante remarked that "faith healing Wilbur Whateley was not on my bingo card."

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• Wilbur Whateley, patient.
  • An unnamed front-desk nurse.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: • The episodes do not explain what the "white oak" and "the basement" refer to, or whether Wilbur's recovery lasts (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Andre says Wilbur had been "ridden shotgun" and pretending to be catatonic for "like five years," although the first arc is set only about a year earlier (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horrors 02 (mentioned)
  • Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Room 111
docs.text:
Room 111 is the Smith Hotel room next to the team's, staged with wine and chocolates, where the Biz secretly planted a spy camera and microphone on instructions from a coded message.

Type Location Region Smith Hotel, Dahlonega, Georgia First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The room has a bed made up, a TV with a VCR underneath, a bedside drawer holding a Gideon Bible, a big box of condoms and lubricant, and a ventilation duct over the bed. A delivered basket holding two big bottles of wine and a box of chocolates was waiting on the table (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The assignment. In Appalachia 01 the Biz called a sweepstakes line that he had recognized as a KGB front. The coded message sent him to the Smith Hotel in Dahlonega, Georgia, to install a hidden camera in room 111 before midnight, retrieve it 24 hours later and mail the undeveloped film to an address to be supplied the following day. He did not tell the rest of the team. See Spy Camera and Microphone and KGB. The team's own rooms (109 and 110) were next door.

The plant. In Appalachia 02 the hotel's front-desk clerk reported room 111 to the Biz as suspicious. It was booked under one name and paid for with a card in another name, and the man who booked it, armed, rude, short-haired, military-looking and Midwestern-sounding, offered the clerk $100 to keep quiet. The clerk lent the Biz the master key. Inside, the Biz tucked the motion-sensing film camera in among the cables beside the VCR, facing the bed, and stuck the microphone to the underside of the bedside drawer. He rolled a 10 on Act Under Pressure to leave no fingerprints. He concluded it was a setup, though not for him, and that it "might involve kids." (Appalachia 02)

The neighbors. In Appalachia 03, Andrew came back to the hotel, hurt, and a curly-haired blonde woman in a bathrobe outside the room next door asked, "Are you okay, honey?" A suited man with a military haircut steered her inside and glared at him. The clerk told the team that the room's guests had booked under a different name than the occupant's, that several scary-looking men were involved, and that one had offered him money. Later Huell glimpsed a laughing man in a big cowboy hat and dark sunglasses entering the room, looking oddly familiar for a split second (Appalachia 03). See Next-door Hotel Guests.

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes never say who the room 111 party was targeting, and the retrieval of the camera and the mailing of the film are never shown. Separately, a scandal over FBI agents allegedly spying on Bill Clinton broke while the team was in town; it is never established whether it is connected to this room. See Clinton Surveillance Scandal.

docs.title: Roosevelt police station
docs.text:
The Roosevelt police station is the headquarters of the Roosevelt Police Department in Roosevelt, Utah: first the place where the wrecked rental car is kept and Yusuf Ansari is pressured into a false confession, and later the site of a massacre, a hideout for the task force, and the morgue of salted bodies where the real Andrew Howard wakes.

Type Location (police station) Aliases Police station; Roosevelt morgue; station garage Region Roosevelt, Utah Status Massacre site and refuge (as of Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 05

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A full police station, larger than anything in Ballard. It has a front lobby with a glass door, cells, an armory, a morgue, a break room, a conference room, a basement with a generator, and a parking lot behind a gate (Walkers 08). The garage holds the wreck. The interrogation room doubles as the lunchroom, with a handcuff bar on the table, and smells of ham (Walkers 06).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The wreck. In Walkers 05 the team finds the pancaked rental (Plymouth Voyager) tucked into the garage. A young officer tells them the police have dusted it and found prints only on the inside, and that a manhunt is on because "there's only so many places that can crush a car". Kurt tests it with loose screws and finds it magnetic. The officer eventually names a local junkyard owner with a car crusher and a magnetic crane, and says the police will bring him in and "really sweat him".

Yusuf's interrogation. In Walkers 06 the junkyard owner, Yusuf Ansari, has already confessed. In the lunchroom, a hungover officer, Carl, eats Lucky Charms from a paper coffee cup and microwaves ham, and the only word anyone offers about it is "Ham." Yusuf says his crusher does not even flatten cars that thin. He confessed because the police threatened immigration trouble and offered a deal: confess, pay a fine of $10,000, and there would be no immigration problems. Kurt records the interview. Huell's pager goes off while the others talk, and Kurt phones Diane from here to check Yusuf's alibi.

The massacre. After the night of the gym, the team returns to a station with the cut chain hanging from the lot gate and the glass door locked. Inside, every officer is shot dead, each missing a small body part (a finger, toe or ear), and there are no keys. Yusuf is found alive in the cells, patched up with a shoulder wound and a missing little toe. He says, "A bunch of naked guys with shotguns just came in and started murdering everybody", that he played dead through a machine-gun burst, and that they cut a piece off of everybody, "whatever they could reach through the bars". The armory is stripped, and the morgue holds dozens of decaying bodies in plastic and rock salt (Walkers 08). See Plastic-wrapped bodies.

Fight and autopsy. Men in gray maintenance uniforms look at the team's cars in the parking lot and demand the substation keys that the station holds; a firefight follows, one man dies and others are captured. In the conference room McManley autopsies the dead man: no stomach, about eight feet of malformed intestine, and a non-human brain-like organ. He tells the team, "This is not a person. This is a vehicle. Somebody made this. And whatever you killed inside of it was its pilot." The living prisoners' pilots later flee into the drop ceiling (Walkers 08). See Pilot organ and Pilot and host biology. The basement generator has been sabotaged.

The real Andrew wakes. At the end of Walkers 08, after the other players have logged off, Andre runs a last scene for Rita alone: "So let's cut to the other Andrew Howard." Andrew is dead, then spasms back to life, naked and wrapped in plastic at the bottom of the morgue pile, as the Monstrous. The Andrew who has been with the team since the gym is the duplicate. In Walkers 09 the real Andrew shouts that he was shot in the chest and woke up under a pile of dead naked people.

Refuge. The recap that opens Walkers 09 says the team breached and cleared the station with the National Guard, from an unrecorded session (see Lost episodes). McManley, his interns and some Guardsmen wait in the station, awake because they stayed indoors, and are picked up at the end (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The Roosevelt police (massacred), Yusuf Ansari, McManley and his interns, and, in the morgue, the salted bodies and the real Andrew.

docs.title: Roosevelt, Utah
docs.text:
Roosevelt, Utah is the neighbouring town of about 6,000 people where the task force's vanished rental car reappears, and which later falls dark, carless and mid-replacement before the farmhouse from Sherman Ranch is launched toward it.

Type Location (town) Aliases Roosevelt Region Utah, a couple of miles from Ballard, Utah Status Dark, carless and being replaced (as of Walkers 08) First appearance Walkers 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Roosevelt sits right next to Ballard, a couple of miles away, and has about six thousand people. It has a police department, a diner, a grocery store, a dentist, a hospital with an emergency room, a repair shop and a theater-loving drama teacher (Walkers 04, Walkers 05). Tow trucks have to come from Duchesne.

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• East Lagoon Street. Where the Voyager is found pancaked and fused into the road (Walkers 04).
  • Good Hills Diner. A busy diner where the team eats French toast while waiting for the police (Walkers 04).
  • Roosevelt police station.
  • Stewart's. A small grocery with its own egg-based ice cream, where an elderly clerk thanks them for not patronizing the Dollar Tree "interloper" (Walkers 05).
  • The dentist. A spare-room practice where the Biz has his lost fillings replaced with gold, the only material on hand that is non-magnetic (Walkers 05).
  • The hospital. A small hospital with a generator for a ventilator patient; its ambulance and radio have been stolen (Walkers 08). The naked intruder dies on a heart-lung machine in its emergency room (Walkers 07).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The car. The rental Plymouth Voyager reappears on East Lagoon Street, backing up morning traffic. A call to Hertz leads the team there, and Officer Hernandez of the Roosevelt Police Department arranges for them to borrow Betsy. The wreck is peeled off the asphalt with some of it left behind (Walkers 04). The later "heat-and-magnet beam" is found to launch objects along a line pointing toward Roosevelt, suggesting the same force is behind both (Walkers 06, Walkers 07).

The confession. The police pressure junkyard owner Yusuf Ansari into a false confession (Walkers 05, Walkers 06).

Mid-replacement. On the morning after the gym fire, Roosevelt has traffic lights out, no cars anywhere and confused people on foot. A resident says the power went out, his car was stolen, and nobody answers at the police station. Mechanics report that every drivable car was stolen and the rest sabotaged by hand. The police are dead, and the team concludes the town is being replaced person by person, starting with the police (Walkers 08). See Skinwalker faction.

The launched farmhouse. In Walkers 09 the ranch farmhouse leaves in a vapor trail, launched in the direction of Roosevelt, and Andre notes that the team is not between it and the town. Most of Roosevelt's cars are piled up inside the community center's fence.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The Roosevelt police, Officer Hernandez, the dentist, the junkyard owner Yusuf, and ordinary residents who are being replaced. After the finale the fate of the town is not shown.

  • Walkers 05
  • Walkers 06
  • Walkers 07

  • Walkers 09

docs.title: Roulet Basement
docs.text:
The Roulet Basement is the dirt-floored cellar of the Roulet house, where the agents dig up parts of two bodies from a chemical-soaked trash pit.

Type Location (cellar) Aliases Trash pit; dirt cellar Region Inside the Roulet House, Exeter, Rhode Island First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The cellar is unfinished, with a dirt floor, a water heater in one corner and amateur electrical wiring running everywhere, which Andre says was not the work of an electrician. A pile of broken appliances is shoved into one corner, and trash has been buried in another. There are buckets of cleansers and a big jug of Dawn dish soap, a bleach spray bottle, Abraxas scrubbing powder and a huge glass jar of cocoa-butter lotion with a hand-shaped scoop taken out of it. A tool area holds a pair of chain cutters. The power and water are cut off at the street, probably for non-payment after the owners went missing. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
In Roulet Estate 01, Kurt checks the cellar and tries the breakers, finding that the power is off at the street. (Roulet Estate 01)

In Roulet Estate 02, Kurt goes down for tools and investigates the trash pile. He concludes that something was poured on the buried trash, perhaps to sterilize it, and that under the chemical smell there is rot. Digging with a crowbar, he is grabbed by veiny hands bursting from the dirt, sees the face of a Vietnamese prison guard and empties his sidearm into the hole. He comes to curled in a fetal position beside the pit, saying he was "back in Saigon." The hand he shot turns out to be real: a withered human hand in a sleeve, shot several times. Kurt: "In my defense, I thought it was the VC." Zack (as Huell): "Probable cause. That's probable cause." (Roulet Estate 02)

Andrew matches the ring on the hand to the wedding photos, identifying Margaret Roulet. Further digging turns up parts of two bodies, too decayed to show a cause of death (the agents would need McManley), with their cloth bleached and dissolved by something caustic, apparently poured in to control the smell. The agents assume the second body is Mr. Roulet. The agents later conclude that Kurt's hallucination, and Andrew's in the chimney, came from the house's drugged water. The local police confirm that there are two corpses. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Roulet Estate 01
  • Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: The Roulet House
docs.text:
The Roulet House is an isolated, abandoned Victorian-style house at 118 Benefit Street in Exeter, Rhode Island, where the task force wakes up hungover on Inauguration Day, 1993, and uncovers a double murder, a hidden intruder and a water supply that gives them hallucinations.

Type Location Aliases 118 Benefit Street; Roulet estate; the Rhode Island house; mailbox 118; the murder house Region Exeter, Rhode Island Owners Margaret Roulet and Mr. Roulet First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The house is old, brick-heavy and poorly insulated, cold enough that the agents can see their breath indoors. Several of its rooms have fireplaces, and a search turns up no way into the attic. One window stands open with birds' nests in it. There is no power (Kurt concludes it is cut off at the street) and the taps are dry. A barn stands in the yard, and a driveway of about fifty feet winds around some trees to a forest road. A river runs through the woods. Andre puts the nearest significant town about two hours away on foot along a winding dirt road, or about an hour of hiking as the crow flies, and Pawtucket an hour and twenty-one minutes away (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02).

The mailbox at the road reads 118. The owners' name is not spoken in Roulet Estate 01. In Roulet Estate 02, Andre recaps that the letter that brought the team came from a Keely Network contact whose friend Margaret Roulet had vanished after reporting "visitations" (Roulet Estate 02). The name is spelled both "Roulet" and "Roulette" in the episode.

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Living room. A television, a huge rack of VHS tapes and the combination-locked steel door of the weapons closet (Roulet Estate 01).
  • Library. Shelves of books on aliens, some Scientology literature, and a partly coded handwritten notebook logging Grey sightings, lights over the house, lost time and feelings of being watched, ending in the fall of 1992. Andrew judges that the owners were a husband and wife who both believed in aliens, the wife more devoutly (Roulet Estate 01).
  • Bedroom. Open suitcases and a safe that Kurt cracks, finding only the wedding photos. The bedroom doors have locks fitted on the inside (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02).
  • Kitchen, larder and a disused guest room (Roulet Estate 01).
  • Roulet Basement. A dirt-floored cellar with a water heater, amateur wiring, a pile of broken appliances and a trash pit in which two bodies are buried (Roulet Estate 02).
  • Barn. Locked with a bike lock, which the agents cut. It holds a riding lawnmower (the exact model Kurt owns at home), gardening supplies and a huge pile of crushed plastic water bottles (Roulet Estate 02).
  • Hidden Attic Lair. Reached only through the secretly modified chimneys (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Roulet Estate 01. The four agents wake on Inauguration Day, 1993, scattered through the dusty living room, with no memory of the night before. They find Diane asleep under a blanket in the back seat of their car, and a bald monk camped out in front with a frying pan of Spam. Kurt and the Biz glimpse a grey-faced figure peeking over the roof. Later a naked, spindly sniper in the woods shoots at the agents with a VSS rifle, hitting Huell in the shin and Andrew in the face; Andrew shrugs the shot off. The car's battery is missing and its phone is dead. Kurt hammers on the floor beside the steel door for about forty-five minutes and loses a minute of time, while Andrew glimpses a low streak of brilliant light through the trees. Andrew squeezes under the door and finds the weapons closet stripped bare (Roulet Estate 01).

Roulet Estate 02. Searching the basement for cutters, Kurt hallucinates veiny hands and a Vietnamese prison guard and empties his gun into the hole. What he shot is a withered human hand in a sleeve, wearing a ring that matches the one in the wedding photos. Further digging turns up parts of two bodies, too deteriorated to show a cause of death, with signs that something caustic was poured into the pit. A grey figure drives off in the agents' car. After a trip to the clown mansion to use a phone, Kurt lights a fire that fills the room with smoke and reveals notches inside the chimney, leading him and Andrew into the attic lair. A local officer confirms "that's two corpses", and a taxi takes the monk away to Pawtucket (Roulet Estate 02).

Roulet Estate 03. The agents are still at the house, still somewhat hungover and woozy from the water, when a young officer reports that their stolen car has been seen at a Brooks pharmacy in a town about 25 miles away. The siege there ends the mystery of the "alien", who proves to be a man in a mask, linked to the lair by beta blockers (Roulet Estate 03). The episodes never explain who killed the Roulets or when.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• Margaret Roulet, identified by her ring as one of the bodies in the basement.
  • Mr. Roulet, presumably the second body, though the episodes never confirm it. Andre describes "the gentleman of the house" as a firearms collector.
  • The Roulet Intruder, who lived in the attic for at least a year.

docs.title: Safe Environment Fund fenced site
docs.text:
The Safe Environment Fund fenced site (also called the fenced polygon or the "scribble site") is a barbed-wire enclosure in the woods near Radford, Virginia, owned by the Safe Environment Fund, where the missing FBI agents were last headed and where the team's trespass leads to the "fence incident."

Type Location (fenced land) Aliases fenced polygon; the scribble site; Safe Environment Fund fence Region Woods near Radford, reached from the area of the Sportsman RV Campground Owner Safe Environment Fund First appearance Radford Horrors 02 (cold open) Other appearances Radford Horrors 03 (aftermath)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The site is one of the irregular polygons on the missing agents' map, found in the missing agents' camp, which also shows an illegible scribble beside one boundary. A quarter mile short of the scribble the team meets an eight-foot chain-link fence topped with barbed wire and wrapped in polymer privacy sheeting printed "Safe Environment Fund / No trespassers," with dim red "solar lights" in the trees. Followed to the left, the new fence joins an older fence matching a polygon on the map. The team reasons that the new fence went up after the agents vanished, so the agents probably went straight to the scribble (Radford Horrors 02).

The "solar lights" are motion-triggered alarms that whoop when tripped. Elsewhere inside the polygon are locked shipping containers and a locked temporary building (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The scribble: the spot where a tree had been cut down and removed that very day, with bleached ground, dug-up patches and heavy foot traffic (Radford Horrors 02).
  • Containers and temporary building: locked; the team does not break in (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
• Cold open. Before the credits, figures in blue gloves and bunny suits comb the woods in a grid while a helicopter circles; a worker hands a blood-streaked handgun to a suited supervisor, who bags it. The camera crosses the barbed-wire fence to reveal the Safe Environment Fund logo (Radford Horrors 02).
  • The fence incident. At dusk the team hikes in. Andrew Howard tears the barbed wire apart bare-handed and the alarm sounds. Kurt gets over with difficulty, Huell is helped over and jolts his injured foot, and Webster fails and hangs from the wire until Andrew pulls him down. Armed security guards arrive on ATVs. Webster screams "FBI!" and levels his shotgun; a guard tasers him and his shotgun fires wide. Kurt fires a P90 burst into the air and the guards retreat. Andrew shoots a guard through the leg, and the guard shoots Andrew in the chest; the bullet stops about an inch from him. A voice on the guard's radio demands the team leave and says "lawyers and emergency response" are coming (Radford Horrors 02).
  • The scene. Lawyers follow and film the team to the scribble, repeatedly asking for a warrant. Kurt finds a professional cleanup: the smell of bleach, dug patches, a removed tree, and luminol that shows nothing, not even wildlife blood. On a high branch he scrapes a glob of pearlescent, oil-sheened goo that smells like the moth's compost-and-rot odor; Webster tastes it (bitter, then a sweet aftertaste) and Andrew whispers "Caterpillar slurry." The team is escorted out and the gate is locked behind them (Radford Horrors 02). See Pearlescent goo.
  • Fallout. FBI Director Rudy Giuliani calls Webster about "the thing with the fence." A Bivens lawsuit is expected, a retroactive warrant is being sought, and a formal reprimand is possible. The guard who tased Webster has already been fired (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Andrew was shot in the chest, and the bullet stopped about an inch from him. Dante's casual recap at the start of Radford Horrors 04 has him shot "in the face" (Radford Horrors 04).
  • It is never established whether the lawyers who follow the team belong to the Safe Environment Fund or to a separate firm.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Armed security guards, lawyers and a radio voice speaking for the property owners; no resident. See Safe Environment Fund.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horrors 02
  • Radford Horrors 03

docs.title: Sherman Ranch
docs.text:
Sherman Ranch is the Wilmarth family's ranch outside Ballard, Utah, rented to the billionaire Robert Bigelow and sitting over a vast cavern; it is the site of a night hum, a levitation ring and a heat-and-magnet beam in The Walkers in Skin, until its farmhouse is launched toward Roosevelt.

Type Location (ranch) Aliases Wilmarth ranch; Skinwalker Ranch; the ranch; Alberta's ranch; Bigelow's ranch Region Near Ballard, Utah and Roosevelt, Utah Owner Alberta Wilmarth (family property) Tenant Robert Bigelow Status Farmhouse launched; only a small wooden barn left standing (as of Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The ranch is an open pastiche of the real Skinwalker Ranch, and the players say so. On the way to Utah, Zack asks "Remind me, we're going to the literal Skinwalker Ranch, right?" and Andre answers "Oh, you guys are going to Sherman Ranch" (Walkers 02). In Walkers 06 Andre says it is "before they renamed it the Skinwalker Ranch". In Walkers 01 Rita and Dante place the real ranch in northern Utah, southeast of Ballard, 512 acres, not near Hill Air Force Base but close enough.

Alberta describes it as cursed: boiled cattle, missing pets, UFO lights, and Navy people investigating radiation (Walkers 01). In person it has a gate guarded by a man with a rifle, sheep, chickens and cattle, a pig pen, an outhouse, a weather station, and a hum at night (Walkers 02). The community center and its substation are visible on the horizon.

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The big house, Bigelow's base and barn.
  • The guest double-wide, where the task force lives.
  • The pig pen, where a burned crow lands (Walkers 04).
  • The cavern under the whole property.
  • The yard fence where the beam appears (Walkers 06).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Alberta's request. Shelly Wilmarth, Alberta's mother, died of a heart attack while out with the cattle; Alberta says it was two years earlier, and the obituary she carries reads winter 1990. Alberta travels to Washington and asks Andrew to force an exhumation. The ranch tenant, "the space guy", has told her he has seen Shelly walking the edges of the property at night (Walkers 01). See Alberta's box.

Arrival. The task force reaches the ranch in Walkers 02. Walt Murphy at the gate tells of a figure he shot at near the barn that came at him at pretty high speed, of sheep that "kinda exploded" like a microwaved egg, and of the goose Nancy. Bigelow reports that the unexplained heat signatures and electromagnetic events are confined to the ranch and about half a mile around, with nothing in town. A cold open shows a coyote standing on two legs among the sheep. See Sherman Ranch phenomenon and Livestock mutilations.

The dusk event. In Walkers 03, 50 feet from the gate, the rental car dies and every device goes dead. A high whine, flickering lightning and a pulsing sky follow; the car is dragged six inches sideways and scorch marks are found in the engine. See The dusk event.

The vanished car. The Voyager disappears from the guest house overnight, with the ground where it sat at about 200 degrees, and is found pancaked in Roosevelt (Walkers 04). See The vanishing car.

The night event and the ring. Ground-penetrating radar finds the cavern (Walkers 05). The same night a psychic modulation event levitates Andrew and removes the Biz's fillings; Bigelow's sky camera records a bright white ring (Walkers 05). See The night event and The white ring.

The beam. At the yard fence a sheet of metal shakes violently along a faintly glowing vertical line; a dropped watch is launched along an arc pointing toward Roosevelt; then the beam is switched off with an electric pop (Walkers 06). See The beam.

The break-in. A naked intruder attacks the guest house, and Bigelow's recordings, drives and three employees vanish (Walkers 07). See Bigelow's recordings.

The launch. In Walkers 09 the farmhouse floats in the sky inside a loose halo of barbed wire, roof panels and horseshoes. As the sun sets a pale purple glow grows, the house vanishes in a vapor trail, launched toward Roosevelt, and a burning white ring about a kilometer across forms above the ranch, echoing the image from the earlier security footage of the levitation. Only the little wooden barn is left standing. The ranch is also the surface of the cavern, whose collapse ends the case.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Alberta (who no longer lives there), Robert Bigelow's research staff and security, Walt Murphy, and Nancy the goose.

docs.title: Smith Hotel
docs.text:
The Smith Hotel is the stately converted plantation-style hotel in Dahlonega, Georgia, where the team took rooms 109 and 110 beside the mysterious room 111 during The Things in Appalachia.

Type Location Aliases the hotel; the team's hotel Region Dahlonega, Georgia First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
A two-story, plantation-style converted house with Indian blankets, cable TV, mini fridges and an ice machine. It has a ballroom with a cheese spread, a stable, and a historic exhibit with a preserved mining camp and a shaft to an old mine. A continental breakfast serves scrambled eggs, local sausages (said to be goat), apple fritters, "the wonderful rainbow of pork products" and the slightly fermented Auraria peach preserves. Andre noted that the doors use conventional locks, as keycards were not yet common (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06).

The team chose it over the de-branded Motel and Suites. Rooms cost $55 per person per room. A conference of dental oncologists filled the hotel, and the team got the last two rooms, 109 and 110; the party's suspicion of the dentists became a running gag (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Rooms 109 and 110. The team's rooms; Andrew shared with Huell and Kurt with the Biz. Kurt swept his room for bugs and cameras and found none.
  • Room 111. The next-door room that the Biz secretly bugged.
  • Front desk. Staffed by a chatty young clerk on the day shift and a night clerk; in Appalachia 07 by the 17-year-old Tully. See Smith Hotel Desk Clerk.
  • Lobby phone and parking lot. Andrew used the lobby phone to call Big Bill, and a payphone outside serves the lot.
  • Mini fridge. Used to store evidence: the folded face and HF lighter in Appalachia 03, and the rabbit pelt in Appalachia 02.
  • Bathroom. The Biz spent several hours developing the film photos here in Appalachia 06.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
• Arrival. The clerk described Auraria, the hunters and the Covenant, and advised against staying in Auraria after dark. Off the record he thought the missing boy had run away and the woman had left her cult (Appalachia 01).
  • The dentists. At breakfast Huell spotted a dental oncologist digging through the scrambled eggs with bare hands (Appalachia 01).
  • The room 111 plant. The Biz planted a camera and microphone in room 111 (Appalachia 02).
  • Andrew's sleepwalk. Andrew woke in the woods, far from town, with a bloody lighter, took a cab home and was let in by the hotel clerk. Huell slept through it (Appalachia 03). See HF Lighter.
  • The lot. Dr. McManley's RV pulled into the lot; a fender bender between a van-life camper and a shiny black Ford truck occurred there, with a fed-looking man in a suit and a woman in a forest-ranger uniform swapping insurance details (Appalachia 04). See McManley's RV.
  • The night vision headset. In the cold open of Appalachia 06, state police searched the bushes outside the hotel and found a night vision headset (see Night-vision Goggles). The door of the room next to the team's had been broken down, and the Biz had a badly twisted ankle after an offscreen night (Appalachia 06).
  • Appalachia 07. The team stopped at the hotel to change socks, and Andrew's call to Big Bill was overheard by Tully (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The desk clerks, the dental oncologists, and the next-door guests. McManley kept his RV parked at the hotel.

docs.text:

  • Appalachia 02
  • Appalachia 03
  • Appalachia 04
  • Appalachia 06
  • Appalachia 07

docs.title: Special Projects Level
docs.text:
The Special Projects Level is the secret underground floor, about four stories down behind a keypad door, at the Spud Hut plant in Dahlonega, Georgia, where the company kept its caged ape-men.

Type Location Aliases Special Projects Region Beneath the Spud Hut Georgia Regional Distribution Center, Dahlonega First appearance Appalachia 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Steel double doors marked "Special Projects," locked with a keypad, lead to the lowest floor, reached by a cage-style cargo elevator and then a second, steel industrial elevator. The floor is largely open, with shelves and corners piled with medical equipment, animal-handling equipment and shovels, a drop ceiling over pipes and railings, cinder-block walls and a concrete floor. A floor grate shows pipes, wires and hissing steam. Andre put the floor four stories underground (Appalachia 08).

Jan Martense introduced it with "Down here we do the toppings," after explaining that the floors above were offices and potato processing (Appalachia 08).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The "break room" (code 441). A dark room behind a hefty steel door opening into the hallway. Jan said it held chairs and a drinks machine and gave the door code 441. It actually holds the ape-creatures; Andre later remarked that it was never a break room, only a door. See The Break Room (code 441).
  • The open floor. Where the team found the medical and animal-handling gear while waiting.
  • The kennel wing. In Appalachia 09 the same floor extends into hallways with no lit exit signs, veterinary equipment and gurneys with thick leather straps, a kennel room with straw and large cages, a kennel security office, a gear room of bear suits, shotguns, pepper spray, air horns and goalie masks, and a forklift loaded with dirt and ore. The elevator's maintenance ladder is sealed behind a steel shutter and a sliding grate, which Kurt judged had been added after the ladder was installed. Clive said the space was meant for a stuffed-pepper expansion that never happened, and Jan told the company he was installing an R&D department there instead (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The cold open of Appalachia 08 slid down a steel corridor to the doors, dropped through the grate into a nearly dark room of rattling steel cages, and ended on a dozen shining eyes turning toward the camera.

The team, with credentials as reporters and a deputy, was led down by Jan, who then said the external phone lines were out and left to make a call on the internal network. Jan sent them to wait in the break room, and as they opened it the elevator rose away. The Biz heard the propped door squeak and saw a huge pale hairy arm. In the ensuing fight, Kurt shot the shoe he had used to prop the door further into the room, Andrew was thrown through the drop ceiling and juggled by one of the creatures, Huell shot another in the neck, and Kurt's Claymore killed the one holding Andrew and destroyed the door frame and the opposite wall. About a minute and a half had passed since Jan's elevator rose. By Andre's count one creature was dead and at least two others badly injured had fled into other parts of the floor (Appalachia 08). See Ape-Men and Claymore Mine.

In Appalachia 09 the team was trapped when the elevator did not return. They met a worker, Clive, who explained the operation, found a forklift, bear suits and shotguns, and reached the gold room and the mines (see Dahlonega Gold Mines). They escaped by a ladder to the woods outside the plant, and the recorded arc ended there; the finale was an unrecorded session (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: The plant exploded shortly after Jan fled it. In Walkers 01 Kurt told Jan that some other force had caused a gas leak under the mines and ignited it (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 08
  • Appalachia 09

docs.title: Sportsman RV Campground
docs.text:
The Sportsman RV Campground is a riverside campground near Radford, Virginia where the missing FBI task force's camp still stands intact, and where the PITF later pitches its own tents beside it.

Type Location (campground) Aliases FBI campsite; the campground; Campsite A (on the tourist map) Region Near the river, a couple of miles from the moth site, in the woods outside Radford First appearance Radford Horrors 02 Other appearances Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The campground is near the river, with a smaller, older traditional campground attached. It is marked "Campsite A" on the tourist map. The FBI team's sites have big lockable stand-up tents, a fire pit, a composting toilet and a shower bag (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text: The missing agents' camp. Five agents' worth of gear stands in two tents plus an admin tent. Their car is still in the lot with two shotguns locked in its trunk (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The first visit (Radford Horrors 02)
docs.text:
The team learns the missing agents' campsite location from the sheriff's office. Kurt checks the map and finds it lies only a couple of miles from where the team faced the moth. Daniel Webster leads the visit. A teenager at the gate lets them in after Webster shows his badge, noting that the earlier "cops" are behind on berth fees. On the way in the team passes a few family campsites and two "extremely hairy men wearing fishing vests" who wave as the car goes by (Radford Horrors 02).

The team cuts open the locked tents. Huell (Investigate a Mystery, 11) finds no signs of haste or foul play, a bag of moldy laundry, and a map of the woods with irregular polygons and an illegible scribble beside one boundary, which he takes (see Missing agents' map). Webster photographs and videotapes the camp; Kurt's luminol turns up only a nosebleed on a pillow. There are no notebooks. A radioed report from a week earlier said the agents were "chasing up some weird stuff" (Radford Horrors 02). The map leads the team to the Safe Environment Fund fenced site.

docs.title: The second visit (Radford Horrors 04)
docs.text:
Having woken Wilbur Whateley in Roanoke (see Roanoke mental hospital), the team returns to Radford with an hour before stores close. They decide not to disturb the missing team's camp, since it is unprocessed evidence, and buy gear: two large three-person tents, a camp stove, Spam, eggs, hot dogs, coffee, water, s'mores supplies, Pabst, sleeping bags and foam rolls. The campground is already closed for the night but lets the FBI in again, and the team pitches beside the missing agents' tents. Kurt's tent goes up well; Huell's stands tilted about 20 degrees with two spare rods (Radford Horrors 04).

At twilight they cook hot dogs and s'mores. Kurt tells Webster the "spaceman" story from the first case, and Webster, with a Sharp 12, pieces together that Andrew's bag holds more than it could, that he shows casual superhuman strength, and that he keeps drinking blood; he chooses not to confront him. Andre ends the night with Kurt sleeping tied in a tree in a poncho and Andrew lifting him up the tree one-handed as Webster watches (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: The missing FBI agents (absent), an unnamed teenage gate attendant, and the PITF during their camp-out.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horrors 02
  • Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Spud Hut Georgia Regional Distribution Center
docs.text:
The Spud Hut Georgia Regional Distribution Center (SHGRDC, "Shugrid") is the concrete processing plant and corporate office on the edge of Dahlonega, Georgia, hiding a secret ape-man gold-mining operation beneath it, and it exploded shortly after the arc ended.

Type Location Aliases the plant; Spud Hut Corporate plant; SHGRDC Region Dahlonega, Georgia Affiliation Spud Hut Status Exploded (as of Walkers 01) First appearance Appalachia 01 (mentioned); Appalachia 02 (cold open)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
A big squat industrial concrete building, three or four stories tall. It has caged yellow lights, hard-hat workers, carts marked "Potato Testing," winding corridors of potato sacks and steam rooms, and steel cage-style cargo elevators with no floor indicator (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 08). Employees wear mandatory gray uniforms after a worker lost an arm in a machine, and about 40 trucks passed the team while they waited to get on the road one night (Appalachia 02). A plant worker at the trailer park, Ed's father, said the smell permeates so thoroughly that you "wake up in the middle of the night sweating potatoes."

The company's guarantee is potatoes "never touched by human hands," harvested with a special tool and a presentation on "the future of hygiene." A fishy smell is explained as a new special taco sauce (Appalachia 08).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The cave fissure. In the woods behind the plant, a rocky fissure with an ancient pickaxe, the scene of the Appalachia 02 cold open, in which a gray-jumpsuited worker followed a baby-like sobbing and was attacked.
  • Special Projects Level. About four stories underground; see also The Break Room (code 441).
  • The sub-basement and mines. Kennel room, gear room, gold room and the mine shafts below; see Dahlonega Gold Mines.
  • Parking garage. Where Jan Martense loaded a large animal crate into a red pickup in the cold open of Appalachia 09.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Suspicion. The team first heard of the plant from the McDonald's counter kid, Eric, who had done a trial shift there (Appalachia 01). The worker said his coworker Aaron Richters went out for a smoke break and never came back (Appalachia 02). Andrew phoned the plant from the gold mine lobby payphone. After verifying his badge, the phone worker Stacy called back to say Aaron had not clocked out of his shift or shown up the next day, and offered to connect him to Jan, who runs the center (Appalachia 03). In Appalachia 04, a Covenant member said the river was getting a lot of runoff from the plant.

Corporate visit. The team arrived behind the sheriff's car, found an investigator chain-smoking in his car and a Fox 5 Atlanta van out front, and entered posing as reporters and a deputy. Receptionist Charlene led them to Jan, who took them to Special Projects (Appalachia 08).

The operation exposed. In the fight and aftermath the team learned from Clive that the sub-basement served the ape-man gold mine, and left via a tarp-covered ladder in the woods outside the plant (Appalachia 09).

After the arc. The finale, Appalachia 10, was an unrecorded session. It is known only from Walkers 01: the plant exploded shortly after Jan fled it. Kurt told Jan that gas had been piped in deliberately from an adjacent cavern, but kept the portal secret. Jan could not explain the explosion and named only the accountant Clyde Harvard as another insider.

Unrecorded session

Details of the finale come only from Kurt's interrogation of Jan in Walkers 01.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: Jan Martense (manager), Clive (animal handler), the secretary Charlene, Stacy at the phones, and the ape-men. See Jan's Conspiracy and Ape-Men.

docs.text:

  • Appalachia 03
  • Appalachia 08
  • Appalachia 09
  • Walkers 01

docs.title: Stately Acres
docs.text:
Stately Acres is a seasonal gated mountain community near the ski lodge outside Radford, Virginia, where the pinball-loving guard Douglas Douglas is stranded at his post and where the Lawson family keeps a cabin.

Type Location (gated community) Aliases gated community Region Mountains near the Alpine Lodge, outside Radford First appearance Radford Horror 07 Inhabitants Douglas Douglas (guard); the Lawson family (seasonal)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The entrance has a wrought-iron sign, a locked road gate and a call box; the surrounding fence is just wire. A portable guard shack sits at the gate, along with a community tool shed. Cabins stand on gravel turnoffs, and the only cameras are on the guard shack. It is used seasonally (Radford Horror 07). The gate is about two miles from the spot where the team earlier saw people emerging from the woods after what looked like a business meeting (Radford Horror 07).

The sign over the gate suggests a holding or property-management company runs the community. Douglas says he cannot leave his post, and the table likens his job to a company-store arrangement (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: The guard shack
docs.text: A portable building with a bed against one wall; the rest of the space is packed with about 30 years of vintage pinball machines, including Space Invaders, Indiana Jones, Universal Monsters Mummy and Dracula, an off-brand Aliens and a Bozo clown machine misprinted "3056" (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: The Lawson cabin
docs.text: See Lawson cabin. A stone-and-timber cabin with a big Lawson sign at the turnoff, a rustic backyard, and weak locks.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
On the midday after the Whateley house raid, the team drives to the gate hunting Dean Lawson. Kurt uses the call box; a voice says the Lawsons use the place in summer and gives a phone number. The guard, whom Andre names Douglas Douglas on the spot, offers to show his pinball collection and buzzes the team in (Radford Horror 07).

  • Douglas's situation. He cannot leave his post or he is fired, must buy food from the company, gets supply drops every three months, and gets one unpaid month off per three. Andrew urges him to "investigate your rights," and later writes the Department of Labor's numbers for him. Kurt suggests a sign for a pinball hall in town; Douglas draws one on printer paper and asks the team to hang it alongside the missing-dog posters.
  • Fashion advice. He tells Andrew, "You look the most like a Fed of anyone I've ever seen," and gives him tie advice.
  • The shovel lead. Douglas volunteers that Dean was up recently and has been seen several times carrying a shovel to the family cabin. "Burying bodies? I don't know... He kicked one of my cats." He allows the team to look around as long as he is not fired.
  • The dig. While Andrew keeps Douglas talking about aliens and the poster, the Biz steals a fiberglass-handled shovel from the community tool shed (Act Under Pressure, 11 with Andrew's Help Out). Digging at the cabin turns up several Ziploc bags holding about $40,000 in hundred-dollar bills and a small tin key. Inside the cabin a locked Samsonite briefcase under a loose floorboard holds four parcels of slightly cut South American heroin (see Dean Lawson's heroin and cash).
  • Departure. Douglas begs for toilet paper; Kurt fetches some from the trunk. The team returns the toilet paper, collects the sign, and Douglas shakes Kurt's hand for twenty seconds (Radford Horror 07).

Douglas reappears in 1993 as the owner of the Douglas Pinball Emporium, whose lawsuit-funded opening is traced back to the team's earlier case (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Andre named the guard on the spot after the table suggested joke names such as Clyde Behringer and "George number five". Andre explained "Douglas. Like the writer," then clarified that he meant Frederick Douglass, and Ezra remarked that the guard was "about to become the most important character" (Radford Horror 07).
  • Zack, as Huell, whispers "Serial killer" to Andrew about Douglas, a gag that goes nowhere (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: The stealth wreck
docs.text:
The stealth wreck is a sunken, radar-evading vessel on an underwater shelf off Marblehead, found during the unrecorded Summer Service 02 dive and later revealed to be the boat of the radio contact's "advanced team".

Type Location (undersea wreck) Aliases dive site; the shelf; boat with a bite out of it Region Ocean off Marblehead, Massachusetts First appearance Summer Service 02 (unrecorded), recapped in Summer Service 03

Unrecorded session

The dive happened in Summer Service 02, which was never recorded. It is known only from the team's phone briefings to Big Bill in Summer Service 03 and from a remark in Summer Service 06.

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
According to the recap, the team dived in an experimental submarine with some college students, one of whom had earlier found a dead body under a sunken vessel. At the shelf they found a wreck designed to minimize its radar signature, with no 90-degree angles and a sawtooth shape on all the flat parts. Kurt remembered a turret with big capacitors on it (Summer Service 03).

The body was gone. The part of the wreck that had covered it had a chunk "eaten" out, and Andrew Howard told Big Bill that the boat had been "eaten" where the body lay; Big Bill concluded that whoever came back had cut part of the boat out and taken the body (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: The capacitor turret
docs.text: Kurt explained to Big Bill that capacitors meant the weapon discharged a large amount of electricity, so it could be a directed-energy weapon, a rail gun or a Gauss cannon. Big Bill compared it to Reagan's "Star Wars" proposal and said he would try to get a submarine out to take a closer look at the wreck (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
• The dive (unrecorded). While the team was at the wreck, a vessel covered in lights, "gyroscope" shaped, returned and hummed at a frequency that threatened their own submarine. The team lost power, left everything off and hid, and were not found. The vessel moved as if searching for something, then left. It matches the description of the later angel thing (Summer Service 03).
  • Exposure. Kurt, Huell and Andrew were poisoned by the synthetic nerve agent around this time; the Biz was not (Summer Service 03).
  • Identification. In the finale, Rita asks the radio contact whether his "advanced team" were the dead crew at the bottom of the ocean, and Dante names "the boat with a bite taken out of it". The radio contact confirms and apologizes that their broad-spectrum nerve agent leaked when they "got blown up" (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: Who the advanced team and the contact's organization really are (see Mystery covert group), what blew the vessel up, and what ate the piece out of it.

docs.title: The substation
docs.text:
The substation is the overloaded, arcing electrical substation near the Sherman Ranch turnoff, built alongside the community center, whose keys the cleanup crew wants and which is found blown up by grenades after Coyote's attempt to sabotage it during the finale.

Type Location (electrical substation) Aliases Electrical substation Region Near the ranch turnoff outside Ballard, Utah Status Wrecked by grenades (as of Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: A gray substation behind fabric-screened chain-link, about four miles from town and in sight of the ranch, next to the community center (Walkers 02, Walkers 03). Alberta says the ranch always hums at night, perhaps because of the substation; Robert Bigelow dismisses the idea, noting that there are substations everywhere and that the effects are confined to the ranch (Walkers 02).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The pop. After the dusk event, on the road toward the community center, the team hears loud popping from the substation and sees flickering light. Andrew notes the time and the team stops. Kurt rolls Investigate a Mystery (a 10) and learns that the equipment is arcing into the ground, smells of hot metal, and is being driven far harder than designed. Learning more would mean breaking in, which they judge unsafe (Walkers 03). Later the pop and the car's sideways shift are matched with spikes on Bigelow's EM meters, though the data are noisy (Walkers 04).

The keys. After the massacre at the Roosevelt police station, men in gray maintenance uniforms look over the team's cars and say the police keep the keys to the substation and they need them. A firefight follows (Walkers 08). See Utah cleanup crew.

The sabotage. In Walkers 09 the substation is arcing violently onto its surroundings and has started a large fire on both sides of the road, forcing the convoy off-road. Kurt suggests sabotaging it, since it looked overloaded and may be causally tied to the effect at the ranch. The major asks for volunteers, and Coyote (Walt Murphy) steps forward with his illegal rocket launcher and takes an APC back with a few Guardsmen and grenades. When the party passes later, the APC lies on its side among dead bodies and blown-up station wagons, and the substation has been exploded with grenades. There is no sign of Coyote from the outside. The party assumes his team destroyed it, but Andre says they cannot confirm this. With the interference gone, the APC's long-range radio reaches the National Guard outpost in Salt Lake City.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The episodes never establish whether the substation caused the ranch's effects or was only drawn on by them.

docs.title: USS Oklahoma City
docs.text:
USS Oklahoma City is a US Navy attack submarine seen in the cold open of the Summer Service finale, where its crew fire on the glowing sea creature off Marblehead.

Type Location (vessel) Affiliation US Navy Status Fate unknown; last seen with the creature closing on it at 80 knots (as of Summer Service 06) First appearance Summer Service 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The submarine appears only in the "A few seconds from now" half of the episode's intercut cold open. Its sonar operator, Davy, swears the bogey went onto land, then reports a small explosion like a grenade, followed by "the craziest sound I've ever heard". Andre explains at the table that the explosion is presumably the claymore the team set off on the truck (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Events aboard
docs.text:
The captain, who is drinking coffee, orders a single ping to see whether the bogey is sitting still. It is back, making the crazy noise and closing at 60 to 70 knots. He declares he is done with "this spooky shit", orders a full about turn and has the tubes flooded and everything conventional fired at it. The weapons station reports multiple positive contacts, then the sonar operator whispers "80 knots" and the show cuts to credits (Summer Service 06).

Quote

"I am done with this spooky shit. I don't care what it is... Whatever the fuck this is, it's gonna be God's problem soon." (Andre as the submarine captain)

Later, the radio contact tells the team the creature is chasing one of their submarines. When Andrew reports in, Big Bill says there was an attack on the plant "and we lost one of our submarines too" (Summer Service 06). In Summer Service 04 Big Bill had said he was retasking a Los Angeles-class fast attack submarine to look at the situation off Marblehead (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: It is never stated that the lost submarine is the Oklahoma City, or that the Oklahoma City is the boat Big Bill retasked, or whether the captain and Davy survived.
