docs.title: Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp
docs.text:
Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp is a Russian prison camp, abandoned since 1962, where the Russians hold Dick "The Biz" Baxter in the spring of 1993.

Type Location Aliases Vorkuta Region Russia Status Abandoned since 1962, according to the episode's on-screen subtitle First appearance Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Roulet Estate 03 introduces the camp with a shot of a rotting sign and a subtitle reading "Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp (abandoned since 1962)". The Biz's cell is freezing stone with a barred window and a slot in the door through which he is fed bread. The breath of the senior officer who visits him is visible in the cold (Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
After the siege at the Brooks pharmacy, the Biz vanishes from the hospital. Ezra suggested that the Russians had taken him, as a consequence of his past actions, and Andre chose "abducted and still in custody". The camp scene takes place roughly two weeks after the interrogations and regular beatings stopped; since then the Biz has seen only room searches, bread deliveries and the occasional kick. His leg wound was treated at what Andre calls the best hospital in Russia before the torture began (Roulet Estate 03).

The Biz frees his frozen waste bucket from the wall and lives on the bread from the slot. To keep his spirits up he sings unhinged sea shanties, including a parody of the Gilligan's Island theme about a bucket frozen to the icy wall, and talks to a cockroach, addressing it as "Skipper" (Roulet Estate 03).

A senior officer, recognizable by his mustache, looks through the slot with steel eyes. The Biz greets him with a very polite "Welcome, come in" in Russian, and the officer, repulsed, orders (in subtitles) "Get this man on a plane". After a lukewarm shower the Biz is flown first class, handcuffed beside an FSB officer who eats his steak, to Moscow, where he is shackled to a chair in the former Soviet Parliament building and meets Boris Yeltsin, who offers him a cigar (Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text:
• Dick "The Biz" Baxter, prisoner.
  • The camp's cruelest guard, whom Andre calls "the kickiest gentleman in this place", and a less aggressive guard the Biz had gotten along with, who is no longer there.
  • The senior officer who orders his removal.

docs.title: The Weapons Closet
docs.text:
The Weapons Closet is a panic-room-style gun room in the Roulet House, sealed behind a steel door and emptied of nearly all its firearms before the agents arrive.

Type Location Aliases steel door room; gun room; weapons locker Region Exeter, Rhode Island (inside the Roulet House) First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The door sits in the living room, near the television and the VHS rack, and has a combination lock like the door to a panic room. Nobody has the combination. Through a gap beneath it Andrew sees empty racks on the walls, which Andre says once held about twenty firearms, and a single World War II flamethrower left against the rear wall (Roulet Estate 01).

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
Kurt bashes at the wooden floor beside the door with the iron stand that holds the fireplace tools, for about forty-five minutes, while the others watch the windows. During the hammering Rita (as Andrew) steps outside and shouts "Can we just talk?" into the woods, then glimpses a low, brilliant light streaking through the trees; when she turns to look, it is gone. When the noise stops, the others find Kurt staring at the door, dizzy, having lost a minute of time. Andrew takes over, the floorboards cave, and he squeezes his head and a flashlight under the door. He concludes that the couple's "arsenal closet" was "looted by our extraterrestrial neighbors" (Roulet Estate 01).

In Roulet Estate 02 the agents find the missing guns, including a Kalashnikov and WWII-era Russian pistols, stored in the hidden attic lair, and bring them down the chimney. Andre says the gentleman of the house seems to have been a firearms collector. The players take this to explain the sniper's VSS and to make a KGB plot less likely (Roulet Estate 02). In Roulet Estate 03, Officer Todd reports that the pharmacy gunman has a flamethrower, a machine gun and a heavy wooden rifle (Roulet Estate 03). It is never established whether that flamethrower is the one left in the closet.

docs.title: Whateley house
docs.text:
The Whateley house (also the Whateley residence) is a cookie-cutter suburban home in Radford, Virginia where the Whateley family lived, with a shrine-like bedroom, a comatose son's room, and a root cellar under the garage that holds a mummified body, a spacesuit and, according to the police, Wilbur's journal.

Type Location (house) Aliases Whateley residence; the root cellar; the hidden basement Region A neighborhood near the Lucky house, within a mile of it, bordering the woods Inhabitants Yobiah Whateley, Irene Whateley, Wilbur Whateley; formerly Abelforth Whateley First appearance Radford Horror 01 (mentioned); first visited in Radford Horror 02 Appearances Radford Horror 01, 02, 06, 07, 08

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The house sits in a nicer, cookie-cutter subdivision than the Luckys' neighborhood. The yard is bare of toys, flags or signs and slightly neglected, with a double driveway (Radford Horror 02). The kitchen has a panoramic window by the mud door; the tree line is about fifty feet away. Upstairs are the parents' room and bath at the front and the twins' rooms at the back. The garage is crammed with dusty outdoor sports gear, a small boat and a jet ski. The whole house smells musty (Radford Horror 02; Radford Horror 06).

The woods behind the house are part of the national forest; dense ground cover hides tracks within about a dozen feet. Houses sit in enclaves, one direction leading back to civilization within a mile and others leading miles into forest (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• The kitchen window. Where Irene stood at the sink, dropped her pan and walked into the woods (Radford Horror 02).
  • Abe's room. An untouched shrine: a shuttle poster, star-and-moon pajamas, a UFO painting, and shelves of UFO and pop-science books. The Biz finds a hidden book of amateur alien-abduction illustrations, a hollowed-out Where the Sidewalk Ends holding $120 to $130, overdue library books, and a receive-only Circuit City radio tuned to the same Art Bell station as the Pay n' Stay clerk (see Abe's radio) (Radford Horror 02).
  • Wilbur's room. A boy in a wheelchair slumped by the window among pinned butterflies and insects (Radford Horror 02).
  • The parents' room. Prozac and lithium prescribed by Dr. Lori, both expired with pills left (Radford Horror 02).
  • The root cellar. An unfinished cellar under the garage, entered through rotten double doors under a tarp and padlocked. It is about five feet high and hung with ratty tarps. It holds a dog skeleton, shredded fibers, a root-like growth wrapped around a floor joist, discarded spacesuit pieces and a mummified teenager (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 01. Sheriff Roosevelt mentions that Mrs. Whateley, a neighbor less than a mile from the Luckys, saw something from her kitchen window while making dinner, put down her pan and walked into the night while her husband watched. The house itself is not yet visited (Radford Horror 01).
  • Radford Horror 02. The team visits the morning after. Yobiah ignores a glass of water while neighbors fuss; forensics has already dusted the kitchen. The Biz tracks two sets of footprints about the same size, one with a heavier shoe, lost after about a dozen feet. Yobiah says Irene looked "surprised" rather than angry or scared and thought it was a coyote. Neighbor Meg Gunderson blames Abe. The team learns that one son (Abe) robbed a store in a homemade spacesuit and vanished, and the other (Wilbur) crashed a car and has not spoken since (Radford Horror 02).
  • Radford Horror 06. After a stakeout from the water tower, the team sees a craft descend on the Whateley backyard; Huell tackles a spacesuited boy in a clearing and is lifted above the treeline (see Radford Moth). Later that night, treating it as hot pursuit, Kurt picks the lock and the team sweeps the dark house. Mr. Whateley is unresponsive on sleeping pills. In the third room, Wilbur lies in bed beside his wheelchair, smelling musty and clammy; smelling salts bring only a vacant stare and soft crying. In the garage Kurt finds the cellar doors; the Biz and Kurt cut the padlock and discover the mummified teenager nailed to the wall through the wrists and ankles in a NASA T-shirt, head stove in. The Biz hides a live radio bug behind the loose flag patch of the handmade spacesuit. About 11:30 p.m. Wilbur's room is empty: he went out the window. In the morning Mr. Whateley is led out nearly catatonic during the canvass (Radford Horror 06).
  • Radford Horror 07. The sheriff is dismantling the house for forensic examination, which Kurt fears will expose "the garage" (Radford Horror 07).
  • Radford Horror 08. The police theory is that a hidden basement contained the spaceman costume with a journal and the body of Abelforth Whateley, "never ran away," killed around April 17th; Wilbur is cast as a serial killer. The journal records the larva found June 3rd and hatching August 15th (Radford Horror 08). See Wilbur's journal and Spaceman suit.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Dante repeatedly calls Abelforth "Albert" at the table. Ezra's summary of the cellar: "Corpse cellar alien really rolls off the tongue" (Radford Horror 06).
  • The team calls the space a root cellar under the garage; the sheriff's department, in Radford Horror 08, calls it a hidden basement under the residence. The police say the body is probably Abelforth but that DNA and dental testing is still under way; the identification is never confirmed on screen (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Wheat field near Moscow
docs.text:
The wheat field near Moscow is a rain-soaked field off a dark highway between Moscow and Oryol Oblast, where Dick "The Biz" Baxter hides the wounded Russian president after a convoy ambush, kills a pursuer, and is blinded in one eye.

Type Location (field) Aliases the wheat field Region Countryside outside Moscow, on the road toward Oryol Oblast First appearance Radford Horrors 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The ambush takes place on a dark, rainy highway where feral dogs roam and shabby apartment buildings line one side; the wheat field lies beyond. The Biz kills the car lights and swerves into the field, following the field's crushed trail in the rain (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The ambush and escape
docs.text:
At about 3 to 3:30 a.m., the president meets the Biz in the Hotel Metropol lobby and tells him there has been "an unusual aircraft crash in Oryol Oblast" and that he wants the Biz to look at it (see Hotel Metropol and Boris Yeltsin). The convoy is an armored limo with two cars ahead and one behind; the Biz rides in the squat rear car between two guards (Radford Horrors 03).

Past Moscow, a 1960s Russian car rams the president's limo and explodes. The Biz (Read a Bad Situation, 10) hears Chechen and Russian voices, multiple cars of gunmen and an elaborate ambush. He crawls to the limo, finds the president unconscious beneath a guard, and with the surviving guard's help drags him to the rear car. With a Luck point burned, he reverses about half a kilometer under fire, the windshield shattering. A security radio picks up an unknown channel, and he calls "Mayday, Mayday, is anyone here?" in Russian. When a heavy Soviet car with four or five men gains on him, he kills the lights and swerves into the field, burning more Luck on fancy stunt driving to lose the pursuers (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: In the field
docs.text:
• The car's trunk opens with the dead guard's quick-release key. Inside the Biz finds the president's medical cooler on dry ice (blood bags, biologics and anti-nerve-agent drugs), a grenade launcher, grenades, automatic weapons and a first aid kit.
  • He gives first aid: dry ice wrapped in his jacket on the president's head (uneven pupils, a severe concussion) and a shot of injectable ibuprofen.
  • A man jogs toward the car along the crushed trail. The Biz props the dead guard by the driver's door, fireman-carries the president 50 feet into the wheat, and hides. He reads the pursuer as wearing mismatched, outdated paramilitary gear and is about 90 percent sure the man is not Russian security.
  • The Biz circles with the guard's knife in his teeth, burning another Luck on his Kick Some Ass roll. He stabs the man between body armor and helmet, choosing "inflict terrible harm": a cut artery and severed gun-arm tendons. The man gouges the Biz's eye, leaving him permanently blind in that eye (1 harm). The Biz wrestles the gun away and the man faints from blood loss and collapses.
  • A Russian helicopter with a spotlight lands. The Biz drops his guns, leads the crew to the president, and both are flown off. He has spent three Luck and has three left before he is Doomed.

(Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: In the next episode the Biz wakes in a locked hospital room with an armed guard, and is summoned at dawn to see Yeltsin, who is sutured at the head and torso and praises his "impressive stunt driving" (Radford Horrors 04). Yeltsin says intelligence thinks the attack was "opportunistic and fairly half-assed" (Radford Horrors 04). Who sent the ambushers is never established; see Convoy ambushers.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Ezra (as the Biz), over the radio before killing the lights: "I'm going into a wheat field. You're gonna have to find me." (Radford Horrors 03)
  • The president is never named in Radford Horrors 03, where he addresses the Biz as "Richard"; he is named as Yeltsin in Radford Horrors 01 and again in Radford Horrors 04.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horrors 03

docs.title: Woods Trail and Rabbit Site
docs.text:
The Woods Trail and Rabbit Site is the hiking trail near Auraria, Georgia, where the team met Frotter Comstock, found staged Bigfoot footprints, and recovered a gutted white rabbit pelt from a treetop.

Type Location Aliases the circle Region Near Auraria, Georgia First appearance Appalachia 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The team set out on the trail from Auraria. The Circle Chasers had marked on a map where they thought Bigfoot was based, and the team drew a circle around that area. Within it lie a footprint spot, a hill with a crumbled side where the Chasers filmed, and a tree about 100 feet from the rabbit snatch (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Notable places within
docs.text:
• Comstock meeting point. About ten minutes in, the team saw a light and met Frotter Comstock, a bearded man in overalls hauling a cart of bottles and chemistry equipment, who described himself as from a long line of Comstock bootleggers and said he had been helping the Auraria church with a methanol problem in their ritual beverage. His own land is described at Comstock's Property.
  • Footprint spot. The Biz rolled an 8 on Investigate a Mystery, got a boost from Kurt's Help Out, and asked what was being concealed. The team found two clean, giant footprints, the edge of a sneaker print beside them and a cigarette butt. Kurt photographed everything and said he leaned more toward a fake Bigfoot print than a real one.
  • Rabbit snatch hillside. The Circle Chasers showed a three-second clip on a '90s VHS camcorder of a rabbit frozen in the trail, eyes glowing in the lights, before a gray, man-sized blur grabbed it.
  • The blood tree. After about half an hour of searching, blood dripped on Andrew from a tree about 100 feet from the snatch. Huell climbed (Andrew gave him a boost with Help Out, exposing himself to danger), slipped, caught himself under both arms and took 1 harm, and retrieved a white rabbit's pelt with its insides gone, ripped apart rather than cut or chewed (Appalachia 02). See White Rabbit Pelt.

docs.title: History of events there
docs.text:
The team walked the trail at night, having left their night vision in the decontaminated car; Kurt passed a Preparedness roll to have luminol and a UV light. Huell and the Biz flanked in the dark while Kurt and Andrew approached Comstock. An unearthly howl later scattered birds before the Circle Chasers arrived, and Harvey the Great Dane leapt on Andrew (Appalachia 02).

The Chasers offered theories: Eddie Jones argued that Bigfoot might be feral humans, comparing them to feral hogs, while Andrew argued for a werewolf, because in the footage the creature crawled rather than walking upright. Kurt made a mental note of everyone's footwear (hiking boots; Delilah in flats) to check against the sneaker print, and wondered whether the creature had returned to hang its prey in the tree. Andre's answer to the Biz's question "Where did it go?" was that the creature is very comfortable moving vertically.

The team marked the ridge where a witness had seen the creature, the spot on the road and the rabbit site on the map to get a range. Andre said the line pointed toward town (Appalachia 02). The faked prints later fed the Bigfoot hoax; in Appalachia 06 the team found a snapped-off plaster-of-Paris toe and matching fake prints on Comstock's land.

docs.title: Inhabitants
docs.text: None. The bootlegger Comstock lives on a nearby ridge homestead.

docs.title: Main cast and recurring
docs.text: Page Alternate history The alternate history of PITF is the campaign's version of 1992 and 1993: an early-1990s United States that looks like ours until the Paranatural Incident Task Force starts to change it. The paranatural The paranatural is the catch-all term for the creatures, technologies and unexplained events that the Paranatural Incident Task Force is sent to investigate. The show The show is the framing device of the whole campaign: every session of PITF is played as an episode of an early-1990s television series about the Paranatural Incident Task Force. Timeline The timeline is the chronology of in-fiction events in PITF, from the backstory of its towns and characters to the latest recorded session, Radford Horrors 04. Unresolved mysteries Unresolved mysteries collects the questions the campaign has left open as of the latest session, Radford Horrors 04.

docs.title: Across several cases
docs.text: Page The Masters The Masters are the benevolent, ascended beings at the center of Andrew Howard's faith, who in his account have guided humanity since the Stone Age and whose number includes Jesus Christ. Moby-Dick book cipher The Moby-Dick book cipher is the code system, keyed to a 1980 reprint of Moby-Dick, through which the Biz's Russian correspondents send him numbered messages by recorded "sweepstakes" phone lines.

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: Page The Bigfoot Hoax The Bigfoot Hoax is the staged series of Bigfoot sightings, footprints and photographs around Dahlonega, Georgia, which Jan Martense's gold-mining ring used to discredit real sightings of escaped ape-men. Clinton Surveillance Scandal The Clinton Surveillance Scandal is the October 1992 news story, announced by a Georgia State Police official, that FBI agents had been spying on presidential candidate Bill Clinton in Dahlonega, Georgia. Covenant Beliefs Covenant Beliefs are the doctrines and rites of the Covenant, the religious community led by Elijah Ray in the Georgia ghost town of Auraria: a holy meteor, Auraria as the Garden of Eden, a coming apocalypse, visions... The Crack in the Air The Crack in the Air is a hard-edged rift in space in a side tunnel of the Dahlonega mines, with a metal pipe running through it that pumps gas into the mine. The Land Dispute The Land Dispute is the year-long campaign of eviction letters and pressure by unnamed "corporate goons" to push the Covenant off its land in Auraria, Georgia.

docs.title: Acceptable fact pattern
docs.text:
The acceptable fact pattern is the phrase Rudy Giuliani uses when he orders the task force to produce a presentable official account of the first Radford case, after President Perot rejected the original reports.

Type Lore / directive Aliases cover story directive Issued by FBI Director Rudy Giuliani Status Standing order; the team is never shown delivering such an account First appearance Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
At FBI headquarters, Giuliani tells the team that a number of people are missing near the site of one of their old cases and that the original FBI task force sent to investigate has gone AWOL. Perot found the classified reports from that investigation of unacceptable quality; former Director Sessions stood by them and was fired. The team become consultants under Special Agent Daniel Webster's operational authority, "strictly there for informational purposes", with two goals: first, establish what happened to the previous FBI team; second, "establish an acceptable fact pattern for the previous investigation" (Radford Horrors 01).

Andre restates the order in Radford Horrors 02 as the second of two priorities: find and recover the previous task force, and "determine an acceptable fact pattern for the previous case". In the same recap, Perot reads the intelligence from the team's last deployment ("What the fuck is this? This says it was like a giant bug."), Sessions answers "Yeah, it's a giant bug", and Perot fires him and appoints Giuliani (Radford Horrors 02). See Alternate history for the Perot administration.

docs.title: Reception at the table
docs.text:
The players read the order as a cover-up. Dante guesses that Perot does not like reading "that it's fucking aliens and shit", while Ezra suggests that the original report may itself have been a cover story (Radford Horrors 01). Andre explains that Webster believes the team is "dirty as hell" and covered something up in Radford (Radford Horrors 01). In Radford Horrors 02 Dante sums up the first leads as a "secondhand, kind of hand-wavy cover-up" (Radford Horrors 02).

The order sits alongside the other official explanations met in Radford, such as the LA treatment cover story for the disappearances and the bleach-cleaned woods at the SEF fence site, which Kurt calls a professional cleanup (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: The phrase is used only in these two episodes. The team is never shown delivering a finished account, and it is never established whether Perot objected to the supernatural content itself.

docs.title: Alternate history
docs.text:
The alternate history of PITF is the campaign's version of 1992 and 1993: an early-1990s United States that looks like ours until the Paranatural Incident Task Force starts to change it. The largest change is the 1992 election, which Ross Perot wins.

The politicians and celebrities on this page are fictional versions of real people, written and voiced by Andre as characters in a story. For dates, see the timeline. For the supernatural side of the setting, see the paranatural.

docs.title: How the setting differs
docs.text:
The world does not split from ours at a single stated moment. When the campaign opens in May 1992 the Soviet Union has collapsed, George H. W. Bush is president, and the agents carry pagers and stop to ask for directions ("There is no Google Maps"). The first difference is hidden: cryptids, parasites and stranger things are real, and a handful of people in government know it. (Radford Horror 01)

The public differences come later and are mostly the player characters' fault. A coastal town becomes the site of a nuclear incident, a surveillance scandal upends a presidential race, and two Utah towns are emptied. From the night of the election onward the table calls the result the "Perot-verse". (Appalachia 01, Walkers 07, Walkers 09, Radford Horrors 04)

Quote

Zack (out of character): "Have we entered the Perot-verse?" (Walkers 07)

docs.title: The Bush administration and the task force
docs.text:
In the premiere Andrew Howard is offered a new task force that "reports almost directly to the president": the chain of command runs from Andrew to Big Bill Nelson, to the deputy director Floyd Clark, to Bush. Andrew's old boss warns him that it "has boondoggle written all over it" and "smells like career suicide". (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03)

Bush later tells Andrew the real reason. His son "has an interest in these things" and made him promise that if he won the election he would get to the bottom of it. (Walkers 01)

The government's machinery for such things includes:

  • SKYHOOK, the code word under which the team's reports are classified. (Summer Service 03)
  • The Foreign Influence Task Force, Big Bill's unit, which has the team because "alien visitations are foreign by definition". (Summer Service 03)
  • The Foreign Threat Investigation Task Force, or "something like that": the bland name under which the team is described on television. (Walkers 01)
  • The Atolean Paranatural Index, which ranks towns by UFO and cryptid sightings and disappearances per capita, and is used to pick cases. (Radford Horror 01)
  • UTAW, the CIA branch where Kurt Larson once did "psychic dream exercises", and Black Site Omaha, a CIA prison five stories below the ocean surface. (Walkers 01, Radford Horrors 03)

The NSA is the "Puzzle Palace", which Andre explains is the CIA's name for it. (Radford Horror 04, Summer Service 01, Appalachia 07)

docs.title: The 1992 election
docs.text: In our history Bill Clinton won in 1992 and Perot took about 19 percent of the popular vote, a figure Zack looks up at the table. (Appalachia 07, Walkers 08)

docs.title: The Georgia scandal
docs.text:
While the team is in Dahlonega hunting ape-men, Governor Bill Clinton is in the same town. Dick "The Biz" Baxter has secretly taken a job from his KGB contacts to plant a camera and microphone in a hotel room. Georgia state police then call a press conference to say that the FBI is in Dahlonega surveilling a presidential candidate, and that fingerprints from something recovered at the scene match an FBI agent. A reporter asks whether it is "the next Watergate". (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08)

Quote

Rita (as Andrew Howard): "We're not surveilling Bill Clinton. We're surveilling dead Chewbacca." (Appalachia 07)

The arc's finale was never recorded, so the outcome is known only from the next session. Polaroids of Clinton, taken with a Russian camera, have become public. Bush's account is that a criminal with "a bunch of ape-men", Jan Martense, was surveilling Clinton in the same town at the same time. The state police say they found the Biz's night-vision goggles in a rose bush, and he is "the most hated cop in America". The full story is on the Clinton surveillance scandal page. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Two October surprises
docs.text:
Andre's summary of the alternate history is that Perot "just needed two October surprises", and that one event supplied both: the incumbent was caught spying on the challenger, and the pictures hurt the challenger too. He calls it "kind of Watergate and Monica Lewinsky at the same time". After the "double scandal" Perot polls above 45 percent and Bush clearly leads only in Texas. (Walkers 01, Walkers 08)

Bush expects to lose and reads the affair as a deliberate attack on the continuity of American leadership, perhaps by China, by "the remnants of the Soviets" or by "something else altogether, from somewhere else". This is his theory of enemy action. (Walkers 01)

Quote

Andre (as Bush): "There is coincidence, there is miracle, and there is enemy action. That is enemy action." (Walkers 01)

With the election close, the Bureau wants its version of the story out, and the price is putting the Biz on television. His appearance on Late Night with David Letterman opens the fourth arc, and in Utah he is recognized "from Leno". (Walkers 01, Walkers 02)

docs.title: Election Day
docs.text: Election Day, 3 November 1992, falls in the middle of the Utah case, with the phones down. When Donald McManley next reaches the team the count is unfinished and Perot has taken Ohio. The team hears of his victory on the radio as they leave the ruins of the community center. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: The Perot presidency
docs.text:
Perot takes office in January 1993. As President-elect he tells Big Bill "in no uncertain terms" that he believes the task force is "a cover for Bush's weaponization of the FBI against his political enemies", which is how the Clinton affair looks from outside. He asks Big Bill to resign and disbands the task force on Inauguration Day. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

Quote

Dante (out of character): "Guess what, Ross Perot? You're gonna have a rough first fucking day." (Roulet Estate 01)

A few months later he calls Andrew himself. (Roulet Estate 03)

Quote

Andre (as Perot): "This is the President of the United States. I need you to come in. Something's happened in Virginia." (Roulet Estate 03)

Other changes under Perot:

  • The FBI. William Sessions is still Director in early 1993, with Floyd Clark rumored as his replacement. Perot fires him after reading the classified reports from Radford, which he finds unacceptable and Sessions stands by, and brings in Rudy Giuliani. Andre notes that Giuliani was then running for mayor of New York, an election he wins in our world. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)
  • A new team. Perot forms his own task force for "the insurgency incidents", as he sees the old team's cases. Its agents go missing in Radford (the missing FBI task force). (Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Consultants. The old team returns "strictly for informational purposes" under Daniel Webster, who helped with the rescue of Perot's employees from Iran and believes the old task force did Bush's political dirty work. Their orders are to find the missing agents and to establish an acceptable fact pattern. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Russia and Yeltsin
docs.text:
The Soviet Union is gone, but Marblehead locals still blame their offshore explosion on a "Russian bombing". The KGB survives as a network of fronts that reaches the Biz through a sweepstakes phone line and the Moby-Dick book cipher. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 04, Appalachia 01)

In January 1993 Russians take the Biz from an American hospital. He is held first at the abandoned Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp, is then flown to Moscow to meet Boris Yeltsin, and by April is living at the Hotel Metropol as Yeltsin's guest. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)

Yeltsin's Russia knows more than Washington admits to knowing:

  • Soviet detectors recorded a surge in the cosmic microwave background and traced it to the nuclear incident at Marblehead. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Russian intelligence knows of the Marblehead worms and of the "people who were not people" in Utah, whom Yeltsin compares to Koschei the Deathless. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Yeltsin shows the Biz a broken, half-melted flashlight weapon and says, "We are developing a test." (Radford Horrors 01)
  • A triangular craft has crashed in Oryol Oblast. On the way there Yeltsin's convoy is ambushed by attackers speaking Chechen and Russian. (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

Quote

Andre (as Yeltsin): "I have faith in my military officers, but I do not have faith that my military officers are my military officers." (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: The official record
docs.text:
The public history of this world is a set of cover stories. After Marblehead Andre describes three versions of each case: the code-word report that goes to Big Bill, the one the rest of the government gets, and the one the public gets. (Appalachia 01)

Event The official version Source Radford, May 1992 The Whateley boy, a heroin connection to a Mexican cartel, a firefight at the old church and a fire (Radford Horror 08, Radford Horrors 02) Marblehead, June 1992 An extremist cult with nerve agent and a rogue ex-Soviet nuclear device, which attacked a nuclear plant when investigators arrived; the worms are played down (the terrorist cover story) (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01) Dahlonega, October 1992 A criminal with ape-men who was surveilling a presidential candidate (Walkers 01) Ballard and Roosevelt, November 1992 A radical domestic insurgency: extremists under the community center who "went full Jonestown" when investigators showed up (Roulet Estate 01) Radford, 1993 Missing people are said to be in rehab in California (the LA treatment cover story) (Radford Horrors 02)

Andre stresses that Marblehead "was on the news for a while". The agents leave the spin to Big Bill. (Appalachia 01, Roulet Estate 01)

Quote

Dante (out of character): "Yeah, I mean, we're the X-Files guys. We're not the cover-up guys." (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Invented places, companies and media
docs.text:
• Spud Hut. A baked-potato restaurant chain "founded in the area" of Dahlonega. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)
  • Pay n' Stay. Radford's run-down motel. (Radford Horror 01)
  • Sons of Adam. Marblehead's church, whose scripture sends Jesus to Lemuria. (Summer Service 01)
  • Keely Network. The message boards through which Andrew hears about the Roulets. (Roulet Estate 02)
  • Safe Environment Fund. The body that fences off Radford's woods in 1993. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Tropical Storm Andrew 2. The storm that cuts off Marblehead. (Summer Service 05)
  • Mr. Root. An off-brand root beer. Kurt has "never had a Mr. Root". (Appalachia 02)
  • Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable. An OVA that plays on hotel cable in Georgia. It is the campaign's non-canon one-shot. (Appalachia 02)

Sherman Ranch is not invented. Andre confirms that it is the real Skinwalker Ranch, "before they renamed it". (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Real people as characters
docs.text:
Besides the presidents and Yeltsin, the fiction borrows:

  • David Letterman, who interviews the Biz on Late Night. (Walkers 01)
  • Robert Bigelow, the tenant of Sherman Ranch. When Zack recognizes the surname of "the Skinwalker Ranch guy", Dante says it is "probably intended to be the same guy". (Walkers 02)
  • Rudy Giuliani and William Sessions at the FBI. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Jay Leno and Howard Stern, heard of but never met. (Appalachia 01, Walkers 02)

Andre looked up Perot's voice just before playing him. Dante's verdict: "Why is Ross Perot a D&D goblin?" (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Popular culture
docs.text:
Most of the period detail is real, and the table checks it as it goes.

  • Television. Watching Roseanne is Huell's "rock bottom". In Moscow the Biz watches Los ricos también lloran dubbed into Russian. The office has seven copies of Close Encounters, and the team watches it there on a slow Monday. (Appalachia 01, Radford Horrors 01, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Radio. Art Bell plays in the Pay n' Stay office. "Baby Got Back" comes on in Radford after Andre checks what was charting in 1992, and "Radar Love" plays in two cold opens. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03, Appalachia 07, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Food and shops. The team eats at McDonald's in Marblehead and Dahlonega, and the players look up which Happy Meal toys were on offer. Arby's, Taco Bell and Blockbuster Video all appear. (Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 01, Appalachia 01, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Recent news. Ruby Ridge, the Gulf War and Iran-Contra have happened as in our world, and Dante notes that the CIA's psychic-spy programs were real. The World Trade Center bombing and Waco still happen under Perot. (Summer Service 04, Appalachia 03, Walkers 09, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Not yet
docs.text:
A running device is dramatic irony about things the characters cannot know. Huell shows off a World Trade Center postcard, and Kurt says the towers "will stand for a thousand years". The office's toy alien is named OJ, after "my favorite football athlete". During the Marblehead siege the table establishes that "Waco hasn't happened yet". (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 05)

Andre rules anachronisms in or out on the spot: no Beast Wars toys, no purple Game Boy ("those won't be out for another four years"), and Tasers only just, in early 1993. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03, Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Crystal Pepsi is treated two ways. In the premiere Andre finds that it is advertised but "not available yet"; in Marblehead a month later it "had just come out". (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03)
  • When the scandal breaks, one of the players asks who Bill Clinton was in 1992, and Andre reminds the table that it is October of that year. (Appalachia 07)
  • Ezra jokes that the Russians who questioned the Biz about Clinton were "the Bill Clinton team", now sent to Siberia, and that a small "Ross Perot team" suddenly has all the budget. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Yeltsin's first question to the Biz is "Tell me everything you know about the humanists." Who they are has not been explained. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Speculating about where the Perot-verse goes next, Dante teases "wait till you fuckers find out about 417", and Andre offers that "there's, like, a bureaucratic fuck-up and the US accidentally nukes North Dakota". Nothing of the kind has happened in an episode. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Andrew's Condition
docs.text:
Andrew's Condition is the set of physical changes in Andrew Howard after the Utah disaster: bullet resistance, a craving first for rare steak and then for human blood, and a healing power that fails at a crucial moment, none of which his doctors and church officials seem able to explain.

Type Lore Aliases bullet resistance; iron deficiency; blood craving; blood hunger; special horse Affects Andrew Howard First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: By Christmas Eve 1992, Andre tells Rita, Andrew still has to eat normally but has "an additional requirement": Rita describes it as iron deficiency, and Andre adds an intense craving for very rare steak. Andrew was shot about five times in the torso in Utah and, in Andre's words, "just kind of walked it off". He is doing religious soul-searching ("Have I been chosen?"), and Huell is not in the loop about any of it (Roulet Estate 01).

docs.title: Bullet resistance
docs.text:
Rita explains that Andrew negates 2 harm normally, and 3 with his pendant; she calls him "just a beefy boy". He gets +1 when pursuing, but -1 to Act Under Pressure (Roulet Estate 01).

At the Roulet House, the Roulet Intruder shoots him in the face with a VSS. Andrew negates the harm, and the shooter's body language reads as shock. When Kurt asks about the "bullet splash" on his collar, Andrew rubs his face and says he ran through something (Roulet Estate 01).

docs.title: Speed
docs.text: By Roulet Estate 02 Andrew's normal walking speed has risen to seven or eight miles an hour, which annoys the rest of the party as he opens doors for them from 45 feet ahead (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: Blood craving
docs.text: During the pharmacy siege in Roulet Estate 03, the sight of the Biz's blood and a gut-shot hostage's pool of blood triggers a craving. Rita rolls Act Under Pressure (8, at -1) and takes -2 to the rest of the fight rather than give in. After the gunman is subdued, Andrew tries to use his space-healing power on the Biz, and nothing happens. He applies a tourniquet instead and licks the blood from his fingers afterward, looking very upset that the power failed. Rita says Andrew is not in control of the behavior (Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: Doctors and church
docs.text:
In the months after the case, Andrew takes a week at home to talk to his doctor and church officials, who tell him his powers can be unpredictable, especially in moments of personal crisis, and promise tests. For the first time in his life he gets the impression that they do not know what they are talking about, "more like they were sort of shushing a panicking horse". Rita asks whether he feels like one of many beloved horses or a special one; Andre rules "for sure a special horse", and Andrew begins to realize he is the test case. They X-ray him but never show him the results or give him paperwork. At his request, his doctor starts mailing him human blood weekly, disguised as frozen orange juice packed in dry ice. Andrew does not ask where it comes from (Roulet Estate 03).

Shirtless in his New York hotel room, scratching the scar on his chest while the blood thaws in a Brita pitcher, Andrew wonders whether he died, whether he is an alien hybrid, and whether his weird dreams are actually his father. He is working a desk job analyzing the World Trade Center bombing, which Rita says he is fine with because of "the whole 'I can get shot now and not die' mystery" (Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The cause is never settled. Andrew's own guesses are that he died and came back, that he is an alien hybrid, or that his dreams come from his father. When Dante calls him a vampire during the siege, Rita answers, "I'm not a vampire. This is Vietnam." The episodes do not say what his doctor and church officials really know (Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: Disappearances in Ballard
docs.text:
The disappearances in Ballard are the unexplained absence of more than half the town's high school students and many other residents, noticed by the task force in Walkers 06 and tied in Walkers 07 and 08 to the bodies stored in the gym ceiling and the Roosevelt morgue. (Walkers 06, Walkers 08)

Type Phenomenon Aliases missing townspeople phenomenon; missing students Location Ballard, Utah Cause Replacement of residents by the skinwalker faction, with the bodies stored in the school and later the Roosevelt morgue First appearance Walkers 06

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In Walkers 06, the Ballard sheriff, Sheriff McDermish, tells Kurt that a county spot-check found more than 50 percent of the high school's students absent, while the school's own attendance records "show no problems"; asked about it, the school called it "an oversight for today's numbers." He has phoned parents, and many do not pick up. At the houses he visited, those who answered each gave a different excuse for their child's absence, and others were empty, among them a trailer with mail piled up in the slot. The diner, which would usually hold ten or fifteen people at that time of day, has three, and there is no traffic. Rita's Andrew asks whether the absent were all Mormon, and the sheriff answers "Most of 'em. But that don't mean much." For the last few weeks, he says, things have felt a little weird. (Walkers 06)

The sheriff gives Kurt a Post-it with the names and addresses of the absent families and a Remington Model 870 shotgun, then leaves town with his son: "Anywhere but here." Kurt calls his boss Big Bill to ask that the Utah National Guard be put on standby. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Theories
docs.text: At the table, Dante's Kurt first suspects a giant fly, since the team has already fought a giant moth and something is consuming huge amounts of sugar. Zack's Huell wonders whether something is being preserved in the sugar, and Rita's Andrew lectures on Scandinavian folklore about trolls that feed on sugar. The anonymous note had also warned that "some of your friends aren't who you think." (Walkers 06) The sugar evidence, such as the packed fridge in City Hall, is collected at sugar clues.

docs.title: Development
docs.text: In Walkers 07 Kurt warns Walt "Coyote" Murphy that half the high school is missing and that people are covering it up, telling him to trust nobody, and briefs Robert Bigelow in the same terms. (Walkers 07) During the gym fire, the ceiling gives way and a tube of melted plastic falls, smelling of rot "like a really, really bad fridge." Huell unrolls it to find a putrefied corpse in white powder, and several more fall from the gym ceiling. Afterward the party recognizes the smell of a mass grave and reasons that the killing has been going on for at least a few months. (Walkers 07) See plastic-wrapped bodies.

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text: In Walkers 08, the team finds dozens upon dozens of bodies wrapped in plastic piled in the Roosevelt police station's morgue, leaking fluid onto the floor. Andre describes them as "the bodies from the library ceiling," evidently meaning the gym ceiling of Walkers 07. The party concludes that Ballard has been emptied except for Bigelow, that the leaders were taken over first, and that Roosevelt is now being "eaten" in the same way. (Walkers 08) See replication and pilot and host biology.

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: Why the victims were mostly Mormon is never explained; at the table it is both a joke about Utah and a clue.

docs.title: Ballard water contamination
docs.text:
The Ballard water contamination is a separate FBI case, first seen in Walkers 02, in which the public fountains and tap water of Ballard, Utah contain live sperm and arsenic, a mystery the task force warns locals about but never solves. (Walkers 02)

Type Phenomenon / side case Aliases live sperm in the water; fountain pervert case; tainted town water Location Ballard, Utah Cause Never established First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
On their first visit to the FBI Salt Lake City field office, Dante's Kurt rolls Investigate a Mystery (9) on the previous team's corkboard and learns that it concerns a different local case: "a spate of unacceptable levels of semen showing up in public water fountains." He notes it "in case it's related." Agent Carl Gardner says "We got a drinking fountain pervert to catch," and when Rita's Andrew asks whether the building's own fountains are safe, he calls for another drinking-fountain test kit. (Walkers 02)

At the ranch, Robert Bigelow already knows. His team measures everything, including the water, and has seen the sperm under a microscope: "They got tails and they swim around." Kurt reasons that live sperm means the culprit may be close. Bigelow's own guess is "perverts," and he adds that the water also contains a lot of arsenic, so his team uses reverse osmosis. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: Theories
docs.text: At the table, Dante jokes that if the cause is in his well water "gnomes is real," and Andre suggests CHUDs; Zack's Huell guesses a ghost, and a Post-it reading "perverts" goes up on the corkboard. (Walkers 02) In Walkers 03 the bartender Maggie reasons that the quantity points to bulk-purchased animal semen, probably horse, which would leave a paper trail, while Rita's Andrew suggests that it might be "on the fixtures" rather than in the supply. (Walkers 03)

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text: The party spreads a "don't drink the water" warning to everyone it meets: Walt "Coyote" Murphy, who answers "This is like a pervert thing"; the clerk at the Ballard general store; and others in town. Dante's Kurt says "We're from the government. Don't drink the water unless it's bottled or from a well." (Walkers 02) In Walkers 03, Huell and Kurt warn the sheriff off the tap water, and a drunk Huell tells Maggie that "there's cum in it." Dante half-confirms it as a matter "the bureau's looking into," and the Biz coins "Half-Gallon Howard" when Maggie jokes about men with ten-thousand-gallon output. (Walkers 03)

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The cause is never explained, and no later episode connects it to the skinwalkers.

docs.title: The Bigfoot Hoax
docs.text:
The Bigfoot Hoax is the staged series of Bigfoot sightings, footprints and photographs around Dahlonega, Georgia, which Jan Martense's gold-mining ring used to discredit real sightings of escaped ape-men.

Type Lore (cover story) Aliases fake Bigfoot sightings; faked Bigfoot prints; the Chewbacca figure; fake Bigfoot Region Dahlonega and Auraria, Georgia Responsible Jan's Conspiracy First appearance Appalachia 01 (sightings); Appalachia 02 (faked prints)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The team first meets Bigfoot as a local panic. Their case file lists four or five sightings in the last week, with a grainy Dahlonega Times photo. Huell Kendrick rolls well enough to learn that it looks like the Patterson-Gimlin film, but it could just as easily be a man in an ape costume. Sheriff Carter Burke says the recent sightings look "real fake" and are probably a prank. Kurt Larson tells him to report them all anyway, since a weirdo in an ape costume stealing a kid is not the craziest thing to cross his desk (Appalachia 01).

The staged sightings mingle with sightings of the real ape-men, and the investigators cannot tell them apart until Appalachia 09.

docs.title: The clean prints
docs.text: In Appalachia 02 the team searches near the circle where the Circle Chasers have been filming. Dick "The Biz" Baxter uses Investigate a Mystery and asks "What is being concealed here?" The answer is a pair of cleanly pressed giant footprints, about twice human size, with the edge of a sneaker print beside them and a cigarette butt. Kurt photographs everything and says he leans toward fake Bigfoot prints (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: The naked, hairy figure
docs.text: In Appalachia 04 Monica Cartwright tells the team that about a month before her son Gene vanished, a hairy, naked figure stood at the end of her driveway. She insists he "looked exactly like Chewbacca". He carried a backpack, was not facing the house, and got into the back of a black sedan. The sheriff dismissed the report, telling her she was drunk, which she admits she was (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: The dead man in the costume
docs.text:
In Appalachia 06 Frotter Comstock reports a dead Bigfoot on his land and refuses to touch it. The "squatch" is a man in an expensive Chewbacca costume soaked in real blood. Andrew recognizes the wound from Academy photographs of gangland executions: the back of the head has been blown out. The scene also turns up:

  • a snapped plaster-of-Paris toe and fake Bigfoot footprints in mud, with a broken edge on one mold and no sign of its pair, so some equipment is missing;
  • the costume's bandolier taken off, with mud rubbed into the fur;
  • faded Navy tattoos, including a trident, which the Biz and Kurt read as SEAL insignia. Kurt checks him against his own old unit: "he's not UTAW, he's not one of my boys" (Dante (as Kurt Larson), Appalachia 06).

The team traces the costume to the photographer Derek Edwards. He says he bought it for cash at Comic-Con and sent it to be dry cleaned, and it vanished from the rack at Apollo's eight months ago. The dry cleaner recognizes the dead man as an out-of-town drifter who stood watching and was sometimes on a walkie-talkie. At the Spud Hut, the counter kid says the man ordered on three occasions, four, nine and 25 days earlier, and a plant auditor says he is not on the employee list. At the Motel and Suites he was registered as "John Doe" (Appalachia 06).

Going through the garbage thrown out from his room, the team finds snakeskin boots with a coil of animal hair tucked in one and a walkie-talkie in the other, plus plastic bags, duct tape, and a briefcase whose lining hides a slot for a high-caliber handgun and about $10,000 in hundreds and twenties (Appalachia 06).

Kurt's working theory is that someone hired a SEAL or Marine to fake Bigfoot, perhaps to keep people off Spud Hut land, while a real ape-man hybrid also exists (Appalachia 06). In Appalachia 07 Andre names the dead man as Troy Cleaver. The team spends the found cash on dinner, and Rita (as Andrew Howard), reporting to Big Bill, says "We're not surveilling Bill Clinton. We're surveilling dead Chewbacca." (Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Explanation
docs.text:
In Appalachia 09 the worker Clive says the conspiracy had five people: himself, Jan, a mercenary who melted down the gold, and two bodyguards. When Kurt describes the dead man in the Bigfoot costume with ex-military tattoos, Clive realizes he must be the mercenary. He says he did not know where the mercenary got the costume and had told him "people was gonna know it was Chewbacca". Some workers had escaped and been seen, and Jan, worried about attention, wanted "some real fake ones to kind of discredit him" (Andre (as Clive), Appalachia 09).

Table running joke

Kurt dismisses the setup as "Scooby-Doo bullshit" and the players call the Circle Chasers the "Scooby gang" (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Who shot the man in the costume. Kurt suggests Jan, but the episodes never confirm it.
  • Whether Monica Cartwright's hairy figure was the same man in the costume. Her account fits, but it is never stated.

docs.title: Bivens lawsuit
docs.text:
The Bivens lawsuit is the legal action Rudy Giuliani warns the task force to expect after the shootout at the Safe Environment Fund's fence in the woods near Radford, Virginia.

Type Lore / legal fallout Aliases fence incident Parties The agents (Webster, Andrew, Kurt, Huell) versus the Safe Environment Fund and its guards Status Expected; no suit is ever shown being filed or resolved First appearance Radford Horrors 02 (the incident); Radford Horrors 03 (the warning)

docs.title: The fence incident
docs.text:
In Radford Horrors 02 the team follows the missing agents' map toward a squiggle marked in the woods and finds an eight-foot chain-link fence, topped with barbed wire and wrapped in privacy material printed with the Safe Environment Fund logo and "No trespassers. Keep out." The team climbs over; Daniel Webster gets caught on the barbed wire and Andrew lifts him down. Armed guards arrive on ATVs and warn them off. Webster screams "FBI! Get on the ground!" and levels his shotgun, but his Manipulate Someone roll (a 5) fails. A guard tases him for 1 harm and his shotgun goes off wide. Kurt Larson fires a burst into the air. Andrew Howard shoots a guard through the leg for 2 harm; as the guard tumbles down the hill he shoots Andrew in the chest, and the bullet slows to a stop an inch from him. The other guards put down their weapons after their boss orders them to stand down over the radio (Radford Horrors 02).

Webster radios in for an ambulance, and lawyers for the property owners turn up. They insist the agents need a warrant, and Kurt and Webster answer that they have probable cause at an active crime scene where federal agents went missing. The lawyers follow the team with cameras to the scribble. Andre tells the table that, for the record, the agents are legally in the wrong, which Rita disputes on the grounds that evidence at an active crime scene may be destroyed (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The warning
docs.text:
While the team waits at the Radford ER, Webster takes a call from Giuliani, who asks about "the thing with the fence". Webster claims probable cause, saying the guards refused to listen, shot at them and one agent fired back and put a man in hospital. Giuliani tells him (Radford Horrors 03):

  • a Bivens lawsuit, which lets the guards sue federal officers for damages over constitutional violations, is coming if the probable cause is disputed;
  • the FBI is seeking a retroactive warrant to cover the search so it does not fall under the "poison fruit" provision;
  • FBI counsel will decide whether the probable-cause claim can be defended in court;
  • a formal reprimand is possible, though it would be a different story had they found the missing agents.

Giuliani asks whether the team wants to press charges against the guard who tased them. Webster sees the charges as leverage against a suit, and Zack wants them extended to the guards' employers. Giuliani says the guard has already been fired, and that the property owners' lawyers have mentioned that one agent carried a spear gun. Kurt, out of the earshot of the call, insists it was "sporting goods equipment". Giuliani adds that the guard claims he did not believe the FBI would carry a spear gun and that he has a hearing impairment, which might let him argue he did not know they were agents (Radford Horrors 03). See Kurt's spear gun.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: In Radford Horrors 04 Andre mentions that Webster was reprimanded and told the president wants no more "cowboy shit" on the case. When Giuliani brings up the spear gun again, Webster brushes off the incident as an "unfriendly interaction with some locals" and Kurt rolls his eyes (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Black Sun
docs.text:
The Black Sun is the symbol that Robert Bigelow names when he shows the party a strange white ring recorded by his sky camera, tying it to its pagan roots, its appropriation by the Nazis, and to Revelation 6:12. (Walkers 05)

Type Lore / interpretation Aliases Revelation 6:12 Source Bigelow's reading of the ring First appearance Walkers 05

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
On the night of the electrical disturbance at the Sherman Ranch, a white floodlight-like glow wakes Bigelow, who phones the guest house to ask, "Do you folks see a light?" The party later finds his staff pausing the VHS tape on one frame. Bigelow points to the circle and says, "This was the light we saw. This is the sky. This is our sky camera." He asks Dante's Kurt whether he has heard of the Black Sun. Kurt guesses "the Nazi thing," and Bigelow answers that "The Nazis appropriated it, but it actually has a long history in pagan mythology." (Walkers 05)

Bigelow then asks whether Kurt knows his Bible, and quotes Revelation 6:12: "When he opened the sixth seal, I looked, and behold, there was a great earthquake, and the sun became black as sackcloth, and the full moon became like blood." Kurt objects that the ring looks pretty bright, and Bigelow replies, "But it's dark in the middle." Kurt adds that it is also lumpy, which Bigelow agrees is odd. (Walkers 05)

In motion the footage shows a bright white ring with a slightly purple glow, oscillating over several seconds. Bigelow calls it a clear-cut event, escalating nonlinearly for weeks, and says they "may be on the verge of making contact." (Walkers 05) The recording is covered at Bigelow's recordings, and the phenomenon itself, which returns in the final battle as a kilometer-wide ring, is covered at the white ring. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Reception
docs.text: No other character endorses Bigelow's interpretation. At the table Bigelow is dismissed as "a rich, crazy man" and an "eccentric enthusiast." Bigelow agrees to Kurt's request to put a big ring of cameras around the party's house. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: Later episodes treat the ring as part of the Sherman Ranch phenomenon and, in the final battle, as part of the field in which ferrous metal levitates, with no further reference to the symbol. Whether the Black Sun reading has any bearing on what the ring is is never established. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 05

docs.title: Chimney Passages
docs.text:
The Chimney Passages are a network of secret climbing routes cut into every chimney of the Roulet House, which let the intruder reach any major room from his hidden attic lair.

Type Lore (architecture) Location Roulet House First appearance Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Every chimney in the house has been modified in the same way, invisibly from the outside. Inside each flue are climbing notches and a gap in the side. On top of each chimney sits a flap that keeps the weather out, also blocks smoke from below, and can be lifted from inside as an exit. The agents had searched the house in Roulet Estate 01 and found no way into the attic (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Kurt breaks up furniture and lights a fire in one fireplace. The room fills with smoke, and he douses it ("My Vietnam instincts are tingling"), then uses a mirror and flashlight to see a gap in the chimney's side and the notches. The other chimneys prove to be the same, and the modifications cannot be seen from outside. Kurt and Andrew climb up; the Biz and Huell cannot fit. A gap where about five by six bricks have been removed opens into the hidden attic lair (Roulet Estate 02).

Andre tells Kurt that someone has lived in the attic for at least a year, probably without the owners' knowledge, and could enter every major room by chimney. The owners had added inside locks to their bedroom doors. The route accounts for the attic Polaroids of the sleeping Roulets (Roulet Estate 02).

Climbing down, Andrew hallucinates that the bricks around him turn into rolling muscle that swallows him, drops three feet onto Kurt, and is talked down by Dante (as Kurt) with "Is it really worse than your dad?" He then realizes that the water he has been drinking tastes strange (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The episodes do not say who built the passages: the intruder, or someone before him. Nor do they explain how the intruder moved so freely through the house without the Roulets noticing (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Clinton Surveillance Scandal
docs.text:
The Clinton Surveillance Scandal is the October 1992 news story, announced by a Georgia State Police official, that FBI agents had been spying on presidential candidate Bill Clinton in Dahlonega, Georgia. It made Dick "The Biz" Baxter briefly "the most hated cop in America".

Type Lore (political scandal, alternate-history election event) Aliases Bill Clinton wiretap scandal; Watergate-type story; the Clinton thing; the Clinton Polaroids Date October 1992 (Letterman epilogue on November 1, 1992) Place Dahlonega, Georgia Principals The Biz; Andrew Howard; Big Bill; Georgia State Police First appearance Appalachia 06 (the night-vision headset); Appalachia 07 (the press conference)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The scandal has its roots in a private errand. In Appalachia 01 the KGB tasks the Biz with planting a camera and microphone in room 111 of the Smith Hotel (see Spy Camera and Microphone), and he keeps the job from the rest of the team. A newspaper clipping in the same episode mentions that Clinton is giving a big campaign speech in Atlanta in the next couple of days (Appalachia 01).

The table never spells out what caused the scandal. The pieces the episodes provide are these:

  • At the start of Appalachia 06, state police officers searching the bushes outside the team's hotel find a night-vision headset. One says, "Bag it and tag it, the Secret Service fellows I want to take a look at that" (Appalachia 06).
  • In Appalachia 07 the sheriff relays what a friend at the state police told him: the Secret Service tipped them off, they found a piece of surveillance equipment, and its prints matched an FBI employee in the database (Appalachia 07).
  • In Walkers 01, Letterman asks the Biz about "the night vision goggles that the state police recovered", which they say they found in a rose bush. The Biz wants them back.

docs.title: The press conference
docs.text:
Donald McManley asks the team whether they have been watching the news. A state police official has held a press conference saying the FBI is in Dahlonega surveilling a presidential candidate, and fingerprints from something "recovered from the scene" match an unnamed FBI agent. Kurt Larson, long out of the country, does not know who Clinton is, and Andre reminds the table that the Democratic nominee is about to win an election in October 1992 (Appalachia 07).

Big Bill calls Andrew Howard and berates him. He says there are only four FBI officers in Dahlonega, demands a detailed inventory of everything the team has done in the last 50 hours, and asks how many people are dead. Andrew's answer leads to a plea of "We're not surveilling Bill Clinton. We're surveilling dead Chewbacca." Bill ends the call with "Don't have surveilled Bill Clinton" (Rita (as Andrew Howard) and Andre (as Big Bill), Appalachia 07).

The players treat the story as a distraction and a possible frame-up. The Biz suggests it is someone faking a Watergate-type smear, and the team wonders whether something was stolen from their stolen car. Later, in the mine, the Biz says he wishes the "state police creeps" would come down and see it, since it is "way weirder than Bill Clinton" (Ezra (as Dick "The Biz" Baxter), Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Media fallout
docs.text: By Appalachia 08 the team is dodging the press. At the Spud Hut plant a Fox 5 Atlanta crew recognizes "Andrew Howard with the FBI", and a reporter asks him on live TV about "the Bill Clinton wiretap" and whether it is "the next Watergate". Andrew answers "Nothing" and then "Thank you for your time". At the table, Dante jokes that the Biz has no bug left to plant on Jan Martense because he "used them all up on Clinton" (Appalachia 08).

docs.title: Aftermath and the 1992 election
docs.text:
The epilogue in Walkers 01 is set on November 1, 1992. It opens with Letterman's monologue, which jokes that the allegations "hit a lot harder when there's Polaroids". Letterman interviews the Biz as "the most hated cop in America". The Biz tells him none of the team knew Clinton was in town, and Letterman adds that, as he understands it, the Polaroids were taken with a Russian camera, which the Biz had not heard. Pressed on why a gold miner would spy on Clinton, the Biz offers "Maybe he's a Republican" (Ezra (as Dick "The Biz" Baxter), Walkers 01).

In the same episode President Bush tells Andrew he expects Clinton to be sitting in his chair in a couple of days. He does not believe it was coincidence that "some criminal with a bunch of ape-men" was surveilling Clinton in the same town as the task force, and calls it enemy action (see Enemy Action). Andre also tells the table that Ross Perot is polling above 45% in most polls since "the double scandal", and Bush clearly leads only in Texas (Walkers 01). In Walkers 08 Andre explains the alternate history: Perot needed "two October surprises", and both came from the same event, the incumbent caught spying on the challenger and the challenger caught in a sex scandal, "Watergate and Monica Lewinsky at the same time". See Alternate history.

The scandal follows the Biz into later arcs. At the Salt Lake City field office a staffer recognizes him as "the fella who spied on Clinton" and says Clinton "had it coming" (Walkers 02). In Ballard, the bartender says "you spied on Bill Clinton" (Walkers 03). Robert Bigelow tells the team that "a lot of interesting stories follow in your wake", and Zack (as Huell) raises the "Clinton thing" only to be told it "didn't even make the list" (Walkers 02).

docs.title: How the case ended
docs.text:
Unrecorded session

The finale of the Appalachia arc, Appalachia 10, was never recorded. Walkers 01 is the only account of how the case ended.

According to Letterman's questions in Walkers 01, Jan Martense, described as "the illegal gold miner for the food company", was the one surveilling Clinton. Jan is by then held at the CIA black site Omaha, and the Biz's night-vision monocular was recovered by the state police in a rose bush. When Kurt visits him, Jan is the one asking why the Spud Hut corporate facility exploded after he fled it (Walkers 01).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Which equipment was used to watch Clinton. The Biz's KGB errand and the Polaroids' Russian camera point the same way, but no one connects them aloud.
  • Why the KGB wanted a camera in room 111, and who was meant to be filmed.
  • How the Polaroids reached the press.
  • Appalachia 07 says the equipment's prints matched an FBI employee, while Walkers 01 puts Jan behind the camera. The episodes never reconcile the two.

docs.title: Cosmic microwave background surge
docs.text:
The cosmic microwave background surge (CMB spike) is a burst of cosmic microwave background radiation that Soviet detectors recorded and triangulated to the Marblehead nuclear incident, giving Boris Yeltsin his reason to question the Biz.

Type Lore / anomaly Aliases CMB spike Detected by Soviet (Russian) detectors Traced to Marblehead, Massachusetts First appearance Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In the Metropol opera house in Moscow, Yeltsin asks Dick "The Biz" Baxter whether he knows what the galactic cosmic microwave background is. Ezra decides the Biz has only a vague memory of it from college, and Andre notes that it was discovered in 1964. Yeltsin explains it as "a kind of echo" of the Big Bang. The Soviets built detectors to study it, and "last year" they spiked, registering an unusual surge. When they triangulated the source, it coincided with the nuclear incident in Marblehead. "Nuclear reactors do not emit cosmic microwave background," Yeltsin says (Radford Horrors 01). See The Marblehead explosion.

docs.title: Role in the Biz's interrogation
docs.text:
The surge leads Yeltsin into a longer conversation about Marblehead. The Biz sticks to a vague version of events: the military got involved, he was there in an advisory capacity, and he does not know what munitions were used. He does not admit that the team deployed a very small nuclear weapon against the creature in the water. Yeltsin already knows about the engineered, weaponized worms and says Russian intelligence suggests there was "another organism, or something like an organism". The Biz confirms there was a huge sea creature connected to the worms. He did not go down in the submarine, but he saw it chase their car, "a big, confusing grub creature with rings rotating around it" (Radford Horrors 01). See The angel thing.

Yeltsin never says outright that the creature caused the surge, and the episodes never explain it.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: The same conversation covers other matters: Yeltsin says Russia is "developing a test" for people who are not who they seem, and shows the Biz a broken, half-melted copy of the flashlight weapon, taken from a man wearing very dark, welding-style glasses (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Covenant Beliefs
docs.text:
Covenant Beliefs are the doctrines and rites of the Covenant, the religious community led by Elijah Ray in the Georgia ghost town of Auraria: a holy meteor, Auraria as the Garden of Eden, a coming apocalypse, visions from a peach drink, and baptism in red clay.

Type Lore (religion) Aliases meteor clay; Garden of Eden; red-clay river baptism; clay god Followers The Covenant Leader Elijah Ray First appearance Appalachia 02

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: In Appalachia 04 Andre summarizes the faith for the table. The Covenant holds that the community has returned to the original site of the Garden of Eden, the only place that will be preserved "when the earth turns up and consumes everyone in the biblical apocalypse". They are, he says, technically Protestants, in that direct communion with God is possible, but they also believe their leader has a special relationship with God and is a prophet, "not, like, Jesus 2.0". Auraria is a real Georgia gold-rush ghost town, and a local tells the team in Appalachia 01 that religious folks took it over about ten years earlier (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 04).

docs.title: Origin
docs.text: According to Primenthol "Prim" Greengrass, who left the church, Elijah Ray had a prophetic dream and then heard on TV about a shooting star over the area. A few days later he moved the congregation out to cheap land and started trying to grow potatoes. The Covenant believes a holy meteor struck nearby and infused the local clay with divine energy. Prim says much of the doctrine fails the "sniff test" (Andre (as Prim Greengrass), Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Auraria as Eden
docs.text: Mother Dahlia Riversand and the member River describe Auraria as "the promised land, the Garden of Eden". River says Elijah Ray called the people pressing the community to leave "agents of Satan, come to take this away from us" (Andre (as River), Appalachia 04). See The Land Dispute.

docs.title: Daily practice
docs.text: Members do not eat meat. Dahlia runs a one-room schoolhouse teaching Latin and times tables, and Elijah Ray teaches a comparative religion course there and is said to have taught at Harvard. The camp has no electricity (Appalachia 04). Members live in white tents, plus the old church and a community building, in robes or sack dresses (Appalachia 02). Prim and Willow were renamed in the group's style at age three, and Elijah Ray has several wives; Prim calls him "a pretty nice guy. For a bigamist" (Appalachia 02). River says Elijah Ray encourages members not to spend too much time with family and to focus on "our new family and God" (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: The peach drink and visions
docs.text: The ritual drink is a jar of dark liquid with peaches floating in it. Prim says peaches alone would not give visions, but "they are if you grow the right funguses", and warns "if they offer you a vision quest, don't take it" (Andre (as Prim Greengrass), Appalachia 02). Frotter Comstock tells the team he had been helping the community with a methanol problem in the drink, caused by their insistence on fermenting with natural yeast (Appalachia 02). See Covenant Peach Preserves for the related product the community sells.

docs.title: Red-clay baptism
docs.text:
The cold open of Appalachia 04 shows the rite. At night a door-to-door vacuum cleaner salesman (Jeremy) changes into a thin white robe and follows a candlelit path to a river red with clay. Four women in white dresses kneel in the mud. An older man with high cheekbones kisses his forehead and hands him the peach drink, which he drinks deeply. The man chants in Latin, wades in holding a candle and plunges the salesman into the mud, and he vanishes beneath the surface (Appalachia 04).

In the daytime scene Dahlia offers the team a place at "the baptism this evening" for a salesman they talked into joining. He is waiting in a preparation tent for his "rebirth and renaming", and Andrew speaks to him through the tent wall. The team does not intervene and moves on to other leads (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Whether the red clay is truly special. The players' guesses range from the "clay god" to contamination: River says the community bathes in the river despite a lot of runoff from the Spud Hut plant, and the women suffer frequent yeast infections (Appalachia 04).
  • Whether the older man in the cold open is Elijah Ray, and what happened to Jeremy.
  • Whether the peach drink played any part in Willow's disappearance.

docs.text:

  • Appalachia 02
  • Appalachia 04

docs.title: The Crack in the Air
docs.text:
The Crack in the Air is a hard-edged rift in space in a side tunnel of the Dahlonega mines, with a metal pipe running through it that pumps gas into the mine. The party found it in Appalachia 09.

Type Lore (anomaly) Aliases portal; rift Location A side tunnel in the Dahlonega Gold Mines beneath the Spud Hut plant First appearance Appalachia 09

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The side tunnel is lit with rippling light, like pool caustics, around a hard-edged cut in space "as if cut with a scalpel". A metal pipe passes through the crack and hisses gas. Through the opening the party sees faint industrial machinery in darkness. Flashlight beams do not pass through normally. Standing close electrifies and freezes the fingers. Andrew Howard compares its edge to the "absence" from his pepper spray (Appalachia 09). See Andrew's Pepper Spray.

docs.title: Properties
docs.text:
• The gas. The party hears the hissing before they find the crack. Voices go high-pitched, like a Mickey Mouse impression, but nobody feels lightheaded, and the effect fades with distance. Kurt Larson guesses hydrogen, bans gunfire and sparks, and gets everyone out. He tries to pack the pipe (Appalachia 09).
  • The pipe. Kurt calls it "such a jackass redneck solution with such space-age technology". The players treat the arrangement as portal technology used to siphon gas, far beyond anything Spud Hut should have, and Kurt wonders what stage of life someone on the other side could be in to use it this way (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: History
docs.text: Clive, the animal handler, says that as far as he knows Jan has no portal. Kurt answers, "Somebody fucking does" (Dante (as Kurt Larson), Appalachia 09). Dick "The Biz" Baxter sets the timer on his spy camera and photographs the crack, including through it. His fingers feel electrified and freezing, but he gets the shot. See Spy Camera and Microphone. Afterward Kurt fears that someone will blow up the mine with hydrogen (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Later accounts
docs.text:
Unrecorded session

The finale of the Appalachia arc was never recorded. Everything below is known only from the epilogue, Walkers 01.

The Spud Hut corporate facility exploded shortly after Jan fled it. Visiting the imprisoned Jan, Kurt says that explosive gas was piped into the mines deliberately, probably from an adjacent cavern, and that the culprit is unknown. Jan can name no one with an interest in the mines. Kurt tells the table he is "not fucking telling him about the portal", since Jan seems not to know of it (Walkers 01).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Who is on the other side, and whether it was meant to kill, flood or blow up the mine.
  • Whether the crack is tied to the ape-men. Rita (as Andrew Howard) asks whether extraterrestrial ape-men would have portal technology (Appalachia 09).
  • Who built the pipe, and whether it is the source of the later explosion.
  • What the Biz's photographs show. The episodes never mention the film again.
