docs.title: The paranatural
docs.text: The paranatural is the catch-all term for the creatures, technologies and unexplained events that the Paranatural Incident Task Force is sent to investigate. This page surveys what the task force has met in each case, the patterns that recur between cases, how magic works at the table, and how the authorities hide all of it. For the questions that remain open, see Unresolved mysteries.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The campaign never hands the agents a single explanation. Each case has its own threat, and most cases turn out to contain two unrelated things at once. The table noticed the habit itself: Dante listed "a cult and aliens" and "a cult and worms", Ezra said it had been two things every time, and Zack asked whether the gold mine with Yeti hybrids was really just one. (Roulet Estate 02)

Three rules of thumb hold across the campaign:

  • The strange is physical. Almost everything the team meets bleeds, smells, leaves residue and can be shot, burned or run over. Andrew Howard puts the house view plainly: ghosts are not real because they have no physical body, the "astral body" is a name for kinds of telepathic communication, and the things people call angels are real beings whose bodies nobody comprehends. (Walkers 06)
  • Not every case is real. By the Georgia case Andre says the task force has handled about ten cases, most of which "washed out" too quickly to be shown. Kurt Larson later says he cannot have "another Kansas City" on his hands, a case that is never described. (Appalachia 04, Appalachia 09)
  • Human crime runs alongside the monster. In Radford a hypnotized boy did the killing for the creature, and a drug trade ran through the same town. Andre remarked early on, "I think the greatest monster is man." (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 08)

In the fiction the government tracks such things with the Atolean Paranatural Index, which counts UFO and cryptid sightings per capita. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
The first case centers on the Radford Moth: a car-sized, telepathic creature resembling a giant Morpho menelaus, first taken for a silent UFO that flared blue when lit. It hypnotizes with the light of its wings, can make a victim act against their will, drains flesh and blood through a proboscis, and is badly hurt by fire. It was raised from a larva by Wilbur Whateley, who was mentally bound to it and felt its pain. It took dogs from yards along the forest (see Radford's missing dogs) and left a chalky white powder and a smell of rot and compost wherever it fed. The moth died in the church fire, and its body was taken away before the team returned. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08)

The same case introduces the Spaceman, which proved to be Wilbur in a spacesuit, and Agent Murphy, a man with an NSA badge and a burning flashlight weapon. The scorched papers in his briefcase include the words "Menelaus", "local resources" and "unknown servitor act[ivity]". (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Marblehead holds two threats. The first is the worms, a parasite spread through the communion wine of the Sons of Adam. Early infection gives vigor and the glow; late infection turns people and animals into bloated worm bags that keep moving after decapitation. Fire, salt and alcohol kill the worms. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05)

The second is the angel thing, a glowing, ringed creature in the sea whose hum threatens a submarine and which closes on it at 60 to 70 knots. It survives a half-kiloton warhead from the M28 Davy Crockett and dies only when Andrew hits it with the flashlight weapon, sprouting the legs of every kind of animal before burning out in a crater. Drips of volcanic glass on the lighthouse wall (see Melted shoreline) point to something extremely hot on that coast, though no episode says what melted it. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 06)

A third party is also present: the people of the radio contact, whose lost advance team brought the synthetic nerve agent that leaked into the harbor when they were blown up. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
The Georgia case splits into a hoax and a real thing. The Bigfoot in the newspapers is Troy Cleaver in a Chewbacca costume (see The Bigfoot Hoax). The pale, immensely strong creatures in the mines are the ape-men: fast-growing hominids kept on ketamine and worked as gold miners by Jan Martense under the Spud Hut plant, each wearing an arm band with a blinking red light. The largest, Big Bob, hunts the party through the tunnels. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 06, Appalachia 09)

Deep in the mine the team also finds the Crack in the Air, a cut in space lit by rippling light, with a metal pipe coming through it and gas hissing from the pipe. Nothing else in the mine is on that level. The visions of the Covenant, by contrast, come from a hallucinogenic fungus in their peach preserves. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 09)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
The Utah case has the most layers. On the surface is the Sherman Ranch phenomenon: a night hum, electromagnetic spikes, livestock mutilations, the dusk event, the vanishing car, the night event, the beam and the white ring. Around the ranch move upright coyotes and upright horses, animals that act with intent. (Walkers 02, Walkers 05, Walkers 07)

Underneath are the skinwalkers: small brain-like "pilot" organisms that ride in copies of real people and can eat only sugar (see Pilot and host biology, Replication and Sugar clues). They replaced the leaders of Ballard first and stored the originals as plastic-wrapped bodies. They copied Andrew (see Andrew Howard (duplicate)) and Huell Kendrick (see Skinwalker Huell). (Walkers 07, Walkers 08)

At the bottom is the portal in the cavern, a machine built into a dead grub-angel, through which the skinwalkers were carrying tanks of blood. Black triangular craft and hazmat teams then close the site. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text: Rhode Island is the campaign's great fake-out. The grey figure in the woods traces back to the Roulet Intruder, a man in a foam-latex mask who had been living in the attic. The house's water was drugged (see The Drugged Water), which leaves the household's visitations by the Greys and the lights and eyes in the woods impossible to sort into real and imagined. The plainly paranatural element of the arc is Andrew's condition. (Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text: The return to Radford opens with the missing FBI task force being killed by the Radford woods predators beneath the hanging figures. The team finds moth-scented pearlescent goo at a scrubbed site, and a small moth-like intruder is carried off by the gray van crew. Wilbur reveals that the moth was pregnant and needed hosts, "like a parasitic wasp" (see Moth life cycle). In Russia, the Biz sees a crashed triangular craft and its survivor, who names the servitors. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Recurring patterns
docs.text: Few of these links are confirmed in the episodes. Each entry below says what is stated on screen and what is only a resemblance.

docs.title: Angels
docs.text:
Beings called angels appear in three arcs. The Sons of Adam preach that angels are terrifying monsters built by God (Summer Service 01). Andre calls the Marblehead sea creature an angel, and when the team sees the machine in the Utah cavern he tells them the dead creature it is built into is "one of those"; Zack remembers it as "a biblical angel" (Summer Service 06, Walkers 09). This is the one link between cases that the game master states outright.

The anonymous note left for Andrew in Ballard says its writer knows he is not one of the replaced because "you have angels"; Andrew replies that he has no angels, only something people call by that name (Walkers 06). Boris Yeltsin later says Soviet detectors recorded a cosmic microwave background surge whose source coincided with the nuclear incident at Marblehead (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: The flashlight weapons and their owners
docs.text:
The flashlight weapon gives a blinding blue-purple flash with an electric clacking sound, sets clothing and trees alight, and can overheat and destroy itself. Kurt refuses to believe the NSA has a beam weapon the CIA lacked. (Radford Horror 03)

Seen Holder Source Radford mountain road Agent Murphy. His device overheats and he vanishes in a pulse of light; the team finds his half-burned remains the next day on a circle of ground melted to glass (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04) Old-town church The cleanup crew. The team takes one from a searcher who also wears the shadow poncho (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08) Marblehead The team, against a worm-ridden dog and then the angel thing (Summer Service 05, Summer Service 06) Utah Kurt's flame light, used on the killdozer's boarders; in the cavern it glows and melts itself (Walkers 09) Russia A broken, half-melted copy held by Yeltsin, taken from a man in very dark glasses "like welding glasses" (Radford Horrors 01)

Two men carrying NSA identification were struck by cars while crossing a road at night in black suits: Murphy in Virginia, and, in Georgia, the man from whom Jan Martense took the ape woman Shelly. Dante's reaction at the table: "Maybe they're aliens and they're unaware of Earth customs, like look both ways." No episode says the two men served the same employer. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Cleanup crews
docs.text:
Most of the real cases end with strangers arriving to remove the evidence.

  • Radford, 1992: soldiers without insignia and men in metal "volcanologist" suits with flamethrowers clean out the burned church and remove the moth's body. Kurt's complaint afterward is that nobody knows who they work for or how they knew about the moth when the task force did not. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08)
  • Marblehead: the mystery covert group behind the radio contact supplies a poison for the worms, and the contact says plainly that all the infected will have to be killed. (Summer Service 06)
  • Dahlonega: the plant explodes shortly after Jan flees. Kurt tells Jan that some other force filled the mines with explosive gas. The explosion itself happened in an unrecorded session and is known only from Walkers 01. (Walkers 01)
  • Utah: black triangles, hazmat teams and a white powder that falls from the sky, a mild amnesiac that costs most of the soldiers present about twenty hours of memory (see Utah cleanup crew). (Walkers 09, Roulet Estate 01)
  • Radford, 1993: the gray van crew and the Safe Environment Fund, with bleach, fences and lawyers. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03)

It is never established whether any of these groups are the same organization.

docs.title: Portals and resources
docs.text: When the team sees the Utah portal, the players ask whether it is like the Georgia crack. Andre answers that it has similar qualities but does not open onto the same place (Walkers 09). Both move material: gas into the mine, tanks of blood out of the cavern. After the Russian crash survivor says that servitors "need resources", Dante points out that the team has seen resources going through portals before, and the Biz tells Yeltsin as much, adding that it "presented differently" (Radford Horrors 04). Kurt holds that the portal and the scale of the Utah operation imply "some greater intelligence" behind the skinwalkers, who individually were good mimics and poor strategists (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: "Survey" and the servitors
docs.text:
Quote

"Not aliens. The opposite of aliens."

Andre (as the crash survivor), to Yeltsin (Radford Horrors 04)

Asked why it is here, the survivor answers "Survey." The word "servitor" had already appeared a year earlier in Murphy's burned papers, alongside "Menelaus", the species name of the moth, and a fragment Kurt read as "...and the clock survey". Kurt said the pages looked like no classified NSA document he had seen, and the Biz wondered whether they were planted to trace a leak. The Biz tells Yeltsin he has not heard of servitors. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Hosts and riders
docs.text: Three unrelated threats work by occupying a body: the moth held Wilbur as a thrall and needed human hosts to breed, the worms hollow out people and animals, and the skinwalker pilots drive copied bodies. In Utah a fourth rider leaves the naked intruder when Andrew casts it out. No episode connects the four. (Radford Horrors 04, Summer Service 03, Walkers 07, Walkers 08)

docs.title: The Masters and Andrew
docs.text: Andrew belongs to the Aetherius Society, which teaches that the Masters, ascended extraterrestrials, guide humanity and that Jesus was one. The church issues him equipment that works: the church mace and later pepper spray that project an erasing "nothing", a pendant that turns aside blows, and a satchel that holds more than it should. His superior Mr. King tells him he is not wholly of this world. The moth calls him "Changeling" and, dying, cries that he knows the ones who made it. After he dies in Utah and returns (see Andrew Howard (the Monstrous)), he is faster, harder to kill and craves blood. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 07, Walkers 08, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Hoaxes and misdirection
docs.text: The campaign repeatedly dresses ordinary people as monsters: the Spaceman, the Chewbacca-suited Bigfoot, and the masked "Grey" of Rhode Island. In each case a real paranatural thing sits beside the fake. (Radford Horror 08, Appalachia 06, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: How magic works at this table
docs.text:
The campaign uses Monster of the Week; see Game mechanics for the rules in full. Magic is rare, costly and almost entirely Andrew's.

  • Healing. Andrew's laying on of hands works because higher powers act through the healer, and the healer pays: he takes part of the harm himself, shown as worsening nosebleeds. When Andrew returns from death as the Monstrous, Rita gives up laying on of hands and Cast Out Evil, reasoning that the change has cut him off from their source; Andre suggests that his humanity had been guiding his powers, and that with less of it they come out nastier. (Radford Horror 03, Appalachia 01, Walkers 08)
  • Cast Out Evil drives a possessing thing out of a body. The emptied body dies within hours. (Walkers 07)
  • What I Need When I Need It lets Andrew draw any small object he could plausibly own from a space only he can reach (see the What I Need When I Need It bag). Rita keeps the move through the change of playbook. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08)
  • Use Magic is rolled with Weird and picks from a fixed list of effects, such as healing one harm, banishing a spirit, barring a place or portal, or speaking with something that shares no language. Andrew uses it to reach Wilbur's mind. (Radford Horrors 04)
  • Resisting. Hypnosis and mental attack are resisted with Weird. (Radford Horror 07)
  • Dread is a house mechanic borrowed from Lovecraft-style games: a Sharp or Weird roll to process horror. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05)

Kurt supplies the secular side. UTAW ran psychic exercises, and tulpas are a recurring half-joke: he thinks he may once have taken part in summoning one, "always heard Mothman was a tulpa", and admits "we never successfully summoned a tulpa". (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 08, Appalachia 06, Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: How the authorities cover things up
docs.text:
The task force's reports are classified under the code word SKYHOOK. It sits under the Foreign Influence Task Force of Big Bill Nelson, on the reasoning that alien visitations are foreign by definition. (Summer Service 03)

The agents do not see cover stories as their job. Big Bill handles them; under Ross Perot, Rudy Giuliani orders the team to establish an acceptable fact pattern for the first Radford case. (Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 01)

Case Official story Source Radford, 1992 A drug cartel, a church shootout and a fire (Radford Horror 08, Radford Horrors 02) Marblehead A nerve-agent cult and a rogue Soviet nuclear weapon; see Terrorist cover story (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01) Utah A cult compound under the community center whose members "went full Jonestown" and killed most of the town (Roulet Estate 01) Radford, 1993 The missing are in treatment in Los Angeles; see LA treatment cover story (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03)

The team keeps secrets of its own. It agrees to deny firing the Marblehead warhead, leaves Andrew's sleepwalking out of its reports, and keeps the Georgia portal to itself. (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 03, Walkers 01)

docs.title: Outside the canon
docs.text: The one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable has its own aliens, ki users and a werewolf president. It is non-canon and none of it applies here.

docs.title: The show
docs.text:
The show is the framing device of the whole campaign: every session of PITF is played as an episode of an early-1990s television series about the Paranatural Incident Task Force. Andre, the game master, narrates camera moves, cold opens, credits and title cards, and the players treat their characters as that show's cast.

This page covers the television devices only. For the stories themselves, see the episode guide.

docs.title: Premise
docs.text:
The device is set up in the first line of the first session. Andre opens with "If this were a TV show, which let's say it is" and describes a helicopter shot over a forest with white text in the corner of the screen: "Jefferson National Forest, Virginia, 1992." (Radford Horror 01)

The show is treated as a real production. Andre speaks of "the fiction of the TV show" when deciding where an episode cuts to credits, calls the team's meals at Spud Hut "kind of a plot point of the show", and credits "the producers of the show" with buying song rights. (Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 04, Roulet Estate 03)

The series is set in 1992 and 1993, in the alternate history in which Ross Perot becomes president. Its in-fiction chronology is on the timeline.

docs.title: Cold open
docs.text:
Nearly every session begins with a short scene before the credits. Of the 37 recorded canon sessions, 35 have one; Summer Service 05 and Walkers 08 start mid-scene instead. Almost all of them show something the player characters are not present for: a victim, a monster, a villain or a stranger cleaning up. In the third session Zack tries to act in the scene and is told "you're not here"; by the sixth the table expects it, and Ezra asks "Is there a cold open again?" (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 06)

The cold opens work as teasers and as clues. Several are only explained later. The fleeing woman of Radford Horror 05 is identified in the same session as Amanda Lucky, which Andre says makes the scene "presumably a flashback". The night-vision headset of Appalachia 06 belongs to the Biz. The face that rises from a tank in Walkers 07 is answered two sessions later by a second Huell eating Twizzlers outside the community center. (Radford Horror 05, Appalachia 06, Walkers 07, Walkers 09)

The full list is in the table below.

docs.title: Credits and title cards
docs.text:
The cold open ends on Andre's stock phrase, "we cut to credits". In the premiere he plays the intro music and describes the title sequence: double exposures of the characters' faces over "scenes of urban decay and supernatural cult imagery", with the cast "looking off into the middle distance, looking super serious, wearing suits". As the music tapers out, the name of the episode comes up in a plain white-on-black font: "The Radford Horror". (Radford Horror 01)

Each case has its own title. Andre shows the players "the new title screen for the show" when the second case begins, and a title card for Utah at the end of the Georgia epilogue. Individual episodes have no titles. (Radford Horror 08, Walkers 01)

Credits also close some episodes. Radford Horror 07 cuts to black on Kurt's last line, which the table settles as "Aw heck." Andre describes the end of Walkers 06 as the point where "we got to the closing credits". Radford Horrors 01 skips the credits after its cold open and holds them until the very end, where Ezra reads the new title aloud. (Radford Horror 07, Walkers 06, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Recaps
docs.text: The show has no scripted "previously on". After the credits Andre usually places the characters with a line such as "when we left off", or asks the table "who remembers where we were?" and lets the players reconstruct it. When a recap is needed he gives it himself, sometimes before the cold open, and once nearly forgets the cold open altogether: "Oh right, we should do the cold open." (Appalachia 07, Walkers 05, Walkers 07, Walkers 09, Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Camera and editing
docs.text:
Scenes are joined with editing terms: "we cut to", "we smash cut to", "we cut to an hour later". Andre calls shots such as "the camera tracks in on Andrew Howard's face", "a slow Hitchcock zoom" and "an establishing shot over Washington, DC", and the baptism cold open of Appalachia 04 switches to "a series of Dutch angles". (Radford Horror 05, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04, Radford Horrors 01)

On-screen text places and dates scenes. Location captions open three arcs: "Jefferson National Forest, Virginia, 1992", "Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest, 70 miles north of Atlanta" and "Inauguration Day, 1993". The Marblehead finale uses "A few hours ago" and "A few seconds from now", and the Rhode Island arc uses "78 days ago", "Twenty-five days ago" and "Present day". Subtitles introduce the Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp "(abandoned since 1962)" and translate Russian dialogue. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01, Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Music
docs.text: Andre scores the show live, starting with the intro music of the premiere. The players comment on his choices as they play, most often the Psycho strings and "Tubular Bells", which returns in several arcs. "Radar Love" plays in two cold opens. When the music fails, that is noted too: Andre stops a scene to say "This is the wrong music", and in Radford Horrors 02 the credit music cannot be played because Discord has broken it. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 07, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Endings and cliffhangers
docs.text: Most sessions simply stop at a convenient point. A few end on planned cliffhangers. In Radford Horror 04 Andre says "I have an opportunity to end on a cliffhanger, so I'm gonna do it" and has Molly Underhill take the agents aside to report a girl's body found by the interstate; the players answer with Law & Order "Dun-dun" stings. The Rhode Island arc ends on a phone call from the president and a cut to black. (Radford Horror 04, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Commercial breaks
docs.text: The show itself never cuts to commercial. The only commercial breaks are inside the fiction: the Late Night broadcast in the Walkers 01 cold open ends as it "prepares to cut to commercial", and backstage a production assistant tells the Biz to watch for the light that warns of a break. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Cold opens by episode
docs.text:
Episode Cold open Radford Horror 01 Helicopter shot over the Jefferson National Forest at twilight; something blue darts over the tree line. Radford Horror 02 A man in a dark suit watches through binoculars from a rooftop, swears at what he sees, and speeds off in a white van. Radford Horror 03 A pile of dog collars in the woods; footsteps, and one more collar is thrown on. Radford Horror 04 Beside burning trees, a coyote approaches a slumped, smoldering figure and begins to eat him. Radford Horror 05 A young woman in a bloody dress runs through the woods clutching her stomach; something passes overhead. A flashback to Amanda Lucky. Radford Horror 06 A teenager buries three Ziploc bags of cash in a dark yard. Radford Horror 07 A man in a suit sifts the ash where the team's assailant exploded, lights a cigarette and waves soldiers and men in reflective suits into the woods. Radford Horror 08 None for the Radford finale. Late in the session the next case opens on four men in an unlit boat aiming a mounted gun at something in the dark: "Mr. Miller, you may fire when ready." Everything explodes. Summer Service 01 Slow zoom into the mouth of a sea cave; something big moves inside. Summer Service 03 Jester carries a tray of food to a chained house at night; a dog growls behind the door and something thumps against it again and again. Summer Service 04 A woman of about ninety jogs through pouring rain and tells her daughter, "Pastor says God is coming." Summer Service 05 None. The session opens mid-scene. Summer Service 06 Two captioned scenes: Big Bill answers a phone in bed ("A few hours ago"), and the USS Oklahoma City fires on a contact that has come back from the shore and is closing at 80 knots ("A few seconds from now"). Appalachia 01 A woman carrying a sack of peaches through the Chattahoochee-Oconee National Forest is dragged off-screen. Appalachia 02 A Spud Hut worker, locked out on a smoke break, follows a sobbing sound into a fissure and is attacked. Appalachia 03 A gold mine tour; a boy with a Game Boy vanishes into a roped-off tunnel. Appalachia 04 A vacuum salesman changes into a white robe in a gas-lit tent, drinks from a jar of peaches and is plunged into a river red with clay. Appalachia 06 State police comb the bushes outside the hotel and bag a night-vision headset. Appalachia 07 A Spud Hut truck driver listens to "Radar Love" at sunset; something breaks out of the back and the truck crashes. Appalachia 08 The camera glides to the "Special Projects" doors and drops through the floor into a dark room of cages; a dozen eyes turn toward it. Appalachia 09 Jan Martense brushes past his secretary, loads a large animal crate into a red pickup and drives away. Walkers 01 An old television in a derelict room switches itself on to Late Night with David Letterman; someone breathes heavily behind the camera. Walkers 02 A rancher patrols at night and finds nothing. After he leaves, a coyote stands up on two legs. Walkers 03 Rows of human shapes wrapped in clear plastic in a dark industrial space; the last one moves. Walkers 04 A man in a desert trailer lifts a plate of Jell-O to his chin and grey tendrils spool out of his mouth. Walkers 05 A woman drives into the desert, is ringed by coyotes, and pours white powder down the throat of one of them. Walkers 06 A woman lets herself into the same trailer and finds cupboards full of Jell-O ("What the fuck, Doug") and a wrapped figure in a chair; Doug comes in behind her. Walkers 07 Tanks of dark liquid in a dim room; Huell's face rises from the last one. Walkers 08 None. The session opens mid-scene. Walkers 09 A high shot of the fortified community center, panning down to a wet, naked Huell eating Twizzlers beside a bulldozer. Roulet Estate 01 Caption: "Inauguration Day, 1993". The four agents lie ill in an abandoned living room; the Biz vomits into a Stetson. Roulet Estate 02 A nude man with an unnaturally shaped head loads shotgun shells one at a time in a dark, dusty space. Roulet Estate 03 The camera pans up from the back seat of the stolen car to a grey alien at the wheel, humming along to "Radar Love" as the fuel needle drops. Radford Horrors 01 Found-footage style: FBI agents are chased through snowy woods and picked off from above. Runs straight into the first scene with no credits. Radford Horrors 02 Workers in bunny suits comb fenced woods and bag a blood-streaked handgun; the camera pulls back to a "Safe Environment Fund" logo. Radford Horrors 03 A long pan down an aisle of pinball machines; a Taser cracks and a masked man carries a woman out. Radford Horrors 04 A slow pan over frozen Russian countryside to a triangular craft buried where a farmhouse used to be.

The one-shot Philosopher's Fist has no cold open or credits.

docs.title: Experiments with structure
docs.text:
• Vignettes. Arc openers follow the cold open with a solo scene for each character before the team assembles. (Appalachia 01, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Intercutting. The Georgia epilogue cuts between the Oval Office, a CIA black site and a talk-show set. (Walkers 01)
  • Non-linear opening. Roulet Estate 01 starts with the hangover, jumps back 78 days, forward to Christmas Eve, and returns by smash cut. Andre had realized that "the time skip skipped over Christmas", so the Christmas episode was done as a flashback. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Epilogue montage. After the pharmacy siege, each character gets a scene months later, staged as cuts with subtitles. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Two storylines. In The Radford Horrors the Biz's scenes in Russia alternate with the team's in Virginia. (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)
  • The scene after the episode. Walkers 08 continues after the other players have said good night, with Andre telling Rita, "So let's cut to the other Andrew Howard." (Walkers 08)
  • Scenes the cast does not see. For secrets, Andre asks the other players to leave the call, as with the Biz's KGB business. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Casting, credits and production jokes
docs.text:
• Guest stars. During the first title sequence Andre has the table roll to see whether Chevy Chase is in the show as a guest star. The result is a mixed success. (Radford Horror 01)
  • Joke credits. Zack adds "Made by Vagina Lovecat" to the first title sequence and "Created by Dick Wolf" to the first cliffhanger. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 04)
  • Casting. When an enormous naked intruder appears in Utah, Dante casts him at once as Ving Rhames, and Andre agrees. Zack had been about to say Laurence Fishburne. (Walkers 07)
  • Music rights. When "Radar Love" plays in the Roulet Estate 03 cold open, Andre says "the producers of the show sprang for the rights to another song this time". (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Sponsorship. The team eats at McDonald's so often that Andre says the table "should have negotiated a sponsorship deal". (Summer Service 05, Appalachia 01)

Quote

Dante (out of character): "We just really want you to associate the taste of McDonald's with worm parasites. That's just, you know, core part of our brand." (Summer Service 05)

  • Episode titles. The players supply their own. Dante titles the Rhode Island opener "The gang gets unemployed", and Zack says the latest episode would have been called "Opposite of Aliens". (Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 04)
  • The sequel. When the sixth arc is revealed as The Radford Horrors, plural, Dante and Zack say Andre "did an Aliens". (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Rejected cold opens. Dante pitches his own for the second case, "Amanda Lucky's corpse explodes and a thousand moths come out", and a narration gag after the real one: "Freeze frame. I'm Mothman. You're probably wondering how I got here." (Radford Horror 08)
  • Television inside the show. The characters watch a good deal of it. Watching Roseanne is Huell's "rock bottom", and the Biz's appearance on Late Night with David Letterman is itself a cold open. (Walkers 01, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The OVA: a show within the show
docs.text:
Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable is a one-shot played in a different game system with different characters, on a planet that is all one country and is run by a werewolf president. It is non-canon. (Philosopher's Fist)

It was tied to the main series afterwards. At the top of the next session of the campaign, Andre "decided, right, retroactively, that the stupid fucking shonen arc we did was an OVA that Huell watched on the hotel's cable TV as he was falling asleep". Because Zack had not been at the one-shot, Andre added that Andrew half remembers it from turning the television on at the Smith Hotel. That makes it an anime video playing on a television inside a television show. (Appalachia 02)

The one-shot has its own framing. Late in the session Andre shows the players "the title of the anime that we are in", which Dante reads out as "Three Point J over Two", and he encourages Rita to do "a dub voice". See the 1992 OVA framing. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Lost episodes
docs.text: Five sessions were played but never recorded: Summer Service 02 and "05.5", Appalachia 05 and 10, and Walkers "08.5". Their events are known only from later recaps. See Lost episodes.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The only cold open with no following credits is Radford Horrors 01. Andre: "This time we don't cut to credits." (Radford Horrors 01)
  • The recording of Appalachia 02 begins mid-recap because Andre forgot to start it. (Appalachia 02)
  • Andre noted "for the record" that he had written down the 4:30 a.m. pager call of Radford Horror 04 before the players chose to spend the night on excursions of their own. (Radford Horror 04)
  • The night after Andrew's sleepwalk, Andre begins the same smash cut a second time ("we slowly zoom in on Andrew's face as his eyes close, and then we smash cut") before admitting he is kidding. (Appalachia 03)
  • Kurt's interrogation of Jan Martense is short on screen. Andre explained that it "is quick for dramatic purposes, not for in-universe purposes". (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Timeline
docs.text:
The timeline is the chronology of in-fiction events in PITF, from the backstory of its towns and characters to the latest recorded session, Radford Horrors 04. The campaign runs from May 1992 to April 1993 in an alternate history of the United States.

Exact dates, such as 24 May 1992, were stated at the table. Dates marked "about" are worked out from statements such as "three years ago", and entries labelled "that night" or "the next day" give only the order of events. Where two episodes give dates that cannot both be right, the entry uses the better-supported one and the disagreement is listed under Date conflicts. The non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable takes place in another world and has no dates of its own; its only place on this timeline is as a program on a hotel television in October 1992.

docs.title: Distant past
docs.text:
• Colonial era. Radford's original settlement, the "old town" by the river, is destroyed by a flood. Only its stone church and a few other stone buildings survive. (Radford Horror 08)
  • 1800s. The Georgia gold rush founds Dahlonega. Cherokee land is seized, and the mass eviction becomes the Trail of Tears. Auraria is left a ghost town. The theory of Lemuria also dates from this century. (Appalachia 01, Summer Service 01)
  • Atomic bomb era. The Radford Arsenal makes guncotton for the atom bomb. Locals later say this cursed the town. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: 1950s to 1980s
docs.text:
• 2 November 1957. The Levelland, Texas case (stalled vehicles and a reported UFO), which Andrew Howard later cites as a precedent in Utah. (Walkers 03, Walkers 04)
  • 1960s. The Roulets marry; their wedding photos appear to have been taken in Arizona. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • 1962. The Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp is abandoned. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Vietnam War and after. Kurt Larson serves in Vietnam and then in UTAW, a CIA branch. He works with the fixer Carter for about five years and once saves his life. Iran-Contra, which was Carter's idea, ends both careers. (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 04, Roulet Estate 02)
  • Before the campaign, year not given. Daniel Webster, then at the State Department, handles US-side logistics for the rescue of Ross Perot's employees from Iran. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • About 1982. The Covenant takes over Auraria ("about 10 years ago"). (Appalachia 01)
  • Summer 1986. Walt Murphy spends six months trying to get people to call him "Coyote". (Walkers 02)
  • About 1987. Jan Martense, drunk on a Georgia back road, hits and kills a man in a black suit who carries NSA identification. In the man's van he finds an ape woman strapped to a gurney. He names her Shelly and sinks the body and car in a lake. He tells Kurt this was five years before his arrest. (Walkers 01)
  • June to August, about 1988. Wilbur Whateley finds a larva by the old-town church on 3 June and keeps it in the basement. It hatches on 15 August. (Radford Horror 08)
  • About April 1989. In Radford, thirteen-year-old Abelforth Whateley robs the Radio Shack in a homemade spacesuit (the Radio Shack spacesuit robbery) and is believed to have run away. Wilbur's journal for 16 to 18 April records what really happened to him. After his twin's disappearance Wilbur has a breakdown, crashes a car and is left in a vegetative state. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 08)

Wilbur's journal

The journal entries carry a day and month but no year. Andre confirms that 17 April lines up with the date Abelforth went missing, which the sheriff's office puts "three years ago" in May 1992. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: 1990 to spring 1992
docs.text:
• Winter 1990. Shelly Wilmarth dies on the family ranch in Utah, according to her obituary. (Walkers 01)
  • About November 1990. Irene Whateley begins treatment with Dr. Lawrence Lori ("a year and a half ago"). She stops about a year later. (Radford Horror 02)
  • About spring 1991. Jan Martense's gold-mining operation with the ape-men begins; in October 1992 he says he has been at it "a year and a half". (Appalachia 09)
  • May 1991 to September 1992. The Roulets record their "visitations" on labelled tapes. Someone lives hidden in their attic for at least a year. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)
  • About autumn 1991. "Corporate goons" arrive at Auraria with paperwork claiming the Covenant's land (the land dispute). (Appalachia 04)
  • About February 1992. A Chewbacca costume vanishes from a Dahlonega dry cleaner, eight months before it turns up on a corpse. (Appalachia 06)
  • Early May 1992. With the Soviet Union gone, President George H. W. Bush authorizes a paranormal task force, keeping a promise to his son. Andrew, Kurt, Dick "The Biz" Baxter and Huell Kendrick are reassigned to it a couple of weeks before their first case. (Radford Horror 01, Walkers 01)

docs.title: The Radford Horror (May–June 1992)
docs.text:
• 22 May 1992. Amanda Lucky, 17, vanishes from her third-story bedroom in Radford, Virginia. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02)
  • 24 May 1992. The Paranatural Incident Task Force assembles at its barbershop office at about 7 a.m., receives the Radford file, and drives four hours to the Pay n' Stay. (Radford Horror 01)
  • 25 May. In the morning Irene Whateley sees something from her kitchen window and walks into the woods. The team meets Sheriff Frank Roosevelt, searches the Lucky and Whateley houses and interviews Dr. Lori. After dark a white van tails them, a blue object flies over the mountain road, and Agent Murphy burns Kurt with a flashlight weapon before dying in an explosion. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03)
  • That night. Kurt is treated at the ER. The Biz sees the flying thing take a dog and photographs Lori's files. At 4:30 a.m. the agents' pagers go off. Phoebe Augustine has vanished in the night, and that morning Amanda's body is found by the interstate. (Radford Horror 04)
  • 26 May. Autopsy, the highway scene at about 11 a.m., and a town safety meeting in the evening. That night the team stakes out the town. Huell is carried into the air, a mummified body is found nailed up in the Whateley cellar, and Derek Augustine kidnaps Lori. The team waits out the night in the car; by morning Wilbur has vanished from his bed. (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06)
  • The next day. The team finds cash and heroin at the Lawson cabin, charters a plane, and at dusk fights the Radford Moth in the old-town church, rescuing Phoebe and Wilbur. A cleanup crew with flamethrowers closes in. The team takes a shadow poncho and a flashlight weapon from one of its men and is flown out by helicopter. Andre gives this day as 29 May (see Date conflicts). (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08)
  • Early June. In hospital the team agrees a cover story. Lori and Derek Augustine confess to abusing Amanda, and the killings are pinned on Wilbur. The burned church has been stripped of evidence. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The Summer Service (June 1992)
docs.text:
• Early June. An unexplained explosion off Marblehead, Massachusetts blows out windows and sickens residents. An EPA/USGS survey team sent to investigate is not heard from after its first couple of days in town. (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 01)
  • 15 June 1992. The Marblehead file reaches the office, where the air conditioning is broken. The team sets out and stops for the night in Jersey City, near Hoboken. (Radford Horror 08)
  • 16 June. Arrival at the Ram and Arms Inn. The survey team's field notes describe residents who fell ill after the explosion. (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 01)
  • The first day in town. A severed arm washes up, the Biz steals a crystal sphere from Jester, and the team attends Amos Shaw's evening service and drinks his communion wine. (Summer Service 01)

Unrecorded session

Summer Service 02 was never recorded. Its events are known only from later episodes: the team dived in an experimental submarine, found a sunken stealth vessel with a piece cut out of it, hid from a humming, light-covered vessel, and were exposed to the nerve agent in the water. (Summer Service 03)

  • That night and the next day. Huell finds Shaw's blood-soaked house. The wine proves to be full of worms. Big Bill escalates the case toward the White House. At the lighthouse the team finds an interrogation site and the scientists' field journal. A tropical depression moves in. (Summer Service 03)
  • Storm day. The team sends for Ivermectin, obtains a Davy Crockett nuclear device through Carter, and faces the Board of Selectmen in the evening. The Biz decodes a message from Russian intelligence. (Summer Service 04)
  • That night. At his island house the team destroys Arnold Weathers and his dog Puddles, both far gone with worms. Before dawn police and church members besiege the hotel and the team escapes with Donald McManley. Tropical Storm Andrew 2 cuts off the town. (Summer Service 05)

Unrecorded session

A session known as "05.5" was never recorded. Its events are known only from references in the finale: the team found the missing researchers alive, fought worm bags, set off a claymore on a truck and was contacted by radio by an unidentified military group. (Summer Service 06)

  • Finale. In the rain the angel thing comes ashore at the nuclear power plant. Huell fires the Davy Crockett and Andrew finishes the creature with the flashlight weapon. The National Guard takes control of Marblehead under a terrorist cover story. Andrew says the team has been in town "less than a week"; Kurt later tells Congress it was "about three or four days". (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01)
  • Aftermath. Soviet detectors record a surge in the cosmic microwave background and trace it to Marblehead. The EPA and NRC clean up and impound the team's car. (Radford Horrors 01, Appalachia 01)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia (October 1992)
docs.text:
• Late September. Gene Cartwright, 7, is taken from a field behind a Dahlonega trailer park, about a week before the case is assigned. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)
  • Sunday 3 October 1992. Kurt testifies to a House subcommittee about Marblehead. The Biz accepts a job from his KGB contacts by book cipher. Huell visits a shaken McManley. Andrew sees his church's doctor. Willow Greengrass goes missing near Auraria. (Appalachia 01)
  • Monday 4 October. The Dahlonega file arrives: two disappearances and a run of Bigfoot sightings. (Appalachia 01)
  • Tuesday 5 October. The team leaves at 8:45 a.m. and reaches the Smith Hotel at about 7 p.m. Huell falls asleep to an OVA on the hotel cable, which is how the one-shot Philosopher's Fist fits into the fiction. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)
  • Wednesday 6 October. The team meets the Circle Chasers and Sheriff Carter Burke, interviews the families, eats at the Spud Hut and finds faked Bigfoot prints. That night the Biz plants his camera and microphone in room 111. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)
  • Thursday 7 October. Andrew sleepwalks into the woods and wakes before dawn holding a bloody lighter. The team finds the death cave. A German boy, Frederick, vanishes on a gold mine tour, and a pale creature mauls Kurt in a hidden tunnel. In the afternoon the team hands evidence to McManley and visits the Covenant, where a salesman is to be baptized that evening. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04)

Unrecorded session

Appalachia 05 was never recorded. Its events are known only from the next session's recap: the Biz spent a night away on business of his own and came back with a badly twisted ankle, and the hotel door next to the team's was broken down. (Appalachia 06)

  • Friday 8 October. In the morning state police find a night-vision headset in the bushes outside the hotel. Frotter Comstock's "dead Bigfoot" is Troy Cleaver, shot in the back of the head in the stolen Chewbacca costume. That evening the Clinton surveillance scandal breaks at a state police press conference. A Spud Hut truck is found wrecked, its cab bloody and its cargo dirt. (Appalachia 06, Appalachia 07)
  • The following day. At the Spud Hut distribution center, Jan Martense leaves the team in the Special Projects level with a pack of ape-men. The team crosses the gold mines, finds the crack in the air, kills Big Bob and climbs out into the woods. (Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09)

Unrecorded session

Appalachia 10, the finale, was never recorded. Its events are known only from references in the next arc: Kurt shot Jan, Jan shot Andrew in the face, a falling ape broke Jan's skull, the Biz shot a man in the woods and had a heart attack, and the plant exploded the same day. Jan was taken to Black Site Omaha. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin (October–November 1992)
docs.text:
Election Day, 3 November 1992, is the fixed point of this arc. The Utah dates below are counted back from it; the Washington scenes of Walkers 01 are dated later than that count allows (see Date conflicts).

  • Late October. With the election a few days away, the Biz appears on Late Night with David Letterman as "the most hated cop in America". President Bush tells Andrew he suspects enemy action, and Kurt interviews Jan at Omaha. The next day Alberta Wilmarth asks Andrew to have her dead mother exhumed. (Walkers 01)
  • About 31 October. The team lands in Salt Lake City at about noon and drives to Sherman Ranch near Ballard, Utah, meeting Robert Bigelow. (Walkers 02)
  • The dusk event. At sunset an electrical event kills and moves the rental car. The team starts the exhumation request. (Walkers 03)
  • That night. On patrol with Walt, the team sees an upright coyote. In the small hours the rental car vanishes upward; it is found the next morning fused into a street in Roosevelt. (Walkers 04)
  • The night after. The night event hits the guest house: shared hallucinations, levitation, and a ring of light that Bigelow calls the Black Sun. The next morning radar shows a huge cavern under the ranch. (Walkers 05)
  • 2 November. Ballard is emptying. Sheriff McDermish flees the state, Huell is bitten, and Andrew gets an anonymous note calling him to the school gym. At the ranch a beam hurls sheet metal toward Roosevelt. Late that night a naked intruder breaks into the guest house. (Walkers 06, Walkers 07)
  • 3 November 1992, Election Day. After midnight, in the Ballard High School gym, Andrew is overpowered by his own double, and the replica leaves in his place. (Walkers 07)
  • Later that day. The phones are down. The team finds Roosevelt cut off and its police station massacred. McManley brings the first election news: the count is unfinished and Perot has taken Ohio. An autopsy shows some townspeople are engineered bodies with a non-human pilot. In the Roosevelt morgue the real Andrew returns to life as something else. (Walkers 08)

Unrecorded session

A session known as "08.5" was never recorded. Its events are known only from Andre's recap in the finale: the team rode horses around the roadblock, carried a generator to a radio station, called in the National Guard, fought through the bridge blockade and cleared the police station. (Walkers 09)

  • About 5 November. A Guard convoy attacks the community center. The real Andrew, missing for about two days, reappears and the replica is exposed. In the cavern below, the team wrecks the portal machine and the building collapses. Hazmat teams and black triangular craft move in. The radio reports that Ross Perot has won the election. (Walkers 09)
  • Aftermath. In a medical tent at the edge of Roosevelt the team learns that 300 to 400 people are dead across the two towns. Big Bill builds a cover story of a cult compound and a Jonestown-style killing. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: The Roulet Estate (December 1992–spring 1993)
docs.text:
• 24 December 1992. After fifty-three days of paperwork Andrew types his last Utah report. Big Bill tells the team that the President-elect has asked him to resign and will disband the task force on Inauguration Day, and hands Andrew a foil-wrapped letter. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • The eve of Inauguration Day, January 1993. Officials come to take the team's files. The agents get drunk in a dive bar and have Diane drive them about seven hours to Rhode Island, picking up a hitchhiking monk. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Inauguration Day, 1993. The agents wake in mid-afternoon in the abandoned Roulet house. A figure like a Grey, the Roulet Intruder, shoots Huell in the shin and Andrew in the face with a VSS rifle. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)
  • The Roulet house. The team finds the body of Margaret Roulet and a second body in the basement, the intruder steals their car, and they discover the attic lair and the drugged water. Big Bill is due to be fired the same day. (Roulet Estate 02)
  • The pharmacy siege. With police searching for the stolen car, the intruder takes hostages at a Brooks Pharmacy. The agents end the siege; he is a man in a mask. The Biz and Huell are badly shot. Andrew's healing fails and he feels a craving for blood (Andrew's condition). (Roulet Estate 03)
  • January 1993. The Biz is taken from his hospital bed by Russians and held at Vorkuta. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)
  • March 1993. Huell is on workers' compensation in a wheelchair. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Spring 1993. Kurt, back from an assignment in Sri Lanka, lectures to agents at Quantico. The Biz is flown to Moscow, where Boris Yeltsin questions him. Andrew, working on the World Trade Center bombing investigation in New York, takes a call from President Perot: "Something's happened in Virginia." (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors (spring 1993)
docs.text:
• About October 1992. The Douglas Pinball Emporium opens in Radford, about six months before the team's return. (Radford Horrors 03)
  • About February 1993. Gray vans appear in Radford, and Billy Thornton is dragged into one. (Radford Horrors 04)
  • Late March 1993. A five-agent FBI task force picked by Perot, sent to look into Radford's missing people, makes its last radio report about a week before the old team is called in. It is attacked from above in snowy woods and goes silent. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Early April 1993. The Biz, now a guest at the Hotel Metropol, joins Yeltsin at the opera. In Washington the others search the Biz's apartment and find his bug-out briefcase. Perot fires FBI Director William Sessions and installs Rudy Giuliani, who puts the team under Daniel Webster and asks for an acceptable fact pattern. It is "a little less than a year" since the first Radford case. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Return to Radford. In one afternoon and night the team walks into an IRS raid at the Ferry Lodge, finds the missing agents' camp, and trades fire with guards at the Safe Environment Fund site. During the night a rabid mouse bites Webster. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Meanwhile in Russia. In the middle of the night attackers ambush Yeltsin's convoy on the way to a crash site in Oryol Oblast. The Biz carries him to safety. (Radford Horrors 03)
  • The next day. Molly Underhill, now sheriff, reports that Elizabeth George has vanished from the Pinball Emporium. (Radford Horrors 03)
  • Latest events. At the Oryol crash site a survivor of a triangular craft tells the Biz it is "not aliens, the opposite of aliens". In Virginia the team learns a gray van crew took something from the emporium. Andrew heals Wilbur Whateley at a Roanoke hospital, and Wilbur describes the moth's life cycle. The team camps beside the missing agents' site to wait for McManley. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Date conflicts
docs.text:
• The Radford church fight. Radford Horror 01 dates the team's arrival to 24 May, and Radford Horror 02 to 07 follow them through three nights, which puts the church fight on 27 May. In Radford Horror 08 Andre says, "I think it's May 29th now." (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 08)
  • The Marblehead explosion. The briefing in Radford Horror 08 puts it "about a month" before 15 June. In Summer Service 01 two townspeople place it "about a week and a half ago". (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 01)
  • Arrival in Dahlonega. Appalachia 01 and 02 have the team drive down on Tuesday 5 October and start work on Wednesday the 6th, which makes the press conference of Appalachia 07 fall on the 8th. In Appalachia 04, a day later than Appalachia 02, Andre still calls it Wednesday, and in Appalachia 07 he says "we got here on the 4th of October" and that it is now the 7th. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 07)
  • The Utah case. In Walkers 01 Andre dates the Letterman taping to "November first" and Alberta Wilmarth's visit to "the day before the election", before the team has left Washington. Walkers 02 to 07 then show three nights in Utah before midnight brings Election Day, 3 November, and in Walkers 03 Ezra looks up the sunset for 30 October. (Walkers 01, Walkers 03, Walkers 07)
  • Shelly Wilmarth's death. In Walkers 01 her obituary gives winter 1990 and her daughter says "two years ago". In Walkers 05 Andre says she died "about two months ago". (Walkers 01, Walkers 05)
  • The Roulet captions. Roulet Estate 01 counts back from "Inauguration Day, 1993": "Twenty-five days ago" for the scene Andre sets on Christmas Eve, and "78 days ago" for the Roosevelt medical tent. Seventy-eight days before 20 January is Election Day itself, although Walkers 07 to 09 put the end of the Utah case at least two days after it. Later in Roulet Estate 01 Andre also calls the present "early January". (Roulet Estate 01, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Tropical Storm Andrew 2
docs.text:
Tropical Storm Andrew 2 is the Atlantic storm that arrives over Marblehead during the Summer Service case, flooding roads, grounding helicopters and delaying the National Guard, and whose name is a gag on the name of PC Andrew Howard.

Type Weather event Aliases Tropical depression; the storm Region Marblehead, Massachusetts Effect Flooding, washed-out roads, no air support, delayed reinforcements First appearance Summer Service 03 (as a tropical depression)

docs.title: Course of the storm
docs.text:
Summer Service 03. On the radio the team hears that a tropical depression is moving in from the Atlantic, which explains why the day is noticeably colder than the last few. Diane warns Andrew that the governor may call out the National Guard. (Summer Service 03)

Summer Service 04. The weather turns for the worse: a nasty cold wind off the sea, a yellowy-gray sky and then steady rain that keeps worsening. Storefront owners nail boards over their windows, and the mayor says he will be boarding up his own windows the next day because "a tropical storm" is coming in. Kurt's fever and joint pain get worse in the rain, and McManley's assistant Henry takes a Vespa to Salem through the storm to fetch the ivermectin. Big Bill says the Guard has run into weather trouble and washed-out roads and will probably arrive the next day. (Summer Service 04)

Summer Service 05. Rain blows in sideways. A woman at the inn is listening to the weather report, which names the storm "Andrew 2." Seawater spills across the bridge to the island, and Andrew's car hydroplanes through turns while following Madeline. When Zack's Huell demands a helicopter on the phone, Andre makes clear that the storm will keep one from being sent. The Guard is blocked about forty miles out and hopes to arrive by morning. Wind gusts later lift the team's modified vehicle onto two wheels. (Summer Service 05)

Summer Service 06. The freeway is flooded to wheel-well height and a few cars in the convoy flood out. A radio contact says his side has a "Casaba" that cannot be fired from the ground without killing the shooter, and that the wind speeds are too high to fly it. Big Bill's party spent two days stuck in feet of mud, and at the end of the case he is about 15 miles outside Marblehead, behind a stretch of road four feet underwater, waiting for a boat; he says, "Goddamn tropical storms." (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Role in the story
docs.text: The storm cuts the task force off from the help it requests: no helicopter, a delayed Guard and a Big Bill who cannot reach the town. It also grounds the radio contact's air-delivered weapon, which leaves the team's own Davy Crockett as the heavy option in the finale. (Summer Service 05, Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The name is a gag on the name of Rita's character, Andrew Howard; it is first heard as "Andrew 2" on the radio in Summer Service 05. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:

  • Summer Service 04
  • Summer Service 05
