docs.title: Unresolved mysteries
docs.text:
Unresolved mysteries collects the questions the campaign has left open as of the latest session, Radford Horrors 04. Each section sets out the evidence from the episodes, the theories the players voiced at the table, and, in a marked box, fan speculation. Speculation is not canon. For the established picture, see The paranatural.

Several sessions were never recorded (see Lost episodes), so a few of these threads may have been answered at the table without leaving a record.

docs.title: What are the servitors, and what is "Survey"?
docs.text:
The evidence. In Russia, Boris Yeltsin has doctors wake the survivor of a crashed triangular craft. Asked why it is here, it says "Survey." Asked about its people, the aliens, it answers:

Quote

"Not aliens. The opposite of aliens."

Andre (as the crash survivor) (Radford Horrors 04)

Its last words before passing out are "Servitors... need resources." Yeltsin adds the detail that puzzles him most: the survivor is taking O-negative blood, which should not work on an alien. (Radford Horrors 04)

The word is older than that scene. The burned papers of Agent Murphy in 1992 included the fragments "unknown servitor act[ivity]", "...and the clock survey", "Menelaus", "local resources", "acceptable leakage", "Salem, Colorado", "abstract/annihilation device", "religious ecstasy" and what looked like "Big Bill" (see Murphy's briefcase and documents). (Radford Horror 04)

At the table. In 1992 Kurt Larson said the pages looked like no classified NSA document he had seen, and the Biz described how counterintelligence plants doctored papers to trace leaks; Kurt answered that Murphy had fought too hard for the briefcase for it to be bait. In 1993 Zack's reading of "the opposite of aliens" was "to them, we're the aliens", and Ezra groaned that "the History Channel guy was right". Dante pointed out that the team has seen resources moved through portals before; the Biz passed that on to Yeltsin, with the caution that it "presented differently" and that he had never heard of servitors. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horrors 04)

Speculation

Murphy's papers put "servitor", "Menelaus" and "local resources" on the same pages a year before anyone said the word aloud. If they were genuine, his employers already classed the Radford Moth as servitor activity. "The opposite of aliens" taking human blood would fit something native to Earth, or made from people.

docs.title: Who was Agent Murphy, and who carries the flashlights?
docs.text:
The evidence. Murphy stepped into the road in a black suit, showed an NSA badge and told the team they were ruining his operation. His flashlight weapon overheated and he vanished in a pulse of light; the next day the team found the back half of him on a circle of ground melted to glass, with no trace of the device. The same weapon turns up with the cleanup crew at the old church and, as a broken copy taken from a man in dark glasses "like welding glasses", in Yeltsin's hands. A second man with NSA identification was run down at night in Georgia by Jan Martense, who took the ape woman Shelly from him. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 08, Walkers 01, Radford Horrors 01)

After Utah come hazmat teams, black triangular craft and a white powder that wipes about twenty hours of memory. Yeltsin's survivor came from a triangular craft too, though no episode connects the two. (Walkers 09, Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 04)

At the table. In Radford the Biz called it a secret NSA project; Kurt did not believe Murphy was NSA "for a fucking second". Dante joked that the two men hit by cars might be aliens who had never learned to look both ways, and George H. W. Bush half agreed, listing "something else altogether, from somewhere else" among possible enemies and reminding Andrew that "you hit one of them with your car". After the church, Kurt's standing complaint was that nobody knew who the men in heat suits worked for, or how they knew about the moth when the task force did not. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 08, Walkers 01)

Still open. Murphy's real identity and employer; whether the Radford crew of 1992, the Utah crews and the gray van crew of 1993 answer to the same people; and who employs any of them.

Speculation

The ground under Murphy was melted to glass, and so was the Marblehead shore (see Melted shoreline). The flashlight is also the only thing that killed the angel thing. The weapon may have been built with that kind of target in mind.

docs.title: What is Andrew Howard?
docs.text:
The evidence.

  • His church superior Mr. King tells him that Jesus and the Buddha "were not wholly of this world, and neither are you". (Radford Horror 01)
  • The moth calls him "Changeling" and, dying, cries "You know the ones who made me". (Radford Horror 07)
  • A voice at his ear tells him to "wake up and get your gun"; he sleepwalks in Georgia; he dreads the Shadow Men at night; and he dreams of a father with a Hollywood smile who keeps trying to kiss him (see Andrew's alien dad). (Summer Service 05, Appalachia 03, Walkers 01, Radford Horrors 03)
  • The anonymous note in Ballard says he cannot be one of the replaced because "you have angels". The writer is never identified. (Walkers 06)
  • Killed in Utah, he comes back to life at the bottom of the corpse pile in the Roosevelt morgue (see Andrew Howard (the Monstrous)). Afterward he craves human blood (see Andrew's condition). (Walkers 08, Roulet Estate 03)
  • The dream father mouths "Don't take it" shortly before a doctor arrives with rabies shots. (Radford Horrors 03)

At the table. Rita wondered whether the Aetherius Society knew what Andrew was and showed the world only "the clean side of it". Andre replied that the Society may not be getting the full story from whoever it is in contact with, and that Andrew's humanity had been guiding his powers until now. Kurt's suggestion for the dream father:

Quote

"Well, you know, it could be a tulpa, you know. It might be a dad tulpa. That wouldn't be the first dad tulpa."

Dante (as Kurt) (Radford Horrors 03)

Related: the next Master. Mr. King tells Andrew that the next of the Masters is coming, "maybe next year, maybe in three or four, but not ten", and that the church must fight "the forces of silence". Who the Master is, who the forces of silence are, and whether Mr. King's deadline is tied to anything the task force has met are all unanswered. (Radford Horror 01)

Speculation

The gray-skinned dream visitor of Marblehead also kissed Andrew, said "I wish I wasn't dead" and asked him to "give your mom a hug for me". He and the smiling dream father may be the same figure. If the Masters are whoever the Society is "in contact with", Andrew may be what they made him, which would explain why the moth thought he knew its makers.

docs.title: What are the angels?
docs.text:
The evidence. The angel thing shrugged off a nuclear warhead and died to a flashlight, sprouting the limbs of every kind of animal as it went. Earlier a dream visitor had warned Andrew to stay away from the water: "I think they damaged it. It can't cool itself anymore... It's not like the bug thing. I don't think you can hurt it." He suggested a nuclear strike and said that getting close would kill Andrew "or change you". The radio contact signs off with "Sorry about this, by the way. We didn't mean for it to get out." In Utah a long-dead creature of the same kind is wired into the portal machine; Andre confirms it is "one of those". (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 06, Walkers 09)

Yeltsin says Soviet instruments recorded a cosmic microwave background surge that coincided with the Marblehead incident, and that Russia has intelligence about another organism there besides the worms. (Radford Horrors 01)

At the table. Andrew first guessed an alien submarine. Kurt wondered whether the nerve agent and "the glowy thing" belonged to a rival faction trying to contain the worms. Andrew holds that angels are physical beings whose bodies nobody comprehends. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05, Walkers 06)

Still open. Who "they" were and how they damaged it; who the dead dream visitor was and how he knew about "the bug thing" in Radford; what melted the Marblehead shore; what moved in the sea cave in the opening shot of the arc; and why a dead angel can power a portal. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Who built the portals?
docs.text:
The evidence. The Crack in the Air under Dahlonega had a metal pipe through it hissing gas into the mine. The plant then exploded; Kurt told Jan Martense that "some other force" had filled the mines with gas, and the only person Jan could name with a grudge and the knowledge was the accountant Clyde Harvard. The Utah portal, by Andre's ruling, had similar qualities but opened somewhere else. Nobody learns who built the machine in the cavern. (Appalachia 09, Walkers 01, Walkers 09)

At the table.

Quote

"That's such a jackass redneck solution with such space-age technology."

Dante, on the pipe (Appalachia 09)

Rita (as Andrew) asked whether extraterrestrial ape-men would have portal technology. After Utah, Kurt argued that the portal and the size of the operation imply "some greater intelligence" than the skinwalkers themselves, and the Biz agreed that something intelligent is behind the scenes. (Appalachia 09, Radford Horrors 01)

Speculation

The crack in Georgia is lit by rippling light "like the caustics on the bottom of a pool", the same light that plays on Andrew's ceiling when the dream visitor comes in Marblehead. The visitor may have arrived the way the pipe did.

docs.title: Who made the Radford Moth, and did it breed?
docs.text:
The evidence. Wilbur Whateley said in 1992 that the moth had to breed and that its kind are born pregnant. A year later he says it "needed hosts, like a parasitic wasp. Those women—", that he found it under a white oak, and something about "the basement". His own journal describes finding a giant larva in the woods by the old church. A moth lays 40 to 500 eggs. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08, Radford Horrors 04)

Both Amanda Lucky and Irene Whateley were found disemboweled, and about five percent of Amanda's blood volume was foreign matter the coroner could not identify. In 1993 the team finds pearlescent goo with the moth's smell at the Safe Environment Fund fenced site, and a small moth-scented intruder enters the Douglas Pinball Emporium before the gray van crew takes it away. (Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 08, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

At the table. In 1992 the players split on the disembowelments: Dante thought Amanda had been killed to keep her quiet, Zack thought the Whateley boy did it, and others thought the moth ate them. On returning, Andrew admits the team "never went looking for the kids or eggs", and Kurt thinks the gray van crew came for a juvenile moth or a thrall. See Moth life cycle and Crucifixion MO. (Radford Horror 08, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

Still open. Who "the ones who made" the moth are; whether any young survived the church fire; where the cleanup crew took the body; and who physically nailed up the victims and supplied the sedatives.

Speculation

Wilbur's "those women" reads as an answer to the oldest puzzle of the first case: the women were disemboweled because something came out of them. The foreign matter in Amanda's blood would then be the moth's, and the creatures of 1993 would be the brood.

docs.title: What killed Perot's task force?
docs.text:
The evidence. The cold open of the current arc shows the missing FBI task force dying in the Radford woods: something flying picks agents off from above, and naked, emaciated men with swollen, rippling bellies hang from the trees by their punctured hands (see Radford woods predators and Hanging figures). (Radford Horrors 01)

The site marked on the missing agents' map has since been fenced, bleached and dug over. The Safe Environment Fund guards it with armed men and lawyers, and townspeople who vanish, including Elizabeth George, are said to be in treatment in Los Angeles (see LA treatment cover story). (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

At the table. Daniel Webster arrived believing the old team was Bush's political dirty-work unit and that the alien material was cover. Billy Thornton's tale of a van full of chimpanzees left Zack suspecting that "the space chimpanzees weren't actually chimpanzees". On why President Perot rejected the original reports, Dante thinks he "doesn't like reading that it's fucking aliens"; Ezra thinks the report was a cover story. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

Still open. Whether the hanging men are victims or hosts; who is behind the Safe Environment Fund; and where the missing people really are.

Speculation

Punctured hands and rippling bellies look like the crucifixions and the hosting of 1992 combined. Wilbur spoke of women as hosts, and the hanging figures are men, so the new generation may be less particular.

docs.title: Who was on the radio?
docs.text:
The evidence. The radio contact knows about the worms, has a poison for them, and says the nerve agent leaked because his advance team "got blown up". He explains that they brought something broad-spectrum "because we weren't sure what it was gonna make". He says he is only allowed to tell the team what they already know, and that he has done this before. When Kurt names the M28 Davy Crockett:

Quote

"I don't recognize the model name. It might be different where I'm from."

Andre (as the radio contact) (Summer Service 06)

The session before the finale was not recorded, so how the team first reached him is not known. A cold open months earlier showed four men in dark camouflage on a steel boat, aiming a huge oval-barreled gun at something that "has a human with it". (Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 06)

Still open. Who he works for and where he is from; whether the boat crew were his advance team (see Mystery covert group); and which vessel Big Bill meant when he said "we lost one of our submarines too".

Speculation

"Where I'm from" could mean another country or service. Set beside the portals found later, another world, or another version of this one with differently named weapons, is also possible. The rule about only confirming what the team already knows suggests someone worried about changing events.

docs.title: Did the Sons of Adam know what was in the wine?
docs.text:
The evidence. The worms reached Marblehead through the communion wine of the Sons of Adam, but the episodes never establish whether the congregation spread them knowingly or was itself infected and led by them, or where the worms came from. The body found in Amos Shaw's house is not Shaw's and is never identified. Nobody says who chained up Arnold Weathers, or whose severed arm, in a black sleeve and glove, washed up among the dead fish, or what the unscratchable crystal marbles are. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05)

At the table. The Biz declared the marbles diamonds. Kurt's "factional dispute" theory (above) has someone else using the nerve agent to contain the worms before the team ever arrived. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05)

Speculation

The radio contact's "we weren't sure what it was gonna make" sounds as though the worms, or the angel thing, produce other creatures, and that his people had seen it happen before.

docs.title: Where did the ape-men come from?
docs.text:
The evidence. Clive knew only that the ape-men arrived looking about six years old and were full-grown in two months. After Jan's capture the team learns the line began with Shelly, taken from a man with NSA identification whom Jan killed with his car. Why that man had her is unknown. (Appalachia 09, Walkers 01)

At the table. Zack (as Huell) "figured there was a population in the wild" that Jan wanted to protect; Andrew proposed an extraterrestrial origin. When the answer came, Rita admitted she had expected to be disappointed. (Appalachia 09, Walkers 01)

Still open. Where Shelly came from; what attacked the Spud Hut truck; what became of Willow Greengrass; whether the man baptizing a salesman into the red mud was Elijah Ray, and where the salesman went; and who the client is behind the lawyers pressing the Covenant for its land (see The Land Dispute). The arc's finale was not recorded. (Appalachia 04, Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Was the Clinton scandal enemy action?
docs.text:
The evidence. Polaroids of Bill Clinton in a Dahlonega hotel room, reportedly taken with a Russian camera, sank his campaign (see Clinton Surveillance Scandal). The Biz had planted a camera and microphone in room 111 of the same hotel for the KGB, which sent him coded instructions (see Moby-Dick book cipher). No one at the table ever says aloud that his camera took the pictures. President Bush saw design in it:

Quote

"There is coincidence, there is miracle, and there is enemy action. That is enemy action."

Andre (as George H. W. Bush) (Walkers 01)

Bush believed some power wanted him out of office to break the continuity of the government's response, and warned of agents inside American organizations (see Enemy Action). (Appalachia 01, Walkers 01)

Still open. Whether the Biz's handlers were simply the KGB or a front for someone else, and what the fragment the team decoded in his apartment, "instructions to cause soon submarine lost near", refers to. (Radford Horrors 01)

Speculation

A submarine was lost at Marblehead on the night of the finale. If the decoded fragment refers to it, the Biz's correspondents knew about that night, or caused it.

docs.title: Where did the skinwalkers go?
docs.text:
The evidence. Before the portal failed, skinwalkers were carrying tanks of blood with creatures in them through it, and fifty or sixty were still in the cavern. Among them was the false mayor, Wilford Hiram, whose fate is not shown. Nobody learned who makes the host bodies or what lies on the other side. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

On the night Andrew was replaced, someone with keys also emptied Robert Bigelow's ranch of every tape and drive and took three of his staff (see Bigelow's recordings). The same night Andrew cast something out of a naked intruder, who died hours later. (Walkers 07)

Yeltsin calls them "the people who were not people", asks how convincing they were, and says Russia is developing a test. (Radford Horrors 01)

At the table. The Biz's verdict to Yeltsin: good mimics, poor strategists. Kurt's: someone smarter is directing them. (Radford Horrors 01)

Still open. Who wrote the note that lured Andrew to the gym, and whether its "list" existed; who robbed Bigelow; and what was inside the intruder.

docs.title: What drives the Sherman Ranch phenomenon?
docs.text:
The evidence. The ranch phenomenon lifted a car, heated a sheet of metal and launched it toward Roosevelt, and ended in the white ring. No episode explains it or says whether it has anything to do with the skinwalkers. The grave of Shelly Wilmarth, who appears in local news footage shot after her death, was never opened in a recorded session (see Exhumation of Shelly Wilmarth). (Walkers 01, Walkers 07, Walkers 09)

At the table. Walt offered ball lightning for the burned crow and, in a moment of "sanity time", a cargo plane and skyhook for the car. Robert Bigelow offered the Black Sun. (Walkers 04, Walkers 05)

Speculation

Given what the skinwalkers were, the Shelly on the news footage was most likely a copy, which would make her one of the earliest replacements.

docs.title: What happened at the Roulet house?
docs.text:
The evidence. The Roulet Intruder was unmasked as a human, but his name and motive were never learned. The episodes never say who killed the Roulets or confirm that the second body in the basement pit is Mr. Roulet. Also unexplained: the older subjects of the attic Polaroids; what drug was in the water (see The Drugged Water); the lights and eyes in the woods and Kurt's lost minute; who sent the foil-wrapped letter that started the case; and what is on the visitation tapes Kurt carried off and nobody watched. The Roulets' sketches of black triangles match the craft the team saw over Utah. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

At the table. Andre noted that, as cops, the agents ought to be suspicious of "two things" at once, a serial killer and an alien; Ezra answered that it has been two things every time. Dante allowed that it might be a regular serial killer "and we're all just tripping balls off of toilet water".

Quote

"Look, what I wouldn't give to just investigate a regular serial killer right now."

Ezra (Roulet Estate 02)

Speculation

The matching triangles are the one detail the drugged water cannot explain away. The Roulets may have been watching something real before the man in the attic arrived.

docs.title: Who are "the humanists"?
docs.text:
The evidence. One line. Yeltsin opens his questioning of the captured Biz with:

Quote

"Tell me everything you know about the humanists."

Andre (as Boris Yeltsin) (Roulet Estate 03)

The later Russian scenes turn to skinwalkers and the crash, and the word does not come up again. (Radford Horrors 01)

Speculation

Next to "the opposite of aliens", "humanists" may be a Russian name for the servitors' masters, or for a human faction working with them.

docs.title: Smaller loose ends
docs.text:
• The fate of Dean Lawson, who vanished before the team could interview him. (Radford Horror 08)
  • The "Kansas City" case that Kurt never wants to repeat. (Appalachia 09)
  • "Salem, Colorado", which appears in Murphy's papers and nowhere else. (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: The vanishing car
docs.text:
The vanishing car incident is the night in the first days of November 1992 when the party's rental Plymouth Voyager rose straight up from the guest house parking spot at the Sherman Ranch and was later found miles away in Roosevelt, pancaked into the road.

Type Anomalous event Aliases Vanishing car phenomenon; car abduction; the abducting force Location Departure: the ranch's guest house. Arrival: East Lagoon Street, Roosevelt Cause Not established; the party suspects the beam or a UFO First appearance Walkers 04

docs.title: The disappearance
docs.text:
During the night of Walkers 04, the Voyager's alarm and lights go off with nothing visible nearby, and someone at the big house shouts something inaudible until the party silences the alarm. Later, back at the guest house, the van is gone. One set of tire tracks leads into the parking spot and none leave. Zack (as Huell) inspects the tracks and concludes that the car most likely went straight up, and that the ground where it sat is quite hot, around 200 degrees.

At the big house, a staff member plays the tape from the sky camera, in which the car shows as a slightly different grey patch next to the house. Asked about radar and electrical phenomena, Bigelow says that the radar showed nothing, but "some of the EM meters went nuts," with spikes matching both the pop at the substation and the earlier dusk event, when the van slid sideways, though the data is noisy (Walkers 04).

docs.title: The wreck in Roosevelt
docs.text: At about 10 a.m., Hertz pages Howard to say that the car is blocking East Lagoon Street in Roosevelt. Rita (as Howard) tells the others, "Anyway, our car's back. It got unabducted." In Roosevelt, the Voyager is pancaked about a foot thick and fused into the roadway, in a slight crater. Zack's Investigate a Mystery roll fails, but Dante (as Kurt) reasons that the flattening came from dropping the car. Five officers, some from outside agencies, strain with jacks and two-by-fours to pry it out of the road. The local officer first guesses that someone with a car crusher and a flatbed did it, and the Roosevelt police lend the party the old squad car Betsy as a replacement (Walkers 04). Items in the van, including a map in the glove compartment and Kurt's stilts, were lost with it.

docs.title: Examination
docs.text:
In Walkers 05, the party examines the wreck in the Roosevelt police station garage. Dante (as Kurt) tests it with loose screws and finds the car is magnetic, though it was not when it was parked. A Roosevelt officer points out that the upholstery is slightly melted and that the car smells of coyote pee. Kurt's examination suggests that the damage came from the car hitting the ground at terminal velocity, moving sideways quite fast and skewed in the direction away from the ranch, and that it landed upside down (Walkers 05).

Rita (as Howard) reads the evidence as an abduction: "Car got abducted. They didn't want it, though." Dante (as Kurt) later tells Alberta Wilmarth that the car disappeared and reappeared, smashed, a county over (Walkers 05).

docs.title: Theories
docs.text:
• Abduction. Andrew believes a UFO lifted and dropped the car (Walkers 04, Walkers 05).
  • The junkyard. The Roosevelt police arrest the junkyard owner Yusuf Ansari, because "there's only so many places that can crush a car." Kurt urges the officer to match the physical evidence before trusting any confession (Walkers 05). In Walkers 06, Yusuf admits he did not do it.
  • The beam. At the end of Walkers 06, the party finds a switchable heat-and-magnet beam at the ranch fence whose arc points toward Roosevelt, and Kurt suggests this may be what happened to the car.

The cause is never confirmed. See also the Sherman Ranch phenomenon.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: The loss is part of a running gag about ruined rentals. In Walkers 04, Dante says, "And we are not being very good with rentals lately," and Ezra (as the Biz) notes that "one hundred percent of the cars I've driven in the state have been turned into pancakes."

docs.title: The white ring
docs.text:
The white ring is a luminous ring with a faint purple glow, first caught on Robert Bigelow's sky camera over the Sherman Ranch during the night event, and seen again in the finale as a burning circle about a kilometer across.

Type Anomalous phenomenon Aliases Black Sun ring; ranch levitation ring; the ring Location The sky over the Sherman Ranch Cause Never explained First appearance Walkers 05

docs.title: The footage
docs.text:
After the night event, Bigelow shows the party a frozen frame from his sky camera and asks about the Black Sun, its pagan roots and its appropriation by the Nazis, and quotes Revelation 6:12. Dante (as Kurt) remarks that the image, though bright, looks lumpy and odd. Much of Bigelow's equipment broke during the event, and the thermal camera whited out (Walkers 05).

The party then watches the footage in motion: a very bright white ring surrounded by a slightly purple glow, oscillating and vibrating in the sky. Bigelow calls it one of the most clear-cut events they have had, part of an escalation dating back a few weeks, and says they "may be on the verge of making contact." He agrees to set up a big ring of cameras around the party's house (Walkers 05). The recording is covered under Bigelow's recordings.

docs.title: The finale
docs.text:
In Walkers 09, the convoy of Guardsmen and agents nears the ranch and sees what looks like a cloud blocking the sun. It turns out to be the ranch farmhouse floating in the sky, surrounded by a loose halo of barbed wire, metal roof panels and probably some horseshoes. Nothing is left on the horizon but the little wooden barn, which has no major metal components. Andre tells the players to stay well away from the ranch property (Walkers 09).

As the sun sets, a faint violet glow grows over the ranch. Near the community center the farmhouse vanishes in a vapor cone, launched toward Roosevelt, and the glow snaps into a burning white ring floating over the ranch, which Andre says is about a kilometer across. The party recognizes it as the image from the security footage taken when Andrew Howard was levitated. Andre compares the change to the field in a plasma ball, which snaps from an amorphous glow into a coherent shape. Invisible waves then rock the Humvees and armored vehicles, everyone gets headaches, time skips a second or two ahead, people freeze mid-sentence, and the armored killdozer begins to levitate intermittently (Walkers 09). The major halts the convoy and orders the soldiers to proceed on foot with the heavy equipment they can easily carry (Walkers 09).

The ring is not explained. Its relationship to the portal beneath the community center, if any, is never stated. The ring belongs with the other unexplained events collected under the Sherman Ranch phenomenon.

docs.title: About this wiki
docs.text: This is a fan wiki for PITF, a tabletop role-playing campaign about the Paranatural Incident Task Force: four mismatched federal agents sent to look into things the government would rather not explain, in an early 1990s that is not quite ours. The campaign is played with Monster of the Week and is framed at the table as a television show, with cold opens, credits and cliffhangers.

docs.title: What it covers
docs.text: The wiki covers the campaign's six story arcs and one non-canon one-shot: 38 recorded sessions in all, plus what later episodes establish about five sessions that were never recorded. It has pages for the episodes, the characters, the monsters, the places, the organizations, the items and the lore, and for the people at the table.

docs.title: Where to start
docs.text:
• Episode guide: every session in story order.
  • Cast and players: who plays whom.
  • The player characters: Andrew Howard, Kurt Larson, Dick "The Biz" Baxter, Huell Kendrick and Daniel Webster.
  • Paranatural Incident Task Force: the unit itself.
  • Timeline and Alternate history: when it all happens, and how this 1992 differs.
  • The paranatural and Unresolved mysteries: what the team has found, and what it still does not understand.
  • Tropes, Quotes and Running gags: the fun pages.

docs.title: Where the information comes from
docs.text:
The wiki was compiled from automatic transcripts of the session recordings. It was not compiled from the game master's own material or from the players' character sheets. A reader should keep four things in mind.

  • Only what was said aloud is here. Anything settled in a private message, written on a character sheet or decided between sessions appears only if someone mentioned it during a session. The Game mechanics page has gaps for this reason.
  • Names may be misspelled. Automatic transcription guesses at names, and the same name can come out several different ways. The wiki uses one spelling per subject. That spelling is a best guess, not an official one. Notable variants are listed under Trivia or Aliases on the subject's page.
  • Some speaker attributions are uncertain. Five sessions were recorded on a single mixed track, so it is not always clear which player is speaking. They are listed on the Lost episodes page. Quotations are given as transcribed and may differ by a word or two from what was said.
  • Some sessions were never recorded. Five sessions were played without a recording. Their events are known only from recaps and remarks in later episodes, and are labeled as such wherever they are used. See Lost episodes.

Where two episodes disagree, usually over a name or a date, the page says so.

docs.title: How episodes are cited
docs.text:
Statements are cited to the session they come from, in italic parentheses, like this: (Radford Horror 03). The short names are:

Cited as Arc Radford Horror 01–08 The Radford Horror Summer Service 01–06 The Summer Service Appalachia 01–10 The Things in Appalachia Philosopher's Fist Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable Walkers 01–09 The Walkers in Skin Roulet Estate 01–03 The Roulet Estate Radford Horrors 01–04 The Radford Horrors

The first and last arcs have nearly the same name. The Radford Horror (singular) is the first case. The Radford Horrors (plural) is the return to the same town.

Episode numbers follow the order the sessions were played in, including the unrecorded ones, so the numbering has gaps: there is no recording of Summer Service 02, Appalachia 05 or Appalachia 10. Two more unrecorded sessions were never numbered and are called Summer Service 05.5 and Walkers 08.5 here.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• Voice. Pages about the fiction are written from inside it, like an encyclopedia of the show: Ross Perot is the president, and Nancy is a goose. Pages about the table, such as the player pages, are written from outside it.
  • Status. Character statuses ("alive," "missing") are given as of the latest recorded session, Radford Horrors 04, unless a page says otherwise.
  • Dates. In-fiction dates are those stated at the table. Where the table was unsure, the Timeline notes the conflict.
  • Labeled boxes. "Unrecorded session" marks anything known only from later recaps. "Uncertain" marks material where the episodes are unclear or disagree.
  • Real people. The campaign's alternate history includes fictional versions of real public figures: presidents, a talk-show host, a billionaire. The wiki writes about them as characters in a story. Nothing on those pages is a claim about the real people.
  • Players. The players are named by first name only, and the wiki describes them only as players at this table.

docs.title: The one-shot
docs.text:
Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable is a one-session side story with different characters, a different world and a different rule set. It is not canon to the main campaign. Within the fiction it is an anime OVA that Huell watched on hotel cable, which is as much as the two stories have to do with each other. (Appalachia 02)

Its characters, places and lore have their own pages, all labeled non-canon, and its facts are kept off the main campaign's pages.

docs.title: Spoilers
docs.text: The wiki describes the whole campaign up to the latest recorded session, and no page hides anything. That includes the fates of the player characters and the secret Rita kept from the rest of the table in The Walkers in Skin. If you intend to listen to the sessions first, start with the episode guide and read one episode page at a time.

docs.title: Game mechanics
docs.text:
PITF is played with Monster of the Week, a game about hunting monsters in which the game master is called the Keeper and each player character is built from a playbook. This page covers the rules as they are used at this table: each character's playbook, ratings and moves, how Luck, harm and experience have come up, the house rulings, and the rolls that changed the story.

Everything here is what was said aloud during the sessions. Character sheets are never shown, so a rating or move appears below only if someone read it out.

docs.title: The basics
docs.text:
• The roll. Two six-sided dice plus a rating. A 10 or more is a full success, 7 to 9 is a mixed success, and 6 or less is a miss. Ezra asks how rolls work in the first session, and as late as the second arc Zack is reminding the table that the dice are "2d6, it's different." (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 06)
  • Experience. A missed roll marks experience. Andre opens the second session with the reminder that "we need to remember to do the experience stuff when you guys screw up a roll." (Radford Horror 02)
  • The basic moves heard in play are Act Under Pressure, Help Out, Investigate a Mystery, Kick Some Ass, Manipulate Someone, Protect Someone, Read a Bad Situation and Use Magic.
  • Ratings are Charm, Cool, Sharp, Tough and Weird.
  • Advanced moves. A basic move can be marked as advanced on a level-up, which unlocks a better result on a 12 or more. (Radford Horror 02, Walkers 01)
  • Combat. Andre's warning in the second session: "Monster of the Week combat tends to turn into like a slugging match where people die really quickly unless you're being kind of tactical about it." He recommends Help Out as the way to contribute to a fight without taking damage. (Radford Horror 02)

The non-canon one-shot uses a different game. See The one-shot below.

docs.title: Andrew Howard (Rita)
docs.text:
Andrew Howard has had two playbooks.

The Divine (Radford Horror 01 to Walkers 07):

Ratings Charm is negative. Rita: "It's just you can always tell there's something wrong with me." His other ratings as a Divine are not read out. Lay on Hands His healing move ("It's my actual move"). Healing someone causes him to take on some of the harm himself. What I Need When I Need It "I can store any small object into a magical space, and I can retrieve it at any time": any small object he owns "or could feasibly own." In the fiction this is his satchel. Cast Out Evil Used twice in Walkers 07, on rolls of 12 and 14. Holy weapon From the Divine's gear list: a three-harm weapon, first a mace and then re-themed as pepper spray that sprays "nothingness." Harm reduction "I have two different things that let me negate one harm": two harm off every hit, three with his pendant. One of the two is a Resilience move under which "wounds count as one harm less." Text bonus +1 on "rolls that involve looking through books, newspapers, or other text for information."

(Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08, Walkers 07, Walkers 08, Roulet Estate 01)

The second point of harm reduction arrives in Appalachia 08: "I got another upgrade, so I reduce all damage by two now." (Appalachia 08)

The Monstrous (from Walkers 08): after the real Andrew dies and revives, Andre tells Rita "You are now the Monstrous," and the two rebuild the character in a private scene after the session. Andre's instruction is to "pretend as though you'd been Monstrous the whole time and had done the same level-ups."

Ratings Charm −1, Cool −1, Tough +2, Weird +3. Rita plans to raise Tough to +3 on a later level-up, and by Radford Horrors 04 she says "I'm three Weird." Dropped Lay on Hands and Cast Out Evil, on the idea that the transformation "has severed me from that power source." Kept What I Need When I Need It, as a move from another playbook, because "it's tied to an item." Resilience is taken again. New moves Unquenchable Vitality and Immortal. Mental Dominion, Unnatural Appeal, Preternatural Speed and Unholy Strength are discussed as later picks. Natural attack "Life drain at a range." Curse He "now has to drink blood." Harm reduction Two harm without the pendant, three with it.

(Walkers 08, Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 04)

See Andrew Howard (the Monstrous). Between the end of the gym scene in Walkers 07 and the swap back in Walkers 09, Rita played a duplicate instead. Its instructions included the line "I deteriorate," and Andre's summary was: "you have leukemia, and you don't feel great." (Walkers 07, Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Kurt Larson (Dante)
docs.text:
Kurt Larson is the Expert. Andre looks one of his moves up "under the Expert" and later checks, "you're the Expert, right?" (Appalachia 09, Walkers 04)

Ratings Sharp +3 from Summer Service 01 ("Guess who has a plus three to Sharp now?"), Cool +2, Weird +1, Charm 0, Tough 0. Haven "Dante got an armory as part of his character build": the basement arsenal under the barbershop. Preparedness Rolled with Sharp to have the right thing on hand. Andre: "You need something unusual or rare," which can be information as well as an object; "if you roll a full success on Preparedness, you just have it." Often Right "If they come to me for advice and they take my honest advice, they get a plus one ongoing while following it." Dark Past "Just for the record, I took Dark Past as my level-up."

(Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 01, Appalachia 03, Walkers 04, Roulet Estate 01)

Kurt also has a resource of Dante's own invention: four molars loaded with different drugs. Biting the amphetamine tooth in the church fight is worth +1 forward. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 07)

Dante mentions further level-ups in Radford Horror 08 (held over because "there wouldn't actually be time in the story"), Walkers 06 and Walkers 08. What he took for them is not said. (Radford Horror 08, Walkers 06, Walkers 08)

docs.title: Dick "The Biz" Baxter (Ezra)
docs.text:
The playbook of the Biz is never named on a recording. His moves are.

Ratings Charm +2 at the start and +3 by Walkers 04. Cool 0, raised to +1 as a level-up in Radford Horror 04 and +2 by Roulet Estate 03. His other ratings are not read out. Crime bonus "When hiding evidence of a crime, he can add one to the roll." Fixer "If I need to buy something, sell something, or hire someone, roll +Charm." Zack calls it "Know a Guy." Grifter When he is about to manipulate someone, he "can ask the Keeper what will convince this person to do what I want." Ezra: "I don't know why I always forget I have it." Charlatan Taken in Walkers 01: "When you want people to think you're using magic, roll +Cool." He uses it for a card trick on Letterman. Advanced moves Investigate a Mystery and Manipulate Someone, both marked advanced in Walkers 01.

(Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 04, Appalachia 09, Walkers 01, Walkers 04, Walkers 08, Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

The Biz gained experience faster than anyone in the first arc, because Ezra missed so often. His track was "full up" in Radford Horror 03, and by Radford Horror 08 he was "marking X's over top of the X's" and one failure from "a double level up." He spent the backlog in Walkers 01, before the Letterman interview, on the grounds that "this could be the end of the Biz, so I might as well go out with a bang." (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 08, Walkers 01)

docs.title: Huell Kendrick (Zack)
docs.text:
The playbook of Huell Kendrick is not named on a recording either.

Ratings Cool +3, Sharp +1, Tough +1, Charm −1. Weird is not read out. Cool for Sharp "My thing that lets me use Cool for Read a Bad Situation." Interview bonus A +1 when interviewing an uncooperative subject. First aid "You have a full first aid kit and training to heal people. Roll Cool. On a 10-plus, the patient is stabilized and healed of two harm." Hoodlum His first level-up pick, borrowed from another playbook: "the Crooked has this one that lets you use toughness for instead of charm. I'm taking that." It applies to Manipulate Someone "as long as I'm using violence."

(Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 03)

Huell was the first character to level up, in Radford Horror 03. In the Marblehead finale Zack marks experience and announces, "That gets me to level four." (Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Daniel Webster (Ezra)
docs.text: Almost nothing mechanical is heard for Daniel Webster. Ezra arrived at his first session without a name for him, and his playbook and ratings are never read out. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Luck
docs.text:
"Everybody starts with seven." A point of Luck turns a roll into a success, and it can be spent after the dice are seen: asked whether that is allowed "after you roll and it's not good," Andre says, "Yeah, yeah, no, you are." A character who runs out is Doomed. (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01, Radford Horrors 03)

Luck spent on the recordings:

Session Who What it bought Radford Horror 07 The Biz "I'm just gonna use luck to force it," late in the church fight. Summer Service 04 Kurt Andre offers the spend out of character, and Kurt's weapons contact sends a Davy Crockett. "It would have been a Scorpion if you hadn't burned the luck point." Summer Service 06 Huell A 7 becomes a clean hit with the Davy Crockett. Appalachia 01 Huell Rescuing a bad roll. Zack: "I can appreciate that it's maybe a waste, but I don't give a shit." Walkers 01 The Biz "I'm gonna burn a luck point to change that to a twelve," on David Letterman's show. Walkers 03 Huell Winning a game of darts. Radford Horrors 03 The Biz Several points in one action sequence in Russia.

After Radford Horrors 03, "Dick has three Luck left before he is Doomed." Ezra: "I don't know what Doomed means." (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Harm
docs.text:
Characters have seven harm boxes. A character over four harm is unstable and keeps getting worse until someone stabilizes them. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08)

  • Healing has come from Andrew's Lay on Hands, Huell's first aid move and hospitals. (Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 05)
  • Lasting injuries carry penalties. After Huell breaks his arm, Zack rolls Tough at "probably minus one because of my arm." (Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07)
  • The worst night. At the church in Radford Horror 07 Kurt reached five harm and the Biz was unstable as well. Rita: "So we just half-TPK'd." (Radford Horror 07)
  • Small harms. Being hit with a Taser is one harm. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Magic
docs.text:
Magic at this table has mostly come through Andrew's Divine moves rather than the basic Use Magic move: Lay on Hands, Cast Out Evil and his holy weapon. When Andre first asks for a Use Magic roll, to heal Kurt, Rita corrects him: "No, it's Lay On Hands. It's my actual move." (Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 05, Walkers 07)

Use Magic proper is rolled in Radford Horrors 04, by which time Andrew is the Monstrous and has dropped his Divine moves. Rita rolls a 10 and adds Weird +3 for a 13. Andre reads out the effects she can choose from: inflict harm; enchant a weapon; do one thing that is beyond human limitations; bar a place or portal; trap a specific person; banish a spirit; summon a monster into the world; communicate with something that you do not share a language with; observe another time or place; heal one harm from an injury, or cure a disease, or neutralize a poison. Zack's advice: "Summon the monster!" (Radford Horrors 04)

For how the supernatural works in the fiction, see The paranatural.

docs.title: Dread
docs.text: Andre added a dread track in Summer Service 03, when he asked Rita to "roll for dread" during one of Andrew's dreams and told her, "You take five dread." Asked what dread is, he said, "You don't know yet. Well, you're gonna find out," and then, "I'm borrowing it from some of the Lovecraft games." In Summer Service 05 a group roll with no complete success cost everyone five dread, and the players asked where on the sheet to write it. In Walkers 07 it was Zack who asked whether a scene was worth any ("I've got this little marker that hasn't gone up in a long time"; "I don't think my dread has gone up since we nuked a kaiju"), and Andre gave everyone one and the Biz two. Zack prompted him again in Walkers 09: "Remember the dread mechanic if you want to use it." What dread does when it builds up has not been shown. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05, Walkers 07, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Other rulings
docs.text:
• Two questions on a 12 before the advanced move was unlocked: "Well, you still get two." (Radford Horror 02)
  • A perfect 12 required. "If you roll a perfect 12 on a Sharp check, I will let you modify this thing to go faster. If you don't, you are going to either injure yourself or break it." (Roulet Estate 02)
  • Flat luck checks. Andre rolls a plain 2d6 "as a luck check for you guys" when the question is whether the world cooperates. (Summer Service 04)
  • A secret GM roll for Kurt's bluff against Jan Martense: "That's not how we're doing this one. 'Cause it's more fun that way." (Appalachia 08)
  • Rolling for NPC gear. "I am gonna do something I haven't done before here, and I am going to roll for Freak and his maintenance of the Cessna." (Radford Horror 07)
  • Cocked dice are rerolled. (Walkers 07)
  • Proxy rolling. When a player's dice roller is broken, Andre rolls for them. (Radford Horrors 03)
  • Rolling for casting. Whether Chevy Chase guest-stars in the show was put to the dice. It was a mixed success. (Radford Horror 01)

Minutes later he falls from the craft for four harm and a broken arm. Summer Service 03 The Biz, investigating 14, twice Both at the lighthouse; the first finds a bloody fingerprint by the door. Summer Service 05 Andrew, with his holy weapon 2 The spray takes the attacking dog's head off and passes through Kurt's hand for three harm. docs.title: The one-shot
docs.text:
Non-canon

Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable is a non-canon one-shot and uses a different rule set.

The one-shot runs on a different game, which is not named at the table. Andre calls it "a really wordy game document" and looks rules up as he goes. (Philosopher's Fist)

  • Ratings heard: Danger and Savior.
  • Conditions: Afraid, Angry, Guilty, Insecure, Hopeless.
  • Moves heard: Directly Engage a Threat (rolled with Danger) and a Defend move.
  • Derk (Dante) is "the Bull": as a defender he can "roll Danger instead of Savior." His best roll of the session is a 15.
  • Mirabeth (Rita) has Danger −1 and a move called Symbol of Authority, and refers to one of her moves as "a Legacy one." She is told to mark Insecure after one exchange.

(Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Lost episodes
docs.text:
Five sessions of PITF were played but never recorded. All that is known of them is what later episodes say: recaps, callbacks and consequences. This page lists each lost session and what later episodes establish about it. It also lists the five recordings that come from a single mixed audio track, where it is not always certain who is speaking.

Lost session Falls between What it contained Summer Service 02 Summer Service 01 and Summer Service 03 The submarine dive Summer Service 05.5 Summer Service 05 and Summer Service 06 The rescue of the scientists and the start of the chase Appalachia 05 Appalachia 04 and Appalachia 06 The Biz's private night at the hotel Appalachia 10 Appalachia 09 and Walkers 01 The arc finale Walkers 08.5 Walkers 08 and Walkers 09 Horses, the radio station and the National Guard

Unrecorded sessions

Everything below comes from later episodes. Where a detail is stated outright it is given as fact; where it is only implied, the text says so. Each lost session also has its own page in the episode guide.

docs.title: The Summer Service 02
docs.text:
The second session of The Summer Service covered the team's second day in Marblehead. Summer Service 03 picks up that night and treats its events as known; most of what follows comes from Andrew's phone report to Big Bill in that episode. (Summer Service 03)

  • The dive. In Andrew's words, "we went down in an experimental submarine with some college kids," one of whom "was gonna show us the dead body that she found while doing her submarine research." They went over the shelf to the stealth wreck. The body was no longer there. (Summer Service 03)
  • The thing with the lights. Something arrived while they were at the wreck: "Covered in lights, gyroscope fucking looking something or other... And most importantly, it like hummed." Big Bill concludes that whoever it is, "they're guarding the wreck." This is the first sighting of what the team later calls the angel thing. (Summer Service 03)
  • Who was aboard. Andrew describes the dive first-hand. The Biz was not on it: "I didn't go down in the submarine." (Summer Service 03, Radford Horrors 01)
  • The nerve agent. Members of the team were exposed to something that the lab says "wasn't VX exactly, but wasn't that far from VX." Kurt is still recovering from it in Summer Service 03; all he says of his own exposure is "I just got my hands wet." (Summer Service 03)
  • Chicken pox. Kurt also has adult chicken pox by the start of Summer Service 03. (Summer Service 03)
  • The marbles. The team already knows that the church's crystal spheres are diamonds. Andre: "I think Ezra told you guys the marbles are diamonds." (Summer Service 03)
  • Huell had been awake for 48 hours by the end of the day, and still could not sleep. (Summer Service 03)

Probably also in this session, though no one says so directly: the first meeting with Donald McManley, who was expected at the end of Summer Service 01 and is already at work in Marblehead in Summer Service 03. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03)

docs.title: The Summer Service 05.5
docs.text:
An unnumbered session was played between Summer Service 05 and the finale. Summer Service 05 ends with the party clear of town and deciding whether to take the Ivermectin. Summer Service 06 opens with no recap, with the team on the road in a stolen car. Everything known about the session between comes from passing remarks. (Summer Service 05, Summer Service 06)

  • The scientists were found alive. Andrew tells the radio contact: "we found our research guys. They were alive." Kurt later says that the previous team "had been kidnapped." (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01)
  • The cure. Huell took the deworming medicine: Andre tells Zack "you can feel that the deworming agent is kicking in." (Summer Service 06)
  • The cars. The team is driving a car they stole (Andre: "I will point out that you stole this car"), having left the Biz's Buick behind. Their own FBI car is no longer with them. They next see it in Summer Service 06, driven by Jester in the convoy until it sticks in a dip in the road. How the cars and the Davy Crockett changed hands is not said. (Summer Service 06)
  • The explosion. The radio contact mentions an explosion, which Andre identifies as "the claymore that you guys set off on the truck." (Summer Service 06)
  • The radio contact. The team had already spoken to the radio contact's side. He opens with an apology "for my commanding officer's rudeness earlier." (Summer Service 06)
  • McManley's lab techs were left behind. Dante: "We left the lab tech guys there, right, with the RV and shit." (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia 05
docs.text:
The fifth session of The Things in Appalachia covered one evening and night in Dahlonega. Appalachia 06 opens partway through a recap of it. (Appalachia 04, Appalachia 06)

  • The Biz's night. Part of the session was a private storyline between Andre and Ezra ("Your nonsense." "My thing, yes."). Andre says "the only part of that that was visible to you guys" was that the Biz wandered in the next morning in slept-in clothes, that "the hotel door next to yours had been broken down," and that "the Biz has a badly twisted ankle." State police searching the hotel bushes that morning find a pair of night-vision goggles. This follows from the camera the Biz planted in Room 111, and it leads to the Clinton surveillance scandal. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06, Walkers 01)
  • The ape-man result. By Appalachia 06 the team talks about "human hybrid tissue" and "an actual ape-man hybrid" as settled. At the end of Appalachia 04 the question was still open. (Appalachia 04, Appalachia 06)
  • The auditor. A Spud Hut financial auditor who had been following the team is an established contact in Appalachia 06. (Appalachia 06)
  • Frotter's bear. Frotter Comstock had asked the agents to deal with a bear on his land and been turned down. He opens Appalachia 06 still complaining about "the bear situation" and being left "defenseless." (Appalachia 06)
  • Andrew "was previously covered in blood" and has changed into a Bigfoot T-shirt. What happened to him is not said. (Appalachia 06)

It is never established whether the team attended the baptism of Jeremy that was planned at the end of Appalachia 04.

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia 10
docs.text:
The finale of the arc was not recorded. Appalachia 09 ends with the injured party making its way out while Jan Martense escapes. Walkers 01, set afterwards, does not recap the finale; what is known comes out in Kurt's interrogation of Jan and the Biz's appearance on Letterman in that episode. Andre confirms that it all happened "the same day." (Appalachia 09, Walkers 01)

  • The confrontation. Jan shot Andrew in the face, and Kurt shot Jan. Dante (as Kurt): "Ah, you shot my leader in the face. Seemed only fair." The Biz, on television: "I shot a Polish man in the woods with a shotgun." (Walkers 01)
  • Andrew was "shot in the face and thrown around by the foot like a ragdoll." In Walkers 02 Kurt's comment is "Thank God for helmets." (Walkers 01, Walkers 02)
  • Jan was crushed by a falling ape, which broke his skull. He was captured, and Kurt interrogates him at Black Site Omaha. (Walkers 01)
  • Shelly. An ape woman, Shelly, was alive and was trying to kill the team. (Walkers 01)
  • The explosion. The Spud Hut facility blew up. Kurt believes the gas was deliberate: "They piped it in. It wasn't exactly a leak." (Walkers 01)
  • The fallout. The state police said they had found the Biz's night-vision goggles "in a rose bush," the Clinton surveillance became public, and the Biz became "the most hated cop in America." The Biz is also recovering from a heart attack. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin 08.5
docs.text:
An unnumbered session falls between Walkers 08 and the finale. Walkers 08 ends with the team turned back at the bridge blockade. Walkers 09 opens with the National Guard already on the scene, and Andre's opening recap lists what happened in between. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

  • The team "went and got some horses so that you could get around the roadblock."
  • They "took a generator to the radio station and called the National Guard."
  • They "met the National Guard on horseback outside of the town."
  • They "fought your way through the road barricade in between Ballard and Roosevelt."
  • They "breached and cleared the police station" in Roosevelt.
  • The plan when they stopped was "to go back to the community center to find out what's going on."

(Walkers 09)

Zack also recalls the team marking themselves with X's to tell themselves from copies ("Did we put X's on ourselves? I feel like we did"). Throughout this session Rita was still secretly playing the duplicate Andrew, who had ridden in the Guard's Humvee for part of it. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Other gaps
docs.text:
A few things happened off the recording even in sessions that were recorded:

  • Appalachia 02 opens in the middle of a recap because Andre had "forgotten to start the recording." (Appalachia 02)
  • Private messages between Andre and a player are not heard, and some private scenes were handled off the call. The Biz's secret storyline is the main casualty. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 06)
  • The Biz's capture and his months in Russian custody between Roulet Estate 03 and Radford Horrors 01 were never played; they are described after the fact. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Recordings with uncertain speakers
docs.text:
Most sessions were recorded with a separate audio track for each person. Five survive only as a single mixed track, so it is not always certain who is speaking:

Session What is uncertain Radford Horror 01 The campaign premiere. Many lines are hard to assign, especially between Ezra, Zack and Andre. Radford Horror 08 The first arc's finale. Speakers are uncertain throughout. Summer Service 04 Many attributions are uncertain. Appalachia 04 Several lines could belong to Zack, Dante or Ezra. Appalachia 07 Lines for all five regulars are uncertain, and a few jokes cannot be credited to anyone.

What happens in these sessions is clear from context. Who said a particular line, or who made a particular roll, is the most likely reading and no more than that.

docs.title: Quotes
docs.text:
This page collects the best lines of PITF, grouped by arc in story order and then by episode. Each entry names the player, the character they are speaking as, and the moment. Lines marked "out of character" were said by the player at the table and not by a character. Every non-player character is voiced by Andre, the game master.

An ellipsis marks a place where a line has been trimmed or where someone else at the table cut in. The unrecorded sessions have no quotes. For the jokes that recur across episodes, see Running gags.

docs.title: Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable
docs.text:
Non-canon

These lines come from the non-canon one-shot, an in-universe 1992 OVA. Dante plays Derk and Rita plays Mirabeth.

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
Two Andrews

Rita plays the real Andrew through the gym fight in Walkers 07. From the end of that scene she is secretly playing the duplicate, and Andre voices the real Andrew when he turns up in Walkers 09. The swap back comes later in that episode, after which Rita is the real Andrew again.

docs.title: Walkers 01
docs.text:

  • Andre (as George H. W. Bush): "You, Andrew Howard, are personally responsible for the survival of the United States of America." The Oval Office charge.
  • Rita (as Andrew Howard): "I mean, sir, that's been my responsibility my entire life. You didn't have to ask." Leading into the Aetherius lecture.

docs.text:

docs.text:

  • Andre (as Boris Yeltsin): "I have faith in my military officers, but I do not have faith that my military officers are my military officers."
  • Andre (as Boris Yeltsin): "Nuclear reactors do not emit cosmic microwave background." On the Marblehead spike.
  • Andre (as Boris Yeltsin): "We are no longer communist here either." His reply to "I'm not really ideological."
  • Zack (as Huell Kendrick): "Of course, I didn't notice when you got replaced with an alien." To Andrew, who asked whether the Biz is a double agent.
  • Dante (as Kurt Larson): "There are degrees of double agent. Let's be clear here." Then, asked if he is one: "Not currently."
  • Dante (as Kurt Larson): "Well, I'm guessing this is his bug-out bag. Totally normal thing to own." On the Noah Mueller kit.
  • Andre (as Apartment staff): "Oh, thank God, the police are finally here about Baxter... Is he dead?"
  • Andre (as Rudy Giuliani): "Establish an acceptable fact pattern for the previous investigation."
  • Andre (as Rudy Giuliani): "Now, what can you tell me about Radford, Virginia?" The cliffhanger.
  • Ezra (out of character): "Fuck me, I didn't actually come up with one." Before naming Daniel Webster.
  • Dante (out of character): "He doesn't think a big moth got him. And a big moth got him." On the AWOL FBI team.

docs.title: Radford Horrors 02
docs.text:
• Dante (as Kurt Larson): "I bled for this country. I continue to bleed for this country." Arguing with airport security over the spear gun.
  • Dante (as Kurt Larson): "Kind of a fidget." Explaining the grenade to the IRS.
  • Rita (as Andrew Howard): "Unrelated. Like, dude, there's only two places to stay in this town, and the other one's full of bedbugs." To the IRS.
  • Ezra (as Daniel Webster): "Kurt, your reaction to somebody announcing that they're the police cannot be to pull a gun on them."
  • Dante (as Kurt Larson): "The grenade is a time-buying tactic for you to get proper identification, right?"
  • Ezra (as Daniel Webster): "I am recording everything. It's for my own protection."
  • Zack (as Huell Kendrick): "Sorry about the mess." A Han Solo exit after vomiting in the diner bathroom.
  • Rita (as Andrew Howard): "Caterpillar slurry." After Webster tastes the goo.
  • Dante (as Kurt Larson): "Man, sketchiest environmental agency ever."
  • Ezra (as Daniel Webster): "Without using words like 'aliens,' what do you think we're going to find in these woods?" Kurt: "Foreign element."
  • Andre (as GM): "A spree skinning and not serial skinning."
  • Dante (out of character): "Aliens aren't real, but none of you seem rich, and also none of you seem like you could work with anyone." Summing up Webster's conspiracy problem.
  • Andre (as ER doctor): "Not again. Not you guys. What have you done this time?"
  • Dante (as Kurt Larson): "This isn't coming out of my coke budget." The final line, on the bill for rabies shots.

docs.title: Radford Horrors 03
docs.text:
• Andre (as Boris Yeltsin): "Richard, there has been an unusual aircraft crash in Oryol Oblast. I need you to come take a look at it with me and tell me what you see." The call to adventure.
  • Dante (out of character): "Somewhere Andrew is tingling." Reacting to "aircraft crash".
  • Ezra (as The Biz): "I'm going into a wheat field... You're gonna have to find me." On the radio, before killing the lights.
  • Ezra (out of character): "I don't know what Doomed means." Burning the last Luck.
  • Dante (out of character): "The Biz is just aging, like, 20 fucking years in one night."
  • Ezra (as The Biz): "He's just really fucking up the feng shui, frankly." Dragging a dead guard out of the car.
  • Rita (as Andrew Howard): "If I die from this vaccine, just send me to California. They'll figure it out."
  • Ezra (out of character): "'If I die, please cover it up' would be a really funny sentence."
  • Dante (as Kurt Larson): "I had a piece of sporting goods equipment on me. Not a weapon: sporting goods equipment, purchased from a sporting goods store."
  • Ezra (as Daniel Webster): "Pay n' Stay is not getting a good review."
  • Ezra (as Daniel Webster): "Could people stop going missing?"
  • Dante (out of character): "Somewhat alarming that Andrew appears to have load-bearing rabies, maybe."
  • Dante (as Kurt Larson): "It could be a tulpa... It might be a dad tulpa. That wouldn't be the first dad tulpa."

docs.title: Radford Horrors 04
docs.text:
• Andre (as Crash survivor): "Not aliens. The opposite of aliens." Answering Yeltsin.
  • Andre (as Crash survivor): "Servitors... need resources." His last words before passing out.
  • Dante (as Kurt Larson): "You wake up to spears once, never again." Why he sleeps in a tree.
  • Zack (as Huell Kendrick): "Get down here, we've got goo." Phoning McManley.
  • Andre (as Donald McManley): "Is there a face this time?" ... "Small fucking mercies."
  • Rita (as Andrew Howard): "I wouldn't worry about me. I don't think it's contagious. It might be rabies." To the Blockbuster clerk.
  • Rita (as Andrew Howard): "This is my protein mix... This is meds." Passing off blood to Webster.
  • Andre (as Wilbur Whateley): "It was pregnant. It needed to breathe... it needed hosts, like a parasitic wasp."
  • Andre (as Wilbur Whateley): "I found it under a white oak." His final line before being escorted out.
  • Ezra (as Daniel Webster): "I'm trying to put together a story that isn't weird, and I'm coming up extremely short. It's just weird."
  • Ezra (as Daniel Webster): "Did we just torture a mental patient for no reason?"
  • Andre (as Rudy Giuliani): "That seems really reckless to me, Webster, running lunatics in the field."
  • Dante (out of character): "Faith healing Wilbur Whateley was not on my bingo card."
  • Andre (as Motel girl): "I don't feel good about this summer job, but I am getting that fucking horse."
  • Zack (as Huell Kendrick): "Yeah, that's why we call you Half Gallon Howard."

docs.title: Running gags
docs.text:
PITF is a horror campaign that the table cannot stop laughing through. This page traces the jokes and bits that came back session after session, both in the fiction and around the table, followed by a record of notable dice luck. For individual lines, see Quotes; for the television framing of the campaign, see The show.

Gags from the non-canon one-shot are kept in their own section near the end.

docs.title: The bedbugs of the Pay n' Stay
docs.text:
The Pay n' Stay in Radford set the standard for every bad motel that followed. The first night produced the bedbug saga: a shower curtain, aluminum foil, a wetsuit and a rash. (Radford Horror 01) Huell Kendrick was the main victim (Dante, as Huell rolled to shrug off the bites: "Hashtag built different"), and by the fifth session he had welts, the diner waitress was threatening arson if the bugs spread, and the party was proposing lye, Everclear and gunfire as cures while Kurt Larson scalded the sheets with coffee. Kurt's verdict: "At least the fucking Vietnamese jungle doesn't have bedbugs." (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05) The table also kept up "pay-per-view" and thin-wall jokes about the place, and Dante ruled that "Nobody's taking a bullet for the Pay n' Stay." (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05)

The motel followed the team out of town. In Georgia the motif came back with "Lurch" jokes and a vow of no more "Addams Family" motels. (Appalachia 01) In Utah Kurt was still asking for "some place where I don't have to sleep in a wetsuit not to get bed bug bites." (Walkers 02) When the task force went back to Radford, Andrew Howard told the IRS that "there's only two places to stay in this town, and the other one's full of bedbugs," the team was hosed with pesticide at the "Big Bug Hotel," and being "Pay n' Stayed" became a verb. Daniel Webster concluded that "Pay n' Stay is not getting a good review." (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: The dental oncologists
docs.text: Wherever the task force goes, a dental conference has already booked the good hotel. The seed is the "tooth botherers" joke about oral surgeons in the first session. (Radford Horror 01) In Dahlonega the Smith Hotel is full of dental oncologists, Andrew wonders whether "they're the Bigfoot perverts," and Kurt starts to suspect they are following the team: "Every time we go to a town, the hotel full up with dentists, every single time. It's like a curse or something." (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02) Andrew later tells Donald McManley that the town is hosting the conference. (Appalachia 03) The complaint is still alive in Utah, where Kurt says the team has had to move "to a worse one because of an enormous conference of dentists" for three or four investigations running. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: The Biz's digestion
docs.text:
The insides of Dick "The Biz" Baxter are a plot hazard from the first drive: gas station donuts and corn dogs, a failed Act Under Pressure roll at Harrisonburg, a no-flush toilet, the "toilet anaconda," and wet plumbing noises in the car. (Radford Horror 01) The Radford Arby's added a bathroom chapter. (Radford Horror 02) By the fourth session Andre had noticed that his crime move "is the one that by far gets the most use," and he had picked up the names "Mr. G.I. Tract" and a Wet Bandits calling card. (Radford Horror 04) A doctor's obsession with his fiber intake (kale salads) led Dante to announce, "We're switching the Biz to a different, higher-fiber wet food." (Radford Horror 08)

The bit never went away. The table was still joking about fiber and Gatorade in Georgia, and in Utah Kurt test-flushed the ranch toilet and glanced nervously at the Biz while Andre narrated, "You suddenly find yourself wishing you had bought vegetables." (Appalachia 06, Walkers 02) The Biz had the last word from Russia: "There's something honest about being made to shit in an ice-cold bucket." (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Arby's
docs.text: Andre holds that Arby's is the worst chain in America, and the players disagree every time it comes up. The Radford Arby's supplied the "wettest pork sandwiches," Zack rolled a lucky 11 there ("he got a Big Mac"), and Zack summed up the town's dining as "either Arby's or Howard Johnson's." (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 05) The smell and the jingle came back in Marblehead, and the argument resurfaced as a tangent as late as Utah. (Summer Service 05, Walkers 08)

docs.title: McDonald's, official sponsor
docs.text: In Marblehead, McDonald's was treated as the only safe food in town. Andre said he ate McDonald's himself "for the sake of immersion," and the table began joking about a sponsorship deal; Dante's version was "We just really want you to associate the taste of McDonald's with worm parasites." (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05) The team kept ending up there in Georgia too, where Huell explained his trust: "McDonald's is a big corporation. They hire lawyers in case I get a tapeworm." (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: "Perverts"
docs.text: Sheriff Frank Roosevelt used one word as his catch-all explanation for the Radford case. His position on the bait-dog plan: "It's not fishing. It's perverts. You don't go fishing for perverts." (Radford Horror 02) The table adopted the word as a theory of first resort. Andrew proposed "Bigfoot perverts" in Georgia, and after ruling out UTAW Kurt concluded, "Kinda narrows it down to pervert, doesn't it?" (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Kurt's trunk
docs.text:
Kurt travels with an enormous inventory, tracked by the players in a shared document. Its first audit turned up stilts, wolf urine and didgeridoos ("Why do you have that?" "Why wouldn't I?"). (Radford Horror 03) Later sessions added waders, a Super Soaker, glow sticks and a welding mask ("Never approach a hitchhiker without a welding mask"). (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 06) The Biz noted that Kurt packs stilts but no shovel; Kurt said he likes stilts for minefields. (Radford Horror 07) Of the wolf urine he later protested, "You know how hard that was to get?" (Radford Horror 08)

The list kept growing: a duct-taped coffee thermos, a fanny pack full of grenades, a stack of women's shelter cards that he presses on everyone (a detail Andre loved), stacks of fake IDs, and Hawaiian shirts as "the real urban camo." (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08) When a rental car was crushed in Utah, Kurt mourned at the trunk: "I had those stilts since Vietnam." Replacement stilts turned up in the trunk of Betsy. (Walkers 04) His spear gun got the same treatment in the final arc: confiscated at the airport, admired because "clearly it has presence" in an interrogation room, used on a rabid mouse, and defended at length as "a piece of sporting goods equipment... Not a weapon." (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03) The table's own summary is "Always with the flamethrowers." (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Kurt's pharmacy
docs.text:
Kurt's relationship with controlled substances began with expired Mandrax ("actually gets a lot stronger once it's expired") and the reveal that one of his teeth holds LSD, "one of four teeth," with the others holding "different drugs." (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03) Heroin became a universal tool: a bribe for the pilot Freak, a sedative, something to blow in an opponent's eyes. The table's summary was "our party just collects drugs," and Dante added, "Every passing moment is reinforcing my decision to do drugs." (Radford Horror 07) After a mauling in Georgia Kurt's first words were "Please, please, do you have any yayo?", and he ran through the mine on ketamine: "Racehorses take this stuff. I'm like a racehorse." (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 09)

Later sessions kept it going with ketamine for Chester, the LSD tooth and cocaine in Utah (Andre: "You are now on cocaine and LSD, which is clearly superior"), a cocaine comedown, "I rubbed some coke on it" as first aid for Huell's shin, and the last line of an episode: "This isn't coming out of my coke budget." (Walkers 01, Walkers 05, Walkers 06, Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Kurt's war stories
docs.text:
Any situation reminds Kurt of his service. He was shot "in the exact same place, twice, in Vietnam, five years apart," spent "a lot of time in Vietnam pretending to be dirt," and regrets what he "could have done to Castro with that heat ray." (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 08) Tabasco-boarding is his standard interrogation threat, first as a table joke and then in character. (Radford Horror 02, Summer Service 01) The stories grew to include an accidentally exploded dog belonging to Fidel Castro and lines of yayo "done in front of a dolphin." (Appalachia 09, Walkers 05) In the Roulet house the flashbacks became literal: he was "back in Saigon there for a second" and shot at a buried corpse's hand because "I thought it was the VC." (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

His signature technique is the "psionic flashbang," a phrase said aloud while resisting the creature in the fight with the Radford Moth: "The accident wasn't your fault." He later offered a list of alternatives, including "I still love you" and "Do you forgive me, Mother?" (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: "You ever been shot?"
docs.text: Huell asked an elderly witness named Howard, "Hey, Howard, you ever been shot?" Andrew Howard answered instead ("Yeah, what's up?"), and Zack had to explain that he meant "the other Howard." (Radford Horror 03) The payoff came at the end of the arc, when Huell greeted the other Howard in the hospital: "Hey Howard, you've been shot, buddy. Welcome to the team." (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Believing in aliens, and hating them
docs.text: Andrew wants every case to be aliens, and the others resent it when he is right. The Biz declared that "Aliens are back off the menu. So, you know, sorry, Andrew Howard," and Huell thanked Andrew sarcastically for a case that was "unusual in that there weren't aliens involved." (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04) Then the craft arrived. Kurt summed up Huell's conversion as "I didn't believe in aliens, and now I'm racist against them," and the Biz followed a session later with "I now believe in aliens, and I hate them." (Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07) Andrew's disappointment is its own bit: he was "really hoping for, like, a tractor beam," complained after a near miss in Utah that "I almost got abducted. Why weren't the windows open?", and Rita noted of Andrew that "He wants to be abducted." (Radford Horror 04, Walkers 05, Walkers 07) When a crash was reported in Russia, Dante's comment was "Somewhere Andrew is tingling." (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: 1992 and the anachronism police
docs.text:
The campaign is set in the early 1990s, and the table polices the period closely. One half of the joke is dramatic irony: World Trade Center and Oklahoma City postcards ("Those things will stand for a thousand years, I swear"), O.J. Simpson as a hero, and Huell hearing Howard Stern and predicting "This'll never last." (Radford Horror 01, Appalachia 01) The other half is fact-checking. Andre and the players have looked up, mid-session, Crystal Pepsi, Combos, Safeway, the Reservoir Dogs trailer, HIPAA, Sour Patch Kids, SoBe, Beast Wars, keycard locks, the Bellagio, Utah's stand-your-ground law, Netscape, Tasers and the Taco Bell menu. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 04, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 04, Walkers 01, Walkers 04, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04) Andre once wanted a purple Game Boy in a scene, but they did not exist yet. (Appalachia 03)

Characters slip anyway. Kurt said "Sometimes you really gotta pull out the rizz" in 1992, and the table has joked about Yelp reviews of towns, Googling "mud room," and Twitter. (Radford Horror 05, Summer Service 03) Dante's contribution from Utah: "In a few years, everybody's gonna be photographing their food." (Walkers 03)

docs.title: The Perot-verse
docs.text: The campaign's alternate history became a running joke once the election went to Ross Perot. The table joked about Perot winning before it happened, Zack asked on Election Day "Have we entered the Perot-verse?", and in the next arc Dante said, "Guess what, Ross Perot? You're gonna have a rough first fucking day." (Walkers 01, Walkers 07, Roulet Estate 01) Andre looked up Perot's voice to play him; Dante said the result sounded like a D&D goblin. (Roulet Estate 03) Perot-verse jokes continue through the last recorded sessions. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Blame Bill Clinton
docs.text:
After the Clinton surveillance scandal broke over the task force, Bill Clinton became the table's answer to every open question. Andrew's defense to Big Bill set the tone: "We're not surveilling Bill Clinton. We're surveilling dead Chewbacca."
