(Appalachia 07) The theories escalated to exploding people, a clone army, the ape-man's father, and Andre's "The sex scandals were a cover-up for Scanners," with Dante adding that "the Biz has nothing to do with it." (Appalachia 08) After the portal, the Biz wished the state police would come and look: "This is way weirder than Bill Clinton." (Appalachia 09)

The scandal follows the team to Utah, where the Biz is recognized everywhere, Huell tries to use it to flirt, and Robert Bigelow tells them it "didn't even make the list." The bartender Maggie doubts that "Bill Clinton would be caught dead in Ballard, Utah." (Walkers 02, Walkers 03) In Rhode Island, when the Biz dials the FBI, Dante sighs, "It's Bill Clinton again, man, I'm afraid." (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Splitting the party
docs.text: "I like how we split the party, like, immediately in this campaign," Ezra observed in the third session, after dividing two, three and then four ways. (Radford Horror 03) Andre's view, given in Marblehead, is that "it just kills all your players." (Summer Service 03) It keeps happening anyway, and a late session is bookended by split-party scenes. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Andre and the names
docs.text:
Andre names most NPCs on the spot and does not always remember what he chose. Early sessions had him forgetting a father, a doctor and a street; the whole table mixing up the Whateley twins as Albert, Walter, Wilbur and Abelforth; and Andre calling the Whateleys "Lucky boys." (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 08) Douglas Douglas was named in the moment, with the table predicting "he's about to become the most important character." (Radford Horror 07) Esteban was briefly Alejandro and Jose before Andre landed on it ("Esteban. Ding."). (Summer Service 04) Deborah Wells was renamed Misabelle by mistake, and Andre asked the table to "retcon that in your minds." (Walkers 03) He has also confused Big Bill with Big Bob, had Big Bill call Kurt "Howard," and conceded, "I really gotta keep my notes in a more organized fashion." (Appalachia 09, Walkers 04, Walkers 06)

He does defend the method: names are hand-picked, with jokes or relevance, not generated. (Appalachia 04) The players are no better. Rita forgot Andrew's surname on the phone ("three-first-name boy"), Zack repeatedly mixed up Howard and the Biz, Zack forgot the names of Huell's ex-wife and daughter, and Ezra had to invent "Daniel Webster" on the spot: "Fuck me, I didn't actually come up with one." (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 07, Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Andre's production values
docs.text:
Andre runs a soundtrack. He once cued Psycho-style shower music because he had forgotten to pack "relaxed suspense music," played "Tubular Bells" in the moth fight (Dante: "getting weird") before swapping to something scarier, and used "Baba O'Riley" in the arc finale. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08) He played real opera audio and showed pictures of the Hotel Metropol for the Moscow scenes, and once forgot the background music for an hour. (Radford Horrors 01, Walkers 01)

His maps are less admired. One had a rectangle "labeled dog." (Radford Horror 04) His props are better: he read out a roughly hundred-item Spud Hut menu in full, and he posted a photograph of the Davy Crockett when Kurt acquired one. (Appalachia 02, Summer Service 04)

docs.title: The church mace
docs.text: Andrew carries a church mace that sprays nothing at all. It prompted Kira to ask, "Where do I buy that mace?", and Andre to rule, "Your pepper spray is void." (Radford Horror 08) In Marblehead Andrew warned Kurt to "Hold it away from you!", and a bad roll sent what Andre called "the spray of nothingness" through Kurt's hand anyway. Rita's reaction: "Oh shit. Shit, I forgot this wasn't pepper spray." (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Toothbrush Man
docs.text: The desk clerk Jester refused Huell a toothbrush: "Not a bed-and-toothbrush." (Summer Service 01) The grudge paid off in the finale, when Jester recognized him with "It's you, Toothbrush Man!", and Huell, discovering the truth, replied, "You motherfucker, you had toothbrushes." Andre described the crushed Jester as "this pretzel man," and Ezra took it up as a chant: "Pretzel Man, Pretzel Man." (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: "Thanks, worms"
docs.text: Once Andrew had announced "Guys, we have worms!", the worms took the blame for everything. (Summer Service 03) Huell's sudden fitness drew steroid, meth and hairline jokes, and when Zack was told the parasite had made Huell jacked he said, "Thanks, worms." (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04) The Biz asked Kurt, who was loading grenades into a fanny pack, "Is this you, or is this the worms?" (Summer Service 04) Dante supplied the advertising copy ("Ask your doctor if being worms is for you"), Kira repeated a nematode fact "three or four times" by Andre's count, and by the finale she wanted to buy nightcrawlers and make worm chowder. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 06) Kurt, meanwhile, could not stop mentioning that he also had chicken pox. (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05, Summer Service 06)

docs.title: The nuke
docs.text: Kurt asked his weapons contact what "would be the ticket" if he "ever had to shoot Godzilla." (Summer Service 03) The answer was an M28 Davy Crockett, and Andrew's response ("I'm sorry, you have a nuke?") opened a session of jokes: it was laundry, it was a telescope, "get a goldfish first." (Summer Service 04) In the finale a rock-paper-scissors for the nuke was sent privately to Andre, and Huell feigned shock afterwards: "That scoundrel. What?" (Summer Service 06) It remains on Huell's resume: "I've seen dogs on their hind legs before, and also I've nuked a monster before." (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Bean juice
docs.text: Esteban was certain that someone was "putting bean juice in the laundry," which gave the table the bean-smell bit, the phrase "bean virgin," and the Biz's reflection that "You never know when you might need to make someone smell like beans." (Summer Service 04) Esteban himself was remembered only as "Bean boy" when Zack tried to recall his name, and an arc later he was still "the character functionally known as Bean Boy," with Zack claiming credit: "I named him." (Summer Service 05, Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Water people
docs.text: Andrew corrected Kurt's Wicker Man comparison in Marblehead: "No, they're not wicker people. They're definitely water people. They're wet. They're wet people." (Summer Service 01) The phrase stuck. In Georgia Huell claimed that "My grandpa called them the water people," a hotel clerk declined to get "wicker-manned," and the table was still reaching for "water people" a session later. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Spud Hut
docs.text:
Spud Hut is an invented restaurant chain that swallowed an arc. Andre read out its roughly hundred-item menu in full while the table refused to stop him ("stopping you would be like losing"), and admitted afterwards, "I should have prepared five hundred." Rita chose an order with a d100. (Appalachia 02) The savant counter kid became Kurt's project ("Son, you gotta get out of here. Your mind is an incredible gift"), with the unvarying answer that Spud Hut changed, or saved, his life. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06)

The team suspects the chain of everything ("It all comes back to Spud Hut") and eats there anyway. The whole table groaned at another dinner there, Kurt promised "Just one more dinner at Mr. Lecter's place, and then we'll start investigating him," and a joke about the team's expense receipts put the count at 72 visits in 36 hours. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 07) Menu items include a spinach and artichoke spud that everyone loves, a shrimp scampi that mysteriously makes nobody sick, margarita spuds and an octopus spud. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 07) The joke reached its peak when the counter man handed over a cryptogram with the words "That is the menu," and when Jan Martense explained the lowest floor of his plant: "Down here we do the toppings." (Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08) Huell dreaded another potato case as soon as the team reached Utah, and Andrew later complained about Kurt "recruiting high schoolers out of every case that we do. The Spud Hut one and now this one?" (Walkers 02, Walkers 04)

docs.title: "We're getting a boiler"
docs.text: Every member of the Covenant answers every question about hygiene with the same sentence, with the delivery date slipping from next year to February. Kurt was unmoved: "And the Viet Cong prison camps had hot water." (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Andrew looks like a fed
docs.text: Douglas Douglas told Andrew, "You look the most like a Fed of anyone I've ever seen." (Radford Horror 07) It has been true ever since. He is identified as a cop in every scene in Georgia, including by a motel clerk who reads his Bigfoot T-shirt as proof that he "took off your cop outfit." (Appalachia 06) Kurt resolved to take him to dance classes once the case was over. (Appalachia 07) His flight from a Fox 5 microphone with a sweaty "Thank you for your time" became an in-fiction viral clip, complete with an imagined trip-hop remix. (Appalachia 08) In Utah the table settled on "ACAB" as "assigned cop at birth." (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Evidence nobody wanted to carry
docs.text: The task force's samples for McManley are a recurring horror. They have transported a severed arm that left its smell in the Biz's car through layers of Tiger Balm, a live dog head, and a folded face in a bag, which McManley received "Like Christmas." (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 03) The table eventually adopted a rule: "no transporting human remains unless it's really gross." (Appalachia 06) When Huell phoned to say "Get down here, we've got goo," McManley answered, "Is there a face this time?" ... "Small fucking mercies." (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Nancy the goose
docs.text:
Nancy, the goose at Sherman Ranch, is the most feared creature of the Utah arc. She appears at windows as a jump scare, wins every battle of wills, and is protected by a house rule: "keep the fucking goose happy." (Walkers 02) Kurt moved to the Jeep in two-man elements to watch for her, complained that geese are "immune to capsaicin," improvised a "ham bang" when he had no flashbangs, and lost his baloney to her after a Preparedness roll produced it. (Walkers 02, Walkers 03, Walkers 04) He also called her a swan and reported feeling "less pressure from the enemy forces" in a trench. (Walkers 05) Walt "Coyote" Murphy considers her his biggest problem in life and intends to eat her. (Walkers 02, Walkers 03)

She was blamed for chewed wires and for most other things before the real culprits were known, and her name would not stay with the table. Zack decided that Huell thinks she is called Betsy, like the squad car ("It's a dumb joke"), and by the finale Rita could not remember the name at all while Dante guessed "Beatrice." (Walkers 06, Walkers 07, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Half-Gallon Howard
docs.text: In Ballard the team learned of the town's water contamination and began warning everyone they met: "We're from the government. Don't drink the water unless it's bottled or from a well." (Walkers 02) The nickname was the Biz's, coined at Maggie's bar during a conversation about what could have tainted the groundwater: he "couldn't imagine half-gallon Howard." He then introduced Andrew to the bartender as "my friend, Half-Gallon Howard," while Andrew turned further and further away. By the next session Andre reckoned Andrew had been called it "conservatively five times this evening." (Walkers 03, Walkers 04) The name has outlasted the arc. It came back in Rhode Island and ran all through the return to Radford, and Huell was still using it at the end: "Yeah, that's why we call you Half Gallon Howard." (Walkers 05, Roulet Estate 02, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Rental cars and Betsy
docs.text: "We are not being very good with rentals lately." The Plymouth Voyager came back from the vanishing-car incident pancaked, and the Biz pointed out that all of the cars they had driven in Utah had been pancaked, on top of one irradiated earlier. Andrew reported the recovery as "Our car's back. It got unabducted." (Walkers 04, Walkers 05) The replacement, a loaner squad car named Betsy, smells of "high school sadness," is stuffed with Cats costumes and has a novelty horn; Rita is protective of her. (Walkers 05, Walkers 08) The table once tallied which arcs involved hitting someone with a vehicle: men in black were hit twice in the moth arc, including Agent Murphy, which Kurt regretted mainly because it was "a borrowed car." (Radford Horror 03, Walkers 08)

docs.title: Ham
docs.text: Carl, a hungover cop at the police station, says only "Ham." The table built outward from there: ham-boarding, ham choking, "Tim Hortons Ham Horkers," a clerk offering ham, and a plan to introduce the goose to the ham guy. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: Magnets
docs.text: The beam at the ranch gave the table "Magnets, how do they work?", "Utah, you can't throw a rock without hitting a magnet," and Dante's four-word case summary, "Magnet stole sheet metal." (Walkers 06)

docs.title: "I hate it here"
docs.text: The refrain of bystanders caught up in a PITF case. The assistant Henry ended a session with "I hate it here. It sucks so bad." (Summer Service 05) Yusuf Ansari, the junkyard owner, repeated "I hate it here so much" as a refrain. (Walkers 08) Dante used it out of character about the team's lack of a mobile phone. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Phones
docs.text: The task force has no phone it can keep. The Biz reasoned that "If they really wanted us to contact them, they would give us car phones," and Ezra's request for one was left "waiting to hear back." (Walkers 03) Andre later admitted a "small mistake" about a car phone, and Dante is still angry that a pharmacy in an earlier session had a mobile phone when the team has never held on to one. (Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Roseanne
docs.text: Roseanne is the show's symbol of rock bottom. Huell bonded with McManley over it, all three of Huell, Kurt and Andrew ended up watching it, and it was on the Biz's television in Moscow (Dante: "Goddamn, you can't escape"). (Appalachia 01, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: "Ghosts aren't real"
docs.text: Andrew, who believes in ascended Masters and flying saucers, draws the line at ghosts. "Oh, ghosts aren't real," he tells Diane at the start of the Utah case. The line broke up the table, and Zack explained why: "it's a long-running gag too... It's a callback to our last campaign." (Walkers 01)

docs.title: The Indestructo-twink
docs.text: Jokes about Andrew's slight build started in Georgia, with his striped pajamas and sleeping cap, and Zack guessing that his unrevealed middle name is Marion. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03) Once he had proved bullet resistant, the plan became "We send in the Indestructo-twink first." (Roulet Estate 01) His condition supplied the next round: blood passed off to Webster as "my protein mix," a "Not a vampire" defense, and Dante's diagnosis that "Andrew appears to have load-bearing rabies." (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04) Andre observed that Andrew "proved you were human... by being bulletproof." (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Andrew's dad
docs.text: Andrew's dreams usually involve someone "talking to me or crouching over me or licking my face." (Appalachia 03) The table's gag about a kiss from his alien dad was echoed when his double leaned in to kiss him. (Walkers 07) In the Roulet house Kurt talked him down from a hallucination with "Is it really worse than your dad?", and Andrew answered, "It's like I'm being swallowed by my dad." (Roulet Estate 02) A later dream had his father dunking on him at beach volleyball, and in the same session Kurt floated "a dad tulpa. That wouldn't be the first dad tulpa." (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Copies
docs.text: When the Skinwalker plot produced duplicates, Zack said, "Copies is like my favorite thing," and imagined playing many Huells. Rita, secretly playing Andrew's replica, complained about "the fact that I have to play an idiot." (Walkers 07) The jokes about the copies as "Gundam" and "Stevangelion" lasted into the next session, and Huell later needled Andrew: "Of course, I didn't notice when you got replaced with an alien." (Walkers 08, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Every case is two things
docs.text: The table tracks the pattern of its own campaign. After the moth and the worms, Ezra asked "What next, guys?" and Kira answered "Snail." (Summer Service 05) Ezra described the Utah mystery as thinking "you got the strawberry jelly bean, but it turned out to be apple." (Walkers 03) In Rhode Island the players listed "two things every time": a cult and aliens, a cult and worms, a gold mine with Yeti hybrids (Zack disputed the list). (Roulet Estate 02) Dante's verdict on the first arc was "Last mystery, we solved almost no questions," and the Biz's wish is on record: "what I wouldn't give to just investigate a regular serial killer right now." (Summer Service 01, Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Krisp and other gremlins
docs.text: The recordings are haunted by their own software. Noise suppression swallowed Dante's yell in the moth fight, caused a "warbly" glitch when Andre turned it off to perform the creature's fluting noise, and "ate" Zack's Geiger-counter mouth noises. (Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 06) Zack's space heater was "a jazz musician," his microphone has sounded like a Speak & Spell and been declared "haunted," and Andre's dropouts were once played as a seance. (Radford Horror 04, Appalachia 08, Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 04) A music bot once looped through the call, and a broken dice roller left Andre rolling for the players in several late sessions. (Appalachia 08, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Private scenes
docs.text: Andre runs secret scenes by moving the other players out of the voice call: Kurt's rooftop confrontation in Marblehead, the Biz's private business in Georgia, and a secret message for Huell in Utah. (Summer Service 01, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 06, Walkers 06) Ezra once did the reverse, sharing a theory with the table while Andre had his headphones off so that he could not react. (Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: Kira's corner
docs.text: Kira, a guest at the table, has her own recurring suggestions: a "roll to eat pancakes," steady urging that the party eat the mysterious root, a wish to adopt Lena Scott, and the worm chowder. (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Philosopher's Fist gags
docs.text:
Non-canon

These come from Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, the non-canon one-shot.

  • Derk is not clever. Andre noted that "it's amazing how Derk being fucking stupid has dominated the tone of this one-shot," and Dante admitted that he "really pushed all the onus of, like, actual thinking, planning onto Rita." Derk is told to use his "inside voice," admits "I can't really count," and rolls with what Dante calls "my default minus one." (Philosopher's Fist)
  • Mr. Doggy. Derk keeps assuming everyone in charge is a werewolf ("you turn into a dog, right?"), not just the president. (Philosopher's Fist)
  • "Asteroid." Derk's word for steroids: "Mirabeth, I've been on asteroid before. Am I gonna get in trouble?" (Philosopher's Fist)
  • Hot dog accounting. Derk measures everything in hot dogs: a cart sells him 98 of them, and an $86 motel room prompts "How many hot dogs is that?" (Philosopher's Fist)
  • Mirabeth's lies. Mirabeth accumulates cover stories, among them an MLM and the claim, made to get the 21-year-old Derk under an age limit of fifteen, that "I do believe he's fourteen years old." (Philosopher's Fist)
  • Bugs. Derk's jumps coat him in insects, leading to a fountain bath and a licked-tissue cleanup. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Notable dice luck
docs.text:
PITF uses Monster of the Week: two six-sided dice plus a rating, where 6 or less is a miss, 7 to 9 is a mixed success and 10 or more is a full success. A miss earns experience, which is why bad nights are also level-up nights. See Game mechanics for the rules as played.

Episode Player What happened Radford Horror 01 Ezra The Biz totals 6 three times, once even with +2 to Charm. Ezra: "I roll like bullshit. I got a six again." Radford Horror 03 Ezra, Zack Ezra rolls double sixes on the flashlight roll ("Double sixes, baby"), and both he and Zack level up. Andre: "Lots of experience this session." Radford Horror 06 Ezra, Dante Ezra rolls double sixes for a 14; snake eyes turn up for Dante late in the session. Radford Horror 07 Everyone Dante rolls snake eyes looking for a shovel, and the moth fight goes so badly that Rita sums it up: "So we just half-TPK'd." Radford Horror 08 Ezra So many misses that he is "marking X's over top of the X's," one failure short of a double level-up. Summer Service 03 Ezra The Biz, with +3 to Investigate a Mystery, rolls 14 twice. Summer Service 05 Zack, Rita Zack rolls a 14 and a 15; Rita's 2 sends the church mace's spray through Kurt's hand. Summer Service 06 Ezra Calls a 10 "Not great" and has to be reminded that on 2d6 it is a complete success. Dante: "This ain't D&D, baby." Appalachia 01 Zack Rolls a 3 and burns a Luck point to rescue it. Ezra: "He chooses now to burn a Luck point." Appalachia 03 Dante Snake eyes. Appalachia 06 Rita, Dante A hot night: Rita opens with a 12 and Dante rolls back-to-back 11s. Appalachia 09 Dante, Rita Dante rolls 11 three times, the second saving him from the ape-men; Rita rolls a 4. Walkers 01 Ezra Burns a Luck point to turn a roll into a 12, which is the only reason David Letterman says yes. Walkers 03 Zack, Ezra Zack spends Luck on a game of darts. Ezra: "I appreciate blowing it on stupid shit." Walkers 04 Zack, Ezra Zack rolls double sixes twice ("I'm gonna get a lot of 12s today"); Ezra rolls 12 twice running. Walkers 06 Zack Double ones for a total of 3, then an 11 near the end of the session. Walkers 07 Zack, Rita Zack's 15 on first aid; Rita rerolls a cocked die into a 13. Walkers 08 Rita Rolls a 3: "there's no amount of addition that will save that." Later she announces a 10 and Andre answers, "You actually didn't... You got a zero." Walkers 09 Zack Rolls 12, 14 and 14: "Damn, I'm on fire today." Roulet Estate 01 Ezra A natural 12 for a total of 15. Roulet Estate 03 Zack A streak of 11s: "I've been rolling good today." Radford Horrors 01 Ezra Finds his dice in a drawer in another room and rolls an 11 on the key roll. Radford Horrors 02 Zack A 6, a 4 and another 6 ("I'm not doing good today"), while Dante rolls 10s and 11s. Radford Horrors 03 Ezra Burns Luck three times in one session, once to turn a roll into a 12: "I don't know what Doomed means." Philosopher's Fist Dante In the one-shot Dante rolls a 15 in spite of Derk's standing −1: "Holy shit, I got a fifteen."

Andre also keeps a roll's result to himself when it suits the scene: "'Cause it's more fun that way." (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Tropes
docs.text:
Quote

"I have to go into work. The Protestants are trying to kill my detectives."

Andre (as Big Bill), summing up the premise on his way out of bed (Summer Service 06)

PITF is an early-1990s network drama about the Paranatural Incident Task Force, a tiny FBI unit staffed by four people nobody else wanted: a true believer raised in a UFO church, a divorcing skeptic, a constipated con artist with a badge, and a Vietnam-era spook with drugs in his teeth. It is also, depending on which side of the screen you sit on, a Monster of the Week campaign run by Andre for Rita, Zack, Ezra and Dante, with a rotating bench of guest players. See The show for how seriously the table takes the framing (answer: there are credits).

Across six arcs the team investigates a moth in Virginia, worms in Massachusetts, ape-men under a potato company in Georgia, body snatchers in Utah, a "Grey" in a Rhode Island attic, and then the moth again, because nothing in Radford ever stays dealt with. Along the way they fire one tactical nuclear weapon, lose rental cars at an alarming rate, and live through a 1992 election that Ross Perot wins.

Somewhere in the middle there is also an anime. It has its own section.

Examples below are sorted alphabetically and cited by episode. Beware of unmarked spoilers: this page gives away every twist the campaign has, including the one the players did not know about.

docs.title: A–C
docs.text:
• Abandoned Mine: Dahlonega's tourist gold mine swallows a boy on a guided tour and leaves his Game Boy on the floor. Then the team falls through a boarded floor into a hidden shaft from the electric era, which is worse. (Appalachia 03)
  • Affably Evil: Jan Martense explains his ape-man breeding scheme with the cheerful candor of a man describing a kitchen remodel. (Walkers 01)
  • Agent Mulder: Andrew Howard, who keeps a mental list of UFO shapes and quizzes witnesses from it. (Radford Horror 04)
    • Inverted with Walt "Coyote" Murphy, whose explanation for a thing that fell burning out of the sky is ball lightning. Half an hour of Andrew's UFO case histories gets him as far as grudging respect. (Walkers 04)
  • Agent Scully: Huell Kendrick and the Biz start as the doubters. Huell holds out until he is hanging off an astronaut that something is lifting into the sky; the Biz is officially "on board" by Georgia. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06, Appalachia 04)
    • Daniel Webster inherits the role in the final arc, and his notebook soon contains the line "Andrew Howard is a vampire?" (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Alien Abduction: Phoebe Augustine is taken, though not by tractor beam: something swoops down and lifts her. Years later Billy Thornton tells an abduction story nobody will listen to. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Alien Autopsy: The examiner opens a Ballard corpse and finds it is not human. (Walkers 08)
  • Aliens Steal Cattle: The Utah case opens with exploded sheep and mutilated cattle at the Sherman Ranch. The previous FBI team blamed lightning and drink. (Walkers 01, Walkers 02)
  • The Alleged Car: A proud lineage.
    • The task force's shabby 1961 Lincoln Continental. (Radford Horror 01)
    • Betsy, a loaner squad car that smells of "high school sadness" and comes with Cats costumes. (Walkers 04, Walkers 05, Walkers 08)
    • Aerial variant: Freak's house-painted Cessna "Annabelle", which has a disco ball, misfires, and barely clears a pine on takeoff. (Radford Horror 07)
  • Alternate History: Perot wins in 1992, fires the FBI director, and puts Rudy Giuliani in the chair. See Alternate history. (Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Anachronism Stew: Averted with a vengeance. Andre fact-checks HIPAA, OxyContin, Tasers and the purple Game Boy mid-session, while Kurt says "rizz" in 1992 and gets called on it. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 05, Appalachia 03, Radford Horrors 03)
  • Anticlimax: The Marblehead finale. The party nukes the boss from a mile away, finishes it with a flashlight when that is not enough, and declines to enter the facility. Andre admits the session ended early as a result. (Summer Service 06)
  • Anyone Can Die: Arnold Weathers and his dog Puddles are both worm hosts by the time anyone thinks to check on them. (Summer Service 05)
  • Apocalypse Cult: The Sons of Adam, with sea baptisms, a Revelation 13 sermon and a town council waiting for the second coming. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 04)
  • Apocalypse Not: The skinwalkers' evacuation through the portal is foiled and the world is not destroyed. The community center is. (Walkers 09)
  • Bad Boss: Jan locks his own staff underground with the ape-men and leaves. (Appalachia 09)
  • Bag of Holding: Andrew's satchel, later formalized as the What I Need When I Need It bag, which produces a grenade at the worst possible moment in Utah. Andrew thinks he just forgets what he put in there. Andre's assessment of the mechanic: "the combinatorics are fucked." (Appalachia 07, Walkers 07)
    • Kurt's fanny pack and car trunk are the mundane version. They contain stilts. (Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 04)
  • Bait-and-Switch: Webster braces for the team's insane account of Radford and is handed a calm, mundane-sounding story about a spaceman. It is true. (Radford Horrors 04)
  • Bavarian Fire Drill: Henry is sent to Salem on a Vespa, in a storm, with Kurt's concealed carry permit as his credentials. (Summer Service 04)
    • The party bluffs its way past both stoned teenagers and police. (Walkers 04)
    • The Biz, a prisoner in Moscow, blends truth and exaggeration about how seriously the United States takes all this. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Bears Are Bad News: The half-faced bear. Big Bill does not want to hear about the bears. (Appalachia 07)
  • Beware the Nice Ones: Ballard's friendly sheriff and friendly Walt, in a town with a great deal behind the friendliness. (Walkers 03)
  • Big Friendly Dog: Harvey the Great Dane adores Andrew, knocks him flat twice, and gets scooped up and cradled like a baby. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 07)
  • Bigfoot, Sasquatch and Yeti: The whole Appalachian arc. The party spends weeks arguing real versus costumed, and the answer is "both". (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 03)
  • Bittersweet Ending: Two for two on arc finales.
    • Marblehead: the threat dies, a lot of people die with it, and there is fallout. (Summer Service 06)
    • Rhode Island: the case is solved, the team is shot up, scattered and disbanded. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Bizarre Alien Biology: Per Wilbur, the Radford Moth has to breed, and its young are born pregnant. (Radford Horror 07)
  • Black Comedy: The young cop steps out of his squad car and a rifle shot takes off the top of his head, leaving his colleagues locked in the back seat and Kurt searching the body for the keys. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Black Helicopter: Upgraded to silent black triangles, with hazmat teams underneath. (Walkers 09)
  • Body Horror: Pick an arc.
    • A partially eaten body by the interstate, and a proboscis that drains flesh and fat. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 07)
    • Bloated, translucent, hairless worm bags, and Huell attempting self-surgery. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05)
    • The half-a-man crash survivor, tubed to a soldier. (Radford Horrors 04)

  • Brick Joke: In the first Marblehead episode Jester refuses Huell a toothbrush. In the last, Huell's death ray misses him and he knows exactly who is holding it. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 06)

    Quote

    "It's you, Toothbrush Man!"

    Andre (as Jester) (Summer Service 06)

  • Burger Fool: The Spud Hut counter savant, a kid with perfect recall working a potato register. Kurt campaigns to get him a better job. The kid's position:

    Quote

    "Spud Hut saved my life."

    Andre (as the counter kid) (Appalachia 06)

  • By-the-Book Cop: Webster, clean-cut and shiny-shoed, dropped into this team. (Radford Horrors 01)

    • Big Bill demands clean hands in Georgia. He does not get them. (Appalachia 03)
  • The Call Is Coming from Inside the House: The Roulet intruder has been living in the owners' attic for a year, photographing them asleep. (Roulet Estate 02)
  • Came Back Wrong: Andrew is shot point-blank, wakes under a pile of bodies in a morgue, and comes back fast, bulletproof and thirsty. See Andrew Howard (the Monstrous). (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)
  • Car Fu: Kurt hits Agent Murphy with a borrowed car. By Utah, Andre just asks whether he wants to hit them. (Radford Horror 03, Walkers 08)
  • Cassandra Truth: Practically a recurring cast member.
    • Andrew's sea-monster guess is brushed off; Madeline Weathers's report was ignored. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 05)
    • Edward Nick saw something real and his mother filed it under "Bigfoot nonsense". (Appalachia 02)
    • Alberta Wilmarth was ignored by everyone until the FBI arrived. (Walkers 02)
    • The party truthfully warns Ballard about the water and Ballard hears a joke. (Walkers 03)
    • Kurt's portal warnings, post-disbandment, reach nobody. (Roulet Estate 03)

  • Catchphrase: Andrew, who believes in aliens, angels and the Masters, has one firm line. (Walkers 01, Walkers 06)

    Quote

    "Oh, ghosts aren't real."

    Rita (as Andrew) (Walkers 01)

  • Chekhov's Armoury: The basement arsenal under the D.C. barbershop, and whatever is in Kurt's trunk this week. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 06)

  • Chekhov's Gun: Nearly every episode loads one. Highlights:
    • The bug in Dr. Lori's vent and the pink butterfly hair tie. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 05)
    • Everclear, bolt cutters and a tinfoil-lined welding mask, all packed before the church and all used in it. (Radford Horror 07)
    • The Davy Crockett, carried for three sessions before it is fired. (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 06)
    • Kurt's Claymore, carried since the previous mystery. (Appalachia 08)
    • Kurt's hollow molars. The LSD one is first spat into Agent Murphy's mouth in Radford, and its twin is bitten on purpose in Utah. (Radford Horror 03, Walkers 05)
    • The beta blockers from the attic lair, which resurface with the gunman. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Chew Toy: Andrew is berated by Big Bill, mistrusted by witnesses, airsick, bitten by an old woman, and eventually murdered and replaced. (Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 07, Walkers 08, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Cliffhanger: Andre ends on them deliberately.
    • Molly Underhill reveals a mutilated body. (Radford Horror 04)
    • Soldiers and flamethrower men close in on a half-dead party. (Radford Horror 07)
    • The session stops with the Ivermectin unopened and the team hunted. (Summer Service 05)
    • The Appalachia recordings end unresolved; the finale itself is one of the lost episodes. (Appalachia 09)
    • Giuliani closes the premiere of the last arc by asking about Radford. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Clingy MacGuffin: The folded face, which travels in a bag. Later arcs still ask "Is there a face this time?" (Appalachia 04, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Closed Circle: Three flavors.
    • Tropical Storm Andrew 2 isolates Marblehead and grounds the cavalry. (Summer Service 05)
    • Phones, power, cars and the road are all cut around Ballard and Roosevelt. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08)
    • The Roulet House: snow, no car, no phone, no power. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)
  • Cloudcuckoolander: Rutherford, night clerk and Anunnaki theorist. (Radford Horror 04)
    • Robert Bigelow, and Drebin with his iguana. (Walkers 05)
    • Eduardo Hooper, the drunk who orders off the secret menu. (Appalachia 07)
  • Cold Open: Nearly every episode has one, usually ending on Andre saying "cut to credits". The player characters are often nowhere in them. Subverted in the last arc's premiere, which runs a found-footage attack on FBI agents, announces "This time we don't cut to credits", and holds them back until the final line of the episode. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Company Town: Douglas Douglas cannot leave his guard shack, must buy his food from his employer, and gets supply drops every three months. Andrew writes down the Department of Labor's number for him. (Radford Horror 07)
  • Conspiracy Theorist: Rutherford and his Art Bell radio. (Radford Horror 01)
    • The table itself, whose CIA/Soviet/bioweapon theories escalate hourly. (Appalachia 03)
    • Webster, who is sure it is all Bush-era dirty tricks. It is a moth. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Corrupt Corporate Executive: Jan Martense of Spud Hut. (Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09)
  • Cosmic Horror Story: The moth's wings touch the mind, and its last words to Andrew imply makers. The game even borrows a Dread mechanic from Lovecraft-style systems. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 03)
  • Covert Group with Mundane Front: The Safe Environment Fund, whose bunny-suited staff sweep crime scenes. (Radford Horrors 02)
    • The KGB's sweepstakes front. (Appalachia 01)
    • Spud Hut's distribution center, which has a Special Projects level. (Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09)
  • Crazy-Prepared: Kurt's inventory has included stilts, a jug of wolf urine, didgeridoos, rollerblades, lawn darts, a black Super Soaker, caltrops and a steel plate. Asked why he has that, he asks why he wouldn't. (Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 06, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Creepy Basement: The Whateleys' root cellar. (Radford Horror 06)
  • Crucified Hero Shot: Played for horror with Amanda Lucky, and again with the stations in the old-town church. (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 07)
  • Cult: At least one per arc if you count generously.
    • The Sons of Adam. (Summer Service 01)
    • The Covenant of Auraria, who are really nice and are getting a boiler. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 04)
    • The Aetherius Society, which is Andrew's church. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: D–F
docs.text:
• Da Chief: Big Bill, who pages, berates, wants Georgia done strictly by the book, and does not care about the bears. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 07)
  • Dead Drop: A paving-stone cache under a bench, with flash paper. (Appalachia 01)
  • Dead Man's Switch: Kurt's answer to an IRS raid is a grenade. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Deadpan Snarker: The Biz and Huell in character; Dante, Zack and Ezra out of it. (Radford Horror 02, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 08)
  • Death Ray: The flashlight weapon, a handheld device that sets people and trees ablaze. The party takes one off a searcher after the church fire, and in Marblehead it does what a nuclear warhead could not. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 06)
    • The invisible heat-and-magnet beam over the ranch, tested with a penny and Kurt's broken watch, which leaves at speed. (Walkers 06)
  • Disaster Dominoes: Power cut, portal collapse, cavern collapse, sinkhole. (Walkers 09)
  • Doppelgänger: Andrew meets himself in Utah. It does not go well for the original. See Andrew Howard (duplicate). (Walkers 07)
  • Double Agent: The Biz has a KGB contact and a secret mission, run in private scenes with the other players muted. In the last arc everyone keeps asking whether he or Kurt is one. (Appalachia 01, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Dr. Feelgood: Dr. Lori, accused of over-prescribing. (Radford Horror 02)
  • Dramatic Irony: Period-flavored: World Trade Center and Oklahoma City postcards, and O.J. Simpson as a hero. (Radford Horror 01)
    • Table-flavored: Andre clears Dante, Ezra and Zack off the call to tell Rita she is now playing the replica, and the real Andrew's revival is played after they have left. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08)
  • Dreaming of Things to Come: Andrew is visited in sleep paralysis by a dead gray stranger who says to stay away from the water. (Summer Service 03)
    • He dreams of a naked double shortly before acquiring one. (Walkers 06)
    • He plays beach volleyball beside a blood-red ocean, and his alien dad warns him off the rabies treatment. The fever follows. (Radford Horrors 03)
  • Dutch Angle: Called for by name: the camera tilts as a vacuum salesman's baptismal peach drink kicks in. (Appalachia 04)
  • Eccentric Millionaire: Bigelow, with his UFO lab on a cursed ranch. (Walkers 02, Walkers 05)
  • Elaborate Underground Base: Spud Hut's Special Projects level, four floors down, with medical and animal-handling equipment. (Appalachia 08)
    • The cavern under Ballard's community center, reached through a door marked "Ballroom". (Walkers 09)
  • Eldritch Abomination: The angel thing, which dies sprouting the legs of every animal species. (Summer Service 06)
  • Eldritch Location: The glass-scorched lighthouse. (Summer Service 03)
  • Evil Twin: Asked to open its mouth, the replica says "I don't wanna", shoots Kurt in the leg and bolts. (Walkers 09)
  • Eye Scream: The Biz drives his fingers into the moth's eyes. Karma collects in Russia. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horrors 03)
  • Fall Guy: Wilbur takes the blame for the moth's crimes. (Radford Horror 08)
    • Yusuf Ansari is coerced into a suspiciously convenient confession. (Walkers 05, Walkers 06)
  • Fantastic Drug: The Covenant's peach preserves, served at breakfast. (Appalachia 01)
    • Spud Hut keeps its ape-man workforce on ketamine. (Appalachia 09)
  • Feathered Fiend: Nancy the goose. She wins every battle of wills, and is the leading suspect for the eye on the roof. (Walkers 02, Walkers 05)
  • Feel No Pain: The naked intruder ignores his foot wounds. (Walkers 07)
  • Fish out of Water: Federal agents in a town with three cops; East Coasters among Utah customs; a Spud Hut financial auditor reduced to tailing the FBI; the Biz at a Russian opera. (Radford Horror 02, Appalachia 06, Walkers 02, Radford Horrors 01)
  • Flashback: The Amanda cold open turns out to be earlier events. (Radford Horror 05)
    • Rhode Island runs on "78 days ago" title cards. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Foreshadowing: Kurt feels off after the communion wine. (Summer Service 01)
    • A coyote stands up in a cold open in the same episode that introduces a man nicknamed Coyote. (Walkers 02)
    • A bullet slows down before it reaches Andrew, long before anyone asks why. (Radford Horror 07)
  • Found Footage: The style of the cold open that kills the previous task force. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Frame-Up: The Biz stages a junkie burglary. (Radford Horror 04)
    • FBI prints turn up on surveillance equipment during the Clinton scandal. (Appalachia 07)
  • Frazetta Man: The ape-men: pale tunnel things that imitate a crying baby, and that Spud Hut has put to work mining gold. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 09)
  • Functional Addict: "Our party just collects drugs," as the table puts it. Heroin serves as bribe, sedative and bonding exercise in a single episode. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: G–L
docs.text:
• Gallows Humor: Constant. Arm-in-a-cooler jokes, jokes about eating the corpse, Vietnam banter about getting shot in the ass. (Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 01, Walkers 03)
  • Ghost Town: Ballard empties out a few residents at a time, leaving dust and an unattended City Hall. Then Roosevelt goes dark. (Walkers 06, Walkers 08)
  • Gilded Cage: The Biz at the Hotel Metropol: pampered, guarded, not allowed to leave. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Gold Fever: Everyone pockets gold bars as "civil forfeiture" while Clive looks on. Huell and the Biz take enough to slow themselves down. (Appalachia 09)
  • Gone Horribly Right: The Biz's awkward Letterman interview leaves him less hated and considerably more famous, which is not what a man with a KGB contact wants. (Walkers 01)
  • Government Conspiracy: A presidential task force, a rooftop watcher, SKYHOOK classifications, a mystery group with an unnamed commanding officer, and whoever keeps sending the men in volcanologist suits. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 06)
  • The Greys: The Greys of Rhode Island, including a naked one on the roof with a VSS rifle. See "Scooby-Doo" Hoax. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Haunted House: An isolated Victorian in the snow, with secret chimney passages. (Roulet Estate 02)
  • Healing Hands: Andrew's Lay On Hands, which works by transferring the harm to Andrew. (Radford Horror 03, Appalachia 03)
  • Hell Hotel: The Pay n' Stay. Bedbugs on the first visit. On the second, Kurt hoses both rooms with pesticide before anyone unpacks, and a rabid mouse bites a guest anyway. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Heroic BSoD: Huell is genuinely sad to learn cryptids are real. (Radford Horror 08)
    • Sheriff Burke hugs a tree. (Appalachia 09)
  • Heroic Sacrifice: Huell fills all seven harm boxes going back into a burning church to free the Biz from under the moth. He lives. (Radford Horror 07)
    • Coyote's APC run on the substation looks like one, until the team rights the overturned vehicle and finds him alive inside. (Walkers 09)
  • Hillbilly Horrors: Invoked by the table on arrival in Georgia, mostly through Deliverance jokes. (Appalachia 01)
  • Historical Domain Character: Perot, Boris Yeltsin, Bill Clinton, George H. W. Bush, Giuliani, Letterman and Bigelow all appear or loom. Andre looked up Perot's voice; Dante says it came out as a D&D goblin. (Walkers 02, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Horror Hunger: Andrew's blood craving. Faced with a pool of a hostage's blood he takes a penalty for the whole fight rather than drink, then licks his hands clean afterwards while the Biz watches. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Hostage Situation: A naked "alien" in a Brooks Pharmacy demands a Range Rover and that all police come inside nude. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • I Want to Believe: Andrew hopes it is aliens every time. After the moth, the Biz would rather it were not. (Walkers 03)
  • Improvised Weapon: A toilet tank lid. (Summer Service 05)
  • In Medias Res: The agents wake hungover with no memory of the night. (Roulet Estate 01)

  • Insistent Terminology: The party did not carjack that couple. "Commandeer" is the preferred nomenclature. (Radford Horror 06)

    • It is not a spear gun.

    Quote

    "I had a piece of sporting goods equipment on me. Not a weapon: sporting goods equipment, purchased from a sporting goods store."

    Dante (as Kurt) (Radford Horrors 03)

  • Jump Scare: The Biz shrieks at an arm, four floors underground. (Appalachia 08)

  • Jurisdiction Friction: Sheriff Roosevelt is wary of feds and has his own theory.

    Quote

    "It's not fishing. It's perverts. You don't go fishing for perverts."

    Andre (as Sheriff Roosevelt) (Radford Horror 02)

    • Inverted in Rhode Island, where Officer Todd "officially surrenders operational command" to Andrew, who would rather he had not. (Roulet Estate 03)
    • Kill and Replace: The skinwalkers grow copies from tissue; Andrew's is wearing his outfit. Half a high school is missing. See Replication. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08)
    • Kill It with Fire: The moth hates it; a thrown bottle of Everclear turns the fight, and the church burns with the creature padlocked inside. (Radford Horror 07)
    • Dante's verdict by Rhode Island: "Always with the flamethrowers." (Roulet Estate 01)
    • Lampshade Hanging: The table notes that Spud Hut stocks every ingredient known to man and serves only potato. (Appalachia 02)
    • Ezra, taking stock of the cases so far: "I feel like it's been two things every time, actually." (Roulet Estate 02)
    • Language Barrier: The Finnish Hare Krishna monk, whom the party keeps taking with them. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)
    • Laser-Guided Amnesia: The white powder that falls on Utah, and the gap it leaves. (Walkers 09, Roulet Estate 01)
    • Let's Split Up, Gang!: "I like how we split the party, like, immediately in this campaign," says Ezra, in a session that splits it three times. Andre's opinion of the practice is that it kills all your players. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 03)
    • Locked Room Mystery: Amanda's bedroom is locked from the inside and the way out was up. (Radford Horror 01)
    • A comatose boy vanishes after being checked on. (Radford Horror 06)
    • Lovecraft Country: A New England fishing town with a strange church and something in the water. Dante is calling it Innsmouth by the first episode. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: M–P
docs.text:
• Mad Scientist Laboratory: Special Projects. (Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09)
  • The Masquerade: Maintained almost entirely by paperwork.
    • Radford: strangers scrub the church and the police blame the cartel. (Radford Horror 08)
    • Marblehead: "terrorists". Three official versions exist by the next arc. See Terrorist cover story. (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01)
    • Utah: a cult compound and a Jonestown-style mass killing. (Roulet Estate 01)
    • Radford again: Giuliani wants an acceptable fact pattern, and the missing are said to be in treatment in LA. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

  • The Men in Black: Agent Murphy, in black suit and sunglasses, introduces the type.

    Quote

    "I'm Agent Murphy. I'm NSA. You are fucking this up for me."

    Andre (as Agent Murphy), having just been hit by a car (Radford Horror 03)

    • The cleanup crew in volcanologist gear. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08)
    • The gray van crew. (Radford Horrors 04)
    • Mind Control: The moth makes Huell shoot Andrew, and has been "wearing" Wilbur for years. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08, Radford Horrors 04)
    • Mind Screw: During the night event each PC gets a different hallucination. Andrew seals himself in the refrigerator. (Walkers 05)
    • Missing Time: Kurt loses a minute. (Roulet Estate 01)
    • Molotov Cocktail: Everclear, thrown by Kurt, which also rains on Kurt. (Radford Horror 07)
    • Monster Clown: The Clown Mansion, with a clown-head door knocker. Nobody at the table will touch it. (Roulet Estate 02)
    • Monster of the Week: The format, and also the literal name of the rulebook. See Game mechanics.
    • Mood Whiplash: Bean laundry, then the grimmest town meeting of the arc. (Summer Service 04)
    • A corpse with hanging eyes, then spud-menu comedy. (Appalachia 06)
    • Pop songs over the horror. (Walkers 07)
    • Mr. Exposition: McManley analyzes the evidence and supplies the skeptical alternate theory. (Appalachia 04)
    • Mugging the Monster: The Fed-looking team walks into the "break room" trap, carrying a Claymore. (Appalachia 08)
    • The Russians who snatch the Biz end up with a prisoner who saves their president. (Radford Horrors 03)
    • Mundane Utility: Somebody at Spud Hut has an unexplained crack in the air and uses it to feed a pipe. (Appalachia 09)
    • Cocaine as dental anesthetic; napkins as playing cards. (Walkers 01, Walkers 05)
    • Mushroom Samba: The Roulet House's water supply is dosed, and Kurt has been drinking from the toilet tank. (Roulet Estate 02)
    • Mysterious Informant: The dead NSA man and his unlabeled papers. (Radford Horror 04)
    • The radio contact, who is only allowed to tell the team things they already know. (Summer Service 06)
    • Whoever left the anonymous note in Andrew's bed, warning that some of his friends "aren't who you think". (Walkers 06)
    • Mysterious Watcher: The rooftop watcher with binoculars, a briefcase and a white van with fake plates. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 05)
    • Naked People Are Funny: A naked giant with a shotgun. (Walkers 07)
    • The party infiltrates the cavern nude, since everyone else down there is. Kurt later commandeers a Humvee in the same condition. (Walkers 09)
    • Kurt ends the pharmacy standoff wearing only a gun, having tied up the suspect with his own underwear. A helpful officer cuts leg holes in a winter hat. (Roulet Estate 03)
    • Nigh-Invulnerability: Murphy gets up after a 50 mph collision. Kurt complains. (Radford Horror 03)
    • The angel thing survives a half-kiloton warhead. (Summer Service 06)
    • Andrew shrugs off a shot to the face. (Roulet Estate 01)
    • Nothing Is Scarier: A lights-out human chain through the tunnels. (Appalachia 03)
    • A silent crowd standing in the rain. (Summer Service 05)
    • A single eye on the roof. (Walkers 05)
    • Nuke 'Em: Kurt owns an M28 Davy Crockett. It is assembled, hidden as laundry, and fired at a glowing sea creature near a nuclear power plant. Huell wins the trigger at rock-paper-scissors. Told afterwards that somebody used a tactical nuke, the team feigns surprise. (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 06)
    • Our Angels Are Different: The Marblehead creature gets called an angel, and Utah's portal machine is built into the corpse of another one. Andrew, for the record, does not believe in ghosts but does believe in angels. (Summer Service 06, Walkers 06, Walkers 09)
    • Our Vampires Are Different: Post-Utah Andrew craves blood and shrugs off bullets. Rita's official position: "Not a vampire." See Andrew's Condition. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)
    • Overly Long Gag: Andre reads out a roughly hundred-item Spud Hut menu in full. The table refuses to stop him on the grounds that stopping would be losing. (Appalachia 02)
    • Overt Operative: Every NPC identifies Andrew as a cop on sight, in a civilian shirt. Fox 5 recognizes him instantly. Douglas Douglas says he looks more like a Fed than anyone he has ever seen. (Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 06, Appalachia 08)
    • Pajama-Clad Hero: Andrew sleepwalks into a murder scene in his pajamas and hikes out with the top wrapped round his feet. McManley meets the Marblehead siege in floral pajamas and a nightcap. (Appalachia 03, Summer Service 05)
    • Paper-Thin Disguise: Andrew's undercover look is a slouch, a mustache and platform shoes. (Appalachia 07)
    • Parasite Zombie: Advanced worm hosts keep moving after decapitation and burst into worms when struck. (Summer Service 05)
    • People in Rubber Suits: In-universe. See "Scooby-Doo" Hoax.
    • Photographic Memory: The Spud Hut counter kid, who has the entire menu and every order. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06)
    • Police Are Useless: The Roosevelt Police Department closes its case with threats. Later, some of them are not police. (Walkers 06, Walkers 08)
    • Previously On: Andre opens sessions with one. (Walkers 09, Radford Horrors 04)
    • Product Placement: In Marblehead, McDonald's is the only safe food in town. Andre ate some during a session "for the sake of immersion". (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05)
    • Psychic Link: Wilbur screams when the moth is shot. (Radford Horror 07)
    • Psychic Nosebleed: The price of Andrew's healing, escalating to vomiting blood. Huell gets one from the moth. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 07)
    • Puppeteer Parasite: The worms, delivered in communion wine. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05)
    • The skinwalker "pilots", brain-creatures that drive a body and leave by the mouth. See Pilot and host biology. (Walkers 08, Walkers 09)
    • Putting the Band Back Together: The scattered, disbanded task force is summoned back by the President for one more trip to Radford. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Q–S
docs.text:
• Ragtag Bunch of Misfits: The assault on the community center: a National Guard convoy, three FBI agents on horseback, and one patriot in a homemade tank. (Walkers 09)
  • Real After All: Georgia's Bigfoot sightings are a hoax covering for something real. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 09)
  • Reassigned to Antarctica: Every PC arrives at the task force as a punishment or a dead end. (Radford Horror 01)
  • Red Herring: Enough to stock a fishmonger.
    • "Perverts", the sheriff's explanation for the missing dogs. (Radford Horror 02)
    • The brown station wagon. Station wagons were almost all brown. (Radford Horror 04)
    • Coyotes, a bear, a werewolf. (Radford Horror 05)
    • Briggs's Russian bombing theory, and the mayor blaming Satan. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 04)
    • The Covenant, who are a cult and are not the culprits. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 04)
    • The fountain case and the sugar heist. (Walkers 02)
  • Red Shirt: Henry, the borrowed assistant, whose imminent death is a running joke. (Summer Service 05)
  • Repetitive Name: Douglas Douglas, named on the spot after the table rejected several worse options. (Radford Horror 07)
  • Retcon: Misabelle becomes Deborah Wells because Andre forgot he had already named her. The table is asked to retcon it in their minds. (Walkers 03)
    • The doomed salesman's vacuums are briefly Kirbys, at Zack's suggestion, before settling on an invented brand. (Appalachia 04)
    • Kurt's welding mask is retroactively tinfoil-lined. (Radford Horror 07)
  • Retired Badass: Kurt, ex-CIA and ex-UTAW, consulting. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Ripped from the Headlines: The Sherman Ranch and Robert Bigelow are a thin disguise for Skinwalker Ranch. (Walkers 02)

  • Rule of Cool: Ned Simpson's killdozer, finished that morning. It ends the episode in a tree.

    Quote

    "Now, you see, in the CIA, this is what we call an asset."

    Dante (as Kurt) (Walkers 09)

  • Running Gag: Too many for one bullet; they have their own page. A sampler:

    • Dental oncologists fill every hotel the team books. Kurt suspects they are following him. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Walkers 02)
    • "Half Gallon Howard." (Walkers 03, Walkers 04, Radford Horrors 01)
    • John Travolta. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)
    • Kurt's stilts. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 07, Walkers 04)
    • Roseanne as the universal sign of rock bottom. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)
    • "We're getting a boiler." (Appalachia 04)

  • "Scooby-Doo" Hoax: Played straight twice, and both times the hoax is hiding something worse.

    • Georgia's Bigfoot is Troy Cleaver in a Chewbacca costume with fake footprints. A group of meddling kids with a Great Dane is on hand to make the comparison unavoidable. See The Bigfoot Hoax. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06, Appalachia 09)

    Quote

    "What kind of Scooby-Doo-ass bullshit is going on in this town?"

    Andre (as the Spud Hut investigator), on hearing about a potato truck full of dirt (Appalachia 08)

    • Rhode Island's Grey is a man in a foam-latex mask, given away by a seam at the neck. (Roulet Estate 03)
    • Sequel Hook: The Marblehead case file lands on the desk before Radford's ashes are cold. (Radford Horror 08)
    • A "next time" title card for Utah. (Walkers 01)
    • Shell-Shocked Veteran: Kurt hallucinates Saigon whenever something tampers with his head. (Roulet Estate 02, Walkers 05)
    • Andrew, dissociating out a car window after Marblehead. (Summer Service 06)
    • Shout-Out: Dozens. Among them: The X-Files, Twin Peaks, Columbo, Psycho, Scooby-Doo, Jurassic Park, Die Hard, Scanners, The Thing, Invasion of the Body Snatchers, Planet of the Apes and Weekend at Bernie's. (Radford Horror 06, Appalachia 08, Walkers 08, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 03)
    • Show Within a Show: The campaign is one. Inside it: the Letterman broadcast, a three-hour telenovela that makes the Biz's guard weep, and a 1992 OVA. (Radford Horror 01, Walkers 01, Radford Horrors 01)
    • Shrine to the Fallen: Abe Whateley's room, preserved untouched for three years. (Radford Horror 02)
    • Sinister Minister: Amos Shaw, sixty and built like an athlete, and the mayor who takes his pulpit. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04)
    • Sleepwalking: Andrew wakes up miles away with no memory of the trek. (Appalachia 03)
    • Spot the Imposter: Two Andrews, one horse. The tests tried include a quiz on cigar-shaped craft at gunpoint, whether he can keep down solid food, and whether he will open his mouth. (Walkers 09)
    • Stakeout: Kurt spends hours in a hayloft behind paper boxes. The sequel features McMuffins. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 06)
    • Stockholm Syndrome: The Biz cases the windows and downspouts of his hotel, hides some bed sheets, and then finds he does not actually want to escape. (Radford Horrors 01)
    • Sweet Tooth: The Ballard mayor's candy and the fridge full of sugar are clues. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: T–Z
docs.text:
• Tampering with Food and Drink: Communion wine, peach preserves, tap water. Do not consume anything in this show that did not come from a McDonald's. (Summer Service 01, Appalachia 01, Roulet Estate 02)
  • Tempting Fate: Kurt tells the major to bail out if a vehicle starts rising into the sky. (Walkers 09)
  • Time Skip: The Rhode Island epilogue jumps months ahead. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Toilet Humor: The Biz's digestive saga runs from the first episode's gas-station corn dogs onward and has its own medical subplot about fiber. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 08, Appalachia 06)
  • Tomato in the Mirror: The moth calls Andrew "changeling", and Wilbur tells him that he of all people should understand. By Rhode Island he is wondering whether he died and whether he is a hybrid. (Radford Horror 07, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Too Dumb to Live: Huell throws a brick through the police station's glass door while Kurt is still picking the lock. (Walkers 08)
    • Webster tastes the unidentified goo. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Total Party Kill: Narrowly missed in the church: every PC reaches critical harm, and the table calls it a "half-TPK". (Radford Horror 07)
  • Town with a Dark Secret: Radford (disappearances, a curfew, a curse rumor), Marblehead (the church runs the council) and Ballard (the town leadership is not the town leadership). (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 04, Walkers 02)
  • Uncanny Valley: Upright horses and coyotes that stand too still. (Walkers 07)
    • The crash survivor's almost-human face. (Radford Horrors 04)
  • Unreliable Narrator: The replica Andrew gives the team a cleaned-up account of what happened in the gym. (Walkers 07)
    • Kurt's spy stories. (Walkers 05)
  • Weirdness Magnet: The team. By the last arc even the motel has rabies. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Wham Episode: The original Andrew turns up naked and sprinting at 35 mph, the replica is unmasked, a farmhouse is launched into the sky, and the community center goes into a sinkhole. (Walkers 09)

  • Wham Line: The moth, burning, cut off mid-sentence about the ones who made it. (Radford Horror 07)

    • Yeltsin's question for the Biz. (Roulet Estate 03)

    Quote

    "Tell me everything you know about the humanists."

    Andre (as Yeltsin) (Roulet Estate 03)

  • "Where Are They Now" Epilogue: One vignette per PC after the task force is dissolved: workers' comp, Quantico, a labor camp, and a desk. (Roulet Estate 03)

  • Zerg Rush: The worm convoy rams the plant fence and is cut down by pop-up guns. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Andrew Howard
docs.text:
Played by Rita. See Andrew Howard.

  • Agent Mulder: The believer of the unit, raised in the Aetherius Society.
  • Bishōnen: The table, Primenthol Greengrass and assorted NPCs will not let his looks go. (Appalachia 02)
  • Can't Hold His Liquor: His first hangover is a plot point. (Roulet Estate 01)
  • Friend to All Living Things: Harvey loves him and Nancy follows his trail into a war zone. (Appalachia 02, Walkers 09)
  • Naïve Newcomer: A desk agent on his first field job. (Radford Horror 05, Appalachia 06)
  • Tomato in the Mirror: Changeling, "special horse", possible hybrid. He begins to sense that his church does not know what it is talking about. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Trauma Conga Line: Shot by a teammate, airsick, sleepwalked, bitten, killed, replaced, resurrected. (Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 03, Walkers 08)
  • Unwitting Test Subject: He was X-rayed and never shown the films. He concludes that he is the test case. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Huell Kendrick
docs.text:
Played by Zack. See Huell Kendrick.

  • Agent Scully: Refuses to believe in the lights until he grabs hold of the spaceman, gets lifted off the ground with him, and falls. (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06)
  • Butt-Monkey: Bedbugs, a broken arm from falling off a levitating astronaut, projectile vomiting, a jawbone in the backside. His body is the show's favorite target. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 06, Appalachia 09, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Drowning My Sorrows: With Roseanne. (Roulet Estate 03)

  • The Nicknamer: Coined "Half Gallon Howard", and insists the goose is called Betsy. Betsy is the car.

    Quote

    "Yeah, that's why we call you Half Gallon Howard."

    Zack (as Huell) (Radford Horrors 04)

  • Temporary Bulk Change: The worms give him muscle and a hairline. The cure takes both back, with interest. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Dick "the Biz" Baxter
docs.text:
Played by Ezra. See Dick "The Biz" Baxter.

  • The Alcoholic: Introduced drunk. His flask later becomes a smoke screen. (Radford Horror 01, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Amusing Injuries: A mouth treated with cocaine from Kurt's shoe heel, a sliced foot, and eventually an eye. He is always having a rough day. (Walkers 05, Walkers 08, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 03)
  • Con Man: Covers his own break-in by staging a junkie burglary, and later makes it official with the Charlatan move. (Radford Horror 04, Walkers 01)
  • Gone Horribly Right: After the Clinton scandal and Letterman, even the Salt Lake City field office knows him as the man who spied on Clinton. (Walkers 02)
  • Hero of Another Story: Spends most of the last arc in Russia saving Yeltsin from a convoy ambush while the others do rabies shots. (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)
  • Perpetual Poverty: The Buick is always one payment from repossession. Then it carries a nuke. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 04)
  • Sticky Fingers: Palms one of Jester's crystal marbles off the hotel desk and hides it even from his teammates. Also liberates a shovel and a prescription pad. (Summer Service 01, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 07)
  • Stockholm Syndrome: See the main list.

docs.title: Kurt Larson
docs.text:
Played by Dante. See Kurt Larson.

  • Combat Pragmatist: "Claymore all the ends" is a philosophy. (Appalachia 03)
  • Crazy-Prepared: See the main list, and the nuke.
  • Functional Addict: He keeps drugs in four hollow molars: LSD in one, amphetamine in another. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 06)
  • Happily Married: His wife packs the road-trip sandwiches, he phones her and the kids from hotel rooms, and his share of the ape gold is "for my wife and kids". (Radford Horror 01, Appalachia 09, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Master of Unlocking: Bump keys, picks, and once while drunk on absinthe. (Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 03)
  • Shell-Shocked Veteran: See the main list.
  • Walking Armory: Packs a spear gun, a P90, a grenade, a claymore and gallons of pesticide for a consulting job. (Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: Daniel Webster
docs.text:
Played by Ezra. See Daniel Webster.

  • Agent Scully: The skeptical minder. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • By-the-Book Cop: Shiny shoes, a notebook, and a recording habit. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Conspiracy Theorist: The mundane kind, which in this setting makes him the one who is wrong. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Naïve Newcomer: The new boss of a team that has already seen a moth, a nuke and a portal. He insists on sharing a room with Kurt. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Straight Man: Named on the spot, to Ezra's audible panic, and assigned to a team of weirdos. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Tropes for Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable
docs.text:
Non-canon

Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable is a one-shot in a different rules system, framed as a 1992 OVA airing on television inside the PITF fiction. Nothing in this section happened to the task force. All examples are from the one-shot.

  • Big Eater: Derk hands a vendor $100 by mistake and receives 98 hot dog tacos and $2 change.
  • Cliffhanger: Derk comes down in the ocean and is last seen outside a McDonald's in Wisukonshin, spending his last two dollars on a call home.
  • Cloudcuckoolander's Minder: Mirabeth, in theory.
  • Con Man: Mirabeth invents an essential-oil MLM, the oil pyramid, and takes a $400 down payment from a mother with a sobbing son.
  • Cool Old Lady: A glamorous senior martial artist who speed-walks an interstate in pumps behind a parasol.
  • Daddy Issues: Ovain and Derk both have them. Derk's attempt to bond over it is a miss.

  • Destructive Savior: Derk saves the president and causes $125,000 in property damage, a ruptured gas line and four evacuated blocks.

    Quote

    "A natural disaster with legs and a mouth."

    Andre (as Colonel Sparago), on Derk

  • Dumb Muscle: Derk. Andre: "it's amazing how Derk being fucking stupid has dominated the tone of this one-shot."

  • Fish out of Water: A feral alien prince in a world of libraries and Motel 6s.
  • Gentle Giant: He gives piggyback rides and wants the stone to resurrect his friend Fatty Gibbs.
  • Kamehame Hadoken: Ovain's white fire and ki jets.
  • Literal-Minded: Told to use his inside voice, Derk speaks with a hand over his mouth for the rest of the scene.
  • Malaproper: "Asteroid" for "steroid", every time.
  • Mentor Archetype: Mirabeth. Rita picked the option where she "was supposed to have mentored somebody and now it's embarrassing."
  • Nigh-Invulnerability: A groin punch lands on Derk with a metallic clang.
  • Our Presidents Are Different: The Werewolf President, a genial man who agrees privately that turning into a dog is cool.
  • Power Incontinence: Derk cannot aim a jump. One ends in space.
  • Rule of Funny: The governing law of the planet.
  • Show Within a Show: See the note above.
  • Super-Speed: Mirabeth's legendary pace.
  • Sympathetic Villain: Ovain is a shaky former conqueror in therapy whose online dating went badly. He leaves the planet "and its Tinder".
  • Tournament Arc: Promised by the World Martial Arts Tournament and then subverted when the whole thing is suspended over a judge on steroids before a single bout.
  • Training from Hell: Fourteen years alone on a high-gravity planet, eating scorpions.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Actor Allusion: Dante's accent for Kurt gets compared to his earlier characters, and Ezra cracks that Dante collects skulls in every game. (Radford Horror 05, Summer Service 04)
  • Ascended Extra: Douglas Douglas was named as a joke at a gate. He returns in the last arc, and so does the pinball collection, now the Douglas Pinball Emporium. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Missing Episode: Summer Service 02 and "05.5", Appalachia 05 and 10, and Walkers "08.5" were played but never recorded. Their events are known only from later recaps. See Lost episodes.
  • The Other Darrin: In-universe and at the table at once: Rita secretly played the duplicate Andrew, and at the moment of the swap Andre took over the copy while Rita took back the real one. (Walkers 07, Walkers 09)
  • Throw It In: Douglas Douglas, Betsy's Cats costumes and Kurt's stack of women's shelter cards all started as table riffs and stayed canon. Rita picked Andrew's Spud Hut order by rolling a d100 against the menu, which Andre says was AI-generated with human tuning. (Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 04, Walkers 08)
  • Troubled Production: Krisp noise suppression eats yells, a creature's cry and Zack's Geiger-counter impression. Discord breaks the credit music, the dice bot breaks too, and Andre rolls for the players. (Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 06, Radford Horrors 03)
  • Shown Their Work: Rita reads real UFO sightings aloud in character, and Andrew can cite the 1957 Levelland case from memory. Andre supplies the Davy Crockett's real code name. (Summer Service 04, Walkers 04, Walkers 09)
  • Several names are spelled variously: Roulet and Roulette, Lori and Laurie, Jan and Yan. This wiki uses the first of each.

docs.title: YMMV
docs.text:
• Arc Fatigue: The table groans at each new dinner at Spud Hut, and Huell arrives in Utah dreading another potato-centered case. (Appalachia 04, Walkers 02)
  • Broken Base: Arby's. Andre maintains it is the worst chain in America, and the team keeps eating there anyway. (Radford Horror 03)
  • Crosses the Line Twice: The Biz's toilet saga, the arm in the cooler, and Dante's ruling that "there's no way worm people have rights." (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 01, Summer Service 06)
  • Ensemble Dark Horse: Nancy the goose, a hostile bird who outlasts most of Ballard. The counter savant and Douglas Douglas are close behind.
  • Fridge Horror: The Covenant's fermented peach preserves, served at breakfast. (Appalachia 01)
    • Literal: Andrew, in the fridge. (Walkers 05)
  • Memetic Mutation: In-universe, Andrew's sweaty "Thank you for your time again" to a Fox 5 microphone is replayed on the news every ten minutes for the rest of the day. Dante predicts the trip-hop remix. (Appalachia 08)
  • Nightmare Fuel: The plastic-wrapped figure that moves; corpses falling from a gym ceiling; a farmer vomiting his brain into a tank. (Walkers 03, Walkers 07, Walkers 09)
  • Nightmare Retardant: The terrifying Grey of Rhode Island turns out to be a skinny man with matted hair who needs his beta blockers. Andrew kicks over a card display in disappointment. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Signature Scene: Huell firing a nuclear recoilless rifle after winning rock-paper-scissors. (Summer Service 06)
  • The Woobie: Douglas Douglas, who begs visiting federal agents for toilet paper. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: Andrew's alien dad
docs.text:
Andrew's alien dad is a gaunt, shirtless figure in aviator sunglasses who appears in Andrew Howard's recurring dreams and warns him, "Don't take it," just before the task force's rabies treatment.

Type Dream figure (nature unknown) Aliases Dream dad; dad tulpa Abilities Dominates Andrew in the dream; mouths a warning Status Unknown First appearance Radford Horrors 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Andrew's "dad" is a gaunt, pale, shirtless humanoid in blue jeans and aviator sunglasses, with a big Hollywood smile and perfect white teeth. In Andrew's recurring dreams he tries to kiss him. Andrew does not know his own father and assumes the figure is his dad through a "vague psychological relation." (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text: In the dream described in Radford Horrors 03, Andrew finds himself playing shirtless beach volleyball. The ocean is blood red and smells of metal and decay, the sun is bright blue and the sand burnt orange. The opposing team is eight foaming-at-the-mouth men and his "dad." Andrew's Act Under Pressure roll is 8 with a -1 modifier, and he gets creamed. A jet-engine roar builds; the dad mouths "Don't take it," and Andrew wakes in the Radford ER. (Radford Horrors 03) See Radford ER.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
After the dream, Andrew has been sweating and chilled since the rabies immunoglobulin (RIG). He privately tells Kurt Larson about the dream and the warning: "I had a weird dream where my alien dad told me that I shouldn't take it, but he didn't tell me what I shouldn't take. If I die from this vaccine, just send me to California. They'll figure it out." Kurt offers the agency's free counseling and a theory from his UTAW experience: "It might be a dad tulpa. That wouldn't be the first dad tulpa." Rita (as Andrew) replies that he does not think the figure is really his father, whom he has never known, only that he assumes so because of a "vague psychological relation," and that he wishes the tulpa would stop trying to kiss him. Kurt's Sharp roll (10) shows Andrew pale, sweating and yellow-eyed, in worse shape than Webster. (Radford Horrors 03) See UTAW.

The ER doctor explains the treatment: RIG, then a four-vaccine series on four consecutive Tuesdays, with a DFA test on the rabid mouse to be run at the Roanoke hospital. If the rat tests negative the series stops. (Radford Horrors 03) According to Andre's recap at the start of Radford Horrors 04, the whole team began treatment, and Andrew was discharged against medical advice with a cooler full of syringes. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Whether the dad is a psychological stand-in, a tulpa or something real; Kurt and Andrew only speculate.
  • What "Don't take it" refers to; the dream does not say.
  • The meaning of the surreal imagery: the blood-red ocean, blue sun, orange sand, jet-engine roar and eight foaming men.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Rita (as Andrew) jokes that Andrew, who has not been ill at all since he died, may be a "rabies construct."
