docs.title: The angel thing
docs.text:
The angel thing is the fire-hot, humming, light-covered entity that lives in the sea off Marblehead and is the final enemy of The Summer Service.

Type Monster / entity Aliases The glowy thing; glowy ring thing; spinning death wheel; the alien submarine; the thing under the water Abilities Intense heat; a hum that nearly broke a submersible; amphibious travel at 60 to 80 knots; screeching vibration Weaknesses The flashlight weapon; survived a half-kiloton nuclear blast Status Dead (as of Summer Service 06) First appearance Unrecorded Summer Service 02 (known from the team's account in Summer Service 03); first on screen in Summer Service 06

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The team never settles on one name for the thing. Kurt Larson calls it the "glowy ring fuck thing that scared the shit out of me underwater" and the "spinning death wheel under the water that eats ships for dinner" (Summer Service 03), and in the finale simply "a big glowy thing" (Summer Service 06). Andre calls it "the angel thing" in his narration of the finale. Andrew Howard describes what the team saw on the dive as something "covered in lights, gyroscope looking something or other" that "hummed" (Summer Service 03).

In the finale it appears as a bright light rising from the ocean, screaming and trenching out the ground as it moves. At one point it freezes, makes a long, unearthly fluting noise and turns back toward the sea; a guest at the table calls the sound "a whale with depression" (Summer Service 06).

Unrecorded session

The team's first encounter with the thing was in Summer Service 02, a session that was played but never recorded. It is known only from what the characters tell others in Summer Service 03. See Lost episodes.

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
• Heat. As it closes in on the team, paint blisters, the tires of their car catch fire and burst, and the upholstery starts to burn. Andrew's flashlight case begins to melt in his hand (Summer Service 06).
  • Hum. On the dive, Andrew says, the thing resonated at a frequency that might have broken apart the team's submersible (Summer Service 03).
  • Speed and range. A submarine's sonar tracks it at 60 to 70 knots, then 80 knots, and the operator swears it "went on land." On land it heads straight for the team (Summer Service 06).
  • Vibration. Near it, the team struggles to function under a vibration that seems to be shaking them apart (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Weaknesses
docs.text: Huell Kendrick fires the W54 warhead from the team's Davy Crockett at the "mysterious light." The blast knocks down the plant's fence and sets distant trees alight, but the creature screams and comes on, brighter and faster. Andrew Howard then sticks his hand out of the car and hits it with the flashlight weapon (a Kick Some Ass roll of 8, so both sides take harm). The creature lurches, spirals into the ground about 20 feet from the car, sprouts bubbling legs of every kind of animal ("a panda," says Zack) and dies, then burns as a pillar of flame at a very high temperature. The Geiger counter in the car barely reacted to the nuke but starts going off when the thing dies (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
The dive and the wreck (unrecorded). Andrew tells Big Bill that the team's dive found a stealth wreck with a bite out of it, and that a lit, humming craft returned while they hid with their power and lights off, moving as if searching for something. He says he no longer thinks it is a sea monster but an "alien submarine" (Summer Service 03). See The stealth wreck.

The dream. That night Andrew is visited by the gray-skinned dream visitor, who says "I think they damaged it. It can't cool itself anymore." He warns Andrew to stay away from the water: "It's not like the bug thing. I don't think you can hurt it." He asks whether Andrew is high enough in government to order a nuclear strike ("That might work"), and says that getting too close "will kill you. Or change you" (Summer Service 03).

The weapon. The next morning Kurt, still shaken by what he saw underwater, asks his private contacts for a Davy Crockett, a MOAB or at least the meanest anti-materiel rifle he can find. His old arms-dealer contact Carter sends the Davy Crockett in Summer Service 04 (Summer Service 03; Summer Service 04).

The chase. The finale opens with a cold open aboard the USS Oklahoma City. The sonar operator reports that the contact went on land, an explosion, and then "the craziest sound I've ever heard." It returns, closing at 60 to 70 knots and then 80 knots, and the captain orders everything conventional fired. Later in the episode, Big Bill tells Andrew that "we lost one of our submarines too" (Summer Service 06).

The finale. On the flooded freeway the creature trenches toward the team, stops, cries out and turns back toward the sea. The radio contact says the team "pissed it off" with their earlier claymore, and explains that it is not there to help the convoy of infected, so it will have to come out of the water when the convoy attacks the nuclear power plant. The team fires the nuke when the creature comes into view, and finishes it with the flashlight (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Its origin, and whether it is a vessel (Andrew's "alien submarine") or a living creature. Its legs of every animal species at the moment of death suggest the latter.
  • Whether it is connected to the worms in the communion wine. In Summer Service 05, Kurt wonders aloud whether the glowy thing and the nerve agent are parts of a factional dispute, with someone else trying to contain the worms before the team arrived (Summer Service 05).
  • Why Andre calls it an angel. The sermon in Summer Service 01 describes angels as "terrifying monsters constructed by God to wipe out sin," but no one at the table connects the sermon to the creature (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Ape-Men
docs.text:
The Ape-Men are pale, fast-maturing, ketamine-addicted hominids bred by Jan Martense to mine gold under Dahlonega, Georgia; the escapees are the "Bigfoot" and "Yeti" that terrorized the town in The Things in Appalachia.

Type Monster / bred hybrid Aliases Yetis; the shift; hybrids; chimp-men; troglodytes; cave yeti; OmniChimp; mineshaft creature; Appalachian predator; Bigfoot; Sasquatch Abilities Great strength and speed, climbing, voice mimicry (Shelly), recognizing gold Weaknesses Fear of dark tunnels, loud high-pitched noise, dependence on ketamine Affiliation Jan's Conspiracy Status Survivors left in the mines (as of Appalachia 09); fate after the unrecorded finale unknown First appearance Appalachia 01 (cold open, as "Bigfoot")

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The creatures are large, pale, furry and chimp-like, "not that different from chimps" according to the handler Clive, but much stronger. In the Spud Hut basement the team saw five of them: pale, hairy, hunched, with long sharp fingernails, reflective eyes and partly human features. The players read them as cave-dwelling troglodytes rather than former people; Kurt compared the feeling to meeting a family of black bears on a trail (Appalachia 08). The working shift wears hi-vis vests and safety helmets, carries pickaxes and has armbands with blinking red lights (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
• Strength and speed. In the first mine encounter a white blur charged the team, hurled Kurt into Andrew and a wall, and tore a long cut up his back; the team described it as pale, furry, fast and armed (Appalachia 03). In the basement one picked Andrew up and threw him through a drop ceiling and repeatedly "juggled" him, and another punched a dog whistle into Kurt's throat (Appalachia 08).
  • Climbing and hunting. The creature in the early cases lured prey with a baby-like cry, moved on all fours, and was very comfortable moving vertically through trees. It ripped a rabbit apart and hung a child's shoe high in a tree (Appalachia 02). The team assumed that the early sightings and disappearances were these same creatures escaping from the mines; Clive, who had been underground for two months, knew of escapes only through Jan's assurance that he had "taken care of" them (Appalachia 09).
  • Rapid growth. Ape-men arrive looking about six and are full-grown in about two months. A dissected specimen had an adrenaline gland about twice the size of a fist (Appalachia 09).
  • Trainability. They respond to clickers, reinforcement and imitation, and mine in shifts of 25. Kurt summed up the operation: "Apes mine gold. Tell nobody, 'cause ape." (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Weaknesses
docs.text: The handlers' only containment is the creatures' fear of dark tunnels; they lit only the routes they wanted the shift to use. The ape-men dislike loud noises and hunger, and without ketamine they fight, wreck enclosures and cannot focus. Kurt got past the shift by eating ketamine-packed Combos in front of them, putting on a show of enjoying them (Appalachia 09). A Claymore mine killed one and drove off the rest in the basement (Appalachia 08), and Andrew's pepper-spray "absence" beam severed the arm of Big Bob.

docs.title: Early sightings
docs.text:
The arc opens with a woman dragged off by something hairy in the woods (Appalachia 01). The team later found a child's shoe with pale, soft, body-like hair in the laces, and a rabbit pelt with the insides gone (Appalachia 02). In the Consolidated Gold Mine the team met the "cave yeti" in a hidden modern tunnel, shot it, and followed its blood to an old elevator shaft where they found a German boy's shoe. A small red light was blinking on or near it (Appalachia 03). Kurt argued the light was inorganic, a recorder or tracker, which meant people were involved (Appalachia 04). The tracker matched the SHA tag found in a bear's vomit (see SHA Tracking Device) (Appalachia 07).

Meanwhile fake Bigfoots confused the picture: a man in a Chewbacca costume was found shot, and faked prints turned up near Auraria (see The Bigfoot Hoax). Kurt kept the two separate, believing a real ape-man hybrid exists alongside the hoax and asking McManley to compare Frotter Comstock's gore smear against hybrid tissue he already held (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: The Special Projects level
docs.text: Beneath the Spud Hut corporate plant, on a floor marked "Special Projects", the cold open of Appalachia 08 shows a dozen eyes turning toward the camera in a dark room of rattling cages. Jan Martense led the team down and left them in a "break room" (code 441). The creatures behind the door ambushed the team; by Andre's count at the end of the session one was killed and at least two more were badly injured (one shot through the neck by Huell), and the survivors fled (Appalachia 08). See Break Room. Andre's adjudication in Appalachia 08 has one ape-man killed by the Claymore, but the recap that opens Appalachia 09 says two were "evaporated", and the team tells Clive that two of the five rejects are dead.

docs.title: The shift and the mines
docs.text: Clive explained the operation: a lot of gold remained under Dahlonega and ape-men dig it because they do not talk. The operation had run a year and a half, Jan "kept getting more", and a 25-strong shift needed to be led back and fed. Five ape-men were "rejects" whose temperament did not take to training; two died in the basement blast. The tunnels' unguarded ladder explained the escapes, and the missing children, truck driver and Spud Hut workers were tied to those escapes. Kurt won over the shift with the ketamine Combos, and Big Bob, a huge ape-man, hunted the party until it was killed (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Origin
docs.text:
The finale was never recorded, so the origin is known only from Jan's account to Kurt at Black Site Omaha in the epilogue. Five years before, Jan hit and killed a man in a black suit with NSA ID on a Georgia road, and found an ape woman strapped to a gurney in his van. He named her Shelly and kept her to make money. She aged fast, and Jan tried every kind of ape semen, then used his own by artificial insemination. The offspring aged even faster; only males survived. A lab told him the chromosome numbers did not line up. Jan considered Shelly "a bright chimp", very strong and good at voice mimicry, nothing supernatural (Walkers 01). See Shelly (ape woman).

Unrecorded session

The climax in the Dahlonega gold mines happened in Appalachia 10, which was never recorded. The epilogue says a falling ape broke Jan's skull and that Andrew was thrown and juggled in the caves, but gives no further detail.

docs.title: Later references
docs.text: In Walkers 05, McManley is still insisting that the earlier ape-men should have been "basically chimpanzees" (Walkers 05).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Where the ape-men truly come from and why they grow so fast. Andrew wondered about an extraterrestrial origin and Kurt said "Somebody fucking does" have portals, tying them to The Crack in the Air, but Jan denied any portals (Appalachia 09).
  • What happened to the drugged shift of ape-men when the Spud Hut facility exploded.

docs.title: Big Bob
docs.text:
Big Bob is a huge, fast ape-man that hunts the task force through the tunnels beneath Dahlonega, Georgia, until Andrew Howard's pepper spray severs its arm.

Type Monster / ape-man Abilities Great strength and speed; survives gunfire on adrenaline Weaknesses Blood loss Status Dead (as of Appalachia 09) First appearance Appalachia 09

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Big Bob is the largest and fastest ape-man the team meets. Its name comes from the handler Clive, who announces a scuttling and growl behind the party with "that is Big Bob" and warns they must run once they are past the drugged shift. The name has nothing to do with the task force's superior Big Bill (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text: Big Bob is fast enough to close a 20-foot gap and survives a unison shotgun volley. In the fight it swings Andrew by the ankle into a wall (four harm), throws Kurt into the Biz, punches Andrew in the chest (his anti-bear suit cuts it to 1 harm and cracks a rib), and holds Huell over its head and crushes him (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
After the party squeezes past the shift of ape-men, Kurt orders a unison shotgun volley on three. In the first round no one rolls a full success, though several shots hit, and Andrew takes the harm meant for Huell. In the second round, with Big Bob bleeding heavily, Kurt's chest shot should be fatal but the ape-man keeps going on adrenaline. Andrew then rolls a 10 on Kick Some Ass and uses his pepper spray's "absence" beam to sever the ape's arm. Big Bob looks at the stump and gently topples over dead (Appalachia 09). See Andrew's Pepper Spray.

Afterward, Clive says he once dissected a dead ape-man and found an adrenaline gland twice the size of a fist, and that he will "kinda miss" Big Bob. Andrew keeps the severed hand despite Kurt's warning that it is bad luck.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Andre, voicing Clive, calls the ape-man "Big Bill" once and corrects himself.
  • It is never established whether Big Bob was one of the five "rejects" that Clive said had not taken to training.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Appalachia 09

docs.title: Black triangular craft
docs.text:
The black triangular craft are silent, plain black triangles that appear over the Roosevelt community center at the climax of The Walkers in Skin, alongside crews in hazmat suits.

Type Craft / unknown operators Aliases black triangles Abilities Silent flight; plane-like maneuvers Status Operators and origin never established First appearance Walkers 09

docs.title: Description
docs.text: After the party reaches the rear hallway of the community center, the outside has gone deadly quiet. A fine white powder falls like snow, and a black triangular craft streaks overhead. When the party presses Howard for details, Andre describes the craft as "pretty much just a triangle," not particularly aerodynamic, with nothing like the look of a Nighthawk or a B-2 (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text: According to Howard, they are completely silent, and they do mostly what a plane could do. He reports seeing "a whole armada" of them while running to the community center, and one of them looked as though it had been shredded in midair by something invisible (Walkers 09).

docs.title: History
docs.text: When the party climbs out of the cavern and flees across the field, everyone outside is unconscious and black craft swoop overhead. Dozens of people in hazmat suits are loading up bodies as the party drives away, and Howard snaps a few dozen blurry Polaroids of the cleanup, with several indistinct black aircraft circling above. In his report over the radio, Kurt Larson states for the record that there is a cover-up they did not cause: men in hazmat suits and unidentified craft taking personnel as well as victims, after something drugged the whole area (Walkers 09).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The episodes never establish who operates the craft, where they come from, or whether they are connected to the hazmat cleanup teams or to the white powder that knocked everyone out. A triangular craft also appears in The Radford Horrors; no episode connects the two.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 09

docs.title: Crash survivor
docs.text:
The crash survivor is the bisected, hairless non-human recovered from the triangular craft that crashed into a Russian farmhouse; he tells President Boris Yeltsin that his people are "not aliens" but "the opposite of aliens."

Type Non-human entity Aliases Half a guy; the being Abilities Answers questions in English when stimulated; shares fluids with a human; accepts O-negative blood Weaknesses Barely alive; pushing him further is "very risky" Status Alive but critical, in Russian custody (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The survivor is about 55 percent of a person: one arm is missing and everything below the navel is gone. He is hairless and pale with wrong teeth and jaw, large eyes set too far apart and mottled subcutaneous bruising. His anatomy raises the hair on the neck of Dick "The Biz" Baxter and sets off a "wrongness" reaction. The only thing it reminds the Biz of is the subtle change over Andrew Howard since he died, "but much more so." (Radford Horrors 04)

He lies in a tent bed beside a shirtless Russian soldier, the two connected by tubes that exchange blood, urine and other fluids. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
• Answers in English when woken with a syringe; Yeltsin first tries Russian, which does not work.
  • Exchanges fluids with the soldier and accepts O-negative blood; Boris Yeltsin wonders why that would work on an alien. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Radford Horrors 04 the Biz, who has just saved Yeltsin from the wheat-field ambush, is flown through the night with Yeltsin's hospital bed to the Oryol crash site. Inside a double-walled plastic curtain under arc lamps is the partly excavated triangular craft, a little smaller than the space shuttle, which annihilated a farmhouse. The two beds stand in the tent beside it. (Radford Horrors 04)

Yeltsin has doctors wake the being with a syringe. In Russian, then English:

Interrogation

"Why are you here?" "Survey." "Why are your people here? The aliens." "Not aliens. The opposite of aliens." "What do you want?" "Servitors... need resources."

He then passes out. The doctors warn that pressing him further is very risky, so Yeltsin ends the questioning. (Radford Horrors 04)

Afterward Yeltsin asks the Biz for insight in private. The Biz says these are not the aliens he has dealt with: he has seen resources go through portals, but it "presented differently," and he has never heard of servitors. (Radford Horrors 04) See Servitors.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: His origin, what servitors are, what "resources" they need, and any relation to the Radford Moth or to Andrew's condition are all unresolved. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Zack jokes the episode should be called "Opposite of Aliens." (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horrors 04 (the craft appears in the cold open)

docs.title: Emporium intruder
docs.text:
The Emporium intruder is a small, non-human shadow seen on diner security footage moving inside the Douglas Pinball Emporium window before a gray van crew bagged it and carried it away.

Type Entity (unidentified) Aliases Juvenile moth Abilities Moth smell and slime trail; entered via the office window Status Removed in bags by the gray van crew (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The intruder is seen only as a non-human moving shadow, much smaller than the Radford Moth, at the left of the front window of the Douglas Pinball Emporium, where the floor has been recently cleaned. It carries the moth's smell and slime. The footage shows it seemingly trying to get out as the door was opened. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
When the overnight maintenance tech Elizabeth George vanishes from the emporium, the team finds a cleaned-up smear of blood and hair, a broken Taser tine and a wiped security tape. Sheila the waitress fixes her diner camera and finds the raid: at about 4 to 5 a.m. a gray van arrives, five men enter, a non-human shadow moves in the window, one man opens the lock, there is a scuffle, and three men carry out two bags before others carry out equipment. (Radford Horrors 04) See Diner security tape and Sheila.

Kurt Larson rolls 10 on Investigate a Mystery and concludes it was an organized paramilitary cleanup team, not military, and that the shadow was not human. The office window, which opens onto the alley, is large enough for a man. Kurt's working theory is that a juvenile moth, or a thrall like "the astronaut kid" (Wilbur Whateley), was in the emporium; the crew came for it; and Elizabeth, who had been repairing a Flash Gordon machine, was caught in the crossfire. (Radford Horrors 04) See Gray van crew.

Opalescent slime found above the emporium window, and earlier in a tree at the Safe Environment Fund site, is to be analyzed by McManley; a sample of the moth goo made Wilbur stiffen. See Pearlescent goo. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Whether it was a juvenile moth, a thrall or something else.
  • Where the crew took it, and who employs them; Kurt wonders whether they are tied to the Safe Environment Fund.
  • Elizabeth George's fate. (Radford Horrors 04) See also Moth life cycle.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: The Greys
docs.text:
The Greys (also Grays, gray aliens, or beings from Zeta Reticuli) are the classic big-eyed gray aliens blamed for the "visitations" at the Roulet house, and the subject of Andrew Howard's firm and sometimes contradicted beliefs about extraterrestrials.

Type Entity (alleged) Aliases Greys; Grays; gray aliens; Zeta Reticuli Abilities Alleged: lost time, experiments on sleepers, lights in the sky Status Never confirmed to exist in the campaign First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The Roulets' handwritten notebook of sightings, much of it in code, covers several months and ends in the fall of 1992. It lists incidents in which the couple saw Greys out in the woods, saw lights flying over the house, lost time, or were experimented on while they were asleep. The VHS rack includes tapes labelled "September '92 visitation," "May '91 visitation" and "Lights in the sky, July '92" (see Visitation Tapes). After reading the library, Andrew tells Kurt that, "just like the letter said," it is a classic case of two people being abused by the Greys. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Andrew's beliefs
docs.text:
Andrew is a committed UFO believer who dislikes the Greys. Asked what he knows about them, Rita (as Andrew) answers, "Well, they're not big into consent," and later says she does not want the intruder to be a gray alien "because they're non-consensual perverts." Andrew also says the Greys have been on Earth "for, like, generations upon generations." (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

His working taxonomy is that Greys have no external genitalia and no nipples, because they do not nurse their young. While giving the police a description for the APB, Rita says as much, and Andre points out that the man Andrew saw in the woods did have nipples, and Andrew shouts "Eh, nipples!" in the middle of a sentence. In Roulet Estate 03, while the police keep asking to see his badge, Andrew rants about whether a gray alien could have a belly button and what that would imply about hybrid breeding. After the gunman at the pharmacy is revealed to be a circumcised human, Dante exclaims, "I fucking knew a Grey wouldn't be circumcised," and Rita adds that Greys have no genitalia and no classic reproductive characteristics. (Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

The players also compare other alien types at the table. Zack points out that Zeta Reticuli beings are usually the gray aliens, and the conversation turns to the blond "Nordic" aliens and the Hyperboreans. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Roulet Estate 01, Kurt tells Andrew, "You know that scene in Close Encounters of the Third Kind, after they've landed and the little guy walks out? I think I just saw him on the roof." Andrew is hungover, paralyzed and starstruck. Later, after glimpsing a low streak of light in the woods, he gives the woods the finger and says, "I hate the Greys. They suck so much." Rita (as Andrew) wonders whether the task force was lured out to Rhode Island by whoever ran the cleanup in Utah, and says she does not think they have done anything to warrant being assassinated by the Greys, since "we didn't piss them off personally, as far as I can tell." The first apparent Grey is the figure on the roof and in the woods; see The Roulet Intruder.

In Roulet Estate 02, Diane complains that "this one seemed like a bastard" and that a species meeting humans for the first time ought to be on its best behavior. Andrew replies that the Greys have been here for generations and are not nice people.

At the Brooks Pharmacy the "gray alien" turns out to be a man in a foam-latex mask. In Roulet Estate 03 Andrew later wonders, in New York, whether he is himself one of "those alien hybrids" and whether his strange dreams are really his father. See also Andrew's Condition.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Whether the Greys had anything to do with the Roulets' "visitations," or whether the visits were the intruder and the drugged water.
  • Whether the lights and eyes in the woods were Greys.
  • Whether any real Grey was ever present. The episodes never settle it.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Roulet Estate 01
  • Roulet Estate 02
  • Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Dead grub-angel power core
docs.text:
The dead grub-angel power core is the corpse of a giant, glowing grub-like being, built into the portal machine in the cavern beneath the community center at the end of The Walkers in Skin.

Type Entity (dead) Aliases biblical angel; the dead angel Status Long dead; the portal machine is wrecked and the cavern ceiling comes down (Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 09

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The portal machine in the cavern is roughly the size of half a dozen semi-trailer trucks and is built into the corpse of a creature. Andre reminds the players of "the thing that you fought in the seaside town," and describes it: probably a thousand-pound grub covered in odd mechanical or insectile limbs, with several revolving rings around it. That is how it looks when alive; this one has clearly been dead for a while, with cords and tubes running from it into the machine. Zack calls it "a biblical angel." It is the same kind of being as the angel thing fought off Marblehead in The Summer Service (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text: The dead body is wired into the machine, which creates a roughly 20-foot portal. Skinwalkers and tanks of blood with creatures floating in them are carried through it in what looks like an evacuation. On the far side is a burned, blasted landscape under a sky full of smoke, with a trail of emergency lights (Walkers 09).

docs.title: History
docs.text: The party descends the shaft and watches the evacuation from near the portal machinery. The players ask whether the portal opens onto the room where they last saw one in Georgia; Andre says it has similar qualities but does not exit there. When the cavern's power cuts out, the portal flickers and spasms, a diffuse scream in an unknown language sounds, and people rush through. Huell Kendrick throws a grenade unusually far into the middle of the support machinery, and the portal winks out, leaving 50 or 60 skinwalkers stranded on this side. Explosions in the dark then bring chunks of the ceiling down on the crowd (Walkers 09).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The episodes never explain why a dead angel powers the machine, or who built it. The players compare the portal to the one in Georgia from The Things in Appalachia (the crack in the air).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Walkers 09

docs.title: Half-faced Bear
docs.text:
The Half-faced Bear is a bear "with, like, half a face" that chased the Circle Chasers from the spot where they found a pool of bloody vomit holding a blinking tracking device; Kurt insists it is not a bear at all.

Type Unidentified creature Aliases "Squatch" Status Unknown First appearance Appalachia 07

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The only account comes from the teenage Chasers, who describe being chased by a bear "with, like, half a face" and mark the location on a map in their RV. Vanessa blurts the words "Bear vomit" when the team meets them at the Spud Hut, and the group explains that the vomit was full of blood and held a blinking light, which they took with them. The Chasers had gone to check the most recent sighting, a "squatch" reportedly lying on the ground in some trees, and found the vomit while exploring the area (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: History
docs.text: In the Chasers' blacklit RV the teens produced a Ziploc bag holding a blinking red light and pointed out the sighting location. Kurt told them "Not a bear" and warned them to stay away. Huell advised the teens on guns, suggesting 7.62 and slugs and telling them not to shoot what they cannot kill. The device turned out to be etched "Inventory Control, SHA Tracking, SS994-0851" (see SHA Tracking Device), which the team connected to the logo on the wrecked Spud Hut truck (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• What the creature is. The etching marks the device as Spud Hut property, but the episodes never say how it came to be in the vomit, or whether the creature is one of the ape-men.
  • Whether it has any relation to the "bear" that Frotter Comstock blamed for a gore streak on his land in Appalachia 06.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Appalachia 07

docs.title: Hanging figures
docs.text:
The hanging figures are emaciated naked men with distended, rippling bellies, seen suspended from tree limbs by their punctured hands in the snowy Radford woods in the cold open of Radford Horrors 01.

Type Entity (unidentified; apparent hosts or victims) Aliases Hanging men Abilities Mouth silently; bellies ripple from within Status Unknown First appearance Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In a clearing in the snowy night woods, FBI agents in yellow-lettered jackets find a naked, emaciated man hanging from a tree limb by his punctured hands. His belly is distended, and bulges ripple under the skin. He mouths silently. More similar figures hang from other trees behind him. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text: The figures are shown doing nothing beyond mouthing silently, struggling for breath, while bulges ripple under the skin of the first man's belly. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The scene is a found-footage style cold open. Agents sprint through the woods with bouncing flashlights while something swoops overhead and picks them off. They reach the clearing and see the hanging men, and one agent at its edge is then lifted and drained by a hidden shape. See Radford woods predators. Unusually, the cold open does not cut to the credits: Andre says "This time we don't cut to credits," and it runs straight into the Biz's scene in Moscow. (Radford Horrors 01)

After the credits, Andre tells the table the president put together a handpicked task force to follow up on the PCs, and the players realize the dead agents were that team, the Missing FBI task force. Andre calls the first Radford case "a UFO, and then it was actually a giant moth," adding, "There was no man element. It was just moth." The episode does not say whether the hanging figures and the woods predators are connected to the Radford Moth. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: It is never established whether the figures are victims, hosts or something else. For the first case's crucified victims and moth hosting, see Crucifixion MO and Moth life cycle; no episode ties them to these figures. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Lights and Eyes in the Woods
docs.text:
Lights and Eyes in the Woods are an unexplained low streak of light and a pair of blinking eyes that Andrew Howard sees around the Roulet house, never accounted for by the episodes.

Type Entity / phenomenon (unidentified) Aliases Streaking light; brilliant light; blinking eyes Region Woods around the Roulet House, Exeter, Rhode Island First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In Roulet Estate 01, while the group hammers at the floor of the weapons closet, Andrew steps outside and shouts "Can we just talk?" into the woods. He gets no response. As he heads back inside he glimpses a brilliant light streaking low through the trees, which is gone when he turns to look. He gives it the finger and says, "I hate the Greys. They suck so much." Soon afterwards the hammering stops, and the others find Kurt staring at the door, dizzy and disoriented, having lost a minute of time. (Roulet Estate 01)

In the recap that opens Roulet Estate 02, Andre reminds the table that Andrew had just seen streaks of light in the woods. While Kurt is digging in the basement, Andrew keeps stepping out the front of the house to shout abuse at the Greys and then going back inside to throw up. On the third trip he sees eyes in the woods that blink at him several times and then disappear. He yells, "Get the fuck over here! At least talk! Don't be creepy!" and flips them off. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Whether the light and the eyes belong to the Roulet Intruder, the Greys or something else.
  • Whether the light caused Kurt's lost minute. The episodes only place the two in sequence.
  • Whether any of it was real. The agents had drunk the house's drugged water, and neither episode settles whether these sightings were hallucinations.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Roulet Estate 01
  • Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Minor monsters and entities: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: Minor monsters and entities of The Things in Appalachia: lesser creatures, rumored beasts and unseen presences. The main creatures are covered under Ape-Men, Big Bob, the Half-faced Bear and the Thing That Attacked the Spud Hut Truck.

docs.title: Ape Man
docs.text: "The Ape Man" is the table's name for the ape-man specimen the team had tested before Appalachia 08. Dante says that "we know the Ape Man had a human father," and the table jokes about who the father might be. See Ape-Men. (Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Ape-man Hybrid Tissue
docs.text: In Appalachia 06 Kurt wants the gore smear on Frotter Comstock's property compared with human-hybrid tissue from an ape-man. He believes a real ape-man hybrid exists and is separate from the man in the Chewbacca costume. The result of any comparison is never shown. See Ape-Men. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Frotter's Bear
docs.text: Frotter Comstock insists a bear is responsible for the large streak of gore beside a shack on his property, which he calls "the bear incident" and says the agents should have shot. Kurt suspects the gore could be hybrid tissue. Andre's table ruling is "bears are just real." See also the Half-faced Bear. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Giggling Presence
docs.text: In the cold open of Appalachia 03, a boy on the Consolidated Gold Mine tour hears giggling from a roped-off passage. Moments later the rope poles are tipped over and his Game Boy is bleeping on the floor. The source of the giggle is never identified. See Frederick. (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Hidden Ape-man
docs.text: Clive says there was always one ape-man he was never allowed to see, in a room he was not permitted to enter. He knew it existed only from the amount of food, and concedes it could have been two small ones. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Man in Black
docs.text: The Man in Black is a black-suited foe the team hit with their car in the middle of a road, who wielded a "magic flashlight that burns things." In Walkers 01, Dante compares him with the dead NSA agent whom Jan Martense says he hit on a Georgia road, since both were struck crossing a road at night, and jokes that they might both be aliens unaware of Earth customs. See also Dead NSA Man in Black. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Rabbit Thing
docs.text: The "rabbit thing" is the creature that snatched a rabbit on the Circle Chasers' three-second clip: a rabbit freezes on the trail and a gray, man-sized blur grabs it. Searching later, the team finds a white rabbit's pelt, ripped open and gutted, in a treetop near the site. See White Rabbit Pelt. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Rejects
docs.text: The "rejects" are the ape-men Jan Martense's operation could not train. Clive says they did not take to the training because of temperament, and that Jan, who was "sensitive" about disposing of ape-men, kept them. When Clive learns the party killed some of them, Dante says "Two, I think." See Ape-Men and Clive. (Appalachia 09)

docs.title: Wog of Winder
docs.text: The Wog of Winder is a dog-like Georgia cryptid. Rita (as Andrew) warns the Circle Chasers that skeptics will dismiss their footage as the Wog, since the area is not far north of its range. It never appears. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Minor monsters and entities: Radford (The Radford Horror and The Radford Horrors)
docs.text: This page lists the minor creatures and false alarms from the two Radford arcs, along with one creature borrowed from an earlier case.

docs.title: Bedbugs
docs.text: The Pay n' Stay's bedbug infestation is a comic recurring menace that leaves Huell covered in welts and sends the team back to the hospital, scratching. Andre notes that the bugs die when heated to 130 degrees Fahrenheit for ten minutes. The infestation also provokes the diner waitress to threaten arson for the insurance money. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06) See Pay n' Stay and Radford ER.

docs.title: Coyotes
docs.text: A pack of coyotes devours the remains of the burned NSA man, and Andre describes them as "mildly high". They scamper off into the woods when Kurt approaches. Later, the coroner blames post-mortem coyotes for the damage to Amanda Lucky's face, though he admits it is a lot of damage for so short a time, and Dante doubts they caused most of it. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05) See Agent Murphy and Dr. Harvey Mauden.

docs.title: Hairy men in fishing vests
docs.text: Two extremely hairy men in fishing vests wave at the group as they drive past at the Sportsman RV Campground. They appear to be ordinary campers, and nothing further comes of them. (Radford Horrors 02) See Sportsman RV Campground.

docs.title: Humanzees
docs.text: The "humanzees" are the gold-mining ape-men of the Appalachia case, mentioned in passing in the Radford Horrors arc. When the team tells Webster about the earlier case, the players argue over whether Bigfoot and the humanzees are the same thing, and Ezra remarks that Webster's career is flashing before his eyes. Dante recalls it as a humanzee mining operation run through a Spud Hut. They are covered in full under Ape-Men. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Minor monsters and entities: The Roulet Estate
docs.text: Minor entities of The Roulet Estate. The main creature of the arc is The Roulet Intruder.

docs.title: Utah UFOs
docs.text: The craft that Andrew Howard photographed over Ballard during the events of The Walkers in Skin; see also Black triangular craft. In Roulet Estate 01 Andrew carries three treasured Polaroids of them in his satchel, and when the agents discuss the UFO sightings associated with the Rhode Island house, Kurt asks whether they match what the team saw in Utah. In Roulet Estate 02 Andre recalls that the black triangles in the house's materials came from a sketch. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Veiny Hands and the Prison Guard
docs.text: Kurt's hallucination in the basement of the Roulet house, brought on by the drugged water. While digging in the trash pit, Kurt Larson sees veiny hands burst from the dirt and grab his wrists, and a Vietnamese prison guard's face appears. He fires into the hole and the guard's face crumples in on itself as other hands crawl out to grab him. He comes to curled in the fetal position, with Andrew shaking him, and says he was "back in Saigon." The hand in the hole turns out to be real: it belongs to a corpse, and a ring on it matches the wedding ring in the wedding photos, identifying Margaret Roulet. Kurt's explanation is "In my defense, I thought it was the VC." (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Minor monsters and entities: The Summer Service
docs.text: These are the minor creatures, legends and unexplained presences of the Marblehead case. The main threats have their own pages: the angel thing, the worms, worm bags and Puddles.

docs.title: Beast from the sea
docs.text: Also called the suspected sea monster. In Summer Service 01 Andrew, speed-reads a Bible with a doomsday tone around its Revelation passages and announces that he thinks the townspeople might sacrifice people to a sea monster. Later, on a call with a contact at the Bureau, he says he thinks the explosion was a sea monster and that the town is probably feeding it, or trying not to feed it, something. Amos Shaw's sermon on Revelation 13, with its seven-headed beast rising out of the sea, seems to support the idea. See also Amos Shaw and the Marblehead sea monster legend. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Cold-open sea target
docs.text: Also described as the thing "with a human with it." In the cold open of Radford Horror 08, four men in a steel boat at night aim a hydraulic gun at a target that the gunner reports "has a human with it." Mr. Miller fires, everything explodes at once, and the scene cuts to credits. The target is never identified, and the episode does not say where the boat is. See Boat crew. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Marblehead sea monster legend
docs.text: Also called the tentacled worm. In the case file delivered at the end of Radford Horror 08, Marblehead is described as famous for its sea monsters, with a local Loch Ness analogue: a big tentacled worm said to grab people and drag them under the water. Ezra jokes that it is a "worm with bonus worms." The legend predates the worm infection the team later finds, and the episodes do not say whether the two are connected. See also The worms and Marblehead. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Thing in Shaw's house
docs.text: Whatever tore through Amos Shaw's house. The upstairs bathroom door has been forced outward from inside, with its hinges partly pulled from the wall, the bathroom is wrecked and the window smashed, and a long broken stretch of the hallway wall looks as if something was shoved through it and dragged along, with blood on it. McManley documents about a full body's worth of blood loss, concludes the victim is dead, and says the blood was lost in the bathroom, so "there may have been a second party present" to knock the door down. The cause is never explained. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Thing in the sea cave
docs.text: Something big that moves inside a cave open to the ocean in the cold open of Summer Service 01. Andre describes a long, slow zoom into the cave mouth, with water flowing in and out, and just before the darkness swallows the image something large inside moves a little, then cuts to credits. It is never identified. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Whispering voice
docs.text: Also called the alien dad's ghost. In the middle of the night before the hotel siege, a voice whispers "Wake up and get your gun" in Andrew's ear, brushing his ear with lips. Waking, he meets the gaze of the fish ornament on his nightstand. He tells the Biz, "I think the ghost of my alien dad is telling me something's going on." The voice's source is never confirmed,. (Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Worm-hollowed fish
docs.text: Also called the mash-up fish. The EPA researchers' field journal describes fish that are not known species, some of them distorted versions of known fish and some like taxidermy mash-ups with a piece of one attached to another. It also describes normal-looking fish packed with worms that have replaced their vital organs, yet which, unlike the other fish, are not dead. See EPA field journal. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Minor monsters and entities: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text: This page lists the minor creatures, sightings and unexplained phenomena of The Walkers in Skin; the main threats are the skinwalkers and the upright coyotes.

docs.title: Barn snooper
docs.text: A figure seen snooping around the barn on the Sherman Ranch. Gardner reports that a former Army Ranger on the property shot at it and believed he hit it, but investigators found no physical evidence. The shooter was the gate guard Walt, who tells the team that he gave a warning before firing and that the figure came at him "at pretty high speed"; Bigelow backs "Walt's judgment". In Walkers 04 Walt, catching Harrison in the barn, warns him that there are people with guns on the property and says, "I shot at a guy not two months ago." The episodes never say what the figure was. (Walkers 02, Walkers 04)

docs.title: Burned crow
docs.text: A crow that falls from the sky into the ranch's pig pen with no sound and no flash, carbonized: its feathers crumble, its eyes have burst and its bones are cracked open by heat. Walt suggests ball lightning, and Andrew cites the 1957 Levelland case. The party bags the crow in a dog-waste bag for McManley. That night Andrew dreams of the goose, in the form of the cremated crow, explaining radar physics. See the Levelland case. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Maggie's bright object
docs.text: A fast bright object that Maggie the bartender saw streak past her car on the ranch's back road and shoot straight up. She thinks it was ball lightning, while the man who was with her swears they nearly got abducted. In Walkers 04 Walt also says ball lightning has been seen on the property, quiet and without a flash. The party treats it as a possible second sighting alongside the dusk event. (Walkers 03, Walkers 04)

docs.title: Mothman
docs.text: A "big moth thing" from an earlier arc that nearly killed the team and left Kurt with a scar on his neck, which he touches while joking about his "giant moth wound." The Biz calls it Mothman and cites it as the reason he is cautious about hoping for aliens. It is recalled at the bar and again in Walkers 06. See the Radford Moth. (Walkers 03, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Off-brand Bigfoot
docs.text: A creature from an earlier arc that beat Kurt up, mentioned in passing in Walkers 03 alongside the moth. See the Ape-Men. (Walkers 03)

docs.title: Radar-chewing culprit
docs.text: Something that chewed through the thick wire bundles of the ground-penetrating radar from underneath, even though the machine had been left standing upright. Kurt works this out with a successful investigation roll, and the table jokes about the goose, ape men and squirrels. Huell repairs the wiring, and the radar indicates a solid object in the coffin of Shelly Wilmarth. Nothing is ever shown doing the chewing. See ground-penetrating radar. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: The eye on the roof
docs.text: An eye watching from the roof of the big house while the party chains the squad car Betsy in front of it. Andre first describes two eyes, then amends it to one after Dante notes that the goose's eyes would be front-facing. Kurt orders everyone to back away slowly without turning their backs to the house. At about 50 feet, Nancy the goose drops from the roof, and the party runs for the house. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Tooth troll
docs.text: Andrew's theory that the candy-crunching mayor, Wilford Hiram, has been replaced by a Scandinavian sugar-eating tooth troll. It is offered half-seriously at the table, alongside Kurt's giant sugar-eating fly and Huell's sugar-preserved something. See sugar clues. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: White powder
docs.text: A powder that falls from the sky like snow during the cleanup in Walkers 09, as silent black triangular craft pass overhead. Kurt inhales a little and gets dizzy, and everyone outside is later found unconscious. He bags a sample, in keeping with the FBI joke that scraping white powders into baggies is a core part of the job. The episodes do not explain the powder, or say whether it is the same substance that the coyote-feeding woman pours in Walkers 05. See black triangular craft. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Plastic-wrapped bodies
docs.text:
The plastic-wrapped bodies are human-shaped bundles wrapped in plastic that recur through The Walkers in Skin: moving figures in two cold opens, putrefied corpses packed in white powder in the ceiling of the Ballard gym, and a huge pile of salted bodies in the Roosevelt morgue.

Type Entities / victims Aliases plastic-wrapped figures; shiny-wrapped figure; plastic bundles; gym ceiling bodies; salted bodies Status Cold-open figures unexplained; the bodies in the gym and morgue are corpses First appearance Walkers 03 (cold open)

docs.title: Cold-open figures
docs.text:
The cold open of Walkers 03 is a long, slow zoom through a dark, dusty, crowded industrial space of wires and pipes, lit only by thin shafts of light from below, with the distant sound of people shouting and talking. The camera passes rows and rows of human-shaped figures wrapped in clear plastic; as it approaches the last one, the figure moves slightly, and the show cuts to credits.

The cold open of Walkers 04 shows a pale, obese man in a desert trailer with a human-shaped figure wrapped in something shiny propped up in the other chair, out of focus. The man lets fine gray tendrils spool from his mouth onto a plate of Jell-O. See Doug.

docs.title: The gym-ceiling bodies
docs.text: In Walkers 07, after the grenade explosion in the gym of Ballard High School, part of the burning ceiling gives way and drops a tube of melted plastic wrapped in a spiral, "like a spring roll." The smell is overwhelming, like "a really, really bad fridge." Huell unrolls it and finds a fairly putrefied corpse in a pile of white powder; more bundles fall from the ceiling. Reporting back, Huell describes dead bodies with white powder on them, and Kurt asks whether it is lye or salt. Having smelled it on Huell, Kurt concludes that whatever is going on has been under way for at least a few months. See Disappearances in Ballard and white powder.

docs.title: The morgue piles
docs.text: In Walkers 08 the party finds "where the bodies from the library ceiling went" (Andre's slip for the gym) in the morgue of the Roosevelt police station: dozens and dozens of bodies wrapped in plastic and piled everywhere, with fluid leaking onto the floor. Many are too decomposed to identify, and some are missing fingers or toes. It looks as though someone covered them in rock salt and wrapped them in plastic, with poor results. Rita later notes that the skinwalkers' utility bags hold guns, plastic and bungee cords, matching the sheet plastic on the ceiling bodies. Andrew Howard, killed earlier, wakes naked and bound in plastic and duct tape at the bottom of this pile, as the Monstrous. See skinwalkers and Roosevelt police station.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: Why the cold-open figures are wrapped and why the last one in the Walkers 03 opening moves is never explained on screen. The players assume the gym and morgue bodies are the missing townspeople and students, but no episode confirms it.

docs.title: Puddles
docs.text:
Puddles is the worm-infected Doberman of Arnold Weathers, the first fully transformed host the task force fights in The Summer Service.

Type Monster / infected animal Aliases Worm dog; Arnold's Doberman; the dog head Abilities Shrugs off a forehead gunshot; keeps moving after being cut in half; vomits streams of worms Weaknesses Fire and the flashlight weapon; leg wounds slow it Status Destroyed; its still-living head was handed to McManley's team (as of Summer Service 05) First appearance Summer Service 05

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Puddles is a bloated, hairless, swollen white Doberman with fluid streaming from its mouth and a collar cutting into its neck. Clumps of hair lie around the entryway of Arnold's house, and the air smells of blood, feces and vomit (Summer Service 05). The dog's name comes from Arnold's niece Madeline Weathers, who recognizes the head when Andrew Howard shows it to her. The Biz first answers "Puddles? Yeah," then retracts it: "That wasn't Puddles when we found it" (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
• A bullet through the forehead (2 harm) has no effect.
  • It charges and bites. It sinks its teeth into Huell Kendrick's neck and shoulder and drags him backward into the house, then bites deep into Kurt Larson's forearm.
  • Its body keeps moving after it is cut in half, and thousands of worms poke from the stump of its neck. It rears back and vomits a stream of worms (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Weaknesses
docs.text: A shot from Kurt that takes a chunk of bone and meat out of a leg makes it drop Huell. Fire kills it: Andrew points Kurt's flashlight weapon at the headless body in the pantry, setting it on fire for 4 harm, and Huell finishes it with 2 more, though it topples onto him, burning and dripping worms (Summer Service 05). See also the worms, which are killed by heat, salt and alcohol.

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
When the team opens Arnold's door, Huell's flashlight reveals the dog. The Biz panics and fires a burst that wrecks vases and windows but does no harm to it. Andrew sprints back from the car, shouts "Hold it away from you!" and uses his holy weapon, which he has been treating as pepper spray. The spray of nothingness bisects the dog and also passes through Kurt's arm, costing Kurt 3 harm; the body falls away, leaving the head clamped on his arm (Summer Service 05).

Once Huell pries the head off, he sees worms riddling the back of its neck and its eyes still moving under closed lids. When the team reopens the door, the body is gone. Andrew bags the head and puts it in the trunk. In the kitchen the headless body is standing upright in the lattice-doored pantry. The team burns it, then douses the pantry and burns the spreading worms (Summer Service 05).

Andrew wordlessly hands the bagged, still-living head to an assistant at Donald McManley's RV: "Be real careful. It still moves." McManley examines it, and a garbage can with a cinder block on top is later put over it in the back of the RV. The team abandons the RV, head included, behind the abandoned gas station (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: Whether Puddles was infected before Arnold or after, and what became of the head after the RV was abandoned. The episodes do not say.

docs.title: Appearances

docs.title: Rabid mouse
docs.text:
The rabid mouse is a foaming, stiff-legged rodent from the bat-infested Pay n' Stay motel in Radford, Virginia, which bit Special Agent Daniel Webster and was speared by Kurt before being sent to Roanoke for testing.

Type Animal (rabid) Aliases The rat; rabid rat Abilities Rabies; climbs bedding Weaknesses Spear gun Status Dead; DFA result never reported First appearance Radford Horrors 02

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The mouse is foaming, stiff-legged and jerky in its movements (Radford Horrors 02). The table calls it a mouse and, more often later, "the rat."

docs.title: History
docs.text:
At about three in the morning in the Pay n' Stay, the mouse crawls up Daniel Webster's stomach. He flicks it off with his gun barrel (Kick Some Ass 9, a mixed result), and it bites him through his shirt on the nipple for 1 harm. Kurt Larson rolls a 10 and spears it to the floor with his spear gun. Andrew Howard pulls the spear from the floor, and Huell later picks the remains off it. (Radford Horrors 02)

Charm, the teenage clerk, arrives and admits a rodent problem: the motel's bat infestation gives the mice rabies. She offers the team their money back and says she does not sleep there herself. See Charm. (Radford Horrors 02)

In Radford Horrors 03 the team shares a patient room in the Radford ER. The doctor says, "Rabies, huh? All right, give me the rat," and Kurt hands over the harpoon with the rat still on it, in a plastic bag. There is no local DFA test, so the animal goes to Roanoke, which also supplies the HDCV vaccine. RIG begins at once: IV for everyone but Webster, who gets about twenty shots around his gumball-sized, hot nipple after a scrub and iodine soak. The treatment stops if the rat tests negative; otherwise the vaccine series is four shots, every Tuesday for four weeks. (Radford Horrors 03) The treatment sets off Andrew's alien dad dream and his feverish reaction.

In Radford Horrors 04, Andre's recap and the team's own talk mention the mouse only as the reason everyone is on rabies treatment (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The DFA result is pending as of Radford Horrors 03,. The episodes never report the result. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Kurt had been sleeping with the spear gun beside him and fires it from his bed. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • Kurt insists the harpoon is "a piece of sporting goods equipment" and "not a weapon" (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The Radford Moth
docs.text:
The Radford Moth is a car-sized, telepathic blue morpho-like moth that the task force first meets as a silent, light-blotting "UFO" over Radford, Virginia, and which takes dogs and young women, enthralls Wilbur Whateley, and burns to death in an old church at the end of The Radford Horror.

Type Monster (giant moth) Aliases The moth; the craft; blue butterfly creature; "She"; giant Morpho menelaus; flying creature; UFO; Mothman (Kurt's comparison); the thing in the woods Abilities Flight and silent hovering; hypnotic blue light; telepathy; mind control; draining proboscis Weaknesses Fire (damage doubled); thin wings; cuttable legs and proboscis; unarmored eyes Status Dead, killed in the burning church; body removed by the cleanup crew (as of Radford Horror 08) First appearance Radford Horror 01 (cold open, as a blue blur)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
As a flying object the moth is huge, dark and silent, between an ultralight and a Cessna in size. At about 50 to 60 feet up it looks like two round shapes joined like a Venn diagram. It blots out starlight, produces no light and no glow in night vision, and flares a dazzling, evanescent blue under flashlights or streetlights. Close up it smells of rotting wood, black mold, compost and a musty closet, and it leaves chalky white powder and a "terrarium" smell. Observers glimpse "narrow, jointed, folded, corrugated shapes like bendy straws." (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 06)

Inside the church it is revealed as a car-sized mass (the wings make it larger) with blue butterfly wings, a long curved, razor-sharp chitinous proboscis with rasping leech-like teeth inside, mantis-like clawing forelegs, an abdominal stinger, bullet-deflecting armor plates and segmented bug eyes. Its wing tissue is like wet leaves or rotten fabric and its ichor is warm and yellow. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
• Flight: VTOL-capable; it kept pace with a car at about 50 mph, patrolled the treelines behind houses, and swooped into a yard to take a dog. Its silhouette shrinks when diving and expands when rising. (Radford Horror 04)
  • Hypnosis: rolling its wings produces blue light that overwhelms minds; the sensation is of sinking into the ocean. Characters resist with Weird. (Radford Horror 07)
  • Telepathy and mind control: it speaks in the mind ("Changeling", "Save me, child! You know the ones who made me--"), delivers a psychic blast that blinds and hurts (it did 2 harm to Kurt in Radford Horror 06), and made Huell shoot Andrew. (Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07)
  • Draining: its proboscis drains flesh and blood; it filled all seven of Huell's harm boxes. (Radford Horror 07)
  • Psychic link: Wilbur feels its pain as physical agony without wounds. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: Weaknesses
docs.text: Kurt learns in the fight that it hates fire (damage doubled), that its legs and proboscis are thin and can be folded or cut, that its wings are thin and easily shredded, and that its eyes are unarmored. (Radford Horror 07)

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
The campaign's cold open shows a helicopter shot over Jefferson National Forest in 1992, with something blue darting over the tree line (Radford Horror 01). In Radford Horror 02 the team learns of large dogs vanishing from houses backing onto the national forest, at night, with rising frequency over six to eight months, and of locals reporting UFOs and lights (Radford Horror 02). See Radford's missing dogs.

In Radford Horror 03 a silent craft circles over the team's car, following them specifically and blocking out stars; it flares blue under flashlights, makes a noise nobody has heard, and speeds away. Andrew believes aliens; the Biz suggests birds and then a secret NSA project; Kurt suggests surveillance, a stealth RC aircraft or drones. (Radford Horror 03)

In Radford Horror 04 the team concludes the creature fled the flashlight, took a dog and apparently scooped Phoebe Augustine from a clearing; Kurt toys with a stealth aircraft, and a burned document fragment mentions "Menelaus" and an unknown "servitor" activity. (Radford Horror 04) In Radford Horror 05 what the team has actually seen is still "darks in the sky," and Kurt still favors a stealth drone. (Radford Horror 05) See Murphy's briefcase and documents.

In Radford Horror 06 the team stakes out the Whateley house. The craft descends, Kurt marks it with glow-stick fluid, a "punch in the brain" blinds him, and it lifts the astronaut-suited figure (Wilbur Whateley) away; Huell Kendrick, clinging to the figure, loses his grip and falls, breaking his right arm. The party theory is that the craft may be a living creature rather than a machine. (Radford Horror 06) See The Spaceman.

In Radford Horror 07 the team flies over Radford, finds an old church whose caved-in roof shows a flash of dazzling blue, and enters it at evening. Inside, a woman (Phoebe) is crucified above the pulpit, Wilbur rocks naked and mutters, and the creature waits in the rafters. Wilbur says "it has to breed" and "they're born pregnant." The creature drops on the team, hypnotizes them, takes over Huell and has him shoot Andrew, and slashes Kurt and the Biz. Andrew rolls Everclear across to Kurt, who smashes it on the creature as a Molotov, the roof catches fire, Huell cuts off a leg with bolt cutters, and the Biz gouges out its eyes. The team evacuates; a burning beam pins the creature. Kurt re-padlocks the door and Andrew hears "Save me, child! You know the ones who made me--" dissolving into screaming and silence. (Radford Horror 07) See Old-town church, Crucifixion MO and Andrew's mace for the aftermath.

In Radford Horror 08 the police close the case on Wilbur and "the cartel." Wilbur's journal records a larva found June 3rd, hatching August 15th the year before, the voice in his head, and the moth eating his dog; it was raised in the basement and then in the church. When the team returns to the burned church, its body is gone: Andre confirms that the special forces-style strangers removed it (see The cleanup crew). The team concludes the moth manipulated Wilbur and Huell. Kurt remarks "I always heard Mothman was a tulpa." (Radford Horror 08) See Wilbur's journal and Moth life cycle.

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
In Radford Horrors 01 Andre says of the first case that "there was no man element. It was just moth," and the table identifies Radford as the arc where the UFO turned out to be a giant moth (Radford Horrors 01). In Radford Horrors 02 Kurt calls it "the primary threat," and Andrew worries it bred or left eggs. Pearlescent "caterpillar slurry" with a sourer version of the moth's compost smell is found at the cleaned site (Radford Horrors 02); see Pearlescent goo.

Radford Horrors 04 adds that moths lay 40 to 500 eggs, and Wilbur, healed by Andrew, recalls finding an oversized Morpho menelaus caterpillar in the woods under a white oak. It was pregnant, he says, and "needed hosts, like a parasitic wasp." A smaller moth-smelling shadow in the Pinball Emporium may be a juvenile or a thrall; see Emporium intruder. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: Why it grew so large, where it came from, whether eggs or offspring exist, whether it caused the disembowelments of Amanda Lucky and Irene Whateley, who the people that removed its body were, and who made it. It told Andrew he knew "the ones who made me." It dies out of sight: its voice dissolves into screaming behind the locked door, and the cleanup crew has taken the body by the time the team returns. In Radford Horror 04 Rutherford, the Pay n' Stay clerk, insists the beings behind such sightings are the Anunnaki, and in Radford Horror 07 Rita (as Andrew) calls it one of the things the Masters had warned the group about. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Radford woods predators
docs.text:
The Radford woods predators are the unidentified killers glimpsed in the cold open of Radford Horrors 01, which hunt the missing FBI team through the snowy woods: a shape that drains a man to a skeleton, a swooping flier and a mind-turned agent.

Type Entities (unidentified) Aliases The draining shape; the flying thing; mind-controlled agent Abilities Flight; draining blood and fat; apparent mind control Status Unknown First appearance Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The cold open shows three separate things (Radford Horrors 01):

  • The flying thing: a flier that swoops over the fleeing agents and picks them off one by one from above. No clear details are seen.
  • The draining shape: a dim shape hidden in the brush at the edge of the clearing. It lifts an agent and drains him of blood and fat "like a pouch of Capri Sun" until he is nearly skeletal, then tosses him like a ragdoll.
  • The mind-controlled agent: a female agent aims at the shape, goes rigid, her eyes bloodshot and her nose bleeding, and turns her gun on a colleague. Whether the shape or something else compels her is not shown.

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text: Flight, a draining attack that leaves the victim skeletal, and an apparent psychic compulsion. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The attack takes place in the snowy night woods outside Radford, among the hanging figures. The agents wear yellow-lettered jackets and run with bouncing flashlights; one sobs. (Radford Horrors 01)

After the credits, the players conclude that the agents were President Perot's handpicked follow-up team, who went AWOL in Radford (see Missing FBI task force). The cold open implies they were killed. Special Agent Daniel Webster believes the team is dirty and covered something up in Radford. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: It is never established whether the predators are related to the Radford Moth, which Andre described as a UFO sighting that turned out to be "just moth," or what the shape and the flier are. (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: The Roulet Intruder
docs.text:
The Roulet Intruder is the naked, spindly figure who snipes at the task force from the woods around the Roulet house, lives in a hidden chimney attic, steals the agents' car and is finally unmasked at the Brooks Pharmacy as a drug-ravaged man in a foam-latex alien mask.

Type Human (disguised as a Grey) Aliases Gray alien; Grey-like sniper; attic dweller; nude man; masked gunman; hostage taker Abilities Skilled marksman; fast, erratic movement through the woods Weaknesses Needs beta blockers; begins to collapse without them Status Arrested (Roulet Estate 03) First appearance Roulet Estate 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The figure is tall, pale, hairless and naked, with an unnaturally large head, large oval black eyes, long spindly fingers and a long, spindly physique. At the pharmacy Andre adds that he is circumcised and has tattoos. The agents note that the proportions looked unnatural; Dante remarks that it would be "hard to be a guy in a suit, physically." While reviewing the case, Zack shared paintings by David Huggins as a visual reference for the Grey face. The face never changes expression, but its body language shows shock when its shot fails to hurt Andrew. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

Later Andrew realizes that the figure he saw in the woods had nipples, which contradicts what he believes about Greys. He tells the police it was shirtless, pale and bald. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Roulet Estate 01: the sniper
docs.text: Kurt and the Biz spot a classic gray-alien face poking over the crest of the roof, which ducks out of sight. After a car window is shot out and a monk tackles Andrew to safety, the party chases a naked, spindly, long-limbed figure east through the woods. It moves erratically and Andrew cannot keep his eyes on it. It picks up a VSS rifle and shoots Huell in the shin (2 harm). It then takes careful aim and shoots Andrew in the face, and Andrew takes no harm. The figure flees to a river where the trail ends, and Andrew finds that it has abandoned the rifle. Andrew later finds that the car's battery is missing. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Roulet Estate 02: the attic
docs.text:
The episode opens on a nude man with an unnaturally shaped head, a bed sheet wrapped around his shoulders, loading shotgun shells one at a time in a dark, dusty space. This is the Hidden Attic Lair. (Roulet Estate 02)

While the agents are in the Roulet Basement, they hear wheels spinning outside and see a gray alien drive off in their car around the corner of the driveway. The battery has evidently been put back in. Searching the house, Kurt and Andrew climb the chimney passages and find the lair. Andre tells them that someone has probably been living there for at least a year without the owners' knowledge, entering every major room by chimney. The lair held cigarettes, a cot, MREs, looted guns, a briefcase of money that looks abruptly abandoned mid-packing, beta blockers with the label scraped off, a jar of green slurry in which Kurt finds peyote, and a blood-crusted butterfly knife in an ornate case. The photos of sleepers give Andrew a strong serial-killer vibe. In the basement, the agents had also found a jar of cocoa-butter lotion with a hand-shaped scoop taken out of it. (Roulet Estate 02)

The party debates whether the culprit is an alien, a human serial killer, or both, noting that several of them saw a gray alien, which Dante calls a "weirdly consistent hallucination." Ezra says, "what I wouldn't give to just investigate a regular serial killer right now." The local police issue an APB on the stolen car. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Roulet Estate 03: the siege
docs.text:
The cold open shows the gray alien at the wheel of the stolen car in slushy snow, a black nine-millimeter pistol in his left hand, tuning the radio to "Radar Love". He takes hostages at the Brooks Pharmacy, shoots a pharmacist non-fatally, kills the young balding cop with a rifle shot, and demands a Range Rover and that all cops strip and surrender. He carries a Mosin-Nagant and claims to have a rocket-propelled grenade. (Roulet Estate 03)

The Biz shoots first from the drop ceiling to save Kurt, hits the gunman in the shoulder, and is shot through the thigh (3 harm), falling out of the ceiling. Huell tackles the gunman and is shot through the foot (3 harm). Kurt, naked himself, ties the gunman's hands with his own underwear and then reinforces it with Huell's handcuffs. He notices a seam around the gunman's neck. Police tear a foam-latex mask off his head, revealing a skinny man with herpes blisters around his mouth and "meth-head hair". Dante exclaims, "I fucking knew a Grey wouldn't be circumcised." (Roulet Estate 03)

As police lead him to the squad car he begins to crumple, and Kurt guesses that he needs beta blockers, like those in the attic. The pharmacist confirms that the man had hunted for them in the back and never found the supply. Police have a pharmacist fetch him some, and he is put in the car before the ambulance arrives. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• The man's name and motive are never stated.
  • Whether he killed the Roulets, though the attic lair, the looted guns and the beta blockers tie him to the house.
  • Who the people in the older attic Polaroids are; see Attic Polaroids.
  • Whether the "visitations" the Roulets recorded were his doing.
  • Where he got the mask.

docs.title: Servitors
docs.text:
Servitors are beings named by the crash survivor in Russia as the people who "need resources," the "opposite of aliens"; a fragment of a burned document in Radford uses the same word.

Type Entities (unidentified) Aliases The opposite of aliens Abilities Unknown; the survivor's body accepts O-negative blood Status Unknown First appearance Radford Horror 04 (document fragment); named by the survivor in Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Description
docs.text: Nothing is known directly about servitors. The only description comes from what the crash survivor says under questioning by President Yeltsin: when asked why his people are there, "The aliens," he answers "Not aliens. The opposite of aliens," and "Servitors... need resources" before passing out. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text: None are stated. Observations about the survivor himself: he shares fluids with a Russian soldier and accepts O-negative blood, which Yeltsin finds odd for an alien. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 04, the burned remains of Murphy's briefcase and documents yield legible fragments, among them "Menelaus," "Big Bill," "samples," "acceptable leakage" and "unknown servitor act[ivity]." Ezra (as Dick Baxter) mutters, "Whatever the fuck a servitor is," and later warns the team that the papers might be a trap. (Radford Horror 04) See Agent Murphy and Radford Moth.

In Russia, the Biz tells Yeltsin that these are not the aliens he has dealt with: he has seen resources go through portals, but it "presented differently," and he has never heard of servitors. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: What servitors are, what "resources" they need, whether they relate to the moth, to Andrew Howard's condition, or to the document fragment's "unknown servitor activity," and whether the Radford Horror 04 papers are genuine at all. (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Skinwalker Huell
docs.text:
Skinwalker Huell is the replica of Huell Kendrick grown by the skinwalker faction of Ballard and Roosevelt, Utah. It is never used to replace Huell and is destroyed in the battle outside the community center.

Type Monster (replica) Aliases Huell clone Abilities Tendrils from the mouth; physical match for the original Weaknesses Gunfire; trampled by a horse Status Destroyed (Walkers 09) First appearance Walkers 07 (cold open)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The cold open of Walkers 07 takes place in a dim room full of metal stock tanks of dark liquid, crisscrossed with hoses and wires, with the murmur of voices and the squeak of shoes in the distance. The camera stops at the last tank, and Huell Kendrick's face rises from the liquid and opens its bloodshot eyes. At the table this prompted Rita's joke that Zack would "end up having to play like four Huells in the next chapter."

docs.title: Origin
docs.text: At the end of the gym scene in Walkers 07, after Andrew is overcome by the tendrils, Andre gives Rita a private handout and explains that the faction clones people from tissue samples: Andrew Howard's from the ring that cut him on the mayor's hand, and Huell's from the bite of the "homeless" man in Ballard (the homeless biter). Only Rita knows this at the table at the time. The bite itself happened in Walkers 06. See Replication.

docs.title: History
docs.text: The Huell clone does not appear again until the finale. In Walkers 09, during the fight outside the community center, a naked copy of Huell reaches up from below, pulls Huell off his horse and crawls on top of him with tendrils coming from its mouth. Zack rolls exactly a 10 on Kick Some Ass and frees himself, though one tendril enters his mouth for an instant and he gets a flash of the way his childhood bedroom smells. Huell's horse stomps the clone while it clings to his leg. The duplicate Andrew, played by Rita, shoots it, and the horse puts a hoof through its head.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
