docs.title: Skinwalkers
docs.text:
The Skinwalkers are brain-like organisms that pilot engineered, childlike copies of human bodies, replacing the leaders, police and townspeople of Ballard and Roosevelt, Utah, in the arc The Walkers in Skin.

Type Monster (parasitic or symbiotic species and its copies) Aliases walkers in skin; body snatchers; snatchers; pilots; clones; replicators; worm people; tendril-mouthed replicators Abilities Piloting engineered host bodies; tendril "kiss" replacement; memory probing; coordinated sabotage; opening an unnaturally wide mouth Weaknesses Can digest only simple sugars and starches; flawed, deteriorating copies; die with the host on a head wound; can be detected by a mouth check or a flashlight in the eye Affiliation Skinwalker faction Status Main force stranded when the community center collapsed in Walkers 09; at least one pilot escaped First appearance Walkers 04 (cold open)

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
The visible copies look like ordinary townspeople, but they are manufactured "vehicles" rather than possessed humans. In the autopsy in Walkers 08, Donald McManley found that a captured host had no stomach, about eight feet of malformed intestine instead of the normal thirty-two, a slightly undersized liver with signs of fatty liver disease, and green fluid in the head wound. Its own brain was a shrunken lump, and its body ran a couple of degrees warm and had bad teeth. Andre (as McManley) described the body as "a 200-pound baby" (Walkers 08).

The pilot itself is a non-human, brain-like organ with swirls of iridescent purple and green, and long tendrils covered in small suckers. McManley told the team: "This is not a person. This is a vehicle. Somebody made this. And whatever you killed inside of it was its pilot." (Walkers 08) See Pilot and host biology and Pilot organ in Tupperware.

Seen from outside, the copies have fine grey filaments that spool out of the mouth, flat black eyes in at least one early sighting, and a rainbow-gray slick for blood. When pressed, the captured copies dropped "the facade of acting like a person" entirely and would not talk (Walkers 08). In the final session the copies were naked, fearless and tactically poor (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
• Replacement. A copy opens its mouth impossibly wide and extends tendrils to "kiss" a victim; sweet-smelling vomit and tendrils into the mouth complete the swap (Walkers 07). The faction clones people from tissue samples, such as the cut from the mayor's ring and the bite taken from Huell. See Replication.
  • Memory probing. Tendrils entering Huell Kendrick's mouth pulled up childhood memories, including the smell of his childhood bedroom and his father eating bacon (Walkers 09).
  • Sabotage and coordination. The Roosevelt police were massacred, each officer missing a small body part, every drivable car was stolen and the rest disabled, and a blockade closed the only road out (Walkers 08).
  • Animal allies. Upright horses and a pack of unnaturally clean coyotes acted for the faction in and around the gym (Walkers 07). The episodes never say whether the animals are themselves skinwalkers. See Upright horses and Upright coyotes.

docs.title: Weaknesses
docs.text:
• Diet. Pilots feed on the host's blood and can digest only simple sugars and starches, which fits the sugar clues (Walkers 08). In Walkers 09 the team tested whether a suspect could eat solid food.
  • Flawed copies. Hurried copies are made wrong: the replica Andrew had leukemia and a deterioration track, and sickly duplicates refused to open their mouths (Walkers 07, Walkers 09).
  • Head wounds. A pilot killed by a head wound dies inside the host, though a living pilot can flee a dying body into a drop ceiling. A flashlight shone through an eye shows light at the back of an empty mouth (Walkers 08).
  • Pepper spray. Andrew's pepper spray erased the head of Andrew's double for a moment and sent it into a seizure (Walkers 07).

docs.title: Early signs (Walkers 03 to 06)
docs.text: The cold open of Walkers 03 showed rows of plastic-wrapped human-shaped figures, one of which moved. The cold open of Walkers 04 showed a pale man spooling grey tendrils onto a plate of Jell-O while a shiny-wrapped figure sat in the next chair. In Walkers 06 the same man, addressed as Doug, pushed tendrils into a woman's mouth. A bite from a "homeless" man in Ballard (see The "homeless" man) later gave the faction Huell's tissue.

docs.title: The gym and the replacement (Walkers 07)
docs.text: In the Ballard High School gym, a double of Andrew Howard greeted the real Andrew while horses and armed townspeople looked on. After the double collapsed in a seizure, it crawled over the pinned Andrew and pushed its tendrils into his mouth. The faction was said to hold about sixty percent of Ballard (Walkers 07). See Andrew Howard (duplicate).

docs.title: Roosevelt (Walkers 08)
docs.text: The team found the police station massacred, killed one of three skinwalker "cleanup" men in gray maintenance uniforms and captured two, whose pilots then fled into the ceiling. They met a blockade of twenty to twenty-five heavily armed copies, most dressed as police, at the bridge (Walkers 08). See Utah cleanup crew.

docs.title: The evacuation (Walkers 09)
docs.text: The copies piled hundreds of cars and supplies in the community center and carried tanks of blood with writhing creatures down a shaft to a portal machine built into a dead grub-angel. The team wrecked the machine, stranding fifty to sixty copies, and the brain-creature of Andrew's double wriggled out of its mouth and scuttled away (Walkers 09). See The portal, Skinwalker Huell and Dead grub-angel power core.

docs.title: Later mentions
docs.text: Speaking to Boris Yeltsin, the Biz called the creatures skinwalkers and described them as good at mimicry but not strategic; they grow more convincing the longer they have been around. Yeltsin compared them to Koschei the Deathless (Radford Horrors 01). Dante remarks in the same episode that "the last kind of body snatcher we did could only do sugar".

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Who builds the host bodies, and where the pilots came from; the table jokes about aliens (Walkers 08).
  • What lies beyond the portal, and what happened to those who went through (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The cold opens never name the tendril-mouthed figures; they connect to the main plot through the matching grey tendrils later seen on Andrew's double in the gym.
  • The name "skinwalker" is used by the players only sparingly in the arc: the first mentions in Walkers 06 refer to the Skinwalker Ranch legend, and the term is applied to the creatures themselves in Walkers 09. In Walkers 08 the players mostly say "body snatchers", while McManley calls them vehicles and pilots.

docs.title: The Spaceman
docs.text:
The Spaceman is the helmeted figure in white seen above the Lucky house on the night Amanda Lucky vanished, who turns out to be the Whateley twins' homemade Apollo 11 spacesuit, worn first by Abelforth Whateley in a robbery and later by Wilbur Whateley under the control of the Radford Moth.

Type Unidentified figure; costume Aliases Man in white with a helmet; astronaut twin; the "Spaceman" Abilities Leaves fingerprints; jogs calmly into the woods; psychically linked to the moth Status Costume recovered in the Whateley cellar (as of Radford Horror 08) First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
Four-year-old Tyler describes "a spaceman" all in white with a helmet and a light shining on him, above or on the Lucky house, who "just went down" without obviously falling or using a ladder. (Radford Horror 01) An artist's sketch from the child's account is attached to the first case file and later posted by Molly Underhill (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 05).

The suit itself is a hand-sewn Mercury or Apollo 11 replica with an American flag patch and an Apollo command cap (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 06). See Spaceman suit.

docs.title: Early theories
docs.text: The team has no answer in Radford Horror 01. Kurt suggests a motorcyclist or a person in a suit and helmet and, privately, a hazmat-suited person; the Biz suspects a sleepy child mistook a motorcyclist; Sheriff Roosevelt thinks Tyler dreamed it. Out of character, Dante and Ezra joke that a spaceman took Amanda. (Radford Horror 01)

docs.title: The robbery and the Whateleys
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 02 neighbor Meg Gunderson says Abe robbed a store wearing a homemade spacesuit made for a school presentation. At the sheriff's station the team reads the file: Abe threw a cinder block through the Radio Shack window, entered in the suit, could not lift heavy items (leaving fingerprints) and left with lightweight modems and a cellular phone, then bought a bus ticket to Richmond. The sheriff had not known about the suit and admits it "gives a different color" to the earlier conversation; Kurt notes Abe may be the only person in town with a spaceman outfit. (Radford Horror 02) See Radio Shack spacesuit robbery and Abelforth Whateley.

In Radford Horror 05 Molly Underhill reports that the only match for the fingerprints from the first crime scene is the electronics-store "spaceman" robbery, so there is "a pretty good chance that Abelforth Radford is back in town." She puts out an APB and has photos taken of his brother. (Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: The astronaut in the woods
docs.text:
In Radford Horror 06 Huell points out a figure jogging into the woods, and Kurt identifies it through the scope as someone in an Apollo 11 astronaut suit. Huell chases and tackles him and pulls off the helmet: under the Apollo command cap is one of the Whateley twins. A huge silent craft descends. The boy says calmly, "It's okay. You don't have to fight this," and is lifted; as Huell hangs on above the tree line, the boy tells him, "It's okay. It's worth it." Huell falls and breaks his right arm. Kurt radios the other team, "Target is marked, maintain visual, track where it goes," and tells Andrew, "It's got the Whateley boy." (Radford Horror 06)

The suit pieces are later found discarded in the Whateley cellar beside a mummified teen in a NASA T-shirt, nailed to the wall. Dick Baxter plants a live radio bug behind the flag patch. (Radford Horror 06)

docs.title: Resolution
docs.text:
The police theory in Radford Horror 08 is a hidden basement containing the spaceman costume and a journal, with the cadaver likely Abelforth and Wilbur the culprit. Radford Horror 07 has already shown Wilbur, naked and scarred, in the church with the moth, which makes him the one the team chased in the suit. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08) See Wilbur's journal.

In Radford Horrors 04 Dante (as Kurt) speculates that the Emporium raid might involve "the astronaut kid," enthralled by a juvenile moth, and Wilbur is called the "Astronaut Kid." Kurt also tells Daniel Webster a simplified "Whateley spaceman story" in which Wilbur's brother, a space enthusiast, made an accurate astronaut costume and went around kidnapping people in it. Webster says it makes him feel a little better. (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: It is never established whether Tyler's sighting above the Lucky house was Wilbur, Abelforth or the robber from the earlier Radio Shack incident; the only link is the match to the suit. Radford Horror 05 gives the fingerprint suspect as "Abelforth Radford," a variant of his name. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: Thing That Attacked the Spud Hut Truck
docs.text:
The Thing That Attacked the Spud Hut Truck is the unidentified creature that climbed into the cab of a Spud Hut delivery truck near Dahlonega, Georgia, killed the driver, and carried off what was left of him.

Type Unidentified creature (presumed escaped ape-man) Aliases The attacker Status Unknown First appearance Appalachia 07 (cold open)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: The creature is never seen. The cold open of Appalachia 07 follows a heavyset driver in a gray Spud Hut jumpsuit, driving at sunset to "Radar Love". He hears a clang and ripping behind the cab, then breaking glass and a growl from the rear of the cab. He reaches for a Glock under his seat and misses; there is a blur of motion and he screams. The truck swerves through a barricade and stops among trees with the song still playing quietly (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
At the crash site on the freeway, the sheriff showed the cab: blood on every surface including the photo of a blonde taped to the dash, no body and no face, no direction to the spatter, far too much blood to survive, broken instruments and eight gunshots through the cabin. The back window broke inward, while the windshield broke outward after the crash. The vinyl roof was ripped as if by fingers. Kurt reasoned that something crawled in through the rear window, mauled the driver, and left through the front with what remained. Kurt called the scene "weirdly meticulous for what a mess it was" (Appalachia 07). See Freeway Crash Site and Spud Hut Truck.

In the next session the team's visit to the Spud Hut plant turned up the five ape-men on the Special Projects floor. Spud Hut's manager called the death a "tragic accident", and the sheriff talked the receptionist into opening the door by telling her "a man exploded today" (Appalachia 08). When the team later told Clive about the missing children, truck driver and Spud Hut workers, he was dismayed; the team tied the disappearances to the ape-men escaping through the unguarded mine ladder (Appalachia 09). The attacker was never specifically identified.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Whether the attacker was an escaped ape-man, one of the "rejects", or something else.
  • Why the driver was killed, and what link there is to the SHA tag found in the bear's vomit (see Half-faced Bear).
  • Where the driver's body went.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 07
  • Appalachia 08

docs.title: Upright coyotes
docs.text:
The upright coyotes are unnaturally clean coyotes in the Ballard, Utah area that rise onto two legs, appear in the cold opens of The Walkers in Skin, and turn up as a stalking pack at Ballard High School.

Type Monster (animals acting with intent) Aliases standing coyote; bipedal coyote; two-legged coyote; cold-open coyote; coyote pack Abilities Walking on hind legs; advancing in step; mass rushes Weaknesses Retreat when one is shot or when two shooters oppose them Affiliation Possibly the Skinwalker faction Status One dead coyote kept for examination; the pack retreated First appearance Walkers 02 (cold open)

docs.title: Description
docs.text: In their first appearance a coyote steps out from behind a flock of sheep, trots to the pasture's edge and stands on two legs after a rancher in an ATV has driven away (Walkers 02). The player characters did not see it. The pack in the school hallway stood stock-still and staring, and Andre described the dead coyote that Huell carried out as looking "kind of new" (Walkers 07). Kurt later called it "weirdly fresh" (Walkers 08).

docs.title: Cold opens
docs.text: The opener of Walkers 02 is the standing coyote described above. In Walkers 05 a woman drives a pickup into the desert as coyotes encircle it. One coyote's mouth opens unsettlingly wide and grey fibers swim up out of its throat; she scoops white powder from a backpack with a coffee cup and pours it down the animal's throat. The grey fibers resemble those of the tendril-mouthed figures in other cold opens (see Skinwalkers), though the scene never says so.

docs.title: Kurt's stalker (Walkers 04)
docs.text:
Walking back to the guest house, Kurt Larson realized he was being followed. He pulled a wad of baloney from his pocket on a successful preparedness roll, threw it and turned to find a coyote standing on two legs with glinting eyes. He used a "verbal flashbang", "Parlez-vous français?", and the coyote stared for a beat, then ran off into the dark, dropping to four legs as it picked up speed. The goose stole the baloney. Reporting to the others, Dante (as Kurt) said: "Either somebody's got trained coyotes or there's something in the water." (Walkers 04)

In Walkers 05 Kurt told Alberta Wilmarth about the coyote. Andre (as Alberta) answered: "Oh no, if he's on two legs and following you, that's probably one of the weird ones."

docs.title: The pack at the school (Walkers 07)
docs.text:
While Andrew Howard was in the gym, Huell Kendrick searched the hallway and found a pack of coyotes standing still and staring. He backed away and shot at the air around them, then shot the front coyote; it kept advancing a few steps, bleeding, and the pack stopped. When he went back through the gym, ten or twelve coyotes were standing on their hind legs, and one clamped onto his arm. Andrew's replica rounded the corner with a gun, Huell shot the biting coyote through the chest, and the pack retreated into a hallway at the back of the gym (Walkers 07).

Huell carried one body to the car, where it lay on the Cats costumes in the trunk. At the ranch it went into a beer cooler under ice, awaiting Donald McManley. Dante (as Kurt) joked, "All right, maybe the Mormons are training coyotes." Kurt's cursory examination found nothing more than that the animal looked new.

docs.title: Aftermath
docs.text: In Walkers 08 Huell asked locals he met whether coyotes seemed regular. One answered, "Coyotes? Not more than usual." The question became a running gag.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Whether the coyotes are skinwalkers, directed animals, or something else. The players raised both a trained-animal and a "something in the water" theory.
  • What the white powder fed to the cold-open coyote does, and who the woman was.
  • Why the dead coyote looked new; McManley never examined it on screen.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Walt Murphy says he tried in the summer of 1986 to get people to call him "Coyote" (Walkers 02), and the table uses the name for him throughout the arc.
  • The cold open of Walkers 02 drew the table joke "Regular coyote" from Ezra, answered by Andre with "Yeah, just normal."

  • Walkers 05

docs.title: Upright horses
docs.text:
The upright horses are horses in Ballard, Utah that stand on their hind legs, gesture politely with their hooves and fight on behalf of the faction that replaced Andrew Howard in the Ballard High School gym.

Type Monster (animals acting with intent) Aliases standing horses Abilities Standing and gesturing on hind legs; stamping and kicking; shielding allies Weaknesses Cast Out Evil can disable one; a grenade killed at least one Affiliation Skinwalker faction Status At least one dead and one burned in the gym fire First appearance Walkers 07

docs.title: Description
docs.text: At the gym, the real Andrew Howard found a line of yellow light under the door and the latch taped over. When he knocked politely, nobody answered; inside, two horses stood on their hind legs beside the door, and one gestured him in with a hoof (Walkers 07). Andrew's player, Rita, answered with an awkward nod and a polite grimace.

docs.title: The gym (Walkers 07)
docs.text: Inside, a double of Andrew waved and shook his hand while the two horses flanked the real Andrew and armed townspeople filed in. After Andrew's pepper spray dropped the double in a seizure, a horse brought a hoof down on the back of Andrew's neck (4 harm) and someone shot him in the stomach with a shotgun (3 harm). Andrew pulled a grenade from his bag, and a horse kicked him (3 harm) as he tried to leave. The grenade slipped from his hand, and one horse threw itself onto it; the blast hurled a piece of the horse into his back. Another horse kept stamping on him, and he used Cast Out Evil on it, which made it go limp, though it still pinned him. A burning horse ran from the wrecked gym across the parking lot past Huell Kendrick, and afterward a dead horse lay by the door with horse pieces piled in the middle of the room (Walkers 07).

docs.title: The blockade (Walkers 08)
docs.text: At the bridge on the only road toward Bridgeland, the team scouted a barricade of about a dozen cars manned by twenty to twenty-five heavily armed people, most dressed as police. Andre added, "You also see some horses," and Dante (as Kurt) said he didn't like killing horses. The episode does not say whether those horses stood upright (Walkers 08). See Bridge blockade.

docs.title: Not the same horses
docs.text: In Walkers 09 the team and the ranch people rode horses because horses are nonferrous and the ranch phenomenon lifts metal. These were ordinary mounts: Huell enjoyed riding and whooped a great deal, and a horse put a hoof through the head of the Huell clone.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: • Whether the horses are skinwalkers, animals under control, or loyal to the faction by some other means.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Zack briefly took the burning horse for a "demon horse"; Andre confirmed it was "just a horse".
  • The horse that throws itself on the grenade is a rare heroic act by one of the arc's antagonists.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 07
  • Walkers 08 (blockade)
  • Walkers 09 (ordinary horses only)

docs.title: Worm bags
docs.text:
Worm bags are the late-stage human and animal hosts of the Marblehead worm parasite: bloated, hairless, translucent bodies that shrug off bullets and burst into worms.

Type Monster / infected hosts Aliases Infected townspeople; infected hosts Abilities Bullet resistance; keep moving after losing the head; burst into worms; some can still speak Weaknesses Heat and fire; salt; vodka; the anti-worm agent Status A convoy was shot up at the nuclear plant; survivors are being dewormed (as of Summer Service 06) First appearance Early stage seen in Summer Service 04; full form in Summer Service 05

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
"Worm bags" is the radio contact's term in the finale, and it echoes the drawings in the EPA field journal of fish that are essentially bags of worms (Summer Service 03; Summer Service 06). The infection progresses from the "glow" of vigor to bloating and then to pale, near-translucent skin. At the selectmen's meeting the mayor, the chief of police and a few others are swollen and nearly translucent, the priest has started to bloat, and the banker Horace Cromwell looks more bloated than most, tense and struggling not to vomit (Summer Service 04).

In the fully developed form seen in Summer Service 05, hosts are hairless and very soft, with "the texture like overcooked vegetables or like a rotting pumpkin," and leak dark fluid (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
• Bullet resistance. A shot through the forehead does nothing to Puddles (Summer Service 05). In the finale a handful of infected townspeople ignore machine-gun fire and rush into the nuclear plant, howling (Summer Service 06).
  • Survive losing the head. Puddles' headless body stands up in the pantry. Arnold Weathers's head comes off on the bathroom sink and the body collapses into worms (Summer Service 05).
  • Burst into worms. Arnold ruptures when Andrew Howard tackles him, spilling worms and gore down Andrew's suit; the worms try to burrow into flesh (Summer Service 05).
  • Behavior varies. Puddles attacks. Arnold, soaking in a tub of black liquid with broken handcuffs cutting into his wrist, tries to get past the team rather than fight (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Weaknesses
docs.text: Fire (the flashlight weapon), salt, vodka and the anti-worm agent; see the worms. Once the team takes the deworming agent, the effects of the infection fade and a fever sets in, and the Guard officer says that some patients will not pull through (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Early signs. At the selectmen's meeting the party sees that the town leaders are visibly swollen (Summer Service 04).

Arnold's house. The first full hosts are Puddles and Arnold. The armed church members and police who gather at the team's hotel around 4 a.m. are not described as late-stage hosts (Summer Service 05).

The convoy. In the finale a convoy of infected townspeople, including the team's stolen FBI car, crosses marshland toward the nuclear power plant. The radio contact warns the team not to soften up the convoy because "they got like eight" worm bags. The stolen car, driven alone by Jester, sticks in a water-filled dip and falls behind; when the team pulls up he dives through their window and sinks his teeth into Huell's neck, Andrew scrapes him off against the stuck car and backs over him, and he dies gushing blood, bile and worms. When the convoy rams the perimeter fence, the ground beyond drops six inches and dozens of tires pop. Pop-up machine guns shred the convoy, though a handful of howling infected run past the bullets into the facility and one gun stops firing (Summer Service 06).

Aftermath. The Guard takes the town and distributes deworming medicine. The older Guard officer relays his medics' reports of "profoundly wild things" (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: How many townspeople are infected, how many survive deworming, and what became of the infected who reached the plant interior (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Summer Service 04 (early stage)
  • Summer Service 05
  • Summer Service 06

docs.title: The worms
docs.text:
The worms are the microscopic parasites spread through Marblehead's communion wine and food, which first give their hosts vigor and a youthful glow and then hollow them out into the bloated worm bags of The Summer Service.

Type Monster / parasite Aliases Worm parasite; communion-wine worms; Marblehead worms Abilities Boost strength, hair and vigor in early hosts; bloat and hollow later hosts; burrow into flesh and flee air Weaknesses Heat, heavy salt, vodka and alcohol; Ivermectin; the radio contact's anti-worm agent. Communion wine does not harm them Status Being treated by the National Guard (as of Summer Service 06) First appearance Wine tasted in Summer Service 01; worms identified in Summer Service 03

docs.title: Description
docs.text:
In Summer Service 03, Donald McManley examines the communion wine that Andrew spat into an empty Crystal Pepsi bottle and finds it "absolutely swimming with microscopic worms." He is not a parasitologist, but says they "look a lot like tapeworms or nematodes," and tells Andrew to find a horse doctor and get Ivermectin into his body as soon as possible: "People are drinking this" (Summer Service 03). Congregants drink it at the church's three services a day (Summer Service 03). When the worms turn up in Summer Service 05, Ezra remarks, "First moth, now worm. What next, guys?", a nod to the earlier Radford case (Summer Service 05).

Outside a host the worms are slow, and they flee a dying host. Inside flesh they try to burrow (Summer Service 05; Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Abilities
docs.text:
Early stage: the glow. Infected people gain vigor, muscle, hair regrowth and a youthful look. After drinking the wine, Huell Kendrick cannot sleep after 48 hours awake, looks significantly more muscular, has an advancing hairline, a faint glow and +1 Tough (Summer Service 03). By Summer Service 05 he has "all the worm strength" and heals back to full in about an hour (Summer Service 05). See The glow.

Late stage. Hosts become swollen, near-translucent and hairless; see worm bags. The affliction also shows in animals: Puddles is the first fully transformed animal, and the EPA field journal's drawings show fish that are essentially bags of worms yet still alive (Summer Service 03).

Symptoms in the party. In Summer Service 04 the team agrees that the town's food and drink are full of worms and that they all have parasites. Kurt has an itchy back spreading around his ribs, fever and joint pain, tangled up with chicken pox and the nerve agent (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Weaknesses
docs.text:
In Summer Service 05, the team tries things on the worms that escape Arnold's body. Andre rules that salt works pretty well, though not at concentrations safe for people, that alcohol bothers them, and that vodka "seems to cause problems for them." Kurt Larson later reports that straight vodka and heat kill them. He reasons that since the church gives the worms to people in communion wine, wine evidently does not kill them, and wonders whether alcohol explains why Ma Gramoire, who offered him absinthe, is unaffected (Summer Service 05).

The anti-worm liquid from the radio contact works against them in bulk; once the team is dewormed, Huell loses his bonus, gets a pounding headache and runs a high fever from the dead worms (Summer Service 06). At the end of Summer Service 05, Kira points out that killing a host's parasites all at once can flood the body with necrotic tissue, and the team decides to hold off on Ivermectin until it is out of the firefight (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Origins of the infection. The wine is served as "Blood of the Lamb." It tastes fishy, which Dante calls "fucked-up Pruno," and Zack drinks it at the first service (Summer Service 01); see Communion wine. Kurt tells the FBI by phone that the church is infecting people intentionally and en masse and asks for antiparasitics (Summer Service 05).

The cure. After the fight at the nuclear plant, the Guard distributes deworming medicine. The team's cover story tells the military that a terrorist group seeded the parasite through the food supply; see Terrorist cover story (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The source and purpose of the worms, and whether the angel thing is connected to them. Zack jokes in Summer Service 05 that "their god's definitely real, I have a mason jar full of it right here" (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Aetherius Society
docs.text:
The Aetherius Society is the church of Andrew Howard: a cosmic-minded faith devoted to the Masters, which raised him, issued him his church mace and, in later arcs, looks after his health.

Type Organization (religious group) Aliases Andrew's church; the Masters' church; "the cult" (Andre's description in Appalachia 01) Affiliation Andrew Howard and his mother First named Walkers 01 (the group appears unnamed from Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Aetherius Society is never shown on screen. It exists in the campaign through what Andrew says about it and through the few things it has given him. Its object of devotion is the Masters, ascended extraterrestrial beings who guide humanity. Andrew's account of its teaching, given to President Bush in Walkers 01, is that cosmic forces push humanity toward a violent future while the society's members hold them off by pushing their good energy into a "spiritual battery" (Walkers 01). In Radford Horror 08 Andrew complains that the church does not have as big a following on the East Coast (Radford Horror 08).

Before Walkers 01 the group is called only "the Masters" or Andrew's church, and in Appalachia 01 Andre calls it a cult from Andrew's childhood (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Andrew Howard, a lifelong follower. George H. W. Bush calls him "the only true believer" among the people serving under him (Walkers 01).
  • Andrew's mother, who stays with him in his small apartment during Radford Horror 08 and presses him to attend more church social functions. She is never seen on screen (Radford Horror 08).
  • Dr. Arthur, Andrew's childhood family doctor, who is also in the group (see below).
  • Unnamed doctors and church officials who see Andrew after the Roulet case (Roulet Estate 03).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text: In Radford Horror 04, standing over the remains of the NSA man, Andrew explains the Masters to the others. The Biz, a lapsed Catholic, objects that calling Jesus one of the Masters is blasphemy (Radford Horror 04). In the climactic fight, Andrew shouts "Did you know Jesus is one of the Masters?" to distract a man, then fires the church-issued mace, which sprays a "nothing" that erases matter (Radford Horror 08). Andre rules that the mace was given to him by his church, and Rita adds that he had carried it for years as a self-defense weapon without using it. Later, in the hospital, Andrew gives an inspirational speech about the Masters and the other things in the universe; it falls flat (Manipulate Someone, 5) and is followed by a long silence (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: Andre frames Andrew's family doctor, Dr. Arthur, as another member of the cult. Andrew has healed squad members twice, each time with a nosebleed. Dr. Arthur tells him the effort is a channeling with a "backlash effect", offers a meditation seminar, and advises him to carry tampons for the nosebleeds (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text:
In the Oval Office, after Bush tells Andrew he is "personally responsible for the survival of the United States of America", Andrew replies that this has been his responsibility his whole life and delivers a long lecture on the Aetherius Society, the Masters and the spiritual battery. Bush's face slowly goes blank. This is the first time the society is named (Walkers 01).

Late in the arc, Rita muses that if the society knew about the darker side of Andrew's powers, it would explain why all of its outward material shows only a "clean" version (Walkers 08). Andre adds that the society may not have been told the full story by whoever it is in contact with.

docs.title: The Roulet Estate
docs.text: After the case, Andrew spends a week at home with his doctor and church officials, who run tests and X-ray him without showing him the films. Andre confirms that he is, in the table's words, a "special horse" to them (Roulet Estate 03). See Andrew's Condition. In Roulet Estate 02 Andrew says he knows a couple of Masters but not who is or is not one these days (Roulet Estate 02).

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text: When the team views its tape in a Blockbuster back room, Andrew explains the Aetherius Society to the clerk Harold, who then tells them what he saw of a man dragged into a van (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The name is the real-world Aetherius Society, a UFO religion. The campaign uses it for Andrew's church and never gives a place of worship or a leader.

docs.title: Armed group in the woods
docs.text:
The armed group in the woods is a party of five or six people with flashlights and at least one shotgun, one of them heard speaking Spanish, with a muscular teen and a jumpy man introduced as "Uncle Trevor," whom Andrew Howard and Huell Kendrick encounter in a clearing on a dirt road down the mountain from the Alpine Lodge.

Type Unidentified armed group Aliases Campers Members Five or six people; a letterman-jacket teen; "Uncle Trevor" Affiliation Unknown; possibly the cartel Status Unknown (as of Radford Horror 03) First appearance Radford Horror 03

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The group is seen only once. The people claim to be camping, and act as though nothing is wrong when approached. They meet in a dirt road clearing midway down the mountain, the same area that Dean Lawson's red Miata came from. (Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Five or six people with flashlights and at least one shotgun, around an idling vehicle with its headlights on. Huell hears someone speaking Spanish in a tense conversation.
  • A muscular teen in a letterman jacket, who does the talking and says they are camping.
  • "Uncle Trevor": a tall, thin white man in his late thirties or early forties, in an oversized coat, "methy" and jumpy, who reaches into his coat and stops himself. The teen introduces him as "my uncle Trevor."

(Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
After tailing Dean's Miata down the mountain at dusk, the team stops where it turns onto the dirt road. Huell Kendrick goes on foot with a night-vision scope, while Andrew Howard stays at the car with the elderly couple (see Howard and his wife). Huell gets close enough to hear tense Spanish. He breaks a twig, the voices cut out, and several flashlights click on as the group spreads into the woods. His Read a Bad Situation roll (11) gets three answers, among them that one of the flashlight carriers has a shotgun, and he works his way back toward the car. (Radford Horror 03)

Two members then reach Andrew's car: the teen and the twitchy man. The teen says they are camping and the man is "my uncle Trevor." Andrew bluffs that he is driving his parents home from the ski lodge (Manipulate Someone, 7), greeting them with "Oh, fuck! Scared the crap out of me." Sensing the situation will turn bad if he stays, he drives off, waits about fifteen minutes, and comes back. (Radford Horror 03) See Alpine Lodge.

In Radford Horror 07, the helicopter pilot Freak says he bought Mexican heroin from a young man at a party whom he identifies from Dean's description, and that the young man got it from "a bunch of Mexicans." In Radford Horror 08 the police close the case on Wilbur and the cartel. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08) See Dean Lawson's heroin and cash.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Ezra points out that "you're allowed to go camping with shotguns and your friends." (Radford Horror 03)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: The episodes never establish whether this group supplied Dean Lawson's heroin, or belonged to the cartel the sheriff later blames.

docs.title: Ballard town government
docs.text:
The Ballard town government is the small-town leadership of Ballard, Utah, made up of Mayor Wilford Hiram and city treasurer and school superintendent Deborah Wells, who push a controversial community center and its substation near Sherman Ranch.

Type Organization (local government) Aliases Ballard town leaders; Ballard city government Members Wilford Hiram (mayor); Deborah Wells (treasurer and superintendent) Base Ballard City Hall Status City Hall found abandoned in Walkers 06; the mayor is later revealed to be a skinwalker First appearance Walkers 02 (mentioned)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Ballard is a town of a few hundred to about a thousand people with a high school, a courthouse, a general store, a church and mostly double-wides (Walkers 02). Its leaders back a community center with its own substation, built about four miles from the part of town where anything is, in view of the ranch. Locals dislike the mayor and Wells: Walt Murphy says some town leaders "make my skin crawl", and the general store clerk blames the mayor and "the goddamn busybody" Wells (Walkers 02).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Mayor Wilford Hiram. A mustached man in big rings who drives a new Cadillac and constantly eats lemon candies from a tin (Walkers 05). His desk at City Hall was covered in Tootsie Roll wrappers (Walkers 06).
  • Deborah Wells. School superintendent, town treasurer and organizer of church community events, described as the community center's driving force. Maggie, the bartender, went through every grade of school with her and dislikes her (Walkers 03). She is never met on screen.
  • The Ballard sheriff, Sheriff McDermish, runs a separate one-man office.

docs.title: The community center push (Walkers 02 and 03)
docs.text: Walt Murphy tells the team that the town says the community center will swallow the ranch area, but that Alberta Wilmarth will never sell (Walkers 02). Maggie says it is being built half a county away from the community, that Pueblo ruins were bulldozed for it despite a protest, and that Wells "dug in like a child" once people objected (Walkers 03).

docs.title: The mayor's visit (Walkers 05)
docs.text: Mayor Hiram arrived at the ranch, shook Andrew's hand so hard his rings cut it, offered condolences about the destroyed car and asked why federal agents were in so small a town. He offered the help of "the government of Ballard, Utah". Andrew and Kurt wondered afterward about embezzlement and a "community center scam" (Walkers 05).

docs.title: City Hall (Walkers 06)
docs.text: The party found City Hall abandoned for days or weeks, with a padlocked fridge full of bags of sugar. When the mayor arrived, he was nervous, chewing a lemon candy. He told them the junkyard lay in Ballard County but outside the municipality, that a fire a few years back had destroyed most of the geological records, and that his candies were a "special order" from Spain (Walkers 06). See Sugar clues.

docs.title: Replaced (Walkers 07 to 09)
docs.text: In Walkers 07 Andre told Rita that the faction had Andrew's tissue from the cut made by the mayor's ring. In Walkers 08 Andre told the team they now suspected the mayor was one of the creatures, and that what they had found in the trailer suggested he had been taken over a couple of months earlier. In Walkers 09 the mayor appeared in the cavern carrying supplies for the evacuation. Wells's fate is never shown. See the Skinwalker faction and Disappearances in Ballard.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • In Walkers 03 Andre first gave Wells's name as "Misabelle" in Maggie's mouth, then corrected it to Deborah and told the players to retcon it.

docs.title: Bigelow's research operation
docs.text:
Bigelow's research operation is the private UFO and paranormal study run by billionaire Robert Bigelow at Sherman Ranch near Ballard, Utah, with scientists, a couple of ex-Navy staff, instruments and armed security.

Type Organization (private research group) Aliases Bigelow's research group; ranch staff; Bigelow's estate security; Bigelow's security force; Coyote's ranch group Leader Robert Bigelow Members Walt "Coyote" Murphy; Ponytail Lady; Marina; an unnamed staff psychiatrist; armed guards Base The big house at Sherman Ranch Status Robbed of its recordings and three employees in Walkers 07; still at the compound in Walkers 08 First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Bigelow rents the big house and barn on Alberta Wilmarth's ranch. The FBI agents in Salt Lake City told the team he had "some security people out there and some scientists and, I think, a couple of Navy guys" (Walkers 02). His team records electromagnetic and electrical phenomena and heat signatures onto big tape reels. Many staff are away on university rotations, and Bigelow buys food for the maximum headcount (Walkers 03). The ranch has cameras on the big house and the utility sheds, but none on the guest house where the team stays (Walkers 04).

Bigelow reported many unexplained heat signatures and electromagnetic events plus exploded sheep, confined to the ranch and about half a mile around, with nothing in town. He dismissed the nearby substation as unrelated (Walkers 02).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Robert Bigelow. Sour-faced and expensively dressed.
  • Walt "Coyote" Murphy. Gate guard and patrol driver.
  • Ponytail Lady. The security woman at the big house, who sets the house rules: keep Bigelow happy, keep the goose happy.
  • Marina. A staffer with recurring drowning nightmares (Walkers 05).
  • A staff psychiatrist, who spends 45 minutes taking the party's account after the night event.
  • Guards. Among them a burly enforcer who makes pancakes for everyone in the morning (Walkers 08).

docs.title: Arrival and monitoring (Walkers 02 to 05)
docs.text: The operation shared its data with the task force. After the rental car vanished and reappeared in Roosevelt, the big house cassette showed the car only as a slightly different patch of grey next to the guest house, and the electromagnetic meters went off; the data was blurry (Walkers 04). After the night event, Bigelow showed the party a sky-camera frame of a bright white ring, discussed the Black Sun and Revelation 6:12, and agreed to set up a big ring of cameras around the party's house (Walkers 05). See Bigelow's recordings and The white ring.

docs.title: Theft and protocol blue (Walkers 07)
docs.text: After a naked intruder broke into the guest house, Bigelow raged that "somebody broke in and stole all our hard drives, all our tapes, all of our recordings, and three of my fucking employees", and that the barn had been cleared out as well. He declared "protocol blue", unlocked the big cabinet, handed out SPAS-12s and M16s, set a ground-floor perimeter and asked the party to stay as backup. Two guards went to back up Coyote on the hospital run (Walkers 07).

docs.title: The compound (Walkers 08 and 09)
docs.text: The compound is the team's base in Walkers 08. The team considered going back for the rest of Bigelow's security force and asked whether Bigelow had ideas about the area. In Walkers 09 the ranch people rode horseback behind the National Guard convoy, and Coyote volunteered for the assault with an illegal rocket launcher. The ranch farmhouse floated into the sky and was launched toward Roosevelt, leaving only the barn (Walkers 09). See Sherman Ranch phenomenon.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Andre accidentally had Bigelow call Alberta "Madeline" and corrected himself mid-line (Walkers 02).
  • In Walkers 02 the Salt Lake City agents describe a former Army Ranger on the ranch who said he shot a prowler by the barn, and Gardner says Bigelow's security man fired the shot. Later in the same episode Bigelow says he has "total faith in Walt's judgment" about "whatever the situation was the other month", and Walt himself tells the team at the gate that he gave the man a warning before firing. Walt was the shooter.

docs.title: The cartel
docs.text:
The cartel is the Mexican drug-smuggling organization that the Radford Sheriff's Department names as the official explanation for the heroin and violence of the Radford killings. The task force never meets a member, and the "cartel" is never shown on screen.

Type Organization (alleged; never seen) Aliases Mexican cartel Affiliation None established Status Still being hunted by the sheriff's office in Radford Horrors 02 First appearance Radford Horror 07 (as speculation); Radford Horror 08 (as the official theory)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: In the first Radford arc the cartel is a theory rather than a presence. The team finds a heroin connection to the missing girl Amanda Lucky: a briefcase of slightly cut heroin and cash hidden in the Lawson cabin of her boyfriend Dean Lawson (Radford Horror 07). When the team tests a sample on the charter pilot Freak, he snorts it, says "I love Mexican heroin," and recognizes it as the same stuff a young man once sold him at a party. Shown a description of Dean, Freak says Dean told him he got it from "a bunch of Mexicans." Kurt remarks that the team "might get Dean Lawson murdered by a cartel or something" (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: The official theory
docs.text:
After the church fight, the sheriff visits the team in the hospital and lays out the police theory. Wilbur Whateley is a serial killer who faked his brother's departure, and the body in the hidden basement is probably Abelforth. The sheriff says heroin found in the old-town church is how drugs have been reaching Radford, and suggests Wilbur was "in bed with the cartel," which would explain the shootout and the heroin used to sedate his victims. The kidnapping case is closed on Wilbur and the cartel, though the sheriff says his office will keep looking for "the cartel people." Ezra and Dante play along, Dante adding that cartel hitmen can be vicious (Radford Horror 08).

Before leaving town, the team tips the sheriff off to Dean Lawson, citing the heroin and drug money at his place while keeping the seized drugs and cash. Dean's parents report that he has not answered his phone, and Dante wonders aloud whether Dean was the man beaten up by the cartel near the church; the sheriff says Dean may have "got on the wrong side of the cartel" (Radford Horror 08).

The cartel story also serves as a convenient explanation for the unidentified cleanup crew that scrubbed the church. No character establishes a link, and the only heroin trade the team traces runs through Dean.

docs.title: Return in The Radford Horrors
docs.text: Months later, Sheriff Molly Underhill recaps the first case for the new agents. She says "some kind of cartel people" were at the church as well as the Whateley boy, and that the dead and the injured looked like the victims of an ambush. She suspects the cartel may be back, running a cover operation behind the torture of the missing agents' suspects. She gives them the local case file, which differs from the internal FBI file: the town saw nothing of the aliens or the moth. Daniel Webster is skeptical of the vague "it was the cartel" explanation and of the church's convenient fire. Andre confirms that the file has a heroin connection to the Mexican cartel through Dean (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Heroin becomes a running gag in the first arc: the players use it as a bribe, a would-be sedative and a bonding tool (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: CIA
docs.text:
The CIA (Central Intelligence Agency) is the home agency of Kurt Larson, who serves with the Paranatural Incident Task Force on loan, and the keeper of the undersea prison where the villain of the Georgia case ends up.

Type Organization (U.S. federal agency) Aliases the Agency; Langley Known branches and sites UTAW; Black Site Omaha Status Active First appearance Appalachia 01 (Kurt's CIA superior); mentioned from Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The CIA reaches the story almost entirely through Kurt. He is a case officer and Vietnam veteran who was lent to the FBI's Counterterrorism Task Force, downsized from there into the paranatural unit, and expected to return to the Agency when his contract ends. He carries CIA credentials and no FBI badge ("I'm not a federal agent, by the way. I'm a hooligan"), and finds it strange to work on American soil, where people talk to him because of authority instead of money, drugs or threats. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03)

Quote

"I am not a federal agent or a traditional CIA agent." (Dante, on Kurt, Radford Horror 02)

Much of what Kurt says about the Agency is tall tale. For his own division, see UTAW.

docs.title: Members and contacts
docs.text:
• Kurt Larson, case officer on loan.
  • Kurt's unnamed CIA superior, a man in a black suit and a tie covered in nautilus shells, who sits silently beside him at the House subcommittee hearing on Marblehead. (Appalachia 01)
  • Carter, a former CIA fixer turned arms dealer, who by Kurt's account came up with Iran-Contra. Kurt worked with him for about five years and once saved his life; Carter repays him with the Davy Crockett. (Summer Service 04)
  • The Spud Hut counter savant, a Georgia teenager for whom Kurt arranges a CIA job. (Walkers 01)
  • A private CIA dentist. Kurt keeps special molars, each loaded with a different drug. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Kurt's career
docs.text:
By his own telling, Kurt's CIA work included a plot against a Cuban dictator, despots, sewer crawling, interrogation ("Now, if I were at my old job, you would already be zip-tied to a chair, being Tabasco-boarded"), being sent to South America at no notice, and so many years abroad that in October 1992 he does not know who Bill Clinton is. He says he was legally declared dead years ago. He tells Daniel Webster it was "wet work", and that he has been shot in nearly every country. (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 01, Appalachia 07, Radford Horrors 02)

He knows the real psychic-spy programs of the era through the Agency, and knows of CIA and DARPA beam-weapon projects, which is why the man-portable flashlight weapon alarms him: the ones he has seen need a car full of batteries. (Radford Horror 03, Appalachia 03)

After the task force is disbanded the Agency takes him back. In early 1993 he is sent to Sri Lanka, then recalled to train American agencies at Quantico. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Black Site Omaha
docs.text:
Unrecorded session

Jan Martense's capture happened in Appalachia 10, which was never recorded. It is known from dialogue in Walkers 01.

After the Georgia case Jan is held at Black Site Omaha, five stories under the ocean beneath a naval research base that serves as its cover. Kurt gets in past a keycode door with a gift of cigarettes for the desk guard, is cleared for four hours, and interviews Jan in a steel room with rounded furniture. He learns where the first ape woman came from: the van of a dead man carrying NSA identification. He also promises Jan a set of approved playing cards, and keeps the promise. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Reputation
docs.text:
Local reactions to "CIA" vary. Sheriff Frank Roosevelt notes it and bans "cowboy bullshit". Sheriff Carter Burke recognizes Kurt's "agency boy" manner. Jan, raised in East Germany, says he understands the arrangement when Kurt bluffs that the CIA must work alongside federal agents at home. An eager young local helping with the Utah case is starstruck. And the junkyard owner Yusuf Ansari is horrified. (Radford Horror 01, Appalachia 04, Appalachia 08, Walkers 05, Walkers 06)

Quote

"Not the CIA. Not again." (Andre as Yusuf, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Kurt on the Agency
docs.text:
• On paying an $8,000 bill: "Government's money, it's fine... Also, I'm not poor. I work for the CIA." (Radford Horror 04)
  • On keeping a drug dealer's cash: it is "how the CIA secures funding". (Radford Horror 07)
  • On guarding a body in the woods: "CIA standard procedure. Don't worry about it." (Appalachia 06)
  • On hotwiring a forklift: "I'm CIA. I'm certified for anything." (Appalachia 09)
  • On the Agency's animal programs: "I have seen tens of hundreds, if not thousands, of lines of yayo done in front of a dolphin, but it just doesn't get it." He also says "we tried to train geese to attack", and they would not. (Appalachia 09, Walkers 02)
  • On the armored bulldozer and its driver: "Now, you see, in the CIA, this is what we call an asset." (Walkers 09)
  • On his standards: "I'm CIA, and I have standards, thank you very much." (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• "The Puzzle Palace is what the CIA calls the NSA", a detail Andre shared with the table when Kurt sent a cryptogram there. (Appalachia 07)
  • Dante's motto for the Agency: "We're CIA, not fucking CI-Lose." Andre and Dante then improved it to "Not C-I-Flunked." (Appalachia 08)
  • A running table joke holds that odd things are CIA projects and therefore classified, down to a Cheeto shaped like Charizard. (Walkers 04)
  • Kurt never votes: "conflict of interest". (Walkers 05)

docs.title: The Circle Chasers
docs.text:
The Circle Chasers are a group of teenage paranormal hunters who travel in a crop-circle-painted trailer around Dahlonega, Georgia, hunting Bigfoot and UFOs, and who the task force privately calls the Scooby gang.

Type Amateur investigators Aliases Bigfoot hunters; UFO people; Scooby gang; Scooby-Doo gang Members Sloth, Eddie Jones, Vanessa, Delilah, Harvey the Great Dane Status Active (as of Appalachia 07) First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Chasers are young hunters who travel with a streamlined silver trailer with a crop circle painted on its side, run a bulletin-board service, and film their outings with an expensive home video camera. They triangulated the Bigfoot sightings: recent ones in town, including the newspaper photo, and older ones near Auraria around when the boy vanished, which put the search zone in between (Appalachia 01). The team treats them as a Scooby-Doo parody; their dog is a Great Dane "trained to smell the paranormal", and Appalachia 07 calls them "20% weedier" than the original (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Sloth, said by another Chaser to have been a competitive sharpshooter in his youth. In Appalachia 02 he sides with the werewolf theory.
  • Eddie Jones, who argues that Bigfoot is people going feral in the woods, like domestic pigs gone wild.
  • Vanessa, who argues that Bigfoot is an undiscovered hominid.
  • Delilah, the red-haired member with the big VHS camcorder; the table compares her to Daphne in Appalachia 07.
  • Harvey, an enormous black Great Dane who leaps on Andrew and, in Appalachia 07, is scooped up by him and cradled like a baby.

docs.title: First meeting
docs.text: On the morning of the first day in Dahlonega, the team stopped at the Chasers' trailer on the way to the sheriff's station. Kurt gave them his pager number and warned them about missing people and the "religious weirdos". Andrew felt uneasy at being filmed (Appalachia 01). The Smith Hotel clerk had earlier refused them RV hookups for the trailer and told the team that at least one of them was probably armed and another stoned (Appalachia 01).

docs.title: The rabbit snatch
docs.text: That evening on the trail near Auraria the team ran into the Chasers, who showed them a three-second VHS clip: a rabbit frozen in the trail, then a gray man-sized blur grabs it. Kurt noted everyone's footwear to check against a sneaker print found beside giant footprints (Appalachia 02). After the exploded body and missing boys, Kurt called the Chasers to warn them that disappearances were accelerating, but they had no phone and he could only page them (Appalachia 04), and McManley mentioned teenagers in a van with "a real weird dog" on the hill near the Chewbacca body (Appalachia 06).

docs.title: The tracking device
docs.text: In Appalachia 07 the Chasers run into the Spud Hut lot while the team is at dinner. They explain that they found bear vomit full of blood and a blinking light, show it in their blacklit RV, and describe being chased by a bear "with, like, half a face" (see Half-faced Bear). The device turns out to be a SHA Tracking Device. Huell pays for the group's dinner with cash found in a garbage can; Delilah eats four chicken pot pie spuds (Appalachia 07).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• The group's home is called a trailer in Appalachia 01 and an RV in Appalachia 07; the episodes never say whether these are different vehicles.
  • Harvey says "Woof" after the Chasers' claims in Appalachia 01, a recurring table gag. See Running gags.

docs.title: The cleanup crew
docs.text:
The cleanup crew is an unidentified armed group of soldiers without insignia and heat-suited "volcanologists" with flamethrowers, who converge on the old-town church at the end of The Radford Horror and afterward scrub it of evidence and remove the moth's corpse.

Type Organization (unidentified) Aliases Special forces; volcanologists; soldiers without insignia; flamethrower team; strangers Affiliation Unknown Status Unknown First appearance Radford Horror 07 (cold open)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The group is never named or identified. It consists of two kinds of men: camouflaged, special-forces-looking soldiers with no insignia, and men in metal or reflective "volcanologist" suits who carry flamethrowers, heat-ray flashlights and "shadow" ponchos (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 08). The episodes never say who they work for, or how they knew about the moth when the task force did not.

docs.title: Radford Horror 07
docs.text:
The episode's cold open shows a man in a suit finding the burned ground and ash pile where the party's mountain assailant exploded. He squats and riffles the ashes, lights a cigarette, and waves a team of soldiers and men in reflective volcanologist gear deeper into the woods (Radford Horror 07).

At the end of the church fight, with the team stabilized but badly hurt, Kurt moves to the tree line and sees soldiers without insignia, flanked by metal-suited volcanologists with flamethrowers, heading in his direction. Dante compares their flashlights to the one that set Kurt on fire in an earlier episode (Radford Horror 07).

docs.title: Radford Horror 08
docs.text:
Kurt and the others drag the Biz into the woods before the strangers enter the clearing. They watch the special-forces men gesture at the burning church while the volcanologists circle it and break glass at the back. One stranger notices that the door was barred and orders a search of the surroundings, and Kurt recognizes the sound of flamethrowers (Radford Horror 08).

A searcher carrying one of the strange flashlights and wearing a shadow poncho closes in on the team's hiding place. Kurt kicks him in the groin so that his head bends into spray range, and Andrew fires the church-issued mace. Nothing comes out of the mace; instead the "nothing" passes through the man's head, and he collapses in a grand mal seizure. The team ties him up, strips him of the poncho and takes his flashlight, and the other searchers look in the wrong places, so the team slips away undetected. The tied-up man is not seen again (Radford Horror 08).

After the team is discharged from the hospital, they hike back to the old-town church. It is under police tape and mostly burned. The big stained-glass window has been smashed out, the moth's corpse is gone, and the cascade of gore from the crucifixion sites and the dog collars have been cleaned away. Dante and the others conclude that someone removed the evidence on purpose (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Equipment
docs.text:
• Flamethrowers and heat-suited "volcanologist" outfits (Radford Horror 07).
  • Heat-ray flashlights. Kurt tests one by the river in a welding mask and finds a blinding, unnaturally ultraviolet beam that turns a patch of water to steam (Radford Horror 08).
  • Shadow ponchos: a dark, near-transparent cloth that packs down to almost nothing and passes impact straight through, yet is strong enough to hold a man's weight. Kurt guesses it is some kind of armor (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes never establish who the men work for or why they cleaned the church. The official police story, which blames the cartel, looks like a convenient cover for them, but no character says so.

docs.title: Convoy ambushers
docs.text:
The convoy ambushers are the gunmen who bomb and attack the Russian president's motorcade on the road to Oryol Oblast in Radford Horrors 03. One of them costs the Biz the sight in one eye.

Type Organization (unidentified attackers) Aliases Chechen ambushers; paramilitary attacker; gunman in the wheat Affiliation Unknown; Chechen and Russian voices are heard, and the Biz judges one gunman to be paramilitary Status Unknown; the one gunman seen up close was left badly wounded or dead First appearance Radford Horrors 03

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The group is known only from a single night. They use a bomb car and several carloads of gunmen to ambush the presidential convoy. The Biz recognizes Chechen from his intelligence work and hears both Chechen and Russian voices, but their allegiance is never resolved (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The ambush
docs.text:
The Russian government's guards take the Biz in the rear car of a convoy to look at an "unusual aircraft crash" in Oryol Oblast at the request of the president. In the dark beyond Moscow, an old 1960s Russian-made car rams the president's limousine and explodes, and the guards in the Biz's car bail out. A Read a Bad Situation roll tells the Biz that this is an elaborate ambush with several cars of gunmen, speaking Chechen and Russian, and that the armored limo is damaged but not everyone in it is dead (Radford Horrors 03).

The Biz crawls to the limo, gets the unconscious president out, and flees in the guards' car under heavy fire. He kills the lights and veers into a wheat field, spending Luck to lose the pursuers (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: The gunman in the wheat
docs.text:
In the rain, one attacker follows the car's trail through the wheat with an AK. His tactical gear is mismatched and partly out of date, which looks more paramilitary than military, and the Biz is "maybe 90 percent sure" he is not with the Russians. The gunman kicks the dead guard the Biz had posed outside the car and then peers into the back seat. The Biz circles behind him with a knife in his teeth and, spending Luck, inflicts terrible harm: the blade severs an artery in the neck and the tendons of the gun arm. In the struggle the man jams a finger into the Biz's eye, and the Biz takes one harm and can no longer see out of it. The Biz wrestles the gun away, and the gunman collapses from blood loss and a blow to the head (Radford Horrors 03).

A Russian helicopter then lands, picks up the Biz and the concussed president, and flies them away. The Biz has three Luck left before he is Doomed (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes do not say who sent the ambushers, or whether the attack was tied to the crashed craft the president wanted examined.

docs.text: • Radford Horrors 03

docs.title: The Covenant
docs.text:
The Covenant is a religious community led by the prophet Elijah Ray that occupies the Georgia ghost town of Auraria near Dahlonega, known locally for its fermented peach preserves, a hallucinogenic peach drink and red-clay river baptisms.

Type Religious community / cult Aliases Auraria religious community; the cult; Auraria folks Leader Elijah Ray Base Auraria, Georgia Status Active; in a land dispute (as of Appalachia 04) First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Smith Hotel clerk in Dahlonega describes Auraria as a little gold-rush mining town taken over by "some religious folks" about ten years earlier. The members wear long dresses and robes, live in tents, have no electricity or phones, and talk about the end of the world. Morning glories grow everywhere. He advises the team not to stay there after dark (Appalachia 01). The team finds a sign reading "Welcome to the Covenant. Try our peaches," a pre-Civil War church, glowing white tents, and robed members who ignore them (Appalachia 02).

The membership is a couple of hundred at most, possibly under a hundred. Locals call them the "heebie-jeebies", but the Covenant is isolated rather than closed and allows outsiders to speak to its members (Appalachia 02). For their beliefs see Covenant Beliefs.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Peach products. The members grow peaches, potatoes and morning glories, make preserves and quilts, and run stills. The preserves are fermented and malty (see Covenant Peach Preserves). A ritual peach drink with a hallucinogenic fungus gives visions, and Primenthol Greengrass warns the team never to take a vision quest (Appalachia 02).
  • Baptism. New members are submerged in a red-clay river by Elijah Ray after drinking a jar of dark liquid with peaches floating in it, as the cold open of Appalachia 04 shows with the vacuum salesman Jeremy (Appalachia 04).
  • Diet and schooling. The members do not eat meat. Mother Dahlia Riversand runs a one-room schoolhouse teaching Latin and times tables, with Elijah Ray teaching comparative religion and said to have taught at Harvard (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Elijah Ray, the prophet. Prim describes him as "pretty nice guy. For a bigamist"; a prophetic dream and a TV report of a shooting star led him to move the congregation to Auraria (Appalachia 02).
  • Mother Dahlia Riversand, the elder.
  • Willow Greengrass, who vanished.
  • Clover, a shy young woman, and River, Willow's close friend, who runs the stills (Appalachia 04).
  • Angie, Elijah Ray's youngest wife, mentioned by Prim.
  • Jeremy, a recovering Quaalude addict being baptized.

docs.title: The disappearance
docs.text: The team's first contact with the Covenant comes through Willow's disappearance. Sheriff Burke thinks she left the cult, and Prim is certain she would have come to her sister. The team does not approach the members on its first visit to Auraria, but returns to question them in Appalachia 04 (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 04).

docs.title: The Covenant in Appalachia 04
docs.text:
The Covenant is economically desperate. Dahlia and River explain that "corporate goons" arrived about a year earlier with paperwork claiming the land and threatening eviction. Elijah Ray calls it a lie and says the men are agents of Satan, and the orchard deal and the sale of preserves and quilts are meant to fund a lawyer. The eviction letters name only a law firm, Jackson and Lee's, and not the client. Dahlia says the river water has been boiled and treated with chlorine tablets for about a year after intestinal trouble; one member lost two toes to an infected toenail. Clover says the members often get yeast infections from bathing in the river, "a lot of runoff from the Spud Hut plant", and that the Covenant is "getting a boiler" (Appalachia 04). See The Land Dispute and Spud Hut.

Kurt, Huell and Andrew do not meet Elijah Ray. Andrew says he has an idea for meeting him "but not for today", and the team leaves without stopping Jeremy's baptism (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: Suspicion
docs.text: When the team finds a creature in the Consolidated Gold Mine, Andrew suggests a cult could keep a mine secret, and the sheriff's face darkens. In the same episode a message from Big Bill reminded the team to keep everything by the book because of Ruby Ridge, Marblehead and the fact that "there is a cult involved in this one" (Appalachia 03). The Covenant is never shown to be involved with the mining or the ape-men, and the later episodes do not return to it.

docs.title: Dahlonega Sheriff's Department
docs.text:
The Dahlonega Sheriff's Department is the small local law-enforcement agency, led by Sheriff Carter Burke, that investigates the disappearances in and around Dahlonega, Georgia and works alongside the task force in The Things in Appalachia.

Type Local law enforcement Aliases Dahlonega Sheriff's Office; sheriff's department Leader Sheriff Carter Burke Base Dahlonega Sheriff's Station Status Active (as of Appalachia 09) First appearance Appalachia 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
By Burke's own count the department is a secretary, two deputies and temporary staff. The station is a small building with an evidence locker, and Burke's office has animal heads and guns on the wall (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 04). The older woman at the front desk fetches Burke from the restroom, where he has IBS, on the team's first visit. The only phone line fit for a private call is in the break room, which Burke clears for the call with the missing boy's mother (Appalachia 04).

One deputy, String Bean, is absent and staying with family because of personal troubles; his spare uniform becomes Andrew's disguise (Appalachia 08). The department also leaks. The Spud Hut investigator says he has a friend at the sheriff's office who called to tell him about the truck crash, and guesses that the reporters have the same friend: "She talks to people" (Appalachia 08).

docs.title: The missing persons case
docs.text:
Burke tells the team that the manhunt for Gene Cartwright found little and that he suspects coyotes, a bear or a drifter. He thinks Willow Greengrass simply left the Covenant, and he shows the only evidence, a bag of peaches, in the evidence locker (Appalachia 01). Burke admits his deputies should have looked up when they searched the field where Gene vanished, and apologizes for volunteers who trampled the scene (Appalachia 02).

When a German boy, Frederick, vanishes in the Consolidated Gold Mine, the department mobilizes deputies and volunteers. The sheriff learns Kurt has spelunking experience and puts him in charge of the team's safety underground (Appalachia 03).

docs.title: Overwhelmed
docs.text: By Appalachia 04 Burke tells the team there are five missing people in two days, and that the FBI arrived before it was clear there were even two. He has asked the Georgia State Police for two deputies plus temporary staff and asks the team to call them too. Kurt's pitch of a curfew and a "truth-adjacent" cover story about a fatal tick-borne disease gets a squint; his line "If we were a beach town, I would close the beach" sums up the problem of keeping people out of the woods (Appalachia 04).

docs.title: The body on Comstock's land
docs.text: The sheriff, not named in that episode, brings Frotter Comstock to the team's hotel to report a dead Bigfoot, and scolds Andrew that a man is dead and every death deserves gravity. He later drives Comstock away in the squad car (Appalachia 06). See Troy Cleaver.

docs.title: The crash and the Spud Hut
docs.text: The sheriff radios in the truck accident on the freeway, leads the team through the evidence, slits a bag labelled "Potatoes" to show it holds dirt, and relays gossip from a state police friend about the Clinton scandal (Appalachia 07). He then leads the team to the Spud Hut plant, swears Andrew in as a deputy to cancel the penalty for looking like a federal agent, and talks the receptionist into opening the door. During the ape-man fight he screams continuously and dives through the "break room" door when the Claymore appears (Appalachia 08).

docs.title: Underground
docs.text: Burke accompanies the team into the sub-basement, where he screams until Kurt quiets him. He believes the party are Men in Black responsible for the ape-men, the explosions and the "spying on the presidential candidates". He takes some gold "to sort out the legality later" and ends the recorded arc hugging a tree (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: EPA/USGS survey team
docs.text:
The EPA/USGS survey team is the eight-person field team that was sent to Marblehead after the offshore explosion, was threatened by town officials, and vanished before the task force arrived in The Summer Service.

Type Organization (government field team) Aliases Missing EPA scientists; the previous team; the scientists; field team Affiliation EPA and U.S. Geological Survey Members Eight unnamed scientists Status Missing, then found alive in an unrecorded session (as of Summer Service 06) First appearance Radford Horror 08

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: About a month before the task force's case begins, an unexplained explosion blew out windows in Marblehead and made many townspeople sick; see The Marblehead explosion. The EPA and the U.S. Geological Survey sent a field team to find out what happened, out of concern about a seabed gas leak. After the first couple of days none of the team was heard from again. The case file that Andrew Howard receives at the end of The Radford Horror lists eight missing people and says that local law enforcement has been unresponsive "suspiciously so" (Radford Horror 08). No member is ever named.

docs.title: Before the task force
docs.text: The team interviewed locals made ill by the explosion and judged their symptoms inconsistent with natural-gas poisoning: they tested for carbon monoxide and methane and found neither. Their journal in the hotel box was mostly empty (Radford Horror 08). In Summer Service 01, the field notes list contacts: the Cartwright family, Ma Gramoire, Lana Scott and Denver O'Donnell. The last entry says they were going to meet town leaders (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Arrival
docs.text: The team had stayed at the Ram and Arms Inn. The innkeeper tells the task force that "fellas from the government" were there about a week earlier, and sends up the team's belongings: suitcases, clothes, IDs, technical manuals, sampling equipment and wallets (Radford Horror 08); see Survey team's field notes. In the first recorded Marblehead session, the Scott family say the scientists took blood samples from their daughter Lena after she recovered from the hospital, promised to follow up and were never heard from again (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: The lighthouse
docs.text: In Summer Service 03, Big Bill orders the team to recover the missing scientists before the National Guard arrives, since the Guard's arrival could ruin any chance of finding them alive. Andre says the scientists have been missing "coming up on two weeks," and Andrew tells the others he thinks Big Bill is an idiot for believing they might be alive. Ma Gramoire tells the team the scientists said they were going to check out the lighthouse after talking to the Board of Selectmen. In its basement the team finds blood-stained rope cut into two- or three-foot lengths, two teeth, two bloodied chairs and an EPA field journal. Luminol shows blood that someone cleaned with bleach, so someone was beaten in a chair and taken elsewhere. The journal concludes that the poisonings are some sort of nerve agent, describes unknown and distorted fish species and normal-looking fish packed with worms but still alive, and records that the scientists were threatened by the mayor and senior officials after going before the selectmen. The last entry says they were going to check the lighthouse (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: The selectmen's account
docs.text: When asked, the mayor says the scientists came to the board and left suddenly just over a week earlier, saying they might return to Washington for resources, and that their accusation that runoff was poisoning the fish "was not very well received here." The party suspects that he is lying; Kurt Larson worries that if the scientists are alive, drawing attention to them might get them killed (Summer Service 04). In Summer Service 05, Kurt asks Madeline Weathers to hold off burning the church because kidnapped scientists might still be inside (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Found
docs.text:
In the finale Andrew tells the radio contact, "we found our research guys. They were alive," distinguishing them from the contact's own dead "advanced team." This is the only mention of the rescue; it happened in an unrecorded session between Summer Service 05 and 06 (Summer Service 06).

Unrecorded session

How and where the scientists were found is known only from this passing line. See Lost episodes.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The length of the team's absence is stated differently at different points: about four days in the Radford Horror 08 briefing, nearly two weeks in Summer Service 03, and just over a week in the mayor's account.
