docs.title: FBI Salt Lake City field office
docs.text:
The FBI Salt Lake City field office is the medium-sized local Bureau office where the task force picks up the case file on Sherman Ranch before heading to Ballard.

Type Organization (FBI field office) Aliases Salt Lake City field office Parent agency FBI Members Carl Gardner; Philip Bishop; Shelly (staff); an unnamed secretary Status Last visited in Walkers 02; mentioned in Walkers 03 First appearance Walkers 02

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The office is medium-sized compared with the one in D.C. Big Bill set one condition for the Utah trip: stop here for case files on earlier reports from the area, and work with the local FBI (Walkers 02). The team flew in, picked up a rented 1990 Plymouth Voyager at the airport and drove to the office; the field office itself lent them nothing. A secretary confirmed that Big Bill had phoned ahead and sent them to a second-floor conference room. See Plymouth Voyager.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Carl Gardner. Short, heavy and hearty, with a big personality. He thumps shoulders, calls people "son", prefers Leno to Letterman, dislikes Clinton, and recognized Dick Baxter as "the fella who spied on Clinton". He had heard of Kurt's CIA branch, UTAW, as the "explode the cigars" outfit.
  • Philip Bishop. Gardner's tall, thin, silent partner. He stiffened at Huell's "So, Mormons, am I right?" and four minutes of sweaty silence followed.
  • Shelly. Staff voice on the intercom, called when Gardner needs another drinking-fountain test kit.

docs.title: The briefing (Walkers 02)
docs.text:
Gardner's rundown covered four earlier reports: a Native American former Army Ranger on the ranch who said he shot a snooper by the barn (no physical evidence), a young woman who saw her dead mother (they checked for twins), cattle mutilation blamed on lightning, and informal reports of lights and lost time that Gardner put down to drinking (Walkers 02). He added that "the billionaire" tenant "skeeves me the hell out", and after stepping out to find the name said it was Robert Bigelow, a real estate baron whose security man had fired the shot. He gave the team a copy of the case file, to be checked back in when they leave.

The conference-room corkboard of yarn and Post-its was not about the ranch. It concerned a separate local case, "a drinking fountain pervert", over live sperm in public water. Gardner offered tips: Bigelow's Budget Suites of America hotels, a "friend of Bonaparte" discount at a nearby gas station, and Utah food such as funeral potatoes, dirty soda and Jell-O salad. See Ballard water contamination.

docs.title: Later mentions (Walkers 03)
docs.text: In Walkers 03 Asked whether the task force has "men on" the town's water problem, Dante recalls that the FBI does: "we talked to the guys that were investigating; that was their little corkboard with the thread and whatnot."

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The table ran a gag about dentists' conferences bumping the team out of hotels, and Dante (as Kurt) asked before the meeting whether the agents were "a bunch of narcs" (Walkers 02).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 02
  • Walkers 03 (mentioned)

docs.title: FBI
docs.text:
The FBI (Federal Bureau of Investigation) is the parent agency of the Paranatural Incident Task Force and the employer of three of its four investigators.

Type Organization (U.S. federal agency) Aliases the Bureau; Federal Bureau of Investigation Headquarters Washington, D.C. Director William S. Sessions (to April 1993); Rudy Giuliani (from April 1993) Status Active First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The Bureau of the campaign is a post-Cold War agency shedding people. In spring 1992 its counterintelligence and counterterrorism work is being downsized ("The Soviets are gone. The Chinese are making radios for us. We beat the evil empire"), and the new presidential task force is where four surplus careers are parked. (Radford Horror 01)

To the team in the field the FBI is mostly a set of services at the other end of a payphone: couriers who bring the case files, a switchboard, a secretary pool that trades gossip, a lab that takes days, translators, and an accounts office that reimburses motel rooms and pays for wrecked cars. It is also the cover. The agents present themselves as ordinary FBI men looking into missing persons, and "We're the FBI" is the team's answer to most obstacles, including Kurt, who is not. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 03, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 04)

Institutionally it treats the task force as a joke, then as an asset, then as a scandal. (Radford Horror 01, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 07, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Structure
docs.text:
• Director. William S. Sessions is Director until April 1993, when President Ross Perot fires him, with no transition, for standing by the task force's Radford reports, and installs Rudy Giuliani the same morning. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)
  • Deputy Director. Floyd Clark, the link between Big Bill and the President, and at one point the rumored replacement for Sessions. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03, Roulet Estate 03)
  • Foreign Influence Task Force. Big Bill's umbrella organization, which owns the paranatural unit because alien visitations were determined to be "foreign by definition". (Summer Service 03)
  • Counterintelligence. The Biz's old section. In June 1992 one of its agents watches the Biz from a rooftop in Marblehead: he is a person of interest, vulnerable to leverage because of money problems. Kurt sends the watcher away and keeps it from the Biz. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 01)
  • Counterterrorism Task Force. Where Kurt was on loan from the CIA before the downsizing. (Radford Horror 01)
  • Salt Lake City field office. A medium-sized office whose agents, Carl Gardner and Philip Bishop, hand the team the Ballard file. (Walkers 02)
  • Records, the lab, counsel. Records refuses the boxes left in the barbershop and later takes in Diane; the lab processes the team's samples; FBI counsel spends four hours debriefing Daniel Webster after the fence incident. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 06, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 03)
  • Quantico. Where Kurt lectures young agents on breaching in spring 1993. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Andrew Howard, Dick "The Biz" Baxter and Huell Kendrick, the task force's agents. Kurt Larson is a CIA consultant attached to them, not an FBI agent.
  • Big Bill, their superior, forced out by Perot.
  • Diane, the task force secretary.
  • Donald McManley, forensic scientist.
  • Daniel Webster, Special Agent, the team's minder in 1993.
  • Rudy Giuliani, Director from April 1993.
  • Carl Gardner of the Salt Lake City office.
  • The five agents of the missing FBI task force.
  • Minor figures: Agent Cooper, who clears boxes from the barbershop; the courier; the Biz's coworkers Toby and Donner; and Todd, Kurt's acquaintance at headquarters. See Minor characters: Radford.

(Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03, Walkers 02, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

docs.title: 1992: the task force years
docs.text:
The Bureau houses the new unit in a derelict barbershop it had been using for document storage and sends it to Radford. Sheriff Frank Roosevelt, who has never dealt with the FBI, has his deputy phone Washington to check their identification. (Radford Horror 01)

At Marblehead the Bureau is the team's lifeline. Big Bill takes the reports to the Oval Office, retasks a Navy submarine and calls out the National Guard; when he cannot be reached, the switchboard reports the Guard's delay and an intercepted shipment of illegal M16s bound for the town, and says it cannot send a helicopter. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05)

After Marblehead, Andre says, "the rest of the FBI has finally kind of stopped bullying you guys". That lasts until October, when the Georgia State Police announce that the FBI is surveilling candidate Bill Clinton. The Bureau's public position is that it had nothing to do with it. The original plan was for a representative with formal public-relations credentials to do the news tour; instead it coached the Biz and sent him onto David Letterman's program, and afterwards housed him in a safe house. See Clinton Surveillance Scandal. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 07, Walkers 01, Walkers 02)

In Utah the FBI pays for the flights, the rental car and the Biz's gold fillings, and the team spends the last days of the case unable to reach it at all. (Walkers 01, Walkers 03, Walkers 07, Walkers 08)

docs.title: 1993: after the task force
docs.text:
With the unit disbanded, the Bureau keeps Andrew on a desk in New York working the World Trade Center bombing. He cannot be dismissed because his misdeeds are buried in classified cover-ups, and lower-level offices run betting pools on whether he is blackmailing Director Sessions or sleeping with him. Huell draws workers' compensation. The Biz's file shows a granted six-month personal leave for a "family emergency" and a stack of unanswered reminders. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)

Kurt, visiting headquarters in April, finds the building as tense as it was after Iran-Contra. Sessions has been fired three hours earlier. Giuliani recalls the old team as consultants under Webster, to find Perot's missing agents in Radford and to produce an "acceptable fact pattern". (Radford Horrors 01)

The first week in Radford brings an expected Bivens lawsuit over the Safe Environment Fund fence, a retroactive warrant, and a reprimand for Webster. Giuliani wants the missing agents found within 24 hours, dead or alive. (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

Quote

"That seems really reckless to me, Webster, running lunatics in the field." (Andre as Giuliani, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Rules and customs
docs.text:
• Domestically, the FBI's jurisdiction outranks the NSA's, according to Kurt. (Radford Horror 04)
  • Agents can commandeer vehicles in an emergency, at the risk of being chewed out. (Radford Horror 03)
  • The 48-hour hold rule applies to the team as to any other agents. (Summer Service 04)
  • "The chocolate milk in the canteen is not very good, and nobody likes it at the FBI": a fact offered by the Counterintelligence watcher at Marblehead as proof that he is genuine. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• When the Biz phones for backup from Rhode Island in January 1993 and mentions his task force, the FBI operator is "not familiar" with it. (Roulet Estate 02)
  • Ezra, during the Radford Horrors premiere, said he had forgotten there were ever any other agents involved in the team's cases. Andre: "There weren't." (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Zack's summary of the job: "One of the main things you do as the FBI is scrape white powders into baggies." (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
The FBI figures in every canon session as the team's employer. Its headquarters, officials or offices appear directly in:

  • Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 08
  • Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05
  • Appalachia 01, Appalachia 07
  • Walkers 01, Walkers 02
  • Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03
  • Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Foreign Influence Task Force
docs.text:
The Foreign Influence Task Force is the FBI task force headed by Big Bill Nelson, which sits above the player characters' own unit in the chain of command and treats alien visitation as "foreign by definition."

Type Organization (FBI task force) Aliases None Affiliation FBI Leader Big Bill (Big Bill Nelson) Status Active (as of Summer Service 03) First appearance Summer Service 03

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: In Summer Service 03 Andre spells out the chain of command, which he calls unusual. Andrew Howard reports to Big Bill, "who's the head of the Foreign Influence Task Force, since it was determined that alien visitations are foreign by definition." Nelson reports to Floyd Clark, the FBI's deputy director, and Clark reports to George H. W. Bush. Everything in the team's reports is classified under the code word SKYHOOK. Zack asks whether Clark is "just like the contemporary Hoover"; Andre says he is not the director, but is the deputy director. Big Bill has a lot of sway within the FBI, and if he escalates a request to Clark, that carries weight across the government (Summer Service 03). The player characters' own unit is the Paranatural Incident Task Force.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Big Bill: head. He answers calls with "Hello, this is Big Bill Nelson. What can I do for you?" and, when Andrew says it feels weird to call him Big Bill, tells him "Sir's fine" (Summer Service 03).
  • Floyd Clark: FBI deputy director above Nelson, mentioned only (Summer Service 03).
  • Big Bill's secretary: an unnamed man who takes Kurt Larson's request to have Ma Gramoire's National Guard son Jordan assigned to the deployment (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: History
docs.text: During the Marblehead case Andrew briefs Big Bill on the dive, the stealth wreck with a bite out of it and the humming craft, and adds the cult, the spherical diamonds and the communion wine. Big Bill says there is "a serious counterintelligence situation ongoing" and that the national security concerns come first. He says he will take it to the Oval Office and try to retask national security assets to look at the wreck with better instruments, and he orders the team to find the missing scientists before the National Guard arrives (Summer Service 03). In later sessions he sends the Guard, retasks a Los Angeles-class submarine, and agrees on the "terrorists" cover story, although those sessions do not name the task force (Summer Service 04; Summer Service 06).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The name Foreign Influence Task Force is given only in Summer Service 03. It is the umbrella organization over the Paranatural Incident Task Force, which is Andrew's unit inside it; Andre calls it "the umbrella organization of the task force" in Appalachia 07. (Summer Service 03, Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 03

docs.title: Fox 5 Atlanta
docs.text:
Fox 5 Atlanta is the Atlanta television station whose news crew covers the story of the FBI allegedly spying on Bill Clinton, and whose camera catches Andrew Howard outside the Spud Hut plant in Dahlonega, Georgia.

Type Television station / news crew Aliases Fox 5 news crew; Fox 5 reporters Status Active (as of Appalachia 08) First appearance Appalachia 08

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: A Fox 5 van and camera crew wait in the parking lot of the Spud Hut corporate plant when the task force arrives. The crew is there over the truck accident and the Clinton surveillance story, which a state police press conference had made public (Appalachia 08). See Georgia State Police and Clinton Surveillance Scandal.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Kurt's plan was for the team to enter the plant disguised as reporters, with the sheriff as escort, while Andrew wore a borrowed deputy's uniform. The Fox 5 crew immediately recognizes "Andrew Howard with the FBI", declares everyone an FBI agent, and a reporter asks Andrew on live TV about the "Bill Clinton wiretap" and whether it is "the next Watergate". Andrew says "Nothing," then "Thank you for your time," and power-walks to the door. At the locked door, once the receptionist has let them in, he turns back and says sweatily, "Thank you for your time again". Andre says the clip of that second "Thank you for your time" plays on the news about every ten minutes for the rest of the day (Appalachia 08).

The sheriff keeps the reporters outside, and the receptionist locks the door behind the team. Andrew's main worry afterward is the next phone call from Big Bill (Appalachia 08).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: The players riff on the clip: they joke that remixes of "Thank you for your time" would become a trip-hop or techno track (Appalachia 08).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Appalachia 08

docs.title: Russian Government / FSB
docs.text:
The Russian Government / FSB is the Russian state apparatus that abducts Dick "The Biz" Baxter from his hospital bed, holds him at the Vorkuta labor camp and flies him to Moscow to be questioned by Boris Yeltsin.

Type Government / intelligence service Aliases FSB; the Russians Leader Boris Yeltsin (President) Base Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp; Moscow First appearance Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: After the Brooks Pharmacy siege, the Biz is wounded and taken to a hospital, and in the epilogue of Roulet Estate 03 he vanishes from it. Ezra, deciding what becomes of the Biz after the task force is disbanded, suggests that this is the time for "consequences for fucking up," and Andre rules that he was "abducted and still in custody." The rest of the task force knows only that the Biz disappeared from the hospital, and assumes he simply ran off. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: History
docs.text:
• Vorkuta. The Biz is held in a freezing stone cell at the Vorkuta Corrective Labor Camp, a sign outside giving the date "abandoned since 1962". The cell has a barred window and a slot in the door through which bread is pushed. His leg was patched up at the best hospital in Russia before the torture began. About two weeks after the guards stopped beating him with any enthusiasm and stopped interrogating him, he passes the time by making up increasingly unhinged sea shanties and talking to a cockroach. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • The officer. A new, senior-looking man with a mustache, steel eyes and a red, slightly runny nose looks through the slot. The Biz greets him in polite Russian ("Dobro pozhalovat'. Zakhodite, pozhaluysta."). The officer turns to one of the guards and orders, in a line subtitled "Get this man on a plane." (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Moscow. After a better shower than his processing one, the Biz flies first class, handcuffed beside an FSB officer who eats his steak but lets him keep the rest of the meal. They land and drive in an FSB car to the former Soviet Parliament building, where he is handcuffed to a chair by both hands and an ankle. Yeltsin sits across from him, offers a Cuban cigar, cuts the end off, lights it for him with a small silver lighter and says, "Tell me everything you know about the humanists." (Roulet Estate 03)

Meanwhile, when Diane phones Andrew in New York to ask after everyone, he says he hopes the Biz is not "ruining another presidential election," and suggests the US government may simply have grown tired of him. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Who "the humanists" are; nothing else is said about them.
  • How the Biz was taken out of the country and whether Yeltsin's government acted on its own initiative.
  • What happens to the Biz after this scene. Russian government figures appear again in later arcs; see Russian government and The Radford Horrors.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Georgia State Police
docs.text:
The Georgia State Police is the state agency that Sheriff Burke calls in to help with the Dahlonega disappearances, and that then finds a pair of night-vision goggles outside the task force's hotel, holds a press conference accusing the FBI of spying on Bill Clinton, and leaks the Biz's name.

Type State law enforcement Aliases State police Status Active (as of Walkers 01) First appearance Appalachia 04 (requested by Burke)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The state police first appear as help that Sheriff Carter Burke has requested: two deputies plus temporary staff. He asks the team to call them too, and Huell agrees (Appalachia 04). Within days they become the task force's main public enemy.

docs.title: The night-vision headset
docs.text:
The cold open of Appalachia 06 shows tired state police taking prints and swabs among bushes ringed with caution tape outside the team's hotel. An officer emerges with a night-vision headset and says, "Bag it and tag it, the Secret Service fellows I want to take a look at that." The goggles belonged to the Biz and were connected to his solo adventure the previous night, which was played out privately between Ezra and Andre in the unrecorded Appalachia 05 (Appalachia 06). See The Biz's Night-vision Goggles.

Unrecorded session

What happened in the Biz's night is known only through its consequences, which Andre recapped in Appalachia 06: the Biz came back wearing his clothes from the night before with a badly twisted ankle, the hotel door next to the team's room had been broken down, and the goggles were found in the bushes.

docs.title: The press conference
docs.text:
By Appalachia 07 a state police official has held a press conference claiming the FBI is in Dahlonega surveilling presidential candidate Bill Clinton, with fingerprints from something "recovered from the scene" matching an unnamed FBI agent. McManley passes on the news, and Kurt does not know who Clinton is, and Andre scolds the table that it is October 1992. The sheriff later relays gossip from a state police friend that the Secret Service tipped them off, that they found surveillance equipment, and that its prints matched an employee in the FBI database (Appalachia 07). See Clinton Surveillance Scandal.

Andrew, ordered by Big Bill to keep silent, spends the next sessions avoiding reporters; the Fox 5 crew at the plant catches him on camera (Appalachia 08). See Fox 5 Atlanta.

docs.title: The aftermath
docs.text:
In the epilogue, the Biz appears on Late Night with David Letterman to defend himself. Letterman notes that the state police say they found the goggles in a rose bush and still have not returned them; the Biz says the goggles were stolen by the state police and, of the state police, that "they probably can't afford 'em". He accuses them of endangering him and the case by releasing his name, and describes being yelled at in public while housed in an FBI-provided hotel. The Letterman show bills him as "the most hated cop in America" (Walkers 01).

In the sub-basement beneath the Spud Hut, the Biz says "I wish the state police creeps would come down here. This is way weirder than Bill Clinton." (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: The item is a "night vision headset" in Appalachia 06 and "night vision goggles" in the Letterman interview, where Ezra specifies a night-vision monocular. At the table, Ezra looked up the PVS-7 and put its price at roughly $4,500 (Walkers 01).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 04
  • Appalachia 06
  • Appalachia 07
  • Appalachia 09 (mentioned)
  • Walkers 01

docs.title: Gray van crew
docs.text:
The gray van crew is a five-man paramilitary-style team that drives gray vans around Radford, abducts people, scrubs crime scenes of evidence, and bags the creature in the Douglas Pinball Emporium. Their employer is unknown.

Type Organization (unidentified) Aliases Paramilitary cleanup; pinball arcade kidnappers Affiliation Unknown; the team suspects the Safe Environment Fund Status Active (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horrors 03 (the arcade abduction, cold open)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The crew first appears as the unseen force behind the abduction of the arcade's overnight worker Elizabeth George. The cold open of Radford Horrors 03 shows muffled thrashing, the sound of a Taser, a woman's limp arm and a man in a black balaclava carrying her off. When the team investigates the Douglas Pinball Emporium, they find a broken Taser tine with blood, a smear of blood on a machine corner, a missing first-aid kit and hand towels, and signs of recent cleaning. The security tape has been swapped, and the back fence has been cut and repaired (Radford Horrors 03). The kidnappers are evidently professionals.

docs.title: The diner footage
docs.text:
In Radford Horrors 04 the waitress at the Lonely Mountain Diner gets her camera working, and its footage shows the raid on the emporium across the street at about four or five in the morning. A gray van pulls up and five men hop out: one with long brown hair in a ponytail, the others with military haircuts, several with their faces covered. A shadow that moves wrongly shows in the emporium window. One man opens the lock with what could be a bump key, there is a scuffle inside, and a few minutes later three of the men carry two bags to the van. The others follow with equipment, and the van leaves (Radford Horrors 04).

Kurt's Investigate a Mystery roll reads this as an organized cleanup team, more paramilitary than military. The ponytailed man moves like an action movie rather than a real combat veteran, and Andre likens him to a LARPer. The shadow in the window was not human and seemed to be trying to get out as the door opened (Radford Horrors 04). It is the emporium intruder.

docs.title: Earlier activity
docs.text:
• The waitress says she has seen the gray vans for a couple of months, around the time of the "right to roam" dispute over the woods, and that several vans were also parked around the Ferry Lodge during the IRS raid. Kurt wonders whether they are associated with the Safe Environment Fund (Radford Horrors 04).
  • Harold, the Blockbuster clerk, saw a homeless man dragged into a van by a man with a ponytail a month and a half to two months earlier; the man later reappeared. Andre confirms that this matches Billy Thornton, who had complained to the team about being abducted (Radford Horrors 04).
  • Sheriff Molly Underhill has seen gray vans around town and assumed they belonged to the construction work (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The employer is never established. The team suspects the Safe Environment Fund because the vans appeared when it did, and Daniel Webster passes that suspicion to FBI Director Rudy Giuliani, who says he will put a researcher on it (Radford Horrors 04). It is not confirmed on screen that the same crew took Elizabeth George.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Ponytails become a running gag after Billy Thornton's story of being "kidnapped by chimps and molested by John Travolta." It culminates in Zack asking, "Does she have a ponytail?" about a customer Harold describes (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horrors 03
  • Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Hazmat cleanup teams
docs.text:
The hazmat cleanup teams are dozens of unidentified hazmat-suited personnel who appear under silent black triangular craft at the end of The Walkers in Skin to load and clear bodies after the community center collapses.

Type Organization (unidentified) Aliases hazmat teams Affiliation Unknown Status Unknown First appearance Walkers 09

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: When the team came out of the shaft, white powder had fallen like snow and everyone outside was on the ground, unconscious. Black craft swooped overhead, and the killdozer hung in a tree as the community center slid into a sinkhole. As the team drove away in a Humvee, still naked, they saw dozens of people in hazmat suits loading up and cleaning up the bodies. Andrew Howard took a few dozen blurry Polaroids of the hazmat crews with several indistinct black aircraft circling overhead. Zack asked whether the craft were triangular, and Andre said yes (Walkers 09). See Black triangular craft.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Using the longer-range radio in an armored personnel carrier, Kurt Larson reported to the National Guard outpost in Salt Lake City that there was a cover-up the team had not caused: hazmat teams and unidentified craft kidnapping personnel in addition to the victims, and the area drug-seeded to knock everyone out. Huell said it would be in his report (Walkers 09).

The Roulet Estate arc refers back to Utah. In the opening scene, CDC-style personnel in hazmat suits bring casualties into a medical tent at the edge of Roosevelt, and Andre notes that searchers had found no sign of "the hazmat troops that you people saw". The cover story given for the disaster was that a cult had built a compound under the community center and embezzled funds for an uprising, ending in a Jonestown-style mass killing. Later in the arc, Rita (as Andrew) wonders aloud whether the team was lured out by "whoever did the cleanup after in Utah" (Roulet Estate 01). Andrew also carries three Polaroids from Ballard.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Who commands the teams, and whether they are linked to the black craft.
  • Who spread the powder.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Walkers 09
  • Roulet Estate 01 (mentioned)

docs.title: IRS Criminal Investigations
docs.text:
IRS Criminal Investigations (IRS CI) is the federal tax-enforcement unit whose SWAT-style team raids the Ferry Lodge in The Radford Horrors at the end of an eight-month fraud investigation, just as the task force arrives to check in.

Type Government agency (federal) Aliases IRS agents Leader An unnamed, exasperated agent who pulls off his helmet Status Active; shut down the Ferry Lodge (as of Radford Horrors 02) First appearance Radford Horrors 02

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The team is a SWAT-style unit led by an unnamed agent. Its eight-month fraud investigation targets the Ferry Lodge and its new management, whom locals describe as arriving four or five months earlier and being "snooty" and secretive, bringing in their own staff and refusing to hire locals. The episodes never say what the fraud was (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The white van and the watchers
docs.text:
When the task force reaches Radford in Radford Horrors 02, Kurt notices that the Ferry Lodge parking lot is half empty. He spots a nondescript white van across the street and two men standing on street corners doing nothing "in a way that is very specific," whom he reads as relatively inexperienced field agents. The team notes the van's license plate, and it circles the block as they walk in (Radford Horrors 02).

After the raid, Kurt asks an IRS agent at the door whether the van and watchers were his, and the agent confirms it. Kurt critiques the surveillance: "No one ever stands somewhere doing nothing." When Kurt mentions a molestation complaint from a homeless man, the agent recognizes him and says "he talked to us too." The man is Billy Thornton (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The Ferry Lodge raid
docs.text:
The SWAT team storms in just as the desk clerk hands the agents their keys. Kurt goes prone and draws, then pulls the pin on a grenade and holds it as a dead man's switch, and a Manipulate Someone roll keeps him from being shot. The raiders announce themselves as "IRS Criminal Investigations" and demand to know who the task force is. Daniel Webster sides with the raiders and vaults the counter to tackle the clerk. She runs to the back room, shreds documents and tips over file cabinets, setting them on fire. Kurt tosses a stapler to fake a grenade throw and she sprints out; Andrew catches her with Protect Someone and hands her to Webster (Radford Horrors 02).

The IRS puts out the fire, pulls paperwork from the shredder and makes arrests. The leader pulls off his helmet and demands to know why the team has a grenade; Kurt calls it "kind of a fidget." Andrew tells him the team's presence is unrelated, since there are only two places to stay in town and the other is full of bedbugs. The team is escorted out while the lodge is locked down, the clerk is handcuffed and interrogated by four agents, and Kurt drops a caltrop in front of an IRS vehicle (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Later
docs.text: The diner waitress mentions that gray vans were crowded around the lodge during the raid (Radford Horrors 04). The IRS team does not reappear after the raid, and it is never established whether the fraud is tied to the Safe Environment Fund.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The spear gun, grenade and caltrops Kurt carries in this episode all get used by the end of it (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Radford Horrors 02

docs.title: Jan's Conspiracy
docs.text:
Jan's Conspiracy was the ring, led by Spud Hut manager Jan Martense, that mined gold with the labor of captive ape-men beneath Dahlonega, Georgia, and used fake Bigfoot sightings as cover.

Type Criminal conspiracy Aliases The gold-mining ring Leader Jan Martense Base Spud Hut Georgia Regional Distribution Center and the Dahlonega Gold Mines Status Collapsed; Jan is in CIA custody (as of Walkers 01) First named Appalachia 09

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In Appalachia 09, Clive, the large-animal handler, described the conspiracy as five people: Jan, Clive himself, a mercenary who melted the gold down, and two bodyguards ("Five was the biggest conspiracy you could possibly keep"). Its goal was at least $100 million in gold, dug by a "shift" of ape-men kept docile with ketamine. Clive said Jan insisted on that figure and that he himself would have settled for one or two million (Appalachia 09). The Spud Hut distribution center served as the front, and its trucks hauled the dirt away.

The ring also manufactured the Bigfoot hoax. Clive explained that some of the workers had escaped and been seen, and that Jan staged fake sightings to discredit the real ones (Appalachia 09).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Jan Martense, the Spud Hut manager and head of the operation. His one condition of employment, as Clive tells it, was "Don't ask questions about the ape-men."
  • Clive, the large-animal handler who trained the ape-men for a promised third of the gold. He survived and guided the party out of the tunnels.
  • The mercenary, who melted the gold into bars and supposedly "put down" escaped ape-men. When the party described the dead man in the Chewbacca costume, shot in the back of the head and carrying ex-military tattoos, Clive confirmed that he was this man; who shot him is only assumed (Appalachia 09). See Troy Cleaver and the Chewbacca costume.
  • Two bodyguards, never seen. Their fate is never established.
  • Clyde Harvard, a Spud Hut accountant. Jan named him in his interview as the one other person who knew ("That was necessary"), so he was a knowing outsider rather than one of Clive's five (Walkers 01).

docs.title: History
docs.text:
During the arc the party gradually uncovered the ring: the odd dirt trucks and the savant counter worker at the Spud Hut, the Bigfoot sightings, and the hidden tunnel beneath the plant. In Appalachia 08 Jan sent the party to wait in a "break room" that was never a break room, only a door with caged ape-men behind it, and the ape-men came out. In Appalachia 09 the party fought through the shift with Clive's help, and he showed them a gold room with hundreds of pounds of cast bars, about half already gone. The episode opens with Jan leaving the building in a red pickup with a large animal crate (Appalachia 09).

Unrecorded session

The finale, Appalachia 10, was never recorded. It is known only from the epilogue in Walkers 01, where Jan is held at Black Site Omaha with stitches and bruising from the climax, in which he was shot and then crushed by a falling ape that broke his skull.

In that interview, Kurt put it to Jan that the team had been meant to die, and Jan agreed. Hiring the animal handler, he said, had halved his take and doubled the risk of a leak, but he could not manage the ape-men alone. The ape-men were used because they were strong, could recognize gold, and meant no contractors were needed. Jan planned to melt the gold, sell it to a dealer, and work out the laundering later through acquaintances. Kurt assumed Jan had "taken care of" the mercenary in the woods (Walkers 01).

  • Walkers 01

docs.title: Keely Network
docs.text:
The Keely Network is a community of UFO enthusiasts who trade messages on electronic message boards, and the source of the letter that sent the task force to the Roulet house.

Type Online community (message boards) Members An unnamed correspondent who knew Andrew Howard; a friend of Margaret Roulet First appearance Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
In the recap that opens Roulet Estate 02, Andre explains the origin of the trip: someone from the Keely Network message boards who knew Andrew wrote to him that their friend Margaret Roulet had been experiencing "visitations" and then vanished. (Roulet Estate 02)

The letter reached Andrew on Christmas Eve, when Big Bill handed over a padded envelope that an FBI courier had asked him to drop off. It had no return address and held a second envelope wrapped in aluminum foil, which contained the letter and a hand-drawn pencil sketch of some trees (see Foil-Wrapped Letter). Andre later says that the black triangles came from the sketch. The correspondent is never named. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The name is of uncertain spelling.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Roulet Estate 01
  • Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: KGB
docs.text:
The KGB is the Soviet security service, which in The Things in Appalachia reaches out to Dick "The Biz" Baxter through a fake sweepstakes line and trades information on the "Massachusetts matter" for a favor in Dahlonega, Georgia.

Type Organization (foreign intelligence) Aliases The sweepstakes front; the Canada maple syrup sweepstakes line Affiliation Soviet intelligence, still operating after the Soviet collapse First appearance Appalachia 01 Contact An unnamed voice on the sweepstakes line

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The KGB never appears in person. It speaks only through a sweepstakes mailer and a phone number, and it addresses only the Biz. In Appalachia 01 Andre describes the sweepstakes invitation as something the Biz "pretty much immediately twig[s] as being a KGB front". This is the only episode in which Andre or any player names the organization behind the Biz's Russian contact; in other episodes "KGB" comes up only as a figure of speech or a worry, as when Ezra wonders in Roulet Estate 02 whether a Russian rifle found at a house means "is this the KGB?" The team's other members are sent off the call and are not told what the Biz learns (Appalachia 01).

The same book code, a gutted copy of Moby-Dick, is used to decode its messages; see Moby-Dick book cipher.

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text:
In Appalachia 01 the Biz calls the number from a payphone across town. An old man's voice answers: "Hey, sweetie, this is the Canada maple syrup sweepstakes line. Do you want to hear the numbers of the day?" The numbers (13, 45, 196 and so on) decode with the Moby-Dick codebook into a message: "We have information on Massachusetts matter. Need favor. You will be sent to George I A soon. Collect equipment at old drop spot before you leave. We'll pay $10,000 and information on completion." ("Georgia" is not a word in Moby-Dick, hence "George I A".) Andre voices the speaker first as an old man and then as "she" (Appalachia 01).

The "Massachusetts matter" is the Marblehead case from the end of The Summer Service. The KGB claims to hold information about it, and the episodes never reveal what that information is.

Distrusting his old dead drop (a loose paving stone under a park bench near his old house, which the handlers had used to get money to him before), the Biz pays a homeless man about $50 to fetch the package. It contains a covert recording microphone, a compact hidden film camera and a sheet of thin paper meant to be burned or eaten. The instructions are to install the camera in room 111 of the Smith Hotel in Dahlonega before midnight in two days' time, retrieve it afterwards, and mail the undeveloped film to an address to be supplied the following day (Appalachia 01). See Spy Camera and Microphone and Room 111.

In Appalachia 02 the Biz carries out the job alone. The desk clerk tells him room 111 was booked under one name with a credit card in another, that the man who booked it offered him $100 to keep quiet, and that the man was carrying a gun, sounded Midwestern and was rude. The Biz recognizes the description: "That is him." He tucks a black, motion-sensing film camera among the cables beside the television's VCR, angled at the bed, and sticks the microphone to the drawer of the bedside table, taking care to leave no fingerprints (Appalachia 02). The episode does not name the KGB in this scene.

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text:
• Why the KGB wants room 111 watched, and who the booker is.
  • Whether the Biz ever retrieved the film or mailed it, and whether he was paid or given the promised information.
  • What the "Massachusetts matter" information is.

docs.text:

docs.title: Marblehead Board of Selectmen
docs.text:
The Marblehead Board of Selectmen is the town's governing council, which in the world of The Summer Service is an eleven-seat board bound to the Sons of Adam church and led by the bloated mayor.

Type Organization (town government) Aliases The council; town leadership; town leaders Affiliation Sons of Adam Seat Second-floor meeting room, Marblehead town hall Status Intact, with one empty seat (as of Summer Service 05) First appearance Mentioned in Summer Service 01; met in Summer Service 04

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Andre notes that the group of selectmen is not his invention: it is how real Marblehead is run. Here the board is a church-linked body. Its meeting room on the second floor of the town hall has eleven chairs with name plaques arranged in a circle, and a huge seal on the rear wall reads "Sons of Adam" and shows Jesus standing in the midst of parted waters (Summer Service 04). The board believes the second coming is imminent, blames Satan for the town's illnesses and dead fish, and is outwardly polite but hostile. Andre tells the players that the members come across as fanatics but not necessarily insincere, except for one man at the back whom the party cannot read (Summer Service 04). See Second coming and eschaton.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• The Mayor of Marblehead: chairs the board and preaches in the priest's place.
  • The priest, Amos Shaw: attends the meeting with early bloating, although his house has been found wrecked and bloodied.
  • The Chief of Police, called "Jimmy."
  • Jester: his plaque reads "J. Evans, businessman." He is also the hotel's front-desk clerk.
  • Horace Cromwell: the banker, a large silent man at the back, more bloated than most and visibly tense.
  • Arnold Weathers: his plaque marks the empty seat.
  • Several others, unnamed. Ten of the eleven seats are occupied (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
Before the meeting. The task force's first lead in Summer Service 01 is that the missing scientists went to meet "town leaders" (Summer Service 01). The EPA field journal later says that the mayor and senior officials threatened the survey team (Summer Service 03).

The 6:30 meeting. Jester offers to take the party to the board, which meets at 6:30. Everyone in the room has the glow, including the party. The mayor, the chief and others are bloated with near-translucent skin. Asked about the scientists, the mayor says the board was "given to understand that the scientists left town pretty suddenly": they had come to see the board, said they were making little progress and "might return to Washington, D.C." for more resources, and were not heard from again, so the board assumed they had gone. People glance nervously at Arnold Weathers's empty chair. The session ends with the party debating arrests: Andre says they have grounds to arrest the priest, Amos Shaw, on suspicion of murder and the chief for concealing evidence of a crime (Summer Service 04).

The missing seat. Summer Service 05 opens at the end of the same meeting, with the hostile atmosphere in the room increasingly clear. Andrew Howard excuses himself when his radio clicks, and the team leaves (Summer Service 05). The team then finds Weathers in a tub of black liquid in his own house, a hairless worm host who is destroyed in the struggle. In his bedroom they find two sets of the town's financial books and a shoebox full of clear marbles, which suggests he was tied into town finances and secrets; see Two sets of financial books and Crystal marbles. Kurt Larson tells the FBI he suspects a conspiracy by the town's leadership behind the outbreak, and the FBI reports an intercepted shipment of illegal M16s bound for a Marblehead citizen (Summer Service 05).

Aftermath. The National Guard takes command of the town in Summer Service 06. What happens to the selectmen is never stated.

docs.text:
• Summer Service 01 (mentioned)
  • Summer Service 03 (mentioned)
  • Summer Service 04
  • Summer Service 05

docs.title: Marblehead police
docs.text:
The Marblehead police are the town's hostile local force, suspected by the task force of the lighthouse interrogation and the bug left there, and aligned with the Sons of Adam cult when it besieges the task force's hotel in The Summer Service.

Type Organization (local police) Aliases Local PD; cops; posse Affiliation Town of Marblehead; aligned with the Sons of Adam Leader The Chief of Police ("Jimmy") Status Hostile (as of Summer Service 05) First appearance Radford Horror 08 (mentioned)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The police are never friendly. The case file given to the task force in Radford Horror 08 says that local law enforcement has been unresponsive and not helpful, "suspiciously so." In Summer Service 03, when Huell asks for police support and a forensics examiner at the abandoned house, Kurt Larson insists: "let our guys look at it before the hometown cops do. They seem like maybe they're not on the level." The team later agrees not to use the police radio (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Members
docs.text: The only member identified is the Chief of Police, who is also a selectman; see Marblehead Board of Selectmen. The other officers are not named.

docs.title: The Summer Service
docs.text:
The lighthouse. At the lighthouse, Kurt finds a walkie-talkie of the kind local police departments use, with its button taped down. The team concludes that it was a bug and speaks carefully near it; see Police walkie-talkie. The blood trail in the basement led to where a car would park, but the episodes never say who carried out the interrogation. On leaving, Andrew notices the end of a squad car, and Kurt calls the lighthouse "an active trap" (Summer Service 03; Summer Service 04).

The chief. At the selectmen's meeting the chief glares at Jester, refuses Kurt's request to smoke, and goes very still when the team brings up the melted shoreline. The mayor tells him to look into it. Andre tells the players that they have grounds to arrest the chief for concealing evidence of a crime (Summer Service 04).

Ignoring Arnold. Madeline Weathers tells the team that the police did nothing when she reported her uncle missing, and that she thinks they are "all fucking involved" (Summer Service 05).

The siege. Around 4 a.m. in Summer Service 05, a police car pulls up at the team's hotel while silent, armed church members gather in the rain; a second car arrives later. Huell sees the first cop car pass him on the road and calls the FBI switchboard from a payphone: "I think the local police are trying to form a posse to murder us." Police come up the stairs as the team escapes through the second-floor bathroom window into the alley (Summer Service 05).

Aftermath. The Guard takes command of the town in Summer Service 06. The episodes do not say what happened to the police.

docs.title: Minor organizations: The Things in Appalachia
docs.text: Minor organizations of The Things in Appalachia: the agencies, businesses, committees and loose groups that do not have pages of their own.

docs.title: ATF
docs.text: The Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco and Firearms is the last federal presence the Dahlonega locals remember. Edward Nick Sr. tells the team that the previous feds in the area were ATF agents after moonshiners. The agency is only mentioned. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Dahlonega Times
docs.text: The Dahlonega Times is the local paper that printed the grainy, Patterson-Gimlin-style Bigfoot photograph in the case dossier, with a Bill Clinton campaign story below the fold. Huell judges the photo blurry enough to be a man in an ape suit. The photo is credited to Charlie Briggs. Auraria has its own paper, the Gold Bug. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Dental Oncologists' Conference
docs.text: A conference of dental oncologists fills the Smith Hotel when the team arrives, leaving only two rooms, and Kurt comes to believe the dentists follow the team from hotel to hotel. One guest is caught digging through the scrambled eggs with his bare hands at breakfast, and Andrew jokes that they may be "the Bigfoot perverts." Dentists fill the hotels in other arcs too, making this one of the show's running gags. See the Smith Hotel. (Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03)

docs.title: EPA and NRC
docs.text: After Marblehead, the Environmental Protection Agency and the Nuclear Regulatory Commission clean up the radiological mess left by the sea creature and the Davy Crockett device. They hold the team's car and equipment, and the team is left driving a 1991 Ford Explorer. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Gold Bug
docs.text: The Gold Bug is a small newspaper with a storefront in Auraria, framed front pages in its window. It ran the Bigfoot photos by contract photographer Derek Edwards, who runs its website and hunting-blind cameras. An older, pinched employee shows Kurt Derek's number in a Rolodex. (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: House Subcommittee
docs.text: A House subcommittee investigating the Marblehead incident takes Kurt's testimony on October 3, 1992. Its chairman, Congressman Bradley, asks about the worms and the church leaders who died of infection. Big Bill has two of his questions struck. (Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Jackson and Lee's
docs.text: Jackson and Lee's is the law firm named on the eviction letters that the "corporate goons" gave the Covenant. The letters name only the firm, not its client, so the party never learns who wants the Auraria land. Kurt says he will put out feelers about the firm. See also The Land Dispute. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Jeep Hunters
docs.text: Monica Cartwright reports drunk, out-of-season hunters in gray jumpsuits and sunglasses, driving a Jeep with a big cage and shotguns, who were around before her son Gene vanished. They are never traced. See Monica Cartwright. (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Late Night with David Letterman
docs.text: The talk show on which the Biz appears after the Clinton surveillance scandal. The in-fiction broadcast opens The Walkers in Skin as a cold open, billing Gary Oldman, Patti Smith and "the most hated cop in America." See David Letterman. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Secret Service
docs.text: The Secret Service is the protective detail of candidate Bill Clinton. In Appalachia 06 a state police officer says the Secret Service will want to see the night-vision headset found in the hotel bushes; in Appalachia 07 the sheriff relays that they tipped the state police off to surveillance gear whose fingerprints matched an FBI employee. See the Clinton Surveillance Scandal. (Appalachia 06, Appalachia 07)

docs.title: Underground Gold Mine Tours
docs.text: Underground Gold Mine Tours is a local tour operator whose Vietnam-surplus flatbed, topped with a terrifying prospector dummy, sits outside the Nicks' trailer park. Andrew wants to take the tour. The Consolidated Gold Mine later has a similar animatronic prospector outside. See Consolidated Gold Mine. (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Minor organizations: Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable (non-canon one-shot)
docs.text:
Non-canon

These groups appear only in Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, a non-canon one-shot presented as an in-universe anime OVA. Nothing here is part of the main campaign's continuity.

Minor groups of the one-shot who do not have their own pages, in alphabetical order. The larger groups have pages of their own: the World Martial Arts Tournament, the Secret Service, The Alien Faction, Pure Human Martial Artists and Animal Control.

docs.title: Corporate Sponsors
docs.text: Almost everyone at the World Martial Arts Tournament wears sponsor branding. Sponsors fund fighters in return for a share of the prize pool, and most fighters live on fixed incomes from them. Mirabeth and Derk did not submit their paperwork in time, though a dog-food company had shown interest. After the Ovain fight, Colonel Sparago tells Mirabeth that Derk "probably needs to be sponsored." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Wizards
docs.text: A medium-sized group of entrants at the safety briefing, "basically wizards," who specialize in psychic or magical attacks. They study the core magic curriculum some eighteen hours a day in their formative years, so they are dim and barely literate outside it, and as a clan they have a terrible reputation. They are one of the three notable groups Mirabeth considers eavesdropping on, along with the Alien Faction and the Pure Human Martial Artists. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Minor organizations: Radford (The Radford Horror and The Radford Horrors)
docs.text: This page lists the minor groups, businesses and institutions of the two Radford arcs.

docs.title: Ferry Lodge management
docs.text: Under "new management", the Ferry Lodge has been remodeled with payphones, brighter lights, new windows, hot tubs, a pool and a mud-mask spa, yet it stays half empty. The owners are secretive and snooty, refuse to hire locals, and are the subject of an eight-month fraud investigation; IRS Criminal Investigations raids the lodge as the team watches. It is never established whether the management is connected to the Safe Environment Fund or the lawyers who threaten those asking about the missing. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04) See IRS Criminal Investigations.

docs.title: Garland Air Conditioning Repair
docs.text: Garland Air Conditioning Repair is the business of PTA dad Toby Garland, mentioned when he chats with Kurtis at the school science fair. (Radford Horrors 01) See Toby Garland.

docs.title: Highway Patrol and state police
docs.text: The highway patrol and state police respond to the APB in Radford Horror 06, rescue Dr. Lori from his kidnapper and hold Derek Augustine at their station. In Radford Horror 07 Rita notes that Highway Patrol has "that one guy", a lead the team postpones to the next day. (Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07) See Derek Augustine and Dr. Lawrence Lori.

docs.title: Lawson family
docs.text: The Lawsons are Dean's parents, who cannot be reached and own the stone-and-timber cabin near the ski lodge. A voice at the Stately Acres call box says they use it as a summer place. (Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07) See Dean Lawson and Lawson cabin.

docs.title: Mr. King's organization
docs.text: Mr. King's organization is a cosmic-leaning group awaiting "the next master" and fighting the "forces of silence" that cover up the cosmic. In a flashback, Mr. King tells Andrew that the next master is coming and that Andrew is "the tip of the spear". The organization is not named in the scene. (Radford Horror 01) See Mr. King and The Masters.

docs.title: Narconon
docs.text: Narconon is named in the letters of the missing people as a supposed Los Angeles addiction center; in the first conversation Sheriff Molly Underhill calls it a rehab in California "like Narconon". It permits no visitors, which the team finds suspicious, and the FBI agrees to research it. (Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04) See LA treatment cover story.

docs.title: Oral surgeons' convention
docs.text: An oral surgeons' convention, a running joke ("tooth botherers", "Tooth Doc conference"), fills the Ferry Lodge and forces the team into the Pay n' Stay. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 05) See Pay n' Stay.

docs.title: Radford church community
docs.text: The congregation of the Radford church hosts the 4:30 p.m. community meeting, announced by Molly, at which the curfew is explained. The priest gives the closing sermon and townsfolk ask about a serial killer and about dogs. (Radford Horror 05) See Curfew and community meeting.

docs.title: Stately Acres management company
docs.text: The property-management company that runs the gated mountain community of Stately Acres employs Douglas Douglas under company-store conditions. (Radford Horror 07) See Stately Acres and Douglas Douglas.

docs.title: The scary lawyers
docs.text: The scary lawyers are an anonymous law firm that threatens anyone investigating the missing people, including Phoebe's supposed rehab. Their phone number is on the missing posters Molly gives the team. Lawyers also follow the team with cameras at the Safe Environment Fund site, though it is never established that these are the same lawyers. (Radford Horrors 02) See Safe Environment Fund.

docs.title: Minor organizations: The Roulet Estate
docs.text: Minor organizations of The Roulet Estate, in alphabetical order.

docs.title: LTTE
docs.text: The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam, the Sri Lankan insurgent group that Kurt Larson says he was sent to fight in early 1993. He mentions it in passing in the epilogue, where he says he postponed the assassination of Ranasinghe Premadasa before being called back after Waco. The group never appears. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Perot's Insurgency Task Force
docs.text: The new unit that President-elect Ross Perot is forming to investigate the "insurgency incidents." On Christmas Eve 1992 Big Bill tells the agents that Perot believes their task force is a cover for George H. W. Bush weaponizing the FBI against his political enemies. Perot has asked him to resign and will disband and reassign the Paranatural Incident Task Force on Inauguration Day. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Salvation Army
docs.text: The charity for which the teenage carolers collect at the task force office on Christmas Eve 1992. Huell Kendrick gives the carolers his remaining cigarettes and the Biz gives one of his gold nuggets. (Roulet Estate 01) See also Salvation Army Carolers.

docs.title: The Humanists
docs.text: The group about which Boris Yeltsin questions the Biz. After offering him a Cuban cigar in the former Soviet Parliament building, Yeltsin says, "Tell me everything you know about the humanists." Nothing more is revealed about who they are. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Minor organizations: The Summer Service
docs.text: These are the agencies, groups and businesses that touch the Marblehead case without getting their own page. The larger groups include the Sons of Adam, the EPA/USGS survey team and the Marblehead Board of Selectmen.

docs.title: Boat crew
docs.text: Also called the cold-open gunners. Four men in dark camouflage, black hats and face paint, aboard a steel boat with no running lights at night in the cold open of Radford Horror 08. They aim a hydraulic tripod gun with a thermal scope at a target that "has a human with it," and one of them is Mr. Miller. Their commander tells the others to keep their eyes up because "if we don't kill it, it's going to be on us in a second." Their affiliation is never stated. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: CDC, FEMA and NCEH
docs.text: The health and emergency agencies that start calling the FBI after McManley finds worms in the wine and a nerve-agent-like toxin. Diane relays that they are calling the secretary pool, that the governor may deploy the National Guard and close the beaches, and that many more people will arrive in a day or two. The team argues over what to tell the CDC, and Ezra says they should not let it "go into this blind and then blow the lid on something way spookier than just a regular disease." Their personnel are still days away when the case ends. See Synthetic nerve agent. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: College protesters
docs.text: Students who gather outside Marblehead's City Hall with signs reading "No more dead fish! No fish for science!", "No Nukes" and "Close Seabrook!" They blame the newly opened Seabrook plant for the fish die-off. Huell tells the Biz to flick a cigarette at one, and it hits a student in the eye, so that he drops his sign crying. See Marblehead town hall. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: EPA and USGS
docs.text: The Environmental Protection Agency and the U.S. Geological Survey sent a field team to Marblehead about a month after an unexplained explosion blew out windows and made townspeople sick, to check whether a seabed natural-gas leak had gone off and whether human life was at risk. The team went missing, and by the case file's account had been gone about four days. The missing scientists are covered at EPA/USGS survey team. (Radford Horror 08; Summer Service 03)

docs.title: FBI counterintelligence
docs.text: A branch of the Bureau that has surveilled the Biz for a couple of weeks because of his money problems. The Biz does not know. When Kurt confronts the watcher on the roof, he tells the agent his unit is his to govern and that the matter will be fine, and then plays it down to the rest of the team. See FBI. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: The "Marines"
docs.text: Also called the frequency B voices. Unseen, frightened voices on the radio during the hotel siege, who tell the team to "get off the fucking line," claim to be "the goddamn Marines" and order everyone to switch to frequency B before the line goes dead. Dante wonders why Marines would be in radio range and apparently in fear for their lives, and later says the team should find out why they heard them. In Summer Service 06 Andre again calls the radio contacts who track the creature "the Marines." See Mystery covert group. (Summer Service 05; Summer Service 06)

docs.title: McManley's forensics team
docs.text: Also called McManley's crew, the M.E. team or the interns. A set of browbeaten interns and assistants working out of McManley's RV under Donald McManley. They process Amos Shaw's house, examine the worms and wine, and in Summer Service 05 receive Puddles' head. McManley lends the party his assistant Henry for the ivermectin run. See also M.E. assistant in pajamas. (Summer Service 03; Summer Service 04; Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Scott Insurance
docs.text: Also given as Scott Insurance, Boat Specialty. The family boat and car insurance business that Irene Scott runs from the Scott home. The phone is answered "Scott Insurance, we do boats and cars," and the sign outside reads "Scott Insurance, Boat Specialty." Irene wants to know whether the scientists ever sent off the blood samples they took. See Irene Scott, Lena Scott and The Scott home. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: U.S. Navy
docs.text: Also called the Navy. Following the unrecorded Summer Service 02, Big Bill says in Summer Service 03 that he can probably get a submarine out to examine the wreck with better instrumentation, and in Summer Service 04 he reports that a Los Angeles-class fast attack submarine, which had been hunting Soviet boats, has been retasked to look at it. In the finale a submarine, the USS Oklahoma City, fires everything conventional at the creature and is pursued, and Big Bill reports afterward that "we lost one of our submarines too." See The stealth wreck and USS Oklahoma City. (Summer Service 03; Summer Service 04; Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Minor organizations: The Walkers in Skin
docs.text: This page lists the minor businesses, institutions and communities that appear in The Walkers in Skin; larger groups include Bigelow's research operation and the skinwalker faction.

docs.title: Ballard Sheriff's Office
docs.text: The law enforcement of Ballard, Utah, which amounts to one man, Sheriff McDermish, working from a double-wide trailer that is also his home. In Walkers 03 he serves sweet tea at a card table with a Monopoly game underway. In Walkers 06 he reports that over half the high school is absent, that houses have been empty for days and that the diner is nearly empty, and he then arms Kurt and flees the state with his son. By Walkers 07 and Walkers 08 the department is empty, and the party only mentions that the sheriff left town. See the sheriff's double-wide and disappearances in Ballard. (Walkers 03, Walkers 06, Walkers 08)

docs.title: Budget Suites of America
docs.text: A hotel chain owned by Bigelow and recommended by Gardner, who promises kitchens and no bed bugs. Kurt asks whether dentists are staying there, a nod to the table's running gag about dentists' conferences bumping the team from hotels. (Walkers 02)

docs.title: Dollar Tree
docs.text: A rival discount store in Roosevelt, loathed by the cashier at Stewart's, who thanks the party for not patronizing the "interloper" and complains that "they don't pay copyright on the songs." See Stewart's. (Walkers 05)

docs.title: Hertz Rent-A-Car
docs.text: The rental company that supplied the party's Plymouth Voyager. After the van vanishes and reappears, a Hertz clerk pages Andrew to report it blocking East Lagoon Street in Roosevelt. See the Plymouth Voyager and the vanishing car. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Mormon community of Ballard
docs.text: The religious majority in Ballard and the surrounding area, and the group the party first suspects. The community's church holds the grave of Shelly Wilmarth, and in Walkers 01 Alberta asks the FBI to force it to exhume her mother. Sheriff McDermish complains about "nosy Mormons," the bartender suspects Andrew of being a "Mormon fed," and in Walkers 06 the sheriff notes that most of the missing townspeople are Mormon. After the gym fight, the duplicate of Andrew guesses "Mormons or a religious cult thing," and the players joke about Mormons training coyotes. See the exhumation. (Walkers 01, Walkers 03, Walkers 06, Walkers 07)

docs.title: Roosevelt high school drama department
docs.text: The source of the Cats fundraiser costumes that the party finds in the trunk of the loaner squad car Betsy. Walt identifies them as Cats costumes and credits the Roosevelt drama teacher, described as a "big musical theater lady." See Cats costumes. (Walkers 04)

docs.title: Missing FBI task force
docs.text:
The missing FBI task force is the team of five veteran FBI agents that President Ross Perot had handpicked to redo the Radford investigation, who vanish in the Virginia woods and leave behind an intact campsite.

Type Organization (FBI field team) Aliases Perot's handpicked task force; previous FBI team; five agents; the original task force Affiliation FBI Members Five unnamed career agents, all over forty Status Missing; presumed dead by the task force (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horrors 01 (cold open)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: After President Ross Perot found the quality of the earlier Radford reports unacceptable, and FBI Director Sessions stood by them and was fired, Perot had a list drawn up of very reliable career agents to run an independent investigation. The five chosen are all over forty, have served through multiple administrations, and are considered "very professional guys." Their names are never given (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Cold open and assignment
docs.text:
The first episode of The Radford Horrors opens on FBI agents in yellow-lettered jackets sprinting through snowy woods at night, flashlights bouncing; one sobs, and something swoops overhead and picks them off one by one from above. They reach a clearing with a suspended, emaciated man and similar figures hanging from the trees, and one agent is drained to a husk by a shape in the brush while another is forced to turn her gun on a colleague. The players take these to be the missing team (Radford Horrors 01).

New FBI Director Rudy Giuliani tells the reassembled task force that there are a number of missing people in Radford and that the original FBI team sent to look into them has gone AWOL. His two priorities are to establish what happened to the previous team and then to establish an "acceptable fact pattern" for the previous case (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02). The Director does not believe the agents are dead; the players, having seen the cold open, assume they are (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: The campsite
docs.text:
The agents spent a night at the Pay n' Stay, then drove to Roanoke for good camping gear. About a week before the task force arrived, they radioed in to say they were still fine and chasing up some odd things, with no strong leads. Sheriff Molly Underhill tells the team that people who looked into the disappearances got the strong arm from scary lawyers, that she called the FBI, and that the agents who came have vanished too. She gives the team directions to the campsite (Radford Horrors 02).

At the Sportsman RV Campground, the team cuts open the locked tents. Huell's Investigate a Mystery roll finds no sign of haste or foul play and gear for five people: two tents with three cots and two, plus an administrative tent. In the administrative tent is a map of the woods marked with irregular polygons and an illegible scribble beside one boundary. Huell takes the map. The agents' car is still in the lot, with two shotguns locked in a case in the trunk, and the camp is only a couple of miles from the moth site (Radford Horrors 02). The map leads the team to the fenced land of the Safe Environment Fund; see the missing agents' map.

In Radford Horrors 04 the team returns to the campground and pitches its own tents immediately beside the missing agents' tents (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Giuliani's deadline
docs.text: In Radford Horrors 04, Webster reports to Giuliani that the missing locals have all left letters claiming they went to an addiction center in Los Angeles, which is out of character, and that the team suspects the gray vans and the Safe Environment Fund. Giuliani says that if the team can find the FBI agents in the next twenty-four hours, "dead or alive," it would make his next conversations easier. He says he already has a man looking into the fund. See also the LA treatment cover story.

docs.title: Theories
docs.text:
• Daniel Webster suspects the earlier task force was a political dirty-work unit of President George H. W. Bush and that the "alien stuff" is a cover (Radford Horrors 02).
  • The cold open shows the agents hunted by a flying thing, one of the Radford woods predators. It is never established whether the same creature took the agents from their campsite, or whether it is connected to the first arc's moth.

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The agents' fate, their names, and any link to the Safe Environment Fund's fenced site remain open as of Radford Horrors 04.

docs.title: Mystery covert group
docs.text:
The mystery covert group is the unidentified armed organization behind the voice on the task force's pocket radio, whose dead "advanced team" leaked the nerve agent into Marblehead's water in The Summer Service.

Type Organization (unidentified) Aliases Advanced team; the contact's side; the Marines Affiliation Unknown Spokesman The radio contact Status Active, unidentified (as of Summer Service 06) First appearance Summer Service 05 (as the voices calling themselves the Marines)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The group is known only through the radio contact. It has a commanding officer, an "advanced team" that is dead at the bottom of the ocean, a liquid anti-worm agent, a weapon called a "Casaba" that must be fired from the air, and the ability to track the glowing angel thing (Summer Service 06). The spelling "Casaba" is as heard in the recording.

docs.title: The Marines
docs.text: In Summer Service 05, unseen voices cut into the team's frequency, bark "We're the goddamn Marines. Get off the line," and tell everyone to switch to frequency B. Kurt Larson wonders why Marines would be in radio range and apparently afraid for their lives, and resolves to make phone calls once back in town. In Summer Service 06 the radio contact apologizes for "my commanding officer's rudeness earlier," and Andre later describes updates from "the Marines" on the creature's position (Summer Service 05; Summer Service 06).

docs.title: The advanced team
docs.text: Andrew Howard asks over the radio whether the "advanced team" was the dead crew in the boat with a bite out of it, found on the dive. The contact answers, "Oh, you do know about the advanced team," and apologizes that the broad-spectrum synthetic nerve agent leaked when "we got blown up" (Summer Service 06). The wreck itself was found on the dive in the unrecorded Summer Service 02; see The stealth wreck.

docs.title: The worm campaign
docs.text: The group knows about the worms and has developed the anti-worm agent from captured samples. The contact says "we're gonna have to kill all these people" once they no longer have special support, and adds that the agent "won't kill anything else, probably." Kurt suggests crop-dusting after the storm. The group plans the shot at the creature with Kurt and the team and leaves the canister on the freeway (Summer Service 06).

docs.title: What remains unknown
docs.text: Who the group serves, who its commanding officer is, and what "where I'm from" means. Its relationship to the angel thing is also unclear: the contact says the creature is "not there to help" the convoy of infected, which is why it will have to come out of the water (Summer Service 06). In Summer Service 05, Kurt wonders whether the nerve agent in the water was another party's attempt to contain the worms; the Summer Service 06 revelation fits that only partly, since the group also plans to kill the infected (Summer Service 05; Summer Service 06).

docs.text:
