docs.title: National Guard
docs.text:
The National Guard is the military reserve force called out twice to back up the Paranatural Incident Task Force: in Massachusetts, where it arrives after the fighting is over, and in Utah, where it fights beside the team and takes heavy losses.

Type Organization (state military forces) Aliases the Guard; Guardsmen; Utah National Guard Known members The major; older Guard officer; Sergeant Jefferson (or Johnson); Jordan Gramoire Status Active First appearance Summer Service 06; mentioned from Summer Service 03

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The task force has no troops of its own. When a case outgrows four investigators, the request goes up through Big Bill, and what comes back, eventually, is the Guard. Both times it is told a cover story about what it is dealing with. (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 06, Walkers 06)

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• The major, commander of the Utah convoy; the players also call him "the general". Skeptical, but he takes Kurt's advice. (Walkers 09)
  • The older Guard officer, an older man in a lieutenant's uniform who debriefs the team at Marblehead. (Summer Service 06)
  • Sergeant Jefferson, who announces the Guard's arrival at Marblehead by radio. Andre gives the name as Jefferson and then as Johnson within the same broadcast. (Summer Service 06)
  • A young lieutenant at the Marblehead checkpoint. (Summer Service 06)
  • Jordan Gramoire, son of Ma Gramoire, who serves in the Guard: "He's still alive, he just don't call." Mentioned only. (Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Marblehead (June 1992)
docs.text:
With federal health agencies converging on Marblehead, Diane warns that the governor may call out the Guard and close the beaches. Big Bill orders the team to find the missing survey team before it arrives. Ma Gramoire, for her part, will talk to the government only when it brings her Guardsman son back. (Summer Service 03)

The Guard is sent, but the storm washes out the roads. One day Big Bill has no solid numbers on when it will arrive; the next it is blocked about forty miles out, and the FBI cannot send a helicopter. Kurt's message for the soldiers is "don't eat nothing here. Eat from packs". (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05)

The Guard reaches Marblehead only as the team is finishing the case at the power plant. A sergeant broadcasts on all frequencies: "We have arrived at Marblehead. We've taken command of the situation. There's some awfully weird shit out here. If you're in range, would appreciate a consult." At the checkpoint a lieutenant first turns the team away. They hand over the anti-worm canister, which goes to a chemist, and give the older officer the agreed story: a religious terrorist group that seeded the food supply with a parasite. He tells them the military is handing out deworming medicine, that some townspeople will not pull through, and, on his way out, that "apparently someone used a tactical nuke at the nuclear power plant". The team feigns surprise and goes to sleep in the medical tent. See Terrorist cover story. (Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Utah (November 1992)
docs.text:
As the Ballard case turns dangerous, Kurt phones Big Bill from the sheriff's office and asks for the Utah National Guard to be put on standby. Big Bill had hoped Ballard would not be "an additional thing I had to worry about on top of the, you know, political stuff". (Walkers 06)

They need it. After the night at Ballard High School the plan is to drive out at sunrise and call the Guard in, but the phones are down, Salt Lake City is 141 miles away, and the roads are blocked. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08)

Unrecorded session

How the Guard was reached is known only from Andre's recap at the start of Walkers 09, which covers the end of session 08 or the unrecorded Walkers 08.5. The team fetched horses to get around the roadblock, carried a generator to the radio station and called the Guard, met it on horseback outside town, fought through the barricade between Ballard and Roosevelt and cleared the Roosevelt police station.

A convoy of Humvees and APCs then drives on the community center at dusk, with the team and the ranch people on horseback and Ned Simpson's killdozer falling in behind. The major's jaw drops when Kurt points out that the cloud ahead is the ranch farmhouse hanging in the sky. When invisible waves start shoving the vehicles he halts the convoy and orders an advance on foot, with a megaphone surrender attempt first. (Walkers 09)

The megaphone party gets as far as "This is the National Guard, please, sir--" before it is answered with gunfire. Two Guardsmen take an APC back with Walt "Coyote" Murphy to knock out the substation. While the team is underground, white powder falls over the battlefield and everyone outside is knocked unconscious; unidentified hazmat teams and black craft move over the field. Kurt takes a medic's Humvee, the party rights the overturned APC, and Kurt uses its long-range radio to put a report on record with the Guard's Salt Lake City outpost: there is a cover-up, and the team did not cause it. The Guardsmen left at the police station with Donald McManley stayed conscious because they were indoors; they had helped with the autopsies, and are evacuated with him. (Walkers 09)

The cost is given in the next arc. At least 50 to 60 Guardsmen are dead. The powder was a mild amnesiac, and most of the surviving soldiers have no idea what happened over the previous twenty hours; searchers find no trace of the hazmat troops. The Guardsmen who watched the autopsies are debriefed by national security officials. Big Bill's public story is a domestic insurgency. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Andre's inventory of the Utah column: "Humvees, a couple of APCs, an armored bulldozer, a bunch of horses, one police car, and one elderly vehicle, Betsy". (Walkers 09)
  • At Marblehead the Guard is the cavalry that arrives late: Diane had asked the team to tell her if something big was trying to kill them "so I can send in the cavalry". (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 06)
  • The major's fate after the powder fell is not shown in the Walkers finale; in the next arc he is carried into the medical tent on a stretcher with the other casualties. (Walkers 09, Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Next-door Hotel Guests
docs.text:
The Next-door Hotel Guests are a group of secretive occupants of a room at the Smith Hotel in Dahlonega, the room the Biz bugged in Appalachia 02.

Type Group of unnamed guests Aliases Room 111 party Location Smith Hotel, room 111 Affiliation Unknown Status Unknown First appearance Appalachia 02

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The group's room was booked under one name, occupied by someone else, and paid for with a card in a third name. The desk clerk told the party that scary men came and went and that one of them had offered him money to keep quiet (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• The booker (unseen): an armed, rude, short-haired, military-looking man who sounded Midwestern and paid the clerk $100 for silence. When the clerk described him, the Biz said "That is him" (Appalachia 02).
  • A curly-haired blonde woman in a bathrobe, who asked a battered Andrew Howard "Are you okay, honey?" in the hall (Appalachia 03).
  • A suited man with a military haircut, who whispered to the woman, steered her back inside and glared at Andrew.
  • A laughing man in a big cowboy hat and dark sunglasses, whom Huell Kendrick glimpsed entering the room and found oddly familiar for a split second. He is never identified on screen.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
In Appalachia 02 the clerk reported the room to Dick "The Biz" Baxter and lent him a master key. The Biz entered room 111 alone, found a delivered basket of wine and chocolates and a room that looked staged for a sexual encounter, and hid a motion-sensing spy camera and microphone there, the camera beside the VCR and the microphone in the bedside drawer. He suspected a setup, possibly involving kids (Appalachia 02).

The guests crossed paths with the party in the hall in Appalachia 03, after Andrew returned to the hotel by cab (Appalachia 03).

In the epilogue in Walkers 01, the public story is that FBI agents were caught surveilling Governor Clinton in a Georgia hotel room, and a talk-show host blames Jan Martense for it. The Biz, interviewed, says he thought he had been spying on a prostitute and had not known Clinton was in town. The episodes never state outright that the guests were Clinton's party, but the sequence points that way. See the Clinton surveillance scandal.

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Appalachia 02
  • Appalachia 03
  • Walkers 01 (consequences only)

docs.title: NSA
docs.text:
The NSA (National Security Agency) is a U.S. intelligence agency that never acts openly in the campaign but whose identification turns up twice on dead men in black suits.

Type Organization (U.S. federal agency) Aliases National Security Agency; the Puzzle Palace First appearance Radford Horror 03

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
No confirmed NSA employee ever appears. The agency matters as a name on two badges, and as the thing the team is afraid might be listening. "The Puzzle Palace is what the CIA calls the NSA", as Andre explained to the table, and Kurt has a CIA man's contempt for it: its people are "pencil-pushing weenuses" who do not deserve alien technology. (Radford Horror 04, Appalachia 07)

According to Kurt, "our jurisdiction trumps them on domestic soil". Andrew Howard still does not want to go around "pissing off the NSA", and Diane spells out "M-O-T-H" on the telephone because nobody can hear the call "except for the NSA". (Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05, Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
Both known "members" are dead men whose only link to the agency is the identification they carried.

  • Agent Murphy, who claimed to be NSA. No record of him exists. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 08)
  • The dead man in black killed by Jan Martense, who carried NSA identification. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Agent Murphy
docs.text:
On a mountain road outside Radford, Kurt and the Biz hit a man in a black suit with their car. Vomiting blood, he refuses a hospital and shows a badge. (Radford Horror 03)

Quote

"I'm Agent Murphy. I'm NSA. You are fucking this up for me. Get back in your car and drive away." (Andre as Agent Murphy, Radford Horror 03)

Quote

"I don't believe he's NSA for a fucking second." (Dante, Radford Horror 03)

Murphy carries a briefcase and the first flashlight weapon the team sees. He burns Kurt with it, flees into the woods and dies there when it overheats. Kurt recovers scorched teeth and a wallet holding nothing but an NSA card and a little cash; the papers in the briefcase look nothing like the classified NSA documents he has seen. The Biz warns that the agency will deny everything and that the whole thing could be a plant. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04)

A couple of weeks later Kurt's illegal contacts report on the badge: it is not a counterfeit, but there is no one in the records with that name. If it is a forgery, it is the best they have ever seen. (Radford Horror 08)

Quote

"But hey, you know what that means. I didn't kill an NSA agent, officially." (Dante, Radford Horror 08)

Whether the armed cleanup crew that burned the old-town church, which carried the same weapons, has anything to do with the NSA is unresolved. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The second man in black
docs.text:
In CIA custody, Jan Martense tells Kurt where his first ape woman came from. Five years earlier, driving drunk in the Georgia countryside at night, he hit and killed a man in a black suit who was crossing the highway. The man was Hispanic and carried NSA identification, and in his van was an ape woman strapped to a gurney and being fed drugs. Jan put the body "in the passenger seat of his car", drove it into a lake and kept her. (Walkers 01)

The players noticed that both "NSA" men were struck by cars while crossing a road at night ("they have gotta start training their dudes better"), and Dante describes the second as "a different guy pretending to be an NSA agent". (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Other contact
docs.text:
• Kurt sends the cryptogram menu from the Spud Hut to the Puzzle Palace to decode. (Appalachia 07)
  • Kurt's Secret Santa gift to Diane at Christmas 1992 is a Herman Miller chair stamped "Property of the National Security Agency". (Roulet Estate 01)

Quote

"It's a little used, I hope you don't mind, but they're, like, you know, eight grand new, but it should work just fine." (Dante as Kurt, Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text:
• It is never established whether Murphy or the Georgia man actually worked for the NSA, or only carried its identification. (Radford Horror 08, Walkers 01)
  • Nor do the episodes say whether the two men in black are connected to each other, to the flashlight weapons, or to the cleanup crews that follow the team's cases, or why an NSA-badged man had a drugged ape woman in his van. (Radford Horror 08, Walkers 01)

docs.title: Paranatural Incident Task Force
docs.text:
The Paranatural Incident Task Force (PITF) is the small FBI unit, created at presidential request in 1992 and run out of a derelict Washington barbershop, whose four investigators are the player characters of the campaign and whose name is the title of the show.

Type Organization (FBI task force) Aliases PITF; the task force; the Paranatural Task Force; "Pitfa"; Foreign Threat Investigation Task Force (FTIT, public name) Parent FBI, under Big Bill's Foreign Influence Task Force Leader Andrew Howard Headquarters D.C. barbershop Founded Assembled May 24, 1992 Status Disbanded on Inauguration Day 1993; members recalled as consultants in April 1993 (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The task force investigates disappearances, sightings and incidents that nobody else in the Bureau wants. Andrew's own description on the first morning is "we're hunting aliens", and he calls the unit "the first task force of its kind made for the FBI": "We're bleeding edge here, guys." Explaining it to a Georgia sheriff later, Kurt describes "an early warning system" that looks for patterns of disappearances, most of which turn out to be nothing. In Utah, Andrew calls it "kind of an oddball task force... kind of like the front line of people being weird". (Radford Horror 01, Appalachia 04, Walkers 05)

Officially the unit is real but classified. Its reports go up under the code word SKYHOOK, and the public is given a different story about every case it closes. Once the Georgia scandal made the unit famous anyway, it was known publicly as a national security task force; asked for its public name, Andre settled on the "Foreign Threat Investigation Task Force", which Dante immediately shortened to "the FTIT". (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 06, Walkers 01)

The name "Paranatural Incident Task Force" is not spoken in the first session, where it is just "the task force". It is first heard at the end of the first arc, when a visitor to the office asks Andrew how to abbreviate it: "Pitfa?" Big Bill later calls it "the Paranatural Task Force". (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 08, Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Founding
docs.text:
The task force was created at the request of President George H. W. Bush. In spring 1992, with the Soviet Union gone and the FBI's Counterintelligence and Counterterrorism sections being downsized, four people are told separately that they are being moved to it. (Radford Horror 01)

  • Andrew Howard, who wanted the job, is warned by his boss that the thing "has boondoggle written all over it" and "smells like career suicide".
  • Kurt Larson, a CIA officer on loan to an FBI counterterrorism task force that is being downsized, is offered a "real sweetheart gig... hunting for ghosts and little green men for the president".
  • Dick "The Biz" Baxter of Counterintelligence is laterally transferred to what his chief vaguely calls "an investigatory task force related to possible technological threats to national security".
  • Huell Kendrick is thrown out of his old office and onto a "punishment detail": "some kind of make-work task force the president's idiot brother wanted".

Other agents treat the unit as make-work; the agent clearing boxes out of the new office wishes them "good luck with the aliens". (Radford Horror 01)

They meet for the first time on May 24, 1992, and a courier delivers their first file the same morning. (Radford Horror 01)

Bush gives Andrew the real reason for the unit that autumn, and it is not the "idiot brother" of Huell's office rumor: "my son asked me to." His son, identified at the table as George W., has an interest in such things and made him promise to get to the bottom of them if he won the election; Bush was "humoring the boy". Having read the files, he no longer treats it as a joke. (Walkers 01)

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
Member Role Played by Andrew Howard FBI agent; leader of the task force Rita Kurtis "Kurt" Larson Consultant on loan from the CIA, formerly of UTAW; carries no FBI badge Dante Dick "The Biz" Baxter FBI agent, formerly Counterintelligence Ezra Huell Kendrick FBI agent Zack Diane Secretary; runs the office and the phones Andre Donald McManley Forensic support from The Summer Service onward, with two interns and an RV laboratory Andre Daniel Webster FBI Special Agent placed over the recalled team in The Radford Horrors Ezra

(Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03, Radford Horrors 01)

At the start Andrew is the only one who knows that Kurt is CIA rather than FBI. Kurt is variously introduced as "Special Agent Kurtis", as a private investigator, and as CIA "assisting the FBI". (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 08)

OJ, a 25-pound stuffed alien sent to Huell as an insult by his old narcotics colleagues, is the unit's mascot, with a tie and a badge. See OJ the stuffed alien. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: Chain of command
docs.text:
Andrew reports to Big Bill, head of the FBI's Foreign Influence Task Force, which is the unit's parent body because "it was determined that alien visitations are foreign by definition". Big Bill reports to Deputy Director Floyd Clark, who reports to the President: the team is three levels down from Bush. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 03)

In the field the team is told to route anything strange up the chain, to keep the true purpose of the unit out of what it tells other agencies ("that's for the report. With appropriate classification"), and, repeatedly, to do things by the book. Expenses are reimbursed and the Bureau pays for damage. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 05, Summer Service 06, Appalachia 03)

docs.title: The barbershop
docs.text:
The office is a run-down, disused barbershop in Washington, five or six miles south of FBI headquarters. It is former Capitol Police property with asbestos, water damage and fifteen years without renovation, which the FBI had been using for document storage. The building has three floors. The ground floor is still the barbershop, with its chairs, washbasins and a radio; upstairs are a few administrative rooms, at first with one desk, a telephone and an IBM PC with a modem. The basement is behind a keypad-locked steel door, which Kurt attacks with luminol and a blacklight, and holds a Vietnam-era arsenal including M16s, napalm, an RPG and landmines. (Radford Horror 01)

By June 1992 there are desks, chairs and a struggling window air conditioner, and the lockup has gained flamethrowers, claymores and the captured flashlight weapon. By October, after Marblehead, the office has four window units, no roof leak, a front desk with a bell "downstairs in front of the barber stuff", and a stock of joke copies and posters of E.T., Alien and Close Encounters sent by colleagues; what Diane calls "the petty cash" is the drug money taken in Radford. On Christmas Eve 1992 Diane decorates it, the tree trips the breaker, and Kurt restores power from the neighbors' building. (Radford Horror 08, Appalachia 01, Roulet Estate 01)

See D.C. barbershop and PITF office.

docs.title: Cases
docs.text: Cases arrive by FBI courier as a file. By October 1992, Andre noted, the unit had handled about ten cases, most of which "washed out". (Appalachia 04) The first was picked because Radford is a hotspot on the Atolean Paranatural Index, which tracks sightings and disappearances per capita. Between cases, leads fizzle: disappearances where the person turns up, pirate radio "Scooby-Doo stuff". The Utah case walks in off the street when Alberta Wilmarth knocks on Andrew's door; Diane had been asking what to do about the "crazy people" coming by, and the team had agreed on a tip box. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 08, Walkers 01)

docs.title: Vehicles
docs.text:
• A black, ticket-covered 1961 Lincoln Continental with no air conditioning, the unit's original loan car. (Radford Horror 01)
  • The Biz's Buick Regal, used at Marblehead. After that case the EPA and NRC refuse to return the team's car and equipment. (Summer Service 01, Appalachia 01)
  • A nearly new 1991 Ford Explorer, issued once the unit is respected. (Appalachia 01)
  • In Utah, a rented Plymouth Voyager and then the loaner squad car Betsy. (Walkers 02, Walkers 04)

docs.title: The Radford Horror (May 1992)
docs.text: The first case, the disappearance of Amanda Lucky in Radford, Virginia, ends with the Radford Moth and a fight at a burning church that puts the whole team in the emergency room for a week. The sheriff closes the kidnapping case after two locals confess to abusing her. An unidentified cleanup crew got to the church before and after them. (Radford Horror 08)

docs.title: The Summer Service (June 1992)
docs.text:
Sent to Marblehead, Massachusetts after an EPA/USGS survey team vanished, the team finds the Sons of Adam, a parasite and a creature offshore, and ends the case with a tactical nuclear weapon, the Davy Crockett, obtained through Kurt's old contacts. Big Bill takes it to the Oval Office, a Navy submarine is lost, and the National Guard takes over the town. Big Bill's order is that the unit's real purpose stays in the classified report. (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04, Summer Service 06)

Three versions of Marblehead then exist: the classified report, the version the rest of the government gets (an extremist cult with nerve agent and a rogue nuclear device from the collapse of the Soviet Union), and a different public one. See Terrorist cover story. (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01)

docs.title: The Things in Appalachia (October 1992)
docs.text:
The unit is at its high point: the Bureau has stopped bullying it, the office is refurbished, and Andrew is formally a field agent. Kurt is questioned about Marblehead for a House subcommittee investigation, with Big Bill on one side of him and his CIA superior on the other. (Appalachia 01)

In Dahlonega, Georgia the team uncovers Jan Martense's gold-mining ring and its ape-men. It also becomes the center of the Clinton surveillance scandal, when the state police announce that the FBI is spying on candidate Bill Clinton and Andrew is identified on live television. Big Bill demands a full inventory of men and equipment and flies down. (Appalachia 07, Appalachia 08)

Quote

"Howard, don't fuck this up." (Andre as Big Bill, Appalachia 07)

Unrecorded session

The end of the Georgia case, Appalachia 10, was never recorded. Dialogue in Walkers 01 establishes that Jan was captured and is held at the CIA's Black Site Omaha, that the Spud Hut plant exploded, and that the Georgia State Police released the Biz's name.

docs.title: The Walkers in Skin (October to November 1992)
docs.text:
The fallout is handled at the top. Bush calls Andrew to the Oval Office and tells him he is "personally responsible for the survival of the United States of America". The FBI sends the Biz on television to deny everything, with Huell backstage; Kurt is ordered to stay away from the taping. The unit is now publicly known, as the FTIT, and recognized wherever it goes. (Walkers 01, Walkers 02)

Big Bill approves a trip to Utah ("It's your task force. If you think it's worth looking into, you know, be my guest") to exhume Shelly Wilmarth. The case at the Sherman Ranch becomes a war with the skinwalker faction of two towns, fought alongside the Utah National Guard. Andrew is killed and replaced during it, and comes back changed; see Andrew Howard (duplicate) and Andrew Howard (the Monstrous). (Walkers 01, Walkers 06, Walkers 09)

Roughly 300 to 400 people die across the two towns, at least 50 or 60 of them Guardsmen, in the team's second mass-casualty case in six months. Big Bill's cover story is a radical domestic insurgency. (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Disbandment (December 1992 to January 1993)
docs.text:
After 53 days of paperwork, on Christmas Eve, Big Bill comes to the office party with the news. President-elect Ross Perot believes the task force is a cover for Bush using the FBI against political enemies. He has asked Big Bill to resign, will disband and reassign the unit on Inauguration Day, and is forming his own task force for the "insurgency incidents". (Roulet Estate 01)

Officials take the team's files. On Inauguration Day 1993 the four agents, technically in limbo and not yet reassigned, wake up hungover in the Roulet house in Rhode Island with Diane asleep in the car, having driven there overnight talking about finding proof for Perot. When the Biz phones the FBI for backup and mentions his task force, the operator is "not familiar" with it. The case ends with the Biz and Huell shot at a pharmacy. (Roulet Estate 01, Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

By spring 1993 the unit no longer exists. Its cars and car phone have been taken back. Huell is on disability, Kurt is training other agencies at Quantico, Andrew is on desk duty in New York, Diane is in FBI records, Big Bill has been fired, and the Biz has vanished from his hospital bed into Russian custody. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: The Radford Horrors (April 1993)
docs.text:
Perot's replacement team, five career agents sent to Radford, disappears; see Missing FBI task force. Perot telephones Andrew himself. The new FBI Director, Rudy Giuliani, brings the old team back as consultants "strictly there for informational purposes", under the operational authority of Daniel Webster, with two goals: find the missing agents, and establish an "acceptable fact pattern" for the first Radford case. (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

The recalled team is Andrew, Kurt, Huell and Webster in Radford, with the Biz still in Moscow advising Boris Yeltsin. Within days it has a lawsuit pending over a standoff at a Safe Environment Fund fence, and Giuliani is telling Webster that running "lunatics in the field" is reckless. (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Standing
docs.text:
• Inside the Bureau. A punishment posting at the start, briefly respected after Marblehead, and a liability after Georgia. Andrew cannot be fired because his misdeeds are buried in classified cover-ups; colleagues run betting pools on whether he is blackmailing or sleeping with the Director. (Radford Horror 01, Appalachia 01, Roulet Estate 03)
  • With Big Bill. Protective and frequently furious. He retasks a submarine and sends the Guard for them, and pays for it with his job. (Summer Service 04, Roulet Estate 03)
  • With Bush. Started as a favor to his son; by the end he considers it essential. (Walkers 01)
  • With Perot. A political dirty-tricks unit to be shut down, and then the only people who know anything about Radford. The Biz privately expects Perot to axe it for good. (Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 01)
  • With Webster. He arrives believing it was Bush's political dirty-work unit, pronounces it the "worst political wetworks group I've ever... had the displeasure of dealing with", and soon admits its behavior fits no political conspiracy. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • With the public. Known through the Biz's television appearance and, in Robert Bigelow's words, as a "pretty interesting little task force" with "a lot of interesting stories" in its wake. (Walkers 02)
  • With FBI Counterintelligence. It surveilled the Biz at Marblehead over his money problems until Kurt told its agent that the unit was his to govern. (Summer Service 01)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Three task-force names are easy to confuse. The Foreign Influence Task Force is Big Bill's umbrella organization; the Paranatural Incident Task Force is Andrew's unit inside it; the Foreign Threat Investigation Task Force is the name the public knows. (Summer Service 03, Radford Horror 08, Walkers 01)
  • The first day's send-off comes back at the end of the arc, when a visitor leaves the office with "best of luck with the aliens". (Radford Horror 08)
  • Dante's proposed title for the disbandment episode was "The gang gets unemployed". (Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
The task force appears in every canon session.

  • The Radford Horror 01 to 08
  • The Summer Service 01 to 06
  • The Things in Appalachia 01 to 10
  • The Walkers in Skin 01 to 09
  • The Roulet Estate 01 to 03 (disbanded during this arc)
  • The Radford Horrors 01 to 04 (as recalled consultants)

docs.title: The Alien Faction
docs.text:
Non-canon

The Alien Faction belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Alien Faction is the largest cluster of entrants at the World Martial Arts Tournament briefing, a loose group of aliens who are friends and train together. Its spokesman is Moraniel. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type Organization (non-canon one-shot) Spokesman Moraniel Affiliation World Martial Arts Tournament entrants First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: After the briefing in the tent at the Athletes' Village, the entrants split into huddles. The aliens are the biggest group; the others include the Pure Human Martial Artists and a medium-sized group of wizards. Moraniel is in the middle of saying that "the reputation of the alien faction has been seriously compromised already," and the group wants "standards on who counts as an alien." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Members
docs.text: • Moraniel, the faction's spokesman. He questions Derk about what he is, decides he is a lost child and sends him back to his "state appointed" guardian.

docs.title: History
docs.text: Mirabeth sends Derk to chat with the faction. Moraniel asks whether he is human or an extraterrestrial and whether his parents know where he is, and he politely shoos Derk away once Derk mentions Mirabeth. On Derk's way out, a Superior roll of 6 lets him overhear one member saying "they are not sending their best" and another asking what happened to "that Gandekian," who "looks like someone stepped on him." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Animal Control
docs.text:
Non-canon

Animal Control belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

Animal Control is the agency the library calls about a "shaved baboon," which is Derk. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type Organization (non-canon one-shot) Aliases Child services (called alongside it) First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Library staff call both child services and Animal Control "just to cover our bases" after Derk eats just under half the snack table in the children's room of the Public Library, among crying toddlers. The responders arrive saying they "got a call about some kind of shaved baboon" and ask someone to point them to the baboon. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text: Mirabeth sends Derk off along the emergency-exit signs, tears the butcher-paper drawing off the floor and walks past Animal Control on her way out. During her debriefing, a grizzled detective asks whether she had anything to do with "an animal control call to a public library that ended in a riot." He says Animal Control "was sick of prank calls," and Mirabeth observes that there was no animal there. The riot is never explained. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.text: • Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Pure Human Martial Artists
docs.text:
Non-canon

The Pure Human Martial Artists belong to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Pure Human Martial Artists are the entrants who rely on technique and ki alone, and who plan to ally with the authorities so as to look like the stable, safe heroes. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type Organization (non-canon one-shot) Aliases Human martial artists Affiliation World Martial Arts Tournament entrants; later deputized alongside the Secret Service First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The group is strictly vanilla humans, with martial-arts technique and ki and nothing else. They argue that no pure human martial artist has ever taken over the world and killed the president, and that the president and his party have always preferred a defender like them to an outsider. Their strategy is to work with the police and the Secret Service, so that the tournament is not canceled and they cement themselves as "the stable, responsible heroes." They expect the other champions, the "freaks," to be shot by the Secret Service. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text: Mirabeth eavesdrops on them after the briefing, and they break off when they notice her ("Can I help you, Mirabeth?"). She says she has lost an earring. At the Presidential Event Hall the next morning, they are mixed in among the Secret Service, apparently deputized to protect the president. An older, heavyset woman monk among them recognizes Mirabeth and stares at her. After Mirabeth rolls a 12 on Pierce the Mask, the monk's shoulders slump, and she lets it pass and has a word with the other monks. Mirabeth also worries that they will deal with Ovain before she and Derk can. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Secret Service
docs.text:
Non-canon

This Secret Service belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The Secret Service protects the werewolf president in the one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable. (Philosopher's Fist)

Type Organization (non-canon one-shot) Protects The Werewolf President First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: After Ovain's outburst at the briefing, Colonel Sparago leaves to call the Secret Service. At the children's event the next morning, the Pure Human Martial Artists are mixed in among its agents, apparently deputized to help protect the president. They had expected the service to shoot the other champions on sight. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: History
docs.text: When Ovain attacks and Derk prepares another jump, Mirabeth raises a force field around herself and the president. The Secret Service has her move the field, herself and the president into one of the safe rooms, where she waits several hours before the state of emergency is called off. About eighteen hours of debriefing follow. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: World Martial Arts Tournament
docs.text:
Non-canon

The World Martial Arts Tournament belongs to the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable, not to the main campaign.

The World Martial Arts Tournament (WMAT) is the quinquennial contest at the heart of the world of Philosopher's Fist, a talent pipeline for superhumans whose grand prize is a few minutes with the Philosopher's Stone.

Type Organization (sporting event) Aliases WMAT Frequency Every five years Status Suspended over a doping scandal, possibly to be canceled First appearance Philosopher's Fist

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The tournament exists because aliens, androids or similar threats attack the planet once or twice a decade. It cultivates a supply of useful superhumans who can fight them: the enormously strong, psychics, ki-blast users, wizards and pure martial artists. Tryouts are open, so some four or five hundred people make it past the initial screening. (Philosopher's Fist)

Companies sponsor fighters in exchange for a share of the prize pool, and most fighters live on fixed incomes from their sponsors. Almost every entrant wears corporate branding. Mirabeth and Derk missed the paperwork deadline, though a dog-food company had shown interest in Derk. Matches are scored out of ten for style, effectiveness and diversity of technique unless there is a TKO, in a standard bracket by weight and power class. (Philosopher's Fist)

The grand prize is access to the Philosopher's Stone for a couple of minutes, usually used in a high-efficiency hospital setting. Derk enters to resurrect Fatty Gibbs. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: The champion problem
docs.text: Twice in the last forty years, a champion has taken over the world and killed the president, so the tournament is on thin ice and a matter of public controversy. Colonel Sparago says that champions usually wait until they win before turning, which is why the staff put sedatives in the victory punch, and that another dead president would end the tournament for good. The current werewolf president is moderately against the event and would not veto a ban passed by the World Congress. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Groups among the entrants
docs.text:
• The Alien Faction, the largest cluster at the safety briefing, whose spokesman is Moraniel.
  • Pure Human Martial Artists, who plan to ally with the authorities as the "safe" heroes.
  • Wizards, a medium-sized group of psychic and magical attackers, described as dim and barely literate outside the magic curriculum because they study eighteen hours a day in their formative years.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
The mandatory safety briefing takes place in a tent in the Athletes' Village with some four or five hundred sweaty entrants. Just as Sparago is about to dismiss them, an official announces that the tournament is suspended because of a doping scandal: one of the judges was found to be on steroids. The president has ordered a suspension until an investigation can be performed, so there will be no tournament for at least a few days, and it may be canceled. Mirabeth remarks that the president "was just looking for an excuse." Last year's champion Ovain then breaks down and attacks, and he later returns to attack the president's children's event. After the fight, Mirabeth tells Sparago she hopes to see him at next year's tournament, and he answers, "You know that I will." (Philosopher's Fist)

The one-shot gives two age limits: fifteen for the president's children's event and seventeen for entry in the tournament itself. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Radford Sheriff's Department
docs.text:
The Radford Sheriff's Department is the small, understaffed local law-enforcement agency of Radford, Virginia, and the task force's main local contact across both Radford arcs.

Type Local law enforcement Aliases Radford Sheriff's Office; sheriff's office; sheriff's station Headquarters The sheriff's station (with a small morgue and a broom-closet paper archive) Leaders Sheriff Frank Roosevelt; later Sheriff Molly Underhill Status Active (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The department serves a town of sixteen thousand and the surrounding metro area with a sheriff, one deputy, a patrolman and a secretary, and keeps its records on paper in a broom-closet archive. It is short on funds ("take it up with the taxpayers"), and the sheriff admits to "a little bit of a meth problem" (Radford Horror 02). Part-time volunteer deputies are called in for the search for Phoebe Augustine and for guard duty (Radford Horror 05). The department is cooperative and small-town, though the sheriff wants to run things "by the book" and is wary of the FBI at first (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Sheriff Frank Roosevelt: older, with a warm handshake. He wants ground rules set with the FBI and no "cowboy" behavior in his town, and he dislikes talk of UFOs (Radford Horror 01).
  • Molly Underhill: the deputy who verifies the team's credentials, handles radio contact, pulls files and delivers news of the body. She is promoted to sheriff by the time of The Radford Horrors (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horrors 02).
  • Harvey Mauden: the older coroner, who works in the station's small morgue (Radford Horror 05).

docs.title: The Radford Horror
docs.text:
• The team first phones the station from the Pay n' Stay; Deputy Underhill fetches the sheriff, who takes the call as "Sheriff Roosevelt." After he sets his ground rules, Molly confirms the team is legitimate (Radford Horror 01).
  • At the station the team reads the Radio Shack robbery file and finds the thick missing-dog folder in the paper archive; the sheriff's notes in it say "perverts," underlined (Radford Horror 02).
  • Molly's 4:30 a.m. call about Phoebe Augustine's disappearance sets off the search of the woods (Radford Horror 04).
  • The station's small morgue is the autopsy site. The department issues an APB on Abelforth Whateley and on the unmarked white van, and the sheriff imposes a curfew (Radford Horror 05).
  • The sheriff tells Andrew about a school truancy complaint against Dean Lawson and lends the team a squad car (Radford Horror 06).
  • The department dismantles the Whateley house top to bottom for forensic examination, and Molly promises to call the hospitals and send people on foot after the team reports trouble at the church (Radford Horror 07).
  • After the church fight the sheriff presents the official theory that Wilbur is a serial killer tied to "the cartel," reports that Dr. Lori and Derek Augustine confessed to inappropriate relationships with Amanda Lucky, and closes the kidnapping case (Radford Horror 08). See the cartel.

docs.title: The Radford Horrors
docs.text:
• Underhill is now sheriff after a "battlefield promotion": the old sheriff had a heart attack earlier in the year. She recaps the first case, supplies the missing-agents map, the lawyers' number and missing posters, and asks the team to look into the Safe Environment Fund (Radford Horrors 02).
  • She brings coffee, offers the team the unused mother-in-law suite in the back, and presents the Elizabeth George case, driving the team to the Douglas Pinball Emporium (Radford Horrors 03).
  • She identifies the homeless man as Billy Thornton, and says she has seen gray vans around town and assumed they were construction (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The sheriff is called "Frank" and "Sheriff Roosevelt" in the first episode but is often just "the sheriff" afterward (Radford Horror 01).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horror 01, 02, 04, 05, 06, 07, 08
  • Radford Horrors 02, 03, 04

docs.title: Local Rhode Island Police
docs.text:
The Local Rhode Island Police are the local officers who secure the Roulet crime scene near Exeter, issue an APB on the agents' stolen car, and lose an officer during the Brooks pharmacy siege.

Type Law enforcement Aliases Local police; uniforms; Exeter police Region Exeter and neighboring towns, Rhode Island Members Officer Todd; The Young Balding Cop; unnamed officers First appearance Roulet Estate 02

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The force is small and rural. Snow delays its backup at the pharmacy siege, and the squad car that took the call about the stolen car has a radio that does not work while the car is moving. (Roulet Estate 02, Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Roulet Estate 02
docs.text: After the agents call the FBI's DC office from the clown mansion, a chubby officer who was supposed to be on holiday break arrives at the Roulet House, inspects badges and the basement ("Yep, that's two corpses"), and promises to call the medical examiner and take statements. He asks for a description for an APB on the stolen car. Andrew hesitates, then describes it as shirtless, pale and bald. Moments after the officer leaves, Andrew realizes that the figure had nipples and shouts it across the room, and a passing officer gives a slow thumbs-up. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Roulet Estate 03
docs.text:
The next day the agents wait at the house hungover and drugged, while officers ask to see Andrew's FBI ID about four times. The agents had reported the murders only by police radio to a secretary at the force, who said she would relay it to the FBI; no reply has come. (Roulet Estate 03)

A young officer, the balding cop, drives them toward the Brooks Pharmacy, where he is shot dead. Todd surrenders command to Andrew. Two other cops behind their squad car decline to cross the lot, and Huell vows to get them fired. After the siege, officers arrive in force, cut leg holes in a big fluffy winter hat so the naked Kurt has something to cover himself with, rip off the gunman's mask and arrange for his pills. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Roulet Estate 02
  • Roulet Estate 03

docs.title: Roosevelt Police Department
docs.text:
The Roosevelt Police Department is the small-town police force of Roosevelt, Utah, which lends the team its car Betsy, forces a false confession out of Yusuf Ansari, and is later massacred and replaced by skinwalkers.

Type Organization (local police) Aliases Roosevelt PD; Roosevelt Police Base Roosevelt police station Notable members Officer Hernandez; an eager young officer; Carl ("Ham") Status Destroyed in the offscreen massacre before Walkers 08 First appearance Walkers 04

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The department is small. At the scene of the wrecked rental car, five cops handle the traffic jam, some of them in different uniforms, which suggests outside officers were brought in (Walkers 04). The station's interrogation room doubles as the lunchroom (Walkers 06). Andre put Roosevelt's population at about six thousand (Walkers 04).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Officer Hernandez. Took charge at the wreck and, after looking at Howard's FBI identification, waived the tickets and arranged the loaner squad car Betsy (Walkers 04).
  • The eager young officer. Starstruck by the team, and frightened of being sent back to "the burger hut"; he leaks the junkyard lead and later phones Andrew about the confession (Walkers 05). The episodes never say whether he is Hernandez.
  • Carl. A hungover cop who says only "Ham", microwaves Canadian bacon, and eats Lucky Charms from a paper coffee cup (Walkers 06). He is distinct from FBI agent Carl Gardner.

docs.title: The wrecked car (Walkers 04 and 05)
docs.text: Officers struggled to clear the pancaked rental from East Lagoon Street, and a tow truck had to come from Duchesne (Walkers 04). The wreck then sat in the station garage. The department said it had a manhunt under way and named a local junkyard owner with a car crusher, a magnetic crane, several priors and no alibi (Walkers 05). Kurt urged the officer to match the physical evidence before trusting any confession.

docs.title: The false confession (Walkers 05 and 06)
docs.text: The junkyard owner, Yusuf Ansari, confessed after the police questioned him. Yusuf told the team the police had threatened immigration trouble and said that if he confessed it would be just a fine of $10,000 with no immigration problems. He then said he had not crushed the car: the crusher does not flatten them that much, and the magnetic lifter does not move (Walkers 06). The decision on whether to press charges was deferred.

docs.title: The massacre (Walkers 08)
docs.text:
By the time the team returned, every officer in the station had been shot dead, each missing a small body part removed after death, usually a finger, in one case an ear. The receptionist's pointer finger was gone. The armory was empty, and the basement generator had been cut and smashed. The only living person found in the cells was Yusuf, who had been shot, played dead under a pile of bodies and woken to find his little toe cut off (Walkers 08).

As the team left the station, a group of people in police uniforms approached it, and the bridge blockade was manned by about twenty to twenty-five heavily armed people, most dressed as cops (Walkers 08). See Skinwalker faction and Bridge blockade.

docs.title: The station afterwards (Walkers 09)
docs.text: Donald McManley, his interns and wounded Guardsmen waited at the station, where they had been helping with autopsies, while the team went to the community center; the team picked them up on the way out (Walkers 09).

  • Walkers 05
  • Walkers 06
  • Walkers 08
  • Walkers 09 (station only)

docs.title: Russian government
docs.text:
The Russian government is the set of officials, guards, doctors and soldiers around President Boris Yeltsin that first holds the Biz as a captive in Moscow and then, in The Radford Horrors, treats him as a trusted foreign adviser on the paranatural.

Type National government and military Aliases Yeltsin's people; Russian military; security forces; the Biz's captors Leader President Boris Yeltsin Notable members The Biz's rotating guards, a colonel who travels with the president, military doctors Status Active (as of Radford Horrors 04) First appearance Radford Horrors 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The Biz has been held in Russia for months. His earlier captors, who kicked him and questioned him about Bill Clinton, are long gone, and the newer, much friendlier ones want to know only about aliens (Radford Horrors 01). He is confined to a room in the Hotel Metropol with a polite guard always present. See also the Biz's guards and the Hotel Metropol.

docs.title: Radford Horrors 01
docs.text:
The Biz's guard cries at the telenovela Los ricos también lloran and eats the borscht the Biz rejected. A higher-ranking officer summons the Biz to the president's opera box, and he sits beside Yeltsin in the Metropol's opera house. Yeltsin explains that Soviet detectors spiked in the cosmic microwave background last year and triangulated to the Marblehead incident. He unwraps a broken, half-melted copy of the team's flashlight weapon, taken from a man in very dark, welding-style sunglasses (Radford Horrors 01). The Biz also explains skinwalkers to him, and Yeltsin compares them to Koschei the Deathless; see Skinwalkers.

Yeltsin states his central fear: "I have faith in my military officers, but I do not have faith that my military officers are my military officers." He says Russia is "developing a test," and he is meeting the Biz in person for that reason. He also asks about Andrew Howard and whether the Biz is a communist (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: Radford Horrors 03
docs.text: Before dawn a Russian officer, whom the guard recognizes as a colonel who works closely with the president and often travels with him, takes the Biz to the presidential convoy for a trip to an "unusual aircraft crash in Oryol Oblast." Yeltsin calls the Biz "Richard." The convoy is ambushed (see the convoy ambushers); the Biz saves the concussed president and a Russian helicopter flies both away (Radford Horrors 03).

docs.title: Radford Horrors 04
docs.text: The Biz wakes in a hospital room on an evacuated floor with four armed guards outside. A guard who watched him at the hotel escorts him to a sutured but gracious Yeltsin, who says he understands the Biz may have saved his life and that intelligence thinks the attack was "opportunistic. And fairly half-assed." The Biz is flown to the Oryol crash site, where the army has put a tent over a partly excavated triangular craft. Inside, doctors have the crash survivor tubed to a Russian soldier. Asked why he is here, the survivor says "Survey," then "Not aliens. The opposite of aliens," and finally "Servitors... need resources." The doctors warn that pushing him further is very risky, so Yeltsin ends the interrogation (Radford Horrors 04). See also Servitors.

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes do not reveal what Yeltsin's "test" for replaced officers is, what Russia does with the crash site, or why the president takes the Biz so far into his confidence.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Yeltsin calls the Biz "Richard" once, although the character is Dick Baxter; when a guard starts to do the same in the next episode, Andre corrects it to "Mr. Baxter" (Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04).
  • Andre played real opera audio during the Yeltsin scene (Radford Horrors 01).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text:
• Radford Horrors 01
  • Radford Horrors 03
  • Radford Horrors 04

docs.title: Russian intelligence
docs.text:
Russian intelligence is the Russian agency that reaches the Biz through a fake phone sweepstakes line during the Marblehead case, using a book cipher to tell him that two submarines have been lost near Massachusetts.

Type Organization (foreign intelligence service) Affiliation Russia (the Biz is later shown in contact with Boris Yeltsin) First appearance Summer Service 04

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Russian intelligence appears only once, as a recorded voice on a payphone. The Biz's instructions required a particular 1980 reprint of Moby-Dick, which he did not carry, so he spent part of the day finding the right edition at the independent bookstore Readful Things (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: The sweepstakes message
docs.text:
About four hours after the team returned to the hotel, the Biz sent everyone out of the room and walked to a payphone farther from the hotel than the nearest one. He had already completed the first step of the procedure, leaving a request for information. The recorded voice welcomed him to the "Miss Finn Amy[?] promotional sweepstakes" (the name is garbled in the recording) and read out a list of winning numbers beginning "178, 14, 97, 325", ending with "Best of luck! Everyone's a winner!" After about ten minutes of decoding against the book, the Biz had the message: "Two secret[?] submarine lost near Massachusetts. Cause unknown. Instructions to follow soon." The word "secret" is hard to make out in the recording (Summer Service 04). The method is described on the Moby-Dick book cipher page.

The Biz took the message as confirmation that the Russians were probably not behind the Marblehead events, since, as Ezra put it, "They also lost submarines." He was unsure whether he could share the information with the rest of the team (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Context
docs.text: Earlier in the arc, the fisherman Briggs blamed "the goddamn Russians" for the blast, and the Biz joked that the Russians could not do anything to the team that they were not already doing to themselves (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Appearances
docs.text: • Summer Service 04

docs.title: Safe Environment Fund
docs.text:
The Safe Environment Fund (SEF) is a nominally environmental research and advocacy group that buys and fences off large stretches of the woods around Radford, Virginia, protecting them with armed guards, lawyers and a professionally cleaned site.

Type Front organization (apparent) Aliases SEF Activities Land purchase, fencing, private security, legal intimidation Key site Safe Environment Fund fenced site Status Active (as of Radford Horrors 04); true purpose unknown First appearance Radford Horrors 02

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The SEF presents itself as an environmental research group and buys woods around Radford, enclosing them with eight-foot chain-link and barbed wire wrapped in a polymer privacy screen printed "Safe Environment Fund / No trespassers." Its sites have motion-triggered "solar light" alarms, construction equipment, locked shipping containers and a locked temporary building, and are patrolled by armed security on ATVs and by lawyers who film intruders (Radford Horrors 02). The land was long held by the university and local companies, who let hikers use it, until the SEF purchases (Radford Horrors 02). The diner waitress ties the gray vans to a local "right to roam" dispute over the woods (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Cold open
docs.text: The cold open of Radford Horrors 02 shows figures in blue gloves and bunny suits combing the woods in a grid while a helicopter circles. A worker holds out a blood-streaked handgun, a suited supervisor bags it, and the camera pans across a barbed-wire fence to reveal the SEF logo (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: The standoff at the fence
docs.text:
Sheriff Molly Underhill asks the team to deal with the SEF, and also warns that "scary lawyers" threatened anyone investigating the disappearances (Radford Horrors 02). Following the missing agents' map, the team reaches the new fence, which joins an older fence matching a polygon on the map. The team reasons the new fence was added after the agents vanished. Armed guards on ATVs arrive; Daniel Webster shouts "FBI!" and is tased, Kurt fires a burst into the air, Andrew shoots a guard in the leg, and the guard shoots Andrew in the chest, but the bullet slows and stops an inch from him. A radio voice claiming to speak for the property owner orders the team off, says lawyers and emergency response are coming, and later orders the guards to stand down (Radford Horrors 02).

The lawyers follow and film the team, repeatedly asking whether it has a warrant, and refuse to comment on the smell of bleach. At the "scribble" site Kurt finds a thoroughly professional cleanup: many people trampled through, a bleach smell, dug-up ground, a tree cut down and removed that day, and luminol showing nothing at all. He scrapes pearlescent goo from a branch; see pearlescent goo. The team is escorted out and the gate is locked behind them (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Fallout
docs.text: FBI Director Rudy Giuliani warns of a Bivens lawsuit over the fence incident and a possible reprimand. The tasing guard has already been fired (Radford Horrors 03). In Radford Horrors 04 Giuliani says he already has a man looking into the SEF. The team suspects the SEF is linked to the gray van crew, since the vans arrived with it, and the opalescent slime found on an SEF tree turns up again above the emporium window (Radford Horrors 04).

docs.title: Unresolved
docs.text: The episodes never establish who funds the SEF, what its locked containers and building hold, or whether it employs the gray van crew. The "scary lawyers" who threatened earlier investigators are not explicitly tied to the fund, though lawyers on the SEF site film the team and demand a warrant (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Dante regrets that the SEF's electric fence was "not on" during the standoff (Radford Horrors 04).
  • Webster, out of character, notes that shooting the guards makes the team unlikely allies for any political conspiracy, and that nobody has mentioned Clinton, the Bushes or the Kennedys (Radford Horrors 02).

docs.title: Skinwalker faction
docs.text:
The Skinwalker faction is the organized group of skinwalker copies that holds most of Ballard, Utah, massacres the Roosevelt police, steals every car, runs the bridge blockade and hoards supplies at the community center.

Type Organization (hostile) Aliases Ballard faction; body snatcher faction; the cult; Skinwalker community of Roosevelt; fake police Members Skinwalkers; the mayor (Wilford Hiram); the double of Andrew Howard Base Ballard, then the community center Status Main force stranded and crushed in Walkers 09; some copies and pilots escaped First appearance Walkers 07

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: The faction is never given a name in the show. The players called it "the cult" and suspected a religious cult, a Mormon theory with no evidence behind it, until the autopsy in Walkers 08 showed the members were piloted copies. After the gym scene in Walkers 07, Andre privately briefed Rita, who from then on played the replica of Andrew Howard. The briefing said the faction controlled about 60% of Ballard, was nearly ready to drop pretenses, cloned people from tissue, commanded animals and armed townspeople, and worried that the outsiders could bring real reinforcements.

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Copies of townspeople, including the mayor, the copies seen in the gym, and the "fake police".
  • The double of Andrew Howard, who rejoins the team in Andrew's place.
  • Skinwalker Huell.
  • Horses and coyotes acting on their behalf: Upright horses and Upright coyotes.

docs.title: Quiet replacement (before Walkers 07)
docs.text: By the time the team arrived, the sheriff reported more than half the high school student body absent, houses empty for days and attendance records showing nothing wrong (Walkers 06). The theft of every recording and three employees from Bigelow's ranch happened the same night as the gym ambush (Walkers 07). See Disappearances in Ballard.

docs.title: Open action (Walkers 07 and 08)
docs.text:
After the gym, the faction massacred the Roosevelt police station and stole all drivable cars, sabotaging the rest by hand: batteries taken, wires and belts cut, tires slashed, and sugar put in gas tanks (Walkers 08). Three men in maintenance uniforms came to find the substation keys; see Utah cleanup crew. A blockade of about twenty to twenty-five heavily armed people, most dressed as police, turned traffic back at the bridge, including a FedEx truck; see Bridge blockade.

The team concluded that the outside world was probably normal, that Ballard was lost, and that Roosevelt was being replaced person by person, starting with the police.

docs.title: The stronghold and the evacuation (Walkers 09)
docs.text: A cold open showed hundreds of cars piled inside the fence of the community center, with armed, mostly naked townspeople hauling supplies. The copies fought the National Guard force, with Ned Simpson's killdozer grinding through them, then carried tanks of blood with creatures down the shaft to the portal. When the cavern's power failed and Huell's grenade struck the support machinery, fifty to sixty copies were stranded in the dark; the community center collapsed into a sinkhole (Walkers 09).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Rita's secret turn as the replica begins at the end of the gym scene in Walkers 07, when Andre breaks off and hands her a private handout, telling her she is now playing a replica. No duplicate of Andrew appears in Walkers 06.

docs.title: Sons of Adam
docs.text:
The Sons of Adam are the millenarian, ocean-obsessed church that dominates Marblehead, Massachusetts, with its own Bible, a worm-filled communion wine and a congregation that includes the town's selectmen, its police chief and its hotel clerk.

Type Organization (church; the task force calls it a cult) Aliases The church; Shaw's church; the Marblehead church; the cult; the worm cult Leader Amos Shaw at first; later the Mayor of Marblehead preaches in his place Base The colonial church; the seal also hangs in Marblehead town hall Status The National Guard takes control of the town in Summer Service 06 First appearance Radford Horror 08 (the Bible); Summer Service 01 (the congregation)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
The name "Sons of Adam" is not spoken as the church's name in the early sessions. It first appears on the self-published Bible offered at the Ram and Arms Inn (Radford Horror 08), and later on the huge seal on the rear wall of the selectmen's meeting room, which shows Jesus standing amid parted waters (Summer Service 04).

The church's Bible is thick with additional material. It places the Garden of Eden on a sunken land bridge between India and Madagascar (see Lemuria), insists that continental drift is false, and teaches that on Judgment Day everyone will physically return to Eden (Summer Service 01). Shaw preaches on the seven-headed beast from the sea and tells his congregation that angels are terrifying monsters constructed by God to wipe out sin, and that good things are not the same as nice things. He argues that Noah's "floodgates of heaven" imply a source of holy water, that the world comes from water and returns to water, and asks, "Was Christ not himself a fisherman?" (Summer Service 01). At the selectmen's meeting, the board speaks of the second coming as imminent and describes the sickness in town as the devil being forced into the open as "game day" approaches (Summer Service 04); see Second coming and eschaton.

docs.title: Practices
docs.text:
• Services. The church holds three services a day. The team attends one at nine in the evening in the first session and one at 7 a.m. in the third (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03). The fisherman Briggs says the congregation baptizes about forty white-clad people and babies in the sea, speaks in tongues and disapproves of alcohol (Summer Service 01).
  • Communion. Communion is wine only, called the "Blood of the Lamb" (the replacement priest in Summer Service 03 says "Blood of Christ"). It tastes fishy, and Shaw calls it "a local variety". Under McManley's microscope it is swimming with worms, and the congregation drinks it three times a day (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03). See Communion wine and The worms.
  • The glow. Regular churchgoers gain a healthy glow. In an advanced form the skin turns pale, translucent and bloated (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04); see The glow.
  • Reach into private life. Esteban complains that his uncle, a church member who volunteers to take the family laundry to the laundromat, has been putting bean juice in it (Summer Service 04).
  • Arms. Armed congregants turn out during the storm. Separately, the team is told that a shipment of illegal M16s bound for a Marblehead citizen has been intercepted (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Amos Shaw, the preacher, "Mr. Shaw, not Father"; about sixty and built like a bodybuilder. His house is found wrecked, but he later sits at the selectmen's table (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04).
  • Jester, the hotel clerk, described by Shaw as "very devout", who sits on the board as "J. Evans, businessman".
  • The Mayor of Marblehead, who takes the pulpit in Shaw's place in Summer Service 03.
  • The Chief of Police, Horace Cromwell the banker and Arnold Weathers, all members of the eleven-seat Board of Selectmen. Ten seats are occupied at the meeting; the empty one is Weathers'.
  • The Marblehead police, who act with the armed congregation at the hotel (Summer Service 05).
  • Ordinary townspeople, including business leaders and fishermen (Summer Service 01), and the "worm bags" of the final session (Worm bags).

docs.title: Radford Horror 08
docs.text: The innkeeper at the Ram and Arms offers the team a King James Bible, a Gideon's Bible or "the local flavor", the Sons of Adam Bible, which he highly recommends (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Summer Service 01
docs.text: The team attends the evening service. Huell drinks all of the wine, Kurt only pretends to finish his, and afterward Shaw gently scolds the Biz for swearing ("God's house"). When Kurt asks about the wine, Shaw answers that it is a local variety, and a flicker of reaction crosses his face (Summer Service 01).

docs.title: Summer Service 03
docs.text: Shaw is missing from the 7 a.m. service. A new priest, whose skin has gone translucent and slightly swollen, preaches against doubt and the secular world, watches Andrew as he takes communion, and says "Blood of Christ." Andrew holds the wine in his mouth and spits it into a bottle outside; the priest does not believe she swallowed it (Summer Service 03).

docs.title: Summer Service 04
docs.text: The team attends the selectmen's meeting and learns that the board is the church in civic dress. The new priest from the previous session turns out to be the mayor, and Shaw sits at the table too. The mayor insists that the scientists left on their own and that Satan causes the sickness (Summer Service 04).

docs.title: Summer Service 05
docs.text: After the meeting a silent man in a suit watches the team from the parking lot in the rain. At about 4 a.m. armed congregants and the police surround the hotel, and the team escapes with the Davy Crockett and the RV. Madeline Weathers vows to "burn that fucking church to the ground", and Kurt asks her to wait until any surviving scientists are accounted for. Kurt also tells a contact that the church is infecting people with the worms intentionally and en masse (Summer Service 05).

docs.title: Summer Service 06
docs.text: A convoy of infected locals, with Jester at the wheel of one vehicle, heads for the nuclear plant. In the debriefing the team tells the Guard that a religious terrorist group is responsible, citing the murals in City Hall and literature about returning to the ocean, and says the group seeded the local food supply with a parasite (Summer Service 06). See Terrorist cover story.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The episodes never establish whether the congregation knowingly spread the worms or was itself infected and led by them, or where the worms came from. The team's terrorist account in Summer Service 06 is a simplified story told to the military.

docs.title: Spud Hut
docs.text:
Spud Hut (also Spud Hut America, SHA) is a Dahlonega-based stuffed-potato restaurant chain whose distribution center fronted an illegal gold mine worked by ape-men.

Type Corporation, fast-food chain Aliases The Spud Hut; Spud Hut America; SHA; Spud Hut Corporate; SHGRDC; Shugrid Headquarters Dahlonega, Georgia Key people Jan Martense (manager) Status Plant destroyed by an explosion after the finale (as of Walkers 01) First appearance Radford Horrors 04 (mention); Appalachia 01 (in person)

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Spud Hut is a regional Southern chain, which Andre compared to Buc-ee's, whose menu covers nearly every cuisine in a potato. It has a liquor license, a cryptogram secret menu, and about 100 numbered specials, which Andre said were AI-generated with some human tuning (Appalachia 02; Appalachia 07). See the Spud Hut menu. The company guarantees that its potatoes are "never touched by human hands" (Appalachia 08).

The original Spud Hut is a tiny walk-up window in Dahlonega with a neon potato sign wider than the building. The Regional Distribution Center is the town's main employer, and employees wear mandatory gray uniforms (Appalachia 02).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Jan Martense, manager of the distribution center and head of the gold-mining operation.
  • Aaron Richters, an employee who went missing (Appalachia 03).
  • The Spud Hut counter savant, a worker with perfect recall who says "The Spud Hut changed my life" (Appalachia 02).
  • A corporate financial auditor (unnamed), who met the party for lunch (Appalachia 06).
  • Clyde Harvard, the accountant who knew of the mine, named by Jan (Walkers 01).
  • Clive, the ape-men's handler, and Jan's other conspirators; see Jan's Conspiracy.

docs.title: History
docs.text:
Later references. In Radford Horrors 04, Dante's character jokes that Spud Hut was a deal "thanks to the ape-man," and the players recall the earlier case as a humanzee gold-mining operation run from a potato restaurant (Radford Horrors 04).

Suspicion. The team first heard of the chain when a McDonald's clerk recommended the original Spud Hut (Appalachia 01). Around forty company trucks passed the party on the road, a number the players found unreasonable (Appalachia 02). In Appalachia 03 the players suspected illegal mining, dirt hauling or bioweapons. In Appalachia 04 a Covenant member told the party that runoff from the Spud Hut plant drained into the river where the Covenant bathed (Appalachia 04).

The dirt trucks. A wrecked company truck carried bags marked "Potatoes" that held dirt, and a tracking device etched "Inventory Control, SHA Tracking" was found in bear vomit (Appalachia 07). The Spud Hut truck page covers the wreck. The party had avoided Spud Hut Corporate for months before planning a visit.

The plant visit. In Appalachia 08 the team toured the squat concrete plant while a Fox 5 Atlanta crew waited outside. They found cage-style elevators with no floor indicators and a locked Special Projects level, and were sent to wait in a "break room" (keycode 441) that held ape-creatures (Appalachia 08).

The finale. Beneath the plant, a tunnel network linked to the Dahlonega Gold Mines. Clive explained that a planned stuffed-pepper expansion had left an unused part of the facility, which Jan declared an "R&D" department, and that the company had begun an internal investigation into the disappearing dirt (Appalachia 09). The episodes never establish whether anyone above Jan knew; the only other insider Jan names is the accountant Clyde Harvard.

Aftermath. The finale was never recorded. In Walkers 01, Kurt tells Jan that the Spud Hut corporate facility exploded shortly after Jan fled, and offers the theory that someone piped explosive gas in from an adjacent cavern. Kurt also arranges a CIA job for the savant teen from the Spud Hut.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • The chain's Georgia plant is variously abbreviated SHGRDC and nicknamed "Shugrid."

docs.title: Utah cleanup crew
docs.text:
The Utah cleanup crew is a group of three skinwalkers in gray maintenance uniforms, armed and carrying plastic sheeting and bungee cords, whom the team confronts outside the Roosevelt police station.

Type Organization (three-man squad) Aliases maintenance-uniform men; cleanup crew Affiliation Skinwalker faction Status One killed, two captured; their pilots fled into the ceiling First appearance Walkers 08

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: While the team was inside the station, they saw three men in gray maintenance uniforms looking over the team's cars in the parking lot. The men claimed they needed the substation keys kept at the station. When told they would be searched, one drew a gun (Walkers 08). Their utility bags held guns, plastic sheeting and bungee cords, like the sheet plastic on the bodies in the gym ceiling at Ballard High School, which the team read as a cleanup crew.

docs.title: The firefight (Walkers 08)
docs.text:
Kurt drew fast enough that the gunman's shot went wide, and shot him through the arm. The replica Andrew, played by Rita, rolled a 3, panicked, shattered a window of Betsy with a stray round, and was hit in the shoulder (see Andrew Howard (duplicate)). The gunman was shot dead with a head wound that McManley later swabbed and the team credited to the Biz, while the other two ran. Kurt rammed them with Betsy against the wrought-iron parking-lot gates and restrained them. Both stayed silent, and Andre said that "the facade of acting like a person has just completely dropped away" (Walkers 08).

Donald McManley examined the survivors, who had a slightly high body temperature, irregular pupils and bad teeth. The dead man's autopsy showed no stomach, about eight feet of intestine, a small fatty liver and green fluid in the head wound, and his skull held a non-human brain-like organ; see Pilot and host biology and Pilot organ in Tupperware. Later the two prisoners were slumped and empty-headed, and a flashlight through an eye showed light at the back of the mouth: their pilots had fled into the drop ceiling.

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• Kurt fetched a bone saw from the morgue in a trash-bag suit and showered afterwards in the locker room, smelling of Old Spice and cadaver (Walkers 08).
  • In Roulet Estate 01 Rita (as Andrew) wonders whether the team was lured out there by "whoever did the cleanup after in Utah". The episode does not connect this to the three men; compare Hazmat cleanup teams.
