docs.title: UTAW
docs.text:
UTAW (Unorthodox Tactics and Warfare) is the fictional division of the CIA in which Kurt Larson served before he was loaned to the FBI, and the source of most of his stranger skills and stories.

Type Organization (CIA division) Aliases Unorthodox Tactics and Warfare; "unorthodox tactics and weapons division"; "my unit" Parent CIA Known members Kurt Larson (former) Motto "Anything done in defense of the American people is legal" (unofficial) First appearance Mentioned in Radford Horror 01; never seen

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: UTAW never appears. Everything known about it comes from Kurt, usually as a one-line explanation of why he knows how to do something alarming, and much of it is tall tale. Its reputation precedes it: when Kurt introduces himself to the FBI in Salt Lake City as CIA, "UTAW division", agent Carl Gardner has "heard of those boys, you know, explode the cigars and all that". (Radford Horror 01, Walkers 02)

docs.title: Name
docs.text: Kurt first mentions the unit on the task force's first morning, and when a colleague hears it as "Utah" he spells it out: "unorthodox tactics and weapons division". At the end of the Marblehead case Dante gives the same expansion, "Unorthodox Tactics and Weapons", and then corrects it: "Oh, Tactics and Warfare." The corrected form is used here. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 06)

docs.title: Motto
docs.text:
Kurt gives the unit's motto, which he admits is unofficial, as the team limps away from Marblehead.

Quote

"Just always keep in your heart UTAW's motto: anything done in defense of the American people is legal." (Dante as Kurt, Summer Service 06)

He repeats it in Georgia with one word changed.

Quote

"Just remember, anything done in service to the American people is legal. At least that's what they always told me in my unit." (Dante as Kurt, Appalachia 03)

docs.title: What UTAW did
docs.text:
All of the following is Kurt's account.

  • Animal weapons. "We were on the cutting edge, man: bombs on bats, dolphins, dogs, gerbils, rats, cats, frisbees", and boomerangs. His conclusion is that it was a bad idea and that any plan with moving parts around an animal falls apart; Andre calls this "the voice of experience with hundreds of failed bat bombs". (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 04)
  • Directed energy. It never had anything like the flashlight weapon, to Kurt's lasting resentment: "You know what I could have done to Castro with that heat ray?" (Radford Horror 04)
  • Castro. Exploding cigars, by reputation. (Walkers 02)
  • Drugs and training. "LSD live-fire" exercises, which Dante says were part of his original pitch for the character; crews kept in sleep shifts; and training "not to jump to conclusions, but instead maintain a possibility space of potential likelihoods". (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 04)
  • The occult. "Psychic dream exercises", and a tulpa summoning with LSD involved that Kurt thinks may have worked. He later insists that "we never successfully summoned a tulpa" and that "you're not allowed to"; when Zack reminded the table that Kurt tried to make one, Dante answered, "Tried nothing. Carl is dead." (Radford Horror 04, Appalachia 06, Walkers 01, Radford Horrors 03)
  • Paperwork. "We burned half the paperwork, but, like, what didn't get burned was mostly fine." (Walkers 01)

docs.title: In the field
docs.text:
Kurt uses UTAW methods throughout the campaign. After the dusk event in Utah he runs a few quick safety checks "in UTAW fashion", starting by throwing some trash out of the car window. (Walkers 03)

He also uses it as a yardstick. Examining a dead man in a Chewbacca costume in Georgia, he checks the body for armor, finds none and rules out his old unit: "he's not UTAW, he's not one of my boys. So that's one whole theory crossed off." (Appalachia 06)

Quote

"Kinda narrows it down to pervert, doesn't it?" (Dante as Kurt, Appalachia 06)

In Utah he offers to recruit a promising local kid: "UTAW could reach out. Always need free thinkers." (Walkers 03)

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text:
• UTAW is heard as "Utah" both times its name is explained. In the Marblehead finale Andre asks "Is that Utah's motto?", and Ezra agrees that it is probably not the motto of the state. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 06)
  • Zack's reaction to the motto was that it sounded like "more of a CIA thing". (Appalachia 03)
  • Asked how many of his people would wear a Chewbacca costume, Kurt says it comes up: "We do birthday parties... we got Guevara." (Appalachia 06)
  • Rita, on a mystery about a house's water supply: "That's UTAW's problem." (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Whateley family
docs.text:
The Whateley family is a churchgoing Radford household of four, Yobiah, Irene and their identical twin sons Abe and Wilbur, whose house holds a shrine-like bedroom, a butterfly collector's room and a hidden cellar, and is where the Radford Moth was first raised.

Type Family Aliases The Whateleys Members Yobiah Whateley, Irene Whateley, Abelforth "Abe" Whateley, Wilbur Whateley Residence Whateley house Status Irene reported dead and Abe presumed dead; Wilbur in custody (as of Radford Horror 08) First appearance Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Before the team arrives, the sheriff describes the Whateleys as a family that has seen a great deal of tragedy: one twin vanished after a computer-store robbery, the other had a breakdown and a car accident and has been in a vegetative state ever since, and then the mother walked off into the woods (Radford Horror 02). They go to church every Sunday. The family lives in a cookie-cutter subdivision less than a mile from the Luckys (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: Members
docs.text:
• Yobiah Whateley: Irene's husband, a big man of about sixty. After Irene walks away he sits on the couch and says he thought she was chasing a coyote (Radford Horror 02).
  • Irene Whateley: the mother. She was treated by Dr. Lori for depression after her son's accident (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02).
  • Abelforth "Abe" Whateley: a space and UFO obsessive. Three years before, he threw a cinder block through a Radio Shack window in a homemade Mercury-replica spacesuit and took a bus to Richmond; see the Radio Shack robbery (Radford Horror 02).
  • Wilbur Whateley: Abe's identical twin and a butterfly and insect collector. He was in a car accident at fifteen, after his brother vanished, and sits in a wheelchair by his window (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: The disappearance of Irene
docs.text: Irene stood at the kitchen's panoramic window making dinner, saw something, dropped her pan and walked out into the woods. Two sets of footprints, one apparently following the other, lead a dozen feet into the trees before the ground cover swallows them. Her disappearance is investigated alongside the Amanda Lucky case (Radford Horror 02).

docs.title: The house
docs.text:
In the house, the Biz finds Abe's room, untouched since he vanished and covered in space and UFO paraphernalia, including a big shuttle poster, with a hundred-odd dollars hidden in a hollowed-out book. Wilbur's room holds his butterflies (Radford Horror 02).

During the stakeout in Radford Horror 06, Huell tackles a figure in an Apollo-style spacesuit in the woods and pulls off the helmet to reveal one of the Whateley boys. Later the team bolt-cuts the cellar doors beneath the garage and finds, in the dark root cellar, bare feet hanging two inches off the floor: a withered corpse in a NASA T-shirt, nailed to the wall by the wrists and ankles. The team photographs it, and Wilbur's bedroom window is found open and the boy gone (Radford Horror 06).

docs.title: The solution
docs.text: After the church fight, the sheriff's theory is that the cellar body is probably Abelforth, killed around April 17th; that Wilbur is a serial killer who faked his brother's departure; and that Mrs. Whateley's body was found in the back of the church, crucified, burned and disemboweled. DNA and dental tests are pending (Radford Horror 08). Wilbur's journal records finding a larva in the woods by the old-town church on June 3rd, a voice in his head, and "She hatched hungry. The dog is dead" on August 15th. Its April 16th to 18th entries describe moving the dog to the old church and "I did something," which the team lines up with Abe's disappearance. The team concludes that the moth influenced Wilbur (Radford Horror 08). See also the Radford Moth and the moth life cycle.

docs.title: Afterward
docs.text:
Months later, Sheriff Underhill reports that Wilbur is in a mental hospital in Roanoke, "either being catatonic or pretending to be," and that the sheriff's office believes he faked his catatonia all along (Radford Horrors 02).

Unresolved

The cellar body is never confirmed on screen to be Abelforth: the sheriff calls it "probably Abelforth," pending DNA and dental tests. Irene was found crucified, burned and disemboweled; who or what did it is not established (Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Trivia
docs.text: • Yobiah is called "Josiah" in his first scene. Andre once slipped and called Abelforth "Albert" and the Whateley boys "Lucky boys" (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 08).

docs.title: Cast and players
docs.text: PITF is played by one game master and four regular players, with a handful of guests who sit in on the call. This page lists who plays whom and which sessions each person is heard in.

docs.title: The regular cast
docs.text:
Player Role Characters Recorded sessions Andre Game master (Keeper) Every NPC, monster and narrator voice All 37 canon sessions and the one-shot Rita Player Andrew Howard; briefly his duplicate; Mirabeth in the one-shot All 37 canon sessions and the one-shot Dante Player Kurt Larson; Derk in the one-shot All 37 canon sessions and the one-shot Ezra Player Dick "The Biz" Baxter; Daniel Webster All 37 canon sessions Zack Player Huell Kendrick All 37 canon sessions

All four regulars are heard in every recorded canon session, from Radford Horror 01 to Radford Horrors 04. The only canon session in which a regular's main character does not appear is Radford Horrors 02, where the Biz is a prisoner in Russia and Ezra plays Daniel Webster instead. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 04)

The non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable has a smaller cast: Andre running, Rita and Dante playing, and a guest commenting from the sidelines. Ezra and Zack are not in it. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.text:

docs.title: Uncertain speakers
docs.text: Five recordings come from a single mixed audio track, so it is not always certain which player is speaking: Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 04, Appalachia 04 and Appalachia 07. docs.title: Andre
docs.text:
Andre is the game master (Keeper) of PITF. He runs every recorded session, voices every NPC and monster, and narrates the campaign as if it were an early-1990s television show.

Role Game master (Keeper) Plays All NPCs and monsters Sessions All 37 recorded canon sessions and the one-shot First session Radford Horror 01

docs.title: The campaign as a TV show
docs.text:
Andre's defining habit is to describe the game as something being filmed. In the very first session he says "If this were a TV show, which let's say it is," and from then on scenes begin with "cut to", the camera zooms and pans, and nearly every session opens on a cold open that ends with "we cut to credits." (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 03, Appalachia 03)

The cold opens almost never feature the player characters. They show a victim, a villain or a place the party has not found yet: a pile of dog collars in the woods, a teenager burying cash, a worker attacked in a cave, rows of plastic-wrapped figures, a triangular craft buried in a Russian field. By Radford Horror 06 the players expect one and ask for it. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 06, Appalachia 02, Walkers 03, Radford Horrors 04)

He varies the device when it suits the story. Summer Service 06 intercuts two scenes with on-screen captions ("A few hours ago", "A few seconds from now"). Roulet Estate 01 is told out of order under title cards ("Inauguration Day, 1993", "78 days ago", "Present day."). Radford Horrors 01 opens with found footage and, for once, does not cut to credits until the end. He will also end on a cliffhanger on purpose: "I have an opportunity to end on a cliffhanger, so I'm gonna do it." (Summer Service 06, Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horror 04)

See The show for the full list of cold opens and framing devices.

docs.title: Sound and pictures
docs.text:
Andre scores the sessions. He plays intro music for the show, cues music from The Thing under a search and Psycho strings for a shock, and opens one session with the remark that "the producers of the show sprang for the rights to another song this time." He plays opera audio during the Boris Yeltsin scene. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)

He draws maps for the players on request, of varying quality: "All right, this is the worst map, but here you go." (Radford Horror 04)

docs.title: Period detail
docs.text: The campaign is set in 1992 and 1993, and Andre checks. He looks up when Crystal Pepsi went on sale and what Ross Perot sounded like ("I literally just looked up what Ross Perot sounds like"). When a detail turns out to be wrong for the year he changes it: a CD becomes a floppy disk, and the purple Game Boy he wanted for a lost child is dropped because "those won't be out for another four years." Players join in, and the anachronism check is a standing table ritual. (Radford Horror 01, Roulet Estate 03, Roulet Estate 01, Appalachia 03, Walkers 04)

docs.title: Improvisation
docs.text:
Andre runs from "a big Google Doc" and "a lot of fucking PDFs" and invents freely around them. Names are a known weak spot: he forgets or swaps NPC names often enough that it is a running joke, and several characters carry the scars as aliases (Esteban was also Alejandro and Jose; Deborah Wells was briefly Misabelle). Ezra's observation is that Andre does not use a name generator and that his names usually have "a joke to the name or a relevance to it"; Douglas Douglas is the standard example. (Radford Horror 01, Summer Service 04, Walkers 03, Appalachia 04, Radford Horror 07)

His most committed piece of improvised worldbuilding is the Spud Hut menu: about a hundred potato dishes, read aloud in full because the table refused to stop him. His verdict afterwards was "I should have prepared five hundred." (Appalachia 02)

He owns his mistakes on the recording ("I really gotta keep my notes in a more organized fashion") and corrects them in play, asking the table to "retcon that in your minds." (Walkers 04, Walkers 03)

docs.title: NPC voices
docs.text:
Andre voices the whole supporting cast, including every recurring NPC: Diane, Big Bill, Donald McManley and the campaign's versions of Ross Perot and Boris Yeltsin. Some that drew comment at the table:

  • Harvey the Great Dane, who backs up his owners' claims with "Woof." (Appalachia 01)
  • Ross Perot. Dante: "Why is Ross Perot a D&D goblin?" Andre: "Yeah, that's what he sounded like." (Roulet Estate 03)
  • The Rhode Island police, for which he stopped to ask the table what a Rhode Island accent sounds like. (Roulet Estate 02)
  • Robert Bigelow: "He almost got his own voice, and then I got lazy." (Walkers 02)
  • Yusuf Ansari, mid-scene: "I'm not doing his accent very well." (Walkers 08)
  • The creature in the storm, a fluting noise he could only perform after switching off his noise suppression. (Summer Service 06)

He also plays whole crowds at once, such as the Covenant members who each answer hygiene questions with "We're getting a boiler." (Appalachia 04)

docs.title: Secrets and private scenes
docs.text:
Andre keeps secrets between players. He removes people from the voice call for solo scenes, sends private messages and handouts, and lets players hold information their characters would not share. Ezra's whole KGB subplot for the Biz runs this way across several arcs. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 04, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06, Walkers 06)

The largest example is the Andrew Howard switch. In Walkers 07 he tells the table "I'm going to eject everybody except Andrew Howard," runs the gym scene alone with Rita, and ends it by telling her she is now playing a replica. Rita plays the copy in front of the other three players through Walkers 08 and into Walkers 09, when the reveal comes mid-scene. After the others leave Walkers 08 he runs one more private scene with Rita showing what happened to the real Andrew. (Walkers 07, Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Tone and danger
docs.text:
He warned the players early that Monster of the Week combat "tends to turn into like a slugging match where people die really quickly unless you're being kind of tactical about it," and he delivered on it at the church in Radford Horror 07, which Rita summed up as "we just half-TPK'd." Andre: "I wanted this to be a tense combat encounter." He is equally willing to shorten a fight when the fiction calls for it, ending Summer Service 06 early because the party was too sick to do more. (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 06)

He lets consequences stand. When the task force is disbanded he asks each player what their character does next and is ready to assign a fate to anyone without an idea; Ezra offers abduction or a life under the radar, and Andre sends the Biz to a Russian labor camp. (Roulet Estate 03)

docs.title: Rules
docs.text: Andre teaches the system as he goes in the early sessions, reading out question lists and explaining moves, and he adds to it. The dread track is his own import ("I'm borrowing it from some of the Lovecraft games"), introduced as a mystery mechanic: asked what dread is, he says "You don't know yet. Well, you're gonna find out." In later arcs Zack is the one who reminds him it exists. See Game mechanics for his rulings. (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Summer Service 03, Walkers 07, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Memorable rulings
docs.text:
• The Chevy Chase roll. In the first minutes of the campaign the players ask whether Chevy Chase is a guest star. Andre has them roll for it. The result is a mixed success. (Radford Horror 01)
  • Two questions for a 12. When Rita rolls a 12 on Investigate a Mystery and points out that the 12-plus result is an advanced move she has not unlocked, he answers "Well, you still get two." (Radford Horror 02)
  • Luck after the roll. Asked whether Luck can be spent once a bad roll is on the table: "Yeah, yeah, no, you are." (Appalachia 01)
  • A secret roll. He rolls Kurt's bluff against Jan Martense himself and keeps the result hidden: "That's not how we're doing this one. 'Cause it's more fun that way." (Appalachia 08)
  • Rolling for the NPC's plane. "I am gonna do something I haven't done before here, and I am going to roll for Freak and his maintenance of the Cessna." (Radford Horror 07)
  • The OVA. He decides "retroactively" that the one-shot, "the stupid fucking shonen arc we did," was an OVA Huell watched on hotel cable. (Appalachia 02)
  • No ear-gauge puck. Dante, still sore about it: "Andre wouldn't let me have the fucking ear gauge puck with, like, supplies hidden in it." (Radford Horror 07)
  • A perfect 12 or nothing. "If you roll a perfect 12 on a Sharp check, I will let you modify this thing to go faster. If you don't, you are going to either injure yourself or break it." (Roulet Estate 02)
  • Rolling for the players. When a player's dice roller is broken he rolls for them. (Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Table moments
docs.text:
• "For the sake of immersion, I have just eaten some McDonald's." (Summer Service 03)
  • Needing a school anthem on the spot, he had a chatbot write one and sang it in character. Dante: "Art is dead." (Walkers 04)
  • On the campaign as a whole: "It's an erotically charged campaign." (Walkers 09)
  • Forgot to start the recording, so Appalachia 02 opens in the middle of a recap. (Appalachia 02)
  • Briefly thought "we've been doing Investigate a Mystery wrong the whole time," then corrected himself. (Radford Horrors 01)
  • Told Ezra, who had forgotten the other FBI agents in their past cases: "There weren't." (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Dante
docs.text:
Dante plays Kurtis "Kurt" Leonard Larson, the task force's ex-CIA consultant, and the alien prince Derk in the non-canon one-shot.

Role Player Characters Kurt Larson; Derk (one-shot) Sessions All 37 recorded canon sessions and the one-shot First session Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Kurt Larson
docs.text: Dante has played Kurt in every recorded canon session. Kurt is an Expert: a Vietnam veteran and former CIA case officer from a unit called UTAW, on loan to the FBI, with an armory, a wheeled travel case and a contact for everything. Andre confirms the playbook at the table more than once ("you're the Expert, right?"). (Radford Horror 01, Appalachia 09, Walkers 04)

docs.title: Derk
docs.text: In Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable Dante plays Derk, a near-indestructible and very dim alien prince who was raised on scorpions and loves dogs and hot dogs. It is the opposite of Kurt in every respect. Dante admitted, "I really pushed all the onus of, like, actual thinking, planning onto Rita for this one," and Andre replied that "it's amazing how Derk being fucking stupid has dominated the tone of this one-shot." Derk's best roll of the session was a 15. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Procedure first
docs.text:
Dante plays Kurt as the person at the table who knows how the thing is actually done, and he brings the detail himself. Searches are run as an inverted wedge with every print photographed. Rooms are entered as a four-man stack. Caves are navigated by glow stick with a kneeling front rank. He lectures on the fatal funnel, calls for "Ear pro!" and has Kurt check a stopped car with a bare non-dominant hand. By Roulet Estate 03 Kurt is lecturing at Quantico, and the lecture is Dante's. (Appalachia 02, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 08, Walkers 03, Roulet Estate 03)

The same instinct makes him the party's usual lead in interviews, phone calls and crime scenes: the autopsy in Radford Horror 05, the Whateley break-in in Radford Horror 06, the arcade in Radford Horrors 03, most of the detective work in Radford Horrors 04. (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: The trunk
docs.text: Kurt's Preparedness move lets Dante produce gear on a roll, and he has used it to build the campaign's longest-running prop joke: a trunk containing stilts, wolf urine, waders, a wetsuit, a welding mask, a Super Soaker and, when challenged on any of it, the answer "Like, why wouldn't I?" The stilts keep coming back; in Utah Kurt says, "I had those stilts since Vietnam." Dante's more serious acquisitions include an M28 Davy Crockett and a P90. (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 04, Walkers 04)

docs.title: Tall tales
docs.text: Kurt's backstory is delivered as a stream of unverifiable anecdotes, most of them invented on the spot: three of Castro's body doubles, a dictator poisoned through a handshake, a tulpa summoning that may or may not have worked, four molars loaded with different drugs. Dante says outright when he is making something up: having Kurt reminisce about college in Appalachia 09, he admitted he could not "think of, like, a good plausible college right now." He also habitually adds small details to past scenes after the fact (Kurt was counting his paces all along). (Summer Service 04, Radford Horror 05, Walkers 01, Radford Horror 03, Appalachia 09, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 01)

docs.title: Arguing the fiction
docs.text: Dante pushes back when something seems implausible, in or out of character. He insists a Claymore and gunfire underground cannot go unheard, that forklifts are fast and ape-proof, and that a hostage taker run by the GM "knows everything the DM knows" and so should not be taken at his word. He predicted that a guide's plan had "too many steps for this to possibly go correctly" ("Statistics is against us"), and it did go wrong. He is still annoyed that a pharmacy once had a mobile phone and the team has never kept one. (Appalachia 08, Appalachia 09, Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Gallows humor
docs.text: His jokes are dry and usually land on Kurt's past or the party's condition: "Once immolated, twice shy"; "Ask your doctor if being worms is for you"; "We're switching the Biz to a different, higher-fiber wet food." His one-line summary of an entire arc finale was "Got the real Andrew back, fucking killdozered a community center." (Radford Horror 04, Summer Service 03, Radford Horror 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Signature moments
docs.text:
• Spitting LSD into Agent Murphy's mouth. Set on fire by Agent Murphy, Kurt bites his LSD tooth and spits it into his attacker's mouth. (Radford Horror 03)
  • "Aw heck." The first arc's climactic session cuts to black on Kurt's line. Dante's first pitch for it had been "I still love you." (Radford Horror 07)
  • The Davy Crockett. Dante burns a Luck point on Kurt's weapons contact and comes back with a tactical nuclear recoilless gun, then spends the finale teaching the rest of the party to fire it from the back seat of a stolen car. (Summer Service 04, Summer Service 06)
  • Women's-shelter cards. Kurt carries a stack and presses one on every Covenant member he meets. Andre loved the idea. (Appalachia 04)
  • The ape-whisperer. Underground and surrounded, Dante talks his way through with a ketamine-and-Combos plan, a hotwired forklift and three rolls of 11. (Appalachia 09)
  • "Parlez-vous français?" Faced with a coyote standing on two legs, Kurt throws baloney and tries a verbal flashbang. (Walkers 04)
  • The spear gun. Kurt is hassled over it at airport security, decides it would have "presence" in an interrogation room, and finally uses it to nail a rabid mouse to a motel floor. (Radford Horrors 02)
  • The Vietnam flashback. Digging in the Roulet basement, Kurt hallucinates a prison guard and empties his sidearm into the hole. (Roulet Estate 02)

docs.title: Dice
docs.text: Dante's luck runs in streaks. There is a run of 10s in Radford Horror 05, three 11s in Appalachia 09, and a night in Walkers 08 of which he says, "I've genuinely just been rolling really fucking good tonight." Against that: snake eyes in Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07 ("so I don't have a shovel") and Appalachia 03, and a 3 in Summer Service 01 greeted with "This keeps happening." He grumbles about his dice in Radford Horrors 01. (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 01, Appalachia 03, Appalachia 09, Walkers 08, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Attendance
docs.text: Dante is heard in every recorded canon session, Radford Horror 01 through Radford Horrors 04, and for the one-shot. Kurt has never been absent from a recorded session.

docs.title: Ezra
docs.text:
Ezra plays Dick "The Biz" Baxter, the task force's counterintelligence man, and from The Radford Horrors onward also plays Special Agent Daniel Webster. He is the only player with two characters in the main campaign.

Role Player Characters Dick "The Biz" Baxter; Daniel Webster Sessions All 37 recorded canon sessions First session Radford Horror 01

docs.title: The Biz
docs.text:
Ezra has played the Biz since the first session: a cynical, paranoid, chronically broke FBI counterintelligence agent with a nickname he enjoys ("I'm getting mileage out of the Biz"). Ezra asked how rolls worked in the first session. He had not planned a voice, said Australian was "like the only accent I can consistently pull off," and later settled on Columbo as the model ("You know what, Columbo is totally the voice"). (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 06)

Ezra's mental image of the character is the man "in every Japanese or Korean movie who's in his mid-40s and is fairly competent and maybe even somewhat likable," in fairly nice clothes but with a rough look: "someone who looks like he spent a lot of time in casinos." (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Daniel Webster
docs.text:
When the Biz's story took him to Russia, Ezra needed someone to play in Virginia. Asked for the new character's name at the table, he said, "Fuck me, I didn't actually come up with one," then "Daniel—Daniel Webster," and added, "I hope that that's not a real name of somebody." Webster is the Biz's opposite: a by-the-book agent who "looks about twenty-five percent more like a Fed than Andrew Howard" and suspects the old task force of having been a political dirty-work unit. Ezra plays him in "a normal, boring voice." (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02)

In Radford Horrors 02 Ezra plays only Webster. In Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 03 and Radford Horrors 04 he plays both, switching between the Biz's solo scenes in Russia and Webster's scenes with the party. (Radford Horrors 01, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 04)

Ezra has also named his next character in advance, should the Biz die: an Australian bush pilot. (Walkers 06)

docs.title: The secret keeper
docs.text:
More of Ezra's game happens off the recording than anyone else's. Andre passes him private notes, pulls him out of the call and sends him direct messages, because the Biz is carrying a plot the other characters do not know about: coded messages from Russian intelligence read through a Moby-Dick book cipher, a dead drop, a camera planted in a hotel room. Ezra kept it from the other players for whole arcs. They saw only the consequences, such as the Biz limping in with a twisted ankle and slept-in clothes. Andre, to the others: "you guys don't know, but Biz is just having a rough day." (Summer Service 04, Appalachia 01, Appalachia 02, Appalachia 06)

He uses the same channel to set things up himself, privately sending Andre a plan in Summer Service 03 and the idea for the Biz's Secret Santa gift in Roulet Estate 01 ("I just made Andre's life a little bit harder"). (Summer Service 03, Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: Choosing the hard road
docs.text: Ezra tends to pick the option that costs his character something. Asked what the Biz did after the task force was disbanded, he reasoned that this was the time for "consequences for, you know, fucking up the way that he did," offered Andre a choice between the Biz being abducted and living under the radar, and got abduction by the Russians. He burned three Luck points in a single action sequence to keep a president alive, leaving the Biz three short of doom, with the comment "Let's find out what Doomed does." (Roulet Estate 03, Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: The skeptic
docs.text: He plays the Biz as the party's doubter, and lets the doubt erode on schedule: "Do aliens climb trees?" in Radford Horror 05; "I now believe in aliens, and I hate them" two sessions later; and by the third arc, "before I joined this task force, my impression was that anybody who believes in any of this stuff is nuts." Webster restarts the cycle from zero. (Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 04, Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: "I'm gonna be that guy"
docs.text: Ezra is the table's most persistent fact-checker after Andre. He takes a sunset time to Wolfram Alpha ("All right, you know what? I am gonna be that guy") and prices the Spud Hut menu ("Expensive spud for 1992. Not gonna lie"). He also asks for "someone who's good at taking notes" when the decisions pile up. (Walkers 03, Appalachia 02, Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Jokes that do not land
docs.text: He commits to bits whether or not the table follows: "Three days out of a cave?", the dog-inbreeding saga of "Pimpy 3X," and "Is your name Frotter Cumsock?" In one early session he has Andre take his headphones off so that he can pitch a theory to the other players without the GM hearing it. (Summer Service 05, Appalachia 06, Radford Horror 02)

docs.title: Signature moments
docs.text:
• The toilet anaconda. The Biz's digestion is the campaign's first running gag, beginning with a corn dog in the first scene and ending, in Andre's words, when he is "finally able to dislodge a toilet anaconda." (Radford Horror 01)
  • Blinding the Moth. With no armor and no melee weapon, the Biz climbs the Radford Moth and gouges its eyes, then burns a Luck point to wake up afterwards. Ezra: "I'm gonna level up so hard if I live." (Radford Horror 07)
  • The party investigator. Two rolls of 14 on Investigate a Mystery at the lighthouse. (Summer Service 03)
  • Letterman. Ordered onto David Letterman's show as "the most hated cop in America," the Biz turns a failing roll into a 12 with Luck and comes out with an ally. (Walkers 01)
  • Know a guy. Two 12s in a row on the Biz's Fixer move produce a ground-penetrating radar and a bomb collar. (Walkers 04)
  • Through the ceiling. Hidden in a pharmacy's drop ceiling as the fail-safe, the Biz shoots first to save Kurt, is shot in the thigh and falls through. (Roulet Estate 03)
  • Saving Yeltsin. Alone in Russia, the Biz gets Boris Yeltsin out of an ambush and loses an eye doing it. (Radford Horrors 03)
  • Reading the title. Ezra speaks the name of the new arc over the credits: "The Radford Horrors." (Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Dice
docs.text:
Ezra's dice are extreme in both directions. He rolled double sixes in Radford Horror 03 ("Double sixes, baby") and Radford Horror 06, and a natural 12 for a total of 15 in Roulet Estate 01. He also failed so often in the first arc that his experience track overflowed: by Radford Horror 08 he was "marking X's over top of the X's" and one failed roll away from "a double level up." (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 06, Roulet Estate 01, Radford Horror 08)

Several late sessions found him without a working dice roller or without his sheet, so Andre or Zack rolled for him. In Radford Horrors 01 he announced that he had found his dice again. (Roulet Estate 03, Walkers 08, Radford Horrors 02, Radford Horrors 03, Radford Horrors 01)

docs.title: Attendance
docs.text: Ezra is heard in every recorded canon session. He is not in the one-shot. The Biz is missing from one session, Radford Horrors 02, where Ezra plays Webster.

docs.title: Guest players
docs.text:
Four guests sit in on the PITF recordings: Kira, Ben, Ethan and Matt. None of them plays a character in any recorded session. They listen in on the call, joke with the regular cast, and now and then nudge the game from the sidelines.

Guest Sessions Role at the table Kira 12 sessions across the first three arcs Commentator and fact-checker Ben 6 sessions across four arcs Listener, mostly muted Ethan 1 session A few out-of-character remarks Matt The one-shot Commentator

docs.title: Kira
docs.text:
Kira is the most frequent guest, heard in twelve sessions from the second episode of the campaign to the start of The Things in Appalachia: Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 04, Radford Horror 05, Radford Horror 06, Radford Horror 08, Summer Service 01, Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05, Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01 and Appalachia 02. She has no character of her own. She supplies facts, rules questions and jokes.

Her contributions:

  • Fact-checks. When the table confuses Amanda Lucky with a singer, she sorts it out: "Amanda Palmer is the musician." In the Marblehead finale she settles an argument about Utah's state motto: "I have found the motto on utah.gov. It is 'Industry.'" (Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 06)
  • Worm biology. During the worm arc she explains why adult chicken pox is dangerous and why the cure matters more "the greater your, like, parasitic load is." Her favorite fact came up often enough for Andre to keep count. Kira: "Have I told you about the bag of worm mutation in nematodes?" Andre: "You have. I think three or four times." (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 05)
  • Rules questions. She asks whether the Biz's bonus "for concealing evidence of a crime" applies, and whether anyone has a first aid kit. (Radford Horror 04, Summer Service 06)
  • Urging the party on. During the Whateley house search: "I'm trying to convince them to eat the root." (Radford Horror 06)
  • "Roll to eat pancakes." Her suggestion at the diner. (Radford Horror 05)
  • The dread answer. When Zack asks what the new dread mechanic is, she answers for Andre: "None of your business. The answer is none of your business. Take some." (Summer Service 03)
  • Lena Scott. Of the child Lena Scott: "I want to adopt her." Of another character in the same session: "I'd pet him." (Summer Service 03)
  • "Can I still come?" Asked when Andre was about to run a scene that some of the players were meant to stay out of. (Summer Service 01)
  • The warhead. Dante writes her into the back seat with the Davy Crockett: "Kira, you cuddle with the warhead in the backseat." This is the closest any guest comes to appearing in the fiction. (Summer Service 04)
  • Worm chowder. By the finale: "I have an intense urge to buy a bucket of nightcrawlers and make worm chowder." (Summer Service 06)
  • The smell check. "Did you just canonically smell that kid?" (Appalachia 01)

Her last recorded appearance is pre-game banter at the top of Appalachia 02, with advice on naming a pet: "decide how you would feel yelling it on your porch at 3 a.m." (Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Ben
docs.text:
Ben is heard in six sessions: Radford Horror 07, Summer Service 06, Appalachia 09, Walkers 01, Walkers 02 and Walkers 08. He is a listener more than a talker and is often muted.

  • Radford Horror 07, the church fight, is his most talkative session. He jokes along with the table, asks Rita whether Andrew is a cleric (her answer: "No. I'm an alien cultist"), and signs off with "This was really fun to watch." (Radford Horror 07)
  • In Summer Service 05 he joins the call late and is not heard. Andre greets him with "Hey, Ben, you've missed a bunch of really horrifying shit," and asks that nobody use the soundboard. (Summer Service 05)
  • In Summer Service 06 Andre tells him, "Ben, you are making horrible noises." Dante: "Well, it's hard to strangle a drifter quietly." Kira: "Mute yourself, Ben." (Summer Service 06)
  • In Appalachia 09 he asks the table one question during the last fight: "For reference, how much health do you guys have?" (Appalachia 09)
  • In Walkers 01: "I've been muted, but I laughed. It made me laugh pretty good." (Walkers 01)
  • In Walkers 02 he speaks once: "I like this man being like, 'Hey, I hear you have trauma. Let me ask you deep personal questions about it.'" (Walkers 02)
  • In Walkers 08 he is the only person besides Rita and Andre still on the call for the after-session scene that reveals what happened to the real Andrew Howard, and he asks Rita the obvious question: "So did you know what was happening this whole session?" The other three players had already left. (Walkers 08)

Zack also addresses him once in Summer Service 04 ("What was that, Ben?"), but Ben is not heard in that session. (Summer Service 04)

docs.title: Ethan
docs.text:
Ethan is heard briefly in the pre-game chat of Radford Horrors 02, where he sums up the real-world career of the arc's new FBI director: "Giuliani, he pioneered the perp walk and basically took down the Mafia and then lost his mind in the mid-2000s." (Radford Horrors 02)

He is also the subject of a joke in Appalachia 06, a session he is not heard in. Ezra: "For Ethan's sake, you're gonna have to give us the make and model of all of these air conditioners." Dante: "It's the only way Ethan will be satisfied." (Appalachia 06)

docs.title: Matt
docs.text: Matt is the guest for the non-canon one-shot Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable. He plays no character; he comments while Rita and Dante play ("That's just the plot of Hunter x Hunter"; "This man about to lose his life"). When the table debates whether the dog on Derk's hand-drawn flag is recognizable, Matt vouches for it: "Oh, that's a corgi, I promise." (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: What guests do not do
docs.text: No guest rolls dice for a character, takes a turn in a scene or appears in the fiction under a name in any recorded session. All of the campaign's player characters belong to the four regulars: see Cast and players.

docs.title: Rita
docs.text:
Rita plays Andrew Howard, the earnest, alien-believing leader of the task force. For part of The Walkers in Skin she secretly played a duplicate of him in front of the other players. She also plays Mirabeth in the non-canon one-shot.

Role Player Characters Andrew Howard; Andrew Howard (duplicate); Mirabeth (one-shot) Sessions All 37 recorded canon sessions and the one-shot First session Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Andrew Howard
docs.text:
Rita has played Andrew in every recorded canon session. He begins as an agent who is "34 and had no expectations of being a field agent," raised in a church that teaches about benevolent alien Masters, and put in charge of three men who all know the job better than he does. Asked by a guest whether Andrew is a cleric, Rita sums up the concept: "No. I'm an alien cultist." (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 07)

The character has changed more than any other. He started as a Divine, with healing hands and a satchel that holds whatever he needs. He died in a school gym in Utah and came back as something else: faster, stronger, hard to hurt and in need of blood. Rita rebuilt him on a new playbook, the Monstrous, and describes the result the same way she described the old one: "I'm just a beefy boy." (Walkers 08, Roulet Estate 01)

docs.title: The duplicate
docs.text: Rita played the real Andrew through the gym fight in Walkers 07, a scene Andre ran with the other three players out of the call. At the end of it he told her: "you are not in Andrew Howard's body. You are in a replica." She played the copy from then on, through all of Walkers 08 and the unrecorded session after it and into Walkers 09, behaving as the real Andrew would while quietly serving the copy's side. After Walkers 08 she listed some of what she had been doing "subtly": "I'm the one that stole the sugar from the break room." She also said she had tried "not to sabotage them too hard, because I don't think they'd enjoy that." The reveal came mid-scene in the finale, when Andre said, "Now that the game is up, Rita, let's swap back who we're controlling." (Walkers 07, Walkers 08, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Mirabeth
docs.text: In Philosopher's Fist 3.J/2: Unchainable Rita plays Mirabeth, a vain, scheming 72-year-old would-be mentor of heroes with godlike beauty and a talent for lying. Andre asked for an anime dub voice; Rita had only her one "old person voice" and used that. With Dante playing a character who could not count past ten, the thinking in that session fell to her. (Philosopher's Fist)

docs.title: Sincere and awkward
docs.text: Rita plays Andrew without irony. He shakes hands, says "sir" and "ma'am," tells strangers about spiritual frequencies, and cannot hide that he is a federal agent in any outfit, including a Bigfoot T-shirt. His Charm is negative and she leans on it: "It's just you can always tell there's something wrong with me." The rest of the table builds on what she gives them, with jokes about his striped pajamas, his three first names and his feminine looks, and she plays him as self-conscious about all of it ("Guys, I'm handsome, right?"). (Radford Horror 03, Appalachia 06, Appalachia 07, Appalachia 02, Walkers 03)

docs.title: The UFO file
docs.text:
Andrew's expertise is real because Rita's research is. Andre noticed in the first arc: "I like that Rita clearly has a list of UFO shapes." She has Andrew mutter about "the similarities to the Levelland case that happened in the '50s" and hold firm opinions about the Greys, and in the Utah finale she goes looking for a list of real cigar-shaped UFO sightings mid-session. (Radford Horror 04, Walkers 03, Roulet Estate 02, Walkers 09)

She is just as clear about where his knowledge ends: "I can't play a guy that knows cryptids 'cause I don't know any cryptids." (Appalachia 03)

docs.title: Knowing the rules
docs.text: Rita is the regular who knows the rulebook best. She pointed out in the second session that a 12-or-better result was an advanced move she had not unlocked yet ("That's an advanced move. I gotta unlock that"), and explains her own harm-negating moves to the table. She announces Andrew's upgrades herself: "I got another upgrade, so I reduce all damage by two now." (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 05, Roulet Estate 01, Appalachia 08)

docs.title: Playing the dreams straight
docs.text: A good deal of Andrew's story comes to Rita as private or solo material: dreams of grey visitors, a father who may be an alien and keeps trying to kiss him, a note left in his bed. She plays the fallout in character, with Andrew keeping the dreams from the team, and lets the table turn the alien-dad kiss into a running gag ("I wish my dad tulpa wouldn't try to kiss me so often"). (Summer Service 03, Walkers 06, Walkers 07, Radford Horrors 03)

docs.title: Signature moments
docs.text:
• Peeing in the sink. In the first session Andrew does this at headquarters on the grounds that "it's better to be assertive." (Radford Horror 01)
  • Laying on hands. Andrew's healing works for the first time on a burned Kurt, at the cost of a nosebleed that lasts into the next day. Rita plays him as "riding a spiritual high that I have never once experienced before, because that shit has never worked." (Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 04)
  • The 2. A roll of 2 on Act Under Pressure sends Andrew's holy weapon, a spray of "nothingness," through Kurt's hand. (Summer Service 05)
  • The decisive shot. In the Marblehead finale, after two failed rolls stuck in the mud, Rita's 8 with the flashlight weapon is the hit that counts. (Summer Service 06)
  • "Thank you for your time." Cornered by a news crew, Andrew says it, walks away, then turns round "very sweatily" to say it again. The clip is replayed on the news. (Appalachia 08)
  • Severing Big Bob's arm. Andrew drops to the back of the line to shield Huell, takes the hit, stands up and cuts through Big Bob's arm with his pepper spray. He keeps the hand. (Appalachia 09)
  • The d100 spud. Faced with the Spud Hut menu, Rita "rolled a d100" and had to work out "which one number twenty-nine was." (Appalachia 02)
  • The gym. Having banished something from an intruder with Cast Out Evil on a 12 earlier in the session, Andrew goes alone to a late-night meeting at the school gym, uses the move again in a panic on a 14, and does not come back. (Walkers 07)
  • Waking Wilbur. Andrew lays a hand on the catatonic Wilbur Whateley and brings him round. (Radford Horrors 04)
  • The wedgie. Near the end of the most recent recorded session Andrew lifts Kurt one-handed by the belt. Dante: "It's a hell of a wedgie, but I'm interrogation resistant, so it's okay." (Radford Horrors 04)

docs.title: Dice
docs.text: Rita's rolls are steadier than most (9, 10, 12 in Appalachia 03; a 12 in Appalachia 06), with a knack for the badly timed low one: the 2 in Summer Service 05, a 4 on a Help Out in Appalachia 09, and in Walkers 08 a 3 in the firefight, when the Andrew at the table was not the real one. In Walkers 07 she rerolled a cocked die and got a 13. (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 06, Summer Service 05, Appalachia 09, Walkers 08, Walkers 07)

docs.title: Attendance
docs.text: Rita is heard in every recorded canon session, Radford Horror 01 through Radford Horrors 04, and for the one-shot.

docs.title: Zack
docs.text:
Zack plays Huell Kendrick, the task force's veteran cop: a laconic, chain-smoking FBI agent with a large knife and the highest Cool in the party.

Role Player Characters Huell Kendrick Sessions All 37 recorded canon sessions First session Radford Horror 01

docs.title: Huell Kendrick
docs.text:
Zack has played Huell in every recorded canon session. Huell is a divorced career lawman from Louisiana who came into the first case assuming the missing girl was a runaway, and who has since been lifted by a UFO, filled with worms, bitten by a goose and shot in the foot by a man in an alien mask. Dante's description of his build, which Zack adopted, is "Disco Elysium skinny fat." (Radford Horror 01, Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 03, Walkers 03, Roulet Estate 03, Appalachia 03)

Zack is not in the one-shot, though Huell is its in-fiction audience: Andre ruled that the whole thing was an OVA Huell watched on hotel cable while falling asleep. (Philosopher's Fist, Appalachia 02)

docs.title: Deadpan
docs.text: Zack plays Huell dry. The humor is a cop's: blunt, tired and slightly rude to everyone. "Kid's dead, though. Here's the shoe." "Ma'am, it's Georgia. I understand." "Sir, sir, I am an officer. Do not touch me. I am listening to the menu." He asks odd questions at odd times ("Hey, Howard, you ever been shot?") and keeps Huell skeptical well past the evidence: after the rest of the party has seen a craft in the sky, Zack notes that Huell is "still not convinced. I wasn't in the car that saw it personally." (Appalachia 03, Appalachia 02, Radford Horror 03, Radford Horror 05)

docs.title: Choosing the interesting option
docs.text: Zack regularly picks the outcome that is worse for Huell and better for the scene. In the church fight he "was kinda hoping I'd get hit by it, 'cause it's more interesting," and Huell duly shot Andrew in the chest under mind control. Huell stays asleep through a team meeting "just because I think it's in character. To be shitty about it." Zack ruled that Huell "doesn't know how to ride a bike. I think that's funny," and played him as torn about taking the worm cure because of what the worms had done for him. (Radford Horror 07, Radford Horror 05, Walkers 04, Summer Service 03)

docs.title: Naming things
docs.text: Zack names Huell's things. The knife is Muriel, and Huell calls Nancy the goose "Betsy," a deliberate joke on Zack's part: the goose's name is Nancy. (Summer Service 05, Walkers 07)

docs.title: Cool under pressure
docs.text: Huell's Cool of +3 covers most of what Zack rolls, and he knows it: "I'm plus three on Cool, so I'm so fucking cool." He uses it to help other players, to give first aid, and to wait in the car as the party's "anti-rabbiter" in case a suspect bolts. Zack wants Huell to have cool slides and entrances, and holds his gun with the flashlight "cool-style." (Radford Horror 02, Radford Horror 06, Summer Service 05)

docs.title: Notes and catch-ups
docs.text:
Zack's notes are a table joke of their own. Andre said a page of them "lacks the quiet dignity of the string board"; Dante said it "looks like a page in the Necronomicon." Zack resolved to "keep better notes this time" at the start of the second arc. He is the player most likely to ask for a recap of what the party is doing and why, and he could not recall what he had named Huell's ex-wife and daughter when they came up. Andre: "Well, okay, we'll put a pin in that." (Radford Horror 03, Summer Service 01, Radford Horrors 04, Roulet Estate 01)

He is also the one who remembers the things Andre forgets. It was Zack who noticed the dread mechanic had gone missing, and who reminded Andre of it again in the next finale. (Walkers 07, Walkers 09)

docs.title: Signature moments
docs.text:
• Lifted by the craft. Huell grabs the figure in the spaceman suit, threatens it at knifepoint with his new move, clings on as the craft carries the figure off, and falls into the trees: four harm and a broken arm. (Radford Horror 06)
  • Shooting Howard. Mind-controlled at the church, Huell shoots Andrew in the chest, then cuts off the creature's leg with bolt cutters and takes a hit that fills every harm box. He is still bringing it up arcs later ("Howard, I shot you"). (Radford Horror 07, Appalachia 06)
  • Thanks, worms. Infected in Marblehead, Huell gets stronger, younger-looking and unable to sleep. Zack: "being a wormwolf sounds pretty cool." (Summer Service 03, Summer Service 04, Summer Service 05)
  • Toothbrush Man. A grudge against the hotel clerk Jester over toothbrushes pays off in the finale with a string of one-liners. (Summer Service 01, Summer Service 06)
  • Firing the nuke. After a round of rock-paper-scissors for the honor, Zack burns a Luck point to make the shot a clean hit, and asks for Huell "to sneeze suddenly, jerking the weapon in the wrong direction, to indicate the luck I just had." (Summer Service 06)
  • Double sixes, twice. Two rolls of double sixes in one session, the second for a total of 15. (Walkers 04)
  • Darts. He spends a Luck point to win a bar game of darts. Ezra: "All right, I appreciate blowing it on stupid shit." (Walkers 03)
  • Roseanne. After the task force is disbanded Huell ends up in front of Roseanne. Andre reminded Zack that Huell had once told McManley that "watching Roseanne was rock bottom for him." (Roulet Estate 03)
  • The grenade. In the Utah finale Huell throws a grenade "unusually far" into the middle of the machinery in the cavern. (Walkers 09)

docs.title: Dice
docs.text:
Zack's dice swing between sessions more than anyone's. Hot nights: an 11 and a 15 in Summer Service 05; double sixes twice in Walkers 04 ("I'm gonna get a lot of 12s today"); two 12s and two 14s in Walkers 09 ("Damn, I'm on fire today"); a streak of 11s in Roulet Estate 03 ("Man, I've been rolling good today"). Cold nights: Walkers 06, where he rolled double ones twice ("I'm not having good luck"). Huell was the first character to level up, in Radford Horror 03. (Summer Service 05, Walkers 04, Walkers 09, Roulet Estate 03, Walkers 06, Radford Horror 03)

He is heard spending Luck three times: on the nuke, on a failed attempt to charm Donald McManley, and on the darts. (Summer Service 06, Appalachia 01, Walkers 03)

docs.title: Attendance
docs.text: Zack is heard in every recorded canon session, Radford Horror 01 through Radford Horrors 04. He is not in the one-shot.
